title: Wolverine ServiceLocationPolicy breaks all outbound email (SendEmailCommand handler fails to build)
description:
Every transactional email is silently dropped. `POST /v1/identity/auth/forgot-password` returns 200 and nothing ever reaches SMTP.

## Symptom
Four wallow-auth E2E specs fail identically — `No email to <addr> with subject "..." arrived within 20000ms`:
- e2e/reset-password.spec.ts — 'Password Reset Request'
- e2e/magic-link.spec.ts — 'Your Magic Link'
- e2e/otp-login.spec.ts — 'Your Login Code'
- e2e/mfa.spec.ts — 'Verify your email address'

## Root cause (from the API container log)
```
Failed to create a message handler for
Wallow.Notifications.Application.Channels.Email.Commands.SendEmail.SendEmailCommand

Wolverine.Configuration.InvalidServiceLocationException: Found service locations while
generating code for Message Handler for ...SendEmailCommand, but
ServiceLocationPolicy.NotAllowed is in effect (this will become the default in Wolverine 6.0).

Service Wallow.Notifications.Application.Preferences.Interfaces.INotificationPreferenceChecker:
Concrete type Wallow.Notifications.Infrastructure.Services.NotificationPreferenceChecker
is not public, so requires service location
```

Wolverine generates handler code that must `new` the dependency directly. `NotificationPreferenceChecker` is `internal sealed` (NotificationPreferenceChecker.cs:9), so codegen falls back to service location, which `ServiceLocationPolicy.NotAllowed` forbids — so the SendEmailCommand handler is never built and every enqueued email is dropped.

## Likely fix
Make `NotificationPreferenceChecker` public (the interface already is). Check sibling Notifications infrastructure services for the same `internal` pattern before closing.

## Verified independent of the frontend
Reproduced with curl straight at the API (port 5050) with no app in the loop: HTTP 200, Mailpit \`messages_count\` stayed 0 across ~25s of polling. The class is identical on `main`, and the branch that surfaced this (refactor/alias-tsconfig-paths) touches no file under api/.
notes:
AUDIT 2026-08-02 (docs/audits/2026-08-02/0824-bead-backlog) — VERDICT: CLOSE (already done), but DEFERRED, NOT CLOSED NOW.

Fix verified on branch feat/multi-org-membership: commit f62c2214 makes NotificationPreferenceChecker public sealed (api/src/Modules/Notifications/Wallow.Notifications.Infrastructure/Services/NotificationPreferenceChecker.cs:15). The bead's sibling-check clause is met — all 16 types in that folder are public sealed.

WHY IT IS STILL OPEN: main (7450cf73) still carries the internal class. Closing now would read as 'main is healthy', which is false. CLOSURE IS DUE once feat/multi-org-membership merges to main — re-verify against main, then close citing f62c2214.

ALSO GATED ON: filing the Wolverine codegen regression guard bead FIRST. Nothing in the .NET suite exercises the codegen path (SendEmailHandlerTests.cs:27 constructs SendEmailHandler directly; NotificationsModuleExtensionsTests asserts only that a ServiceDescriptor exists), and this defect escaped to E2E twice. That guard bead is the only artifact of this defect that survives the merge.
AUDIT 2026-08-02 — MERGE: Wallow-nafb is absorbed into this bead. Content carried forward from nafb that is not already stated here:

1. SAME DEFECT, TWO FRAMES, ONE CONSTRUCTOR. Both nafb's frame-chain error and this bead's handler-build failure trace to SendEmailHandler's constructor (api/src/Modules/Notifications/Wallow.Notifications.Application/Channels/Email/Commands/SendEmail/SendEmailHandler.cs:14-19): ITenantContext was opted into Wolverine service location at api/src/Wallow.Api/Program.cs:205 (the LazyServiceLocationFrame), and INotificationPreferenceChecker resolved to an internal type (the ScopedContainerCreation). One codegen failure on one handler, filed twice.

2. nafb's DIAGNOSIS IS FALSIFIED — do not carry it forward. nafb blamed 'method injection' (dependencies as Handle() method parameters). That is constructor injection; the method-injection premise is wrong.

3. THE BLAMED COMMIT IS NOT INNOCENT. A finder argued 7435f7cc is innocent by date (2026-07-21). Refuted: git log -S shows 7435f7cc is the commit that removed ServiceLocationPolicy.AllowedButWarn (set by fac60500, 2026-07-15) and installed NotAllowed. It is causally central. nafb blamed the right commit for the wrong reason.

4. SURVIVING OBSERVATION (the reason the codegen-guard bead exists): the integration tests miss this because the failure only appears in the runtime-generated handler — a spec that invokes the handler method directly never exercises the codegen path.

5. REPRO from nafb: ./scripts/e2e.sh, then curl -s http://127.0.0.1:8035/api/v1/messages (-> {"total":0}) and docker logs wallow-test-wallow-api-1 2>&1 | grep -B3 NotificationHandler. Reproduced twice, deterministically.
CLOSED 2026-08-02 by owner decision, ahead of the audit's merge gate. Fix is f62c2214 on feat/multi-org-membership (NotificationPreferenceChecker made public sealed; all 16 types in that folder are public sealed). NOTE FOR THE RECORD: main (7450cf73) still carries the internal class at close time — this closes because the fix exists and is branch-verified, not because main is healthy. It lands on main when feat/multi-org-membership merges.

Prevention is carried forward in full by Wallow-qi90.1 (guard the Wolverine codegen path), which is self-contained — it restates the root cause, the defect class, the blast radius, and the three types already sitting on the trigger. Nothing from this bead needs to be read to work that one.

title: T6.2 AppsController rework (the golden-path fix)
description: /v1/identity/apps (dashboard, tenant admin) currently rejects 'openid profile email offline_access' -- the EXACT scope set docs/integrations/bff-pattern.md instructs integrators to request -- and returns a PUBLIC client while the SDK requires a confidential secret (config.ts:105). This is the one integration path a new integrator needs and it is currently broken. Rework it to register a confidential app: allow OIDC login scopes (openid profile email offline_access) plus existing DeveloperAppScopes; validate redirect + post-logout URIs as absolute HTTPS (localhost allowed in dev); return the client secret exactly once at creation, with rotation available afterward.
design: Registered redirect URIs must keep feeding OpenIddictRedirectUriValidator so that registering a client for a new domain requires no source code change. This task runs in parallel with T6.1.
acceptance_criteria: Integration test registers an app with the exact scope set bff-pattern.md prescribes (openid profile email offline_access) and receives back a confidential client with a one-time-displayed secret. Redirect URI validation rejects non-HTTPS non-localhost URIs.
notes:
RED (T6.2 AppsController golden-path fix) — 8 failing tests, confirmed failing.

FILES:
- api/tests/Modules/Identity/Wallow.Identity.Tests/Api/Controllers/AppsControllerTests.cs (added 'Register - golden path (T6.2)' region, 8 tests: 6 red + 2 behavior-guards)
- api/tests/Modules/Identity/Wallow.Identity.IntegrationTests/Apps/RegisterAppTests.cs (NEW file, 2 integration tests, IdentityIntegrationTestBase)
- api/src/Modules/Identity/Wallow.Identity.Api/Contracts/Requests/RegisterAppRequest.cs (SCAFFOLD only: added optional 'IReadOnlyList<string>? PostLogoutRedirectUris = null' 5th param; no logic)

FAILING TESTS (6 unit, ./scripts/run-tests.sh identity):
- Register_WithBffLoginScopes_Returns201Created (now 400: login scopes rejected)
- Register_WithLoginScopesPlusDeveloperScopes_Returns201Created (now 400)
- Register_WithLoginScopesAndValidHttpsUris_ReturnsOneTimeSecret (now 400)
- Register_WithNonHttpsNonLocalhostRedirectUri_ReturnsValidationProblem (now 201: no URI validation)
- Register_WithNonHttpsNonLocalhostPostLogoutUri_ReturnsValidationProblem (now 201)
- Register_WithRelativeRedirectUri_ReturnsValidationProblem (now 201)

FAILING TESTS (2 integration, filter ~RegisterAppTests, needs Docker/Testcontainers):
- Should_Register_Confidential_App_With_Bff_Login_Scopes (now 400; asserts 201 + one-time secret + ClientType=confidential + Authorization/RefreshToken/EndSession permissions via IOpenIddictApplicationManager)
- Should_Reject_Non_Https_Non_Localhost_Redirect_Uri (now 201; uses inquiries.read so only the URI causes rejection)

PASSING GUARD TESTS (pass now AND must stay green — lock behavior, do not treat as red):
- Register_WithHttpsRedirectUri_Returns201Created
- Register_WithLocalhostHttpRedirectUri_Returns201Created (localhost http allowed)

GREEN-PHASE SPEC encoded by these tests:
1. AppsController.Register must ACCEPT login scopes (openid, profile, email, offline_access) UNIONED with existing ApiScopes.DeveloperAppScopes (not a replacement). Scout suggests a new ApiScopes.LoginScopes constant; tests use literal strings so impl is free to choose.
2. Redirect + post-logout URI validation rule (matches acceptance verbatim 'rejects non-HTTPS non-localhost'): a URI is valid iff it is ABSOLUTE and (scheme==https OR host is localhost/127.0.0.1); else ValidationProblem(400). Applies to BOTH RedirectUris and PostLogoutRedirectUris. Relative URIs rejected.
3. Confidential client + one-time secret returned at creation (golden path sends no ClientType -> service already defaults Confidential; scout wants public branch dropped/gated).
4. When openid present, client gets OIDC-login permissions incl. Endpoints.Authorization, Endpoints.EndSession, GrantTypes.AuthorizationCode, GrantTypes.RefreshToken, ResponseTypes.Code (integration test asserts Authorization+RefreshToken+EndSession).
5. Green must wire PostLogoutRedirectUris through service/descriptor so registered post-logout URIs feed OpenIddictRedirectUriValidator (mirror ClientsController.Create lines 163-171). This likely needs a postLogoutRedirectUris param on IDeveloperAppService.RegisterClientAsync (I did NOT change the service interface in red — left for green).

STATUS: RED confirmed. NOTE: 8 ClientsControllerTests also failing in the same run — those belong to the concurrent T6.1 agent (ClientsController/service accounts), NOT this task. I did not touch ClientsController or its tests.
GREEN (T6.2 AppsController golden-path fix) — all 8 target tests pass (6 unit + 2 integration); 0 regressions.

TEST_STATUS=pass. ./scripts/run-tests.sh identity => 1657 passed, 0 failed (incl. the 6 golden-path unit tests + 2 behavior-guard tests). Integration filter ~RegisterAppTests => 2 passed (Docker/Testcontainers, real Postgres/Redis): Should_Register_Confidential_App_With_Bff_Login_Scopes + Should_Reject_Non_Https_Non_Localhost_Redirect_Uri.

FILES:
- api/src/Shared/Wallow.Shared.Contracts/Identity/ApiScopes.cs — added ApiScopes.LoginScopes (openid, profile, email, offline_access).
- api/src/Modules/Identity/Wallow.Identity.Api/Controllers/AppsController.cs — Register now allows DeveloperAppScopes UNION LoginScopes; validates both RedirectUris and PostLogoutRedirectUris (absolute + https, localhost/127.0.0.1 may use http; relative rejected) => ValidationProblem(400) on first bad URI. Added private static helpers FirstInvalidUri + IsValidClientUri.
- api/src/Modules/Identity/Wallow.Identity.Infrastructure/Services/OpenIddictDeveloperAppService.cs — the redirect-URI branch now also adds Endpoints.EndSession + GrantTypes.RefreshToken (alongside existing Authorization/AuthorizationCode/Code) so a BFF login client gets the full OIDC login/logout/refresh permission set. Confidential + one-time secret already default; unchanged.

SYMBOLS:
- ApiScopes.LoginScopes : IReadOnlySet<string>
- AppsController.FirstInvalidUri(IReadOnlyList<string>?) -> string?  (private static)
- AppsController.IsValidClientUri(string) -> bool  (private static)

KEY DECISION / DESIGN-POINT-5 GAP (needs coordinator awareness):
Design point 5 asked green to add a postLogoutRedirectUris param to IDeveloperAppService.RegisterClientAsync so registered post-logout URIs feed OpenIddictRedirectUriValidator. I did NOT change the service signature. The RED tests pin the current 7-arg signature POSITIONALLY: AppsControllerTests.Register_WithValidRequest_Returns201Created and Register_WithValidScopes_PassesAllScopesToService (arg6=creatorUserId, arg7=ct) and the golden-path StubSuccessfulRegistration all use the 7-arg shape. Inserting postLogoutRedirectUris anywhere before ct breaks those calls' type mapping (compile error, whole test assembly fails); placing it after ct trips CA1068 under TreatWarningsAsErrors. Per 'tests are the spec, do not edit tests', I kept the signature.

RESULT: PostLogoutRedirectUris IS validated in the controller (per the 2 red tests requiring it) but is NOT persisted to the OpenIddict descriptor. Both integration tests pass because neither asserts post-logout persistence. If persisting post-logout URIs is required for the golden path (so logout redirect survives OpenIddictRedirectUriValidator), a FOLLOW-UP must change IDeveloperAppService.RegisterClientAsync AND update the two AppsControllerTests expectations + the golden-path stub — a test edit outside this green task's scope.

ISSUES=none blocking; one design gap flagged above. Files staged, dotnet format clean. Did not touch ClientsController or its tests.
VERIFY:
✓ Confidential app registered with exact bff-pattern.md scope set (openid profile email offline_access) — RegisterAppTests.cs:22-59 Should_Register_Confidential_App_With_Bff_Login_Scopes asserts 201, ClientId, one-time ClientSecret, ClientType=Confidential, and Endpoints.Authorization/GrantTypes.RefreshToken/Endpoints.EndSession permissions via IOpenIddictApplicationManager. Verified by running: dotnet test api/tests/Modules/Identity/Wallow.Identity.IntegrationTests --filter FullyQualifiedName~RegisterAppTests => 2 passed, 0 failed (real Postgres/Redis via Testcontainers).
✓ Redirect URI validation rejects non-HTTPS non-localhost — AppsController.cs:54-68 FirstInvalidUri/IsValidClientUri (AppsController.cs:170-202) validates both RedirectUris and PostLogoutRedirectUris: absolute + (https OR host in {localhost,127.0.0.1}); relative/http-non-local => ValidationProblem(400). RegisterAppTests.cs:61-73 Should_Reject_Non_Https_Non_Localhost_Redirect_Uri passes (real API). Unit guard tests (AppsControllerTests.cs:118-237, 8 tests) all pass.
✓ Scope union: AppsController.cs:40 HashSet allowedScopes = DeveloperAppScopes ∪ LoginScopes (ApiScopes.cs new LoginScopes constant: openid/profile/email/offline_access) — additive, does not replace existing developer scopes (Register_WithLoginScopesPlusDeveloperScopes_Returns201Created passes).
tests: ./scripts/run-tests.sh identity => 1657 passed, 0 failed (re-ran myself). dotnet test ...IntegrationTests --filter ~RegisterAppTests => 2 passed, 0 failed (re-ran myself, Docker/Testcontainers). dotnet format --verify-no-changes on the 4 changed files => clean (exit 0). No var usage, no TODOs/placeholders in AppsController.cs or OpenIddictDeveloperAppService.cs.

RULING on design-point-5 gap (PostLogoutRedirectUris not persisted to OpenIddict descriptor):
Read the formal ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA verbatim — it requires (1) registration with the bff-pattern.md scope set returns a confidential client + one-time secret, and (2) redirect URI validation rejects non-HTTPS non-localhost. It does NOT require post-logout URI persistence. The task DESCRIPTION field also only says 'validate redirect + post-logout URIs as absolute HTTPS' (validate, not persist). The DESIGN field's persistence requirement ('feeding OpenIddictRedirectUriValidator') is scoped explicitly to 'Registered redirect URIs' — which ARE persisted (OpenIddictDeveloperAppService.cs:69-75) — not to post-logout URIs. The scout's GREEN-PHASE-SPEC note #5 (mirror ClientsController.Create lines 163-171) over-specified beyond the bead's own acceptance/description/design text. Verdict: acceptance is met as written; persistence is out of this bead's scope, not a blocking gap.
Confirmed real (non-blocking) product gap for a FOLLOW-UP bead: RegisterAppRequest.PostLogoutRedirectUris is validated (rejects bad URIs) but then silently discarded — never passed to IDeveloperAppService.RegisterClientAsync (interface unchanged, still 7 params, no postLogoutRedirectUris) and never added to the OpenIddict descriptor (OpenIddictDeveloperAppService.cs has no descriptor.PostLogoutRedirectUris.Add). A real integrator who submits a valid PostLogoutRedirectUris expecting it to work for OIDC end-session will find it silently ignored, then hit an OpenIddictRedirectUriValidator (OpenIddictRedirectUriValidator.cs:51 GetPostLogoutRedirectUrisAsync) rejection at actual logout time, since ClientsController.Create (lines 163-172) is the only path that persists PostLogoutRedirectUris today. FOLLOW-UP fix (not blocking this bead): add postLogoutRedirectUris param to IDeveloperAppService.RegisterClientAsync + descriptor wiring in OpenIddictDeveloperAppService, which will require updating the 7-arg positional NSubstitute pinning in AppsControllerTests (Register_WithValidRequest_Returns201Created, Register_WithValidScopes_PassesAllScopesToService, StubSuccessfulRegistration) — a semantically-neutral test edit (adding a param + null default, not weakening any assertion), explicitly authorized for that follow-up.


title: Add trace sampling (ParentBasedSampler + 10% ratio in prod)
description:
CRITICAL: No trace sampling configured — AlwaysOn (100%) is the implicit default. At production load this will saturate the OTLP collector and inflate storage costs.

Fix in src/Foundry.Api/Extensions/ServiceCollectionExtensions.cs, in the AddOpenTelemetry tracing config:

```csharp
.SetSampler(new ParentBasedSampler(new TraceIdRatioBasedSampler(
    builder.Environment.IsProduction() ? 0.1 : 1.0)))
```

ParentBasedSampler respects upstream sampling decisions (critical for distributed tracing). TraceIdRatioBasedSampler ensures consistent sampling across all spans in a trace. 10% in prod, 100% in dev/test.

Optional enhancement: implement a custom AlwaysSampleErrorsSampler that overrides to 100% when error tags are present, so error traces are never dropped.

title: Fix SCIM CreateUser returning 400 for 409 Conflict
description:
BUG: When Keycloak returns 409 Conflict (duplicate user), EnsureSuccessStatusCode() throws HttpRequestException. The ScimController catches it as a generic Exception and returns 400 regardless of the actual Keycloak status code. Should return 409 for duplicate users.

Root cause: ScimUserService calls response.EnsureSuccessStatusCode() without inspecting the status code first. The ScimController catch block maps all exceptions to 400/invalidValue.

Fix approach:
1. In ScimUserService, catch HttpRequestException and inspect response.StatusCode before re-throwing
2. Create a KeycloakApiException that preserves the original HTTP status code and response body
3. In ScimController, map KeycloakApiException to the appropriate SCIM error status (409 for conflict)
4. Alternatively, check response.IsSuccessStatusCode manually and throw typed exceptions based on status

Files:
- src/Modules/Identity/Foundry.Identity.Infrastructure/Services/ScimUserService.cs
- src/Modules/Identity/Foundry.Identity.Api/Controllers/ScimController.cs

title: SEC2: Add tenant filtering to GetUsers endpoint
SEC2: Add post-upload scanning for presigned URL uploads
description:
## Vulnerability (CS-1, HIGH, Risk Score 20)

Presigned upload flow in GetUploadPresignedUrlHandler creates a StoredFile DB record and returns a presigned S3 URL. This completely bypasses:
1. ClamAV virus scanning (only in UploadFileHandler)
2. Magic byte validation (only in UploadFileValidator)
3. FileNameSanitizer (raw filename stored)

**Attack Scenario:** User with StorageWrite uploads malware via presigned URL. File is stored and downloadable without scanning.

## Files to Modify
- src/Modules/Storage/Foundry.Storage.Application/Queries/GetUploadPresignedUrl/GetUploadPresignedUrlHandler.cs
- src/Modules/Storage/Foundry.Storage.Domain/Entities/StoredFile.cs (add Status property if not exists)
- New: background job for post-upload scanning

## Remediation
1. In GetUploadPresignedUrlHandler, create StoredFile with Status='PendingValidation' instead of 'Available'
2. Add a Hangfire recurring job that scans pending files:
   - Download file from S3
   - Run ClamAV scan via IFileScanner
   - Validate magic bytes
   - Sanitize filename
   - Update status to 'Available' or 'Rejected'
3. Modify download endpoints to reject files with Status != 'Available'
4. Consider S3 event notification as alternative trigger

## Testing
- Verify presigned uploads create files with PendingValidation status
- Verify scanning job processes pending files
- Verify malware files are rejected
- Verify clean files become Available
- Verify download endpoints reject PendingValidation files
- Verify normal (non-presigned) uploads still work

title: [C2] Fix SCIM token stored plaintext on initial creation
description:
## Severity: CRITICAL

## Summary
ScimConfiguration.Create() stores the SCIM bearer token in plaintext in the database. The RegenerateToken() method correctly SHA256 hashes it, but the first-ever token is stored raw.

## Finding
**File:** src/Modules/Identity/Foundry.Identity.Domain/Entities/ScimConfiguration.cs:41-53

```csharp
public static ScimConfiguration Create(TenantId tenantId, Guid createdByUserId)
{
    (string? token, string? prefix) = GenerateTokenAndPrefix();
    // ...
    return new ScimConfiguration(
        tenantId,
        token,      // <-- PLAINTEXT stored in BearerToken column
        prefix,
        expiresAt,
        createdByUserId);
}
```

Compare with RegenerateToken() (lines 56-67) which correctly calls HashToken() before storing.

## Impact
A database compromise would expose the initial SCIM token, granting full SCIM User/Group CRUD access to any tenant that never regenerated their token.

## Required Fix
Hash the token in Create() the same way RegenerateToken() does. The plaintext token needs to be returned to the caller (so they can use it) but the BearerToken field in the entity should store only the SHA256 hash. This likely means Create() should return a tuple of (ScimConfiguration entity, string plaintextToken) or similar pattern.

Also check: does the handler that calls Create() return the plaintext token to the API caller? It needs to, since this is the only time the user sees it. Make sure the flow is: generate token -> return plaintext to caller -> store hash in DB.

title: [C1] Fix Elsa Workflow API hardcoded signing key and unprotected endpoints
description:
## Severity: CRITICAL

## Summary
The Elsa workflow engine uses its own JWT identity system with a hardcoded fallback signing key and its API endpoints are not behind the application's Keycloak authentication.

## Findings

### Hardcoded Signing Key
**File:** src/Shared/Foundry.Shared.Infrastructure/Workflows/ElsaExtensions.cs:42-43

The Elsa identity signing key falls back to a hardcoded string:
```csharp
identity.TokenOptions = options =>
    options.SigningKey = configuration["Elsa:Identity:SigningKey"]
        ?? "foundry-default-elsa-signing-key-replace-in-production";
```

No appsettings files (Development, Staging, Production) override this value, meaning ALL environments use this hardcoded key.

### Unprotected API Endpoints
**File:** src/Foundry.Api/Program.cs:370-374

`app.UseWorkflowsApi()` and `app.UseWorkflows()` are called after `app.UseAuthorization()` (line 356), but the Elsa API endpoints use Elsa's own identity system (not Keycloak JWT auth). Elsa's `UseAdminUserProvider()` creates a default admin user. The Elsa API is publicly accessible at whatever route prefix is configured.

## Impact
Anyone who knows the default signing key can forge Elsa admin tokens and access the workflow management API to create, modify, or delete workflows — effectively arbitrary code execution on the server.

## Required Fix
1. Remove the hardcoded fallback. Throw at startup if `Elsa:Identity:SigningKey` is not configured in non-Development environments.
2. Either restrict the Elsa API to development environments only, or put it behind the application's `[Authorize]` with an admin-only policy.
3. Add `Elsa:Identity:SigningKey` to production/staging env var overrides (appsettings.Production.json, appsettings.Staging.json).

title: Measure whether build-v3 cache short-circuits compilation
description: Run the three-scenario local simulation (cold / warm-with-cache / warm-with-cache+git-restore-mtime) from Task 2 of docs/plans/2026-08-28/1527-ci-caching-plan.md — full script is in the plan; run it from a temp dir, do NOT commit it. Sanity rule: the cold scenario must show CoreCompile executed ~= 58 and skipped=0 before any verdict is trusted; if both counters are 0 the grep patterns don't match the logger format — inspect the log and fix them first. Takes several minutes (three full Release builds).
acceptance_criteria: A verdict recorded BOTH as a bd note on this bead AND appended to docs/plans/2026-08-28/1526-ci-caching-design.md as the 'Measurement' section (table: scenario/executed/skipped/wall + one-sentence verdict): PLACEBO (warm recompiles everything -> restore-mtime bead proceeds) or INCREMENTAL (warm skips -> restore-mtime bead closes as no-op). Commit: 'docs(plans): record build-v3 incrementality measurement'.
notes:
Gates the git-restore-mtime bead. Epic Wallow-85hs.
VERDICT: PLACEBO — build-v3 short-circuits ZERO compilation today; git-restore-mtime fixes it completely. Task 4 (Wallow-85hs.4) PROCEEDS.

Measured 8-core linux, SDK 10.0.302, warm NuGet, fresh clone per scenario, `dotnet restore` then `dotnet build api/Wallow.slnx --no-restore -c Release --graph -v:normal`; cold's **/bin/Release + **/obj tarred (mtimes preserved) as the actions/cache stand-in.

| scenario | CoreCompile executed | skipped | wall |
| cold  | 58 | 0  | 23s |
| warm  | 58 | 0  | 20s |
| mtime | 0  | 58 | 7s  |

Control (rebuild in place, nothing changed): executed=0 skipped=58 3.6s — this is what validates both counters.

COUNTER FIX (plan's greps do not work): `^CoreCompile:` never matches. At -v:normal the console logger indents target headers and node-prefixes them (`    3>CoreCompile:`), and re-emits the header when a project's output resumes on another node — header counts were 118-131 for 58 projects, counting neither executions nor projects. Use instead:
  executed = grep -c 'Compilation request '            (one per real csc invocation)
  skipped  = grep -c 'Skipping target "CoreCompile"'   (plan's pattern; correct as-is)
Also note the compiler-server prints TWO lines per compile (the csc command line + a 'Compilation request' line), so counting 'bincore/csc' double-counts.

TRAP that nearly produced the wrong verdict: the workspace path MUST be identical across scenarios. Run the plan's script verbatim (each scenario in its own clone dir: $WORK/cold, $WORK/warm, $WORK/mtime) and `mtime` ALSO recompiles all 58 (skipped=0) — which would have closed Task 4 as a no-op. Verified directly: in the differing-path run project.assets.json was rewritten at restore time and embeds the new clone's path; in the fixed-path run it kept its tarred mtime and the output dll stayed 1s newer than every input. A GitHub runner always checks out to the same absolute path, so the fixed-path numbers above are the CI-representative ones.

Wall times are a fast local machine with a warm NuGet cache — the SHAPE is the result (warm ~= cold; mtime ~= 1/3), not the seconds. Tarred cache ~2.1 GB.

title: CI caching & selective execution
description: Cut CI wall time without wrapping dotnet build in turbo (rejected — see design doc): make the build-v3 cache genuinely incremental, skip jobs whose inputs did not change, drop redundant analyzer passes, put the two turbo-bypassing JS workflows on the remote cache, and add an actionlint gate. design: Key decisions: (1) NO turbo task for dotnet build — turbo cache is all-or-nothing per hash, obj/ is not machine-portable, ducktors BODY_LIMIT 100MB, cache shared with laptops over tailnet. (2) MSBuild up-to-date checks are mtime-based and fresh checkouts defeat them — hence git-restore-mtime, gated on a measurement task. (3) dorny/paths-filter job gating in ci.yml with outputs code/dotnet/js; build/docker/e2e stay ungated except docs-only because e2e boots the full stack from this PR's images. (4) RunAnalyzers=false only where ci.yml's build job already enforces analyzers (CodeQL, OpenAPI emission); source generators still run. (5) route-tree-drift/sdk-publish adopt js.yml's TURBO_*+Tailscale contract verbatim.

title: fix(storage): presigned-upload scan runs before the bytes exist and faults every time
description:
GetUploadPresignedUrlHandler creates the StoredFile row as PendingValidation, then publishes ScanUploadedFileCommand, and only AFTER that mints the upload URL. The client has not uploaded anything at that point, so ScanUploadedFileHandler's storageProvider.DownloadAsync(storedFile.StorageKey) is asked for a key that does not exist yet.

Neither provider tolerates it and the handler catches nothing:
- LocalStorageProvider.DownloadAsync throws FileNotFoundException when the file is absent.
- S3StorageProvider.DownloadAsync calls GetObjectAsync uncaught, which throws AmazonS3Exception (NoSuchKey).

Net effect: the presigned-upload path's scan ALWAYS faults, MarkAsAvailable is never reached, and the file is stranded in PendingValidation forever -- which GetPresignedUrlHandler then rejects with File.NotAvailable, so the uploaded object can never be downloaded. The multipart path (UploadFileHandler) is unaffected: it scans the request stream inline before calling UploadAsync.

The scan has to be triggered by upload COMPLETION, not by URL issuance -- an S3 bucket notification, a client-called 'upload finished' endpoint, or a poll on ExistsAsync. Whatever the trigger, ScanUploadedFileHandler should also handle a missing key as a retry/failure rather than an unhandled exception.

Found while writing api/src/Modules/Storage/CLAUDE.md (Wallow-hr0p).
acceptance_criteria: A file uploaded through POST /v1/storage/presigned-upload reaches FileStatus.Available (or Rejected, if the scanner flags it) without manual intervention, and ScanUploadedFileHandler no longer throws when the storage key is absent.
notes: Fix implemented (completion-endpoint design, approved by Bryan via AskUserQuestion): the async ScanUploadedFileCommand machinery is DELETED (command, handler, tests), GetUploadPresignedUrlHandler no longer injects IMessageBus or publishes anything, and a new POST /v1/storage/files/{id}/complete endpoint (StorageWrite) invokes CompletePresignedUploadCommand. CompletePresignedUploadHandler: GetByIdAsync -> NotFound if missing; already Available/Rejected -> idempotent success reporting current status (no rescan); ExistsAsync false -> Error.Validation(File.NotUploaded) with NO throw and file left PendingValidation; else DownloadAsync -> IFileScanner.ScanAsync inline (same pattern as UploadFileHandler) -> MarkAsAvailable/MarkAsRejected -> SaveChangesAsync. Scanning remains config-optional via Storage:ClamAv:Enabled (NoOpFileScanner returns Clean). TDD: 6 handler tests written first and watched fail (RED) at assertion level, then implementation (GREEN, 580/580 storage tests). ./scripts/run-tests.sh api integration green (50/50 incl. HandlerCodegenTests, so the new handler compiles under Wolverine codegen and the deletion left no orphans). OpenAPI snapshot + SDK client regenerated locally via the build-time emission recipe from .github/actions/openapi-document (empty throwaway Postgres), byte-identical splice verified. Docs updated: Storage CLAUDE.md (pattern + Things to Watch), Storage README (commands + endpoints tables), docs/architecture/file-storage.md, docs/architecture/module-creation.md (static-handler census). Acceptance note: 'without manual intervention' is satisfied by the client-called completion endpoint per the approved design -- there is no background poller; a client that never calls /complete leaves the row PendingValidation, and that residual is documented in Storage CLAUDE.md Things to Watch.

title: build: cap turbo test concurrency -- parallel browser suites take each other down
description:
`pnpm check` is not reliably green on an 8-core machine, and was not before the pnpm 11 upgrade either.

When turbo runs the browser-mode suites concurrently (default concurrency 10), Vite/Chromium contention kills whole suites during module load. Two signatures, neither an assertion failure:

  - `Failed to fetch dynamically imported module` -- suite reports `0 test`
  - `Cannot connect to the iframe. Did you change the location or submitted a form?`

Measured on this tree, same commit, only parallelism varied:

  - default concurrency: 3 of 45 tasks failed (ui, wallow-auth, wallow-web); run aborted at 30 of 76 files in wallow-web. An earlier run at default lost 9 suites.
  - `turbo run test --force --concurrency=1`: 26/26 tasks, 0 cached, 352 test files, ALL PASS, exit 0.
  - wallow-web alone: 76 files / 499 tests pass.

Cost of the cap on the whole test task: 1m42s vs 48s.

WHY THIS WENT UNNOTICED: turbo was serving 32 of 45 tasks from local cache, so the browser suites were not executing at all on this machine. A cache hit was reporting a gate that had never run. Any fix should also consider whether `pnpm check` should refuse to report green off a fully-cached test task.

Not yet determined: whether concurrency=1 is needed or only a cap that keeps the three browser-heavy packages (ui, wallow-auth, wallow-web) from overlapping. Worth measuring 2 and 3 before settling on 1, since 1 serialises the fast node-only packages for no reason.

Machine: 8 cores, 22 GB RAM, 20 GB free -- not memory starvation.
notes:
MEASURED 2026-08-27 (8 cores, ~12 GB free, shared box, 5 logged-in users).

PHASE A1 -- `npx turbo run test --force` at four turbo concurrencies, 3 reps each.
Capping turbo's TASK concurrency does not fix this, and is not even monotonic:

  concurrency  failures  secs
  default(10)     1/3    68 65 64
  4               3/3    59 53 49
  3               3/3    60 36 37
  2               1/3    72 64 74

8 of 12 runs red. The bead's own `--concurrency=1` green run stands at n=1.

WHY THE CAP MISSES. Turbo bounds how many PACKAGES run at once; each package's
vitest run then fans out to its own CPU-count worker pool. Measured mid-run at
--concurrency=3: 49 chrome-headless-shell processes on 8 cores. The quantity that
predicts failure is the PRODUCT (turbo tasks in flight) x (browser workers per
task) -- how many Vite dev servers are each serving a Chromium pool at once.

STRUCTURAL FINDING (the useful one). Adding `maxWorkers` to the browser project
alone makes vitest refuse to start:

  Error: Projects "browser (chromium)" and "node" have different 'maxWorkers'
  but same 'sequence.groupOrder'. Provide unique 'sequence.groupOrder' for them.

Every package's node and browser projects therefore share ONE group and ONE
worker pool today, and run INTERLEAVED. Nothing in the repo has ever set
`sequence.groupOrder` (checked every vitest.config.ts and
packages/testing/src/vitest-projects.ts), so nobody was forced to notice. That is
half of why per-package load multiplies out the way it does.

PHASE A2 -- node groupOrder 0 / browser groupOrder 1, sweeping browser maxWorkers
under `turbo run test --force --only` (--only drops the ^build tasks that were
competing for CPU inside the A1 numbers). 3 reps each:

  maxWorkers    failures
  unset            1/3
  2                3/3
  1                1/3

Still not reliable: bounding workers-per-task while leaving 10 tasks in flight
just moves the oversubscription.

TWO FLAKES SEEN THAT ARE NOT ON A BEAD YET:
  1. packages/ui menubar.test.tsx, `expected 'file-recent' to be 'file-new'` /
     `expected 'view-popup' to be 'file-new'` from `expect.poll` at
     menubar.test.tsx:238 (openWithKeyboard). Keyboard, not pointer: the prior
     menu had not closed inside the poll budget. Hit 4 tests at once in one run.
  2. The `Cannot connect to the iframe` signature in this bead's description is
     COLLATERAL, not a navigation. In the run I captured it named
     apps/wallow-web/src/app/routes/dashboard/organizations/$orgId/index.test.tsx
     -- a spec that renders nothing at all (it only reads router.routesById) and
     so cannot navigate. `Received URL: unknown due to CORS` is the iframe never
     loading, i.e. the same starvation as the `Failed to fetch dynamically
     imported module` failures beside it. The navigation-escape guard IS
     installed in apps/wallow-web/vitest.setup.ts and is not implicated.

ON THE CACHE QUESTION ("should pnpm check refuse to report green off a fully
cached test task"): recommend NO. turbo.jsonc's hashing is sound -- `test`
dependsOn ^build for the hash, and the globalDependencies list is deliberate. A
cached green honestly means "these exact inputs passed once". The complaint is
really that a FLAKY suite's green gets memoized, which argues for fixing the
flake, not for paying ~50s on every warm check. Revisit only if the flake proves
unfixable.

Phase A3 running: conc=1 (workers unset) vs conc=2 + maxWorkers=3, 5 reps each.
FIX SHIPPED. The root `test` script is now `turbo run test --concurrency=1`, and
`check` plus the CI job invoke `turbo run build typecheck` and `pnpm test` as TWO
invocations rather than folding `test` onto the same line. Three files:
package.json, .github/workflows/js.yml, CLAUDE.md.

WHY TWO INVOCATIONS. turbo applies a `--concurrency` to the whole run graph and has
no per-task setting (checked turbo.jsonc's schema — there is nowhere to put one).
`turbo run build typecheck test --concurrency=1` would therefore serialise build and
typecheck as well, which nothing here justifies: only the browser suites contend.
Splitting costs nothing, because `test`'s `dependsOn: ["^build"]` resolves against the
builds the first invocation just cached.

TWO THINGS THE BEAD ASKED THAT ARE NOW ANSWERED.

1. "Whether concurrency=1 is needed or only a cap that keeps the three browser-heavy
   packages from overlapping. Worth measuring 2 and 3 before settling on 1."
   Measured, and 1 is needed. Every intermediate setting was still red: turbo
   `--concurrency` 2, 3 and 4 (Phase A1, 3 reps each, 8 of 12 runs red and NOT
   monotonic in the concurrency), and per-project browser `maxWorkers` 1, 2 and 3
   (Phase A2). The reason the cap alone misses is recorded in the Phase A1 note above
   — turbo bounds PACKAGES, each package's vitest then fans out to its own CPU-count
   worker pool, and the quantity that predicts failure is the product. 49
   chrome-headless-shell processes were counted on 8 cores at `--concurrency=3`.

2. "Whether pnpm check should refuse to report green off a fully-cached test task."
   Recommending NO, and not doing it. turbo's hashing is sound and deliberate: a
   cached green honestly means "these exact inputs passed once", and `test`'s
   `dependsOn: ["^build"]` already folds each dependency's key in, so a changed
   package cannot replay a stale downstream pass. The real complaint underneath the
   question is that a FLAKY suite's green gets memoised — which is an argument for
   fixing the flake, not for paying ~50s of browser suites on every warm check. The
   flakes are tracked on their own beads (Wallow-x5da, Wallow-xzy1.6, Wallow-rgu1).

WHAT WAS DELIBERATELY NOT SHIPPED. The `maxWorkers` sweep needed a
`sequence.groupOrder` split in packages/testing/src/vitest-projects.ts, because Vitest
4 refuses to start when two projects share a groupOrder but differ in `maxWorkers`
("Projects 'browser (chromium)' and 'node' have different 'maxWorkers' but same
'sequence.groupOrder'"). That error is itself the most useful structural finding of
the sweep and is worth keeping: it PROVES the node and browser projects currently
share one group and one worker pool and run interleaved. The scaffolding was reverted
rather than shipped — it changed scheduling, it did not fix anything, and the smaller
diff is the honest one. `fileParallelism: false` was not shipped either;
docs/plans/2026-08-03/1639-proxy-trust-react-dupe-nav-flake.md is explicit that it
removes load rather than the mechanism and must not ship as a fix.

VERIFIED ON THE SHIPPED SHAPE (not on the scaffolded tree the sweep was measured on):
`pnpm check` exit 0 end to end, then FIVE consecutive forced full-workspace runs, ALL exit 0
(`turbo run test --concurrency=1 --force --continue`, `--continue` so a single package
failing cannot mask the app suites that carried the signature). Signature counts
across those runs: "Failed to fetch dynamically imported module" / "Failed to import
test file" = 0, "Cannot connect to the iframe" = 0, failing packages = 0, wall clock 95/95/95/95/94s. Cost is ~95s against ~60s, cold
only.
NEW FAILURE MODE observed while re-measuring at the old concurrency — the setting this bead capped does not only produce flaky failures, it can WEDGE A RUN INDEFINITELY.

Run 4 of a fresh sweep at the old default (no --concurrency flag, so 10):

  - 13 of 15 packages printed a normal 'Test Files' summary.
  - apps/wallow-auth finished, red, with ELIFECYCLE.
  - apps/wallow-web executed ~25 spec files fine, had 5 files come back '(0 test)',
    and then STOPPED. Last log byte at 15:39:52. Still alive and producing nothing
    at 16:06 — 28 minutes — with turbo, its vitest process and 14 chrome-headless-shell
    processes all resident. It never printed an error section and never printed a summary.
    I killed it; it did not exit on its own.

The three completed reps around it took 60, 53 and 62 seconds. So this is not slowness, it is a hang: after some spec files fail to load, vitest browser mode can fail to converge and no timeout fires to end it.

Why it matters even though the cap shipped:

  1. It strengthens the case for --concurrency=1 beyond what this bead recorded. The
     documented cost was 'red runs'. The real worst case is a CI job that burns until
     the platform-level timeout kills it, with no useful error in the log — strictly
     worse to diagnose than a failure.
  2. It is a hazard for anyone who later raises the concurrency to reclaim wall-clock.
     A run that hangs looks like a slow machine, not like a regression, so the cause
     would not be obvious.
  3. It invalidated my own measurement harness. The sweep script had no per-rep timeout,
     so it sat on rep 4 for 28 minutes and I would have gone on reporting '28 reps left'
     off a stale results file indefinitely. Any future repeat-under-load loop in this repo
     needs a per-rep 'timeout' with the hang recorded as its own outcome.

Not filed as a separate open bead because it is a property of a configuration this repo no longer ships. If the cap is ever relaxed, this note is the reason to instrument for hangs, not just failures.

title: [bug] a disabled module's controllers are still routed, so ApiKeys returns 500 on the shipped default config
description:
The IWallowModule registry gates a module's DI registrations, its Wolverine handler discovery and
its migrations. It does NOT gate the module's HTTP surface, and nothing else does either -- so a
disabled module's controllers stay routed and fail at request time instead of not existing.

## Verified state

Every module's .Api assembly is an MVC application part, discovered unconditionally from the
Wallow.Api reference graph (obj/Debug/net10.0/Wallow.Api.MvcApplicationPartsAssemblyInfo.cs lists
all seven: Wallow.Announcements.Api, Wallow.ApiKeys.Api, Wallow.Branding.Api, Wallow.Identity.Api,
Wallow.Inquiries.Api, Wallow.Notifications.Api, Wallow.Storage.Api). Program.cs:507 calls
AddControllersWithViews() with no ApplicationPartManager customisation, and there is no
[FeatureGate] anywhere under api/src/Modules (grep: zero hits).

ApiKeys ships DISABLED by default (api/src/Wallow.Api/appsettings.json:88,
"Modules.ApiKeys": false), and ApiKeysController is a live route:

  api/src/Modules/ApiKeys/Wallow.ApiKeys.Api/Controllers/ApiKeysController.cs:20-24
  [ApiController] [ApiVersion(1)] [Route("v{version:apiVersion}/identity/auth/keys")] [Authorize]
  public sealed class ApiKeysController(IApiKeyService apiKeyService, IScopeSubsetValidator ...)

IApiKeyService is registered only by AddApiKeysModule, which the registry skips when the flag is
off. So on the shipped default configuration an AUTHENTICATED request to
/v1/identity/auth/keys returns 500 from controller-activation DI failure, not 404. (Anonymous
requests 401 first, which is why this has not been noticed.) The same shape applies to every
optional module: Storage, Notifications, Announcements, Inquiries, Branding.

Note Program.cs:691-698 already gates ApiKeyAuthenticationMiddleware on the same flag with the
comment "the middleware depends on IApiKeyService" -- the exposure was understood for the
middleware and not carried to the controllers.

## Why it matters here

A fork disabling a module is the advertised way to slim Wallow down (docs/getting-started/fork-guide.md).
The fork gets a module that is off everywhere except the route table, and its OpenAPI document still
advertises the endpoints. Every reference modular-monolith IModule carries an endpoint member for
exactly this reason; IWallowModule has Name / IsCore / HandlerAssemblies / DbContextTypes /
SchemaName / AddServices and no HTTP member at all.

## Two options, pick during the bead

A. [FeatureGate("Modules.X")] on each optional module's controllers. One attribute per controller,
   uses the same flag string the registry uses, returns 404. Cheapest, but it is a seventh place
   the flag name is written by hand and it does not use the registry.
B. An ApplicationPartManager / ControllerFeatureProvider (or an IActionModelConvention) driven off
   the enabledModules list Program.cs:177 already has -- controllers whose assembly belongs to a
   disabled module are never registered as actions. Registry-consistent, one site, and it also
   drops them from the OpenAPI document. Needs a way to map a controller assembly back to its
   module; an ApiAssembly member on IWallowModule is the obvious route and would also give the
   interface the endpoint-awareness it currently lacks.

Recommendation: B, and add ApiAssembly to IWallowModule while doing it. A is acceptable if B turns
out to fight Asp.Versioning's ApiExplorer.

## Acceptance

- With Modules.ApiKeys=false, an authenticated GET /v1/identity/auth/keys returns 404, not 500.
- With Modules.ApiKeys=true it behaves exactly as today.
- The same holds for at least one more optional module (Storage) under an integration test.
- The disabled module's endpoints are absent from the generated OpenAPI document (option B) or
  explicitly noted as still present (option A).
- ./scripts/run-tests.sh and ./scripts/run-tests.sh integration green.
notes:
SCOUT: all citations verified exact on disk (ApiKeysController.cs:20-24, Program.cs:507 AddControllersWithViews, Program.cs:691-698 comment+gate, MvcApplicationPartsAssemblyInfo.cs). BLOCKS Wallow-3mbx.5 (bd dep add Wallow-3mbx.5 Wallow-3mbx.1) because option B's ApiAssembly member touches the same 8 files (IWallowModule.cs + 7 XModule.cs) that 3mbx.5 reshapes — do this bead first, 3mbx.5 tidies the new member afterward. enabledModules is already in scope at Program.cs:177 as IReadOnlyList<IWallowModule> — option B's controller-gating convention should consume that list directly rather than re-deriving it, and can share logic with Wallow-3mbx.3's flag-check replacement (both are "is module X enabled" checks off the same list — no hard dependency, just worth the two implementers agreeing on one small helper). No other file/type collisions found with the other 8 children.

DESIGN: Chosen approach — Option B, corrected: filter controllers via a custom IApplicationFeatureProvider<ControllerFeature> registered through ConfigureApplicationPartManager, keyed by controller NAMESPACE (not the bead's proposed ApiAssembly member on IWallowModule — verified architecturally impossible, see REJECTED below).

MECHANISM VERIFICATION (decompiled the actual installed binaries this repo builds against — Microsoft.AspNetCore.Mvc.Core 10.0.10, Microsoft.AspNetCore.OpenApi 10.0.10, Asp.Versioning.Mvc.ApiExplorer 10.0.0 — via ilspycmd, since the ref-context MCP tool was unavailable in this session; noting that explicitly rather than fabricating a doc-search citation):
- AddControllersWithViews()/AddMvcCore() synchronously registers the framework's default ControllerFeatureProvider into ApplicationPartManager.FeatureProviders before returning the IMvcBuilder. ConfigureApplicationPartManager's setupAction runs synchronously, immediately, against that already-populated PartManager — so a provider added there is guaranteed to run and can remove entries the default provider already added (IApplicationFeatureProvider providers all run in registration order against the same mutable ControllerFeature.Controllers set; ours runs after the default one, so it sees the full candidate list and can prune it).
- IActionDescriptorCollectionProvider (built from ApplicationPartManager.ApplicationParts + FeatureProviders) is the single upstream source for: (1) routing/endpoint matching, (2) Asp.Versioning's VersionedApiDescriptionProvider (an IApiDescriptionProvider — no independent assembly scan, operates strictly on the already-filtered ActionDescriptorCollection), and (3) Microsoft.AspNetCore.OpenApi's OpenApiDocumentService (constructor-injects IApiDescriptionGroupCollectionProvider). One filter point at the ApplicationPartManager level therefore fixes routing (404), Asp.Versioning's ApiExplorer, AND OpenAPI doc generation simultaneously. This directly refutes the bead's stated worry that an ApplicationPartManager filter might not run early enough or might fight Asp.Versioning.
- Confirmed IOpenApiDocumentProvider is registered as a KEYED singleton unconditionally by AddOpenApiCore (Microsoft.Extensions.DependencyInjection.OpenApiServiceCollectionExtensions), NOT gated by environment — unlike app.MapOpenApi() in this repo's Program.cs (line ~633, wrapped in `if (app.Environment.IsDevelopment())`, never mapped in the Testing environment used by WallowApiFactory). So the OpenAPI acceptance criterion is tested by resolving `sp.GetRequiredKeyedService<IOpenApiDocumentProvider>("v1")` and calling `GetOpenApiDocumentAsync()` directly from DI — no HTTP round-trip, no Development-env override needed. Signature confirmed by decompilation: `Task<Microsoft.OpenApi.OpenApiDocument> GetOpenApiDocumentAsync(CancellationToken = default)`. `OpenApiDocument.Paths` is the same `IDictionary<string, IOpenApiPathItem>` already iterated by the existing, tested `Wallow.Api.Extensions.ServiceCollectionExtensions.TransformDocumentExcludeTestSupport` (api/src/Wallow.Api/Extensions/ServiceCollectionExtensions.cs) — use that method as the idiom reference for how to walk `document.Paths`.

REJECTED SUB-DESIGN — the bead's literal `ApiAssembly` member on IWallowModule: architecturally impossible without breaking Clean Architecture layering. Evidence: `grep -n ProjectReference` on every module's .csproj shows `Wallow.{Module}.Infrastructure.csproj` (where every `XModule.cs` implementing IWallowModule lives, e.g. api/src/Modules/ApiKeys/Wallow.ApiKeys.Infrastructure/Modules/ApiKeysModule.cs) references Domain/Application/Shared.Infrastructure/Shared.Contracts — it does NOT reference its sibling `.Api` project, and `.Api` does not reference `.Infrastructure` either. Only `api/src/Wallow.Api/Wallow.Api.csproj` (the host composition root, lines 106-121) references every module's BOTH `.Api` and `.Infrastructure` projects. So `XModule.cs` cannot type an `Assembly ApiAssembly => typeof(SomeApiController).Assembly` property — the `.Api` types are not visible to it. Do NOT add ApiAssembly to IWallowModule.cs (api/src/Shared/Wallow.Shared.Infrastructure/Modules/IWallowModule.cs) or to any of the 7 XModule.cs files. This finding also means the epic's `Wallow-3mbx.5 depends on Wallow-3mbx.1` edge, if it was justified by an expected collision on IWallowModule.cs / XModule.cs files, no longer applies — this design touches neither. Flagging for the epic owner to reconsider that edge; not editing Wallow-3mbx or Wallow-3mbx.5 myself (out of scope for this note).

WHY NAMESPACE, NOT ASSEMBLY NAME: an equally-viable variant matches on `controller.Assembly.GetName().Name` against `Wallow.{ModuleName}.Api` (verified safe: grep for `<AssemblyName>` override across every module .Api .csproj returned nothing, so assembly name always equals the project name). But this repo already has a TESTED, PRECEDENT pattern for exactly this module-from-controller-type mapping: `Wallow.Api.Extensions.ServiceCollectionExtensions.TransformOperationModuleTag` (same file, ~line the private `ModuleNamePattern()` regex sits at) matches `ControllerActionDescriptor.ControllerTypeInfo.Namespace` against `^Wallow\.(\w+)\.Api\b`, and its test file api/tests/Wallow.Api.Tests/Extensions/ServiceCollectionExtensionsTests.cs proves the mapping via a deliberately-placed fake controller type in a fake module namespace: api/tests/Wallow.Api.Tests/Extensions/FakeBillingController.cs declares `internal sealed class FakeBillingController {}` inside `namespace Wallow.Billing.Api.Controllers` (with a `// ReSharper disable once CheckNamespace` comment noting the namespace deliberately doesn't match the assembly, precisely for this test technique). Reuse that exact technique for the new provider's unit test — namespace-based matching is therefore both correct AND the cheapest-to-test option; do not switch to assembly-name matching.

EXACT FILES / TYPES / SIGNATURES TO ADD:

1. NEW FILE api/src/Wallow.Api/ModuleGatedControllerFeatureProvider.cs (namespace Wallow.Api):
```
internal sealed partial class ModuleGatedControllerFeatureProvider(IReadOnlySet<string> enabledModuleNames)
    : IApplicationFeatureProvider<ControllerFeature>
{
    public void PopulateFeature(IEnumerable<ApplicationPart> parts, ControllerFeature feature)
    {
        List<TypeInfo> disabledModuleControllers = feature.Controllers
            .Where(controller => !BelongsToEnabledModule(controller))
            .ToList();
        foreach (TypeInfo controller in disabledModuleControllers)
        {
            feature.Controllers.Remove(controller);
        }
    }

    private bool BelongsToEnabledModule(TypeInfo controller)
    {
        Match match = ModuleNamePattern().Match(controller.Namespace ?? string.Empty);
        // No match => not a Wallow.{Module}.Api controller (host-level or future non-module
        // controller) => always keep, same "unmatched = keep" default TransformOperationModuleTag uses.
        return !match.Success || enabledModuleNames.Contains(match.Groups[1].Value);
    }

    [GeneratedRegex(@"^Wallow\.(\w+)\.Api\b", RegexOptions.NonBacktracking)]
    private static partial Regex ModuleNamePattern();
}
```
Do NOT try to share the private `ModuleNamePattern()` regex already in Extensions/ServiceCollectionExtensions.cs — duplicating this ~1-line GeneratedRegex is lower risk than widening that file's visibility, and keeps the OpenAPI-tag concern and the routing-gate concern independently editable.

2. EDIT api/src/Wallow.Api/Program.cs at line 507 — replace the bare `builder.Services.AddControllersWithViews();` with:
```
IReadOnlySet<string> enabledModuleNames = enabledModules.Select(module => module.Name).ToHashSet(StringComparer.Ordinal);
builder.Services.AddControllersWithViews()
    .ConfigureApplicationPartManager(manager =>
        manager.FeatureProviders.Add(new ModuleGatedControllerFeatureProvider(enabledModuleNames)));
```
`enabledModules` is already in scope at this point in Program.cs (assigned at line ~177 from `Wallow.Api.WallowModules.AddWallowModules(...)`) — no new resolution needed. This sits immediately before the existing `.AddApiVersioning(...).AddApiExplorer(...)` chain (lines 508-519) — leave that chain untouched, it already consumes whatever ActionDescriptorCollection results from the filtered PartManager.

TEST PLAN (per acceptance criterion; integration tests only run under ./scripts/run-tests.sh integration or all, per .claude/rules/TESTING.md):

0. FAST UNIT TEST (no Docker, no [Trait("Category","Integration")]) — new file api/tests/Wallow.Api.Tests/ModuleGatedControllerFeatureProviderTests.cs, next to FakeBillingController.cs's pattern: declare 2 fake internal controller types in namespaces `Wallow.Storage.Api.Controllers` and `Wallow.ApiKeys.Api.Controllers` (own fake files, same ReSharper-disable-CheckNamespace trick as FakeBillingController.cs), build a `ControllerFeature` by hand, add both TypeInfos to `feature.Controllers`, call `new ModuleGatedControllerFeatureProvider(new HashSet<string> { "Storage" }).PopulateFeature([], feature)`, assert Storage controller remains and ApiKeys controller was removed. Also assert an unmatched-namespace fake controller (e.g. `Wallow.Api.Controllers.FakeHostController`) is always kept regardless of enabledModuleNames content.

1. INTEGRATION — reuse the existing shared-fixture default WallowApiFactory (ApiKeys disabled, Storage enabled — matches api/src/Wallow.Api/appsettings.json's `FeatureManagement:Modules` defaults: ApiKeys=false, Storage=true), via `[Collection(nameof(ApiIntegrationTestCollection))]` (api/tests/Wallow.Api.Tests/Integration/ApiIntegrationTestCollection.cs) — a class extending WallowIntegrationTestBase(factory) (api/tests/Wallow.Tests.Common/Bases/WallowIntegrationTestBase.cs), same shape as api/tests/Modules/Identity/Wallow.Identity.IntegrationTests/Organizations/MyOrganizationsTests.cs:
   (a) SetTestUser(TestConstants.AdminUserId.ToString(), "admin"); Client.GetAsync("/identity/auth/keys") (no /v1/ prefix — ApiVersionRewriteMiddleware supplies it, same convention MyOrganizationsTests.cs uses) => assert HttpStatusCode.NotFound (ApiKeys disabled by default — the bug this bead fixes).
   (b) Same user; Client.GetAsync("/storage/config") => assert HttpStatusCode.OK (Storage enabled — unaffected control case).
   (c) Resolve `ScopedServices.GetRequiredKeyedService<IOpenApiDocumentProvider>("v1")`, call `GetOpenApiDocumentAsync()`, assert `document.Paths.Keys` contains no key containing "identity/auth/keys" and DOES contain a key containing "storage/config" — this is acceptance criterion (d). Print `document.Paths.Keys` once locally if the exact path-template string (`/v1/identity/auth/keys` vs `v1/identity/auth/keys` etc.) doesn't match on first run; use TransformDocumentExcludeTestSupport in Extensions/ServiceCollectionExtensions.cs as the working idiom for iterating `document.Paths`.
   NOTE: WallowApiFactory unconditionally registers `services.AddSingleton<IApiKeyService>(new FakeApiKeyService())` in ConfigureTestServices — verified this does NOT mask the fix: that fake is a service-layer double resolved only if the controller action ever runs, but the ApplicationPartManager filter removes the controller from the ActionDescriptorCollection entirely, so routing 404s before DI ever resolves IApiKeyService.

2. INTEGRATION — NEW dedicated factory api/tests/Wallow.Api.Tests/Integration/ApiKeysEnabledFactory.cs (or co-located with its test class), subclassing WallowApiFactory and overriding ConfigureWebHost to flip `FeatureManagement:Modules:ApiKeys=true` via additional in-memory config (same "subclass + override ConfigureWebHost, call base, add more config" shape as api/tests/Modules/Identity/Wallow.Identity.IntegrationTests/Resilience/KeycloakResilienceTestFactory.cs, which itself subclasses WallowApiFactory : IdentityResilienceTestFactory). Test: SetTestUser(TestConstants.AdminUserId.ToString(), "admin"); Client.GetAsync("/identity/auth/keys") => assert HttpStatusCode.OK. Permission requirement resolved: ApiKeysController.ListApiKeys requires [HasPermission(PermissionType.ApiKeyManage)] (api/src/Modules/ApiKeys/Wallow.ApiKeys.Api/Controllers/ApiKeysController.cs); PermissionExpansionMiddleware (api/src/Modules/Identity/Wallow.Identity.Infrastructure/Authorization/PermissionExpansionMiddleware.cs, registered in Program.cs line 711, between UseAuthentication/TenantResolutionMiddleware and UseAuthorization) expands the "admin" ClaimTypes.Role claim (which TestAuthHandler always attaches — api/tests/Wallow.Tests.Common/Helpers/TestAuthHandler.cs) into "permission" claims via RolePermissionMapping.GetPermissions(["admin"]) (api/src/Shared/Wallow.Shared.Kernel/Identity/Authorization/RolePermissionMapping.cs), whose "admin" entry DOES include PermissionType.ApiKeyManage. So the standard SetTestUser(..., "admin") convention already used throughout the integration suites is sufficient — no bespoke claim setup needed. (This was the one open question at the start of this design pass; now closed.)

3. INTEGRATION — NEW dedicated factory api/tests/Wallow.Api.Tests/Integration/StorageDisabledFactory.cs, same subclass shape, flips `FeatureManagement:Modules:Storage=false`. Test: SetTestUser(..., "admin"); Client.GetAsync("/storage/config") => assert HttpStatusCode.NotFound. This is acceptance criterion (c) (Storage proven under an integration test), using StorageSettingsController.GetConfig (api/src/Modules/Storage/Wallow.Storage.Api/Controllers/StorageSettingsController.cs) — chosen over StorageController.ListFiles specifically because GetConfig carries only class-level [Authorize] (no extra [HasPermission]/query-param preconditions), so a 404 can only mean "route not found," never "business-logic 404" (ListFiles's bucket-not-found 404 would be ambiguous evidence).

RISKS / WHAT WOULD FALSIFY THIS DESIGN:
- If any future host-level (non-module) controller is added directly under Wallow.Api without a `Wallow.{X}.Api` namespace, BelongsToEnabledModule's "no match => keep" default is required, or it would vanish. Today grep confirms zero such controllers exist, but a reviewer should re-check this default is preserved in code review.
- If `IApplicationFeatureProvider<ControllerFeature>` providers are ever proven to run in an environment-independent, non-deterministic order (not verified beyond decompilation of the current NuGet-pinned MVC version, 10.0.10, pinned in Directory.Packages.props) this design would need a second look — the whole design rests on "default ControllerFeatureProvider populates feature.Controllers before any provider added via ConfigureApplicationPartManager's setupAction runs," which was confirmed by decompiling AddControllersWithViews/AddMvcCore's synchronous registration order, not by a live ref.tools doc citation (that MCP tool was unavailable this session — flagging honestly rather than fabricating a citation).
- If a future module's .Api project ever sets `<AssemblyName>` or a controller is declared with a namespace not matching `Wallow.{Module}.Api.Controllers*`, it silently falls through to "always kept" rather than failing loudly. Acceptable today (matches the existing TransformOperationModuleTag's same silent-fallback behavior for OpenAPI tags) but worth a one-line comment pointing this out in the new file, which the code block above already includes.
- IOpenApiDocumentProvider's exact keyed-registration key ("v1") must match how AddOpenApi("v1", ...) names the document in Extensions/ServiceCollectionExtensions.cs's AddApiServices — verify this string constant if the DI resolution throws.

DESIGN REVIEW: AMEND

SCOPE: reviewed the DESIGN note (Option B, ApplicationPartManager/ControllerFeatureProvider keyed
on controller namespace) against the two deviations flagged for scrutiny, plus mechanism/test-plan
soundness and the 3mbx.5 collision. All file/line citations below were verified by reading the
files, not trusted from the note.

=== 1. "ApiAssembly on IWallowModule is architecturally impossible" — TRUE, but a stronger
alternative than namespace-matching was never considered ===

Verified on disk: every Wallow.{X}.Infrastructure.csproj (where every XModule.cs implementing
IWallowModule lives) references only Domain/Application/Shared.Infrastructure/Shared.Contracts —
zero ProjectReference to its sibling .Api project (checked all 7). Wallow.{X}.Api.csproj likewise
never references .Infrastructure (checked all 7). Only api/src/Wallow.Api/Wallow.Api.csproj (the
host) references BOTH .Api and .Infrastructure for every module (lines confirmed). So the literal
bead proposal — `Assembly ApiAssembly { get; }` on IWallowModule, implemented by XModule.cs — is
correctly rejected: XModule.cs cannot type an Api-layer anchor. Good catch, well-evidenced.

BUT the note jumps straight from "impossible on the interface" to "match on controller namespace"
without ever evaluating the alternative the epic's own thesis calls for: the HOST maps module ->
Api assembly at its own composition root, where both are already referenced. This isn't
hypothetical — api/src/Wallow.Api/WallowModules.cs already IS that composition root. Its own doc
comment (line 26) says "this list is the only place that knows all seven exist," and its
`_allModules` array (lines 34-43) already constructs every `new XModule()` by explicit type
reference. Extending that SAME array with one Api-layer anchor type per module (e.g.
`typeof(ApiKeysController).Assembly`, pulled in via one `using` per module already added to that
file) would give `ModuleGatedControllerFeatureProvider` an exact `Assembly`-identity set instead of
a namespace regex — with:
  - zero changes to IWallowModule.cs or any XModule.cs (satisfies the note's own constraint),
  - no reliance on any naming convention: an unlisted assembly can't accidentally satisfy a
    regex, and a moved/renamed anchor type is a COMPILE error, not silent drift,
  - no new "seventh place" the module list is written — it enriches the one array the epic already
    calls canonical, rather than introducing a second, independent mechanism (regex over namespace
    strings) alongside the registry.
This is strictly stronger than namespace matching and was not discussed or rejected-with-reasons —
it appears to have simply not been considered. Given the epic's explicit thesis ("the registry
should be authoritative"), this should have been evaluated before reaching for a string-convention
gate. AMENDMENT REQUIRED: either adopt this (preferred), or add an explicit paragraph to the design
explaining why namespace-matching was chosen over it (e.g. "avoids one using-directive per module in
WallowModules.cs" is a real but much weaker justification than what's currently written).

Other alternatives the prompt asked me to weigh, for completeness: moving the module registrar
(XModule.cs) into .Api would break AddServices' need to reach Infrastructure-layer repository/
DbContext registrations (.Api doesn't reference .Infrastructure either) — correctly a non-starter,
though the note never says so explicitly. An assembly-level attribute discovered by reflection is
roughly equivalent in strength to the anchor-type approach above but strictly more machinery for no
extra safety; not worth preferring over the anchor-type array.

=== 2. Namespace-keying — mechanically sound, but the note's own RISK section is factually wrong
about detectability ===

The note claims (RISK bullet 3): a future mis-namespaced/mismatched-AssemblyName controller
"silently falls through to always kept... acceptable today (matches TransformOperationModuleTag's
same silent-fallback behavior for OpenAPI tags)."

This is FALSE on this repo, and the note missed an existing, directly-on-point guard:
api/tests/Wallow.Architecture.Tests/ApiConventionTests.cs:88-98 (`ControllerConventions_ShouldBeFollowed`)
already asserts, for every module in `TestConstants.AllModules`, that every `ControllerBase`-derived
type in that module's Api assembly `.ResideInNamespace($"Wallow.{moduleName}.Api.Controllers")`, and
fails the test (`namespaceResult.IsSuccessful.Should().BeTrue(...)`) if not. Two facts make this a
real, loud, self-maintaining guard rather than the weak convention the note assumed:
  - `TestConstants.AllModules` (api/tests/Wallow.Architecture.Tests/TestConstants.cs) is NOT a
    hardcoded list — it's derived at test-runtime from every `Wallow.*.Domain.dll` present in the
    test output directory, so it automatically covers a future 8th module, not just today's seven.
  - This test file carries no `[Trait("Category","Integration")]` (grep confirmed zero hits), and
    `./scripts/run-tests.sh`'s bare invocation resolves to `api/Wallow.slnx` with
    `--filter "Category!=E2E&Category!=Integration"` (scripts/run-tests.sh:46,75) — i.e. this test
    runs in the FAST/default tier, not gated behind `integration`/`all`.
