PRIOR ART: how mature .NET module systems remove a disabled module's HTTP surface. Ecosystem
research (ref-context MCP working this session; ABP/Evently/Modulith/Grzybek read via `gh api`
against the live repos; ASP.NET Core behaviour read from dotnet/aspnetcore main and the installed
SDK targets). VERDICT UP FRONT: option (c) — host-side module->assembly mapping at the composition
root, applied by REMOVING the disabled module's ApplicationPart, not by a ControllerFeatureProvider
and not by [FeatureGate]. This AMENDS the current DESIGN note in two ways (mechanism: ApplicationParts
instead of FeatureProviders; key: Assembly identity instead of namespace regex) and RETRACTS its
"architecturally impossible" framing of an ApiAssembly member.

=== 1. THE FINDING THAT SETTLES OPTION (a): [FeatureGate] DOES NOT FIX THIS BUG ===

Microsoft.FeatureManagement.AspNetCore's FeatureGateAttribute is declared
  [AttributeUsage(...)] public class FeatureGateAttribute : ActionFilterAttribute, IAsyncPageFilter
(microsoft/FeatureManagement-Dotnet, src/Microsoft.FeatureManagement.AspNetCore/FeatureGateAttribute.cs).
It is an ACTION filter. Its OnActionExecutionAsync resolves IDisabledFeaturesHandler, defaulting to
NotFoundDisabledFeaturesHandler.

ASP.NET Core runs the controller factory BEFORE action filters. Verified in
dotnet/aspnetcore main, src/Mvc/Mvc.Core/src/Infrastructure/ControllerActionInvoker.cs:
  - line 456: `protected override Task InvokeInnerFilterAsync()` starts the state machine at
    `var next = State.ActionBegin;` (line 460)
  - line 65 `case State.ActionBegin:` -> line 72 `_instance = _cacheEntry.ControllerFactory(controllerContext);`
    -> line 84 `goto case State.ActionNext;`
  - line 87 `case State.ActionNext:` -> `_cursor.GetNextFilter<IActionFilter, IAsyncActionFilter>()`

So on `[FeatureGate("Modules.ApiKeys")] ApiKeysController`, the activator still tries to construct
the controller, IApiKeyService is still unregistered, and the request still fails 500 at
controller activation BEFORE the gate ever executes. Option (a) as written in the bead body does not
satisfy the bead's own first acceptance criterion. It would only appear to work on a controller
with no module-scoped constructor dependencies. Treat this as disqualifying, not as a style
preference. (FeatureGate's 404 IS real and IS configurable — Microsoft Learn,
azure-app-configuration/feature-management-dotnet-reference, "Disabled action handling": "a
registered implementation of IDisabledFeaturesHandler is invoked. By default, a minimalistic
handler is registered that returns an HTTP 404 error. You can override this handler by using
IFeatureManagementBuilder" — but the 404 is never reached here.)

Secondary problems with (a) even where it works: the action stays in the route table, stays in
Asp.Versioning's ApiExplorer, and stays in the OpenAPI document. The bead's acceptance criterion
about OpenAPI is unsatisfiable under (a) without an extra document transformer.

=== 2. WHAT THE ECOSYSTEM ACTUALLY DOES ===

(2a) ABP Framework — the most mature module loader in .NET. Every HTTP-carrying module class adds
ITS OWN assembly as an application part, explicitly, in PreConfigureServices:

  // abpframework/abp, modules/identity/src/Volo.Abp.Identity.HttpApi/Volo/Abp/Identity/AbpIdentityHttpApiModule.cs
  [DependsOn(typeof(AbpIdentityApplicationContractsModule), typeof(AbpAspNetCoreMvcModule))]
  public class AbpIdentityHttpApiModule : AbpModule
  {
      public override void PreConfigureServices(ServiceConfigurationContext context)
      {
          PreConfigure<IMvcBuilder>(mvcBuilder =>
              mvcBuilder.AddApplicationPartIfNotExists(typeof(AbpIdentityHttpApiModule).Assembly));
      }
  }

  // abpframework/abp, framework/src/Volo.Abp.AspNetCore.Mvc/Microsoft/Extensions/DependencyInjection/AbpMvcBuilderExtensions.cs
  public static void AddApplicationPartIfNotExists(this IMvcBuilder mvcBuilder, Assembly assembly)
      => mvcBuilder.PartManager.ApplicationParts.AddIfNotContains(assembly);
  // AddIfNotContains: `applicationParts.Add(new AssemblyPart(assembly))` unless an AssemblyPart with
  // that same Assembly instance is already present. Keyed on Assembly IDENTITY. Not on name, not on
  // namespace.

The same call is present in ~30 ABP module classes (Docs, Blogging, CmsKit, Account, FeatureManagement,
PermissionManagement, SettingManagement, VirtualFileExplorer, the module template...). ABP's plug-in
docs (abp.io/docs/latest/framework/architecture/modularity/plugin-modules) repeat it verbatim:
"mvcBuilder.PartManager.ApplicationParts.Add(new AssemblyPart(typeof(MyMvcUIPlugInModule).Assembly)) ...
This is required by ASP.NET Core. Otherwise, your controllers or views inside the plug-in doesn't work."

Structurally: ABP has NO enable/disable flag for HTTP surface. A module is either in the
[DependsOn] graph (loaded, part added, controllers exist) or it is not in the graph at all
(never loaded, no part, no controllers, no route, no OpenAPI entry). "Disabled" == "absent from
the composition graph". That is the dominant idiom.

(2b) Milan Jovanovic's "Evently" (the modular-monolith course sample; canonical modern reference).
Read at tamer-m-bayoumi/milanjovanovic-ModularMonolithCourse. Directly load-bearing for us:

  // src/Modules/Events/Evently.Modules.Events.Infrastructure/Evently.Modules.Events.Infrastructure.csproj
  <ProjectReference Include="..\Evently.Modules.Events.Application\..." />
  <ProjectReference Include="..\Evently.Modules.Events.Presentation\..." />   <-- INFRASTRUCTURE -> PRESENTATION

  // src/Modules/Events/Evently.Modules.Events.Presentation/Evently.Modules.Events.Presentation.csproj
  references only Application + Common.Presentation  (Presentation -> Application; no Infrastructure edge)

  // src/Modules/Events/Evently.Modules.Events.Infrastructure/EventsModule.cs
  public static IServiceCollection AddEventsModule(this IServiceCollection services, IConfiguration configuration)
  {
      services.AddDomainEventHandlers();
      services.AddIntegrationEventHandlers();
      services.AddInfrastructure(configuration);
      services.AddEndpoints(Presentation.AssemblyReference.Assembly);   // <-- HTTP surface, from Infrastructure
      return services;
  }

  // src/API/Evently.Api/Program.cs — composition root, one AddXModule call per module, then a single
  //   app.MapEndpoints();  which iterates the IEndpoint services that AddEndpoints registered.

This is EXACTLY Wallow's shape (module class lives in Infrastructure; HTTP lives in a sibling
project that references Application). Evently resolves the visibility problem the DESIGN note called
"architecturally impossible" with ONE csproj line: Infrastructure references its own module's
Presentation project, and hands its `AssemblyReference.Assembly` to the endpoint registrar. Note
also `AssemblyReference.cs` marker classes in every Presentation/Application project — the same
"assembly anchor" idea Wallow-3mbx.5 wants. Evently's own NetArchTest suite
(src/Modules/Events/Evently.Modules.Events.ArchitectureTests/Presentation/PresentationTests.cs)
does not treat Infrastructure->Presentation as a violation.

CORRECTION TO THE EXISTING DESIGN NOTE: "ApiAssembly on IWallowModule is architecturally
impossible" is too strong and should be retracted. It is currently unwired, and wiring it costs one
`<ProjectReference>` per module (Wallow.X.Infrastructure -> Wallow.X.Api). Verified acyclic on
disk: Wallow.ApiKeys.Api references only Application + Shared.Api/Contracts/Kernel and does NOT
reference Infrastructure, so Infrastructure -> Api introduces no cycle. The real objection is a
different one and should be argued on its merits, not on impossibility: it makes every module's
Infrastructure assembly transitively depend on ASP.NET Core MVC, which the migration-only host also
loads, and it inverts Wallow's documented Domain->Application->Infrastructure->Api ring order.

(2c) ardalis/Modulith (the repo Wallow-vmns.1 cites as a model). ModuleRegistrationExtensions.cs
(working/content/modulith/Modulith.Web/ModuleRegistrationExtensions.cs) is a directory scan of
`{SolutionName}.*.dll` in AppDomain.BaseDirectory, filtered by name (IsModuleAssembly excludes
".Web.", ".Tests.", "SharedKernel", ".UI.", ".HttpModels."), then AppDomain.Load per assembly and
reflection-invoke of a static `ConfigureServices` on the type implementing IRegisterModuleServices.
HTTP is FastEndpoints, which discovers endpoints from the loaded assemblies. So: MODULE PER ASSEMBLY,
enabled == assembly loaded. Program.cs even keeps the manual alternative in a comment:
"// Call the method where you are registering services for each module:
 // NewModuleModuleServiceRegistrar.ConfigureServices(builder.Services, builder.Configuration);"
Modulith is a WEAKER precedent than ABP/Evently — the filter is a hardcoded substring list on
file names and it BuildServiceProvider()s mid-registration (same smell as Wallow's ResolveEnabledModules,
cf. Wallow-3mbx.6). Do not copy its discovery; do copy its "module == assembly" premise.

(2d) Kamil Grzybek, modular-monolith-with-ddd. Notable NEGATIVE result: there are no per-module
HTTP assemblies at all. All 16 controllers live in the host project in per-module folders —
src/API/CompanyName.MyMeetings.API/Modules/{Meetings,Payments,UserAccess,Administration}/*Controller.cs.
Startup.cs does a plain `services.AddControllers()` and composes modules explicitly via Autofac
(`containerBuilder.RegisterModule(new MeetingsAutofacModule())` x4) plus an explicit
`InitializeModules(container)`. There is no enable/disable flag and no application-part manipulation
anywhere in the repo. The canonical DDD modular monolith puts HTTP in the composition root and
composes modules by explicit, hand-written registration. That is a vote for option (c)'s
"do it where both halves are visible" instinct, and against any discovery-and-filter scheme.

(2e) eShop / eShopOnContainers: not applicable. Those are separate processes per service; each
service is its own host with its own reference graph, so the question never arises.

=== 3. IS NAMESPACE-KEYED CONTROLLER FILTERING USED ANYWHERE REPUTABLE? NO. ===

Plainly: no reputable .NET codebase keys module HTTP registration on controller namespace, and I
found zero instances of it. GitHub code search for `IApplicationFeatureProvider ControllerFeature
Namespace language:csharp` (651 hits) is, once framework ref-assemblies and aspnetcore forks are
excluded, almost entirely GENERIC-CONTROLLER SYNTHESIS — providers that ADD closed generic
controller types, not ones that prune by name:
  - MUnique/OpenMU  src/Web/Shared/Services/GenericControllerFeatureProvider.cs  (adds
    JsonDownloadController<T,TSerializable> per supported type pair)
  - linq2db/linq2db  Source/LinqToDB.Remote.HttpClient.Server/ServiceConfigurationExtensions.cs
    (`SpecificControllerFeatureProvider<T>` adds exactly typeof(T))
  - ThomasBleijendaal/RapidCMS CollectionControllerFeatureProvider, DeeJayTC/net-dynamic-api
    GenericTypeControllerFeatureProvider, signumsoftware/framework SignumDynamicApiControllerProvider,
    mo-esmp GenericRestControllerFeatureProvider, AzureAD/microsoft-identity-web
    MicrosoftIdentityAccountControllerFeatureProvider
  - the framework's own docs sample (dotnetcore/aspnetcore-doc-cn .../app-parts/sample/.../GenericControllerFeatureProvider.cs)
All of these key on a TYPE the code names, never on a string namespace.

The one on-point REMOVAL precedent found — ivanpaulovich/clean-architecture-manga,
accounts-api/src/WebApi/Modules/Common/FeatureFlags/CustomControllerFeatureProvider.cs — removes
controllers at PartManager level, but keys on the [FeatureGate] ATTRIBUTE METADATA already present
on the controller type (walks controller.CustomAttributes, matches FeatureGateAttribute, reads its
enum ctor arg, calls IFeatureManager.IsEnabledAsync, feature.Controllers.RemoveAt(i)). That is a
hybrid of (a) and (b) and is exactly the fix for the activation-ordering defect in section 1: keep
the declaration on the controller but remove it upstream so the route genuinely never exists.
It is a legitimate design and worth knowing about. It is still not namespace-keyed.

Verdict on (b)-by-namespace: not an anti-pattern in the sense of "will break", but it is
UNPRECEDENTED and it is strictly dominated. It converts a compiler-checked fact (this assembly)
into an unchecked string convention, at zero benefit — verified on disk that assembly identity and
namespace are 1:1 today anyway (see section 4). The existing DESIGN note justified the namespace
key by in-repo precedent (TransformOperationModuleTag's ^Wallow\.(\w+)\.Api\b regex). That
precedent is legitimate for what it does — tagging OpenAPI operations, where you only have a
ControllerActionDescriptor and want a display string — but it is not a reason to key a
CORRECTNESS gate on a regex when the composition root is holding the Assembly object itself.

=== 4. ASP.NET CORE'S OWN GUIDANCE — PARTS, NOT PROVIDERS ===

Microsoft Learn, mvc/advanced/app-parts (aspnetcore-10.0), verbatim:
  "The main use case for application parts is to configure an app to discover (or AVOID LOADING)
   ASP.NET Core features from an assembly."
  "### Prevent loading resources
   Application parts can be used to *avoid* loading resources in a particular assembly or location.
   Add or remove members of the Microsoft.AspNetCore.Mvc.ApplicationParts collection to hide or make
   available resources. The order of the entries in the ApplicationParts collection isn't important.
   Configure the ApplicationPartManager before using it to configure services in the container...
   Call Remove on the ApplicationParts collection to remove a resource."
with the sample:
   services.AddMvc().ConfigureApplicationPartManager(apm => {
       var dependentLibrary = apm.ApplicationParts.FirstOrDefault(part => part.Name == "MyDependentLibrary");
       if (dependentLibrary != null) apm.ApplicationParts.Remove(dependentLibrary);
   });

Feature providers are described separately and narrowly: "Application feature providers examine
application parts and provide features for those parts... The order of feature providers in the
ApplicationPartManager.FeatureProviders can impact run time behavior. Later added providers can
react to actions taken by earlier added providers." Nothing in the doc proposes a feature provider
as the way to exclude an assembly — that job is given to ApplicationParts.Remove.

So the documented layering is: ApplicationParts answer "which assemblies participate"; feature
providers answer "what counts as a controller inside a participating assembly". A module
enable/disable flag is the first question, not the second. The existing DESIGN note's mechanism
verification (default ControllerFeatureProvider registered synchronously by AddControllersWithViews;
custom provider appended after it; PopulateFeature iterates in order over one mutable feature;
IActionDescriptorCollectionProvider is the single upstream source for routing, Asp.Versioning's
VersionedApiDescriptionProvider and Microsoft.AspNetCore.OpenApi's OpenApiDocumentService) is all
CORRECT and all still applies — part removal sits STRICTLY UPSTREAM of the point that note verified,
so every conclusion it drew (404 + ApiExplorer + OpenAPI all fixed at one site; no fight with
Asp.Versioning) holds a fortiori. Its OpenAPI test recipe
(GetRequiredKeyedService<IOpenApiDocumentProvider>("v1").GetOpenApiDocumentAsync()) is unaffected
and should be kept verbatim.

Also verified for the opt-in variant: the automatic reference-graph scan is an MSBuild feature,
disableable with a single property. /home/bcordes/.dotnet/sdk/10.0.302/Sdks/Microsoft.NET.Sdk.Razor/
targets/Microsoft.NET.Sdk.Razor.MvcApplicationPartsDiscovery.targets line 20:
  <GenerateMvcApplicationPartsAssemblyAttributes Condition="'$(GenerateMvcApplicationPartsAssemblyAttributes)' == '' AND '$(OutputType)' == 'Exe'">true</...>
Setting it false in Wallow.Api.csproj stops emission of Wallow.Api.MvcApplicationPartsAssemblyInfo.cs
entirely and makes explicit AddApplicationPart the sole source of parts.

Wallow-specific fact that makes assembly-keying exact (grep for ControllerBase/`: Controller` across
api/src, counted by owning project):
  Wallow.Identity.Api 18, Wallow.Notifications.Api 4, Wallow.Announcements.Api 4,
  Wallow.Storage.Api 2, Wallow.Inquiries.Api 1, Wallow.Branding.Api 1, Wallow.ApiKeys.Api 1
ZERO controllers in Wallow.Api or Wallow.Shared.Api. Every controller is in exactly one
Wallow.{Module}.Api assembly, so removing that assembly's part is exactly, completely, and
provably the module's whole HTTP surface. This also means the namespace key and the assembly key
select identical sets today — the namespace key buys nothing and can drift.

=== 5. RANKING FOR WALLOW ===

1st — (c) HOST-SIDE module->assembly mapping at the composition root, applied as
       ConfigureApplicationPartManager(apm => remove the AssemblyPart of every module NOT in
       `enabledModules`).
  + Microsoft's documented mechanism for exactly this ("Prevent loading resources").
  + Keyed on Assembly identity, compiler-checked; a renamed/moved project is a build error, not a
    silent 404. (ABP keys on Assembly identity too.)
  + Lives in Wallow.Api/WallowModules.cs, the ONE place that already references all seven .Api and
    all seven .Infrastructure projects — Grzybek's "compose where you can see both halves".
  + Consumes the existing `IReadOnlyList<IWallowModule> enabledModules` from Program.cs:177,
    satisfying the epic's registry-authoritative thesis.
  + Touches neither IWallowModule.cs nor any XModule.cs, so the stale Wallow-3mbx.5 -> Wallow-3mbx.1
    dep edge stays droppable (both prior notes already flagged this).
  + Default-on posture matches the fork story: a new module works the moment it's referenced; only
    an explicitly-disabled one disappears.
  Concrete shape: give each Wallow.{Module}.Api project an `AssemblyReference` marker class
  (Evently's pattern; also what Wallow-3mbx.5 wants), and widen `_allModules` from IWallowModule[]
  to a single array of (IWallowModule Module, Assembly ApiAssembly) pairs so an eighth module is
  still ONE list edited ONE time.

2nd — EXPLICIT OPT-IN AddApplicationPart (GenerateMvcApplicationPartsAssemblyAttributes=false +
       AddApplicationPart per enabled module).
  Philosophically the best answer and the closest match to ABP; it is what a from-scratch design
  would do. Ranked 2nd only for Wallow, for three concrete reasons:
  (i) The property is global. Killing the scan also kills auto-discovery for Wallow.Shared.Api, the
      host's own assembly, any Razor/CompiledRazorAssemblyPart, and anything the plugin system
      (AddWallowPlugins / InitializeWallowPluginsAsync) relies on. Every one of those becomes a new
      hand-maintained registration.
  (ii) It inverts the failure mode from "forgot to disable -> module appears when it shouldn't"
      to "forgot to enable -> module silently 404s everywhere". For a FORK-FIRST product whose
      advertised flow is "add a module", that is the worse of the two.
  (iii) It is strictly more change for the same observable outcome as #1 — #1 already yields exact
      routing + ApiExplorer + OpenAPI removal.
  Adopt it later if Wallow ever hosts modules that are NOT in the host's compile-time reference
  graph (real runtime plug-ins). At that point ABP's shape becomes the right one wholesale.

3rd — (b) ControllerFeatureProvider, whether keyed on namespace or on assembly.
  Works (the DESIGN note's mechanism verification is sound), and has one reputable removal
  precedent (clean-architecture-manga). But it answers the wrong question at the wrong layer:
  ApplicationParts decide participation, FeatureProviders decide what-is-a-controller. It is more
  code than #1 for the same effect, and the namespace variant additionally trades a checked fact for
  an unchecked string. If it is kept anyway, key it on `controller.Assembly` (ABP's key), never on
  `controller.Namespace`, and fix the unescaped-dot regex the DESIGN REVIEW already flagged.

4th — (a) [FeatureGate] per controller. DISQUALIFIED, not merely last: section 1 proves it does not
  produce a 404 for the reported failure, because the controller is constructed before action
  filters run. It also leaves the endpoints in the route table and the OpenAPI document. Its only
  defensible use in Wallow is per-endpoint PRODUCT flags on controllers with no gated dependencies —
  not module lifecycle.

=== 6. RECOMMENDATION AND WHAT WOULD FALSIFY IT ===

RECOMMEND #1: at the composition root, map each IWallowModule to its .Api assembly and remove the
AssemblyPart of every disabled module inside ConfigureApplicationPartManager, before any
AddControllersAsServices-style call. Keep the DESIGN note's test plan unchanged — all four
acceptance criteria are satisfied at a strictly earlier point in the same pipeline.

Falsifiers — any ONE of these should send the decision back:
1. A disabled module's .Api assembly contributes something the host still needs when the module is
   off (a shared filter, an IApplicationModelConvention, an ApiExplorer convention, embedded views,
   a tag helper). Removing the whole part removes all of it. CHECK: enumerate non-controller MVC
   types in each Wallow.{Module}.Api before implementing. If any exist, drop to the assembly-keyed
   variant of (b), which prunes only ControllerFeature.Controllers.
2. A controller for module X ever lands outside Wallow.X.Api. Today: none (section 4, zero
   controllers in Wallow.Api/Wallow.Shared.Api). If that changes, assembly-keying silently misses
   it — pin it with an architecture test asserting every ControllerBase subtype lives in a
   Wallow.*.Api assembly (ApiConventionTests.ControllerConventions_ShouldBeFollowed is the existing
   hook).
3. Removing a part turns out NOT to be observable through IOpenApiDocumentProvider in the Testing
   environment (i.e. the OpenAPI acceptance test fails for a reason unrelated to routing). Would
   indicate something re-populates parts after ConfigureApplicationPartManager. Nothing found that
   does, but it is the one runtime assumption not yet executed.
4. The team decides Infrastructure -> Api is acceptable after all (Evently ships exactly that edge,
   section 2b). Then PROMOTE the mapping onto IWallowModule as `Assembly ApiAssembly => Api.AssemblyReference.Assembly`
   and delete the host-side table — strictly better, because the module declares its own HTTP surface
   the same way it already declares HandlerAssemblies/DbContextTypes/SchemaName, and the epic's
   "one list, one time" goal is met by the module list alone. Cost to weigh: every Infrastructure
   assembly gains a transitive ASP.NET Core MVC dependency, including in the migration-only host,
   and the documented ring order needs amending. This is the one falsifier that IMPROVES the
   outcome rather than blocking it.

DESIGN v2 (SUPERSEDES the first DESIGN note): mechanism is now REMOVE THE DISABLED MODULE'S AssemblyPart from ApplicationPartManager.ApplicationParts, keyed on Assembly identity — not a ControllerFeatureProvider, not namespace regex. This is the PRIOR ART note's verdict, adopted verbatim.   using System.Reflection;
  using Microsoft.AspNetCore.Mvc.ApplicationParts;
  using Wallow.Announcements.Api.Controllers;
  using Wallow.ApiKeys.Api.Controllers;
  using Wallow.Branding.Api.Controllers;
  using Wallow.Identity.Api.Controllers;
  using Wallow.Inquiries.Api.Controllers;
  using Wallow.Notifications.Api.Controllers;
  using Wallow.Storage.Api.Controllers;

  /// <summary>
  /// Anchors each module's HTTP-carrying assembly on one of its own controller types, keyed by
  /// <see cref="IWallowModule.Name"/>. Deliberately NOT expressed as a positional zip against
  /// WallowModuleRegistry.All / _allModules (whichever this checkout currently has) — a Name-keyed
  /// side table survives either shape and stays correct if a module is ever reordered. Renaming or
  /// deleting one of these controller types is a compile error here, not a silent 404 — that is the
  /// point of anchoring on a real type instead of a namespace string.
  /// </summary>
  private static readonly (string ModuleName, Assembly ApiAssembly)[] _moduleApiAssemblies =
  [
      ("Identity", typeof(UsersController).Assembly),
      ("Branding", typeof(ClientBrandingController).Assembly),
      ("Notifications", typeof(NotificationsController).Assembly),
      ("Announcements", typeof(AnnouncementsController).Assembly),
      ("Storage", typeof(StorageController).Assembly),
      ("ApiKeys", typeof(ApiKeysController).Assembly),
      ("Inquiries", typeof(InquiriesController).Assembly),
  ];

  /// <summary>
  /// Removes the ApplicationPart for every module's .Api assembly that is NOT in
  /// <paramref name="enabledModules"/>, so a disabled module's controllers never enter the
  /// ActionDescriptorCollection that routing, Asp.Versioning's ApiExplorer, and
  /// Microsoft.AspNetCore.OpenApi's document generator all read from. Call this from
  /// ConfigureApplicationPartManager, immediately after AddControllersWithViews(), before the part
  /// manager is used to build any of those three.
  /// </summary>
  internal static void RemoveDisabledModuleApiParts(
      ApplicationPartManager manager, IReadOnlyList<IWallowModule> enabledModules)
  {
      HashSet<string> enabledNames = enabledModules.Select(m => m.Name).ToHashSet(StringComparer.Ordinal);
      HashSet<Assembly> disabledApiAssemblies =
      [
          .. _moduleApiAssemblies
              .Where(entry => !enabledNames.Contains(entry.ModuleName))
              .Select(entry => entry.ApiAssembly),
      ];

      List<ApplicationPart> partsToRemove =
      [
          .. manager.ApplicationParts.Where(part =>
              part is AssemblyPart assemblyPart && disabledApiAssemblies.Contains(assemblyPart.Assembly)),
      ];

      foreach (ApplicationPart part in partsToRemove)
      {
          manager.ApplicationParts.Remove(part);
      }
  }

=== 5. RISKS / WHAT WOULD FALSIFY THIS DESIGN ===

1. A future host-level (non-module) controller under `Wallow.Api` or `Wallow.Shared.Api` would be UNAFFECTED by this design either way (it lives in an assembly `_moduleApiAssemblies` never names, so its `AssemblyPart` is never a removal candidate) — this is actually safer than the superseded namespace-regex design's "unmatched = keep" default, because there is no matching step to get wrong; only assemblies explicitly on the list can ever be removed.
2. If a module's controller(s) are ever moved OUT of the anchor type chosen above (e.g. `UsersController` deleted/renamed for Identity), the anchor `typeof(UsersController).Assembly` becomes a COMPILE ERROR, not a silent gap — this is intentional and matches ABP's own AssemblyPart-removal precedent (keyed on Assembly identity via `typeof(Module).Assembly`, not on any string).
3. If a module ever ships an .Api project with a non-controller MVC extension point another module or the host needs even while that module is disabled (view component, tag helper, `IApplicationModelConvention`) — checked and absent today for all 7 (section 2's falsifier check) — whole-assembly-part removal would drop it too. Re-check this falsifier if a module's .Api project ever grows something other than `Controllers/*` and `Contracts/*`.
4. UPGRADE PATH, not a blocker: if the team later decides Infrastructure -> Api is an acceptable edge after all (Evently ships exactly this), promote the map onto `IWallowModule.ApiAssembly` and delete `_moduleApiAssemblies` — verified acyclic here, a second time. Cost to weigh at that time: (a) every module's Infrastructure assembly, and therefore Wallow.MigrationService transitively, gains a dependency on Microsoft.AspNetCore.Mvc; (b) the documented Domain->Application->Infrastructure->Api ring order needs an explicit exception; (c) it collides with Wallow.Modules.Registry's entire reason for existing (Infrastructure-only, shared by both hosts) — that project would need to either grow an Api reference too (reintroducing the leak into MigrationService) or the ApiAssembly map would need to live somewhere else again. Not worth it today; the zero-marginal-cost host-side map already satisfies the epic's registry-authoritative thesis (one place, `WallowModules.cs`, states which modules exist AND which HTTP assembly each owns) without paying any of these three costs.
5. Runtime-order assumption (reused from the DESIGN note, still unverified beyond decompilation): `IApplicationFeatureProvider<ControllerFeature>`/`ApplicationPartManager.PopulateFeature` ordering. Part removal happens strictly BEFORE any feature provider runs at all (parts, not features), so this design is actually LESS exposed to that assumption than the superseded one — but flag it for the reviewer regardless, since it underpins why `ConfigureApplicationPartManager`'s setup action seeing the fully-populated `ApplicationParts` list (not an empty one) is safe to rely on.
6. `IOpenApiDocumentProvider`'s keyed registration name (`"v1"`) must keep matching `AddOpenApi("v1", ...)` in `Extensions/ServiceCollectionExtensions.cs:47` — re-verify that string if the DI resolution in test 1(c) throws.

title: [epic] module registry follow-through — the gaps the IWallowModule registry left open
description:
The IWallowModule registry (Wallow-af3h, landed 2026-08-05) made the host stop guessing which
modules exist: handler discovery, DbContext registration and migration schemas are now declared by
each module instead of inferred from an AppDomain scan. Measured against JasperFx's own
modular-monolith guidance the Wolverine half is now essentially by-the-book -- MessageStorageSchemaName,
MultipleHandlerBehavior.Separated and AutoApplyTransactions are all set as the tutorial prescribes,
ApplicationAssembly is pinned, and MessageIdentity.IdAndDestination was correctly declined
(no external transport; AcquireOutgoingEnvelope already gives each local-queue copy a fresh Id).

This epic collects what the registry did NOT reach, found by a review of the change on 2026-08-05.
The common thread: the registry is authoritative for DI, Wolverine discovery and migrations, but
three other consumers still answer "which modules exist / are enabled" their own way, and one
module-owned fact (the schema name) is now stated in three places with nothing pinning them equal.

Children, in the order they are worth doing:

1. Wallow-k2zp / Wallow-lw4a (pre-existing) -- the module list still exists three times.
2. The HTTP surface is not gated at all. Highest runtime impact; ApiKeys ships disabled and its
   controller is still routed.
3. Schema name declared three times per module.
4. Feature-flag string literals in Program.cs that bypass the registry.
5. The temp-ServiceProvider in ResolveEnabledModules.
6. IWallowModule surface polish.
7. Wallow-scul / Wallow-juxf (pre-existing) -- the appsettings Modules.* blocks.

Done when every child is closed and adding an eighth module means editing one list, one time.

title: run-tests.sh never runs Wallow.Api.Tests integration tests, including HandlerCodegenTests
description:
Found by Wallow-af3h.2 (2026-08-04) while migrating HandlerCodegenTests. VERIFIED.

## The gap

`./scripts/run-tests.sh` NEVER RUNS `Wallow.Api.Tests`'s integration tests — including
`HandlerCodegenTests`, which is the repo's only guard that every discovered Wolverine
handler actually COMPILES under `ServiceLocationPolicy.NotAllowed`. That is the guard
protecting against the failure mode that silently dropped every outbound email
(Wallow-0tor / Wallow-nafb).

Mechanism:
- Every `run-tests.sh` invocation except the `integration` shorthand appends
  `--filter "Category!=E2E&Category!=Integration"`.
- The `integration` shorthand resolves to `Wallow.Identity.IntegrationTests` ONLY.

So neither `HandlerCodegenTests` nor the new `MultipleHandlerSeparationTests` is reachable
through the script, in any invocation. A developer can run the documented command, see
4912 green, and have exercised neither.

CI is NOT affected: `.github/workflows/ci.yml` runs
`dotnet test api/Wallow.slnx --filter "Category=Integration"` across the whole solution and
picks both up.

## Why this matters beyond convenience

`.claude/rules/TESTING.md` and `api/CLAUDE.md` both direct all backend testing through
`./scripts/run-tests.sh` and forbid bare `dotnet test`. Following the documented workflow
therefore silently skips the integration guards. Every agent on epic Wallow-af3h reported
"green" from a command that never compiled a handler chain.

## Local reproduction (what the script should be doing)

    dotnet test api/tests/Wallow.Api.Tests/Wallow.Api.Tests.csproj \
      --settings api/tests/coverage.runsettings --filter "Category=Integration"

Result at time of filing: 36 passed / 0 failed.

## Fix

Make `run-tests.sh integration` cover BOTH integration projects
(`Wallow.Api.Tests` Category=Integration + `Wallow.Identity.IntegrationTests`), not just
Identity's. Consider whether a bare `./scripts/run-tests.sh` should include them too, or at
minimum print a line stating that integration tests were excluded and how to run them —
silent exclusion is what made this invisible.

Keep `--settings api/tests/coverage.runsettings` on every path (TESTING.md requirement).

## Do not

Do not just document the gap. `.claude/rules/TESTING.md` says constraining how code is
exercised is the tooling's job, and a comment in a script does not stop the next agent from
reporting a false green.
notes:
FIXED. scripts/run-tests.sh now reaches every Category=Integration test, and a run that skips
them cannot be mistaken for one that ran them. No file under api/src/ was touched.

## The gap was bigger than filed

`integration` resolved to Wallow.Identity.IntegrationTests ONLY, so the script could not reach
the Category=Integration tests in SEVEN other assemblies, not just Wallow.Api.Tests:
Wallow.Storage.Tests (21), Wallow.Announcements.Tests (18), Wallow.Inquiries.Tests (17),
Wallow.Identity.Tests/Integration (6), Wallow.Shared.Infrastructure.Tests (11),
Wallow.Api.Tests (36). Measured: the shorthand went from 136 tests in 1 assembly to
245 in 7.

## What changed (scripts/run-tests.sh)

1. `integration` now runs `api/Wallow.slnx --filter "Category=Integration"` — the same selector
   .github/workflows/ci.yml uses. Selecting by CATEGORY rather than by project is what makes it
   correct as new integration suites appear; a project list would rot again.
2. New `all` shorthand: the whole solution with NO category filter (fast + integration, one run).
3. New optional SECOND argument, `integration` or `all`, narrowing that tier to whatever the
   first argument selected: `./scripts/run-tests.sh api integration` runs exactly the 36
   Wallow.Api.Tests integration tests. This is now the supported way to iterate on
   HandlerCodegenTests — previously the bead's own repro command was bare `dotnet test`, which
   .claude/rules/TESTING.md forbids. Any other second argument exits 2 rather than being ignored.
4. Shorthand matching is now case-insensitive for the tier decision too. Before,
   `./scripts/run-tests.sh Integration` resolved the Identity project but STILL appended the
   exclusion filter (the guard was `[[ "$MODULE_FILTER" != "integration" ]]`, case-sensitive), so
   it ran 0 tests and printed RESULT: PASS. A second silent false green, now impossible (see 5).
5. TOTAL == 0 is now RESULT: FAIL, exit 1. A selector that matches nothing can never report green.
6. Per-assembly rows are named from the TRX's own codeBase instead of the TRX filename.
   `LogFilePrefix=results` yields `results_<tfm>_<timestamp>.trx`, so EVERY row used to print
   "net10.0" — in a solution-wide run all 16 rows read "net10.0" and the FAILED TESTS section was
   headed "net10.0:". Rows now read "Wallow.Api.Tests PASS (passed: 36, ...)", which is what lets a
   reader confirm by eye that the codegen assembly was in the run. Assemblies matching no test are
   counted on one line, not listed (a category selector hits every project in the solution).
7. `--settings api/tests/coverage.runsettings` is unchanged and still on EVERY path.

Bug found and fixed during verification: `grep ... | head -1` under `set -o pipefail` SIGPIPEs grep
and killed the whole script at exit 141, mid-parse. Uses `grep -m1` now. Verified.

## DECISION: should a bare run include integration tests? NO — but silence is gone.

Rejected folding them into the bare run, for three reasons:
- **Docker.** They are Testcontainers-backed. Making the repo's most-run command hard-fail on any
  machine without a Docker daemon trades a visibility bug for an availability bug, and it hits
  forks and sandboxed agents hardest.
- **Cost.** Measured here: fast suites 4705 tests in ~90s; the integration tier adds ~2-4 min of
  container startup. That is a TDD inner loop paid dozens of times an hour.
- **CI already separates them** into two jobs with different services and hang timeouts
  (60s vs 5m). Merging them locally diverges from CI's shape for no gain.

What made this bug invisible was silence, not exclusion. So the exclusion now announces itself
in four places, three of which are mechanical rather than prose:
- a header line before the run ("Integration tests: EXCLUDED ... -- ./scripts/run-tests.sh integration");
- a `SCOPE:` line immediately UNDER the totals, so a pasted "4705 passed" carries its own scope;
- a closing `!! INTEGRATION TESTS DID NOT RUN !!` banner naming both commands that do run them;
- exit-code teeth: zero-test runs now FAIL (5 above), and named assembly rows (6 above) make the
  presence or absence of Wallow.Api.Tests visible instead of inferable.
Plus: CONTRIBUTING.md and the PR template now name `./scripts/run-tests.sh all` as the backend
gate, so the box a human ticks is the complete one.

## VERIFICATION (measured on this machine, Docker available)

Discovery — `Wallow.Api.Tests --filter Category=Integration` is exactly 36 tests and includes
`HandlerCodegenTests.EveryDiscoveredHandler_Compiles`,
`BootstrapAdminHandlerCodegenTests.BootstrapAdminCommand_CompilesAndRunsThroughTheWolverinePipeline`,
and all four `MultipleHandlerSeparationTests`.

- Clean HEAD (temporary git worktree, no working-tree edits), via the NEW script:
  `./scripts/run-tests.sh integration` -> `Wallow.Api.Tests PASS (passed: 36, failed: 0, skipped: 0)`.
  The two named classes EXECUTED and passed. Before this change no invocation ran them at all.
- Working tree, `./scripts/run-tests.sh integration` -> TOTAL 245 across 7 named assemblies
  (Wallow.Api.Tests 36, Wallow.Identity.IntegrationTests 136, Storage 21, Announcements 18,
  Inquiries 17, Shared.Infrastructure 11, Identity.Tests 6). Old behaviour: 136, one assembly.
- `./scripts/run-tests.sh api integration` -> TOTAL 36, and the FAILED TESTS list names only
  PerformanceTuningTests x3 + ValidatorRegistrationTests x1, i.e. the codegen guards ran green.
- Previously-working invocations still work: bare `./scripts/run-tests.sh` ran all 15 assemblies,
  4705 tests, with a BYTE-IDENTICAL command line to before
  (`... api/Wallow.slnx --filter Category!=E2E&Category!=Integration`); `kernel` 341 PASS;
  `Kernel` (uppercase) 341 PASS; `identity` 1603 PASS; path pass-through
  `api/tests/Wallow.Tests.Common` resolves and now correctly FAILs as a zero-test run (exit 1);
  `kernel bogus` exits 2 with a message.

## Failures observed that are NOT mine

- `api integration` fails 4/36 in the working tree (PerformanceTuningTests x3,
  ValidatorRegistrationTests x1). The SAME 36 pass 36/36 at HEAD in a clean worktree. They are
  attributable to the concurrent unstaged change in api/src/Wallow.Api/Program.cs
  (UseEntityFrameworkCoreTransactions(Lightweight) + Policies.AutoApplyTransactions()).
  Worth flagging to whoever owns that change: a bare run does not surface it. This bead's thesis,
  demonstrated live.
- Transient mass failures during parallel runs (Storage 21/21, Identity.Tests 6/6, then
  Identity.Tests 720 in the bare run) were Docker/Testcontainers contention from my own concurrent
  verification runs. Each passes in isolation: `storage integration` 21 PASS, `identity integration`
  6 PASS, `identity` 1603 PASS. Note for future work: a solution-wide integration run starts many
  Postgres containers in parallel and is sensitive to host load.

## Docs updated (kept in lockstep with the script)

api/CLAUDE.md (Commands + shorthand list + the two-argument form), .claude/rules/TESTING.md (new
bullet: a bare run does NOT cover integration; do not report green off one), .claude/agents/
csharp-developer.md (build commands + a step 10 in its TDD loop), docs/development/testing.md,
docs/getting-started/developer-guide.md, docs/getting-started/onboarding.md, README.md (both test
blocks), CONTRIBUTING.md, .github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md,
api/tests/Modules/Identity/Wallow.Identity.IntegrationTests/README.md.

## FOLLOW-UPS (not done here)

1. THREE FILES UNDER api/src/ STILL SAY THE OLD THING — I was locked out of api/src/ by the
   concurrent Program.cs work: api/src/Modules/Identity/CLAUDE.md and
   api/src/Modules/Identity/README.md both document `run-tests.sh integration` as
   "Wallow.Identity.IntegrationTests" (it is now solution-wide Category=Integration), and
   api/src/Wallow.Api/README.md lists only the bare and `api` forms. Small edits, needs doing.
2. A THIRD TIER EXISTS AND IS UNDOCUMENTED: `Wallow.Identity.IntegrationTests.OAuth2.
   CrossOrgRoleIsolationTests` (3 tests) carries `[Trait("Category", "CrossTenant")]`, NOT
   Integration. CI runs it as its own job (`--filter "Category=CrossTenant"`). Consequences: the
   old project-scoped `integration` ran them incidentally; now they run in a BARE run and in `all`,
   but not in `integration`. They are Testcontainers-backed, which means a bare
   `./scripts/run-tests.sh` ALREADY requires Docker today — verified, they passed inside the bare
   run above. Someone should decide whether CrossTenant belongs in the excluded tier; if it does,
   the bare filter should exclude it and `integration` should include it.
RESOLVED in 5d030931.

CORRECTION to this bead's severity framing: CI was NOT blind to the gap.
.github/workflows/ci.yml:174 runs `dotnet test api/Wallow.slnx --filter
"Category=Integration"` solution-wide in its own job, and HandlerCodegenTests
has carried [Trait("Category","Integration")] the whole time (verified against
HEAD~4). So the guard has been running on every PR. The gap was LOCAL-ONLY:
no run-tests.sh invocation could reach it, and every CLAUDE.md points agents at
run-tests.sh. Real impact = agents reporting green off a bare run, not an
unguarded codebase. The 'unrun for months' wording is now corrected in the
script comment.

Also corrected while reviewing: the agent's 'eight assemblies' figure was an
off-by-one. Measured seven -- Api, Identity.IntegrationTests, Identity,
Storage, Announcements, Inquiries, Shared.Infrastructure. (The two integration
base classes in Wallow.Tests.Common propagate the trait by inheritance, but
their derived set is a strict subset of the assemblies that declare it, so they
add nothing.) Matches the measured run: 245 tests across 7 assemblies. Fixed in
6 files, plus two dependent 'other seven' -> 'other six' counts.

Stale docs the agent flagged but was locked out of, now fixed: it reported 3
files under api/src/; there were 2 (Modules/Identity/CLAUDE.md,
Modules/Identity/README.md). Two MORE it missed in files it HAD edited:
api/CLAUDE.md still called `integration` Identity's shorthand, and
developer-guide.md:287 called Identity's the 'only integration-test project in
the repository'. Identity's integration suite now has no shorthand at all --
documented as path + tier, since the default filter excludes all its specs and
a zero-test run is now a failure.

Verified: bash -n clean; invalid second arg exits 2.

title: introduce IWallowModule registry to replace the AppDomain handler-discovery loop
description:
Plan: docs/plans/2026-08-04/2129-wolverine-module-registration.md — Problem 2 & 7, Phase 3.
THE CENTRAL BEAD OF THE EPIC. Read the plan's Design section before starting.

Supersedes the APPROACH in Wallow-vmns.1 (which proposed a hand-rolled assembly attribute
carrying `(name, DbContext type, feature-flag key)`). An interface carries the DbContext
types, schema name and migration ordering that shape omits.

## The interface

Goes in `Wallow.Shared.Infrastructure`. VERIFIED: that project ALREADY has
`<FrameworkReference Include="Microsoft.AspNetCore.App" />`
(`Wallow.Shared.Infrastructure.csproj:11`), so `WebApplication`/`IServiceCollection`/
`IConfiguration` are in scope with NO new package, and all 7 module `.Infrastructure`
projects already reference it. No architecture test is violated: `CleanArchitectureTests`
forbids `Microsoft.AspNetCore` only in Domain and Application, never Infrastructure, and
does not inspect `Wallow.Shared.*` at all.

    public interface IWallowModule
    {
        string Name { get; }                       // "Storage" -> FeatureManagement:Modules.Storage
        bool IsCore { get; }                       // Identity: always on, migrates first
        IEnumerable<Assembly> HandlerAssemblies { get; }

        IServiceCollection AddServices(
            IServiceCollection services,
            IConfiguration configuration,
            IHostEnvironment environment);
    }

**`IHostEnvironment` is REQUIRED.** Six modules match `AddXModule(services, configuration)`,
but `IdentityModuleExtensions.cs:12-19` is
`AddIdentityModule(this IServiceCollection, IConfiguration, IHostEnvironment)` and
`WallowModules.cs:46` passes `builder.Environment`. Identity is the one module the registry
cannot make optional, so it is the one the interface must fit. Six wrappers carry an unused
parameter — cheaper than special-casing Identity out of the registry.

**`InitializeAsync` is deliberately OMITTED.** All seven `InitializeXModuleAsync` methods
are no-ops returning `Task.FromResult(app)`. Delete them rather than keeping an interface
member alive for seven methods that do nothing.

**Marker types are NEW WORK, not reuse.** `typeof(StorageApplicationMarker)` does not
exist — the repo has exactly ONE marker (`INotificationsApplicationMarker.cs`) and it is
unreferenced dead code. PREFER using an already-public handler type per assembly
(e.g. `typeof(SubmitInquiryHandler).Assembly`) over authoring 8 new marker files.

## Handler census (drives `HandlerAssemblies`) — verified, do not re-derive

Notifications 45 Application / 0 Infra · Announcements 12/0 · Inquiries 11/0 ·
Storage 10/0 · Identity 9/3 (returns TWO assemblies) · ApiKeys 0/0 · Branding 0/0.

ApiKeys and Branding declare their Application assembly anyway — harmless, and it is what
makes the latent codegen bug impossible.

## Wolverine wiring

    foreach (Assembly assembly in enabledModules.SelectMany(m => m.HandlerAssemblies))
    {
        opts.Discovery.IncludeAssembly(assembly);
    }

replacing the `AppDomain.CurrentDomain.GetAssemblies()` loop at `Program.cs:229-234`.

**Why not `[assembly: WolverineModule]`:** it discovers unconditionally. A disabled
module's handlers would be found, codegen would build chains, and
`ServiceLocationPolicy.NotAllowed` (`Program.cs:214`) would throw on DI that was never
registered.

## "Resolve once" — the threading MUST be specified, or this bead is cosmetic

Today `IFeatureManager` is resolved TWICE FROM DIFFERENT PROVIDERS:
`AddWallowModules` (`WallowModules.cs:36-39`) builds a TEMPORARY `ServiceProvider` from the
unfinished `builder.Services` and resolves synchronously; `InitializeWallowModulesAsync`
(`WallowModules.cs:93`) resolves again from the final `app.Services`. So:

1. Compute the enabled set at the `AddWallowModules` call site (`Program.cs:175`) — the
   only point before `UseWolverine` at `:182` needs it.
2. Hold it in a `<Main>$`-scoped local for the Wolverine lambda to capture.
3. CHANGE `AddWallowModules`'s return (currently `IServiceCollection`) and
   `InitializeWallowModulesAsync`'s signature (currently `WebApplication` only) to carry the
   precomputed list rather than re-resolving.

Without step 3 this regresses to today's two independent resolutions and only removes
`if`/`else` syntax.

## Second consumer — do not miss it

`api/src/Wallow.Api/Extensions/AsyncApiEndpointExtensions.cs:15-17` runs the SAME
`AppDomain.CurrentDomain.GetAssemblies().Where(name.StartsWith("Wallow."))` pattern to feed
`EventFlowDiscovery` for the AsyncAPI document — same load-order dependency, producing an
AsyncAPI doc that varies with JIT order. Point it at `HandlerAssemblies` too.

## OPEN MEASUREMENT — do this first, it scopes the bead

Whether the `.Application` assemblies (where most handlers live) stay unloaded when a flag
is off was NOT settled by source reading. Log `AppDomain.CurrentDomain.GetAssemblies()`
inside the `UseWolverine` lambda with a module disabled, and `bd note` the result before
writing code.

## Tests this breaks — ALL FOUR must be deleted, verified by reading the file

`api/tests/Wallow.Architecture.Tests/ModuleRegistrationTests.cs`:

| Lines | Method | Why it breaks |
|---|---|---|
| `:23-31` | `WallowModules_ShouldRegister_AllModules` | `File.ReadAllText` + text contains `Add{Module}Module(configuration` |
| `:54-62` | `WallowModules_ShouldInitialize_AllModulesWithDbContext` | `File.ReadAllText` + text contains `Initialize{Module}ModuleAsync()` |
| `:169-177` | `AllDiscoveredModules_ShouldBeRegistered_InWallowModules` | same, over reflection-discovered names |
| `:102-127` | `Module_ShouldProvide_InitializeModuleExtensionMethod` | NOT a source-text test — reflects for `Initialize{Module}ModuleAsync` and asserts `GetParameters().HaveCount(1)`; the seven methods are being deleted, so `GetMethod` returns null |

The first three violate `.claude/rules/TESTING.md` outright ("no `readFileSync` over
`src/`"): **delete, do not port.** `MigrationRemovalTests.cs:37,49` (`File.ReadAllText` over
the seven `*ModuleExtensions.cs` paths listed at `:9-18`) is the same violation.

SAFE — leave alone: `Module_ShouldProvide_AddModuleExtensionMethod` (`:70-95`) checks only
parameters `[0]` and `[1]` by position and never asserts a count, so appending
`IHostEnvironment` to the six `AddXModule` signatures leaves it green.

## Also in scope

Delete the unused `Wallow.Identity.Api.csproj:18` ProjectReference to
`Wallow.Identity.Infrastructure` — grep confirms ZERO usages in `Wallow.Identity.Api`.
Two-character diff; `CleanArchitectureTests.ApiLayer_ShouldNotDependOn_InfrastructureLayer`
stays green.

## Out of scope (do not touch)

The `.slnx` entry and `Wallow.Api.csproj` ProjectReferences stay manual.
`ServiceLocationPolicy.NotAllowed` and the six `AlwaysUseServiceLocationFor` entries
(`Program.cs:214-220`) stay exactly as written. `CustomizeHandlerDiscovery` excluding
`IAuthorizationHandler` (`Program.cs:227`) stays.

## Acceptance

`./scripts/run-tests.sh` green. Adding a Wolverine handler to ApiKeys or Branding (with the
flag ON) compiles and runs — this is the latent bug the registry exists to close.
notes:
CROSS-CHECK from Wallow-af3h.8 (closed): that agent independently flagged ModuleRegistrationTests.cs:23-24 and :54-55 as File.ReadAllText-over-src/ TESTING.md violations. Already in scope here — this bead deletes :23-31, :54-62 and :169-177 outright. No extra work; recording the agreement so it is not re-litigated as a new finding.

Consequence for Wallow-vmns.7: those three methods are being DELETED, not derived. vmns.7 should not plan to 'derive the list' for them.
PRE-FLIGHT VERIFICATION (read-only, by the coordinator while af3h.3 held Program.cs). Three load-bearing claims re-confirmed against source, so the implementer does not have to:

1. 'All seven InitializeXModuleAsync are no-ops' — CONFIRMED, all seven read exactly
   'return Task.FromResult(app);' with no other statement (Announcements, Branding, Storage,
   Inquiries, ApiKeys, Identity, Notifications). Omitting InitializeAsync from the interface and
   deleting the seven methods is safe.

2. 'Six modules are (IServiceCollection, IConfiguration); Identity alone adds IHostEnvironment' —
   CONFIRMED verbatim. Inquiries:10, ApiKeys:9, Notifications:30, Storage:10, Announcements:20,
   Branding:9 take two parameters; IdentityModuleExtensions.cs:12-15 takes three. So the
   interface must carry IHostEnvironment and six wrappers carry an unused parameter, exactly as
   the bead specifies.

3. Handler census — the STRUCTURAL claim is confirmed: Identity is the only module with handlers
   in both its Application and Infrastructure assemblies (hence HandlerAssemblies returns TWO for
   it), and ApiKeys and Branding have zero handlers in either. Those are the two facts the design
   turns on. I did NOT re-derive the exact per-module counts — the bead marks them verified, and
   my check was a cruder file-level grep, so where it differed by one I am deferring to the bead
   rather than recording a correction.

Still OPEN and still first: the AppDomain measurement (whether .Application assemblies stay
unloaded with a flag off). It needs a temporary edit to Program.cs, so it could not be done while
af3h.3 was in flight.
SCOPE OVERLAP — do not do this twice. This bead's 'Also in scope' item (delete the unused Wallow.Identity.Api.csproj:18 ProjectReference to Wallow.Identity.Infrastructure) is ALREADY an independent open bead: Wallow-0s76 'chore(identity): drop the unused Wallow.Identity.Api -> Wallow.Identity.Infrastructure ProjectReference'. Whoever gets there first does it and closes the other; it is a two-character diff and does not need to gate the registry work either way.
OPEN MEASUREMENT — RESOLVED. Ran 2026-08-05. Method: temporary probe inside the UseWolverine
lambda, immediately before the AppDomain discovery loop, dumping every loaded assembly named
Wallow.*. Probe reverted; git status clean. Measured on the REAL host (dotnet run against
Wallow.Api, Development, bogus DB/Redis endpoints — the lambda runs at builder.Build(), long
before any connection is attempted), NOT only the test host, because the test host turned out to
be a confound (see finding 4).

ANSWER TO THE QUESTION AS ASKED: YES — a disabled module's .Application assembly stays UNLOADED.

1. All six optional modules OFF (Storage, Announcements, ApiKeys, Inquiries, Notifications,
   Branding). Absent at Wolverine-config time: all six .Application assemblies, and five of the
   six .Domain. Present: all six .Infrastructure, plus Identity's three (Identity is always on).
2. All modules ON: all seven modules' .Application + .Domain + .Infrastructure are loaded.

So the AppDomain loop is CORRECT TODAY — but by coincidence, and the coincidence is now named:

- .Infrastructure loads because JIT-ing AddWallowModules resolves the AddXModule call targets in
  branches that are NOT taken. Load says nothing about enablement.
- .Application loads only when AddXModule's BODY actually executes and touches an Application
  type. That is what makes the disable case work — and it is not a guarantee, it is a property
  each module's registration body happens to have.

3. THE LATENT BUG, RESTATED PRECISELY. The bead says adding a handler to ApiKeys or Branding
   would not be discovered. As measured that is NOT true today: with the flag on, both modules'
   .Application assemblies ARE loaded before Wolverine configures, so a handler added there WOULD
   be found. The real defect is the dependency itself — discovery is a function of what earlier
   code happened to touch. A module whose AddXModule body stopped touching its own .Application
   assembly (a refactor moving an interface to Domain would do it) would silently lose every
   handler in that assembly, with no error: Wolverine would just build fewer chains.
