title: enable Policies.AutoApplyTransactions()
description:
Plan: docs/plans/2026-08-04/2129-wolverine-module-registration.md — Problem 5, Phase 1.

BLOCKED BY the Testing-persistence bead and the `Separated` bead. Do not start until both
are closed — see those beads for the measured failure and the ordering rationale.

## Change

`api/src/Wallow.Api/Program.cs`, inside the `UseWolverine` lambda:

    opts.Policies.AutoApplyTransactions();

Measured effect: `transactional` 0 -> 65 chains.

## Two hazards to check for during implementation

1. **Commit-boundary shift.** `EFCorePersistenceFrameProvider` moves `SaveChangesAsync`
   into a middleware postprocessor. `SendNotificationHandler` currently saves explicitly
   and then pushes to realtime. Any handler refactored to drop its explicit save would push
   BEFORE commit, creating a read-your-writes race for SSE consumers. Audit handlers that
   both save and dispatch.
2. **Multi-DbContext chains become fatal.** `EFCorePersistenceFrameProvider
   .DetermineDbContextType` THROWS when a chain's transitive dependencies reach more than
   one DbContext. None exists today, but with 7 module DbContexts the first cross-module
   handler injecting two repositories becomes a codegen failure on first message. Note this
   in `api/CLAUDE.md` if it is not already implied by the existing codegen guidance.

## Acceptance

`./scripts/run-tests.sh` green. `bd note` the final transactional chain count.
notes:
FROM Wallow-af3h.1 (blocker, now done): persistence in Testing is fixed, but it is NOT the only
prerequisite. A SECOND, environment-independent blocker was found and its fix was verified.

Enabling `opts.Policies.AutoApplyTransactions()` alone still fails. Three
Wallow.Identity.IntegrationTests CrossOrgRoleIsolationTests (Category=CrossTenant — they DO run in
./scripts/run-tests.sh) return 500 on login, server-side cause:

  System.InvalidOperationException: The configured execution strategy
  'NpgsqlRetryingExecutionStrategy' does not support user-initiated transactions.
     at ...EmailMessageRepository.SaveChangesAsync
     at Internal.Generated.WolverineHandlers.SendEmailCommandHandler...

All seven modules call `npgsql.EnableRetryOnFailure(...)` in their DbContext registration
(Announcements:42, Inquiries:35, ApiKeys:47, Branding:46, Notifications:63, Identity:241,
Storage:62). NpgsqlRetryingExecutionStrategy rejects user-initiated BeginTransactionAsync, which
is precisely what AutoApplyTransactions' DEFAULT TransactionMiddlewareMode.Eager issues.

SHIP THIS LINE WITH THE POLICY (verified green, deliberately left out of af3h.1's diff because it
is inert without the policy):

  using Wolverine.Persistence;   // for TransactionMiddlewareMode
  opts.UseEntityFrameworkCoreTransactions(TransactionMiddlewareMode.Lightweight);
  opts.Policies.AutoApplyTransactions();

Lightweight (Wolverine 5.15+) uses DbContext.SaveChangesAsync() as the sole transaction boundary
instead of an explicit BeginTransactionAsync, so it runs inside EF's own execution strategy and
EnableRetryOnFailure keeps working. Rejected alternative: removing EnableRetryOnFailure from all
seven modules — that surrenders transient-fault retry on every DB call in the product, HTTP paths
included, to fix a message-handler problem.

MEASURED with both lines on: chains=88, transactional=66 (bead text said 65 — one chain more now).
./scripts/run-tests.sh 4912/4912 PASS, and `--filter "Category=Integration"` (incl.
HandlerCodegenTests) all PASS.

Measurement gotcha: under Lightweight the policy's frames are plain JasperFx MethodCall frames, so
counting by frame.GetType().Name reports 0 — unwrap MethodCall.HandlerType/.Method. Each of the 66
chains gains a `<Module>DbContext.SaveChangesAsync` POSTPROCESSOR (SendEmailCommand's chain ends
with NotificationsDbContext.SaveChangesAsync).

CAVEAT Lightweight gives up: two bulk ops bypass SaveChangesAsync and stay outside the handler's
unit of work — Notifications TenantPushConfigurationRepository.cs:45 (ExecuteDeleteAsync) and
NotificationRepository.cs:53 (ExecuteUpdateAsync). Single statements, atomic on their own; Eager
would have covered them.

Full detail on Wallow-af3h.1's note.
GREEN. FILES=api/src/Wallow.Api/Program.cs (working tree, uncommitted); api/CLAUDE.md (see WARNING below).

## Change shipped

Both lines together, as af3h.1's note demanded:

  using Wolverine.Persistence;   // TransactionMiddlewareMode
  opts.UseEntityFrameworkCoreTransactions(TransactionMiddlewareMode.Lightweight);
  opts.Policies.AutoApplyTransactions();

Replaces the bare opts.UseEntityFrameworkCoreTransactions() that was at :249. Both carry a comment
block recording WHY Lightweight rather than the default Eager (NpgsqlRetryingExecutionStrategy vs
user-initiated BeginTransactionAsync), the rejected alternative (ripping EnableRetryOnFailure out of
seven modules), the two bulk ops Lightweight does not cover, and the two newly-fatal hazards.
Mode confirmed against JasperFx's own docs (guide/durability/efcore/transactional-middleware.md,
sample_using_lightweight_ef_core_transactions) — not from memory.

## MEASURED COUNTS (temporary probe in Wallow.Api.Tests, since deleted; tree verified clean)

  topLevelChains (HandlerGraph.Chains)     = 88
  allChains      (HandlerGraph.AllChains())= 94
  transactional                            = 66

The bead/af3h.1 expected 'chains=88'. Both numbers are right and they are not in conflict: 88 is
Chains, 94 is AllChains(). Under MultipleHandlerBehavior.Separated (af3h.2) the four multi-handler
message types replace 1 placeholder parent with N sticky sub-chains: EmailVerifiedEvent 2,
InquirySubmittedEvent 3, InquiryCommentAddedEvent 3, InquiryStatusChangedEvent 2 = 10 sub-chains for
4 parents, so 88 - 4 + 10 = 94. transactional=66 matches af3h.1 exactly.

Measurement gotcha confirmed as described: the policy's frames are plain JasperFx MethodCall, so
frame.GetType().Name reports 0. Unwrapped via MethodCall.HandlerType (assignable to DbContext) +
MethodCall.Method.Name (SaveChangesAsync). Each of the 66 gains a <Module>DbContext.SaveChangesAsync
POSTPROCESSOR. Spot-checked: SendEmailCommand -> NotificationsDbContext.SaveChangesAsync,
SubmitInquiryCommand -> InquiriesDbContext, BootstrapAdminCommand -> IdentityDbContext,
UploadFileCommand -> StorageDbContext, PublishAnnouncementCommand -> AnnouncementsDbContext.

Note EmailVerifiedEvent -> InquiriesDbContext appears as its OWN sub-chain. That is the plan's
Phase-1 ordering warning resolving correctly: because Separated landed first, only the Inquiries
handler's sub-chain is transactional. The Notifications handler for the same event reaches no
DbContext and stays non-transactional. Under the old combined behaviour this would have been one
shared cross-module transaction.

## HAZARD 1 — commit-boundary shift: AUDITED, NO ACTION TAKEN (as instructed)

The middleware ADDS a SaveChangesAsync postprocessor; it does not remove any explicit save. So
nothing changes today. The risk is purely future: deleting an explicit save on the theory the
postprocessor covers it.

Save BEFORE dispatch (correct today, must stay that way):
  - SendNotificationHandler (Notifications InApp) - save :31, notificationService.SendToUserAsync :33.
    Confirmed as the bead described. INotificationService -> SseNotificationService -> ISseDispatcher
    -> RedisSseDispatcher. Genuinely external/observable; this is the read-your-writes race case.
  - SendPushHandler - save :42, PublishAsync(DeliverPushCommand) :55.
  - GetUploadPresignedUrlHandler (Storage) - save :62, PublishAsync(ScanUploadedFileCommand) :64.
  - PublishAnnouncementHandler - repository.UpdateAsync :28 (AnnouncementRepository saves internally
    :44-47), bus.PublishAsync(AnnouncementPublishedEvent) :32.
  - SendEmailHandler - save :44, SMTP :48, save :62 (save/send/save).
  - SendSmsHandler - save :38, Twilio :42, save :61 (save/send/save).
  - BootstrapAdminHandler - indirectly via OrganizationService: saves :60/:61/:75, publishes :77.

FOUND: four handlers ALREADY dispatch BEFORE they save. Pre-existing, unrelated to this change,
NOT touched, reported for the record:
  - DeliverPushHandler (Notifications Push) - provider.SendAsync :30, save :53 inside a finally.
    Push leaves the process before the delivery record commits.
  - UploadFileHandler (Storage) - storageProvider.UploadAsync :59, save :78. Failed save orphans
    the object in S3/local.
  - DeleteFileHandler (Storage) - storageProvider.DeleteAsync :25, save :29. Failed save leaves a
    row pointing at a deleted key.
  - DeleteBucketHandler (Storage) - DeleteAsync in a loop :40, save :48. Same shape, N objects.
These are object-store/push-provider calls rather than SSE fan-out, so a different failure mode from
the read-your-writes race, but the ordering is dispatch-then-save in all four. Worth a separate bead;
not filed here.

Handlers that dispatch but never persist (no ordering risk at all): all
Notifications.Application/EventHandlers/*, and the three Inquiries domain-event relays.

## HAZARD 2 — multi-DbContext chains: CONFIRMED CLEAN, TWO WAYS

(a) Static audit of all 80 handler-bearing files under Modules/*/Wallow.*.{Application,Infrastructure}
    plus Shared.Infrastructure, resolving every injected type to its Infrastructure implementation.
(b) Empirically, in the probe: counted DISTINCT DbContext types per chain across all 94 chains.
    Zero chains reached more than one. Max is 1.

The reason it stays clean is that the shared cross-module service interfaces reach NO DbContext:
ISseDispatcher -> RedisSseDispatcher (Redis), IEmailService -> EmailProviderAdapter -> SmtpEmailProvider,
IEmailTemplateService -> SimpleEmailTemplateService (ILogger + IConfiguration), IStorageProvider ->
Local/S3, IFileScanner -> ClamAv/NoOp, ITenantContext -> POCO. All Wolverine middleware is static
Before(Envelope, ...) with no EF deps.

Near-misses checked and cleared:
  - EmailVerifiedInquiryLinkHandler: cross-module EVENT but injects only IInquiryRepository. Inquiries only.
  - PublishAnnouncementHandler: IAnnouncementTargetingService injects two Announcements repositories
    + TimeProvider, NOT IUserQueryService. Announcements only.
  - Service-account handlers: IServiceAccountService -> OpenIddictServiceAccountService uses
    IOpenIddictApplicationManager, and OpenIddict is bound to IdentityDbContext
    (IdentityInfrastructureExtensions.cs:59-60). Both legs land on IdentityDbContext, not ApiKeys.
  - IUserService / IUserQueryService / IApiKeyService: grepped repo-wide. IUserService has ZERO
    consumers anywhere; the other two appear only in controllers and middleware. NONE is injected
    into any Wolverine handler, so RedisApiKeyService -> ApiKeysDbContext never enters a chain.
  - ExpireInvitationsHandler injects IdentityDbContext DIRECTLY - the only handler taking a raw
    DbContext. Still one context.
  - BrandingDbContext: Branding exposes no Wolverine handlers at all. Zero risk.

ONE THING TO KNOW (not an offender, but the closest thing to one): AuthAuditEventHandlers
(Identity.Infrastructure/Handlers/) reaches an EIGHTH DbContext, AuthAuditDbContext, via AuthAuditService
(Shared.Infrastructure.Core/Auditing/AuthAuditService.cs:7-9). It is injected as
IDbContextFactory<AuthAuditDbContext>, which is NOT assignable to DbContext, so
DetermineDbContextType does not see it and those chains get no transaction middleware at all
(the probe confirms they are among the 28 non-transactional). It is the one place a second context
type is reachable from a handler chain, and it would surprise anyone if Wolverine's detection ever
widened to factories.

## KNOWN CAVEAT — bulk ops outside the unit of work: LIST CONFIRMED COMPLETE

grep for ExecuteDeleteAsync|ExecuteUpdateAsync across api/src/Modules AND all of api/src returns
exactly the two the bead named, and nothing else anywhere in api/src:
  - Notifications/.../Repositories/TenantPushConfigurationRepository.cs:45  ExecuteDeleteAsync
  - Notifications/.../Repositories/NotificationRepository.cs:53             ExecuteUpdateAsync
Both single statements, atomic on their own. Eager would have covered them; this is the one thing
Lightweight gives up. No others exist.

## TEST RUNS — all four, final sequential pass, each reported separately

1. ./scripts/run-tests.sh                                        PASS  4912/4912, 0 failed
     (SCOPE line: fast suites only, Category=Integration filtered out)
2. ./scripts/run-tests.sh integration                            PASS   245/245,  0 failed
     (7 assemblies solution-wide, incl. HandlerCodegenTests)
3. dotnet test Wallow.Api.Tests --filter Category=Integration    PASS    36/36,   0 failed
4. dotnet test api/Wallow.slnx --filter Category=CrossTenant     PASS   196/196,  0 failed
     Shared.Infrastructure 4, Identity.Tests 185, Storage 4, Identity.IntegrationTests 3.
     The Identity.IntegrationTests 3 are the CrossOrgRoleIsolationTests that fail under Eager. Green.

dotnet build api/Wallow.slnx: 0 Warnings, 0 Errors (AnalysisMode=All + TreatWarningsAsErrors).
dotnet format api/Wallow.slnx: run, no changes produced.
No var used. No logger.LogInformation added (no logging added at all).

## THE 4 REPORTED FAILURES (PerformanceTuningTests x3, ValidatorRegistrationTests x1) — NOT REPRODUCIBLE, ENVIRONMENTAL

The coordinator relayed that a parallel agent saw these fail against my working tree while passing
at HEAD. I could not reproduce them in 9 consecutive runs against this exact working tree:
  - 3x dotnet test Wallow.Api.Tests --filter Category=Integration  -> 36/36 every time
  - 2x dotnet test Wallow.Api.Tests (ALL categories)               -> 363/363 every time
  - plus the 4 authoritative runs above
I DID see the same shape twice early on and both were provably environmental: one run failed 7
tests with coverlet reporting 'The process cannot access the file Wallow.Identity.Application.pdb
because it is being used by another process' (a second test process running concurrently), and one
failed 3; both went green on immediate re-run with no code change.

Two concrete mechanisms, neither caused by this change:
  (a) Coverlet instrumentation contention when two agents run the same assemblies at once.
  (b) A real pre-existing global-state race: WallowApiFactory sets ConnectionStrings__DefaultConnection
      as a PROCESS-WIDE environment variable (WallowApiFactory.cs:75) and nulls it on dispose (:120).
      PerformanceTuningTests lives in its own collection (PerformanceTuningTestCollection) with its
      OWN WallowApiFactory, and xUnit runs distinct collections in PARALLEL. Whichever disposes first
      clears the variable for the whole process, including the other collection's live factory and any
      host it builds afterwards via WithWebHostBuilder. That produces exactly 'PerformanceTuningTests
      x3 + a knock-on' and it is timing-dependent. It exists at HEAD too — af3h.1's
      `?? throw new InvalidOperationException("Database connection string not configured")` is what
      turned it from a silent miss into a hard host-build failure. Worth its own bead.

ON THE COORDINATOR'S SPECIFIC HYPOTHESIS (do the WithWebHostBuilder secondary hosts lose the
persistence registration?): NO, and there is no silent-drop path. WithWebHostBuilder re-runs Program.cs
end to end, and opts.PersistMessagesWithPostgresql(...) sits unconditionally in the UseWolverine lambda
with the connection string resolved via `?? throw`. A secondary host therefore either gets message
persistence or fails to build loudly — it cannot come up quietly without a store. Separately, the
hypothesised failure needs a transactional chain to RUN, and PerformanceTuningTests never sends a
message; it only reads IOptions<KestrelServerOptions> and IConfiguration. Under TypeLoadMode.Dynamic
codegen is lazy, so no chain is ever compiled on those hosts. The mechanism is not reachable from
those tests. I did not modify either test.

## WARNING FOR THE COORDINATOR — my api/CLAUDE.md edit landed in someone else's commit

Hazard 2 was not implied by the existing codegen guidance, so per the bead I added two bullets to
api/CLAUDE.md 'Backend Patterns': (1) a handler chain may reach exactly ONE module DbContext, and it
throws on the FIRST MESSAGE not at startup, so cross-module work goes through an integration event
rather than a second repository; (2) a handler that saves and then dispatches must keep that order,
the middleware adds a save rather than replacing one, and bulk ExecuteDelete/ExecuteUpdate sit outside
the unit of work.

While I was working, the Wallow-w5nb agent committed 5d030931 'fix(scripts): make run-tests.sh reach
every integration assembly' and it SWEPT UP my uncommitted api/CLAUDE.md edit. The content is intact
and committed (api/CLAUDE.md:110ff), but it is attributed to the wrong commit. I did not commit, push,
or rewrite anything. My own working tree now shows ONLY api/src/Wallow.Api/Program.cs modified.

ISSUES=none blocking. Follow-ups worth filing separately: (1) the four dispatch-before-save handlers;
(2) the WallowApiFactory process-global env-var race across parallel collections.
Follow-ups filed from this bead's closing report: Wallow-qck0 (WallowApiFactory process-global env vars) and Wallow-rqqx (four handlers dispatch-before-save). Note that qck0 records a CORRECTION to the mechanism stated here: the two Wallow.Api.Tests collections do NOT run in parallel — xunit.runner.json sets parallelizeTestCollections: false as well as parallelizeAssembly: false. The surviving hazard is collection-fixture LIFETIME OVERLAP, not concurrency.
CORRECTION — the real transactional pair, measured. Supersedes the single "66" figure in my earlier note.

The coordinator caught a genuine inconsistency: Program.cs said "66 of 88", api/CLAUDE.md said
"66 of 94". Both could not be right. Re-measured with a probe that enumerates BOTH collections in
the same host, and the answer is that neither denominator was being used with the right numerator.

## THE PAIR

  HandlerGraph.Chains      = 88   transactional = 65
  HandlerGraph.AllChains() = 94   transactional = 66

My original probe enumerated AllChains() ONLY, so the 66 I reported was always the AllChains figure.
"66 of 88" in Program.cs was wrong. "66 of 94" in api/CLAUDE.md was right and is left alone.

## THIS RESOLVES THE 65-vs-66 DISCREPANCY THE BEAD ITSELF FLAGGED

The bead text said transactional=65; af3h.1's note said 66 and explained it as "one chain more now".
That explanation was wrong. They are the SAME measurement over DIFFERENT collections:
65 is over Chains, 66 is over AllChains(). Nothing changed between the two runs. Arithmetic:
  Chains 88 = 65 transactional + 23 non-transactional (the 23 include the 4 empty parents)
  AllChains 94 = 88 - 4 parents + 10 sticky sub-chains
  transactional 66 = 65 + exactly 1 sticky sub-chain

## DOES AutoApplyTransactions REACH THE SEPARATED STICKY SUB-CHAINS? YES — MEASURED, NOT INFERRED

This was the coordinator's real concern and it is answered. Enumerated HandlerChain.ByEndpoint for
every parent:

  PARENT EmailVerifiedEvent          handlers=0 parentTransactional=False subChains=2
      SUB EmailVerifiedNotificationHandler   transactional=False
      SUB EmailVerifiedInquiryLinkHandler    transactional=TRUE
  PARENT InquirySubmittedEvent       handlers=0 parentTransactional=False subChains=3
      SUB InquirySubmittedInAppHandler / NotificationHandler / SseHandler   all False
  PARENT InquiryCommentAddedEvent    handlers=0 parentTransactional=False subChains=3
      SUB InquiryCommentAddedInAppHandler / NotificationHandler / SseHandler all False
  PARENT InquiryStatusChangedEvent   handlers=0 parentTransactional=False subChains=2
      SUB InquiryStatusChangedNotificationHandler / SseHandler              all False

  stickySubChains = 10, transactional = 1

All four parents confirm handlers=0 and parentTransactional=False — a placeholder parent is never
transactional, exactly as the coordinator suspected it could not meaningfully be.

The 1-of-10 split is CORRECT, not a gap. Verified by reading all ten:
  - EmailVerifiedInquiryLinkHandler (Inquiries) injects IInquiryRepository and calls
    SaveChangesAsync -> reaches InquiriesDbContext -> correctly gets the postprocessor.
  - The other nine are all Notifications.Application/EventHandlers/* static relays whose ONLY
    parameters are IMessageBus, ILogger, IEmailTemplateService (SimpleEmailTemplateService, no EF)
    and IConfiguration. They persist nothing themselves; they publish SendNotificationCommand /
    SendEmailCommand, and THOSE commands have their own transactional chains (both appear in the 66).
    A handler that touches no DbContext correctly gets no transaction middleware.

So the policy discriminates correctly at the sub-chain level: it transacted precisely the one
separated handler that touches a DbContext, and skipped the nine that do not. The af3h.2-then-af3h.3
ordering the plan demanded is doing exactly what it was supposed to.

## FIX APPLIED

api/src/Wallow.Api/Program.cs only — replaced "Measured: 66 of 88 chains become transactional" with
the full pair (65 of 88 Chains / 66 of 94 AllChains), the 88-4+10=94 derivation, the fact that the
policy reaches the sticky sub-chains with 1 of 10 transactional, and a note to quote AllChains() when
quoting a single number. api/CLAUDE.md NOT touched — its "66 of 94" was already correct.

Re-verified after the edit: dotnet format clean, build 0 Warnings / 0 Errors, Wallow.Api.Tests
Category=Integration 36/36 PASS. Temp probes deleted; git status shows only Program.cs modified.

title: enable Wolverine message persistence in Testing so AutoApplyTransactions can land
description:
BLOCKER for the AutoApplyTransactions bead. Land this first.

Plan: docs/plans/2026-08-04/2129-wolverine-module-registration.md — Problem 5.

## Measured failure

Turning on `opts.Policies.AutoApplyTransactions()` flips `transactional` from **0 to 65**
chains (live measurement, 2026-08-04). `Wallow.Api.Tests` integration tests then fail:

    System.InvalidOperationException : This Wolverine application is not using Database
    backed message persistence
       at Wolverine.EntityFrameworkCore.Internals.EfCoreEnvelopeTransaction..ctor(...)

Cause: `api/src/Wallow.Api/Program.cs:241-246` deliberately SKIPS
`PersistMessagesWithPostgresql` in the Testing environment. Today nothing is transactional
so that constructor is never reached. With 65 transactional chains it is.

## Do not confuse these two APIs

`opts.UseEntityFrameworkCoreTransactions()` (`Program.cs:249`, already present) registers
the frame PROVIDER — the capability. `Policies.AutoApplyTransactions()` is an `IChainPolicy`
that APPLIES it to every chain whose `ServiceDependencies` transitively reach a DbContext.
They are not companions; the first draft of the plan wrongly said they were.

## Options

(a) Enable Postgres message persistence in the Testing environment, or
(b) gate `AutoApplyTransactions()` on `!env.IsEnvironment("Testing")`.

(b) is cheaper but leaves the transactional path untested, which is most of the value.
Prefer (a) if the Testcontainers Postgres already in the fixture can host the `wolverine`
schema (`Program.cs:238` sets `MessageStorageSchemaName = "wolverine"`).

## Acceptance

`./scripts/run-tests.sh` green with `AutoApplyTransactions()` temporarily enabled locally.
Record which option was taken and why via `bd note`.
notes:
GREEN. DECISION: option (a) — Postgres message persistence is now enabled in the Testing
environment. Option (b) was NOT taken.

FILES: api/src/Wallow.Api/Program.cs (only file touched; ~:249-268)

## What changed

1. PersistMessagesWithPostgresql(connString, "wolverine") is now unconditional — the
   `if (!builder.Environment.IsEnvironment("Testing"))` guard is gone.
2. New Testing-only line: `opts.Durability.Mode = DurabilityMode.Solo;`.

Why (a) worked. WallowApiFactory (api/tests/Wallow.Tests.Common/Factories/WallowApiFactory.cs)
already stands up a real Testcontainers Postgres and exports its connection string via the
`ConnectionStrings__DefaultConnection` env var BEFORE WebApplication.CreateBuilder runs, so
GetConnectionString("DefaultConnection") resolves inside the UseWolverine lambda. Wolverine
migrates its own "wolverine" schema into that container on startup — AutoBuildMessageStorageOnStartup
defaults to CreateOrUpdate (wolverinefx.net guide/durability/managing.html). No fixture change,
no migration, no seed change was needed.

Why Solo. The old comment justified the skip as "prevent polling after containers disposed".
Solo mode is JasperFx's own recommendation for test harnesses (guide/testing.html — "Running
Wolverine in Solo Mode"): it skips leadership election / node assignment and starts durability
agents immediately, so each of the ~40 per-class hosts in the suite does not pay Balanced mode's
election round-trips. WallowApiFactory.DisposeAsync already stops the host before disposing the
containers, so the original polling worry is handled there. Observed: zero post-disposal polling
errors across two full suite runs.

Left ALONE deliberately: `UseDurableInboxOnAllListeners()` / `UseDurableOutboxOnAllSendingEndpoints()`
are still skipped in Testing (Program.cs ~:322). Turning those on would make local-queue delivery
durable and asynchronous, changing the timing semantics every existing integration test relies on.
Message *storage* existing is what EfCoreEnvelopeTransaction needs; durable *endpoints* are not.

## PROOF (temporary AutoApplyTransactions, since removed)

Measured with a throwaway probe test in Wallow.Api.Tests that reads
`((WolverineRuntime)sp.GetRequiredService<IWolverineRuntime>()).Handlers.Chains`. Both the probe
and the policy line have been deleted; `git diff` shows only the Program.cs persistence hunk.

  chains=88 (unchanged from the plan's baseline)
  transactional=66 with AutoApplyTransactions on   (the plan/bead said 65 — one more chain now)
  transactional=0  with it off

CAUTION on measuring this: under Lightweight mode the frames the policy adds are plain
JasperFx MethodCall frames, so counting by `frame.GetType().Name` reports 0. You have to unwrap
`MethodCall.HandlerType`/`.Method`. Under Lightweight the 66 chains each gain a
`<Module>DbContext.SaveChangesAsync` POSTPROCESSOR — e.g. SendEmailCommand's chain ends with
`NotificationsDbContext.SaveChangesAsync`. The transactional path is genuinely exercised, not
silently skipped.

Results with AutoApplyTransactions temporarily on:
  ./scripts/run-tests.sh                                  4912/4912 PASS
  dotnet test --settings coverage.runsettings
      --filter "Category=Integration"                     all PASS (incl. HandlerCodegenTests)

Results with it removed (tree as it stands now):
  ./scripts/run-tests.sh                                  4912/4912 PASS
  dotnet build api/Wallow.slnx                            0 warnings, 0 errors
  dotnet format api/Wallow.slnx                           no changes

The `Category=Integration` run is the one that reproduced the original defect and it is NOT
reachable through scripts/run-tests.sh (the script hard-codes `Category!=Integration` on every
path except the `integration` shorthand, which resolves to the Identity project only). CI runs it
as a separate job — .github/workflows/ci.yml:174. Invoked with --settings coverage.runsettings, so
not a bare `dotnet test`.

## SECOND BLOCKER FOUND — af3h.3 cannot land on persistence alone

Fixing persistence exposed a different, environment-INDEPENDENT failure. With
AutoApplyTransactions on, three CrossOrgRoleIsolationTests (Wallow.Identity.IntegrationTests,
Category=CrossTenant, so they DO run in scripts/run-tests.sh) fail with a 500 on login, and the
server-side cause is:

  System.InvalidOperationException: The configured execution strategy
  'NpgsqlRetryingExecutionStrategy' does not support user-initiated transactions. Use the
  execution strategy returned by 'DbContext.Database.CreateExecutionStrategy()' to execute all
  the operations in the transaction as a retriable unit.
     at ...EmailMessageRepository.SaveChangesAsync
     at Internal.Generated.WolverineHandlers.SendEmailCommandHandler...

All seven modules call `npgsql.EnableRetryOnFailure(...)` in their DbContext registration
(Announcements:42, Inquiries:35, ApiKeys:47, Branding:46, Notifications:63, Identity:241,
Storage:62 — each in <Module>Infrastructure/Extensions/*.cs). That installs
NpgsqlRetryingExecutionStrategy, which refuses any user-initiated BeginTransactionAsync — which is
exactly what AutoApplyTransactions' DEFAULT `TransactionMiddlewareMode.Eager` issues. This has
nothing to do with Testing; it would fail identically in production.

VERIFIED FIX (one line, proven green, deliberately NOT shipped in this bead):

  opts.UseEntityFrameworkCoreTransactions(TransactionMiddlewareMode.Lightweight);
  // using Wolverine.Persistence; — the enum is Wolverine.Persistence.TransactionMiddlewareMode

Lightweight (Wolverine 5.15+) drops the explicit BeginTransactionAsync and uses
DbContext.SaveChangesAsync() alone as the transaction boundary. SaveChangesAsync runs inside EF's
own execution strategy, so EnableRetryOnFailure survives untouched. With Lightweight +
AutoApplyTransactions the whole suite is green (numbers above). The alternative — ripping
EnableRetryOnFailure out of all seven modules — was rejected: it would surrender transient-fault
retry on every DB call in the product, HTTP request paths included, to fix a message-handler
problem.

Not shipped here because the mode is meaningless without the policy (no [Transactional]
attributes and no sagas exist in the repo), so it belongs with af3h.3's diff, same as the policy
line itself. Noted onto Wallow-af3h.3.

KNOWN CAVEAT for af3h.3 under Lightweight: two bulk operations bypass SaveChangesAsync and so sit
outside the handler's unit of work —
Notifications/.../Repositories/TenantPushConfigurationRepository.cs:45 (ExecuteDeleteAsync) and
NotificationRepository.cs:53 (ExecuteUpdateAsync). Both are single statements, atomic on their own.
Eager mode would have covered them; that is the one thing Lightweight gives up.
Separately, Identity/.../Services/LastOwnerGuard.cs:19-32 already shows the EF-sanctioned pattern
(CreateExecutionStrategy().ExecuteAsync around BeginTransactionAsync) — it is unaffected either way.

TEST_STATUS=pass; ISSUES=af3h.3 needs TransactionMiddlewareMode.Lightweight in addition to this bead.
COORDINATOR REVIEW (accepted, with one residual risk recorded).

Diff verified: Testing-scoped, well-justified, temp probe fully removed. Option (a) was the right call and the Lightweight finding on af3h.3 is high-value — it would have blown up that bead.

RESIDUAL RISK — the original guard's stated rationale was dropped without being addressed. The removed comment read:

  'PostgreSQL persistence for durable outbox/inbox (disabled in Testing to prevent polling after containers disposed)'

The replacement comment explains thoroughly WHY Testing now needs a message store, but never addresses the ORIGINAL concern: a durability agent polling a Testcontainers Postgres that has already been disposed at the end of a test class. DurabilityMode.Solo arguably sharpens this rather than softening it — Solo 'starts the durability agents immediately' per the added comment.

Evidence it is fine: ./scripts/run-tests.sh 4912/4912 PASS, run twice (with and without the AutoApplyTransactions probe), plus a Category=Integration run. That is real evidence.

Why it is still worth watching: post-disposal polling typically shows up as intermittent CI noise or a slow/hanging teardown, NOT as a red test. Two green runs on one machine do not rule that out.

ACTION: if flaky teardowns or 'connection refused' log noise appear in CI on this epic's branch, look here first. A targeted fix would be disposing the Wolverine host before the container in WallowApiFactory, or setting a short durability polling interval in Testing.

title: set MultipleHandlerBehavior.Separated and migrate HandlerCodegenTests to AllChains()
description:
Plan: docs/plans/2026-08-04/2129-wolverine-module-registration.md — Problem 3, Phase 1.

## Change

`api/src/Wallow.Api/Program.cs`:

    opts.MultipleHandlerBehavior = MultipleHandlerBehavior.Separated;

NOTE: the other enum member is `ClassicCombineIntoOneLogicalHandler` (the default). There
is **no member named `Combined`** — an earlier plan draft invented it.

## Why

Under the default, all handlers for a message form one logical handler with ONE retry
loop, so a late failure re-runs already-committed earlier handlers. FOUR message types are
affected (verified by parsing all 96 handler methods under `api/src/Modules` and grouping
by first parameter type):

| Message | Handlers | Note |
|---|---|---|
| `EmailVerifiedEvent` | 2 | CROSSES MODULES — Inquiries + Notifications |
| `InquirySubmittedEvent` | 3 | all Notifications |
| `InquiryCommentAddedEvent` | 3 | all Notifications |
| `InquiryStatusChangedEvent` | 2 | all Notifications |

`EmailVerifiedEvent` is the lead case: `EmailVerifiedInquiryLinkHandler` (Inquiries) does a
real `await repository.SaveChangesAsync(ct)` and `EmailVerifiedNotificationHandler`
(Notifications) is the sibling. A Notifications failure currently retries the Inquiries
link-up — a module-boundary violation expressed as a retry policy.

The defect is DUPLICATED SIDE EFFECTS (duplicate emails, duplicate notification rows), NOT
transaction rollback. Measured baseline: `chains=88, transactional=0`; the three
`InquirySubmitted*` handlers are `public static` and touch no DbContext.

## THIS BREAKS AN EXISTING TEST — fix it in the same change

`api/tests/Wallow.Api.Tests/Integration/HandlerCodegenTests.cs` →
`EveryDiscoveredHandler_Compiles` fails for all four message types with
`NoHandlerForEndpointException`. `Separated` moves handlers into per-endpoint sub-chains
(`ByEndpoint`, each on its own `local://` queue) and the parent chain resolves to nothing.

FIX: iterate `HandlerGraph.AllChains()` — which DOES yield the sub-chains — and resolve
with the endpoint-aware overload. This is the repo's highest-value Wolverine guard; do not
skip or `[Skip]` it.

## Two behavioural changes to document in the PR body

- Handlers become CONCURRENT: separate local queues, no ordering guarantee between email /
  in-app write / SSE push. Previously they ran sequentially in one chain.
- Durable inbox/outbox rows MULTIPLY: one publish of `InquirySubmittedEvent` becomes 3
  outbox + 3 inbox rows, across 4 affected message types. Not observable in Testing
  (durability disabled there) — needs a non-Testing run to quantify.

## Ordering

If Phase 1 is split across commits, this bead lands BEFORE AutoApplyTransactions. Under the
current mode `AutoApplyTransactions` was measured to flip `EmailVerifiedEvent`'s chain to
transactional with the DbContext resolved through `IInquiryRepository` — creating exactly
the cross-module shared transaction that does not exist today.

## Acceptance

`./scripts/run-tests.sh` green. A new test proving separation: fail one handler, assert its
siblings still commit — covering all four message types, `EmailVerifiedEvent` primary.
notes:
GREEN: FILES=api/src/Wallow.Api/Program.cs (modified), api/tests/Wallow.Api.Tests/Integration/HandlerCodegenTests.cs (migrated), api/tests/Wallow.Api.Tests/Integration/MultipleHandlerSeparationTests.cs (new); SYMBOLS=none exported (host wiring + tests only); TEST_STATUS=pass; ISSUES=see FLAGS below.

## 1. The change

Program.cs, inside UseWolverine, immediately after `opts.ApplicationAssembly = ...` and before the
handler-discovery loop:

    opts.MultipleHandlerBehavior = MultipleHandlerBehavior.Separated;

Carries a comment block covering the defect (one retry loop replaying committed siblings), the four
affected message types, the module-boundary case, and the concurrency consequence. The comment names
MultipleHandlerSeparationTests as the pin.

## 2. Graph structure, measured (not derived)

Confirmed against the running Testing host by reflecting over WolverineRuntime.Handlers:

  HandlerGraph.Chains    = 88 top-level chains
  HandlerGraph.AllChains = 94
  sticky parents         = 4, each with Handlers.Count == 0 and Endpoints.Count == 0
  sticky sub-chains      = 10 (2 + 3 + 3 + 2), one per handler
  chains with Endpoints  = 10, i.e. EXACTLY the sticky sub-chains

Each sub-chain listens on its own queue, e.g.
  local://wallow.inquiries.application.eventhandlers.emailverifiedinquirylinkhandler/
  local://wallow.notifications.application.eventhandlers.emailverifiednotificationhandler/

The bead's census is confirmed exactly: EmailVerifiedEvent 2 (cross-module), InquirySubmittedEvent 3,
InquiryCommentAddedEvent 3, InquiryStatusChangedEvent 2. No fifth multi-handler message type exists.

## 3. HandlerCodegenTests migration

Now iterates AllChains() and resolves via HandlerFor(messageType, endpoint) when
chain.Endpoints.Count > 0, falling back to HandlerFor(messageType) otherwise. The
`Endpoints.Count > 0` branch keys on precisely the 10 sticky sub-chains measured above.

Not skipped, not narrowed, and coverage went UP: 88 -> 94 compiled chains. Added an assertion that
AllChains().Length >= Chains.Length so a future regression to `Chains` cannot silently drop the ten
multi-handler chains. Verified the test still passes under ClassicCombineIntoOneLogicalHandler too
(AllChains() degrades to Chains when nothing is sticky), so the migration is behaviour-neutral rather
than mode-specific. Collected exception messages are still aggregated into one failure.

## 4. New test: MultipleHandlerSeparationTests (4 facts, all four message types)

Reuses ApiIntegrationTestCollection / WallowApiFactory. NO new fixture, NO test double, NO change to
any shared test helper.

The failure lever is DATA: SendEmailValidator rejects a `To` that is not an email address and
FluentValidation runs as Wolverine middleware, so an event carrying `separation-probe-not-an-email`
makes exactly the email handler throw inside its bus.InvokeAsync. Verified from the log:
`FluentValidation.ValidationException ... Internal.Generated.WolverineHandlers.SendEmailCommandHandler`.
Nothing in the host is stubbed.

IMPORTANT API FINDING (cost a diagnostic round-trip): a handler that exhausts its retries is recorded
in ITrackedSession.MovedToErrorQueue, NOT MessageFailed. MessageFailed was EMPTY for a
ValidationException under OnAnyException().RetryTimes(1).Then.MoveToErrorQueue(). The measured ledger
for one InquiryStatusChangedEvent publish:

  Received          x2 on the notification-handler queue (attempt 0, 1), x1 on the sse-handler queue
  MessageSucceeded  x1 on the sse-handler queue
  MovedToErrorQueue x1 on the notification-handler queue
  Sent              x2 initial routing (one per queue) + x1 DLQ send carrying ValidationException

Assertions per message type (AssertHandlersRanIndependently):
  - exactly 1 MovedToErrorQueue record  (guards against a vacuous pass if validation ever stops firing)
  - exactly handlerCount-1 MessageSucceeded records, on unique destinations, none of them the poisoned queue
  - Received: >1 delivery to the poisoned queue, and EXACTLY ONE to each other queue
    (deliberately not pinned to the exact retry count, so tuning the error policy does not rewrite the test)

Plus committed-state assertions:
  - EmailVerifiedEvent (primary, cross-module): seeds a real unlinked Inquiry whose Email is the
    poisoned string, then asserts Inquiry.SubmitterId == the verified user's id after the Notifications
    welcome email has failed and been dead-lettered.
  - InquirySubmittedEvent: exactly 1 Notification row for a fresh admin user id.
  - InquiryCommentAddedEvent: exactly 1 Notification row for a fresh submitter user id.
  - InquiryStatusChangedEvent: envelope ledger only — its sole healthy sibling is the SSE push, whose
    only effect is a Redis publish that leaves nothing readable. Documented in the test.

MUTATION-PROVEN. Flipped Program.cs to ClassicCombineIntoOneLogicalHandler and reran: all 4 facts FAIL,
the other 32 Wallow.Api.Tests integration facts (HandlerCodegenTests included) still pass. Flipped back
to Separated: 36/36 pass. So the new test measures the setting and nothing else.

## 5. Outbox/inbox multiplication

The row multiplication is 1:1 with envelope fan-out, because each Sent to a durable sending endpoint is
one outbox row and each Received on a durable listener is one inbox row. Measured fan-out per publish:

  EmailVerifiedEvent         1 -> 2 envelopes
  InquirySubmittedEvent      1 -> 3
  InquiryCommentAddedEvent   1 -> 3
  InquiryStatusChangedEvent  1 -> 2
  --------------------------------------------
  one of each                4 -> 10   (2.5x across the affected types)

The other 84 message types have exactly one handler and are unchanged, so this is not a global 2.5x.

CORRECTION TO THE BEAD'S PREMISE: sibling af3h.1 registered PersistMessagesWithPostgresql in every
environment, but Program.cs still gates UseDurableInboxOnAllListeners() /
UseDurableOutboxOnAllSendingEndpoints() on `!IsEnvironment("Testing")`. So local queues remain BUFFERED
in Testing and there are still no rows to count there — af3h.1 made the message store present, not the
queues durable. The numbers above are therefore the measured envelope fan-out (from the tracked-session
ledger) rather than counted rows; they equal the production row counts by the 1:1 identity above. A
genuine row count still needs a non-Testing run.

## 6. FLAGS — ordering, not fixed per instructions

(a) Handlers for the four message types now run CONCURRENTLY on independent local queues. Confirmed
    per-envelope scoping works: each handler gets its own scope, DbContext and restored ITenantContext,
    and the tenant-filtered Notification rows were still found by the tests.

(b) TWO PLACES WHERE A CLIENT COULD SEE A NEW ORDER. Not a broken handler — a UI race:
    - InquirySubmittedEvent: InquirySubmittedSseHandler broadcasts "InquirySubmitted" tenant-wide while
      InquirySubmittedInAppHandler writes the Notification row and pushes "NotificationCreated". These
      are now unordered, so an admin client that refetches its notification list when "InquirySubmitted"
      arrives can now see the list without the new row.
    - InquiryCommentAddedEvent: same shape — InquiryCommentAddedSseHandler's "InquiryCommentAdded" push
      vs InquiryCommentAddedInAppHandler's row + "NotificationCreated" push.
    No handler READS another handler's output, so nothing is incorrect server-side, and Classic never
    guaranteed the order either (it was discovery order, not a contract). Flagging, not fixing.

(c) No handler in the affected set shares state through the request scope, so nothing else depends on
    the old single-scope, single-chain execution.

## 7. Verification

  ./scripts/run-tests.sh                                   4912 passed / 0 failed
  ./scripts/run-tests.sh integration                        139 passed / 0 failed  (Identity)
  dotnet format api/Wallow.slnx                             no changes
  dotnet build api/Wallow.slnx                              0 warnings / 0 errors

TOOLING GAP WORTH KNOWING: ./scripts/run-tests.sh NEVER RUNS THESE TESTS. Every invocation except
`run-tests.sh integration` appends --filter "Category!=E2E&Category!=Integration", and the `integration`
shorthand resolves to Wallow.Identity.IntegrationTests ONLY. So neither HandlerCodegenTests nor
MultipleHandlerSeparationTests is reachable through the script. CI is fine — .github/workflows/ci.yml
runs `dotnet test api/Wallow.slnx --filter "Category=Integration"` across the whole solution, which does
pick both up. To reproduce locally:

  dotnet test api/tests/Wallow.Api.Tests/Wallow.Api.Tests.csproj \
    --settings api/tests/coverage.runsettings --filter "Category=Integration"

Result: 36 passed / 0 failed. Also ran the CI CrossTenant filter (196 passed) since Separated changes
per-envelope tenant restoration. Suggest a follow-up bead to make `run-tests.sh integration` cover both
integration projects rather than just Identity's — I left the script untouched, it is outside this bead.

Not committed, not pushed, bead not closed.

title: Wolverine 6.x correctness — explicit module registry, correct handler settings
description:
Wolverine 6.21.0 is wired against pre-6.0 assumptions. Fix the wiring; keep the
architecture. **No project structure changes** — all 28 module assemblies stay, layer
boundaries stay compiler-enforced.

PLAN (source of truth, committed):
docs/plans/2026-08-04/2129-wolverine-module-registration.md

That plan was adversarially reviewed by four agents on 2026-08-04 (architecture, .NET
concurrency/messaging, C# feasibility, citation fact-check). The messaging reviewer took
live measurements by temporarily patching Program.cs and restoring it (verified restored:
`git status --porcelain` clean). Several first-draft claims were WRONG and are corrected
in the plan under `[R]` markers. Read the plan before starting any child.

## What is actually broken

1. Handler discovery is a load-order-dependent `AppDomain.CurrentDomain.GetAssemblies()`
   loop (`Wallow.Api/Program.cs:229-234`), duplicated verbatim at
   `Wallow.Api/Extensions/AsyncApiEndpointExtensions.cs:15-17`. It is NOT feature-flag
   aware (a first-draft claim that was disproved: `Program.cs:26`/`:561` load
   `Wallow.ApiKeys.Infrastructure` unconditionally). It causes no damage today only
   because ApiKeys and Branding have zero Wolverine handlers. LATENT BUG: adding one
   handler to either module would fail codegen under `ServiceLocationPolicy.NotAllowed`
   (`Program.cs:214`), because a disabled module's services are never registered.

2. `MultipleHandlerBehavior` is left at the default
   `ClassicCombineIntoOneLogicalHandler` (NOTE: there is no enum member named
   `Combined`), so all handlers for a message share ONE retry loop. FOUR message types
   are affected, not one: `EmailVerifiedEvent` (2 handlers, CROSSES MODULES —
   Inquiries + Notifications), `InquirySubmittedEvent` (3), `InquiryCommentAddedEvent`
   (3), `InquiryStatusChangedEvent` (2). The defect is DUPLICATED SIDE EFFECTS ON RETRY
   (duplicate emails, duplicate notification rows) — NOT a shared-transaction rollback;
   measured baseline is `chains=88, transactional=0`.

3. `ExtensionDiscovery.ManualOnly`'s comment (`Program.cs:180-181`) describes a code path
   Wolverine deleted in 6.0 (GH-2902 replaced the bin-directory `AssemblyFinder` with a
   compile-time `JasperFx.SourceGenerator` manifest read via the reference graph).

4. `opts.ApplicationAssembly` is never pinned.

## Verified facts children should not re-derive

- WolverineFx 6.21.0, five packages, `api/Directory.Packages.props:58-62`.
- Handler census — Notifications 45 / Announcements 12 / Inquiries 11 / Storage 10 /
  Identity 9 Application + 3 Infrastructure / ApiKeys 0 / Branding 0.
- `Wallow.Shared.Infrastructure.csproj:11` ALREADY has
  `<FrameworkReference Include="Microsoft.AspNetCore.App" />`, so `IWallowModule` needs
  no new package. All 7 module `.Infrastructure` projects reference it.
- Exactly ONE `internal` declaration exists across all seven modules
  (`StorageInfrastructureExtensions.cs:139`). An earlier count of 4 was wrong.
- All seven `Wallow.*.Domain.dll` ARE in the arch-test output dir
  (`Wallow.Architecture.Tests.csproj:24` references `Wallow.Api`), so arch tests DO cover
  ApiKeys and Inquiries. A planned defect claiming otherwise was withdrawn as a non-bug.

## Rejected alternative (decision, do not relitigate)

Collapsing the 4-assembly-per-module structure was evaluated and REJECTED. JasperFx's
own modular-monolith guidance and all five `JasperFx/CritterStackSamples` monoliths are
single-project, and ceremony is real (Branding = 4 projects for 727 LOC). But Wallow is a
**fork-first base platform**: module boundaries are shipped to downstream forks, where
"the compiler rejects it" and "a test in a suite they may have deleted rejects it" are not
equivalent. Rationale in full in the plan's Non-goals section.
notes:
EPIC COMPLETE — 10/10 children closed, 2026-08-05. All four stated defects addressed:

1. Load-order-dependent AppDomain handler discovery — replaced by the IWallowModule registry
   (af3h.6, commit 27c684d8). Both consumers repointed: Wolverine discovery AND
   AsyncApiEndpointExtensions, which mattered more than 'duplicated verbatim' suggested — measured,
   the two scans ran at points where DIFFERENT assembly sets were loaded (zero .Api assemblies at
   Wolverine-config time vs a larger set after Build()), so they saw systematically different
   inputs, not merely different orderings.
2. MultipleHandlerBehavior — Separated, with MultipleHandlerSeparationTests pinning it.
3. ExtensionDiscovery.ManualOnly's stale comment — rewritten (af3h.5) to describe 6.x reality and
   its coupling to UseRuntimeCompilation().
4. opts.ApplicationAssembly — pinned at Program.cs:279.

CORRECTION TO THIS EPIC'S OWN DESCRIPTION, recorded because the plan is committed and other beads
cite it. The description says: 'LATENT BUG: adding one handler to either module would fail codegen
under ServiceLocationPolicy.NotAllowed, because a disabled module's services are never registered.'
Measured on the real host, NEITHER half holds. Flag ON: the module's .Application assembly is loaded
and its services are registered, so a handler there is discovered and compiles fine. Flag OFF: the
assembly is never loaded, so no chain is built and there is nothing to fail. Evidence is on
Wallow-af3h.6 under 'OPEN MEASUREMENT — RESOLVED'. The genuine defect — the one the registry closes —
is that discovery was a function of which types earlier code happened to touch first, which no
test could have caught because a missed handler produces fewer chains, not an error.
docs/plans/2026-08-04/2129-wolverine-module-registration.md is marked completed with the same
correction inline.

DEBT DELIBERATELY LEFT, all filed rather than absorbed:
• Wallow-k2zp — the seven-module list now exists twice (WallowModules._allModules and
  ModuleMigrations.All). Introduced by af3h.7; cannot share a home today without a new project,
  since Shared.Infrastructure is referenced BY the modules. A cheap behavioural guard is available.
• Wallow-lw4a — RunTestMigrationsAsync's third hardcoded nine-context list, plus MigrationServiceTests's
  fourth. Blocked on af3h.7, now unblocked.
• Wallow-qck0, Wallow-rqqx — found during af3h.3/.9, unrelated to the registry.
• The Wallow-vmns.1 / vmns.7 scope collision over the hardcoded module lists is still open. af3h.6
  DELETED three of the test methods vmns.7 planned to 'derive', so vmns.7's scope has shrunk and
  should be re-read before it is started.

title: production compose fails closed; prod-secrets.sh bootstraps .env.production
description:
Harden docker/docker-compose.production.yml and give it a bootstrap path.

1. FAIL CLOSED. Every operator secret in the production compose is now ${VAR:?message}: POSTGRES_{USER,PASSWORD,DB}, VALKEY_PASSWORD, the four GARAGE_* secrets, ADMIN_EMAIL/ADMIN_PASSWORD, Clients__0__Secret, both OPENIDDICT_*_CERT_PASSWORD, SMTP_PASSWORD, IDENTITY_SIGNING_KEY, BFF_COOKIE_PASSWORD. Previously several were bare or defaulted, so an unset IDENTITY_SIGNING_KEY produced a running API issuing forgeable tokens rather than a refusal to start.

Verified empirically: a missing required var aborts the WHOLE interpolation pass regardless of which service names it, including services behind an inactive profiles:. Two consequences, both encoded in comments: one :? per secret is the entire guarantee (no need to repeat at the other four POSTGRES_PASSWORD sites), and GF_ADMIN_PASSWORD CANNOT fail closed because grafana-lgtm is profiles: [observability] - requiring it would abort startup for every deployment that never enables it.

YAML trap hit twice while writing the messages: a plain scalar containing colon-space parses as a mapping. Messages use backticks (generate with `openssl rand -hex 32`), never 'generate: openssl ...'.

2. ONLY WHAT NEEDS ENV IS ENV. GARAGE_S3_PORT / GARAGE_ADMIN_PORT are now the literals 3900/3903 in both docker-compose.yml and docker-compose.production.yml, and are gone from both example files. They are container-internal; the dev host mappings and the prod Storage__S3__Endpoint are themselves literals, so the only thing the knob could do was desync them. The garage entrypoint still defaults them, so the AppHost is unaffected. GARAGE_REGION stays env.

3. COOKIE ROTATION WIRED. wallow-web now receives COOKIE_PASSWORDS: ${BFF_COOKIE_PASSWORDS:-}, alongside the existing singular COOKIE_PASSWORD. Safe unconditionally because packages/sdk/src/server/config.ts trims and treats empty string as unset. The rotation procedure (prepend a new key ID, redeploy, wait past SESSION_TTL_SECONDS, drop the old) is documented in .env.production.example and docs/operations/deployment.md.

4. scripts/prod-secrets.sh (pnpm secrets:prod). Renders .env.production.example to docker/.env.production with 13 generatable secrets randomised to their required shapes: GK + exactly 24 hex for the Garage key ID, exactly 64 hex for its secret, -hex 48 for IDENTITY_SIGNING_KEY, -hex 24 for GF_ADMIN_PASSWORD, a mixed-class password for ADMIN_PASSWORD, -hex 32 for the rest. Hex not base64 throughout - VALKEY_PASSWORD lands inside redis://:${VALKEY_PASSWORD}@valkey:6379 where a base64 / or @ truncates the host silently.

Bootstrap only, per an explicit product decision: it refuses to overwrite an existing .env.production. Rotating a live secret is a database or cluster operation, not a text substitution. Writes mode 600. Leaves SMTP_PASSWORD (provider-issued) and the deployment-identity values alone and prints both lists.

Verified: runs under macOS bash 3.2; output is line-for-line the template with only values changed; every shape assertion passes; the generated file makes the fail-closed compose parse clean with only the three deliberate optional BCORDES_* warnings; a second run refuses.

Docs: docker/CLAUDE.md (fail-closed convention + the one-:?-per-secret reasoning + the YAML trap, the pruned Garage ports, the script, cookie rotation), docs/operations/deployment.md (generate rather than cp, hex-not-base64 with the reason, the fail-closed rule and its one exception, the rotation procedure, corrected variable table), docker/.env.production.example header.

pnpm check green. pnpm lint:env green on all three pairs.
close_reason: Implemented and verified; pnpm check green.

title: decide how the navigation-escape guard should handle apps/wallow-auth's deliberate OIDC hand-offs
description:
@bc-solutions-coder/testing/navigation-escape (packages/testing/src/navigation-escape.ts) is a Vitest browser-project guard: installNavigationEscapeGuard() listens for the Navigation API's `navigate` event, records any CROSS-DOCUMENT destination, and calls preventDefault() so the runner's Chromium iframe stays put; assertNoNavigationEscape() (called in an afterEach) throws naming the escaped URL(s), then clears. Without it, a real cross-document navigation inside a browser-mode spec silently tears down that spec's iframe, Vitest attributes the resulting connection error to whichever file it tries to load NEXT (not the file that actually leaked), and every file behind it in that run never reports. `location` is `[Unforgeable]` in real Chromium, so `vi.stubGlobal("location", ...)` cannot intercept this — the Navigation-API listener is the only working mechanism. The guard is same-document-safe by design (it returns early on `event.destination.sameDocument`), so it does not interfere with an ordinary router route change.

As of Wallow-xg9t.3, the guard is wired on-by-default into three of the repo's five Vitest browser projects: packages/navigation (original, via Wallow-tkyq), packages/forms, apps/wallow-web, and packages/ui (both its plain browser project and its Storybook project, via two independent wiring mechanisms). apps/wallow-auth is the one remaining browser project and is explicitly and deliberately left unwired.

## Why wallow-auth cannot simply be wired the same way

wallow-auth is the one app in the repo that navigates the real browser for a living — a full-page hand-off IS the product behaviour of its OIDC flow, not a bug. Eight source files assign `globalThis.location.href` / `.assign` / `.replace` as the actual mechanism of that hand-off:
- src/features/accept-terms/components/AcceptTermsScreen.tsx
- src/features/consent/components/ConsentScreen.tsx
- src/features/invitation/components/InvitationScreen.tsx
- src/features/login/components/LoginScreen.tsx
- src/features/mfa-challenge/components/MfaChallengeForm.tsx
- src/features/mfa-enroll/components/MfaEnrollForm.tsx
- (plus two specs' own test harnesses)

Ten spec files already implement a per-spec copy of essentially the same guard to test that hand-off deliberately: AcceptTermsScreen, ConsentScreen, InvitationScreen, LoginScreen, LoginMfaHandOff, MagicLinkLoginForm, OtpLoginForm, MfaChallengeForm, MfaEnrollForm, and one more (10 files total). Each registers its own Navigation API `navigate` listener (`captureHandoff()` or equivalent), reads `event.destination.url`, calls `preventDefault()`, and asserts the captured URL — AcceptTermsScreen.test.tsx's own header even states the seam verbatim, citing the same `[Unforgeable]`/Navigation-API reasoning the shared guard is built on.

When apps/wallow-auth/vitest.setup.ts was experimentally wired with the shared guard (same shape as the other three projects), the app went from 55 files / 808 passing tests to **70 FAILING tests across those same 10 files**. Every failure is the shared guard's OWN afterEach throwing "Navigation escaped the test iframe" — not an assertion failure inside any test; the specs' own behavioural assertions all still pass. Mechanism: both the spec's own listener and the shared guard's listener are registered on the same `navigation` object; both fire on the same deliberate `preventDefault()`-guarded hand-off; the spec is satisfied, but the shared guard's project-level afterEach has no way to know the escape it recorded was already intercepted and asserted by the spec itself, so it reports it as an unhandled escape anyway.

This was investigated and reverted, not overlooked: wiring wallow-auth was explicitly part of Wallow-xg9t.3's original scope, was tried, produced the 70 failures above, and the implementer correctly refused to weaken the shared guard (e.g. loosening its afterEach, or making it opt-in) to force wallow-auth green, since a weakened guard defeats the entire point of the epic it belongs to (Wallow-xg9t, "fix the guards that do not guard" — see docs/plans/2026-08-02/1744-no-source-tests-design.md). wallow-auth's setup file and tsconfig were left completely untouched; the app remains at its original 55 files / 808 passing tests, unwired.
design:
This is a real open QUESTION, not a prescribed fix. Whoever picks this up should evaluate the options below on their merits, not implement the first one that comes to mind. Options seen so far, worth weighing against each other:

(a) Make the 10 specs consume the SHARED guard's own record instead of running a second, independent listener beside it. Two shapes surfaced during the wiring attempt:
    - Each spec's capture helper calls `clearNavigationEscapes()` (already exported from packages/testing/src/navigation-escape.ts) once it has read the URL it needed, so the shared record is empty by the time the project-level afterEach runs.
    - packages/testing grows a new, explicit `expectNavigationEscape()` / `consumeNavigationEscapes()` helper that a spec asserting a deliberate hand-off calls instead of rolling its own listener — this reads better at the call site and preserves the property that "a spec which forgot to assert still fails", which a bare `clearNavigationEscapes()` call does not.
    This is real design work, not wiring: it touches all 10 spec files and roughly 70 tests, and changes what "the guard fires" means for a spec that WANTS a hand-off to happen.

(b) Teach the guard itself to distinguish a deliberate, same-app OIDC hand-off from an accidental escape — e.g. an explicit "expected destination" allow-list or a scoped variant of the guard that a spec can install for the duration of one test. Weigh this against (a): it changes packages/testing's shared surface (a cross-cutting change every wired project inherits) rather than touching only wallow-auth's specs.

(c) Scope the guard to exclude wallow-auth's specific navigating flows rather than the whole app — e.g. install it in apps/wallow-auth/vitest.setup.ts but let the 10 specs opt out locally for the duration of their one deliberate-navigation test, then reinstate it. Consider whether this is meaningfully different from (a)'s second shape.

(d) Decide wallow-auth legitimately cannot carry this guard at all, and document that as an accepted hole rather than build any of (a)-(c). This is a PERMISSIBLE outcome, but only if it is written down explicitly with the same rigor as the plan's own "Accept the holes" section (docs/plans/2026-08-02/1744-no-source-tests-design.md), which explains precisely why `wallow/no-source-tests` reaches only five nested trees and not the repo root, and enumerates every spec left outside its reach by name. The epic Wallow-xg9t's own through-line, stated in its description, is "a guard that does not guard is the defect" — silently leaving wallow-auth's 10 navigating specs able to lose their runner (and, per the mechanism above, its OTHER 45 non-navigating specs collaterally, the same class of damage Wallow-tkyq fixed for packages/navigation) is not an acceptable silent outcome. If (d) is chosen, it must be written into packages/testing/CLAUDE.md's wiring roster (which currently already notes wallow-auth as the exception, per Wallow-xg9t.3) with the same explicit reasoning, not left as an omission someone has to rediscover.

Before implementing anything, re-verify the false-positive surface directly against the CURRENT source — the scout pass that originally cleared wallow-auth for wiring (see "Scout miss" below) grepped only for anchor/Link click patterns and concluded "no false-positive risk found" across all four target packages; that conclusion was WRONG for wallow-auth specifically, and the class of navigation this bead is about (direct `globalThis.location.href` / `.assign` / `.replace` assignment) does not show up in an anchor/Link-only grep at all.

## Scout miss — record so it does not repeat

The scout pass that cleared apps/wallow-auth as safe to wire searched only for `href`/`Link`/`click`/`location`/`router.navigate` text patterns and read every hit that matched, then concluded no opt-out mechanism was needed anywhere. That grep did catch `location` textually, but it read every wallow-auth hit as either "never clicked" or "mocked router", and never distinguished a spec's OWN deliberate navigate-listener assertions (which the guard's afterEach cannot see are already asserted) from an unhandled click. The actual failure mode is a DIRECT, programmatic `globalThis.location.href` / `.assign` / `.replace` assignment inside application source (not a click on an `<a>`/`Link` at all), paired with a spec that already has its own Navigation-API listener watching for exactly that assignment. A grep for anchor/Link click safety cannot see this class of risk. The next scout evaluating a similar guard-wiring task should grep application source for direct `location.*=`/`location.assign`/`location.replace`/`location.href` assignment, not only for clicked anchors and router Link usage, and should specifically check whether the target spec files already run their own competing listener on the same global object the guard installs on.
acceptance_criteria:
1. A decision is recorded and justified among the options in DESIGN (or another option discovered during the work) — not merely "wire it in", since that was tried and produced 70 failing tests.
2. If a fix is implemented: apps/wallow-auth/vitest.setup.ts calls installNavigationEscapeGuard() and registers afterEach(assertNoNavigationEscape) (matching the other three wired projects), apps/wallow-auth/tsconfig.json's include gains vitest.setup.ts, and all 10 previously-conflicting spec files (AcceptTermsScreen, ConsentScreen, InvitationScreen, LoginScreen, LoginMfaHandOff, MagicLinkLoginForm, OtpLoginForm, MfaChallengeForm, MfaEnrollForm, and the tenth) pass using whichever mechanism was chosen, without weakening the shared guard's behavior for the other three already-wired projects.
3. A throwaway probe spec proves the guard is live in wallow-auth by provoking an UNHANDLED cross-document navigation (one the app does not already intercept) and observing it fail exactly one test naming the escaped URL, with no sibling file taken down — mirroring the live-proof method used for the other three projects in Wallow-xg9t.3. Probe deleted after confirming, no debris in git status.
4. pnpm test (= pnpm -r test) file/test counts for apps/wallow-auth match its pre-change baseline of 55 files / 808 tests exactly (no regression, no test silently dropped to force green).
5. Full pnpm check passes at least once at the end (format:check, lint, lint:tests, typecheck, test, build, check:exports).
6. If instead the decision is "accept the hole" (option (d)): no code changes to apps/wallow-auth are required, but packages/testing/CLAUDE.md's project-wiring roster must be updated with an explicit, reasoned statement of why wallow-auth is excluded — written with the same rigor and specificity as docs/plans/2026-08-02/1744-no-source-tests-design.md's "Accept the holes" section (which names every excluded file and the mechanical reason it cannot be reached) — not a placeholder sentence. This satisfies the epic's own "a guard that does not guard is the defect" doctrine by making the gap loud and permanent rather than silent.
notes:
Filed unparented (backlog), by explicit instruction — NOT a child of Wallow-xg9t. The user decided that epic should close rather than absorb newly-discovered follow-ups; this bead exists precisely because Wallow-xg9t.3 needed narrowing to close cleanly (see the note on Wallow-xg9t.3 explaining the narrowing).

Priority P1: this is not cosmetic cleanup. It is a real, currently-silent gap in the ONE app in the repo whose entire purpose is triggering real browser navigations — wallow-auth is the app with the most to lose from an unguarded cross-document leak, and today an accidental leak there (as opposed to the 10 specs' deliberate, already-intercepted ones) would reproduce exactly the class of collateral damage Wallow-tkyq fixed for packages/navigation: one spec's leak silently takes down every file scheduled after it in that run, misattributed to the wrong file. That the app already has 10 specs defending themselves individually is not equivalent to having the shared, always-on guard the other four browser projects now have.

Cross-reference: Wallow-xg9t.3 (sibling bead, now scoped to the three packages that DID get wired) and Wallow-tkyq (closed; built the guard and the sameDocument filter this all depends on).
SCOUT FINDINGS (re-verified against current source, 2026-08-03)

1. APP-SOURCE ASSIGNMENT SURFACE (grep for globalThis.location.href/.assign/.replace = across apps/wallow-auth/src, excluding *.test.*): confirms exactly the bead's 6 named files, 7 assignment sites — no others exist:
   - src/features/accept-terms/components/AcceptTermsScreen.tsx:296
   - src/features/consent/components/ConsentScreen.tsx:340
   - src/features/invitation/components/InvitationScreen.tsx:448
   - src/features/login/components/LoginScreen.tsx:375
   - src/features/mfa-challenge/components/MfaChallengeForm.tsx:478,497 (two sites, one file)
   - src/features/mfa-enroll/components/MfaEnrollForm.tsx:564
   src/features/login/components/ExternalProviders.tsx:183 also matches `location.href` textually but only READS it (`... : globalThis.location.href`, a returnUrl fallback) — not an assignment, not a hand-off trigger. Excluded correctly.

2. CORRECTION TO THE BEAD: only 9 spec files register their own Navigation API listener, not 10. Re-verified with five independent grep strategies (addEventListener("navigate"), NavigateEvent type-shim declarations, destination.url reads, window.navigation/globalThis.navigation references, installNavigationEscapeGuard imports) — all five converge on the identical 9-file set. Also manually inspected every OTHER wallow-auth spec that even mentions the word "navigate" (18 files total match that loose grep): the other 9 are router-mock (`mocks.navigate = vi.fn()`) specs with no Navigation-API involvement (RegisterForm, MfaEnrollForm.start-pending, MagicLinkLoginForm.verify, index.ssr, NotFoundPage, auth-layout x2, ResetPasswordForm) or LogoutScreen.test.tsx, which asserts a resolved `<a href>` URL but never clicks it and registers no listener. No 10th candidate exists under any of these searches. Confirmed 9:
   - AcceptTermsScreen.test.tsx — `captureHandoff()`, called per-test, add+removeEventListener, asserts exactly 1 escape
   - ConsentScreen.test.tsx — `captureHandoff()`, same shape
   - InvitationScreen.test.tsx — OUTLIER: registers its listener ONCE at module scope (top-level side effect, not inside a function), no add/removeEventListener pairing; `recordedNavigations` array is reset in a `beforeEach` (line ~174) instead. Asserts `.length > 0`, not `=== 1`.
   - LoginScreen.test.tsx — `captureHandoff()`, per-test, add+remove
   - LoginMfaHandOff.test.tsx — `captureHandoff()`, per-test, add+remove
   - MagicLinkLoginForm.test.tsx — `captureHandoff()`, per-test, add+remove
   - OtpLoginForm.test.tsx — `recordHandoff()`, per-test, add+remove
   - MfaChallengeForm.test.tsx — `recordNavigation`/`navigationApi()`, per-test, add+remove
   - MfaEnrollForm.test.tsx — `interceptNavigation()`, per-test, add+remove
   All 9 read `event.destination.url`, all call `event.preventDefault()`, all assert on the captured URL(s) with `vi.waitFor`. 8 of 9 wrap this in a per-test capture/cleanup function; InvitationScreen is the sole module-scope exception. Flag this discrepancy explicitly for whoever implements — do not go hunting for a "tenth" file that does not exist; if a 10th surfaces later it was not found by any of the above.

3. WIRING TEMPLATE (from a wired project): apps/wallow-web/vitest.setup.ts calls `installNavigationEscapeGuard()` then `afterEach(() => assertNoNavigationEscape())`, imported from `@bc-solutions-coder/testing/navigation-escape`. apps/wallow-web/tsconfig.json's `include` array lists `vitest.setup.ts` alongside `src/**/*.ts(x)`/`vite.config.ts`/`vitest.config.ts` — the exact two edits ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA #2 asks for. The "live proof" template spec (mirrors ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA #3's probe) is packages/navigation/src/navigation-escape.test.tsx: renders an anchor with an unprevented `href`, clicks it, asserts `navigationEscapes()` records it and `assertNoNavigationEscape()` throws naming the URL, PLUS a fourth case using `globalThis.location.assign(...)` for the programmatic path. No such spec exists yet inside packages/testing itself — the guard's own behavioural proof lives only in the first wired consumer (packages/navigation), not centrally.

title: guard the Wolverine codegen path so a non-inlinable handler dependency cannot ship
description:
Wolverine 6 generates a handler adapter per message type and inlines the
constructor calls for that handler's dependencies. When it cannot inline one it
falls back to a service locator, and Wallow.Api/Program.cs:208 sets
ServiceLocationPolicy.NotAllowed, which turns that fallback into
InvalidServiceLocationException. Codegen is LAZY -- it runs on the first message
of that type, not at startup -- so the exception surfaces inside a background
envelope, three retries later, in the dead-letter queue, behind an HTTP 200.

That is exactly how Wallow-0tor / Wallow-nafb happened: SendEmailHandler took an
INotificationPreferenceChecker whose implementation was internal sealed, and
every email in the product died silently. Fixed by f62c2214. Nothing in the repo
would stop the next one.

## The defect class

Wolverine falls back to service location when a handler dependency with a SCOPED
or TRANSIENT lifetime is either:
  - a non-public concrete type (internal sealed Foo : IFoo, AddScoped<IFoo,Foo>), or
  - an opaque lambda registration (AddScoped(sp => ...)), which includes anything
    behind AddDbContext, ASP.NET Identity's UserManager, and OpenIddict's managers.
Singleton dependencies are inlined into the adapter's own constructor and are immune.

## Why it escaped to E2E twice

  - Nothing in the .NET suite compiles a handler. SendEmailHandlerTests.cs:27
    constructs SendEmailHandler with `new`; NotificationsModuleExtensionsTests
    asserts only that a ServiceDescriptor exists. Neither touches the generated
    adapter.
  - The only guard that exists today is XML doc comments. Six classes carry a
    hand-written "Public because Wolverine's generated handlers construct their
    dependencies inline" paragraph (NotificationPreferenceChecker, LastOwnerGuard,
    AccessRequestRecipientResolver, MembershipReviewService,
    DefaultMemberRoleResolver, UserEnrollmentService). A comment is not a control.
  - E2E only covers the handful of messages the browser specs happen to trigger.

## Blast radius

Notifications has 22 event handlers and every one funnels into SendEmailCommand.
One constructor parameter took out email verification, magic links, OTP login,
password reset, invitations, access requests, inquiry notifications and org
membership mail simultaneously.

## Already sitting on the trigger (not bugs YET)

  - NoOpClaimsEnricher / NoOpRegistrationValidator / NoOpExternalClaimsMapper --
    internal sealed, TryAddScoped, consumed only by Identity controllers today.
    They become bugs the day a Wolverine handler takes one.
  - HtmlSanitizationService is internal but AddSingleton, so immune by lifetime --
    and would become a live defect if anyone re-registered it scoped.

## The work

LAYER 1 -- compile every handler in CI. This is the only layer that covers every
handler rather than the ones a test happens to dispatch.
`dotnet run -- codegen write` discovers every handler and runs the same codegen
passes the host runs at startup; any policy violation fails the command. Two
prerequisites, both real:
  a) Program.cs never wires the JasperFx CLI -- it ends in `await app.StartAsync()`
     / `await app.WaitForShutdownAsync()` inside a Serilog try/catch. It needs
     `return await app.RunJasperFxCommands(args)`. The ApplicationStarted logging,
     the non-Development credential guard, and Log.CloseAndFlushAsync() in the
     finally block must all survive that edit. This is the riskiest change here.
  b) Program.cs eagerly throws on a missing ConnectionStrings:DefaultConnection
     BEFORE Wolverine's own codegen-mode detection can suppress persistence.
     Wolverine documents that codegen write needs no live DB or broker, but our
     eager read does. Prefer exporting a syntactically valid dummy
     ConnectionStrings__DefaultConnection in the CI step over guarding Program.cs
     with CodeGeneration.IsRunningGeneration() -- keeps codegen out of Program.cs.
Ship as a CI job shaped like the existing openapi-drift.yml / route-tree-drift.yml:
run codegen write to a scratch path, fail on non-zero exit. Do NOT check the
generated code in and do NOT move to TypeLoadMode.Static -- separate decision,
own drift cost.

LAYER 2 -- compile every handler in the test suite, so this fails before push
rather than after. WallowApiFactory already boots the real Program against
Testcontainers and Wallow.Api.Tests/Integration already runs in the
Category=Integration CI job. Generalize BootstrapAdminHandlerCodegenTests from one
handler to all: enumerate the discovered handler chains and force each adapter to
build, asserting none throws.
UNCONFIRMED: whether WolverineFx 6.21.0 exposes a supported API to force adapter
compilation without dispatching a message (IWolverineRuntime.Handlers and its chain
collection are the entry point). Confirm at implementation time. If there is none,
DROP this layer and let Layer 1 carry it -- do NOT implement it by sending a real
message per handler, that dispatches side effects. If dropped, lift
BootstrapAdminHandlerCodegenTests' class comment into whatever survives; it is the
clearest statement of this problem in the repo.

LAYER 3 -- fail at the point of the mistake. Layers 1 and 2 say "handler X failed
codegen" after the build; an arch rule fails on the offending line. Add to
Wallow.Architecture.Tests/WolverineConventionTests.cs:
  Rule A: for each module, take the constructor parameter types of every discovered
    handler, resolve each to its registered implementation, and assert the
    implementation is public whenever its lifetime is Scoped or Transient. Exempt
    interfaces on the AlwaysUseServiceLocationFor allow-list. Needs the fully-built
    IServiceCollection, which no arch test constructs today -- if that proves
    disproportionate, degrade to a coarser static form: every concrete class in a
    *.Infrastructure assembly implementing an interface from the matching
    *.Application assembly must be public.
  Rule B: assert the types passed to AlwaysUseServiceLocationFor in Program.cs equal
    an explicit expected list in the test. That list (ITenantContext,
    ITenantContextSetter, ISetupStatusChecker, IBootstrapAdminService,
    IOrganizationService) is correct and well-commented today, but it grows one
    entry at a time in reaction to production-shaped failures and no test asserts
    what is on it. Same source-reading technique ModuleRegistrationTests uses.

LAYER 4 -- make a dead-lettered envelope loud. Independent of codegen, and the
reason a P0 sat undetected. ConfigureStandardErrorHandling retries any exception
once then moves to the error queue; the publisher already returned 200. Minimum:
log DLQ moves at Error with message type and exception so the log pipeline can
alert. Better: an error-queue depth metric alongside the existing custom
instruments, so "email stopped working" is a graph and not an E2E timeout.
This is a different defect (observability) that the incident revealed -- split it
out if it slows the rest down.

## Rejected

  - ServiceLocationPolicy.AlwaysAllowed -- hides the symptom, reinstates the silent
    scoping hazard the Wolverine docs warn about (including for IMessageBus), and
    discards a genuinely useful compile-time check.
  - Make everything public -- removes encapsulation everywhere to fix a rule that
    applies to a subset of types.
  - One more per-handler codegen test each time this happens -- that IS
    BootstrapAdminHandlerCodegenTests, and it is why the doc-comment count is six.
    Scales linearly with handlers and only covers the ones someone already got wrong.
  - TypeLoadMode.Static with checked-in generated code -- would make Layer 1 free as
    a build side effect, but couples every handler edit to regenerate-and-commit and
    adds its own drift class. Revisit for AOT/startup, not for this.

## Docs follow-on

Once Layer 3 lands, add one line to api/CLAUDE.md "Backend Patterns" -- implementations
of interfaces that Wolverine handlers depend on must be public, enforced by the
architecture tests -- and delete the six hand-written XML comment paragraphs, which
will then be restating a checked rule.

Secondary: add a throwaway handler taking a newly-written internal sealed scoped dependency and confirm the Layer 3 arch rule names the file; delete it afterward.
