Shipped as 5116d29d. Layers 2 and 3 in, layer 1 deliberately skipped, layer 4 split to Wallow-qi90.2.

LAYER 2 — the bead's UNCONFIRMED question resolved affirmatively. HandlerGraph.HandlerFor(Type) forces adapter compilation without dispatching, so no real message per handler is needed and the layer did not have to be dropped. api/tests/Wallow.Api.Tests/Integration/HandlerCodegenTests.cs enumerates runtime.Handlers.Chains and calls HandlerFor on each, collecting every failure rather than stopping at the first. HandlerGraph hangs off the concrete WolverineRuntime; IWolverineRuntime does not expose it, hence the cast.

It found two live faults on unmodified main:
  1. Six ServiceAccount commands/queries (Create/Revoke/RotateSecret/UpdateScopes + Get/GetAll) would have thrown InvalidServiceLocationException the first time anyone routed ClientsController through IMessageBus. It calls IServiceAccountService directly today, so the handlers were orphaned and the fault latent. Fixed with AlwaysUseServiceLocationFor<IServiceAccountService>() — OpenIddict's IOpenIddictApplicationManager is an opaque lambda registration, same as the existing five.
  2. MfaPartialAuthorizationHandler and PermissionAuthorizationHandler match Wolverine's discovery convention exactly (name ends in Handler, AuthorizationHandler<T> exposes public HandleAsync), so Wolverine was building a message chain for AuthorizationHandlerContext whose SignInManager/UserManager deps cannot be inlined. Fixed with Discovery.CustomizeHandlerDiscovery(types => types.Excludes.Implements<IAuthorizationHandler>()).

LAYER 3 — api/tests/Wallow.Architecture.Tests/WolverineCodegenPolicyTests.cs. Three rules: (A) every non-nested concrete class in Wallow.{Module}.Infrastructure implementing an interface from Wallow.{Module}.Application OR Wallow.Shared.Contracts must be public; (B) the AlwaysUseServiceLocationFor list read out of Program.cs source must equal an explicit six-entry list; (C) the IAuthorizationHandler discovery exclusion must still be there. Rule A widened past the bead's spec to include Shared.Contracts because that is the one assembly every module references across boundaries — that widening is what caught NoOpRealtimeAccessRevoker.

Rule A flagged five pre-existing latent traps, all internal sealed + TryAddScoped Identity extension points, now public: NoOpClaimsEnricher, NoOpExternalClaimsMapper, NoOpRegistrationValidator, NoOpMfaExemptionChecker, NoOpRealtimeAccessRevoker. HtmlSanitizationService is internal but lives in Shared.Infrastructure.Core with its interface in the same assembly, so no module rule reaches it; it is a singleton and HandlerCodegenTests covers it precisely.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERION MET. Reverting f62c2214 (NotificationPreferenceChecker back to internal sealed) goes red in BOTH halves, before any e2e run:
  - ./scripts/run-tests.sh — WolverineCodegenPolicyTests.InfrastructureImplementations_OfApplicationInterfaces_ShouldBePublic("Notifications") names the type directly.
  - CI integration job — HandlerCodegenTests reports exactly SendEmailCommand, SendSmsCommand, SendPushCommand, the three handlers f62c2214 fixed.
The split matters: HandlerCodegenTests is Category=Integration, which the default run-tests.sh filter excludes, so layer 3 is what carries the local half. Secondary criterion is satisfied a fortiori — rule A judges every implementation regardless of whether a handler takes it today, which is the point.

LAYER 1 SKIPPED, deliberately. The bead argued the CI codegen step was 'the only layer that covers every handler', but that rested on layer 2 possibly needing to dispatch a real message per handler. It does not — HandlerFor gives full coverage of the same discovery graph Program.cs configures. Meanwhile CI's existing integration job already runs Category=Integration solution-wide, so HandlerCodegenTests ships to CI with zero workflow changes, and layer 1's marginal coverage is near zero against the riskiest edit in the bead (replacing app.StartAsync/WaitForShutdownAsync with RunJasperFxCommands in Program.cs). Reopen only if a handler ever escapes the runtime graph.

DOCS FOLLOW-ON DONE in the same commit: one paragraph added to api/CLAUDE.md 'Backend Patterns', and all six hand-written 'public because Wolverine' XML comment blocks deleted (NotificationPreferenceChecker, LastOwnerGuard, AccessRequestRecipientResolver, MembershipReviewService, DefaultMemberRoleResolver, UserEnrollmentService).

VERIFIED: ./scripts/run-tests.sh 4911/4911 pass; Wallow.Api.Tests full run incl. integration 359/359 pass.

title: state the no-source-tests rule and ship wallow/no-source-tests
description:
Phase 0 of docs/plans/2026-08-02/1744-no-source-tests-design.md.

THE GATE. This bead exists to be done FIRST, before any sweep is deleted.

There is currently no rule against source tests. `doctrine` and `shape pin` appear in ZERO
markdown files in this repo - the phrase lives only in bead prose. The nearest written
guidance is packages/testing/CLAUDE.md:186 ("assert a feature seam by identity, not
presence"), which points the right way but constrains nothing.

That absence is the actual defect behind Wallow-e6gz, and it is why the sweep inventory has
gone 23 -> 18 -> 16 rather than down: files leave when a sweep is deleted, and new ones
arrive because nothing forbids writing them. Two of the current sixteen -
packages/navigation/src/shell-source.test.ts and packages/logger/src/charter.test.ts -
landed HOURS AFTER Wallow-e6gz was filed to fix them.

Deleting sixteen sweeps without this rule in place just resets the counter.

## Deliverable 1 - the rule in .claude/rules/TESTING.md

Exact text is in the design doc's "The rule" section. Two clauses matter and are easy to
drop:

- "prefer deleting the constraint to relocating it" - most of the sixteen die with NOTHING
  replacing them. Without this clause the rule reads as "convert all sixteen to lint
  rules", which is the opposite of the plan.
- the single exception: @bc-solutions-coder/testing's ./browser-styles-wiring, which reads
  a consumer's BUILD CONFIG (vite config / setup / stylesheet) to prove the browser project
  has CSS attached. Build wiring, not application source, and it has no behavioural
  equivalent short of rendering everything and noticing it is unstyled. Approved to stay.

## Deliverable 2 - wallow/no-source-tests

Follow packages/lint/src/rules/text-heading-variant.ts as the template; read
packages/lint/CLAUDE.md before touching any .oxlintrc.json. Rule specs shell out to the real
oxlint binary and read its JSON report (packages/lint/src/fixtures.test.ts) - that pattern
is the behavioural way to test a lint rule and is NOT itself a source test.

Bans readFileSync / readdirSync / existsSync in **/*.test.{ts,tsx}.

TWO OVERRIDES, and each MUST RE-DECLARE the root's options rather than extend them - an
oxlint overrides entry REPLACES the root rule's options and later overrides win:

- packages/lint/**  (rule specs legitimately read fixture files off disk)
- packages/testing/src/browser-styles-wiring.ts  (the sanctioned exception)

## This bead lands RED-ADJACENT, on purpose

The rule fires against the very sweeps it exists to remove. Phase 0 therefore also carries
whatever override keeps pnpm check green over the 16 existing call sites; Wallow-e6gz phase
4b deletes the sweeps AND that override together. Do not reorder: a gate installed after the
sweep is not a gate.

## Not this bead

Writing wallow/module-imports, or deleting any sweep. Both are Wallow-e6gz.
acceptance_criteria: .claude/rules/TESTING.md carries the no-source-tests bullet naming packages/testing ./browser-styles-wiring as the single exception. wallow/no-source-tests is implemented in packages/lint/src/rules/, registered in packages/lint/src/index.ts, and covered by a fixtures spec that shells out to the real oxlint binary. It fires on readFileSync/readdirSync/existsSync in **/*.test.{ts,tsx}. Overrides for packages/lint/** and packages/testing/src/browser-styles-wiring.ts re-declare the root options rather than extend them (oxlint overrides REPLACE). pnpm check is green WITH the 16 existing sweeps still in place - the overrides that permit them are removed in Wallow-e6gz phase 4b, not here.
notes:
SCOPE DECISION (user, this session): accept the coverage holes. wallow/no-source-tests is registered only in the five existing nested configs (apps/wallow-web, apps/wallow-auth, packages/ui, packages/forms, packages/navigation). The plugin is NOT moved to the root config; packages/lint/CLAUDE.md's 'must not be moved there' stands.

MEASURED CONSEQUENCE - three of the sixteen sweeps resolve to the ROOT config and are therefore NOT guarded by the rule:
  - apps/examples/minimal-app/src/sdk-wiring.test.ts
  - packages/env/src/charter.test.ts
  - packages/logger/src/charter.test.ts
Any future test-reading sweep in sdk/query/auth/utils/testing/styles/config/lint is likewise unguarded. For those the .claude/rules/TESTING.md rule is the only gate. The rule covers 13 of 16.

Root registration WAS proven to work before the decision (relative specifier ./packages/lint/src/index.ts loads; negative control errors loudly; a planted no-tinted-text violation fired in packages/logger; dual root+nested registration lints clean). The single blocker is oxlint-guardrails.test.ts:396 copyFileSync of the root config into a temp dir, reproduced exactly as packages/lint/CLAUDE.md documents. If the holes ever matter, the fix is to strip jsPlugins when materialising that mirror config - the mirror exists to prove no-restricted-imports, a built-in Rust rule.

FOLLOWS FROM THE DECISION - both overrides the acceptance criteria asks for are unreachable and must NOT be written as dead config:
  - packages/lint/** has no nested config, so the rule never fires there.
  - packages/testing/src/browser-styles-wiring.ts has no nested config AND is not a *.test.* file, so it is outside the rule's glob twice over.
The sanctioned exception survives as prose in TESTING.md, not as an override.
DONE. pnpm check green end to end (format:check, lint, lint:tests, build, typecheck, test,
check:exports; exit 0). Test totals after the sweep: sdk 1033, ui 1447, wallow-auth 808,
wallow-web 501+1 skipped, navigation 132, logger 129, styles 101, forms 88, testing 60, env 57,
utils 38, auth 31, query 8, minimal-app 8, lint 4.

## What shipped

1. `.claude/rules/TESTING.md` — the no-source-tests rule, including the "prefer deleting the
   constraint to relocating it" clause. Most sweeps died with nothing replacing them.

2. `wallow/no-source-tests` — `packages/lint/src/rules/no-source-tests.ts`, registered in
   `packages/lint/src/index.ts`. Bans the `node:fs` family (`fs`, `fs/promises`, `node:fs`,
   `node:fs/promises`) in a `*.test.*` file, across static imports, dynamic `import()` with a
   literal specifier, and `require()` with a literal argument.

   Keyed on the IMPORT, not on `readFileSync`: aliasing (`import { readFileSync as rf }`) defeats
   name-matching, and `fs.readFileSync(...)` member calls escape it entirely. The import is the
   one chokepoint.

   Fixtures: `packages/lint/fixtures/no-source-tests/{invalid.test.ts,valid.test.ts,valid.ts}`.
   `valid.ts` is a NON-spec file importing `node:fs` — the only thing proving the filename gate
   exists rather than the rule banning fs everywhere. `valid.test.ts` pins the boundary:
   `node:path`/`node:url`, a `vite.config.ts` imported as an OBJECT, the module under test,
   `import.meta.glob`, and a computed dynamic import all draw nothing.
   4 tests green in `packages/lint`.

3. Registered in all FIVE nested configs (wallow-web, wallow-auth, ui, forms, navigation), in the
   top-level `rules` block. NOT in the root config — a `jsPlugins` entry there makes packages/sdk's
   temp-dir root-config copy unloadable and 0 tests run.

   THE TRAP, recorded in a comment in each override block: every nested config turns four/five
   `wallow/*` rules off for `*.test.*`. Listing `no-source-tests` there would disable it
   ENTIRELY, because specs are the only thing it judges. It appears in no override and no
   exemption anywhere.

4. The sweep, all 77 files: 44 deleted outright, 30 thinned in place, one replaced
   (`packages/sdk/src/server/h3-free.test.ts` grepped source for the string "h3";
   `web-standard-handlers.test.ts` CALLS each handler with a real `Request`).

   Boundary: delete anything asserting file existence, folder layout, manifest/config TEXT, doc
   prose, or the text of source files. Keep anything that imports a module and asserts behaviour
   or export identity; keep the two specs running the real oxlint binary
   (`packages/lint/src/fixtures.test.ts`, `packages/sdk/src/oxlint-guardrails.test.ts`) — those
   assert a tool's diagnostics, which is behaviour; keep specs parsing the committed data
   contracts (`packages/sdk/openapi/v1.json`, `packages/styles/styles.css`), which are artifacts.

5. Every CLAUDE.md and doc that cited a deleted spec was rewritten to say what actually holds the
   constraint now — or to state plainly that nothing does. packages/{lint,ui,sdk,forms,query,
   utils,env,logger,navigation}/CLAUDE.md, apps/CLAUDE.md,
   docs/development/{component-library,frontend-setup}.md.

## Vacuity check — the rule was proven to fire

A green `pnpm lint:tests` is also what a rule that never loads produces. Temporarily prepended
`import { readFileSync } from "node:fs";` to apps/wallow-web/src/query-facade.test.ts and ran
oxlint on it: `error wallow(no-source-tests)` at 1:30. Restored from backup.

## Accepted holes (user decision: "Accept the holes")

Enforcement is the five configured trees. Seven `node:fs` specs survive outside them — the two
oxlint-binary runners, packages/query/src/index.test.ts, packages/sdk's generated-query-surface
and openapi-regen, packages/styles' assets and theme-css. The doctrine holds repo-wide; it is
enforced in five places. Decision, not oversight.

Coverage genuinely lost in the widened sweep is enumerated under "Deliberate holes" in
docs/plans/2026-08-02/1744-no-source-tests-design.md — SDK server-handler import isolation, the
base-path Dockerfile/nitro/router.basepath trio, brand-asset importProtection + second-copy
checks, the react-query single-DECLARATION check (imports still banned by root
no-restricted-imports; pnpm strict node_modules still fails an undeclared import), wallow-auth's
internal-href sweep, packages/env's cross-app resolver sweep, the hand-rolled-button-utility half
of shell-source.test.ts, and the devtools-gating sweep.

Nothing is committed yet; all of the above is working-tree.
Committed as 40b915a3 on feat/multi-org-membership (not pushed). Precise counts: 77 source-reading specs inventoried; 74 changed — 44 deleted outright, 30 thinned in place, with one of the deletions (packages/sdk/src/server/h3-free.test.ts) replaced by web-standard-handlers.test.ts. Three kept unchanged: packages/lint/src/fixtures.test.ts, packages/sdk/src/oxlint-guardrails.test.ts (both run the real oxlint binary) and @bc-solutions-coder/testing's build-config reader. Earlier notes on this bead say 'all 77 deleted' — read that as 'all 77 judged', 74 changed.
close_reason: Shipped: .claude/rules/TESTING.md rule, wallow/no-source-tests (3 fixtures, registered in all five nested configs, proven to fire), and the full 77-file sweep. pnpm check green.

title: SeederService: a fatal step exception is logged then swallowed by BackgroundService, exiting the container 0
description:
Severity: HIGH. Discovered while diagnosing Wallow-smvc (ILastOwnerGuard missing from the seeder's
DI container), and independent of that bug's fix.

SeederWorker.ExecuteAsync (api/src/Wallow.SeederService/SeederWorker.cs:19-46) wraps its whole
sequence of seed steps in try/catch/finally:

    try
    {
        ... SeedRolesAsync / SeedApiScopesAsync / SyncOpenIddictScopesAsync / BootstrapAdminAsync /
            SyncOrganizationsAsync / SyncClientsAsync ...
        LogSeederCompleted();
    }
    catch (Exception ex)
    {
        LogSeederFailed(ex);
        throw;
    }
    finally
    {
        lifetime.StopApplication();
    }

The catch block logs and rethrows, which looks correct in isolation. But BackgroundService's own
exception handling (the .NET default BackgroundServiceExceptionBehavior, which this host never
overrides to StopHost) does not turn an unhandled exception from ExecuteAsync into a non-zero
process exit code by itself in a Worker Service host -- the host's Main just awaits
host.RunAsync(), the exception unwinds and stops the host via IHostApplicationLifetime (which
`finally { lifetime.StopApplication(); }` here does explicitly), and RunAsync returns normally
once the host has stopped. Nothing in Program.cs inspects whether ExecuteAsync's Task ended
faulted vs completed before letting the process exit.

CONFIRMED IN THE WILD (Wallow-smvc's repro): with the ILastOwnerGuard registration missing,
`docker inspect wallow-test-wallow-seeder-1` showed ExitCode 0 even though SyncOrganizationsAsync
threw and the "Client Sync" step (which seeds every OpenIddict application row) never ran. Because
docker-compose.test.yml's dependent services key on `depends_on: condition:
service_completed_successfully`, wallow-api and wallow-web started anyway against a database with
zero seeded OIDC clients -- a silent, cascading failure with no error surfaced to
`./scripts/e2e.sh` or its log. Wallow-smvc's actual DI gap is now fixed, but this exit-code masking
is a systemic risk independent of that specific bug: ANY future exception thrown by ANY seed step
will reproduce the same silent-success-on-failure behavior.

FIX (not dictated further -- whoever picks this up should choose the right mechanism): make the
process exit non-zero when SeederWorker's ExecuteAsync ends on the exception path. Likely
candidates: set `BackgroundServiceExceptionBehavior.StopHost` on HostOptions (verify what that
actually does to the process exit code in a non-Web Worker host -- confirm, don't assume), or have
Program.cs explicitly check the hosted service's execution result / call
`Environment.Exit(1)`/throw out of `RunAsync` in a way that propagates to the process exit code, or
wrap `host.RunAsync()` and rethrow to let it escape Main unhandled. Whatever the mechanism, add a
regression test (likely in Wallow.SeederService.Tests, following the existing
SeederWorkerBootstrapAdminTests.cs pattern) proving that a thrown exception from one of the seed
steps results in a non-zero process/host exit, not just a logged Critical entry.

Discovered while fixing Wallow-smvc; filed as its own bead per that bead's instructions -- not
part of Wallow-smvc's scope.
notes:
ROOT CAUSE CONFIRMED EMPIRICALLY (.NET SDK 10.0.302, minimal Worker repro reproducing SeederWorker's exact try/catch-rethrow/finally-StopApplication shape). Three variants, real process exit codes:

  default   (no HostOptions config) -> exit 0
  stophost  (BackgroundServiceExceptionBehavior.StopHost set explicitly) -> exit 0
  exitcode  (Environment.ExitCode = 1 on the failure path) -> exit 1

TWO CORRECTIONS TO THIS BEAD'S ANALYSIS:

1. The bead says the host "never overrides to StopHost". StopHost is ALREADY THE DEFAULT (has been since .NET 6). The repro's default-mode run emitted the framework's own crit message verbatim: "The HostOptions.BackgroundServiceExceptionBehavior is configured to StopHost. A BackgroundService has thrown an unhandled exception, and the IHost instance is stopping."

2. Therefore the bead's FIRST suggested fix candidate -- setting BackgroundServiceExceptionBehavior.StopHost -- IS A NO-OP. It is already on, and the process still exits 0. Do not spend time on it.

MECHANISM: Host.TryExecuteBackgroundServiceAsync catches the faulted ExecuteAsync task, logs "BackgroundService failed" (evt 9) + the StopHost crit (evt 10), then calls _applicationLifetime.StopApplication(). It never rethrows and records the failure nowhere the host surfaces. RunAsync() thus completes SUCCESSFULLY. Program.cs's top-level `await host.RunAsync();` returns no value, so the process exits with Environment.ExitCode, still 0. StopHost controls WHETHER the host stops, never the exit code.

SCOPE IS WIDER THAN THIS BEAD: Wallow.MigrationService/MigrationWorker.cs has the same defect and is arguably worse -- ExecuteAsync has NO try/catch/finally at all, so a failed migration is not even logged at Critical by our own code, and the same silent exit 0 results. docker-compose.test.yml gates BOTH wallow-seeder (line 103) and wallow-migrations on depends_on: condition: service_completed_successfully, so a failed migration cascades identically to the failed-seed case already observed under Wallow-smvc. Fixing only the seeder leaves half the hole open.

THE FIX CLOSES THE LOOP: scripts/e2e.sh runs `set -euo pipefail` with `compose up --wait`, and compose fails a service_completed_successfully dependency on a non-zero exit. So once the exit code is right, the failure surfaces loudly in e2e.sh instead of silently starting api/web against an unseeded database.

RECOMMENDED MECHANISM: do not rely on Environment.ExitCode written from inside the worker (global mutable state, awkward to assert, parallel-unsafe under xUnit). Prefer a small injected outcome/result sink singleton the worker marks on the failure path, with Program.cs returning `outcome.Failed ? 1 : 0` after `await host.RunAsync()`. That makes the regression test deterministic: drive ExecuteAsync with one seed step rigged to throw, assert the sink records failure -- no Environment/global state, and it follows the existing NSubstitute + RecordingLogger pattern in SeederWorkerBootstrapAdminTests.cs. Program.cs itself is excluded from coverage.runsettings, so the one-line return needs no test.

Repro kept at scratchpad/exitrepro (session-local, disposable).
Implementation plan written: docs/plans/2026-08-02/1503-worker-exit-code.md (local-only, gitignored).

Design chosen: a WorkerRunOutcome singleton in Wallow.ServiceDefaults (both hosts already reference it), marked by the worker's catch block, read by Program.cs.

ADDITIONAL MEASURED FINDING that changes the obvious implementation: HostingAbstractionsHostExtensions.RunAsync DISPOSES the host in a finally block. So 'return host.Services.GetRequiredService<WorkerRunOutcome>().ExitCode;' AFTER await host.RunAsync() throws ObjectDisposedException -- verified in the repro. The sink MUST be resolved from host.Services BEFORE awaiting RunAsync. Confirmed exit codes for the exact proposed pattern: resolve-before + step throws -> 1; resolve-before + all steps succeed -> 0; resolve-after -> ObjectDisposedException.

Plan covers both SeederService and MigrationService (Tasks 5-6 are separable into their own bead if the bead boundary should stay strict). Also creates the missing Wallow.MigrationService.Tests project, registers it in Wallow.slnx, adds a 'migrations' shorthand to run-tests.sh, and moves RecordingLogger into Wallow.Tests.Common so both test projects share it.

Verification includes a real-database proof that the failure path now exits 1: point the seeder at a created-but-unmigrated database and check the exit code (0 before the fix, 1 after).

title: SeederService: OrganizationService missing ILastOwnerGuard registration crashes 'Sync Organizations', silently blocking ALL OIDC client seeding
description:
Severity: HIGH. This blocks every OIDC-client-dependent e2e flow in the containerised test stack (docker/docker-compose.test.yml) -- and, since it's a Wallow.SeederService/Program.cs code bug rather than a compose/test config issue, almost certainly `pnpm backend` (Aspire) too, wherever the seeder actually runs SyncOrganizationsAsync against a database that reaches it.

ROOT CAUSE: commit fa80e5ff ("feat(identity): keep an organization from losing its last owner") added `ILastOwnerGuard lastOwnerGuard` as a constructor parameter of `OrganizationService` (api/src/Modules/Identity/Wallow.Identity.Infrastructure/Services/OrganizationService.cs:21) and registered it in the module's own DI extension (`IdentityInfrastructureExtensions.cs:418: services.AddScoped<ILastOwnerGuard, LastOwnerGuard>();`), but did NOT add the same registration to Wallow.SeederService/Program.cs, which hand-picks its own DI subset instead of calling the full `AddIdentityInfrastructure` extension (it separately registers IOrganizationRepository, IMembershipRepository, IMembershipRoleResolver, IOrganizationService, AddMembershipAccessRevocation(), IMessageBus, TimeProvider -- but never ILastOwnerGuard).

OBSERVED FAILURE: SeederWorker.ExecuteAsync runs SyncOpenIddictScopesAsync -> Bootstrap Admin -> SyncOrganizationsAsync -> SyncClientsAsync in order (api/src/Wallow.SeederService/SeederWorker.cs:30-33). SyncOrganizationsAsync resolves OrganizationSeedSyncService, which resolves IOrganizationService (-> OrganizationService), which throws at DI construction time:

  System.InvalidOperationException: Unable to resolve service for type
  'Wallow.Identity.Application.Interfaces.ILastOwnerGuard' while attempting to
  activate 'Wallow.Identity.Infrastructure.Services.OrganizationService'.
    at ... SeederWorker.SyncOrganizationsAsync(...) SeederWorker.cs:line 183

BackgroundServiceExceptionBehavior.StopHost then tears the host down -- but the CONTAINER STILL EXITS 0 (`docker inspect wallow-test-wallow-seeder-1` -> ExitCode 0), so docker compose's `depends_on: condition: service_completed_successfully` is satisfied and wallow-api starts anyway, with SyncClientsAsync (the step that seeds every OpenIddict application/client row, including wallow-web-client and bcordes-bff) never having run.

CONFIRMED BY QUERY: after a full fresh `docker compose ... down -v` + `up -d --wait wallow-api wallow-web bff-example` cycle, `identity."OpenIddictApplications"` has ZERO rows. Every OIDC-client-driven login (wallow-web's own /bff/login, bff-example's /bff/login) fails at /connect/authorize with:
  error: invalid_request
  error_description: The specified 'client_id' is invalid.
and wallow-api logs: "The authentication demand was rejected because the client application was not found: 'wallow-web-client'" / "'bcordes-bff'".

This breaks apps/wallow-web/e2e-cross-app/login-journey.spec.ts (both tests, pre-existing, unrelated to any Wallow-yp3e.4 work) and the new external-origin-login.spec.ts identically -- neither can reach a login form because there is no valid OIDC client to authorize against.

NOT the cause of the 7 wallow-auth suite failures (Wallow-n9i6) -- those specs authenticate via direct password/otp/magic-link POSTs with no client_id/OIDC path involved, and reproduce identically whether or not this bug is present.

FIX: add `builder.Services.AddScoped<ILastOwnerGuard, LastOwnerGuard>();` to api/src/Wallow.SeederService/Program.cs alongside the other hand-picked Identity Infrastructure registrations (or reconsider whether SeederService should keep hand-picking individual services at all, given how easily this class of registration drifts out of sync with OrganizationService's constructor -- that's a design question for whoever picks this up, not dictated here). Also worth a follow-up: the seeder exiting 0 after a fatal BackgroundService crash defeats depends_on's `service_completed_successfully` gate for every consumer of this container; fixing the immediate DI gap unblocks the current epic, but the silent-exit-0-on-crash pattern is a separate, systemic risk worth its own look.

REPRODUCE:
  cd docker && docker compose --project-name wallow-test -f docker-compose.test.yml up -d --wait wallow-api wallow-web
  docker compose --project-name wallow-test -f docker-compose.test.yml logs wallow-seeder | grep -A5 "ILastOwnerGuard"
  docker exec wallow-test-postgres-1 psql -U wallow_test -d wallow_test -c 'SELECT "ClientId" FROM identity."OpenIddictApplications";'

Discovered while verifying Wallow-yp3e.4 (external-origin sign-in e2e). Blocks that bead's acceptance from being demonstrated at all in the containerised stack until fixed -- filed as an independent, higher-priority sibling, not part of yp3e.4's own scope (the FirstPartyClients compose edit under review there is unrelated and exonerated).
notes:
IMPLEMENTER START: confirmed root cause matches yp3e.4's report. OrganizationService (api/src/Modules/Identity/Wallow.Identity.Infrastructure/Services/OrganizationService.cs:21) requires ILastOwnerGuard; IdentityInfrastructureExtensions.cs:418 registers it as AddScoped<ILastOwnerGuard, LastOwnerGuard> but Wallow.SeederService/Program.cs never does. LastOwnerGuard's own ctor only needs IdentityDbContext (already registered in Program.cs), so the fix is a single AddScoped line, same lifetime/implementation as the module extension. Plan: extract Program.cs's hand-picked Identity DI subset into an internal, testable extension method (SeederServiceCollectionExtensions.AddSeederIdentityServices) so a DI-resolution test can build the REAL seeder container and resolve every service SeederWorker.ExecuteAsync's steps need (RoleManager<WallowRole>, OpenIddictScopeSyncService, IBootstrapAdminService, OrganizationSeedSyncService incl. IOrganizationService, PreRegisteredClientSyncService) -- this is the only way to prevent the same class of drift bug recurring, per the coordinator's ask. Wallow.SeederService.csproj gets InternalsVisibleTo Wallow.SeederService.Tests (existing repo pattern).
RED: api/tests/Wallow.SeederService.Tests/SeederIdentityServiceRegistrationTests.cs, 6 tests (1 direct + 5 theory cases), confirmed failing before the fix -- exactly the 2 that resolve OrganizationSeedSyncService/PreRegisteredClientSyncService fail with 'Unable to resolve service for type ILastOwnerGuard while attempting to activate OrganizationService' (RoleManager<WallowRole>, OpenIddictScopeSyncService, IBootstrapAdminService pass, matching SeederWorker's actual step order: the crash happens exactly at Sync Organizations, same as yp3e.4's reproduction). To get a real DI-graph test rather than a 'is X registered' check, extracted Program.cs's hand-picked Identity DI subset into internal Wallow.SeederServiceCollectionExtensions.AddSeederIdentityServices(IServiceCollection, IConfiguration, string connectionString) in api/src/Wallow.SeederService/SeederServiceCollectionExtensions.cs; Program.cs now just calls it. Test project gets InternalsVisibleTo via api/src/Wallow.SeederService/Wallow.SeederService.csproj. title: guard Wolverine codegen — every discovered handler must compile under ServiceLocationPolicy.NotAllowed
description:
Nothing in the .NET test suite exercises Wolverine's handler CODEGEN path, so the failure mode that
silently dropped every outbound email (Wallow-0tor / Wallow-nafb) can return with a fully green
suite.

## The gap

`Wallow.Api/Program.cs` sets `ServiceLocationPolicy.NotAllowed` (~:204). Under that policy Wolverine
generates handler code that must `new` each dependency directly; a dependency whose concrete type is
not `public`, or one opted into service location, makes codegen FATAL and the handler is never
built. The message is then enqueued and dropped with no exception at the call site — which is why
`POST /v1/identity/auth/forgot-password` returned 200 while nothing reached SMTP.

Every existing test misses it:

- `SendEmailHandlerTests.cs:27` does `new SendEmailHandler(...)` directly, so codegen never runs.
- `NotificationsModuleExtensionsTests` asserts only that a `ServiceDescriptor` is registered.

The defect escaped to E2E twice.

## Live near-miss, so the guard must be lifetime-agnostic

`RedisSseDispatcher` (`RedisSseDispatcher.cs:7`) is `internal sealed` and is injected into three
Wolverine handlers. It is harmless TODAY only because it is registered `AddSingleton`
(`Program.cs:324`) — a one-word lifetime change on `ISseDispatcher` reproduces the outage in the SSE
path. A guard that checks the whole discovered handler set covers this; one that special-cases
`NotificationPreferenceChecker` does not.

## What to build

A test that boots the real Wolverine configuration — the same `ServiceLocationPolicy.NotAllowed` the
API sets — asks it for EVERY discovered message handler, and compiles each one, failing with the
offending handler and service named. Wolverine ships assertion helpers for exactly this; look the
current API up (ref.tools) rather than reconstructing the codegen call by hand.

The handler set must be DISCOVERED, never enumerated as a hardcoded list — a hardcoded list is the
same hole one level up.

Run it through `./scripts/run-tests.sh`, never bare `dotnet test`.

## Why this bead exists separately from the defect

`Wallow-0tor` and `Wallow-nafb` both close once `f62c2214` reaches `main`. This bead is the only
artifact that survives that closure, and it is what stops the highest-severity failure mode in the
backlog from returning uncovered.
acceptance_criteria: A test in the .NET suite compiles every Wolverine-DISCOVERED message handler under ServiceLocationPolicy.NotAllowed and fails when any handler cannot be generated, naming both the handler and the offending service. The handler set is obtained by discovery, not from a hardcoded list. Two independent reverts each turn it red: making NotificationPreferenceChecker internal again, and changing ISseDispatcher's registration from AddSingleton to AddScoped. ./scripts/run-tests.sh is green with neither revert applied.
notes:
Filed from the bead backlog audit of 2026-08-02 (docs/audits/2026-08-02/0824-bead-backlog), finding H2. Filed deliberately BEFORE Wallow-0tor and Wallow-nafb close, so their closure does not remove the only record of this hazard. The audit also corrected the closure rationale for 0tor: 21 internal classes remain in api/src, so the defensible statement is not 'no internal classes remain' but 'no scoped or transient internal implementation reaches a Wolverine handler' — which is exactly what this test would enforce mechanically.
Likely ALREADY SATISFIED by api/tests/Wallow.Api.Tests/Integration/HandlerCodegenTests.cs (EveryDiscoveredHandler_Compiles), which boots real Wolverine config via WallowApiFactory and compiles every discovered chain. Verification tracked as Wallow-af3h.9. Caveat: that test BREAKS under MultipleHandlerBehavior.Separated (NoHandlerForEndpointException) and is being migrated to HandlerGraph.AllChains() in Wallow-af3h.2 — verify against the migrated version.
SATISFIED — verified by mutation testing on 2026-08-05 (tracked as Wallow-af3h.9). Closing.

The guard is api/tests/Wallow.Api.Tests/Integration/HandlerCodegenTests.cs →
EveryDiscoveredHandler_Compiles, added after this bead was filed and migrated to
HandlerGraph.AllChains() by Wallow-af3h.2. Verified against the MIGRATED version, as this bead's
caveat required.

Every acceptance criterion, checked:

- 'compiles every DISCOVERED handler under ServiceLocationPolicy.NotAllowed' — MET. Boots the
  real configuration via WallowApiFactory and compiles 94 chains (AllChains(), which is what
  reaches the sticky sub-chains; Chains alone is 88 and would silently skip the four
  multi-handler message types).
- 'fails when any handler cannot be generated' — MET, and reports ALL failures, not the first.
- 'naming both the handler and the offending service' — MET. Actual output under mutation A:
  'Service Wallow.Notifications.Application.Preferences.Interfaces.INotificationPreferenceChecker:
  Concrete type Wallow.Notifications.Infrastructure.Services.NotificationPreferenceChecker is not
  public, so requires service location'. Interface, concrete type, and reason.
- 'handler set obtained by discovery, not a hardcoded list' — MET. No type literals; the test also
  asserts the graph is non-empty so a discovery regression cannot make it vacuously pass.
- 'two independent reverts each turn it red' — MET, both run:
    A. NotificationPreferenceChecker public -> internal: 35/36, the ONLY failure being
       EveryDiscoveredHandler_Compiles.
    B. ISseDispatcher AddSingleton -> AddScoped (Program.cs:452, NOT :324 as this bead states):
       32/36. EveryDiscoveredHandler_Compiles plus three MultipleHandlerSeparationTests, since
       scoped RedisSseDispatcher also breaks the SSE handlers at runtime.
- './scripts/run-tests.sh green with neither revert applied' — MET. Baseline 36/36 before, 36/36
  after both reverts were backed out; git status clean.

This closes the hazard the bead was filed for: the live near-miss it named (internal sealed
RedisSseDispatcher surviving only because it is AddSingleton) is now mechanically caught by a
one-word lifetime change.

title: Thread actorId through member add/remove and role assign/remove
description:
PREREQUISITE for the audit publisher. MembershipTransitionedEvent declares
`required Guid ActorId`, and MembershipTransition includes Added, Removed,
RoleAssigned and RoleRemoved. The four methods that cause those transitions take
no actor, so the publisher cannot construct the event for them at all.

Four signatures need an actorId (all in Wallow.Identity.Application/Interfaces):

  IOrganizationService.AddMemberAsync(Guid orgId, Guid userId, string roleName, ct)
  IOrganizationService.RemoveMemberAsync(Guid orgId, Guid userId, ct)
  IUserManagementService.AssignRoleAsync(Guid userId, Guid organizationId, string roleName, ct)
  IUserManagementService.RemoveRoleAsync(Guid userId, Guid organizationId, string roleName, ct)

Impls: Wallow.Identity.Infrastructure/Services/OrganizationService.cs and
UserManagementService.cs (AssignRole ~line 218, RemoveRole ~line 253).

This matches the established convention on the same interface - ArchiveAsync,
ReactivateAsync, UpdateSettingsAsync, UpdateEnrollmentAsync and
UpdateBrandingAsync already take `Guid actorId`. Follow that shape (non-optional
Guid, positioned before ct), not a nullable.

BootstrapAdminService.AssignRoleAsync(userId, roleName, ct) is a DIFFERENT,
global/system path - out of scope, leave it alone.

TDD: write the failing tests FIRST. The prior agent's commit message claimed
tests already demand actorId here; they do not (verified). Nothing currently
forces this, so it must be written before it can drive the change.

Callers to update include OrganizationsController and any seeder/enrollment path
that adds members - find them from the compile errors after changing the
signatures.

DONE WHEN: signatures carry actorId, all callers pass a real actor (not
Guid.Empty), tests assert the actor reaches the published event, solution builds.
notes:
DONE - committed ac214e10 on feat/multi-org-membership.

All four signatures now take Guid actorId before the CancellationToken:
  IOrganizationService.AddMemberAsync / RemoveMemberAsync
  IUserManagementService.AssignRoleAsync / RemoveRoleAsync

Callers: OrganizationsController uses its existing ActorId() helper; UsersController
uses Guid.Parse(User.GetUserId()!). PreRegisteredClientSyncService passes Guid.Empty -
config-driven seeding has no human actor, and Guid.Empty is the repo's existing
system-actor fallback (see OrganizationService.CreateOrganizationAsync).

The bug was real and was NOT just a missing parameter: OrganizationService and
UserManagementService passed `userId` into Membership.Grant/AssignRole/RemoveRole,
whose second parameter is the ACTOR (it feeds SetUpdated -> AuditableEntity.UpdatedBy).
So the member appeared to have granted themselves the access.

Three guard tests added, all mutation-verified (reverted the fix, watched them fail):
  OrganizationServiceTests.AddMemberAsync_StampsTheMembershipWithTheActorNotTheSubject
  UserManagementServiceTests.AssignRoleAsync_StampsTheMembershipWithTheActorNotTheSubject
  UserManagementServiceTests.RemoveRoleAsync_StampsTheMembershipWithTheActorNotTheSubject

Suite: identity 1522/1547 (was 1519/1544 - +3 tests, +3 passing, failures unchanged
at 25). arch 302/302.

RemoveMemberAsync has no UpdatedBy to assert against because the membership row is
deleted, so its actor is only observable through MembershipTransitionedEvent - that
assertion belongs to Wallow-yp3e.1.2, which is now unblocked.

TWO ENVIRONMENT TRAPS HIT HERE, both cost a cycle:

1. `dotnet format api/Wallow.slnx` will SILENTLY GENERATE STUB METHODS that throw
   NotImplementedException when an interface member is unimplemented. It did this to
   UserManagementService after a bad `git checkout` wiped the impl but left the
   interface. The solution then BUILDS CLEAN and the failure only appears at runtime
   as NotImplementedException. Watch for "Unable to fix CS1503 ... GenerateMethodCodeFixProvider"
   in format's output - that means it wrote stubs. Always build+test after formatting.

2. `git checkout <file>` to undo a one-line mutation test reverts the ENTIRE file.
   Use a targeted revert or stash instead.

Also removed 7 stale untracked bin/obj-only directories under api/src and api/tests
(Wallow.Auth, Wallow.Web, Wallow.Auth.Tests, Wallow.Auth.Component.Tests,
Wallow.E2E.Tests, Wallow.Web.Tests, Wallow.Web.Component.Tests). They were leftovers
from before those Blazor projects were deleted upstream and were failing 7
WallowAuth/WallowWebDeletionTests arch assertions. Not a code regression - a fresh
clone never sees it.

title: Migrate the org-detail route to the $orgId directory form
description: apps/wallow-web/src/app/routes/dashboard/organizations/$orgId.tsx is a leaf route with no <Outlet/> ($orgId.tsx:20-27). Adding any sibling under $orgId would promote it to a layout and blank every child page. Convert it to the directory form so the two $orgId-scoped membership screens can be added as plain siblings. Plan: docs/plans/2026-08-01/2019-membership-dashboard-screens.md section 2.
design:
A route directory with no route.tsx creates path nesting and NO layout component - grounded in routes/dashboard/organizations/ itself, which has no organizations.tsx and no route.tsx, and whose two routes attach straight to the /dashboard layout (routeTree.gen.ts:90-97).

Moves:
- organizations/$orgId.tsx -> organizations/$orgId/index.tsx; createFileRoute id becomes '/dashboard/organizations/$orgId/' (trailing slash), matching how organizations/index.tsx:40 spells its own.
- organizations/$orgId.test.tsx -> organizations/$orgId/index.test.tsx, with its describe titles and path assertions updated.
- organizations/__screenshots__/$orgId.restyle.test.tsx/ -> organizations/$orgId/__screenshots__/ .
- apps/wallow-web/src/app/routes/dashboard/page-shell.test.ts: PAGE_FILES (lines 27-35) entry 'organizations/$orgId.tsx' -> 'organizations/$orgId/index.tsx'. It is a hand-kept list; a page missing from it is silently exempt from the PageContainer-width and no-hand-rolled-h1 invariants.

Existing <Link to="/dashboard/organizations/$orgId"> call sites need NO edit: routeTree.gen.ts:131 shows index routes lose their trailing slash in FileRoutesByTo, the map 'to' is typed against. OrganizationList.tsx is unaffected.

Rejected alternative: the trailing-underscore un-nesting convention ($orgId_.requests.tsx). It is real - the installed generator strips a trailing _ from the path at @tanstack+router-generator@1.167.21/dist/esm/utils.js:320 - but has zero precedent in this repo, and the directory form needs no convention at all.

Do NOT create $orgId/route.tsx. Do NOT hand-edit routeTree.gen.ts; it regenerates from a build. Strip the stale 'Wallow-8w1h.4.4' bead reference from the moved file's header ($orgId.tsx:11) per .claude/rules/TESTING.md comment rules.
acceptance_criteria:
- organizations/$orgId/index.tsx exists and organizations/$orgId.tsx does not; the route id is '/dashboard/organizations/$orgId/'.
- The moved spec and its __screenshots__ directory sit under organizations/$orgId/ and pass.
- page-shell.test.ts's PAGE_FILES names the new path and the suite passes.
- No <Outlet/> is introduced and no $orgId/route.tsx is created.
- routeTree.gen.ts is REGENERATED by 'pnpm --filter @bc-solutions-coder/wallow-web build' and committed (route-tree-drift.yml fails on a diff).
- Navigation to /dashboard/organizations/$orgId still renders OrganizationDetail; existing Link call sites are unchanged.
- pnpm check passes.
notes:
RED (TDD red phase, frontend-only, apps/wallow-web).

FILES (all under apps/wallow-web/src/app/routes/dashboard/):
- organizations/$orgId/index.test.tsx  — the moved spec (git mv from organizations/$orgId.test.tsx), rewritten to import ./index and to pin the directory form. 5 tests.
- organizations/$orgId/index.tsx — STRUCTURAL SCAFFOLD ONLY, no logic: 'export const Route = createFileRoute("/dashboard/organizations/$orgId/")({})'. Green replaces its body with the content of organizations/$orgId.tsx (component + loader), then DELETES organizations/$orgId.tsx.
- page-shell.test.ts — PAGE_FILES entry 'organizations/$orgId.tsx' -> 'organizations/$orgId/index.tsx'.

TEST_STATUS=red — 5 failing, each on the intended assertion (no import errors, no timeouts):
1. page-shell 'takes organizations/$orgId/index.tsx width from the catalog container' — scaffold does not import PageContainer.
2. $orgId/ (route) 'exposes a route component' — Route.options.component undefined.
3. $orgId/ (route) 'prefetches org detail + members via a loader' — Route.options.loader undefined.
4. $orgId/ (router registration) 'registers the index route under the $orgId directory' — routesById lacks '/dashboard/organizations/$orgId/' until routeTree.gen.ts is regenerated.
5. $orgId/ (router registration) 'contributes no $orgId layout route' — routesById still holds the bare '/dashboard/organizations/$orgId' leaf id today; after the move that id must be ABSENT (its presence post-move would mean a $orgId/route.tsx layout exists).

One test is deliberately green now and must STAY green: 'leaves /dashboard/organizations/$orgId addressable by existing links' (router.routesByPath). That is the acceptance criterion about unchanged Link call sites.

Grounding for the assertions (routeTree.gen.ts at HEAD): FileRoutesById carries index routes WITH a trailing slash ('/dashboard/organizations/', '/dashboard/apps/') and FileRoutesByTo WITHOUT ('/dashboard/organizations'). dashboard/apps/ is the in-repo precedent for a route directory with no route.tsx: it produces ids '/dashboard/apps/' and '/dashboard/apps/register' and NO '/dashboard/apps' id. router.routesById is public API (@tanstack/router-core 1.171.15 router.d.ts:629).

GREEN CHECKLIST (from the failures above):
- git mv organizations/$orgId.tsx over organizations/$orgId/index.tsx, changing createFileRoute id to '/dashboard/organizations/$orgId/' (trailing slash) and stripping the stale 'Wallow-8w1h.4.4' bead ref from the file header.
- Do NOT edit organizations/$orgId/index.test.tsx.
- Run 'pnpm --filter @bc-solutions-coder/wallow-web build' to regenerate routeTree.gen.ts; tests 4 and 5 cannot pass without it. Do not hand-edit the generated tree.
- Do NOT create $orgId/route.tsx and introduce no Outlet.

ISSUES:
1. The acceptance criterion 'the moved spec and its __screenshots__ directory sit under organizations/$orgId/' is partly MOOT. organizations/__screenshots__/$orgId.restyle.test.tsx/ is an ORPHAN: no $orgId.restyle.test.tsx exists anywhere in the app (find -name '*restyle*' confirms), and all __screenshots__ dirs are gitignored and untracked ('git ls-files' on the organizations dir lists only the 4 .tsx files). Nothing depends on moving it; it can be deleted or left. Green should not treat its absence under $orgId/ as a failure.
2. Vitest browser mode wrote failure screenshots into $orgId/__screenshots__/ during this red run; deleted so they do not confuse the green phase.
3. During red both organizations/$orgId.tsx and organizations/$orgId/index.tsx exist.
