title: first-run setup wizard cannot complete: bootstrap admin gets no membership
description:
SetupStatusChecker now asks 'does an Active membership hold a role granting AdminAccess'. The seeded path satisfies that (PreRegisteredClientSyncService enrolls seedMembers with seedMemberRoles), but POST /v1/identity/setup/admin does not: BootstrapAdminHandler creates a WallowUser and writes AspNetUserRoles, which nothing reads for authorization. So on an UNSEEDED instance the wizard can be driven repeatedly and setup never reports complete.

Not an escalation - an admin created that way holds no permission anywhere, because roles resolve from memberships. It is a usability dead end.

Fixing it needs a product decision the multi-org plan does not make: which organization does the first administrator belong to? Options: add organizationName to CreateAdminRequest (API/contract changes are free here, and no frontend consumes this endpoint today), or have bootstrap create a single implicit organization. Related plan work: Task 1.9 (the role write path) already owns BootstrapAdminService, and Phase 4 owns enrollment.
notes:
FIXED as part of Wallow-4wdu (the two are the same change: 4wdu's acceptance criteria requires
the wizard to complete once and then report setup not required).

PRODUCT DECISION: option 1 -- organizationName is now a required field on CreateAdminRequest.
Confirmed with the repo owner. No frontend consumes POST /v1/identity/setup/admin, so the
contract change was free; packages/sdk/openapi/v1.json and the generated client are regenerated
from the live spec.

BootstrapAdminHandler now: EnsureRoleExistsAsync("admin") -> CreateUserAsync ->
IOrganizationService.CreateOrganizationAsync(name, creatorUserId: newUserId). Passing the
creator is what mints the Active OWNER membership carrying the admin role, and
RolePermissionMapping["admin"] includes AdminAccess, so SetupStatusChecker flips to false. The
ordering matters and is covered by a test: the organization resolves the admin role BY NAME to
enroll its creator, so EnsureRoleExists must run first.

SECOND BUG FOUND WHILE VERIFYING -- the wizard was ALSO returning 500 before any of this, and
would have kept doing so. Wolverine's ServiceLocationPolicy.NotAllowed is evaluated when a
handler is COMPILED, i.e. the first time the message is sent, so it never surfaces at startup
or in a unit test that news the handler up. BootstrapAdminCommand's handler reaches
IBootstrapAdminService (-> ASP.NET Identity UserManager) and IOrganizationService (-> OpenIddict
managers registered as opaque lambda factories); neither can be inline-constructed by the
codegen. Both are now opted in via opts.CodeGeneration.AlwaysUseServiceLocationFor<T>() in
Program.cs, alongside the existing ITenantContext / ITenantContextSetter / ISetupStatusChecker
entries. Guarded by a new test,
Wallow.Api.Tests/Integration/BootstrapAdminHandlerCodegenTests, which sends the command through
the real IMessageBus -- it failed with InvalidServiceLocationException before the fix.

VERIFIED LIVE (local Postgres, identity schema dropped and remigrated, NOT seeded):
  GET  /v1/identity/setup/status -> {"setupRequired":true}
  POST /v1/identity/setup/admin  -> 204
  GET  /v1/identity/setup/status -> {"setupRequired":false}
  POST /v1/identity/setup/admin  -> 409 Conflict
  db: wizard@wallow.dev / Wizard Org / Active / admin across memberships + membership_roles

title: fix(observability): connect the frontend logger to Alloy in every environment
description:
The logger is not connected to Grafana anywhere. Three independent breaks, all silent because emitOtlp never throws and a valid batch answers 204 regardless of collector health (packages/logger/CLAUDE.md failure rule 3).

1. api/src/Wallow.AppHost/Program.cs - neither AddJavaScriptApp registration sets OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT, so pnpm backend falls back to consoleSink (server.ts ~230).
2. docker/docker-compose.production.yml - the wallow-auth service sets no endpoint at all, same console fallback.
3. docker/docker-compose.production.yml:533 - wallow-web points at http://alloy:4317, which is gRPC. emitOtlp POSTs OTLP/JSON and needs 4318.

Contributing cause: the comment block at docker/docker-compose.yml:66-76 documents 4317 as the Alloy endpoint inside a section scoped to 'The Wallow API'. Correct for .NET's gRPC exporter, misleading for the Node logger, which is HTTP/JSON only.

Fix: point wallow-web at http://alloy:4318; add the same to wallow-auth; add .WithEnvironment("OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT", "http://localhost:4318") to both AddJavaScriptApp calls; amend the compose comment to distinguish the two exporters.

Verify a record actually lands in Loki rather than assuming a 204 means delivery. Alloy already has otlp receivers on both 4317 and 4318 (docker/alloy/config.alloy:5-9) and binds 127.0.0.1 in dev.

See docs/plans/2026-07-31/2318-logging-telemetry-decision-record.md Finding B.
notes:
DONE (config bead, no TDD phase). All three breaks fixed, the contributing-cause comment corrected,
and delivery verified live into Loki.

FILES
- api/src/Wallow.AppHost/Program.cs — both AddJavaScriptApp registrations now set
  OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT=http://localhost:4318 and OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_PROTOCOL=http/json,
  from two file-scoped consts with the rationale above them.
- docker/docker-compose.production.yml — wallow-web 4317 -> 4318; wallow-auth gains the same
  endpoint (no OTEL_SERVICE_NAME beside it, see below).
- docker/docker-compose.yml — the OBSERVABILITY comment block now distinguishes the two exporters
  and their ports instead of documenting 4317 as "the" Alloy endpoint.
- docs/development/logging.md, docs/operations/observability.md, docs/operations/deployment.md —
  the same 4317/4318 distinction, and one sentence in observability.md that my change falsified
  ("sets exactly these for the API and web containers").

CORRECTION TO THE BEAD'S DIAGNOSIS OF BREAK 1
The bead says pnpm backend "falls back to consoleSink" because no endpoint is set. It is not
unset. Aspire's AddJavaScriptApp -> CreateDefaultJavaScriptAppBuilder -> WithNodeDefaults() calls
WithOtlpExporter() (dotnet/aspire src/Aspire.Hosting.JavaScript/JavaScriptHostingExtensions.cs),
and AddOtlpEnvironment sets OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT + OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_PROTOCOL to the
DASHBOARD's OTLP endpoint — gRPC, and HTTPS per this repo's launchSettings
(DOTNET_DASHBOARD_OTLP_ENDPOINT_URL=https://localhost:21147). So dev was not printing to console;
it was POSTing JSON at an HTTPS gRPC port and dropping every batch with a console.warn — worse
than the bead assumed, and it means the fix HAD to be an explicit override rather than merely
"setting" the variable. The override wins because WithOtlpExporter registers its env callback at
AddJavaScriptApp time and ours registers after; both write the same dictionary key in order.
Second consequence, from the existing Valkey note in the same file: Aspire configures no
certificate trust for JavaScript app resources, so the dashboard's HTTPS endpoint could not have
worked for a Node client even over the right protocol.

WHY OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_PROTOCOL IS ALSO SET (beyond the bead's text)
Aspire leaves OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_PROTOCOL=grpc next to the endpoint. The logger never reads it,
but "grpc" naming an HTTP port is the same trap this bead exists to close.

WHY wallow-auth GETS NO OTEL_SERVICE_NAME
The ingest handler stamps the record's service from its own config (SERVICE = "wallow-auth" in
log-ingest.server.ts); nothing in the Node path reads OTEL_SERVICE_NAME. wallow-web's pre-existing
one is left alone (out of scope), but a matching one on auth would have been dead config that
reads as if it named something.

ALLOY CONFIG CHECKED, NOT ASSUMED
docker/alloy/config.alloy: otelcol.receiver.otlp "default" declares BOTH grpc 0.0.0.0:4317 and
http 0.0.0.0:4318, routes logs/metrics/traces to otelcol.exporter.otlp "backend", which ships to
grafana-lgtm:4317. So 4318 is a real receiver and it does reach Loki.

LIVE VERIFICATION (observed, not inferred)
Against the running dev stack (wallow-alloy + wallow-grafana-lgtm already up from
pnpm backend:infra):
1. packages/logger's emitOtlp, one record, via tsx:
   http://localhost:4318 -> {"ok":true,"status":200}
   http://localhost:4317 -> {"ok":false,...}   <- the bug, reproduced
2. The REAL createLogIngestHandler from @bc-solutions-coder/logger/server, configured exactly as
   the apps configure it (service, allowedOrigins fn, otlpEndpoint read from
   process.env.OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT), handed a real POST /logs Request: 204.
3. Loki, queried inside wallow-grafana-lgtm
   (curl localhost:3100/loki/api/v1/query_range), returned both records:
   {service_name="wallow-web", event_name="verify.otlp", scope_name="@bc-solutions-coder/logger",
    severity_text="INFO", marker="wallow-bzdy-1785556709681"}
   {service_name="wallow-auth", event_name="verify.ingest", severity_text="WARN",
    marker="wallow-bzdy-ingest-1785556915936"}
Both the collector leg and the handler leg are therefore observed end to end. The one leg NOT
exercised live is Aspire actually launching the node processes with the new env (dotnet run of the
AppHost was not performed); that claim rests on the Aspire source read above plus a clean build.

GATES
dotnet build api/src/Wallow.AppHost — 0 warnings, 0 errors.
dotnet format api/Wallow.slnx --verify-no-changes — clean.
docker compose config — dev stack OK; production stack renders API=4317, both Node apps=4318.
No pnpm gate applies: nothing under apps/ or packages/ was touched (oxfmt's paths), and the docs
edits are markdown.

NOT A BREAK, DELIBERATELY LEFT
docker/docker-compose.test.yml (the E2E stack) has no alloy service and sets no OTEL vars, so its
apps log to stdout. That is consistent, not the bug in this bead.

Not committed, not pushed.
VERIFY (independent, read-only):

[OK] Aspire override-ordering claim verified against actual Aspire 13.4.6 source (decompiled via ilspycmd, not accepted on the report's word):
  - WithNodeDefaults (called by AddJavaScriptApp) calls OtlpConfigurationExtensions.WithOtlpExporter<T>(builder) -> AddOtlpEnvironment -> adds a raw EnvironmentCallbackAnnotation to resource.Annotations whose callback resolves the dashboard's OTLP endpoint (grpc-preferring when protocol unspecified) and writes OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT/_PROTOCOL into the shared EnvironmentCallbackContext.EnvironmentVariables dictionary.
  - ResourceBuilderExtensions.WithEnvironment<T>(name, value) adds an EnvironmentAnnotation, and internal sealed class EnvironmentAnnotation : EnvironmentCallbackAnnotation (constructor: base(name, () => value)) -- i.e. it is literally the SAME annotation type/collection/pipeline as WithOtlpExporter's callback, not a separate mechanism that could be applied in a different pass.
  - Both therefore live in the same ordered resource.Annotations collection and write the same dictionary keys when the environment is resolved; since Program.cs's .WithEnvironment("OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT", ...) is chained AFTER AddJavaScriptApp(...) returns (which already ran WithNodeDefaults/WithOtlpExporter internally), its annotation is appended later in the same list and its write overwrites the dashboard's. The ordering claim holds -- confirmed at the annotation-type level, not just asserted.

[OK] docker-compose.test.yml genuinely needs no treatment: grepped it directly -- no alloy service, no OTEL_* env vars on wallow-web/wallow-auth, consistent with 'apps log to stdout' in the e2e stack. Not an oversight.

[OK] Live Loki verification narrative is internally consistent with the diff: compose now sets wallow-web/wallow-auth to alloy:4318 (was 4317 on web, unset on auth), matching docker/alloy/config.alloy's dual grpc(4317)/http(4318) receivers.

[OK] dotnet build api/src/Wallow.AppHost/Wallow.AppHost.csproj -- ran myself, 0 warnings/0 errors, matches the report.

[OK] Prose changes in docker-compose.yml, docs/development/logging.md, docs/operations/observability.md, docs/operations/deployment.md all correctly distinguish the 4317 (gRPC/.NET) vs 4318 (HTTP/Node logger) split and match the actual compose values; no leftover 'sets exactly these for the API and web containers' overclaim (that sentence was correctly narrowed to the API container only).

[OK] No stray debug artifacts in the diff (grepped the whole patch for console.log/debugger/TODO/.only/.skip).

No pnpm gate applicable (nothing under apps/ or packages/ touched by this bead) -- correct, this bead's files are all .cs/.yml/.md.

verdict=CLOSE.

title: fix(logger): stop trusting the inbound client-IP header on the ingest route
description:
createLogIngestHandler derives BOTH the rate-limit key and the stamped clientIp from the inbound x-wallow-client-ip header (packages/logger/src/server.ts:227,256,292). That header is an INTERNAL SEAM header the host is supposed to stamp, but nothing strips it inbound: apps/wallow-web/src/app/routes/bff/logs.ts passes the request through untouched, and docker/caddy/Caddyfile.example has no header_up rules. The headers.delete(CLIENT_IP_HEADER) in packages/sdk/src/server/forwarded.ts guards only the OUTBOUND API hop.

Impact: anything that can produce a valid Origin (including page script on a same-origin fetch) can set the header and (1) defeat the per-IP rate limit by rotating the value, since the limiter key is fully attacker-chosen and the route is unauthenticated by design; (2) forge client.address in the OTLP record (otlp.ts:177), in a field that reads as server-stamped. parseLogBatch's field-by-field rebuild does not defend it because the value arrives as a header, not in the body.

Fix: replace the clientIpHeader option with clientAddress?: (request: Request) => string | undefined. The handler must stop reading any inbound header for the IP. Both apps supply request.ip (srvx PeerRequest) - the proven pattern from bff.server.ts:151 and api-passthrough.server.ts:79. Confirmed available in Start server routes: routes/api/$.ts:24 already passes one into handleApiRequest(request: PeerRequest).

Secondary benefit: sendBeacon can set no headers, so today every terminal pagehide flush shares the single UNKNOWN_CLIENT bucket and one noisy client can exhaust the tab-close budget for everyone. A host-supplied peer address keys beacons correctly.

See docs/plans/2026-07-31/2318-logging-telemetry-decision-record.md Finding A.
notes:
GREEN: FILES=packages/logger/src/server.ts, packages/logger/src/log-event.ts, packages/logger/src/server.test.ts, packages/logger/CLAUDE.md, apps/wallow-web/src/app/lib/log-ingest.server.ts, apps/wallow-auth/src/shared/lib/log-ingest.server.ts, apps/wallow-web/src/log-headers.test.ts, docs/development/logging.md

SYMBOLS (breaking, as intended):
- LogIngestOptions.clientIpHeader?: string  -->  REMOVED
- LogIngestOptions.clientAddress?: (request: Request) => string | undefined  -->  ADDED
- DEFAULT_CLIENT_IP_HEADER  -->  DELETED from log-event.ts and from the ./server export list

WHAT THE HANDLER DOES NOW
peerAddress(request, options.clientAddress) is resolved ONCE, immediately before the limiter check, and the same value feeds both the rate-limit key (falling back to the UNKNOWN_CLIENT bucket) and the stamped clientIp (omitted when absent). An empty string is read as no answer, matching the old header handling. request.headers.get() is no longer called for the address anywhere in the module -- the only header the package reads a value out of is now REQUEST_ID_HEADER.

DECISION ON DEFAULT_CLIENT_IP_HEADER: deleted.
Nothing in the logger reads it once the handler stops reading headers, so keeping the export would publish a constant whose only remaining meaning is 'the header we deliberately ignore' -- surface a fork would reasonably wire something to. The SDK-facing outbound path is unaffected: both apps import CLIENT_IP_HEADER from @bc-solutions-coder/sdk/server directly (bff.server.ts, api-passthrough.server.ts) and never went through the logger's copy. apps/wallow-web/src/log-headers.test.ts therefore drops its second it() and now pins only REQUEST_ID_HEADER parity, which is still true and still the drift that is invisible at runtime; its header comment was rewritten from 'two header names' to one.

REGRESSION TESTS ADDED (packages/logger/src/server.test.ts)
- 'gives a caller rotating the client-IP header no fresh buckets' -- limit 1, two requests rotating x-wallow-client-ip, second is 429. This is the rate-limit half of the vulnerability.
- 'ignores a client-IP header the caller sent' -- stamped clientIp is undefined. This is the forgery half.
- 'prefers the host's address over a header claiming another' -- host wins when both are present.
- 'puts every caller in one bucket when the host supplies no address' -- pins the failure direction.
- 'stamps no client address when the host answers with an empty string'.
REWRITTEN: 'rate-limits per client address' -> 'rate-limits per address the host supplies', and 'stamps the client address from the host header' -> '...the host supplies'. Both now drive the clientAddress seam. Specs vary the address through an x-spec-peer header read by a hostPeer() helper standing in for the socket read -- the header is a spec fixture, not a contract.

WIRING
Both apps declare the local 'interface PeerRequest extends Request { readonly ip?: string | undefined }' (a third/second copy of the same three lines already in bff.server.ts and api-passthrough.server.ts -- deliberately duplicated rather than imported, so the logging module gains no edge to the BFF/passthrough module) and pass clientAddress: (request: PeerRequest) => request.ip. Because ip is optional, the callback is assignable to (request: Request) => ..., so no cast is needed and NEITHER ROUTE FILE NEEDED EDITING -- apps/wallow-web/src/app/routes/bff/logs.ts and apps/wallow-auth/src/app/routes/logs.ts pass Start's request straight into handleLogIngest(request: PeerRequest) and typecheck clean. The bead listed the routes as mount points to wire; they turned out to need nothing.

CHARTER: untouched. No new dependency, no node:* , no process.env, no @types. charter.test.ts passes unchanged. Zero-dependency invariant is if anything stronger -- one fewer exported string mirroring the SDK.

PROSE UPDATED
- server.ts module header: the rate-limit bullet now says the key is host-supplied, and the stamping bullet says clientIp comes from clientAddress, never off the wire.
- log-event.ts REQUEST_ID_HEADER comment: notes it is the only header a value is read from, and points at clientAddress.
- packages/logger/CLAUDE.md: rate-limit bullet amended, new paragraph 'The client address arrives through a callback, not a header' explaining why a header cannot be the source and what both apps answer with; the 'It does not depend on the SDK' section rewritten to one mirrored constant.
- docs/development/logging.md: the clientIp row in the record table, a new paragraph beside the service/userId forgery argument, and the per-IP rate limit bullet.

SECONDARY BENEFIT NOW REAL: a sendBeacon flush sets no headers, so under the old code every terminal pagehide flush shared UNKNOWN_CLIENT and one noisy client could exhaust the tab-close budget for everyone. Keyed on the peer address, beacons now bucket correctly.

TEST_STATUS=pass
- pnpm --filter @bc-solutions-coder/logger test: 7 files, 156 tests, all pass
- pnpm --filter ./apps/wallow-web test: 86 files, 693 pass / 1 skipped
- pnpm --filter ./apps/wallow-auth test: 62 files, 971 pass
- pnpm --filter @bc-solutions-coder/sdk build then pnpm typecheck: clean across all 13 workspace members
- pnpm lint exit 0, pnpm lint:tests exit 0 (386 files), pnpm format:check exit 0
- packages/logger rebuilt so apps typecheck against fresh dist/

NOT DONE (per instructions): no commit, no push, no full pnpm check.
ISSUES=none. docker/caddy/Caddyfile.example still has no inbound header_up strip rules, which is now moot for this route but remains true for any future header seam; not filed, since the package no longer trusts one.
VERIFY (independent, read-only):

[OK] Guard chain is the only source of clientIp/rate-limit key. Grepped the whole repo for x-wallow-client-ip / DEFAULT_CLIENT_IP_HEADER / CLIENT_IP_HEADER: the logger module (server.ts, log-event.ts) no longer reads any header for the address; the only remaining CLIENT_IP_HEADER usages are the SDK's own outbound seam (forwarded.ts/passthrough.ts/proxy.ts, appending to X-Forwarded-For and stripping the header before the API hop) plus its own tests. No leak, no leftover default export anywhere.

[OK] Regression tests pin real behavior, reasoned against old code (not reverted, per instructions):
  - 'gives a caller rotating the client-IP header no fresh buckets': old clientKey() reads x-wallow-client-ip directly, so the two different header values in the test hash to two different keys -> both requests would 204 under old code. New assertion (second=429) FAILS old code. Real regression pin.
  - 'ignores a client-IP header the caller sent': old code stamps clientIp straight from the header ('203.0.113.7'), test expects undefined -> FAILS old code.
  - 'prefers the host address over a header claiming another': clientAddress is a new option old code does not read at all; old code would stamp the header's value (203.0.113.7), test expects the hostPeer value (198.51.100.4) -> FAILS old code.
  All three are load-bearing, not vacuous.

[FINDING, non-blocking] request.ip is NOT proxy-aware anywhere in this stack, which weakens the 'per-client fairness' half of the claim (the security half is unaffected). Verified against srvx 0.11.22 source (_trust-proxy.mjs, adapters/node.mjs): request.ip only reads x-forwarded-for when server.options.trustProxy is set; otherwise it is the raw socket remoteAddress. Grepped every app/compose file: trustProxy/TRUST_PROXY is configured NOWHERE (not in vite.config.ts, not in nitro's node-server.mjs preset call to srvx's serve(), not as an env var in either compose file). Confirmed nitro's built node-server.mjs passes serve({port, hostname, tls, fetch, plugins}) with no trustProxy. Consequence: behind docker/caddy/Caddyfile.example in production, request.ip on every request to wallow-web/wallow-auth is Caddy's own container address for EVERY real user -- not the real client. This is not a NEW regression from this bead: the browser's log.ts never sent x-wallow-client-ip either, so under the OLD code every legitimate production caller already fell into the single UNKNOWN_CLIENT bucket (only an attacker deliberately setting the header got individual treatment -- and unlimited rotation). The NEW code makes legitimate and adversarial traffic share one real (unspoofable) bucket instead -- strictly closes the bypass, does not reopen anything -- but the bead's secondary-benefit claim ('a host-supplied peer address keys beacons correctly') and the existing bff.server.ts doc comment claiming request.ip already 'fixes' per-client rate limiting are both optimistic in the actual multi-hop production topology. This is a pre-existing gap (same pattern already shipped in bff.server.ts/api-passthrough.server.ts for the outbound CLIENT_IP_HEADER hop, Wallow-tt5j/Wallow-vufu.4.2) that this bead inherits rather than introduces. Worth its own follow-up bead (wire srvx's trustProxy to the Caddy container's known compose-network address) but does not block this fix landing.

[OK] Charter intact: dependencies={}, peerDependencies={} in package.json, charter.test.ts untouched (no diff), packages/logger build clean (vite build && tsc), 7 files/156 tests pass (ran myself, matches implementer's report exactly). No stray console.log/debugger/TODO/.only/.skip anywhere in the diff.

[OK] Prose (CLAUDE.md, docs/development/logging.md) matches the new code; no surviving clientIpHeader/DEFAULT_CLIENT_IP_HEADER reference anywhere outside history/plan docs and the SDK's own (unrelated, correctly-scoped) CLIENT_IP_HEADER.

verdict=CLOSE. The trustProxy gap is real and worth a follow-up bead, but it is pre-existing, does not reopen the vulnerability this bead closes, and is out of this bead's stated scope.

title: Make the fork's repository/docs URLs settable per environment
description:
`forkRepositoryUrl` / `forkDocsUrl` (packages/styles, added in Wallow-gqfh.8) resolve from
`branding.json` at BUILD time with an upstream constant as the fallback. A fork that runs one
image against several environments (staging docs vs production docs, a private mirror vs the
public repo) cannot change them without rebuilding.

WANTED: the two links settable from the environment, resolved per request, easy to set.

## Why the obvious shapes are wrong

- `import.meta.env.VITE_*` inside packages/styles is WRONG TWICE. The package ships a prebuilt
  `dist/`, so a bundler substitution there bakes the LIBRARY's build env, not the consuming app's
  — the same trap already documented for BASE_PATH (packages/styles/CLAUDE.md: "a base path is an
  argument here, never a read"). And a `VITE_*` value is frozen into the client bundle at app
  build time, while the Docker image is built once and run in several environments.
- packages/env cannot read them either. Its charter is "it reads no environment of its own"
  (`src/charter.test.ts` asserts no `process.env`, no `import.meta.env`, no `import` statement in
  every shipped module) — `resolveInternalOrigin` takes the env record as a PARAMETER.

## Shape to build

1. packages/styles gains a PURE resolver — `resolveForkLinks(env: Record<string, string |
   undefined>)` — returning `{ repositoryUrl, docsUrl }`. Precedence: env var, then
   `branding.json`, then the existing `UPSTREAM_*` constant. No env read of its own; the current
   module-level `forkRepositoryUrl` / `forkDocsUrl` stay as the zero-argument defaults.
2. wallow-web calls it from `src/app/start.ts`'s server-only global middleware — the channel that
   already exists for exactly this (it reads `process.env` inside the server callback and pushes
   values into the start context, which `getRouter()` lifts into router context). wallow-auth
   needs the same if its screens link out.
3. Screens read the links off router context, NOT the module constants. Keep the constants as the
   fallback so `PublicLayout` / `LandingPage` specs and Storybook — which render with no router —
   keep working unchanged.

Name the two variables in `docker/.env.example`, the production compose env file, and
`docs/getting-started/configuration.md`. Suggested: `WALLOW_REPOSITORY_URL` /
`WALLOW_DOCS_URL`.

Acceptance: setting the env var changes the rendered href with no rebuild; unset falls back to
`branding.json`; neither set falls back to the upstream constant; specs that render without a
router still get a link.

title: scripts/e2e.sh reuses a stale app image, so a run can silently test old code
description:
scripts/e2e.sh brings the stack up with `docker compose up -d --wait wallow-api wallow-web`.
Compose builds a service's image only when one is ABSENT, so any wallow-web-react:test /
wallow-auth-react:test image left over from an earlier run is reused verbatim — no matter how
far the working tree has moved since.

Observed: after the packages/navigation extraction, the wallow-web suites were about to be run
against an image built two days earlier, i.e. against the pre-extraction app. The image build
had in fact been BROKEN that whole time (missing packages/config COPY, missing
tsconfig.build.base.json — fixed separately), and nothing surfaced it, because a run that
reuses a stale image never builds.

The failure mode is the dangerous kind: green E2E that proves nothing about the code under
test. It is also invisible in CI-shaped runs, where E2E_SKIP_IMAGE_BUILD=1 makes reuse the
intended behaviour for the .NET images.

Fix direction (pick one, the first is closest to how the script already reasons):
  - Always `up -d --wait --build` for the two services that HAVE a build block (wallow-web,
    wallow-auth). Docker layer caching makes a no-change rebuild cheap; a changed source tree
    rebuilds, which is the point. E2E_SKIP_IMAGE_BUILD already exists for the .NET images and
    could gain the same meaning here for a caller who really wants reuse.
  - Or fingerprint the build context (git rev-parse HEAD plus `git status --porcelain` over
    apps/ and packages/) into an image label, and rebuild when it differs.

Acceptance:
  - A run whose working tree changed since the last run drives an image built from that tree.
  - A repeat run with no changes does not pay a full rebuild (layer cache hit).
  - .claude/rules/E2E.md states which env knob, if any, still opts into reuse.
notes:
FIXED 2026-08-27. Took fix direction one (always --build), as docs/plans/2026-08-27/1127-backlog-triage-and-sequencing.md Step 2 chose.

CHANGE. scripts/e2e.sh now assembles the up invocation as an array and adds --build unless E2E_SKIP_IMAGE_BUILD is set:

    UP_ARGS=(up -d --wait)
    if [[ -z "${E2E_SKIP_IMAGE_BUILD:-}" ]]; then
      UP_ARGS+=(--build)
    fi
    UP_ARGS+=("$UP_SERVICE" wallow-web bff-example)

An array rather than a bare flag string so the empty case is never an unquoted expansion under set -u. The guard is the same [[ -z ]] shape the dotnet-publish block at :82 already uses, so both halves of the knob agree on set-but-empty.

SCOPE IS WIDER THAN THE BEAD ASSUMED. The bead says 'the two services that HAVE a build block (wallow-web, wallow-auth)'. There are actually FOUR: garage, wallow-auth, wallow-web and bff-example (docker-compose.test.yml:62,203,251,316). --build reaches every one in the up set, so garage - which had the identical stale-reuse exposure and was not mentioned in the bead - is covered too.

E2E_SKIP_IMAGE_BUILD REDEFINED, per the bead's suggestion, from 'skip the dotnet publish' to 'reuse whatever :test images exist, build none of them'. This is load-bearing for CI: .github/workflows/ci.yml's docker-images-app job preloads wallow-api, wallow-auth-react, wallow-web-react, wallow-migrations and wallow-seeder from cache and the e2e job sets E2E_SKIP_IMAGE_BUILD=1, so without gating, --build would rebuild exactly what CI just restored. Verified the CI invocation is byte-identical to before:

  unset            -> up -d --wait --build wallow-api  wallow-web bff-example
  =1 (CI)          -> up -d --wait         wallow-auth wallow-web bff-example
  set-but-empty    -> up -d --wait --build wallow-api  wallow-web bff-example

bff-example is the one image no CI job caches, so compose builds it either way - unchanged.

ACCEPTANCE, MEASURED (docker 29.5.0, compose build of wallow-web, --progress plain):

1. 'A run whose working tree changed drives an image built from that tree.' CONFIRMED. Appended one line to apps/wallow-web/src/app/routes/__root.tsx: '#38 COPY apps/wallow-web apps/wallow-web  DONE 0.1s' (cache invalidated) and '#39 RUN pnpm --filter ./packages/* build && pnpm --filter @bc-solutions-coder/wallow-web build  DONE 6.2s' (re-ran). Total 8s. Source restored, tree clean.
2. 'A repeat run with no changes does not pay a full rebuild.' CONFIRMED, and stronger than 'not full': the same two layers report CACHED and the whole build takes 0s. Cold build for reference was 43s.
3. '.claude/rules/E2E.md states which env knob opts into reuse.' DONE - new paragraph naming E2E_SKIP_IMAGE_BUILD=1 as the single opt-in and warning not to set it merely to speed a local run.

NOTE ON A BAD ORACLE, so nobody repeats it: image ID is NOT a valid check here. BuildKit resolves a provenance attestation on every build, so wallow-web-react:test got a fresh ID (c91760260085 -> 834cf59230e4 -> ab9406cd92ed) across three builds INCLUDING ones where every layer was cached. Read CACHED vs DONE on the layers instead.

Also proved the flag combination works for real rather than only parsing: 'up -d --wait --build garage' built wallow-garage:test (absent beforehand - only wallow-garage:v2.2.0 existed), started it, blocked to Healthy, EXIT=0.

Docs updated: .claude/rules/E2E.md, docs/development/testing-e2e.md (knob table + usage), docs/development/testing.md (the CI paragraph), apps/wallow-web/e2e/CLAUDE.md.

Gates: bash -n, format:check, lint, lint:env all pass. No TS/JS source changed, so build/typecheck/test are unaffected.

title: Collapse the 7-point module registration footgun to assembly-attribute discovery
description:
Today a new module must be registered in 7 places outside itself (doc section 3):
Wallow.slnx; Wallow.Api.csproj:106-121 (ProjectReference to BOTH .Api and .Infrastructure,
because controller discovery is a referenced-assembly scan and there is no AddApplicationPart
anywhere in api/src); WallowModules.cs (three edits — AddXModule, InitializeXModuleAsync,
MigrateIfRegistered<XDbContext>); appsettings{,.Development,.Production}.json FeatureManagement
.Modules.X; MigrationService/Program.cs (AddDbContext + DbContextMigrationRunner); the test
project + scripts/run-tests.sh:22-36 shorthand; and HARDCODED module lists in the architecture
tests.

## The hardcoded lists — SIX, not four (citations corrected by Wallow-af3h.8)

All six re-verified 2026-08-04 by reading the files. This bead previously said "at least FOUR",
gave one of them the wrong project, and mischaracterised another. The corrected inventory:

**FIVE hardcoded MODULE-NAME lists**

1. `api/tests/Wallow.MigrationService.Tests/MigrationServiceTests.cs:189` — `featureModules`
   inside `GetFirstFeatureModuleIndex()`. **Note the project.** This bead previously cited it as
   `Wallow.Architecture.Tests/MigrationServiceTests.cs`; there is no such file. The line number
   189 was correct all along, only the project was wrong.
2. `api/tests/Wallow.Architecture.Tests/ModuleRegistrationTests.cs:37-41` — `modulesWithDbContext
   = ["Notifications", "Announcements", "Identity", "Storage"]` in
   `WallowModules_ShouldInitialize_AllModulesWithDbContext`. Already silently stale: ApiKeys,
   Inquiries and Branding all own DbContexts and are all outside the assertion, and the test is
   green.
3. `ModuleRegistrationTests.cs:66-69` — the four `[InlineData]` rows on
   `Module_ShouldProvide_AddModuleExtensionMethod` (same four names).
4. `ModuleRegistrationTests.cs:98-101` — the four `[InlineData]` rows on
   `Module_ShouldProvide_InitializeModuleExtensionMethod` (same four names).
5. `api/tests/Wallow.Architecture.Tests/Modules/ModuleToggleTests.cs:24-28,51-55` — the in-memory
   `FeatureManagement:Modules.*` configuration blocks in `DisabledModule_ShouldNotRegister_Services`
   and `AllModulesEnabled_ShouldRegister_AllModules`, five keys each; ApiKeys and Branding absent
   from both. **Cite these by test-method name, not line number** — as of this edit there is
   uncommitted work in the tree (another Wallow-af3h bead) that renames the first method to
   `CoreModule_ShouldStillRegister_WhenFeatureFlagDisabled`, inserts a third flag block, and pushes
   the second block from `:51-55` to `:74-78`. The `:24-28,51-55` numbers are correct at commit
   bdd26027 and will drift the moment that work lands.

**ONE hardcoded FILE-PATH list, which needs a DIFFERENT fix**

6. `api/tests/Wallow.Architecture.Tests/MigrationRemovalTests.cs:9-18` — `_moduleExtensionFiles`
   is **not** a module list. It is seven paths to `*ModuleExtensions.cs`, consumed by
   `File.ReadAllText` at `:37` and `:49` to regex source text. That is a
   `.claude/rules/TESTING.md` violation ("no readFileSync over src/") and the rule's own guidance
   is to prefer deleting the constraint over relocating it. **The correct action is DELETE the
   suite, not derive its list.** This bead previously listed it as a module list to derive.

`TestConstants.AllModules` is derived from the `api/src/Modules/` directory and is NOT one of the
six.

**Ownership is UNRESOLVED.** Lists 3 and 4 are named by NEITHER this bead NOR `Wallow-vmns.7`,
so nothing owns them today. Lists 2 and 5 are claimed by BOTH. That scope collision between this
bead and `Wallow-vmns.7` is deliberately NOT decided here — settle it before either bead starts.

Model: ardalis/modulith's Modulith.Web/ModuleRegistrationExtensions.cs reflects over solution
assemblies, finds each module's registrar, and invokes it — DI needs no wiring at all.

Wallow's equivalent is an assembly-level attribute per module (name, DbContext type, feature-flag
key) that the host discovers, so AddXModule/InitializeXModuleAsync/MigrateIfRegistered and the
migration runner all resolve from one declaration.

Non-goals: the .slnx entry and the ProjectReference stay manual (they are what makes the assembly
discoverable at all). Getting 7 down to 2 is the win.
acceptance_criteria: Adding a module requires editing only Wallow.slnx and Wallow.Api.csproj. WallowModules.cs has no per-module code. MigrationService discovers contexts. Every hardcoded module list this bead ends up owning derives its list instead of hardcoding it — CITATIONS CORRECTED by Wallow-af3h.8: api/tests/Wallow.MigrationService.Tests/MigrationServiceTests.cs:189 (the project is Wallow.MigrationService.Tests, NOT Wallow.Architecture.Tests as this criterion previously said; line 189 was correct), api/tests/Wallow.Architecture.Tests/ModuleRegistrationTests.cs:37-41, and Modules/ModuleToggleTests.cs:24-28,51-55. title: Scaffolding & fork ergonomics — delete the module footgun, then skill it
description:
Adding a module to Wallow is 7 host touch points by hand, every time. Prior art says
fix the host before writing a scaffolding skill: fullstackhero's add-module skill exists only
because its host has a four-place registration footgun, while ardalis/modulith deleted the
footgun with assembly reflection instead of documenting it.

Research doc: `docs/plans/2026-07-31/2134-mit-prior-art-harvest.md` (local, gitignored). Read the cited section before starting.
Prior art is platformplatform/PlatformPlatform (MIT) — copying source is fine with the
original copyright notice retained on any file copied substantially. Sections 3 and 7.

This epic has NO dependency on the multi-org membership plan. It is the one to start.

## Briefing every child needs

1. The 7 touch points are enumerated in doc section 3, with file:line for each.
2. ApiKeys is the smallest complete module (4 projects, 20 files) and is the reference to copy.
3. Wallow already has most of the thing that makes scaffolding trustworthy: 10 architecture-test
   suites under api/tests/Wallow.Architecture.Tests/ (ModuleIsolationTests,
   ModuleRegistrationTests, CleanArchitectureTests, CqrsConventionTests,
   WolverineConventionTests, and six more). Extend those rather than trusting a skill checklist.
   But TWO of the ten do not actually judge a new module with zero edits — they hardcode a
   per-module list and pass green while asserting nothing about a module absent from it:
   ModuleRegistrationTests.cs:37-41 (whose list already omits ApiKeys and Inquiries, both of
   which have DbContexts) and Modules/ModuleToggleTests.cs:24-28,51-55. Treat the "zero edits"
   claim as true of eight suites, not ten, until those two derive their lists.
4. Deployment status says breaking main is free. Take it — do not carry the footgun forward.
acceptance_criteria: A new module can be added without editing WallowModules.cs. AND every skill this epic still owns exists and has been run once end-to-end: the four in Wallow-vmns.2 (add-module, add-feature, add-integration-event, create-migration) PLUS add-frontend-slice in Wallow-vmns.3. That is FIVE — this criterion previously said "the four skills", which its own child .3 falsifies. Wallow-vmns.6 (pull-upstream-wallow) is DEFERRED and sits outside these criteria until its reopen trigger fires; the docs restructure and the fork-config isolation audit have been reparented out of this epic and are not covered here either.

title: S4 — packages/navigation
description:
Scaffold `@bc-solutions-coder/navigation` and migrate wallow-web onto it. The largest slice.

## Manifest — RECONCILED, no longer open

Derived by reading the actual imports of the five moving modules, not by preferring a document.
The design doc was right on every disputed point; the older slice plan was wrong on every one.

```jsonc
"dependencies":     { "@bc-solutions-coder/ui": "workspace:*", "lucide-react": "^0.5xx.x" },
"peerDependencies": { "react": "catalog:react", "react-dom": "catalog:react",
                      "@tanstack/react-router": "^1.170.18", "zustand": "catalog:react" },
"devDependencies":  { /* the four peers again, at the same ranges */ }
```

- `ui` — four per-component subpath imports: `/error-banner`, `/navigation-menu`, `/theme-toggle`,
  `/button`.
- `lucide-react` — `nav-icons.ts` imports eight named icons. Its header documents why that library:
  per-icon ES exports, no icon font, no runtime deps, peers React 19.
- `@tanstack/react-router` — `Link`/`LinkProps` in `DashboardNav`, `Outlet` in `DashboardLayout`.
  A LITERAL `^1.170.18`, not `catalog:start`: a library peering a caret range against an app
  pinning exactly is correct practice.
- **NO `@bc-solutions-coder/styles` edge.** Nothing in the five modules imports it; `ui` already
  depends on it and the tokens arrive as CSS through the app's stylesheet.
- **NO `@bc-solutions-coder/utils` edge.** Nothing calls anything utils-shaped. Add one only if
  the migration turns up a real call site.
- **NO `auth` edge** — the visibility predicate is an app-supplied `can()` prop.
- **NO `sdk` edge — but the code has one TODAY.** `DashboardNav.tsx:1` imports `logout` from
  `@bc-solutions-coder/sdk`. The "logout control is a footer slot" decision is what DELETES that
  import. This is a migration task, not a declared dependency. An implementer who reads the import
  and adds `sdk` to the manifest has silently reversed a decision.

## Content

1. **`ui-store.ts` moves wholesale as `useNavStore`** — decided, not open. All five members
   (`isNavCollapsed`, `toggleNavCollapsed`, `isMobileNavOpen`, `openMobileNav`, `closeMobileNav`)
   are navigation state and every consumer is `DashboardNav`, `DashboardLayout` or one of their
   nine specs. There is no non-navigation part to leave behind.
   - **Carry the `TWO AXES, NOT ONE` comment across VERBATIM**: `isNavCollapsed` is the desktop
     rail, `isMobileNavOpen` is the mobile drawer, and neither may be derived from the other. That
     comment records a real regression, not a preference.
   - The store is a module-global singleton. Two resolved copies means two stores and a nav that
     silently desyncs — the same hazard class `@bc-solutions-coder/query` exists to solve for
     `QueryClient`. Hence `zustand` as a PEER, and export the store from exactly ONE entry, never
     duplicated across subpaths.
   - Move `ui-store.test.ts`'s re-import identity case with it, strengthened to assert identity
     across a PACKAGE import rather than a relative one.
   - **`apps/wallow-web/src/shared/stores/` is DELETED** — no pass-through re-export, no empty
     store. A shim that exists only to preserve an import path is what a fork inherits and never
     removes.
2. Move `DashboardNav.tsx`, `DashboardLayout.tsx`, `nav-icons.ts`, `use-is-desktop.ts` and their
   specs. `use-is-desktop`'s only two consumers are the two components, so it rides along.
   **Preserve the module-graph hazard documented atop `DashboardNav.tsx`**: it imports
   `@bc-solutions-coder/ui` by per-component subpath, NOT the root barrel, because a spec stubs
   `@tanstack/react-router` down to `Link` and the barrel drags in `FocusOnNavigate` ->
   `useRouterState`, which the stub cannot satisfy. Keep that comment with the code.
3. Testids derive from `testIdPrefix` + `id`, defaulting to `"dashboard"` — this reproduces
   `dashboard-nav-organizations`, `dashboard-nav-drawer` and `dashboard-logout-link` EXACTLY, so
   the E2E specs and the seven `__screenshots__` suites do not churn.
4. Preserve all three modes and `data-nav-open`, including the collapsed rail's icon-only
   rendering with the label moved to `aria-label`.
5. **`shared/` allowlist**: `stores` AND `testing` both empty out across this epic. Drop them from
   the allowlist in `packages/lint/src/rules/zone-dag.ts`, with a fixture, in the change that
   empties them — or the rule goes stale in the PERMISSIVE direction.
6. **SSR hazard**: `use-sync-external-store/shim` can load a second React during SSR and break
   every zustand-backed component. Both apps already alias around it; a fork consuming this
   package will need the same and will not know that. Document the required `resolve.alias`
   entries in `packages/navigation/CLAUDE.md`, and add an SSR spec that `renderToString`s the
   shell — that failure is SILENT (empty document, client-only fallback), so it needs a test.
7. Testing: stories are the render coverage (one per mode, per the `packages/ui` pattern); a
   co-located spec covers behavioural edges stories cannot express (Escape dismissal, `can()`
   gating dropping the whole `<li>`, collapsed-mode `aria-label`); plus the SSR spec.

**Out of scope**: `PublicLayout` stays in wallow-web and `auth-layout.tsx` stays in wallow-auth.
Folding them in is the over-reach that made the deleted `web-shell` a grab-bag.

## Acceptance
Epic acceptance criteria, plus **E2E**: `./scripts/e2e.sh` runs all three Playwright suites
against the containerised stack and comes back clean. The testid and screenshot constraints exist
precisely so it does. A churned screenshot baseline means step 3 was not honoured.
notes:
E2E verification (the outstanding gate) — DONE, and it turned up a separate pre-existing defect.

Both wallow-web Playwright suites pass against a containerised stack built from this branch:
  - e2e/routes.spec.ts .................. 2 passed (renders / and /bff-demo)
  - e2e-cross-app/login-journey.spec.ts . 2 passed (full OIDC journey + authenticated
    mutation + logout through the extracted shell's footer slot)
No screenshot baseline churn, so the testid derivation held byte-identical.

Blocker found on the way, now fixed here: `docker compose build wallow-web` had been broken
since packages/config landed. Neither app's Dockerfile copied packages/config (or
packages/lint), and both were missing the root tsconfig.build.base.json, so the image build
died in the PACKAGE build step with `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND: Cannot find package
'@bc-solutions-coder/config' imported from .../.vite-temp/vite.config.ts.timestamp-*.mjs`
and then `error TS5083: Cannot read file '/repo/tsconfig.build.base.json'`. It stayed hidden
because scripts/e2e.sh only builds an app image when one is ABSENT — the stale 07-29 image was
reused, so every prior run drove pre-extraction code.

Fix, applied to BOTH apps:
  - Dockerfile: COPY packages/config + packages/lint (manifest and source lines), and add
    tsconfig.build.base.json to the root COPY.
  - src/docker-workspace-copies.test.ts: the guard read only `dependencies`, which is exactly
    why config (a devDependency, and a real build input via every package's vite.config.ts)
    slipped through. It now scans dependencies + devDependencies, and its vacuity guard names
    `config` so a regression to deps-only fails.

wallow-auth E2E: 4 failures, all pre-existing and unrelated — every Mailpit spec times out
because no mail is ever sent. Root cause is in the API logs, not the frontend:
`Wolverine.Configuration.InvalidServiceLocationException: Found service locations while
generating code for Message Handler for SendEmailCommand, but ServiceLocationPolicy.NotAllowed
is in effect`. Already filed as Wallow-0tor (P0). Because scripts/e2e.sh runs the three suites
sequentially with no error tolerance, that failure is what stopped the wallow-web suites from
running in the first place.

Two acceptance items did not apply and were deliberately NOT done:
  - "Drop stores/testing from the shared/ allowlist in packages/lint/src/rules/zone-dag.ts" —
    no such allowlist exists. zone-dag derives its zones from each app's tsconfig.json
    compilerOptions.paths (readApp -> commonDirectory -> zoneOf); there is no hardcoded
    subdirectory list, so emptying shared/stores cannot make the rule stale.
  - "stories are the render coverage, per the packages/ui pattern" — no Storybook added.
    ui needs stories because only its `storybook` vitest project loads Tailwind + the fork
    theme; packages/navigation gives its BROWSER project both (wallowStyles() +
    vitest.setup.ts), so a second Storybook instance would measure nothing the 17 spec files
    do not already measure. Reasoning is written into packages/navigation/CLAUDE.md.
pnpm check exits 0 after the Dockerfile + guard fixes: format:check, lint, lint:tests, typecheck, build, check:exports all clean; every suite green — packages/navigation 17 files, apps/wallow-web 84, apps/wallow-auth 62, packages/ui 120, packages/sdk 40.

title: S0 — delete style-contract.ts and convert its 12 consumers
description:
Delete `apps/wallow-web/src/shared/testing/style-contract.ts` (288 lines, 12 consuming specs) and
convert its consumers to computed-value assertions.

**Why deleted and not rehomed.** `.claude/rules/TESTING.md` names this file directly as a
delete-on-sight pattern: "any `it()` whose body only reads `element.classList` (the
`shared/testing/style-contract.ts` helpers): a component can render the right classes and be
broken, or restyle correctly with different classes and fail. Assert the computed value, never
the class string — `cn()` merges a caller's `className` over the recipe." Moving it into
`packages/testing` would promote a banned pattern into shared API and hand it to every fork.

Each of the 12 consumers resolves one of three ways:
- Assert the COMPUTED value instead (`getComputedStyle`, normalised through a canvas for colours —
  the fork palette is oklch and Chromium may serialize `oklch()`/`color()`).
- Delete the assertion where a `wallow/*` lint rule already says it by construction
  (`no-tinted-text`, `no-sidebar-inversion`, `text-heading-variant`).
- Delete the whole `it()` where it only asserted that a migration happened.

Also in scope: delete the untracked `apps/wallow-web/src/routes/` and `apps/wallow-auth/src/routes/`
directories. Both are orphaned `__screenshots__` baselines left behind when `src` moved into zones
(`git ls-files` returns 0 for both); the live baselines are under `src/app/routes/__screenshots__/`.
They poison every source grep, as does each app's `.output/`.

Biggest single reduction of `shared/` in the epic, and it blocks nothing — run it first.

## Acceptance
- `style-contract.ts` gone; no file imports it.
- `pnpm test` green in both apps; `pnpm lint` and `pnpm lint:tests` pass.
- No new `classList` assertion introduced anywhere.
- Both untracked `src/routes/` dirs gone.
notes:
S0 DONE. pnpm check EXIT=0; wallow-web 779 tests / 99 files pass.

The file was far less load-bearing than its 288 lines suggested: only 8 of 24 exports had a
consumer. The 16 dead ones (every recipe constant, expectBadge, expectListCard, expectListRow,
expectEmptyState, expectTokenColorsOnly, expectPrecedes) plus expectPageContainer -- which had
ZERO call sites, only doc-comment mentions -- were simply deleted.

Of the 8 live exports, 6 are LOCATOR helpers, not classList assertions: byTestId (39 uses),
waitForTestId (26), allByTestId (14), within (6), expectTag (6), parentOf (5). TESTING.md's ban
is on classList assertions, which these are not, so they survive as
apps/wallow-web/src/shared/testing/locators.ts. That file is S5's input -- which is exactly why
S5 depends on S0. Design doc S5 row updated to name it.

Only 4 banned call sites existed: expectClasses x3 and a locally-defined expectNoClasses.
Converted to measured assertions (probe element + effectiveBackground/textContrast for colour,
getBoundingClientRect for footprint, getComputedStyle for radius/decoration/alignment, a
transition-aware poll for hover).

Two things the class-string assertions were hiding, both found by converting:

1. The old spec asserted 'inline-flex' was in the CTA's class list and passed. The element
   computes display:flex -- a flex item's inline-flex is BLOCKIFIED by CSS. Class present,
   computed value different: the exact failure mode TESTING.md describes.
2. Measuring the CTA's resting fill initially read hover:bg-primary/90, because the pointer was
   still parked on the CTA from the earlier click cases. renderPage() now parks the mouse after
   every render. A classList assertion is blind to this by construction.

One config change: apps/wallow-web/.oxlintrc.json test/story override gains
unicorn/prefer-number-coercion: off. Number('1px') is NaN, so parseFloat is the only correct
reader of a computed length; packages/ui already carries this override for the same reason and
documents the rationale in its CLAUDE.md. wallow-web measures computed lengths for the first
time here.

Also deleted: both untracked apps/*/src/routes/ orphan __screenshots__ trees (47 PNGs, 0 tracked
files). Stale comments in page-container.ts and page-shell.test.ts that cited the deleted
expectPageContainer were removed.

title: S1 — packages/utils
description:
Scaffold `@bc-solutions-coder/utils` — the bottom of the dependency graph and zero-risk, which is
why it goes first: it proves the new-package pipeline (manifest, exports map, build,
`check:exports`, workspace link, Dockerfile COPY lines) before a slice with real behaviour rides
on it.

Model the manifest on `packages/query` (the smallest existing package).

**Five subpaths, and the names are public API — DO NOT RENAME:**
`./format`, `./string`, `./array`, `./result`, `./guards`.

**Machine-enforce the charter** — this is the whole reason a generic utility package is allowed
to exist at all:
- a spec asserting `dependencies` and `peerDependencies` are both empty;
- `"lib": ["ESNext"]` and `"types": []` in its tsconfig, so a DOM or Node API will not compile;
- an oxlint override banning `react`, `react-dom`, `zustand` and `@bc-solutions-coder/*` under
  `packages/utils/**` — and, because an oxlint `overrides` entry REPLACES the root rule's options
  rather than merging them, re-declaring the root's `no-restricted-imports` bans;
- an export-coverage spec diffing the exports map against the source tree.

**Seed each subpath from something that already exists in the apps, not from imagination.**

## Acceptance
Epic acceptance criteria, plus: the four charter guards above exist and fail when violated.
notes:
S1 DONE — commit bc7c5c73. `pnpm check` EXIT=0.

SCOPE CHANGE, user-approved. The bead names five subpaths as public API AND says
"seed each subpath from something that already exists in the apps, not from
imagination." Those two contradict each other for ./array and ./result. Survey
of both apps found:

  ./guards  readScalar (login.tsx) + scalarToWireString (logout.tsx) — identical
            logic under two names; plus 3 inline `typeof x === "string" ? x : undefined`
            sites (login.tsx x3, auth-result.ts, MemberList.tsx). STRONG.
  ./format  formatGraceDeadline (LoginScreen.tsx). The ONLY toLocale*/Intl call
            site in the entire workspace.
  ./string  providerTestId's slug pipeline (ExternalProviders.tsx). The only
            other candidate, `kebab` in packages/forms/src/core/test-id.ts, is a
            private one-liner in a package, not an app — left alone.
  ./array   NOTHING.
  ./result  NOTHING generic. The `kind:` unions that exist (auth-result.ts,
            zone-dag.ts) are domain vocabulary, not Result<T,E>.

User chose: ship the three with seeds, leave ./array and ./result unbuilt until
a consumer needs them. Adding a subpath later is additive, not breaking.

EXPORTED (every one extracted, call sites rewired in the same commit):
  ./guards  asString, scalarToString
  ./format  formatLongDate
  ./string  toSlug

FOUR CHARTER GUARDS — all four verified to fail when violated, not assumed:
  1. deps/peerDeps both {} — added `"lodash"`, spec failed.
  2. tsconfig.json lib ["ESNext"] + types [] — `import "node:fs"` in src gave
     TS2591, `document.title` gave TS2584. Flipping types to ["node"] failed the
     spec.
  3. root .oxlintrc.json override on packages/utils/src/**/*.ts — probe file
     importing react + zustand + @bc-solutions-coder/ui produced 3 oxlint errors.
  4. export-coverage — an orphan src/*.ts failed 6 cases at once.

TWO TSCONFIGS, deliberate. tsconfig.json is the strict charter one and covers
shipped source only. tsconfig.node.json covers the specs (they read the manifest
off disk) and vite.config.ts (reaches @bc-solutions-coder/config, which imports
node:url). `typecheck` runs BOTH. Neither excluded file is in `exports`.

COLLATERAL — packages/sdk/src/oxlint-guardrails.test.ts. Its facadeExemption()
helper selected the facade override by SHAPE: "the only override that re-declares
no-restricted-imports". The utils charter override is now a second one, so that
premise is dead. Rewrote it to select by files, and added a new case pinning the
FULL set of re-declaring overrides to exactly the two legitimate ones (facade
exemption, utils charter) — which preserves the original tripwire and names both.
Anyone adding a third re-declaring override must add it there.

ALSO WIRED: both apps' package.json + Dockerfile COPY lines, scripts/check-exports.sh
(publint + attw both green on all three subpaths), root CLAUDE.md layout table,
apps/CLAUDE.md package list, packages/utils/CLAUDE.md.

FLAKE, not a regression: wallow-web's CreateInquiryForm.forms.test.tsx timed out
on one click during the first full run after the lockfile changed — Vite was
re-optimizing deps while two browser projects ran in parallel. Passes in
isolation and on the clean re-run.

title: Shared package extraction v2 — utils, env, logger, navigation, rehomes
description:
Extract shared packages so a fork inherits them instead of re-deriving them, and rehome the
tail of helpers that belong in an existing package rather than in an app's `shared/` zone.

**Design doc:** `docs/plans/2026-07-31/1933-shared-packages-extraction-v2.md` (local, gitignored).
Read it before claiming any child. It SUPERSEDES `docs/plans/2026-07-30/1347-shared-packages-extraction.md`,
whose premises about `aliases.ts`, `zone-dag.test.ts` and `packages/config` are all false now.

## Briefing every child needs

1. Both apps are three-zone: `src/app/`, `src/features/<name>/` (each with an `index.ts` barrel),
   `src/shared/` (`components`, `lib`, `stores`, `testing`, `types`). Root-level `src/*.test.ts(x)`
   are app-wide policy specs.
2. Cross-zone imports use `@app/*`, `@features/<name>`, `@shared/*`, declared ONCE in each app's
   `tsconfig.json` `paths`. There is no `aliases.ts` and there never was.
3. The import DAG is the `wallow/zone-dag` oxlint rule in `packages/lint`, NOT a spec. Its
   `shared/` subdirectory allowlist is in `packages/lint/src/rules/zone-dag.ts`, proven by
   `packages/lint/fixtures/zone-dag/`. Editing it is a rule + fixture change.
4. Version pins come from pnpm catalogs, never literals: `catalog:react`, `catalog:start`,
   `catalog:tooling`. Exception: a library PEERING on the router uses a literal caret range
   (`^1.170.18`) against the apps' exact pin. That is correct practice, not drift.
5. `.github/workflows/sdk-publish.yml` runs `pnpm publish --no-git-checks`, which resolves both
   `catalog:` and `workspace:*` at pack time.
6. A co-move leaves its specifier untouched: when both ends of a relative import move by the same
   amount, the specifier does not change. This shipped as a bug twice.
7. The vitest two-project split is keyed on file EXTENSION. A `.test.ts` can never run in Chromium;
   a browser spec must be `.test.tsx` and cannot use `node:fs`. A `.tsx` spec that renders through
   `react-dom/server` and never mounts a DOM is named `*.ssr.test.tsx`.
8. `packages/config` is the VITE PRESET package (`./vite/library`, `./vite/app`) — never built,
   never published, no relative imports between its modules, no app-shaped dependencies. The env
   package is `packages/env`. Do not confuse them.

## Acceptance criteria for every new package

- `pnpm --filter @bc-solutions-coder/<pkg> build` succeeds.
- The package is added to the `packages=(...)` array in `scripts/check-exports.sh` AND
  `pnpm check:exports` is clean. Without the array edit that check passes VACUOUSLY.
- No literal versions for anything the catalogs cover.
- `apps/*/src/docker-workspace-copies.test.ts` passes in both apps (two Dockerfile COPY lines per
  consuming app: manifest before `pnpm install`, sources before the build RUN).
- `pnpm lint` AND `pnpm lint:tests` pass. If `shared/`'s shape changed, the `packages/lint`
  fixture suite covers the new allowlist.
- `pnpm check` green from a clean install.
- Docs guide exists, is in `docs/toc.yml`, and the repo-map tables in `CLAUDE.md` and
  `apps/CLAUDE.md` name the package — including `packages/lint`, which is missing today.

## Serialization hazard

Every "wire into both apps" task edits the same four files: both apps' `package.json` and both
`Dockerfile`s. Every docs task edits `docs/toc.yml` plus the repo-map tables in `CLAUDE.md` and
`apps/CLAUDE.md`. Chain those tasks so exactly one runs at a time, even when parent features run
in parallel.

## Decisions — DO NOT REOPEN

- `packages/utils` subpaths are `./format`, `./string`, `./array`, `./result`, `./guards`.
  Subpaths are public API; a rename is breaking for forks.
- `packages/utils` has empty `dependencies` and `peerDependencies`, `"lib": ["ESNext"]`,
  `"types": []` — machine-enforced by a spec, not a convention.
- The env package is `packages/env`. `packages/config` is taken and cannot absorb it.
- `base-path.ts` goes to `packages/config` as `./base-path`, NOT to `packages/env`.
- `packages/navigation` deps: `@bc-solutions-coder/ui` + `lucide-react`; peers `react`,
  `react-dom`, `@tanstack/react-router` (`^1.170.18` literal), `zustand` (`catalog:react`).
  NO `styles`, NO `utils`, NO `auth`, NO `sdk` edge.
- `ui-store.ts` moves wholesale into `packages/navigation` as `useNavStore`. Carry the
  `TWO AXES, NOT ONE` comment verbatim — it records a real regression.
- `apps/wallow-web/src/shared/stores/` is DELETED with NO pass-through re-export.
- `zustand` is a peerDependency (and devDependency) at `catalog:react` — the store is a
  module-global singleton; two copies means two stores and a nav that silently desyncs.
- `DashboardNav` imports `@bc-solutions-coder/ui` by per-component SUBPATH, never the root
  barrel. Keep the explanatory comment with the code.
- Nav testids derive from `testIdPrefix` + `id`, defaulting to `"dashboard"`.
- `style-contract.ts` is DELETED, not moved.
- `site-links.ts` goes to `packages/styles` (this overrides the design doc, which said navigation).
- `SelectControl` is ABSORBED into `packages/ui`'s `Select`, not moved as a file.

## Still open

- `apps/examples/minimal-app` and `scripts/fork-smoke/` scope: do they take the new packages?
  `minimal-app` holds the THIRD copy of `request-origin.ts`, so S2 must decide it, not defer it.
notes:
CORRECTION to the epic decision list: 'base-path.ts goes to packages/config as ./base-path, NOT to packages/env' is REVERSED. base-path.ts goes to packages/env, as a dependency-free and side-effect-free ./base-path subpath. packages/config keeps its zero-runtime invariant and its CLAUDE.md needs no change. The subpath must carry no zod and no side effects: wallow-auth's vite.config.ts imports it at config load time in plain Node ESM, so a side-effectful import would make vite build fail on a missing runtime env var. See the S2b child.
All eight slices landed on main (S0 6 slices + S2b + S6). Final shape:
packages/utils, packages/env (./request-origin, ./internal-origin, ./base-path), packages/logger
(browser core + ./server ingest), packages/navigation, the testing consolidation, and the S6

title: Add wallow/zone-dag and retire both apps' zone-dag.test.ts
description: Retires apps/wallow-web/src/zone-dag.test.ts and its byte-identical wallow-auth twin — 748 lines across the two apps — onto one rule. BOTH FILES DELETE OUTRIGHT; nothing is carried over.
design:
Three blocks per file, none survives:
- describe('the zone walk itself') 263-280: deleted. It guards the sweep, and the sweep is going. Its fail-closed role passes to the harness's number_of_files assertion.
- describe('the import DAG') 282-355: retires onto the rule, all six assertions.
- describe('shared/') 357-374: deleted AS A POLICY CHANGE. shared/ is NO LONGER shape-locked to a fixed subdirectory list. Drop the assertion and the SHARED_SUBDIRS constant; do not port either to the rule. Do NOT confuse this with the DAG edge 'shared/ may not import a feature', which is about the DIRECTION of a dependency and stays as one of the rule's six checks.

Implementation: port zoneOf() (spec lines 194-204) and targetOf() (207-238) essentially verbatim — already correct TypeScript. Replace the disk sweep with visitors.
- App-root resolution: walk up from context.filename to the nearest dir with a tsconfig.json carrying compilerOptions.paths; cache per directory in createOnce. This is what makes the rule work in both apps with ZERO options — do not add an option for the src path. Strip // comments before JSON.parse (spec lines 52-63); tsconfig.json carries them and JSON.parse rejects them.
- Visitors: ImportDeclaration, ExportNamedDeclaration, ExportAllDeclaration, and ImportExpression. The spec's header calls dynamic import 'exactly how a module reaches something it may not reach at module scope' — a rule blind to it has a hole shaped like the violation it exists to catch. Only string-literal specifiers are judged, matching the spec.
- BARREL_ZONES: an option defaulting to ['features']. @features/login is the contract; @features/login/anything reaches around it.
- SPEC_MAY_REACH_APP: a spec may import @app/*, because mounting the real route is how a screen's contract is tested. Express this as a per-messageId exemption INSIDE the rule, NOT a config override — an override turning the rule off for **/*.test.tsx would also exempt specs from the other five checks, a widening the spec never granted.
- Zone 'root' (a policy spec directly under src/) is outside the product graph and reports nothing.
- routeTree.gen.ts is already in both apps' ignorePatterns so the rule never sees it. CONFIRM that rather than assuming — it is the difference between 'exempt' and 'silently unchecked'.
- One messageId per violation kind: relativeCrossZone, deepIntoFeature, siblingFeature, reachesBackIntoApp, sharedReachesFeature, escapesSrc. Each carries the guidance its corresponding spec assertion's comment carries today; those comments are the rule's documentation, do not paraphrase them away.

Fixtures need a directory tree the rule can read: fixtures/zone-dag/tsconfig.json declaring the three zone paths, plus src/app/routes/, src/features/login/, src/features/signup/, src/shared/. valid.tsx must exercise the boundary — a relative import WITHIN the zone and an aliased @shared/* — not merely avoid it.
acceptance_criteria: Fixtures green (write them and watch the harness fail BEFORE implementing). Then 'wallow/zone-dag': 'error' in both app configs and pnpm lint reports ZERO violations — both specs are green on main, so anything reported is either a rule bug or something the spec's regex MISSED. Investigate before suppressing; the second case is a real bug and is the entire argument for this migration. Then both spec files deleted and pnpm test green.
notes:
wallow/zone-dag written, enabled in both apps, and both 374-line specs deleted (748 lines retired). Commit 5b0fa89d.

WHAT WENT AS DESIGNED: zoneOf/targetOf ported essentially verbatim; app root resolved by walking up to the nearest tsconfig.json carrying compilerOptions.paths, memoised per directory across the process, so the rule takes ZERO options and nothing in it names src, a zone, or an app; all four specifier visitors (Import/ExportNamed/ExportAll/ImportExpression); six messageIds carrying the spec comments' guidance; describe('shared/') and SHARED_SUBDIRS dropped entirely per the policy reversal.

THE SPEC EXEMPTION IS PROVEN, NOT ASSUMED. A probe spec importing BOTH @app/router and @features/mfa/api reported the deep-into-feature and sibling-feature diagnostics and stayed SILENT on @app/router — which is exactly what a config override turning the rule off for **/*.test.tsx could not have done, and is the concrete argument for keeping the exemption inside the rule.

ZERO VIOLATIONS ACROSS BOTH APPS, and that was verified as a positive rather than read off an exit code: temp files planted in apps/wallow-web/src/features and apps/wallow-auth/src/shared drew relativeCrossZone, reachesBackIntoApp and sharedReachesFeature from the real gate before being deleted. So the clean run means the DAG holds, not that the rule no-op'd. No violation the old regex sweep had missed turned up.

Derivation detail worth keeping: srcDir is the longest common directory prefix of the tsconfig paths targets, not a hardcoded 'src'. Fixture tree therefore needs only its own tsconfig.json declaring the three zones.

Gates: pnpm lint clean, lint:tests 368 -> 366 files (the two deleted specs), fixture harness 3/3, wallow-web 777 tests in 99 files, wallow-auth 987 tests in 63 files.

FOR BEAD .9 — the residual doc references are WIDER than .9 currently lists. 'rg zone-dag.test' still hits: apps/CLAUDE.md (2), apps/wallow-web/tsconfig.json and apps/wallow-auth/tsconfig.json comments (1 each), docs/development/frontend-setup.md (3, incl. a directory-tree listing), apps/wallow-web/README.md (2). title: Build the on-disk fixture harness
description: One generic spec drives every rule. fixtures/<rule>/ holds valid.tsx (reports nothing) and invalid.tsx (every expected diagnostic marked by '// expect-error: wallow/<rule>' on the preceding line). The real oxlint binary runs once per fixture directory and the reported (file, line, rule) multiset must equal the annotated one EXACTLY — an unannotated diagnostic and an annotation nothing fired on BOTH fail.
design:
Full implementation is in the plan doc (Task 6) — its details are measured, not stylistic. Key points:
- fixtures/fixture.oxlintrc.json turns EVERY category off, because -c replaces the root config but leaves oxlint's default correctness category ON; without it, unrelated built-in diagnostics pollute every fixture.
- The harness writes a per-run temp config enabling exactly wallow/<rule>, with an ABSOLUTE plugin path so it resolves from the temp dir. An optional fixtures/<rule>/options.json supplies rule options.
- Parse JSON from the first '{' (the 'No files found to lint.' prefix), then assert number_of_files — otherwise 'matched no files' reads as 'the valid fixture is clean'. That assertion is the fail-closed guard.
- Throw loudly when a diagnostic has no 'code': that means the fixture does not parse and all lint diagnostics in it are suppressed.
- Read annotations from EVERY fixture file, not just invalid.tsx — the zone-dag bead needs a nested directory tree, and valid.tsx simply carries none.
The harness lives INSIDE packages/lint with vitest as a devDependency; there is no root-level vitest in this workspace.

First fixture is no-tinted-text. valid.tsx must include bg-foreground/40 (the drawer-scrim case the rule must NOT report) — a valid fixture that only omits violations proves nothing about the rule's boundary.
acceptance_criteria: Harness passes. THEN prove it fails correctly: append an unannotated text-primary/70 to valid.tsx, confirm it fails naming the exact 'file:line rule', revert. A harness never seen red is a harness you do not know works.
notes:
Harness landed as planned and was proven RED in BOTH directions before being restored: an unannotated text-primary/70 in valid.tsx failed naming 'fixtures/no-tinted-text/valid.tsx:6 wallow/no-tinted-text' as extra, and an annotation on a clean line failed naming it as missing. Two deviations from the plan's code, both forced:
1. The plan's harness was not lint-clean — 'pnpm lint:tests' flagged 5: unicorn(max-nested-calls) on the nested mkdtempSync/join/tmpdir call, eslint(preserve-caught-error) on the no-JSON throw, and curly/no-continue on the annotation loop. Fixed by extracting temporaryDirectory, adding { cause: error }, and restructuring the loop to 'if (match !== null) { ... }' with braced while.
2. FIXTURE EXCLUSION HAS A THIRD REGISTRATION POINT the plan and bead .5 both missed: .lintstagedrc.mjs PROTECTED_PATTERNS. The pre-commit hook passes staged files to oxfmt --write and oxlint --fix by EXPLICIT PATH, and an explicitly-named file that the config ignores makes oxfmt die with 'Expected at least one target file. All matched files may have been excluded by ignore rules' — the same failure the file already documents for pnpm-lock.yaml and routeTree.gen.ts. Worse, 'oxlint --fix' would have rewritten the deliberate violations the fixtures exist to state. Added '**/packages/lint/fixtures/**' there. Any future fixture directory is covered; a fixture tree placed ELSEWHERE would need all three.

title: Web-app test & comment audit (epic)
description: Strip stale/prohibitive prose from apps/wallow-web + apps/wallow-auth specs and delete migration-pinning satellites. Plan: docs/plans/2026-07-31/1330-web-test-comment-audit-execution.md (gitignored, local). Doctrine: 1320-test-comment-doctrine.md. Scope: 159 files / 33,199 lines, 32 guard specs excluded (owned by guard-test-audit.md).
notes:
PROMOTE candidates harvested from shard 01 (feed into Task 9, .claude/rules/TESTING.md):
1. location is [Unforgeable] in real Chromium — a spec cannot stub globalThis.location to observe a full-page hand-off. Observe at the Navigation API 'navigate' event: record event.destination.url and preventDefault() so the runner stays put. Applies workspace-wide.
2. Ask the generated factory for a query key, never spell one as a literal. The key carries the client's baseUrl, so a drifted literal makes getQueryData/getQueryState return undefined rather than fail — a no-op assertion every implementation passes.
3. A render helper must distinguish an explicit undefined prop from an absent one ('prop' in props, not props.prop ?? DEFAULT) whenever the absent branch is under test.

notes:

2.1 the 7 packages/*/package.json: exports -> src/ entries, add publishConfig.exports -> the current dist/ map. Only sdk and styles are published; add publishConfig uniformly anyway so a future publish cannot regress.
2.2 add --configLoader runner to apps/wallow-web, apps/wallow-auth, apps/examples/minimal-app. THIS is the actual single-app-build failure: Node's ESM resolver, not tsc, dies loading the app's own vite.config.ts because it imports styles/dist/vite.js. Project references were rejected precisely because they fix only tsc.
2.3 packages/sdk/tsconfig.json does not extend tsconfig.base.json and redeclares everything - drift, not deliberate; verified it compiles clean under full base semantics. Also rewrite the tsconfig.build.json header, which states four things that are false (claims ^5.6.0 and 'no own pin'; real peer range is >=5.5.3 || >=6.0.0 and the package pins catalog:tooling-tsc6).
2.4 the 7 tsconfig.build.json compilerOptions blocks are byte-identical -> extract a base. KEEP per-package: rootDir (TS7 errors TS5011 without it, verified) and the hand-listed include (load-bearing - it keeps test files and configs out of the declaration program so no stray .d.ts leaks into dist/).

EXPECTED RED at 2.4: packages/forms/src/core/package-scaffold.test.ts 'provides a declaration-only tsconfig.build.json narrowed to the entry'. Step 1.2 was scoped to vite/vitest specs so it survived Phase 1. Delete it here. Mapped at guard-test-audit.md line 118 - not a surprise.

ACCEPTANCE TEST for the whole phase: find . -maxdepth 3 -type d -name dist -not -path '*/node_modules/*' -exec rm -rf {} + ; then pnpm typecheck (exit 0, 10/10 projects), pnpm --filter @bc-solutions-coder/wallow-web build (exit 0, full SSR+Nitro), pnpm build && pnpm test && pnpm check:exports. check:exports is the one that proves publishConfig is right.
Commit: build: resolve workspace packages from source in-repo, dist on publish
DONE - commit 584adc3b. pnpm check exit 0 run from a completely empty dist/: format:check, lint, build, typecheck, 5505 tests, check:exports (attw/publint all green). Full acceptance test passed incl. standalone wallow-web SSR+Nitro build and 10/10 typecheck projects.

Test delta 5509 -> 5505 (-4), matching prediction exactly: sdk -2, ui -1, forms -1.

2.4 deviated from plan toward a BETTER design after a review question: the shared config is at the REPO ROOT (tsconfig.build.base.json, beside tsconfig.base.json), not under packages/, and hoists all four compilerOptions PLUS the shared exclude list - not just declaration/emitDeclarationOnly. The enabler is \${configDir} (TS 5.5+), which resolves against the config doing the extending. Measured first: a plain outDir in a base resolves against the BASE's own directory and built packages/query into packages/dist with no packages/query/dist at all. Proved inert by diffing all 250 emitted .d.ts paths across a from-scratch rebuild - identical.

Four unmapped reds (the audit is authoritative but not exhaustive on exports shape-locks), all loosened to the invariant each spec's own comment states:
- styles/src/assets.test.ts: ./assets equalled an exact dist pair -> defined and NOT equal to the main entry.
- sdk/src/server/build.test.ts: two exact-dist-pair specs deleted (nested-not-flat is already asserted against emitted files; resolution is attw's job); passthrough loosened to 'declared, not an alias of ./server'. Describe renamed off 'tsup'.
- ui + forms package-scaffold: both asserted NO publishConfig on a private package. Plan 2.1 adds it uniformly on purpose, so a package later dropping private cannot publish a src-pointing manifest. private:true is the real invariant.

Two consequences the plan did not name:
- FIVE more --configLoader runner sites, not three. Any vitest.config.ts importing @bc-solutions-coder/testing hits the same Node-ESM failure, so packages/{ui,forms} + all 3 apps needed it on test/test:watch. The two specs pinning scripts.test to the exact string 'vitest run' were loosened to containment.
- styles/src/branding.ts needs 'with { type: "json" }' on the api/branding.json import. Storybook evaluating packages/ui/.storybook/main.ts reaches it through styles/vite under plain Node ESM (ERR_IMPORT_ATTRIBUTE_MISSING).

One spec DELETED not loosened: ui dist-structure 'is importable by subpath from a consuming app' spawned Node to import @bc-solutions-coder/ui/button. In-repo that cannot be true by design now. scripts/check-exports.sh HAD to change for the gate to pass: attw --pack shells out to npm pack, and npm does NOT apply publishConfig.exports, so attw resolved the src map against a dist-only tarball and called all 4 sdk entrypoints unresolvable. auth and query 'passed' only because they declare no files field, so src ships in their tarballs - passing for the wrong reason. Script now packs with pnpm pack into an EXIT-trapped mktemp -d and hands attw the tarball path.

Also added tsconfig.build.base.json to the root format/format:check script lists, which name tsconfig.base.json explicitly.
