title: adopt 20px (text-xl) as the catalog-wide heading standard
description: Retune the shared packages/ui recipes so 16px is the heading standard catalog-wide, not just in wallow-auth (which was scoped that way in Wallow-lrlm.13). Known blast radius from Wallow-lrlm.13's report: retuning cardTitleRecipe moves 6 wallow-web + 2 minimal-app headings; retuning the Text subheading moves 6 wallow-web headings + EmptyState. User decision on 2026-07-31: go catalog-wide.
notes:
DECISION (user, 2026-07-31): standard is 20px / text-xl, NOT 16px. Rationale: 16px is the browser default body size, so a 16px heading matches body copy and hierarchy would rest entirely on weight/colour. 20px keeps headings one step above body text. Also lower churn: the Text subheading is already text-xl, so its 6 wallow-web consumers + EmptyState do not move. SCOPE NOTE: wallow-auth's 16 headings were standardized to 16px in commit 23408a9c (bead Wallow-lrlm.13) and must now be REDONE to 20px — the specs and canvas-normalised measurement approach from that bead are reusable, only the expected value changes.
RED PHASE HALTED BEFORE WRITING EXHAUSTIVE TESTS — per coordinator instruction. The
inventory found (a) a real hierarchy INVERSION, (b) a scale hole, (c) a duplicate-spelling
collapse, and (d) blast radius materially larger than this bead states. All four bear on
WHICH mechanical change is correct, so the tests should not be written until that is settled.

=== INVENTORY, RE-DERIVED FROM DISK (do not trust the counts below to the predecessor) ===

packages/styles carries NO type-scale override (packages/styles/styles.css has no text-*,
--text-*, or font-size rule). So text-base=16px, text-lg=18px, text-xl=20px are Tailwind's.

A. cardTitleRecipe (packages/ui/src/components/card/card.styles.ts:24, 'text-lg font-semibold
   text-card-foreground') — 15 render sites in 10 files. Bead says '6 wallow-web + 2
   minimal-app'; that is correct FOR THE APPS and misses all 7 packages/ui sites.

   apps/wallow-web (6) — all 18px -> 16px, no className override anywhere:
     src/app/routes/__root.tsx:104                                       'Something went wrong'
     src/app/routes/__root.tsx:128                                       'Page not found'
     src/features/organizations/components/CreateOrganizationForm.tsx:52 organization-create-heading
     src/features/settings/components/ProfileSection.tsx:86              'Profile'
     src/features/mfa/components/MfaSettingsSection.tsx:298              'Multi-Factor Authentication'
     src/features/mfa/components/MfaEnrollFlow.tsx:203                   'Set up two-factor authentication'
   apps/examples/minimal-app (2) — 18px -> 16px:
     src/routes/__root.tsx:72          BoundaryCard, shared by all THREE boundaries
     src/features/hello/HelloCard.tsx:23
   packages/ui (7) — MISSED by Wallow-lrlm.13's report except partially:
     components/card/card.stories.tsx:18, :54
     components/card/card.test.tsx:125, :133, :143
     components/centered-card-layout/centered-card-layout.stories.tsx:20, :45  <-- ABSENT from the
       predecessor's blast-radius list entirely. Two more rendered card headings.

   HARD FAIL on retune (this is the correct, intended failure):
     card.test.tsx:33  const TITLE_CLASSES = ["text-lg", "font-semibold", "text-card-foreground"]
     card.test.tsx:128 asserts the exact class SET against it.
   GOES VACUOUS (still passes, now meaningless):
     card.test.tsx:132-139 'lets a caller className override the heading size' asserts
     contains("text-lg") === false while overriding with text-2xl. After the retune the recipe
     no longer emits text-lg, so the assertion can no longer fail.

B. Text 'subheading' step (packages/ui/src/components/text/text.styles.ts:30, 'text-xl
   font-semibold') — 6 wallow-web call sites, but only FOUR change size. Bead says '6
   wallow-web headings + EmptyState'; the effective number is different in both directions.

   MOVES 20px -> 16px (4):
     src/features/organizations/components/OrganizationDetail.tsx:243 organization-detail-clients-heading
     src/features/organizations/components/MemberList.tsx:109         organization-members-heading
     src/features/inquiries/components/CreateInquiryForm.tsx:122      thank-you h2
     src/features/inquiries/components/CreateInquiryForm.tsx:150      inquiry-create-heading
   DOES NOT MOVE — caller className beats the recipe (2):
     src/features/landing/components/LandingPage.tsx:164-172 as="h3" variant="subheading" className="text-lg"
     src/features/landing/components/LandingPage.tsx:210-218 as="h3" variant="subheading" className="text-lg"
     Both stay 18px. This is the inversion source; see FINDING 1.
   packages/ui reach the bead does not mention:
     components/empty-state/empty-state.tsx:74 renders the MESSAGE as <Text as="h2"
       variant="subheading">. Five wallow-web sites render it, so five MORE headings move
       20 -> 16: OrganizationList.tsx:68, AppList.tsx:48, InquiryList.tsx:74,
       MemberList.tsx:430, OrganizationDetail.tsx:297.
     components/text/text.tsx:35 AS_DEFAULT_VARIANT h4 -> 'subheading' (public API; no as="h4"
       call site on disk today, verified by sweep).
     components/text/text.stories.tsx:33 TypeScaleSheet renders it in BOTH schemes.
   So subheading's true reach is 9 moving headings (4 direct + 5 via EmptyState), plus the h4
   default and the scale sheet. Not '6 + EmptyState'.

=== FINDING 1 (BLOCKING) — h3 would render LARGER than h2, app-wide ===
LandingPage's two h3s keep 18px because className wins over the recipe; every subheading h2 in
wallow-web drops to 16px. After a subheading retune an <h3> is 18px while an <h2> is 16px.
Worse, the specs that pin this INVERT their own meaning and STILL PASS:
  apps/wallow-web/src/features/landing/components/LandingPage.restyle.test.tsx:62
    'keeps each feature title one step below the subheading default'
  ...:72
    'keeps each quick-start step title one step below the subheading default'
Both assert expectClasses(title, "text-lg ...") and classList.contains("text-xl") === false.
After the retune the title is one step ABOVE the default and both assertions are still
satisfied. This is precisely the class-string blindness in the epic lessons: the class is
present, the relationship it claims to encode is now false, and nothing goes red.

=== FINDING 2 — the retune deletes two steps and opens an 8px hole ===
Text's scale would become display 36 / title 30 / heading 24 / subheading 16 / body 16 /
bodySm 14 / caption 12. Both 20px and 18px leave the catalog and there is nothing between 24
and 16. AS_DEFAULT_VARIANT then maps h3 -> 24px, h4 -> 16px, h5 -> 16px: h4 and h5 become the
same size, and the h3->h4 drop is 8px.

=== FINDING 3 — 'subheading' becomes a duplicate spelling of body+semibold ===
'text-base font-semibold' computes identically to variant="body" weight="semibold", which is
EXACTLY the standard Wallow-lrlm.13 adopted for wallow-auth (it deliberately did not use
subheading). The catalog would carry two names for one style. packages/ui/src/components/
empty-state/empty-state.test.tsx:83 asserts classSet(message) equals
recipeSet(textRecipe({variant:"subheading"})) — self-referential, so it survives the retune
but can no longer distinguish the two spellings. Retuning subheading contradicts the standard
it is supposed to be adopting.

=== FINDING 4 — an existing committed spec fights the change either way ===
apps/wallow-web/src/typography.test.ts:307-315 REQUIRES CreateInquiryForm.tsx, MemberList.tsx
and OrganizationDetail.tsx to literally spell variant="subheading", reasoning 'or the restyle
silently doubles the section-heading scale'. Those are 3 of the 4 call sites that would
migrate under the cleaner option. This spec must be rewritten under either route.
Also apps/CLAUDE.md:76 states the shared recipes are deliberately untuned and ends with 'Do
not describe 16px as a catalog-wide standard' — that paragraph has to move with the change.

=== RECOMMENDATION — split the change; do NOT retune subheading ===
(A) Retune cardTitleRecipe text-lg -> text-base. Clean: 8 app headings move 18 -> 16, no scale
    hole, no inversion, nothing else in the catalog is redefined. Only intended failure is
    card.test.tsx TITLE_CLASSES.
(B) Leave 'subheading' at text-xl. Migrate the 4 wallow-web section headings AND EmptyState's
    message to variant="body" weight="semibold" — the exact wallow-auth spelling. This lands
    the same 9 headings on 16px, keeps 20px as a real step, keeps h2 >= h3 (LandingPage's h3s
    stay 18px, now BELOW their 20px conceptual parent instead of above a 16px one), and makes
    the catalog-wide standard ONE spelling rather than two.
Cost of (B) over a blunt retune: 5 more files touched, and typography.test.ts:307-315 inverts
from 'must say subheading' to 'must say body+semibold'.
If the user prefers the blunt retune of both recipes anyway, that is a legitimate call — but
FINDING 1 must be paid for explicitly by dropping LandingPage's two className="text-lg"
overrides, otherwise the app ships h3 > h2.

=== TEST-PLACEMENT FINDING (corrects the coordinator's premise) ===
'The browser project loads NO Tailwind' is true for packages/ui ONLY. It is FALSE for the apps:
  apps/wallow-web/vitest.config.ts wires plugins: wallowStyles() and setupFiles:
  ['./vitest.setup.ts'] onto the browser project, which compiles vitest-styles.css and loads
  the fork theme. That is how Wallow-lrlm.13's heading-scale.test.tsx measured computed sizes.
So the measurement split is:
  packages/ui  -> 'storybook' project (card, centered-card-layout, empty-state, text). The
                  'browser' project there genuinely has no Tailwind.
  wallow-web   -> 'browser' project (has Tailwind + fork theme).
  minimal-app  -> apps/examples/minimal-app/vitest.config.ts:16 is 'projects: [node, browser]'
                  with NO wallowStyles and NO setupFiles. Its 2 CardTitle headings CANNOT be
                  measured in-app. They must be covered by a disk-derived source sweep, or by
                  measuring cardTitleRecipe itself in packages/ui's storybook project. Do not
                  plan an in-app measured spec there without first adding wallowStyles.

NO TEST FILES WRITTEN, NO SOURCE TOUCHED. git status is unchanged from session start.
AMENDED — the 20px decision landed WHILE the inventory above was being written. That note was
written against the 16px target in the bead DESCRIPTION. Re-judged against 20px/text-xl:

ALL FOUR BLOCKING FINDINGS ARE RESOLVED BY THE 20px DECISION. The user's call is the right one
and it is strictly cleaner than the 16px route:
  FINDING 1 (h3 renders larger than h2) — GONE. 'subheading' stays text-xl, so LandingPage's
    two className="text-lg" h3s (18px) stay BELOW the 20px h2s. Their source comment
    'subheading is text-xl; the card title sits one step down' stays TRUE, and
    LandingPage.restyle.test.tsx:62/:72 keep meaning what they say.

    which is byte-identical to textRecipe({variant:"subheading", color:"onCard"}). That is
    exactly what Wallow-lrlm.13's ORIGINAL acceptance asked for and never got — 'CardTitle
    derives its scale from the Text recipe, not from its own literal'. CardTitle can now
    literally compose <Text as="h2" variant="subheading" color="onCard"> and one recipe backs
    both sides.
  FINDING 4 (typography.test.ts:307-315 fights the change) — GONE. Those 3 wallow-web files
    keep variant="subheading"; the spec stays valid and unedited.

immediately before the assertion and ran the full suite. It printed HOVERED= true on the
failing run. buttonRecipe's primary arm is
  "bg-primary text-primary-foreground hover:bg-primary/90"        (button.styles.ts:33)
over a base carrying "motion-safe:transition-colors"              (button.styles.ts:25)
so the spec reads the element while the hover transition toward alpha-0.9 is still running —
alpha 0.98 is that transition roughly a fifth of the way through. The instrumentation is
reverted; the file is byte-identical to red's version.

WHY IT STARTED NOW. The spec has no hover of its own (grep: no hover/userEvent/click anywhere
in the file), so the pointer is parked from an EARLIER TEST FILE in the same browser session —
the documented "mouse position persists" hazard in packages/ui/CLAUDE.md, which applies to the
apps' browser project too. Raising the heading 16px -> 20px pushed the card contents down ~5px
and moved the approve button under that stale coordinate.

EVIDENCE IT IS THIS CHANGE AND NOT AMBIENT FLAKE — controlled, both directions:
  ConsentScreen.tsx heading reverted to variant="body" weight="semibold"  -> 3 runs, 0 failures
  ConsentScreen.tsx heading at variant="subheading"                       -> 4 runs, 3 failures
  the spec file run ALONE, heading at subheading                          -> 3 runs, 0 failures
Alone it passes because the pointer starts at the origin; only whole-suite file ordering parks
it over the button.

WHY I DID NOT FIX IT. The defect is in the spec, I am the implementer, and reshaping a spec to
make my own change green is the exact move this epic keeps paying for. It is a real regression
against the 1366/1366 baseline and it is mine by causation, so it is reported, not hidden.
The fix is one line in the spec, not in the component: settle the transition before reading
(expect.poll on the computed colour), or move the pointer off before renderPrompt(). Either
belongs to a FIX pass or its own bead.

## DOCS

REWRITTEN  apps/CLAUDE.md — the bullet at line 71 replaced outright. It claimed "wallow-auth
card headings are one 16px scale, and that standard is app-scoped", that the shared recipes
were "deliberately not retuned", and closed with "Do not describe 16px as a catalog-wide
standard". The replacement states the 20px/text-xl catalog-wide rule, names all four moved
recipes, names toastTitleRecipe/popoverTitleRecipe as deliberately excluded transient chrome,
gives the 16px-is-body-size rationale, records the new wallow-auth spelling (no weight prop),
points at .storybook/heading-scale.tsx as the recipe-level pin, and ends on the assert-computed
-size-not-class-string rule.
VERIFIED CLEAN, no edit needed (checked myself, did not take red's word):
  packages/ui/CLAUDE.md               — grep for text-lg|16px|18px|20px|text-xl|subheading
                                        returns nothing; it carries no type-scale claim.
  docs/development/component-library.md:29 — names the subheading variant in a list of variant
                                        names, asserts no px value, stays true.
  docs/development/frontend-setup.md  — no heading-scale claim.
  root CLAUDE.md                      — no heading-scale claim.
No wallow-auth or wallow-web source comment mentioned 16px/18px/text-lg/text-base (swept).

## UNRELATED CONCURRENT EDITS IN THE WORKTREE — NOT MINE, flagging for whoever commits

Two files were modified by another agent while I worked; they appeared in git status after my
first test run and are nothing to do with this bead. Do not sweep them into this commit
without checking who owns them:
  packages/ui/vitest.config.ts   — extraBrowserOptimizeDeps emptied, storybook optimizeDeps
    line deleted, baseUiSubpaths/recipeRuntime kept alive with void
  apps/wallow-web/vite.config.ts — the two use-sync-external-store/shim -> react aliases removed
FIX (fix-hover pass): the one wallow-auth failure is closed. wallow-auth 1367/1367.

## WHAT WAS CHANGED — one file, test-side only
apps/wallow-auth/src/features/consent/components/ConsentScreen.catalog.test.tsx
No app/component/recipe file touched. ConsentScreen.tsx still carries exactly
green's single edit (variant="body" weight="semibold" -> variant="subheading"),
verified by git diff. No assertion weakened, skipped, deleted or loosened.

1. parkPointer() + `await parkPointer()` appended to the existing beforeEach.
   Creates a `position:fixed;bottom:0;right:0;4x4` div, userEvent.hover()s it,
   removes it. Runs BEFORE the fixture mounts. This is not a new invention — it
   is the idiom already committed at packages/ui/src/components/preview-card/
   preview-card.test.tsx:290-318, copied deliberately.
2. "paints approve on the primary surface" now reads the approve background
   through `await expect.poll(...).toEqual(probe)` instead of a single
   synchronous read. The probe is still read once and still guarded by
   isTransparent(probe) === false.

## WHY IT IS ROBUST, NOT LUCKY — measured, both directions

The root cause is that the spec's claim is a REST-STATE claim while nothing in
the file established rest. buttonRecipe gives approve `hover:bg-primary/90` and
deny `hover:bg-accent` over a `motion-safe:transition-colors` base
(button.styles.ts:25,33,40). The pointer position persists across spec FILES, and
the browser re-evaluates :hover when content is inserted under a stationary
cursor — so the file inherited whatever coordinate the previous file left, and
io5f's +5px heading moved the button onto it.

Parking BEFORE the mount is what removes the cause rather than dodging it: the
buttons are never under the cursor at any point in their lifetime, so no hover
arm ever applies and no transition ever starts, whatever file ran first. That is
strictly stronger than the two rendered-park sites in wallow-web
(dashboard-nav-park / control-park), which park only AFTER the mount and so still
let a transition begin. It is also file-wide by construction, which matters
because the deny spec's own words are "no surface at rest" (line 214) and
`hover:bg-accent` would have broken it the same way on the next layout change.

CONTROLLED EVIDENCE (full suite each time, not the file alone):
  before the fix                       1366/1367 — reproduced, alpha 0.984
  park + poll                          10 runs, 10 x 1367/1367
  spec file alone, park + poll          3 runs,  3 x 9/9
  POLL ONLY, park removed               5 runs, 1 FAILURE (run 3), 4 pass
The poll-only run is the load-bearing negative control. It proves the poll is NOT
what fixes this and that a fix which merely waits is still a coin flip: on the
failing run the poll ran its full 1239ms and timed out, i.e. the hover was
SUSTAINED and the colour settled at bg-primary/90 — exactly what a parked cursor
predicts. The park is the fix; the poll is a second, independent guard on the one
axis that is a transition rather than a static value.

VACUITY CHECK — the fixed spec can still fail. Mutated ConsentScreen.tsx's
approve to `variant="secondary"` and re-ran the file:
  x paints approve on the primary surface
  expected { r:234, g:227, b:220, a:1 } to deeply equal { r:207, g:155, b:0, a:1 }
The poll's only exit is that exact equality against the bg-primary probe, so a
wrong surface still fails — one second later instead of instantly. Mutation
reverted; git diff on ConsentScreen.tsx confirms it.

## FULL GATES
  apps/wallow-auth        1367 / 1367   (10 consecutive full-suite runs)
  packages/ui             1515 / 1515
  apps/wallow-web         1098 / 1098
  apps/examples/minimal-app  27 /   27
  pnpm typecheck   clean
  pnpm lint        clean (exit 0)
  pnpm format:check clean

## FOLLOW-UP FILED
Wallow-h9k1 (P3) — hoist the beforeEach-safe park into
@bc-solutions-coder/testing and add the hazard to .claude/rules/TESTING.md.
Today it is documented ONLY in packages/ui/CLAUDE.md, and that text says "make
the hovering spec LAST IN THE FILE", which does not cover the cross-FILE case
that actually bit here. Three packages now carry three hand-rolled parks. Filed
rather than done, to keep this bead's diff to the one failing spec.

## THE TWO DISCLAIMED CONFIGS — VERDICT: NEITHER BELONGS TO THIS BEAD, AND BOTH
## ARE ALREADY CLEAN. Nothing to commit, nothing to revert.

packages/ui/vitest.config.ts   — `git diff` EMPTY, absent from `git status`.
apps/wallow-web/vite.config.ts — `git diff` EMPTY, absent from `git status`.

Both were dirty when green wrote its report and have since been reverted by
whoever made them. On disk right now:
  packages/ui/vitest.config.ts:86   extraBrowserOptimizeDeps: [...baseUiSubpaths,
                                    ...recipeRuntime]        <- populated again
  packages/ui/vitest.config.ts:107  optimizeDeps: { include: [...] } on the
                                    storybook project        <- present again
  apps/wallow-web/vite.config.ts:49-50  both use-sync-external-store/shim -> react
                                    regex aliases            <- present again
i.e. the exact three things green reported as emptied/deleted/removed.

EVIDENCE THEY ARE NOT io5f's:
1. The team-lead hypothesis was that the new packages/ui/.storybook/heading-scale.tsx
   story might need a baseUiSubpaths entry. It does not: that file's only imports
   are `storybook/test` and a type-only `react` import. No Base UI subpath at all.
2. The direction is wrong for that hypothesis anyway — the observed edit EMPTIED
   the list and DELETED the storybook optimizeDeps line. That is removal, not the

3. This bead is green on both packages with the configs at their COMMITTED state:
   packages/ui 1515/1515 and apps/wallow-web 1098/1098, just re-run. io5f needs
   no config change.
4. Neither file has a commit after the ones already in history
   (ui/vitest.config.ts last touched by 165bc6a2; web/vite.config.ts by 3d5d6870),
   so the edits were never committed anywhere.
5. `bd search optimizeDeps` and `bd search use-sync-external-store` both return
   nothing, and `bd list --status in_progress` is empty — no bead claims them.

READ: transient experiments by a concurrent agent, self-reverted. They were never
io5f's red phase. Do not sweep, do not restore.
VERIFY (independent re-derivation, all claims checked by reading code/running tests, not trusting reports):

1. FOUR RECIPES ✓ — read packages/ui/src/components/{card,dialog,alert-dialog,drawer}.styles.ts directly: cardTitleRecipe, dialogTitleRecipe, alertDialogTitleRecipe all "text-xl font-semibold ..."; drawerTitleRecipe "text-xl font-semibold" (still colourless, comment intact). All four confirmed text-xl.

Read every one of the 16 render sites: all `<Text as="h2" variant="subheading" color="onCard" ...>` with NO weight prop. Confirmed no leftover `variant="body"`+`weight="semibold"` as="h2" anywhere. MfaEnrollForm.tsx:367's weight="semibold" is on a `<p variant="bodySm">`, not a heading — correctly left alone.

title: Repo-wide: delete the 16 source-reading sweeps; lint owns structure
description:
Phases 4a and 4b of docs/plans/2026-08-02/1744-no-source-tests-design.md.

## THE APPROACH CHANGED - read this before the notes below

This bead previously said: recover the 185-line left-to-right comment scanner from
5641bcf2^, hoist it into packages/testing on a node-safe subpath, and repoint all 16 call
sites. That is now the OPPOSITE of the plan. The scanner is NOT recovered. We delete its
reason to exist instead.

The stripper defect is real and measured - block comments stripped before line comments, so
`// /v1/**` opens a block comment running to the file's next `*/`; spans of 2871, 2884 and
4041 characters of real wallow-auth source silently removed from what the guards read. On a
NEGATIVE scan (packages/env asserts process.env does NOT appear) over-deletion is
indistinguishable from a clean module.

But a better scanner makes sixteen unsound specs sound and leaves the seventeenth free to be
written next week. The inventory went 23 -> 18 -> 16 because nothing forbids writing a new
one; two of the current sixteen landed HOURS after this bead was filed. Wallow-xg9t.1
installs the rule that stops that, and BLOCKS this bead.

Precedent: this conversion already happened here once and worked. See the header of
packages/lint/src/rules/text-heading-variant.ts - a 523-line disk sweep became one AST rule,
"a rule reads the parsed JSX, fires in the editor, and cannot be out-run by formatting."

## PHASE 4a - write the rule while the sweeps still run

wallow/module-imports, options { allow, allowRelative, exportStar }. One options-driven rule
rather than three narrow ones, following text-heading-variant's precedent. Absorbs:

- apps/wallow-web + apps/wallow-auth feature-barrels.test.ts ("barrel is re-exports only",
  "reaches only its own modules")
- apps/wallow-auth/src/features-api-seam.test.ts ("api.ts is a re-export and nothing else",
  "reaches only the SDK's entries")
- packages/env/src/charter.test.ts "imports nothing at all" (allow: [])

Deliberately NOT given a rule: packages/env's "reads no environment of its own". process.env
already fails to typecheck under the compilerOptions.types: [] the SAME charter asserts
separately, and import.meta.env alone does not justify a rule. Five-line addition later if it
proves to matter.

Land 4a with the sweeps STILL RUNNING, so the rule is proven to fire before anything is
deleted. The overlap is the point.

## PHASE 4b - the deletions

BUCKET A - delete, no successor. The constraint is not worth enforcing in any tool:

- apps/examples/minimal-app/src/sdk-wiring.test.ts - WHOLE FILE. Every it() regex-matches a
  file it read; its own header concedes "there is nothing left to unit-test". Includes two
  README assertions (expect(readme).toMatch(/frontend-state\.md/u) plus a broken-link
  checker), an existsSync(...)===false pinning a file deleted in a past refactor, and "adds
  no live queries" - a spec that FAILS WHEN A DEVELOPER IMPROVES THE EXAMPLE APP.
- packages/navigation/src/shell-source.test.ts - WHOLE FILE. Two of its seven it()s test the
  spec's OWN REGEX HELPERS against inline string literals, asserting nothing about the app.
  Plus /\bnavControlClass\b/ (a word-presence check) and "asks for the outline variant at
  both call sites".
- the five packages/ui *.composition.test.ts - "ships the five-file catalog anatomy"
  (existsSync x5 per component) and the class-string pins ("hard-codes no layout or colour
  utility in its JSX", "carries no opacity-suffixed colour in its recipe", "derives the row's
  test id" via toMatch(/-item/u)).
- features-api-seam.test.ts - "owns a co-located api.test.ts", "names a surface".
- shared-current-user.test.ts - the archaeological half ("declares no queryFn of its own",
  "no second current-user probe survives anywhere under src/").
- the three features/*/api.test.ts - "never adopts the generated mutation factory", "has no
  bare operation on the generated entry to prefer instead".
- ALL FILES: the vacuity meta-guards ("finds the features it is meant to cover", "finds seams
  to check at all", "is scanning a source tree that still has the route in it"). They exist
  only to prove the sweep is not scanning an empty list, so they die with it.
- env + logger charters: "publishes the same subpaths it resolves from source", "gives every
  subpath a lib entry", "points the published conditions at the built files" - duplicates of
  pnpm check:exports (publint + attw over real dist/).

BUCKET C - KEEP. Do not sweep these away with the rest:

- The IDENTITY re-exports in the three features/*/api.test.ts:
  expect(api.forgotPassword).toBe(sdkForgotPassword). Per packages/testing/CLAUDE.md:186 this
  is the one construct a call site cannot observe - a hand-written look-alike carries the same
  name, shape and type, passes every behavioural spec, and reaches an undocumented endpoint.
- The ui composition barrel dynamic imports (typeof barrel.listRowRecipe === "function").
- shared-current-user.test.ts's async specs ("hands this app the current-user hook", "holds a
  resolved user long enough that a re-mounted probe is a cache read").
- THE KEYSTONE: the .oxlintrc.json wiring assertions in the env and logger charters ("keys an
  override on this package's source", "restates every ban the root config makes", "bans every
  other workspace package"). These read CONFIG, not source, through readJsonc
  (line-comments-only, JSONC) - they never touch the defective stripper. They get MORE
  load-bearing under this plan, not less: if lint becomes the primary guard, these are the
  only thing between us and a silently inert plugin. Wallow-mlc3 (closed 2026-08-02) was
  exactly that failure - wallow/* rules inert over three packages, passing everything.

## DELIBERATE HOLES - recorded so they are not re-filed as bugs

Every feature has a public barrel (wallow/zone-dag already bans deep imports, so a
barrel-less feature is unreachable and fails the typecheck at the import site); the catalog's
five-file component anatomy; minimal-app's README link integrity and ./query mention (docs
build, not pnpm test); minimal-app ships no live query (the constraint was actively harmful);
the shell's hand-rolled button/hover colours (partly covered by the shipped
wallow/no-tinted-text, residue dropped).

## Net effect

Two files deleted outright, fourteen survive substantially thinner, two new lint rules (this
bead's module-imports plus Wallow-xg9t.1's no-source-tests). No 185-line scanner, no
adversarial fixture tree, no thirteenth subpath export on packages/testing.
acceptance_criteria: grep -rln "replaceAll(/\/\*" over apps and packages test files returns ZERO - by DELETION, not by hoisting a scanner. No comment scanner is recovered from 5641bcf2^ and packages/testing gains no ./strip-comments subpath. apps/examples/minimal-app/src/sdk-wiring.test.ts and packages/navigation/src/shell-source.test.ts are deleted outright. wallow/module-imports ships in packages/lint, is registered, and has a fixtures spec. Bucket C survives intact: the identity re-exports in the three features/*/api.test.ts, the ui barrel dynamic-import checks, shared-current-user.test.ts async cache specs, and the .oxlintrc.json wiring assertions in the env and logger charters. pnpm check is green, and the packages/lint override that permitted the sweeps under wallow/no-source-tests is removed with them.
notes:
RE-DERIVED FROM DISK (scout pass, read-only, no edits made):

COUNT: 23 copies, not ~20. grep -rl 'replaceAll(/\/\/*' across *.test.ts/*.test.tsx:
- packages/ui (5): list-card, muted-text, empty-state, list-row, page-header *.composition.test.ts
  — sweep only their OWN component dir (narrow, 1-3 files each).
- packages/forms (1): src/core/query-facade.test.ts — sweeps whole packages/forms/src recursively.
- apps/wallow-web (5): feature-barrels.test.ts, zone-dag.test.ts (sweeps EVERY .ts/.tsx under src/,
  widest reach), dashboard-control-catalog/nav-suppression/chrome-tokens.test.ts (narrow: 5 named
  DashboardLayout/DashboardNav/etc files via componentsDir).
- apps/wallow-auth (11): generated-mutations, feature-barrels, features-api-seam, catalog-adoption,
  shared-current-user, query-facade, zone-dag (widest reach, same as web's), 3 feature api.test.ts
  (mfa-enroll/forgot-password/reset-password), MfaEnrollForm.start-mutation.test.ts (narrow, one file).
- apps/examples/minimal-app (1): sdk-wiring.test.ts — sweeps whole minimal-app src/.
(wallow-web's src/typography.test.ts + src/app/typography.test.ts are NOT in this list — already
fixed by Wallow-lrlm.14, now import the real scanner.)

WHAT THEY GUARD (not cosmetic): all 23 are architecture/design-system invariants, not lint nits.
- Import-boundary "one door" seams: zone-dag x2 (the whole app-zone import DAG), feature-barrels x2
  (every feature has exactly one public barrel), query-facade x2 + generated-mutations +
  features-api-seam + shared-current-user + sdk-wiring + 3 feature api.test.ts — these all assert a
  SINGLE approved path to react-query/SDK/current-user exists and no second hand-rolled copy does.
- Design-system composition/anatomy: 5 packages/ui composition specs (component composes over
  Card/Text rather than reimplementing it; 5-file catalog folder shape).
- Design-token/no-hand-rolled-styling: 3 wallow-web dashboard-*.test.ts (colour-token naming,
  catalog Button vs hand-rolled, className not out-merging the catalog).
- catalog-adoption.test.ts: wallow-auth's sibling of the ORIGINAL typography.test.ts bug (heading
  scale / Text usage) — same family as what Wallow-lrlm.14 fixed in wallow-web, just not yet ported.

SAME BUG vs DIFFERENT: 22 of 23 share the IDENTICAL dangerous defect — unconditional
`.replaceAll(block).replaceAll(line)`, block pass first, no string/template/regex-literal context,
so a `/*`-shaped sequence anywhere (incl. inside a `//` comment, a regex literal, or a string)
opens a block-delete that runs to the file's NEXT `*/`. Two line-comment second-pass variants exist
(`/\/\/[^\n]*/gu` vs `^\s*\/\/.*$/gmu` restricted to whole-line comments) but this only changes
exposure to "URL embedded mid-line trips the line pass" — it does NOT touch the shared block-pass
defect, which is the dangerous one. catalog-adoption.test.ts (wallow-auth) is the ONE exception:
single-alternation `/\/\*[\s\S]*?\*\/|\/\/[^\n]*/gu`, which per Wallow-lrlm.14's own measured table
cures exactly 1 of 6 adversarial constructs (glob-in-line-comment) and remains unsound for the other
5 (url-in-string, url-in-template-literal, url-in-jsx-text, //-in-regex-literal, /*-in-regex-literal,
"/*"..."*/" string pair). None of the 23 has the full left-to-right scanner; that only exists in the
already-fixed wallow-web typography pair.

BLIND IN PRACTICE — SPOT-CHECKED, NOT LATENT IN WALLOW-AUTH: grepped both apps' non-test src for a
`//` line comment containing an embedded `/*`-shaped sequence. wallow-web: none found (matches
Wallow-lrlm.14's own finding, extended here). wallow-auth: THREE real, non-test files currently
contain the trigger — `app/start.ts` ("// ... /v1/**"), `AcceptTermsScreen.tsx` ("/v1/**"),
`MfaEnrollForm.tsx` ("/connect/**"), `LoginScreen.tsx` ("/mfa/*"). Ran the exact regex against these
files with node: the block pass DOES fire on the embedded sequence and swallows real subsequent
source up to the next `*/` — measured spans of 2871, 2884, and 4041 chars (dozens to ~100 source
lines) silently deleted in LoginScreen.tsx and MfaEnrollForm.tsx alone, in the text that
zone-dag.test.ts (widest sweep: every .ts/.tsx under src) and feature-barrels/query-facade/etc then
read. Checked whether this CURRENTLY flips a result any of these guards care about: all static
`import` statements and both `useMutation(` call sites in these 3 files sit BEFORE the swallowed
span, and no dynamic `import()` exists in them, so zone-dag's DAG walk and
MfaEnrollForm.start-mutation.test.ts's assertions are not currently flipped by this — but this is
luck of line position, not soundness, and I did not exhaustively re-check every assertion in every
one of the 11 wallow-auth specs against these files. This is a live, currently-firing defect (real
source is being deleted from what the guards read today), not merely a future risk, even though the
specific assertions I checked happen to still pass. catalog-adoption.test.ts's partial
single-alternation fix DOES cure this exact glob construct for its own sweep. Did not find a live
trigger in the narrow-surface sweeps (5 dashboard-* target files, 5 packages/ui component dirs,
minimal-app src) — spot-checked, not exhaustive.

COST TO FIX — cheap, no package-boundary obstacle: @bc-solutions-coder/testing already exists, is
already a devDependency of apps/wallow-web, apps/wallow-auth, apps/examples/minimal-app,
packages/ui, and packages/forms, and already publishes multiple sub-path exports (./render,
./sdk-harness, ./contrast, ./render-with-wallow) via package.json `exports`. Adding
`./strip-comments` following that exact pattern, moving
apps/wallow-web/src/shared/testing/strip-comments.ts + its 11 fixtures into
packages/testing/src/, and swapping each of the 23 call sites (plus wallow-web's own two
already-fixed typography specs, per the bead's acceptance) to import from
@bc-solutions-coder/testing/strip-comments is a mechanical, low-risk change — every consumer

title: Button stamps role="button" on anchors composed through render — links announce as buttons
description:
VERIFIED ON DISK during Wallow-lrlm.7.1 verification, not inferred.

@base-ui/react 1.6.0 internals/use-button/useButton.js:167-171 merges
`isNativeButton ? { type: "button" } : { role: "button" }` into the returned
button props. So `<Button render={<a href=... />} nativeButton={false}>` — the
catalog Button’s own documented composition pattern, pinned by
packages/ui/src/components/button/button.test.tsx "composes onto another element
through the render prop" — tells the accessibility tree that a NAVIGATION is an
ACTION.

WHY THIS IS A REAL DEFECT AND NOT COSMETIC:
- The anchor is dropped from a screen reader’s links list (JAWS/NVDA "list
  links", VoiceOver rotor) and appears in the buttons list instead, so a user
  navigating by control type cannot find it.
- The announced role contradicts the retained behaviour: the element still has
  an href, so the browser still offers open-in-new-tab / copy-link-address /
  middle-click, and still shows the target in the status bar. Announcing
  "button" is a WCAG 2.2 SC 4.1.2 Name/Role/Value mismatch.
- It degrades SILENTLY. Of wallow-auth’s 8 anchor-composed Buttons, exactly ONE
  (verify-email-confirm-continue) had a role-based assertion
  (VerifyEmailConfirm.test.tsx:221, getByRole("link", { name: /continue/iu })).
  The other 7 had none, so nothing would have caught the regression.

Base UI already distinguishes the case internally: isValidLinkElement() at
useButton.js:185 (`tagName === "A" && href`) is used for keyboard handling at
line 107, and simply is not applied to the role.

FIX (packages/ui/src/components/button/button.tsx): when the render element is
an anchor with an href, Button should supply role="link" itself rather than
making every caller remember. `otherExternalProps` merges LAST in useButton, so
a role passed by Button wins — that mechanism is already proven by the 8
role="link" props wallow-auth ships today.

CALL SITES TO CLEAN UP WHEN THIS LANDS (delete the role="link" prop and its
comment at each):
  apps/wallow-auth/src/features/login/components/ExternalProviders.tsx:125
  apps/wallow-auth/src/features/invitation/components/InvitationScreen.tsx:305,357,365
  apps/wallow-auth/src/features/privacy/components/PrivacyPage.tsx:136
  apps/wallow-auth/src/features/register/components/RegisterForm.tsx:485
  apps/wallow-auth/src/features/terms/components/TermsPage.tsx:129
  apps/wallow-auth/src/features/verify-email/components/VerifyEmailConfirm.tsx:159

ACCEPTANCE: a Button composed onto an <a href> exposes role "link" with NO
caller opt-in; a Button composed onto a non-anchor keeps role "button"; a
packages/ui spec asserts both arms; the 8 wallow-auth role="link" props are
removed and each of those call sites gains (or keeps) a getByRole("link")
assertion so the next regression is loud.
notes:
RED (Wallow-lrlm.12) — 6 specs added, 2 FAILING for the right reason.

FILE (the only file I touched): packages/ui/src/components/button/button.test.tsx
New block: `describe("Button link semantics")` at the end of the file, plus a
`StandInRouterLink` helper and a `ComponentProps` type import. No source change,
no story change (role is a computed-a11y edge a story cannot assert), no change
to the three coupled catalog-set files (no new component).

Run: `pnpm --filter @bc-solutions-coder/ui exec vitest run --project browser button.test.tsx`
Result: Tests 2 failed | 74 passed (76). Both failures are the new red arms.
Failure text is exactly the defect: `expected null to be <a href="/docs" role="button" …>`.
oxlint --deny-warnings: clean. oxfmt --check: clean. tsc --noEmit: clean.

=== THE SIX SPECS AND THE PROOF EACH ONE CAN FAIL ===

I proved non-vacuity by applying three candidate implementations to button.tsx,
running, and reverting. button.tsx is back to its committed content (verified via
git status). P1 = `role={undefined}` before `{...rest}`. P2 = `role="link"` after
`{...rest}`. P3 = ref callback doing `setAttribute("role","link")` when tagName==="A".

| spec                                              | now  | P1   | P2   | P3   |
|---------------------------------------------------|------|------|------|------|
| announces an anchor composed through render …     | FAIL | pass | pass | pass |
| announces a component-typed render … as a link    | FAIL | pass | pass | pass |
| keeps button semantics for a non-anchor           | pass | FAIL | FAIL | pass |
| keeps button semantics for an anchor with no href | pass | FAIL | FAIL | FAIL |
| lets a caller's explicit role win                 | pass | pass | pass | FAIL |
| leaves a native button carrying no role attribute | pass | pass | FAIL | pass |

Every spec fails under at least one realistic implementation, and every candidate
implementation is rejected by at least one spec. P3 — the most likely fix shape —
gets BOTH red arms green and is caught only by the two overshoot guards, so the
set steers the implementer rather than merely scoring them.

Assertions read the ROLE ENGINE (`screen.getByRole(...).query()`), not
`getAttribute("role")`. The defect is what the accessibility tree reports, and a
correct fix may either set `role="link"` or omit the attribute and let the
anchor's implicit role apply. Pinning the literal attribute would pick one and
reject the other. `.query()` avoids retry-to-timeout on the negative cases.

=== PREMISE RE-VERIFIED ON DISK ===

@base-ui/react 1.6.0, internals/use-button/useButton.js. `getButtonProps` ends:
`mergeProps({handlers}, isNativeButton ? {type:'button'} : {role:'button'},
focusableWhenDisabledProps, otherExternalProps)`. merge-props/mergeProps.js
documents "the rightmost object's fields overwrite the conflicting ones", so a
`role` supplied by the catalog Button wins. Confirmed.

`isValidLinkElement` (tagName "A" && href) at the bottom of the same file is used
at the keyboard branch — `shouldClick = isNativeButton ? isButton : !isLink` — so
Base UI ALREADY suppresses Space/Enter synthesis for anchors-with-href. Only the
role disagrees with the element. That is what makes this a narrow, safe fix.

=== FINDING 1: BASE UI OFFERS NO OPT-OUT, AND DECLINES TO ===

Asked for on the bead, so answered from the official 1.6.0 docs, not memory
(base-ui docs/react/components/button, read via ref.tools):

  "Links: The Button component enforces button semantics (role="button",
   keyboard interaction, disabled state). It should not be used for links."
  "If a link needs to look like a button visually, style the <a> element
   directly with CSS rather than using the Button component."

There is NO prop. `nativeButton` only chooses between `type="button"` and
`role="button"`; the Button.d.ts surface is NativeButtonProps +
BaseUIComponentProps + focusableWhenDisabled. So the answer to "is the correct
fix a Base UI prop rather than a workaround" is: neither. Base UI's position is
that this composition should not exist.

That does not make the bead wrong, but it changes what the fix IS. Two options:

  (A) AS SPECCED — catalog Button detects a link and supplies the role itself.
      Deletes 9 workarounds, zero call-site churn, and rides the documented merge
      order rather than a private API. It knowingly overrides a usage guideline
      whose stated rationale (button semantics get enforced) is the exact thing we
      want overridden, and Base UI's own keyboard code already agrees with us.
  (B) LIBRARY-SANCTIONED — stop composing Button onto anchors. Expose the recipe
      for a plain styled `<a>`, or add a catalog `ButtonLink`. More churn (new
      component + 9 call sites rewritten) but no fighting the library, and it
      permanently removes the drift class.

RECOMMENDATION: (A). It matches this bead's acceptance, it is a much smaller
blast radius, and the specs above are written to the CONTRACT ("a thing that
navigates announces as a link") rather than to a mechanism, so they largely
survive a later move to (B). But this is a knowing deviation from a documented
"should not", so the team should decide it consciously rather than discover it.
If the team picks (B), the two red arms in this block get deleted rather than
made green — do not silently paper over them.

=== FINDING 2: THE INVENTORY IS 9 SITES, NOT 8 ===

Re-derived by grep rather than trusted. The 8 on the bead are correct, and there
is a NINTH of a different shape that the bead misses:

  apps/wallow-web/src/app/routes/dashboard/apps/index.tsx:46 — `role={undefined}`
  (not `role="link"`), which is why a `role="link"` grep never found it. Its
  comment already diagnoses this exact defect and its sibling spec
  index.navigation.test.tsx already pins "absence of role=button". So wallow-web
  independently hit this and worked around it a second way.

The 8 wallow-auth sites, re-derived and matching the bead:
  ExternalProviders.tsx:125, InvitationScreen.tsx:305/357/365,
  PrivacyPage.tsx:136, RegisterForm.tsx:485, TermsPage.tsx:129,
  VerifyEmailConfirm.tsx:159.

=== FINDING 3: THE HARD ARM — COMPONENT-TYPED RENDER ===

The wallow-web site composes `render={<Link to="…" />}` (TanStack Router). Its
`render.type` is a function and `render.props` has no `href` — nothing about the
element says "anchor" until it has mounted. So an implementation that inspects
`render.type === "a"` fixes the 8 wallow-auth sites and leaves the wallow-web one
broken. That is why spec 2 exists and uses a `StandInRouterLink` stand-in (a
local 6-line component, so packages/ui takes no router dependency).

Implication for GREEN: the fix almost certainly needs the mounted element, not
the element descriptor — a ref/layout-effect that reads `tagName === "A" &&
hasAttribute("href")` and drives the role through state. That is the same family
as Base UI's own `updateDisabled` layout effect in this very hook, so it is not a
hack. Two constraints the guards enforce: gate on the href (not the tag alone),
and make the role a DEFAULT that a caller's explicit role beats — spec 5 fails
against a naive `setAttribute` that clobbers the caller.

=== SCOPE CHECKS (all verified, none acted on) ===

- Base UI parts that call useButton: Button, CheckboxRoot, DialogTrigger,
  MenuTrigger, PopoverTrigger, ToastAction, ToastClose, Toggle. Only Button is in
  scope here.
- packages/ui ListRow is NOT affected — it uses `useRender` directly, no
  useButton, so its `render={<Link/>}` rows keep link semantics. Verified.
- NavigationMenu.Link is NOT affected (no useButton), so DashboardNav's composed
  Links are fine. Verified.
- Toggle IS affected in principle (toggle.test.tsx:174 composes onto `<a
  href="#bold">`), but a Toggle is semantically a button (aria-pressed), so
  anchor composition there is questionable on its own terms. NOT fixed here, NOT
  filed — flagging it for a decision.

=== WORK LEFT FOR GREEN ===

The call-site half of the acceptance is deliberately NOT in this red commit,
because it cannot be red: those 9 sites pass `role="link"` / `role={undefined}`
today, so a `getByRole("link")` assertion added now passes for the wrong reason
and proves nothing. It becomes non-vacuous only in the same commit that deletes
the workaround props. So GREEN should, together: (1) fix packages/ui Button,
(2) delete the 9 workaround props and their now-stale comments, (3) add/keep a
`getByRole("link")` assertion at each site.

Sites that ALREADY have a role assertion (keep as-is): VerifyEmailConfirm.test.tsx
:221; InvitationScreen.test.tsx:357 ("back to sign in"); index.navigation.test.tsx
(wallow-web, asserts absence of role=button). Sites needing a NEW assertion:
TermsPage, PrivacyPage, ExternalProviders, RegisterForm's external-provider button
(RegisterForm.test.tsx:500/503 assert the terms/privacy anchors, which are plain
`<a>`s, NOT the composed Button at :485), and the two remaining InvitationScreen
buttons (:305 home, :355 register).

=== TREE STATUS ===

At the moment I started, `git status --porcelain` was EMPTY and the branch was
main, ahead of origin/main by 30 commits — so the earlier commit agent's work is
committed but NOT pushed. During my run the concurrent Wallow-lrlm.13 agent's
edits appeared (13 modified apps/wallow-auth feature files + untracked
apps/wallow-auth/src/heading-scale.test.tsx). Those are FOREIGN to this bead. My
only change is packages/ui/src/components/button/button.test.tsx. I committed
nothing.
GREEN (Wallow-lrlm.12) — 2 red arms green, all 6 link-semantics specs pass, 0 test edits to button.test.tsx.

=== PATH TAKEN: (A), THE SPECCED APPROACH — AND THE EVIDENCE THAT (B) CANNOT WORK ===

I was told to PREFER the anchor path (apply the button cva recipe to a real <a>,
never route a link through Base UI's Button) and to fall back only on stated
infeasibility. I IMPLEMENTED the anchor path first and RAN it rather than arguing
from theory. Result:

  vitest run --project browser button.test.tsx  ->  Tests 1 failed | 75 passed
  FAIL "announces a component-typed render that resolves to an anchor as a link"
  expected null to be <a class="..." href="/dashboard/apps/register" role="button" tabindex="0">

The implementation was: if `render` is a valid element whose `type === "a"` and
whose `props.href` is a non-empty string, cloneElement it with cn(recipe, own
className) and never touch BaseButton. It fixed spec 1 and left specs 3/4/5/6
green — it is a WORKING anchor path for the 8 wallow-auth sites. It cannot fix
spec 2, and the reason is structural, not a detail I could route around:

  A component-typed `render` (`<Link to=... />`, the SHIPPED wallow-web shape)
  has `type === function`. React cannot tell you what a component renders before
  it renders. There is no render-time predicate that sees an anchor there.

So the anchor path can only be SELECTED after mount, and selecting it after mount
means changing the component identity at that position (BaseButton -> host "a"),
which React implements as unmount + remount: the DOM node is destroyed and
rebuilt, dropping focus and, for `<Link>`, tearing down and recreating the router
link. A remount as the fix for an accessibility annotation is worse than the
defect.

WHAT ELSE THE ANCHOR PATH WOULD HAVE LOST (asked for explicitly):
1. A hybrid (static anchor path + runtime role for component renders) has to gate
   the static arm on the href to keep spec 4 green — and
   InvitationScreen.tsx:303 swaps `href` between `undefined` and HOME_HREF while
   the accept POST is in flight. That control would REMOUNT mid-interaction on
   every submit. This is a real shipped call site, not a hypothetical.
2. Bypassing BaseButton drops useButton's real contributions on the non-link
   arms: Space/Enter click synthesis for non-native elements, focusableWhenDisabled,
   the disabled -> aria-disabled/pointer-events handling, tabIndex, and the
   dev-mode native-button check. Spec 3 (<div/>) only asserts the role, so a
   bypass would pass the spec while silently making a div-composed Button
   keyboard-inoperable.

CONCERN WORTH RECORDING (I proceeded anyway, per instruction): (A) is still a
knowing deviation from Base UI 1.6.0's documented "should not be used for links".
The narrow reading that makes it defensible: Base UI's OWN isValidLinkElement
(tagName A + resolved href) already suppresses its Space/Enter synthesis for
exactly these elements — the library already treats them as links everywhere
EXCEPT the role. We override one attribute on the set Base UI itself has already
classified as links.

=== THE FIX (packages/ui/src/components/button/button.tsx, +96 lines) ===

Button reads the MOUNTED element, not the render descriptor:
  - useState seeded by rendersAnchorWithHref(render) — an OPTIMISTIC seed only,
    so the SSR HTML already says "link" for the 8 intrinsic-<a href> sites
    instead of shipping role="button" until hydration. Same value on the client's
    first render, so no hydration mismatch.
  - useIsomorphicLayoutEffect (useLayoutEffect in the browser, useEffect on the
    server — both apps SSR this catalog) with NO dep array, re-measuring every
    render, is the authority: `element instanceof HTMLAnchorElement && element.href !== ""`.
    That mirrors Base UI's own isValidLinkElement — HTMLAnchorElement.href reads
    back the RESOLVED url and is "" exactly when the attribute is absent. Layout
    (not passive) effect means the corrected role lands BEFORE paint, so no user
    or AT observes the intermediate value. Re-measuring every render is what makes
    InvitationScreen's disappearing href correct: Decline stops being a link for
    exactly the window it has no destination.
  - A merged ref (useCallback keyed on the caller's ref) so Button's own
    measurement does not steal a ref a caller passes.
  - The role is SPREAD conditionally — `{...(isLink ? { role: "link" } : {})}` —
    and placed BEFORE {...rest}.

    NON-OBVIOUS AND LOAD-BEARING: it must NOT be written
    `role={isLink ? "link" : undefined}`. I read mergeProps.js: mutablyMergeInto
    is Object.assign semantics, so an OWN key with value undefined DELETES Base
    UI's role="button". That is precisely the mechanism wallow-web's
    `role={undefined}` workaround exploited. Writing it the ternary way passes
    specs 1/2/5/6 and silently breaks 3 and 4 (a composed <div> would announce as
    nothing). The red set's overshoot guards catch this exact slip.

Base UI merge order re-verified on disk, not taken from the red note:
useButton.js getButtonProps ends `mergeProps(handlers, isNativeButton ?
{type:'button'} : {role:'button'}, focusableWhenDisabledProps, otherExternalProps)`
and Button.js passes `props: [elementProps, getButtonProps]`, so props given to
BaseButton land in otherExternalProps and win; useRenderElement merges the render
element's OWN props last, which is why spec 5's role="menuitem" beats us from the
caller's side.

=== SITE INVENTORY: RE-DERIVED, 9 CONFIRMED, ONE BEAD CLAIM CORRECTED ===

description:
Every commit of the alias/tsconfig-paths work lives only on `refactor/alias-tsconfig-paths`
(worktree `~/Repos/Wallow-alias-research`). This phase gets it onto `main` so the zone-alias
layout, the zone-DAG guard, the SSR QueryClient fix (Wallow-ka3m) and the `*.server.*` import-
protection convention (Wallow-v940) are the trunk state rather than a side branch.

## Branch state at filing

8 commits, oldest first:

```
c88f5b39 build: pin typescript once in a tooling catalog and upgrade to 7.0.2
799b8a74 refactor(web): resolve zone aliases from tsconfig paths natively
3f601487 refactor(web): drop the alias map and its mirror-lock spec
2ebeca31 refactor(auth): resolve zone aliases from tsconfig paths natively
1dd961f5 test: derive the zone-DAG guard's zones from tsconfig paths
b350075a docs: describe the tsconfig `paths` alias declaration
e5a63659 fix(web,auth): keep one React Query instance in the SSR bundle
4aadcd88 fix(apps): name server-only modules *.server.* so import protection fires
```

All 8 are pushed to `origin/refactor/alias-tsconfig-paths`.

## MEASURED: there are no conflicts today

`main` has not moved since the branch left it. Verified at filing time:

- `git merge-base origin/main HEAD` = `1585962c` = `git ls-remote origin refs/heads/main`
- `git rev-list --left-right --count origin/main...HEAD` = `0	8` (main 0 ahead, branch 8 ahead)
- `git merge-base --is-ancestor origin/main HEAD` exits 0

So the rebase is a no-op and the merge is a fast-forward. Whoever picks this up should
RE-MEASURE those three commands first rather than trusting this paragraph — if `main` has
advanced by then, work the conflicts; if it has not, do NOT invent a rebase that git says is
unnecessary. There is no open PR and `main` carries no branch protection.

## Where conflicts would land if main has moved

The branch's diff is concentrated and easy to predict:

- `apps/wallow-{web,auth}/tsconfig.json` — `paths` added; a change touching either app's
  compiler options collides here.
- `apps/wallow-{web,auth}/vite.config.ts` and `vitest.config.ts` — `resolve.tsconfigPaths`,
  the new `ssr.noExternal` block, the rewritten `importProtection` comment, and the per-project
  `resolve` repetition in the vitest `test.projects` entries. The vitest landmine matters when
  merging: a root-level `resolve` is NOT inherited by `test.projects`, so a conflict resolution
  that collapses the duplication builds fine and fails the suite.
- `apps/wallow-{web,auth}/src/zone-dag.test.ts` and `src/server-only-naming.test.ts` — both
  files are BYTE-IDENTICAL across the two apps by design. Any conflict resolution must keep
  them identical; `cmp` the pair before committing.
- File renames — `wallow-web/src/app/lib/bff.ts` -> `bff.server.ts` and
  `wallow-auth/src/shared/lib/api-passthrough.ts` -> `api-passthrough.server.ts` (specs too).
  A rename/edit conflict is the likeliest real one; take the branch's rename and re-apply
  main's edit on top.
- Deleted files — `aliases.ts` and `alias-map.test.ts` in both apps. A modify/delete conflict
  resolves in favour of the delete.
- `apps/CLAUDE.md`, `apps/wallow-web/README.md`, `docs/development/frontend-setup.md`,
  `docs/integrations/{typescript-sdk,integration-cookbook}.md`.

## Steps

1. `git fetch origin`, then re-run the three divergence commands above and record what they say.
2. If `main` moved: `git rebase origin/main` and resolve. If it did not: skip to 3.
3. `pnpm --filter @bc-solutions-coder/sdk build` (apps typecheck against `dist/`), then
   `pnpm check` — the one-command gate (format:check, lint, typecheck, test, build,
   check:exports). It exits 0 on the branch as filed; it must still exit 0 after landing.
4. `./scripts/e2e.sh`. EXPECT 4 wallow-auth failures from **Wallow-0tor** (P0, open): the API's
   `SendEmailCommand` throws `Wolverine.Configuration.InvalidServiceLocationException`, no mail
   reaches Mailpit, and the forgot-password/reset specs time out. That failure reproduces on
   `main` and is untouched by this branch — do NOT treat it as a landing regression, and do not
   let it block the merge. Note that `e2e.sh` bails after the first failing suite, so the two
   wallow-web suites need a manual re-run against the kept stack
   (`E2E_KEEP_STACK=1`, then `E2E_BASE_URL=http://localhost:5053`).
5. Land it. Default to a PR (`gh pr create`) so CI and release-please see it the normal way;
   a direct fast-forward push is only acceptable if the user says so.
6. Confirm `git status` reports up to date with origin, then clean up the
   `~/Repos/Wallow-alias-research` worktree.

## Do not

- Do not `git add` anything under `docs/plans/` — it is gitignored.
- Do not force-push `main`.
- Do not resolve a conflict by reintroducing `aliases.ts`, an inline query key, or a
  `@tanstack/react-query` import outside `packages/query` — each is separately lint- or
  spec-enforced and would fail step 3 anyway.

title: wallow-auth /login throws 'No QueryClient set' during SSR
description: Booting apps/wallow-auth/.output/server/index.mjs and requesting / (307 -> /login) logs: 'Error in renderToReadableStream: Error: No QueryClient set, use QueryClientProvider to set one' from useClientBranding -> useQuery inside LoginRoute. The response is still HTTP 200 / 6604 bytes because React falls back past the failed SSR subtree, but the login screen is not server-rendered. PRE-EXISTING at c88f5b39 — confirmed by stashing an unrelated change and rebuilding the baseline, which produces the identical error and identical chunk hashes (login-CQMy6x8h.mjs, QueryClientProvider-BNsUFlg0.mjs). Likely the same linked-facade duplication that vitest.config.ts's extraBrowserOptimizeDeps works around for tests: LoginRoute's useClientBranding reads a QueryClient from a react-query copy the provider did not set. Not reproducible in the test suite (57 files / 1085 tests green), so only a booted bundle or E2E catches it. Found while migrating aliases to tsconfig paths; unrelated to that work.
notes: Fixed on refactor/alias-tsconfig-paths (e5a63659). Root cause: Vite externalizes every SSR dep EXCEPT linked ones, so @bc-solutions-coder/query (a workspace link) arrived BUNDLED carrying react-query, while @tanstack/react-router-ssr-query stayed external and Nitro bundled it with a SECOND react-query. Two createContext calls -> setupRouterSsrQueryIntegration installed the provider from its copy while components read the facade's -> 'No QueryClient set' under SSR. Fix: ssr.noExternal = ['@tanstack/react-router-ssr-query','@tanstack/react-query'] in both apps' vite.config.ts. Verified on a booted .output/server/index.mjs: 1 context, 0 errors, SSR body 6604 -> 13320 bytes with login-email/login-password/login-submit present. wallow-web carried the same split but never surfaced it (its SSR routes are public and query-free). vitest cannot catch this class of bug: it never builds the Nitro bundle.

title: Wolverine codegen frame-chain error kills every email notification handler
description:
Every Wolverine handler that resolves a service by METHOD INJECTION fails at
runtime with a JasperFx codegen error, so no notification email is ever sent.

## Symptom

Discovered by `./scripts/e2e.sh` — four wallow-auth E2E specs fail identically,
all waiting on a mail that never arrives at the test Mailpit (`:8035`, which
reports `{"total":0}` for the whole run):

- `e2e/magic-link.spec.ts` — "Your Magic Link"
- `e2e/otp-login.spec.ts` — "Your Login Code"
- `e2e/reset-password.spec.ts` — "Password Reset Request"
- `e2e/mfa.spec.ts` (totp enrollment) — "Verify your email address"
  (`mfa.spec.ts` totp challenge is then skipped as a dependent)

The other 25 wallow-auth specs pass, as do both wallow-web suites and the
cross-app login journey, so the OIDC path and the passthrough are fine — it is
only the notification pipeline.

## Root cause

`docker logs wallow-test-wallow-api-1`:

    System.InvalidOperationException: Frame chain is being re-arranged, tried to
    set JasperFx.CodeGeneration.Services.ScopedContainerCreation as the 'Next'
    property on JasperFx.CodeGeneration.Services.LazyServiceLocationFrame
      at Wallow.Notifications.Application.EventHandlers
         .EmailVerificationNotificationHandler.Handle(...)
      at Internal.Generated.WolverineHandlers
         .EmailVerificationRequestedEventHandler1042315412.HandleAsync(...)

The envelope retries, fails three times, and is moved to the error queue. The
publisher (Identity) logs success — "Email verification requested for ..." — so
nothing surfaces at the API boundary and the failure is invisible to the caller.

`EmailVerificationNotificationHandler.Handle` takes its dependencies as method
parameters (`IEmailTemplateService`, `IMessageBus`), which is exactly the
service-location codegen path `7435f7cc refactor(api): opt tenant context and
setup checker into wolverine service location` and `0a3aff83 fix(api): register
fluentvalidation validators once per command` changed. Every notification event
handler is shaped the same way, which is why all four mail subjects are missing
rather than one.

## Not a frontend issue

Found while gating `refactor/slice-0-app-zones`, which touches zero files under
`api/` (`git diff --stat main...HEAD -- api/` is empty), so the API container is
built from unmodified `main` sources. Pre-existing on main.

## Repro

    ./scripts/e2e.sh          # or E2E_SKIP_IMAGE_BUILD=1 E2E_KEEP_STACK=1 ...
    curl -s http://127.0.0.1:8035/api/v1/messages     # -> {"total":0,...}
    docker logs wallow-test-wallow-api-1 2>&1 | grep -B3 NotificationHandler

Reproduced twice, deterministically.

## Fix direction

Check what the two service-location commits did to the generated frame chain for
method-injected handler parameters — a `LazyServiceLocationFrame` should not be
receiving a `ScopedContainerCreation` as its `Next`. Worth checking the
JasperFx.CodeGeneration / Wolverine version pairing at the same time.

The integration tests do not catch this because the failure only appears in the
runtime-generated handler; a spec that invokes the handler method directly never
exercises the codegen path.
notes:
AUDIT 2026-08-02 (docs/audits/2026-08-02/0824-bead-backlog) — VERDICT: MERGE INTO Wallow-0tor. NOT CLOSED YET; closure is branch-gated, inherited from Wallow-0tor.

This bead and Wallow-0tor are one codegen failure on one handler rendered as two beads. Both frames trace to SendEmailHandler's constructor (SendEmailHandler.cs:14-19): ITenantContext opted into Wolverine service location at Wallow.Api/Program.cs:205 (the LazyServiceLocationFrame) and INotificationPreferenceChecker resolving to an internal type (the ScopedContainerCreation).

This bead's own 'method injection' diagnosis is FALSIFIED — the dependencies in question are constructor-injected, not method parameters.

Everything worth keeping has been copied onto Wallow-0tor, including the one surviving observation (the codegen path is untested) and the correction that the blamed commit 7435f7cc is NOT innocent: git log -S shows it removed ServiceLocationPolicy.AllowedButWarn (set by fac60500) and installed NotAllowed, making it causally central. This bead blamed the right commit for the wrong reason.

WHY IT IS STILL OPEN: closure inherits Wallow-0tor's gate. The fix is verified on feat/multi-org-membership (f62c2214) but main (7450cf73) still carries the internal class. Close this as a duplicate of Wallow-0tor once that branch merges to main, and after the Wolverine codegen regression-guard bead is filed.
CLOSED 2026-08-02 as a DUPLICATE of Wallow-0tor. One codegen failure on one handler (SendEmailHandler's constructor), filed twice: this bead saw the frame-chain error, 0tor saw the InvalidServiceLocationException. This bead's 'method injection' diagnosis was falsified — the dependencies are constructor-injected.

Fixed by f62c2214 on feat/multi-org-membership. Prevention carried forward by Wallow-qi90.1.

title: useAppForm: add TError generic so generated SDK mutation factories are assignable
description: useAppFormOptions.mutation is typed UseMutationOptions<TData, unknown, TVars>, but every generated SDK mutation factory returns UseMutationOptions<TData, DefaultError, TVars>. These are not assignable because TError is contravariant in onError, producing a hard TS2322 at every real call site. packages/forms' own tests only ever pass a hand-made { mutationFn }, so the gap was never covered. Wallow-ov6w.4.1 shipped a local workaround (destructuring mutationFn and passing mutation: { mutationFn }); .4.2 and .4.3 hit the same wall. Full diagnosis is on the Wallow-ov6w.4.1 bead note.
design: Thread a TError generic through useAppForm / UseAppFormOptions (defaulting so existing call sites keep compiling) so a generated SDK factory's UseMutationOptions is directly assignable. Add package-level test coverage that passes a REAL generated SDK mutation factory, not a hand-made { mutationFn } — the absence of that coverage is why this shipped broken.
acceptance_criteria: 1. A generated @bc-solutions-coder/sdk/query {operation}Mutation() result is assignable to useAppForm's mutation option with no cast and no destructuring workaround. 2. packages/forms has a test exercising a real generated mutation factory end-to-end. 3. The Wallow-ov6w.4.1 workaround in wallow-web is removed and that form uses the full mutation object (preserving its onSuccess wiring). 4. forms + wallow-web tests, typecheck, lint, format, build all pass.
notes:
RED (packages/forms lane, worktree /Users/traveler/Repos/Wallow-forms @ feat/forms-package).

NEW FILE (only file touched, nothing else in the repo):
  packages/forms/src/form/use-app-form.sdk-mutation.test.tsx  (4 cases)
Naming follows the sibling lanes' *.forms.test.tsx / *.sdk-mutation.test.tsx convention; it sits
beside the existing use-app-form.test.tsx, which is NOT edited.

*** HOW THE RED IS OBSERVED — READ THIS FIRST ***
The gap is COMPILE-TIME ONLY (TS2322 assignability), so the red signal is the package's
typecheck gate, not the vitest runner:

  pnpm --filter @bc-solutions-coder/forms typecheck     # tsc --noEmit, part of `pnpm check`

RED, verified just now:
  BEFORE the new file: tsc --noEmit exit 0 (clean).
  AFTER  the new file: exit 1 with EXACTLY 2 errors, both TS2322, both on the `mutation:` line
  of a harness, each for the intended reason (read from the messages, not just the count):

  1. src/form/use-app-form.sdk-mutation.test.tsx(134,5) TS2322
     UseMutationOptions<CreateOrganizationResponse, Error, Options<OrganizationsCreateData>>
       not assignable to UseMutationOptions<CreateOrganizationResponse, unknown, ...>
       -> 'onError' incompatible -> "Type 'unknown' is not assignable to type 'Error'."
  2. src/form/use-app-form.sdk-mutation.test.tsx(170,5) TS2322
     UseMutationOptions<AppRegistrationResponse, ProblemDetails, Options<AppsRegisterData>>
       not assignable to ... , unknown, ...>
       -> 'onError' incompatible -> "Type 'unknown' is not assignable to type 'ProblemDetails'."

  i.e. exactly the contravariant-TError diagnosis on Wallow-ov6w.4.1, reproduced inside the
  package that owns the bug. No collateral errors: TData and TVariables ALREADY infer correctly
  from the factory (CreateOrganizationResponse / Options<OrganizationsCreateData> appear in the
  message), so `data.organizationId` and the `toVariables` bodies all typecheck today. TError is
  the only broken slot.

HOW GREEN IS CONFIRMED:
  1. pnpm --filter @bc-solutions-coder/forms typecheck  -> exit 0 with the test file UNEDITED
     (no `as`, no `as any`, no `{ mutationFn }` destructuring, no re-annotation may be added to
     it — that is the whole point of the file; acceptance criterion 1).
  2. pnpm --filter @bc-solutions-coder/forms test       -> 15 files / 104 tests pass.
  3. pnpm --filter @bc-solutions-coder/forms build, oxlint --deny-warnings, oxfmt --check.

RUNTIME STATE TODAY (deliberate, not a miss): all 4 cases PASS already — vitest transpiles via
esbuild and never typechecks, and there is no runtime defect (the workaround was type-only).
They are still load-bearing: they are acceptance criterion 2 (the package had ZERO coverage of a
real generated factory), and they lock the behaviour the TError fix must not disturb. Baseline
re-verified both ways: without the file 14 files / 100 tests pass + tsc clean; with it 15 files /
104 tests pass + tsc fails with the 2 errors above.

WHAT THE 4 CASES DO (end to end, real chain, one stand-in):
Real createWallowSdk({ baseUrl: "/api", fetch: recordingStub }) — so the client carries its REAL
CSRF + RFC 7807 error interceptors — real generated operation, real AppForm/TextField/FormError/
SubmitButton shell, real QueryClient, headless Chromium. The ONLY stand-in is the transport: a
fetch that RECORDS the outgoing request (method/path/JSON body) and answers it. Assertions are on
the HTTP call the SDK genuinely made and the WallowError it genuinely raised — nothing is mocked,
no jsdom, no vi.mock, @bc-solutions-coder/ui untouched.
  1. organizationsCreateMutation success: POST /api/v1/identity/organizations with body
     { name: "Acme", domain: null } (proves toVariables + the generated operation really ran),
     onSuccess receives the parsed { organizationId: "org-1" }, no banner.
  2. organizationsCreateMutation blocked by the zod schema: field message "Name is required" at
     organization-create-name-error AND transport.sent is EMPTY (no HTTP call at all).
  3. appsRegisterMutation success: POST /api/v1/identity/apps/register, 201 ->
     onSuccess gets clientId.
  4. appsRegisterMutation 400 RFC 7807: real problem-details body with
