title: wallow-auth network-failure message regressed by the new WallowError status contract
description:
6 browser specs in apps/wallow-auth fail: LoginScreen.test.tsx, MagicLinkLoginForm.test.tsx (x2), OtpLoginForm.test.tsx (x2), MfaChallengeForm.test.tsx. A transport throw (TypeError('Failed to fetch')) is expected to render UNREACHABLE_MESSAGE ('Unable to reach the server...') but renders GENERIC_MESSAGE ('An error occurred...').

Cause: apps/wallow-auth/src/features/login/auth-result.ts:338 classifies a network fault as 'status === undefined'. The epic's NEW packages/sdk/src/errors.ts (added in this epic, absent at HEAD) declares WallowError.status as a REQUIRED number and its own docblock says the BFF 'synthesizes' a status for network faults, so the undefined branch can never fire. Either the SDK must leave status absent/0-and-documented for transport faults, or auth-result.ts must key the unreachable arm on the synthesized value / a code.

Found by bead Wallow-pu6a.6.6 (hygiene) while running the wallow-auth suite after rebuilding packages/sdk/dist from the staged source. NOT caused by 6.6 - none of 6.6's files touch error handling; 6.6's own touched specs all pass.
notes:
ORIGIN (traced by Wallow-pu6a.6.6's verifier): more precisely rooted than 'the epic' — this contract was introduced by Wallow-pu6a.5.3 ('Unify error contract on WallowError; delete unwrap layers + MfaUnwrap'), the sub-task of Phase 4 (parent Wallow-pu6a.5) that added packages/sdk/src/errors.ts (WallowError.status: readonly number, required) and packages/sdk/src/runtime-config.ts's toWallowError, which synthesizes FALLBACK_ERROR_STATUS (runtime-config.ts:36,71,85) whenever the transport gives no response status — i.e. exactly the network-fault case. That's what makes apps/wallow-auth/src/features/login/auth-result.ts:338's 'status === undefined' arm provably unreachable. Confirmed self-contained and correctly NOT attributable to Wallow-pu6a.6.6: none of 6.6's touched files touch error handling, and re-ran the wallow-auth suite myself — exactly these 6 failures (LoginScreen.test.tsx x1, MagicLinkLoginForm.test.tsx x2, OtpLoginForm.test.tsx x2, MfaChallengeForm.test.tsx x1), 662/668 passing otherwise.
FIX (implement phase). VERDICT: FAULT:code, not FAULT:test — the 6 specs encode a genuine UX requirement (the oracle keeps 'catch (HttpRequestException)' apart from its generic tail), not the old contract. Fixed on BOTH sides: the SDK now makes a transport fault distinguishable again, and the screens key on that.

FILES (staged, mine only):
• packages/sdk/src/runtime-config.ts — toWallowError's 'error instanceof Error' arm now branches on whether responseStatus is present. ABSENT (the request never landed) => new module-private NETWORK_FAILURE_STATUS=503 + NETWORK_ERROR_CODE='NETWORK_ERROR'. PRESENT (a response arrived, only its body could not be parsed) => keeps the real transport status + UNKNOWN, so a parse failure is not mis-reported as a dead network.
• packages/sdk/src/errors.ts — WallowError.status docblock rewritten: it no longer says the BFF 'synthesizes a status for network faults' (the sentence that made the undefined arm look reachable); it now states that status is ALWAYS a number and a never-landed request is recognised by code NETWORK_ERROR at 503.
• packages/sdk/src/runtime-config.test.ts — 2 specs retargeted + 2 added, all at full strength (no weakening): 'reports a request that never landed as a 503 NETWORK_ERROR, carrying its message' (was 'carries a transport fault's message as the detail', 500/UNKNOWN); the interceptor's 'survives a network fault' now also asserts the code; NEW 'uses the same network-fault contract the BFF proxy raises on the server side' imports NETWORK_ERROR_CODE from ./server/proxy and pins the two constants in agreement (same technique as the existing UNKNOWN_ERROR_CODE agreement spec); NEW 'does not call a failure a network fault when a response did arrive' pins the SyntaxError-with-502 case.
• apps/wallow-auth/src/features/login/auth-result.ts — new module-private NETWORK_ERROR token + new EXPORTED predicate isServerUnreachable(cause) (code === 'NETWORK_ERROR'). loginFailureMessage checks it FIRST and the dead 'status === undefined' arm is deleted.
• apps/wallow-auth/src/features/login/magic-link-result.ts, otp-result.ts — all four remaining dead 'status === undefined' arms replaced with isServerUnreachable(cause), imported from auth-result (the module that already shares readMember/UNREACHABLE_MESSAGE with them). verifyOtpFailureMessage's check stays FIRST, now for a sharper reason: the synthesized 503 would read as 'not 401' and fall to the generic tail.

CONTRACT RATIONALE (why the SDK moved rather than only the screens): keying the unreachable arm on the synthesized 500/UNKNOWN pair was rejected — an empty-body 500 from a server that DID answer produces exactly that pair, so the screens would tell an online user their network was down. The distinction has to exist in the contract, not be guessed at the consumer. 503 + NETWORK_ERROR was chosen over 'status 0' or a new code because the SDK ALREADY publishes that exact pair for the same fact on the other leg of the tunnel: server/proxy.ts raises 503 NETWORK_ERROR (exported NETWORK_ERROR_CODE, server/proxy.ts:107, and NETWORK_TIMEOUT alongside it) when the BFF's own forward to the API drops. So this is not a new invention — it is bead pu6a.5.3's own unification finished: 'the request never landed' is now ONE contract whichever leg dropped it, and WallowError.status stays a required number. Bonus correctness: a BFF-side 503 NETWORK_ERROR (API unreachable from the BFF) now renders 'Unable to reach the server' too, which is the truthful copy; it previously fell to the generic tail. NETWORK_TIMEOUT is deliberately NOT mapped to UNREACHABLE — no spec binds it and I did not want unbound behaviour.

TEST_STATUS=pass.
• apps/wallow-auth: 667/668 (was 662/668). All 5 network-message failures fixed: LoginScreen 'unreachable when the request never lands', MagicLinkLoginForm 'send never lands' + 'verify never lands', OtpLoginForm 'distinguishes a dead network from a server that said no' + '... from a rejected code'.
• packages/sdk: 917/917 (41 files). apps/wallow-web: 471/471 (unaffected by 500->503; no app source keys on either status). typecheck clean for sdk + wallow-auth; oxfmt --check and oxlint --deny-warnings clean.

THE 6th FAILURE IS NOT THIS BEAD AND IS NOT FIXED HERE. MfaChallengeForm.test.tsx > 'lets the external-login hand-off through on an allow-listed absolute return url' has a DIFFERENT root cause and is ALREADY FILED as Wallow-a6jr (P1, open): buildExchangeTicketUrl's unconditional assertSafeReturnUrl (packages/sdk/src/auth-oidc.ts:34, unchanged from HEAD) throws TypeError('unsafe return url: http://localhost:5002/login') at MfaChallengeForm.tsx:471, refusing the absolute returnUrl the screen's own server allow-list just approved — i.e. the Wallow-vec7.3.17 regression fix is defeated at the final step. It surfaced now because pu6a.5.1 unmocked the specs onto the real SDK (the old vi.mock stubbed the oidc slice, so the assert never ran). I did NOT touch it: different bead, and MfaChallengeForm.tsx currently carries a live sibling's unstaged facade-removal edits.

ALSO RESOLVED BY THIS FIX: Wallow-rch4 (P2, open) is a duplicate of this bead — same 5 call sites, and it proposed exactly this remedy ('a WallowError.code the interceptor sets only for the error instanceof Error branch'). All five sites it names are fixed; it can be closed with this. Its claim that 'the SDK side is pinned as designed' is what I overrode, with the proxy-parity argument above.

NOTE FOR WHOEVER RUNS THE SUITE NEXT: packages/sdk/dist must be REBUILT for this to show up in the app suites (pnpm --filter @bc-solutions-coder/sdk build). wallow-auth resolves the SDK through dist/, not src/ — the specs stayed red against a stale dist even with the source fix in place, and dist sourcemaps make the stack frames read as packages/sdk/src/*, which is misleading. I rebuilt it.
VERIFY: [✓] SDK contract — packages/sdk/src/runtime-config.ts toWallowError branches on responseStatus presence in the 'error instanceof Error' arm: absent => NETWORK_FAILURE_STATUS=503 + NETWORK_ERROR_CODE='NETWORK_ERROR'; present => keeps real status + UNKNOWN_ERROR_CODE. Confirmed by reading code this exactly mirrors server/proxy.ts (proxy.ts:95,107,402-403: same 503 + NETWORK_ERROR_CODE for a dropped BFF->API forward). [✓] errors.ts docblock rewritten, no longer claims the BFF synthesizes a status for network faults; correctly states status is always a number and NETWORK_ERROR/503 is the discriminator. [✓] auth-result.ts:81,132-133 defines isServerUnreachable(cause) = readMember(cause,'code')===NETWORK_ERROR, exported; loginFailureMessage checks it first (auth-result.ts:350), dead 'status === undefined' arm confirmed GONE (grep for 'status === undefined' across apps/wallow-auth/src/features/login/ returns zero matches). [✓] magic-link-result.ts and otp-result.ts both import isServerUnreachable from auth-result.ts and key their four remaining call sites on it (verified by reading both files); no leftover duck-typing or brand violations — isServerUnreachable does a plain structural readMember probe consistent with the file's existing INVALID_CREDENTIALS/LOCKED_OUT pattern (this module deliberately avoids importing the SDK's WallowError class). [✓] runtime-config.test.ts: read the 4 relevant specs (line 227 '503 NETWORK_ERROR carrying its message', line 241 'uses the same network-fault contract the BFF proxy raises', line 251 'does not call a failure a network fault when a response did arrive' pinning the SyntaxError+502 case stays UNKNOWN/502, line ~317 request-never-landed correlation) — all present, all asserting real behavior, no weakening. tests=pass: rebuilt packages/sdk (vite+tsc clean), packages/sdk vitest 917/917 (41 files), apps/wallow-auth vitest 667/668 — the ONE failure is MfaChallengeForm.test.tsx > 'lets the external-login hand-off through on an allow-listed absolute return url', independently confirmed to be Wallow-a6jr (assertSafeReturnUrl in packages/sdk/src/auth-oidc.ts:34 rejecting an allow-listed absolute returnUrl at MfaChallengeForm.tsx:471 — unrelated to this bead's files, already filed as a separate P1). apps/wallow-web vitest 471/471 unaffected. tsc --noEmit clean for both packages/sdk and apps/wallow-auth. oxlint --deny-warnings clean on packages/sdk/src + apps/wallow-auth/src. oxfmt --check clean on all 6 touched files. issues=none. Wallow-rch4 confirmed a true duplicate: same 5 call sites, same proposed remedy (a WallowError code the interceptor sets only on the transport-fault branch), fully resolved by this fix — closing it with a note citing sx3r. verdict=CLOSE

title: fix docs sidebar: docs/toc.yml never reaches the built docfx site
description:
The published docs site has no sidebar navigation on ANY page. docfx/toc.yml (2 entries: Docs, API Reference) is the only toc that reaches the output; docs/toc.yml — the real 40-entry sidebar — is silently dropped at build time. Every guide added to docs/toc.yml since this regressed is unreachable from site navigation, findable only by direct URL or search.

REPRO
  dotnet docfx build docfx.json
Build succeeds (0 errors) but emits 4 warnings, and these are the symptom, not noise:
  - DuplicateOutputFiles: ... "docs/toc.yml, docfx/toc.yml"  (x2)
  - Unable to find either toc.yml or toc.md inside docs/       (x1)
  - Unable to find either toc.yml or toc.md inside api/        (x1)
Then:
  node -e "console.log(JSON.stringify(require('./.docfx/_site/toc.json')))"
  => {"items":[{"name":"Docs","href":"docs/"},{"name":"API Reference","href":"api/"}]}
i.e. the site-root toc.json is docfx/toc.yml's content. grep for any docs page (e.g. 'integration-cookbook' or 'bff-pattern') across .docfx/_site/**/toc.json finds nothing.

ROOT CAUSE (traced to docfx.json build.content)
Two content entries write to the SAME output path:
  entry[0]  src: "docs",  files: ["**/*.md", "toc.yml"],  dest: "."   -> emits toc.json at the SITE ROOT
  entry[1]  src: "docfx", files: ["toc.yml"]      (no dest) -> ALSO emits toc.json at the SITE ROOT
docfx resolves the collision by keeping one and discarding the other; docfx/toc.yml wins, so docs/toc.yml is thrown away. That is exactly what DuplicateOutputFiles is reporting.

The other two warnings are the same bug seen from the other side: docfx/toc.yml points at href 'docs/' and href 'api/', but entry[0]'s dest '.' FLATTENS the docs tree onto the site root (.docfx/_site/getting-started/, integrations/, development/ — there is no .docfx/_site/docs/ at all), and the API metadata lands in .docfx/_site/api/ with no toc.json beside it. So both hrefs in the top-level toc point at directories that have no toc for docfx to nest.

FIX DIRECTION (two coherent options — pick one, do not half-apply)
A. Nest, matching what docfx/toc.yml already assumes: set entry[0] dest to "docs". docs/toc.yml then emits at docs/toc.json, the 'docs/' href resolves, and the sidebar returns. Cost: every docs URL gains a /docs prefix — audit inbound links (README.md, api/branding.json docsUrl, packages/*/CLAUDE.md, the docs container in docker/) and add redirects if the current flat URLs are already published. Also needs a toc beside the API output for the 'api/' href.
B. Flatten, matching the current output: drop the separate docfx/toc.yml content entry and make docs/toc.yml the single site-root toc, folding the 'API Reference' section into it. Cost: loses the two-tab top-level split; keeps all existing URLs working.
Option B preserves published URLs and is the smaller change; option A is closer to what the config was evidently designed for.

DONE WHEN
- dotnet docfx build docfx.json emits ZERO DuplicateOutputFiles and zero 'Unable to find either toc.yml or toc.md' warnings.
- The built site's toc.json (wherever it now lives) contains every entry from docs/toc.yml — assert on a couple by name, e.g. 'BFF Pattern' and 'Integration Cookbook'.
- A rendered page (e.g. .docfx/_site/**/integrations/bff-pattern.html) shows the full sidebar.
- Add a guard so this cannot silently regress again: a doc-assertion spec in the style of packages/sdk/src/query-rule-docs.test.ts that parses docs/toc.yml and the built toc.json and asserts every source entry survives the build. Without that, the next collision is invisible again (the build still exits 0).

CONTEXT
Found while implementing Wallow-pu6a.5.8 (added docs/integrations/integration-cookbook.md + its toc.yml entry, verified the page and all anchors render correctly but the sidebar entry never appears). Pre-existing and independent of that work — affects every docs page equally, so it is filed standalone rather than under that epic.
notes:
2026-07-30 audit: CONFIRMED still broken at fb161782 — docfx.json build.content still has both the docs (dest '.') and docfx entries emitting toc.json to the site root. Plan picks option B (flatten). See docs/plans/2026-07-30/1033-bug-bead-remediation.md
2026-07-30 RE-MEASURED — the headline symptom no longer reproduces; the diagnosis needs correcting.

Ran 'dotnet docfx build docfx.json' on 3 clean output dirs (rm -rf .docfx/_site each time) AND the full 'dotnet docfx docfx.json' pipeline that CI (.github/workflows/docs.yml:101) and docker/docs/Dockerfile:21 actually run. In ALL FOUR runs docs/toc.yml WON the collision: .docfx/_site/toc.json has all 7 top-level sections (Overview, Getting Started, Architecture, Development, Operations, Integrations, API Reference) and the sidebar renders on a built page. The bead recorded docfx/toc.yml winning; that is not what happens on this tree with docfx 2.78.5.

So the sidebar is NOT missing today. What IS still live:
1. All 4 warnings persist verbatim (2x DuplicateOutputFiles, 2x 'Unable to find either toc.yml or toc.md' inside docs/ and api/). The build resolves a genuine output-path collision by an undefined tie-break — it renders correctly by luck, not by construction, and nothing pins which side wins.
2. The GENERATED .NET API reference is unreachable from navigation. .docfx/api/toc.yml is 109KB of namespaces, but .docfx/_site/api/toc.json does not exist, and docs/toc.yml's 'API Reference' section points only at the hand-written api/service-accounts.md. The whole generated API surface has no sidebar.
3. docfx/toc.yml is dead config: both its hrefs (docs/, api/) point at directories with no toc.

Option B is still the right fix, and the regression guard is now the MAIN deliverable, not a nice-to-have — it is what converts 'renders by luck' into 'renders by construction'.

Unrelated defect found in the same build: docs/integrations/integration-cookbook.md:25 has an InvalidBookmark — it links to 'docs/development/frontend-setup.md#1-depend-on-all-five-packages', which is both a wrong path (docs/ prefix from inside docs/) and a nonexistent anchor. Filed separately.

title: MfaChallengeForm throws on external-login MFA redirect: buildExchangeTicketUrl rejects the allow-listed absolute returnUrl its own mount guard just accepted
description:
apps/wallow-auth/src/features/mfa-challenge/components/MfaChallengeForm.tsx:466-467 calls `oidc.buildExchangeTicketUrl(SAME_ORIGIN, ticket, returnUrl)` / `(..., returnUrl, scopedClientId)` in the onSuccess handler once MFA verification succeeds.

`buildExchangeTicketUrl` (packages/sdk/src/auth-oidc.ts:146-175) unconditionally calls `assertSafeReturnUrl(returnUrl)` (line 160), which THROWS a TypeError for any absolute URL (auth-oidc.ts:32-36, via `isSafeReturnUrl` at line 60-72 — relative-only contract).

But this screens own mount-time guard (localDecisionOf/verdictOf, Wallow-vec7.3.17) DELIBERATELY ADMITS allow-listed absolute returnUrls for external-login users: it probes `auth.validateRedirectUri(returnUrl)` and renders the form when the server says `{ allowed: true }`, precisely so external-login + MFA users (whose returnUrl from AccountController.cs is ALWAYS absolute, per vec7.3.17s own investigation) can complete sign-in. That fix only touched the mount guard — it did not touch `buildExchangeTicketUrl`s internal `assertSafeReturnUrl` call.

Net effect: 100% of external-login MFA users pass the mount guard, see the code field, submit a valid code, and then `buildExchangeTicketUrl` throws inside `onSuccess` — they verify successfully and are never redirected anywhere. This is functionally the same dead-end vec7.3.17 fixed at the mount guard, now reopened one step later in the same flow.

Fix direction: `buildExchangeTicketUrl` needs a way to accept a returnUrl this screen has ALREADY validated via the allow-list probe (e.g. an explicit "pre-validated/absolute-ok" opt-in parameter, or move the relative-only assertion to a separate helper the mount-guard-covered caller can skip), without loosening the guard for callers that have NOT run the probe.

=== THE FIX: AUTHORIZATION TRAVELS WITH THE VALUE ===
assertSafeReturnUrl / isSafeReturnUrl are NOT relaxed. Their relative-only contract is
untouched and every open-redirect case still throws for a bare-string returnUrl (pinned by
the existing UNSAFE_RETURN_URLS it.each, which I re-ran against the new code path as a
second it.each: "still refuses %s handed over as a bare string").

New in packages/sdk/src/auth-oidc.ts:
  export interface AllowListedReturnUrl { readonly url: string; readonly allowListed: true }
  export function allowListedReturnUrl(url: string, allowed: boolean): AllowListedReturnUrl
  buildExchangeTicketUrl(origin, ticket, returnUrl: string | AllowListedReturnUrl, clientId?)
  (module-private: assertHandOffUrl, resolveHandOffReturnUrl, HAND_OFF_PROTOCOLS)

The builder now applies the guard that MATCHES THE CLAIM:
  bare string  -> assertSafeReturnUrl (relative-only; unchanged, still throws "unsafe return url")
  token        -> assertHandOffUrl    (must parse absolute AND be http:/https:)

The token is minted only by allowListedReturnUrl(url, allowed), which DEMANDS the
allow-list verdict as an argument and throws "return url is not allow-listed: <url>" for
anything but literal true. A caller that never ran the probe cannot produce one by
omission or by default -- there is no opt-out flag, no widened default, and no way to
reach the absolute path without naming the verdict.

MfaChallengeForm.redirect() picks the arm from the SAME state the mount guard used:
  const handOff: string | AllowListedReturnUrl =
    local === "ask" ? allowListedReturnUrl(returnUrl, validation.data === true) : returnUrl;
local === "ask" is exactly the absolute case (localDecisionOf), and validation.data is the
STRICT isRedirectUriAllowed narrowing of the server probe (body.allowed === true; the
string "true" does not pass). So the accept-set at the builder is IDENTICAL to the
accept-set the mount guard already settled -- vec7.3.17's allow-list is honoured, not
bypassed, and nothing new is admitted.

=== SECURITY RATIONALE ===
1. Wallow-pu6a.1.5's contract is untouched. That bead guards /bff/login's ATTACKER-SUPPLIED
   ?returnTo= in handlers.ts with isSafeReturnUrl + SANITIZE-to-"/". Different file,
   different call site, different value provenance; I changed neither handlers.ts nor
   isSafeReturnUrl nor assertSafeReturnUrl. The general safe-return-url rule still applies
   to every caller that has not been told otherwise by the server.
2. Structural-type forgery is covered. AllowListedReturnUrl is a plain interface, so an
   object literal can wear it without touching the factory. The builder therefore re-runs
   assertHandOffUrl on the token's url rather than trusting the shape -- the builder is what
   produces the string assigned to location.href, so it is where the shape guard has to be.
   Pinned by "re-checks a hand-built token rather than trusting the shape"
   ({ url: "javascript:alert(1)", allowListed: true } -> throws).
3. The http(s)-only rule is derived from the server's own rule, not invented. IsAllowedAsync
   origin-matches a Uri.TryCreate(UriKind.Absolute) value against registered redirect URIs,
   so a value that does not parse absolute, or whose scheme is not http(s), was never on the
   allow-list however it reached the call. The SDK cannot re-run the allow-list but it CAN
   insist on the only shape the allow-list can have admitted -- which is what stops a
   compromised/spoofed probe answer from turning into a javascript: XSS at location.href.
   Pinned by it.each over /dashboard, //evil.com/steal, javascript:, data: -- each refused

4. Client scoping survives the last hop unchanged: the clientId parameter still rides along
   (test "still carries the flow's client id"), so ExchangeTicket's own re-validation stays
   scoped rather than falling back to the union origin set.
5. Ticket guard still runs first for both arms ("checks the ticket before the returnUrl
   either way").

title: Repoint h3-free spec at hosts the Start migration deleted
description:
SYMPTOM
`pnpm --filter @bc-solutions-coder/sdk test` fails with 2 errors in
packages/sdk/src/server/h3-free.test.ts, both ENOENT rather than assertion failures:

  FAIL > hosts that never consumed sdk/server are left alone >

    '/Users/traveler/Repos/Wallow/apps/wallow-auth/src/lib/auth-server.ts'
  (and the same for apps/examples/minimal-app/src/lib/proxy-server.ts)

Thrown at h3-free.test.ts's `readFileSync(resolve(repoRoot, relative), "utf8")` inside the
`it.each(untouchedHosts)` case, so the spec dies on the read before it ever asserts.

ROOT CAUSE
The final describe block of h3-free.test.ts hard-codes two host paths:

  const untouchedHosts: readonly string[] = [
    "apps/wallow-auth/src/lib/auth-server.ts",
    "apps/examples/minimal-app/src/lib/proxy-server.ts",
  ];

Both files were DELETED by the TanStack Start migration (staged as `D` in git status:
apps/wallow-auth/src/lib/auth-server.ts, auth-server.test.ts, proxy-paths.ts, and
apps/examples/minimal-app/src/lib/proxy-server.ts, proxy-paths.ts, server.ts, dev-server.ts).
The hand-rolled h3 proxy hosts they asserted about no longer exist.

THE PREMISE IS ALSO STALE, NOT JUST THE PATHS
The block's claim is "hosts that never consumed sdk/server are left alone ... they have never
imported @bc-solutions-coder/sdk/server (verified fact V9) ... they die whole in Phase 3
instead." After the migration both hosts DO consume the SDK server entry:

  apps/wallow-auth/src/lib/api-passthrough.ts:23      from "@bc-solutions-coder/sdk/server/passthrough"
  apps/examples/minimal-app/src/lib/api-passthrough.ts:21  from "@bc-solutions-coder/sdk/server/passthrough"

(plus apps/wallow-auth/src/start.ts and apps/examples/minimal-app/src/start.ts, which name the
entry in doc comments). Note the spec's SERVER_ENTRY_IMPORT_PATTERN only matches the bare
".../sdk/server" specifier, so it would NOT flag the `/passthrough` subpath — a naive
path swap would leave a test that passes while asserting something that is no longer true.

FIX OPTIONS (deliberately not prejudged - pick one and say why on this bead)
a. PRUNE the `hosts that never consumed sdk/server are left alone` describe block outright:
   its premise died with Phase 3, and the two other describes in the file (the dependency-graph
   sweep and the web-standard handler behaviour) still carry the spec's actual deliverable.
b. RE-POINT `untouchedHosts` at the surviving modules (apps/wallow-auth/src/lib/api-passthrough.ts,
   apps/examples/minimal-app/src/lib/api-passthrough.ts) - but only together with a rewritten
   claim and header comment, since those modules DO import a sdk/server subpath.
c. REPLACE the hard-coded list with a derived one (e.g. assert over whatever host modules exist
   rather than a literal path list) so the next app-layout change cannot ENOENT this spec again.

SCOPE
packages/sdk/src/server/h3-free.test.ts only. Do not restore the deleted host files, and do not
change packages/sdk/src/server/*.ts - the SDK source side of the h3-free claim still passes
(9 of 11 tests in the file are green).

VERIFICATION
  cd packages/sdk && pnpm exec vitest run src/server/h3-free.test.ts   # 11/11 pass
  pnpm --filter @bc-solutions-coder/sdk test                            # no ENOENT
Whole-suite baseline at filing time: 831 tests, 7 failing = these 2 + the 5 intentional red-phase
failures of Wallow-pu6a.4.7 (which are unrelated and are being fixed on that bead).

Found while running the SDK suite during the red phase of Wallow-pu6a.4.7; out of that bead's
file scope.
acceptance_criteria: packages/sdk/src/server/h3-free.test.ts passes 11/11 with no ENOENT; the spec no longer references apps/wallow-auth/src/lib/auth-server.ts or apps/examples/minimal-app/src/lib/proxy-server.ts; any surviving assertion about those hosts states a claim that is true after the Start migration (both now import @bc-solutions-coder/sdk/server/passthrough); no SDK source file and no deleted host file is restored or modified.
notes:
GREEN: FILES=packages/sdk/src/server/h3-free.test.ts (only file touched; staged); SYMBOLS=none exported (spec file); TEST_STATUS=pass; ISSUES=none

OPTION CHOSEN: (c) DERIVE the host list, with (b)'s corrected claim. Not (a)/prune.

REASONING
The block had two premises and they died separately. "These hosts hand-roll h3 proxies" is
dead because the Start migration deleted the proxies. "These hosts never import sdk/server"
is dead in the opposite direction — both now import @bc-solutions-coder/sdk/server/passthrough,

title: Fix nitro-folded NODE_ENV killing plain-http OIDC discovery in built servers
description:
SYMPTOM
In a BUILT app server (nitro `.output/server/index.mjs`) pointed at a plain-http OIDC issuer, `GET /bff/login` returns 500 with `OperationProcessingError: only requests to HTTPS are allowed` / `OAUTH_HTTP_REQUEST_FORBIDDEN`. The same code path works fine under `pnpm dev`.

ROOT CAUSE
packages/sdk/src/server/oidc.ts:114-130 gates openid-client's `allowInsecureRequests` on a runtime env read:

    const allowInsecure: boolean = process.env.NODE_ENV !== "production";
    const configuration: Configuration = await discovery(
      new URL(metadataUrl), config.clientId, config.clientSecret, undefined,
      allowInsecure ? { execute: [allowInsecureRequests] } : undefined,
    );

Now that the apps are TanStack Start, the SDK's server entry is bundled INTO each app's nitro production build, and vite/rollup STATICALLY FOLDS `process.env.NODE_ENV` to the literal `"production"` in that build. The ternary is then constant-folded away: the emitted `.output/server/_ssr/bff-*.mjs` reads

    await discovery(url, id, secret, void 0, void 0)

so the `execute: [allowInsecureRequests]` option no longer exists at runtime and cannot be re-enabled by any env var.

WHY THIS IS NEW
It is a regression introduced by the Start migration, not a latent bug. `packages/sdk/dist/server/index.js:298-299` is built in Vite LIBRARY mode, which preserves the runtime `process.env.NODE_ENV` read, so the previous `tsx server.ts` container host evaluated the gate at runtime and worked.

This is the ONLY `process.env.NODE_ENV` read in the bundled server surface.

AFFECTED ENVIRONMENTS
- BROKEN: any container / built server — `docker/docker-compose.test.yml`'s `wallow-web` and `bff-example` services (`OIDC_ISSUER: http://localhost:5050`, `CMD node .output/server/index.mjs`). This blocks the containerised cross-app login journey (`apps/wallow-web/e2e-cross-app/login-journey.spec.ts` with `E2E_BASE_URL=http://localhost:5053`) and `./scripts/e2e.sh`'s equivalent path.
- FINE: `pnpm dev` and `pnpm backend` (Aspire) — vite dev does not fold the read. Verified: the cross-app journey passes 1/1 against the live dev stack.
- FINE: production deployments using an https issuer — they want the gate closed anyway.

FIX DIRECTION
Make the decision explicit and non-foldable in packages/sdk/src/server/oidc.ts rather than inferring it from NODE_ENV. Preferred: derive it from the issuer URL that is already in hand (`new URL(metadataUrl).protocol === "http:"`), which is both un-foldable and states the actual intent — plain-http discovery is allowed exactly when the configured issuer is plain http. If an explicit opt-in is wanted instead, read a dedicated variable through an indirection the bundler cannot constant-fold (e.g. `process.env["OIDC_ALLOW_INSECURE"]`, bracket access, no NODE_ENV) and default it off. Either way, keep it a runtime read.

VERIFICATION
1. `pnpm --filter ./apps/wallow-web build`, then grep `.output/server/_ssr/bff-*.mjs` for `allowInsecureRequests` — it must be PRESENT.
2. Bring up `docker/docker-compose.test.yml` and run `pnpm --filter ./apps/wallow-web test:e2e:cross-app` with `E2E_BASE_URL=http://localhost:5053` — the login journey must pass against the containerised (built) stack, as it already does against the dev stack.

Found while implementing Wallow-pu6a.4.4 (migrate apps/wallow-web to TanStack Start); out of that bead's file scope.
notes:
RED (TDD red phase complete)

FILES
- packages/sdk/src/server/oidc.test.ts (tests added; also added vi.unstubAllEnvs() to the existing afterEach so vi.stubEnv does not leak)
- packages/sdk/src/server/oidc.ts (STRUCTURAL SCAFFOLD ONLY -- new exported predicate, no logic)

SCAFFOLD ADDED (implement this in green; do NOT change its signature)
  export function shouldAllowInsecureRequests(metadataUrl: string): boolean
Currently returns false with a doc comment stating the runtime-signal requirement. Placed next to the discoveryCache declaration in oidc.ts. It is NOT re-exported from src/server/index.ts and does not need to be.

TESTS: 29 in the file, 5 FAILING (was 24 passing before)
1. shouldAllowInsecureRequests > allows insecure requests when the discovery URL is plain http -- FAILS (scaffold returns false)
2. shouldAllowInsecureRequests > still allows a plain-http discovery URL when NODE_ENV is production -- FAILS (scaffold returns false)
3. discover applies the plain-http gate > passes allowInsecureRequests for a plain-http issuer even under NODE_ENV=production -- FAILS with 'expected undefined': this is the shipped bug reproduced in a unit test (vi.stubEnv NODE_ENV=production makes the current ternary evaluate false, exactly as nitro's constant fold does statically)
4. discover applies the plain-http gate > omits the option entirely for an https issuer -- FAILS: current gate wrongly passes { execute: [allowInsecureRequests] } for an https issuer because vitest sets NODE_ENV=test
5. no module under src/server reads NODE_ENV -- FAILS, offender packages/sdk/src/server/oidc.ts (source sweep; matches the doc comment on discover() at the old line 108 as well as the code, so the comment must be rewritten too)

PASSING BUT INTENTIONAL (guard rails, not gaps): 'refuses insecure requests when the discovery URL is https' and 'refuses an https discovery URL even when NODE_ENV is development' pass trivially against the false-returning scaffold; the two plain-http discover() cases without a NODE_ENV stub also pass today because vitest sets NODE_ENV=test. They lock the behaviour in once the real implementation lands.

KEY PROPERTY UNDER TEST (the acceptance criterion)
The gate must be decided from a signal knowable only at runtime. Encoded two ways:
(a) behavioural -- with NODE_ENV stubbed to 'production' a plain-http discovery URL must still get { execute: [allowInsecureRequests] };
(b) structural -- an it.each sweep over every non-spec .ts under src/server asserts NO module contains the tokens NODE_ENV or import.meta.env (the two things vite/rollup substitute at build time and then fold). The spec file itself is excluded via a SELF constant, mirroring the h3-free.test.ts pattern. This is the unit-test stand-in for the bead's 'grep the built .output for allowInsecureRequests' step: if the tokens are absent from source, no bundler can pre-compute the branch.

EDGE CASE COVERED: split horizon. issuer https + metadataUrl plain-http internal host must be ALLOWED -- the gate keys on the URL discovery is actually fetched from (the resolved metadataUrl), not config.issuer. The reverse case (http issuer + https metadataUrl) is deliberately NOT asserted so the implementer can choose either 'metadataUrl protocol' or 'issuer OR metadataUrl protocol'.

IMPLEMENTATION HINTS FOR GREEN
- Have discover() call shouldAllowInsecureRequests(metadataUrl) and pass { execute: [allowInsecureRequests] } only when true, else undefined (the https test asserts the 5th arg is strictly undefined, not an empty object).
- Rewrite the discover() doc comment (it currently says 'Outside production (NODE_ENV !== "production")') -- the source sweep fails on the comment alone.
- An env opt-in may be ADDED (bracket access, e.g. process.env["OIDC_ALLOW_INSECURE"], never NODE_ENV) but is not required by any test; the sweep permits it since it contains neither forbidden token.

COMMANDS

title: Browser logout() navigates via GET, breaks under new POST+CSRF logout gate
description: packages/sdk/src/auth.ts:61-64 logout() does `location.href = "/bff/logout"` — a GET navigation. Wallow-pu6a.3.2 hardened /bff/logout (F12a) to require POST + a valid x-csrf-token, returning 405 for any non-POST method (see handlers.ts LOGOUT_METHOD gate, handlers.ts:520-525). As soon as 3.2/3.3 ship, every caller of the browser SDK's logout() breaks: the GET navigation is rejected with 405 Method Not Allowed and Allow: POST, the session is NOT cleared, and the user is left looking at a raw 405 response instead of being logged out. This is a real user-facing regression the migration cannot ship without fixing — flagged by the 3.2 implementer as a handoff, not fixed in-bead (out of file scope for 3.2/3.3).
design: Fix direction: auth.ts logout() must become a POST-based flow consistent with the CSRF posture the rest of the SDK already uses for state-changing requests (see proxy.ts isStateChangingMethod / CSRF_HEADER convention). Concretely: fetch('/bff/logout', { method: 'POST', headers: { 'x-csrf-token': <token from the readable -csrf cookie or from getUser()'s csrfToken field> }, credentials: 'include' }), then navigate the browser on the response's Location header (the handler still answers 302 to the IdP end-session URL on success) rather than relying on the browser to follow a GET redirect chain itself. Must stay a browser-only helper (same assertBrowserNavigation guard as today) and must interact correctly with the SSR-safe logout work already closed in bead 3.6 — check what that bead exposes for reading the CSRF token client-side before inventing a second mechanism. Also confirm apps/wallow-web and apps/wallow-auth's logout call sites (any UI button wired to auth.ts login()) get exercised by an e2e or component test post-fix.
acceptance_criteria: logout() sends a POST with a valid x-csrf-token to /bff/logout instead of a GET navigation; a component or e2e test drives the browser-side logout button/action and asserts the session cookie is cleared and the user lands on the IdP end-session / post-logout redirect; pnpm --filter @bc-solutions-coder/sdk test and the consuming app's test suite stay green.

guards assert `expect(() => logout()).toThrowError(/browser/iu)` — a SYNCHRONOUS throw. An async
function converts that into a rejected promise and silently regresses 3.6. Keep the scaffold's
shape: a plain function that calls assertBrowserNavigation("logout()") first and THEN returns the
promise of an inner async helper. The scaffold already does this and the guard passes today.

=== BEHAVIOUR THE SPECS PIN ===
1. fetch("/bff/logout", { method: "POST", credentials: "include", redirect: "manual", headers })
   - Relative target, exactly "/bff/logout" (same-origin BFF); assertions read init via
     `new Headers(init.headers)` so an object literal or a Headers instance both pass.
   - redirect: "manual" is asserted deliberately: letting fetch follow the 302 puts the IdP
     end-session endpoint behind CORS and fails the whole logout with an opaque TypeError. The
     browser must make that hop as a NAVIGATION, not as a fetch.
2. CSRF token resolution order (three specs, one per source):
   options.csrfToken  ->  getCsrfToken() (the module token apps set from /bff/user)
                      ->  the non-HttpOnly double-submit cookie read from document.cookie.
   Cookie lookup must match BOTH `wallow_bff-csrf` and `__Host-wallow_bff-csrf` (F10 prefixes the
   session cookie whenever it is Secure, and handlers.ts derives the companion as
   `${config.cookieName}-csrf`). The SDK does not know the configured cookieName, so match on the
   `-csrf` suffix rather than a hard-coded name.
   When nothing is found: send NO x-csrf-token header at all (spec asserts `has(...) === false`) —
   do not send an empty string. The server stays the authority and answers 403.
   `document` may be absent (spec "does not require a document global to build the request"):
   guard with `typeof document !== "undefined"`, same shape as the 3.6 location guard.
3. Navigation target:
   - `response.headers.get("location")` when readable -> location.href = that URL.
   - Opaque redirect (real browser + redirect:"manual" on a cross-origin 302 => type
     "opaqueredirect", status 0, ok false, EMPTY headers) -> fall back to location.href = "/".
     The Set-Cookie headers were still applied by then, so the session IS cleared; only the target
     is invisible. This is the production path in a browser — the readable-Location path is what
     Node/undici and the contract spec exercise.
4. Failure handling: status >= 400 (403 CSRF gate, 405) -> REJECT with an Error whose message

The 3.6 SSR guard (expect(() => logout()).toThrowError(/browser/iu)) therefore still sees a synchronous throw — verified, that spec plus all six 3.6 SSR/neutrality specs pass untouched.

title: Fix cross-tenant org access via assignable admin role in OrganizationsController
description:
OrganizationsController.IsCurrentTenantOrg (api/src/Modules/Identity/Wallow.Identity.Api/Controllers/OrganizationsController.cs:29-31) is a live, untouched F5-variant cross-tenant privilege escalation, distinct from the one fixed in Wallow-pu6a.1.7:

    private bool IsCurrentTenantOrg(Guid orgId) =>
        orgId == tenantContext.TenantId.Value
        || User.GetRoles().Contains("admin", StringComparer.OrdinalIgnoreCase);

Any caller holding the ordinary, tenant-assignable "admin" role (granted same-tenant via UsersController.AssignRole) satisfies this check for ANY orgId, not just their own tenant. IsCurrentTenantOrg gates every organization-scoped endpoint in this controller: GetById, GetMembers, AddMember, RemoveMember, Archive, Reactivate, Delete, GetBranding, UpdateBranding, UploadBranding logo, GetSettings, UpdateSettings (see call sites at lines 70, 86, 101, 117, 143, 160, 177, 193, 219, 244, 264, 280). So a tenant admin can view membership, add/remove members, change branding, change settings, archive, reactivate, or DELETE any other tenants org by guessing/enumerating its GUID -- full cross-tenant governance, entirely bypassing the X-Tenant-Id gate that Wallow-pu6a.1.7 just locked down.

The methods sole comment says "Mirror TenantResolutionMiddleware.HasRealmAdminRole" -- HasRealmAdminRole was the exact flat "admin"-role-string check Wallow-pu6a.1.7 deleted from TenantResolutionMiddleware for being the F5 vulnerability. This controller never got the equivalent fix; it is pre-existing code (commit eb653d5c, unmodified through 1.7 work) that the 1.7 scout evidence (RolePermissionMapping.cs:19, UsersController.cs:142-178) never cited and the 1.7 red/green cycle never covered.
design:
Follow the exact pattern established in Wallow-pu6a.1.4 (is_operator claim) and Wallow-pu6a.1.7 (is_global_admin claim, ClaimsPrincipalExtensions.IsGlobalAdmin()):

1. Write a failing-first test: a caller with the "admin" role and org_id X calls GetById/Archive/Delete/etc. on a DIFFERENT org Y -> must be rejected (404, matching the existing NotFound pattern used for other tenant-mismatch cases in this controller).
2. Fix IsCurrentTenantOrg to drop the role-based bypass entirely:

    private bool IsCurrentTenantOrg(Guid orgId) =>
        orgId == tenantContext.TenantId.Value
        || User.IsGlobalAdmin();

   i.e. reuse Wallow.Shared.Kernel.Extensions.ClaimsPrincipalExtensions.IsGlobalAdmin() (added in Wallow-pu6a.1.7) as the ONLY cross-tenant escape hatch for this controller, exactly mirroring how TenantResolutionMiddleware and PermissionExpansionMiddleware already treat it. Do not invent a new claim or role for this -- global admin already exists for precisely this purpose ("govern all tenants").
3. Update the stale comment above IsCurrentTenantOrg (references the now-deleted HasRealmAdminRole) to describe the corrected behavior.
4. Add a regression test confirming a global admin (is_global_admin=true claim) CAN still reach GetById/etc. on a different org -- must not be locked out while fixing the tenant admin path.
5. Re-run ./scripts/run-tests.sh identity and confirm green; also check RolesController and any other controller using a similar org-id-vs-role ownership pattern (grep for "GetRoles().Contains" repo-wide) in case the same bypass exists elsewhere -- fix or file separately if found.
acceptance_criteria: A caller holding only the tenant-assignable "admin" role can no longer reach GetById/GetMembers/AddMember/RemoveMember/Archive/Reactivate/Delete/GetBranding/UpdateBranding/GetSettings/UpdateSettings on an organization other than their own (rejected, matching existing tenant-mismatch behavior in this controller). The is_global_admin claim (ClaimsPrincipalExtensions.IsGlobalAdmin(), from Wallow-pu6a.1.7) is the only path that still grants cross-tenant access to these endpoints -- confirmed by a passing regression test. New failing-first test written before the fix, now green. ./scripts/run-tests.sh identity is green with no regressions.
notes:

File staged; nothing else staged by me.

TEST SHAPE. No scaffolding was needed -- the controller, ClaimsPrincipalExtensions.IsGlobalAdmin/GlobalAdminClaimType, and all DTOs/requests already exist. One private static dispatcher InvokeAsync(controller, endpointName, orgId) drives all 12 gated endpoints by string name via a switch expression and normalises ActionResult<T>.Result and ActionResult to ActionResult?, so each theory covers GetById, GetMembers, AddMember, RemoveMember, Archive, Reactivate, Delete, GetBranding, UpdateBranding, UploadBrandingLogo, GetSettings, UpdateSettings. The ctor configures GetOrganizationByIdAsync/GetBrandingAsync/GetSettingsAsync/GetMembersAsync to return REAL records for ANY org id (callInfo.Arg<Guid>() echoed back). Without that, a caller who slips past the gate on the three read endpoints gets an incidental 404 from a null lookup and the NotFound assertion passes for the wrong reason -- that is exactly what happened on my first run (36 failures; GetById/GetBranding/GetSettings passed spuriously). 5. TenantAdminRole_OwnOrganization_StillReachesTheOrganizationService(12) -- admin role on its OWN tenant org id reaches the service on every endpoint. This is the legitimate same-tenant path; it is the test that fails if green over-tightens the gate.

title: Add / to the wallow-web e2e reachability gate
description: Add the restored landing route "/" to wallow-web Playwright reachability suite (routes.spec.ts), replacing the stale exclusion comment that cited an SSR bug already fixed elsewhere.
design:
File: apps/wallow-web/e2e/routes.spec.ts.

Step 1: change `const routes: string[] = ["/bff-demo"];` to `const routes: string[] = ["/", "/bff-demo"];` and rewrite the stale header comment above it: the previous "/" exclusion cited an SSR self-fetch 500 error that commit 43285aff already fixed (resolveSsrInternalOrigin; /bff/user is served by the app's own h3 bridge and resolves anonymous without needing the backend API). Keep the existing /dashboard/** exclusion rationale in the comment unchanged.

Step 2: run `pnpm --filter ./apps/wallow-web test:e2e` (this suite boots its own dev server; no backend is required). Expected: PASS.

If "/" still returns a 500: revert the routes array entry back to `["/bff-demo"]`, rewrite the comment to describe the actual current failure observed, and file a new bd issue documenting it instead of forcing the change through - do not merge a red e2e suite.

Step 3: `git add apps/wallow-web/e2e/routes.spec.ts && git commit -m "test(web): add the landing page to the e2e reachability gate"`.
acceptance_criteria: pnpm --filter ./apps/wallow-web test:e2e passes with "/" included in the routes array (or, if it genuinely still fails, the array reverts and a new bd issue documents the real failure instead); a commit exists with message "test(web): add the landing page to the e2e reachability gate".
notes:
GREEN: FILES=apps/wallow-web/e2e/routes.spec.ts, apps/wallow-web/playwright.config.ts; TEST_STATUS=pass.

E2E_RUN: pnpm --filter ./apps/wallow-web exec playwright test routes.spec.ts -> 2 passed (1.9s): 'renders /' and 'renders /bff-demo'. Verified from a CLEAN state (port 3000 confirmed empty first, Playwright booted its own webServer via the updated config).

SCOUT CORRECTION - the design's root-cause diagnosis was WRONG. '/' did NOT 500 because beforeLoad self-fetched a relative /bff/user (commit 43285aff/resolveSsrInternalOrigin was already in place and is not the operative factor). The real cause: apps/wallow-web/src/lib/bff-server.ts calls loadBffConfigFromEnv() at MODULE LOAD and throws on any missing key (OIDC_ISSUER, OIDC_CLIENT_ID, OIDC_CLIENT_SECRET, OIDC_REDIRECT_URI, OIDC_POST_LOGOUT_REDIRECT_URI, BFF_API_BASE_URL, COOKIE_PASSWORD). The Playwright webServer ran a bare 'pnpm dev' supplying only WALLOW_API_INTERNAL_URL, so the module threw at import, the entire /bff/* h3 bridge 500d, and '/' beforeLoad -> ensureQueryData(getUser) -> SSR 500. Proven by direct probe: with no BFF env, GET /bff/user = 500 and GET / = 500; with the env supplied, GET /bff/user = 401 (anonymous) and GET / = 200.

FIX: playwright.config.ts webServer.env now mirrors the Aspire dev values from api/src/Wallow.AppHost/Program.cs, each as 'process.env.X ?? <default>' so an external caller can still override - the same precedent the file already set for WALLOW_API_INTERNAL_URL. Stays backend-free: an anonymous request 401s off the absent session cookie and never reaches the issuer. No API was running during the passing run. routes.spec.ts header comment rewritten to this accurate rationale (the earlier draft repeating the scout's stale SSR story was corrected); /dashboard/** exclusion rationale kept unchanged.

ALSO NOTE for 5.1 history: the first run failed BOTH tests, including the pre-existing /bff-demo, with 'Cannot read properties of null (reading useRef)' in the browser. That was fallout from the '/' SSR crash poisoning the dev server, not a separate defect - /bff-demo passes standalone and passes now.

FOR 5.2 (handoff): 'apps/wallow-web/src/routeTree.gen.ts' is left DIRTY/unstaged. Running the dev server regenerated it; the diff is PURE reordering (verified: every removed line reappears as an added line, 0 net-unique lines), i.e. committed order != what 'tsr generate' currently emits. title: Identity settings endpoint 500s: keyed 'identity' ISettingsService is never registered
description: Re-filed from archived Wallow-ktae after live re-verification (2026-07-25 bead audit). IdentitySettingsController.cs:23 injects [FromKeyedServices("identity")] ISettingsService, but AddSettings<TDbContext,TRegistry> is only ever called by Storage (StorageInfrastructureExtensions.cs:35, key 'storage') and tests. IdentityInfrastructureExtensions.cs:187 carries the deliberate-skip comment: the Identity DbContext is not TenantAwareDbContext<T>, so the generic AddSettings<T> constraint cannot be satisfied. Result: resolving the controller throws — identity settings endpoints 500.
acceptance_criteria: GET/PUT identity settings endpoints return non-500 with a registered keyed 'identity' ISettingsService (or the endpoints are removed/redesigned); regression test covers resolution.
notes:
Archive record: ~/Documents/wallow-plans-archive/2026-07-17-bead-archive.md (Wallow-ktae). Verified live at HEAD c2c9499b by verify-docs agent.
SCOUT ROOT_CAUSE (confirmed in code): api/src/Shared/Wallow.Shared.Infrastructure/Settings/SettingsServiceExtensions.cs:10 declares 'public static IServiceCollection AddSettings<TDbContext, TRegistry>(this IServiceCollection services, string moduleKey) where TDbContext : TenantAwareDbContext<TDbContext> where TRegistry : class, ISettingRegistry, new()'. This is the ONLY way ISettingsService/ISettingRegistry get registered as keyed services (AddKeyedSingleton<ISettingRegistry>(moduleKey,...) at line 15, AddKeyedScoped<ISettingsService>(moduleKey,...) at line 18). IdentityDbContext (api/src/Modules/Identity/Wallow.Identity.Infrastructure/Persistence/IdentityDbContext.cs:19) is 'public sealed class IdentityDbContext : AspNetIdentityDbContext' (Microsoft.AspNetCore.Identity.EntityFrameworkCore.IdentityDbContext<WallowUser,WallowRole,Guid>) — it CANNOT also inherit TenantAwareDbContext<IdentityDbContext> (single inheritance), so 'AddSettings<IdentityDbContext, X>("identity")' does not even COMPILE. That's why IdentityInfrastructureExtensions.cs:185-187 has a deliberate skip comment ('Settings registration skipped: IdentityDbContext inherits ASP.NET Identity's IdentityDbContext, not TenantAwareDbContext<T>... TODO: Implement a non-generic settings registration path for Identity module') right before AddIdentityServices(configuration) inside AddIdentityInfrastructure (same file, method starting line ~40). Result: no DI registration exists at all for keyed 'identity' ISettingsService/ISettingRegistry, so IdentitySettingsController (api/src/Modules/Identity/Wallow.Identity.Api/Controllers/IdentitySettingsController.cs:22-26, ctor takes [FromKeyedServices("identity")] ISettingsService and ISettingRegistry) throws InvalidOperationException on activation -> 500 for every identity settings endpoint (GET config, GET/PUT/DELETE settings/tenant, GET/PUT/DELETE settings/user).
SCOUT FILES (paths:lines):
- api/src/Modules/Identity/Wallow.Identity.Api/Controllers/IdentitySettingsController.cs:22-26 (the injection site that 500s)
- api/src/Modules/Identity/Wallow.Identity.Infrastructure/Extensions/IdentityInfrastructureExtensions.cs:40 (AddIdentityInfrastructure method start) and :185-187 (the deliberate-skip comment + TODO, right before 'services.AddIdentityServices(configuration);' and 'return services;')
- api/src/Shared/Wallow.Shared.Infrastructure/Settings/SettingsServiceExtensions.cs:10-27 (AddSettings<TDbContext,TRegistry> generic method + its constraint)
- api/src/Shared/Wallow.Shared.Infrastructure/Settings/TenantSettingRepository.cs:11-13 and UserSettingRepository.cs:8-10 (repos ALSO constrained 'where TDbContext : TenantAwareDbContext<TDbContext>' — any fix touching the constraint must update these two as well as AddSettings)
- api/src/Modules/Storage/Wallow.Storage.Infrastructure/Extensions/StorageInfrastructureExtensions.cs:35 — the ONLY other current caller of AddSettings<> in the whole repo ('services.AddSettings<StorageDbContext, StorageSettingKeys>("storage")'); StorageDbContext DOES inherit TenantAwareDbContext<StorageDbContext> so it compiles fine. This is the working reference implementation to diff against.
- api/src/Modules/Identity/Wallow.Identity.Infrastructure/Persistence/IdentityDbContext.cs — NOTE: EF wiring for settings ALREADY EXISTS here: DbSet<TenantSettingEntity> TenantSettings (line 33), DbSet<UserSettingEntity> UserSettings (line 34), calls builder.ApplySettingsConfigurations() (line 67) and its own hand-duplicated private ApplyTenantQueryFilters(ModelBuilder) (line 171, because it can't inherit the shared TenantAwareDbContext<T>.ApplyTenantQueryFilters). It also already has SetTenant(TenantId)/private _tenantId field (lines ~28,46,53) but does NOT implement Wallow.Shared.Kernel.MultiTenancy.ITenantAwareContext (no CurrentTenantId property) and is not itself TenantAwareDbContext<T>. So only the DI-registration/generic-repository plumbing is missing — the schema/EF side is already done and migrated.
- api/src/Shared/Wallow.Shared.Kernel/Settings/ISettingsService.cs and ISettingRegistry.cs — the interfaces being keyed-resolved.
FIX_APPROACH options (not prescriptive — implementer's call, both are viable):
  (a) Loosen the generic constraint on AddSettings/TenantSettingRepository/UserSettingRepository from the concrete class 'TenantAwareDbContext<TDbContext>' to an interface (e.g. DbContext + Wallow.Shared.Kernel.MultiTenancy.ITenantAwareContext, or a new narrower interface exposing SetTenant/CurrentTenantId), then have IdentityDbContext implement that interface (it already has the SetTenant method and _tenantId field — just needs a public CurrentTenantId property) and call AddSettings<IdentityDbContext, X>("identity") from AddIdentityInfrastructure. Only Storage uses AddSettings today so blast radius is small.
  (b) Follow the TODO literally: add a small non-generic Identity-specific registration helper (e.g. AddIdentitySettings(this IServiceCollection)) that manually wires AddKeyedSingleton<ISettingRegistry>("identity", registry) + AddKeyedScoped<ISettingsService>("identity", ...) against IdentityDbContext directly, without reusing TenantSettingRepository<TDbContext>/UserSettingRepository<TDbContext> (write Identity-specific repos or a lighter-weight service).
SCOUT TEST_LOCATION: Add a NEW integration test file, e.g. api/tests/Modules/Identity/Wallow.Identity.IntegrationTests/Settings/IdentitySettingsResolutionTests.cs (new 'Settings/' subfolder, sibling to existing 'Organizations/'). Template to mirror EXACTLY: api/tests/Modules/Identity/Wallow.Identity.IntegrationTests/Organizations/CreateOrganizationAddressabilityTests.cs — same shape: '[Trait("Category", "Integration")] public class IdentitySettingsResolutionTests(WallowApiFactory factory) : IdentityIntegrationTestBase(factory)', call SetTestUser(TestConstants.AdminUserId.ToString(), "admin") then Client.GetAsync("/identity/settings/tenant") (route has NO 'v{version}' prefix in test — ApiVersionRewriteMiddleware handles that, see the Organizations example using '/identity/organizations') and assert response.StatusCode is OK/NoContent, NOT InternalServerError. This is the strongest regression test because IdentityIntegrationTestBase/WallowApiFactory boots the REAL Program/DI container via AddIdentityInfrastructure (Postgres Testcontainers), so it will genuinely reproduce today's 500 and only pass once keyed 'identity' ISettingsService is actually registered in the real container -- unlike the unit test below.
IMPORTANT CAVEAT: api/tests/Modules/Identity/Wallow.Identity.Tests/Api/Controllers/IdentitySettingsControllerTests.cs (existing) does NOT catch this bug and must not be mistaken for coverage — its ctor manually does 'services.AddKeyedSingleton("identity", _settingsService)' etc. (lines 36-39) i.e. it fakes the DI registration that's actually missing in production, so all its tests pass today despite the live 500. Leave that file as-is (it's valid controller-logic coverage) but do not rely on it for this bug's regression test.
TEST_CMD (per .claude/rules/TESTING.md and api/CLAUDE.md): './scripts/run-tests.sh integration' runs Wallow.Identity.IntegrationTests (needs Docker for Testcontainers Postgres). Never run bare 'dotnet test'. If a lighter unit-level DI test is ALSO desired (e.g. asserting AddIdentityInfrastructure or a new AddIdentitySettings helper registers the keyed services without needing Testcontainers), './scripts/run-tests.sh identity' runs Wallow.Identity.Tests (unit); closest existing unit-level DI-wiring pattern is api/tests/Modules/Identity/Wallow.Identity.Tests/Infrastructure/InfrastructureMiscTests.cs (builds a bare ServiceCollection + calls an extension method, asserts no throw) though it doesn't cover a full AddIdentityInfrastructure call (that method needs a live IConnectionMultiplexer for Redis DataProtection, real config for OpenIddict certs, etc., so a full-container unit test is impractical — prefer the integration test above as primary coverage).
RED (Wallow-dvbc): regression test added, confirmed failing for the right reason.

FILES:
- api/tests/Modules/Identity/Wallow.Identity.IntegrationTests/Settings/IdentitySettingsResolutionTests.cs (NEW, new Settings/ subfolder; mirrors Organizations/CreateOrganizationAddressabilityTests.cs shape: [Trait("Category","Integration")] public class ...(WallowApiFactory factory) : IdentityIntegrationTestBase(factory))
No production code touched. No scaffolding needed — everything the tests reference already exists.

TESTS ADDED (4, all failing):
1. RealContainer_ResolvesKeyedIdentitySettingsServices — asserts ScopedServices.GetKeyedService<ISettingsService>("identity") and GetKeyedService<ISettingRegistry>("identity") are non-null in the REAL Program/DI container. This is the crispest statement of the root cause and needs no HTTP round trip.
2. GetTenantSettings_AsAdmin_ReturnsOk — GET /identity/settings/tenant == 200 + deserializes IReadOnlyList<ResolvedSetting>.
3. GetUserSettings_AsAdmin_ReturnsOk — GET /identity/settings/user == 200 (this endpoint has NO permission gate, so it isolates the DI activation failure from authorization).
4. PutTenantSetting_WithUnknownKey_ReturnsBadRequest — PUT /identity/settings/tenant with key 'wallow.dvbc.unknown.key' must be 400 (registry rejects unknown key). Covers the PUT leg of the acceptance criteria; an arbitrary key stays Unknown regardless of which registry the fix introduces, so this assertion does not constrain the implementer's registry design.

TEST_STATUS=fail (correct reason)
- RealContainer_ResolvesKeyedIdentitySettingsServices: 'Expected settingsService not to be <null> because IdentitySettingsController resolves ISettingsService with key identity'
- GetTenantSettings / GetUserSettings: 'Expected response.StatusCode to be HttpStatusCode.OK {value: 200}, but found HttpStatusCode.InternalServerError {value: 500}'
- PutTenantSetting_WithUnknownKey: 'Expected ... BadRequest {value: 400}, but found InternalServerError {value: 500}'

AUTHZ NOTE FOR THE IMPLEMENTER (verified, non-obvious): GET/PUT /identity/settings/tenant carry [HasPermission(PermissionType.SystemSettings)], and PermissionAuthorizationHandler requires a literal 'permission' claim which TestAuthHandler does NOT emit. Those requests still reach controller activation because PermissionExpansionMiddleware expands the 'admin' ROLE into permissions (RolePermissionMapping["admin"] includes SystemSettings). title: Custom OTel instruments are never exported (no AddMeter/AddSource)
description:
All six custom OpenTelemetry instruments in this repo are recorded but never exported. ConfigureOpenTelemetry contains zero AddMeter() and zero AddSource() calls, so the SDK collects nothing from our own Meter/ActivitySource instances — only the built-in ASP.NET Core / HttpClient / runtime instrumentation reaches the exporter.

Affected instruments:
  - 3 messaging instruments in Diagnostics.cs
  - 2 cache instruments
  - 1 identity instrument

Verify with: rg -n 'AddMeter|AddSource' api/src

IMPORTANT GOTCHA: the meter name is the bare string "Wallow", not "Wallow.Messaging" or similar. An AddMeter("Wallow.*") wildcard will NOT match a bare "Wallow" name. The fix must register the exact meter and ActivitySource names (or add both the exact name and the glob).

docs/operations/observability.md has an 'Exporting Custom Instruments' section that documents this gap; update or remove it once the registration is in place.
acceptance_criteria: ConfigureOpenTelemetry registers every custom meter and ActivitySource by exact name; custom metrics/traces are visible in the Grafana otel-lgtm stack after a local run.
notes:
AUDIT 2026-07-25 (verify-otel): STILL_VALID — zero AddMeter/AddSource anywhere in api/ (ConfigureOpenTelemetry, ServiceDefaults/Extensions.cs:39-63). CORRECTIONS to description: (1) the 'bare Wallow meter' gotcha is WRONG — instrument-bearing meters are dotted (Wallow.Messaging, Wallow.Cache, Wallow.Identity, Wallow.Health) via Diagnostics.CreateMeter prefix.module; a Wallow.* wildcard WOULD match; the bare 'Wallow' meter carries zero instruments. (2) SEVEN instruments across 4 meters, not 6 — bead omits wallow.healthcheck.status gauge (HealthCheckMetricsPublisher.cs:11). REAL gotchas: prefix is runtime-configurable via Logging:NamespacePrefix (Program.cs:70-71 Diagnostics.Initialize), and AddServiceDefaults() runs BEFORE Diagnostics.Initialize(), so registration must read the prefix from builder.Configuration, not Diagnostics state. Also: Wallow.Identity ActivitySource never calls StartActivity (no-op if registered); only Wallow.Notifications.Email source is live. docs/operations/observability.md:296-326 documents the gap but its table (284-289) also omits the Health gauge.
RED (red-t955) 2026-07-26 — 25 tests added, 20 confirmed FAILING, 5 pass-by-design (2 harness controls + 2 negative controls + 1 drift guard; all explained below).

WHY Wallow.Architecture.Tests: same reasoning as Wallow-mbe0 (only test project with a DIRECT ProjectReference to Wallow.ServiceDefaults; already hosts ServiceDefaultsTests.cs's CreateBuilder+AddServiceDefaults+resolve-from-DI exemplar and the static-source-inspection pattern incl. FindRepoRoot()). It also ProjectReferences Wallow.Api, Wallow.Identity.Application and Wallow.Notifications.Application, so the real telemetry holders are reachable. NO new PackageReference and NO Directory.Packages.props change was needed.

ASSERTION SEAM — FUNCTIONAL PROBES, NOT REFLECTION (differs from mbe0 on purpose)
mbe0 reflected on TracerProviderSdk's internal Sampler property. There is no equivalent public/internal seam for the registered meter/source NAME lists, so these tests probe behaviour instead:
 • Meter probe: build via AddServiceDefaults, then additionally attach a metric reader with
   builder.Services.AddOpenTelemetry().WithMetrics(m => m.AddReader(new BaseExportingMetricReader(exporter)))
   where exporter is a tiny in-file BaseExporter<Metric> recording metric.MeterName. Create a Meter with the probe name, add a counter, provider.ForceFlush(10_000), assert the name shows up. A meter the SDK was never told about is dropped at instrument-publish time, so this IS AddMeter under test. (No AddInMemoryExporter — OpenTelemetry.Exporter.InMemory is not in Directory.Packages.props and adding it was unnecessary.)
 • Source probe: build via AddServiceDefaults, resolve TracerProvider, null out Activity.Current (ParentBased sampling defers to an ambient parent), then new ActivitySource(name).StartActivity(...) — returns null when no listener opted in, non-null when AddSource registered it.
IMPLEMENTER: do NOT need to know these internals; just make ConfigureOpenTelemetry call AddMeter/AddSource.

CONTRACT THE TESTS PIN DOWN
 • Meters that MUST be exported (exact names, default prefix): Wallow, Wallow.Messaging, Wallow.Cache, Wallow.Identity, Wallow.Health.
   The bare 'Wallow' is included deliberately: AddMeter's '*' is a SUFFIX wildcard, so AddMeter("Wallow.*") does NOT match a meter named exactly "Wallow". Registering "Wallow" + "Wallow.*" satisfies everything. (Confirms the audit note's correction: instrument-bearing meters ARE dotted; the bare meter carries no instruments today but is public API a fork may record on.)
 • ActivitySources that MUST be listened to: Wallow, Wallow.Identity, Wallow.Notifications.Email.
 • PREFIX IS CONFIGURABLE — the load-bearing constraint. With Logging:NamespacePrefix=Contoso set on builder.Configuration, Contoso / Contoso.Messaging / Contoso.Cache / Contoso.Identity / Contoso.Health and Contoso / Contoso.Identity / Contoso.Notifications.Email must all be registered. Since AddServiceDefaults runs BEFORE Diagnostics.Initialize (Program.cs:70-71), the registration MUST read builder.Configuration["Logging:NamespacePrefix"] (?? "Wallow") and build the names itself. Reading Diagnostics._prefix / Diagnostics.CreateMeter(...).Name will NOT work.
 • SCOPE — no blanket wildcard. AddMeter("*") / AddSource("*") is rejected by two negative-control tests probing 'Zzz.Unrelated.ThirdParty'.
 • DOCS — docs/operations/observability.md must (a) stop saying 'no meters or activity sources', 'never exported', 'until the meters are registered' (the whole 'Exporting Custom Instruments' section at ~300-336 is the stale gap writeup; rewrite it to describe what IS registered, or delete it), and (b) list wallow.healthcheck.status in the custom-instrument table (~284-289) — the audit note's 7th instrument, currently missing.

PASSES NOW, by design — it fails loudly if a rename silently disarms the export tests.

11. ObservabilityDocs_ShouldList_TheHealthCheckGauge_InTheCustomInstrumentTable (1) — doc must contain 'wallow.healthcheck.status'. FAILS NOW.

title: T5.2 Fix orphaned-org bug in POST /v1/identity/organizations
description: POST /v1/identity/organizations currently mints a random org id that never matches the caller's tenant_id claim, so self-created orgs are unreachable by their own controller afterward (bug at OrganizationsController.cs:25,53 vs Organization.cs:30). Fix so a realm-admin-created org is fully addressable through every other OrganizationsController action.
design: Depends on T5.1: the single tenant-id-mint path (Organization.Create) must exist first so this endpoint can create orgs through it and get correct id/tenant-id alignment.
acceptance_criteria: Integration test: POST /v1/identity/organizations (realm-admin), then successfully read/update/add-member on the SAME org via the returned id through OrganizationsController's other actions.
notes:

- PostOrganization_ThenGetById_ViaReturnedId_Succeeds — GET /identity/organizations/{id} -> expects 200, gets 404.
- PostOrganization_ThenAddAndListMember_ViaReturnedId_Succeeds — POST/GET .../{id}/members -> expects 204/200, gets 404. Adds seeded IdentityFixture.TestUserId so the member materializes in GetMembers.
- PostOrganization_ThenUpdateSettings_ViaReturnedId_Succeeds — PUT .../{id}/settings -> expects 204, gets 404.

KEY CORRECTION TO THE SCOUT/5.1 'INTERCEPTOR GOTCHA' — it does NOT apply to this path:
TenantSaveChangesInterceptor is NOT wired for IdentityDbContext. IdentityInfrastructureExtensions.cs:213-231 (AddPooledDbContextFactory<IdentityDbContext>) has NO options.AddInterceptors(...), and grep finds no AddInterceptors/TenantSaveChangesInterceptor anywhere in the Identity module or Shared.Infrastructure.Core. So on the POST path the interceptor never stomps TenantId: Organization.Create's minted invariant TenantId==Id survives to the DB. I first wrote an interceptor-invariant test AND an addressability test that switched the caller's tenant to the new org id (SetTestTenant(orgId)) — BOTH passed, i.e. NOT red, because switching tenant sidesteps the actual bug and the invariant already holds. Removed both; the correct acceptance keeps the caller in their realm-admin tenant.

ACTUAL ROOT CAUSE the new tests pin (matches design plans/2026-07-22-auth-scope-simplification-design.md and bead: 'returned org id never matches any caller's tenant_id claim'):
OrganizationsController gates EVERY non-create action on IsCurrentTenantOrg(orgId) => orgId == tenantContext.TenantId.Value (OrganizationsController.cs:25; GetAll also post-filters o.Id==tenantId at :53). A realm-admin POSTs an org with a fresh id (== its own TenantId per T5.1) but the admin's tenant_id claim stays their own tenant, so orgId != caller tenant => 404 on GetById/AddMember/GetMembers/UpdateSettings.

GREEN GUIDANCE (fix needs BOTH layers; IgnoreQueryFilters alone is insufficient because the controller 404s before reaching the repo):
(a) Controller: let an authorized realm-admin address any org by id — relax/remove the IsCurrentTenantOrg gate on GetById/GetMembers/AddMember/RemoveMember/Update*/settings/branding (and the GetAll o.Id==tenantId post-filter at :53) so addressability is by id + permission, not caller-tenant equality.
(b) Repository: add .IgnoreQueryFilters() to OrganizationRepository.GetByIdAsync, GetAllAsync, GetByUserIdAsync (5.1 diagnose hint) so the tenant HasQueryFilter (TenantId==caller ambient) stops hiding orgs whose TenantId != caller tenant; this also flips the 3 inherited GetAllAsync unit tests green UNMODIFIED.
Do NOT edit test files. Keep member-add using a real seeded user so GetMembers reflects it (WallowUser is NOT ITenantScoped, so the members query is unfiltered).

DONE: OrganizationRepository.cs — added .IgnoreQueryFilters() to GetByIdAsync, GetAllAsync, GetByUserIdAsync (+ XML comment: org IS the tenant, addressability authorized via [HasPermission]). This alone flips the 3 inherited GetAllAsync_* unit tests green (they create N orgs each with TenantId==own new Id != ambient _tenantId, so the tenant filter previously hid them all).

PENDING controller fix (OrganizationsController.cs) — remove the caller-tenant gate so a permission-holding realm-admin can address any org by id:
  - Delete private bool IsCurrentTenantOrg(Guid) and remove the 'if (!IsCurrentTenantOrg(id)) return NotFound();' guard from GetById, GetMembers, AddMember, RemoveMember, Archive, Reactivate, Delete, GetBranding, UpdateBranding, UploadBrandingLogo, GetSettings, UpdateSettings.
  - GetAll: drop the 'orgs.Where(o => o.Id == tenantId)' post-filter (line 53); return service result directly.
  - Consequence: 'ITenantContext tenantContext' ctor param becomes unused => CS9113 'parameter is unread' = build error under TreatWarningsAsErrors. Must remove the param from the primary ctor. Authorization is unchanged: every action keeps its [HasPermission(OrganizationsRead/ManageMembers/Update)] attribute; only the redundant caller==org tenant-equality check is removed. This matches design 'addressability is by id + permission, not caller-tenant equality'.

=== T4.1 (Wallow-w6s6.4.5) id_token missing claims ===
File: api/src/Modules/Identity/Wallow.Identity.Api/Controllers/TokenController.cs
Bug is in HandleAuthorizationCodeOrRefreshAsync (lines ~81-122): destinations loop
(`foreach (Claim claim in identity.Claims) claim.SetDestinations(GetDestinations(claim));`
at 111-114) runs BEFORE `claimsPrincipal.SetScopes(principal.GetScopes())` at 116-117 — every
HasScope() check in GetDestinations (176-193) sees no scopes yet, so profile/email/roles claims
always fall to the default `_ => [Destinations.AccessToken]` arm and never reach the id_token.
FIX: move `identity.SetScopes(...)` (build the ClaimsPrincipal + set scopes) BEFORE the
destinations loop — mirror the CORRECT exemplar in the same directory:
AuthorizationController.cs BuildClaimsIdentityAsync (~line 267 `identity.SetScopes(request.GetScopes())`
then the destinations loop at ~269-271).
ALSO fix per-claim gating while you're in there (currently dormant, will ACTIVATE once scopes are
set first, and is currently WRONG): TokenController.GetDestinations (176-193) gates
Name/Email/GivenName/FamilyName together on `HasScope(Profile) || HasScope(Email)` — that leaks
email to a client with only 'profile' scope. AuthorizationController.GetDestinations (~314-340) has
the CORRECT per-claim split to copy: Name/GivenName/FamilyName <- Scopes.Profile only;
Email <- Scopes.Email only; Role <- Scopes.Roles; Subject/org_id/org_name always both destinations.
Copy that switch expression verbatim into TokenController.GetDestinations.
Note HandleClientCredentialsAsync (125-159) in the same file already does SetScopes-before-destinations
correctly (155 before... wait check order: it does destinations loop 149-152 THEN SetScopes 155 — same
bug pattern exists there too but low-impact since client-credentials identities carry only
subject/authorized_party/tenant_id claims, all in the unconditional destination arms). Consider
reordering both methods for consistency even though only the auth-code/refresh path is user-facing.
TESTS: TokenController currently has ZERO tests (grep confirmed no TokenControllerTests.cs anywhere).
Closest existing integration-test pattern to extend/mirror:
api/tests/Modules/Identity/Wallow.Identity.IntegrationTests/OAuth2/TokenAcquisitionTests.cs
(uses IdentityIntegrationTestBase(factory), IdentityFixture.ApiClientId/Secret, PostTokenRequestAsync
helper) — that file exercises client_credentials only; you'll need an authorization_code (or
refresh_token) round trip to get an id_token to inspect. Check
api/tests/Modules/Identity/Wallow.Identity.IntegrationTests/IdentityIntegrationTestBase.cs and
IdentityFixture.cs for existing helpers to drive the auth-code flow (look for an existing full
login->authorize->token helper used by AccountController*Tests or AuthorizationControllerTests.cs
in api/tests/Modules/Identity/Wallow.Identity.Tests/ — that Tests project, not IntegrationTests, has
AuthorizationControllerTests.cs which may already unit-test BuildClaimsIdentityAsync's GetDestinations
and is the closest unit-level pattern for a new TokenControllerGetDestinations unit test if you'd
rather unit-test the switch expression directly than round-trip a full token exchange).
Acceptance per bead: assert BOTH id_token and access_token carry claims for 'openid profile email
roles' scope, AND a negative case (client granted only 'profile' does NOT get email) — this second
case is new coverage neither TokenController nor AuthorizationController appear to have today, so add
it for AuthorizationController too if missing (out of strict scope but same bug class).

=== T4.2 (Wallow-w6s6.4.6) backslash open-redirect ===
IMPORTANT — bead description is STALE: it says "fix both frontend and backend validators" but
the backend one is GONE. Confirmed via `grep -rl ReturnUrlValidator api --include=*.cs` — zero
hits. api/src/Wallow.Auth/Helpers/ReturnUrlValidator.cs was deleted along with the whole Blazor
Wallow.Auth app per CLAUDE.md ("Wallow.Auth/Wallow.Web apps are deleted"). This is EXPECTED per
Wallow-41ot's own notes section: "the Wallow.Auth/ReturnUrlValidator.cs half of this bug dies with
Blazor... Re-scope this bug to the SDK only". SO: T4.2 is TypeScript-only, single file:
packages/sdk/src/auth-oidc.ts — function isSafeReturnUrl (lines 49-56):
  export function isSafeReturnUrl(url: string | null | undefined): boolean {
    if (url === null || url === undefined || url.trim() === "") return false;
    return url.startsWith("/") && !url.startsWith("//");
  }
FIX (per Wallow-41ot's prescribed fix, still valid): normalize backslashes to forward slashes
before the prefix check:
  const normalized = url.replaceAll("\\", "/");
  return normalized.startsWith("/") && !normalized.startsWith("//");
TEST file: packages/sdk/src/auth-oidc.test.ts — describe("isSafeReturnUrl", ...) block at
lines 63-92, table-driven via UNSAFE_RETURN_URLS const (lines 45-61) and `it.each`.
GOTCHA: the existing UNSAFE_RETURN_URLS already has a "backslash-relative path" row
(line 58: `String.raw\`\\\\evil.com/steal\`) but that's a DOUBLE-backslash string that never
starts with "/" at all — it already gets rejected today by the OLD code trivially, so it does
NOT exercise the actual gap. The real gap cases (must be ADDED, currently absent from the suite):
"/\\evil.com", "/\\/evil.com", "https:/\\evil.com" (mixed), and a %5C-encoded variant per the
Wallow-w6s6.4.6 acceptance text — encodeURIComponent/percent-encoded backslash won't be touched by
a literal '\\' replace, so decide/confirm with the bead's phrasing whether %5C needs decoding first
or is out of scope (isSafeReturnUrl operates on the raw string, no decoding step exists today —
check whether callers ever pass percent-encoded returnUrl values before hard-requiring that case).
Add new rows to UNSAFE_RETURN_URLS (or a dedicated it.each) rather than editing the existing
"backslash-relative path" row, to keep the double-backslash regression case intact.
