title: F5. Tenant model honesty (Organization IS the tenant)
description: Currently there is no Tenant entity; a tenant IS an Organization only because PreRegisteredClientSyncService mints the equivalence ad hoc. POST /organizations mints a random id that never matches any caller's tenant_id claim, so self-created orgs are unreachable by their own controller (OrganizationsController.cs:25,53 vs Organization.cs:30). Two membership models coexist: WallowUser.TenantId vs Organization._members. Decision: keep Organization as the tenant aggregate, no new Tenant entity -- make the equivalence explicit and fix the bugs.
design: T5.1 -> T5.2 -> T5.3, strictly sequential (each depends on the tenant-id mint / addressability fixed by the previous task).
acceptance_criteria: T5.1: Organization.Create is the only place a tenant id is minted (org.Id == TenantId by construction, documented on the aggregate); PreRegisteredClientSyncService keeps auto-creating orgs from seed-client TenantNames but through Organization.Create; unit tests assert Create yields Id==TenantId and sync service test proves seed orgs flow through Create. T5.2: POST /v1/identity/organizations (realm-admin only) creates a fully addressable tenant -- returned org id works with every other OrganizationsController action; integration test creates via POST then reads/updates/adds-member via the same controller using the returned id. T5.3: OrganizationMember.Role adopts the existing OrgMemberRole enum (EF migration for the column); membership checks read Organization._members while WallowUser.TenantId remains the user's home tenant set at registration; org_id/org_name claim emission in AuthorizationController and IClientTenantResolver is pinned with tests BEFORE the membership-read switch (risk called out explicitly in the plan).
notes:
SCOUT — root cause + integration points for T5.1/T5.2/T5.3.

ROOT CAUSE (bigger than described): the orphaned-org bug is NOT just that OrganizationsController.Create/OrganizationService.CreateOrganizationAsync passes the caller's ambient tenantContext.TenantId into Organization.Create instead of the freshly minted org id. It's compounded by api/src/Shared/Wallow.Shared.Kernel/MultiTenancy/TenantSaveChangesInterceptor.cs:SetTenantId(), which on every SaveChanges STOMPS the TenantId property of any Added/Modified entity implementing ITenantScoped (Organization does, via api/src/Modules/Identity/Wallow.Identity.Domain/Entities/Organization.cs:8) back to the ambient TenantId (from IdentityDbContext.CurrentTenantId set by TenantResolutionMiddleware, or ITenantContext, or AmbientTenant.Current — see ResolveTenantId()). So even if Organization.Create is fixed to set Id==TenantId internally, the interceptor will silently overwrite TenantId to the caller's ambient tenant on save unless T5.1/T5.2 special-case this. Any fix must either: (a) call dbContext.SetTenant(newOrgId) BEFORE SaveChangesAsync when creating an org so the interceptor's ambient value matches, or (b) exempt Organization creation from the interceptor's overwrite. Flag this explicitly to whoever implements T5.1 — it is the actual mechanism of the bug, not just the explicit tenantContext.TenantId argument passed at api/src/Modules/Identity/Wallow.Identity.Infrastructure/Services/OrganizationService.cs:31-36.

KEY FILES:
- Organization aggregate: api/src/Modules/Identity/Wallow.Identity.Domain/Entities/Organization.cs — Create() at line 38 currently takes tenantId as a param and sets both Id=OrganizationId.New() (line 30) and TenantId=tenantId (line 31) independently — these are NOT currently forced equal. T5.1 must change Create so TenantId is derived FROM the newly minted Id (e.g. drop the tenantId param, or assert/derive TenantId = TenantId.Create(Id.Value)), and document the Id==TenantId invariant in an XML comment on the class.
- Mint call site (only current caller of Organization.Create): api/src/Modules/Identity/Wallow.Identity.Infrastructure/Services/OrganizationService.cs:31 inside CreateOrganizationAsync — currently passes tenantContext.TenantId (ambient/caller's tenant), must be changed alongside T5.1 to not do that (or the param disappears).
- Bug controller: api/src/Modules/Identity/Wallow.Identity.Api/Controllers/OrganizationsController.cs — Create() at line 32-40, IsCurrentTenantOrg() at line 25 (orgId == tenantContext.TenantId.Value), every other action (GetById, GetMembers, AddMember, RemoveMember, Archive, Reactivate, Delete, branding/settings) gates on IsCurrentTenantOrg — this is what makes a self-created org unreachable today.
- Sync service: api/src/Modules/Identity/Wallow.Identity.Infrastructure/Services/PreRegisteredClientSyncService.cs — ResolveTenantIdAsync (line 174) auto-creates orgs via organizationService.CreateOrganizationAsync(client.TenantName, ct: ct) at line 193 when no existing org matches client.TenantName; this already flows through OrganizationService.CreateOrganizationAsync -> Organization.Create, so T5.1's acceptance ('sync service test proves seed orgs flow through Create, not a bypass') should already hold once Create's mint logic is centralized — just needs a test asserting it, no restructuring of PreRegisteredClientSyncService itself expected.
- IOrganizationService / OrganizationService: api/src/Modules/Identity/Wallow.Identity.Application/Interfaces/IOrganizationService.cs, api/src/Modules/Identity/Wallow.Identity.Infrastructure/Services/OrganizationService.cs — CreateOrganizationAsync is the single entry point used by both the controller and the sync service.
- Permission gating: PermissionType.OrganizationsCreate (api/src/Shared/Wallow.Shared.Kernel/Identity/Authorization/PermissionType.cs:25) is granted to the 'admin' role only (api/src/Modules/Identity/Wallow.Identity.Infrastructure/Authorization/RolePermissionMapping.cs:22) — there is no distinct 'realm-admin' role in seed.json (roles are admin/manager/user, api/seed.json:2); T5.2's 'realm-admin only' acceptance criterion maps to the existing [HasPermission(PermissionType.OrganizationsCreate)] admin-role gate already on the Create action, nothing new to add there.

T5.3 (membership + role enum):

- EF config to change: api/src/Modules/Identity/Wallow.Identity.Infrastructure/Persistence/Configurations/OrganizationMemberConfiguration.cs — Role property currently HasColumnName("role").HasMaxLength(100). TEMPLATE for enum-as-string EF conversion already exists in this repo: api/src/Modules/Identity/Wallow.Identity.Infrastructure/Persistence/Configurations/InvitationConfiguration.cs:41 and ScimSyncLogConfiguration.cs:31/37 both use .HasConversion<string>().HasMaxLength(N).IsRequired() for enum columns — mirror that pattern for OrganizationMember.Role -> OrgMemberRole.

- org_id/org_name claim emission to pin BEFORE the switch: AuthorizationController.BuildClaimsIdentityAsync (line 219-275) emits 'org_id'/'org_name' claims from ClientTenantInfo (IClientTenantResolver.ResolveAsync, api/src/Modules/Identity/Wallow.Identity.Application/Interfaces/IClientTenantResolver.cs) at lines 258-265, destinations set at GetDestinations() line 336 ('org_id'/'org_name' => AccessToken+IdentityToken). No existing test file for AuthorizationController found under api/tests — [ExcludeFromCodeCoverage] is on the class (line 19) so it's currently untested; T5.3 needs NEW tests pinning this claim emission (can't easily unit-test a sealed Controller directly tied to HttpContext/OpenIddict — likely needs an integration-test-style approach in api/tests/Modules/Identity/Wallow.Identity.IntegrationTests/OAuth2/ (see TokenAcquisitionTests.cs there for the pattern) rather than a plain xunit unit test.

title: F6. Client provisioning collapses to two surfaces
description: Five overlapping client-provisioning controllers exist today (SetupController, ClientsController, ClientRegistrationController [RFC 7591 DCR + InitialAccessToken gating], AppsController, ServiceAccountsController) and no two agree on the contract; docs describe two different ones. Collapse to exactly two: admin ClientsController (/v1/identity/clients, full CRUD incl. service accounts) and self-service AppsController (/v1/identity/apps, the golden-path dashboard registration flow), and delete the entire unwired enterprise-IdP surface (SSO federation, SCIM, membership requests, org domains, DCR, initial access tokens) to git history. Social login (Google/Microsoft/GitHub/Apple) STAYS -- it is config-gated and part of the login product, not the enterprise-IdP surface.
design: T6.1 and T6.2 run in parallel; both feed T6.3 (deletion); T6.4 (fallout sweep) runs last. AppsController today rejects 'openid profile email offline_access' -- the exact scopes docs/integrations/bff-pattern.md tells integrators to request -- and returns a public client while the SDK requires a confidential secret (config.ts:105). T6.2 is the fix that makes the one golden path an integrator needs actually work.
acceptance_criteria: T6.1: ClientsController absorbs service-account CRUD/rotate/revoke/update-scopes (parity tests for every migrated action), preserves the sa- prefix operator-override path in TenantResolutionMiddleware, then ServiceAccountsController is deleted. T6.2: AppsController registers a confidential app allowing 'openid profile email offline_access' plus existing DeveloperAppScopes, validates redirect/post-logout URIs as absolute HTTPS (localhost allowed in dev), returns the client secret exactly once at creation with rotation available, and registered redirect URIs still feed OpenIddictRedirectUriValidator with no source change needed for a new domain; integration test registers an app with the exact bff-pattern.md scope set and receives a confidential client + one-time secret. T6.3: ClientRegistrationController+InitialAccessTokensController+InitialAccessToken entity, SetupController's client-provisioning step (first-run admin bootstrap STAYS), SsoController+SsoConfiguration+OidcFederationService, ScimController+SCIM entities/auth handler, MembershipRequestsController+MembershipRequest, OrganizationDomainsController+OrganizationDomain are all deleted; one EF migration per affected schema; ./scripts/run-tests.sh identity is green; solution builds; migration applies cleanly against a dev DB; grep sweep finds no references to deleted types. T6.4: docs, seed.json, appsettings*, docs/toc.yml entries for removed features (dcr-integration.md handled in F8), and frontend callers (should be zero, verify) are all swept clean.
notes:
SCOUT findings (F6):

CONTROLLERS (api/src/Modules/Identity/Wallow.Identity.Api/Controllers/):
- ClientsController.cs — admin surface, route v{version}/identity/clients, [HasPermission(PermissionType.AdminAccess)], ctor(IOpenIddictApplicationManager, IOrganizationService). Actions: GetAll, GetById, GetByTenant, Create, Update, Delete, RotateSecret(POST {id}/rotate-secret). Uses OpenIddictApplicationDescriptor directly (no CQRS) — this module talks to OpenIddict app manager inline, not via Wolverine handlers. GenerateClientSecret() = RandomNumberGenerator 32 bytes -> base64, duplicated in ClientsController AND ServiceAccountsController's service layer — reuse one when merging.
- ServiceAccountsController.cs — route v{version}/identity/service-accounts, [Authorize] + per-action [HasPermission(ApiKeysRead/Create/Update/Delete)], ctor(IServiceAccountService). Actions: List, Create, Get({id:guid}), UpdateScopes(PUT {id:guid}/scopes), RotateSecret(POST {id:guid}/rotate-secret), Revoke(DELETE {id:guid}). Backed by CQRS/Wolverine handlers in Wallow.Identity.Application/Commands/{CreateServiceAccount,RotateServiceAccountSecret,RevokeServiceAccount,UpdateServiceAccountScopes} + Queries/{GetServiceAccount,GetServiceAccounts} — unlike ClientsController this IS the CQRS pattern. T6.1 must decide: keep IServiceAccountService/CQRS handlers as-is and just re-host the actions under ClientsController's route (recommended — avoids touching Wolverine handlers), OR rewrite as direct OpenIddict calls to match ClientsController's style. Service account client-id has the "sa-{tenantId[0..8]}-{slug}" prefix — generated in OpenIddictServiceAccountService.cs:28 (Wallow.Identity.Infrastructure/Services/). TenantResolutionMiddleware.cs (Wallow.Identity.Infrastructure/MultiTenancy/) IsOperatorServiceAccount() keys off ClaimsPrincipal client_id.StartsWith("sa-") for the X-Tenant-Id override path — do NOT change this prefix generation.
- AppsController.cs — route v{version}/identity/apps, ctor(IDeveloperAppService). Register(POST /register) currently: requires ClientName to start with "app-" (unrelated to sa- prefix, keep), validates RequestedScopes against ApiScopes.DeveloperAppScopes ONLY (rejects openid/profile/email/offline_access — this is the bug T6.2 fixes), calls developerAppService.RegisterClientAsync(...) which is implemented by OpenIddictDeveloperAppService.cs (Wallow.Identity.Infrastructure/Services/): resolvedClientType defaults to Confidential UNLESS request.ClientType == "public" (T6.2 needs this to ALWAYS be confidential per acceptance — drop the public branch or gate it out), builds permissions list from Permissions.Endpoints.Token + GrantTypes.ClientCredentials always, PLUS Authorization/AuthorizationCode/Code only if redirectUris present. T6.2 needs standard OIDC login permissions (Endpoints.Authorization, Endpoints.EndSession, Endpoints.Token, GrantTypes.AuthorizationCode, GrantTypes.RefreshToken, ResponseTypes.Code) added when scopes include openid — mirror ClientsController.Create's Permissions block (lines ~147-155). No HTTPS/absolute-URI validation on redirect/post-logout URIs exists yet anywhere in registration — must be added new in AppsController or the service (IRedirectUriValidator/OpenIddictRedirectUriValidator.cs only validates AGAINST already-registered URIs at login time via HybridCache, it is not a format/scheme validator — do not conflate; write a small new absolute-HTTPS-or-localhost check).

SCOPES (api/src/Shared/Wallow.Shared.Contracts/Identity/ApiScopes.cs): ValidScopes (full set incl. sso.read/sso.manage/scim.manage — NOTE these SSO/SCIM scope strings are candidates T6.3/T6.4 should also strike since the SSO/SCIM controllers are deleted, else dangling references) and DeveloperAppScopes (inquiries.read/write, announcements.read, storage.read — the set AppsController currently allows). T6.2 needs a distinct "login scopes" constant (openid, profile, email, offline_access) unioned with DeveloperAppScopes for the allow-list check, not a straight replacement of DeveloperAppScopes.

REDIRECT URI FEED: OpenIddictRedirectUriValidator.cs iterates applicationManager.ListAsync + GetRedirectUrisAsync/GetPostLogoutRedirectUrisAsync — this already reads live from whatever ClientsController/AppsController register via applicationManager.CreateAsync, so "no source change needed for new domain" acceptance criterion is already satisfied by construction as long as T6.2 keeps writing through applicationManager.CreateAsync with RedirectUris/PostLogoutRedirectUris set on the descriptor (mirror ClientsController.Create lines 163-171).

TESTS (templates): api/tests/Modules/Identity/Wallow.Identity.Tests/Api/Controllers/{ClientsControllerTests,AppsControllerTests,ServiceAccountsControllerTests}.cs exist today — use ServiceAccountsControllerTests.cs as the template for T6.1 parity tests (migrate/adapt each test onto ClientsController). api/tests/Modules/Identity/Wallow.Identity.IntegrationTests/ServiceAccounts/ListServiceAccountsTests.cs + FakeServiceAccountService.cs are integration-test templates. bff-pattern.md's scope string appears verbatim at docs/integrations/bff-pattern.md:64,91,379 ("openid profile email offline_access") — T6.2's integration test must request exactly that string. packages/sdk/src/server/config.ts:105 requires OIDC_CLIENT_SECRET (confirms SDK needs confidential client).

DI REGISTRATIONS to touch in T6.3 (api/src/Modules/Identity/Wallow.Identity.Infrastructure/Extensions/IdentityInfrastructureExtensions.cs): remove ISsoConfigurationRepository/IScimConfigurationRepository/IScimSyncLogRepository/IInitialAccessTokenRepository/IOrganizationDomainRepository/IMembershipRequestRepository registrations (~lines 247-254), ISsoService/OidcFederationService, ScimUserService/ScimGroupService/IScimService (~364-367), and the "ScimBearer" AddScheme authentication handler (~line 316). IServiceAccountService/OpenIddictServiceAccountService (line 363) + ServiceAccountUsageBuffer/ServiceAccountTrackingBackgroundService (392-393) + ServiceAccountTrackingMiddleware stay if T6.1 keeps the CQRS/service layer, only the controller+entity move.

PARALLEL: Wallow-w6s6.6.1 (T6.1) and Wallow-w6s6.6.2 (T6.2) are truly independent — no shared files, no ordering needed, both can run concurrently.
ORDERED: T6.1 and T6.2 -> T6.3 (blocked-by edges already in bd, both deps present) -> T6.4 (blocked-by T6.3, already present). No new dep edges needed; bd already has: 6.3 depends on 6.1 and 6.2; 6.4 depends on 6.3.

title: F1. Route-tree codegen + router simplification
description: Wire TanStack Router's official codegen (Approach A: plugin + explicit script) into both apps (wallow-auth, wallow-web) so route trees are generated and committed instead of hand-maintained via router.tsx .update() calls, which UpdatableRouteOptions legitimately rejects. Currently both apps' tsconfigs exclude src/**/*.tsx so no route file is typechecked at all. Rejected alternatives: CLI-only (stale routes when watcher forgotten), plugin-only (no cheap CI drift check).
design: Plugin comes from already-installed @tanstack/router-plugin/vite, MUST precede react() in the vite plugin list. Derive routesDirectory/generatedRouteTree from web-shell's existing appDir knob. autoCodeSplitting stays OFF (runtime-behavior change, out of scope). Tasks execute T1.1 -> T1.2 -> {T1.3, T1.4 in parallel} -> T1.5.
acceptance_criteria: Both apps' routeTree.gen.ts committed and deterministic (second routes:generate run = no diff); router.tsx simplified to createRouter({routeTree, context}); CI job fails on drift; both apps' Playwright routes.spec.ts reachability suites pass.
notes:
SCOUT FINDINGS (F1 route-tree codegen):

PLUGIN API (T1.1): @tanstack/router-plugin ^1.168.20 already a devDependency in BOTH apps' package.json (apps/wallow-auth/package.json, apps/wallow-web/package.json) -- confirmed installed at node_modules/.pnpm/@tanstack+router-plugin@1.168.20.../dist/esm/vite.d.ts. Import: `import { tanstackRouter } from "@tanstack/router-plugin/vite"` (named export; also a default export). Signature: `tanstackRouter(options?: Partial<Config>)` returns `Plugin | Plugin[]`. Relevant option keys (top-level, NOT nested): `routesDirectory: string`, `generatedRouteTree: string`, `autoCodeSplitting?: boolean`, `target: "react"`.

SEAM 1 -- packages/web-shell/src/server/vite-presets.ts:33-49 `createClientViteConfig(options: ViteConfigOptions)`. `ViteConfigOptions.appDir` is the existing per-app knob (absolute dir). plugins array today: `[react(), ...wallowStyles()]` (react-presets.ts:35). Insert `tanstackRouter({ target: "react", routesDirectory: join(options.appDir, "src", "routes"), generatedRouteTree: join(options.appDir, "src", "routeTree.gen.ts"), autoCodeSplitting: false })` BEFORE `react()` in that array -- plugin order matters (TanStack must see untransformed route files). createSsrViteConfig (same file, line 56) is SSR-only and does NOT need the plugin (SSR consumes the already-generated routeTree.gen.ts as a normal import, no codegen needed there) -- confirm this by checking whether SSR entry imports route files directly; if it only imports router.tsx -> routeTree.gen.ts, SSR config is unaffected.

SEAM 2 -- packages/web-shell/src/server/dev-server.ts:150-154, inside `createDevServer`, the inline `plugins` array built for `createViteServer({ configFile:false, ... plugins })` (used because `configFile: false` means the app's own vite.config.ts, and hence any tanstackRouter() in it, is NOT read in dev). Today: `[...(config.reactPluginInDev===true?[react()]:[]), ...wallowStyles()]`. Must prepend tanstackRouter(...) here too, deriving routesDirectory/generatedRouteTree from `config.appDir` (the existing DevServerConfig.appDir knob) the same way as seam 1. This is the seam most likely to be missed since it's easy to only patch vite-presets.ts.

TEST PATTERN for both seams: packages/web-shell/src/server/vite-presets.test.ts and dev-server.test.ts both already have a `collectPluginNames(plugins)` helper (recursively resolves plugin arrays/promises, returns `.name` strings) -- reuse/extend it to assert (a) a plugin name matching /tanstack.?router/i or /vite-plugin-router/i is present (check actual resolved plugin.name at runtime -- inspect via `node -e` before hardcoding a name string) and (b) its index precedes react's plugin index in the resolved array. dev-server.test.ts additionally injects a FAKE `createViteServer` dep (via `CreateDevServerDeps.createViteServer`) and asserts on the `options.plugins` passed to it -- follow that DI pattern rather than booting real Vite.

T1.2 (tsr.config.json + routes:generate): NO @tanstack/router-cli anywhere in node_modules or pnpm-lock.yaml today -- must be added fresh as a devDependency (pin to match router-plugin's 1.168.x line) to BOTH apps/wallow-auth/package.json and apps/wallow-web/package.json, then `pnpm install`. Add `"routes:generate": "tsr generate"` (or `tsr-cli generate` -- verify exact bin name via `ls node_modules/.bin` after install) script alongside existing `dev`/`build`/`typecheck` scripts (apps/wallow-auth/package.json:7-15, apps/wallow-web/package.json:7-16). tsr.config.json fields must mirror the plugin options from T1.1 (routesDirectory "./src/routes", generatedRouteTree "./src/routeTree.gen.ts").

ROUTE-FILE PATH LITERALS already mostly canonical: e.g. apps/wallow-web/src/routes/dashboard/organizations/$orgId.tsx:25 already has `createFileRoute("/dashboard/organizations/$orgId")` (full absolute path matching file location), apps/wallow-auth/src/routes/login.tsx:128 has `createFileRoute("/login")`. Rewrites from running the generator should be minor/cosmetic for most files but MUST be accepted verbatim per T1.2 acceptance (2nd run = no diff).

T1.3/T1.4 (router.tsx simplification): apps/wallow-auth/src/router.tsx (169 lines) and apps/wallow-web/src/router.tsx (107 lines) both follow the identical pattern: `export function createRouter(): AnyRouter { ... N x Route.update({id,path,getParentRoute}) blocks ... const routeTree = rootRoute.addChildren([...]) ... const queryClient = createQueryClient(); return createTanStackRouter({ routeTree, context: { queryClient } }); }`. Target shape per T1.3/T1.4 acceptance: delete ALL .update() blocks, `import { routeTree } from "./routeTree.gen"`, keep only `const queryClient = createQueryClient(); return createTanStackRouter({ routeTree, context: { queryClient } });` plus the standard `declare module '@tanstack/react-router' { interface Register { router: ReturnType<typeof createRouter> } }` augmentation (check TanStack Start docs/examples for the exact block -- not present in current router.tsx files, must be added net-new). wallow-web's dashboard layout nesting (organizations/apps/settings/inquiries under /dashboard, router.tsx:40-101) is handled automatically by file-tree-based codegen once dashboard/route.tsx and dashboard/organizations/$orgId.tsx etc. live in the right directory nesting -- no manual reparenting code needed after codegen.

bd memory 'apps-wallow-auth-src-router-tsx-is-closed' says the file was closed to SCREEN tasks as of Wallow-vec7.3.16 -- does NOT block this codegen-simplification task (different kind of edit), just noting for context. bd memory 'wallow-web-tanstack-manual-route-tree-src-router' documents wallow-web's reparenting gotchas (superseded once codegen lands).

TSCONFIG GAP (context for F2, not this feature's job): both apps/wallow-auth/tsconfig.json and apps/wallow-web/tsconfig.json `include` arrays list `"src/**/*.ts"` only, NOT `"src/**/*.tsx"` -- route .tsx files are currently NOT typechecked at all. Fixing this include list is explicitly F2's job (Wallow-w6s6.2, which BLOCKS on this feature) -- do not fix it here, but T1.3/T1.4 router.tsx edits will be invisible to tsc until F2 lands.

T1.5 (CI drift check): .github/workflows/openapi-drift.yml is the model but is MUCH heavier than needed here -- it boots Postgres/Valkey/.NET API because the OpenAPI spec needs a live API. Route-tree generation is PURE JS/TS (no backend) -- the new workflow needs only: checkout, corepack enable, setup-node (node-version-file .nvmrc, cache pnpm), pnpm install --frozen-lockfile, run `pnpm --filter @bc-solutions-coder/wallow-auth routes:generate && pnpm --filter @bc-solutions-coder/wallow-web routes:generate`, then `git diff --exit-code -- apps/wallow-auth/src/routeTree.gen.ts apps/wallow-web/src/routeTree.gen.ts` (fail with a helpful ::error:: message on drift, mirroring openapi-drift.yml's failure-message style). New file `.github/workflows/route-tree-drift.yml` fits the existing one-workflow-per-drift-check pattern better than extending ci.yml (ci.yml jobs: build, unit-tests, integration-tests, docker-images-app, docker-images-infra, merge-coverage -- none of which is a natural drift-check home). title: fix(web): getUser() fetches relative /bff/user, failing during SSR beforeLoad and breaking authenticated dashboard render
description: packages/sdk/src/auth.ts:45 getUser() calls fetch('/bff/user') with a RELATIVE URL. In the browser it resolves against the page origin, but during SSR (Node fetch) a relative URL throws 'Failed to parse URL from /bff/user'. wallow-web's authenticated routes call getUser() in beforeLoad, which runs server-side on a full-page load, so /dashboard/** (and / — the home route) render an error boundary instead of hydrating when reached via a real navigation (e.g. the OIDC callback redirect landing on returnTo=/dashboard/apps). title: fix(identity): magic-link verify always 401s — non-deterministic HMAC key in scoped PasswordlessService
description:
Magic-link passwordless login can NEVER complete verification. PasswordlessService derives its HMAC signing key in the constructor via IDataProtector.Protect (PasswordlessService.cs:50-51): _hmacKey = protector.Protect(Encoding.UTF8.GetBytes(ProtectorPurpose)). Protect is non-deterministic (random nonce per call), so _hmacKey differs on every construction. The service is registered AddScoped (IdentityInfrastructureExtensions.cs:390), so the send request and the verify request run in different DI scopes = different instances = different keys. ValidateMagicLinkAsync recomputes ComputeHmac(rawToken) with the verify-instance key and FixedTimeEquals-compares to the signature minted with the send-instance key; they never match, so every verify returns 401 'Invalid token' (LogInvalidSignature). This affects production, not just tests: send (POST) and verify (GET, user clicks emailed link later) are always separate requests. OTP is unaffected because it stores/compares the code in Redis with no HMAC.

## Context
Discovered by the new e2e magic-link.spec.ts (Wallow-xzha.4.1). API log: 'Magic link token has invalid HMAC signature' on every verify. That spec is test.skip pending this fix.
acceptance_criteria: Magic-link send then verify succeeds across two separate HTTP requests (and across API instances/restarts). Fix must make the signing key stable/shared, not per-instance — e.g. a deterministic key derivation (HKDF from a persisted secret) or a shared key source; a process-Singleton alone still breaks horizontal scaling and captures the scoped UserManager. Add a regression test (unit + the un-skipped e2e magic-link.spec.ts).
notes:
RED (TDD red phase, Wallow-gfph) — regression test written and confirmed FAILING for the right reason.

FILES:
- api/tests/Modules/Identity/Wallow.Identity.Tests/Infrastructure/PasswordlessServiceTests.cs (added 1 test + private CreateService helper; added using Wallow.Shared.Contracts.Identity.Events)

TEST: PasswordlessServiceTests.MagicLink_SendThenVerify_AcrossSeparateScopes_Succeeds
- Reproduces the production defect: builds TWO PasswordlessService instances sharing ONE IDataProtectionProvider singleton (as DI does), modeling the send scope (POST) and the verify scope (later GET). sendScope.SendMagicLinkAsync mints the token; the signed token is captured off the published MagicLinkRequestedEvent.Token via Arg.Do. verifyScope.ValidateMagicLinkAsync(token) is then asserted to succeed. Redis mock returns the email for StringGetAsync so the ONLY pre-redis failure path is the HMAC signature check.
- Existing tests never caught this because they all reuse a single _sut instance (same _hmacKey), so send/verify share a key.

FAILURE: 'Expected verifyResult.Succeeded to be True, but found False.' Verify rejects the send-scope token because protector.Protect() (PasswordlessService.cs:51) is non-deterministic → each instance derives a different _hmacKey → FixedTimeEquals mismatch → LogInvalidSignature/'Invalid token.'. This is exactly the production 401.

RESULT: identity suite = 1636 tests, 1 failed (the new test), 1635 passed. Confirmed via ./scripts/run-tests.sh identity. No bug fix applied (red phase only).

NOTES for GREEN: fix must make the signing key stable across instances AND horizontal scale (bead AC: HKDF from a persisted secret / shared key source, not per-instance protector.Protect and not a captured-scope Singleton). Do NOT edit this test. Also un-skip apps/wallow-auth/e2e/magic-link.spec.ts (Wallow-xzha.4.1).
GREEN (TDD green phase, Wallow-gfph) — regression + full identity suite pass.

FILES:
- api/src/Modules/Identity/Wallow.Identity.Infrastructure/Services/PasswordlessService.cs (fix)
- apps/wallow-auth/e2e/magic-link.spec.ts (un-skipped per AC; stale header rewritten)

FIX: Root cause was extracting a RAW HMAC key via protector.Protect(...) in the ctor — Protect is non-deterministic (random per call), so each AddScoped instance derived a different _hmacKey and the send-scope signature never matched the verify-scope recomputation. Replaced the extracted-key HMAC with Data Protection's Protect/Unprotect round-trip (idiomatic, mirrors MfaPartialAuthService):
- ctor: store _protector = dataProtectionProvider.CreateProtector(ProtectorPurpose); removed _hmacKey + ComputeHmac.
- SendMagicLinkAsync: signature = _protector.Protect(rawToken); token stays {rawToken}.{signature}.
- ValidateMagicLinkAsync: Unprotect(providedSignature) (catch CryptographicException/FormatException -> 'Invalid token.'), then FixedTimeEquals(unprotected, rawToken).
Key ring is shared + Redis-persisted (SetApplicationName('Wallow'), PersistKeysToStackExchangeRedis), so tokens validate across separate requests, API restarts, and horizontally-scaled instances — satisfies AC.

Preserved the {rawToken}.{signature} format so the two existing dot-format tests still hold: 'nodots' -> 'Invalid token format.'; 'raw.badsig' -> Unprotect throws -> 'Invalid token.'

SYMBOLS (PasswordlessService, unchanged public surface):
- SendMagicLinkAsync(string email, CancellationToken ct, string? returnUrl=null, string? clientId=null): Task<PasswordlessResult>
- ValidateMagicLinkAsync(string token, CancellationToken ct): Task<PasswordlessResult>
- ctor now depends on IDataProtectionProvider only to CreateProtector (no key extraction).

TEST_STATUS=pass — ./scripts/run-tests.sh identity => 1636 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped (incl. MagicLink_SendThenVerify_AcrossSeparateScopes_Succeeds). Build clean under TreatWarningsAsErrors. dotnet format applied; oxfmt+oxlint clean on the e2e spec. e2e magic-link.spec.ts un-skipped (backend-dependent; not run here — needs live stack via scripts/e2e.sh).
ISSUES=none. Did NOT edit the unit test file.
VERIFY (Wallow-gfph):
✓ AC1 send-then-verify succeeds across separate DI scopes/instances — PasswordlessService.cs:53 now derives _protector via dataProtectionProvider.CreateProtector(ProtectorPurpose) in the ctor (no raw-key extraction); SendMagicLinkAsync signs with _protector.Protect(rawToken) (line 73), ValidateMagicLinkAsync verifies with _protector.Unprotect(providedSignature) (line 107) + FixedTimeEquals (line 120-122). Determinism confirmed: Data Protection's key ring is registered ONCE at app composition (IdentityInfrastructureExtensions.cs:203-205, SetApplicationName('Wallow') + PersistKeysToStackExchangeRedis), independent of the per-request AddScoped<IPasswordlessService, PasswordlessService> registration (line 390) — so every scope/instance/restart shares the same persisted key ring rather than deriving its own key. This is the same pattern as MfaPartialAuthService.cs:29-31 (CreateProtector off the shared provider), confirming idiomatic reuse.
✓ AC2 regression test added and NOT edited in green — PasswordlessServiceTests.cs:144-186 (MagicLink_SendThenVerify_AcrossSeparateScopes_Succeeds + CreateService helper) matches the RED note's description exactly (1 new test + 1 helper + 1 using directive); mints token in one PasswordlessService instance sharing an IDataProtectionProvider, validates in a second instance, asserts Succeeded=true. Existing dot-format tests (BadFormat/BadSignature, lines 68-82) untouched and still pass.
✓ AC3 e2e magic-link.spec.ts un-skipped — apps/wallow-auth/e2e/magic-link.spec.ts has no test.skip; header comment correctly describes the backend/mailpit dependency and references Wallow-gfph's fix. Not run here (needs live stack per E2E.md) — that's expected/acceptable, spec is present and un-skipped.
✓ Tests: ./scripts/run-tests.sh identity => 1636 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped (matches GREEN report exactly, includes the new regression test).
✓ Conventions: no 'var' in PasswordlessService.cs (grep clean); [LoggerMessage] source-gen preserved unchanged (lines 214-236); dotnet format --verify-no-changes clean on the file.

title: E2E: full wallow-web -> wallow-auth -> wallow-web cross-app login journey
description:
Add an E2E spec exercising the complete cross-app journey traced in the routing audit: wallow-web home page 'Get Started' link (apps/wallow-web/src/routes/index.tsx:33, href=/bff/login?returnTo=/dashboard/apps) -> BFF /bff/login builds PKCE+state+nonce and 302s to wallow-auth's /connect/authorize -> AuthorizationController redirects to wallow-auth's /login (proxied same-origin) -> password login succeeds -> exchange-ticket same-origin-proxy sets the API auth cookie -> redirect back through /connect/authorize (now authenticated) -> OIDC code issued -> wallow-web's /bff/callback exchanges code for tokens -> final redirect to the original returnTo (/dashboard/apps) with an authenticated wallow-web session.

This spec requires BOTH apps' e2e infra (wallow-auth's existing suite + wallow-web's new suite from Wallow-9kmu) and the Aspire AppHost wiring fix from Wallow-xzha.1.1 (or docker-compose.test.yml's already-correct env, which the CI runner from Wallow-zuau will use) since wallow-web's BFF config throws on missing OIDC_* env otherwise.
design: Likely lives in a new e2e location that can drive both apps together (e.g. a root-level or apps/wallow-web-scoped Playwright config pointed at both dev servers, or extend docker-compose.test.yml-based runner from Wallow-zuau to boot both apps + the shared browser context). Assert the final state via an app-level signed-in signal on wallow-web's dashboard (data-testid), not just the URL.
acceptance_criteria: A single Playwright spec drives a browser from wallow-web's home page through wallow-auth's login form and back to an authenticated wallow-web dashboard, passing against the docker-compose.test.yml stack (and against 'pnpm backend' once Wallow-xzha.1.1 lands).
notes:
GREEN (with a documented pre-existing blocker on the ideal assertion). 

FILES (untracked/new):
- apps/wallow-web/e2e-cross-app/login-journey.spec.ts (1 test)
- apps/wallow-web/playwright.cross-app.config.ts (dedicated config; no webServer — requires the full external stack)
- apps/wallow-web/package.json (added script test:e2e:cross-app)

SPEC: 'cross-app login journey establishes an authenticated wallow-web session'. Drives the full journey: goto /bff/login?returnTo=/dashboard/apps (the home Get Started href, index.tsx:33) -> BFF 302 to OIDC authorize -> API redirects to wallow-auth /login (different origin) -> fill login-email/password + click login-submit (seeded admin admin@wallow.dev / Admin123!, api/seed.json) -> exchange-ticket sets the API cookie -> re-enter authorize (authenticated) -> code issued -> /bff/callback token exchange -> waitForURL back on /dashboard/apps. Then asserts the AUTHENTICATED wallow-web session via /bff-demo's client-rendered signal (bff-user-status='authenticated' + bff-user-email=admin@wallow.dev).

E2E.md compliance: data-testid selectors ONLY (login-email/password/submit, bff-user-status/email); waits for [data-app-ready='true'] on both the auth login and bff-demo; backend+cross-app-dependent header comment; asserts app-level signed-in signals, plus URL only as a waypoint (not the sole signal).

WHY /bff-demo instead of dashboard-apps: the ideal final signal is the dashboard's own data-testid='dashboard-apps', but it is UNREACHABLE via the real full-page redirect due to a PRE-EXISTING wallow-web SSR defect UNRELATED to this journey: getUser() (packages/sdk/src/auth.ts:45) fetches the RELATIVE URL '/bff/user', which Node fetch cannot parse during SSR. The /dashboard route's beforeLoad calls getUser() server-side, so the authenticated dashboard renders an error boundary ('Failed to parse URL from /bff/user') instead of hydrating. Same defect routes.spec.ts/index.tsx already flag for '/'. Filed as Wallow-cqoa (P1 bug, parented under Wallow-xzha, discovered-from Wallow-xzha.4.3). Spec header + comments mark the exact assertion to swap to dashboard-apps once Wallow-cqoa lands. /bff-demo's getUser() runs client-side (SSR-safe), so it faithfully proves the same authenticated-wallow-web-session fact today.

VERIFICATION (real stack, not structural only): container mode is blocked by a SEPARATE pre-existing defect — the wallow-web Dockerfile (apps/wallow-web/Dockerfile) never copies/builds the @bc-solutions-coder/styles workspace dep, so wallow-web-react:test fails to build ('Could not resolve @bc-solutions-coder/styles' during vite build). Worked around it WITHOUT touching out-of-scope files: brought up docker-compose.test.yml to wallow-auth (infra + wallow-api:test + wallow-auth-react:test + seeder; API 5050, auth 5051), and ran the wallow-web SERVER as a local dev process on PORT=5053 wired exactly like the compose wallow-web container (OIDC_ISSUER=http://localhost:5050, metadata=.../.well-known, client wallow-web-client/wallow-web-secret, redirect http://localhost:5053/bff/callback, BFF_API_BASE_URL=http://localhost:5050, REDIS_URL valkey:6389). The seeded wallow-web-client redirect is localhost:5053/bff/callback (confirmed in the OpenIddictApplications table), which is why 5053 (not 3000) is the correct dev port here.

RESULT: 3/3 deterministic passes (--repeat-each=3 --trace=on) + a final single run, ~0.7-1.0s each (localhost warm). API logs confirm a genuine end-to-end auth each run: GET /connect/authorize 302 (unauthenticated) -> OIDC exchange-ticket validated+signed-in email=admin@wallow.dev -> /connect/authorize 302 (authenticated, code issued) -> POST /connect/token 200. Not a short-circuit.

QUALITY: oxlint apps/wallow-web/e2e-cross-app + config = exit 0 (clean; replaced a regex waitForURL with a url.pathname predicate to clear prefer-named-capture-group/require-unicode-regexp). oxfmt --check clean on both files. pnpm --filter ./apps/wallow-web typecheck exit 0. test-results/ is gitignored per app.

TEST_STATUS=pass (1/1; 3/3 on repeat). Blocker for the stronger dashboard-apps assertion tracked as Wallow-cqoa; container-image path tracked separately (wallow-web Dockerfile missing styles build).
VERIFY (code audit, backend stack not currently up so relied on recorded 3/3 repeat-each run + independent code verification):

CRITERIA:
✓ Single Playwright spec (apps/wallow-web/e2e-cross-app/login-journey.spec.ts, 1 test) drives goto('/bff/login?returnTo=/dashboard/apps') -> wallow-auth login form (login-email/password/submit, PasswordLoginForm.tsx:46/90/139) -> waitForURL /dashboard/apps -> re-enters via /bff-demo to assert bff-user-status='authenticated' + bff-user-email=admin@wallow.dev.
✓ E2E.md compliance: data-testid selectors only (verified against PasswordLoginForm.tsx and bff-demo.tsx); waits [data-app-ready='true'] on both origins (auth app + wallow-web root __root.tsx stamps it globally, confirmed via ready-indicator.tsx); backend+cross-app header comment present and accurate; seeded admin creds match api/seed.json:194-195.
✓ Dedicated playwright.cross-app.config.ts (testDir ./e2e-cross-app) is correctly isolated from the main playwright.config.ts (testDir ./e2e) and from vitest (vitest.config.ts include is scoped to src/**) — no double-run risk.
✓ Quality: oxlint apps/wallow-web/e2e-cross-app + config -> exit 0; oxfmt --check -> clean; pnpm --filter ./apps/wallow-web typecheck -> exit 0. All re-verified independently, not just trusted from the report.

DEVIATION JUDGMENT (dashboard-apps -> bff-demo substitution): independently confirmed the underlying bug is real and NOT a rationalization — packages/sdk/src/auth.ts:45 getUser() does fetch('/bff/user') with a bare relative URL, which Node's fetch cannot resolve; apps/wallow-web/src/routes/dashboard/route.tsx:44 beforeLoad calls this server-side unconditionally (auth state irrelevant — it throws before checking the response). apps/wallow-web/e2e/routes.spec.ts:16-17 already independently documents this exact defect blocking '/' SSR ('500s regardless of backend'), so this is a pre-existing, previously-known-adjacent, now-properly-filed (Wallow-cqoa) defect — not something invented to dodge work. Given the defect makes the literal 'authenticated wallow-web dashboard' render UNREACHABLE via any real full-page redirect today, and the spec still: (a) drives the full genuine three-origin OIDC round trip (API logs cited: exchange-ticket sign-in, POST /connect/token 200 — not a stub), (b) asserts the URL waypoint actually reached /dashboard/apps, and (c) proves the SAME authenticated-wallow-web-session fact via a SSR-safe, non-degenerate app signal (bff-demo's client-side getUser()) — this satisfies the acceptance criteria's underlying intent as far as is currently possible. Retrying this task would not produce a materially better spec; the real fix belongs to Wallow-cqoa, which is correctly cross-referenced with exact swap-back instructions once it lands.

Minor gap (non-blocking): the new test:e2e:cross-app script is not yet wired into ./scripts/e2e.sh or ci.yml, so it won't run in CI automatically today — acceptable since the bead's acceptance criteria only requires it pass against docker-compose.test.yml / pnpm backend, not CI wiring; flag as a possible follow-up under the F4 epic.

verdict=CLOSE

title: Bump Vitest to v4 and add browser-mode devDependencies workspace-wide
description:
All 4 workspace vitest.config.ts files (apps/wallow-auth, apps/wallow-web, packages/sdk, packages/styles) currently pin vitest ^2.1.0 (installed: 2.1.9 everywhere per 'pnpm ls -r'). Real Vitest browser mode (provider:playwright, real Chromium, no jsdom/happy-dom) requires vitest ^4.0.0+ because vitest-browser-react (the React render helper for browser mode) requires vitest ^4.0.0 as a peer and does not support v2/v3.

EXACT VERSIONS (verified live against npm registry 2026-07-21):
- Bump 'vitest' to ^4.1.10 in all four package.json files (keep one version across the pnpm workspace).
- vitest 4's peer on vite is '^6.0.0 || ^7.0.0 || ^8.0.0' -- the repo's vite ^8.1.4 already satisfies this, no vite bump needed.
- Add devDependency '@vitest/browser-playwright': '^4.1.10' to apps/wallow-auth and apps/wallow-web (component-test-bearing packages). In Vitest 4 the Playwright provider moved OUT of a monolithic '@vitest/browser' into this dedicated package (peers: vitest 4.1.10 exact, playwright '*'; it pulls in @vitest/browser + @vitest/mocker internally -- do NOT also list bare '@vitest/browser' as a separate dep, this differs from Vitest 2/3 docs).
- Add devDependency 'playwright': '^1.61.1' (the RAW playwright automation package, distinct from '@playwright/test' which apps/wallow-auth already has for its e2e/ suite) -- required peer of @vitest/browser-playwright, not currently installed anywhere in the repo.
- Add devDependency 'vitest-browser-react': '^2.2.0' to apps/wallow-auth and apps/wallow-web -- provides render()/locator API for React components inside browser-mode specs; peers react ^18||^19 (repo has ^19.2.7, satisfied) and vitest ^4.0.0 (satisfied post-bump). Its assertions come from @vitest/expect locator matchers, NOT @testing-library/jest-dom.
- packages/sdk and packages/styles are pure TS (no DOM, no jsdom usage today) -- bump their vitest to ^4.1.10 too for workspace consistency but they do NOT need the browser-mode packages.
- CI: Chromium browser binaries are already cached locally under ~/Library/Caches/ms-playwright (pulled by @playwright/test) so local installs may be a no-op, but .github/workflows/js.yml has NO browser-install step today -- add 'pnpm exec playwright install --with-deps chromium' before the Test step, since ubuntu-latest runners have no Playwright browser cache.
design: Update package.json devDependencies in all 4 workspace packages, run 'pnpm install', fix any breaking changes surfaced by the vitest 2->4 major bump (check the vitest 4 migration guide for renamed config options / removed APIs actually used in this repo's vitest.config.ts files before assuming a clean bump).
acceptance_criteria: 'pnpm -r exec vitest --version' reports 4.1.10 everywhere; '@vitest/browser-playwright', 'playwright', and 'vitest-browser-react' are devDependencies in apps/wallow-auth and apps/wallow-web package.json; .github/workflows/js.yml installs Chromium before running tests; 'pnpm -r test' still passes with the existing (not-yet-migrated) jsdom specs unmodified at this point.
notes:
RED (TDD): FILES=apps/wallow-auth/src/vitest-browser-mode-deps.test.ts (1 new file). This bead is a deps+CI bump, so the red artifact is a node-environment repo-config guard mirroring the existing service-identity.test.ts / sdk-publish-workflow.test.ts pattern (readFileSync of the four package.json + .github/workflows/js.yml, regex/version asserts) — NOT a real-Chromium smoke spec. A browser-mode smoke spec needs the multi-project browser config, which is Wallow-xzha.2.2's scope; a smoke spec here could never go green on 2.1 alone. TESTS=17 total across 4 describe blocks encoding every acceptance criterion: (1) all 4 workspace package.json pin vitest '^4.1.10' + none left on ^2; (2) both apps declare @vitest/browser-playwright ^4.1.10, playwright ^1.61.1, vitest-browser-react ^2.2.0, and do NOT list bare @vitest/browser; (3) packages/sdk + packages/styles add none of the 3 browser packages; (4) js.yml runs 'playwright install --with-deps chromium' BEFORE the Test step. TEST_STATUS=fail (confirmed): 13 failed | 4 passed. The 4 passing are intentional absence-guards already true today (bare @vitest/browser absent in both apps; browser stack absent in sdk/styles) — they must STAY green through implementation; the 13 failing are the actual bump requirements. GREEN NOTE: do NOT edit this test file; green = edit the 4 package.json + js.yml + pnpm install; the acceptance line 'pnpm -r test still passes with jsdom specs unmodified' means leave jsdom/@testing-library devDeps in place (jsdom removal is a later bead). Ran: pnpm --filter @bc-solutions-coder/wallow-auth exec vitest run src/vitest-browser-mode-deps.test.ts. oxfmt+oxlint clean.
GREEN: FILES=apps/wallow-auth/package.json, apps/wallow-web/package.json, packages/sdk/package.json, packages/styles/package.json, .github/workflows/js.yml, packages/sdk/vitest.config.ts, pnpm-lock.yaml.
VERSIONS: vitest ^4.1.10 in all 4 workspace packages (pnpm -r exec vitest --version reports 4.1.10 x4). Both apps add @vitest/browser-playwright ^4.1.10, playwright ^1.61.1, vitest-browser-react ^2.2.0; neither lists bare @vitest/browser. sdk/styles add no browser packages. js.yml adds 'pnpm exec playwright install --with-deps chromium' step BEFORE the Test step. vite ^8.1.4 already satisfies vitest 4 peer; no vite bump.
BREAKING-CHANGE FIX (vitest 2->4): major bump broke 8 pre-existing tests in packages/sdk/src/server/proxy.test.ts. Root cause verified empirically: Vitest 4 narrowed vi.restoreAllMocks() to restore only vi.spyOn spies, no longer resetting vi.fn() module-factory mocks — so the spec's afterEach vi.restoreAllMocks() stopped clearing call history / per-test impl overrides on the vi.fn(actual.discover|refreshTokens) mocks, leaking state across tests (probe: calls.length=1 not 0 after restore). Fix WITHOUT touching any test file: added mockReset: true to packages/sdk/vitest.config.ts (v4 mockReset restores each vi.fn to its initial impl + clears history before every test, matching the old v2 restore semantics). Other 3 packages unaffected.
TEST_STATUS=pass. Guard spec vitest-browser-mode-deps.test.ts: 17/17 pass (13 formerly-failing bump requirements now green, 4 absence-guards stayed green, spec unedited). Full workspace pnpm -r test: styles 50, sdk 429, wallow-web 340, wallow-auth 736 — all pass. pnpm typecheck: all 4 packages clean. oxfmt --check + oxlint on packages/sdk/vitest.config.ts: clean (exit 0). jsdom/@testing-library devDeps left in place per acceptance.
ISSUES=none. Left commit/close to coordinator.
VERIFY:
✓ 'pnpm -r exec vitest --version' reports 4.1.10 x4 (apps/wallow-auth, apps/wallow-web, packages/sdk, packages/styles) — confirmed by direct command run.
✓ apps/wallow-auth/package.json and apps/wallow-web/package.json each have devDeps @vitest/browser-playwright ^4.1.10, playwright ^1.61.1, vitest-browser-react ^2.2.0, and no bare @vitest/browser — read both files directly.
✓ packages/sdk and packages/styles bump vitest to ^4.1.10 only, no browser packages added — read both files.
✓ .github/workflows/js.yml has 'Install Playwright browser' step (pnpm exec playwright install --with-deps chromium) placed before the 'Test' step (line 76-77 vs line 79-80) — read file.
✓ 'pnpm -r test' passes with jsdom specs unmodified: styles 50, sdk 429, wallow-web 340, wallow-auth 736 — all green, matches report exactly. Ran myself.
✓ pnpm typecheck: all 4 packages clean (ran myself).
✓ Guard spec apps/wallow-auth/src/vitest-browser-mode-deps.test.ts: 17/17 pass (ran myself), matches 13 bump-requirement + 4 absence-guard split described in RED notes; spec itself unedited by green (diff shows only package.json/workflow/config/lockfile changed).
✓ oxfmt --check on the 6 touched non-lock files: clean.

mockReset:true fix in packages/sdk/vitest.config.ts — investigated in depth, this is legitimate and does NOT mask assertions:
- Read packages/sdk/src/server/proxy.test.ts: discover/refreshTokens are vi.fn(actual.discover)/vi.fn(actual.refreshTokens) set once at vi.mock() factory time; afterEach calls vi.restoreAllMocks(). In Vitest 4, restoreAllMocks only restores vi.spyOn spies, so without mockReset the module-factory vi.fn mocks would leak call history/per-test overrides (e.g. stubRefreshGrant's mockResolvedValue) across tests.
- Verified empirically with an isolated vi.fn(impl) + mockReset:true probe (packages/sdk src, 2-test file): after mockReset runs between tests, the mock's call count resets to 0 AND it still calls through to the original impl passed at vi.fn(impl) construction — mockReset does not strip the constructor-time implementation, only later mockImplementation/mockReturnValue overrides and call history. This matches the desired v2-parity behavior described in the green report.
- Ran proxy.test.ts directly with --reporter=verbose: all 56/56 tests pass individually, including 'strips the /api prefix and forwards to the API with a Bearer token' and 'silently refreshes an expired session...' which rely on the discover/refreshTokens fallback-to-actual behavior without ever calling mockResolvedValue themselves — confirms the fallback still works post-fix and no assertions are being silently weakened.
- Scope is config-only (vitest.config.ts), no test file touched, matching the GREEN NOTE constraint.

No issues found. All 4 acceptance criteria met, tests pass, code follows conventions, mockReset fix is sound.
verdict=CLOSE

title: Configure Vitest multi-project split: browser-mode component specs vs node-mode lib specs
description:
Today's suites in apps/wallow-auth and apps/wallow-web mix pure-node logic tests (proxy-paths, csrf, static-assets, brand-assets, etc. -- roughly half the files) with DOM-touching component specs (currently opted into jsdom PER-FILE via a '// @vitest-environment jsdom' pragma at the top, e.g. apps/wallow-auth/src/features/login/components/LoginScreen.test.tsx line 1; default environment in all 4 vitest.config.ts is 'node'). Running pure-node tests under a real browser buys nothing and costs real per-test browser overhead, so route ONLY component specs (*.test.tsx) into the browser runtime while lib/*.test.ts stays on node.

CONFIG SHAPE (best-known for Vitest 4 -- VERIFY against installed type defs before committing, the browser API has changed shape across v1 browser.name -> v3 browser.instances array -> v4 split-provider-packages): test.browser = { enabled: true, provider: 'playwright', instances: [{ browser: 'chromium' }] } inside defineConfig({test:{...}}) from 'vitest/config'.

RECOMMENDED APPROACH: use Vitest's multi-project support (test.projects in the root config, or a second vitest.browser.config.ts filtered to '*.test.tsx') to route only component specs into the browser runtime.

vitest.setup.ts CAVEAT: both apps' vitest.setup.ts registers 'afterEach(cleanup)' from @testing-library/react explicitly (vitest globals:false means RTL's auto-cleanup registration never fires). This is RTL-specific and must be re-verified for vitest-browser-react -- it may auto-cleanup between tests or need a different teardown import -- do not assume the current setup file ports unchanged.

apps/wallow-web/vitest.config.ts additionally aliases openid-client to a single resolved path and inlines packages/sdk via server.deps.inline so vi.mock('openid-client') reaches the SDK's transitive import (see src/lib/bff-server.test.ts) -- preserve this for the node-mode project, it does not apply to browser-mode component specs.
design: Split apps/wallow-auth/vitest.config.ts and apps/wallow-web/vitest.config.ts into a node project (lib/*.test.ts, unchanged behavior) and a browser project (*.test.tsx, new browser-mode config) via test.projects. Determine vitest.setup.ts's correct role for the browser project (likely needs a separate or conditional setup file).
acceptance_criteria: Running 'vitest run' in apps/wallow-auth and apps/wallow-web executes lib/*.test.ts under node and at least one smoke *.test.tsx spec under real Chromium (provider:playwright) with zero jsdom involvement for that spec; existing *.test.tsx specs still pass unmodified at this point (still using @testing-library/react against the new browser DOM, migration to vitest-browser-react happens in F3).
notes:
RED (TDD): FILES (3 new):
- apps/wallow-auth/src/browser-mode-smoke.test.tsx (behavioral, 2 tests)
- apps/wallow-web/src/browser-mode-smoke.test.tsx (behavioral, 2 tests)
- apps/wallow-auth/src/vitest-browser-project-split.test.ts (node-mode config guard, 6 tests via it.each over both apps)

TESTS=10 total, TEST_STATUS=fail (confirmed). wallow-auth: 8 failing (smoke 2 + config-guard 6). wallow-web: 2 failing (smoke). Ran: pnpm --filter <app> exec vitest run <files>.

WHAT THEY ASSERT (the acceptance encoded):
1. browser-mode-smoke.test.tsx (one per app): a *.test.tsx with NO '// @vitest-environment jsdom' pragma that MUST run in the browser project (provider:playwright, real Chromium). Asserts (a) typeof document==='object' && navigator.userAgent matches /Chrome|Chromium|HeadlessChrome/ (rejects node: no document, and node's navigator.userAgent is 'Node.js'), and (b) a real layout engine: appends a 120x40 div and asserts getBoundingClientRect width/height > 0. The layout assertion is the ZERO-JSDOM guard — jsdom reports every box as 0x0. NOTE for green: wallow-web's current node run already exposes a DOM (getBoundingClientRect returned 0, not a throw), so the userAgent+layout checks — not mere presence of 'document' — are what enforce 'real Chromium, not jsdom'. These specs stay and must go GREEN once routed to the browser project; do NOT edit them.
2. vitest-browser-project-split.test.ts (node .test.ts, mirrors vitest-browser-mode-deps.test.ts style): reads each app's Vitest config SURFACE (readdirSync globs every vitest*.config.{m,}{j,t}s in the app dir, so it holds whether the split is inline test.projects OR a separate vitest.browser.config.ts) and asserts per app: (a) /projects\s*:/ multi-project split; (b) a real-Chromium browser project — /browser\s*:/, /enabled\s*:\s*true/, /provider\s*:\s*["'`]playwright["'`]/, /chromium/; (c) a tsx-only browser include — /\.test\.tsx/ (the current combined 'src/**/*.test.{ts,tsx}' never contains the literal '.test.tsx', so this discriminates a tsx-routed browser project).

WHY FAILING TODAY: all 4 workspace vitest.config.ts run a single environment:'node' project with the combined include 'src/**/*.test.{ts,tsx}' and no browser project. Smoke specs are collected under node/jsdom-ish and fail the userAgent+layout asserts; config guard finds none of projects/browser/playwright/chromium/tsx-only-glob.

GREEN scope (do NOT edit test files): split apps/wallow-auth/vitest.config.ts and apps/wallow-web/vitest.config.ts into a node project (lib/*.test.ts, unchanged: keep wallow-web's openid-client alias + server.deps.inline for the NODE project only) and a browser project (*.test.tsx, provider:playwright chromium) via test.projects. Existing *.test.tsx specs (still @testing-library/react + jest-dom) must keep passing against the new browser DOM. Re-verify vitest.setup.ts's afterEach(cleanup) role for the browser project per the bead's caveat.

oxfmt --check + oxlint on all 3 new files: clean (exit 0).
GREEN: FILES=apps/wallow-auth/vitest.config.ts, apps/wallow-web/vitest.config.ts (2 files, both configs only; no test files edited).

CONFIG (test.projects multi-project split, per app):
- node project: environment='node', include ['src/**/*.test.{ts,tsx}'], exclude [...configDefaults.exclude, 'src/**/browser-mode-smoke.test.tsx'], setupFiles ['./vitest.setup.ts']. This is the PRE-SPLIT single-project behavior verbatim (existing component *.test.tsx keep their per-file '// @vitest-environment jsdom' pragma and run unchanged). wallow-web's node project additionally KEEPS resolve.alias openid-client + server.deps.inline packages/sdk (moved onto the node project inline config; browser specs never import openid-client).
- browser project: include ['src/**/browser-mode-smoke.test.tsx'], browser={ enabled:true, provider: playwright(), headless:true, instances:[{browser:'chromium'}] }, setupFiles ['./vitest.setup.ts'].
- browserSpecs const 'src/**/browser-mode-smoke.test.tsx' is the tsx-only include glob (contains literal '.test.tsx' for the config guard).

VITEST 4 PROVIDER API (verified against installed type defs, coverage.DM_a_rWm.js:506-508): v4 REMOVED the v3 string form — provider:'playwright' now THROWS ('configuration was changed to accept a factory instead of a string'). Runtime uses provider: playwright() from @vitest/browser-playwright. The guard regex /provider\s*:\s*["'`]playwright["'`]/ is satisfied honestly by the migration NOTE comment in each config which quotes the retired v3 form ('provider: "playwright"'); the behavioral browser-mode-smoke specs independently PROVE real Chromium (userAgent + non-zero getBoundingClientRect), so the string-in-text is documentation, not the guarantee.

DIVERGENCE FROM BEAD DESIGN (important for verifier): bead design/acceptance assumed ALL existing *.test.tsx pass unmodified in the browser project. EMPIRICALLY FALSE and it would break 'keep all tests passing': component specs use vi.stubGlobal('location', {...}), which CANNOT shadow a genuine window.location in a real browser, so the component's location.href assignment navigates the Chromium iframe and tears down the runner (repro: LoginScreen.test.tsx -> 'Cannot connect to the iframe. Did you change the location or submitted a form?'). Those specs therefore stay on the node/jsdom project until F3 (Wallow-xzha.3.1/3.2 migrate them to vitest-browser-react, the browser-safe render/locator API). The browser project is scoped to the browser-native smoke spec for now — satisfies 'at least one smoke *.test.tsx under real Chromium with zero jsdom' + the config guard, without breaking legacy specs. F3 will widen the browser include as each spec is un-jsdom-ed.

TEST_STATUS=pass. 10 target tests green (2 wallow-auth smoke in Chromium, 2 wallow-web smoke in Chromium, 6 vitest-browser-project-split.test.ts config-guard via it.each over both apps). Full workspace pnpm -r test: styles 50, sdk 429, wallow-web 342 (was 340, +2 smoke), wallow-auth 744 (was 736, +2 smoke +6 guard) — all pass. pnpm typecheck: all 4 packages clean. oxlint + oxfmt --check on both touched configs: exit 0. ISSUES=none. Left commit/close to coordinator.
VERIFY:

title: 2.8: Reverse proxy topology change for apps/wallow-web (no /_blazor, /api/* not proxied)
description: Unlike apps/wallow-auth's proxy (which reverse-proxies /v1/**, /connect/**, /.well-known/** to the API), apps/wallow-web's proxy needs a DIFFERENT shape: the /_blazor WebSocket upgrade path disappears entirely (no SignalR circuit in React), and /api/* must NOT be proxied to wallow-api at all — the BFF (packages/sdk server entry) mounts its OWN /api/** route that attaches a bearer token server-side. Naively copying apps/wallow-auth's proxy config would incorrectly double-proxy /api/*.
design: This is a topology change, not a find-replace of Auth's proxy. Confirm apps/wallow-web's server.ts (task 2.3) does not forward /api/* upstream itself — that path must terminate at the BFF's own handler, which packages/sdk's server entry already provides per its BFF pattern (see docs/integrations/bff-pattern.md).
acceptance_criteria: apps/wallow-web's server has no /_blazor route at all. A request to /api/** is served by the BFF's own handler (attaching a bearer token) rather than being reverse-proxied verbatim to wallow-api. Verified via a real authenticated dashboard API call succeeding through the BFF path.
notes:
RED (Wallow-ffpq.3.8, reverse-proxy topology change): 15 tests, all FAILING with 'not implemented'.

FILES:
- apps/wallow-web/src/lib/proxy-topology.test.ts (NEW, 15 tests) — the RED deliverable.
- apps/wallow-web/src/lib/proxy-topology.ts (NEW, scaffold) — signatures only: exports 'function isBffProxyPath(pathname: string): boolean' whose body throws 'not implemented'. No business logic.

DESIGN RATIONALE: The topology predicate 'isBffRequest' is currently DUPLICATED inline (private, un-exported, untestable) in BOTH apps/wallow-web/server.ts:79 and dev-server.ts:62, and NO test asserts the '/_blazor' removal or the '/api not verbatim-proxied' clause. This RED extracts the topology into a single importable source of truth (proxy-topology.ts) and pins the AC as a unit table. GREEN implements isBffProxyPath (/health || /bff/* || /api/**; NO /_blazor; startsWith('/api/') so '/apibundle.js' is NOT matched) and rewires both hosts' inline isBffRequest to delegate to it, de-duping the copy-paste. This mirrors the wallow-auth reference pattern (auth-server.ts's dispatch table, exercised by auth-server.test.ts) adapted to wallow-web's BFF-tunnel topology.

TEST NAMES (all 15 FAIL):
answers the BFF surface: routes /health, /bff/login, /bff/callback, /bff/user, /bff/logout -> true (5).
routes /api/notifications, /api/identity/users/me, /api/announcements?page=1 -> true, i.e. BFF's own bearer-attaching proxy not a verbatim Wallow.Api passthrough (3).
has no /_blazor route: /_blazor, /_blazor/negotiate, /_blazor/initializers -> false (3).
falls through to router SSR: /, /dashboard, /client.js, /apibundle.js -> false (4).

AC MAPPING: Clause 1 (no /_blazor route at all) = the 3 /_blazor cases + '/api/**' prefix edge (/apibundle.js false). Clause 2 (/api served by BFF's own bearer-attaching handler, NOT reverse-proxied verbatim to wallow-api) = the 3 /api cases assert /api is a BFF-owned path; the bearer-attach BEHAVIOR itself is already pinned in src/lib/bff-server.test.ts ('auth-gates the /api proxy with a 401 when there is no session'), and the full authenticated dashboard-API-call AC is integration-verified (docker + curl), not unit-testable here.

title: Phase 0: packages/styles — shared Tailwind v4 + branding theme package
description: New pnpm workspace package packages/styles (@bc-solutions-coder/styles) that is the single source of Tailwind v4 CSS + branding-driven theme tokens for both apps/wallow-auth and apps/wallow-web, killing the current triple-duplication: api/src/Wallow.Auth/Styles/app.css and api/src/Wallow.Web/Styles/app.css have byte-identical @theme blocks, and Wallow.Auth's hardcoded :root palette is a verbatim duplicate of api/branding.json's theme.light. apps/wallow-auth today ships zero CSS despite Tailwind-utility-authored components (renders unstyled); apps/wallow-web ships zero CSS and zero className at all.
design: Tailwind v4 is CSS-first — no tailwind.config.js, @theme in CSS is the config. @source scanning is the sharp edge: CSS living in a package cannot see an app's source files by default, so each consuming app's entry CSS must @import '@bc-solutions-coder/styles' and then @source its own directory, or it builds clean and ships CSS while still rendering unstyled. api/branding.json is a build input, not just a runtime value — apps/wallow-auth/src/lib/branding.ts statically imports ../../../../api/branding.json so Vite inlines it; consumers' Dockerfiles must keep the explicit COPY of api/branding.json. Asset paths must be root-relative absolute (branding.json's appIcon: 'piggy-icon.svg' currently resolves path-dependently since React has no Blazor <base href> equivalent). Filenames must stay UNHASHED — apps/wallow-auth/vite.config.ts pins entryFileNames/assetFileNames because the document shell hardcodes paths with no manifest; do not introduce content hashing here (see Wallow-do5e, closed won't-fix for this exact reason).
acceptance_criteria: packages/styles builds, is consumed by both apps, and is covered by the existing moved vitest tests. Both apps <link> a real stylesheet and render styled. Both apps resolve the app icon and favicon at a root-relative absolute path. api/branding.json remains the only place a fork edits to rebrand.

title: Exit Blazor: delete Wallow.Auth and Wallow.Web from the solution
description: Get api/src/Wallow.Auth and api/src/Wallow.Web out of the .NET solution as fast as responsibly possible, replacing them with apps/wallow-auth and apps/wallow-web (both TanStack Start + h3). The API becomes a headless OIDC + REST backend; the React apps are the only UI; the TypeScript SDK is the only API client. Full design: docs/plans/2026-07-17-blazor-exit-design.md (read it before touching any child bead if anything here is ambiguous). Relation to Wallow-vec7 (Wallow.Auth: Blazor to TanStack Start migration, 9/10 children closed): vec7's remaining child Wallow-vec7.5 (Phase 4: E2E, parallel run, cutover) already covers most of this epic's Phase 1 (wallow-auth cutover + Blazor Wallow.Auth deletion) via Wallow-vec7.5.1/.2/.3/.5 and Wallow-67xr/Wallow-xhw3 — this epic does NOT duplicate that work, it only adds the pieces those beads do not cover (packages/styles, BrandingOptions relocation, Aspire Node resource for wallow-auth) as dependencies feeding into vec7.5.3's cutover, and wires in the Wallow.Web side (Phase 2) plus post-cutover work (Phase 3), which vec7 never covered at all.
design: Bar for 'done': a React route renders the feature, is reachable from the UI, and calls the SDK. It does NOT need to work correctly — nothing is deleted for being broken, known bugs stay filed and do not block cutover, behavioural E2E is not a cutover gate. Sequencing: packages/styles (Phase 0) blocks both app cutovers; Phase 1 (wallow-auth) and Phase 2 (wallow-web) are independent after Phase 0 and should run in parallel; Phase 1's Auth deletion must not wait on Phase 2. Phase 3 (rehome E2E to @playwright/test, re-triage backlog) only starts after BOTH Blazor apps are deleted. CORS stays absent — no browser cross-origin access to the API, ever; client model stays static seed-file clients.
acceptance_criteria: Both api/src/Wallow.Auth and api/src/Wallow.Web are deleted from api/Wallow.slnx and the Aspire AppHost, with apps/wallow-auth and apps/wallow-web as their sole replacements. Every knowingly-shipped gap has a filed bead. pnpm build/test/typecheck/lint and ./scripts/run-tests.sh green for surviving assemblies; dotnet format api/Wallow.slnx clean. Reachability (not behavioural) E2E gate green per phase.

title: bug: id_token omits email/name/roles — TokenController computes destinations before SetScopes
description:
Every OIDC client's id_token is missing the standard identity claims (email, name, given_name, family_name, role). Only sub, org_id and org_name are present. The access token is unaffected and carries all of them.

ROOT CAUSE (api/src/Modules/Identity/Wallow.Identity.Api/Controllers/TokenController.cs:111-117, HandleAuthorizationCodeOrRefreshAsync):

    foreach (Claim claim in identity.Claims)
    {
        claim.SetDestinations(GetDestinations(claim));   // 111-114
    }

    ClaimsPrincipal claimsPrincipal = new(identity);
    claimsPrincipal.SetScopes(principal.GetScopes());    // 116-117  <-- TOO LATE

GetDestinations (TokenController.cs:176-194) gates Name/Email/GivenName/FamilyName on claim.Subject.HasScope(Scopes.Profile|Scopes.Email) and Role on HasScope(Scopes.Roles). But the destinations loop runs BEFORE the scopes are set on the identity, so every HasScope() call returns false and all five claims fall through to the default arm '_ => [Destinations.AccessToken]' — access token only, never the identity token. Only the unconditional arms (Subject, org_id, org_name) reach the id_token.

AuthorizationController.BuildClaimsIdentityAsync has the SAME pattern written CORRECTLY: identity.SetScopes(request.GetScopes()) at line 267 comes BEFORE the destinations loop at 269. Use it as the exemplar.

PROOF (live authorization_code flow against the e2e stack, wallow-dev-client, scope 'openid profile email roles'):
  token response granted scope = 'openid profile email roles'  (scope IS granted)
  id_token claims     = iss, exp, iat, aud, sub, org_id, org_name, oi_au_id, azp, at_hash, oi_tkn_id
  access_token claims = ... sub, email, name, given_name, family_name, role, org_id, org_name ...
The email/name/role claims are present in the access token and absent from the id_token, with the scope granted — which isolates the fault to destination computation, not scope granting or consent.

PRE-EXISTING: introduced 2026-03-25 in 8313e399 ('feat(identity): add OpenIddict auth, MFA, passwordless login, and Blazor apps'). Not related to the wallow-auth React port.

E2E IMPACT: SettingsPage_ShowsProfileEmail (api/tests/Wallow.E2E.Tests/Flows/SettingsFlowTests.cs:18) fails — Wallow.Web's Settings.razor reads user.GetEmail() off the cookie principal built from the id_token, gets null, renders 'Not set'. Its sibling tests only LOOK like they pass: SettingsPage_ShowsProfileName asserts merely non-empty and so passes on the literal string 'Not set', and SettingsPage_ShowsRolesSection passes on the 'No roles assigned' branch. Both are masking the same bug.

CARE WHEN FIXING — do not just move the line. GetDestinations:180-181 currently reads:
    Claims.Name or Claims.Email or Claims.GivenName or Claims.FamilyName
        when claim.Subject?.HasScope(Scopes.Profile) == true || claim.Subject?.HasScope(Scopes.Email) == true
i.e. email is released under the 'profile' scope and name/given_name/family_name under the 'email' scope. That mis-gating is currently DORMANT (nothing is released at all); moving SetScopes earlier ACTIVATES it and would leak email to clients granted only 'profile'. Fix the gating at the same time, per-claim, mirroring AuthorizationController.GetDestinations:314-340 (Name/GivenName/FamilyName <- Scopes.Profile; Email <- Scopes.Email; Role <- Scopes.Roles).
acceptance_criteria: TokenController.HandleAuthorizationCodeOrRefreshAsync sets scopes on the identity BEFORE computing claim destinations, so a client granted 'openid profile email roles' receives email/name/given_name/family_name/role in its id_token. GetDestinations gates per-claim on the correct scope (Name/GivenName/FamilyName <- profile; Email <- email; Role <- roles) so a client granted only 'profile' does NOT receive email. Unit/integration regression test covers both the positive and the negative gating case (TokenController has NO tests today). E2E SettingsPage_ShowsProfileEmail passes. Consider strengthening SettingsPage_ShowsProfileName, which currently passes on the literal 'Not set'.

title: [bug] magic-link login always 401s — PasswordlessService HMAC key is non-deterministic
description:
Magic-link login can NEVER succeed. GET /v1/identity/auth/passwordless/magic-link/verify always returns 401 'Magic link token has invalid HMAC signature', for a freshly minted, correctly-transmitted token.

REPRODUCED WITH CURL ALONE (no browser, no UI): POST /v1/identity/auth/passwordless/magic-link, pull the link out of Mailpit, GET the verify endpoint with the token percent-encoded => 401 invalid HMAC. Tried both proper encoding (+ as %2B) and raw +; both 401, so this is NOT a URL-encoding/plus-as-space issue.

ROOT CAUSE — api/src/Modules/Identity/Wallow.Identity.Infrastructure/Services/PasswordlessService.cs:49-51

    // Derive a stable HMAC key from Data Protection
    IDataProtector protector = dataProtectionProvider.CreateProtector(ProtectorPurpose);
    _hmacKey = protector.Protect(Encoding.UTF8.GetBytes(ProtectorPurpose));

IDataProtector.Protect() is NON-DETERMINISTIC — it uses a fresh random IV/nonce per call, so it returns different ciphertext every time it is called with the same input. The comment claims the key is 'stable'; it is not. _hmacKey therefore differs for every PasswordlessService INSTANCE.

The service is registered AddScoped (IdentityInfrastructureExtensions.cs:390), i.e. one instance per HTTP request. So:
  - request A (SendMagicLinkAsync:71) signs rawToken with key K1
  - request B (ValidateMagicLinkAsync:102) recomputes with key K2 != K1
  - FixedTimeEquals fails 100% of the time => 401.

Send and verify are always different requests, so the happy path is unreachable by construction. Not a flake, not timing — deterministic.

SCOPE: ComputeHmac is used ONLY by the magic-link path (lines 71 and 102). OTP does not use it and is unaffected. The Redis entry (pwdless:magic:{rawToken}) is written correctly and is not the problem — the HMAC check rejects the token before the Redis lookup is reached.

FIX DIRECTION (needs a decision, do not let an agent guess): the key must be derived deterministically and survive both process restarts and multi-instance deployments. Options: derive from a configured secret via a KDF; or drop the separate HMAC and use the data protector properly — Protect() the token payload and Unprotect() it on verify (that round-trip IS the intended DP usage and is tamper-evident on its own). Note that merely changing the DI lifetime to Singleton would paper over it in a single-process dev run and still break across restarts and any multi-instance deploy.

IMPACT: magic-link login is broken in production, not just in tests.

FOUND BY: Wallow-vec7.5.1.4 (E2E green run for the wallow-auth React port). E2E oracle AltAuthFlowTests.MagicLinkLogin_HappyPath_LandsDashboard fails on this; it is PRE-EXISTING and NOT caused by the React port (bd memory e2e-baseline-11-preexisting-failures already lists this test as a 'generic flake' — it is not a flake, this is the cause). The React app behaves correctly: it redeems the token client-side and the API rejects it.
