title: Forward X-Forwarded-For through the wallow-auth h3 proxy (rate-limit by real client IP)
description: The wallow-auth h3 reverse proxy (apps/wallow-auth/src/lib/auth-server.ts) does not send X-Forwarded-For upstream, so the API rate-limits every request against the proxy's own IP as a single bucket instead of the real client IP. This is a REGRESSION against the Blazor component the proxy replaces: api/src/Wallow.Auth/Services/CookieForwardingHandler.cs:35-42 forwards it deliberately, with the comment 'Forward X-Forwarded-For so the API rate-limits by real client IP, not Docker network IP'. Discovered during Wallow-vec7.4.3 (cookie attributes across the proxy), which fixes the sibling X-Forwarded-Proto/Host gap but explicitly leaves XFF out of scope because it cannot be tested through the same seam (see DESIGN). Wallow-vec7.5.3 DELETES CookieForwardingHandler.cs, so at cutover the capability vanishes with no replacement unless this lands first — hence the blocking edge.
design:
WHY IT IS NOT PART OF Wallow-vec7.4.3: that bead's tests drive the proxy through its framework-agnostic handle(request: Request) bridge. A WHATWG Request carries no socket, so there is no client IP to derive and no way to assert XFF at that seam. Fixing this requires reaching the h3 layer (event.node.req.socket.remoteAddress) and a different test seam than auth-server.test.ts's current fake-upstream harness — either drive a real node listener end-to-end (extend the existing createServer harness in auth-server.test.ts to hit the h3 app over a real socket) or inject an IP resolver into createAuthServer. Pick the seam first; that choice IS the work.

CHAINING: mirror the semantics Wallow-vec7.4.3 establishes for X-Forwarded-Proto/Host — an existing inbound X-Forwarded-For from an outer trusted proxy must be APPENDED to (comma-separated, per RFC 7239 / de-facto XFF), not overwritten, since behind a TLS-terminating ingress the leftmost entry is the real client and this proxy's socket only sees the ingress.

TRUST BOUNDARY (decide explicitly, do not skip): api/src/Wallow.Api/Program.cs:376-385 configures UseForwardedHeaders with KnownIPNetworks.Clear() and KnownProxies.Clear(), i.e. it trusts X-Forwarded-For from ANY peer ('Safe because Kestrel is not directly exposed to the internet'). The h3 proxy currently forwards ALL inbound headers verbatim (auth-server.ts:89), so a client that can reach wallow-auth directly can already forge X-Forwarded-For and bypass per-IP rate limiting today. Appending rather than replacing preserves that hole. Either (a) confirm wallow-auth is never directly reachable and document the assumption, or (b) strip/replace inbound XFF at this proxy and accept the loss of ingress chaining. This bead should settle it rather than inherit it silently.
acceptance_criteria: X-Forwarded-For reaches the upstream API carrying the real client IP, with an existing inbound XFF appended to rather than overwritten; covered by a test at whatever seam the DESIGN settles on (the handle(Request) bridge cannot express this — do not force it there); the trust-boundary question in DESIGN is answered in the commit body or a bead note; pnpm --filter @bc-solutions-coder/wallow-auth test green; pnpm --filter @bc-solutions-coder/wallow-auth typecheck green; pnpm lint clean; conventional commit e.g. 'fix(wallow-auth): forward x-forwarded-for so the api rate-limits by client ip'.
notes:
SCOUT (file-overlap resolution vs Wallow-xhw3, requested by coordinator).

CORE FILES (certain): apps/wallow-auth/src/lib/auth-server.ts — createProxyHandler()/applyForwardedHeaders() (lines ~89-121) is where XFF must be appended; apps/wallow-auth/src/lib/auth-server.test.ts — extend the test harness (currently drives the proxy purely via auth.handle(new Request(...)) with NO real socket — confirmed by reading the file: every case calls auth.handle(new Request(...)), never a real HTTP round trip to the auth server itself, only to the fake upstream). This confirms the bead's own DESIGN claim: a WHATWG Request has no socket, so today's harness structurally cannot assert XFF.

SEAM DECISION DRIVES WHETHER server.ts/dev-server.ts ARE ALSO TOUCHED:
- If you inject a resolver/derive XFF purely from already-present request headers (trusting an outer proxy per Program.cs:376-385's wide-open KnownIPNetworks.Clear()), the fix may stay entirely inside auth-server.ts + auth-server.test.ts.
- If you need the REAL socket IP (the actual client hitting wallow-auth, not just header-forwarding), note that BOTH apps/wallow-auth/server.ts and apps/wallow-auth/dev-server.ts convert the real Node IncomingMessage to a WHATWG Request via their own toWebRequest() BEFORE calling authServer.handle(request) (or server.handle(...)) — h3's toWebHandler synthesizes a fresh event with no real socket from that Request. To get the real remoteAddress you would need one of: (a) have server.ts/dev-server.ts stamp req.socket.remoteAddress into an x-forwarded-for-ish header in their own toWebRequest() before calling handle(), or (b) switch the proxy-path dispatch to h3's toNodeListener(app) so h3 owns the real IncomingMessage directly (event.node.req.socket). EITHER path touches apps/wallow-auth/server.ts and apps/wallow-auth/dev-server.ts (their toWebRequest/handleRequest/handleProxy functions), NOT their isProxyRequest gate functions.

OVERLAP WITH Wallow-xhw3: xhw3 touches ONLY isProxyRequest() in dev-server.ts (lines 62-64) and, if it lifts the predicate (its design option a), a NEW apps/wallow-auth/src/lib/proxy-paths.ts plus importing it into server.ts's isProxyRequest. That is a DIFFERENT function than anything tt5j touches even in the worst case (toWebRequest/handleProxy, not isProxyRequest) — but it IS the same two files (dev-server.ts, and possibly server.ts) if tt5j needs the socket-seam. Different functions in the same file rarely produce real git conflicts, but to avoid any rebase churn: SERIALIZE, xhw3 FIRST (it is smaller, mechanical, already blocks Wallow-67xr which is higher urgency), tt5j SECOND once xhw3's final isProxyRequest/proxy-paths shape has landed. If tt5j's implementer determines the header-only seam is sufficient (auth-server.ts only), the two are fully parallel-safe instead — confirm this at the start of tt5j's work and update this note.

TEST APPROACH: vitest, apps/wallow-auth/src/lib/auth-server.test.ts — extend the existing createServer-based upstream harness to also drive the PROXY over a real socket (not just auth.handle(new Request(...))) if the socket seam is chosen, OR add an injected resolver test if the config-injection seam is chosen. A WHATWG Request has no socket, so the Node host (server.ts/dev-server.ts) will stamp req.socket.remoteAddress into an INTERNAL header CLIENT_IP_HEADER=x-wallow-client-ip in its toWebRequest(); the proxy (auth-server.ts) APPENDS that value to any inbound X-Forwarded-For chain then STRIPS the seam header before the upstream hop. title: fix(security): isSafeReturnUrl and ReturnUrlValidator accept backslash-prefixed cross-origin returnUrl
description:
Both returnUrl safety gates -- isSafeReturnUrl (packages/sdk/src/auth-oidc.ts:49-55)
and ReturnUrlValidator.IsSafe (api/src/Wallow.Auth/Helpers/ReturnUrlValidator.cs:18)
use the identical rule: `url.startsWith('/') && !url.startsWith('//')`. A value like
`/\evil.com` (or `/\/evil.com`) satisfies this rule locally -- it starts with one
'/' and its second character is '\', not '/'. But when the browser (or .NET's own
URI resolver) actually resolves it against the current origin, WHATWG URL parsing
treats backslash as an additional path-separator for special schemes (http/https),
so `/\evil.com` normalizes to `//evil.com` -- a protocol-relative URL that resolves
CROSS-ORIGIN to https://evil.com. Verified directly: `new URL('/\\evil.com',
'https://good.example.com/login').href` === 'https://evil.com/'.

This is an open-redirect gap in the core validators, not a bug in any single
screen. It affects both stacks identically (oracle-faithful: the C# validator has
had this gap since before the port; auth-oidc.ts intentionally mirrors it 1:1).

Blast radius (every navigation call site that trusts either validator's true
verdict to redirect the browser):

TypeScript (apps/wallow-auth/src, via getWallowAuthSdk().oidc.isSafeReturnUrl):
  - features/login/components/LoginScreen.tsx:283
  - features/register/components/RegisterForm.tsx:248
  - features/consent/components/ConsentScreen.tsx:294
  - features/mfa-challenge/components/MfaChallengeForm.tsx:383
  - features/mfa-enroll/components/MfaEnrollForm.tsx:479
  - features/verify-email/components/VerifyEmailConfirm.tsx:155
  - features/verify-email/sign-in-href.ts:45
  - packages/sdk/src/auth-oidc.ts:33 (assertSafeReturnUrl, used by URL builders)

C# (api/src/Wallow.Auth/Components/Pages, via ReturnUrlValidator.IsSafe/Sanitize):
  - Login.razor:535
  - MfaChallenge.razor:157
  - VerifyEmailConfirm.razor:32,68
  - MfaEnroll.razor:48 (via Sanitize, forceLoad navigation)

Every one of these treats a "safe" verdict as license to navigate
(location.href / Navigation.NavigateTo / redirect) to the attacker-controlled
origin -- i.e. the full login/register/consent/mfa/verify-email flow surface on
both the React port and the Blazor oracle.
design:
Fix BOTH validators consistently in the same change (they must stay behaviorally
identical -- that parity is asserted by existing tests/comments on both sides).

Normalize backslashes to forward slashes BEFORE applying the relative-path
check, then re-check for a resulting "//" prefix:

  TS (packages/sdk/src/auth-oidc.ts, isSafeReturnUrl):
    const normalized = url.replaceAll('\\', '/');
    return normalized.startsWith('/') && !normalized.startsWith('//');

  C# (api/src/Wallow.Auth/Helpers/ReturnUrlValidator.cs, IsSafe):
    string normalized = url.Replace('\\', '/');
    return normalized.StartsWith('/') && !normalized.StartsWith("//", StringComparison.Ordinal);

Do NOT change the return value contract (still bool; Sanitize's fallback
behavior unchanged) and do NOT change the "starts with exactly one '/'" rule
itself -- only add backslash normalization ahead of it, so legitimate relative
URLs are unaffected. Confirm no in-repo relative returnUrl legitimately contains
a backslash (grep for constructed returnUrls before landing).
acceptance_criteria:
- isSafeReturnUrl('/\\evil.com') === false and isSafeReturnUrl('/\\/evil.com') === false
  (and any equivalent WHATWG-normalizes-to-protocol-relative form).
- ReturnUrlValidator.IsSafe("/\\evil.com") == false and IsSafe("/\\/evil.com") == false,
  same equivalents.
- New regression tests added to both auth-oidc.test.ts and
  ReturnUrlValidatorTests.cs covering the backslash-prefixed forms.
- All existing isSafeReturnUrl / ReturnUrlValidator.IsSafe tests (67+ on the TS
  side per prior bead notes) still pass -- no legitimate relative returnUrl
  (e.g. "/dashboard", "/settings/profile?x=1") is newly rejected.
- Every call site listed in the description (7 TS screens/builders + 4 Blazor
  pages) is re-verified manually or via existing tests to still accept its
  legitimate relative returnUrl after the fix.
notes: RE-SCOPED per docs/plans/2026-07-17-blazor-exit-design.md bead triage: the Wallow.Auth/ReturnUrlValidator.cs half of this bug dies with Blazor (Wallow-vec7.5.3 deletes the file). The identical gap in packages/sdk/src/auth-oidc.ts's isSafeReturnUrl SURVIVES and is a live open redirect (re-verified: new URL('/\evil.com', 'https://good.example.com/login').href === 'https://evil.com/'). Re-scope this bug to the SDK only; do not close it when Wallow.Auth is deleted.

title: fix(wallow-auth): MfaChallenge dead-ends on absolute returnUrl from external login
description:
MfaChallengeForm refuses on mount for 100% of external-login + MFA users, so they can never complete sign-in.

AccountController.cs:313 and :335 (external-login-callback, Path A: existing linked account with MfaEnabled, and the org-MFA-policy grace-expired branch) redirect to {authUrl}/mfa/challenge?returnUrl={encodedReturn}. That returnUrl was normalized at L273-277: it is either a value that passed redirectUriValidator.IsAllowedAsync -- which REQUIRES Uri.TryCreate(uri, UriKind.Absolute) (OpenIddictRedirectUriValidator.cs:24) -- or the authUrl fallback, absolute by construction. So the returnUrl arriving at /mfa/challenge on this path is ALWAYS ABSOLUTE.

isSafeReturnUrl (packages/sdk/src/auth-oidc.ts:55) returns true ONLY for url.startsWith('/') && !url.startsWith('//'). It is false for every absolute URL.

MfaChallengeForm.tsx:297-308 computes returnUrlIsUnsafe = returnUrl !== undefined && !isSafeReturnUrl(returnUrl), and refuses ON MOUNT via navigate({href:'/error?reason=invalid_redirect_uri'}). The two accept-sets are provably disjoint, so every external-login MFA user is bounced to /error before the code field ever renders. They cannot sign in at all.

SCOPE: external-login users ONLY. The password path is unaffected: Login.razor:509 BuildMfaRedirectUrl('/mfa/challenge') threads Login.razor's own ReturnUrl, which is the RELATIVE OIDC returnUrl (ReturnUrlValidator.IsSafe gate at L535; BuildApiReturnUrl(string relativeUrl) at L570). Relative passes isSafeReturnUrl.

THE ORACLE HAS THE SAME BUG, SOFTER: MfaChallenge.razor:157 does 'string? safeReturnUrl = ReturnUrlValidator.IsSafe(ReturnUrl) ? ReturnUrl : null;' so an absolute returnUrl becomes null and falls to L170 'No ReturnUrl -- direct login, not OIDC. Show success state without redirecting.' Blazor users verify successfully and then STRAND on a success screen. The React port converted a soft post-verify strand into a hard pre-verify dead-end -- strictly worse (the Blazor user is at least signed in).
design:
GOVERNING RULE (established by the Wallow-vec7.3.10 security adjudication): guard where the CLIENT picks the destination; defer where the SERVER does.

This screen DOES pick the destination -- MfaChallengeForm.tsx:342 does 'globalThis.location.href = returnUrl' raw on the no-ticket branch. So a guard IS required here (unlike .3.10, whose nav target is a constant path). But the guard must ACCEPT WHAT THE SERVER ACTUALLY SENDS. Deleting it is not the fix; widening isSafeReturnUrl is not the fix either (it is correct for its own relative-only contract and is under 67 tests in .2.2).

FIX: three-state verdict at the mount guard, mirroring the .3.5 Logout precedent (LogoutScreen.tsx:222-243, auth.validateRedirectUri with fail-closed narrowing):
  1. returnUrl === undefined  -> ACCEPT-NO-REDIRECT. The oracle's ordinary direct (non-OIDC) sign-in. No probe, render the form, never navigate.
  2. isSafeReturnUrl(returnUrl) -> ACCEPT. A relative path is decided locally; no network probe. Keeps the password path (the common case) synchronous and unchanged.
  3. otherwise -> PROBE auth.validateRedirectUri(returnUrl) and narrow STRICTLY on { allowed: true }. Anything else -- allowed:false, a rejection (unreachable validator), a non-object body, the string 'true' -- REFUSES to ERROR_HREF. Same allow-list the API itself used to admit this returnUrl at AccountController.cs:274, so a value the server sent is a value the probe accepts.

An empty-string returnUrl short-circuits to REFUSE without a probe (IsNullOrEmpty parity, LogoutScreen's hasRedirectUri gate): '?returnUrl=' is a malformed link, not a destination to ask the server about.

FAIL CLOSED WHILE IN FLIGHT: do not render the form until the verdict lands. A form rendered optimistically is a form a fast user can submit, burning a one-time second factor on a destination we may be about to refuse -- the exact cost the mount-time refusal exists to avoid (ConsentScreen precedent + Login.razor L533-540).

NOT AN OPEN REDIRECT: 'https://evil.example.com/steal' parses absolute, so the probe runs, IsAllowedAsync origin-allow-lists it (OpenIddictRedirectUriValidator.cs:29-31) against registered redirect/post-logout URIs + AuthUrl, returns allowed:false, and the screen refuses. '//evil.example.com/steal' fails Uri.TryCreate(UriKind.Absolute) -> allowed:false -> refused. Fail-closed in every direction, so an unreachable validator never becomes a reason to trust a URI.

TEST DEBT TO CORRECT: MfaChallengeForm.test.tsx:595 'refuses an absolute return url' PINS THE BUG -- it asserts the dead-end using an evil origin, which masks that the same code path also refuses the legitimate allow-listed absolute the server sends. It must be split into the evil case (still refused, now via the probe) and the legitimate allow-listed case (now accepted). The test mocks must gain auth.validateRedirectUri.
acceptance_criteria:
1. An allow-listed ABSOLUTE returnUrl (the shape AccountController.cs:313/335 actually sends, e.g. http://localhost:5002/login) renders the code field and completes verification -- it does NOT navigate to /error. This is the regression test for the dead-end and MUST fail against the current code.
2. A non-allow-listed absolute returnUrl (https://evil.example.com/steal) is still REFUSED to /error?reason=invalid_redirect_uri, and the code field never renders.
3. A protocol-relative returnUrl (//evil.example.com/steal) is still REFUSED.
4. An empty-string returnUrl is still REFUSED, and does so WITHOUT probing the server.
5. A relative returnUrl (/connect/authorize?client_id=web) is accepted with NO validateRedirectUri probe -- the password path stays synchronous.
6. A nullish returnUrl still renders the form and never navigates (direct sign-in).
7. The probe fails CLOSED: a rejected validateRedirectUri call, an { allowed: false } body, a non-object body, and a literal string 'true' all refuse.
8. The form does not render while the probe is in flight (no burning a second factor on an undecided destination).
9. No regression: wallow-auth suite green (baseline 463/463), SDK green (429/429), typecheck + oxlint + oxfmt clean.
notes:
GREEN (Wallow-vec7.3.17). VERDICT: THE CLAIM IS REAL. Verified against the wire, not accepted on assertion. TEST_STATUS=pass 46/46.

=== 1. THE DEAD-END IS REAL, AND TOTAL ===
AccountController.cs:313 (external-login-callback Path A: existing linked account, MfaEnabled) and :335 (org-MFA-policy, grace expired) both do:
  Redirect($"{authUrl}/mfa/challenge?returnUrl={encodedReturn}")
returnUrl was normalized at L273-277: EITHER it passed redirectUriValidator.IsAllowedAsync -- which bails unless Uri.TryCreate(uri, UriKind.Absolute) (OpenIddictRedirectUriValidator.cs:24) -- OR it was replaced by the authUrl fallback, absolute by construction (GetRequiredAuthUrl). There is no third path. So returnUrl reaching /mfa/challenge here is ALWAYS ABSOLUTE.
isSafeReturnUrl (auth-oidc.ts:55) returns true ONLY for startsWith('/') && !startsWith('//').
The two accept-sets are PROVABLY DISJOINT. MfaChallengeForm.tsx:297-308 refused on mount for 100% of external-login MFA users -> /error?reason=invalid_redirect_uri, before the code field ever rendered. They could not sign in AT ALL.

=== 2. SCOPE: EXTERNAL-LOGIN ONLY. Password users unaffected. ===
The other producer is Login.razor:509 BuildMfaRedirectUrl('/mfa/challenge'), which threads Login.razor's own ReturnUrl -- the RELATIVE OIDC returnUrl (gated by ReturnUrlValidator.IsSafe at L535; BuildApiReturnUrl(string relativeUrl) at L570). Relative passes isSafeReturnUrl. Pinned by 'decides a relative return url locally, without asking the server'.

=== 3. THE ORACLE HAS THE SAME BUG, SOFTER (found, not ported) ===
MfaChallenge.razor:157: 'string? safeReturnUrl = ReturnUrlValidator.IsSafe(ReturnUrl) ? ReturnUrl : null;' -> an absolute returnUrl becomes null and falls to L170 'No ReturnUrl -- direct login, not OIDC. Show success state without redirecting.' Blazor external-login MFA users verify SUCCESSFULLY and then strand on a success screen. The React port converted a soft POST-verify strand into a hard PRE-verify dead-end -- strictly worse: the Blazor user is at least signed in. Both are broken; this bead fixes the port and the strand together.

=== 4. THE FIX -- GOVERNING RULE APPLIED, GUARD NOT DELETED ===
Per the .3.10 adjudication: guard where the CLIENT picks the destination; defer where the SERVER does.
This screen DOES pick: MfaChallengeForm.tsx does 'globalThis.location.href = returnUrl' RAW on the no-ticket branch. So unlike .3.10 a guard is REQUIRED -- deleting it would be a live open redirect. What was wrong is not that the guard exists but that it could not recognise what the server actually sends. isSafeReturnUrl was NOT widened either: its relative-only contract is correct and is under 67 tests in .2.2.
Three-state verdict at the mount guard, mirroring the .3.5 Logout precedent (LogoutScreen.tsx:222-243):
  localDecisionOf(returnUrl, isRelativeSafe) -> 'accept' | 'refuse' | 'ask'
    undefined            -> accept  (oracle's direct non-OIDC sign-in; no probe, never navigates)
    isSafeReturnUrl true -> accept  (relative; decided locally, NO network -- the password path stays synchronous)
    ''                   -> refuse  (IsNullOrEmpty parity; a malformed link is not worth asking about -- LogoutScreen's hasRedirectUri short-circuit)
    otherwise            -> ask     (absolute: only the allow-list can tell the hand-off from an attack)
  verdictOf(local, pending, allowed) -> 'accept' | 'refuse' | 'pending'
    'ask' -> useQuery(auth.validateRedirectUri(returnUrl)), narrowed STRICTLY on { allowed: true } via isRedirectUriAllowed (mirrors the C# 'body?.Allowed == true'; the STRING 'true' must not pass, or truthiness would admit allowed:'false').
Same allow-list the API itself used to admit this returnUrl at L274, so a value the server sent is a value the probe accepts. FAIL CLOSED in every direction: rejection (unwrap() throws on non-2xx), allowed:false, non-object body, unreachable validator -> refuse. 'pending' is its own verdict and renders NOTHING -- a form rendered optimistically is a form a fast user submits, burning a one-time second factor on an undecided destination (the exact cost the mount-time refusal exists to avoid).

=== 5. NOT AN OPEN REDIRECT (attack traces) ===
https://evil.example.com/steal -> parses absolute -> probe -> IsAllowedAsync origin-allow-lists (validator L29-31) against registered redirect/post-logout URIs + AuthUrl -> allowed:false -> REFUSED to /error.
//evil.example.com/steal -> fails Uri.TryCreate(UriKind.Absolute) -> allowed:false -> REFUSED.
javascript:alert(1) -> parses with scheme 'javascript', origin is not an http(s) allow-listed origin -> allowed:false -> REFUSED.
Net change to the refusal set: NOTHING new is admitted except origins the server's own allow-list already vouches for.

=== 6. TEST DEBT CORRECTED (the bug was PINNED by a test) ===
MfaChallengeForm.test.tsx:595 'refuses an absolute return url' asserted the dead-end using an EVIL origin, which masked that the identical code path also refused the LEGITIMATE allow-listed absolute the server sends. That one test made the bug look like a feature. Split into:
  'refuses an absolute return url the allow-list does not know'  (evil -> still refused, now for a reason that DISCRIMINATES)
  'lets the external-login hand-off through on an allow-listed absolute return url'  (THE regression test)

  x lets the external-login hand-off through on an allow-listed absolute return url

description: Update the existing .github/workflows/sdk-publish.yml (currently npm-based: npm ci / npm test / npm run build / npm version / npm publish, working-directory packages/typescript-sdk) to use pnpm instead, and point its working-directory at the new packages/sdk path. title: Extend release-please to monorepo/manifest mode (src + packages/sdk + future packages/ui-*)
description: Extend the repo's release-please configuration from its current single-component 'simple' release-type (component '.') to monorepo (manifest) mode with multiple independently-versioned components: 'src' (.NET backend, existing train, unchanged behavior), 'packages/sdk' (semver, published to GitHub Packages), and a placeholder/pattern for future 'packages/ui-*' packages (semver, published). Apps under apps/* are private and must NOT get version-bump PRs — they deploy by git SHA / CalVer instead. Accept and document the trade-off that release-please's manifest mode does not auto-cascade a workspace:* dependency bump (a published UI package depending on the SDK needs a manual scope bump when the SDK bumps; apps are unaffected since they carry no semver).

Check .github/workflows/release-please.yml for how the action is invoked and update its config-file/manifest-file inputs if it currently assumes single-package mode. title: Switch SDK .d.ts emit to tsc --emitDeclarationOnly on TS7 (fallback: pin TS6)
description: TypeScript 7.0 does not ship a stable programmatic compiler API until 7.1, so tsup's dts generation path (via rollup-plugin-dts, which calls the TS API programmatically) can break on TS7. Fix packages/sdk's declaration-file generation to sidestep this: default approach is to run 'tsc --emitDeclarationOnly' as a separate build step (the GA native tsc CLI emits .d.ts fine on TS7) while tsup/esbuild continues to bundle the JS. If that proves impractical, the accepted fallback is to pin TypeScript to v6 for packages/sdk only (trivial with pnpm per-package deps) while the rest of the workspace uses TS7 via tsconfig.base.json (task A3).
design: In packages/sdk/package.json: disable tsup's 'dts: true' option in tsup.config.ts, and add/adjust the 'build' script to run both tsup (JS bundle) and 'tsc --emitDeclarationOnly -p tsconfig.json' (or a dedicated tsconfig.build.json with declaration: true, emitDeclarationOnly: true, outDir matching tsup's dist/). packages/sdk/tsconfig.json should extend the root tsconfig.base.json (task A3). If TS7's tsc --emitDeclarationOnly also has issues, fall back to setting "typescript": "^5.6.0" (current TS6-era pin already in package.json devDependencies) as an override scoped to packages/sdk only — pnpm allows per-package version pins even when the workspace root/other members use TS7. ROOT CAUSE (confirmed): 'oxfmt --write/--check .' and bare 'oxlint' both defaulted to scanning the whole repo tree from cwd, respecting only .gitignore (not extension-aware for oxfmt). .oxfmtrc.json's ignorePatterns:[] meant oxfmt walked ALL non-gitignored files repo-wide (md/json/yaml/html/css), picking up src/Wallow.Api/appsettings.json, seed.json, README.md files under src/Modules and tests/, Wallow.Auth/Web Styles/app.css, pnpm-workspace.yaml, tsconfig.base.json, etc. oxlint was actually already safe in practice (extension-filtered to .js/.ts/.jsx/.tsx/.mjs/.cjs, so it never matched .cs/.json/.md/.css regardless of ignorePatterns) but still reached one non-workspace file (scripts/generate-docs-theme.mjs) since bare 'oxlint' scans cwd.

FIX CHOSEN: allowlist via explicit positional paths in the package.json scripts (the 'Prefer scoping the format scripts to the workspace globs rather than .' option), NOT a denylist ignorePatterns addition. Rationale: an ignorePatterns denylist is exactly the fragile pattern that caused this bug (empty/incomplete deny-list silently leaks scope whenever a new root file/dir is added later). An allowlist of explicit paths can't drift that way — anything not named is never touched, full stop. Verified empirically that oxfmt/oxlint do NOT error on not-yet-existing paths (apps/ doesn't exist yet) — they're silently skipped, confirmed via 'npx oxfmt --check apps packages nonexistentdir123' (exit 0, no error).

FILES CHANGED: package.json only (root). No changes to .oxlintrc.json or .oxfmtrc.json content — both already valid; the scope bug lived entirely in the CLI invocation, not the config bodies.

Before:
  "lint": "oxlint",
  "format": "oxfmt --write .",
  "format:check": "oxfmt --check ."

After:
  "lint": "oxlint apps packages",
  "format": "oxfmt --write apps packages package.json pnpm-workspace.yaml tsconfig.base.json .oxlintrc.json .oxfmtrc.json",
  "format:check": "oxfmt --check apps packages package.json pnpm-workspace.yaml tsconfig.base.json .oxlintrc.json .oxfmtrc.json"

This matches the RETRY note's explicit scope list verbatim: packages/**, apps/**, plus root config files package.json, pnpm-workspace.yaml, tsconfig.base.json, .oxlintrc.json, .oxfmtrc.json. pnpm-lock.yaml deliberately excluded (generated, not hand-formatted).

All reported diagnostics are warnings (no-shadow, consistent-function-scoping, no-underscore-dangle) confined to packages/typescript-sdk/src/server/oidc.test.ts and packages/typescript-sdk/src/generated/@tanstack/react-query.gen.ts. Manually enumerated every one of the 45 paths in the output against the allowlist — zero hits under src/, tests/, docs/, docfx/, seed.json, appsettings.json, branding.json, or any Styles/app.css. The nonzero exit is genuine pre-existing formatting debt in packages/typescript-sdk (real unformatted SDK files from earlier tasks), not a scope leak — expected/acceptable since this bead's job is scoping, not fixing SDK formatting (that's downstream, e.g. Wallow-07t5.2.3).

title: Decide tenancy model: should creating an org switch the creator's active tenant?
description:
Wallow-hg61 fixed the confirmed half of the bug: the org creator is now added as an admin member and audit fields are stamped correctly (OrganizationService.CreateOrganizationAsync now takes an optional creatorUserId).

DELIBERATELY LEFT OUT (needs a product/architecture decision, not a guess):
Production CreateOrganizationAsync creates the org under the CURRENT tenant (tenantContext.TenantId) and does NOT switch the creator's active TenantId. But TestSupportService.CreateIsolatedOrgAsync mints a BRAND-NEW TenantId per org and moves the user onto it. These are two different tenancy models, and the E2E test helper currently relies on the second one.

The open question: does a user belong to exactly one tenant, or can a user be a member of multiple orgs and switch context between them?

This matters MORE now that Wallow.Web is being extracted and the API/SDK becomes the public boundary: SDK consumers creating orgs will hit whichever semantics we choose. Decide the model, then implement (or explicitly reject) tenant switching on org creation.

Do not let an agent guess this.

title: E2E: cover CSRF gate on a real browser mutation in BffFlowTests
description: E2E run for the SDK BFF epic passed 55/0, but BffTunnel_LoginAuthedCallLogout_CompletesFullFlow never exercises the Phase 6 CSRF gate: it clicks only bff-call-api (a GET), and logout() is a plain navigation rather than a fetch. The tanstack-min example's bff-mutate POST button — built specifically to demo the CSRF interceptor — is never clicked. Unit tests mocked fetch, so a real-browser regression where the app fails to send the CSRF token (403 on every mutation) would be caught by NEITHER layer. This bead adds that coverage.
acceptance_criteria: A BffFlowTests E2E test clicks the example's bff-mutate POST button after login and asserts the mutation SUCCEEDS (proving the CSRF token is sent and accepted by the Phase 6 gate). Test uses data-testid selectors per .claude/rules/E2E.md. Full E2E suite re-run green.
notes:
DONE. E2E now covers the CSRF gate on a real browser mutation.

FILES:
- tests/Wallow.E2E.Tests/Flows/BffFlowTests.cs — new test + extracted LoginToExampleAsync helper (reused by the pre-existing flow test; no behavior change to it).
- packages/typescript-sdk/examples/tanstack-min/src/app.ts — bff-mutate now POSTs postV1IdentityOrganizations (was postV1IdentityAuthKeys); writes to new bff-mutate-result testid.
- packages/typescript-sdk/examples/tanstack-min/public/index.html — added data-testid=bff-mutate-result; relabelled bff-mutate button. All pre-existing testids preserved.
- packages/typescript-sdk/examples/tanstack-min/README.md — CSRF section documents the Create org button.
- scripts/run-e2e.sh — BUG FIX (see below).

TEST NAME: BffFlowTests.BffMutation_AfterLogin_CarriesCsrfTokenAndClearsTheGate

E2E RESULT: ./scripts/run-e2e.sh => Test Run Successful. Total 75: Passed 56, Failed 0, Skipped 19. The 55 previously-passing tests all still pass (55 + 1 new = 56); the 19 skips are the same pre-existing [Skip]-annotated ones.

WHAT THE TEST ASSERTS (all three, in order):
1. It captures the actual proxied request via RunAndWaitForResponseAsync and asserts the x-csrf-token header is present AND non-empty on the wire. This is the assertion mocked-fetch unit tests structurally cannot make.
2. Response status == 201 (from the API), i.e. NOT the proxy's 403 CSRF_INVALID, which is raised before forwarding — so a 201 proves the gate accepted the token and forwarded.
3. The DOM (bff-mutate-result via data-testid) shows '201 created org'.
Selectors are data-testid only, per .claude/rules/E2E.md; login goes through the real OIDC flow via the existing LoginPage page object.

NEGATIVE CONTROL (the test is capable of failing — verified, not merely reasoned):
Temporarily commented out request.headers.set('x-csrf-token', ...) in the example's interceptor, rebuilt the bff-example image, re-ran the test => FAILED with 'The mutation was sent without an x-csrf-token header — the SDK's CSRF interceptor did not run.' Then restored and confirmed green again. This is exactly the '403 on every POST' regression class the bead exists to catch.

ISSUES FOUND (2 real bugs, both pre-existing, NOT introduced here):

[1] scripts/run-e2e.sh NEVER BUILT THE bff-example IMAGE (fixed here). The script dotnet-publishes the .NET images and builds 'garage', but never built the Node bff-example image, so docker compose silently reused whatever stale wallow-bff-example:test existed locally. Proof: before the fix, the running container served an index.html with NO bff-mutate button at all — i.e. the image predated T10.2's example update, so every BffFlowTests E2E run to date (including the '55 passed' verification) exercised a STALE example. Fixed by adding an explicit '$COMPOSE_CMD build bff-example' next to the garage build. This is why the gap in Wallow-jgr2.12.1 went unnoticed: the updated example was never actually deployed to the test stack.

[2] PUT /v1/identity/settings/user 500s — ISettingsService IS NOT REGISTERED IN DI. My first attempt pointed the example's mutation at the settings endpoint; it returned 500 with:
  System.InvalidOperationException: Unable to resolve service for type 'Wallow.Shared.Kernel.Settings.ISettingsService' while attempting to activate 'Wallow.Identity.Api.Controllers.IdentitySettingsController'.
This means EVERY endpoint on IdentitySettingsController (GET/PUT/DELETE settings/user and settings/tenant) is dead at runtime in the containerized stack. Out of scope for this bead — NOT fixed. Worth filing as its own bug.

ENDPOINT CHOICE (why not the original auth/keys POST): POST /v1/identity/auth/keys is [HasPermission(ApiKeyManage)], and ApiKeyManage is granted ONLY to the 'admin' role (RolePermissionMapping) or the 'apikeys.manage' scope. A TestUserFactory user has the default 'user' role and the BFF requests only 'openid profile email offline_access', so that POST can only ever return 403 Forbidden — it could never 'SUCCEED' as the acceptance criteria require, and a permission-403 is easily confused with a CSRF-403. POST /v1/identity/organizations is [HasPermission(OrganizationsCreate)], which the default 'user' role DOES have, so it returns a clean 201 — an unambiguous success signal. The example still demonstrates the identical CSRF interceptor on a state-changing POST.
close_reason: CSRF gate now covered by real-browser E2E (negative control verified); also fixed run-e2e.sh not building bff-example image

title: Fingerprint Web/Auth static CSS to fix stale-cache styling loss
description: Deployed Wallow.Web/Auth link CSS at a stable unfingerprinted URL (css/app.css). Fix: migrate both apps to MapStaticAssets + @Assets fingerprinting + ImportMap so CSS URLs are content-hashed and caches auto-bust every deploy.
acceptance_criteria: Both Wallow.Web and Wallow.Auth serve app.css via a content-fingerprinted URL; verified in an actual container publish that the rendered link resolves to a fingerprinted path returning 200 text/css with correct content; web-components and auth-components tests green.
close_reason: Won't-fix: fingerprinting Blazor's MapStaticAssets/@Assets is moot post-Blazor-exit. The React apps deliberately pin UNHASHED filenames because the document shell hardcodes paths with no manifest (see apps/wallow-auth/vite.config.ts's entryFileNames/assetFileNames pins). Cache-busting is a real future concern but needs a manifest, not this fix; a successor bead should be filed if/when that work is prioritized.

title: Fix E2E test failures: MFA org isolation, 401s, and enrollment timeout
description:
Running ./scripts/run-e2e.sh reveals 11/21 E2E test failures with 3 root causes:

1. **MFA org state leaks between tests** (5 failures): AuthenticatedE2ETestBase tests (Dashboard flows, LoginToDashboard) get redirected to /mfa/enroll instead of dashboard. The OrganizationService.UpdateSettingsAsync change sets MFA required on the default org, poisoning all subsequent tests. Tests need per-test org isolation OR the MFA tests need their own org.

2. **401 Unauthorized in CreateWithMfaAsync** (4 failures): TestUserFactory.CreateWithMfaAsync fails at line 33 with 401. MFA enrollment API call after user creation returns unauthorized. Likely the bearer token from login is invalid or expired, possibly because the org now requires MFA and login returns partial auth instead of full auth.

3. **Enrollment backup codes timeout** (1 failure): EnrollmentDuringLogin still times out at MfaEnrollPage.SubmitAsync waiting for backup-codes OR error element. The earlier page object fixes were not sufficient.

4. **Grace period org conflict** (1 failure): CreateInMfaRequiredOrgAsync with gracePeriodDays=3 fails because the org already requires MFA without grace period (from another test).

All issues trace back to test isolation: MFA org settings from one test contaminate the shared default org. The fix should ensure each MFA test creates its own isolated org or resets org state.
close_reason: All 21/21 E2E tests passing. Fixed org isolation, MFA challenge redirect detection, enrollment cookie relay, and QR code JS error.

title: SSE Infrastructure

design: Components: (1) RealtimeEnvelope gets RequiredPermission, RequiredRole, TargetUserId nullable fields. title: Tenant-Scoped Registration & Organization Management

Two registration paths: direct (platform-level, no org) and OIDC flow (tenant resolved from client_id). Includes admin UI in Wallow.Web for org and client management.
design: Extend OpenIddict application Properties JSON with TenantId. Resolve tenant from client_id during OIDC authorize flow, carry through to registration. Add org_id/org_name JWT claims. Block non-members from logging in through tenant-scoped clients. Admin UI for org CRUD + client management scoped to user's orgs. See docs/plans/2026-03-24-tenant-scoped-registration-design.md and docs/plans/2026-03-24-tenant-scoped-registration-plan.md

description: Wire up all new services in DI, implement the admin bootstrap priority chain in Program.cs, register SetupMiddleware, and verify the full integration works end-to-end.
design: In IdentityInfrastructureExtensions: register AdminBootstrapOptions, PreRegisteredClientOptions, ISetupStatusProvider/SetupStatusProvider, PreRegisteredClientSyncService. In Program.cs: run DefaultRoleSeeder, run PreRegisteredClientSyncService.SyncAsync, check CLI args then AdminBootstrapOptions then fall through to setup wizard. Register SetupMiddleware after CorrelationIdMiddleware. CLI args use ASP.NET Core's built-in --AdminEmail/--AdminPassword mapping. See Task 8 and 11 in implementation plan.

title: Setup Wizard API
description: SetupController provides anonymous endpoints for the first-time setup wizard. Step 1: create admin account. Step 2: register clients (shows generated secrets once). Step 3: review and complete. All endpoints check setup status and return 409 Conflict if setup is already complete.
design: RegisterSetupClientCommand creates OpenIddict application with generated 32-byte secret, tags with source=setup. SetupController at /api/v1/identity/setup with endpoints: GET status, POST admin, POST clients, POST complete. API contracts: CreateAdminRequest, RegisterClientRequest, RegisterClientResponse, SetupStatusResponse. Controller uses IMessageBus to dispatch commands. See Tasks 3 (partial) and 6 in implementation plan.

title: Admin Bootstrap & Setup Infrastructure
description: Three mechanisms for creating the initial admin account, evaluated in order (first wins): CLI params, AdminBootstrap config section, Setup wizard. Shared ISetupStatusProvider interface lets middleware check setup state without referencing Identity module. SetupMiddleware blocks all non-setup requests with 503 when setup is required.
design: ISetupStatusProvider in Shared.Contracts. SetupStatusProvider in Identity.Infrastructure checks RoleManager/UserManager for admin existence. AdminBootstrapOptions with IsConfigured computed property. BootstrapAdminCommand creates admin role if missing, creates user, assigns role. IsSetupRequiredQuery delegates to role/user checks. SetupMiddleware allows /api/v1/identity/setup/* paths, blocks all others with 503 JSON response. See Tasks 2-4 and 7 in implementation plan.

title: Config-Driven Client Registration
description: A PreRegisteredClients section in appsettings.json declares OAuth clients declaratively. A hosted service performs declarative sync on startup — creates missing clients, updates changed ones, deletes config-owned clients removed from config. Config-owned clients are tagged with source=config in OpenIddict properties so user-created clients are never touched.
design: PreRegisteredClientOptions bound to config section. PreRegisteredClientDefinition holds ClientId, DisplayName, GrantType, RedirectUris, PostLogoutRedirectUris, Scopes, Secret. IsPublic computed from empty Secret. PreRegisteredClientSyncService uses IOpenIddictApplicationManager for CRUD. See Task 1 and Task 5 in implementation plan.

title: Client Registration & First-Time Setup
description: Replace the implicit IdentityDataSeeder with config-driven client registration, an admin bootstrap priority chain (CLI > Config > Setup Wizard), and a first-time setup wizard. Config becomes the source of truth for pre-registered OAuth clients with declarative sync. Admin accounts are bootstrapped via CLI args, appsettings config, or an interactive setup wizard — in that priority order.
design: Clean Architecture with CQRS. Options classes in Identity.Infrastructure, commands/queries in Identity.Application with Wolverine handlers, shared interface in Shared.Contracts, API endpoints in Identity.Api, middleware and CLI wiring in Wallow.Api. No cross-module calls. See docs/plans/2026-03-24-client-registration-and-setup-design.md and docs/plans/2026-03-24-client-registration-and-setup-plan.md for full spec.

title: Fix Identity ↔ ApiKeys cross-module violations
description: Architecture tests (ModuleIsolationTests) reveal two cross-module dependency violations: Identity.Infrastructure references ApiKeys.Application (via ApiKeyAuthenticationMiddleware using IApiKeyService), and ApiKeys.Api references Identity.Application (via ApiKeysController using ApiScopes, ScopePermissionMapper, IScopeSubsetValidator). These violate the rule that modules only reference Shared.Contracts for cross-module communication. Fix by moving shared contracts to Shared.Contracts/Shared.Kernel, relocating the middleware to ApiKeys.Infrastructure, and removing all cross-module project references.
design: See docs/designs/2026-03-24-identity-apikeys-module-isolation.md for full design. Key decisions: (1) IApiKeyService + records → Shared.Contracts.ApiKeys, (2) ApiScopes + IScopeSubsetValidator → Shared.Contracts.Identity, (3) ScopePermissionMapper → Shared.Kernel (has implementation logic), (4) ApiKeyAuthenticationMiddleware → ApiKeys.Infrastructure, (5) Remove cross-module csproj references.

title: Auth Architecture — Incremental Hardening
description: Harden OpenIddict configuration, externalize all environment-specific values to appsettings.json, add DI extension points so forks customize auth without modifying upstream files, extract Branding and ApiKeys modules from Identity, add MFA infrastructure, prepare DB-per-tenant abstractions, and configure three-app Docker deployment (API, Auth, Web).

DB-per-tenant is abstraction-only (ITenantConnectionResolver) — no implementation yet. Three deployable apps (Wallow.Api, Wallow.Auth, Wallow.Web) share ServiceUrls config section. See docs/plans/2026-03-23-auth-architecture-design.md and docs/plans/2026-03-23-auth-architecture-plan.md

title: Add relative-path guard to Login.razor ReturnUrl
description: In src/Wallow.Auth/Components/Pages/Login.razor, in HandleLogin() method (around line 141), before calling Navigation.NavigateTo(ReturnUrl, forceLoad: true), validate that ReturnUrl is a relative path. Check: if Uri.TryCreate(ReturnUrl, UriKind.Absolute, out _) succeeds, it's an absolute URL — redirect to /error?reason=invalid_redirect_uri instead. Only navigate to ReturnUrl if it's relative. This fixes the open redirect where an attacker crafts login?returnUrl=https://evil.com.

title: Implement OpenIddictRedirectUriValidator
description: Create OpenIddictRedirectUriValidator in Wallow.Identity.Infrastructure/Services/OpenIddictRedirectUriValidator.cs. Implements IRedirectUriValidator. Behavior: (1) Query IOpenIddictApplicationManager.ListAsync() for all registered apps. (2) Extract RedirectUris and PostLogoutRedirectUris from each app. (3) Parse URIs and build HashSet<string> of allowed origins (scheme://host:port). (4) Add AuthUrl (from IConfiguration) and API base URL as implicitly trusted. (5) Cache in IMemoryCache with 5-min TTL. (6) IsAllowedAsync parses incoming URI, extracts origin, checks set membership. Edge cases: malformed URIs return false, null/empty return false, port normalization (80 for HTTP, 443 for HTTPS).

title: Core Validator Service
description: Create the IRedirectUriValidator interface and OpenIddictRedirectUriValidator implementation that validates redirect URIs against registered OpenIddict client origins. Includes DI registration and unit tests.
design: Interface in Wallow.Identity.Application/Interfaces/. Implementation in Wallow.Identity.Infrastructure/Services/. Queries IOpenIddictApplicationManager.ListAsync() for registered apps, extracts origins from RedirectUris and PostLogoutRedirectUris, caches in IMemoryCache with 5-min TTL. title: Redirect URI Whitelist
description: Prevent open redirect vulnerabilities by validating all redirect URIs against registered OpenIddict client applications. This epic adds an IRedirectUriValidator service that checks URIs against registered client origins and hardens all redirect points.
design: Origin-based matching (scheme+host+port). AuthUrl and API base URL implicitly trusted. 5-minute cache TTL via IMemoryCache. Scoped DI registration. Error redirects go to {authUrl}/error?reason=invalid_redirect_uri. See docs/superpowers/specs/2026-03-20-redirect-uri-whitelist-design.md for full spec.

title: Wrap Keycloak HttpRequestException with status code preservation
description:
Multiple services call response.EnsureSuccessStatusCode() on Keycloak API responses, which throws HttpRequestException and loses the original HTTP status code and response body. This makes all Keycloak failures appear as 500 in Foundry.

Affected services:
- KeycloakAdminService (Identity)
- KeycloakServiceAccountService (Identity)
- KeycloakIdpService (Identity)
- ScimUserService (Identity)
- SsoClaimsSyncService (Identity)

Fix approach:
1. Create an ExternalServiceException (or KeycloakApiException) in Shared.Kernel that carries:
   - OriginalStatusCode (int)
   - ServiceName (string)
   - ResponseBody (string, for logging)
2. Replace EnsureSuccessStatusCode() calls with a helper method that inspects the response and throws ExternalServiceException with the original status details
3. Add mapping in GlobalExceptionHandler: ExternalServiceException → map to appropriate status (502 Bad Gateway for upstream failures, or preserve original status where meaningful)
4. Log the original Keycloak response body at Warning/Error level for debugging

Also fix KeycloakAdminService.GetUserAsync/GetUserByEmailAsync/GetUsersAsync which catch Exception, log, and return null — callers may not handle null properly.

2. Add mapping in GlobalExceptionHandler: ForbiddenAccessException → 403 Forbidden with ProblemDetails

title: SEC2: Fix SCIM token validation broken by empty tenant context
description:
## Vulnerability (NEW-IDENT-004, MEDIUM, Risk Score 16)

Middleware order: TenantResolution -> ScimAuth. TenantResolution only sets tenant when context.User.Identity?.IsAuthenticated == true. SCIM requests use a custom Bearer token (not JWT), so user is NOT authenticated at TenantResolution stage. TenantContext is empty when ValidateTokenAsync queries EF Core with tenant query filters, likely causing all SCIM tokens to fail.

## Files to Modify
- src/Modules/Identity/Foundry.Identity.Infrastructure/Authorization/ScimAuthenticationMiddleware.cs
- src/Modules/Identity/Foundry.Identity.Infrastructure/Repositories/ScimConfigurationRepository.cs (if exists)

## Remediation Options (pick one)
Option A: ScimConfigurationRepository should bypass tenant filter for token lookup:
```csharp
public async Task<ScimConfiguration?> GetByTokenAsync(string tokenHash, CancellationToken ct)
{
    return await _context.ScimConfigurations
        .IgnoreQueryFilters()
        .FirstOrDefaultAsync(s => s.TokenHash == tokenHash, ct);
}
```
Then set tenant context from the matched config's TenantId.

Option B: Move SCIM middleware before TenantResolution and have it set tenant context.

Option C: Extract tenant from a header or token claim before validation.

After token validation succeeds, ensure tenant context is set:
```csharp
tenantSetter.SetTenant(TenantId.Create(scimConfig.TenantId));
```

## Testing
- Verify SCIM endpoints work with valid SCIM bearer token
- Verify tenant context is properly set after SCIM auth
- Verify invalid tokens are rejected
- Verify SCIM operations are scoped to correct tenant

title: SEC2: Validate payment currency matches invoice currency
description:
## Vulnerability (B-5, MEDIUM, Risk Score 15)

ProcessPaymentHandler.cs:42 creates payment with command.Currency (user-supplied) but never validates it matches invoice.TotalAmount.Currency. A user could pay in a cheaper currency.

## Files to Modify
- src/Modules/Billing/Foundry.Billing.Application/Commands/ProcessPayment/ProcessPaymentHandler.cs
- src/Modules/Billing/Foundry.Billing.Domain/Billing/Errors/BillingErrors.cs (add CurrencyMismatch error)

## Remediation
Add currency validation before creating the payment:
```csharp
if (!string.Equals(command.Currency, invoice.TotalAmount.Currency,
    StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase))
{
    return Result.Failure(BillingErrors.CurrencyMismatch);
}
```

## Testing
- Verify payment with matching currency succeeds
- Verify payment with different currency returns CurrencyMismatch error
- Verify case-insensitive currency comparison works (USD vs usd)

title: SEC2: Fix partial payment marks invoice as fully paid
description:
## Vulnerability (B-4, MEDIUM, Risk Score 15)

ProcessPaymentHandler.cs:54-57 marks invoice as paid after creating any payment, without checking the payment covers the invoice total. A dollar1 payment on a dollar1000 invoice marks it as fully paid. The overpayment check (line 30) only prevents paying MORE, not LESS.

## Files to Modify
- src/Modules/Billing/Foundry.Billing.Application/Commands/ProcessPayment/ProcessPaymentHandler.cs

## Remediation
After creating the payment, check if total payments cover the invoice:
```csharp
Money totalPaid = invoice.Payments
    .Where(p => p.Status == PaymentStatus.Completed)
    .Aggregate(Money.Zero(invoice.TotalAmount.Currency),
        (sum, p) => sum + p.Amount);

if (totalPaid >= invoice.TotalAmount &&
    invoice.Status is InvoiceStatus.Issued or InvoiceStatus.Overdue)
{
    invoice.MarkAsPaid();
}
```

title: [H5] Validate SignalR hub group membership against tenant
description:
## Severity: HIGH

## Summary
The SignalR RealtimeHub JoinGroup() method accepts any arbitrary group ID without authorization checks. Any authenticated user can join any group and receive real-time messages for other tenants.

## Finding
**File:** src/Foundry.Api/Hubs/RealtimeHub.cs:50-53

JoinGroup(string groupId) adds the caller to the requested SignalR group without validating:
- Whether the group belongs to the caller's tenant
- Whether the caller has access to the resource the group represents

The hub does require authentication ([Authorize] at class level), but any authenticated user from Tenant A could join groups like 'project:tenant-b-project-id' and receive all real-time updates intended for Tenant B.

## Impact
Cross-tenant data leakage via SignalR real-time messages. An attacker could monitor another tenant's notifications, activity feeds, and other real-time events.

## Required Fix
1. Validate that the authenticated user has access to the requested group before calling Groups.AddToGroupAsync()
2. Group IDs should follow a consistent format that embeds tenant context (e.g., 'tenant:{tenantId}:resource:{resourceId}')
3. Extract the tenant from the group ID and compare against the caller's ITenantContext
4. Consider using a group naming convention that makes tenant validation straightforward
5. Add tests to verify cross-tenant group join is rejected with appropriate error

title: [H4] Apply rate limiting policies to endpoints
description:
## Severity: HIGH

## Summary
Three rate limiting policies are registered (auth, upload, global) but zero endpoints use [EnableRateLimiting]. The UseRateLimiter() middleware is registered but does nothing. Authentication endpoints can be brute-forced without throttling.

## Finding
**File:** src/Foundry.Api/Extensions/ServiceCollectionExtensions.cs:135-164

Policies defined:
- 'auth': 5 requests per 5 minutes (fixed window)
- 'upload': 10 requests per hour (fixed window)
- 'global': 1000 requests per hour (fixed window)

A codebase-wide search for [EnableRateLimiting], [DisableRateLimiting], or RequireRateLimiting returns ZERO results. No endpoint or controller applies any rate limiting policy.

**File:** src/Foundry.Api/Extensions/RateLimitDefaults.cs — Constants defined but unused.

## Impact
No rate limiting is enforced anywhere. Authentication endpoints can be brute-forced. Upload endpoints have no throttling. The global rate limit is purely decorative.

## Required Fix
1. Apply [EnableRateLimiting("auth")] to auth endpoints (AuthController)
2. Apply [EnableRateLimiting("upload")] to upload endpoints (StorageController upload actions)
3. Consider setting a global fallback limiter via options.GlobalLimiter for all other endpoints
4. Consider per-IP vs per-user rate limiting keys (currently using fixed window with no partition key, so it's global across all users). For auth, partition by IP. For upload, partition by user.
5. Add tests to verify rate limiting returns 429

title: [H3] Add permission enforcement to Configuration module controllers
description:
## Severity: HIGH

## Summary
FeatureFlagsController and CustomFieldsController use [Authorize] but have no [HasPermission] attributes. Any authenticated user (including basic 'user' role) can create/update/delete feature flags and custom fields, despite comments saying 'admin only'.

## Findings
**Files:**
- src/Modules/Configuration/Foundry.Configuration.Api/Controllers/FeatureFlagsController.cs:27 — Only [Authorize], comments say 'admin only' but no enforcement
- src/Modules/Configuration/Foundry.Configuration.Api/Controllers/CustomFieldsController.cs:16 — Only [Authorize]

Both controllers have comments on individual actions like '(admin only)' but this is never enforced via [HasPermission].

## Impact
Any authenticated user can:
- Create, update, and delete feature flags
- Create, update, and delete custom field definitions
- Create/delete feature flag overrides for any tenant

## Required Fix
1. Define appropriate permission types (e.g., PermissionType.ConfigurationManage or more granular read/write split)
2. Add [HasPermission(PermissionType.ConfigurationManage)] to both controllers at the class level (or per-action for granular control)
3. Add the new permission(s) to RolePermissionMapping.cs — map to 'admin' and possibly 'manager' roles
4. Add corresponding tests to verify unauthorized users get 403

title: [H2] Add fallback authorization policy requiring authentication
description:
## Severity: HIGH

## Summary
There is no fallback authorization policy. Any controller endpoint without an explicit [Authorize] or [HasPermission] attribute is accessible anonymously by default. This is a defense-in-depth gap.

## Finding
**File:** src/Modules/Identity/Foundry.Identity.Infrastructure/Authorization/PermissionAuthorizationPolicyProvider.cs:33-34

GetFallbackPolicyAsync() delegates to the default provider, which returns null (no fallback). ASP.NET Core best practice is to require authenticated users globally via fallback policy, then opt out with [AllowAnonymous] where needed.

Currently all controllers do have explicit [Authorize] or [AllowAnonymous], so the immediate risk is low. But any future endpoint added without an attribute would be silently open.

## Required Fix
Configure the fallback policy to require authenticated users. In the service registration (likely in AddIdentityModule or AddApiServices):

```csharp
services.AddAuthorization(options =>
{
    options.FallbackPolicy = new AuthorizationPolicyBuilder()
        .RequireAuthenticatedUser()
        .Build();
});
```

After this change, verify that all intentionally-anonymous endpoints have [AllowAnonymous]:
- AuthController (login/refresh) — already has it
- ScimController — already has it (uses own auth middleware)
- ChangelogController — already has it
- Health check endpoints — mapped via MapHealthChecks (may need .AllowAnonymous())
- Root info endpoint at / — may need .AllowAnonymous()
- OpenAPI/Scalar endpoints — check if they need anonymous access in dev

description: Add a 'changes' job (dorny/paths-filter@v3) to .github/workflows/ci.yml with outputs code/dotnet/js, then gate: build on code (everything except docs/** and **/*.md), unit-tests/integration-tests/cross-tenant-tests on dotnet (needs: [changes, build]), fork-smoke on js (needs: changes, update its 'No needs:' comment). Leave docker-images-*, e2e-tests untouched (inherit docs-only skip through needs: build) and leave merge-coverage's needs/if alone (adding changes would defeat its always()). Exact YAML including filter lists and comments: Task 3 of docs/plans/2026-08-28/1527-ci-caching-plan.md.
acceptance_criteria: pnpm lint:actions green. Hand-verified scenarios against the final YAML: docs-only PR skips everything; api-only skips fork-smoke only; js-only skips the three .NET test jobs + merge-coverage while build/docker/e2e still run; mixed runs everything. Commit: 'ci: skip .net test jobs and fork-smoke when their inputs are untouched'.
notes:
First confirm on dorny/paths-filter's README that v3 supports negation patterns in filter lists (it has since v2.7.0). Epic Wallow-85hs.
GREEN: FILES=.github/workflows/ci.yml (only file in commit f2926f07 'ci: skip .net test jobs and fork-smoke when their inputs are untouched' + Claude-Session trailer; verified via git show --stat = 1 file changed, 60 insertions, 4 deletions).

DEVIATION FROM PLAN #1 (version): pinned dorny/paths-filter@v4, not the plan's @v3 floor. v4.0.3 is current (gh api releases/latest, published 2026-08-05); the moving @v4 tag resolves to the SAME sha as v4.0.3 (ceb8a2b8f2d89434be7ff52d3de7ec3738c5cc9d, both refs compared). v4.0.0 was a node24 runtime bump only, no filter-semantics change. Major-only pin matches this repo's convention (checkout@v7, cache@v6).

DEVIATION FROM PLAN #2 (LOAD-BEARING BUG IN THE PLAN'S YAML): added predicate-quantifier: 'some-with-excludes' to the filter step. The plan's YAML as literally written DOES NOT WORK. Under paths-filter's DEFAULT quantifier ('some'), a negated pattern is inert -- a file matches if it matches at least one rule, and '!docs/**' is not read as an exclusion. So 'code' would evaluate to TRUE on a docs-only PR ('**' matches the markdown) and the plan's headline scenario (docs-only skips everything) would never fire. The bead note's premise that 'v3 supports negation patterns since v2.7.0' is true only in the sense that the SYNTAX parses; the EXCLUSION behaviour requires an opt-in quantifier. Proven empirically -- see the counter-check below.
  Why 'some-with-excludes' and not 'every': predicate-quantifier is a single step-level input applied to ALL filters in the block, not per-filter. 'every' would require a file to match ALL of a filter's patterns, which is correct for 'code' but makes 'dotnet' (api/**, global.json, scripts/e2e.sh, .github/workflows/ci.yml) PERMANENTLY FALSE, since no single file can match all four. 'some-with-excludes' (match >=1 positive rule AND 0 negated rules) gives the intended semantics for 'code' while leaving the negation-free 'dotnet'/'js' lists behaving exactly as plain any-of lists. It is the only quantifier correct for all three filters in one block. Available since v4.0.3 (dorny/paths-filter PR #322). A load-bearing comment in the YAML records this so a later edit does not delete it.
