title: identity: narrow ClientsController service-account actions from AdminAccess to per-action ServiceAccounts* guards
description:
Implements the decision recorded on Wallow-7zav (see its notes for full rationale; premise history in docs/plans/2026-08-27/1127-backlog-triage-and-sequencing.md and docs/plans/2026-08-04/1113-doc-accuracy-audit.md W-H2).

ClientsController.cs currently guards everything with a class-level [HasPermission(PermissionType.AdminAccess)] (ClientsController.cs:24). The three ServiceAccounts* permissions are declared (PermissionType.cs:73-75), scope-mapped (ScopePermissionMapper.cs:49-51), role-granted to admin (RolePermissionMapping.cs:43-45) and seeded (api/seed.json:81,88,94) but checked nowhere.

WORK: remove the class-level attribute and add per-action [HasPermission] guards (the repo pattern — see UsersController, OrganizationsController):

- [HasPermission(PermissionType.AdminAccess)] — GetAll, GetById, GetByTenant, Create, Update, Delete, RotateSecret (relying-party client CRUD; stays admin — no scope maps to it and docs never promised narrowing there)
- [HasPermission(PermissionType.ServiceAccountsRead)] — ListServiceAccounts, GetServiceAccount
- [HasPermission(PermissionType.ServiceAccountsWrite)] — CreateServiceAccount, UpdateServiceAccountScopes
- [HasPermission(PermissionType.ServiceAccountsManage)] — RotateServiceAccountSecret, RevokeServiceAccount

CONSTRAINTS the split already accounts for — do not 'improve' them:
- The permission check is exact-match (PermissionAuthorizationHandler), and stacked [HasPermission] attributes AND together. The class-level attribute MUST be removed, not supplemented; a leftover class-level AdminAccess makes every service-account action still require admin.
- No permission hierarchy: manage does not imply write/read at the check. Supersets are grant-side (admin role grants all three; tokens combine scopes). Consistent with apikeys.*/users.* — do not add hierarchy.
- UpdateServiceAccountScopes is Write, not Manage: Create already accepts arbitrary scopes, so Manage-gating updates would be theater.

TESTS: admin-authenticated integration suites (Wallow.Identity.IntegrationTests/ServiceAccounts/*) stay green because the admin role grants all three. Add coverage that a principal holding ONLY ServiceAccountsRead can list but gets 403 on create/rotate/revoke, and that ServiceAccountsWrite cannot rotate/revoke — that 403-on-narrower-token gap is exactly what audit finding W-H2 flagged.

DOCS: docs/api/service-accounts.md permission table needs no change (it documents the scope surface, which now becomes true). Verify no doc claims manage implies read/write; if one does, correct it to 'scopes combine; request all three for full management'.

Acceptance:
- Class-level AdminAccess attribute removed from ClientsController; per-action guards exactly as listed above.
- New tests proving the 403 boundaries between Read/Write/Manage.
- ./scripts/run-tests.sh identity green, and the Identity integration suite green (./scripts/run-tests.sh api/tests/Modules/Identity/Wallow.Identity.IntegrationTests integration).
notes:
Implemented in commit 90039107 exactly per the split on this bead. Findings from implementation:

- Test infrastructure gap closed: no role grants a partial ServiceAccounts* set, so TestAuthHandler (Wallow.Tests.Common) gained an X-Test-Scopes header that adds a space-separated 'scope' claim — the test principal then flows through the real PermissionExpansionMiddleware user-scope path (ExpandUserScopes), which is the same path a narrow token takes in production. Reusable for any future permission-boundary test.
- New suite: ServiceAccountPermissionBoundaryTests (15 tests) in Wallow.Identity.IntegrationTests/ServiceAccounts — pins all 403 edges (read cannot create/update/rotate/revoke; write cannot rotate/revoke; manage alone cannot list, documenting no-hierarchy), the positive cases per permission, that serviceaccounts.* scopes do NOT reach the relying-party /identity/clients surface, and that admin retains everything. Verified red-first: the six positive cases 403'd under the old class-level AdminAccess.
- Docs/seed corrected beyond the bead's expectation: docs/api/service-accounts.md:75-90 claimed AdminAccess for all management endpoints (the audit-era doc fix, now stale) — replaced with a per-route permission table + explicit no-hierarchy note. The write/manage descriptions in seed.json AND their duplicate in ApiScopeSeeder.cs (two copies, kept in sync) now say what the scopes actually guard; 'Full Service Account Management' was a hierarchy claim the exact-match check never honored.

Gates: fast suite 4967/4967, solution-wide integration tier 276/276 (both include the identity suites the acceptance names), dotnet format clean.

title: chore(auth): prune snowballed auth surface (legacy SDK trio, duplicate hasRole, unused router context, return-URL guard sprawl)
description:
## Background

An audit of the auth surface against the TanStack Start authentication guide
(https://tanstack.com/start/latest/docs/framework/react/guide/authentication) concluded the
architecture is right and should NOT move toward the guide's DIY session pattern: wallow-auth is
deliberately a stateless reverse proxy (the .NET API owns identity), wallow-web is a true BFF, and
wallow-web's /dashboard gate already matches the guide's `_authed` layout pattern. What makes the
code hard to read is accumulated dead/duplicated surface from earlier iterations, not the design.

## Cleanup worklist (ranked by value)

1. **Delete the legacy imperative trio in the SDK browser entry** — `login()`, `logout()`,
   `getUser()` in `packages/sdk/src/auth.ts`. They hardcode `/bff/*` and assign `location`
   directly; `login()` 500s under SSR (both wallow-web route files carry comments explaining why
   they avoid it), and `getUser()` duplicates `currentUserQuery` against `/bff/user` with no
   cache. Remaining consumers to migrate first: `bff-demo.tsx` and `SignOut.tsx` in wallow-web.

2. **Resolve the two same-named `hasRole` helpers** — `packages/auth/src/authorization.ts`
   (typed `CurrentUserResponse`, case-insensitive) vs `packages/sdk/src/claims.ts` (free-form
   claim bag, different casing semantics). The `packages/auth` barrel re-exports the SDK's
   claim-bag `isAdmin` next to its own typed `hasRole`. Pick one user model at the app boundary;
   make the other internal to the SDK server code.

3. **Delete or adopt `WallowRouterContext`** — exported and spec'd in
   `packages/sdk/src/route-context.ts`, used by nobody; both apps declare their own
   structurally-identical `RouterContext` in `__root.tsx`, and the `user?` field is never
   populated anywhere. Either both apps import it or it goes.

4. **Trim `packages/auth`'s unwired surface** — `hasRole`/`hasPermission` have zero app call
   sites (the only authz gate in any app is `isAdmin` in wallow-web's `dashboard/route.tsx`).
   wallow-auth depends on the package for a single `useCurrentUser` call (`routes/invitation.tsx`)
   while the re-exported `requireAuth`/`loginRedirect` half is unusable there (no `/bff` mount).

5. **Fix CSRF inconsistencies** — the token lives in a module-scope variable
   (`packages/sdk/src/csrf.ts`) while `create-sdk.ts` documents that everything must be
   per-request to avoid cross-user leakage; move it per-instance. Also stop wiring the CSRF
   interceptor in wallow-auth, whose proxy topology has no CSRF token at all.

6. **Consolidate return-URL guarding** — five variants with different empty/unsafe rules:
   `shared/hooks/use-return-url-guard.ts`, `features/login/auth-result.ts` (`authDispositionOf`),
   `features/mfa-challenge/hooks/use-redirect-verdict.ts`, `accept-terms-handoff.ts` (ungated,
   server-adjudicated), and LogoutScreen (server allow-list). Replace with one helper with
   explicit modes (refuse-empty / empty-ok / server-allowlist), keeping each site's documented
   rationale as the mode choice.

7. **Smaller drift** — MFA enrollment UI exists twice (wallow-auth `features/mfa-enroll/` screen
   and wallow-web `features/mfa/components/MfaEnrollFlow.tsx`) over the same three mutations;
   `client_id` search params are renamed at the destructure layer in login/consent but at the
   search-schema layer in register/mfa-challenge — pick one convention.

## Non-goals

- No move to `createServerFn`, `useSession()`, or an AuthProvider context — the repo's server
  routes + SDK presets + TanStack Query current-user pattern are the better fit for this
  topology and the guide's DIY premise (app owns the user store) does not apply.
- No change to the proxy/BFF split or to the beforeLoad gating in wallow-web.

## Acceptance

Each numbered item either lands as its own commit/child bead or is explicitly declined with a
note here. `pnpm check` green after each.
notes:
Item 1 landed (commit 42035fc2), with one deliberate narrowing: login() and getUser() are deleted; logout() STAYS.

- login() -> loginRedirect(): bff-demo's sign-in is now a plain document link (href from loginRedirect("/")); the SSR-500 class the imperative helper caused is gone. index.gate.test.tsx no longer needs to mock the SDK at all.
- getUser() -> getCurrentUser()/currentUserQuery for app code; bff-demo inlines the raw /bff/user fetch (it is the raw-wire demo AND needs the body's csrfToken, which the typed path never exposes).
- logout() retained, not migrated to wallow-web as the bead sketched. Two reasons: (a) it is the browser half of the SDK's own /bff/logout handler contract — CSRF-gated, 405-to-GET, redirect:manual + opaqueredirect handling — and every fork needs exactly it; hand-rolling it per app is the snowball this bead is against. (b) auth-logout.contract.test.ts (helper driven against the REAL handler) only works with both halves in one package: porting it to wallow-web fails on vi.mock("openid-client") — pnpm strict isolation means the app cannot resolve openid-client, and adding it as an app devDependency just to mock it is worse than keeping the helper.
- Also updated: index.test.ts export pins (login/getUser -> DELETED_LEGACY_SYMBOLS), sdk CLAUDE.md, docs/integrations/typescript-sdk.md Browser API section (now documents loginRedirect/getCurrentUser, which it previously never mentioned), stale login() prose in route-context.ts and three wallow-web routes.
pnpm check green.

title: flake: packages/ui menubar keyboard-open lands focus on the last row, not the first
description:
packages/ui menubar.test.tsx flakes under concurrent full-workspace test runs.
The helper `openWithKeyboard` (src/components/menubar/menubar.test.tsx:236-239)
focuses a trigger, presses Enter, then polls for focus to land on the menu's
first row:

    part(triggerTestId).focus();
    await userEvent.keyboard("{Enter}");
    await expect.poll(focusedTestId).toBe(firstRowTestId);   // <- line 238

Under load the poll times out ("Matcher did not succeed in time") with focus
still on a stale element. Two distinct received values observed:

  expected 'view-popup' to be 'file-new'     -- the PREVIOUS menu is still open
  expected 'file-recent' to be 'file-new'    -- right menu, wrong row

Keyboard, not pointer -- so this is NOT the pointer-collision family of
Wallow-x5da. It reads as the prior menu not having finished closing (or the new
one not having finished opening) inside `expect.poll`'s default budget.

MEASURED 2026-08-27 on an 8-core box, 21 full-workspace runs across four turbo
concurrencies and three browser maxWorkers settings: menubar.test.tsx was the
most frequent named failure in the sweep, and in one run it took out FOUR tests
at once ("opens the focused menu with Enter and lands on its first row", "opens
the focused menu with ArrowDown as well", "names the open popup by its trigger
and stamps the bar's id on it", "marks the bar while one of its menus is open
and clears it on close") -- all with the identical 'file-recent' vs 'file-new'
mismatch, which suggests one shared precondition rather than four races.

Never seen in an isolated `pnpm --filter @bc-solutions-coder/ui test` run.

Full run-by-run data and logs: see the measurement notes on Wallow-pr34.

Likely fix is in the helper rather than the component: assert the popup has
actually opened (and the previous one closed) before polling for row focus,
instead of inferring both from where focus ended up.
acceptance_criteria: openWithKeyboard no longer polls for row focus as a proxy for 'the menu opened'. menubar.test.tsx survives repeated full-workspace runs under load with zero occurrences of the 'expected <x> to be file-new' mismatch; state the run count and load conditions.
notes:
CORRECTION — "under load" is wrong; it fires serialised too. 2026-08-27, first forced full-workspace run on the SHIPPED Wallow-pr34 configuration (`turbo run test --concurrency=1 --force`, i.e. exactly ONE package's suite running at a time, no cross-package contention at all): menubar.test.tsx failed 10 of its tests at once — 10 failed | 1471 passed across 122 files, and it was the ONLY failing file in the workspace. Every one of the 10 carried the identical 'expected file-recent to be file-new' mismatch. So the title's "under load" premise does not hold and the bead should not be chased as a contention problem.

Two further facts that narrow it:

1. It is NOT a timeout-with-no-menu. The received value is 'file-recent', the LAST row of the File popup (rows in fixture order: file-new, file-open, file-recent — the last being a Menu.SubmenuTrigger). The popup therefore OPENED and focus went to the last item and stayed there for the whole poll budget. "The menu never opened" and "the previous menu is still closing" both predict a null or foreign activeElement, not a correctly-scoped last row. Something is actively moving focus to the end of the list — note that the file's own '{End}' test (line 417) expects exactly 'file-recent'.

2. The all-or-nothing shape is now much stronger evidence than when this bead was filed: 4-at-once became 10-at-once, and 10 is every keyboard test in the file. One shared precondition, established once per file (or leaked in from the first render), not N independent races.

3. `pnpm check` passed green immediately before this run, so the file is not always-red on the current tree.

Helpers involved: part() is `document.body.querySelector` — FIRST match in the document, so a lingering portal or an uncleaned previous tree would silently shadow the current one; focusedTestId() is a bare `document.activeElement` read. Both are worth auditing before the component is.

Logs: scratchpad pr34/final/run-1.log (kept for this session only).
close_reason: Duplicate of Wallow-egxx (same file, same helper family, same 'expected view-popup to be file-new' signature). Filed during the Wallow-pr34 sweep before egxx was found. All of its evidence has been merged onto Wallow-egxx as a note; nothing is lost by closing this.

title: fix(storage): the three StorageSettingKeys are served by the settings API but enforced nowhere
description:
StorageSettingKeys declares storage.max_upload_size_mb (50), storage.allowed_file_types (jpg,png,pdf,doc,docx) and storage.storage_quota_mb (1024). StorageSettingsController reads and writes all three at tenant and user scope, so an operator can set them and see them come back. Nothing in the module ever READS them: grep for the three symbols outside StorageSettingKeys.cs finds no hits in src/.

What actually limits an upload today is unrelated to the settings: [RequestSizeLimit(100MB)] on the controller action, the per-bucket StorageBucket.MaxFileSizeBytes check inside UploadFileHandler, and UploadFileValidator's magic-byte / blocked-signature checks. There is no extension allowlist and no per-tenant quota accounting at all.

Either wire the three keys into UploadFileValidator/UploadFileHandler (and the presigned path, where only size and extension can be checked because the server never sees the bytes), or delete the keys so the settings surface stops advertising limits that do not apply.

Found while writing api/src/Modules/Storage/CLAUDE.md (Wallow-hr0p).
acceptance_criteria: Each of the three storage setting keys is either enforced on both upload paths or removed from StorageSettingKeys.
notes:
Fixed in commit 75104a84. All three StorageSettingKeys are now enforced on BOTH upload paths (multipart UploadFileHandler + presigned GetUploadPresignedUrlHandler), per the approved design: enforce all three, allowed_file_types default changed to '*' (allow all) so out-of-box behavior is unchanged.

Design notes:
- New StorageLimits value object (Application/Settings) parses the three settings: MB->bytes conversion, comma-separated extension allowlist with '*'/blank = allow all, case-insensitive dot-agnostic matching (ToUpperInvariant, CA1308).
- New IStorageLimitsProvider (Application/Interfaces) + StorageLimitsProvider (Infrastructure/Settings) built on the plainly-registered ITenantSettingRepository<StorageDbContext> — deliberately NOT the keyed ISettingsService, which is an opaque-lambda registration Wolverine codegen cannot construct. Registered AddScoped in StorageInfrastructureExtensions; handler chain still reaches only StorageDbContext.
- Reads tenant-scope overrides ONLY — user-scope overrides ignored so a user cannot raise their own limits. Malformed override values fall back to the code default.
- Quota accounting: IStoredFileRepository.GetTotalSizeBytesAsync sums ALL StoredFile rows under the ambient tenant filter — PendingValidation reservations and Rejected rows included (a rejected row holds its bytes until deleted).
- Check order in both handlers, after bucket checks: max upload size -> extension allowlist -> quota.

TDD: RED verified (build failed on exactly the missing symbols), then GREEN. Tests: StorageLimitsTests (6), StorageLimitsProviderTests (4), 3 new handler tests each side asserting no upload/no row on rejection, integration test for the tenant-scoped sum. One test-fault fixed along the way: the integration test originally seeded the other tenant's row through the ambient context and TenantSaveChangesInterceptor re-stamped it (total 1349 not 350); reseeded via CreateDbContextForTenant.

Verification: ./scripts/run-tests.sh all = 5254/5254 PASS (includes Category=Integration and the Wolverine HandlerCodegenTests, which prove the new 5-dep handlers compile under codegen). Docs updated: Storage module CLAUDE.md Things-to-Watch bullet replaced; docs/architecture/file-storage.md Size Limits section now documents the three keys.

title: flake: menubar keyboard specs fail as a block — wrong row or wrong menu focused
description:
`packages/ui/src/components/menubar/menubar.test.tsx > Menubar > opens a submenu with ArrowRight instead of switching menus` fails intermittently.

Observed 1 failure in 4 runs of the ui suite on an unchanged tree:

    AssertionError: expected 'view-popup' to be 'file-new'
    Caused by: Error: Matcher did not succeed in time.   (1266ms)

The assertion reads as: ArrowRight was expected to open the File menu's SUBMENU
(`file-new`) but focus had instead moved along the menubar to the View menu
(`view-popup`) -- i.e. the keypress was handled as menubar navigation rather than
submenu-open, so the spec is racing the submenu mount.

This is NOT the turbo-concurrency contention issue (Wallow-pr34): it failed inside a
run with `TURBO_CONCURRENCY=1`, where every suite had the machine to itself. Isolated
`pnpm --filter @bc-solutions-coder/ui test` runs passed 122/122 three times.

Likely mechanism, per packages/ui/CLAUDE.md: in the browser project the mouse position
persists across specs IN a file and ACROSS files, so a hover-driven component's state
depends on what ran before it. That guide's own prescription is to name the pointer
state at the assertion (`userEvent.unhover`/`hover`) rather than rely on ambient
position, and to open hover-driven components with `element.focus()`.

Also relevant from the same guide: popup unmount is animation-frame-deferred for the
whole Base UI popup family, so closure/open transitions must be asserted with
`await expect.poll(...)`, never a bare synchronous expect.

Repro is timing-dependent; expect to need several runs. Worth checking whether sibling
menu/menubar/context-menu specs share the pattern rather than fixing only this one.
notes:
MERGED IN Wallow-rgu1, which was a duplicate of this bead filed 2026-08-27 during the Wallow-pr34 sweep before this one was found. Its evidence, which broadens this bead beyond the single ArrowRight spec:

1. THE WHOLE KEYBOARD SURFACE OF THE FILE GOES AT ONCE, not one spec. On a forced full-workspace run at turbo --concurrency=1 with nothing else executing, menubar.test.tsx failed 10 of its tests simultaneously — every keyboard test in the file — and was the only failing file in the workspace (10 failed | 1471 passed across 122 files). An earlier run took 4 at once. All 10 carried one identical mismatch. That all-or-nothing shape argues for ONE precondition established per file (or leaked in from the first render), not N independent races, and it means a fix scoped to 'opens a submenu with ArrowRight instead of switching menus' will not be enough.

2. A SECOND RECEIVED VALUE, and it is more diagnostic than the first. Alongside this bead's 'expected view-popup to be file-new', the sweep saw 'expected file-recent to be file-new'. file-recent is the LAST row of the File popup (fixture order: file-new, file-open, file-recent, the last being a Menu.SubmenuTrigger). So in that variant the correct popup OPENED and focus went to the END of the list and stayed there for the whole poll budget. 'The menu never opened' and 'the previous menu is still closing' both predict a null or foreign activeElement, not a correctly-scoped last row — something is actively moving focus to the end. The file's own '{End}' test (line 417) expects exactly file-recent.

3. HELPERS WORTH AUDITING BEFORE THE COMPONENT. part() is document.body.querySelector — the FIRST match in the document, so a lingering portal or an uncleaned previous tree silently shadows the current one. focusedTestId() is a bare document.activeElement read. openWithKeyboard (lines 236-239) polls for row focus as a PROXY for 'the menu opened', so it cannot distinguish 'did not open' from 'opened, wrong row'. Asserting the popup is open (and the previous one closed) before polling for row focus would at minimum split the two failure modes apart.

4. CORROBORATION of this bead's concurrency-independence finding: the 10-test failure above was on --concurrency=1, as was this bead's original observation. Wallow-pr34's cap is now shipped and does not touch this.

pnpm check passed green immediately before that run, so the file is not always-red on the current tree.
ROOT CAUSE (proven by deterministic repro): in vitest browser mode the Playwright pointer position persists across specs AND across spec files, and Chromium re-dispatches hover events when new content mounts under a stationary cursor. A keyboard-opened Base UI menu popup that mounts under a parked pointer fails one of two ways: (1) deterministic — the row under the pointer gets hover-highlighted, stealing focus from the first row ('expected file-recent to be file-new'); (2) racy — in the frame before the modal pointer-blocker mounts, a synthesized mousemove hits a neighbouring menubar trigger and hover-switches to that menu pointer-style ('expected view-popup to be file-new', File popup closes). Both observed failure values from this bead were reproduced on demand from parked-pointer preconditions via a scratch repro file (since deleted).

WHY 10 SPECS AS A BLOCK: the ten failing specs are exactly the ten that keyboard-open a menu (9 openWithKeyboard callers + the ArrowDown spec). The two closed-bar roving-focus specs never mount a popup, so they never failed. Concurrency-independence follows: the leak is cross-file pointer state, not resource starvation.

FIX (83a5e060): the repo's sanctioned idiom — name the pointer state at the interaction. menubar.test.tsx: openWithKeyboard and the ArrowDown spec now start with 'await userEvent.unhover(part("bar"))' (moves pointer to <body>, off the bar and off every popup footprint); header comment documents the mechanism. menu.test.tsx: same line in the one exposed spec (arrow-key open from trigger); its shared openMenu() helper is safe because it uses a real click that names the pointer itself.

SIBLING AUDIT: context-menu.test.tsx not exposed (only open path is an explicit right-click). select.test.tsx, navigation-menu.test.tsx, combobox.test.tsx share the keyboard-open shape with no observed failures — filed as Wallow-82kx (P3) with the fix recipe rather than changed here.

VERIFICATION: parked-pointer repro red in both modes before the fix, 5/5 forced runs green after; menubar+menu files 3/3 green (52 specs); full ui suite 3/3 consecutive green (122 files, 1481 tests); oxfmt + pnpm lint:tests clean.

title: docs: purge the 'Wolverine scans Wallow.* assemblies by name prefix' claim from messaging/AsyncAPI/operations docs
description:

the deleted per-module registration walkthrough (Initialize{Module}ModuleAsync / manual IsEnabledAsync
blocks in WallowModules.cs). This bead is a DIFFERENT, still-live claim in a disjoint set of files: several
architecture/operations/integrations docs describe Wolverine (and the AsyncAPI catalog generator that reuses
its assembly list) as discovering handlers by scanning every loaded assembly whose name starts with
"Wallow." via an AppDomain.CurrentDomain.GetAssemblies() scan. That mechanism is gone (27c684d8, discovery
now comes from api/src/Shared/Wallow.Shared.Infrastructure/Modules/IWallowModule.cs's HandlerAssemblies,
populated per module and read via api/src/Wallow.Modules.Registry/WallowModuleRegistry.cs). Verified on disk
2026-08-05: api/src/Wallow.Api/Program.cs builds Wolverine's discovery list from
`enabledModules.SelectMany(module => module.HandlerAssemblies)` (no AppDomain scan remains there), and
api/src/Wallow.Api/Extensions/AsyncApiEndpointExtensions.cs's own XML doc says it explicitly replaced its
own former AppDomain.CurrentDomain.GetAssemblies() scan because that scan and Wolverine's saw different
assemblies depending on load order at the time each ran.

Sites (grep the heading text, not the line number -- it drifts):

1. docs/architecture/messaging.md, section "## Handlers": "Wolverine discovers them by scanning every
   loaded assembly whose name starts with `Wallow.` (`api/src/Wallow.Api/Program.cs`), so there is no
   registration step." Replace with: discovery comes from each module's IWallowModule.HandlerAssemblies,
   collected by WallowModuleRegistry.All and filtered to enabledModules in WallowModules.AddWallowModules;
   a disabled module's handlers are excluded (a real behavior change from the old scan-everything
   mechanism, not just a wording refresh -- worth a sentence).
2. docs/architecture/messaging.md, section "## Event Catalog": "`EventFlowDiscovery.cs` reflects over the
   loaded `Wallow.*` assemblies at startup" -- same staleness. It is fed an explicit assembly list built in
   AsyncApiEndpointExtensions.MapAsyncApiEndpoints from the same HandlerAssemblies (plus
   Wallow.Shared.Contracts appended, since that assembly hosts the event types themselves but no handlers).
3. docs/integrations/asyncapi.md, section "## How It Works": "The catalog is generated at startup by
   scanning all `Wallow.*` assemblies" -- same staleness as #2.
4. docs/integrations/asyncapi.md, section "## Troubleshooting": "Verify the handler is in a `Wallow.*`
   assembly (included in assembly scanning)" -- should read "verify the handler's assembly is declared in
   its module's IWallowModule.HandlerAssemblies".
5. docs/operations/troubleshooting.md, section "### Messages Not Being Delivered" -> "**Handler not
   discovered:**": "Wolverine discovers handlers in `Wallow.*` assemblies. Ensure: ... 3. Handler is in a
   `Wallow.*` assembly" -- same staleness as #1.
6. docs/operations/troubleshooting.md, section "### Handler Not Being Discovered" -> "**Assembly not
   included in discovery:**": the whole AppDomain.CurrentDomain.GetAssemblies().Where(name.StartsWith
   ("Wallow.")) code sample plus "If your handler is in a different namespace/assembly, add it explicitly."
   The fix today is adding the assembly to the owning module's IWallowModule.HandlerAssemblies in that
   module's XModule.cs, not touching Program.cs at all -- this section needs a different worked example,
   not a word swap.
7. docs/operations/audit-events.md, section "## Extending Audit Coverage", step "1. Add a Wolverine handler
   in your module's Infrastructure project": "Wolverine scans all `Wallow.*` assemblies, so there is no
   registration call to write" -- lower severity than the others: the MECHANISM claim is stale, but the
   PRACTICAL conclusion ("no registration call to write") still holds for a handler added to an EXISTING
   module, because every IWallowModule implementation already lists both its .Application and
   .Infrastructure assembly in HandlerAssemblies unconditionally (see that interface member's own XML doc).
   A light correction (swap the "Wolverine scans" clause for "the module's HandlerAssemblies already covers
   its own Infrastructure project") is enough here, not a rewrite.

No file in this list is touched by Wallow-3mbx.8's inventory, so no dependency edge against it is required
-- the two beads can be worked in parallel.

IMPORTANT: IFeatureManager is unrelated to this bead's scope -- do not conflate with Wallow-3mbx.8's
IFeatureManager corrections. This bead is entirely about the Wolverine/AsyncAPI HANDLER-DISCOVERY mechanism
(HandlerAssemblies vs AppDomain scan-by-name-prefix), not module enable/disable gating.

The five numbered generator steps below it were checked and are still accurate — left alone.

Now a 4-item list: public static class, Handle/HandleAsync, assembly listed in the module's HandlerAssemblies (with the note that both .Application and .Infrastructure are always declared), and module must be ENABLED.

6. troubleshooting.md '### Handler Not Being Discovered' -> 'Assembly not included in discovery:' — the AppDomain.CurrentDomain.GetAssemblies().Where(StartsWith("Wallow.")) code sample is GONE. As the bead required, this got a different worked example rather than a word swap: it now shows the real handlerAssemblies array from Program.cs to make the point that Program.cs does not scan, then shows the fix in the OWNING module's {Module}Module.cs HandlerAssemblies property, and notes a brand-new module also needs its WallowModuleRegistry.All entry.

Both re-resolve IFeatureManager from the built container and re-derive the flag key as a string
literal, when enabledModules is in scope at both points.

## Failure mode

The literals and the registry can disagree. IsCore is the concrete case: a module the registry
forces on regardless of its flag (Identity today) reads as DISABLED at these call sites, because
IsEnabledAsync only sees the config value. If ApiKeys or Notifications ever became core, its
middleware and its Hangfire job would silently stop registering while the module itself ran.
Wallow-scul already documents that Modules.Identity has no reader and setting it false does
nothing -- these two sites are where that class of lie would come back.

Secondary: the flag string "Modules.{Name}" is a convention IWallowModule.Name owns
(IWallowModule.cs:22-25). Hand-writing it defeats the rename safety the registry bought.

## Fix

Replace both with a check against the list Program.cs already holds, e.g.

  bool IsEnabled(string name) => enabledModules.Any(m => m.Name == name);

or an extension on IReadOnlyList<IWallowModule>. Nothing else in Program.cs should call
IsEnabledAsync("Modules.*") afterwards.

## Acceptance

- No "Modules." string literal remains in Program.cs; grep -n '"Modules\.' api/src/Wallow.Api/Program.cs
  returns nothing.
- With Modules.ApiKeys=false the middleware is still not registered, and with it true it is
  (behaviour unchanged).
- A module marked IsCore has its middleware/job registered even with its flag false -- add or
  extend a test in Wallow.Architecture.Tests/Modules/ModuleToggleTests.cs if it can be reached there.
- ./scripts/run-tests.sh api green.

title: each module declares its Postgres schema three times and the two hosts read different copies
description:
IWallowModule.SchemaName was added so the migration host could stop hand-maintaining schema strings.
It did not replace the two places the same string was already written, so each module now declares
its schema THREE times, and the two hosts read DIFFERENT copies.

## Verified state — per module, three declarations

1. IWallowModule.SchemaName (api/src/Shared/Wallow.Shared.Infrastructure/Modules/IWallowModule.cs:66)
   Read by the MIGRATION host only: ModuleMigrations.AddSchemaScopedDbContext passes it to
   MigrationsHistoryTable("__EFMigrationsHistory", schemaName)
   (api/src/Wallow.MigrationService/ModuleMigrations.cs:117-126).
2. MigrationsHistoryTable(...) inside the module's own AddDbContext, read by the API host. E.g.
   api/src/Modules/ApiKeys/Wallow.ApiKeys.Infrastructure/Extensions/ApiKeysInfrastructureExtensions.cs:46
   npgsql.MigrationsHistoryTable("__EFMigrationsHistory", "apikeys");
   Same pattern in all seven (Announcements:40, Branding:45, Notifications:61, Identity:240,
   Inquiries via InquiriesDbContextFactory:15, Storage).
3. modelBuilder.HasDefaultSchema("...") in the DbContext itself, e.g.
   api/src/Modules/ApiKeys/Wallow.ApiKeys.Infrastructure/Persistence/ApiKeysDbContext.cs:19 --
   this one is baked into the migration snapshots too.

Nothing pins them equal. Grepping api/tests for SchemaName returns ZERO hits; the architecture
tests assert each module owns a separate schema but never compare the registry's string to the
DbContext's.

## Failure mode

Change a module's schema in one of the three and the two hosts disagree about where
__EFMigrationsHistory lives. MigrationService writes its history rows to schema A while the API
looks for them in schema B, so the API's own inline path (Testing) or any future EnsureCreated-style
check sees an unmigrated database and re-applies migrations that have already run. It fails at
runtime against a real database, not at build, and only for the module that drifted.

The exposure is new: before the registry there was one wrong-but-consistent copy per host; now
there is a copy that only one host reads.

## Options

A. Guard test (cheap): a behavioural test that, for every IWallowModule, resolves the module's
   DbContext types and asserts model.GetDefaultSchema() == module.SchemaName, and that the API
   host's registered MigrationsHistoryTable schema matches. Closes the drift risk today.
B. Single source (better): have the module's own AddDbContext take its schema from SchemaName
   rather than a literal, so declarations 1 and 2 collapse. Declaration 3 (HasDefaultSchema) has to
   stay a literal because EF's migration snapshots are generated against it -- but a test can pin
   it to SchemaName.

Recommendation: A now, B when the module-registration path is next touched (it pairs naturally
with Wallow-k2zp's option A, since a shared registry project would give AddDbContext somewhere to
read SchemaName from).

## Acceptance

- Changing one of the three declarations for any module without changing the others fails a test.
- The test is behavioural -- it reads EF model metadata and DI registrations, never source text
  (.claude/rules/TESTING.md bans source tests).
- ./scripts/run-tests.sh arch and ./scripts/run-tests.sh migrations green.

Grepped api/tests for SchemaName: zero hits confirmed. DESIGN: premise verified on disk, no citation drift found.

=== 1. PREMISE: three declarations, confirmed, plus a real (not merely latent) disagreement scenario ===

Per module (ApiKeys as exemplar, same shape all 7):
1. IWallowModule.SchemaName (api/src/Shared/Wallow.Shared.Infrastructure/Modules/IWallowModule.cs:66,
   interface decl) — impl ApiKeysModule.cs:32 `public string SchemaName => "apikeys";`. Read ONLY by
   Wallow.MigrationService/ModuleMigrations.cs:52 (`module.SchemaName` passed into
   AddSchemaScopedDbContext → `npgsql.MigrationsHistoryTable("__EFMigrationsHistory", schemaName)`).
   Since Wallow-k2zp landed, this reads WallowModuleRegistry.All — same instances the API host enables.
2. Literal inside the module's OWN write-DbContext registration, read ONLY by the API host:
   ApiKeysInfrastructureExtensions.cs:46 `npgsql.MigrationsHistoryTable("__EFMigrationsHistory", "apikeys")`
   inside AddApiKeysPersistence → AddApiKeysInfrastructure → AddApiKeysModule → ApiKeysModule.AddServices.
   Same pattern, all 7: AnnouncementsModuleExtensions.cs:40, BrandingInfrastructureExtensions.cs:45,
   NotificationsModuleExtensions.cs:61, StorageInfrastructureExtensions.cs:61,
   IdentityInfrastructureExtensions.cs:240, InquiriesInfrastructureExtensions.cs:34.
3. modelBuilder.HasDefaultSchema("apikeys") in ApiKeysDbContext.cs:19 OnModelCreating — same code object
   for both hosts (one compiled DbContext type), baked into the EF migration snapshot too. Same pattern:
   AnnouncementsDbContext.cs:23, BrandingDbContext.cs:19, NotificationsDbContext.cs:41,
   StorageDbContext.cs:23, IdentityDbContext.cs:62, InquiriesDbContext.cs:20.

WHY THREE STILL EXIST DESPITE SchemaName EXISTING: SchemaName (added by the af3h registry work) was
wired into ONLY the migration host's dynamic reflection path (ModuleMigrations.AddSchemaScopedDbContext).
Nobody went back and pointed declarations 2/3 at it — they still carry independent literals typed by
hand when each module was first built, before SchemaName existed.

CAN THE HOSTS ACTUALLY DISAGREE TODAY — yes, concretely, verified by tracing both call graphs (not
asserted): api/src/Wallow.Api/WallowModules.cs:398 `MigrateContextAsync` — the ONLY place the API host
itself calls `Database.MigrateAsync()` — runs exclusively when `app.Environment.IsEnvironment("Testing")`
(WallowModules.cs:106-108) and resolves the context via `sp.GetRequiredService(contextType)`, i.e. the
SAME DI-registered write context declaration 2 built (AddApiKeysPersistence's AddPooledDbContextFactory).
Outside Testing (Development and Production, per CLAUDE.md/api/CLAUDE.md — "Modules are migrated inline
only in the Testing environment; everywhere else ... Wallow.MigrationService applies them"), only
Wallow.MigrationService ever calls Migrate(), via ModuleMigrations' declaration-1-driven registration —
a SEPARATE DbContextOptions instance from declaration 2's, never unified except by value-equality of two
independently hand-typed strings.
CONCRETE FAILURE: rename a module's schema by editing ONLY IWallowModule.SchemaName (declaration 1) —
e.g. ApiKeysModule.cs:32 "apikeys" → "api_keys" — and touch nothing else. MigrationService now creates/
checks __EFMigrationsHistory in "api_keys" while the migration operations it runs still create the actual
entity tables in "apikeys" (declaration 3, untouched, baked into the migration). First MigrationService
run: succeeds, but leaves an orphaned "api_keys" schema holding only history rows, disconnected from
where the real tables live. Any subsequent Testing-environment run against that SAME physical database
(a locally shared dev Postgres previously migrated via `pnpm backend`, then re-run with
ASPNETCORE_ENVIRONMENT=Testing — a realistic local workflow) resolves declaration 2's context (still
literal "apikeys", unchanged) → `Database.MigrateAsync()` looks for __EFMigrationsHistory in "apikeys" →
finds none (MigrationService wrote it to "api_keys") → treats every migration as pending → issues
CREATE TABLE for tables that already exist in "apikeys" → Npgsql throws "relation already exists" →
RunTestMigrationsAsync throws → host startup fails. This is a real, reachable divergence path, not a
hypothetical; it requires only editing declaration 1 without the other two, which nothing today prevents
or even warns about (api/tests grep for SchemaName: zero hits, confirmed).
No citation drift found versus the bead's own text; all line numbers re-verified fresh this pass.

=== 2. CHOSEN DESIGN: one const per module, not a threaded parameter ===

Rejected: threading SchemaName as a new parameter through each module's AddServices → AddXModule →
AddXInfrastructure → AddXPersistence chain (2-4 layers deep, differs in shape per module — Identity's is
AddIdentityModule(configuration, environment), ApiKeys' is AddApiKeysModule(configuration)). That would
touch every method signature in the chain for 7 modules and still leaves declaration 3 (HasDefaultSchema)
an independent literal, since DbContext.OnModelCreating has no access to a runtime-injected value (EF
constructs the model once, statically, not per-request).

CHOSEN: collapse all three call sites for a module onto ONE C# compile-time constant declared next to
SchemaName, so the compiler — not a convention — makes a second literal impossible to introduce silently.
Per module, in the existing `public sealed class XModule : IWallowModule` file:

    internal const string Schema = "apikeys";

    public string SchemaName => Schema;

Then, same assembly, no new ProjectReference needed anywhere (Module class, DbContext, and the
Infrastructure extension class are ALWAYS in the same `Wallow.{Module}.Infrastructure` project — verified
for all 7):
  - ApiKeysDbContext.cs:19 → `modelBuilder.HasDefaultSchema(ApiKeysModule.Schema);` (add
    `using Wallow.ApiKeys.Infrastructure.Modules;`)
  - ApiKeysInfrastructureExtensions.cs:46 → `npgsql.MigrationsHistoryTable("__EFMigrationsHistory",
    ApiKeysModule.Schema);` (add `using Wallow.ApiKeys.Infrastructure.Modules;`)
Same edit, same 3 files per module, for all 7:
  - Announcements: AnnouncementsModule.cs (new const), AnnouncementsDbContext.cs:23,
    AnnouncementsModuleExtensions.cs:40
  - Branding: BrandingModule.cs, BrandingDbContext.cs:19, BrandingInfrastructureExtensions.cs:45
  - Notifications: NotificationsModule.cs, NotificationsDbContext.cs:41, NotificationsModuleExtensions.cs:61
  - Storage: StorageModule.cs, StorageDbContext.cs:23, StorageInfrastructureExtensions.cs:61
  - Identity: IdentityModule.cs, IdentityDbContext.cs:62, IdentityInfrastructureExtensions.cs:240
  - Inquiries: InquiriesModule.cs, InquiriesDbContext.cs:20, InquiriesInfrastructureExtensions.cs:34
`internal` is sufficient (DbContext + extensions are always same-assembly as XModule); no public-surface
growth, no IWallowModule interface change.

TOUCHES IWallowModule.cs: NO. SchemaName's interface signature (`string SchemaName { get; }`,
IWallowModule.cs:66) is unchanged; only the 7 implementations' property BODY changes from a literal to
`=> Schema`. Flagging per instructions anyway because Wallow-3mbx.5 (in design, "DESIGN: PARTIAL — do
concern #1, collection-type unification") ALSO edits all 7 X Module.cs files (HandlerAssemblies/
DbContextTypes property→field conversion), same files, different properties within each. Real merge
friction if run in parallel; recommend sequencing (either order is fine — the property being touched
doesn't overlap — but the coordinator should not schedule both against the same 7 files concurrently).

RELATED, OUT OF SCOPE — NOT part of this bead's fix, noted for the record: Identity's and Inquiries'
IDesignTimeDbContextFactory (IdentityDbContextFactory.cs:20, InquiriesDbContextFactory.cs:15) ALSO carry
"identity"/"inquiries" MigrationsHistoryTable literals — a 4th declaration site for those two modules
only. Neither host ever constructs these factories (they exist solely for the offline `dotnet ef
migrations add` CLI, verified: MigrationsHistoryTable set there has zero effect on generated migration
files, which only encode HasDefaultSchema). Not part of "the two hosts read different copies." Could
optionally be pointed at the same `XModule.Schema` const for full consistency, but doing so pulls a
Persistence-project reference to the Modules-namespace type into 5 factories that don't have it today —
skip; genuinely lower value than the acceptance criteria asks for.

=== 3. MIGRATION REGEN: NOT NEEDED ===
`modelBuilder.HasDefaultSchema(ApiKeysModule.Schema)` resolves to the exact same string value
`"apikeys"` at compile time as the literal it replaces — `Schema` is a `const`, so this is not even a
runtime indirection, the emitted IL is identical. EF's migration-snapshot diffing compares the STRING
VALUE the model reports, not the C# expression that produced it, so `dotnet ef migrations add` sees zero
model delta. No new migration, no `*ModelSnapshot.cs`/`*.Designer.cs` edits required. This is the "no
migration required" case CLAUDE.md prefers.

=== 4. WHAT ENFORCES THE SINGLE DECLARATION GOING FORWARD ===
Two layers, one structural and one behavioral:
- STRUCTURAL (primary): after this change there is exactly ONE literal per module — `XModule.Schema` —
  and every other site is a compiler-checked reference to that same symbol. You cannot "drift" declaration
  2 or 3 without either (a) editing the shared const (which changes all three at once) or (b) hand-typing
  a brand-new literal back in, which is a code-review-visible regression, not a silent one — and the guard
  test below turns it into a CI-visible one too.
- BEHAVIORAL (guard, catches (b)): a new runtime test asserting the schema each host's ACTUAL constructed
  DbContext reports matches `module.SchemaName`, for both hosts, for all 7 modules. See below.

=== 5. TEST PLAN ===
New file: api/tests/Wallow.Architecture.Tests/Modules/ModuleSchemaTests.cs (same directory as k2zp's
ModuleRegistryTests.cs — mirror its reflection pattern for the MigrationService leg).

Wallow.Architecture.Tests already ProjectReferences Wallow.Modules.Registry directly (added by k2zp,
Wallow.Architecture.Tests.csproj:59) — use `WallowModuleRegistry.All` (typed, no reflection needed) to
get the 7 real IWallowModule instances including ApiKeys/Inquiries (whose Persistence namespaces are NOT
directly referenced by this test project — confirmed by grep of the csproj, only
Identity/Notifications/Announcements/Storage/Branding are). Resolve their DbContext TYPES via
`module.DbContextTypes` (returns `Type`, no direct reference needed) and build/resolve everything through
each host's own real registration code, not hand-rolled DbContextOptions:

  API HOST LEG: mirror ModuleToggleTests.InvokeAddWallowModules (Wallow.Architecture.Tests/Modules/
  ModuleToggleTests.cs:95-107) — Assembly.Load("Wallow.Api") + GetType("Wallow.Api.WallowModules") +
  GetMethod("AddWallowModules", Public|Static), with all 7 FeatureManagement:Modules.<Name> flags "true"
  plus ConnectionStrings:DefaultConnection = a syntactically-valid but unreachable string
  ("Host=localhost;Database=test" — already used by ModuleToggleTests, confirmed no real connection is
  opened by anything below). Build `services.BuildServiceProvider()`. For each module's DbContextTypes
  entry, reflectively resolve `IDbContextFactory<TContext>` (`typeof(IDbContextFactory<>).MakeGenericType
  (contextType)`, GetRequiredService, invoke `CreateDbContext()` via reflection) — this exercises the REAL
  AddPooledDbContextFactory registration (declaration 2 + 3), not a reimplementation of it.

  MIGRATION-SERVICE HOST LEG: mirror k2zp's ReadModuleMigrationsAll-style reflection — but instead of
  reading `.All`, reflectively invoke `Wallow.MigrationService.ModuleMigrations.AddModuleDbContexts`
  (public static, internal class — same public-member-on-internal-class shape k2zp already proved
  reflection reaches, no InternalsVisibleTo needed) against a fresh ServiceCollection + the same dummy
  connection string. Build the provider, `CreateScope()`, and `scope.ServiceProvider.GetRequiredService
  (contextType)` (non-generic overload — AddModuleDbContexts registers via `services.AddDbContext<T>`,
  scoped) to get the real declaration-1-driven context (verified this call chain hits
  ModuleMigrations.cs:52's `module.SchemaName` → AddSchemaScopedDbContext → MigrationsHistoryTable).

  ASSERTIONS, per module, both hosts' constructed `DbContext` instance (cast from the reflected object;
  Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore is already a transitive reference so `DbContext`/`Model`/
  `GetDefaultSchema()` compile directly, no reflection needed past construction):
    1. `context.Model.GetDefaultSchema().Should().Be(module.SchemaName)` — proves declaration 3 (data
       location) tracks declaration 1, for both hosts' context instances.
    2. Migrations-history schema: `using Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore.Infrastructure;
       context.GetService<IHistoryRepository>().GetCreateScript()` — VERIFIED THIS WORKS WITHOUT A LIVE DB
       CONNECTION (ran a throwaway net10.0 console app against the same Npgsql.EntityFrameworkCore.
       PostgreSQL 10.0.3 package this repo pins; `GetCreateScript()` returns pure SQL text, e.g.

    3. Cross-host equality, not just each-vs-module.SchemaName: assert the API host's script/default-schema
       equals the MigrationService host's, for the same module — catches the case where BOTH hosts

  NO SOURCE READING: everything above is reflection over live assemblies, DI resolution, and EF's own
  model/script-generation services — no `File.ReadAllText`, no parsing a `.cs` file, matches
  .claude/rules/TESTING.md.

RUN: `./scripts/run-tests.sh arch` (fast, no Docker — this test opens no DB connection, confirmed). Also
confirm `./scripts/run-tests.sh migrations` and the bare + `integration` runs stay green as a REGRESSION
check (ModuleMigrations.cs and all 7 modules' Infrastructure projects change) — no new test is added to
Wallow.MigrationService.Tests; existing ones must not regress.

=== 6. RISKS / WHAT WOULD FALSIFY THIS ===
- Risk: `context.GetService<IHistoryRepository>()` is resolving a service EF documents as being for
  tooling/advanced scenarios, not typical application code (lives behind `Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore.
  Infrastructure`, one of EF's semi-public "reach into internals" extension points). Verified empirically
  against the exact pinned Npgsql.EntityFrameworkCore.PostgreSQL version (10.0.3) that it compiles and
  runs connection-free — but the implementer should re-verify against whatever this project's actual EF/
  Npgsql package versions are at implementation time (check api/Directory.Packages.props) rather than
  trust this scout's throwaway repro blindly, and use ref.tools if the API shape differs.
- Risk: if a future module's write-DbContext registration stops using `AddPooledDbContextFactory` (e.g.
  switches to plain `AddDbContext`), the reflection in the API-host leg (`IDbContextFactory<T>` lookup)
  breaks. Low risk — all 7 modules use the pooled-factory shape today, verified by reading all 7
  Add*Persistence methods.
- What would falsify "single const, not a threaded parameter": if a future need arises for the schema to
  vary PER DEPLOYMENT (not per module) — e.g. multi-schema-per-tenant — a compile-time const stops being
  enough and the parameter-threading design (rejected above) becomes necessary. Nothing in the current
  codebase or CLAUDE.md's multi-tenancy model (Organization-as-tenant, shared schema, row-level
  filtering — Wallow-tenant-model memory) suggests that is planned; flag to the epic if it ever is.
- What would falsify "no migration regen needed": if `HasDefaultSchema` ever received something other
  than a plain string literal today (e.g. computed at runtime) — verified false for all 7, all are bare
  string literals, confirmed by grep.

title: the seven-module list now exists twice, in WallowModules and ModuleMigrations
description:
Introduced by Wallow-af3h.7 and flagged by its implementer rather than hidden. Wallow-af3h set out
to delete hand-maintained module lists; this one is a new instance of the very defect class, so it
should not sit open indefinitely.

Two identical seven-element 'new XModule()' arrays now exist:
  • api/src/Wallow.Api/WallowModules.cs — _allModules (filtered by IFeatureManager)
  • api/src/Wallow.MigrationService/ModuleMigrations.cs — All (deliberately UNFILTERED; the migration
    host migrates every module's schema regardless of flags, so a disabled module can be switched
    back on without a migration step. The filtering difference is correct and must survive any fix.)

WHY IT COULD NOT BE FIXED IN af3h.7 — verified, do not re-litigate: the list must live somewhere
that references all seven module .Infrastructure assemblies. The only project both hosts share is
Wallow.Shared.Infrastructure, which the modules reference, so it cannot reference them back without a
cycle. There is no existing home for it.

Failure mode if left: adding a module and updating only one list. Miss WallowModules and the module
is never registered in the API; miss ModuleMigrations and its schema is never migrated. Neither
fails loudly.

TWO OPTIONS, pick during the bead:

A. New project (the implementer's suggestion) — e.g. Wallow.Modules.Registry, referencing all seven
   module .Infrastructure projects, referenced by both hosts. Clean, and the list exists once.
   Costs a .slnx entry and a project; note that af3h.6 deliberately kept .slnx edits manual and out
   of scope, so this is the first bead allowed to touch it.

B. A guard test instead, much cheaper. VERIFIED AVAILABLE: Wallow.Architecture.Tests already
   ProjectReferences BOTH Wallow.Api and Wallow.MigrationService, so one test can see both lists and
   assert they contain the same module types. Needs InternalsVisibleTo (or making the two members
   internal-visible) since _allModules is private and ModuleMigrations is internal. This is a
   BEHAVIOURAL test comparing two runtime collections, not a source-text test, so it is fine under
   .claude/rules/TESTING.md — do NOT implement it by reading either file off disk.

Recommendation: B first because it closes the risk in one test today, then A if the duplication
grows past two sites. Do not do A merely for tidiness.

Acceptance: adding an eighth module to only one of the two lists fails a test (B) or is impossible
(A); ./scripts/run-tests.sh and ./scripts/run-tests.sh integration green.

Wallow.Architecture.Tests.csproj already ProjectReferences both Wallow.Api (line 24) and Wallow.MigrationService (line 58) — confirmed, option B's guard test is viable today. BLOCKS Wallow-3mbx.2 (bd dep add Wallow-3mbx.2 Wallow-k2zp already wired) — land this first; its own bead text ties its option A (new registry project) to unlocking 3mbx.2's option B (single-source schema). DESIGN (premise verified, citations exact, no drift):
WallowModules.cs:34-43 _allModules (private static readonly IWallowModule[]) and
ModuleMigrations.cs:49-58 All (public static IReadOnlyList<IWallowModule>) are still two
byte-for-byte-identical 7-element `new XModule()` arrays. Grepped the whole api/ tree for all
seven `new XModule()` constructor calls: exactly these two sites, nothing else (tests included).
Not reconciled since the bead was filed.

CHOSEN: Option A (new project), not the guard test. Reasoning: a guard test proves the two arrays
agree, it does not remove the second array, so "adding an eighth module means editing one list"
(the epic's own done-condition) stays false under B. A now costs one small non-executable class
library plus a one-time .slnx edit (explicitly unblocked by this bead per its own description) —
cheap enough that "recommendation: B first, A only if duplication grows past two sites" undersells
it; we are already at two sites with a real Program.cs/MigrationService.Program.cs runtime failure
mode, and the physical fix removes the failure mode instead of just detecting it. lw4a is
unaffected either way (see below), so B's stated rationale for avoiding A (protecting lw4a from
file churn) does not actually apply.

TESTS (api/tests/Wallow.Architecture.Tests/, new file Modules/ModuleRegistryTests.cs; project

1. Registry_ShouldContain_ExactlySevenModules_OnePerModuleType — direct call,
   `WallowModuleRegistry.All.Select(m => m.GetType().Name).Should().BeEquivalentTo(["IdentityModule",

   "InquiriesModule"])`. Runtime/reflection over the live collection, not source text.

2. ApiHost_EnabledModules_ShouldMatch_MigrationServiceHost_AllModules_WhenEveryFlagEnabled — THE
   regression guard ("would fail if the list were duplicated again"): builds a ServiceCollection +
   IConfiguration with every `FeatureManagement:Modules.<Name>` flag = "true" (mirror

   Modules/ModuleToggleTests.cs), invokes `Wallow.Api.WallowModules.AddWallowModules` via

   BindingFlags.Static) — EXACT pattern already in ModuleToggleTests.InvokeAddWallowModules, no
   InternalsVisibleTo needed because the method is public even though the class is internal — and
   captures its IReadOnlyList<IWallowModule> return value (ModuleToggleTests today discards it;
   this test keeps it). Separately reads `Wallow.MigrationService.ModuleMigrations.All` the same
   reflective way (Assembly.Load("Wallow.MigrationService") + GetType + GetProperty("All",
   BindingFlags.Public | BindingFlags.Static) — ModuleMigrations is `internal static class` but All

   catches a FUTURE regression where somebody hand-rolls a third local array in either host again.
   CORRECTION to this bead's own body: no InternalsVisibleTo/internal-visibility plumbing is

RISKS / WHAT WOULD FALSIFY THIS:
- Risk: a new project referencing all seven module Infrastructure assemblies could look like it
  breaks module isolation. Checked ModuleIsolationTests.cs (NetArchTest) — it only walks each
  module's OWN four layer-assemblies looking for cross-module references; it never scans
  Wallow.Modules.Registry or Wallow.Api (which already references all seven the same way), so this
  is not a new violation class. If a future architecture test is added that forbids ANY project
  outside a module from referencing more than one module's Infrastructure assembly, that would
  falsify this design's project-boundary assumption — none exists today (checked all 8 files in
  Wallow.Architecture.Tests using NetArchTest).
- Risk: dropping Wallow.MigrationService.csproj's seven direct module-Infrastructure
  ProjectReferences could break something else in that project that currently relies on the
  transitive reference silently (e.g. a DbContext type used somewhere outside ModuleMigrations.cs).
  Checked Wallow.MigrationService/Program.cs — only references ModuleMigrations, AuditDbContext,
  AuthAuditDbContext (Shared.Infrastructure.Core.Auditing), no module types. If a future file in
  that project starts referencing a module type directly, it would need its own ProjectReference
  back — that is expected, not a design flaw.
- Risk: EnsureDbContextType / reflection-based AddSchemaScopedDbContext in ModuleMigrations.cs is
  untouched by this design (still reflects into its own private generic method) — this bead does
  not touch that mechanism, only where `All` sources its data from, so that risk surface is
  unchanged.
- What would falsify "Option A over B": if a maintainer decides project-count/slnx-surface-area
  cost outweighs closing the failure mode outright — that is a judgment call already made above
  and by the acceptance criteria (which explicitly accepts either A "impossible" or B "fails a
  test"); implementer should raise it back to the epic if they disagree rather than silently
  reverting to B.
DESIGN REVIEW: APPROVE — adversarial pass verified every claim against the actual csproj/source graph, not just the design's prose.

(1) NEW PROJECT WARRANTED — verified on disk. src/Modules/ApiKeys/Wallow.ApiKeys.Infrastructure.csproj (and every other module Infrastructure csproj) references ..\..\..\Shared\Wallow.Shared.Infrastructure\Wallow.Shared.Infrastructure.csproj, never the reverse — confirmed Wallow.Shared.Infrastructure.csproj's own ProjectReferences (Kernel/Contracts/Core/BackgroundJobs/Plugins only, zero module refs). So a registry living under Shared/ genuinely cycles; the claim is not asserted, it is true. No existing project already sits at 'references all 7 module Infrastructure assemblies AND is referenced by both hosts' — Wallow.Api and Wallow.MigrationService each hold their own full 7-reference set today, independently (grepped both csproj files). Wallow.ServiceDefaults was the other candidate; it is IsAspireSharedProject=true with ZERO ProjectReferences today (by design, confirmed via csproj) and is shared with non-API hosts too — repurposing it to know about all 7 modules would be a worse layering violation than a new project. Host-tier placement (sibling to Api/MigrationService under src/, not under Shared/) is correctly reasoned, and the api/Wallow.slnx <Folder Name="/src/"> block the design edits (lines 7-13) matches exactly what it claims.

(2) DEPENDENCY DIRECTION — no new exposure. The registry must reference all 7 module Infrastructure assemblies to construct 'new XModule()' — but Wallow.Api already does exactly that today and keeps doing so after this change (its own 7 Infrastructure ProjectReferences are explicitly NOT removed, since RunTestMigrationsAsync in WallowModules.cs:127-147 still needs concrete DbContext types — verified by grep, only DbContext usages in that file are in RunTestMigrationsAsync/MigrateIfRegistered, exactly the region the design says to leave alone). Read tests/Wallow.Architecture.Tests/ModuleIsolationTests.cs and CleanArchitectureTests.cs in full: both use NetArchTest.Types.InAssembly() scoped ONLY to each module's own {Module}.{Domain,Application,Infrastructure,Api} assemblies (via TestConstants.AllModules, discovered off *.Domain.dll on disk) — neither ever loads or scans Wallow.Api, Wallow.MigrationService, or would scan Wallow.Modules.Registry. This is not a new violation class, confirming the design's own risk note.

(3) MIGRATIONSERVICE 7→1 REFS — verified feasible. Audited every file in Wallow.MigrationService (Program.cs, ModuleMigrations.cs, DbContextMigrationRunner.cs, MigrationWorker.cs, IMigrationRunner.cs, MigrationRunnerCollections.cs) plus MigrationServiceTests.cs: zero compile-time references to any module's concrete DbContext or module type. ModuleMigrations.cs's usings are only the 7 *.Infrastructure.Modules namespaces (for IWallowModule construction) — no *.Infrastructure.Persistence usings anywhere in the file. AddModuleDbContexts/CreateRunners work entirely off Type objects from IWallowModule.DbContextTypes via reflection (EnsureDbContextType + MakeGenericMethod). SDK-style ProjectReferences are transitive, so routing through one Wallow.Modules.Registry reference still makes the 7 module Infrastructure assemblies (and their DbContext types) loadable at runtime. The drop is real, not cosmetic.

(4) REGRESSION TEST — verified it can actually fail, and verified its real scope. The InvokeAddWallowModules reflection pattern the design cites already exists and runs today in tests/Wallow.Architecture.Tests/Modules/ModuleToggleTests.cs:95-107 (Assembly.Load("Wallow.Api") + GetType("Wallow.Api.WallowModules") + GetMethod(..., BindingFlags.Public|Static) — reflection reaches a public method on an internal class with no InternalsVisibleTo, confirmed by reading the existing passing test). ModuleMigrations.All has the identical accessibility shape (internal class, public member) at src/Wallow.MigrationService/ModuleMigrations.cs:26,49 — same trick applies symmetrically. Confirmed the test's actual failure mode: since the two arrays are TODAY byte-for-byte identical (per the bead's own scout), a guard test alone would already pass before this fix ships — proving the design's own point that a guard test (Option B) can never by itself prove 'one list', only 'the two agree right now'. After Option A, the test guards specifically against someone reintroducing a second hardcoded array that DRIFTS from WallowModuleRegistry.All (e.g. reverting ModuleMigrations.All's delegation) — that is exactly the acceptance criterion's failure mode ('adding an eighth module to only one of the two lists'), not a vacuous check.

(5) SEAM FOR Wallow-3mbx.2 — verified independently, not just read off the design. api/src/Modules/ApiKeys/Wallow.ApiKeys.Infrastructure/Modules/ApiKeysModule.cs confirms 'this.SchemaName' (=> "apikeys") is in scope inside AddServices, which currently calls services.AddApiKeysModule(configuration) without passing it — trivially extendable to pass this.SchemaName, entirely inside the module's own Infrastructure project. IWallowModule.cs:66's SchemaName getter needs no registry project to be readable from AddServices. Confirms 3mbx.2's dependency on this bead is real only for the migration-host leg (ModuleMigrations reading module.SchemaName off the same registry instances the API enables) — the design's correction that 3mbx.2 should NOT block on 'needing a registry project' for its own remaining declarations is accurate and should stand.

MINOR NON-BLOCKING NOTES (do not gate CLOSE):
- The decision to override the bead's own original recommendation ('B first ... do not do A merely for tidiness') is a legitimate judgment call the acceptance criteria explicitly permits, but it re-weighs facts that were already known at filing time (two duplicate sites) rather than new information — flagging for the record, not as a defect.
- tests/Wallow.Architecture.Tests.csproj has no DIRECT ProjectReference to ApiKeys or Inquiries module projects today (only Identity/Notifications/Announcements/Storage/Branding are listed explicitly; ApiKeys/Inquiries arrive only transitively via its Wallow.Api and Wallow.MigrationService references) — harmless given the new tests use reflection/an interface-typed collection, not concrete ApiKeysModule/InquiriesModule references, but worth the implementer's awareness if they add a third direct-reference test later.

No fatal flaw found in any of the five attack vectors. Design is safe to implement as written.

PASSING UNEXPECTEDLY (1), and this is expected, not a defect:
4. ApiHost_EnabledModules_ShouldMatch_MigrationServiceHost_AllModules_WhenEveryFlagEnabled (the DESIGN's test 2, cross-host TYPE equivalence) is GREEN TODAY. This is exactly what the DESIGN REVIEW's point (4) predicted: the two arrays are byte-for-byte identical right now, so a type-equivalence guard alone cannot fail before the fix. It is kept because it is the acceptance criterion's own wording ('adding an eighth module to only one of the two lists fails a test') and it stays meaningful after the fix - but ON ITS OWN IT IS NOT THE REGRESSION GUARD.

HOW THE DESIGN REVIEW'S 'CAN THIS GUARD ACTUALLY FAIL?' CONCERN WAS ANSWERED - the two identity tests are the answer, and it was demonstrated empirically, not argued:
The guard asserts REFERENCE IDENTITY, not type equality. Every module instance a host hands back must be the same object as an instance in WallowModuleRegistry.All (ReferenceEquals). A hand-rolled second array cannot satisfy that even when its contents are byte-for-byte identical, because new XModule() mints fresh instances.
DEMONSTRATION RUN: I temporarily populated WallowModuleRegistry.All with the seven new XModule() entries - i.e. a FULLY BUILT registry sitting beside the two hosts' existing, identical, still-duplicated arrays, which is precisely the 'somebody reintroduced a second list' regression - rebuilt and re-ran. Result: 2 failed / 2 passed. Test 1 flipped to green (registry now has seven) and test 4 stayed green (types still agree), but tests 2 and 3 STILL FAILED on identity. That is the proof: an identical-but-separate list does not pass this guard. I then REVERTED WallowModuleRegistry.All to the empty scaffold and re-confirmed the 3-failing red state, so the repo is left red.
Under the approved design both guards go green for the right reason: ModuleMigrations.All => WallowModuleRegistry.All and ResolveEnabledModules filters WallowModuleRegistry.All, so both hosts hand back the registry's own instances.

NO SOURCE-READING. No File.ReadAllText, no node:fs equivalent, no assertions about file anatomy. Everything is runtime: reflection loads the assemblies, invokes/reads the members, and asserts over the live object graph.

REFLECTION PATTERN (no InternalsVisibleTo needed anywhere, confirming the DESIGN's correction to this bead's own body):
- InvokeAddWallowModules: Assembly.Load(\"Wallow.Api\") + GetType(\"Wallow.Api.WallowModules\") + GetMethod(\"AddWallowModules\", Public|Static) - the exact pattern already in Modules/ModuleToggleTests.cs, except this one KEEPS the IReadOnlyList<IWallowModule> return value instead of discarding it. Redis is substituted (NSubstitute IConnectionMultiplexer) because modules resolve IConnectionMultiplexer at registration time.
- ReadModuleMigrationsAll: Assembly.Load(\"Wallow.MigrationService\") + GetType(\"Wallow.MigrationService.ModuleMigrations\") + GetProperty(\"All\", Public|Static). Same accessibility shape (internal class, public member) - works, verified by the run.
- The arrange block sets all seven FeatureManagement:Modules.<Name> flags to \"true\" (Identity, Branding, Notifications, Announcements, Storage, ApiKeys, Inquiries - names verified against each module's Name property) plus ConnectionStrings:DefaultConnection, so the API host's FILTERED list equals the migration host's UNFILTERED one. The filtering difference the bead says must survive is untouched: nothing here asserts that the migration host filters.

title: four handlers dispatch before saving, so AutoApplyTransactions commits after the side effect
description:
Found by Wallow-af3h.3 (2026-08-05) while enabling opts.Policies.AutoApplyTransactions().

## Context

af3h.3 gave every chain whose dependencies reach a module DbContext a
<Module>DbContext.SaveChangesAsync POSTPROCESSOR. The postprocessor runs at the END of the chain.
It ADDS a save; it does not move or remove work the handler already does.

So for a handler that performs an external side effect and THEN relies on the postprocessor to
commit, the side effect now happens BEFORE the commit. If the commit then fails, the side effect
has already escaped and cannot be taken back. SendNotificationHandler was audited and is correct
(it saves explicitly, then pushes) -- that ordering is now documented in api/CLAUDE.md and in the
Program.cs comment.

## The four that were flagged as dispatch-before-save

- api/src/Modules/Notifications/Wallow.Notifications.Application/Channels/Push/Commands/DeliverPush/DeliverPushHandler.cs
- api/src/Modules/Storage/Wallow.Storage.Application/Commands/UploadFile/UploadFileHandler.cs
- api/src/Modules/Storage/Wallow.Storage.Application/Commands/DeleteFile/DeleteFileHandler.cs
- api/src/Modules/Storage/Wallow.Storage.Application/Commands/DeleteBucket/DeleteBucketHandler.cs

The three Storage ones are the sharper risk: they act on the object store (upload/delete a file,
delete a bucket) and an S3 delete is not undone by a database rollback. A failed commit after a
successful DeleteBucket leaves rows describing a bucket that no longer exists.

## What to do

Paths are verified to exist; the dispatch-before-save CHARACTERISATION is af3h.3's and has NOT
been independently re-read. Confirm it per handler first -- do not assume all four are wrong.

For each genuinely affected handler decide between: an explicit save before the side effect (the
SendNotificationHandler shape), or moving the side effect out of the transactional chain into a
follow-up message that only runs after commit. Prefer the second where the side effect is
irreversible.

Not blocking af3h.3: this hazard predates it in the sense that the handlers already had this
ordering. What af3h.3 changed is that a commit now reliably happens at the end of the chain,
which makes the window well-defined rather than accidental.
notes:
Re-read all four handlers per the bead's instruction not to assume af3h.3's characterisation. Two corrections and two fixes.

FRAMING CORRECTION: all four handlers ALREADY call SaveChangesAsync explicitly. The
AutoApplyTransactions postprocessor is therefore a no-op after them (nothing tracked left to
flush), and none of this is a regression from af3h.3. The defect, where it exists, is the
pre-existing ordering of the side effect against the handler's OWN save. The bead title describes
a mechanism that is not operating here.

PER-HANDLER VERDICTS:
- DeliverPushHandler -- NOT A DEFECT. Sends, then records the outcome (MarkDelivered/MarkFailed)
  and saves in a finally before rethrowing. You cannot persist the result of a send before
  sending. Residual risk is duplicate delivery on Wolverine retry: an at-least-once property, not
  a rollback hazard. No change made.
- UploadFileHandler -- REAL BUT BENIGN, NOT FIXED. Uploads, then inserts the row and saves. A
  failed save orphans a blob; no row points at anything missing. Reversing it would be WORSE (a
  row pointing at an object never uploaded). Correct fix is a GC sweep, not a reorder. Filed
  separately.
- DeleteFileHandler -- REAL, FIXED.
- DeleteBucketHandler -- REAL, FIXED (sharper: the loop could strand a whole bucket's rows).

FIX (both deletes): collect the storage key(s), MarkAsDeleted + Remove, SaveChangesAsync, THEN
delete from the object store. Worst case becomes an orphaned object (garbage, unreferenced)
instead of a row pointing at bytes that are gone (a permanent 404 on read).

Chose the reorder over the bead's preferred post-commit follow-up message: the storage delete is
idempotent, so the message buys only durable retry of a delete, at the cost of a new command type
and handler. Residual: a crash between commit and the storage delete permanently orphans the
object -- the same class of garbage UploadFile already produces, and the same GC sweep covers both.

NOTE for anyone reading DeleteFileHandler: MarkAsDeleted() is not a soft-delete flag before a hard
delete -- it raises FileDeletedEvent. It must stay before SaveChangesAsync.

TESTS: added an ordering guard to each suite (NSubstitute Received.InOrder). Confirmed RED against
the old code (exactly 2 failures, 577 passing), then green. Full backend run INCLUDING
Category=Integration: 5229/5229 pass. dotnet format made no changes.

title: WallowApiFactory mutates process-global env vars that a second factory instance can observe
description:
Found by Wallow-af3h.3 (2026-08-05) while chasing 4 non-reproducing integration failures.

## Mechanism

api/tests/Wallow.Tests.Common/Factories/WallowApiFactory.cs:75 sets
ConnectionStrings__DefaultConnection (and __Redis, and four OpenIddict cert vars) as
PROCESS-GLOBAL environment variables, because modules capture connection strings at service
registration time and the in-memory override in ConfigureWebHost lands too late. Dispose (:120)
nulls all six.

Wallow.Api.Tests has TWO collections that each take ICollectionFixture<WallowApiFactory>, so two
factory instances exist in one process: ApiIntegrationTestCollection and
PerformanceTuningTestCollection (PerformanceTuningTests.cs:92). Collection fixtures are per
collection, not shared.

## CORRECTION to the original diagnosis

af3h.3 attributed this to the two collections running IN PARALLEL. They do not:
api/tests/Wallow.Api.Tests/xunit.runner.json sets BOTH parallelizeAssembly: false AND
parallelizeTestCollections: false. So the parallel-execution mechanism as stated is wrong, and
this bead should NOT be worked on that theory.

The hazard that survives is LIFETIME OVERLAP rather than concurrency: xunit creates collection
fixtures lazily but disposes them at assembly teardown, so factory A's dispose can null the env
vars while factory B is still alive. A host already built has captured its config and does not
care -- but PerformanceTuningTests builds ADDITIONAL hosts via WithWebHostBuilder after its
fixture is up, and those re-run builder creation, re-reading the environment. That is a real
ordering dependency on a process-global.

UNVERIFIED: whether this actually fires today. af3h.3 got 9 consecutive clean runs and traced the
failures it DID see to a coverlet pdb lock from a concurrent test process -- a different cause
entirely. So treat this as a latent hazard found by inspection, not an observed failure. First
task is to prove or disprove it, not to fix it.

## Why it is worth fixing regardless

A process-global set-and-null pair shared by two fixtures is order-dependent by construction, and
the failure mode is a connection string silently becoming null in a host built late. That is
expensive to diagnose -- it already cost af3h.3 most of its run.

Prefer a fix that removes the global: have the factory push config through a mechanism scoped to
the host it is building, or make disposal not null a variable another live fixture may depend on.
notes:
VERDICT: the lifetime-overlap hazard is DISPROVEN empirically for the exact toolchain in use (xunit 2.9.3, xunit.runner.visualstudio 3.1.5, net10.0, parallelizeAssembly:false + parallelizeTestCollections:false).

The bead's surviving theory rested on 'xunit creates collection fixtures lazily but disposes them at assembly teardown'. That claim is wrong for xunit v2: XunitTestCollectionRunner disposes collection fixtures when THAT collection finishes, before the next collection starts. Verified by a minimal repro (two collections each ICollectionFixture of an IAsyncLifetime fixture that sets a process-global env var in InitializeAsync and nulls it in DisposeAsync, same runner.json, same package versions). Observed log ordering:

  fixture#1 InitializeAsync (sets env var)
  TestsInB.B1 running, env=conn-from-fixture-1
  fixture#1 DisposeAsync (nulls env var)
  fixture#2 InitializeAsync (sets env var)
  TestsInA.A1 running, env=conn-from-fixture-2
  TestsInA.A2 running, env=conn-from-fixture-2
  fixture#2 DisposeAsync

Dispose of fixture A is strictly sequenced BEFORE Initialize of fixture B, so no host build (including PerformanceTuningTests' WithWebHostBuilder rebuilds) can ever observe a nulled connection string. There is no window.

Supporting sweep: every WallowApiFactory consumer reaches it via ICollectionFixture (ApiIntegrationTestCollection + PerformanceTuningTestCollection in Wallow.Api.Tests; WallowTestCollection for Wallow.Identity.IntegrationTests, a separate testhost process). Zero direct 'new WallowApiFactory' or IClassFixture uses. Every assembly that consumes the factory sets parallelizeTestCollections:false (only Wallow.Architecture.Tests sets true, and it does not use the factory).

On the 'worth fixing regardless' argument: the sketched fix (dispose does not null what another live fixture depends on) would NOT make collection parallelization safe anyway — two concurrent InitializeAsync calls setting conflicting ConnectionStrings__DefaultConnection race on the SET side, not just the null side. The process-global is inherently single-writer; the real invariant is 'assemblies using WallowApiFactory must keep parallelizeTestCollections:false', which is already the case everywhere, and env vars themselves are load-bearing (modules capture connection strings before ConfigureAppConfiguration applies). Removing the global is not achievable without solving that capture-time problem first.

Recommendation: close as disproven-by-investigation; optionally add a comment at the SetEnvironmentVariable block in WallowApiFactory documenting the single-writer invariant and why disposal ordering makes it safe.
close_reason: Disproven by investigation: xunit v2 disposes collection fixtures at collection end, not assembly teardown; with parallelizeTestCollections:false lifetimes never overlap. Evidence in bead notes; single-writer invariant documented in WallowApiFactory.
