title: extend IWallowModule to drive MigrationService DbContext registration
description:
Plan: docs/plans/2026-08-04/2129-wolverine-module-registration.md — Phase 4.
BLOCKED BY the IWallowModule registry bead.

## Respecified during review — a singular DbContextType does NOT work

`api/src/Wallow.MigrationService/Program.cs:22-56` registers **NINE** DbContexts, of which
`AuditDbContext` (`:26-28`) and `AuthAuditDbContext` (`:30-32`) come from
`Wallow.Shared.Infrastructure.Core.Auditing` and belong to **NO module**. The first plan
draft proposed a singular `DbContextType` + `SchemaName` pair, which cannot express that.

## Change

- `IWallowModule` gains `IReadOnlyList<Type> DbContextTypes` and `string SchemaName`.
- The two auditing contexts stay **HOST-OWNED**, outside the registry.
  `CoreMigrationRunners` (`MigrationService/Program.cs:59-64`) keeps them explicitly
  alongside `IdentityDbContext`.
- Drive the six `AddDbContext` calls and `FeatureMigrationRunners` (`:66-74`) from the
  registry.

Each context's `MigrationsHistoryTable("__EFMigrationsHistory", "<schema>")` schema string
is what `SchemaName` supplies: identity, audit, auth_audit, branding, notifications,
announcements, storage, apikeys, inquiries.

## Test that must keep passing

`api/tests/Wallow.MigrationService.Tests/MigrationServiceTests.cs` —
`ExecuteAsync_MigratesAllNineDbContexts` (`:84-100`) asserts exactly 9 runners and
`ExecuteAsync_MigratesIdentityAndAuditContexts_BeforeFeatureModules` (`:60-81`) pins core-
before-feature ordering. Both mock `IMigrationRunner` directly, so they survive the

title: pin opts.ApplicationAssembly on the Wolverine host
description:
Plan: docs/plans/2026-08-04/2129-wolverine-module-registration.md — Problem 4.

PREVENTIVE HARDENING, not a fix. No open bead attributes a current failure to this. It is
low-risk and independent of every other bead in the epic — take it any time.

## Change

`api/src/Wallow.Api/Program.cs`, inside the `UseWolverine` lambda:

    opts.ApplicationAssembly = typeof(WallowModules).Assembly;

(`WallowModules` is `internal` but lives in the same assembly — verified.)

## Why, and what the first draft got wrong

The resolved application assembly is cached in a PROCESS-WIDE static, so in a test process
standing up multiple hosts, whichever runs first pins it for every later host. Corrections
to the first plan draft:

- The operative static is **`JasperFxOptions.RememberedApplicationAssembly`**, set inside
  `AddJasperFx` via a `DetermineCallingAssembly()` stack walk.
  `WolverineOptions.RememberedApplicationAssembly` measured NULL in this repo.
- The baseline ALREADY resolves correctly to `Wallow.Api`, because every Wolverine host in
  the suite boots the same `Program.cs` through `WebApplicationFactory<Program>` — the
  mitigation the Wolverine docs themselves recommend.
- `AuditInterceptorTests.cs` bootstraps NO host (plain EF Core + Testcontainers) and
  `AuthorizationCodeFlowHarness.cs` consumes an injected factory rather than creating one.
  Neither is evidence. The real multi-host evidence is two separate
  `ICollectionFixture<WallowApiFactory>` collections in `Wallow.Api.Tests`, plus
  `PerformanceTuningTests.cs:25,69` creating further hosts via `WithWebHostBuilder`, and
  three factories in `Wallow.Identity.IntegrationTests`.

Setting it on the main host is sufficient.

## Known benign side effect

The setter also `Fill`s the discovery collection, so `Wallow.Api` appears twice in the
assembly list. Harmless — do not "fix" it.

## Acceptance

`./scripts/run-tests.sh` green.

title: identity: decide whether ClientsController narrows from AdminAccess to ServiceAccountsRead/Write/Manage
description:
identity: decide whether ClientsController narrows from AdminAccess to ServiceAccountsRead/Write/Manage.

PREMISE CORRECTED 2026-08-27 (docs/plans/2026-08-27/1127-backlog-triage-and-sequencing.md). This bead previously said "nothing in the codebase consumes any of them". That is FALSE, and it was the load-bearing claim under the delete option. Re-measured today, the three permissions are wired end-to-end everywhere EXCEPT the check:

  declared   PermissionType.cs:73-75
  scope-mapped   ScopePermissionMapper.cs:49-51 ("serviceaccounts.read|write|manage" -> the three)
  role-granted   RolePermissionMapping.cs:43-45 (to the "admin" role)
  seeded     api/seed.json:81,88,94 (all three scopes exist as seeded scope records)
  CHECKED    nowhere - grep for HasPermission(PermissionType.ServiceAccounts*) returns 0 hits

So they are not "declared-but-dead". They are ISSUED but never ENFORCED: a token carrying serviceaccounts.read already arrives with the permission on the principal, and an admin already holds all three, but no attribute anywhere reads them. ClientsController guards on AdminAccess (ClientsController.cs:24, [HasPermission(PermissionType.AdminAccess)] at class level).

WHAT THIS DOES TO THE DECISION. It is now one-sided rather than balanced:

* NARROW is cheap and additive. The plumbing already exists; the work is changing the class-level attribute on ClientsController to per-action guards on the three permissions. Nothing needs to be created, seeded, or migrated - and admins keep access automatically via the role grant above.
* DELETE is no longer "remove three unused members". It means unwiring four live call sites and dropping three seeded scope records, which is a real change to the issued token surface for any client that has already been granted them.

The bead therefore no longer poses a genuine fork. Unless there is a product reason to want a single coarse admin gate on OAuth client management, NARROW is the answer, and the remaining question is only the read/write/manage split across ClientsController actions.

Found by the 2026-08-04 documentation accuracy audit (finding W-H2); see docs/plans/2026-08-04/1113-doc-accuracy-audit.md section 6.

## Acceptance

* A decision is recorded on this bead: narrow, or delete.
* If narrow, an implementation bead is filed carrying the per-action read/write/manage split.
notes:
DECISION (2026-08-28): NARROW — but scoped to the service-account actions, not the whole controller.

Two findings sharpen the bead's framing:

1. The documented contract only ever covers the service-account endpoints. docs/api/service-accounts.md:214-216 and docs/operations/deployment.md:418 describe serviceaccounts.read/write/manage for the /clients/service-accounts surface; audit finding W-H2's own title is 'Service-account actions are guarded by AdminAccess'. Nothing anywhere promises that the relying-party client CRUD (GetAll/GetById/GetByTenant/Create/Update/Delete/RotateSecret on /clients) narrows — and no scope maps to any RP-client permission, so no client-credentials token could ever exercise a narrower guard there. Registering OIDC relying parties (redirect URIs, grantable scopes incl. roles) is first-party platform administration; it keeps AdminAccess.

2. The check side is exact-match with AND composition. PermissionAuthorizationHandler.cs does permissions.Contains(requirement.Permission) — no hierarchy — and stacked [HasPermission] attributes are separate policies that must ALL pass (class-level + action-level would AND). So the implementation must REMOVE the class-level AdminAccess attribute and go fully per-action (the established repo pattern: UsersController, OrganizationsController, AppsController). And 'manage implies write implies read' does not hold at the check; supersets are grant-side (admin role grants all three via RolePermissionMapping.cs:43-45; a token wanting full management requests all three scopes — serviceaccounts.read is isDefault anyway). This matches every other permission family in the system (apikeys.*, users.*), so no hierarchy work is filed.

The per-action split (rationale on the implementation bead):
- AdminAccess: GetAll, GetById, GetByTenant, Create, Update, Delete, RotateSecret (RP-client CRUD)
- ServiceAccountsRead: ListServiceAccounts, GetServiceAccount
- ServiceAccountsWrite: CreateServiceAccount, UpdateServiceAccountScopes
- ServiceAccountsManage: RotateServiceAccountSecret, RevokeServiceAccount

UpdateServiceAccountScopes sits at Write, not Manage: CreateServiceAccount already accepts arbitrary scopes in the request, so Write can mint an account with any scopes it likes — gating scope *updates* at Manage would be theater. Manage = the credential/destruction pair (rotate-secret invalidates the running consumer's secret; revoke deletes the account), consistent with seed.json's 'create, update, and delete' description.
Implementation bead filed: Wallow-y74w (carries the per-action split and test requirements). Both acceptance items on this bead are now satisfied.

description:

title: run-tests.sh silently mishandles an unknown module name
description:
scripts/run-tests.sh resolve_filter() is a hardcoded case statement mapping module names to test project paths. Its default arm is '*) echo "$filter" ;;', so an unrecognised module name is passed straight through to dotnet test as a project path and fails to resolve with a confusing error.

A new module's tests are therefore unrunnable via the script until someone edits the case statement. docs/architecture/module-creation.md Step 10 now documents adding the arm as a required step, but the script should fail loudly on an unknown name (list the valid module names and exit non-zero) rather than handing a bogus path to dotnet test.

Source: docs audit 2026-08-04 docs/audits/2026-08-04/0917-repo-docs-accuracy/report.md (finding E6).
acceptance_criteria: An unknown module argument exits non-zero with a message naming every valid shorthand (identity, storage, notifications, announcements, inquiries, branding, apikeys, api, arch|architecture, seeder, migrations, shared, kernel, integration), instead of passing the raw string to dotnet test as a project path. Every documented shorthand still runs its suite; ./scripts/run-tests.sh with no argument is unchanged. api/CLAUDE.md, which currently documents the pass-through behaviour, is updated to match.
notes:
MERGED Wallow-tmy4 (P3 task, 'make scripts/run-tests.sh fail loudly on an unknown module name') into this bead on 2026-08-27 per docs/plans/2026-08-27/1127-backlog-triage-and-sequencing.md. Same defect, filed twice by the same 2026-08-04 docs audit - tmy4 from the CLAUDE.md angle, this one from the module-creation.md angle. This bead survives as the P2 bug; tmy4 is closed as a duplicate.

Folded in from tmy4: its acceptance criteria (now this bead's, above), and the enumerated shorthand list resolve_filter() actually maps. Also from tmy4: api/CLAUDE.md documents the CURRENT pass-through behaviour and must be updated as part of the fix - otherwise the docs go stale the moment this lands.

DEFECT RE-VERIFIED 2026-08-27, still live. scripts/run-tests.sh:47:

        *)               echo "$MODULE_FILTER" ;;

so './scripts/run-tests.sh idenity' hands 'idenity' to dotnet test as a path. Note the script already has the right shape elsewhere to copy - the tier argument's default arm at scripts/run-tests.sh:76-80 does exactly what this bead asks for:

    *)
        echo "Unknown tier '${2}'. The second argument, when given, must be 'integration' or 'all'." >&2
        rm -rf "$TRX_DIR"
        exit 2
        ;;

Match that: message to stderr, clean up TRX_DIR, exit 2. Keeping the two arms symmetric is most of the work.
Done in 32d6eb1e. resolve_filter's catch-all now passes through only an argument that EXISTS on disk; anything else exits 2 after rm -rf "$TRX_DIR", mirroring the arm that already did this for an unknown second-argument tier, and prints the full shorthand list.

The -e guard is load-bearing: run-tests.sh's own usage block documents a <project-path> form, and api/CLAUDE.md tells agents to reach Wallow.Identity.IntegrationTests by path because it has no shorthand. Rejecting everything unknown would have broken that.

api/CLAUDE.md's pass-through note updated to say the path must exist. Verified: ./scripts/run-tests.sh identty exits 2 with the list; ./scripts/run-tests.sh 4969/4969 PASS.

title: chore: .beads/README.md is gitignored, so the bd workflow doc never reaches a fresh clone
description:
Found during the 2026-08-04 repo docs accuracy audit (docs/audits/2026-08-04/0917-repo-docs-accuracy/report.md, findings A1 / X6).

The audit told Batch 1 to rewrite .beads/README.md, which was stock 'bd init' boilerplate teaching a nonexistent 'bd sync' command and claiming beads auto-sync with commits. That rewrite is done and is correct for this working copy.

The problem: root .gitignore:21 ignores '.beads/' wholesale, with no negation pattern anywhere (.beads/.gitignore explicitly forbids adding one, citing fork protection in .git/info/exclude). 'git ls-files .beads/' returns nothing. So the rewritten README is untracked -- a fresh clone never receives it, and 'bd init' will regenerate the same wrong boilerplate for the next contributor.

The audit's scope note for X6 ('it is the first file a new contributor opens after bd init fails them') is therefore only half right: it is the first file they open, and it is the boilerplate, not our corrected version.

Needs a decision, which is a config change rather than a docs edit:
  (a) un-ignore just .beads/README.md (needs care -- .beads/.gitignore warns that negation patterns override fork protection), or
  (b) accept that .beads/ is local-only and move the canonical bd workflow into a tracked file. docs/getting-started/developer-guide.md already owns beads setup, sync mechanics, and the husky / 'bd hooks install' conflict, so it is the natural home.

Option (b) is likely correct and cheaper. Either way the tracked copy must state: bd ready / bd show / bd update --status in_progress / bd close / bd note; there is no 'bd sync'; nothing auto-syncs on commit; beads live on refs/dolt/data over HTTPS and only 'bd dolt push' moves them.
notes:
Resolved via option (b), which was already ~95% implemented.

THREE CORRECTIONS to this bead's premises, verified 2026-08-05:

1. 'That rewrite is done and is correct for this working copy' is NO LONGER TRUE. .beads/README.md
   on disk is stock bd init boilerplate, mtime identical to config.yaml (i.e. init time). The
   corrected version is gone -- the bead's own thesis proved itself.
2. The 'bd sync' complaint does not apply to the current bd boilerplate, which teaches
   'bd dolt push' / 'bd dolt pull'. Still wrong for Wallow (no refs/dolt/data, no husky conflict),
   but not for the recorded reason.
3. Option (a)'s stated risk is NOT REAL in this clone. .beads/.gitignore warns a negation pattern
   would 'override fork protection in .git/info/exclude', but that file is the unmodified git
   template -- comments only, no patterns. That warning is bd's generic boilerplate, not a
   Wallow-specific constraint.

docs/getting-started/developer-guide.md already stated everything on the must-state list except
'bd note': commands, .beads/ is gitignored, git push does not carry beads (pre-push exits 0 without
touching refs/dolt/data), HTTPS sync over the same repo, only bd dolt push/pull move data, and the
bd hooks install conflict.

CHANGE: added 'bd note' to the command block and a paragraph declaring this page canonical and
.beads/README.md non-authoritative (untracked, regenerated by bd init on every fresh setup, so
nothing written there survives). Option (a) was rejected independently of correction 3: un-ignoring
one file means fighting bd init forever.

title: wire the console/network/navigation guards into the three unwired vitest browser projects
description:
Audit finding C8 (docs/audits/2026-08-04/0917-repo-docs-accuracy/report.md).

createVitestProjects()'s browserSetupFiles defaults to [] (packages/testing/src/vitest-projects.ts), so the console/network/navigation guards are strictly opt-in per project. Eight browser projects exist; five install the guards via a vitest.setup.ts and packages/ui's storybook project installs them via .storybook/preview.tsx.

Three install nothing:
- apps/minimal-app (vitest.config.ts calls createVitestProjects() with no arguments; it has real browser specs: src/browser-mode-smoke.test.tsx, src/features/hello/HelloCard.test.tsx)
- packages/logger (hand-rolled browser project, no @bc-solutions-coder/testing dependency at all)
- packages/testing itself (four *.test.tsx specs in its own browser project)

Wire a setup file into each so console noise, escaped fetches and navigation escapes fail the test that produced them. packages/logger additionally has to decide whether to take the preset or keep its hand-rolled pair with the guards added.

This is a config change, deliberately out of scope for the docs pass. packages/testing/CLAUDE.md now documents the census and states the guard is opt-in.
notes:
Census correction (docs touch-up pass, 2026-08-04): the description says "Eight browser projects exist". The real count is NINE across eight packages, because packages/ui/vitest.config.ts:89 declares 'projects: [node, browser, storybook]' — two browser-mode projects in one package. Re-derived from every vitest.config.ts in the workspace: minimal-app, wallow-web, wallow-auth, ui(browser), ui(storybook), forms, logger, navigation, testing = 9. The 5-wired / 1-storybook / 3-unwired split in the description is unchanged and correct; only the total was off by one. packages/testing/CLAUDE.md and the audit report have been corrected.
Done in commit 208e2613. All three projects now install the full guard trio (console, navigation, network) in a browser-project setup file, each with one independent afterEach per guard.

Per-project decisions:
- apps/minimal-app: new vitest.setup.ts passed via createVitestProjects({ browserSetupFiles }). Guards only, no stylesheet — its specs assert visibility/wiring, not painted colour.
- packages/logger: KEPT the hand-rolled project pair (its config comment's React rationale holds). Added setupFiles to the browser project + a @bc-solutions-coder/testing devDependency — the guard subpaths import only vitest, so the React-free charter is untouched. Its browser spec's vi.stubGlobal('fetch') doubles sit over the guard wrapper and unstubAllGlobals restores it, so no false escapes.
- packages/testing: new vitest.setup.ts importing guards from ./src (dist-free, same rule as its config). The guard self-tests coexist: installers are idempotent, and Vitest runs afterEach in reverse registration order so a spec's uninstall/clear runs before the project assertion. navigation-escape.test.tsx's 'this package wires none' header corrected.

Verification was sabotage-style: a temp spec per project provoking console.error, an off-origin fetch and a location.assign — all three PASSED unguarded (RED), all nine cases FAILED with the correct guard messages after wiring, deleted before commit. Full suites green after (testing 86, logger 129, minimal-app 14); pnpm check exit 0.

The five older setup files + ui's storybook preview still install only navigation+console; extending the network guard there is Wallow-70fu. Census in packages/testing/CLAUDE.md updated.

title: flake: vi.mock module-mocking rejection in both app suites under concurrent turbo test
description:
Both apps failed a full 'pnpm check' with an Unhandled Rejection, no test-file summary printed:

  Error: [vitest] There was an error when mocking a module. If you are using
  "vi.mock" factory, make sure there are no top level variables inside, since
  this call is hoisted to top of the file.
  at VitestBrowserClientMocker.resolveFactoryModule
  at Proxy.resolveManualMock  (@vitest/browser client.js)

Both @bc-solutions-coder/wallow-auth and @bc-solutions-coder/wallow-web failed together; every other package passed. The stack also shows a playwright RouteHandler frame, so a route handler is in the failing path.

NOT reproducible in isolation: 'pnpm --filter wallow-auth --filter wallow-web test' -> 74 + 51 files, 1323 tests, all pass, exit 0. An immediately following full 'pnpm check' -> exit 0. So it only appeared with all packages' browser-mode suites running concurrently under turbo.

The message text is misleading - it is the generic mocker error, and these specs pass alone, so a genuine top-level-variable-in-factory violation is unlikely. Read it as the mocker failing to resolve a manual mock under load rather than as a hoisting bug.

DISTINCT from Wallow-x5da (app-shell.toggle.test.tsx leaking a real navigation) - different failure mode, and this one takes out both whole app suites rather than one spec.

Left open rather than chased: it is a CI-reliability risk (a green run proves less than it should), not a product defect. Next step is likely to reproduce under load - repeat 'turbo run test --force' - and check whether it correlates with the same fileParallelism question docs/plans/2026-08-03/1639-proxy-trust-react-dupe-nav-flake.md raises for Wallow-x5da.
notes:
NON-REPRODUCTION, 2026-08-27. 21 consecutive full-workspace runs
(`turbo run test --force` at turbo concurrency default/4/3/2, then
`--force --only` with browser maxWorkers unset/2/1) on a heavily loaded 8-core
box. Grepped every log for this bead's signature:

  "error when mocking a module"  -> 0 of 21 logs
  VitestBrowserClientMocker      -> 0 of 21 logs

Zero recurrence. Both app suites DID fail repeatedly across those runs, but every
time with the Wallow-pr34 starvation signature ("Failed to import test file" /
"Failed to fetch dynamically imported module"), never the mocker rejection.

This weakens -- it does not refute -- the unification hypothesis that
Wallow-x5da's navigation escape is a downstream effect of THIS bead (vi.mock
failing to apply, so app-shell.toggle.test.tsx's Link stub is absent and the real
anchor navigates). Neither signature fired in 21 runs, so the two could still be
one defect; there is simply no evidence either way from this sweep.

Worth recording for whoever picks this up: app-shell.toggle.test.tsx's Link stub
is NOT the weak point. It destructures `onClick` out before `{...rest}` and calls
`event.preventDefault()` unconditionally, so a spread handler cannot displace it.
If a real navigation to /dashboard/organizations happened, the stub was ABSENT,
which is this bead's failure mode rather than a defect in the stub.
CONSEQUENCE OF Wallow-pr34, 2026-08-27 (Step 6). The root `test` script now runs at turbo `--concurrency=1` — several packages' browser-mode suites no longer mount at once. This bead's only recorded reproduction required exactly that concurrency ("it only appeared with all packages' browser-mode suites running concurrently under turbo"), so the cap plausibly removes the trigger condition. That is an inference, not a verification: the signature did not fire in the 21 pre-fix runs of the Step 6 sweep either, so there is no before/after comparison. Leaving open. To chase it, re-measure at the OLD concurrency (`turbo run test --force`, no cap) to get a reproduction first — running under the shipped cap will likely just add more non-reproduction. Wallow-x5da carries a companion note refuting the in-document click-geometry theory; the unification hypothesis recorded above (vi.mock failing under load leaves the Link stub absent, so a real anchor navigates) is untouched by that refutation and remains the leading link between the two beads.
CORRECTION to the '21 consecutive full-workspace runs, zero recurrence' note above — the effective sample was smaller than 21, and the shortfall is exactly the runs that mattered.

Re-audited all 21 logs for a per-package 'Test Files' summary line, which is the only proof a package's suite actually executed rather than being aborted:

  packages/navigation  21/21 ran
  apps/wallow-auth     15/21 ran  (no summary in 6)
  apps/wallow-web      16/21 ran  (no summary in 5)

The missing runs are not noise. Those app suites died at module load on the Wallow-pr34 signature ('Failed to fetch dynamically imported module' / 'Cannot connect to the iframe') before reaching the specs this bead is about. So the sweep was measuring a suite that had already been killed by a different defect.

This bead's mocker-rejection lives in the app suites. Its real sample is therefore ~15-16 clean observations, not 21. Under the documented ~13% per-run rate, 15 clean runs at zero is still meaningful evidence against recurrence (p ~ 12%) but it is nowhere near the ~5% the 21-run figure implied, and it should not be cited as a strong non-reproduction.

Worth noting the mechanism that made this measurement bad has since been fixed: pr34 shipped 'turbo run test --concurrency=1', so the app suites no longer get starved out at module load. Any future sweep under the shipped cap will have a full 21/21 sample. But a sweep under the cap also removes the load this bead needs to reproduce, which is the tension recorded in the note below.
REPRODUCED, and the error message's own explanation is wrong for this defect.

Fresh sweep on the current tree at the OLD concurrency (no --concurrency flag, so turbo's default 10; --force --continue). It fired on run 4:

  rep=1 exit=1 secs=60  mocker=0 dynimport=18
  rep=2 exit=1 secs=53  mocker=0 dynimport=26
  rep=3 exit=1 secs=62  mocker=0 dynimport=18
  rep=4 HUNG            mocker=2   <-- hit, in apps/wallow-auth

Full capture: scratchpad repro/hits/hit-4-xzy1.6.txt.

WHAT IT IS NOT. Vitest prints 'If you are using vi.mock factory, make sure there are no top level variables inside, since this call is hoisted to top of the file.' That hint describes a STATIC AUTHORING fault. If it applied, the spec would fail on every run in every environment. This fires on roughly 1 run in N, under load, against unchanged source that passes the other N-1 times. Vitest reuses one canned string for any failure inside factory resolution, so the message is misdirection here. Do not go looking for a hoisting bug in a vi.mock factory — there isn't one.

WHAT THE STACK ACTUALLY SAYS. It arrives as an **Unhandled Rejection**, not a test failure — which is why no spec is named and the run's FAIL count is 0. The outer async stack is:

  @vitest/browser-playwright/dist/index.js:999:37
  RouteHandler._handleInternal   (playwright-core)
  RouteHandler._handleImpl
  RouteHandler.handle
  _BrowserContext._onRoute

and the inner 'Caused by' is:

  VitestBrowserClientMocker.resolveFactoryModule   (in-browser tester bundle)
  Proxy.resolveManualMock                          (@vitest/browser client.js:398)
  onMessage                                        (@vitest/browser client.js:162)

So the sequence is: the in-browser tester posts a message asking for a manual mock -> the node side resolves the factory module -> that resolution is serviced through a **Playwright network-route interception** -> it rejects, outside any test's lifecycle, so nothing owns the rejection.

That makes this a module-DELIVERY failure through the Vite-dev-server-behind-Playwright-routing path, not a mocking-API misuse. It is the same class of failure as Wallow-pr34's 'Failed to fetch dynamically imported module' — a module request that does not come back under load — surfacing at a different layer. Both beads should be read as symptoms of that one path saturating.

Corroborating: in the same run, five wallow-web spec files reported '(0 test)', i.e. loaded nothing. In the three completed runs the '(0 test)' marker and the dynimport error text track each other exactly (9/18, 5/26, 9/18). Run 4 shows 0 dynimport text only because it hung before printing its error section, NOT because the failures were absent.

Implication for a fix: chasing this inside the spec is wasted effort. The lever is the module-delivery path — which is exactly what pr34's --concurrency=1 cap relieves, and it is why this has not been seen since that shipped.
Steps 2-3 of docs/plans/2026-08-27/1618-nav-leak-forensics-and-measurement.md shipped (commits a5c5cc0b, 12c28114): escape-guard forensics + stub-applied assertion in all 13 packages/navigation router-stub specs (silent stub absence now fails by name). Also observed during the gate: the first pnpm-check run after editing packages/testing source killed 6 wallow-web spec files with 'Cannot connect to the iframe ... unknown due to CORS' AT --concurrency=1; the standalone rerun printed 'Re-optimizing dependencies because vite config has changed' and went 76/76 green. Consistent with this bead's diagnosed mechanism: a Vite dep re-optimization landing mid-run interrupts module delivery and kills suites at load time — the cap reduces exposure but a dep-cache invalidation can still trigger it once, on the first run after config/dep-graph changes. Next: Step 4 uncapped sweep.
REPRODUCED, 2026-08-27 — first recurrence since the original observation, and it
settles the bead. In the Step 4 uncapped sweep for Wallow-x5da (25 consecutive
`turbo run test --force --continue` runs, NO --concurrency flag, 8 cores, load
~10-13, warm dep cache, per-run logs), this bead's exact signature fired in
3 of 25 runs (runs 6, 20, 25): "[vitest] There was an error when mocking a
module…" as an Unhandled Rejection through
VitestBrowserClientMocker.resolveFactoryModule / Proxy.resolveManualMock, with
the playwright RouteHandler frame in the stack — byte-for-byte the original
report. Victims: wallow-auth twice, wallow-web once (e.g.
src/shared/components/auth-layout.theme.test.tsx, 
src/features/organizations/components/MemberList.error-state.test.tsx).

CHARACTERIZATION — the failure is LOUD, not silent. In every occurrence the
victim file is reported as "(0 test)" and the package exits non-zero: the mocker
rejection kills the whole file before any test executes. It does NOT fall
through to the real module. Corroborated from the other side: all 13
navigation-package stub files now assert "router stub applied" per test
(commit 12c28114), and that tripwire fired zero times in 25 runs, while the
navigation suite passed 17/17 files in all 25 runs including the 3 mocker runs.

CONSEQUENCE FOR THE UNIFICATION HYPOTHESIS with Wallow-x5da ("vi.mock fails
under load, stub absent, real anchor navigates"): now refuted by observation on
both ends — the observed mocker failure mode is a loud 0-test file death, not a
silent stub absence; and in the runs where the mocker DID fail, x5da did not
fire (nor did it fire in any of the other 22).

CAUSAL STORY (closing on it, per the plan's decision tree). Root cause:
module-delivery saturation under uncapped cross-package browser-mode
concurrency — the mocker resolves manual-mock factory modules over the same
Vite-dev-server-through-playwright-route transport that Wallow-pr34 showed
starving; when a factory fetch fails mid-resolution the mocker surfaces its
generic "top level variables" error, which is misleading (confirmed: the same
specs pass in isolation and at the cap). It co-occurred with the pr34 starvation
class in 2 of its 3 runs and appeared ONLY in saturated uncapped runs — 0
occurrences at --concurrency=1 across this project's entire capped history.
Mitigation is Wallow-pr34's --concurrency=1, which is the shipped supported
configuration. The loud failure mode means the residual CI risk originally
feared (a green run proving less than it should) does not exist: a run hit by
this fails visibly.

RESIDUAL RISKS documented for the record (filed separately as a follow-up bead):
(a) post-completion wedge — 6 of the 25 uncapped runs printed turbo's complete
final summary and then never exited (reaped by timeout at 600s); (b) a Vite dep
re-optimization landing mid-run (observed once, at concurrency=1, triggered by
an in-repo package edit invalidating the dep cache) kills browser suites with
the same iframe/fetch signatures — first run after a dependency-graph change is
the exposed one.

title: document the SDK's BFF env knobs; lint:env cannot see them
description:
packages/sdk/src/server/config.ts reads 8 env keys off an INJECTED env record, not process.env: COOKIE_PASSWORDS, COOKIE_NAME, COOKIE_SECURE, COOKIE_HOST_PREFIX, SESSION_TTL_SECONDS, OIDC_SCOPES, OIDC_METADATA_URL, BASE_URL.

None are interpolated by any docker/*.yml, so scripts/check-env.sh (pnpm lint:env) is structurally blind to them - it only walks compose ${VAR} references. None are in .env.production.example.

Doc state: COOKIE_NAME, SESSION_TTL_SECONDS and OIDC_SCOPES are in docs/integrations/typescript-sdk.md. COOKIE_PASSWORDS and COOKIE_SECURE appear ONLY in superseded plan docs, not on the docs site. COOKIE_HOST_PREFIX is documented nowhere.

These are security-relevant production knobs - COOKIE_PASSWORDS is the cookie-seal KEY ROTATION mechanism, and production compose wires only the singular COOKIE_PASSWORD, so rotation exists in code but is neither wired nor documented for a deployment.

Fix: document all eight (docs/getting-started/configuration.md and/or .env.production.example), and decide whether lint:env should grow a second pass over the SDK's env contract or whether the contract should be surfaced through compose so the existing check reaches it.
notes:
PARTIALLY ADDRESSED by Wallow-xzy1.5. COOKIE_PASSWORDS is now wired (wallow-web gets COOKIE_PASSWORDS: ${BFF_COOKIE_PASSWORDS:-}) and documented in three places: docker/.env.production.example (full rotation procedure), docs/operations/deployment.md section 4, docker/CLAUDE.md. So the security-relevant half of this bead - rotation exists in code but is neither wired nor documented - is closed.

STILL OPEN, and this is now the whole bead. Two of the eight are compose-owned and correctly absent from the example file: OIDC_METADATA_URL is pinned to http://wallow-api:8080/.well-known/openid-configuration (private DNS, not an operator knob) and BASE_URL is derived. The remaining FIVE are neither passed by any compose file nor documented as production knobs, so a deployment silently takes the SDK default: COOKIE_NAME, COOKIE_SECURE, COOKIE_HOST_PREFIX, SESSION_TTL_SECONDS, OIDC_SCOPES. COOKIE_SECURE and COOKIE_HOST_PREFIX are the security-relevant pair.

The structural half also stands: check-env.sh only walks compose ${VAR} references, so it is blind to any env key an app reads directly. Deciding between 'surface them through compose so the existing check reaches them' and 'grow a second pass over the SDK contract' is still this bead's call.
RESOLVED. All five remaining knobs are now wired and documented, and the structural question is decided.

Structural decision: SURFACE THROUGH COMPOSE, do not grow a second pass. docker-compose.production.yml's wallow-web service now passes COOKIE_SECURE, COOKIE_HOST_PREFIX, COOKIE_NAME, SESSION_TTL_SECONDS and OIDC_SCOPES as ${BFF_*:-}, which brings them into range of the check that already exists. A second pass would have to parse TypeScript to find which env keys an app reads, and would still not answer the question that matters (is this knob findable by a fork) - being named in compose is what makes it findable. Passing them unconditionally is safe because the SDK reads blank as unset for all five.

Documented in docker/.env.production.example (new 'the rest of the contract' section, all commented, with defaults and the fail-secure warning), docs/operations/deployment.md (optional-knobs table plus prose on the same-origin cookie collision and losing offline_access), and docker/CLAUDE.md.

DEFECT FOUND AND FIXED while wiring: packages/sdk/src/server/config.ts read COOKIE_NAME with `??`, so an empty value was taken verbatim and the session sealed under a cookie literally named ''. Every other optional key there already treated blank as unset. Proved with a probe (unset -> __Host-wallow_bff, '' -> '', '   ' -> '   '), fixed to trim-and-treat-empty-as-unset, spec added. Wiring the variable would have triggered this on every deployment that did not set the override.

Also fixed scripts/check-env.sh to skip full-line comments - this work's own compose comments tripped it on a variable named VAR in prose. Trailing comments on value lines are still scanned, since clipping from the first # could drop a real reference out of a quoted value. description:
Task 10. Plan (per-screen recipe in Phase 3): docs/plans/2026-08-03/1722-component-composition-implementation.md
MfaSettingsSection:184-217. Absorbs the status query, the disable/regenerate mutations, and all 5 useState (enrolling, confirmAction, password, error, regeneratedCodes).
notes:
Done (79cfd96e). apps/wallow-web/src/features/mfa/hooks/use-mfa-settings.ts + .test.tsx; MfaSettingsSection 331 -> 233 lines, all 39 existing mfa specs unchanged and green.

Hook owns: the status useQuery, the disable/regenerate useMutation pair with their shared status invalidation, and all 5 useState (enrolling, confirmAction, password, error, regeneratedCodes). Component now only picks a surface per state.

Design call: both failure surfaces are returned as READY-TO-RENDER TEXT, not as raw rejections. They speak different protocols — the status READ is RFC 7807 (errorText), the two WRITES are the MFA controllers' { succeeded:false, error } (problemDetail) — so a component handed both raw would have to know which is which. statusErrorText stays a separate field from error because a failed read is a BRANCH (must not claim MFA is off and invite a second enrolment), while a failed write is a banner.

TWO LINT FACTS worth knowing before the next hook extraction:
1. react/jsx-handler-names checks MEMBER EXPRESSIONS but not plain identifiers. onDone={mfa.endEnroll} warns; onDone={endEnroll} does not. So a hook returning callbacks must be DESTRUCTURED at the call site, or every callback has to be named handle*. Destructuring is the cheaper fix and both files here do it (the spec's Probe too).
2. eslint/no-shadow catches an inner onError(error) against an outer  state. Renamed the param to  — unicorn/catch-error-name only governs catch clauses, so this is free.
3. knip flags an exported type nothing imports: ConfirmAction is local (unexported) and referenced structurally by the exported MfaSettings interface.

Spec scope deliberately narrow — it drives the hook through a Probe component and covers only what the card cannot reach by clicking: the residue openConfirm clears (codes + error + password) and the inert submit with no panel open, which the card cannot even attempt since it renders no submit until a panel exists.

FOR Wallow-m5mb (9g, migrate onto forms):  is expected to leave this hook and become useAppForm state in the confirm panel. Absorbing it here was the plan's call so the card could go fully presentational in one step.

description:
Task 9f (350 lines). Plan (per-screen recipe in Phase 3): docs/plans/2026-08-03/1722-component-composition-implementation.md
Record the data-testid contract into this bead BEFORE changing anything — that list is the acceptance criterion.
notes:
data-testid contract (recorded BEFORE any edit; acceptance criterion):

  accept-terms-heading            — the card heading (Text as=h2)
  accept-terms-error              — the ErrorBanner, rendered only when ?error= is present
  accept-terms-checkbox           — Checkbox.Root for Terms of Service
  accept-terms-privacy-checkbox   — Checkbox.Root for Privacy Policy
  accept-terms-submit             — the Create Account button

No e2e spec drives this screen by testid: apps/wallow-auth/e2e/routes.spec.ts only smoke-loads
'/accept-terms'. The whole contract is exercised by AcceptTermsScreen.test.tsx (617 lines).
Done (6a6d4591). AcceptTermsScreen 350 -> ~200 lines across two files, 35 specs unchanged and green.

Shape: AcceptTermsScreen renders <AuthScreen> + <SigningUpAs> + <ConsentGate>. ConsentGate holds useAppForm and IS rooted at <AppForm> — that split is mandatory, not stylistic: react/jsx-max-depth is 2 under --deny-warnings and it counts through render-prop children, so AuthScreen > AppForm > AppField > CheckboxField warns. Same reason RegisterFields exists.

NO api.ts for this feature. The screen issues no request: the user's identity is in the HttpOnly ExternalLoginState cookie, and consent finishes with a full navigation (globalThis.location.href) to /v1/identity/auth/complete-external-registration. So it uses useAppForm's plain-onSubmit escape hatch and the schema is deliberately rule-free — revalidateLogic aborts handleSubmit on any zod failure, and this screen gates on a DISABLED submit, with no field messages and no banner to report a rejection in.

Non-React layer split to accept-terms-handoff.ts: bounceBackMessage (ReadonlyMap, not Record — ?error=toString) and completeRegistrationUrl, carrying the 'no isSafeReturnUrl guard' adjudication verbatim.

Three additions outside the feature:
- packages/ui CardHeader.titleTestId — puts the id on the <h2>, not the wrapper. Every wallow-auth {screen}-heading contract names the heading ELEMENT; the wrapper also holds the description, so a text assertion there would pass on copy the heading lacks. Serves the ~10 screens still to migrate.
- apps/wallow-auth AuthScreen.headingTestId — forwards it, for the same reason errorTestId is a prop.
- packages/forms SubmitButton.disabled — OR'd with pending, never replacing it, so a caller's gate can't re-enable a form mid-request.

BEHAVIOUR CHANGE, deliberate: @shared/components/consent-labels de-duplicates the ToS/Privacy labels (zone-dag forbids accept-terms importing register) and adds target=_blank + rel=noopener to both. RegisterForm previously navigated away; reading a policy must not discard a half-typed signup. Specs already asserted target=_blank on the gate's links.

Cosmetic drift: AppForm's gap is space-y-4 where the hand-rolled form used space-y-6.

SettingsMfaSection the header names is gone with the deleted xUnit suite, so
the specs are the only holder.

  settings-mfa-loading           MutedText, status read pending
  settings-mfa-status            Badge, "Enabled" / "Disabled"
  settings-mfa-status-error      ErrorBanner, status READ failed with nothing cached
  settings-mfa-enable            Button, disabled state only
  settings-mfa-backup-count      Text, enabled state only
  settings-mfa-disable           Button, enabled state only
  settings-mfa-regenerate        Button, enabled state only
  settings-mfa-confirm-password  the password Input in the shared confirm panel
  settings-mfa-confirm-submit    the confirm panel's Confirm button
  settings-mfa-regenerated-codes the <ul>, one <li> per code
  settings-mfa-error             ErrorBanner, disable/regenerate failure

Non-testid contract the specs also pin:
  - card title text "Multi-Factor Authentication"
  - field captions "Status" and "Backup Codes Remaining"
  - label "Password" on the confirm control
  - loading copy "Loading MFA status..."
  - codes-reveal copy "New backup codes - save these somewhere safe. They will
    not be shown again."
  - the enable button enters the inline MfaEnrollFlow (mfa-enroll-begin-setup)
  - a successful write sweeps the status OPERATION (expectSwept)

Note the two derivations that make this a clean migration: with
testIdPrefix="settings-mfa-confirm", the forms layer DERIVES
settings-mfa-confirm-submit (SubmitButton) and settings-mfa-confirm-password
(field name "password") with no testId override needed on either.

Done (bab9432b). Every id in the contract above survives; all 39 pre-existing
mfa specs pass untouched, plus 2 new ones. MfaSettingsSection 331 -> 251 lines
(a further -80 on top of the -98 from Wallow-2247), and the hand-rolled
Field/Label/Input/Button block is gone.

The migration is unusually clean because BOTH ids derive. testIdPrefix
"settings-mfa-confirm" + field name "password" gives
settings-mfa-confirm-password; SubmitButton gives settings-mfa-confirm-submit.
No testId override on either. Worth checking for this before hand-pinning ids
on the remaining screens.

Escape hatch, not a mutation: the write belongs to useMfaSettings, which drives
both actions off one confirmAction and owns the card's settings-mfa-error
banner. So the panel passes plain onSubmit and hands the password back.

submitConfirm changed shape twice over: it takes the password (the form owns it
now) and it SETTLES instead of returning immediately, which is what gives
SubmitButton a real pending state. It resolves either way rather than
rejecting -- mutateAsync would reject, and a rejection reaching the form raises
a SECOND banner restating a failure the card is already showing. The helper is
a small `settled(run)` wrapper over mutate's onSettled.

TWO BEHAVIOUR CHANGES, each with a new spec in MfaSettingsSection.test.tsx:
1. An empty password is refused with "Enter your password to continue." on
   settings-mfa-confirm-password-error instead of being POSTed blank. This is
   the point of the migration -- validation the hand-rolled panel had none of.
2. The panel is keyed by confirmAction, so switching disable <-> regenerate
   mounts a fresh empty form. Before, the password state lived above the panel
   and openConfirm cleared it explicitly; the key replaces that clearing, and
   the spec pins it because the mechanism changed.

Also: the hook no longer holds password/setPassword, which is what
Wallow-2247's closing note predicted.

Two decisions worth carrying to the remaining screens:

1. PLAIN-onSubmit ESCAPE HATCH, not the mutation option. The endpoint answers a bare { succeeded, error } body (not RFC 7807), so splitServerError has nothing to read, and useAppForm exposes no onError to hang registerFailureMessage on. The generated accountRegisterMutation is still used — via useMutation + mutateAsync inside the callback — so the generated-factory rule holds.

2. THE SCHEMA IS RULE-FREE. revalidateLogic aborts handleSubmit on any zod failure, which would preempt the five oracle-ordered guards sharing one register-error banner (5 unit tests + e2e/signup.spec.ts:51 assert it). Guards therefore live in registerGuardMessage, ordered, returning one message.

Forms-package change: CatalogFieldLabelProps.label and CheckboxFieldProps.label widened string -> ReactNode, so a consent box keeps its policy link INSIDE the label (the label is the box's accessible name — getByRole('checkbox', { name: 'I agree to the Terms of Service' })).

Gotcha: react/jsx-max-depth counts attribute JSX as one level deeper than the element carrying it, so <ConsentLabel/> inline in label={} under AppField > CheckboxField is depth 3. Hoisted to module constants.

Footer deliberately NOT on QuietLink (plan step 4): QuietLink is the muted standalone link; this footer is an accent CTA inside muted prose.

title: turbo's ^build rationale cites a dist/ exports map that no longer exists
description:
`turbo.jsonc` justifies `dependsOn: ["^build"]` on `typecheck`, `test` and `dev` with two claims that are false in-repo, and `CLAUDE.md` (the 'Turbo owns build, typecheck, test and dev' paragraph) restates one of them:

- turbo.jsonc, above `typecheck`: 'every member resolves @bc-solutions-coder/* through an exports map pointing at dist/, so a dependency must be BUILT before a dependent can typecheck'
- turbo.jsonc, above `dev`: 'an app resolves its workspace dependencies through dist/, so `pnpm dev` on a fresh clone dies with UNRESOLVED_IMPORT'
- CLAUDE.md: 'All four declare `dependsOn: ["^build"]`, because every member resolves @bc-solutions-coder/* through an exports map pointing at dist/.'

Since 584adc3b every workspace package's `exports` map resolves to `src/`; `dist/` appears only in `publishConfig.exports`, applied by pnpm at pack time. Verified with `tsc --traceResolution` from apps/wallow-web: '@bc-solutions-coder/sdk' resolves to packages/sdk/src/index.ts, with every package's dist/ present on disk.

Same root cause as Wallow-l77c, which fixed the five prose sites in CLAUDE.md/apps/CLAUDE.md/packages/sdk/CLAUDE.md/apps/wallow-web/README.md (plus three the bead had not found, in docs/development/frontend-setup.md, packages/auth/CLAUDE.md and a second wallow-web README block). This one is separate because it is not just prose: the false rationale may be the only thing holding `^build` on typecheck/test/dev, so the fix needs a decision, not a reword.

Two things to settle:
1. Is `^build` still warranted on typecheck/test/dev? The remaining true reason turbo.jsonc gives is hash folding — '^build folds the dependency's source into this task's hash, which is what stops a stale pass being replayed.' Confirm that holds (and that `inputs` alone would not), because if it does the dependency stays and only the comment changes.
2. If it does not hold, dropping `^build` from typecheck/test/dev (and dev especially) removes a build from every warm run. `build` itself keeps `^build` regardless — that one is genuinely topological.

Do NOT reword the comments without answering (1); a rationale that is merely plausible is how this got stale.
acceptance_criteria: turbo.jsonc's comments and CLAUDE.md's turbo paragraph state a rationale that is true of the repo as it stands, verified against the exports maps rather than assumed. If ^build is kept on typecheck/test/dev, the comment names the real reason (hash folding) and says so without claiming dist/ resolution. If it is dropped, pnpm check still passes cold on a fresh clone with no dist/ present.
notes:
Resolved by measurement, not reasoning. Both claims tested directly.

Q1 — is ^build still warranted on typecheck/test? YES, and the hash-folding rationale turbo.jsonc already gave is the correct one. Removed dependsOn from typecheck, populated the cache, appended a line to packages/sdk/src/index.ts, re-ran turbo run typecheck --filter=wallow-web: 12/12 cached, FULL TURBO, stale result replayed. Restored it and repeated the same mutation: 5/12 cached, the app re-checks. So ^build is what makes a packages/*/src edit invalidate a dependent. Kept.

Q2 — dev. Dropped. It is cache: false, so there is no hash to protect, and its stated reason (an app resolves workspace deps through dist/, so pnpm dev on a fresh clone dies with UNRESOLVED_IMPORT) is false. Moved all 11 packages/*/dist off disk and ran each app's dev script directly, bypassing turbo: minimal-app served HTTP 200 in 3s; wallow-web booted and returned its own 500 for missing OIDC env, thrown from packages/sdk/src/server/config.ts — i.e. executing SDK source with no dist anywhere. Zero 'failed to resolve' in either log. All dist restored afterwards; tree clean.

Worth recording: the original design doc (docs/plans/2026-08-03/1206-turborepo-adoption-design.md) already had dev as { cache: false, persistent: true } with no ^build, and already named the hash-folding reason as ^build's 'second job'. The dist/-resolution justification and dev's dependency were both added at implementation time. The design was right; the implementation comment was not.

Also checked packages/styles' ./styles.css and packages/ui's ./source.css, since those exports point outside src/ — both are git-tracked committed files, not build outputs, so nothing at dev time needs a dist either.

Three live sites fixed in e3082fcd: turbo.jsonc (both comments + dev's dependsOn), CLAUDE.md's turbo paragraph, and .github/workflows/js.yml's 'One task graph, not three phases' comment, which restated the same false premise. Plans under docs/plans/ left as-is — historical artifacts.

pnpm check exits 0. Verified after the edit that the invalidation guarantee still holds (warm FULL TURBO, then 5/12 on an sdk source edit).

title: deploy the self-hosted turbo remote cache (turborepo phase 3)
description:
Turborepo is adopted and working locally and in CI (see `docs/plans/2026-08-03/1206-turborepo-implementation.md`, Phases 1-2, all committed). Caching is **local only**: `.turbo/` on a laptop, `actions/cache` per-branch in CI. This bead is the deferred Phase 3 — a self-hosted remote cache so a laptop build and a CI run share artifacts.

Nothing here is blocking. The local benefits are already banked: warm `pnpm check` is ~13 s against a ~64 s baseline, with the whole 45-task build/typecheck/test graph collapsing to ~0.4 s.

## What already exists in the repo

- `docker/turbo-cache/docker-compose.yml` — `ducktors/turborepo-remote-cache` + a `cloudflared` tunnel sidecar. Validated with `docker compose config`; never deployed.
- `docker/turbo-cache/.env.example` — the three values to fill in.

## What is NOT in the repo, deliberately

The `remoteCache` block in `turbo.jsonc` and the `TURBO_*` job env in `.github/workflows/js.yml` were written, verified, then **backed out** rather than left carrying a `<your-zone>` placeholder. Both blocks are in the plan (Tasks 10 and 11) ready to paste back. Verified while they were in place:

- The `remoteCache` block is **inert without `TURBO_TOKEN`** — a full workspace build against an unresolvable host was FULL TURBO with no warning. Safe to land before the server is up.
- `futureFlags.longerSignatureKey` does **not** change the task hash. The plan claims enabling it forces a full miss everywhere; it does not, so turning it on costs no rebuild.

## Work

1. **Generate secrets** (plan Task 7). Two `openssl rand -hex 32` values: `TURBO_TOKEN` and `TURBO_REMOTE_CACHE_SIGNATURE_KEY`. Password manager, GitHub Actions secrets, server `.env`, and your shell. Never committed.
2. **Stand up the cache server** (Task 8 steps 3-4). `.env` from the example, `docker compose up -d turbo-cache`, smoke-test `/v8/artifacts/status` for `{"status":"enabled"}`. Then pin `:latest` to the digest actually pulled — both images.
3. **Publish via Cloudflare Tunnel** (Task 9). Zero Trust -> Networks -> Tunnels, public hostname -> `turbo-cache:3000`. Verify from off-LAN that an authenticated request returns `enabled` **and an unauthenticated one returns 401** — a 200 there means the token never reached the container and the cache is open to the internet; tear the hostname down before continuing.
4. **WAF rule** (Task 9 step 5). turbo sends only `Authorization: Bearer`, so Cloudflare Access service tokens cannot be layered on — the token is the only credential. Restrict by `ip.src` to the GitHub Actions egress ranges (`https://api.github.com/meta`) plus your own network. Those ranges drift; note that in the rule description.
5. **Re-add the `turbo.jsonc` block** (Task 10) with the real hostname in `apiUrl` (bare origin — turbo appends `/v8/artifacts/...`). Prove upload and download: build, `rm -rf .turbo packages/*/dist`, build again, and confirm hits with no local cache present.
6. **Re-add the CI job env** (Task 11) — `TURBO_TOKEN`, `TURBO_TEAM` (`team_wallow`), `TURBO_REMOTE_CACHE_SIGNATURE_KEY`. Fork PRs get no secrets and will run uncached; that is correct, and **not** a reason to switch to `pull_request_target`.
7. **Delete the `actions/cache` step** from `js.yml` — but only after a CI run is observed hitting the remote cache. Keeping both uploads the same artifacts twice.
8. **Document it** (plan Task 12 step 2) in `docs/getting-started/developer-guide.md`: the three env vars, where to get them, and the escape hatches when the cache misbehaves (`turbo run <task> --force`; verify the exact env opt-out name against turbo's docs, and prefer documenting `"remoteCache": { "enabled": false }` if there is no clean override). Read `docs/CLAUDE.md` first.
9. **Mark the two plan docs `completed`** — `1206-turborepo-implementation.md` and `1206-turborepo-adoption-design.md`.

## Watch for

- **Hash divergence between laptop and CI** is almost always an environment variable. `turbo.jsonc` deliberately excludes `CI` from `globalEnv` for exactly this reason. If cross-machine hits do not happen, diff `NODE_ENV` and the declared `globalEnv` between the two before suspecting anything else.
- **Cache eviction.** `ducktors/turborepo-remote-cache` has no GC. Once growth is known, add a server cron (`find /cache -type f -atime +30 -delete`) or call its `POST /clean`. Turbo's `cacheMaxAge`/`cacheMaxSize` govern only the local `.turbo`, not the server.
acceptance_criteria: A CI run shows turbo cache hits for packages built only on a laptop (and vice versa). An unauthenticated request to the public hostname returns 401. The actions/cache step is gone from js.yml. developer-guide.md documents the three env vars and the bypass. Both turborepo plan docs read status: completed.
notes:
CI/config wiring landed (2026-08-28); bead stays open because the Pangolin side + observed cross-machine hit remain. Findings:

1. TURBO_CUSTOM_HEADERS does NOT exist. turbo (2.10.8 and current docs, options + system-env-variables references checked) can attach NO custom headers and no query params to remote-cache requests — it sends only 'Authorization: Bearer $TURBO_TOKEN' and builds the /v8/artifacts URL itself. So the Pangolin access-token bypass (P-Access-Token / P-Access-Token-Id headers, or the p_token query param) is unusable by turbo. The repo secrets P_ACCESS_TOKEN / P_ACCESS_TOKEN_ID are therefore unused; they can be deleted or kept for other tooling.
2. The working design (same shape as the original Cloudflare plan): on the Pangolin resource for the cache server, add an ALLOW rule so matching requests bypass Pangolin auth entirely (Rules tab, or a resource policy). Path rules match segment-by-segment, so the pattern is 'v8/artifacts/*' (covers GET/PUT artifacts, POST events, GET status). Optionally rank CIDR allow rules for known egress IPs above it. The ducktors server's own TURBO_TOKEN bearer check remains the credential — after adding the rule, verify a request WITHOUT the bearer token gets 401 from the server, not a Pangolin login page.
3. Wired in-repo: js.yml build-job env reads TURBO_API/TURBO_TEAM/TURBO_TOKEN from Actions secrets (all three exist as SECRETS, not variables — 'vars.TURBO_API' would resolve empty; confirmed via gh secret list). turbo.jsonc gained a remoteCache block with timeout 60/uploadTimeout 120 and deliberately NO apiUrl — the hostname stays out of the repo and arrives via TURBO_API env. developer-guide.md documents the three vars + escape hatches; root CLAUDE.md caching sentence updated.
4. No TURBO_REMOTE_CACHE_SIGNATURE_KEY secret exists, so artifact signing stays off. Optional follow-up: openssl rand -hex 32, set it on server-side env + Actions secret + laptop, then add signature:true + futureFlags.longerSignatureKey (hash-neutral, verified earlier).
5. Verified locally: with the three vars unset the build is FULL TURBO local-only; with an unreachable TURBO_API turbo warns ('Remote caching unavailable') and the run stays green — CI cannot go red from this landing before the Pangolin rule exists.

Remaining to close: add the Pangolin allow rule; export the three vars locally and prove upload/download (build, wipe .turbo + dist, build again, hits with no local cache); observe a CI run with remote hits; THEN delete the actions/cache step from js.yml; mark both turborepo plan docs completed.
2026-08-28 evening, after Pangolin SSO was turned off on the resource: CI remote cache PROVEN working, with one server-side issue outstanding.

Evidence (run 33192456138, three attempts at the same SHA, gh-cache turbo-* entries deleted between attempts so no local cache existed):
- Attempt 2: 'Remote caching enabled', 0/30 cached (expected: server was empty because attempt 1 hit local cache everywhere and turbo only uploads artifacts for tasks it executes), all 30 executed and uploaded.
- Attempt 3: 'Remote caching enabled', 18/30 build/typecheck tasks served FROM THE REMOTE with no local cache present. Roundtrip proven.

Outstanding issue: in BOTH attempts 2 and 3 the second turbo invocation of the run (the Test step, ~20s after the build step finishes) failed with 'Remote caching unavailable (Could not connect)' while the build step connected fine — and only 18 of the 30 uploads from attempt 2 landed. Pattern: heavy request burst from the build step (30 tasks worth of downloads/uploads), then connection-level refusal. Attempt 1 (all-local hits, nearly zero cache traffic) had BOTH steps connect. Best hypothesis: an IP-level ban/rate-limit in front of the cache server — if the Pangolin stack runs CrowdSec (the installer's default offer), its http flood/crawl scenarios would ban the runner IP mid-run at the firewall level, which matches 'could not connect' (TCP drop) rather than an HTTP error. Check on the server: cscli decisions list (expect a GitHub runner IP), plus docker compose logs turbo-cache to see whether the app ever received the failing requests. Fix: whitelist the cache hostname/path in CrowdSec or raise the rate limit for the resource. NEVER fatal either way — turbo degrades to executing tasks.

Deliberately NOT yet done, pending stable connectivity: deleting the actions/cache step from js.yml (it is now the fallback that keeps flaky-remote runs fast), marking the two plan docs completed, closing this bead. Unauthenticated-401 check: user reports the resource now requires just the bearer token; still worth one explicit curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' $TURBO_API/v8/artifacts/status with no Authorization header — expect 401, and with the bearer expect 200 {"status":"enabled"}.
Design change (2026-08-28, commit f0183cd8): CI now reaches the cache over Tailscale instead of the public Pangolin URL — the runner joins the tailnet as a tag:ci ephemeral node (tailscale/github-action@v4), which removes the CrowdSec/rate-limit failure mode entirely and lets the public resource for the cache be deleted. Both new steps (Tailscale join + a non-fatal tailscale-ping wait for the cache host) gate on TS_OAUTH_CLIENT_ID being non-empty, so fork PRs skip them and stay uncached-but-green.

User-side setup still required before this is live:
1. Tailscale admin console → ACLs: define tag:ci (tagOwners), and allow tag:ci to reach the cache host on the cache port.
2. Create an OAuth client with the auth_keys scope, tags tag:ci; store as Actions secrets TS_OAUTH_CLIENT_ID and TS_OAUTH_SECRET.
3. Ensure the cache host is on the tailnet with the container port published on it, then UPDATE the TURBO_API secret to the tailnet address (http://<host>.<tailnet>.ts.net:PORT or http://100.x.y.z:PORT — plain http is fine, WireGuard encrypts the path) and export the same value on the laptop (must be on the tailnet).
4. Optionally delete the Pangolin public resource for the cache; P_ACCESS_TOKEN/P_ACCESS_TOKEN_ID secrets remain unused either way.

Then: re-run js.yml twice with the gh turbo-* cache entries deleted between runs to confirm stable remote hits in BOTH turbo invocations (the public route consistently dropped the second one), delete the actions/cache step, mark both plan docs completed, close. Follow-up worth filing separately: docker/turbo-cache/docker-compose.yml still ships the cloudflared sidecar from the original plan — replace or drop it now that the tailnet is the access path.
CLOSED VERIFIED. Root causes of the two final failures: (1) TURBO_API secret had a trailing slash, so every turbo path hit the server as //v8/... and Fastify 404d it — turbo reports a non-2xx /v8/artifacts/status as 'Could not connect', which is misleading; (2) the deployment then moved to host port 3000. Final value: http://100.66.144.9:3000 (no trailing slash — that is load-bearing). Proof (run 33198229090, final two attempts): with gh turbo-* caches wiped, first run executed and uploaded all 30 build/typecheck artifacts and pulled 11/26 test tasks from the remote; second wiped run came back FULL TURBO in both invocations (30/30 in 2.1s, 26/26 in 1.1s) with 'Cache not found' from actions/cache — remote-only. actions/cache fallback deleted and both plan docs marked completed in commit f02b859b. Follow-up filed: Wallow-vvi0 (cloudflared sidecar in docker/turbo-cache is dead design). Optional hardening still open: TURBO_REMOTE_CACHE_SIGNATURE_KEY + signature:true.

title: Enable root-level wallow/* oxlint registration (documented blocker does not reproduce)
description: packages/lint/CLAUDE.md and docs/plans/2026-08-02/1744-no-source-tests-design.md both claim jsPlugins (and therefore the wallow/* rules) cannot move from the five nested oxlint configs (apps/wallow-web, apps/wallow-auth, packages/ui, packages/forms, packages/navigation) to the root .oxlintrc.json, because packages/sdk/src/oxlint-guardrails.test.ts copies the root config to a temp directory and any jsPlugins entry allegedly makes that copy unloadable (0 tests run, silently). Investigation (this bead's design notes) reproduced the guardrail spec's exact mechanics standalone against the currently installed oxlint 1.74.0 / pnpm 10.20.0 and found the claimed failure does NOT occur through the invocation path the spec (and pnpm lint) actually use — pnpm's node_modules/.bin/oxlint shim sets NODE_PATH to the workspace virtual store, which resolves the plugin regardless of the config's temp location. Priority: this blocks a real repo improvement (five wallow/* rules — no-sidebar-inversion, no-source-tests, no-tinted-text, zone-dag, no-hand-rolled-mutation, text-heading-variant — currently reach only 5 of 16+ lintable packages/apps; six packages with real .tsx/.test.ts content sit outside their reach today) on a documented constraint that is stale. Fixing it is a small, well-scoped config change (see design), not exploratory.
design:
## The documented blocker: NOT REAL under the current toolchain

`packages/lint/CLAUDE.md` and `docs/plans/2026-08-02/1744-no-source-tests-design.md` both claim
root `jsPlugins` registration is impossible because `packages/sdk/src/oxlint-guardrails.test.ts`
copies the root config to a temp directory and any `jsPlugins` entry makes that copy unloadable
("Failed to parse oxlint configuration file", 0 tests run). Measured against the currently
installed oxlint 1.74.0 / pnpm 10.20.0, **this does not reproduce**.

### Mechanism found

Only ONE half of the guardrail spec copies the config: `lintMirrorTree()` does
`copyFileSync(oxlintConfigPath, join(mirrorRoot, ".oxlintrc.json"))` into a `mkdtemp` dir with no
`node_modules` anywhere in its ancestry. The other half, `restrictedImportDiagnostics()`, never
copies anything — it runs `-c <repoRoot>/.oxlintrc.json` against a scratch **source file** only,
so it was never at risk regardless of `jsPlugins`.

I reproduced `lintMirrorTree`'s exact mechanics standalone: wrote a copy of the real root config
with `"jsPlugins": [{ "name": "wallow", "specifier": "@bc-solutions-coder/lint" }]` added, placed
it at `<mkdtemp>/.oxlintrc.json` (a directory outside the repo entirely, no local `node_modules`),
and ran it via the exact binary path the spec uses:
`resolve(repoRoot, "node_modules", ".bin", "oxlint")`, with `cwd` at the tmp dir. **It succeeded
(exit 0) and the plugin's rules fired correctly** — confirmed by adding
`"wallow/no-source-tests": "error"` and a fixture importing `node:fs`, which correctly drew the
diagnostic even from the tmp dir.

### Why the CLAUDE.md's model is wrong

`packages/lint/CLAUDE.md` states "a `jsPlugins` specifier resolves from the config file's own
directory". That's not what determines success here. `node_modules/.bin/oxlint` is pnpm's
standard shim (`#!/bin/sh`), and it unconditionally exports:

```
NODE_PATH=".../node_modules/.pnpm/oxlint@1.74.0/node_modules/oxlint/bin/node_modules:.../oxlint/node_modules:.../oxlint@1.74.0/node_modules:.../node_modules/.pnpm/node_modules"
```

before `exec`-ing the real binary. That last path — the pnpm virtual store's `node_modules` — is
where `@bc-solutions-coder/lint` (and every other workspace package) is reachable via hard link,
**regardless of the invoking process's cwd or the config file's own directory**. I isolated this:

- Invoking the **raw** Rust/JS binary directly (`node_modules/.pnpm/oxlint@1.74.0/.../bin/oxlint`,
  bypassing the pnpm shim) with `NODE_PATH` stripped reproduces the DOCUMENTED failure exactly:
  `Failed to parse oxlint configuration file. / x Failed to load JS plugin: @bc-solutions-coder/lint
  / | Cannot find module '@bc-solutions-coder/lint'`. So the failure mode is real **in principle**
  — just not through the invocation path the spec (or `pnpm lint`/`pnpm lint:tests`) actually uses.
- Confirmed Node's own ESM `import()` does NOT honor `NODE_PATH` (isolated repro, Node 24.11.1) —
  so oxlint's plugin loader is doing its own NODE_PATH-aware resolution, not falling through to
  bare `import()`. (I could not consult oxlint's official docs to name this mechanism — the
  `ref-context` MCP tools specified in my task were not present in my toolset this session; this
  finding rests entirely on my own reproductions, not documentation.)

Net: **the guardrail spec's `lintMirrorTree` half would keep working if `jsPlugins` moved to
root**, because it's invoked via the same `node_modules/.bin/oxlint` shim that already makes
`pnpm lint` and the five nested configs work today. The blocker as written ("both root placements
were tried and both fail this way … measured on oxlint 1.74.0") does not match what oxlint 1.74.0
actually does when invoked the way this repo invokes it. Either the original measurement used a
different invocation (e.g. the raw binary, or an oxlint version whose plugin loader didn't consult
NODE_PATH), or pnpm's shim generation changed since — I can't tell which from here, only that
it's currently false.

### Failure mode, if it WERE real: loud, not silent

Even in the raw-binary repro that DOES fail, failure is a hard parse error on stdout/stderr with a
named module and a non-JSON-shaped payload preceding the JSON block — `JSON.parse` throwing during
top-level module evaluation (the `lintMirrorTree()` call sits at module scope, line ~518, before
any `describe`/`it`) fails the entire test FILE's collection in vitest, not just the mirror-tree
tests, and produces a visible collection error naming the file, not a quiet 0/0 pass. "0 tests run"
undersold how loud it actually is; a fresh contributor would see a top-level vitest collection
error, not a green run.

## What root registration would newly reach

`pnpm lint`'s roots are `apps packages`. Packages with NO existing nested `.oxlintrc.json` (so
currently get `wallow/*` rules not-at-all, vacuously) that a root-level jsPlugins/rules
registration would newly reach: `apps/examples/minimal-app`, `packages/auth`, `packages/config`,
`packages/env`, `packages/lint`, `packages/logger`, `packages/query`, `packages/sdk`,
`packages/styles`, `packages/testing`, `packages/utils`.

Simulated (single small oxlint invocations against real files, config copied to scratch, never
touching the tracked `.oxlintrc.json`, never running `pnpm test`/`pnpm check`):

- **`wallow/no-source-tests`** (bans `node:fs` in `*.test.*`) fires on exactly the **7** specs the
  no-source-tests plan already names as deliberately kept and outside the plugin's reach:
  `packages/lint/src/fixtures.test.ts`, `packages/styles/src/assets.test.ts`,
  `packages/styles/src/theme-css.test.ts`, `packages/sdk/src/openapi-regen.test.ts`,
  `packages/sdk/src/generated-query-surface.test.ts`, `packages/sdk/src/oxlint-guardrails.test.ts`,
  `packages/query/src/index.test.ts`. `grep -rln 'from "node:fs"' --include="*.test.ts" apps
  packages` confirms these are the only 7 (an 8th, `packages/lint/fixtures/no-source-tests/invalid.test.ts`,
  is already covered by the root `ignorePatterns` entry `packages/lint/fixtures/**`). This is a
  small, enumerable, already-documented set — not a flood. Fix is 7 `"wallow/no-source-tests":
  "off"` file-scoped overrides at root (or one glob list), mirroring the existing
  `no-restricted-imports` exemption pattern already in this same config.
- **The other five rules** (`no-sidebar-inversion`, `no-tinted-text`, `text-heading-variant`,
  `zone-dag`, `no-hand-rolled-mutation`) produced **zero** diagnostics against every `.tsx` file
  that exists in the newly-reached packages (checked individually, not batched, to rule out a CLI
  quirk): `apps/examples/minimal-app/src/{router,routes/index,routes/__root}.tsx`,
  `.../components/ready-indicator.tsx`, `.../features/hello/HelloCard.tsx`,
  `packages/testing/src/{render-with-wallow,theme-wiring,render}.tsx`. (`packages/logger` has one
  `.tsx`, but it's `logger.test.tsx`, a spec, not a render file, and drew nothing.) A prior grep for
  `bg-foreground|text-primary|<h1|<h2|<h3|useMutation|variant=` across those same files found no
  matches either.
- **`zone-dag`** derives its zones from a `tsconfig.json` `paths` map; none of the newly-reached
  packages declare one (checked `apps/examples/minimal-app`, `packages/testing`, `packages/lint`,
  `packages/sdk`, `packages/query`), so it stays inert there exactly as `packages/lint/CLAUDE.md`
  already describes for the three packages that carry it today.

So root registration is NOT a multi-day cleanup. It is a config change plus 7 known,
already-named exemptions.

## `extends` and the five nested configs

Tested separately: a nested config that `extends` a root config carrying `jsPlugins` inherits the
plugin and its rules WITHOUT redeclaring its own `jsPlugins` entry (repro: nested config with only
`{"extends": ["../.oxlintrc.json"]}`, root-sim with `jsPlugins` + `wallow/no-source-tests: error`,
`wallow(no-source-tests)` still fired on a violating file linted from the nested directory). So once
root registers the plugin, the five nested configs' own `jsPlugins` lines become redundant and can
be deleted — they would keep existing only for what they *actually* need per-tree: their own
`wallow/*` rule **selection** (the "who enables what" table — wallow-web enables 4 of 6, the three
packages enable all 6), their scoped exemptions (drawer, `use-app-form.ts`), and the unrelated
"cost of nesting" restatement of app override globs/`ignorePatterns` (relative-glob semantics,
orthogonal to `jsPlugins`). `packages/sdk/src/oxlint-guardrails.test.ts`'s own
"every nested oxlint config inherits the root" checks (`extends` present, no `categories`/`plugins`
redeclared) only inspect `plugins`/`categories`, never `jsPlugins`, so dropping the redundant
`jsPlugins` line from the five nested configs would not trip any existing assertion.

## Fix options evaluated

- **(a) Strip/rewrite `jsPlugins` in the guardrail spec's copy.** Not needed — measurements show
  the copy already loads fine. Could still be added as defense-in-depth against a future pnpm/oxlint
  change, but it's not required to unblock root registration.
- **(b) Symlink `node_modules` into the mirror tmp dir, or use an absolute plugin path at root.**
  Not needed for the same reason as (a) — NODE_PATH resolution via the `.bin/oxlint` shim already
  reaches the workspace regardless of the tmp dir's contents.
- **(c) Point the spec at a purpose-built fixture config instead of the real root config.**
  Recommend AGAINST. This is the one guardrail standing between the repo and a silently inert
  plugin (the `Wallow-mlc3` precedent the plan itself cites) — swapping in a fixture config would
  let the REAL root config drift from what's tested, reopening exactly that failure mode. Costs
  guardrail power for no benefit now that (a)/(b) are shown unnecessary.
- **(d) Root registration with per-tree overrides, recommended.** Move `jsPlugins` + the six
  `wallow/*` rule entries to the root `.oxlintrc.json` (root enables the union — all six — since
  root has no single "who gets what" story the way a nested config's own file does; per-tree
  narrowing, where a tree wants fewer than all six, moves to root `overrides[]` blocks keyed by
  `apps/wallow-web/**` etc., same shape the root config already uses for `unicorn/filename-case`).
  Add the 7 `"wallow/no-source-tests": "off"` file overrides named above. Drop the now-redundant
  `jsPlugins` line from the five nested configs (keep the configs themselves for their scoped
  exemptions and the unrelated glob-restatement need). This is the smallest change that doesn't
  weaken `oxlint-guardrails.test.ts`.

## Recommendation

Advisable. The documented blocker does not reproduce against the toolchain actually in place
(oxlint 1.74.0, pnpm 10.20.0), and root registration's actual blast radius is 7 already-known,
already-exempted specs plus zero observed JSX-rule fallout in the newly-reached packages. Smallest
safe path is option (d): move `jsPlugins` + all six `wallow/*` rules to root with per-tree
`overrides[]` narrowing where a tree wants fewer than six, add the 7 `no-source-tests` exemptions,
and drop the redundant `jsPlugins` line from the five nested configs. `packages/lint/CLAUDE.md`
and the no-source-tests plan's "Accept the holes" section both need rewriting once this lands —
their current text asserts the move is impossible, which this investigation found to be false as
measured today.

One open risk worth flagging rather than resolving here: the mechanism that makes this safe (pnpm's
`.bin` shim setting `NODE_PATH` to the virtual store) is an implementation detail of the invoking
shim, not a documented oxlint contract I could confirm against oxlint's own docs (the `ref-context`
MCP tools named in my task brief were unavailable in this session). If pnpm ever changes how it
generates `.bin` shims, or CI invokes oxlint through a different path than
`node_modules/.bin/oxlint`, this could regress silently back to the documented failure. Whoever
implements this should re-run the `lintMirrorTree` reproduction above as part of the same PR, and
ideally pin an assertion that `oxlintBinPath` is invoked exactly as the working repro does (or
add option (a)'s defensive strip, cheaply, even though it wasn't needed to reproduce success).
