title: app-shell.toggle.test.tsx still leaks a real navigation ~2/15 full-workspace runs despite the Wallow-tkyq guard
description:
packages/navigation/src/app-shell.toggle.test.tsx > "collapses it again when the toggle is activated twice" still triggers a real navigation escape under full-workspace runs, after the Wallow-tkyq central Navigation-API guard (installNavigationEscapeGuard + afterEach(assertNoNavigationEscape) in packages/navigation/vitest.setup.ts) shipped and closed.

MEASUREMENT (from Wallow-uhef's closing note, which ran 15 full-workspace pnpm -r test runs while investigating a different bead): 2 of 15 full-workspace runs failed on exactly this test, both times failing fast (~159-161ms, not a timeout). Both failures were the SAME test in the SAME file, failing two ways at once: the app assertion itself (expected isNavCollapsed true, got false) AND a vetoed navigation escape to /dashboard/organizations (the same destination Wallow-tkyq's own scout and red/green reports reproduced against). The test passes 136/136 in isolation every time; it only fails under the full-workspace run. That is a ~13% (2/15) observed full-workspace failure rate for this one test.

Wallow-uhef's own verifier pass (documented on Wallow-tkyq, "VERIFY" section) independently reproduced this live during closure: one of two verification pnpm check runs at repo root hit app-shell.toggle.test.tsx failing the same way (same destination URL), while the other of the two was clean. So this is not a single anomalous observation; it has now been seen at least 3 times total across two agents' independent runs (2 in Wallow-uhef's 15-run sweep, 1 in Wallow-tkyq's verifier pass), all with the identical signature.

WHAT THE GUARD DOES AND DOES NOT DO. Wallow-tkyq shipped packages/testing/src/navigation-escape.ts and wired it into packages/navigation/vitest.setup.ts. Before that guard, this leak tore down the whole Vitest runner and took 4 sibling files (28 tests) with it, misattributing the failure to whichever file's iframe was loading when the runner died. The guard's job — and the thing it verifiably does — is to veto the resulting navigation at the Navigation API and turn that runner-wide teardown into ONE named, attributed test failure. It has fully succeeded at that: across all these runs, zero collateral damage to sibling files has been observed since the guard landed. What the guard does NOT do, and was never designed to do, is stop the underlying click/race from occurring in the first place — Wallow-tkyq's own acceptance criteria had two clauses ("app-shell.toggle.test.tsx no longer triggers a real navigation" AND "no collateral failures in the 4 sibling files"), and only the second is actually satisfied. The first was believed satisfied at close time based on 3-5 consecutive green full-workspace runs, but Wallow-uhef's later, larger 15-run sample shows the trigger event itself is still live at roughly a 1-in-8 to 1-in-15 rate.

DIAGNOSIS ALREADY DONE — DO NOT RE-OPEN THIS DEAD END. Wallow-tkyq's scout thoroughly investigated an obvious application-side theory: app-shell.toggle.test.tsx's router-Link mock stub declares its own onClick BEFORE {...rest} in the JSX, so a spread onClick from Base UI's merged NavigationMenu.Link handler could in principle clobber the stub's local preventDefault(). The scout CONFIRMED this ordering defect is real (verified by reading Base UI's mergeProps.mjs source) but also PROVED it is not what is firing here: grepping every userEvent.click/keyboard-activation across all 13 nav spec files showed app-shell.toggle.test.tsx's 5 clicks all target dashboard-nav-toggle (a plain <button>), never a Link — so the defective stub ordering cannot be the mechanism, because the file never clicks the kind of element the ordering bug would affect. That latent stub-ordering defect is tracked separately as Wallow-xg9t.2 (open, P3, "reorder the 4 defective router-Link test stubs") and is NOT this bead's concern — do not conflate the two or re-diagnose the stub ordering as the cause here.

THE SCOUT'S WORKING THEORY (also from Wallow-tkyq, unconfirmed, unrefuted): a Vitest browser-mode iframe-orchestration race under @vitest/browser-playwright — a real Chromium pointer event dispatched by one file's userEvent.click (at page-relative screen coordinates) lands on a DIFFERENT, concurrently-mounted iframe if the intended iframe isn't frontmost/interactive at the exact dispatch instant, and whichever nav item is rendered at that shared screen offset in the other iframe absorbs the click. Consistent with: the leaked destination always being the first nav item (fixtureDestinations[0], "/dashboard/organizations") at a small, consistent screen offset across every ShellFixture render; no test anywhere actually clicking that destination; and reproduction rate rising under concurrent system load. This was never confirmed or refuted with Vitest/Playwright internals-level tracing — the scout explicitly flagged it as an analysis, not a proof, and out of budget to pin further.

OPEN QUESTION FOR WHOEVER PICKS THIS UP: is this an application-side defect (and if so, where — NOT the already-refuted stub-ordering theory), a Vitest browser-mode / @vitest/browser-playwright orchestration bug, or some other fixture/timing issue in ShellFixture or the toggle test's own double-click sequence? Wallow-tkyq's guard makes this safe to investigate without risking collateral damage to sibling files, since any recurrence now fails one named, attributed test rather than tearing down the runner.

PRIORITY JUSTIFICATION: P2. Weighing two facts against each other — (a) the collateral-damage failure mode is gone, so this is no longer capable of silently taking out unrelated packages/navigation coverage, which argues for lower urgency than Wallow-tkyq itself carried; against (b) this is a LIVE, currently-reproducing flake (~13% per full-workspace run, confirmed independently by two agents across 17 total observed full-workspace runs) in a package other frontend work depends on (packages/navigation is consumed by both apps), and an intermittent single-test failure in CI/pre-merge gates still costs real engineering time triaging "is this the known flake or a real regression" every time it fires. That ongoing cost, plus the fact the mechanism is still not understood, keeps this at P2 rather than dropping to P3.
design: Not prescribed. The scout's own recommendation in Wallow-tkyq was to flag the iframe-orchestration theory for whoever picks up the fix rather than guess further, since narrowing it needs Vitest/Playwright-internals-level tracing or a DEBUG trace across a caught repro — beyond the reproduction budget available during Wallow-tkyq/Wallow-uhef's work. Whoever takes this should NOT start from the stub-ordering theory (refuted, see description) and should treat the iframe-race theory as the current leading candidate to investigate, not an assumed conclusion. Candidate next steps for an investigator: (1) add DEBUG-level Playwright/Vitest tracing across a caught reproduction to see which iframe actually received the pointer event; (2) inspect whether packages/navigation/vitest.config.ts's browser-mode file concurrency/isolation settings (currently defaults, no fileParallelism/isolate override) can be tightened for this package without unacceptable slowdown, as a way to test the race theory by trying to suppress it; (3) consider whether the toggle test's specific double-click-in-quick-succession pattern (activating the same button twice) is unusually exposed to cross-iframe timing versus other specs' single-click patterns.

notes:
SCOUT DIAGNOSIS (read-only; no files changed, full suite not run). Verified independently by the lead against installed sources.

THE BEAD'S LEADING THEORY IS REFUTED - CLOSE IT. Cross-iframe pointer misrouting cannot happen:
  - @vitest/browser/dist/client/__vitest_browser__/orchestrator-*.js:69 - createTesters() opens with this.iframes.forEach((iframe) => iframe.remove())
  - vitest/dist/chunks/cli-api.*.js:2619 - BrowserPool.runNextTest calls orchestrator.createTesters({ ..., files: [file] }). ONE file per call.
An orchestrator page holds exactly one test iframe at a time; parallelism is across PAGES and CDP input dispatches per page target. Both lines read directly (vitest 4.1.10, @vitest/browser 4.1.10).

SHARED useNavStore SINGLETON ALSO DEAD. It IS a module-level singleton (nav-store.ts:53), but each spec file gets a fresh iframe -> fresh document -> fresh module registry, so every file holds its own instance. Same reasoning kills bleed of the guard's module-level escapes array (navigation-escape.ts:37). beforeEach already resets it (app-shell.toggle.test.tsx:45).

STRONG NEW CANDIDATE: same-iframe coordinate collision during the rail's 200ms width transition.
app-nav.tsx:223 railClass is 'w-16 data-[nav-open=true]:w-64 ... transition-[width] duration-200' - UNCONDITIONAL, not motion-safe gated. With <main> flex-1 p-6 (app-shell.tsx:258) and toggle size-9:
  - rail collapsed (w-16=64): toggle box x[88,124] y[24,60], centre (106,42)
  - rail expanded (w-64=256): menu root px-4 py-4, NavHeader renders null (fixture passes no header), first row px-3 py-2 text-sm = 36px, occupying x[16,240] y[16,52]
  - (106,42) lands INSIDE the first destination row = dashboard-nav-organizations, href=/dashboard/organizations - byte-identical to the vetoed URL.
Uniqueness: at w-16 the rail ends at x=64, so the toggle's coordinates only collide AFTER a first click. Across all 13 nav specs, app-shell.toggle.test.tsx:66-67 is the ONLY place in the repo issuing a second click while that transition is in flight (two bare awaits, nothing awaiting a settled width). Explains both the failed assertion and the destination.

HONEST GAP - NOT CLOSED. Playwright's setupHitTargetInterceptor (playwright-core/lib/coreBundle.js) intercepts 'click' and on mismatch calls preventDefault+stopPropagation+stopImmediatePropagation then RETRIES, which predicts a retry or a 15s timeout, not the observed ~160ms fast fail. The split-target variant (mousedown on toggle at old spot, mouseup on the link after the shift) explains the LOST TOGGLE exactly - Chromium fires click on the nearest common ancestor so neither handler runs - but not how the anchor's default navigation survived. Do not claim this is solved until that step is closed.

CHEAPEST DECISIVE EXPERIMENT: do not chase the 13% flake first. A throwaway spec clicking the toggle once then reading document.elementFromPoint(106,42) mid-transition proves the collision in ONE run. Caveat: headless scales the tester container by min(1, parentW/1280, parentH/800) via transform:scale (setIframeViewport), so read coordinates back rather than trusting the arithmetic.

FIX LEVERS (choose on evidence, not preference): (1) have the spec await a settled data-nav-open/width between the two clicks - fixes the spec; (2) gate the rail motion-safe:transition-[width] and run Chromium reduced-motion - fixes the class of races and is arguably right anyway, since an unconditional transition ignores prefers-reduced-motion.

NOT A FIX: test.browser.fileParallelism:false. packages/navigation/vitest.config.ts overrides none of these; packages/testing/src/vitest-projects.ts:161-167 sets only enabled/provider/headless/instances. fileParallelism defaults true and feeds getThreadsCount; false yields one tab, removing LOAD, not co-mounted iframes (there are none). If the flake vanishes under it that is evidence for a load-sensitive timing race, not for cross-iframe routing. It is a suppression lever. (test.browser.isolate is deprecated in v4 for top-level test.isolate; both default true.)

Plan: docs/plans/2026-08-03/1639-proxy-trust-react-dupe-nav-flake.md
NON-REPRODUCTION, 2026-08-27. 21 consecutive full-workspace runs
(`turbo run test --force`, four turbo concurrencies: default/4/3/2, then
`--force --only` with browser maxWorkers unset/2/1) on an 8-core box under heavy
load. Grepped every log for all four of this bead's signatures:

What DID fail repeatedly in those same 21 runs was a different thing entirely:

CORRECTION to an assumption recorded earlier in this session's thinking: the
"gate the rail motion-safe:transition-[width]" lever cannot be justified as
"restoring the repo convention". It is not the convention. Grepping every
ungated `transition-*` in source: only button, list-row and theme-toggle gate on
motion-safe:. Every other packages/ui component (accordion, alert-dialog,
collapsible, dialog, drawer, menu, navigation-menu, popover, preview-card,

would be a one-off, and it would suppress rather than fix.

The remaining lever is the spec-level one, and it is right on its own merits
independent of this flake: "collapses it again when the toggle is activated
twice" fires two bare `userEvent.click`s back to back across a
`transition-[width] duration-200` that moves <main> (and the toggle inside it)
192px right as the rail goes w-16 -> w-64 (app-nav.tsx:223 + app-shell.tsx:258,
flex siblings). Nothing awaits a settled width between them. The same file
already demonstrates the correct pattern in "flips the nav's own open state":
click, then `await expect.element(...).toHaveAttribute("data-nav-open", "true")`.
IN-DOCUMENT GEOMETRY THEORY REFUTED, 2026-08-27 (Step 6 of docs/plans/2026-08-27/1127-backlog-triage-and-sequencing.md).

A "wait between the two clicks" spec fix was drafted for this bead and then NOT
shipped, because the mechanism it would guard against cannot occur. Recording the
refutation so nobody drafts it again.

The theory was: app-nav.tsx:223 gives the rail `w-16 data-[nav-open=true]:w-64
transition-[width] duration-200`, and the toggle lives in the shell's <main>, a flex
sibling of the rail. So after the first click the toggle travels ~192px right over
200ms. If the second click were dispatched at the toggle's OLD coordinates it would
land on whatever the expanding rail had slid under the pointer — the first
destination row, /dashboard/organizations. That would explain every recorded fact at
once: the always-identical leaked destination, the fast (~160ms) failure, and
isNavCollapsed staying false because the second click never reached the toggle.

It cannot happen. Traced the call path: packages/@vitest/browser-playwright's
PlaywrightLocator.click (dist/locators.js) forwards to the server-side
`click(context, selector)` in dist/index.js, which is
`context.iframe.locator(selector).click(options)` — a real Playwright Locator click,
not a raw page.mouse.click at cached coordinates. Playwright's documented
actionability set for Locator.click is Visible + Stable + Receives Events + Enabled
(playwright docs/src/actionability.md). "Stable" is explicitly "not animating or
completed animation", so the click is withheld until the toggle's bounding box has
settled — i.e. until after the 200ms width transition. "Receives Events" then
hit-tests the computed point and retries if a different element would receive it.
Both checks sit exactly on the failure this theory needs.

WHAT SURVIVES: the scout's CROSS-IFRAME theory from Wallow-tkyq is untouched by the
above. Playwright's hit-target check is scoped to the frame it is driving; an event
delivered by the browser's compositor to a DIFFERENT, concurrently-mounted iframe is
below that check and would not be caught by it. So the leading candidate is still
"another file's iframe absorbed the event", not "this file clicked the wrong element".
The unification theory recorded on Wallow-xzy1.6 (vi.mock failing under load leaves
the Link stub absent, so a real anchor navigates) also survives and is independent.

CONSEQUENCE OF Wallow-pr34. The root `test` script now runs at turbo
`--concurrency=1`, so full-workspace runs no longer mount several packages' browser
suites at once. Every reproduction of this bead on record required that concurrency.
The cap therefore plausibly removes the trigger condition for both this bead and
Wallow-xzy1.6 — but that is an inference, NOT a verification: neither signature fired
in the 21 pre-fix runs of the Step 6 sweep either, so there is no before/after
comparison to make. Leaving this open. Whoever picks it up should re-measure at the
OLD concurrency (`turbo run test --force` with no cap) to get a reproduction first;
chasing it under the shipped cap will likely just produce more non-reproduction.
AMENDMENT to the note immediately above. I wrote there that the scout's CROSS-IFRAME theory 'survives' the Playwright refutation. That is too generous, and docs/plans/2026-08-03/1639-proxy-trust-react-dupe-nav-flake.md already says why, in its 'A note on fileParallelism' section: the shared preset (packages/testing/src/vitest-projects.ts) overrides none of the browser knobs, `test.browser.fileParallelism` defaults true, and what that buys is separate TABS — 'it removes load, not co-mounted iframes, of which there are none'. If there are no co-mounted iframes in the first place, 'the pointer event landed in another concurrently-mounted iframe' has no substrate. A cross-TAB misdelivery is a much stronger claim than the scout made and is harder to reconcile with the driver going through `context.iframe.locator(selector).click()` per frame.

So the accurate state of the theories is:

- in-document click geometry — REFUTED (Playwright Stable + Receives Events, note above)
- cross-iframe pointer routing — no substrate; do not start here
- vi.mock failing under load leaves the Link stub absent (Wallow-xzy1.6) — UNREFUTED, and now the only candidate on the board that explains a REAL navigation happening at all. A stub-less `Link` is the one way an anchor in this fixture reaches the Navigation API.

That makes the case for treating this bead and Wallow-xzy1.6 as one defect stronger than it was, not weaker. Whoever picks either up should pick up both.
CORRECTION to the 21-run non-reproduction recorded above — it carried a confound I introduced myself, and it should be discounted.

Re-audited the 21 logs. Two facts:

GOOD: packages/navigation's suite genuinely RAN and fully passed in all 21 runs — every log has a '@bc-solutions-coder/navigation:test: Test Files N passed (N)' summary line. So the non-reproduction is not an artifact of the suite never executing, which was the obvious way for it to be worthless. (That failure mode WAS real for the app suites; see the companion correction on Wallow-xzy1.6.)

BAD, and this is the confound: the file count in those summaries is 17 for the first two runs and 18 for the other NINETEEN. packages/navigation has 17 spec files today. The 18th was zz-collision-probe.test.tsx — a throwaway browser-mode spec I had written into packages/navigation/src/ in an earlier session and had not yet deleted. So for 19 of the 21 runs there was an EXTRA browser-mode test file sitting in the very package whose flake was being measured, changing that package's file count, its worker scheduling and its iframe/tab count. For a bead whose whole character is a scheduling-sensitive race inside this package, that is not a negligible difference. The probe has since been deleted.

Net: 'zero recurrence in 21 runs' overstates what was shown. The honest version is 'zero recurrence in 2 clean runs plus 19 runs with an extra spec file in the package under test'. Under the documented ~13% rate, 2 clean runs is almost no evidence at all.

A clean sweep on the current tree (probe deleted, no --concurrency flag so turbo's default 10, --continue so nothing masks anything) is running now; its result will be recorded here regardless of outcome.
Still NOT reproduced. Fresh sweep on the current tree (probe file deleted, so packages/navigation is a clean 17 files) at the old uncapped concurrency, --force --continue: 4 runs, navesc=0 and toggleFAIL=0 in all 4. packages/navigation printed a full '17 passed (17)' summary every time, including in the run where wallow-web hung, so the suite genuinely executed.

title: wire the navigation-escape guard into wallow-web, packages/ui and packages/forms
description:
`@bc-solutions-coder/testing/navigation-escape` (packages/testing/src/navigation-escape.ts) is a Vitest browser-project guard: `installNavigationEscapeGuard()` listens for the Navigation API's `navigate` event, records any CROSS-DOCUMENT destination, and calls `preventDefault()` so the runner's iframe stays put; `assertNoNavigationEscape()` (called in an `afterEach`) throws naming the escaped URL(s), then clears. Without it, a real cross-document navigation inside a browser-mode spec (e.g. an unhandled `<a href>` click, or `location.assign(...)`) silently tears down that spec's Chromium iframe, Vitest attributes the resulting connection error to whichever file it tries to load NEXT (not the file that actually leaked), and every file behind it in that run never reports. `location` is `[Unforgeable]` in real Chromium, so `vi.stubGlobal("location", ...)` cannot intercept this — the Navigation-API listener is the only working mechanism.

The guard is a SAME-DOCUMENT-safe filter by design: `vetoNavigation` returns early on `event.destination.sameDocument`, so ordinary router route changes (pushState-driven, same-document) are never touched — only a full-page/cross-document hand-off is vetoed. This was added specifically so the guard is safe to wire into apps running a REAL (unmocked) router.

## Today it is installed in exactly ONE of five browser projects

packages/navigation/vitest.setup.ts calls `installNavigationEscapeGuard()` at module scope and registers `afterEach(assertNoNavigationEscape)`, wired through `browserSetupFiles: ["./vitest.setup.ts"]` in packages/navigation/vitest.config.ts. The other four browser-mode projects in the repo have no such guard and can still lose their runner silently to exactly the failure class packages/navigation just closed:

1. **apps/wallow-web** — apps/wallow-web/vitest.setup.ts today only imports `./vitest-styles.css` and `virtual:wallow-theme.css`, wired via `browserSetupFiles: ["./vitest.setup.ts"]` in apps/wallow-web/vitest.config.ts. This app renders a REAL `@tanstack/react-router` (not mocked) — its route changes are same-document and the guard's `sameDocument` filter is what makes wiring this app safe without breaking routing.
2. **apps/wallow-auth** — same shape: apps/wallow-auth/vitest.setup.ts today only imports the two stylesheets, wired the same way in apps/wallow-auth/vitest.config.ts. Also a real, unmocked router.
3. **packages/ui** — has THREE Vitest projects (node, browser, storybook), not two. The plain `browser` project currently has **no setup file at all** — `createVitestProjects({...})` in packages/ui/vitest.config.ts is called with no `browserSetupFiles` option, so there is nothing to add the guard to yet; a new `packages/ui/vitest.setup.ts` must be created AND wired via `browserSetupFiles: ["./vitest.setup.ts"]`. Separately, the `storybook` project is built by `@storybook/addon-vitest`'s `storybookTest()` plugin and does NOT read `browserSetupFiles` — it loads `.storybook/preview.tsx` instead (which today exports only a `themeDecorator` and `parameters`). Wiring the guard into the `storybook` project needs its own mechanism inside `.storybook/preview.tsx` (Storybook's own per-story hook surface, e.g. a decorator or an exported global hook) — this is NOT the same code path as the two `browserSetupFiles` wirings and must be worked out and verified independently; adding `packages/ui/vitest.setup.ts` alone does NOT cover the `storybook` project. `packages/ui/src/components/focus-on-navigate/focus-on-navigate.test.tsx` already renders router-adjacent behaviour, so this project is not a hypothetical risk.
4. **packages/forms** — same shape as wallow-web/wallow-auth: packages/forms/vitest.setup.ts today only imports the two stylesheets, wired via `browserSetupFiles: ["./vitest.setup.ts"]` in packages/forms/vitest.config.ts.

## Why this bead, and why now

This is the epic's own through-line: a guard installed in one project out of five leaves the other four able to lose a runner silently to the exact class of failure the epic exists to close (see Wallow-xg9t's description — "A cluster of test-infrastructure beads: the machinery that decides whether the suite is telling the truth... invisible in a green run"). This item was explicitly deferred out of Wallow-tkyq (the bead that built and wired the guard into packages/navigation) as its own follow-up, with the sameDocument filter built specifically as this bead's prerequisite.

PLAN: docs/plans/2026-08-02/1744-no-source-tests-design.md.
design:
Mirror packages/navigation/vitest.setup.ts's wiring (import installNavigationEscapeGuard + assertNoNavigationEscape from "@bc-solutions-coder/testing/navigation-escape"; call installNavigationEscapeGuard() at module scope; afterEach(() => { assertNoNavigationEscape(); })) into each project's existing setup file for wallow-web, wallow-auth and packages/forms — those three already have a vitest.setup.ts wired via browserSetupFiles, so this is an addition to an existing file, not new wiring.

For packages/ui's `browser` project: create packages/ui/vitest.setup.ts with the same guard wiring (it has no styling to carry — CLAUDE.md states the browser project deliberately loads no Tailwind), and pass `browserSetupFiles: ["./vitest.setup.ts"]` into the `createVitestProjects({...})` call in packages/ui/vitest.config.ts.

For packages/ui's `storybook` project: investigate and implement Storybook's own equivalent hook surface in .storybook/preview.tsx (a decorator alongside the existing themeDecorator, or an exported global per-story hook if @storybook/addon-vitest's Storybook version supports one) that installs the guard once and asserts no escape after each story. Verify this actually intercepts a story-triggered cross-document navigation before calling it done — do not assume the API exists without confirming it against the installed Storybook version, the way Wallow-tkyq's scout verified the Navigation API directly against the pinned Chromium build rather than trusting docs from memory.

For every project touched, follow the two load-bearing details Wallow-tkyq's implementer already found in packages/navigation and re-verify per project rather than assuming they transfer automatically:
- The setup file must be added to that project's tsconfig.json `include` array if not already present, or the wiring goes untypechecked (`pnpm typecheck` will not catch an error in it). Checked at scouting time: apps/wallow-web/tsconfig.json and apps/wallow-auth/tsconfig.json do NOT currently list `vitest.setup.ts` in `include` (neither app's setup file is typechecked today) — add it for both. packages/forms/tsconfig.json already lists `vitest.setup.ts` — no change needed there. packages/ui/tsconfig.json does not list it either (it does not exist yet) — add it when the new file is created.
- Idempotence: a browser-project setup file re-evaluates per browser context, so a second `installNavigationEscapeGuard()` call on the same page must not double-register a listener. This is already handled INSIDE `installNavigationEscapeGuard()` itself (module-level guard), so no per-consumer work is needed here — just don't wrap the call in anything that would defeat it.
acceptance_criteria:
1. apps/wallow-web/vitest.setup.ts calls installNavigationEscapeGuard() and registers afterEach(assertNoNavigationEscape), and apps/wallow-web/tsconfig.json's include gains vitest.setup.ts.
2. packages/forms/vitest.setup.ts calls installNavigationEscapeGuard() and registers afterEach(assertNoNavigationEscape).
3. packages/ui gets a new vitest.setup.ts wired via browserSetupFiles into its browser project's createVitestProjects() call, with the same guard installed, and packages/ui/tsconfig.json's include gains vitest.setup.ts.
4. packages/ui's storybook project independently gets an equivalent guard (its own investigated wiring point in .storybook/preview.tsx, since storybookTest() does not read browserSetupFiles) — verified live, not assumed: a deliberately-provoked cross-document navigation inside a story fails that story's own test with a message naming the escaped URL, rather than tearing down the storybook project's Chromium instance.
5. Deliberately provoking a cross-document navigation (an unprevented anchor click, or location.assign to an arbitrary path) in a throwaway probe spec in EACH of the three projects / four mechanisms above (wallow-web; packages/forms; packages/ui's plain browser project; packages/ui's storybook project) fails exactly one test naming the escaped URL, and does not take any sibling file down. Delete each throwaway probe after confirming — no debris in git status.
6. No existing spec in apps/wallow-web, packages/ui or packages/forms regresses: pnpm test (= pnpm -r test) file/test counts for those three match their pre-change baselines exactly.
7. Full pnpm check passes at least once at the end (format:check, lint, lint:tests, typecheck, test, build, check:exports).
8. apps/wallow-auth is left completely unwired and unmodified — its vitest.setup.ts and tsconfig.json carry no guard-related edits — because wiring it breaks 70 previously-passing tests across 10 specs whose screens perform a real OIDC hand-off via globalThis.location assignment; the guard itself is not weakened to accommodate it. A separate, unparented follow-up bead exists to resolve wallow-auth's case; this bead does not need it closed or even filed to be considered complete.

  - packages/ui/CLAUDE.md — new gotcha: the guard is wired TWICE here because the
    two browser projects take it through different doors.

extraBrowserOptimizeDeps: NOT needed anywhere (scout correct — the module imports
nothing and is a linked workspace package Vite does not pre-bundle). No
package.json edit needed anywhere; all four already declare
@bc-solutions-coder/testing. No mid-run Vite reload observed in any run.

## PROOF THE WIRING IS LIVE — per mechanism

Method per package: a throwaway two-test probe (one test provokes a
cross-document hand-off, a sibling does not), full suite run, probe deleted, full
suite re-run. In every case exactly ONE test failed, it named the URL, its
sibling passed, and no other file was touched.

1. packages/forms — src/core/guard-probe.test.tsx (unprevented anchor click).
   FAIL src/core/guard-probe.test.tsx > probe > escapes
   "Navigation escaped the test iframe ... http://localhost:63315/probe/forms"
   Run with probe: 1 failed | 15 passed (16 files), 1 failed | 89 passed.

2. apps/wallow-web — src/shared/guard-probe.test.tsx (unprevented anchor click).
   FAIL src/shared/guard-probe.test.tsx > probe > escapes
   "... http://localhost:63315/probe/wallow-web"
   Run with probe: 1 failed | 82 passed (83 files), 1 failed | 502 passed | 1 skipped.

3. packages/ui BROWSER project — src/core/guard-probe.test.tsx (native
   anchor.click(), since this project loads no Tailwind).
   FAIL |browser (chromium)| src/core/guard-probe.test.tsx > probe > escapes
   "... http://localhost:63315/probe/ui-browser"

4. packages/ui STORYBOOK project — src/components/text/guard-probe.stories.tsx,
   a story whose play() calls globalThis.location.assign().
   FAIL |storybook (chromium)| src/components/text/guard-probe.stories.tsx > Escapes
   "... http://localhost:63316/probe/ui-storybook"
   Note the PORT: 63316 vs the browser project's 63315. The two projects run
   separate Vite servers with independent module graphs, so this is genuine
   proof of the storybook wiring and not the browser setup file leaking across.
   Combined ui run with both probes: 2 failed | 117 passed (119 files),
   2 failed | 1449 passed. Each mechanism failed its own one test.

Storybook hook surface verified against the installed build, not assumed:
storybook@10.5.5 dist/csf/index.d.ts declares beforeEach/afterEach on
ProjectAnnotations, and the browser runtime chunk runs `applyAfterEach(context)`
as its own render phase after EVERY story (guarded only by phase !== "errored",
not by the presence of a play function). The live probe above confirms a throw
there fails that story's addon-vitest test case.

All four probe files deleted; `git status` shows no probe debris.

## TEST_STATUS — baseline vs after (identical everywhere)

packages/forms      15 files /   88 tests  ->  15 /   88   pass
apps/wallow-web     82 files /  501 pass, 1 skipped (502)  ->  identical
packages/ui        117 files / 1447 tests  -> 117 / 1447   pass
apps/wallow-auth    55 files /  808 tests  ->  55 /  808   pass (UNWIRED, unchanged)
packages/navigation 17 files /  136 tests  ->  17 /  136   pass (untouched)

pnpm check: EXIT=0 (format:check, lint, lint:tests, build, typecheck, test,
check:exports). One format fixup was needed on the way — oxfmt reflowed
apps/wallow-web/tsconfig.json's include array after the addition.

## FINDING — apps/wallow-auth CANNOT be wired as-is. Left unwired, needs its own bead.

The scout's section 3 concluded "no false-positive risk found" for all four. That
holds for forms, wallow-web and ui. It is WRONG for wallow-auth, and the reason
is a class the scout's grep could not see: it searched for anchors and Link
clicks. wallow-auth does not leak through an anchor — its screens navigate the
browser ON PURPOSE, programmatically, because a full-page hand-off IS the OIDC
flow's product behaviour.

Wired, wallow-auth went from 55 files / 808 passing to 70 FAILING tests across 10
files: AcceptTermsScreen, ConsentScreen, InvitationScreen, LoginScreen,
LoginMfaHandOff, MagicLinkLoginForm, OtpLoginForm, MfaChallengeForm,
MfaEnrollForm (and the probe). Eight source files assign globalThis.location.href
/ .assign / .replace:
  src/features/accept-terms/components/AcceptTermsScreen.tsx
  src/features/consent/components/ConsentScreen.tsx
  src/features/invitation/components/InvitationScreen.tsx
  src/features/login/components/LoginScreen.tsx
  src/features/mfa-challenge/components/MfaChallengeForm.tsx
  src/features/mfa-enroll/components/MfaEnrollForm.tsx
(plus the two specs' own harnesses). No such file exists in wallow-web,
packages/ui or packages/forms — the grep over all four found hand-offs ONLY in
wallow-auth. This is structural to that app, not a stray defect.

MECHANISM. Every one of the 70 failures is the guard's own afterEach throwing
"Navigation escaped the test iframe". Not one is an assertion failure inside a
test — the specs' own behaviour assertions all still pass. Those specs already
implement a per-spec copy of exactly this guard: AcceptTermsScreen.test.tsx's
header states the seam verbatim ("`location` is `[Unforgeable]` ... listen for
the Navigation API `navigate` event ... record `destination.url`, and
`preventDefault()` it"), and its captureHandoff() adds its own navigate listener
and asserts the URL it recovers. Both listeners fire; the spec's assertions are
satisfied; the shared guard then records the same hand-off as an escape and the
project-level afterEach fails the test.

So these are LEGITIMATE, deliberately-provoked navigations that the spec already
intercepts. Per the brief I stopped rather than weakening the guard, and reverted
wallow-auth's setup + tsconfig edits so the tree is green.

WHAT THE FOLLOW-UP BEAD HAS TO DECIDE (not mine to pick unilaterally under a
"straight wiring" brief): the fix is to make those 10 specs consume the SHARED
guard instead of running a second listener beside it. Two shapes worth weighing —
(a) each spec's capture helper calls clearNavigationEscapes() once it has read
the URL, so the shared record is empty by afterEach; or (b) packages/testing
grows an explicit expectNavigationEscape()/consumeNavigationEscapes() helper that
a spec asserting a hand-off calls, which reads better and keeps the "a spec that
forgot still fails" property. Either way it touches 10 spec files and ~70 tests
and is real design work, not wiring. Note the payoff is REAL: wallow-auth is the
one app in the repo that navigates for a living, so it is the app with the most
to lose from an unguarded leak — its per-spec listeners only protect the files
that remembered to add one.

## STORYBOOK SUB-ITEM — folded in, NOT split out

The scout flagged packages/ui's storybook project as a candidate for its own
bead if its interception needed real iteration. It did not. The type surface was
already confirmed on the bead, the hook worked first try, and it cost one export
pair in .storybook/preview.tsx plus one probe story. It is acceptance criterion
#4 of this bead and it is DONE and proven live — do not file a follow-up for it.

## OPEN

- apps/wallow-auth (acceptance criteria 1 half, 5 half, and the epic's own
  through-line) is NOT met and needs the follow-up bead described above. Every
  other criterion (2, 3, 4, 6, 7, and the wallow-web half of 1) is met.
ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA NARROWED (by a follow-up bead-filing pass, not the implementer). Original AC named all four packages (wallow-web, wallow-auth, packages/ui, packages/forms) as one bead. The implementation delivered and proved live exactly THREE of the four: packages/forms, apps/wallow-web, and packages/ui (both its plain browser project and its storybook project, via two independent wiring mechanisms — see the implementation note above for the port-63315-vs-63316 proof). apps/wallow-auth was deliberately reverted: wiring it turned 55 files/808 passing into 70 FAILING tests across 10 spec files, because 8 of its screens assign globalThis.location.href/.assign/.replace as the real, on-purpose OIDC hand-off, and those 10 specs already run their own per-spec navigate listener beside the shared guard — both listeners fire, the spec's own assertions still pass, and the shared guard's afterEach then flags the same deliberate hand-off as an escape. The implementer correctly refused to weaken the guard to make wallow-auth pass, and instead left wallow-auth's setup/tsconfig untouched.

The original AC's item 1 and item 5/6 named wallow-auth explicitly, which would have made this bead permanently unclosable without either weakening the guard (rejected) or resolving wallow-auth's real design question (out of scope for a "wire it in" bead per the epic's own Wallow-tkyq precedent, which deferred exactly this kind of scope split). Title and all 8 acceptance criteria were rewritten to cover only the three delivered targets; substance for those three is preserved unchanged from the original (same file paths, same wiring shape, same live-probe requirement, same regression-count requirement, same full pnpm check gate). New criterion 8 makes wallow-auth's exclusion an explicit, checkable part of THIS bead's "done" rather than a silent gap — it is closable now.

wallow-auth's own resolution is filed as its own unparented bead (see this project's backlog) rather than folded in here or parented under Wallow-xg9t, per the user's decision that the epic should close rather than absorb newly-discovered follow-ups.
VERIFY (independent, code+run-based):

1. THREE WIRINGS REAL/LIVE — ✓. Read packages/forms/vitest.setup.ts,
apps/wallow-web/vitest.setup.ts, packages/ui/vitest.setup.ts (module-scope
installNavigationEscapeGuard() + afterEach(assertNoNavigationEscape), no
per-spec opt-in) and packages/ui/vitest.config.ts (browserSetupFiles:
["./vitest.setup.ts"] added to createVitestProjects()). packages/ui's
storybook mechanism confirmed in .storybook/preview.tsx: named
beforeEach/afterEach exports typed Preview["beforeEach"]/["afterEach"], which
Storybook runs before/after EVERY story — separate door from browserSetupFiles
as the design required. tsconfig.json include gained "vitest.setup.ts" for

change needed, matches report. No probe/guard-probe debris anywhere (grepped
whole tree for probe*/guard-probe*, only unrelated pre-existing
__screenshots__ dirs and generic word hits under apps/wallow-auth found).
Independently re-proved liveness on packages/forms (lowest-risk of the three,
picked to cross-check the implementer's own claim rather than trust it): wrote
src/core/verify-probe.test.tsx clicking a real unprevented anchor, ran pnpm
test — FAIL src/core/verify-probe.test.tsx > escapes, error opened with
NAVIGATION_ESCAPE_MESSAGE and named http://localhost:63315/verify/forms-escape,
run was 1 failed|15 passed (16 files), 1 failed|89 passed, zero collateral on
the other 15 files. Deleted the probe + its __screenshots__ dir, reran: 15/15
files, 88/88 tests, git status packages/forms shows only the intended
vitest.setup.ts diff. Tree left exactly as found.

2. WALLOW-AUTH CLEANLY REVERTED — ✓. git diff apps/wallow-auth/tsconfig.json,
vitest.setup.ts, vitest.config.ts, package.json all empty — zero trace of the
guard wiring. apps/wallow-auth/src/features/consent/.../ConsentScreen.catalog.test.tsx
IS modified in the working tree, but read the diff: it is unrelated
pointer-park-hoist work from a different concurrently-running bead (userEvent.unhover
replacing a parkPointer helper), nothing to do with navigation-escape. Same
pattern confirmed in packages/navigation/src/app-nav.*.test.tsx,

packages/ui's preview-card.test.tsx/toast.test.tsx — all pointer-park-hoist
diffs, not this bead's. Left untouched, correctly out of scope for this

3. GUARD NOT WEAKENED — ✓. packages/testing/src/navigation-escape.ts is
untracked (from Wallow-tkyq, never committed) and this implementer's diff does
not touch it at all — confirmed by reading the full file: sameDocument
early-return, no allowlist, no opt-out, no per-project conditional, identical
to what tkyq's report describes. The wallow-auth accommodation is "leave it
unwired + file a follow-up", not a code-level exemption.

4. WALLOW-AUTH FINDING SPOT-CHECKED — ✓, roughly accurate and sound. Grepped
apps/wallow-auth/src for globalThis.location.(href|assign|replace) outside
tests: 8 source files (AcceptTermsScreen, MfaEnrollForm, MfaChallengeForm,
ConsentScreen, InvitationScreen, auth-result.ts, ExternalProviders, LoginScreen)
— matches report's count. Grepped for addEventListener("navigate": 9 spec
files (AcceptTerms, Consent, Invitation, LoginMfaHandOff, LoginScreen,
MagicLinkLoginForm, OtpLoginForm, MfaChallengeForm, MfaEnrollForm) — report's

Read three of the source assignments directly (InvitationScreen.tsx:448 ->
HOME_HREF, LoginScreen.tsx:375 -> buildExchangeTicketUrl(...),

title: add DLQ observability for Wolverine handler failures
description:
Split out of Wallow-qi90.1 layer 4, which shipped the codegen guards (HandlerCodegenTests + WolverineCodegenPolicyTests) without it.

The codegen guards stop a non-inlinable handler dependency from shipping. They do not tell anyone when a handler fails for any other reason at runtime: a Wolverine envelope that exhausts its retries lands in the dead-letter queue silently, behind whatever HTTP 200 the caller already got. The SendEmailHandler incident was invisible for exactly that reason — the failure was in the DLQ and nothing surfaced it.

Wanted: DLQ depth surfaced as a metric/health signal, and a log line at Error when an envelope is dead-lettered, naming the message type and the exception. Wallow already exports custom instruments (see CustomInstrumentExportTests in Wallow.Architecture.Tests) and runs OpenTelemetry through Wallow.ServiceDefaults, so this should hang off the existing pipeline rather than introduce a new one.

Not urgent — nothing is deployed. This is the observability half of the codegen work, kept separate so it does not gate it.
notes: Implemented per docs/plans/2026-08-28/1709-dlq-observability.md: ServiceDefaults exports Wolverine:* (built-in wolverine-dead-letter-queue counter now leaves the process); WolverineDeadLetterQueueHealthCheck reports wolverine-dlq Degraded on /health (never ready-tagged) and records wallow.messaging.dead_letter_queue.depth; Error log is Wolverine's own MovedToErrorQueue line, pinned by the tracked event in DeadLetterObservabilityTests plus the Serilog-override guard WolverineDeadLetterLoggingTests; docs/operations/observability.md updated and pinned by CustomInstrumentExportTests.

title: reconcile which wallow/* rules the two apps and minimal-app enable
description:
Wallow-mlc3 registered the wallow/* plugin in packages/navigation, packages/ui and
packages/forms and gave all three ALL FIVE rules. That left the apps as the only
configs enabling a subset, and the subsets still disagree with each other for no
recorded reason:

  wallow-web:  no-sidebar-inversion, no-tinted-text, zone-dag
  wallow-auth: no-hand-rolled-mutation, no-sidebar-inversion, text-heading-variant, zone-dag

Two rules are missing from an app that has live violations of them:

- `no-tinted-text` is OFF in wallow-auth, and three files carry the exact spelling
  it bans: `features/not-found/components/NotFoundPage.tsx`,
  `features/error/components/ErrorPage.tsx` and
  `features/access-request/components/AccessRequestPage.tsx` all write
  `text-primary hover:text-primary/80` on a link. Wallow-mlc3 already deleted that
  same spelling from the catalog's `link` button variant, so these three are now
  hand-rolling a treatment the catalog deliberately dropped. Enabling the rule and
  moving them onto `Button variant="link"` (or `hover:underline`) closes both.
- `no-hand-rolled-mutation` is OFF in wallow-web. Whether wallow-web has a live
  violation is unmeasured — turn it on and see.
- `text-heading-variant` is OFF in wallow-web, and that one is NOT an oversight:
  `packages/lint/CLAUDE.md` records that wallow-web's headings are not one shape
  (`LandingPage` runs display/title/h3, the detail routes run title) and that the
  `bff-demo` route deliberately takes Text's derived scale. Deciding what those
  should be is the work, not flipping the switch.

Second gap, found while taking the inventory: `apps/examples/minimal-app` has NO
nested `.oxlintrc.json` at all, so it registers no jsPlugins and every wallow/*
rule passes vacuously over it — the same defect Wallow-mlc3 fixed for the three
packages. It renders UI. Decide whether the example app is meant to be held to the
catalog rules (an example that violates them teaches the violation) and give it a
nested config if so.
acceptance_criteria: Each app config's wallow/* rule set is either the same as the others' or differs for a reason written down in packages/lint/CLAUDE.md. wallow-auth enables no-tinted-text and its three hover:text-primary/80 links are fixed rather than exempted. A decision is recorded for apps/examples/minimal-app — either it gains a nested config registering the plugin, or packages/lint/CLAUDE.md says why it is deliberately outside the gate. pnpm lint and pnpm lint:tests stay green with no rule blanket-disabled.

title: wallow-auth e2e: 7 auth-flow specs fail generically against a freshly-started containerised API
description:
Symptom: running ./scripts/e2e.sh (or the wallow-auth suite alone against docker/docker-compose.test.yml) fails 7 of 30 specs, all of which authenticate the shared seeded admin account (admin@wallow.dev / Admin123! from api/seed.json):

- e2e/login.spec.ts:13 "password login reaches an authenticated state"
- e2e/magic-link.spec.ts:42 "magic-link send then verify reaches an authenticated state"
- e2e/mfa.spec.ts:100 "mfa totp lifecycle > totp enrollment issues backup codes"
- e2e/logout.spec.ts:46 "signed-out landing shows the return link for an allow-listed redirect uri"
- e2e/otp-login.spec.ts:39 "otp send then verify reaches an authenticated state"
- e2e/signup.spec.ts:24 "register happy path reaches the verify-email notice"
- e2e/reset-password.spec.ts:48 "forgot then reset with the emailed token shows the login success banner"

routes.spec.ts (18 no-auth tests) and signup.spec.ts's email_taken test (no real credential submit) both pass, so the split is exactly "hits a real auth POST" vs not.

Confirmed NOT caused by any docker-compose.test.yml edit: reverting docker/docker-compose.test.yml to HEAD (restoring the old Identity__FirstPartyClients__0=bcordes-bff / __1=wallow-web-client overrides) and re-running ./scripts/e2e.sh with E2E_SKIP_IMAGE_BUILD=1 reproduces the IDENTICAL 7 failures and 23 passes. login.spec.ts:13 in particular does a bare `/login` visit with no OIDC returnUrl/client_id at all (see its own header comment), so it cannot be touched by a FirstPartyClients override regardless.

Evidence from apps/wallow-auth/test-results/login-password-login-reaches-an-authenticated-state/error-context.md: the login form renders, fields fill, submit is clicked, but the screen shows a generic "An error occurred. Please try again." banner instead of the login-signed-in testid -- i.e. the credential POST itself errors. reset-password.spec.ts's failure is a distinct symptom: "No email to admin@wallow.dev with subject \"Password Reset Request\" arrived within 20000ms (Mailpit)" -- a mail-delivery timing issue, not a login error.

Container startup itself is clean: postgres/migrations/seeder/api/auth/web all report healthy before the API-ready poll succeeds (typically ~1s).

Working theory (NOT confirmed): Playwright's default parallel workers fire concurrent login/signup/otp/mfa/reset-password attempts against the SAME seeded admin account against a just-started API, and something (rate limiting / account lockout / DB still warming past its health check) causes those concurrent auth POSTs to fail generically. Needs a targeted repro to confirm/deny -- e.g. re-run the wallow-auth suite alone with `--workers=1`, or set E2E_KEEP_STACK=1 and capture `docker compose logs wallow-api` during a failing run (not captured by ./scripts/e2e.sh's own log).

Reproduce:
  E2E_SKIP_IMAGE_BUILD=1 ./scripts/e2e.sh
(prebuilt :test images must already exist locally, or drop the env var to build them first)

Discovered while verifying Wallow-yp3e.4; not part of that epic's scope -- filed as an independent, dependency-free sibling.
notes: VERIFIER: RESOLVED BY WALLOW-SMVC (commit 0fe4d9ff, ILastOwnerGuard registered in seeder DI). Two full ./scripts/e2e.sh runs after that fix (one cold image rebuild, one E2E_SKIP_IMAGE_BUILD=1 reusing the same fixed images) both show wallow-auth 31/31 PASSED, including all 7 previously-failing specs listed in this bead's description. Prior to the fix, two separate runs (implementer's original + my own stash-based causation check) both showed the identical 7/30 failures deterministically. This before/after comparison, run 4 times total with consistent results each side, is decisive. Caveat: SeederWorker.ExecuteAsync runs BootstrapAdminAsync BEFORE SyncOrganizationsAsync (the step that crashed pre-fix), so admin bootstrap should in principle have been unaffected by the later crash — I could not fully reconcile the causal mechanism from code reading alone, only from the empirical fix/no-fix results. Recommend closing; if the team lead wants the mechanism nailed down first, one more standalone confirmatory run would settle it, but I would not block on that. Full detail cross-referenced on Wallow-yp3e.4.

title: fix the guards that do not guard — test and lint infrastructure
description:
A cluster of test-infrastructure beads: the machinery that decides whether the suite is telling
the truth. None changes product behaviour and none is visible in a green run — which is exactly
why they need a container that keeps them from being triaged away one at a time.

PLAN: docs/plans/2026-08-02/1744-no-source-tests-design.md. Read it before picking up any member;
it has been rewritten to match what actually shipped.

## The through-line

Every member is a guard that does not guard: a stripper that blinds the spec reading it, a
timeout that is not the one anyone configured, a colour nothing measures, an idiom copied six
ways because it was never exported.

The design pass found the root cause under the largest of them: THERE WAS NO RULE AGAINST SOURCE
TESTS. Doctrine and shape pin appeared in ZERO markdown files in this repo, which is why the
sweep inventory went 23 -> 18 -> 16 rather than down, and why two new sweeps landed hours after
the bead to fix them was filed.

The resolution: LINT OWNS STRUCTURE, TESTS OWN BEHAVIOUR. A test never reads application source,
README prose, or directory layout off disk. Constraining how code is written is a linter's job —
an AST rule fires in the editor, names the line, and cannot be defeated by formatting. Most
sweeps were deleted with nothing replacing them, because the constraint was rigidity without
correctness.

## Status

Wallow-xg9t.1 shipped the gate AND the sweep in one pass. Scope was widened by the user from the
16 flagged files to every source-reading spec in the repo — 77 files: 44 deleted outright, 30
thinned in place, one replaced with a behavioural spec. Wallow-e6gz is closed as absorbed; its
Phase 4a (wallow/module-imports) was dropped because every sweep that rule would have carried was
deleted rather than converted.

## Remaining members and ORDER — a dependency chain, not a preference

1. Wallow-tkyq (P2) — the app-shell toggle spec leaks a real navigation into the vitest iframe,
   tearing down the runner and taking 4 sibling files (28 tests) with it. packages/navigation
   browser runs must be trustworthy before Wallow-succ adds a spec there. BLOCKS Wallow-succ.
2. Wallow-succ (P3) — cover the nav scrim by DRAWER-DISMISSAL BEHAVIOUR (click the backdrop,
   assert the drawer closes), not by reading its computed alpha. Rewritten: the alpha read did
   not test the risk the bead itself stated. The PublicLayout footer site is dropped from it.
   Blocked by Wallow-tkyq only — the Wallow-h9k1 edge was removed.
3. Wallow-h9k1 (P3) — make the existing colour specs name their pointer state per assertion
   (unhover before the rest half, hover before the hover half) and delete the seven beforeEach
   parks. Rewritten: the park is NOT hoisted into @bc-solutions-coder/testing. It gates nothing.
4. Wallow-uhef (P2) — the browser project's testTimeout. LAST, deliberately: it is a MEASUREMENT
   bead, and the sweep removed 44 node spec files while Wallow-succ adds a browser spec.
   Measuring before the suite settles measures a suite that will not exist.

Wallow-mlc3 is closed and IS a child. It is cited by the plan as the evidence that lint wiring
can be silently absent — a silently inert wallow/* plugin — which is the argument the JSONC
config guards in packages/sdk/src/oxlint-guardrails.test.ts survived the sweep on.
acceptance_criteria:
Every child closed. All seven are parented; the Wallow-mlc3 membership question is decided (it is
a member, closed). This epic is not closable while any child is open; a green suite is not
evidence, since every one of these defects is invisible in a green run.
notes:
Filed from the bead backlog audit of 2026-08-02 (docs/audits/2026-08-02/0824-bead-backlog), the conditional NEW BEAD row. Its precondition — 'the membership list must be re-derived before it is created' — was met at filing: of the six beads originally proposed, Wallow-1lt5 and Wallow-a5mt have since closed and Wallow-uhef was retyped bug->task, leaving four members. FILED EMPTY ON PURPOSE: the filing pass was scoped to creating beads, not to modifying existing ones, so the four members were NOT reparented. That reparent is the epic's first action and is written into its description. Priority deliberately set below its highest-priority member: this is a container, and inflating it would repeat the priority inversion the same audit flagged as H13.
Wallow-tkyq is now a member too — packages/navigation's app-shell.toggle.test.tsx leaks a real navigation into the vitest iframe under full-workspace runs, tearing down the runner and taking 4 sibling files (28 tests) with it. Same subject as the rest of this epic: machinery that decides whether the suite is telling the truth. The 'reparent these four' list in the description is therefore five.
CLEANUP + SHIP, 2026-08-02. Four conventional commits on feat/multi-org-membership, in dependency order:

- 950e3e4c test(testing): add a navigation-escape guard for browser projects — packages/testing/src/navigation-escape.ts plus the ./navigation-escape subpath (package.json exports + publishConfig, vite.config.ts entry, tsconfig.build.json) and the CLAUDE.md entry-table row.
- d8c0805b test: install the navigation-escape guard in four browser projects — setup files for packages/navigation, packages/forms, packages/ui (new file) and apps/wallow-web; packages/ui/vitest.config.ts browserSetupFiles; .storybook/preview.tsx beforeEach/afterEach for the storybook project; three tsconfig.json include lists so the setup files typecheck; packages/navigation/src/navigation-escape.test.tsx as the proof spec; packages/navigation/CLAUDE.md, packages/testing/CLAUDE.md and packages/ui/CLAUDE.md guard prose.
- 341b2b58 test: name pointer state per assertion and delete the seven parks — eight specs across wallow-auth, wallow-web, packages/navigation and packages/ui, plus the pointer prose in packages/testing/CLAUDE.md and packages/ui/CLAUDE.md.
- 80285f55 chore: ignore vitest json reporter output — .gitignore entry for .vitest-run.json (the ten stray artifacts from Wallow-uhef's measurement run were already gone from the tree).

TYPES: no feat and no fix. The epic's own framing is that none of this changes product behaviour, so nothing here should cut a release; test/chore do not.

GATE: pnpm check run over the final tree, EXIT=0, all 15 packages green (packages/navigation 17/17 files). The Wallow-x5da app-shell.toggle flake did NOT reproduce on this run.

title: make the epic backlog's reasoning survive a fresh clone
description:
Beads sync between machines through Dolt (`refs/dolt/data`) and reach every clone. Their reasoning
does not. `.gitignore` ignores `docs/plans/`, `docs/specs/` and `docs/superpowers/` outright, and the
backlog cites documents in those directories by path and section as the justification for the work.

A fresh clone gets the beads with every citation dangling.

## Verified

`bd list --status open,in_progress` returns **15** beads whose text cites a `docs/plans/…` path —
across the epic area (`Wallow-9cx8`, `Wallow-vsi3` and children, `Wallow-qw03` and children,
`Wallow-vmns`) and beyond it (`Wallow-tvn3`). The two load-bearing documents are:

- `docs/plans/2026-07-31/2134-mit-prior-art-harvest.md` (389 lines) — the prior-art research the
  feature-flags, billing and admin-app epics are all derived from. `Wallow-9cx8` cites "section 6"
  for its cost estimate; `Wallow-vsi3.1`'s FK answer is "in the harvest doc §5"; `Wallow-qw03`'s
  design is a port of what it describes.
- `docs/plans/2026-07-31/1954-multi-org-membership-implementation.md` (84,105 bytes) — named by the
  sequencing gate paragraph that four beads carry as their blocking condition.

Both exist only in this working tree. Nobody else can read either one.

## What "done" looks like

For each citation, one of three outcomes — chosen per citation, not applied wholesale:

1. **Inline it.** The conclusion the bead actually depends on gets written INTO the bead, so the
   citation becomes a provenance note rather than a dependency. This is the right answer for most of
   them: what a bead needs from the harvest doc is usually one paragraph, not the document.
2. **Promote it.** Decision content with lasting value moves into the tracked DocFX site under
   `docs/architecture/` (and into `docs/toc.yml`), per `docs/CLAUDE.md`. The prior-art harvest's
   design conclusions are the candidate — but the site is user-facing documentation, so promote
   conclusions, not the working document.
3. **Drop it.** Some citations are session scaffolding that nothing depends on.

A bead is finished on this axis when someone who has only ever run `git clone` and `bd bootstrap`
can act on it without asking anyone for a file.

## Scope note

Leave the `Wallow-yp3e` subtree alone — its three `[doc]` carrier beads (`.8`, `.9`, `.3.6`) hold
whole plan documents in their `design` field and are being handled separately. This bead covers the
`Wallow-9cx8` / `Wallow-vsi3` / `Wallow-qw03` / `Wallow-vmns` area and `Wallow-tvn3`.

Related but distinct: `Wallow-l77c` fixes four documents that assert a stale build ordering. That is
docs being wrong; this is docs being unreachable.
acceptance_criteria: docs/plans/ is tracked in git, so every open bead citing a plan path resolves from a fresh clone. Verified by: git ls-files docs/plans lists the cited documents; the two load-bearing docs (2026-07-31/2134-mit-prior-art-harvest.md and 2026-07-31/1954-multi-org-membership-implementation.md) are among them; docfx build still passes with plans/** excluded from the site; CLAUDE.md no longer instructs archiving plans out of the repo while an open bead cites them. Not closed until the commit is pushed. Audit citations are explicitly NOT covered - see the resolution note.
notes:
Filed from the bead backlog audit of 2026-08-02 (docs/audits/2026-08-02/0824-bead-backlog), finding H3. Re-derived while filing: 15 open beads cite a docs/plans path, not only the 30 in the epic area — Wallow-tvn3 is outside it. Note that Wallow-vsi3.9 (filed in the same pass) inherits the sequencing-gate paragraph and therefore one of these citations; it disappears when the gate paragraph is deleted after feat/multi-org-membership merges. The Wallow-yp3e subtree is deliberately out of scope and is being handled separately.
RESOLUTION CHANGED 2026-08-02, by owner decision: rather than inline/promote/drop each citation, docs/plans/ is simply no longer gitignored. Cheaper and strictly more complete for the plans axis.

What was done:
- .gitignore: dropped the docs/plans/ entry (docs/specs/, docs/superpowers/, docs/claude/, docs/audits/ stay ignored).
- CLAUDE.md: layout table row now says plans are tracked but excluded from the docs site; the archive-out-of-repo instruction is replaced with mark completed/superseded in place, do not archive while an open bead cites it.

It had ALREADY been archived out to ~/Documents/wallow-plans-archive/ and was missing on disk, so the 5 beads citing it (Wallow-qw03, qw03.3, vsi3.2, vsi3.9, h7vb) had a dead path, not just an unreachable one. Archive copy left in place.
- 53 files staged, ~27k lines. docfx.json already excluded plans/** so there is no docs-site impact.

Re-derived counts (the filing said 15; beads have moved since): 9 open beads cite a docs/plans path - 2y1t, 9cx8, h7vb, qw03, qw03.3, tvn3, vmns, vsi3.2, vsi3.9. Only 4 distinct plan documents are cited across all of them. docs/specs/ and docs/superpowers/ do not exist, so those axes are vacuous - but note they are NOT in docfx.json's exclude list, so anything landing there later needs adding before it is tracked.

OUT OF SCOPE, still unfiled: 24 open beads cite a docs/audits/ path - nearly triple the plans problem - and docs/audits/ (96 files, 3.1MB) remains gitignored. title: derive the module lists in ModuleRegistrationTests and ModuleToggleTests
description:
Two architecture test FILES hardcode per-module lists, so they run green while asserting nothing
about any module missing from those lists. This directly contradicts the promise `Wallow-vmns` is
built on — "architecture-test suites that judge a new module with zero edits" — and the lists are
already wrong today.

## The lists — FOUR across the two files, not two (citations corrected by Wallow-af3h.8)

All re-verified 2026-08-04 by reading the files. This bead's prose originally named only the first
and the fourth; the two `[InlineData]` lists below were named by NEITHER this bead NOR
`Wallow-vmns.1`, even though this bead's acceptance criterion ("neither file contains a hardcoded
module-name literal") already sweeps them in by wording.

**`api/tests/Wallow.Architecture.Tests/ModuleRegistrationTests.cs:37-41`** —
`WallowModules_ShouldInitialize_AllModulesWithDbContext` declares:

    string[] modulesWithDbContext = ["Notifications", "Announcements", "Identity", "Storage"];

There are SEVEN DbContexts under `api/src/Modules/`: those four plus `ApiKeysDbContext`,
`InquiriesDbContext` and `BrandingDbContext`. Three modules with real DbContexts are silently
outside the assertion, and the test is green.

**`ModuleRegistrationTests.cs:66-69`** — the four `[InlineData]` rows on
`Module_ShouldProvide_AddModuleExtensionMethod`: Notifications, Announcements, Identity, Storage.
ApiKeys, Inquiries and Branding are never checked for an `AddXModule` extension method.

**`ModuleRegistrationTests.cs:98-101`** — the four `[InlineData]` rows on
`Module_ShouldProvide_InitializeModuleExtensionMethod`, the same four names, with the same three
modules unchecked.

**`api/tests/Wallow.Architecture.Tests/Modules/ModuleToggleTests.cs:24-28,51-55`** — the in-memory
configuration blocks in `DisabledModule_ShouldNotRegister_Services` and
`AllModulesEnabled_ShouldRegister_AllModules` each enumerate five `FeatureManagement:Modules.*` keys
(Identity, Notifications, Announcements, Storage, Inquiries). ApiKeys and Branding are absent from
both. A new module's toggle is asserted by nothing.

**Cite that file by test-method name, not line number.** As of this edit there is uncommitted work
in the tree from another `Wallow-af3h` bead that renames the first method to
`CoreModule_ShouldStillRegister_WhenFeatureFlagDisabled`, adds a third flag block, and moves the
second from `:51-55` to `:74-78`. `:24-28,51-55` is correct at commit bdd26027 only. Whoever picks
this bead up should re-derive the line numbers before trusting them, and expect a THIRD block.

## What to do

Derive all four lists rather than extending them. The module set should come from whatever
mechanism `Wallow-vmns.1` lands (see `Wallow-af3h.6` — the approach is now `IWallowModule`, not the
assembly attribute this bead's prose assumed), or — if this is picked up first — from reflection
over the loaded module assemblies, the way `TestConstants.AllModules` already does. Extending the
literals by hand fixes today's omissions and leaves the footgun in place for the next module.

Adding a new module to `api/src/Modules/` must make all four assertions cover it with no edit to
either file. Prove that, do not assert it.

## Relationship to Wallow-vmns.1 — UNRESOLVED

`Wallow-vmns.1`'s acceptance criterion originally named "the two architecture tests" that derive
their module lists. Wallow-af3h.8 corrected the count and the citations: there are **SIX** hardcoded
lists repo-wide, not two and not four —

- `api/tests/Wallow.MigrationService.Tests/MigrationServiceTests.cs:189` (note the project: NOT
  `Wallow.Architecture.Tests`, which is what `.1` used to cite and which has no such file),
- the four in this bead's two files, listed above,
- and `api/tests/Wallow.Architecture.Tests/MigrationRemovalTests.cs:9-18`, which `.1` previously
  described as a module list but is **not** one: it is seven source-FILE PATHS
  (`_moduleExtensionFiles`) read via `File.ReadAllText` at `:37` and `:49`. That is a
  `.claude/rules/TESTING.md` violation, so its correct fix is DELETE, not derive.

This bead was filed as the alternative to widening `.1`'s criterion — keep `.1` scoped to the
registration collapse and land these lists here. **That choice has NOT been made.** Both beads
currently claim `ModuleRegistrationTests.cs:37-41` and `ModuleToggleTests.cs:24-28,51-55`, and the
af3h plan deliberately left the collision open. Settle ownership before starting either bead; if
`.1`'s criterion is widened instead, close this bead as absorbed rather than doing the work twice.
acceptance_criteria: Neither ModuleRegistrationTests.cs nor Modules/ModuleToggleTests.cs contains a hardcoded module-name literal; both derive their module set from the same mechanism the rest of the architecture suite uses. This covers FOUR literals, not the two the description originally named — ModuleRegistrationTests.cs:37-41, :66-69 and :98-101 (the last two being the [InlineData] theory rows, corrected in by Wallow-af3h.8) plus ModuleToggleTests.cs:24-28,51-55. All seven modules that own a DbContext are covered by the DbContext-initialization assertion, and every module feature toggle is covered by the toggle tests. Adding a new module under api/src/Modules/ brings it under all of them with zero edits to either file, demonstrated rather than asserted. ./scripts/run-tests.sh is green. CAVEAT: ownership of ModuleRegistrationTests.cs:37-41 and ModuleToggleTests.cs:24-28,51-55 is claimed by BOTH this bead and Wallow-vmns.1, and :66-69/:98-101 are claimed by neither. That scope collision is UNRESOLVED and was deliberately not decided by Wallow-af3h.8 or the af3h plan — settle it before starting.
notes:

Re-derived while filing and stronger than the audit states: ModuleRegistrationTests' modulesWithDbContext omits THREE modules that own a DbContext, not two — ApiKeys, Inquiries and Branding. Seven DbContexts exist under api/src/Modules/; the literal names four. CITATIONS CORRECTED 2026-08-05 by Wallow-af3h.8 (all six lists re-read on disk 2026-08-04, re-verified before this edit). Changes to this bead: (1) description retitled from "The two lists" to four, adding ModuleRegistrationTests.cs:66-69 and :98-101 — the [InlineData] rows on Module_ShouldProvide_AddModuleExtensionMethod and Module_ShouldProvide_InitializeModuleExtensionMethod, both listing only Notifications/Announcements/Identity/Storage. Those two were named by NEITHER this bead nor Wallow-vmns.1, though this AC already swept them in by wording. (2) The "Relationship to Wallow-vmns.1" section now carries the corrected repo-wide inventory: MigrationServiceTests.cs is in Wallow.MigrationService.Tests, NOT Wallow.Architecture.Tests; and MigrationRemovalTests.cs:9-18 is a seven-entry source-FILE-PATH array (_moduleExtensionFiles) read by File.ReadAllText at :37/:49, i.e. a TESTING.md violation to DELETE, not a module list to derive. NOT DECIDED HERE: ownership of the overlapping lists between this bead and Wallow-vmns.1 remains open — recorded as unresolved in both the description and the AC, not resolved.
LINE-NUMBER DRIFT HAZARD (2026-08-05). Same as recorded on Wallow-vmns.1: ModuleToggleTests.cs :24-28,51-55 holds only at commit bdd26027. Uncommitted sibling work in the tree adds a third hardcoded FeatureManagement block (in a new OptionalModules_ShouldNotRegister_WhenFeatureFlagsDisabled test) and moves the second block to :74-78. This bead AC says "neither file contains a hardcoded module-name literal", which is drift-proof and still correct — but the description count of FOUR literals becomes FIVE if that work lands. Re-count before starting.
