title: register the wallow/* lint plugin in packages/navigation, packages/ui and packages/forms
description:
The `wallow/*` lint rules are silently inert over three packages that render UI.

`package.json`'s `lint` script is `oxlint apps packages …`, so files under `packages/navigation`,
`packages/ui` and `packages/forms` ARE scanned. But `jsPlugins` is declared only by
`apps/wallow-web/.oxlintrc.json` and `apps/wallow-auth/.oxlintrc.json`; the three packages'
`.oxlintrc.json` files carry no `jsPlugins` key and no `wallow/*` rule entries at all. The plugin is
therefore never loaded for them and every rule in `packages/lint/src/rules/` passes vacuously over
their source. Nothing fails, which is why this has gone unnoticed.

This is a regression created by the shell extraction, not an original oversight: the code these
rules were written to police moved out of `apps/wallow-web` and into `packages/navigation`, leaving
the rules behind.

## What is unprotected

All five rules — `no-sidebar-inversion`, `no-tinted-text`, `text-heading-variant`, `zone-dag`,
`no-hand-rolled-mutation` — over the three packages that now hold most of the UI they were written
for. Concretely: `packages/navigation/src/app-shell.tsx:155` could be changed from
`BACKDROP_SCRIM = "bg-foreground/40"` to bare `bg-foreground` today and neither a rule nor a spec
would object.

## What to do

Add `jsPlugins: [{ "name": "wallow", "specifier": "@bc-solutions-coder/lint" }]` plus the
appropriate `wallow/*` rule severities to `packages/navigation/.oxlintrc.json`,
`packages/ui/.oxlintrc.json` and `packages/forms/.oxlintrc.json`, and add
`@bc-solutions-coder/lint` as a `workspace:*` devDependency to each of the three packages —
`apps/wallow-web/package.json:42` is the pattern.

Do NOT register the plugin from the root `.oxlintrc.json`. `packages/lint/CLAUDE.md` states that
constraint with the measurements behind it; read it before starting.

Decide per rule and per package which severities apply — `packages/ui` is the catalog that DEFINES
the primitives `no-tinted-text` and `text-heading-variant` police, so a rule that is right for a
consumer may need an override or an exemption there. Each of the two apps enables a different
subset today (wallow-web: `no-sidebar-inversion`, `no-tinted-text`, `zone-dag`; wallow-auth:
`no-hand-rolled-mutation`, `no-sidebar-inversion`, `text-heading-variant`, `zone-dag`), which is
itself worth reconciling.

Expect real violations on first run. Fixing them is part of this bead; blanket-disabling a rule to
get green is not.

This is not `Wallow-succ`'s job. `Wallow-succ` adds the missing SPEC for the scrim's computed
colour — one artifact, one file. This bead restores the lint layer over three packages and protects
four rules that have nothing to do with the scrim.
acceptance_criteria: packages/navigation/.oxlintrc.json, packages/ui/.oxlintrc.json and packages/forms/.oxlintrc.json each declare the wallow jsPlugins entry and an explicit severity for every wallow/* rule that applies to them, with any exemption written as a scoped override carrying its reason. Each of the three packages depends on @bc-solutions-coder/lint as workspace:*. The plugin is NOT registered from the root .oxlintrc.json. Introducing a bare bg-foreground into packages/navigation/src/app-shell.tsx makes pnpm lint fail. pnpm lint and pnpm lint:tests are both green with no rule blanket-disabled to achieve it.
notes:
Filed from the bead backlog audit of 2026-08-02 (docs/audits/2026-08-02/0824-bead-backlog), finding H15 — the second of the two missing layers over the mobile scrim. Verified on disk: the three packages' .oxlintrc.json files contain no jsPlugins key, while package.json's lint script scans 'apps packages', so their files are linted with the wallow rules unloaded. The audit records the framing correction too: this is the confirmed case, not a hypothesis to audit. Wallow-succ covers the missing spec and is a separate, smaller bead.
Fixed. All three packages now register the plugin and enable ALL FIVE rules.

Configs: packages/{navigation,ui,forms}/.oxlintrc.json each gained the jsPlugins
entry plus explicit severities, and each package gained @bc-solutions-coder/lint as
a workspace:* devDependency. The root .oxlintrc.json was NOT touched. Reasons are
written as `//` comments beside each entry — oxlint parses its config as JSONC. Two
specs that read a nested config back (packages/sdk/src/oxlint-guardrails.test.ts's
readNestedConfig, packages/forms/src/core/package-scaffold.test.ts) now strip line
comments before JSON.parse; a third reader must do the same.

Severities: all five everywhere, rather than a per-package subset. zone-dag is
structurally inert in a package (it derives zones from a tsconfig.json `paths` map
and none of the three declares one) but costs nothing and goes live the moment one
does. text-heading-variant takes `{ levels: { h2: "subheading" } }` — NOT
wallow-auth's `h1: false`, because packages/ui's PageHeader is where the page's one
level-1 heading legitimately lives. The four class-string rules are off for
*.test.*/*.stories.tsx exactly as in both apps; zone-dag deliberately is not.

Two scoped exemptions, each naming ONE file rather than a folder:
- packages/ui/src/components/drawer/drawer.styles.ts, no-sidebar-inversion.
  drawerIndentBackgroundRecipe FADES a bare bg-foreground in behind the shrinking
  app UI (opacity-0 -> data-[active]:opacity-100); a fixed alpha baked into the
  utility is not something a transition can animate from. This is the case
  packages/lint/CLAUDE.md predicted, and it turned out to be one recipe, not the
  catalog — so the doc's "no-sidebar-inversion must never reach the catalog" is now
  wrong and was rewritten.
- packages/forms/src/form/use-app-form.ts, no-hand-rolled-mutation. Its mutationFn
  states no request; it is the stand-in for the no-mutation escape hatch, there so
  exactly one useMutation runs on every path.

ONE real violation on first run, and it was FIXED not exempted:
packages/ui/src/components/button/button.styles.ts:42 carried
`hover:text-primary/80` on the `link` variant. link's hover is now the underline
alone — the opacity suffix the solid variants use on bg-* has no text-side
equivalent branding.json can reach. button.test.tsx's "gives the %s variant a hover
treatment" case still passes on hover:underline.

Acceptance verified by measurement, not inspection: turning app-shell.tsx:155's
BACKDROP_SCRIM from "bg-foreground/40" into bare "bg-foreground" makes pnpm lint
fail with wallow(no-sidebar-inversion) at that line (then reverted). Probe files
also confirmed text-heading-variant fires in packages/ui and
no-hand-rolled-mutation fires in packages/forms outside the exempted path. pnpm
check exits 0 end to end.

Docs corrected because the code contradicted them: packages/lint/CLAUDE.md (five
registrations, a "Who enables what" table, the JSONC reader note, the vacuous-pass
failure mode), apps/CLAUDE.md (the "the gate must never reach packages/ui" claim),
CLAUDE.md's repo table, and the three packages' own CLAUDE.md files.

Not done, filed as Wallow-8sao: the two apps still enable different subsets, and
wallow-auth has three live hover:text-primary/80 links that no-tinted-text would
catch if it were on there. Also found: apps/examples/minimal-app has no nested
config at all, so every wallow/* rule passes vacuously over it too.

title: create the Billing module skeleton, schema and migration
description:
No child of `Wallow-vsi3` brings the Billing module into existence. `Wallow-vsi3.2` writes a
`billing_events` table, `.3` writes invoices, `.4` adds a Stripe gateway — all into a module that
does not exist. The analogue of `Wallow-qw03.3` (the FeatureFlags skeleton) is simply missing from
this epic, and every schema child of it is unbuildable until this lands.

Ground truth: there are seven modules under `api/src/Modules/` and none of them is Billing. The only
tracked billing-named file in the repo is `FakeBillingController.cs`, and there are zero Stripe
references anywhere in `api/src`. The READMEs that describe a Billing module are describing something
that has never been built.

## What to build

The standard four-project module — Domain, Application, Infrastructure, Api — copying ApiKeys as the
reference module, or using the add-module skill if `Wallow-vmns.2` has produced one by then. Its own
Postgres schema (`billing`), registered through whatever the host registration mechanism is at that
point (`Wallow-vmns.1` may have replaced the 7-touch-point registration with assembly-attribute
discovery before this is claimed — follow whatever is current, do not re-derive it).

No cross-schema foreign key from `billing` to Identity's tables. `Wallow-vsi3.1` records how
subscription-to-tenant is expressed without one; take its answer rather than inventing a second.

This bead brings the module into existence and nothing more — no ledger, no invoices, no gateway.
Those are `.2`, `.3` and `.4`.

SEQUENCING GATE: no schema work here until `feat/multi-org-membership` merges into `main` — every
table in this epic keys off tenant identity, and that branch makes Membership a first-class
aggregate and DROPS `WallowUser.TenantId`, so starting first means rewriting the migrations. The
trigger is the MERGE, not the branch work. Phase 2 of
docs/plans/2026-07-31/1954-multi-org-membership-implementation.md has already landed ON THE BRANCH
(commits 2265cdfd..e03f668d, where `WallowUser.TenantId` is genuinely gone), but `main` still
declares `public Guid TenantId { get; set; }` on `WallowUser`. So the old wording — "until Phase 2
lands" — now reads as "proceed" to anyone checking `main`, which is precisely the case this gate
exists to stop. Check the real condition with:

    git merge-base --is-ancestor e03f668d main

Delete this paragraph only once that command exits 0. Until then the gate is live.

The migration must apply cleanly to a fresh database. No staged migration, no expand/contract, no
backfill — there are no users and no data to preserve.
acceptance_criteria: A Billing module exists under api/src/Modules/Billing as the standard four-project Clean Architecture module, owns its own 'billing' Postgres schema, and is registered with the host through the current registration mechanism. Its initial migration applies cleanly to a fresh database. No foreign key crosses from the billing schema into another module's schema. The module's own architecture tests pass alongside the existing suite, and ./scripts/run-tests.sh is green. No ledger, invoice, gateway or webhook code ships in this bead.
notes: Filed from the bead backlog audit of 2026-08-02 (docs/audits/2026-08-02/0824-bead-backlog), section 4 — the Wallow-vsi3 epic verdict: 'no child brings the Billing module into existence at all, the analogue of qw03.3 is simply missing'. Dependency shape deliberately mirrors the FeatureFlags epic, where Wallow-qw03.3 (skeleton) is blocked by the boundary spike and blocks the evaluator. Wallow-vsi3 itself is DEFERRED (ledger before gateway); this bead is deferred with it and unblocks the moment the epic is picked up.
close_reason: Deferred indefinitely: closed to keep the active backlog clean. Not rejected — the designs stand and remain readable via 'bd show'. Reopen the relevant child if/when the workstream is picked up.

title: build the operator surfaces that are curl-only today, every mutation audited
description:
This is `Wallow-9cx8`'s payload. Without it the epic can be marked complete with its stated goal —
"an operator can sign in to a dedicated admin app and perform the tasks that are curl-only today,
with every mutation audited" — entirely untouched.

The epic's other children are an authentication decision (`.1`), an app scaffold (`.2`) and an
OpenAPI-surface spike (`.3`). None performs an operator task and none delivers mutation auditing.
`Wallow-9cx8`'s acceptance criteria have been narrowed to what that tree actually delivers, and they
name this gap explicitly; widen them back only once this bead lands.

## The curl-only tasks to bring into the admin app

Three controller surfaces exist today with no UI whatsoever. Read the permission story precisely —
it is looser than "admin controllers" implies, and an app built from a skim would gate the wrong
things:

- `AdminAnnouncementsController.cs:22-23` — route `.../admin/announcements`, gated on
  `AnnouncementManage` (NOT `AdminAccess`).
- `AdminChangelogController.cs:18-19` — route `.../admin/changelog`, gated on `ChangelogManage`.
- `ClientsController.cs:22,24` — carries `AdminAccess`, but on route
  `v{version:apiVersion}/identity/clients`, not under `/admin/*` at all. OIDC client administration.

## Mutation auditing

Every write these screens perform must produce an audit event. The mechanism already exists — see
`docs/operations/audit-events.md` and the Identity module's `AuthAuditEventHandlers.cs` — so this is
extending an existing pipeline to a new set of mutations, not inventing one. Auditing is a criterion

title: packages/navigation toggle spec leaks a real navigation into the vitest iframe
description:
Under full-workspace runs (pnpm check / pnpm -r test), packages/navigation/src/app-shell.toggle.test.tsx lets a real navigation escape into the vitest browser iframe. This tears down the runner and takes 4 sibling test files (28 tests) with it as collateral damage. Passes in isolation, so it presents as an intermittent full-run flake.

Pre-existing; found while running the Phase 6 gate for Wallow-yp3e.2 (gate itself passed on a clean re-run with nothing changed).

Fix per .claude/rules/TESTING.md: observe the hand-off at the Navigation API 'navigate' event — read event.destination.url and preventDefault() so the runner stays put. Note location is [Unforgeable] in real Chromium, so vi.stubGlobal cannot shadow it.
acceptance_criteria: app-shell.toggle.test.tsx no longer triggers a real navigation; full-workspace pnpm check passes repeatedly with no collateral failures in the 4 sibling files
notes:
PLAN: docs/plans/2026-08-02/1744-no-source-tests-design.md — Phase 1. Now BLOCKS Wallow-succ: packages/navigation browser runs must be trustworthy before a computed-colour spec is added to that package, or the new spec inherits a file neighbourhood that intermittently tears down the runner.

LEAD, found during the design pass — verify before fixing, this may not be the whole story. app-shell.toggle.test.tsx ALREADY mocks @tanstack/react-router's Link with a preventDefault handler. But the handler is declared BEFORE {...rest} in the JSX, so any onClick arriving through the spread WINS. AppNav renders destinations as NavigationMenu.Link render={<Link … />} (app-nav.tsx:117), and Base UI's render prop merges its own handlers in — which plausibly clobbers the guard. Reordering the spread may be the whole fix.

The bead's prescribed fix (listen for the Navigation API 'navigate' event, read event.destination.url, preventDefault) is the more robust guard regardless, since location is [Unforgeable] in real Chromium and vi.stubGlobal cannot shadow it.
DIAGNOSIS CHALLENGED 2026-08-02 — verify before fixing, per this bead's own instruction.

1. The Base-UI-merged-onClick mechanism requires a NAV LINK CLICK. app-shell.toggle.test.tsx never clicks one: all seven of its userEvent.click calls target dashboard-nav-toggle, a plain <button> (:57, :65, :66, :76, :131). The file that DOES click a destination is app-shell.mobile.test.tsx:139 ('closes the drawer when a nav link is activated'). So the file attribution may just be 'whichever spec was running when the runner died', not the leak site.

2. The onClick-before-spread ordering bug IS real and IS confirmed at app-shell.toggle.test.tsx:24-27 — the preventDefault handler is declared before {...rest}, so a spread onClick wins.

3. But ALL 11 nav specs that mock @tanstack/react-router carry the IDENTICAL defective stub, one preventDefault each: app-nav.catalog, app-nav.contrast, app-nav.destinations, app-nav.modes, app-nav.sidebar-surface, app-shell.catalog-control, app-shell.mobile, app-shell.responsive, app-shell.ssr-flash, app-shell, app-shell.toggle. If the ordering is the bug then the fix is all 11 files or a hoisted shared stub in shell.fixtures.tsx — not one file.

FIRST ACTION: reproduce under a full-workspace run and identify which file actually leaks.
SCOUT REPRODUCTION + DIAGNOSIS (read-only), 2026-08-02.

## 1. REPRODUCED, 2/~40 solo runs, more readily under added load

Command: `cd packages/navigation && pnpm exec vitest run --configLoader runner` (repeated in a
loop). Isolated solo runs: ~1/33 reproduction rate (33 clean solo attempts across several
batches, 1 failure). Under artificial load (three other packages' `pnpm test` running
concurrently in the background: ui, forms, wallow-web), reproduced on attempt 3 of 10. Exact
error, IDENTICAL both times (only the sessionId UUID differs):

```
Error: Failed to run the test /Users/traveler/Repos/Wallow/packages/navigation/src/app-shell.toggle.test.tsx.
Caused by: Error: Cannot connect to the iframe. Did you change the location or submitted a
form? If so, don't forget to call `event.preventDefault()` to avoid reloading the page.
Received URL: http://localhost:63315/dashboard/organizations
Expected: http://localhost:63315/?sessionId=...&iframeId=.../app-shell.toggle.test.tsx
 Test Files  11 passed (16)
      Tests  104 passed (132)
     Errors  1 error
```
132-104=28 tests missing, matches the bead's "28 tests" figure exactly (toggle + 4 siblings = 5
of 16 files never report). The leaked URL is ALWAYS `/dashboard/organizations` — the first
entry in `fixtureDestinations` (shell.fixtures.tsx:28-31, id "nav-organizations", `to:
"/dashboard/organizations"`).

## 2. IDENTIFY THE REAL LEAK SITE — it is NOT app-shell.toggle.test.tsx, and the ordering bug is NOT firing

Grepped every `userEvent.click`/`.focus()`+`keyboard("{Enter}")` across all 13 browser-project
nav spec files (app-nav.*.test.tsx x7, app-shell.*.test.tsx x6). Full inventory:

- app-shell.toggle.test.tsx: 5 clicks, ALL on `dashboard-nav-toggle` (a `<button>`, not a Link).
- app-shell.responsive.test.tsx: 1 click (`dashboard-nav-mobile-menu`, a button) + focus/Enter/Space
  keyboard activation of the same two buttons.
- app-shell.mobile.test.tsx: clicks `dashboard-nav-mobile-menu`, `dashboard-nav-backdrop` (both
  buttons), and **`dashboard-nav-settings`** (line 139 — this is the ONLY click anywhere in the
  package on an actual nav-destination `Link`).
- Every other file (app-nav.catalog/contrast/destinations/modes/sidebar-surface/test/theme,
  app-shell.catalog-control/ssr-flash/test): zero clicks, hover-only or render/assert-only.

**Nothing in the suite ever clicks, focuses, or activates `dashboard-nav-organizations`** — the
exact destination that leaked. So the failure cannot be a stray click on that link; it is
misattributed to app-shell.toggle.test.tsx only because Vitest's orchestrator surfaces the
error at the point it tries to load THAT file's iframe and finds the URL already stolen —
that's a scheduling artifact, not evidence toggle's code did anything wrong.

## 3. THE ONCLICK-BEFORE-SPREAD MECHANISM: CONFIRMED REAL, but not the current leak site

Read `node_modules/.pnpm/@base-ui+react@1.6.0.../merge-props/mergeProps.mjs` (installed
package, no network doc access available to this scout — MCP ref-context tools were not present
in this session's toolset). Confirmed mechanism: Base UI's `mergeProps` DOES merge an `onClick`
computed from `NavItem`'s `onClick={props.onNavigate}` (app-nav.tsx:122) into a single function
that Base UI hands to the `render` element (the mocked `Link`) as a plain `onClick` prop —
merged handlers run right-to-left with `event.preventBaseUIHandler()` as the only escape, but by
the time it reaches our test's `Link` stub it is just one ordinary `onClick` in props. So:

- Stub shape A (SAFE — 9 files: app-nav.catalog/contrast/destinations/modes/sidebar-surface,
  app-shell.mobile/responsive/ssr-flash, plus app-nav.theme has no onClick at all so is moot):
  `onClick` destructured OUT of `...rest` and wrapped — `event.preventDefault()` always fires
  first, `rest` can no longer carry a conflicting `onClick`. Safe regardless of merge order.
- Stub shape B (DEFECTIVE — 4 files: app-shell.toggle.test.tsx:11-32, app-shell.test.tsx:11-32,
  app-shell.catalog-control.test.tsx:11-32, app-nav.test.tsx:11-26): own `onClick` (or none, in
  app-nav.test.tsx's case) declared BEFORE `{...rest}`; if `rest.onClick` exists it wins per JSX
  object-literal semantics, silently discarding the local preventDefault (or, in app-nav.test.tsx,
  there is no preventDefault at all — `<a href={to} {...rest}>`).

**But none of the 4 defective-stub files ever click a Link** (see item 2), so this defect is
currently LATENT, not firing. Do not conflate it with the actual bug — it is real, worth fixing
as defense-in-depth, but it did not cause either of the two reproductions above.

## 4. WORKING THEORY for the actual mechanism: Vitest browser-mode iframe orchestration race

Given (a) the leaked destination is always the first nav item, rendered at a small, highly
consistent screen offset across every `ShellFixture` render regardless of viewport/file, (b) no
test anywhere targets it, (c) reproduction rate rises under concurrent system load, and (d) the
failure always surfaces as "the NEXT file's iframe won't reload, the CURRENT one is stuck at a
navigated URL" — the most consistent explanation is a race in Vitest browser mode's iframe
pool/reuse under `@vitest/browser-playwright`, not an app-level click-handler bug: a real
Chromium pointer event dispatched by one file's `userEvent.click` (page-relative screen
coordinates) lands on a DIFFERENT, concurrently-mounted iframe if the intended iframe isn't
frontmost/interactive at the exact dispatch instant, and whichever nav item is currently
rendered at that shared screen offset absorbs the click. `packages/navigation/vitest.config.ts`
configures a single Chromium `instances: [{ browser: "chromium" }]`
(`createVitestProjects` default) with no `fileParallelism`/`isolate` override, so Vitest's
default browser-mode file concurrency applies. This is an Analysis, not a proof — I could not
pin the exact culprit file/interaction with the reproduction budget available; a further
narrowing would need Vitest's own iframe-scheduling internals or a `DEBUG`-level trace across a
caught repro. Flagging for whoever picks up the fix rather than guessing further.

## 5. FIX SURFACE — recommendation

a) **The Navigation API `navigate`-event guard the bead prescribes IS available and workable
   here.** Verified directly (not via docs) by launching the actual pinned Chromium build via
   `playwright-core` (same binary `@vitest/browser-playwright` drives) and evaluating in-page:
   `chromium version: 149.0.7827.55`, `typeof window.navigation === "object"` at top level AND
   `typeof <nested-iframe>.contentWindow.navigation === "object"`. So a `vitest.setup.ts` (or a
   shared fixture's `beforeEach`) can register `window.navigation.addEventListener("navigate",
   (e) => e.preventDefault())` and it will actually intercept a same-document navigation
   originating inside the vitest browser iframe — this is a real, page-level guard independent
   of any component's own `onClick`/`preventDefault` wiring, and is robust against exactly the
   race described in #4 (it doesn't matter which iframe/element the click actually landed on;
   any resulting top-level navigation inside that iframe is vetoed at the Navigation API).
   **This is the recommended fix** — install it once, centrally, rather than touching 13 stub
   files, precisely because the current evidence shows the click that navigates is not
   reliably attributable to any one spec's stub.
b) The 4 defective router-Link stubs (app-shell.toggle, app-shell.test, app-shell.catalog-control,
   app-nav.test — see file+line list in #3) are still worth reordering (`onClick` destructured
   before `...rest`, matching the other 9 files' shape) as defense-in-depth, but this is
   independent of and does not substitute for (a): fixing them would not have prevented either
   reproduction, since none of the 4 files click a Link.
c) A shared router-Link stub (hoisted next to `shell.fixtures.tsx`, e.g.
   `router-link.fixture.tsx`, imported the same way `shell.fixtures.tsx` already is —
   `import { ... } from "./shell.fixtures"`) does NOT conflict with anything in
   packages/navigation/CLAUDE.md: `shell.fixtures.tsx` is already unexported from `src/index.ts`
   (confirmed by reading `src/index.ts` — no `shell.fixtures` or `router-link` entry), and the
   "one entry" / "no @bc-solutions-coder/ui barrel" rules govern the PACKAGE's own public
   subpath surface, not sibling-file imports between spec/fixture files inside `src/`. So
   hoisting is safe if (b) is done, but (a) alone is the higher-leverage, lower-risk fix given
   the diagnosis above.

## File+line list for whoever fixes this

- Recommended primary fix: new `navigate`-event guard, likely in
  `packages/navigation/vitest.setup.ts` (currently just imports two stylesheets) or a
  `beforeEach` in a shared fixture.
- Defective stub ordering (secondary, defense-in-depth): app-shell.toggle.test.tsx:11-32,
  app-shell.test.tsx:11-32, app-shell.catalog-control.test.tsx:11-32, app-nav.test.tsx:11-26.
- Safe stub shape to copy if hoisting: app-shell.mobile.test.tsx:17-40 (LinkStubProps with
  `onClick` destructured out, wrapped, chained).
RED PHASE, TDD. The guard now has a NAME, an API and a spec; it has no implementation. 4 tests, file confirmed failing.

## FILES

- packages/testing/src/navigation-escape.ts (NEW, scaffold — signatures + doc, all bodies no-op)
- packages/testing/package.json (NEW subpath ./navigation-escape in exports + publishConfig.exports)
- packages/testing/vite.config.ts (entry 'navigation-escape')
- packages/testing/tsconfig.build.json (include src/navigation-escape.ts)
- packages/navigation/src/navigation-escape.test.tsx (NEW, 4 tests — the red spec)

Home is packages/testing, not packages/navigation, per .claude/rules/TESTING.md ('spec helpers live in @bc-solutions-coder/testing'). It is a browser-only module, so it gets its OWN subpath and must never join the barrel — the barrel is loaded in plain Node at vitest config time. packages/navigation already imports @bc-solutions-coder/testing/contrast from three specs with no extraBrowserOptimizeDeps entry, so the new subpath needed none either (confirmed: the spec ran).

## SYMBOLS (packages/testing/src/navigation-escape.ts)

  export interface NavigationEscape { readonly url: string }
  export const NAVIGATION_ESCAPE_MESSAGE = 'Navigation escaped the test iframe'
  export function installNavigationEscapeGuard(): void      // idempotent; setup file calls once
  export function navigationEscapes(): readonly NavigationEscape[]   // non-draining read
  export function clearNavigationEscapes(): void
  export function assertNoNavigationEscape(): void          // throws naming each URL, THEN clears

Why five and not two. navigationEscapes() is non-draining so a spec can poll it with vi.waitFor without each poll eating the result (see the browser-spec-sync-read-races memory — a sync read straight after an awaited userEvent.click races). assertNoNavigationEscape() drains AFTER throwing so one escape fails ONE test rather than every test behind it. clearNavigationEscapes() is what the guard's own spec uses to keep the project afterEach quiet after a deliberate provocation.

## THE RED OUTPUT — deterministic, identical to the bead's symptom

cd packages/navigation && pnpm test

  Error: Failed to run the test .../packages/navigation/src/navigation-escape.test.tsx.
  Caused by: Error: Cannot connect to the iframe. Did you change the location or submitted a
  form? If so, don't forget to call `event.preventDefault()` to avoid reloading the page.
  Received URL: http://localhost:63315/dashboard/organizations
  Expected: http://localhost:63315/?sessionId=...&iframeId=.../navigation-escape.test.tsx
   Test Files  9 passed (17)
        Tests  97 passed (132)
       Errors  1 error

Byte-for-byte the scout's error, including the leaked URL /dashboard/organizations — and it now fires EVERY run instead of ~1/33. Collateral damage is quantified in the same line: 8 of 17 files and 35 of 132 tests never report. None of the spec's own 4 tests report either; the file dies whole. THAT IS THE POINT OF THIS BEAD — today an escape is a teardown that names the wrong file, not an assertion that names the URL.

## PROVOCATION — deliberate, not the race

Per instruction the spec does NOT wait on the intermittent trigger. It provokes two ways, both deterministic:
1. a bare <a data-testid='escape-hatch' href='/dashboard/organizations'> clicked with a real pointer — the exact escape shape and exact URL the scout observed;
2. globalThis.location.assign('/dashboard/organizations') — a programmatic hand-off NO router-Link stub could ever intercept.

(2) is the argument for the central fix over reordering the 4 defective stubs: it is caught by (a) and cannot be caught by (b). Deliberately NOT reproduced: the Base-UI-merged-onClick mechanism. The scout established it is latent and did not cause either reproduction, and pinning Base UI's mergeProps internals in a spec is the brittle-structural-assertion shape this repo's testing rules push back on. Reordering those 4 stubs stays worthwhile as defence in depth but is not what this spec measures.

## FEASIBILITY OF GREEN — VERIFIED END TO END, not just 'the API exists'

Ran a throwaway probe spec inside the real packages/navigation browser project (written, run, DELETED — no debris; confirm with git status). It registered navigation.addEventListener('navigate', e => { seen.push(e.destination.url); e.preventDefault(); }) and drove both provocations:

  Test Files  1 passed (1)
       Tests  2 passed (2)

So inside the vitest iframe, in the pinned Chromium: window.navigation is a live object, the navigate event fires for BOTH an unprevented anchor default and location.assign, event.destination.url carries the absolute URL, and preventDefault() keeps the runner in place. The implementer is not being handed a dead end.

## INERT WHEN NOTHING ESCAPES — proven

With the scaffold present (new module, new subpath, new build entries) but the provocation spec moved aside:

  Test Files  16 passed (16)
       Tests  132 passed (132)

No existing packages/navigation spec is disturbed by the guard existing. The spec's own first test ('raises nothing while a spec navigates nowhere') is the in-file inertness assertion and passes vacuously in red — expected, and it must keep passing in green.

## GATES RUN

pnpm lint = 0, pnpm lint:tests = 0, pnpm format:check = clean, both packages' typecheck = clean, pnpm --filter @bc-solutions-coder/testing build + publint = clean (only the pre-existing 'sideEffects' suggestion).

## ISSUES FOR THE IMPLEMENTER

1. DO NOT LEAVE RED ON MAIN. The provocation spec really navigates until the guard exists. Between red and green the packages/navigation suite is deterministically broken and takes 8 sibling files with it. Green and red must land together.
2. THE WIRING IS PART OF GREEN, and the spec depends on it. The spec deliberately does NOT call installNavigationEscapeGuard() — it proves the PROJECT-WIDE guard, so packages/navigation/vitest.setup.ts must both install it and register afterEach(assertNoNavigationEscape). That setup file is currently two CSS imports and has no vitest import; note packages/navigation/tsconfig.json's include is ['src','vite.config.ts','vitest.config.ts'] — vitest.setup.ts is NOT typechecked, so an error there will not surface in pnpm typecheck.
3. IDEMPOTENCE IS LOAD-BEARING, not decoration. Setup files re-evaluate per browser context; a second install must not double-record or leak a listener.
4. FOUR PLACES, NOT THREE, to add a packages/testing subpath. package.json exports, package.json publishConfig.exports, vite.config.ts entries, tsconfig.build.json include. I missed the last one first: build and typecheck both passed and publint failed with 'publishConfig.exports["./navigation-escape"].types is ./dist/navigation-escape.d.ts but the file does not exist'. Already fixed here; flagged so it is not re-broken.
5. NAVIGATION API TYPES. TS7 (Project Corsa) resolved window.navigation fine for the SPEC, which never touches it. The implementation does. If lib.dom in this toolchain lacks the Navigation API, prefer a narrow local structural type over a global augmentation.
6. SCOPE OFFER, NOT DONE HERE. The guard is now reusable by every browser project (wallow-web, wallow-auth, ui, forms). Wiring those is not this bead and should be its own.
7. THE FAILURE MESSAGE IS PINNED BY REGEX: new RegExp(`${NAVIGATION_ESCAPE_MESSAGE}[\\s\\S]*${ESCAPE_PATH}`, 'u'). The message must open with NAVIGATION_ESCAPE_MESSAGE and carry the escaped URL after it. Prose between and after is free.
GREEN PHASE, TDD. The central Navigation-API guard is implemented and WIRED ON BY DEFAULT. The red spec passes unedited; packages/navigation is 17 files / 136 tests, and a leak now fails one test by name instead of dropping the iframe.

Three reasons, in order of force.

1. IT IS NOT OPTIONAL UNDER THE CONSTRAINT. The red spec imports the literal specifier

## SYMBOLS (packages/testing/src/navigation-escape.ts) — the red phase's API, unchanged

export interface NavigationEscape { readonly url: string }
export const NAVIGATION_ESCAPE_MESSAGE = "Navigation escaped the test iframe"
export function installNavigationEscapeGuard(): void

## ONE DESIGN ADDITION BEYOND THE RED PHASE'S API — cross-document only

`vetoNavigation` returns early on `event.destination.sameDocument`. A same-document `navigate` is
what `history.pushState` and a hash change raise, and what a real router raises on every route
change; it does not touch the iframe, so vetoing it would break routing in exchange for nothing.
Both of the spec's provocations are cross-document, so this narrows nothing this bead measures — and
it is what makes the guard safe to wire into wallow-web/wallow-auth later, where a real
TanStack router IS in the graph. Without this filter that follow-up would be unshippable.

`event.cancelable` is also checked before `preventDefault()`. A traversal the page is not permitted
to stop still gets RECORDED, so the report explains the teardown that follows instead of going
silent.

title: Suspended and Denied memberships are unreachable from any list endpoint
description: reinstate and clearDenial exist as endpoints and cannot be driven from any UI, because nothing lists the memberships they act on. Found while planning Wallow-yp3e.3 (docs/plans/2026-08-01/2019-membership-dashboard-screens.md section 7A).
design:
OrganizationService.GetMembersAsync filters to MembershipStatus.Active (OrganizationService.cs:211-212). MembershipReviewService.GetPendingAsync filters to MembershipStatus.Pending (MembershipReviewService.cs:32-33). Nothing returns Suspended or Denied.

So POST /v1/identity/organizations/{id}/members/{userId}/reinstate (OrganizationsController.cs:245-259) and DELETE .../{userId}/denial (:206-220) have no list to drive them from - and by extension suspend has no way to show its result. This is a BACKEND gap, not a screen gap: the wallow-web membership screens deliberately expose approve/deny/assign/remove/revoke and NOT reinstate/clearDenial/suspend until it is closed.

Two shapes worth weighing: a status filter on GET {id}/members (query parameter, one endpoint, changes an existing contract - free on this pre-release branch), or a sibling listing endpoint alongside members/pending. The filter is the smaller surface and matches how GetPendingAsync already works.

Whichever lands, it needs the OpenAPI snapshot and SDK client regenerated afterwards (packages/sdk/CLAUDE.md).
acceptance_criteria:
- Suspended and Denied memberships are listable through the API by a caller holding OrganizationsManageMembers.
- The listing carries enough to render a row (user identity plus the status and its timestamp).
- Backend tests cover each status appearing in exactly the listing that claims it.
- packages/sdk/openapi/v1.json and the generated client are regenerated and committed.
- ./scripts/run-tests.sh identity passes.

title: Member role management screen (assign/remove, own-org gated)
description: Grant and remove a role on an existing member. Route apps/wallow-web/src/app/routes/dashboard/organizations/$orgId/members.tsx (id '/dashboard/organizations/$orgId/members'), feature component apps/wallow-web/src/features/organizations/components/MemberRoles.tsx. Plan: docs/plans/2026-08-01/2019-membership-dashboard-screens.md section 5.
design:
THE TRAP THAT SHAPES THIS SCREEN - read first.
UsersController.AssignRole writes tenantContext.TenantId.Value at line 179; RemoveRole does the same at line 198. NEITHER TAKES AN ORGANIZATION ID. On a route keyed by $orgId, an operator who can READ a foreign organization would issue a role grant that lands silently in their OWN organization. Nothing in the API rejects it; the request returns 204.

MITIGATION (not optional): render the role controls only when $orgId is the caller's own organization. The available check is organizationsGetAllOptions - OrganizationsController.GetAll filters its result down to exactly the caller's own tenant at lines 76-78 (orgs.Where(o => o.Id == tenantId)) - so the condition is 'the single returned row's id === orgId'. Otherwise render the roster READ-ONLY with an explanatory note (testid member-roles-foreign-org) and mount no mutation. Record this reasoning in the component header.

BACKEND:
- GET /v1/identity/organizations/{id}/members (OrganizationsController.cs:100-110) -> UserDto[]. OrganizationService.GetMembersAsync (:201-231) filters to MembershipStatus.Active (:211-212) and maps PER-ORG role names.
- POST /v1/identity/users/{userId}/roles (UsersController.cs:151-181) - rejects the reserved global-admin role name.
- DELETE /v1/identity/users/{userId}/roles/{roleName} (:187-200).
- GET /v1/identity/roles (RolesController.cs:27-34) -> [{ Name }].
UserDto(Guid Id, string Email, string FirstName, string LastName, bool Enabled, IReadOnlyList<string> Roles).

SDK - all already generated: organizationsGetMembersOptions/QueryKey (react-query.gen.ts:1034/1029), rolesGetRolesOptions (:1209), usersAssignRoleMutation (:1400), usersRemoveRoleMutation (:1415), organizationsGetAllOptions (:976).
Both mutations sweep queriesForOperation(organizationsGetMembersQueryKey({ client, path: { id: orgId } })).

THE FORM - the one place here with a field, so it goes through useAppForm + AppForm. Copy AddMemberForm (MemberList.tsx:211-267):
  useAppForm({ schema, defaultValues, mutation: usersAssignRoleMutation({ client: sdk.client }), toVariables, onSuccess, fallbackError })
  <AppForm form={form} testIdPrefix="organization-member-role" ...>
- The generated factory goes in WHOLE (MemberList.tsx:217). useAppForm infers TError from it; destructuring breaks the RFC 7807 error split.
- Every testid DERIVES from testIdPrefix + the kebab-cased field name; the message id is that + '-error'. Prefix organization-member-role and field roleName give organization-member-role-role-name and -role-name-error. An explicit testId prop overrides BOTH - use it only with a stated reason.
- The field catalog is Text/Textarea/Select/Checkbox/Password only. A role picker is a SelectField. Anything else goes through the AppField render prop.
- Select is NOT a native element: role='option' divs portalled to <body>, only while open. Drive it with chooseOption from @bc-solutions-coder/testing/catalog-select; userEvent.selectOptions only drives an HTMLSelectElement.
- jsx-max-depth is 2, and AppForm > AppField > field.X already spends it - split the field block into its own component the way OrganizationDetail.tsx:132-133 does.
- Fill fields with userEvent.fill, never userEvent.type (one CDP round trip per character; a measured source of intermittent 15s timeouts).

TESTIDS: member-roles-heading, member-roles-table, member-role-item, member-role-remove, member-roles-foreign-org, plus the derived form ids above.
SEAM: re-export through features/organizations/api.ts and index.ts. Add 'organizations/$orgId/members.tsx' to PAGE_FILES in page-shell.test.ts.
Do NOT add the route to apps/wallow-web/e2e/routes.spec.ts. react-query only via @bc-solutions-coder/query.
acceptance_criteria:
- The roster renders each active member with their per-org role names.
- Assigning POSTs /api/v1/identity/users/{userId}/roles with { roleName }; removing DELETEs /api/v1/identity/users/{userId}/roles/{roleName}.
- Both sweep the members query, asserted with expectSwept against organizationsGetMembersQueryKey from the generated factory.
- OWN-ORG GATE, the load-bearing spec: when organizationsGetAll returns an organization whose id is NOT the route's orgId, no mutation control renders and member-roles-foreign-org is present. No request is issued in that state.
- The assign form goes through useAppForm + AppForm with testIdPrefix 'organization-member-role'; its testids are derived, not hand-written.
- The role picker is a SelectField driven in specs with chooseOption.
- A 422 renders the error and leaves the roster mounted; narrowing is structural on error.status, not instanceof.
- Fields are filled with userEvent.fill.
- routeTree.gen.ts regenerated by a build and committed.
- pnpm check passes (pnpm lint:tests included).

RESEARCH COMPLETE. Design locked, starting TDD now.

DATA SOURCES:

title: Outstanding invitations screen (list + revoke)
description: Screen for the invitations already issued, with revoke. Route apps/wallow-web/src/app/routes/dashboard/organizations/invitations.tsx (id '/dashboard/organizations/invitations'), feature component apps/wallow-web/src/features/organizations/components/InvitationList.tsx. Plan: docs/plans/2026-08-01/2019-membership-dashboard-screens.md section 4.
design:
THE ROUTE IS NOT ORG-PARAMETERISED, AND CANNOT BE. InvitationsController.GetByTenant (InvitationsController.cs:41-52) takes skip/take and reads the AMBIENT tenant at line 48 (tenantContext.TenantId.Value). There is no organization-id parameter and no way to ask for another organization's invitations. Passing an orgId would compile - it would land in the query key as a stray arg - and silently do nothing. That is why this route sits OUTSIDE $orgId/.

BACKEND:
- GET /v1/identity/invitations?skip=&take= :41-52
- DELETE /v1/identity/invitations/{id} :54-64
- Projection: MapToResponse :97-106.
InvitationResponse(Guid Id, string Email, string Status, DateTimeOffset ExpiresAt, DateTimeOffset CreatedAt, Guid? AcceptedByUserId).

SDK: everything needed is ALREADY GENERATED - invitationsGetByTenantOptions (react-query.gen.ts:801), invitationsGetByTenantQueryKey (:799), invitationsRevokeMutation (:822). No new SDK surface. This screen is therefore the one that does not strictly block on Wallow-yp3e.2, but land it after so the epic ships against one client.

DATA: invitationsGetByTenantOptions({ client, query: { skip, take } }). The endpoint is paged; a fixed take with no pager is acceptable for the first cut, but spell the query object EXPLICITLY so the key carries it.
REVOKE: onSuccess sweeps queriesForOperation(invitationsGetByTenantQueryKey({ client, query })) built with the SAME query object the list used - a different one matches nothing.

RENDER: 'Outstanding' means the status is still pending. The API returns every invitation regardless of status, so filter client-side and say so in the component header.

TITLED PAGE: it owns its own heading, so it composes the catalog PageHeader (see organizations/index.tsx:33) inside PageContainer. Add 'organizations/invitations.tsx' to BOTH PAGE_FILES and TITLED_PAGE_FILES in routes/dashboard/page-shell.test.ts.

title: [epic] Membership dashboard screens in wallow-web (plan 6.7) — needs its own plan first
description: The backend of the membership lifecycle is complete but has no operator surface. Three screens are needed in apps/wallow-web: pending access requests (approve/deny), outstanding invitations (GET /invitations already returns them paged — this needs a screen, not a backend), and member role management. The implementation plan explicitly refuses to plan this: 'Three screens, each with a route, a query, a form and specs — this is a phase, not a task. Give it its own plan.'
design: Write the plan to docs/plans/<date>/<HHmm>-membership-dashboard-screens.md before opening any file. Constraints already known: keys come from the generated {operation}Options/{operation}Mutation artifacts in @bc-solutions-coder/sdk/query, forms go through useAppForm and the AppForm shell in @bc-solutions-coder/forms, invalidation goes through the curated predicates, new routes must be added to apps/wallow-web/e2e/routes.spec.ts and routeTree.gen.ts committed after a build (route-tree-drift.yml).
acceptance_criteria: A plan exists and is decomposed into task beads under this epic.
notes:
PLAN: docs/plans/2026-08-01/2019-membership-dashboard-screens.md (status: active). Written to be executed without reading the parent design doc; every claim cites a file and line read on this branch at 137f9600.

- Wallow-yp3e.3.2 P2 Pending access requests screen (approve/deny). deps: yp3e.2, yp3e.3.1

- Wallow-yp3e.6 P2 Suspended/Denied memberships unreachable from any list endpoint -> reinstate and clearDenial have no UI to drive them.
- Wallow-yp3e.7 P3 POST organizations/{id}/leave has no member-facing surface (needs a 'my organizations' screen on meGetOrganizations). deps: yp3e.2

FOUR FINDINGS THAT CHANGED THE PLAN:

1. The epic brief's instruction to add the new routes to apps/wallow-web/e2e/routes.spec.ts is WRONG for this app and the plan says so. That spec is a backend-free reachability gate whose header (lines 22-26) states /dashboard/** stays excluded because it is auth-gated; routes is literally ["/", "/bff-demo"]. Adding an auth-gated route makes it redirect to OIDC and fail. The routeTree.gen.ts half of the instruction is correct and is carried in every bead.

2. ROUTE NESTING. organizations/$orgId.tsx is a leaf with no <Outlet/> (:20-27); any sibling under $orgId would promote it to a layout and blank the children. Resolved by the directory form ($orgId/index.tsx + siblings, no $orgId/route.tsx), grounded in routes/dashboard/organizations/ itself - no organizations.tsx, no route.tsx, both routes attaching straight to /dashboard (routeTree.gen.ts:90-97). The trailing-underscore un-nesting convention is real (@tanstack+router-generator@1.167.21/dist/esm/utils.js:320) but has zero precedent here, so it was rejected. Existing <Link to="/dashboard/organizations/$orgId"> call sites survive the move: index routes lose the trailing slash in FileRoutesByTo (routeTree.gen.ts:131).

3. AMBIENT-TENANT ROLE WRITES. UsersController.AssignRole writes tenantContext.TenantId.Value (:179) and RemoveRole the same (:198); neither takes an org id. On a $orgId route pointed at a foreign org an operator can read, a role grant lands silently in their OWN org and returns 204. Mitigation baked into Wallow-yp3e.3.4's acceptance: gate the controls on $orgId matching the single row organizationsGetAll returns (OrganizationsController.cs:76-78 filters to the caller's own tenant), else read-only + member-roles-foreign-org. Same class of trap for invitations: InvitationsController.GetByTenant reads the ambient tenant (:48) and takes no org id, which is why the invitations route sits OUTSIDE $orgId/.

4. THE SNAPSHOT IS STALE, so Wallow-yp3e.2 is a hard dependency of every screen. packages/sdk/openapi/v1.json still describes /v1/identity/organizations/mine (OrganizationsGetMyOrganizations, generated at react-query.gen.ts:1072) and has NONE of members/pending, approve, deny, denial, suspend, reinstate, leave, me/organizations. The plan lists what is already generated with line numbers, lists the predicted new names as PREDICTED, and tells the implementer to read the regenerated file rather than trust them. Note MeController carries [Tags("Me")] (:19), so meGetOrganizations will be tagged 'Me' - a queriesWithTag('Organizations') sweep will not touch it. A repo-wide grep found no consumer of organizationsGetMyOrganizations, so the rename is free.

Constraint honoured: no builds, tests or writes to obj/bin/node_modules; the plan file is the only file touched, uncommitted.

title: Verify sign-in with Wallow from an external origin end to end (plan 5.5.6)
description: Phase 5.5's code and seed work landed — scope descriptions, scp:* permissions on admin-created clients, org_id on userinfo, front-channel logout documented, and seed.json now gives bcordes-bff its own callback port (3003) with sa-bcordes-bff on the Wallow tenant. The gate itself — a real end-to-end sign-in driven from the external origin through createWallowBffServer — has no evidence of having been run.
acceptance_criteria: A sign-in from the external origin completes: authorize, consent with rendered scope descriptions, token, userinfo carrying org_id, and a logout that clears the local session at the other relying party.
notes:
STEP 1 FINDINGS (coverage check):

Existing e2e-cross-app/login-journey.spec.ts covers wallow-web-client (FIRST-PARTY) signing
in through wallow-auth and back, plus an authenticated mutation + logout. It does NOT cover
this bead's acceptance criteria, because:

1. wallow-web-client is first-party (id starts with "wallow-"), so AuthorizationController
   SKIPS consent for it. The bead requires "consent with rendered scope descriptions" -- that
   only renders for a non-first-party client. bcordes-bff (seed.json:221-227, port 3003) is
   the seeded reference for exactly this case, per design doc Sec 14 / plan Sec 5.5.5-5.5.6.
2. No existing spec (TS or C#) asserts org_id on the userinfo response. Grepped
   api/tests + apps/*/e2e* + apps/*/e2e-cross-app for "org_id"/"getOrgId" usage in a live
   flow -- none found. SeedJsonBffClientTests.cs (api/tests/Modules/Identity/.../Infrastructure)
   only asserts seed.json's static shape (redirect URI, scopes, confidential), never drives
   a live authorize/token/userinfo round trip.
3. "the other relying party" (bcordes.dev / bcordes-bff) is a REAL EXTERNAL SITE, not part of
   this monorepo -- confirmed via grep, there is no app/server anywhere under apps/ using
   createWallowBffServer with bcordes-bff's client id. It only exists as a seed.json OIDC
   client registration (port 3003 callback) and the C# static-config test above. There is no
   running listener at localhost:3003 in this repo, so a literal "browser drives the external
   site" test is impossible without first building a new app -- out of scope for a
   verification task.

PLAN: write a new e2e-cross-app spec that plays bcordes-bff's role at the PROTOCOL level
(browser drives the real wallow-auth login+consent UI against /connect/authorize with
bcordes-bff's real client_id; intercept the redirect to the unreachable
localhost:3003/bff/callback to capture the auth code; then do the token exchange + userinfo
call directly via page.request, exactly as an external confidential-client BFF would
server-side). This exercises the real consent-with-descriptions UI and the real org_id-bearing
userinfo endpoint without needing a new frontend app. Will document precisely what this can
and cannot prove (no real second RP session to observe front-channel logout against).
STEP 1b -- MAJOR FINDING, revises the plan above:

There IS a real running "external origin" app: docker/docker-compose.test.yml's
`bff-example` service (port 3003, wallow-web's own Dockerfile/image, but wired with
OIDC_CLIENT_ID=bcordes-bff / OIDC_CLIENT_SECRET=bcordes-bff-secret). It serves the
existing `/bff-demo` route (apps/wallow-web/src/app/routes/bff-demo.tsx) with
testids bff-login/bff-logout/bff-user-status/bff-user-email/bff-call-api/bff-mutate.
It IS started by ./scripts/e2e.sh. No spec anywhere drives it (grepped e2e/e2e-cross-app
for "3003"/"bcordes-bff"/"bff-example" -- zero hits), matching the bead's "no evidence
of having been run."

BUT: docker-compose.test.yml:156 sets
  Identity__FirstPartyClients__0: "bcordes-bff"
which makes AuthorizationController.cs treat bcordes-bff as FIRST-PARTY in exactly the
stack ./scripts/e2e.sh brings up, so the consent screen is skipped server-side no matter
what client drives the authorize request. This is a config override, not something a
Playwright spec can route around. Contrast: api/src/Wallow.Api/appsettings.json:78 (the
Aspire/`pnpm backend` default) has FirstPartyClients: [] -- bcordes-bff is genuinely
third-party there, but no bff-example container runs under Aspire (grepped
Wallow.AppHost, zero hits for bcordes-bff/bff-example/3003), so nothing listens on 3003
in that stack either.

Net effect: as configured today, NEITHER supported stack can produce a browser-driven,
consent-screen-rendering sign-in from an actual running "external origin" app.
docker-compose.test.yml's override looks like a leftover from before Phase 5.5 fixed the
consent screen (design doc Sec 14.3: "consent is on for this client, and the consent
screen is broken" -- historical defect that predates the scope-description/scp:* fixes
in 5.5.1/5.5.2). Now that the screen works, the override defeats the one client it exists
to test.

PROPOSED FIX (flagging to team lead before touching shared e2e infra):
Remove the `Identity__FirstPartyClients__0: bcordes-bff` line from
docker-compose.test.yml, renumber wallow-web-client to index 0, then write the
e2e-cross-app spec against the real bff-example app at :3003 driving the real
bff-demo route through the real consent screen. Nothing else references
bcordes-bff/FirstPartyClients today (grepped), so this looks low-blast-radius, but it
edits shared e2e infra used by every suite via one script, so checking in before
changing it.
STEP 2: drafted apps/wallow-web/e2e-cross-app/external-origin-login.spec.ts (new file) driving the real bff-example (:3003) app through /bff/login -> wallow-auth login -> /consent (real scope descriptions) -> approve -> back to /bff-demo -> asserts bff-user-status=authenticated, bff-user-email, and org_id/org_name via GET ${BFF_EXAMPLE_ORIGIN}/bff/user -> logout via bff-logout -> asserts /bff/user 401. Typecheck (tsc --noEmit) and pnpm lint:tests both clean. NOT YET RUN -- holding on the docker-compose.test.yml FirstPartyClients fix pending team-lead input (message sent, no reply yet); running it as-is today would still pass through /consent with real descriptions ONLY if that override is removed first, since the override makes AuthorizationController treat bcordes-bff as first-party server-side regardless of spec design.
STEP 3 -- team lead approved the compose fix (rationale: a test stack that suppresses the
screen under test is misconfigured, not a constraint to design around; it also disagreed
with the Aspire stack's FirstPartyClients: []; pre-release repo policy prefers correct
design over compatible). Two conditions: run the FULL ./scripts/e2e.sh afterward (not just
the new spec) and report any pre-existing break as a real finding rather than weakening it;
write this note before running.

CHANGE MADE: docker/docker-compose.test.yml -- removed
`Identity__FirstPartyClients__0: "bcordes-bff"`, kept `wallow-web-client` as the sole
override, renumbered it to index 0. Added a comment explaining bcordes-bff's deliberate
absence (superseded pre-5.5.1 workaround; the client exists specifically to exercise the
third-party consent path this bead verifies).

Verified api/tests/Wallow.Architecture.Tests/PublicSeedClientRemovalTests.cs's
TestCompose_FirstPartyClientOverrides_ShouldContinueWhereAppSettingsEnds computes its
expected index range dynamically from dev appsettings.json's FirstPartyClients.Count (0)
and the override count actually present in the compose file, so a single override at index
0 still satisfies it -- confirmed by reading the test, not yet by running it (will run with
run-tests.sh arch below).

NEXT: run ./scripts/run-tests.sh arch to confirm the architecture tests still pass with one
override, then ./scripts/e2e.sh for the full three-suite run (wallow-auth, wallow-web,
wallow-web cross-app including the new external-origin-login.spec.ts).
STATUS PING RESPONSE: ./scripts/e2e.sh is running in background (started after arch tests passed 302/302 post compose-fix). Currently mid-build -- publishing API/migration/seeder container images. Not stalled, just slow (image builds). Will note final pass/fail counts here the moment it finishes.
E2E RUN RESULT: ./scripts/e2e.sh completed (task bbd6t2n4o). wallow-auth suite: 23/30 passed, 7 FAILED. Suite runner stops at first failing suite (memory e2e-sh-stops-at-first-failing-suite) -> wallow-web suite and wallow-web cross-app suite (containing my new external-origin-login.spec.ts) NEVER RAN. Teardown was clean: docker ps -a --filter name=wallow-test shows zero containers, zero wallow-test volumes; the wallow_wallow network that remains is the separate dev-infra stack (docker-compose.yml), not an orphan of this run.

FAILING TESTS (wallow-auth, all against the freshly built :test containers):
- login.spec.ts:13 password login reaches an authenticated state
- magic-link.spec.ts:42 magic-link send then verify reaches an authenticated state
- mfa.spec.ts:100 mfa totp lifecycle > totp enrollment issues backup codes
- logout.spec.ts:46 signed-out landing shows the return link for an allow-listed redirect uri
- otp-login.spec.ts:39 otp send then verify reaches an authenticated state
- signup.spec.ts:24 register happy path reaches the verify-email notice
- reset-password.spec.ts:48 forgot then reset with the emailed token shows the login success banner

ROOT-CAUSE ANALYSIS: NOT caused by my docker-compose.test.yml FirstPartyClients edit. Verified by reading apps/wallow-auth/e2e/login.spec.ts:13 directly -- it does a bare 'await page.goto("/login")' with NO OIDC returnUrl and NO client_id anywhere in the flow (per its own header comment: 'A direct /login visit carries no OIDC returnUrl'). It cannot be touched by a FirstPartyClients override, which only changes AuthorizationController.cs's isFirstParty branch for connect/authorize requests carrying a client_id. error-context.md for this test (apps/wallow-auth/test-results/login-password-login-reaches-an-authenticated-state/error-context.md) shows the login form rendered fine, fields filled correctly, submit clicked, but the page shows a generic banner 'An error occurred. Please try again.' instead of the login-signed-in testid -- i.e. the credential POST itself failed/errored on a plain password login with the seeded admin (admin@wallow.dev / Admin123!). reset-password.spec.ts's failure is a distinct, separate symptom: 'No email to admin@wallow.dev with subject "Password Reset Request" arrived within 20000ms (Mailpit)' -- a mail-delivery timing issue, not a login error.

Container/stack startup itself looked clean in the log: postgres/migrations/seeder all completed (seeder exited 0, api/auth/web all reported Healthy) before '=== Waiting for the API ===' / 'API ready after 1s'. All 7 failures are on tests that authenticate the shared seeded admin account, while routes.spec.ts (18 tests, no auth) and the one signup test that doesn't submit real credentials (email_taken) both passed. Working theory, NOT confirmed: Playwright's default parallel workers fire multiple concurrent login/signup/otp/mfa/reset-password attempts against the same seeded admin account against a just-started API, and something (rate limiting, lockout, or the API/DB still warming up past its health check) causes those concurrent auth POSTs to fail generically. I did not have app-container logs to confirm this (docker compose logs were not streamed into the e2e.sh log, and teardown already removed the containers) -- this needs a targeted follow-up run (e.g. E2E_KEEP_STACK=1 or --workers=1 on the wallow-auth suite alone) to actually diagnose, which is out of scope for Wallow-yp3e.4.

CONCLUSION FOR THIS BEAD: this is a real, pre-existing failure unrelated to the FirstPartyClients compose fix or to external-origin-login.spec.ts -- reporting per instructions, not weakening/skipping it. Because e2e.sh stops at the first failing suite, external-origin-login.spec.ts (the bead's actual deliverable) has NOT been executed against a live stack yet. Blocked on this upstream wallow-auth suite issue being triaged/fixed (or on being told to run the remaining suites by hand against a stack with E2E_KEEP_STACK=1, bypassing e2e.sh's stop-on-first-failure).
VERIFIER STEP 1 (causation check): CONFIRMED pre-existing, unrelated to the FirstPartyClients compose edit. Method: git stash push -- docker/docker-compose.test.yml (restoring original Identity__FirstPartyClients__0=bcordes-bff / __1=wallow-web-client), then E2E_SKIP_IMAGE_BUILD=1 ./scripts/e2e.sh (reusing the :test images already built by the implementer's run). Result: IDENTICAL 7/30 wallow-auth failures with the compose change reverted -- login.spec.ts:13, magic-link.spec.ts:42, logout.spec.ts:46, otp-login.spec.ts:39, mfa.spec.ts:100, signup.spec.ts:24, reset-password.spec.ts:48. Same pass count (23 passed). This is decisive: the compose edit cannot be the cause since removing it changes nothing. Stash restored after the run (git stash pop), compose diff intact. Proceeding to step 3 (run wallow-web + e2e-cross-app suites against a stack that skips the broken auth suite).
VERIFIER STEP 3 (get the actual bead tested): docker-compose.test.yml has a 4th service not in ./scripts/e2e.sh's default up-set -- bff-example (port 3003) -- needed since wallow-web doesn't depend_on it. Brought the full stack up by hand (down -v, up -d --wait wallow-api wallow-web, then up -d --wait bff-example), reused prebuilt :test images. wallow-web/e2e (reachability, 2 tests) PASSED. wallow-web/e2e-cross-app (3 tests) ALL FAILED, including the pre-existing login-journey.spec.ts (both its tests) -- NOT just the new external-origin-login.spec.ts. So this is not a fault in the new spec.

ROOT CAUSE (NOT the FirstPartyClients compose edit -- a separate, more severe, pre-existing code bug): wallow-api logs show 'The authentication demand was rejected because the client application was not found: wallow-web-client' / 'bcordes-bff' at /connect/authorize (error invalid_request / ID2052). Confirmed by querying the DB directly: identity."OpenIddictApplications" has ZERO rows -- no OIDC clients seeded AT ALL. wallow-seeder container logs show why: SeederWorker's 'Sync Organizations' step throws System.InvalidOperationException: Unable to resolve service for type 'ILastOwnerGuard' while activating 'OrganizationService' (SeederWorker.cs:183), which aborts ExecuteAsync before the LATER 'Client Sync' step (SyncClientsAsync, the one that seeds OpenIddictApplications) ever runs. Root cause: commit fa80e5ff added ILastOwnerGuard as an OrganizationService constructor param and registered it in IdentityInfrastructureExtensions.cs -- but Wallow.SeederService/Program.cs hand-picks its own DI subset (IOrganizationRepository/IMembershipRepository/IOrganizationService/AddMembershipAccessRevocation/IMessageBus/TimeProvider, etc.) instead of calling that extension, and was never updated to add ILastOwnerGuard. Doubly dangerous: the seeder container still exits 0 after this crash (docker inspect confirms ExitCode 0), so compose's depends_on: service_completed_successfully gate is satisfied and wallow-api starts anyway with clients unseeded -- silent failure, no error surfaced to ./scripts/e2e.sh or its log.

title: Audit events for every membership transition (plan 6.6)
description: Design doc section 4.7 lists the membership state transitions; none of them emit an audit event today. rg 'AuditEventType\.' over api/src/Modules/Identity returns nothing, and Shared.Contracts/Identity/Events has no Membership* event at all — the closest are the surviving OrganizationMemberAdded/RemovedEvent. 'Who let this person in' is the first question anyone asks after an access-request flow ships.
design: Cover: access requested (Pending created), approved, denied, suspended, reinstated, left voluntarily, removed by an admin, role assigned, role removed, owner marked/unmarked. Emit from MembershipReviewService / UserEnrollmentService / OrganizationService rather than the controllers, so the seeder and any future background path are covered too. Follow the existing Identity integration-event shape in api/src/Shared/Wallow.Shared.Contracts/Identity/Events (record deriving IntegrationEvent, TenantId declared locally).
acceptance_criteria: Every section 4.7 transition emits an event carrying actor, subject user, organization and timestamp; integration tests assert emission on approve, deny, suspend, reinstate and leave.
notes:
SCOUT FINDINGS

1. END-TO-END INTEGRATION-EVENT TRACE (template: login audit)
   - Event record: api/src/Shared/Wallow.Shared.Contracts/Identity/Events/UserLoginSucceededEvent.cs
     `sealed record : IntegrationEvent` (base in api/src/Shared/Wallow.Shared.Contracts/IIntegrationEvent.cs
     gives EventId/OccurredAt); TenantId is a plain `Guid?`/`Guid` prop declared locally per event, not
     inherited. Every Identity event lives flat in that same Events/ folder.
   - Publish call site: api/src/Modules/Identity/Wallow.Identity.Api/Controllers/AccountController.cs:130,148,241
     `await messageBus.PublishAsync(new UserLoginSucceededEvent { UserId = ..., IpAddress = ... })`
     (IMessageBus is Wolverine's, injected via primary ctor).
   - Consumer: api/src/Modules/Identity/Wallow.Identity.Infrastructure/Handlers/AuthAuditEventHandlers.cs
     `public static Task Handle(UserLoginSucceededEvent message, IAuthAuditService authAuditService)` —
     static class, one `Handle` overload per event type, Wolverine auto-discovers (no DI registration).

2. THE AUDIT MECHANISM ALREADY EXISTS — it is NOT an `AuditEventType` enum (that grep returning
   nothing is expected; there never was one). It is a plain-string event_type column:
   - Interface: api/src/Shared/Wallow.Shared.Kernel/Auditing/IAuthAuditService.cs
     `IAuthAuditService.RecordAsync(AuthAuditRecord, ct)`; `AuthAuditRecord` = { EventType (string),
     UserId (Guid), TenantId (Guid?), IpAddress?, UserAgent?, OccurredAt }.
   - Impl: api/src/Shared/Wallow.Shared.Infrastructure.Core/Auditing/AuthAuditService.cs — writes to
     `auth_audit.auth_audit_entries` (AuthAuditDbContext, same folder), swallows+logs exceptions so a
     write failure never fails the caller.
   - Handlers: api/src/Modules/Identity/Wallow.Identity.Infrastructure/Handlers/AuthAuditEventHandlers.cs
     currently has 4 `Handle` overloads (LoginSucceeded/Failed, AccountLockedOut, MfaLockedOut). Add one
     `Handle(TEvent, IAuthAuditService)` overload per new membership integration event, same file.
   - Doc: docs/operations/audit-events.md "Extending Audit Coverage" section is the exact recipe (event
     type naming: PascalCase, module-prefixed only if module-specific).
   - IMPORTANT GAP: `UserRoleChangedEvent` (Shared.Contracts/Identity/Events/UserRoleChangedEvent.cs)
     ALREADY EXISTS and is ALREADY published by UserManagementService.AssignRoleAsync/RemoveRoleAsync
     (below) but AuthAuditEventHandlers has NO case for it yet — role-change audit may need only a new
     `Handle` overload, no new event, unless the "actor" field below is required (it currently isn't
     on this event).

3. MEMBERSHIP TRANSITION CALL SITES (exact methods, what's in scope at each)
   a. api/src/Modules/Identity/Wallow.Identity.Infrastructure/Services/MembershipReviewService.cs
      - ApproveAsync(organizationId, userId, actorId, ct) — publishes OrganizationMemberAddedEvent (reused, no ActorId field)
      - DenyAsync(organizationId, userId, actorId, ct) — publishes NOTHING today
      - ClearDenialAsync(organizationId, userId, actorId, ct) — publishes NOTHING today
      - SuspendAsync(organizationId, userId, actorId, ct) — publishes NOTHING today (calls accessRevoker.RevokeAsync)
      - ReinstateAsync(organizationId, userId, actorId, ct) — publishes NOTHING today
      - LeaveAsync(organizationId, userId, ct) — actor IS the leaving user (no separate actorId param);
        publishes OrganizationMemberRemovedEvent (reused)
      All 6 already have a [LoggerMessage] call recording the transition — the same actor/subject/org
      inputs an audit event needs are already in scope at every one of these call sites.
   b. api/src/Modules/Identity/Wallow.Identity.Infrastructure/Services/UserEnrollmentService.cs
      - RecordRequestAsync (private, called from EnrollAsync when policy=RequestApproval) — publishes
        AccessRequestedEvent (org name/requester email/name, no ActorId — self-service, actor=subject)
      - EnrollDirectlyAsync (private, policy=Open) — publishes OrganizationMemberAddedEvent
   c. api/src/Modules/Identity/Wallow.Identity.Infrastructure/Services/OrganizationService.cs
      - AddMemberAsync(orgId, userId, roleName, ct) — publishes OrganizationMemberAddedEvent.
        NO actorId PARAMETER — gap: caller identity isn't threaded through today.
      - RemoveMemberAsync(orgId, userId, ct) — publishes OrganizationMemberRemovedEvent. Same gap: no actorId param.
      - CreateOrganizationAsync — the ONLY call site of Membership.MarkOwner anywhere in the codebase
        (creatorUserId marks itself owner=true). Grepped: no controller/endpoint calls MarkOwner or
        reads IsOwner for an admin-triggered mark/unmark — "owner marked/unmarked" per the design's
        transition list has no reachable admin call site today beyond org creation.
   d. api/src/Modules/Identity/Wallow.Identity.Infrastructure/Services/UserManagementService.cs:218-281
      - AssignRoleAsync(userId, organizationId, roleName, ct) — calls membership.AssignRole, publishes
        UserRoleChangedEvent. NO actorId param; controller
        (Wallow.Identity.Api/Controllers/UsersController.cs:179) doesn't pass one either — same actor
        gap as OrganizationService's Add/RemoveMemberAsync.
      - RemoveRoleAsync(userId, organizationId, roleName, ct) — same shape/gap; controller call at
        UsersController.cs:198.
   e. Membership aggregate: api/src/Modules/Identity/Wallow.Identity.Domain/Entities/Membership.cs —
      Approve/Deny/RequestAgain/EnrollAgain/Suspend/Reinstate/Grant/AssignRole/RemoveRole all already
      take an actor parameter (named e.g. `approvedByUserId`/`updatedByUserId`) — the domain layer has
      the actor; only the OrganizationService/UserManagementService SERVICE methods above are missing
      an actorId parameter to thread the HTTP caller in.

4. DESIGN DOC (docs/plans/2026-07-31/1410-multi-org-membership-and-access-requests.md, "### 4.7 The
   rest of the member lifecycle", lines 346-376) authoritative "Audit" paragraph, verbatim transition list:
   "invite, accept, request, approve, deny, suspend, reinstate, role change, leave, remove" — every one
   of these "emits an audit event. The repo already has the infrastructure
   (docs/operations/audit-events.md)". Same section covers: Denial (with cooldown + ReviewedAt/ReviewedBy),
   Leaving (self-service, row deleted), Last-owner protection (a guard, not itself an event), Suspension
   (mirrors approval).

5. EXISTING EVENT SHAPES TO MIRROR — none carry an ActorId today (OrganizationMemberAddedEvent/
   RemovedEvent only have OrganizationId/TenantId/UserId/Email). AC requires actor+subject+org+timestamp,
   so new Membership* events (or an extended existing shape) will need an explicit actor field — this
   is new, not copy-paste, on every existing analog.

6. TESTS
   - Unit-test template (mirrors Substitute IMessageBus + Arg.Is<TEvent> predicate pattern), same dir
     api/tests/Modules/Identity/Wallow.Identity.Tests/Infrastructure/:
     MembershipReviewServiceTests.cs, UserEnrollmentServiceTests.cs, OrganizationServiceTests.cs,

This is where the AC's "integration tests assert emission on approve, deny, suspend, reinstate and leave" belongs.
