title: Front-channel logout notification for relying parties
description:
Signing out of one relying party ends the Wallow SSO session for all of them, but Wallow tells none of them: OpenIddict **7.6.0** — the version this repo pins (`api/Directory.Packages.props:86-87`), not the 7.5 this bead was filed against — implements RP-initiated logout only and has no frontchannel_logout_uri/backchannel_logout_uri support at all (no such metadata in OpenIddict.Server or OpenIddict.Abstractions). The other RPs keep a local session that looks live until their access token expires and the refresh is refused.

The documented behaviour today (docs/integrations/bff-pattern.md, 'Logout is global') is that RPs must degrade gracefully: on a refused refresh, drop the session and send the user to login. The SDK BFF already does this; a hand-rolled one must.

Closing the gap means implementing the OIDC front-channel logout spec ourselves:
- a per-client frontchannel_logout_uri (descriptor property + ClientsController + seed.json)
- frontchannel_logout_supported/frontchannel_logout_session_supported in the discovery document
- an end-session response that renders an iframe per RP with an active session, before the post_logout_redirect
- an RP-side logout endpoint in packages/sdk/src/server

Not scoped by the multi-org plan; recorded so the decision is not silently re-litigated.
notes:
Implemented OIDC front-channel logout end to end.

OP side (Identity module):
- AuthorizationController mints a sid per SSO session, re-issues it onto the identity cookie, stamps it into every id_token, and records participating clients in identity.sso_session_clients (SsoSessionClient entity + SsoClientSessionService + migration 20260828040036_AddSsoSessionClients).
- Clients register a frontchannel_logout_uri via a descriptor property (ClientApplicationProperties.FrontchannelLogoutUri; Api+Infrastructure extension twins), settable through seed.json (PreRegisteredClientDefinition + sync) and the ClientsController create/update contracts (validated absolute http/https; null clears; echoed on ClientResponse).
- Discovery advertises frontchannel_logout_supported + frontchannel_logout_session_supported (pinned by DiscoveryDocumentTests, integration tier).
- LogoutController is two-phase: phase 1 signs out the cookie, forgets the session rows, and renders a no-store interstitial loading each participant's URI (+iss +sid) in hidden iframes, then returns to the same URL with wallow_fc=done; phase 2 runs OpenIddict's normal end-session SignOut. HTML-attr-encodes iframe srcs, JS-encodes the completion URL.

RP side (SDK):
- BffSession gains optional sid, captured from the id_token claims in the callback before the userinfo overlay.
- New GET /bff/frontchannel-logout handler (createBffHandlers.frontchannelLogout, routed by createWallowBffServer): destroys the session + clears cookies only when iss (trailing-slash-normalized) matches config.issuer AND sid matches session.sid; every miss is a silent 200 no-store HTML no-op; non-GET answers 405 Allow: GET. Deliberately outside the CSRF gate — the notification is a cross-site GET by spec, and the sid requirement blocks forged teardowns.

Also: OpenAPI snapshot + generated client regenerated (build-time emission, byte-identical to the autoregen recipe); docs/integrations/bff-pattern.md 'Logout is global' section rewritten; reverse-proxy.md production client example + seed.json production example gained frontchannelLogoutUri.

Gates: ./scripts/run-tests.sh 4945/4945; ./scripts/run-tests.sh integration 261/261; pnpm check exit 0.
Follow-up: Wallow-nnk2 (cross-app E2E spec for the full browser flow).

title: CreateInquiryForm browser specs still flake under heavy machine load
description:
The 15s browser testTimeout is exceeded intermittently by the CreateInquiryForm specs (and, under enough load, RegisterAppForm and wallow-auth specs).

Measured:
- userEvent.type cost one CDP round trip per character; fillEveryField() drove 80 characters of setup. 2/6 full-gate runs failed, worst 20647ms. Fixed in dba26270 by converting 20 sites to userEvent.fill (80 round trips -> 5).
- Full CPU saturation alone (14 spinners on 14 cores) inflates the slowest browser test only 1564ms -> 3499ms (2.2x) and reproduces NO failure, with either type or fill.
- The reproducing condition is whole-machine oversubscription: during this investigation a concurrent 'dotnet test' with the coverage datacollector was running in .worktrees/multi-org-membership, taking load average to 257 on 14 cores.

Remaining exposure: the setup still performs three portalled Select drives via chooseOption(), which cannot be collapsed the way keystrokes were.

Open question: whether the browser project needs a contention-aware testTimeout the way the node project already carries a measured 60s (see packages/testing/src/vitest-projects.ts). Deliberately NOT raised yet - the default caught a real inefficiency, and raising it would have hidden that.

To decide it properly, re-run the matched comparison on a QUIET machine: 6x 'pnpm test' with type vs 6x with fill. Only 2 clean fill runs were obtained (both green); runs 3-6 were contaminated by two concurrent gate jobs and are not usable.
notes:
AUDIT 2026-08-02 (docs/audits/2026-08-02/0824-bead-backlog) — RETYPED bug -> task (applied).

Rationale: this is not a defect. The measured userEvent.fill fix landed — apps/wallow-web/src/features/inquiries/components/CreateInquiryForm.forms.test.tsx:24-33 uses fill, not type. What remains is a MEASUREMENT question, not a broken behaviour.

Verified fact the remaining work turns on: the only testTimeout in the workspace is 60_000, and it is set on the NODE project (packages/testing/src/vitest-projects.ts:144). The browser project therefore runs on vitest's 15s default — which is the timeout these specs were flaking against.
PLAN: docs/plans/2026-08-02/1744-no-source-tests-design.md — Phase 5, LAST, deliberately. Now blocked by Wallow-e6gz and Wallow-succ.

WHY LAST: this is a measurement question, and the epic changes what is being measured. Wallow-e6gz phase 4b deletes ~8 node-project source sweeps; Wallow-succ and the colour specs replacing deleted class-string pins ADD browser-project specs. So the node/browser balance, and the CPU contention between the two projects that this bead is actually about, are both different afterwards. A matched comparison run before the epic settles measures a suite that will not exist.

Re-read this bead's own instruction when the time comes: 6x 'pnpm test' on a QUIET machine, and confirm the browser project is still on vitest's 15s default (the only testTimeout in the workspace is 60_000 on the NODE project, packages/testing/src/vitest-projects.ts:144).
DECISION: CHANGE NOTHING. The browser project does NOT need a contention-aware testTimeout. Do not re-open this bead on the strength of a slow run alone — re-open it only if a browser spec actually TIMES OUT (a 15000ms failure), which none of 15 full-workspace runs produced.

## Facts re-confirmed (read, not trusted)
- packages/testing/src/vitest-projects.ts:144 is still the ONLY testTimeout in the workspace (60_000), and it is on the NODE project. grep over the tree returns 3 hits: the module-header comment, the interface field, that value. The browser project sets none.
- The browser default is 15000ms, verified from the INSTALLED vitest 4.1.10, not from memory:
  node_modules/.../vitest/dist/chunks/coverage.DM_a_rWm.js:538
  `resolved.testTimeout ??= resolved.browser.enabled ? 15e3 : 5e3;`
  So browser=15s, node-without-override=5s. Both halves of the bead's premise hold.

## Machine state — NOT perfectly quiet, and I am not pretending otherwise
Baseline load average 3.4-5.0 on 14 cores, from two persistent DreamBot JVMs at ~40% CPU each (~0.8 core). I did not kill them. This handicaps every number BELOW in the conservative direction: the headroom reported is a floor, not a ceiling. It is also ~50x below the load-257 condition the bead records as the original reproducer.

## Six runs (instrumented `pnpm test`), all green
4450 tests each. Wall clock 41.67 / 42.27 / 43.18 / 42.73 / 41.96 / 42.76 s (mean 42.4, sd 0.6). Peak load during runs 8.2-17.3 — the suite oversubscribes 14 cores on its own.
Slowest INDIVIDUAL browser test per run: 5696 / 6032 / 7224 / 5539 / 5914 / 6428 ms (mean 6139, sd 613).
WORST OBSERVED 7224ms = 48.2% of the 15000ms budget => 2.08x headroom.
It is CreateInquiryForm.test.tsx in 5 of 6 runs, so the bead named the right spec.

Per-file worst-of-six (slowest single test in that file, % of 15s):
  CreateInquiryForm.test.tsx        7224ms  48.2%
  CreateInquiryForm.forms.test.tsx  6916ms  46.1%
  CreateInquiryForm.catalog         1549ms  10.3%
  RegisterAppForm.branding          4538ms  30.3%
  RegisterAppForm.forms             2736ms  18.2%
  RegisterAppForm.test              2325ms  15.5%
  wallow-auth worst (LoginScreen)   2997ms  20.0%
No other spec in the workspace exceeds 5696ms. Nothing is within 2x of the timeout.

## The decisive experiment: deliberate saturation
The bead asks for a CONTENTION-aware timeout, so contention had to be the variable. Same instrumented run under N busy-loop spinners held for the whole run:
  0 spinners  peak load 17.3  wall  42.4s  slowest test 7224ms (48.2%)  0 failures
  14 spinners peak load 20.7  wall  53.6s  slowest test 4187ms (27.9%)  0 failures
  42 spinners peak load 58.4  wall 148.7s  slowest test 5895ms (39.3%)  0 failures

THE SLOWEST TEST DID NOT GET SLOWER UNDER SATURATION — it got FASTER, while wall clock grew 3.5x. That inverts the assumption the bead was filed on. Per-test latency here is bounded by the suite's OWN internal concurrency burst (many Chromium instances launching at once), not by whole-machine CPU pressure: external load throttles the suite's parallelism, so any given browser test faces LESS instantaneous intra-suite contention even as the run takes longer.

Consequence: the naive arithmetic that argues FOR a raise is wrong. Applying the bead's recorded 2.2x saturation multiplier to 7224ms gives 15893ms and looks like a timeout waiting to happen. That multiplier came from a 1564ms unloaded baseline and does NOT compose onto a number already measured under intra-suite contention. Measured directly, the product never appears. Extrapolating the only increasing segment (load 20->58 raised the max 1.41x), reaching load 257 would predict roughly 8-9s — still inside 15s.

This also explains the ORIGINAL failure coherently. userEvent.type cost one CDP round trip per character and fillEveryField drove 80 of them. CDP round trips are latency-bound on the runner<->browser channel, and THAT is what whole-machine oversubscription inflates. 80 round trips x inflated latency = the 20647ms failure. dba26270 took it to 5 round trips, removing the multiplier, not just trimming the constant. The three remaining portalled chooseOption Select drives are a handful of round trips, not eighty — which is why CreateInquiryForm now peaks at 7.2s and stops there.

## Guard overhead: not measurable
New since the original numbers, so it was checked. afterEach(assertNoNavigationEscape) toggled on/off, 5 reps INTERLEAVED (ABABAB, so machine drift cancels rather than loading onto one arm), on packages/forms (88 browser tests) and packages/navigation (136):
  forms       wall ON 2.67s / OFF 2.69s (delta -0.02, sd 0.02-0.03); sum-of-test-durations delta +13ms over 88 tests (sd 95, 91)
  navigation  wall ON 3.14s / OFF 3.13s (delta +0.01, sd 0.04-0.05); sum delta +7ms over 136 tests (sd 73, 80)
Every delta is well inside its own run-to-run standard deviation, i.e. indistinguishable from zero. Per-test cost < 0.2ms = under 0.002% of the 15s budget. Expected: assertNoNavigationEscape on the happy path is one array-length check. The guard costs nothing and is not an argument for a raise. Both setup files were restored from backup and verified (guard block present, no measurement remnants); the working tree is byte-identical to how I found it.

## Justification for changing nothing
1. 2.08x headroom at the worst point ever observed, and the worst point occurs on an UNLOADED machine, not a loaded one.
2. The node project's 60s is NOT an analogous precedent. It exists because a deterministic, structural cold Vite transform of the route graph measured 19s against a 5s default — the default was blown by 3.8x by a cost that is not contention at all. Nothing structural on the browser side comes near 15s. Copying the 60s across because "the node project has one" would be cargo-culting a fix for a different failure.
3. The failure mode that motivated this bead was removed at its source in dba26270. Raising the timeout now raises it against a defect that no longer exists.
4. A raised timeout is not free: it is what converts a real hang from a fast, named failure into a long, silent one. The bead's own history is the argument — the 15s default CAUGHT the userEvent.type inefficiency, and a raise would have hidden it. That reasoning has not expired.

## Finding that is NOT this bead's, filed here so it is not lost
2 of the 15 full-workspace runs failed, and NEITHER was a timeout. Both were packages/navigation src/app-shell.toggle.test.tsx > "collapses it again when the toggle is activated twice", failing at 159-161ms — fast, not slow. It fails two ways at once: expected isNavCollapsed true, got false, AND a vetoed navigation escape to /dashboard/organizations. It passes 136/136 in isolation every time; it only fails under the full-workspace run. Reading is that the first click moves the rail, and the second click's coordinates land on a nav destination link instead of the toggle, so a real hand-off is attempted. The Wallow-tkyq guard is doing exactly its job (one named test fails instead of the runner dying and blaming a sibling), but the underlying leak in that spec is NOT fixed. A higher testTimeout would not touch it. Worth a bead against app-shell.toggle.test.tsx.

## Method note
`pnpm test` (= `pnpm -r test`) ABORTS the whole workspace on the first package failure, which truncates a measurement run — the very first run stopped at 19.6s. Runs therefore used `pnpm -r --no-bail --stream run test --reporter=default --reporter=json --outputFile.json=.vitest-run.json`. Output-only deviations; every package still ran its own test script under pnpm's own recursive scheduler, and the instrumented wall clock (41.7-43.2s) matches the uninstrumented (41.7-42.7s), so the reporter costs nothing and the contention is equivalent.

title: Nothing in either app server is proxy-aware — four sites take request.ip at face value behind Caddy
description:
Nothing in either app server is proxy-aware. `trustProxy` appears nowhere in `packages/logger/src`,
`packages/sdk/src` or either app's `src`, so `request.ip` is the address of the immediate peer.
Behind the production Caddy ingress (`docker/caddy/Caddyfile.example`, the sole externally
reachable container) every real user therefore shares ONE bucket keyed on Caddy's own address, and
every outbound client-IP header carries Caddy's address rather than the caller's.

FOUR call sites, not one and not two. Both earlier inventories were short; this is the verified
union:

- `apps/wallow-web/src/app/lib/log-ingest.server.ts:92` — per-IP ingest rate limit key
- `apps/wallow-auth/src/shared/lib/log-ingest.server.ts:52` — same, in the auth app
- `apps/wallow-web/src/app/lib/bff.server.ts:151` — stamps CLIENT_IP_HEADER on the outbound API hop
- `apps/wallow-auth/src/shared/lib/api-passthrough.server.ts:79` — same, in the auth app

So the API's own per-client rate limiting has the same blind spot as the ingest limit. One
trusted-proxy resolution, used by all four, is the fix — not four local patches.

The only inbound `x-forwarded-for` reads in the tree are
`packages/sdk/src/server/forwarded.ts:60-62` (appends to the outbound chain) and `proxy.ts:519`
(a header list). Neither is a trust decision, so neither is a starting point to extend.

Not a regression from Wallow-dayd. Before that fix the handler read `x-wallow-client-ip` off the
inbound request, and Caddy does not set that header, so production already collapsed to the single
UNKNOWN_CLIENT bucket — or to an attacker-chosen one, which was the bug Wallow-dayd closed. This
is strictly better than what it replaced; it is just not yet correct.

Fix direction: derive the client address from X-Forwarded-For, trusting it ONLY when the peer is a
known proxy. Caddy already stamps X-Forwarded-For by default (no `header_up` directives needed).
Trusting the header unconditionally would reintroduce exactly the forgery Wallow-dayd closed, so
the trusted-peer check is the load-bearing part, not the header read.

Found during verification of Wallow-dayd. See
docs/plans/2026-07-31/2318-logging-telemetry-decision-record.md.
acceptance_criteria: One trusted-proxy client-address resolution exists and is used by all four sites (both log-ingest handlers, bff.server.ts and api-passthrough.server.ts). X-Forwarded-For is trusted only when the immediate peer is a configured proxy, with a test proving an untrusted peer cannot forge the address — that check, not the header read, is the load-bearing part. Behind a proxy, two clients at different addresses land in different rate-limit buckets.
notes:
Fixed in 781041f8. Design: docs/plans/2026-08-03/1639-proxy-trust-react-dupe-nav-flake.md §1 (CIDR + right-to-left walk), NOT the WALLOW_TRUSTED_PROXY_HOPS counted-position design in docs/plans/2026-08-01/0137-seven-bead-sweep.md Phase 3, which is now marked SUPERSEDED in place.

WHAT LANDED
@bc-solutions-coder/env/client-address is the one resolution. X-Forwarded-For is consulted only when the immediate peer is inside WALLOW_TRUSTED_PROXIES; otherwise the peer's own address is the answer and the header is not read. When the peer IS trusted the chain is walked from the RIGHT and the first entry that is not itself a trusted proxy is the caller, so the result does not depend on how many proxies are stacked in front. Unset means trust nothing, which is byte-for-byte the prior behaviour. Vocabulary is Caddy's plus Express's presets: CIDR blocks, loopback / linklocal / uniquelocal / private. An unparseable list entry is DROPPED rather than thrown on — a typo narrows trust (the safe direction) instead of failing a boot on a live server. IPv4-mapped IPv6 collapses to dotted-quad so one client keys to one bucket regardless of how the socket bound.

FIVE THINGS THE BEAD OR THE PLANS HAD WRONG
1. FIVE call sites, not four. apps/minimal-app/src/lib/api-passthrough.ts is the fifth and is the scaffold a fork copies, so leaving it stamping the raw peer propagates the bug into every fork.
2. The env read could not live in the module. packages/env's charter forbids the package touching the environment (every app's start.ts is aliased into the CLIENT module graph). createClientAddressResolver(env) is a factory called once at module scope in a per-app server-only file — also better on its own terms, since parsing a CIDR list is start-up work and a per-request resolver would reparse on every log record.
3. A malformed chain entry is SKIPPED during the walk, not treated as a global fallback to request.ip. A global fallback breaks the plan's own reason for walking rightwards: an attacker could prepend garbage and collapse every user into the proxy's shared bucket.
4. The inbound seam header is now DELETED when there is no peer to stamp over. x-wallow-client-ip is an ordinary request header, so a caller can send one and the SDK's forwarded.ts would append it to the outbound chain. This is the forgery hole the 0137 plan found; it is the one thing that phase contributed.
5. The docs row went to docs/operations/reverse-proxy.md, not docs/getting-started/configuration.md — that table is .NET double-underscore options binding, and reverse-proxy.md already owns proxy trust.

COMPOSITION WITH THE BACKEND, verified by reading UseForwardedHeaders' behaviour: it pops the RIGHTMOST XFF entry into Connection.RemoteIpAddress (ForwardLimit 1), which the API's rate limiter keys on. Today the chain reaching the API is 'realclient, caddyAddr' so the pop yields Caddy — one bucket for everyone. Stamping the RESOLVED address makes it 'realclient, realclient', so the pop yields the real client.

TOOLCHAIN FINDINGS, both recorded in packages/lint/CLAUDE.md
- packages/env/src/** needed the no-magic-numbers ignore:[0,1] relaxation that five other globs already carry. Its index arithmetic is ordinary; every number that MEANS something is a named constant.
- A hex literal cannot pass the gate at all: oxfmt lower-cases hex digits and unicorn/number-literal-case demands upper, so format and lint undo each other forever. The masks are derived from the bit widths instead, which also states what they are. The one other place this bites, apps/wallow-auth/e2e/totp.ts, uses a file-level oxlint-disable.

EVIDENCE
pnpm check green end to end, 45/45 turbo tasks, exit 0. packages/env: 88 tests over 4 files. The acceptance criteria are held by named cases in packages/env/src/client-address.test.ts ('ignores a forwarded chain sent by a peer that is not a trusted proxy', 'puts two clients behind one proxy at two different addresses', 'ignores a prefix the caller prepended ahead of the address a proxy appended') and by three cases added to each of the three app specs. One packages/ui menubar run failed under full-gate concurrency and passed 1481/1481 in isolation — that is Wallow-x5da / xzy1.6 territory, unrelated to this change.

FOLLOW-UP FILED: Wallow-cybh — gate resolveRequestOrigin's x-forwarded-proto read on the same trusted set, which the 1639 plan explicitly kept out of scope.

title: GetPlan() reads a 'plan' claim nothing writes — plan-targeted announcements match nobody
description:
Latent bug, found while surveying prior art for a billing module.

api/src/Shared/Wallow.Shared.Kernel/Extensions/ClaimsPrincipalExtensions.cs:84-87 exposes
GetPlan(), reading a "plan" claim. Nothing in the codebase ever WRITES that claim — no token
issuance path emits it.

Its one consumer is `AnnouncementsController.cs:84`, which targets announcements by plan. (This
bead previously cited AnnouncementTargetingService.cs:86 — wrong file, wrong line.) A repo-wide
grep for the literal "plan" claim name returns exactly two lines in api/src, both in
ClaimsPrincipalExtensions.cs — the doc comment and the read — so nothing anywhere issues it.
Because the claim is always absent, a plan-targeted announcement silently matches ZERO users.
No exception, no log line — the feature just never fires, which is why it has gone unnoticed.

Three ways out, in order of preference:
1. Emit the claim from the token-issuance path with a sensible default until real plans exist

title: Two-phase Stripe webhook with layered idempotency
description:
Phase 1: verify the signature, persist the raw event, return 200. Nothing else. Stripe
retries on timeout, so any work done before the 200 is work that can be done twice.
Phase 2: process asynchronously — Wolverine is already the messaging layer, use it.

Idempotency at three layers, because retries arrive by more than one path (webhook redelivery,
manual replay, reconcile):
1. the Stripe event id — already seen, drop
2. the effect — applying it twice is a no-op
3. the ledger row — a natural key prevents a duplicate append

Reconciliation reads Stripe's `events.list`, not the local table: the local table cannot tell
you about an event that never arrived. That inverts the usual instinct and is the reason drift
detection works.

Also: the webhook endpoint is unauthenticated by nature (Stripe calls it) — signature
verification IS the authentication. Make sure it sits outside the tenant-resolution middleware's
assumptions and does not trip the auth pipeline.
acceptance_criteria:
A replayed event produces no duplicate ledger row or duplicate effect; a webhook
that times out mid-processing leaves no partial state; an event missed entirely is recovered by
replaying events.list.

title: Billing module — ledger first, Stripe second
description:
Wallow has NO billing anywhere: no subscription, no plan, no invoice, no payment provider.
Two READMEs claim otherwise (see the separate stale-docs bug bead). PlatformPlatform (MIT) has a
production-shaped Stripe integration worth studying closely and porting selectively.

Research doc: `docs/plans/2026-07-31/2134-mit-prior-art-harvest.md` section 5 — full design,
the port verdict, and an explicit do-not-copy list.

SEQUENCING GATE: no schema work here until `feat/multi-org-membership` merges into `main` — a
subscription is per-tenant, and that branch reshapes tenant identity. The trigger is the MERGE,
not the branch work. Phase 2 of docs/plans/2026-07-31/1954-multi-org-membership-implementation.md
has already landed ON THE BRANCH (commits 2265cdfd..e03f668d, where `WallowUser.TenantId` is
genuinely gone), but `main` still declares `public Guid TenantId { get; set; }` on `WallowUser`.
So the old wording — "until Phase 2 lands" — now reads as "proceed" to anyone checking `main`,
which is precisely the case this gate exists to stop. Check the real condition with:

    git merge-base --is-ancestor e03f668d main

Delete this paragraph only once that command exits 0. Until then the gate is live.

## Order of work, and why

Ledger BEFORE gateway. The append-only billing_events table plus MRR calculation is the piece
with the most value per unit of risk: it needs no payment provider, no PCI surface, no webhook
endpoint, and it is what makes every later step verifiable. Wiring Stripe first and adding
reporting later means the reporting has no trustworthy history to read.

## Ideas worth taking from upstream

- **events.list as the source of truth for reconciliation.** Stripe's event stream, replayed,
  is authoritative — not the local table, and not a webhook that may have been missed. This is
  what makes drift detection possible at all.
- **Two-phase webhook**: acknowledge fast (200 immediately on signature verify + persist), then
  process asynchronously. Stripe retries aggressively on timeout; doing work inline turns a slow
  query into duplicate processing.
- **Layered idempotency**: at the event id, at the effect, and at the ledger row. One layer is
  not enough because retries arrive by more than one path (webhook redelivery AND replay).
- **Append-only ledger**: never update a billing row. Every state change is a new event; current
  state is a fold. Money that can be UPDATEd is money whose history can be lost.
- **Drift detection as a first-class feature**, with a reconcile command an operator can run.

## Explicit do-not-copy list

- Invoices stored as a **jsonb array on the subscription** — that is upstream's shortcut and it
  makes 'list all unpaid invoices across tenants' unindexable. Wallow uses a real table.
- Their in-memory KPI aggregation (see the admin epic — same mistake, different surface).
- Any inline webhook processing.
acceptance_criteria:
A tenant has a plan, a subscription lifecycle backed by an append-only ledger,
invoices in a queryable table, Stripe wired through a narrow interface with a two-phase webhook,
and an operator command that detects and reconciles drift against Stripe's event stream.

title: Evaluator — scope precedence and asymmetric disable
description:
The core behaviour. Resolution walks scopes most-specific-first (User, then Tenant, then
System); the first ENABLE found wins; but an explicit DISABLE at ANY scope short-circuits the
whole resolution to off regardless of how specific an enable below it was. Percentage rollout
applies only when no explicit override matched at any scope.

That asymmetry is a kill-switch guarantee: disabling a broken flag at System scope must not be
overridable by a per-user enable someone set last week. Test it directly and name the test after
the guarantee, not the mechanism.

Also decide and test the unknown-key behaviour: a key present in the DB but absent from code
must be inert, never implicitly enabled. REPORTING that key as drift is NOT this bead's
work — `Wallow-qw03.6` (startup reconciler) owns stale-key reporting in its own acceptance
criteria ("stale keys are reported and left in place"). This bead owns the inert behaviour only.
acceptance_criteria:
Tests cover every precedence pair, the asymmetric disable, percentage fallthrough
when no override matches, and the inert-unknown-key case.

title: Delivery to the browser — flags on the current-user payload, typed key union
description:
Frontend contract. Two parts:

1. **Transport.** Flags ride the existing current-user payload that packages/auth's
   currentUserQuery/useCurrentUser already fetches through the BFF — one round trip, already
   primed in route beforeLoad via ensureCurrentUser, already invalidated on identity change.
   Do NOT add a second flags endpoint the client polls.

2. **Typing.** Generate a FeatureFlagKey string-literal union from the C# declarations so a
   typo is a typecheck failure, not a silently-false flag. The generation must ride the existing
   OpenAPI snapshot -> pnpm --filter sdk generate pipeline (and therefore the CI drift gate), not
   a new bespoke codegen step.

3. **Consumption.** A useFeatureFlag(key) hook in packages/auth, alongside hasRole/hasPermission
   which solve the identical shape of problem. No per-app copy.
acceptance_criteria:
A component reads a flag with full type safety, an unknown key fails typecheck,
no extra network request is issued, and the CI drift gate catches a C#-side flag rename.

Wallow has Microsoft.FeatureManagement wired for MODULE on/off toggles only
(appsettings FeatureManagement.Modules.X, read by WallowModules.cs). There is no per-tenant,
per-user, or percentage rollout capability anywhere. PlatformPlatform (MIT) has a complete,
well-shaped implementation worth porting.

Research doc: `docs/plans/2026-07-31/2134-mit-prior-art-harvest.md` section 4 — full design,
file inventory, and the port verdict with reasons.

SEQUENCING GATE: no schema work here until `feat/multi-org-membership` merges into `main` —
that branch makes Membership a first-class aggregate and DROPS `WallowUser.TenantId`, and every
table in this epic keys off tenant identity, so starting first means rewriting the migrations.
The trigger is the MERGE, not the branch work. Phase 2 of
docs/plans/2026-07-31/1954-multi-org-membership-implementation.md has already landed ON THE
BRANCH (commits 2265cdfd..e03f668d, where `WallowUser.TenantId` is genuinely gone), but `main`
still declares `public Guid TenantId { get; set; }` on `WallowUser`. So the old wording —
"until Phase 2 lands" — now reads as "proceed" to anyone checking `main`, which is precisely the
case this gate exists to stop. Check the real condition with:

    git merge-base --is-ancestor e03f668d main

Delete this paragraph only once that command exits 0. Until then the gate is live.

## MVP cut (decided)

Ship System + Tenant + User scopes ONLY. Drop the plan-tier scope (Wallow has no plan concept
until the billing epic; see the separate `plan` claim bug bead) and drop A/B experiments
(buckets/sequences/pins) — that is a second, larger feature riding on the same evaluator.

## What is worth taking, verbatim where possible

- The **scope model**: a flag resolves against an ordered list of scopes, most specific wins,
  and DISABLE is asymmetric — an explicit disable at any scope beats an enable at a narrower
  one. That asymmetry is the whole safety property; do not "simplify" it away.
- **Van der Corput low-discrepancy bucketing** for percentage rollout: deterministic from the
  subject id, no stored assignment, and stable as the percentage moves up (a subject enabled at
  10%% stays enabled at 20%%). A naive hash %% 100 does not have that property and produces a
  reshuffle on every percentage change.
- **FNV-1a of the flag key as a per-flag offset** into the sequence, so two flags at the same
  percentage do not select the same population.
- **Code-as-source-of-truth**: flags are declared in C#, the database holds only overrides and
  state. A flag that exists in the DB but not in code is drift, and the reconciler is what makes
  that statement true at startup.

## What NOT to take

Their admin UI shape, their plan-tier scope, and any in-memory caching design — Wallow has
Valkey and a different request pipeline.
acceptance_criteria:
A flag can be declared in C#, overridden per-tenant and per-user, rolled out by
percentage, read from a React component through a typed key union, and toggled by an admin —
with the evaluator's precedence and asymmetric-disable rules covered by tests.

title: [spike] Decide who owns the rollout bucket: Identity or the flags module
description:
The largest open design decision in this epic; everything downstream depends on the answer.

Percentage rollout needs a stable per-subject bucket. Two options:

A. **Identity owns it.** WallowUser and Organization each get a RolloutBucket computed on
   creation; Identity publishes it on the existing UserCreated/OrganizationCreated integration
   events. The flags module reads it from its own projection. Pro: one authority, cheap to
   evaluate. Con: touches Identity's aggregates, and backfill for existing rows (free here —
   deployment status says drop and re-seed).

B. **Flags module derives it.** Bucket = hash(subjectId) computed at evaluation time, nothing
   stored. Pro: zero cross-module coupling, no projection, no events, no backfill. Con: the
   bucket cannot be inspected or pinned, and an admin cannot answer "why is this tenant in?"
   without recomputing.

Note that (B) is what the van der Corput approach actually enables — the whole point of a
low-discrepancy sequence is that you do not need to store the assignment. Weigh that against the
support/debuggability cost before defaulting to (A).

Cross-module rule applies either way: the flags module must NOT hold an FK into Identity's
schema. Any shared identity data arrives via Wolverine integration events through
Shared.Contracts.
acceptance_criteria:
A decision recorded on this bead with its reasoning, including how an operator
answers 'why did this subject get this flag?' under the chosen option.

title: S3 — packages/logger
description:
Scaffold `@bc-solutions-coder/logger`. Depends on `utils`.

Transport is **browser -> app server -> OTLP**, NOT "through the BFF". If any copy of an older
design doc still claims BFF transport, the v2 plan wins.

1. Two entries mirroring the SDK's split: `.` is the browser core (buffers and posts); `./server`
   is a web-standard `Request -> Response` handler with no host-framework dependency, the same
   contract `packages/sdk/src/server/handlers.ts` follows.
2. **One transport, one record format, one server handler, TWO mount points.** The browser entry
   takes the ingest path as configuration and knows nothing about CSRF; it takes an optional
   credential hook that the BFF app supplies and the passthrough app does not.
   - `wallow-web` mounts the handler under `/bff/logs` (existing `/bff/$` namespace).
   - `wallow-auth` mounts it as its OWN Start server route. It has a server; that was never the
     problem. Do NOT route logs through `createApiPassthrough`.
3. Events are NAMED, not prose: `log.info("form.submitted", {...})` — dotted, low-cardinality,
   groupable in Grafana. Free-text messages are unqueryable.
4. Wire the existing `x-request-id` correlation contract through log records. `logger` does NOT
   depend on `sdk` — it takes a `getCorrelationId()` binding instead of importing a heavy package.
5. Replace the five `console.*` call sites the audit found.
6. Point it at the `grafana/otel-lgtm` stack already in `docker/`.

## Log ingest security model — DECIDED

**CSRF is not the control this endpoint needs, and never was.** `/bff/logs` inherits the check
because of WHERE IT LIVES — the BFF blanket-rejects every unsafe method that does not echo the
token — not because log ingest has CSRF semantics. Classic CSRF damage requires the endpoint to
act with the victim's authority; writing a log record does not. So `wallow-auth` does NOT get a
CSRF substitute. It gets the controls this endpoint class always needed, and so does `wallow-web`.

`handleLogIngest` applies all of these in BOTH apps:

| Guard | Why, and what already exists |
| --- | --- |
| **Origin allowlist** — reject any POST whose `Origin` is not this app's own | The load-bearing one, and the only one that survives the beacon path: `Origin` is a forbidden header name, so script cannot forge it, and a cross-origin `sendBeacon` carries the attacker's. NEW CODE — there is no origin or `Sec-Fetch-Site` checking anywhere in `packages/sdk/src/server/` today. |
| **Payload caps** — max body bytes, max records per batch, max message length | Reject, do not truncate. `sendBeacon` caps at 64 KiB regardless, so treat that as the ceiling, not the budget. |
| **Per-IP rate limit** | The plumbing exists: `CLIENT_IP_HEADER` and the `PeerRequest.ip` seam were built so the API could rate-limit through the proxy. Reuse that seam; THE LIMITER ITSELF IS NEW — today all rate limiting is backend-side. |
| **Server-side stamping** — timestamp, IP, tenant, `x-request-id` | Never trust a client's copy of any of these, or a forged record can impersonate a real one. |
| **CSRF — `wallow-web` only** | Not optional there: the route is under `/bff/` and the BFF gates all POSTs. `wallow-auth` has no session, so `readCsrfCookie()` returns `null` and there is nothing to check. |

On the BFF path only, the CSRF token rides in the BODY on the `sendBeacon` path (beacons cannot
set headers), and `handleLogIngest` accepts it from either body or header.

**Rejected — do not revisit:**
- *Server-side logging only for `wallow-auth`.* Loses client-side error capture on login, MFA and
  consent — the highest-value logs in the product, from unauthenticated users you have no other
  visibility into.
- *Proxy logs through to the API.* Puts an unauthenticated write endpoint on the real API surface,
  and the passthrough forwards verbatim: no origin check, no caps, no local rate limit.
- *Drop the CSRF check on the shared path so one code path serves both.* The asymmetry is real;
  encode it in configuration, not by weakening `wallow-web`.

**One open sub-question, scoped to `wallow-web` and safe to defer.** The design already uses
`fetch(..., { keepalive: true })` with an `x-csrf-token` HEADER for normal flushes; only the
TERMINAL unload flush uses `sendBeacon`, and only that path needs the body-carried token. MDN's
own note says code needing to set request properties should use `fetch` + `keepalive` instead,
which suggests the terminal flush could too and drop the body token entirely. Evaluate it, but
CHECK BROWSER SUPPORT FIRST — `keepalive` landed in Firefox far later than `sendBeacon`, and both
share the same 64 KiB quota. Changes nothing for `wallow-auth`, so it must not block this slice.
notes:
S3 complete. `pnpm check` green end to end (exit 0).

SHIPPED
- packages/logger: two entries (`.` browser core, `./server` ingest handler + createServerLogger + OTLP encoder + rate limiter). Zero dependencies and zero peerDependencies; `src/charter.test.ts` pins it. 7 files / 151 tests.
- Mount points: wallow-web `/bff/logs` (static sibling out-ranking the `/bff/$` splat, CSRF-verified via the SDK's csrfTokenMatches); wallow-auth `/logs` (own Start server route, NOT createApiPassthrough, no authorize because it holds no session). Same handler both sides.
- Browser singletons at each app's `src/shared/lib/log.ts`; wallow-web also has `src/app/lib/log.server.ts` (split out of log-ingest.server.ts to keep bff.server.ts off an import cycle). wallow-auth gets no server logger: nothing in its server code records anything yet, and an export with no caller rots.
- Docs: `docs/development/logging.md` + toc entry (docs site rebuilt, 0 warnings); repo-map rows in root CLAUDE.md, apps/CLAUDE.md and packages/logger/CLAUDE.md.

DEVIATIONS FROM THE BEAD, both deliberate
1. `createLogIngestHandler(options)` returning the handler, not `handleLogIngest(request, {...})`. The rate limiter is state that must live across requests; a limiter constructed per call counts to one and never refuses anything.
2. `allowedOrigins` accepts a resolver function, and BOTH apps pass `(request) => [resolveRequestOrigin(request)]`. wallow-auth reads three env vars and has no config naming its own public origin, so a WALLOW_LOG_ALLOWED_ORIGINS would have meant four compose edits plus a real empty-list lockout risk in a fork (an empty list rejects everything by design). The resolver is the classic OWASP Origin-versus-target check instead: zero new env vars, zero compose edits, and it honours x-forwarded-proto.

CONSOLE SITES: 3 of 5 replaced (bff.server.ts x2, bff-demo.tsx x1). The other two stay and should NOT be chased:
- packages/sdk/src/server/proxy.ts:518 — replacing it creates an sdk -> logger edge on a package that publishes independently.
- apps/wallow-auth/e2e/global-setup.ts:113 — Playwright setup; console is the correct sink, there is no app server to post to.

OUT-OF-SCOPE FIX FOLDED IN: scripts/check-exports.sh was missing BOTH packages/logger and packages/navigation (an S4 acceptance gap). Added; verified out of band that each passes publint --strict and attw (node16-ESM + bundler green for `.` and `./server`).

STILL OPEN, deferred as the bead allows: the sendBeacon-vs-fetch+keepalive question for wallow-web's terminal flush. Not evaluated. Both share the same 64 KiB quota and keepalive landed in Firefox far later than sendBeacon, so it needs a browser-support check before anyone touches it. Changes nothing for wallow-auth.

description:

- `shared/testing/invalidation.ts` (40) — runs the SDK's real `invalidations` predicates against

- `shared/testing/node-async-hooks-browser-shim.ts` (54) — browser-project plumbing.
- `shared/testing/harness-routes.ts` (127) and wallow-auth's `shared/testing/harness.ts` (20) —

- `browser-styles-wiring.test.ts` -> `assertBrowserStylesWiring({ appDir, extraSpecs })`. Same

- `theme-wiring.test.tsx` -> `assertThemeWiring({ tokens, probeClass })`. Identical probe; differs

**Why both halves are checked separately**: with no utilities a catalog control has no box —

actionability timeout. With no theme every Tailwind colour token maps onto a VALUELESS custom
property, so `bg-card` paints `rgba(0, 0, 0, 0)` and colour assertions pass VACUOUSLY. Two
different silent failures, so two different assertions.

After this, `shared/testing/` is EMPTY in both apps — see the S4 note about dropping `testing`
from the `wallow/zone-dag` allowlist alongside `stores`.

title: S2 — packages/env (server env contract + request-origin x3)
description:
Scaffold `@bc-solutions-coder/env` — the schema-validated, server-only, fail-loudly-at-boot env
contract. This is the "config + zod, server-only" node in the design doc's dependency graph.

NOTE the name: `packages/config` is TAKEN by the Vite preset package and cannot absorb this.
`base-path.ts` does NOT come here — it goes to `packages/config` (see the S2b sibling).

Content:
1. The env contract itself: `WALLOW_API_INTERNAL_URL` and the other boot-time reads, validated
   with zod, failing at startup rather than at the first request. A fork must learn about a
   misconfiguration when the process starts.
2. **All three copies of `request-origin.ts`.** The three source files are BYTE-IDENTICAL:
   `apps/wallow-web/src/shared/lib/`, `apps/wallow-auth/src/shared/lib/`, and
   `apps/examples/minimal-app/src/lib/`. Their own spec header concedes it — "The helper is a
   verbatim copy per Start app, so the drift guard lives here too" and "the guard keeping all
   three copies byte-identical". A hand-written drift guard across three copies is the shape that
   says "this is a package".

**The union of the three test suites is the package's suite, not the intersection.** wallow-web's
copy covers scheme-sanitisation cases the auth copy does not: `javascript:`, `https://evil.example`,
`https@evil.example`, embedded-space values, comma-joined proxy chains, trailing-colon and
upper-case schemes, whitespace-only values. Those are security cases — carry every one across.

**Resolves the open question on `apps/examples/minimal-app`.** It holds the third copy, so this
slice decides whether minimal-app takes the new packages; it cannot defer it. `scripts/fork-smoke/`
documents the canonical fork layout, so its answer is also a docs answer.

## Acceptance
Epic acceptance criteria, plus: zero remaining copies of `resolveRequestOrigin` outside the
package, and a boot-time failure test for a missing/invalid var.
notes:
base-path.ts comes here after all, NOT to packages/config (reversed by the user: env is being built anyway, so one config package beats a split). It must be its OWN ./base-path subpath with zero deps and NO side effects — wallow-auth's vite.config.ts imports it at config load time in plain Node ESM, so if importing it can trip the fail-at-boot env validation, vite build starts failing on a missing runtime var. Scaffold the exports map with that subpath isolation from the start. Tracked as the S2b child.
S2 DONE — packages/env shipped, pnpm check green (exit 0).

WHAT SHIPPED
Subpath-only package, no '.' barrel, dependencies and peerDependencies both {}:
  ./request-origin  → resolveRequestOrigin(request)
  ./internal-origin → resolveInternalOrigin(env, requestOrigin?) + INTERNAL_ORIGIN_ENV_KEY

title: S2b — base-path.ts into packages/env (./base-path subpath)
description:
Move `apps/wallow-auth/src/shared/lib/base-path.ts` (114 lines) into `packages/env` as a
dedicated `./base-path` subpath.

**Why `env` and not `packages/config`.** `packages/env` is being created anyway (S2), and keeping
every "how is this app configured" derivation in ONE package beats splitting base-path off into
the Vite-preset package and asking every future reader to remember the split. `packages/config`
stays exactly what it is: the Vite presets, never built, never published, zero runtime footprint.

## The constraint that makes or breaks this

`apps/wallow-auth/vite.config.ts` imports this module **at config load time**, evaluated as plain
Node ESM before any app bundle exists. That yields three hard requirements:

1. **`./base-path` is its OWN subpath with ZERO dependencies and NO side effects.** It must not
   pull in zod, the env schema, or anything server-only. If importing it can trigger the package's
   fail-loudly-at-boot validation, then `vite build` starts failing on a missing runtime env var —
   which is exactly backwards, since the whole point of the boot check is to fail at *startup*.
   Subpath isolation is what prevents that. Same reason `packages/config` deliberately has no
   barrel.
2. **`packages/env` must be BUILT before wallow-auth's Vite config loads.** This is a real
   build-order edge, and it is the same one `packages/sdk` already has (apps typecheck against
   `dist/`) — a known pattern, not a new hazard, but it must be reflected in the build order and
   in the Dockerfile.
3. **The module stays PURE STRING WORK for all three of its contexts** — `vite.config.ts` (plain
   Node ESM, where `import.meta.env` does not exist at all, hence the optional read behind
   `BASE_PATH`), the SSR bundle (`start.ts`, the passthrough wrapper), and the client bundle
   (`router.tsx`). No `node:` imports; no `process.env` reads outside the config's own call.

Verify requirement 1 with a spec: importing `@bc-solutions-coder/env/base-path` in a bare Node
context with NO environment variables set must not throw.

## Acceptance
- `pnpm --filter @bc-solutions-coder/wallow-auth typecheck` and `build` both green; the app still
  serves correctly under a non-empty `AUTH_BASE_PATH`, and under an empty one.
- `apps/wallow-auth/src/base-path-wiring.test.ts` still passes (or moves with the module).
- Importing `./base-path` with an empty environment does not throw.
- `pnpm check` green.
notes:
DONE — with one deliberate deviation from the bead's literal instruction, plus one requirement
that turned out to be a non-issue.

## Deviation: the file did NOT move whole. It split.

The bead says "move base-path.ts (114 lines) into packages/env". Only the four PURE STRING
functions moved — normalizeBasePath, toViteBase, stripBasePath, withBasePath. Three exports
stayed in apps/wallow-auth/src/shared/lib/base-path.ts: BASE_PATH, toAppHref (whose default
argument binds it), and AUTH_BASE_PATH_ENV_KEY.

The reason is measured, not stylistic. Probe: appended `export const PROBE =
import.meta.env?.BASE_URL` to a packages/env module and ran `vite build`. The emitted dist/
contains:

    var PROBE = "/";

Vite substitutes import.meta.env.BASE_URL with a STRING LITERAL at build time, and a library
build has no base, so it always bakes "/". A BASE_PATH constant living in packages/env would
therefore freeze to "/" in the published dist/ and silently break every based build downstream.
Worse, it would look completely correct in-repo: exports points at src/, publishConfig.exports
remaps to dist/ only at publish, so in this workspace the substitution keeps happening inside
the APP's build where it is right. A landmine that only detonates at publish. Anything a bundler
substitutes belongs in the bundle being built, not in a library.

AUTH_BASE_PATH_ENV_KEY stayed for a different and principled reason, the same seam S2 set for
internal-origin: INTERNAL_ORIGIN_ENV_KEY (WALLOW_API_INTERNAL_URL) is a workspace-wide
convention and ships in the package; AUTH_BASE_PATH is ONE app's variable. The package answers
"what shape is a base path", the app answers "what is mine". No re-export of the package through
the app module, so the seam stays visible at every call site — 4 consumers now import the shape
functions from @bc-solutions-coder/env/base-path directly (router.tsx, start.ts,
api-passthrough.server.ts, vite.config.ts); the other 18 import only BASE_PATH/toAppHref and
were untouched.

## Requirement 2 was a non-issue

The bead calls "packages/env must be BUILT before wallow-auth's Vite config loads" a real
build-order edge. It is not. packages/config already points its exports at src/*.ts and is
imported from vite.config.ts today (wallowAppConfig); Vite's config loader bundles TS sources.
packages/env's exports point at src/ the same way. No build-order edge, no Dockerfile ordering
change beyond copying the package in (done for S2 already).

## Requirement 1 (zero deps, no side effects) is pinned, not just honoured

base-path.ts has no imports at all and reads no environment. base-path.test.ts pins it with a
spec that empties process.env, vi.resetModules(), re-imports the module and asserts it evaluates
and exports exactly the four names. src/charter.test.ts (from S2) independently scans every
shipped module for process.env / import.meta.env / any import statement.

## Acceptance criteria

- pnpm --filter @bc-solutions-coder/wallow-auth typecheck — green
- default (empty) base build — green, via pnpm check
- AUTH_BASE_PATH=/auth build — verified three ways:
  * emitted asset URLs carry the prefix (/auth/assets/*.js, /auth/piggy-icon.svg)
  * decompiled chunk shows `var _ = h("/auth/")` — BASE_PATH computed from the correctly
    substituted literal INSIDE the app's bundle, which is the whole point of the split
  * RUNTIME smoke on the built Nitro output (node .output/server/index.mjs, PORT=3099):
    GET /auth/login -> 200 with prefixed asset refs in the HTML; each of those assets -> 200;
    bare /login -> 307 to /auth/login; GET /auth/v1/me -> ECONNREFUSED to the absent upstream,
    i.e. the route MATCHED and stripBasePath ran (a route miss would be 404)
- base-path-wiring.test.ts unchanged and passing
- pnpm check exit 0; packages/env now 81 tests / 4 files; wallow-auth 963 tests pass

## Guard mutations (each applied, observed to fail, restored)

1. base-path gains an env precondition at import time -> FAILS ✓
2. base-path reads import.meta.env (the substitution trap) -> FAILS ✓
3. the ./base-path subpath dropped from exports -> FAILS ✓
4. the module gains a hidden export the spec does not name -> FAILS ✓

Restored: 81 passing.

Docs: packages/env/CLAUDE.md gained "What a bundler-substituted value cannot be" carrying the
`var PROBE = "/"` measurement, so the next person who wants to "finish the move" finds the
reason before they try.

title: Four documents still claim apps typecheck against packages/sdk/dist/
description:
Stale since `584adc3b` ("build: resolve workspace packages from source in-repo, dist on publish").
`packages/sdk/package.json`'s `exports` map resolves EVERY subpath (`.`, `./server`,
`./server/passthrough`, `./query`) to `./src/*.ts`. `dist/` appears only in the top-level
`main`/`module`/`types` fallback and in `publishConfig.exports`, which npm swaps in at pack time —
so in-repo, nothing typechecks against `dist/` at all.

FIVE wrong statements across FOUR documents, not the two this bead was filed with. Verified on
disk at audit time; re-grep before editing, these line numbers have already moved once:

- `CLAUDE.md:88` — "pnpm --filter @bc-solutions-coder/sdk build   # build the SDK FIRST (apps
  typecheck against dist/)"
- `apps/CLAUDE.md:18` — "**Build the SDK before touching an app** — apps typecheck against
  `packages/sdk/dist/`:"
- `packages/sdk/CLAUDE.md:6` — the section heading "Four entry points (exports map → `dist/`)".
  True only of `publishConfig`; the in-repo `exports` map points at `src/`.
- `packages/sdk/CLAUDE.md:64` — "Apps typecheck against `dist/` — **build the SDK before dependent
  apps**."
- `apps/wallow-web/README.md:22` — "Build the SDK first — the app typechecks against its `dist/`."

`packages/sdk/CLAUDE.md:29` is NOT one of them — it describes the lint rule banning deep imports
into `dist/**` and `src/**`, which is still accurate. Leave it alone.

Each of the five sends a reader to run an unnecessary build and implies a stale-`dist` failure
mode that cannot occur in-repo.

What to say instead, rather than just deleting the sentence: `pnpm check` DOES still need `dist/`,
because its last step `check:exports` (`scripts/check-exports.sh` — publint + attw) runs over the
BUILT package, and `pnpm build` precedes it in the `check` chain for that reason. So the SDK build
is not useless; it is simply not a prerequisite for typechecking an app. Say that.

Found during the web test/comment audit (epic Wallow-s1p3) as an instance of exactly the complaint
that motivated it: stale prose that makes the next reader route around a problem that no longer
exists.
acceptance_criteria: grep -rn "typecheck.*dist" across CLAUDE.md, apps/CLAUDE.md, packages/sdk/CLAUDE.md and apps/wallow-web/README.md returns nothing. Each of the five sites instead states that the SDK build is needed for pnpm check:exports, not for typechecking an app. packages/sdk/CLAUDE.md:29 (the deep-import lint rule) is unchanged.
notes:
Fixed. CLAUDE.md:88 was already corrected by an earlier commit ('turbo run build (topological; no need to build the SDK first)'), so four of the five listed sites remained; all four edited. packages/sdk/CLAUDE.md:29 (deep-import lint rule) untouched as instructed.

The claim was NOT confined to the four documents in the bead. Plan step 4's sweep found three more live-doc copies, all fixed in the same pass:
- docs/development/frontend-setup.md — '# Build the SDK first (apps typecheck and run against dist/)' in the local-dev sequence
- packages/auth/CLAUDE.md — 'Build the SDK first ... or typecheck fails against a missing dist/'
- apps/wallow-web/README.md, second block ('## Run locally') — a '# build the SDK first, from the repo root' step separate from the line 22 site

Verified the premise rather than trusting it: tsc --traceResolution from apps/wallow-web resolves '@bc-solutions-coder/sdk' to packages/sdk/src/index.ts, with every package's dist/ present on disk. Also checked all 12 packages' exports maps — every one resolves to src/, not just the SDK, which is why the replacement prose is phrased about '@bc-solutions-coder/*' generally rather than the SDK alone.

Each site now states that the build is needed for pnpm check:exports (publint + attw over a packed tarball), which is why pnpm build precedes it in the pnpm check chain.

Out of scope, filed as Wallow-xzy1.1: turbo.jsonc justifies dependsOn ['^build'] on typecheck/test/dev with the same false dist/-resolution claim, and CLAUDE.md's turbo paragraph restates it. Not reworded here because the false rationale may be the only thing holding ^build on those three tasks — that needs a decision, not an edit.

title: Move branding.json out of api/ into packages/styles (keep it JSON)
notes:
VERIFIED: nothing in the backend reads api/branding.json. No .cs, .csproj, .props, .targets or appsettings*.json under api/ references it, and there is no BrandingOptions type anywhere in api/src. It is a leftover from the deleted Blazor Wallow.Auth/Wallow.Web apps, which bound BrandingOptions from it.

Do NOT confuse it with the backend's Branding MODULE - that serves per-OAuth-client branding from Postgres (ThemeJson), which mergeClientBranding overlays ON TOP OF this fork file at render time. Different thing, stays where it is.

Every real consumer is JS or build tooling:
- packages/styles/src/branding.ts - the only code reader ('../../../api/branding.json')
- scripts/generate-docs-theme.mjs - takes the path as argv
- docker/docs/Dockerfile - COPY api/branding.json
- apps/wallow-web/Dockerfile + apps/wallow-auth/Dockerfile - COPY api/branding.json api/branding.json
- .gitattributes 'branding.json merge=ours' - a bare filename pattern, so path-agnostic; keeps working unchanged

TARGET: packages/styles/branding.json (NOT the repo root). That package already owns the ForkBranding type and the theme emit, so co-locating the data makes it self-contained. Concrete payoff: branding.ts stops reaching outside its own package root with ../../../, and all three Dockerfiles drop their extra COPY line beyond 'COPY packages/styles'.

KEEP IT JSON - do not convert to CSS. Three reasons, each checked:
1. Six top-level keys are not colours: appName, appIcon, tagline, repositoryUrl, docsUrl, landingPage.enabled. That last is a ROUTE TOGGLE (a boolean deciding whether a page exists). CSS cannot hold it, so converting splits one fork-config file into two.
2. The 25 theme tokens are MERGED, not just rendered. packages/styles/src/branding.ts:197 mergeClientBranding overlays a per-client ThemeJson onto them, live at apps/wallow-auth/src/app/routes/login.tsx:159, per request keyed by client_id. That is a key-by-key object merge; a static stylesheet could only stack two cascades and bet on specificity per token.
3. There is more than one renderer. scripts/generate-docs-theme.mjs emits the DocFX theme from the same values - different selectors, different file. One structured source -> N renderers. CSS-as-source would make the docs generator a CSS parser. The JSON shape also mirrors the C# ThemeJson type, which keeps the client-override contract honest across both languages.

The CSS the idea is reaching for already exists: virtual:wallow-theme.css, renderThemeStyle(...) rendered per request, deliberately NOT a file on disk (packages/styles/CLAUDE.md: a generated theme.css would be stale exactly when it matters, since pnpm check runs test before build).

Scope: 1 import, 3 Dockerfiles, scripts/docs-serve.sh, .claude/agents/docfx-specialist.md, README.md, and ~15 references across docs/ + CLAUDE.md files. Mechanical but wide.
Done — commit 9ed5ca48. api/branding.json is gone; packages/styles/branding.json is canonical. branding.ts no longer reaches outside its package root, and the three Dockerfiles dropped their extra COPY. Kept as JSON per the analysis above.

title: Phase 3: consolidate duplicated vite/vitest config into shared presets
notes:

3.1 defineLibraryConfig() for the 7 package builds. 25 code lines byte-identical across all seven; query and auth are 100% identical once comments are stripped. 341 lines -> ~40 plus 7 short files. packages/ui's componentEntries() STAYS, passed as a parameter: both simpler forms were tested and fail - dropping it stops dist/components/<name>/index.js being emitted, and rolldown 1.1.5 rejects glob entries with UNRESOLVED_ENTRY. Verify with pnpm build then dist-structure.test.ts, which Phase 0.1 armed.

3.2 wallowApp() preset for the app configs, mirroring the existing wallowStyles() pattern. Fixes minimal-app's unguarded QueryClient split (bead Wallow-uc2c). KEEP ssr.noExternal - with noExternal: [] you get two react-query graphs and 'No QueryClient set' on /login; Phase 2 makes it MORE necessary, not less. VERIFY BY BOOTING .output/server/index.mjs and loading /login plus a dashboard route, checking body size and no hook errors. pnpm test does NOT catch this class of bug - vitest never builds the Nitro bundle. This is the step where parallel agents would actually help: three independent app checks.

3.3 replace the hand-maintained pre-bundle lists with include: ['@base-ui/react/*'] - 3/3 cold green at 14.8/12.7/13.0s. vite@8.1.4's expandGlobIds matches against the package's exports-map keys; dep cache _metadata.json showed 45 entries vs the 39 hand-listed. THE MECHANISM STAYS - do not empty the lists: cold with them emptied is ~50% flake, 282s vs 16.4s when it breaks. Remove the 9 dead entries that log 'Failed to resolve dependency' and pre-bundle nothing: 8 of wallow-web's 22 (all seven @base-ui/react/* since it does not declare the package, plus @tanstack/react-query) and vitest-browser-react in packages/ui from the shared baseline. MOVE forms' browser-deps.test.ts resolvability check into the preset (the ONE permitted test change in the plan - a relocation; an unresolvable optimizeDeps entry is only a WARNING in Vite, silently pre-bundles nothing, and never reaches the dep-cache hash, so the failure is silent AND intermittent; three prior false-greens documented in its header). Then delete the 'append your subpath here' ritual from packages/ui/CLAUDE.md AND packages/forms/CLAUDE.md (step 5 of its 'Adding a catalog field' list). Verify: rm -rf <pkg>/node_modules/.vite then 3x cold per package.

3.4 absorb the rest into createVitestProjects. Root resolve + extends: true replaces the per-project repetition - the ''resolve' is PER PROJECT' comment is stale, verified green on wallow-auth (66 files / 1367 tests). Fold in the 3x-duplicated wallowStyles() + setupFiles block. nodeTsxSpecs -> a *.ssr.test.tsx naming convention (4 entries, 3 renames; one file already uses it). KEEP the node:async_hooks shim - reproduced exactly (AsyncLocalStorage is not a constructor, start-storage-context@1.167.17 at module scope). Targets: wallow-web 134->~45, ui 123->~55, forms 85->~30, wallow-auth 78->~25.
3.1 DONE — commit 1fb9f051. 341 lines across 7 vite.config.ts -> 118 plus tools/vite/library.ts at 101. ui componentEntries() kept as a parameter exactly as planned. Uses build.rolldownOptions (NOT rollupOptions): vite@8.1.4's own index.d.ts:858 marks rollupOptions @deprecated in favour of it; rolldown ships as part of vite 8. This contradicts vite-review.md 297-298, which is wrong. Three supporting changes the plan missed: (1) vite added as a ROOT devDependency, since tools/ has no package.json and resolves upward; (2) declaration+outDir removed from all 7 package tsconfig.json - dead after 2.4 but not inert, outDir in a --noEmit config makes tsc INFER a rootDir and vite.config.ts reaching tools/ dies with TS6059; (3) pnpm lint extended to tools/. Verified by hashing all 588 built files before/after: 588/588 byte-identical, twice (post-refactor and post-rename). pnpm check exit 0, 5505 tests unchanged.
GOTCHA for anyone editing .oxlintrc.json: it must stay STRICT JSON, no // comments. packages/query/src/web-shell-removal.test.ts JSON.parse()s it and treats a throw as 'no exemption found', so a single comment reds four unrelated assertions with a message that points nowhere near the cause.
3.2 done — f7367267. Landed as a new workspace package packages/config (@bc-solutions-coder/config), NOT tools/vite/app.ts.

Two subpaths, no barrel: ./vite/library (defineLibraryConfig, git mv'd from tools/vite/) and ./vite/app (wallowAppConfig, new). A barrel typechecks clean and fails every packages/* build with ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND — consumers' Vite configs resolve this package as an external dep via plain Node ESM, which rejects the extensionless './library' that moduleResolution:Bundler permits. No relative imports in that package, ever.

wallowAppConfig() is deliberately plugin-free — server.port, the two use-sync-external-store aliases, ssr.noExternal, environments.client.copyPublicDir. Each app keeps a visible local plugins array. Folding wallowStyles() in would make packages/styles a dep of the package it builds with (cycle). resolve.dedupe deleted, not relocated. base stays app-local.

The package is never built and never published: no build script, no dist/, no publishConfig, exports points at src/ permanently. A config every build imports cannot be a thing every build must build first.

vite removed from the ROOT package.json — nothing outside a package imports it now. That was the whole point of the package: tools/ has no manifest so it resolved upward into root node_modules, which forced four root devDeps (styles, @tanstack/react-start, plugin-react, nitro) in a first attempt the user rejected outright.

.oxlintrc.json tools/** override tested for deadness after the move and RESTORED — tools/oxlint/wallow-lint-plugin.js still trips three no-magic-numbers warnings without it.

All three .output trees byte-identical to a pre-refactor baseline except server/index.mjs + nitro.json, both PROVEN nondeterministic (rebuild the same config twice and they still differ: embedded asset manifest with mtimes and unstable key order; a build date). Next: 3.3 pre-bundle globs.

3.4 (createVitestProjects) done — commit 8146b869. Phase 3 complete.

MEASURED: a project-level resolve MERGES into the inherited one rather than replacing it — wallow-web's browser project declares only the node:async_hooks alias and still gets the root's tsconfigPaths (verified green on routes/bff-demo.test.tsx, 10 tests; control run with the root resolve deleted is red with Failed to resolve import '@app/router').

The old comment's reason — 'importing it would boot a second browser provider' — is false: playwright() returns a descriptor and src/browser-deps.test.ts has imported the same config from the same node project all along.
- Docs: packages/testing/CLAUDE.md, packages/forms/CLAUDE.md (step 5 still said 'append to baseUiSubpaths' — a 3.3 miss), apps/CLAUDE.md, docs/development/testing.md, docs/development/frontend-setup.md.

title: Phase 4: split lint into source and test passes
notes:
Independent of the build work. Files partition exactly: 836 = 437 source + 399 test/story.

TWO CONSTRAINTS - get either wrong and oxlint silently lints ZERO files, which looks like success: oxlint does NOT expand globs in path arguments, and ignorePatterns has no ! negation.

Files: root package.json, .oxlintrc.json, new .oxlintrc.tests.json, new scripts/lint-tests.sh. lint = source only, tests excluded via --ignore-pattern. lint:tests = explicit paths via the script, config via .oxlintrc.tests.json using oxlint's extends. Enable --vitest-plugin on the test side - it exists and is enabled nowhere today.

VERIFY (the critical check, because the failure mode is a silent pass): both passes must report a NON-ZERO file count summing to 836, then introduce a deliberate violation on each side and confirm it is caught.
Commit: build: split lint into source and test passes
Phase 4 DONE.

Shape changed from the plan; outcome did not. The plan's .oxlintrc.tests.json + -c design is measurably wrong here: -c DISABLES oxlint's nested-config lookup, which would strip packages/ui's and packages/forms' test/story overrides (prefer-query-selector, jsx-max-depth, error-message, func-name-matching, prefer-number-coercion, prefer-dom-node-dataset, no-magic-numbers) plus jsx-props-no-spreading, turning the test pass red on arrival. extends would not help either: oxlint inherits only rules/plugins/overrides, NOT ignorePatterns (probe config enumerated 860 files vs the root's 840).

Landed instead:
- package.json: lint (+ lint:fix) gained --ignore-pattern '**/*.test.*' --ignore-pattern '**/*.stories.tsx'; new lint:tests + lint:tests:fix; check now runs format:check && lint && lint:tests && build && typecheck && test && check:exports.
- scripts/lint-tests.sh: enumerates its file list from 'oxlint apps packages tools --debug=files' (oxlint does NOT expand globs in path args), filters to test/story, PRINTS the count, exits 1 on zero, then runs oxlint <paths> --vitest-plugin --deny-warnings "$@". No -c. bash 3.2 compatible (no mapfile).
- .oxlintrc.json: 30 vitest rules turned off inside the EXISTING **/*.test.* + **/*.stories.tsx override. Inert on the source pass (plugin off), active on the test pass (--vitest-plugin). One file still owns every severity.
- .github/workflows/js.yml: new 'Lint tests' step; scripts/** added to both path filters.
- Docs: root CLAUDE.md (two-pass paragraph), .claude/rules/TESTING.md (specs are linted by lint:tests; e2e *.spec.ts stays on the source side), packages/ui/CLAUDE.md (why no -c).

Vitest plugin: unfiltered it produced 3559 diagnostics at --deny-warnings. Measured rule by rule; the 30 that fire are off, the remaining 41 are clean and now locked in - including no-focused-tests, no-disabled-tests, valid-title, valid-describe-callback, no-standalone-expect, no-commented-out-tests, no-conditional-tests, valid-expect-in-promise, hoisted-apis-on-top, require-awaited-expect-poll. Zero fixes required (Rule 6 held).

Three opt-outs are FALSE POSITIVES, not preferences - do not re-enable without re-measuring: valid-expect (13 hits, all against Vitest's legitimate expect(value, message) overload); expect-expect (assertions delegated to a shared helper, e.g. referencesEveryEmittedVar in packages/styles/src/theme-css.test.ts); no-conditional-expect (the if (!isWallowError(value)) { expect.unreachable(...) } narrowing guard in packages/sdk/src/errors.test.ts). The other 27 are style (prefer-expect-assertions alone was 1968).

VERIFY (the bead's own critical check - silent pass is the failure mode):
- Partition exact: source 441 + tests 399 = 840 = the full unsplit set. Both non-zero. (Plan said 836; that figure predates later specs.)
- Deliberate violation, source side: an 'any' in packages/query/src -> pnpm lint exit 1, pnpm lint:tests exit 0.
- Deliberate violation, test side: it.only in a .test.ts -> pnpm lint exit 0, pnpm lint:tests exit 1 with vitest(no-focused-tests).

- pnpm check exit 0.

lint-staged still runs plain 'oxlint --fix' with no --vitest-plugin on staged files - left as is deliberately, since the hook lints an arbitrary subset rather than a partition. Full test pass runs in pnpm check and CI.
