title: with-selector emits __require(react) into the server bundle
description:
use-sync-external-store/shim/with-selector emits __require("react") into the SSR bundle of both zoned apps. __require is createRequire(import.meta.url) - a real runtime require out of node_modules - while React is also bundled into the chunk as require_react(). That is a genuine second React instance under SSR, the classic source of hook-context failures.

SCOPE: 1 chunk per zoned app, not 3. Confirmed on a cache-defeated clean build (removed apps/*/.output, all .nitro dirs and .turbo/cache, then pnpm build --force, "Cached: 0 cached, 14 total"): minimal-app 0, wallow-auth 1 (_ssr/use-app-form-Bn7Jiumh.mjs), wallow-web 1 (_ssr/isElementDisabled-BXrKiEPY.mjs). No need to re-measure before acting.

MECHANISM. Vite leaves react EXTERNAL through the ssr pass, so a CJS require("react") inside a module Vite BUNDLES cannot be linked statically and degrades to createRequire. Nitro rewrites ESM imports of react to its own require_react(), but cannot rewrite an already-emitted createRequire call. minimal-app escapes only because its copy stays external through the Vite pass and reaches nitro intact - the decisive control, since it contains the IDENTICAL with-selector module with ZERO __require. Same module, different LINKAGE.

FIX DIRECTION CORRECTED 2026-08-27 (docs/plans/2026-08-27/1127-backlog-triage-and-sequencing.md). This bead used to direct: "extend the alias in packages/config/src/vite/app.ts to cover use-sync-external-store/shim/with-selector alongside the two specifiers it already anchors." DO NOT DO THAT. It contradicts the code it points at, on three counts:

1. React exports no useSyncExternalStoreWithSelector, so that alias resolves to an undefined import.
2. The anchored regexes at packages/config/src/vite/app.ts:73-74 are anchored PRECISELY to avoid this. The comment above them (lines 67-72) spells it out: a bare string alias matches by prefix, so use-sync-external-store/shim would also swallow .../shim/with-selector and rewrite it to the nonexistent react/with-selector. The exclusion is the guard, not the gap.
3. The existing alias already works. The var shim = __require("react") in the emitted chunk IS the aliased shim resolving to react.

TWO DEAD ENDS, recorded so nobody retries them:

* ssr.external is INERT here. Added external: ["use-sync-external-store"], cleared caches, rebuilt force: counts unchanged AND chunk hashes byte-identical, i.e. zero effect. Control probe adding "@base-ui/react" to the same list with node_modules/.vite cleared: the ssr environment genuinely re-ran (1188 modules transformed) and the chunk was still emitted at an identical 167.82 kB with no base-ui chunk in _libs/. So the external list is ignored outright for this environment - likeliest cause is a noExternal:true short-circuit set by the Start plugin or nitro, not by us.
* Re-pointing the alias has nowhere to point. use-sync-external-store@1.6.0 ships NO ESM build: every entry in its exports map (index.js, with-selector.js, shim/index.js, shim/with-selector.js) resolves to CJS re-exporting from cjs/.

REMAINING OPTIONS, none verified, in preference order:
(a) ssr.noExternal: ["react", "react-dom"] - bundle React into the Vite ssr pass so the CJS require links to it. Same shape as the existing react-query noExternal entry. react-dom must move WITH react or react-dom loads its own copy.
(b) Find and unset whatever sets noExternal:true for the ssr service environment, which would make ssr.external viable again.
(c) Vendor a tiny ESM with-selector in packages/config and alias to it. Last resort, ~20 lines of vendored React code.

Config is currently PRISTINE - no inert config was committed.

Not caused by the build-simplification work; found during it. Distinct from the closed Wallow-pzro. Plan: docs/plans/2026-08-03/1639-proxy-trust-react-dupe-nav-flake.md
acceptance_criteria: After a clean pnpm build, no chunk in any app's .output/server contains __require("react") — measured on a fresh build, not a committed one.
notes:
Even with the use-sync-external-store alias in place, use-sync-external-store/shim/with-selector still emits __require("react") into the .output/server bundle, called from 3 chunks. Latent second-React risk under SSR. Not caused by the build-simplification work; found during it.
MEASURED on a cleaned build (rm -rf apps/*/.output apps/*/.nitro, then pnpm build): minimal-app 0, wallow-auth 1 (_ssr/use-app-form-*.mjs), wallow-web 1 (_ssr/isElementDisabled-*.mjs). Confirms the corrected 1-per-zoned-app scope. Caveat: turbo reported FULL TURBO, so .output was cache-restored on unchanged inputs; re-run cache-defeated before acting.

MECHANISM CONFIRMED, and the bead's stated fix direction is WRONG.

__require is 'createRequire(import.meta.url)' - a real runtime require from node_modules. React IS bundled (require_react(), out of _libs/@tanstack/react-form+[...].mjs and _libs/@tanstack/react-router+[...].mjs), so this is a genuine second React instance under SSR.

The decisive control is minimal-app, which contains the IDENTICAL with-selector module with ZERO __require:
  minimal-app _libs/@tanstack/react-router+[...].mjs:  var React = require_react(); var shim = require_react();
  wallow-web  _ssr/isElementDisabled-*.mjs:            var React = __require('react'); var shim = __require('react');
Same module, different LINKAGE. In minimal-app it stayed external through the Vite SSR build and Nitro bundled it, linking require('react') to the bundled React. In the zoned apps Vite pre-bundled it into an app chunk (isElementDisabled-* is an optimizeDeps artifact name) and, react being external to that Vite build, the require degraded to createRequire.

Two consequences:
1. The EXISTING alias already works. 'var shim = __require("react")' IS the aliased use-sync-external-store/shim resolving to react. The alias is not the gap.
2. DO NOT extend the alias to use-sync-external-store/shim/with-selector as the description directs. React exports no useSyncExternalStoreWithSelector, so that alias produces an undefined import. packages/config/src/vite/app.ts:66-71 already says exactly this in a comment - the bead's fix direction contradicts the code it points at.

New fix direction: name use-sync-external-store in ssr.external in wallowAppConfig so Nitro bundles it, reproducing minimal-app's working linkage. Fallbacks if that does not take: optimizeDeps.exclude, then vendoring a tiny ESM with-selector in packages/config.

Plan: docs/plans/2026-08-03/1639-proxy-trust-react-dupe-nav-flake.md
BASELINE RE-MEASURED, cache defeated. Removed apps/*/.output, all .nitro dirs and .turbo/cache, then 'pnpm build --force'. Turbo reported 'Cached: 0 cached, 14 total' - a genuinely fresh build, not a cache restore. Counts unchanged from the caveated run: minimal-app 0, wallow-auth 1, wallow-web 1. The bead's corrected 1-per-zoned-app scope stands; no need to fix the number before acting.
ATTEMPTED FIX FAILED — ssr.external is INERT in this build. Recorded so nobody retries it.

Added external: ["use-sync-external-store"] to the ssr block in packages/config/src/vite/app.ts, cleared .output/.nitro/.turbo/cache, rebuilt with 'pnpm build --force' (Cached: 0 of 14). Counts UNCHANGED: minimal-app 0, wallow-auth 1, wallow-web 1 — and the chunk hashes were byte-identical (use-app-form-Bn7Jiumh.mjs, isElementDisabled-BXrKiEPY.mjs), i.e. zero effect rather than a partial one.

CONTROL PROBE to check whether ssr.external does anything at all here: temporarily added "@base-ui/react" to the same list and rebuilt wallow-web with node_modules/.vite cleared too. The ssr environment genuinely re-ran ('building ssr environment for production', 1188 modules transformed) and isElementDisabled-BXrKiEPY.js was still emitted at the identical 167.82 kB, with no base-ui chunk in _libs/. So ssr.external is ignored outright for this environment; it is not a matter of the specifier being wrong. In Vite, a noExternal:true short-circuits the external list entirely, which is the likeliest cause — set by the Start plugin or nitro's service environment, not by us.

ALIAS FALLBACK ALSO DEAD. use-sync-external-store@1.6.0 ships NO ESM build — every entry in its exports map resolves to CJS (index.js, with-selector.js, shim/index.js, shim/with-selector.js, all re-exporting from cjs/). There is no ESM entry point to alias the specifier at, so the 'point it somewhere better' shape of fix has nowhere to point. Confirmed by reading the installed package.json and file listing.

MECHANISM, refined. Vite's ssr pass leaves react EXTERNAL, so a CJS require('react') inside a module Vite BUNDLES cannot be linked statically and degrades to createRequire(import.meta.url). Nitro then rewrites ESM 'import ... from "react"' to its own bundled require_react() (visible at the top of the chunk: 'import { i as require_react } from "../_libs/@tanstack/react-form+[...].mjs"'), but it cannot rewrite an already-emitted createRequire call. minimal-app escapes only because its copy stays external through the Vite pass and reaches nitro intact.

REMAINING OPTIONS, none verified, all with real blast radius:
 (a) ssr.noExternal: ["react", "react-dom"] — bundle React into the Vite ssr pass so the CJS require links to it. Follows the same shape as the existing react-query noExternal entry, but react-dom must move with it or react-dom loads its own react.
 (b) find and unset whatever sets noExternal:true for the ssr service environment, which would make option (a) in the original plan viable again.
 (c) vendor a tiny ESM with-selector in packages/config and alias to it — last resort, ~20 lines of vendored React code.
Config left PRISTINE (git checkout); no inert config committed.

Plan: docs/plans/2026-08-03/1639-proxy-trust-react-dupe-nav-flake.md
OPTION (a) IS A THIRD DEAD END — measured AND boot-tested; recorded so nobody retries it.

Applied ssr.noExternal: [..., "react", "react-dom"] in packages/config/src/vite/app.ts. On a cache-defeated forced build (rm -rf apps/*/.output apps/*/.nitro .turbo/cache; pnpm build --force; 'Cached: 0 cached, 14 total') the grep acceptance PASSED: __require("react") file counts 0/0/0 across all three apps, with-selector linked as 'var shim = require_react()' (the minimal-app known-good shape), only Node-builtin __require targets remaining.

But the BOOT TEST FAILED HARD: PORT=3902 node apps/wallow-auth/.output/server/index.mjs, GET /login → 500, body 53 chars ({"status":500,"unhandled":true,"message":"HTTPError"}). Server log: 'TypeError: Cannot read properties of null (reading useEffect)' at _ssr/ssr.mjs:360 exports.useEffect, thrown from QueryClientProvider under renderToReadableStream inside _libs/@tanstack/react-router+[...].mjs.

MECHANISM: noExternal-ing react puts a LIVE React copy into the Vite _ssr graph, while @tanstack/react-router (NOT in noExternal) stays external and Nitro bundles it into _libs WITH react-dom's server renderer and its own require_react() copy. react-dom installs the hooks dispatcher on the _libs React's shared internals; QueryClientProvider (Vite graph) calls useEffect off the _ssr React → null dispatcher. The pre-fix state was one LATENT second React; option (a) makes both copies ACTIVE in the same render. Completing (a) would require noExternal-ing every React-touching external (@tanstack/react-router, react-dom/server path, etc.) — whack-a-mole, rejected.

LESSON: the acceptance criterion's grep is a proxy and CAN pass while SSR is broken. Any candidate fix must also pass the boot probe: built wallow-auth /login returns 200 with ~9.9k body chars (broken alias historic baseline: ~2.6k; option (a): 500/53).

NEXT: option (c) — vendor a ~40-line ESM useSyncExternalStoreWithSelector in packages/config and alias use-sync-external-store/shim/with-selector to it (anchored regex, same pattern as the existing shim aliases). ESM 'import react' stays external through Vite and Nitro rewrites it to require_react — the exact minimal-app linkage, scoped to the one module that misbehaves. Option (b) (find who forces noExternal:true) remains unexplored fallback.
FIXED via option (c) — vendored ESM with-selector, aliased in. VERIFIED end-to-end.

CHANGE: packages/config/src/vite/use-sync-external-store-with-selector.mjs — faithful de-minification of use-sync-external-store@1.6.0's cjs/use-sync-external-store-shim/with-selector.production.js (MIT, attribution in header), with useSyncExternalStore imported from react directly (React >= 18 exports it) and a default export mirroring the CJS-interop shape zustand's ESM build destructures. app.ts gains one anchored alias { find: /^use-sync-external-store\/shim\/with-selector(?:\.js)?$/u, replacement: <absolute path via fileURLToPath(import.meta.url)> } — both specifier spellings covered (bare form used by @base-ui/utils and @tanstack/react-store; .js form by zustand). packages/config/package.json gains react as a plain peerDependency (catalog:react) to satisfy knip; no install warnings (optional:true was rejected — knip flags referenced optional peers). CLAUDE.md updated.

WHY IT WORKS: the vendored module is ESM, so its 'import ... from "react"' stays external through the Vite SSR pass and Nitro rewrites it to the bundled require_react() — the exact linkage minimal-app proves correct — instead of CJS require degrading to createRequire.

VERIFICATION (cache-defeated forced build, Cached: 0 of 14):
- grep acceptance: __require("react") file counts 0/0/0 across all three apps; only Node-builtin __require targets remain repo-wide.
- linkage: wallow-auth _ssr/use-app-form-*.mjs imports require_react from _libs/@tanstack/react-router.mjs; vendored function inlined in the same chunk.
- boot probe: PORT=390x node apps/wallow-auth/.output/server/index.mjs, GET /login → 200, body element 10233 chars with fully SSR'd markup ('Sign in to your account', theme toggle) vs historic healthy ~9895 / broken ~2621 / option-(a) 500. Re-confirmed on the final post-lint-fix build.
- wallow-web boot 500s only on missing OIDC/BFF env (loadBffConfigFromEnv) — environmental, not React; its error page still SSR'd with zero hook errors.
- pnpm check: full gate green (exit 0).

Grep caveat for future probes: GNU grep treats the single-line SSR HTML as binary and silently matches nothing with -o — extract the body with python/perl instead.

title: fix LandingPage.restyle type-scale specs that assert a relation with literals
description:
apps/wallow-web/src/features/landing/components/LandingPage.restyle.test.tsx has two
tests whose NAMES state a relation to a catalog recipe while their BODIES assert only
literal class strings, so neither can detect the relation breaking:

  :62 "keeps each feature title one step below the subheading default"
        expectClasses(title, "text-lg font-semibold text-card-foreground")
        expect(title.classList.contains("text-xl")).toBe(false)
  :72 "keeps each quick-start step title one step below the subheading default"
        expectClasses(title, "text-lg font-semibold")
        expect(title.classList.contains("text-xl")).toBe(false)

WHY IT CANNOT FAIL FOR THE RIGHT REASON. Both titles are `<Text variant="subheading"
className="text-lg ...">` (LandingPage.tsx:164-172 and :210-218) — the caller className
wins the size axis through twMerge, which is what strips the recipe's text-xl. The
assertions therefore pin the CALLER's literal and the recipe's literal, never the two
against each other. Move `Text`'s `subheading` step to any other value and both tests
stay green while their stated claim ("one step below the subheading default") becomes
false — including inverting to one step ABOVE, which is exactly what would have
happened had Wallow-io5f landed at its originally proposed 16px. Neither test measures
a computed font size, so neither would have noticed.

Note that both tests are CORRECT today (18px feature title under a 20px subheading);
this is a coverage defect, not a live regression, and Wallow-io5f deliberately does not
touch this file.

FIX. Assert the relation the names claim: render a `variant="subheading"` probe beside
the titles and compare COMPUTED font sizes (`getComputedStyle(...).font-size`), the
pattern apps/wallow-web/src/heading-scale.test.tsx uses. Keep the
`contains("text-xl") === false` override-wins guard — that part is real. wallow-web's
browser vitest project loads the Tailwind pipeline (wallowStyles + vitest.setup.ts), so
the measurement is available in place.

DISCOVERED FROM Wallow-io5f (catalog-wide 20px heading standard) while auditing whether
the change would flatten a hierarchy. Wallow-io5f neither fixes nor edits this file.
notes:
RESOLVED BY DELETION (epic Wallow-s1p3, branch test/web-comment-audit). LandingPage.restyle.test.tsx is deleted in full. Both it()s named here — 'keeps each feature title one step below the subheading default' and 'keeps each quick-start step title one step below the subheading default' — are gone.

This bead's own diagnosis is the audit's shape-pin rubric arrived at independently: a body of expectClasses(...) + classList.contains(...).toBe(false) cannot detect the relation its NAME claims, because the assertion reads the class string rather than the computed value, and cn()/twMerge lets a caller's className win the size axis while the recipe class is still present.

Verified the whole file is shape pins: its only non-classList assertion is expect(section).not.toBeNull() inside a stepsBand() fixture-lookup helper. No getComputedStyle, no textContent, no canvas anywhere in it.

The type-scale relation these two MEANT to assert is now covered where it can actually fail: heading-scale.test.tsx measures computed font-size in a real browser, and wallow/text-heading-variant holds every file the linter reaches. Nothing to fix.

title: Card headings split across two type scales — CardTitle is text-lg, Text subheading is text-xl
description:
MEASURED during Wallow-lrlm.7.1 verification. Exact counts below; NEEDS USER
SIGN-OFF because it is user-visible.

THE SPLIT. packages/ui/src/components/card/card.styles.ts:24 defines
`cardTitleRecipe = cva("text-lg font-semibold text-card-foreground")` = 18px.
packages/ui/src/components/text/text.styles.ts defines the Text scale with NO
text-lg step: heading = text-2xl, subheading = text-xl (20px), body = text-base.
Wallow-lrlm.7.1 moved wallow-auth’s hand-rolled card headings onto Text, which
forces variant="subheading". Sibling auth screens now render their card heading
at two different sizes.

color="onCard">`, all in apps/wallow-auth/src/):
  features/accept-terms/components/AcceptTermsScreen.tsx:308  "Almost there!"
  features/consent/components/ConsentScreen.tsx:159           "<client> is requesting access"
  features/error/components/ErrorPage.tsx:64                  "Something went wrong"

  features/privacy/components/PrivacyPage.tsx:73              "Privacy Policy"
  features/terms/components/TermsPage.tsx:70                  "Terms of Service"
  features/verify-email/components/VerifyEmailConfirm.tsx:105 "Email Verification"
  features/verify-email/components/VerifyEmailNotice.tsx:30   "Check your email"

SEVEN HEADINGS STAYED AT 18px (still `<CardTitle>`, same app, same card slot):
  features/login/components/LoginScreen.tsx:155           "Sign in to your account"
  features/register/components/RegisterForm.tsx:277       "Create an account"
  features/forgot-password/components/ForgotPasswordForm.tsx:140 "Forgot your password?"

So the login screen’s title is 18px and the consent screen’s is 20px, on the

is affected the moment it does the same migration.

NOT A 7.1 DEFECT. 7.1 had no third option: writing text-lg back as a className
would have reintroduced the second place the scale is decided, which is exactly
what its specs ban. The systemic fix is in packages/ui.

FIX: pick ONE scale and move both sides to it — CardTitle should compose Text
rather than hard-coding its own utilities (i.e. render `<Text as="h2"
variant=... color="onCard">`), so one recipe backs both, the way MutedText
already composes Text. If the chosen scale is subheading (text-xl) the 7
CardTitle screens above grow 18px -> 20px too; if it is a new text-lg step on
Text, the 9 screens above shrink back to 18px. Either way the 16 headings end up
on one step.

ACCEPTANCE: CardTitle derives its scale from the Text recipe, not from its own
literal; all 16 wallow-auth card headings compute the same font-size in a real
browser (asserted by a computed-style spec, not a class-string match); the
chosen scale is signed off by the user before landing.
notes:

ROUTE TAKEN

title: wallow-auth has no lint gate for the catalog migration — F5.T6's gate cannot reach it
description:
F5.T6 (Wallow-lrlm.5.6) added a lint gate that makes 'pnpm lint' fail if a raw

// text element or a bare bg-foreground/text-background sidebar-inversion class is reintroduced. It protects apps/wallow-web ONLY. apps/wallow-auth is completely ungoverned, and F7.T1 (Wallow-lrlm.7.1) migrates wallow-auth onto the same catalog with no gate in its acceptance criteria and no sibling task that would add one (F7.T2 is documentation). Without this, wallow-auth's migration can silently regress the day after it lands. MEASURED, not inferred: an identical probe file 'export function Probe() { return

copy

; }' linted with the repo's own oxlint binary reports 2 errors under apps/wallow-web (react(forbid-elements) and wallow(no-sidebar-inversion)) and ZERO under apps/wallow-auth. DESIGN Add apps/wallow-auth/.oxlintrc.json mirroring apps/wallow-web/.oxlintrc.json, which is the reference implementation — read it first. It needs: - "extends": ["../../.oxlintrc.json"] - "jsPlugins": ["../../tools/oxlint/wallow-lint-plugin.js"] (the wallow JS plugin that owns wallow/no-sidebar-inversion) - rules: "wallow/no-sidebar-inversion": "error" and react/forbid-elements for p, span, h1..h6, each with a message naming Text/MutedText/PageHeader - an overrides block turning BOTH rules off for ["**/*.test.*", "**/*.stories.tsx"] (specs legitimately render raw markup as fixtures) - RESTATEMENTS the nested layout forces (see HAZARDS): the root's apps/wallow-auth/** rules (unicorn/filename-case kebab+Pascal, no-magic-numbers warn ignore [0,1]) re-expressed as "**/*.{ts,tsx}", the src/features/*/api.test.ts no-restricted-imports exemption, no-magic-numbers off in tests, and the applicable ignorePatterns. HAZARDS — each verified on oxlint 1.74.0, do not rediscover them the hard way: 1. DO NOT put these rules (or the jsPlugins entry) in the ROOT .oxlintrc.json. packages/sdk/src/oxlint-guardrails.test.ts proves the root config's import bans by COPYING the root config into a temp dir and running the real binary there; a jsPlugins entry makes that copy unloadable, oxlint emits 'Failed to parse oxlint configuration file' instead of JSON, and that whole suite fails to COLLECT. Scoping jsPlugins to an overrides[] block (the schema allows it) does NOT help — verified, it breaks identically. A bare specifier does not help either: it also resolves from the config file's directory. 2. A nested config RE-ROOTS the parent's overrides[].files globs to the child's directory, so the root's "apps/wallow-auth/**/*.{ts,tsx}" block matches NOTHING once apps/wallow-auth/.oxlintrc.json exists. Verified: adding eqeqeq:error to the root's apps/wallow-auth/** block today makes a wallow-auth file report ERROR, while the same edit to the apps/wallow-web/** block leaves a wallow-web file at WARNING because wallow-web already has a child config. Unrestated, this silently downgrades unicorn/filename-case to the category default. 3. ignorePatterns is NOT inherited by a nested config at all — restate the ones that matter or lint starts failing on generated files (routeTree.gen.ts). 4. Inherited WITHOUT restatement (verified, do not duplicate these): top-level rules (the root's no-restricted-imports still fires), categories, plugins, and the root's "**/*.test.*" block (its glob has no path prefix, so re-rooting is a no-op). Nested configs must NOT restate categories or plugins — packages/sdk/src/oxlint-guardrails.test.ts asserts that, along with 'extends resolves to the root' and 'no repo-rooted override globs', for every nested config in the tree. A new apps/wallow-auth/.oxlintrc.json is automatically subject to those three assertions. 5. The inversion ban must match the BARE form only, by EQUALITY on the whole utility after stripping variant prefixes and a leading '!'. bg-foreground/40 (a translucent scrim) is not an inversion and must stay clean, and border-foreground must NOT be in the ban list. The existing plugin already implements exactly this; reuse it, do not fork it. ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA pnpm lint fails (exit non-zero, with a message naming the rule and pointing at Text / the sidebar-* tokens) when a raw p/span/h1-h6 element or a bare bg-foreground/text-background class is introduced into a non-test apps/wallow-auth source file, and passes clean against the tree as shipped. The gate must NOT reach packages/ui or apps/wallow-web-specific carve-outs. title: wallow-web and wallow-auth browser specs render no fork theme — colour assertions there cannot catch a contrast defect
description:
Neither apps/wallow-web nor apps/wallow-auth loads the fork THEME into its Vitest browser
project, so every colour custom property the Tailwind colour utilities read is undefined and
those utilities compute to transparent. Measured in wallow-web with the drawer open at 390x844:
getComputedStyle(el).backgroundColor === "rgba(0, 0, 0, 0)" on BOTH the nav drawer (bg-sidebar)
and the mobile backdrop (bg-foreground/40).

WHY THIS MATTERS BEYOND TIDINESS. It means a colour assertion in either app's browser project is
STRUCTURALLY INCAPABLE of catching a contrast defect: every foreground and every background
reads as the same transparent value, so any computed-colour check either passes vacuously or
compares two nothings. This is the same blindness class that let a live, user-visible defect
ship through a full green suite once already in this epic — the dashboard nav labels vanished on
hover in light mode because the real class string was the tailwind-merge of a catalog recipe
with a consumer className, and nothing in the suite looked at a rendered colour. Today the gap
is INERT (grep confirms zero getComputedStyle / toHaveStyle assertions anywhere in
apps/wallow-web/src or apps/wallow-auth/src), which is precisely the problem: the first spec
that reaches for a rendered colour will get a confident false answer.

STATE OF THE WIRING TODAY (all three differ, and the divergence is undocumented):
  - packages/forms — FULLY wired. vitest.config.ts adds `plugins: wallowStyles()` and
    `setupFiles: ["./vitest.setup.ts"]`; that setup file imports ./vitest-styles.css AND renders
    the theme from `renderThemeStyle(forkResolvedBranding)` into a <style> in document.head.
    This is the reference implementation.
  - packages/ui — carries equivalent wiring, plus a Storybook project with a theme decorator.
  - apps/wallow-web — HALF wired. vitest.config.ts + vitest-styles.css + vitest.setup.ts exist
    and load the Tailwind UTILITIES, but the setup file deliberately omits the theme.
  - apps/wallow-auth — NOT wired at all. It has no stylesheet in its browser project. Its
    AcceptTermsScreen spec works around this in userland, toggling checkboxes by focus+Space
    with a comment saying the helper "depends on no layout". That app breaks the moment a spec
    CLICKS a catalog control, for the documented reason below.

WHY THE UTILITIES WERE NEEDED AT ALL (already fixed in wallow-web, still open in wallow-auth):
a ui control gets its BOX from a Tailwind utility in its recipe. With no stylesheet,
Checkbox.Root's <span role="checkbox"> measures 0x0 and every userEvent.click on it hangs to
Playwright's actionability timeout (~15s). packages/forms/CLAUDE.md states this failure mode
verbatim under "Test model".

WHY wallow-web OMITS THE THEME — a real blocker, independently reproduced, not an oversight.
Importing @bc-solutions-coder/styles from the setup file lands as the setup runs. It is a LINKED
workspace package, so Vite re-optimizes the dep graph MID-RUN; the reload hands the specs a
SECOND @tanstack/react-router copy, after which a `redirect` thrown through one module instance
no longer satisfies `isRedirect` from the other. Reproduced by appending the theme block from
packages/forms/vitest.setup.ts to apps/wallow-web/vitest.setup.ts: the suite goes from 943/943
to 1 failed / 942 passed, and the single failure is
src/app/routes/index.gate.test.tsx > "throws a BFF-login redirect (not a browser-only login()
call) when the landing page is disabled". Any fix must solve THAT, not just add the import back.
design:
The root cause is a shared one, so prefer a shared fix. packages/testing's `createVitestProjects`
deliberately leaves styling to each consumer, which is why three consumers wired it three
different ways and two of them are wrong. The strongest shape is for packages/testing to own a
STYLED browser project — utilities plus theme, one wiring, one place — and for
packages/forms, apps/wallow-web and apps/wallow-auth to adopt it. Parent this work there if that
is the route taken.

The dep-graph re-optimization is the real engineering problem and must be solved first; the rest
is mechanical. Candidate approaches, in rough order of preference:

1. Make @bc-solutions-coder/styles known to the browser project's dep optimizer up front, so the
   setup file's import cannot trigger a mid-run reload. packages/forms already declares
   pre-bundle lists for exactly this class of hazard (see its vitest.config.ts `baseUiSubpaths` /
   `formRuntime`, and the note in packages/forms/CLAUDE.md that an undiscovered subpath makes
   Vite pre-bundle a second React copy). Adding styles to `optimizeDeps.include` — or dedupe/alias
   for @tanstack/react-router — is the same medicine. VERIFY the router-identity symptom is gone,
   not merely that the suite is green.
2. Emit the theme CSS without importing the styles JS at runtime: have vitest-styles.css carry
   the resolved custom properties (the same `renderThemeStyle(forkResolvedBranding)` output,
   produced at build time by the wallowStyles() plugin), so the setup file imports only CSS.
   This sidesteps the module-graph problem entirely and is worth trying first if (1) is fiddly.
3. Only if both fail: keep the omission but make it LOUD rather than silent — a guard spec that
   fails if any spec calls getComputedStyle on a colour property while the theme is absent.
   This is the fallback, not the goal.

Then wire apps/wallow-auth's browser project the same way (it has none today), and re-check the
AcceptTermsScreen workaround: with a real stylesheet the checkbox has a box, so the focus+Space
helper can become a plain click and its "depends on no layout" comment can go.

Prove the fix does something. Pick a real contrast pair — e.g. the dashboard rail's
bg-sidebar against text-sidebar-foreground in apps/wallow-web/src/shared/components/DashboardNav.tsx —
and assert the two computed colours actually differ. Confirm that assertion FAILS with the theme
absent and PASSES with it present. A green suite is not evidence here; that is the whole point of
this bead.

Specs in both apps run in real headless Chromium via Vitest browser mode. Never jsdom, never
happy-dom (see .claude/rules/TESTING.md).
acceptance_criteria:
- apps/wallow-web's and apps/wallow-auth's Vitest browser projects both render the fork theme, so
  a Tailwind colour utility computes to the fork's real token value rather than transparent.
  Evidence: getComputedStyle on a bg-sidebar element returns a non-transparent colour.
- The re-optimization symptom that forced the omission is genuinely resolved, not worked around:
  src/app/routes/index.gate.test.tsx passes with the theme present, and the specs see exactly ONE
  @tanstack/react-router instance. State on the bead which approach solved it and how that was
  confirmed.
- At least one real contrast assertion exists and is revert-proof: it compares two rendered
  colours that must differ, FAILS with the theme absent, PASSES with it present. Record both runs.
- apps/wallow-auth's browser project loads the Tailwind utilities, and its AcceptTermsScreen
  layout-avoidance workaround is either removed or re-justified in a comment.
- If the wiring is hoisted into packages/testing, packages/forms adopts it too, so there is one
  implementation rather than three. If it is NOT hoisted, say on the bead why per-app wiring is
  correct here.
- pnpm test, pnpm typecheck, pnpm lint (oxlint --deny-warnings) and pnpm format:check all green
  across the workspace.
notes:
SCOUT (read-only; no code changed). Mechanism, fix shape, blast radius, proof plan.

== 1. WHY packages/ui SEES REAL COLOUR AND THE APPS DO NOT (verified in code) ==
packages/styles/styles.css maps EVERY Tailwind colour token onto a bare custom property
(`--color-sidebar: var(--sidebar, var(--foreground))`, etc.) and defines no value for it.
The values come only from renderThemeStyle(forkResolvedBranding) -> `:root{...} .dark{...} .light{...}`
(packages/styles/src/branding.ts:242). No theme <style> => `var(--sidebar)` is invalid-at-computed-value-time
=> background-color falls to `transparent`, color falls back to inherited black. Both sides of any
contrast pair become garbage. api/branding.json defaultMode = "light", so :root carries the LIGHT palette;
a dark-mode assertion needs a `.dark` wrapper (packages/ui/src/components/text/text.stories.tsx has the
lightScheme/darkScheme decorator pattern to copy).

Who supplies each half today:
- packages/ui `storybook` project — .storybook/main.ts viteFinal appends wallowStyles(); .storybook/preview.css
  is the Tailwind entry; .storybook/preview.tsx themeDecorator renders <style>{renderThemeStyle(forkResolvedBranding)}</style>.
  BOTH halves. This is why ui's stories can (and do) assert colour: drawer.stories.tsx:326,
  navigation-menu.stories.tsx:270, menubar.stories.tsx:355, tabs.stories.tsx:200.
- packages/ui `browser` project — NEITHER half, deliberately (vitest.config.ts adds no plugins/setupFiles;
  render coverage is the storybook project's job). Do NOT wire it in this bead; note the divergence instead.
- packages/forms — BOTH halves: vitest.config.ts browser gets `plugins: wallowStyles()` +
  `setupFiles:["./vitest.setup.ts"]`; vitest.setup.ts imports ./vitest-styles.css AND injects
  renderThemeStyle(forkResolvedBranding) into head. Reference implementation.
- apps/wallow-web — utilities only. vitest.config.ts browser has wallowStyles() + setupFiles; vitest.setup.ts
  imports ./vitest-styles.css and its comment states the theme is omitted ON PURPOSE (see section 3).
- apps/wallow-auth — NEITHER half. Browser project is bare (`{...browser, resolve:{alias:resolveAlias}}`).
- apps/examples/minimal-app — NEITHER half. Leave as is (no colour specs); say so on the bead.

createVitestProjects (packages/testing/src/vitest-projects.ts) owns node+browser shape and
optimizeDeps ONLY. It has no styling knob at all — that is the actual gap.

== 2. BLAST RADIUS — every createVitestProjects consumer (re-derived by grep, not from the bead) ==
packages/testing/vitest.config.ts (own), packages/forms, packages/ui, apps/wallow-web, apps/wallow-auth,
apps/examples/minimal-app. packages/auth, packages/query, packages/sdk, packages/styles do NOT use it
(node-only configs).
Existing colour-assertion inventory: ZERO getComputedStyle/toHaveStyle in apps/wallow-web/src,
apps/wallow-auth/src, packages/forms/src, apps/examples/minimal-app/src. Every one lives in
packages/ui/src/components/*/*.stories.tsx (+ scroll-area.test.tsx). So no existing app spec can
FLIP on colour — the risk is layout/paint, not colour:
- wallow-web (adds theme only; utilities already there): low. DashboardLayout.ssr-flash.test.tsx uses
  checkVisibility(), not colour. Colour does not affect hit-testing. Re-run it anyway.
- wallow-auth (goes from NO CSS to full CSS+theme; 55 *.test.tsx, all but src/app/routes/index.test.tsx
  run in the browser project) — this is the real exposure. Watch specifically:
  * ExternalProviders.tsx:106 `<span className="absolute inset-x-0 top-1/2 border-t border-border"/>` —
    once positioning is real this span overlays the divider row and can intercept pointer events for a
    nearby click (LoginScreen / ExternalProviders specs).
  * RegisterForm.tsx:303 `overflow-hidden` strength bar — clipping becomes real.
  * Base UI popups (Select/Menu/Dialog) gain real position:fixed/z-index/transform => element-from-point
    and actionability change for any spec that opens one.
  * Tailwind preflight lands (margin/border/appearance resets) => any geometry assertion.
  * Breakpoints are NOT a risk here: grep found no sm:/md:/lg: in apps/wallow-auth/src components, unlike
    wallow-web whose specs already call page.viewport(1280,800) (DashboardNav.test.tsx:36 etc.). Vitest
    browser default viewport is 414x896.
  * wallowStyles() also installs brandAssetsPlugin => publicDir becomes the brand-assets dir for that
    project's Vite server (already true for wallow-web's browser project). Harmless but state it.
- The four wallow-auth specs carrying the focus+Space checkbox workaround are AcceptTermsScreen.test.tsx,

== 3. THE RE-OPTIMIZE BLOCKER AND THE SMALLEST CORRECT FIX ==
Cause is dep DISCOVERY, not styles itself: importing the linked package @bc-solutions-coder/styles from the
setup file is the first sight of that dep, Vite re-optimizes mid-run and reloads the page, and the reload
hands the specs a second @tanstack/react-router instance (index.gate.test.tsx catches it via isRedirect).
The repo already has the medicine and documents it verbatim for the same class of package: wallow-web's
extraBrowserOptimizeDeps names @bc-solutions-coder/query and @bc-solutions-coder/auth "because Vite does not
pre-bundle a link by default".
Attempt in this order:
  A (one line per app, preferred): add "@bc-solutions-coder/styles" to extraBrowserOptimizeDeps and keep the
    forms-style setup import. Note the resolvability rule from packages/forms/vitest.config.ts: an
    unresolvable optimizeDeps entry is only a WARNING and silently pre-bundles nothing — styles IS a real
    dependency of both apps (checked package.json), so it resolves.
  B (structural fallback, use if A leaves any reload): put the theme in CSS so no JS enters the browser
    graph — add a virtual CSS module to wallowStyles() (packages/styles/src/vite.ts) that serves
    renderThemeStyle(forkResolvedBranding) at e.g. `virtual:wallow-theme.css`; setup file then does
    `import "virtual:wallow-theme.css"` beside `import "./vitest-styles.css"`. Immune by construction.
    (This is the unocss `virtual:uno.css` technique; verify Vitest browser mode serves it.)
  C REJECT: generating a real theme.css file into packages/styles at build time. Local `pnpm check` runs
    test BEFORE build (root package.json), so a generated artifact would be stale exactly when it matters.
Do NOT bother with resolve.dedupe for react-router: it does not address a page reload.

== 4. HOISTING (acceptance criterion "one implementation, not three") ==
Split the two halves:
- The Tailwind ENTRY cannot be hoisted: Tailwind v4 resolves `@source` relative to the declaring stylesheet,
  so each consumer keeps its own root-level vitest-styles.css (packages/forms and apps/wallow-web both
  document this). Record that reason on the bead rather than fighting it.
- The THEME injection CAN and should be hoisted. Recommended shape: give createVitestProjects an opt-in
  (e.g. `browserStyles: { entry: "./vitest-styles.css" }`) that returns the browser project with
  `plugins: wallowStyles()`, `setupFiles` pointing at a NEW browser-only packages/testing subpath that
  imports the entry and installs the theme, and "@bc-solutions-coder/styles" folded into optimizeDeps.
  Opt-in is what keeps packages/ui's browser project and minimal-app off the Tailwind compile — that is
  the cost tradeoff: wallowStyles() makes a project compile the app's whole @source scan once per project
  (forms and wallow-web already pay it), so do not switch it on by default.
  Constraints for that subpath: packages/testing takes a dependency on @bc-solutions-coder/styles; the new
  export MUST be a browser-only subpath, never the `.` barrel (the barrel is loaded in plain Node at config
  time — same rule as ./render, see packages/testing/CLAUDE.md); add it to package.json exports; apps consume
  packages/testing through dist, so rebuild packages/styles + packages/testing before running app tests
  locally (CI's js.yml builds all packages/* before `pnpm test`, local `pnpm check` does not).
  packages/forms must then adopt it and lose its own copy.
  If hoisting proves too invasive, per-app wiring is acceptable ONLY with a written justification on the bead.

== 5. HOW THE FIX IS PROVEN (a spec that FAILS without the theme) ==
Three layers; all three are required, layer (b) is the one the epic actually needs.
 (a) Theme-presence guard, one per app, e.g. apps/wallow-web/src/shared/testing/theme-wiring.test.tsx and
     the wallow-auth twin. MUST be `.test.tsx` — the preset routes `src/**/*.test.ts` to the NODE project.
     Assert getComputedStyle(document.documentElement).getPropertyValue("--background") (and "--sidebar" in
     wallow-web) is non-empty, and that a rendered `bg-sidebar` element's backgroundColor is not
     "rgba(0, 0, 0, 0)". Fails outright with the theme absent; independent of any component's class string.
 (b) Real contrast assertion in wallow-web against DashboardNav (the surface whose hover defect shipped):
     render at page.viewport(1280,800) as the sibling specs do, read the rail
     (data-testid="dashboard-nav", `bg-sidebar text-sidebar-foreground`, DashboardNav.tsx:232) background and
     a nav row's colour (rows carry data-testid="dashboard-nav-<feature>"), assert both non-transparent, that
     they differ, and that the WCAG ratio is >= 4.5 — then repeat AFTER userEvent.hover on the row, which is
     the exact state that shipped at 1.27:1. Do the same for the drawer (data-testid="dashboard-nav-drawer")
     at mobile viewport if cheap.
     IMPLEMENTATION HAZARD: getComputedStyle can hand back `oklch(...)` strings (branding.json's palette is
     oklch), which an rgb() regex cannot parse. Normalise by painting the colour string into a canvas 2d
     context (fillStyle = value; fillRect; getImageData) and reading the sRGB bytes. Put that helper on a
     shared browser-only packages/testing subpath so Wallow-lrlm.6.4/6.5 and packages/ui reuse ONE copy.
 (c) Revert-proofing: an on-disk guard spec per app (node project) asserting the app's vitest.config wires
     wallowStyles() and its setup installs the theme — the pattern already exists at
     packages/ui/src/core/storybook-setup.test.ts:163, which greps preview.tsx for renderThemeStyle.
 EVIDENCE TO RECORD ON THIS BEAD: run (a)+(b) once with the theme install commented out (paste the failure)
 and once with it (paste the pass). A green suite alone is not evidence.

== 6. VERIFICATION COMMANDS / SIGNALS ==
pnpm --filter @bc-solutions-coder/styles build && pnpm --filter @bc-solutions-coder/testing build (dist is
what the apps resolve) -> pnpm --filter ./apps/wallow-web test -> pnpm --filter ./apps/wallow-auth test ->
pnpm --filter @bc-solutions-coder/forms test -> pnpm check.
The re-optimize symptom is proven gone, not merely quiet, when: src/app/routes/index.gate.test.tsx passes AND
the run log contains no "new dependencies optimized" / "Vitest unexpectedly reloaded a test" /
"Vitest failed to find the runner" line. Capture the log; grep it.

== 7. TREE IN FLUX — read before editing ==
Zone aliases are moving off apps/*/aliases.ts onto tsconfig `paths` consumed by Vite 8's native
`resolve.tsconfigPaths: true` (already done in both apps' vite.config.ts; apps/*/vitest.config.ts may still

time, PRESERVE it while adding plugins/setupFiles. Also live right now: RegisterAppForm, the query/invalidation
files, DashboardNav/DashboardLayout. Re-read every file before editing.

== 8. WHAT Wallow-lrlm.6.4 / 6.5 GAIN ==
6.4 (sidebar-aware catalog components): can assert, by measurement instead of by class string, that the
ThemeToggle chip's rendered background is the rail surface and not bg-secondary (Surface 1); that a nav row's
label colour keeps >= 4.5:1 against the rail AT REST AND ON HOVER (Surface 2 — the class-string blindness that
let the 1.27:1 hover defect ship past a green suite, because the real string is the tailwind-merge of recipe +
consumer className); and that the in-rail ErrorBanner's bg-destructive/10 fill clears >= 3:1 against the rail
(Surface 3). None of those is expressible today.
6.5 (nav controls adopt Button outline): can verify the binding "no sidebar palette on these controls" ruling
by measuring glyph-vs-fill contrast on bg-background, and can replace DashboardLayout.restyle.test.tsx's
CONTROL_SURFACE class-string pin ("border border-border text-foreground hover:bg-muted") with an assertion on
the rendered border/text/hover-background — which is what makes the recipe swap safe rather than merely green.
GREEN — Vitest browser specs in both apps now render with the fork theme.

MECHANISM (chose scout option B, the virtual CSS module, over option A optimizeDeps.include)
- packages/styles/src/vite.ts: new `forkThemePlugin` + `THEME_MODULE_ID = "virtual:wallow-theme.css"`,
  added to `wallowStyles()` AHEAD of `@tailwindcss/vite` with `enforce: "pre"` (the id ends in .css,
  so Tailwind's plugin would otherwise claim it and compile it as an entry). `load` returns
  `renderThemeStyle(forkResolvedBranding)` per request — no cached string, no build artifact.
- Why virtual, not a JS import of @bc-solutions-coder/styles from a setup file: styles is a LINKED
  workspace package, so that import re-optimizes the dep graph MID-RUN, reloads the page, and the
  reload gives a SECOND @tanstack/react-router instance — `redirect` thrown through one copy fails
  `isRedirect` in the other (src/app/routes/index.gate.test.tsx catches exactly this). A `\0`-prefixed
  virtual id lives outside node_modules, so the optimizer's scanner never sees it. Immune by
  construction rather than by configuration.
- Why not a generated theme.css on disk: the root `pnpm check` runs `test` BEFORE `build`, so the
  artifact would be stale exactly when it matters (scout correction #2, confirmed).
- Why only the THEME half is hoisted: Tailwind v4 resolves `@source` relative to the DECLARING
  stylesheet, so the Tailwind entry (`vitest-styles.css`) must stay at each app root. The theme half
  is now ONE implementation shared by packages/forms + both apps — packages/forms' setup file used to
  hand-roll `renderThemeStyle` into a `document.createElement("style")`; that block is deleted.
- Deliberately NOT hoisted into packages/testing: that would add a testing->styles dependency and a
  browser-only subpath with rebuild-ordering constraints, for no gain.

WHY MEASURED COLOUR, NOT CLASS STRINGS: the real class is twMerge(recipe, className), so a spec can
pin the recipe, stay green, and still ship a contrast defect. ./contrast parses through a CANVAS, not
an rgb() regex — api/branding.json's palette is oklch() and Chromium preserves the authored colour
space in computed values, so a regex silently fails on the exact tokens this repo uses. It also

description:

OAuth client and then invalidates the bound-clients list so the row it just created appears.
That invalidation has NO test coverage: it can be deleted and the entire wallow-web suite
(116 files / 943 tests) still passes.

Concretely, `RegisterClientFormFields`' `useAppForm({ ..., onSuccess })` calls

    void queryClient.invalidateQueries(
      queriesForOperation(
        clientsGetByTenantQueryKey({ client: sdk.client, path: { tenantId: orgId } }),
      ),
    );

Delete those five lines and `pnpm --filter @bc-solutions-coder/wallow-web test` is still green
(verified: 20 files / 113 tests under src/features/organizations/ all pass). The code is
CORRECT — this is purely a coverage gap. Symptom if it ever regresses: registering a client
succeeds, the one-time client-id/secret reveal appears, and the bound-clients table above it
silently does not grow until the page is reloaded.

The two sibling sweeps in the same feature ARE guarded, and they are the pattern to copy:
  - MemberList.tsx add-member sweep  -> MemberList.test.tsx "sweeps the members query after a
    successful add"
  - InquiryDetail.tsx add-comment sweep -> InquiryDetail.test.tsx "sweeps the comments query
    after a successful add"
Both fail immediately when their sweep is deleted (verified by mutation).
design:
Add ONE case to apps/wallow-web/src/features/organizations/components/OrganizationDetail.clients.test.tsx
(the existing clients spec — today it only asserts the four register controls exist, which is why
the hole is there). Do not create a new spec file.

Copy the mechanism from MemberList.test.tsx's "sweeps the members query after a successful add"
verbatim — it is the in-repo precedent and it is already proven against exactly this shape:
spy on the render's own QueryClient.invalidateQueries, drive a successful register through the
SdkHarness, and assert the spy was called with a predicate that MATCHES a cached
clients-by-tenant query and does NOT match an unrelated one. Assert the predicate's behaviour,
not its identity — generated query keys are flat (`[{ _id, baseUrl, tags, ...args }]`) with no
prefix to sweep by, so `queriesForOperation(...)` returns an opaque predicate object and
comparing it by reference or by shape pins the wrong thing.

Specs here run in real headless Chromium via Vitest browser mode (never jsdom). Use
`createSdkHarness` / `renderWithWallow` from @bc-solutions-coder/testing and select controls by
data-testid: `organization-detail-register-display-name`, `organization-detail-register-submit`.
The form is on @bc-solutions-coder/forms, so a successful submit needs a non-empty display name
(the zod schema rejects empty and whitespace-only with "Display name is required").

VERIFY THE GUARD ACTUALLY GUARDS: delete the five-line invalidateQueries call from
RegisterClientFormFields' onSuccess, confirm the new case FAILS, then restore. A case that
passes either way is the bug this bead exists to fix.

title: F6.T4 — Catalog components rendered inside the sidebar rail must be sidebar-aware
description:
Three @bc-solutions-coder/ui components render INSIDE apps/wallow-web's dashboard rail (apps/wallow-web/src/shared/components/DashboardNav.tsx) but paint themselves with PAGE-surface tokens, because no catalog recipe knows it may be composed onto an inverted surface. After Wallow-lrlm.5.4 the rail is genuinely dark in BOTH modes (bg-sidebar / text-sidebar-foreground), so these three are more visible than before.

SURFACE 1 — ThemeToggle. DashboardNav.tsx:169 (NavThemeToggle, rendered by both NavRail:231 and NavDrawer:255). ThemeToggle hard-codes Button variant=secondary (packages/ui/src/components/theme-toggle/theme-toggle.tsx:91), i.e. bg-secondary text-secondary-foreground = an L 0.92 surface in light mode: a bright chip sitting on an L 0.22 rail.

SURFACE 2 — navigationMenuLinkRecipe's page-surface classes. packages/ui/src/components/navigation-menu/navigation-menu.styles.ts:112 contributes text-foreground, hover:bg-accent, hover:text-accent-foreground and data-[active]:bg-accent / data-[active]:text-accent-foreground to every nav row. The consumer currently has to suppress each one BY NAME through tailwind-merge (packages/ui/src/core/cn.ts). That is fragile and it already failed once: Wallow-lrlm.5.4 dropped one suppressing class and un-hid hover:text-accent-foreground, making the labels near-invisible on hover in light mode. The data-[active] pair is additionally DEAD WEIGHT here — Base UI sets data-active only when its own active prop is passed and the app never passes it (TanStack activeProps is a className merge), so those two classes ride along on all four rows doing nothing, while being a latent light-block-on-dark-rail.

SURFACE 3 — ErrorBanner inside the rail. DashboardNav.tsx:211 renders the sign-out failure message with errorBannerRecipe = border-destructive + bg-destructive/10 (packages/ui/src/components/error-banner/error-banner.styles.ts:15,21). A 10% destructive tint over an L 0.20-0.22 rail is nearly invisible, so the one message a user must not miss is the least legible thing on the rail.
design:
Decide ONE mechanism and apply it to all three; do not solve them three different ways.

Option A (preferred) — give the affected recipes an explicit surface variant, e.g. surface: { page | sidebar }, where the sidebar arm swaps the page tokens for sidebar / sidebar-foreground / sidebar-accent. Follows packages/ui/CLAUDE.md's CVA-recipe convention, keeps the decision in the .styles.ts file, and removes the consumer's need to suppress anything by name. ThemeToggle would need to forward the variant to Button.
Option B — a data-attribute or CSS-variable scope on the rail that the recipes read. Cheaper for consumers but styles by ambient context, which is against the catalog's explicit-props grain.

CONSTRAINTS
- The sidebar-* token family already exists (packages/styles/styles.css:43-45, api/branding.json). Do NOT add a token; Wallow-lrlm.5.3's adjudication rejected inventing sidebar-muted and that precedent stands.
- packages/ui/CLAUDE.md: recipes are CVA-only, no JSX, semantic tokens only; each variant needs story coverage (stories ARE the render coverage in this package); @base-ui subpaths must be listed in vitest.config.ts.
- Tailwind's @source must scan *.styles.ts as well as *.tsx or the new variant emits class attributes with no CSS behind them. Verify by grepping a built app's CSS for a utility only the new variant uses.
- Do not change any data-testid: dashboard-nav, dashboard-nav-drawer, theme-toggle, dashboard-logout-link, dashboard-logout-error, the four dashboard-nav-* ids.
- Whichever option is chosen, the four nav rows must stop depending on tailwind-merge name-by-name suppression for their colour.
acceptance_criteria:
1. ThemeToggle rendered inside the rail paints from the sidebar token family, not bg-secondary, in BOTH light and dark mode.
2. The nav rows' colour no longer depends on the consumer suppressing catalog classes by name through tailwind-merge: the merged class attribute on each row carries no accent-* or foreground/background page-surface colour utility. Assert on the MERGED classList of the rendered anchor, not on the className the app passes in.
3. The inert data-[active]:bg-accent / data-[active]:text-accent-foreground pair is either removed from navigationMenuLinkRecipe or made sidebar-aware — it must not remain a latent light surface on a dark rail.
4. ErrorBanner inside the rail is legible against the sidebar surface.
5. New/updated story coverage exists for each variant added, and pnpm --filter @bc-solutions-coder/ui test + pnpm --filter @bc-solutions-coder/wallow-web test/typecheck/build are green.

- navigationMenuLinkRecipe's data-[active]:bg-accent / data-[active]:text-accent-foreground pair SURVIVES twMerge on every rail row — the app never supplies a conflicting data-[active]: class. title: importProtection does not keep redis out of the client bundle
description: apps/wallow-web/vite.config.ts:83-91 claims importProtection stops app/lib/bff.ts's redis import from reaching a client bundle. It does not: the baseline build exits 0 and redis is present in the client output. TanStack's default importProtection ruleset only covers **/*.server.* files. The srcDirectory: 'src/app' + importProtection: { include: ['src/**'] } pairing IS load-bearing for SCOPE (start-plugin-core adapterUtils.ts:86-87), but the comment overstates what the rule catches. Decide: adopt a *.server.* naming convention for server-only modules, add explicit importProtection rules, or correct the comment to match reality. Evidence: docs/plans/2026-07-30/1640-alias-architecture-decision.md 'Separate finding'.
notes:
Resolved on refactor/alias-tsconfig-paths (4aadcd88) by adopting the *.server.* naming convention (option 1) plus correcting the comment (option 3).

Measured, not assumed. Start's default client ruleset (start-plugin-core import-protection/defaults.js) denies exactly two things: specifiers @tanstack/{react,solid,vue}-start/server, and any IMPORTED FILE matching **/*.server.*. redis, node:* and @bc-solutions-coder/sdk/server are on neither list. Probe: importing src/app/lib/bff.ts from src/shared/components/ready-indicator.tsx built with EXIT 0 and produced a 512 KB client chunk containing redis, generic-pool and createClient. - The part that makes it also satisfy red case 6: AutocompleteRootProps OMITS itemToStringValue from the inherited AriaCombobox props and then RE-DECLARES it (@base-ui/react 1.6.0, autocomplete/root/AutocompleteRoot.d.ts:94). AutocompleteRoot.js forwards it as itemToStringLabel with fillInputOnItemPress: true, so pressing a row writes itemToStringValue(item) into the input. With itemToStringValue={(user) => user.id} the row RENDERS the email and COMMITS the uuid — exactly the acceptance criterion — while the form's value stays a plain string. title: F6.T2 — Apply register-app branding as a post-register upsert (stop discarding it)
description:
Apply the register-app "Branding (optional)" block as a POST-REGISTER upsert, so what a user types there stops being silently discarded.

The bead's original premise ("BrandingSection is unreachable dead code") is FALSE and has been disproven twice on this bead: the section renders unconditionally (apps/wallow-web/src/features/apps/components/RegisterAppForm.tsx:301) on the live, nav-linked /dashboard/apps/register route, with 8 passing tests over it. What IS dead is the DATA path: the three controls (RegisterAppForm.tsx:143-176) are uncontrolled, carry no name, are bound to no form field, and toVariables (:246-254) never reads them -- so a display name, tagline or logo a user enters is dropped on submit with no error and no trace.

The original remedy ("wire into toVariables") is impossible: branding is a DIFFERENT endpoint (POST /v1/identity/apps/{clientId}/branding, operationId ClientBrandingUpsertBranding), multipart/form-data, keyed on a clientId that first exists in the register RESPONSE. Deleting the section is also wrong -- it would regress two closed tasks (Wallow-ffpq.3.6's reachability bar and Wallow-lrlm.4.4's accessible-name fix, landed this same epic).

So: move the three controls onto real useAppForm fields, leave the register request body alone, and fire the branding upsert from the registration mutation's onSuccess using data.clientId -- skipping it entirely when the section is pristine, and handling register-ok/branding-failed on the success view with a retry that re-fires ONLY the branding call (the client secret is one-time and can never be re-minted).
design:
All paths absolute-from-repo-root. Everything below was verified by reading the code, not inferred.

1. SCHEMA (RegisterAppForm.tsx:95-101). Extend registerAppSchema with brandingDisplayName: z.string(), brandingTagline: z.string(), brandingLogo: z.instanceof(File).nullable(); add matching defaultValues ("", "", null) at :234-240. Node 24 has a global File, so evaluating z.instanceof(File) at module load is SSR-safe; fall back to z.custom<File | null>() only if the standard-schema adapter fights it. Add a conditional-required rule (.superRefine on the object, issue at path ["brandingDisplayName"]) firing when a tagline or a logo is present but the branding display name is blank -- the API returns 400 ValidationProblem on a blank DisplayName (api Branding ClientBrandingController.UpsertBranding, the IsNullOrWhiteSpace(request.DisplayName) guard).

2. THE TWO TEXT CONTROLS become catalog fields WITH EXPLICIT testId OVERRIDES, exactly as the four existing fields do (see the file header, RegisterAppForm.tsx:29-34):
   <form.AppField name="brandingDisplayName">{(field) => <field.TextField label="Display name" optional testId="app-branding-display-name" />}</form.AppField>
   ...same for brandingTagline / "app-branding-tagline".
   The override is MANDATORY, not cosmetic: derivation from the shell's testIdPrefix would produce app-register-branding-display-name and break three passing spec files. packages/forms/src/fields/field-parts.tsx useCatalogField shows the override also renames the message id, to app-branding-display-name-error. TextField already offers `optional` and `placeholder` (packages/forms/src/fields/text-field.tsx).

3. THE LOGO has no catalog field -- the catalog is Text/Textarea/Select/Checkbox/Password only (packages/forms/src/index.ts). Use the AppField render-prop escape hatch exactly as ScopeToggles already does in this same file (:295-299):
   <form.AppField name="brandingLogo">{(field) => <LogoInput onChange={field.handleChange} />}</form.AppField>
   LogoInput keeps the shipped markup verbatim -- <Label htmlFor="app-logo-input-control">Logo</Label> plus <input id="app-logo-input-control" data-testid="app-logo-input" type="file" accept="image/*" onChange={(event) => onChange(event.target.files?.[0] ?? null)} />. A file input stays uncontrolled (no value prop). Do NOT add a FileField to packages/forms in this bead.

4. KEEP the <fieldset data-testid="app-branding"> + <Text as="legend" variant="body">Branding (optional)</Text> wrapper, and keep it INSIDE <AppForm> -- RegisterAppForm.forms.test.tsx asserts app-branding / app-branding-display-name / app-logo-input each closest("form") the shell. Simplest shape: turn BrandingSection into a children wrapper (fieldset + legend + {children}) and place the three form.AppField blocks inside it. Do not reach for `withForm`; it is exported by the forms barrel but no app uses it.

5. toVariables (:246-254) IS UNCHANGED -- the register request body contract does not move. Adding branding keys to defaultValues does widen the key list splitServerError uses to route RFC 7807 field errors; harmless, no register error names them.

6. OWNERSHIP OF THE UPSERT MUST SIT IN THE PARENT RegisterAppForm, NOT IN RegisterAppFormFields. :212-214 unmounts the whole form the instant `registration` is set, and react-query drops mutate(vars, { onSuccess }) callbacks when the observing component unmounts. So RegisterAppFormFields' onSuccess(data) reads the branding trio off form.state.values (closing over `form` is safe and is the established idiom here -- CreateOrganizationForm.tsx:80, MemberList.tsx:227-228) and hands both to the parent, e.g. onRegistered(data, branding). The parent owns useMutation(clientBrandingUpsertBrandingMutation({ client: sdk.client })), already re-exported by features/apps/api.ts:13 (the parent will need useRouteContext({ from: "__root__" })), fires it in that same handler, and stays mounted for its callbacks. MfaEnrollFlow.tsx:129-190 is the in-repo template for a component driving two mutations with per-call onSuccess/onError.

7. VARIABLES SHAPE (generated, verified in packages/sdk/src/generated/types.gen.ts ClientBrandingUpsertBrandingData): { path: { clientId: data.clientId }, body: { DisplayName, Tagline, logo } } -- PascalCase DisplayName/Tagline, lowercase logo, ThemeJson omitted. The generated operation already applies formDataBodySerializer and sends Content-Type: null (sdk.gen.ts:185) so the browser sets the multipart boundary: do not hand-build FormData and do not set a content type.

8. PRISTINE SKIP: fire nothing at all when brandingDisplayName.trim() === "" && brandingTagline.trim() === "" && brandingLogo === null. Not an optimisation -- the API 400s on a blank DisplayName, and this is also what keeps RegisterAppForm.test.tsx green (that suite reads harness.last as the register POST and counts harness.calls).

9. PARTIAL FAILURE ON SuccessView. Register-ok/branding-failed must still reveal the one-time secret. SuccessView today takes props: { result: AppRegistrationResponse } (:179). Extend it with the branding outcome, e.g. { result, brandingError: string | null, brandingPending: boolean, onRetryBranding: () => void }. Render the message under data-testid="app-branding-error" and the retry button under data-testid="app-branding-retry" (the apps feature's app-* convention; SuccessView sits OUTSIDE the AppForm shell, so no testIdPrefix derivation applies to it). Build the message with errorText(error, "Could not save the app branding.") from @shared/lib/error-text -- not the mfa-local problemDetail. Retry re-fires ONLY the branding mutation from the parent-held clientId + branding values; registration must never re-run. Leave app-register-success / app-client-id / app-client-secret / app-client-secret-copy exactly as they are.

10. NO CACHE INVALIDATION for the branding call -- nothing in wallow-web reads client branding (clientBrandingGetBranding has no app call site). Leave the existing queriesWithTag("Apps") sweep at :258 alone.

11. SPECS -- EXTEND, NEVER DELETE. Both files below are CLOSED tasks' deliverables; every assertion already in them must still pass unedited.
  - apps/wallow-web/src/features/apps/components/RegisterAppForm.branding.test.tsx (Wallow-ffpq.3.6, closed prior epic). Its 3 reachability assertions stay. ADD: (a) typed branding reaches the wire -- type into app-branding-display-name and app-branding-tagline, submit, assert a SECOND recorded call POSTs /api/v1/identity/apps/client-abc/branding whose multipart body carries those exact DisplayName/Tagline strings (the harness decodes multipart via Object.fromEntries -- packages/testing/src/sdk-harness.ts); (b) pristine skip -- submit with the section untouched, assert exactly one recorded call and no /branding path; (c) a logo chosen through app-logo-input rides along as body.logo. Program the two responses with harness.respond((call) => ...) keyed on call.path.
  - apps/wallow-web/src/features/apps/components/RegisterAppForm.a11y.test.tsx (Wallow-lrlm.4.4, closed IN THIS EPIC). Its 5 accessible-name assertions stay -- they now pass through the catalog Field row instead of the hand-rolled block. ADD: the conditional-required message is ASSOCIATED with the control -- type a tagline only, submit, assert app-branding-display-name-error is present and referenced by the input's aria-describedby with aria-invalid set. That association is precisely what the uncontrolled block could never have had, so it belongs on this file rather than a new one.
  - RegisterAppForm.test.tsx, RegisterAppForm.forms.test.tsx and RegisterAppForm.catalog.test.tsx must stay green with NO assertion edited. (forms.test.tsx's header prose calling the branding block "uncontrolled ... wired to nothing" goes stale; correcting that comment is fine, its assertions are not to be touched.)

12. RISK TO CHECK BY HAND, NOT AN AC: no app in this repo posts multipart through the BFF today (no storageUpload / organizationsUploadBrandingLogo call site anywhere in apps/). If the branding POST fails end-to-end through createWallowBffServer, file that as its own bead -- it is not this bead's fix.

## Finding: BrandingSection is NOT dead code

Independently re-enumerated rather than trusting the F6 scout note. Every claim below is line-cited and verified.

RENDERED, REACHABLE, USER-VISIBLE:

There is no branch, flag, or route condition under which BrandingSection fails to render. 'Unreachable' is factually wrong.

COVERED BY THREE PASSING SPEC SURFACES (8 tests green right now, verified by running them):
- RegisterAppForm.branding.test.tsx — 3 tests, entirely about the three branding controls (Wallow-ffpq.3.6 Blazor-parity reachability bar).
- RegisterAppForm.a11y.test.tsx — 5 tests, 'branding accessible names' (Wallow-lrlm.4.4, CLOSED THIS EPIC).

Ran: vitest run --project browser RegisterAppForm.branding.test.tsx RegisterAppForm.a11y.test.tsx -> 2 files / 8 tests PASS.

## The bead's decision procedure is invalid

DESIGN says: check whether the registerApp mutation's variable shape includes branding fields; if not, it is dead code, delete it. That inference does not hold. Branding was NEVER meant to ride the register request body.

The real endpoint EXISTS AND IS LIVE — verified in packages/sdk/openapi/v1.json:705:
  POST /v1/identity/apps/{clientId}/branding  (operationId ClientBrandingUpsertBranding)
  multipart/form-data: DisplayName, Tagline, ThemeJson, logo (IFormFile)
That is an EXACT field-for-field match for BrandingSection's three controls (:159 display name, :163 tagline, :167 logo file). The SDK already generates it: clientBrandingUpsertBranding (generated/index.ts) and clientBrandingUpsertBrandingMutation (generated/@tanstack/*.ts:265).

So 'appsRegister has no branding fields' is TRUE but proves nothing — it is a different endpoint, a different content type, and it is keyed on a clientId that does not exist until the register RESPONSE comes back. RegisterAppForm.tsx:133-142's own doc comment states exactly this and calls the block 'a structural seam'. Confirmed at origin: git 01fa5ec0 ported it from Blazor RegisterApp.razor's Branding block, which called AppService.UpsertBrandingAsync(display name, tagline, logo file), deliberately deferring the live upsert.

## Neither ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA option is correct

AC offers a binary: 'fully wired into the form and its toVariables remap, OR removed entirely'.
(a) 'Wired into toVariables' is IMPOSSIBLE. toVariables (:246-254) builds the appsRegister JSON body. Branding needs a second, multipart request to a different path, and needs the clientId only available after that first request resolves. It cannot be a toVariables remap under any implementation.
(b) 'Removed entirely' is a REGRESSION, not a cleanup: it deletes a user-visible section from a shipped route, discards the Wallow-ffpq.3.6 Blazor-parity reachability bar, and throws away the accessible-name fix Wallow-lrlm.4.4 landed DAYS AGO IN THIS SAME EPIC. One task in F4 fixing what a task in F6 deletes is a self-inflicted contradiction.

The genuinely correct resolution is a THIRD option the AC does not permit: wire BrandingSection to clientBrandingUpsertBrandingMutation as a POST-REGISTER step, where result.clientId exists (i.e. in/after SuccessView, or an onRegistered continuation). That is a FEATURE, and it is undesigned — multipart file upload from the browser, whether branding is skippable, and what the UX does when register succeeds but the branding upsert fails (the client secret has already been shown once and cannot be re-fetched, so the page cannot simply be re-submitted). None of that is on this bead.

## CLOSED-TASK SPEC CONFLICT (independent reason to stop)

The F6 scout note prescribes, for this bead: 'delete the whole file RegisterAppForm.branding.test.tsx' and 'remove the branding describe block from RegisterAppForm.a11y.test.tsx'. Both are closed tasks' specs:
- RegisterAppForm.a11y.test.tsx — Wallow-lrlm.4.4, status CLOSED (verified via bd show).
- RegisterAppForm.branding.test.tsx — Wallow-ffpq.3.6, a closed prior epic.
Per the standing rule I do not edit closed tasks' specs. Logging as a genuine conflict rather than working around it.

## Judgement calls flagged
1. Read 'dead' as the bead defines it in its own DESCRIPTION ('unreachable or unused') and tested BOTH halves separately. Unreachable: disproven outright. Unused: TRUE in the narrow sense that the three uncontrolled inputs' values are read by nothing and submitted nowhere. Non-functional-but-live is a different defect with a different fix than dead-code, so I did not collapse the two.
2. Did not write a 'pin the absence' test. The instruction to do so was conditional on the resolution being deletion; deletion is not the correct resolution, and such a test would have locked in the regression.
3. Did not write a red test for the correct resolution (post-register branding upsert) either — that is a feature outside this bead's AC, and specifying it in tests would silently re-scope the bead without the coordinator's decision.

Either (A) close 6.2 invalid — BrandingSection is a documented, tested, deliberate seam and 'resolve the dead code' has no dead code to resolve; or (B) re-scope 6.2 to 'wire BrandingSection to clientBrandingUpsertBranding as a post-register step', with new AC covering multipart upload, optional-skip, and the register-succeeded/branding-failed path — and with the two closed-task spec surfaces EXTENDED, not deleted.
