title: F6.T3 — Fix mobile-nav SSR flash from useIsDesktop
description: apps/wallow-web/src/shared/lib/use-is-desktop.ts's getServerSnapshot() always returns true, meaning server-rendered HTML always assumes desktop layout regardless of the actual client viewport. On a mobile client this causes a flash of the desktop rail (DashboardNav's NavRail) before hydration corrects it to the mobile drawer behavior. Fix getServerSnapshot to avoid asserting a specific viewport server-side, and ensure the client-side correction does not visibly flash.
design: Since the server cannot know the real client viewport without a client hint (e.g. a cookie or a User-Agent-based guess, both add complexity), the more robust fix is typically to render a state that is safe for either viewport during the SSR/pre-hydration window (e.g. hide layout-dependent chrome until the first client-side effect resolves the real value, or use a CSS-only responsive approach for the initial paint) rather than committing to one guess. Look at how DashboardNav.tsx and DashboardLayout.tsx consume useIsDesktop today before choosing the exact mechanism.
acceptance_criteria: Loading apps/wallow-web on a mobile-width client no longer shows a flash of the desktop nav rail before switching to the mobile drawer treatment. pnpm --filter @bc-solutions-coder/wallow-web test passes, including a new or updated test covering the corrected server-snapshot behavior.
notes:
RED (write-tests phase). PREMISE HOLDS — re-verified in source, not taken from the scout: use-is-desktop.ts:36-38 getServerSnapshot() { return true }; DashboardNav.tsx:290-293 (if (!isDesktop) return drawer-or-null; else NavRail); DashboardLayout.tsx:140 ({isDesktop ? <NavToggle/> : <MobileMenuButton/>}). Both consumers mount/unmount on the boolean, so the SSR guess is a real paint, not a relayout. Confirmed empirically: the new browser spec puts the server's own renderToString output into the live document at 390x844 and Chromium reports the desktop rail AND the collapse toggle visible. The flash is real and now measured.

FILES (2 new specs + 1 config registration):
• apps/wallow-web/src/shared/lib/use-is-desktop.ssr.test.tsx — NODE project. 3 cases on the server snapshot, via renderToString of a probe component (the repo's SSR-test idiom from src/app/routes/index.test.tsx). FAILING 2/3: 'does not claim the viewport is desktop' (got "true") and 'reports the viewport as unknown' (expected "undefined", got "true"). The third — 'does not claim the viewport is mobile either' — passes today and is a deliberate GUARD against the lazy fix of flipping the constant to false, which only moves the flash onto laptops.
• apps/wallow-web/src/shared/components/DashboardLayout.ssr-flash.test.tsx — BROWSER project. 6 cases. FAILING 2: 'paints no desktop rail on a phone' and 'paints no desktop collapse toggle on a phone' (paintedChrome() === ['dashboard-nav','dashboard-nav-toggle'] at 390x844). Passing 4: the desktop-side symmetric guard, the two hydration-convergence cases, and an instrument self-check.
• apps/wallow-web/vitest.config.ts — added the .ssr.test.tsx to nodeTsxSpecs (scout flagged this; without it the spec runs in Chromium where getServerSnapshot is unreachable and the spec proves nothing), and added 'react-dom/server' to extraBrowserOptimizeDeps. The latter is REQUIRED, not cosmetic: without it Vite discovers react-dom/server mid-run and reloads, and the whole browser spec file fails to import ('Vitest unexpectedly reloaded a test' -> Failed to fetch dynamically imported module).

WHY THIS TEST SHAPE (the coordinator's 'a spec that only mounts cannot see the SSR mismatch' is exactly right). A mount takes getSnapshot + real matchMedia on the very FIRST render, so every existing spec in shared/components (DashboardLayout.mobile/.responsive) is structurally blind to this bug. The browser spec instead reproduces the real sequence: renderToString -> put those bytes in the live document -> set a real viewport -> ask Chromium what it would SHOW, via Element.checkVisibility() (computed style). That is a genuine measurement, not a class-string assertion — the standing lesson about twMerge-blind class assertions was the reason for choosing it.

JUDGEMENT CALLS (flagging all of them):
1. CONSUMER ASSERTIONS ARE MECHANISM-AGNOSTIC ON PURPOSE. They say only 'no viewport-specific chrome is PAINTED at the wrong width'. Omitting the rail from the server markup entirely (the bead's 'hide layout-dependent chrome until the viewport resolves') and emitting it behind a 'hidden md:flex' for the initial paint BOTH satisfy them. The implementer picks; the bead DESIGN offers both and I did not narrow it.
2. THE HOOK CONTRACT IS PINNED, and this is the one place I chose for the implementer: useIsDesktop(): boolean | undefined, undefined = 'no viewport observed yet'. Rationale: any correct fix needs a signal for 'server / first hydration render', and getServerSnapshot IS that signal; the two negative cases already forbid both booleans, so the positive case only names the sentinel. If the implementer prefers a separate useIsHydrated() hook and leaves useIsDesktop returning boolean, the third node case is the ONLY thing that fails and it is a one-line change — deliberately isolated in its own  for that reason. NOTE this shape costs nothing at the existing call sites: useSyncExternalStore consults getServerSnapshot ONLY during SSR and hydration, so a fresh client mount never sees undefined and no existing browser spec changes behaviour (verified — full suite below).
3. HYDRATION-CONVERGENCE CASES INCLUDED (2, both passing now). They stop 'render nothing, ever' from being a passing fix: after hydrating the server markup, a phone must end up with the mobile menu button and no rail, a laptop with the rail and its toggle. They pass today because today's SSR already equals the desktop markup; they become load-bearing the moment the server stops guessing.
4. I did NOT assert 'the rail IS painted at desktop width pre-hydration'. That would forbid the hide-until-resolved option the bead blesses.
5. INSTRUMENT SELF-CHECK ADDED ('reads Tailwind's own utilities, so a hidden element reads as hidden'). vitest.setup.ts loads utilities but NOT the fork theme, so colour reads are worthless here (Wallow-8ytl) — but display/geometry reads are sound, and this case proves the stylesheet is attached. Without it, a stylesheet-load regression would silently report a correctly-hidden rail as a flash and send an implementer chasing a phantom.
6. NO SOURCE-TEXT ASSERTION on the doc comment. The scout is right that use-is-desktop.ts:17-20 currently DEFENDS the desktop guess ('the dashboard's primary form factor') and will be a lie after the fix — but a brittle exact-string spec is worse than the problem. IMPLEMENTER MUST REWRITE THAT COMMENT; verifier please check it by eye.
7. afterEach awaits a macrotask before root.unmount(). hydrateRoot schedules rather than flushes, and unmounting over an unflushed root raised 'This root received an early update, before anything was able hydrate' as an UNHANDLED error that failed the run from the teardown of a passing case. Documented in the file.
8. No scaffolding was needed — no new production symbol is referenced, so nothing about the fix is pre-decided in source. use-is-desktop.ts, DashboardNav.tsx and DashboardLayout.tsx are UNTOUCHED by this phase.

CONFLICTS: NONE. I edited no existing test file. Re-read DashboardNav.tsx and DashboardLayout.tsx before writing: 5.4's sidebar-* palette (DashboardNav.tsx:67-94) and the twMerge hover-contrast suppression are untouched and unasserted-on here; 5.6's BACKDROP_SCRIM carve-out likewise. My new specs assert only presence/visibility of three testids, so they cannot collide with the restyle specs' rulings.

HOW THE FLASH IS PREVENTED — CSS, not JS-after-hydration (the coordinator's stated
preference, and it is the only option that can actually work: a control chosen in
JavaScript cannot be chosen until JavaScript has run, by which point the wrong one has
already painted).

The server no longer guesses. getServerSnapshot() returns undefined, so the SSR render
and React's first hydration render both see 'viewport unknown'. In that one window the
shell emits BOTH viewport-specific treatments and lets the md media query decide which
one paints, at first paint:
  - NavRail with hideBelowMd -> className 'hidden md:flex ' + railClass
  - NavToggle with hideBelowMd -> navControlClass + 'hidden md:inline-block'
  - MobileMenuButton with hideAtMd -> navControlClass + 'md:hidden'
Once the width IS known (isDesktop is a real boolean) nothing changes from before:
exactly one branch MOUNTS, with no display utility, so the steady state is still
'the wrong chrome does not exist', not 'the wrong chrome is hidden'. hideBelowMd/hideAtMd
are strictly a pre-hydration escape hatch.

Why emitting-and-hiding is acceptable for that window: 'hidden' is display:none, which
removes the rail from layout, tab order AND the accessibility tree — the exact
properties use-is-desktop.ts's doc comment argues a 'hidden md:flex' rail would cost.
That argument still holds for the STEADY state (where the rail would be permanent
DOM on a phone) and the code still honours it there; it does not hold for one
pre-hydration render of an inert display:none subtree.

- DashboardLayout's backdrop is now `isDesktop === false && isMobileNavOpen`, not
  `!isDesktop && ...`. An unresolved viewport is not a mobile one, and `!undefined`
  is true — the old expression would have armed the scrim during SSR.
- NavControls exists so the three-way choice is a branch rather than a nested ternary
  in the JSX (jsx-max-depth / readability).

the desktop guess as 'the dashboard's primary form factor' and would have been a lie).
use-is-desktop.ts's SSR paragraph now states the undefined contract, why neither boolean
is answerable, that useSyncExternalStore consults getServerSnapshot for SSR *and* the
first hydration render, that a fresh client mount never observes undefined, and that
consumers resolve the window with a media query. DashboardNav's 'THREE MODES, TWO AXES'
header gained a paragraph placing the unresolved render before the three modes, and
NavRail carries the rationale for hideBelowMd. Verifier: this is the by-eye check the
red report asked for.

EMPIRICAL VERIFICATION (per the epic's standing lesson — not a class-string claim):
1. The two directions of the media query are now genuinely exercised by the passing
   browser spec, where before my change they were vacuous. 'paints no desktop rail on a

mechanical swap inverts a second time. `bg-sidebar text-sidebar-foreground` paints a dark rail

glaring light rail is the bug the sidebar tokens exist to fix.

description: RegisterClientForm, AddMemberForm, and AddCommentForm in apps/wallow-web currently hand-roll their form state/validation/submission instead of using the shared form-authoring layer. Migrate each to useAppForm (zod schema + generated {operation}Mutation + RFC 7807 error split) rendered through the AppForm shell and its pre-bound field catalog, following the canonical template already used correctly by apps/wallow-web/src/features/organizations/components/CreateOrganizationForm.tsx.
design: CreateOrganizationForm.tsx is the canonical useAppForm template in this codebase -- mirror its shape exactly (schema, mutation wiring, AppForm shell, field catalog usage, data-testid derivation from testIdPrefix). apps/wallow-web/src/features/apps/components/RegisterAppForm.tsx is the reference for the toVariables remap pattern when the mutation's variable shape differs from the form's field shape (needed if any of these three forms has that mismatch). See packages/forms/CLAUDE.md and docs/development/forms.md for the full contract.

notes:
SCOUT 5.5 (hand-rolled forms -> useAppForm). Read packages/forms/CLAUDE.md and docs/development/forms.md in full. Re-verify independently -- the three targets below are NOT standalone files, they are private nested functions inside larger detail components, which is exactly the miss pattern F4 warned about (a file-list sweep of "forms" would find zero matches since no file is named *Form.tsx for these three).

THE REQUIRED SHAPE (from docs/development/forms.md + packages/forms/CLAUDE.md), canonical template = apps/wallow-web/src/features/organizations/components/CreateOrganizationForm.tsx:
`useAppForm({schema: <zod object>, defaultValues, mutation: <generated {op}Mutation({client})>, toVariables?, onSuccess?, fallbackError})` returns a form instance with `form.wallow.{pending,serverError,reset,clearServerErrors}`. Render via `<AppForm form={form} testIdPrefix="...">` (owns space-y-5 rhythm -- a className REPLACES it, doesn't merge) wrapping `<form.AppField name="x">{(field) => <field.TextField label="..." testId="..."/>}</form.AppField>` (fields: TextField/PasswordField/TextareaField/SelectField/CheckboxField, each derives BOTH the control id and its -error id from testId), then `<FormError/>` and `<SubmitButton>...</SubmitButton>` (optionally `pendingLabel`). react/jsx-max-depth is 2, so every migrated form must split `<Feature>Form` (owns state/Card) from `<Feature>FormFields` (owns the AppForm tree) exactly like RegisterAppForm.tsx does. Escape hatches: a control the catalog lacks stays on `form.AppField`'s render prop (see RegisterAppForm's ScopeToggles using ToggleGroup/Toggle -- NOT itself a migration target, already done); a field wired to nothing is a plain child of the shell (RegisterAppForm's BrandingSection).

variant success:     bg-success text-success-foreground
variant warning:     bg-primary text-primary-foreground
variant destructive: bg-destructive text-destructive-foreground
Assertions are ORDER-FREE class sets (classList sorted), so tailwind-merge may reorder; the split between base string and variant string is NOT pinned — only the rendered set is. title: Build the Text component
description:
Add a new packages/ui/src/components/text/ folder with the full four-file registration (text.tsx, text.styles.ts, text.stories.tsx, text.test.tsx, index.ts). Text wraps no Base UI part -- there is no headless text primitive -- it is a plain polymorphic element carrying a CVA recipe, in the same shape as the existing MutedText (packages/ui/src/components/muted-text/muted-text.tsx: a thin function taking className+rest, cn(recipe(), className), spreading rest onto the element).

API surface (five props):
- as: one of h1 h2 h3 h4 h5 h6 p span div label legend code -- chooses the rendered ELEMENT. Defaults to p. Each as value maps to a default variant (a lookup table, e.g. h1->display, h2->title, h3->heading, h4->subheading, p->body, span->body, div->body, label->body, legend->caption, code->code -- pick sensible values, keep the table itself as a plain object/Record literal, not a chain of if/else or switch cases).
- variant: one of display title heading subheading body bodySm caption overline code -- chooses the type SCALE (size + weight + leading + tracking). An explicit variant overrides the as-derived default, so Text as=h2 variant=body is legal and decouples semantic heading level from visual weight.
- color: one of default muted primary accent destructive success onSidebar onCard onPrimary -- each maps to EXACTLY ONE semantic token utility class, never an alpha/opacity variant: default->text-foreground, muted->text-muted-foreground, primary->text-primary, accent->text-accent-foreground, destructive->text-destructive, success->text-success (needs F1.T1 new success token), onSidebar->text-sidebar-foreground (needs F1.T1 new sidebar-foreground token), onCard->text-card-foreground, onPrimary->text-primary-foreground. NO slash-NN opacity suffix anywhere in this recipe -- that is the entire point of the component (today apps write text-foreground/60 etc; Text must make that impossible to reproduce).
- weight: normal medium semibold bold -- optional override of the variant own weight.
- align: left center right -- optional.

The overline variant must carry the uppercase-caption treatment the apps hand-roll today (e.g. apps/wallow-web/src/features/settings/components/ProfileSection.tsx FIELD_LABEL constant: block text-xs font-semibold text-foreground/70 uppercase tracking-wider mb-1, and the same string duplicated in apps/wallow-web/src/features/mfa/components/MfaSettingsSection.tsx) MINUS the mb-1 (that is layout/spacing and belongs to the caller, not the recipe) and MINUS the /70 opacity (use a real color prop value instead, e.g. color=muted -> text-muted-foreground).

className is narrowed back to plain string and merged via cn(textRecipe(...), className) so a caller class always wins.
design:
CVA recipe rules (packages/ui/CLAUDE.md + this plan repo-facts section): recipes live in text.styles.ts as CVA only -- no JSX, no React import -- so the recipe file reads and diffs standalone (mirror muted-text.styles.ts shape: exported textRecipe = cva(base, { variants, defaultVariants }) plus exported TextRecipeProps = VariantProps<typeof textRecipe>).

Registration (four files move together in one commit, from this plan repo-facts section): (1) src/components/text/ five-file folder; (2) COMPONENT_FOLDERS array in packages/ui/src/core/package-scaffold.test.ts (currently 48 entries alphabetically sorted -- insert text after tabs and before textarea); (3) packages/ui/src/index.ts root barrel -- components + prop types only, in the same alphabetical slot (the barrel block for a folder is EXACTLY that folder index.ts block from the .tsx export, never the .styles.ts one -- textRecipe/TextRecipeProps stay reachable only via the @bc-solutions-coder/ui/text subpath, not the root barrel); (4) PUBLIC_RUNTIME_EXPORTS + PublicTypeExports tuple in packages/ui/src/index.test.ts.

No new @base-ui/react subpath is needed (Text wraps no Base UI part), so packages/ui/vitest.config.ts baseUiSubpaths list needs no change.

Test model per packages/ui/CLAUDE.md: stories ARE the render/interaction coverage; *.test.tsx covers only edges a story cannot express. Do not duplicate story coverage into the test file.
acceptance_criteria:
Stories in text.stories.tsx cover every variant, every color, and the as-derived defaults, rendered in BOTH light and dark mode (the storybook vitest project has the real Tailwind pipeline and real fork theme attached, per packages/ui/CLAUDE.md, so this is where dark-mode colour correctness is actually visible -- the plain browser project loads no Tailwind).
Tests in text.test.tsx cover: as renders the correct HTML element; an explicit variant prop overrides the as-derived default variant; a caller className beats the recipe own classes; the recipe class string (read via textRecipe({...}) directly, not by rendering) contains no slash opacity token for any color value.
Registered in all four places (folder, COMPONENT_FOLDERS, root barrel, index.test.ts exports); pnpm --filter @bc-solutions-coder/ui test (all three projects) and pnpm --filter @bc-solutions-coder/ui build both green.

DESIGN DECISIONS (the bead asked for one to be picked and documented)
1. THREE-STATE CYCLE, NO aria-pressed. light -> dark -> system -> light. A two-state
   aria-pressed toggle can express \"I want dark\" but has no way back to \"follow the OS\":
   once pressed the choice is pinned forever. The persisted value is a ThemePreference whose
   default IS \"system\", so the control must be able to return there. aria-pressed is a
   two-state attribute and would misreport the third, so it is deliberately absent; state is
   announced via the accessible name (\"Switch to dark theme\") and exposed to tests as
   data-theme-preference / data-theme-mode.
2. theme-provider is STORY-LESS. It renders no visual surface (a context + a <script>), so it
   joins CLAUDE.md's closed exemption list of folders with no *.stories.tsx. theme-toggle has
   the stories (Light, Dark, SystemLight, SystemDark, Disabled, Cycling).
3. The apps supply data-testid=\"theme-toggle\"; packages/ui does NOT default it. Kept
   consistent with the rest of the catalog (testids are app-owned) and asserted in each app's
   spec at the place that supplies it.
4. Precedence is proved by a PURE FUNCTION in the node project, because prefers-color-scheme
   cannot be emulated from vitest browser mode. resolveThemeMode takes systemMode explicitly
   (null = OS states no preference); the browser specs read the LIVE media query and derive
   what they expect from it.
5. No-flash is proved by EXECUTING the real script source: a <script> appended with
   textContent runs synchronously on insertion, so the assertion sits on the very next line
   with no await/waitFor. A useEffect implementation cannot pass. No-hydration-mismatch is
   proved structurally (renderToString output === client container HTML, and the stamped class
   survives mount unchanged) rather than by spying on console.
6. ThemeScript uses React's plain text child of <script> - React does not escape script text
   children (verified empirically), so no raw-HTML escape hatch is needed. This mirrors
   DocumentStyles' <style>{themeCss}</style>. A spec asserts the script source contains no
   \"<\" so it cannot terminate its own element.
7. App shells are asserted from SOURCE, not by rendering: RootDocument is not exported (it
   reaches the router as shellComponent) and renders a whole <html> document, which render()
   cannot mount in a container. Same approach as docker-workspace-copies.test.ts.

theme-toggle:

IMPLEMENTATION NOTES (the non-obvious decisions)

1. resolveThemeMode: only the literals "light"/"dark" pin a mode. null, "system" and junk all fall
   through to `systemMode ?? defaultMode`, which is what makes "stored system re-follows the OS"
   and "junk degrades safely" the same code path.

2. themeInitScript emits an IIFE (`(function(){...})();`) containing no "<" at all, so React can
   render it as a plain text child of <script> exactly as DocumentStyles does for <style>. It reads
   localStorage inside try/catch (blocked-cookies / private browsing throw), asks BOTH
   prefers-color-scheme queries so "OS has no opinion" stays distinguishable, and stamps with
   classList.remove("light","dark") + add(mode) so a stale SSR class is REPLACED, never stacked, and
   unrelated classes on <html> survive.

3. ThemeProvider uses useSyncExternalStore, NOT useState/useEffect. This is the load-bearing choice:
     - the client snapshot READS the DOM class the script already stamped (getSnapshot ->
       readStampedMode) and localStorage, so a plain client render publishes the real theme
       synchronously on the first render — an effect-based version cannot pass the "publishes the
       mode the script already stamped" spec without a flash;
     - the SERVER snapshot returns defaultMode / "system", which is exactly what the SSR markup
       carries, so React hydrates against matching values and then swaps to the live snapshot. That
       is what keeps a visitor whose stored choice differs from branding.defaultMode from producing
       a hydration mismatch in the real apps (the specs only prove the structural half).
   Nothing is applied on mount — the only effect registers a matchMedia("change") + window "storage"
   listener and re-resolves ONLY when one of them fires, which is why "does not touch the class the
   script stamped when it mounts" holds. Cross-tab writes and OS-scheme flips (while the preference
   is "system") therefore re-stamp and re-render; same-tab writes go through setPreference ->
   notifyThemeChange() over a module-level listener set, because neither the DOM nor localStorage
   emits an event for its own tab.

4. ThemeToggle: aria-label announces the DESTINATION ("Switch to dark theme" when preference=light),
   the visible text announces the CURRENT state ("Light"/"Dark"/"System"). No aria-pressed. Pressing
   calls onPreferenceChange(next) when supplied, otherwise theme.setPreference(next) — so it is fully
   controlled for stories and provider-driven in both apps, with no private state either way.

5. App wiring shape (identical in both shells, and what the source-reading specs pin):
     <head> ... <DocumentStyles/> <ThemeScript defaultMode={branding.defaultMode}/> </head>
     <body> <FocusOnNavigate/> <ThemeProvider defaultMode={branding.defaultMode}>{children}</ThemeProvider>
            <ReadyIndicator/> <Scripts/> </body>
   className={branding.defaultMode} stays on <html> as the SSR baseline. FocusOnNavigate/ReadyIndicator
   stay OUTSIDE the provider, which also keeps every element at the same JSX depth as before.

6. DashboardNav imports ThemeToggle from the PER-COMPONENT subpath
   (@bc-solutions-coder/ui/theme-toggle), not the barrel — that file's existing comment explains why
   (the barrel pulls FocusOnNavigate -> useRouterState, and every spec in that directory stubs
   @tanstack/react-router down to Link alone). NavThemeToggle sits in the footer band above NavLogout
   in BOTH NavRail and NavDrawer, so it is present in all three nav modes; the collapsed icon rail

   because the control's state IS its text and there is no icon to fall back to.

title: Widen TypedSuccessResponseTests reflection gate beyond 200-only
description:
api/tests/Wallow.Api.Tests/OpenApi/TypedSuccessResponseTests.cs is the BACKEND-side reflection gate from Wallow-pu6a.2.3 and is still 200-only: EmitsUntypedSuccessResponse hardcodes StatusCodes.Status200OK. It did NOT and could not catch the untyped 201 fixed in Wallow-td30 — only the document-level TS invariant (openapi-regen.test.ts) did. A future bare [ProducesResponseType(201)] on an action returning Task<IActionResult> will again slip past the entire .NET suite and surface only after an SDK snapshot regen.

Not a one-liner like the TS side was: the bare-vs-typed logic and the 'declared.Count == 0 falls back to 200' clause are both 200-specific, and GetInferredSuccessType's ActionResult<T> inference is what currently spares InvitationsController. Widening needs those three pieces reworked together.

Flagged by the Wallow-td30 implementer as a deliberate scope call rather than half-done inside that bead.
notes:
GREEN. Test-only change; no controller edits were needed.

SCOPE FINDING: the only bare non-204 2xx [ProducesResponseType] left in api/src is InvitationsController.Create:29, and it returns Task<ActionResult<InvitationResponse>>, so ApiExplorer back-fills the schema (snapshot confirms POST /v1/identity/invitations 201 $refs InvitationResponse). The widened gate therefore goes green against all seven module assemblies with zero production changes — which also means widening alone has no teeth, so fixture controllers were mandatory rather than optional.

RED-THEN-GREEN OBSERVATION:
Added seven fixture-based detector tests BEFORE widening. Ran ./scripts/run-tests.sh api against the unchanged 200-only detector: 2 failed / 324 passed, failing on exactly the two cases that require widening —
  Detector_CatchesABareCreatedOnAnActionWithNoInferableBody
  Detector_CatchesAnUntypedAcceptedAlongsideATypedOk
The other five (inferred-ActionResult<T> 201, typed 201, 204-only, 404-only, no-metadata) passed on both sides as regression guards on the clauses that must NOT change.
After widening: 326/326.

LOOP-CLOSING PROOF (the bead's core claim): temporarily reverted InquiriesController.AddComment to the pre-Wallow-td30 bare [ProducesResponseType(201)] and re-ran. The widened gate FAILED on the real assembly —
  ModuleControllerActions_DeclareTypedSuccessResponses(moduleName: "Inquiries")
i.e. it now catches the exact defect the 200-only gate could not. Reverted; final run 326/326, dotnet format clean.

DESIGN: EmitsUntypedSuccessResponse restructured into three ordered clauses — (1) inferred ActionResult<T> body spares the action for ALL 2xx (ApiExplorer back-fills bare entries, so this is correct rather than a loophole); (2) declared.Count == 0 stays 200-ONLY, modelling the implicit default 200 that any declared response suppresses; (3) otherwise flag any declared body-bearing 2xx whose attribute names no type. New IsBodyBearingSuccessCode(int) mirrors isBodyBearingSuccessCode in packages/sdk/src/openapi-regen.test.ts (2xx except 204).
FindActionsWithUntypedSuccessResponse now takes IEnumerable<Type> instead of Assembly so fixtures can be fed directly; module test passes apiAssembly.GetTypes().
AliveEndpoint_DeclaresTypedSuccessResponse left 200-only on purpose — it is a minimal-API endpoint that answers only 200.

FILES: api/tests/Wallow.Api.Tests/OpenApi/TypedSuccessResponseTests.cs (only file changed)
close_reason: Widened the backend reflection gate from 200-only to every body-bearing 2xx (non-204), mirroring isBodyBearingSuccessCode in openapi-regen.test.ts. Test-only: no controller changes were needed, since the sole bare non-204 2xx left (InvitationsController.Create) is spared by ActionResult<T> inference. Added seven fixture controllers to give the widening teeth; the two that require it were red before the change and green after, and temporarily reverting InquiriesController.AddComment to its pre-td30 bare 201 makes the Inquiries module scan fail — the defect the old gate could not see. run-tests.sh api 326/326; dotnet format clean.

title: AppHost hardcodes WALLOW_API_INTERNAL_URL to :5001 while the API binds a dynamic port
description:
api/src/Wallow.AppHost/Program.cs passes .WithEnvironment("WALLOW_API_INTERNAL_URL", "http://localhost:5001") to the React app resources, but the Wallow.Api resource under Aspire binds a DYNAMIC host port (observed :64158), not 5001. Under 'pnpm backend' the apps' passthrough proxy therefore targets a port nothing is listening on unless a separate standalone API happens to hold 5001.

Fix direction: reference the API resource's endpoint instead of a literal, e.g. .WithEnvironment("WALLOW_API_INTERNAL_URL", api.GetEndpoint("http")) so Aspire injects the real address.

Related smell in the same file: the AppHost's mailpit container uses WithHttpEndpoint(targetPort: 8025) with no host port, so its HTTP port is dynamic too -- which is why apps/wallow-auth/e2e/mailpit.ts documents that E2E_MAILPIT_URL must be set explicitly when Aspire owns the inbox.

Found during Wallow-4pwv bug remediation; deliberately NOT fixed there to keep that epic scoped to its five filed beads.
notes:
2026-07-30 CORRECTION -- this was filed as a bug on a premise that does not hold, and has been retyped chore. Addressed in 66e65183.

The claim was that WALLOW_API_INTERNAL_URL=http://localhost:5001 targets a port nothing listens on under 'pnpm backend'. Verified against a live Aspire run: DCP listens on 5001 on BOTH stacks ('dcp ... TCP [::1]:5001 (LISTEN)' and 'TCP 127.0.0.1:5001 (LISTEN)'), and the API answers /health and /.well-known/openid-configuration through it within a second of the resource going ready. The dynamic port (:64158) I originally saw is the API process behind that proxy, which is ordinary Aspire behaviour -- project endpoints are proxied and the launchSettings applicationUrl pins the proxy's port. The original observation was taken against a stack whose resources had all exited, so nothing was on 5001 for an unrelated reason.

What was genuinely worth changing, and is what 66e65183 does: the literal was written into three env vars (WALLOW_API_INTERNAL_URL, OIDC_METADATA_URL, BFF_API_BASE_URL), duplicating a port that Wallow.Api's launchSettings owns, and it published into a manifest as a hardcoded localhost URL instead of a per-environment binding. All three now go through api.GetEndpoint("http"), and Wallow.AppHost.Tests asserts the {wallow-api.bindings.http.url} placeholder so a regression to a literal is visible.

Left literal on purpose: OIDC_ISSUER (must equal what the API derives from AuthUrl) and the redirect URIs (must equal what api/seed.json registers). An endpoint reference would agree with those only by coincidence.

The related mailpit observation in the original description STILL STANDS and is not addressed here: the AppHost's mailpit container uses WithHttpEndpoint(targetPort: 8025) with no host port, so its HTTP port really is dynamic. That is why apps/wallow-auth/e2e/mailpit.ts documents E2E_MAILPIT_URL as required when Aspire owns the inbox.

title: Seeder crashes deleting pre-registered clients inside an open reader
description:
PreRegisteredClientSyncService.DeleteRemovedClientsAsync deletes rows while an 'await foreach' over the same NpgsqlConnection is still open, so the delete throws NpgsqlOperationInProgressException ('A command is already in progress') and the seeder exits non-zero. Hit repeatedly while bringing up a local backend for the Wallow-4pwv E2E verification runs.

Fix direction: materialise the enumeration first (ToListAsync) before issuing any delete, or run the deletes on a separate connection/scope. Confirm whether MARS-style overlap exists anywhere else in the seeder.

Found during Wallow-4pwv bug remediation; deliberately NOT fixed there to keep that epic scoped to its five filed beads.
notes:
Reproduce: dev-infra up, then 'dotnet run --project api/src/Wallow.SeederService' with ConnectionStrings__DefaultConnection set. The admin-bootstrap path is unaffected -- only the pre-registered-client sync throws.
2026-07-30 fixed in b7b0f31d. DeleteRemovedClientsAsync now collects the doomed applications during the ListAsync enumeration and deletes them after the reader closes. PopulateAsync/GetClientIdAsync stay inside the loop -- both read the already-materialised entity and issue no command, so only the delete ever violated the constraint.

Evidence: the dev DB still held wallow-dev-client, a config-sourced client dropped from seed.json that the broken path could never remove. First seeder run on the fix logged 'Deleted pre-registered client no longer in config: wallow-dev-client' and exited 0; a second run was a clean no-op, exit 0.

Regression test: PreRegisteredClientSyncServiceTests.SyncAsync_DoesNotDeleteWhileTheApplicationListReaderIsStillOpen. The fake list exposes ReaderIsOpen and the DeleteAsync stub throws the real 'A command is already in progress' message on a mid-enumeration delete. Verified it FAILS against the previous implementation with exactly that exception. The pre-existing tests could not have caught this -- they mock IOpenIddictApplicationManager, which has no reader to be busy.

Backend suite: 4560 passed / 0 failed.

title: Nested oxlint configs in packages/ui and packages/forms lack 'extends', so no root rule applies there
description:
packages/ui/.oxlintrc.json and packages/forms/.oxlintrc.json each contain only
{"$schema": ..., "rules": {"react/jsx-props-no-spreading": "off"}} with NO "extends".
oxlint's nested-config discovery therefore uses those files ALONE for every file in
those two packages: the root .oxlintrc.json's plugins, categories, rules,
ignorePatterns and overrides do not apply there at all. Both packages are effectively
linted with oxlint's built-in defaults plus one rule turned off.

MEASURED (read-only probes, all removed):
- A file importing useQuery from "@tanstack/react-query" in packages/ui/src and in
  packages/forms/src produces ZERO diagnostics. The IDENTICAL file in
  packages/testing/src, apps/wallow-web/src and even scripts/ errors with
  eslint(no-restricted-imports). So the react-query facade ban from Wallow-x4qn.12
  has never covered ui or forms.
- Not even the incidental unicorn(prefer-export-from) warning that fires on that
  probe elsewhere appears in ui/forms, which proves the root's plugins and its
  pedantic/style categories are absent, not just one rule.

NOT CURRENTLY VIOLATED — this is latent config debt, not a live hole:
- packages/ui: no @tanstack/react-query reference anywhere (source, specs, or
  package.json); it declares no react-query dependency in any bucket.
- packages/forms: no direct import either. Its only mentions are prose in CLAUDE.md
  and string constants inside its own guards. forms declares react-query in NO
  dependency bucket (pinned by packages/forms/src/core/package-scaffold.test.ts), and
  packages/forms/src/core/query-facade.test.ts already sweeps every authored module
  under src/ for a raw @tanstack/react-query import (static, dynamic and subpath
  forms) and fails on one. So forms has spec-level enforcement today; ui has none but
  also has no query surface.

SECOND, RELATED GAP (same root cause, fix together):
packages/sdk/src/oxlint-guardrails.test.ts reads ONLY the root .oxlintrc.json. Nested
configs are invisible to it, so the "narrow by construction" property it enforces
(an exemption must RE-DECLARE the rule minus one entry, never switch it off) is
unenforced for scripts/fork-smoke/.oxlintrc.json — the nested config added in
Wallow-x4qn.12 — and would not have caught the ui/forms hole either. A tree-wide
sweep of every .oxlintrc.json closes both.
design:
Two pieces of work, ideally one bead, likely two commits.

PIECE 1 — add "extends": ["../../.oxlintrc.json"] to packages/ui/.oxlintrc.json and
packages/forms/.oxlintrc.json, then clean up what surfaces. This is one line each and
then a real cleanup project.

BLAST RADIUS, MEASURED: `pnpm exec oxlint packages/ui packages/forms --config
.oxlintrc.json` (forces the root config, which is what adding extends effectively
does) yields 1209 diagnostics — 1188 in packages/ui, 21 in packages/forms; 3 errors,
1206 warnings. 228 of those are react/jsx-props-no-spreading, which the nested
configs already turn off and which would therefore NOT surface, leaving ~981 real new
diagnostics. `pnpm lint` runs oxlint with --deny-warnings, so every warning is gate-
failing: all ~981 must be fixed or consciously disabled.

Breakdown of the ~981 (rule -> count):
  unicorn/prefer-dom-node-dataset      443
  react/jsx-max-depth                  378   (root sets it at the default max 2; ui
                                              has 47 component folders of nested JSX)
  eslint/no-magic-numbers               89
  unicorn/prefer-number-coercion        29
  eslint/func-name-matching             11
  eslint/no-duplicate-imports            6
  eslint/no-continue                     6
  unicorn/prefer-query-selector           6
  unicorn/error-message                   3
  hard errors (3): unicorn/prefer-set-has, eslint/no-await-in-loop, oxc/no-map-spread
  plus a long tail (max-nested-calls, no-array-callback-reference, array-type,
  prefer-named-capture-group)

The two dominant rules are the decision: prefer-dom-node-dataset (443) and
jsx-max-depth (378) are 84% of the work and are plausibly per-package overrides
rather than 800 edits. Recommended shape: add extends, then add a
packages/{ui,forms} override in the ROOT config (or in the nested files) that
relaxes exactly those two with a comment saying why, and genuinely FIX the small
tail (the 3 errors, no-duplicate-imports, error-message, prefer-set-has,
func-name-matching). Whichever way it goes, the react-query/web-shell/SDK
no-restricted-imports bans MUST end up in force in both packages — that is the point
of the bead. Verify the same way this gap was found: drop a probe importing useQuery
from "@tanstack/react-query" into each package's src/, confirm pnpm lint errors,
remove the probe.

Note also that without extends those packages lose the root's ignorePatterns
(**/dist/**, **/generated/**, **/routeTree.gen.ts, .output, .nitro, .tanstack), so
confirm the post-extends run is not counting build output.

PIECE 2 — extend packages/sdk/src/oxlint-guardrails.test.ts (or a new sibling spec)
to sweep EVERY .oxlintrc.json in the tree instead of only the root one. Today the
tree holds four: ./.oxlintrc.json, packages/ui, packages/forms,
scripts/fork-smoke. Assert (a) every nested config extends the root, and (b) no
nested config sets no-restricted-imports to "off" — a nested exemption must
re-declare the rule as ["error", {...}] carrying the root's other paths/patterns,
which is the shape scripts/fork-smoke/.oxlintrc.json already uses and the shape the
root's facade override uses. Keep the existing 76 assertions passing.

Constraints to respect:
- scripts/fork-smoke/.oxlintrc.json must stay comment-free JSON: the deleted-package
  sweep in packages/query/src/ JSON.parses lint configs and returns false on throw.
- Do not weaken the root's no-restricted-imports or the existing five-glob facade
  exemption; Wallow-x4qn.12's guard asserts that exemption's files set exactly.
acceptance_criteria: packages/ui/.oxlintrc.json and packages/forms/.oxlintrc.json both carry extends of the root config. A probe file importing useQuery from '@tanstack/react-query' placed in packages/ui/src and packages/forms/src makes pnpm lint exit 1 with eslint(no-restricted-imports) naming @bc-solutions-coder/query; probes removed afterwards and git status clean. pnpm check exits 0 at repo root (so all ~981 surfaced diagnostics are fixed or explicitly overridden with a rationale). packages/sdk/src/oxlint-guardrails.test.ts (or a sibling spec) sweeps every .oxlintrc.json in the tree and asserts each nested config extends the root and none sets no-restricted-imports to 'off'; its existing 76 assertions still pass. scripts/fork-smoke/.oxlintrc.json stays comment-free JSON and packages/query/src/web-shell-removal.test.ts stays 53/53.
notes:
2026-07-30 audit: CONFIRMED. packages/ui/.oxlintrc.json and packages/forms/.oxlintrc.json still lack 'extends'; scripts/fork-smoke/.oxlintrc.json has it and is the correct model. Still latent (no react-query import in either package). Plan: docs/plans/2026-07-30/1033-bug-bead-remediation.md
2026-07-30 MEASURED the fallout of adding 'extends' (added it to both nested configs, ran 'pnpm exec oxlint packages/ui packages/forms', reverted):

981 diagnostics — 3 errors, 978 warnings. pnpm lint runs --deny-warnings, so all 981 are failures.
By package: ui 961, forms 20.
By file class: tests 665, stories 283, real src only 33.
Top rules: unicorn/prefer-dom-node-dataset 443, react/jsx-max-depth 378, no-magic-numbers 89, unicorn/prefer-number-coercion 29.
The 3 errors: oxc/no-map-spread (forms/src/core/query-facade.test.ts:127), eslint/no-await-in-loop (ui/src/components/otp-field/otp-field.stories.tsx:96), unicorn/prefer-set-has (ui/src/index.test.ts:406).

CONFIRMED root 'overrides' DO inherit through 'extends': no-magic-numbers fires 0 times in .test.* files under the nested packages, exactly as the root's '**/*.test.*' override dictates. So the fix is not blocked by broken inheritance.

The 940-of-981 problem is that the root test override covers '**/*.test.*' but NOT '*.stories.tsx', and does not disable the two rules a Base UI component library trips structurally: prefer-dom-node-dataset (packages/ui/CLAUDE.md makes data-attribute assertions the documented way to test component state) and jsx-max-depth (composite Base UI parts nest by design). Extending the override to stories and disabling those two rules for ui/forms test+story files leaves ~33 real src diagnostics to fix properly.

title: Full verification of the query + auth consolidation
description: Run the complete quality gate plus the two production Docker image builds plus the full backend-dependent E2E suite, as the final gate proving the whole epic is safe to merge - especially the wallow-auth mutation-shape rewrite from feature F5's 5c sub-task, which unit/component tests alone cannot fully prove out.
design: Run, in order: pnpm check at the repo root (format:check + lint + typecheck + test + build + check:exports); pnpm why @tanstack/react-query and confirm exactly one 5.x resolution; docker build -f apps/wallow-web/Dockerfile -t wallow-web-react:test . (this step alone catches a broken Dockerfile that pnpm build cannot - see feature F7's step 3 and the docker prerequisite feature F0); docker build -f apps/wallow-auth/Dockerfile -t wallow-auth-react:test .; then ./scripts/e2e.sh, the one-command backend-dependent runner that brings up the containerised stack and runs all three Playwright suites (wallow-auth, wallow-web, and the wallow-web cross-app login journey) against it. E2E is the PRIMARY verification for the mutation-shape rewrite in F5's 5c sub-task, not a formality - apps/wallow-auth/e2e/ covers signup, login, logout, otp-login, magic-link, forgot-password, reset-password and mfa specs alongside the backend-free routes gate, and these specs drive almost exactly the flows whose .mutate(...) variables shape changed in 5c; if a body/path/query mapping is wrong, this is what catches it. Prefer ./scripts/e2e.sh over driving the stack by hand - it was reworked to support E2E_UP_SERVICE, container-mode wallow-auth via E2E_BASE_URL, and E2E_SKIP_IMAGE_BUILD, and because it builds the app images itself it double-checks feature F7's Dockerfile step too. After everything is green, do session completion per the repo's CLAUDE.md: file beads for any remaining leftovers (e.g. the noted future work of converting wallow-auth's remaining mutation call sites to the forms package's useAppForm, which is explicitly out of scope for this epic), then run git pull --rebase && bd dolt push && git push, and verify git status shows the branch up to date with origin.
acceptance_criteria: pnpm check exits zero. pnpm why @tanstack/react-query shows exactly one 5.x line. Both docker build commands succeed. ./scripts/e2e.sh exits zero (all three Playwright suites pass). git status shows nothing to commit and the branch up to date with origin after the final push.
notes:
COORDINATOR — SPEC AMENDMENT (carry into final verification): acceptance criterion F3 'keep react-query in optimizeDeps' for packages/forms was found GENUINELY UNSATISFIABLE and was amended, not merely dropped. Raw react-query in optimizeDeps causes Vite to print 'Failed to resolve dependency' and pre-bundle nothing, because packages/forms has a pre-existing resolution guard that packages/testing lacks. It was replaced by the FACADE entry. Independently reproduced by both the .5 implementer and the .5 verifier. Do NOT fail final verification against the original F3 wording; verify the facade-entry form instead. Note that packages/testing (.4) and packages/forms (.5) therefore differ legitimately on this point.
COORDINATOR: during .12 verification, probe/fixture files were deliberately created and removed to prove the oxlint rule fires (including a packages/query-sibling/** path). Final verification MUST confirm the working tree has NO leftover probe, fixture, or sibling-package artifacts from that exercise, and that git status shows only intended epic changes.
COORDINATOR: .13's verifier disclosed an accidental 'oxfmt --write' that reformatted UNRELATED pre-existing markdown tables (content unaffected, pins re-confirmed 26/26). Final verification + the epic commit must account for this: confirm those hunks are formatting-only, and either include them deliberately or revert them. Do not let them pass unnoticed as part of the query/auth diff.
VERIFY (final epic gate) — VERDICT: GREEN. All criteria verified in scope; nothing papered over.

=== A. pnpm check — EXIT 0 (the real one-command gate, repo root) ===
Pre-step: built in dependency order first (sdk -> styles+query -> ui+auth -> forms+testing), all exit 0.
Then `pnpm check` = format:check && lint && typecheck && test && build && check:exports, EXIT 0.
- format:check (oxfmt --check apps packages package.json pnpm-workspace.yaml tsconfig.base.json .oxlintrc.json .oxfmtrc.json): "All matched files use the correct format." 750 files.
- lint (oxlint apps packages --deny-warnings): clean, no output.
- typecheck (pnpm -r typecheck): 10 of 11 projects, clean.
- test (pnpm -r test): 314 test files / 4256 tests, ALL PASSED, 0 failed:
    styles 6/60, query 4/88, sdk 42/1115, auth 4/37, testing 6/68, ui 97/1162,
    minimal-app 5/27, forms 16/111, wallow-web 81/587, wallow-auth 53/1001.
  (The `error` strings in the log are expected error-boundary console.error output in ui/forms
   specs and asset filenames like error-banner-*.js — not failures.)
- build (pnpm -r build): all packages + both apps' Nitro output, clean.
- check:exports (scripts/check-exports.sh): now runs packages/{auth,query,sdk,styles,testing}.
  auth + query both 🟢 node16-from-ESM (ESM) and 🟢 bundler. Only publint SUGGESTION on the two
  new packages: no "sideEffects" field (non-fatal, same class as the pre-existing ones).

=== B. Docker image builds — BOTH EXIT 0 (bead criterion, ran even though not in the spawn list) ===
docker build -f apps/wallow-web/Dockerfile  -t wallow-web-react:test  .  -> EXIT 0 (1.03GB)

title: Lint enforcement: ban direct @tanstack/react-query imports outside the facade
description: With every package and app routed through @bc-solutions-coder/query, add an oxlint no-restricted-imports rule that makes the facade convention permanent, with a narrow, explicit allowlist for the facade package itself and the handful of SDK files that legitimately import the raw package (an optional-peer dependency declaration).
design: Read packages/sdk/src/oxlint-guardrails.test.ts FIRST - it pins the config and also runs the real oxlint binary over violating/compliant code snippets, and the obvious version of the new test cannot pass without understanding its fixture mechanism. Step 1: in root .oxlintrc.json's no-restricted-imports.paths array, append two entries - one banning the '@tanstack/react-query' package name with a message pointing at @bc-solutions-coder/query as the required import path (mentions it owns the version and defaults, and keeps one QueryClient context instance across the workspace), and one banning '@bc-solutions-coder/web-shell' with a message saying it is deleted and createQueryClient now ships from @bc-solutions-coder/query. Step 2: append a files-scoped override exempting the places that legitimately import the real @tanstack/react-query package - the facade package itself (packages/query/**) and exactly four named SDK files: packages/sdk/src/route-context.ts, packages/sdk/src/route-context.test.ts, packages/sdk/src/query/invalidations.ts, packages/sdk/src/generated-query-surface.test.ts. Do NOT write a blanket no-restricted-imports:off for packages/sdk/** - oxlint has no per-name partial disable, so turning the rule off entirely would also reopen the existing bans on the deleted module-global client exports, the retired query slices and key registry, and the dist/src deep-import patterns across all SDK source. Instead RE-DECLARE the rule inside the override: copy the root rule's paths and patterns verbatim MINUS the new @tanstack/react-query entry, scoped via files to just those five locations (the facade dir plus the four named files). Include the @bc-solutions-coder/web-shell ban from step 1 in the re-declared copy too - nothing in the SDK or the facade may import it. packages/sdk/src/generated/** is already covered by ignorePatterns so it needs no entry; the existing api.test.ts/index.test.ts override is untouched. Step 3: extend oxlint-guardrails.test.ts with two kinds of new coverage. Through the real oxlint binary (the existing mkdtempSync fixture mechanism, which writes fixtures OUTSIDE the repo so any files-glob-based override can never match a fixture path): assert that importing useQuery from @tanstack/react-query produces a no-restricted-imports diagnostic, that importing it from @bc-solutions-coder/query produces none, and the same pair of assertions for @bc-solutions-coder/web-shell. Declaratively (in the existing describe block that reads .oxlintrc.json via readRuleEntry()): assert an override entry exists whose files cover the facade dir and the four SDK files, whose re-declared rule still carries the SDK's original paths/patterns, and whose paths do NOT include @tanstack/react-query - this is what proves the exemption is narrow rather than a blanket off. packages/forms/** needs NO exemption - it is routed through the facade in an earlier feature (F3B), so the ban applies to it like any other package; if pnpm lint flags a forms file here, that earlier feature is incomplete and must be fixed there, not by widening this override.

title: 5d: add features/*/api.ts data-import seams to wallow-auth
description: Give every wallow-auth feature dir that calls a generated SDK operation a thin api.ts re-export seam matching apps/wallow-web/src/features/organizations/api.ts, so 'api.ts is the feature's only data import' holds in wallow-auth the way it already does in wallow-web.
design: Two greps are needed (features split across both SDK entries): grep -rln '@bc-solutions-coder/sdk/query' apps/wallow-auth/src finds login, register, consent, invitation, logout, mfa-challenge, verify-email (plus routes/login.tsx and routes/invitation.tsx); grepping for the plain package import '@bc-solutions-coder/sdk' (not the /query subpath) across apps/wallow-auth/src finds features importing RAW operations that never appear in the first grep: mfa-enroll (5c converts it to generated factories so its seam re-exports from the query entry like the rest), plus forgot-password and reset-password. forgot-password/reset-password are the exception: 5c does not touch them (no-mutation escape hatch), so they own no generated artifact - the raw op is called directly inside useAppForm's onSubmit. They still get a seam (the whole point of 5d is that api.ts is the only data import), but it re-exports the RAW operation from the plain @bc-solutions-coder/sdk package, not from its /query subpath - e.g. re-export accountForgotPassword from @bc-solutions-coder/sdk (and the equivalent for reset-password). Say in the seam's doc comment WHY it differs (no generated Mutation factory exists because the form uses the no-mutation escape hatch) so a future reader doesn't 'fix' it into a generated factory and undo 5c's exclusion. The five feature dirs added after the plan was written - accept-terms, error, not-found, privacy, terms - call no generated operations and need no seam; confirm with the greps rather than assuming. For each of the ten feature dirs that DO need a seam: create src/features/<name>/api.ts mirroring apps/wallow-web/src/features/organizations/api.ts (thin re-export seam with a doc comment, exporting exactly the generated artifacts that feature uses) and a co-located api.test.ts mirroring wallow-web's identity-assertion pattern (asserting each re-exported symbol is reference-identical to the same symbol read off a namespace import of the underlying entry - the lint override at apps/**/src/features/*/api.test.ts already whitelists importing the raw/query entry there). Repoint components to import from the local ../api module instead of importing generated artifacts directly. Routes (routes/login.tsx, routes/invitation.tsx) import from the owning feature's seam rather than the SDK directly.
acceptance_criteria: pnpm --filter @bc-solutions-coder/wallow-auth test passes (full suite, including the new api.test.ts files). No component file under apps/wallow-auth/src/features/*/components imports from the SDK package or its query subpath directly - only from the local ../api module. title: 5c: replace hand-rolled mutations with generated factories in wallow-auth
description: 9 components in apps/wallow-auth still call useMutation with a hand-rolled mutationFn that wraps a raw SDK operation, instead of the generated {op}Mutation() factories that packages/sdk/src/generated/@tanstack/react-query.gen.ts ships. Convert all 9, handle the one GET-based special case, and delete 8 dead retry:false overrides that createQueryClient() already makes redundant.
design: Transformation pattern, using PasswordLoginForm.tsx as the exemplar. Before, the component builds useMutation with a mutationFn that is an async function taking the raw credentials and awaiting accountLogin({ client: sdk.client, body: credentials }), then later calls mutation.mutate with the bare credentials object plus onSuccess/onError callbacks. After, the component builds useMutation directly from accountLoginMutation({ client: sdk.client }), and mutation.mutate is called with an object of the shape { body: credentials } plus the same onSuccess/onError callbacks. The variables shape changes from a bare body to an object with body/path/query keys at every .mutate() call site - update call sites together with the hook, in the same commit/pass. Where the old mutationFn carried a justified type comment (e.g. an untyped anonymous C# response), keep the comment beside the useMutation call; the generated factory's return type governs, and any narrowing stays at the call site (onSuccess) or in the feature's existing panel/result modules. Locate every site via grep -rn mutationFn apps/wallow-auth/src (do not trust a fixed line-number list - files moved after the plan was written) and re-run the grep after the rewrite to confirm zero survive. The 9 sites, by mutationFn parameter signature: features/login/components/PasswordLoginForm.tsx, param named credentials of type Credentials, raw op accountLogin, becomes accountLoginMutation. features/login/components/MagicLinkLoginForm.tsx, param named address of type string, raw op accountSendMagicLink, becomes accountSendMagicLinkMutation. features/login/components/MagicLinkLoginForm.tsx, param named value of type string, raw op accountVerifyMagicLink - this is the GET special case, see below. features/login/components/OtpLoginForm.tsx, param named address of type string, raw op accountSendOtp, becomes accountSendOtpMutation. features/login/components/OtpLoginForm.tsx, param named value of type string, raw op accountVerifyOtp, becomes accountVerifyOtpMutation. features/register/components/RegisterForm.tsx, param named request of type RegisterRequest, raw op accountRegister, becomes accountRegisterMutation. features/invitation/components/InvitationScreen.tsx, param named accepted of type string, raw op invitationsAccept, becomes invitationsAcceptMutation. features/mfa-challenge/components/MfaChallengeForm.tsx, param named attempt (an object with code and useBackupCode fields), raw op accountVerifyMfaChallenge, becomes accountVerifyMfaChallengeMutation. features/mfa-enroll/components/MfaEnrollForm.tsx has two sites, a zero-arg one and an attempt-object one, raw ops mfaEnrollTotp and mfaConfirmEnrollment, becoming mfaEnrollTotpMutation and mfaConfirmEnrollmentMutation. SPECIAL CASE: accountVerifyMagicLink is a GET, so the generator emits accountVerifyMagicLinkOptions, not a Mutation factory. Do not keep the hand-rolled useMutation for it; replace the imperative verify with a call to queryClient.fetchQuery passing accountVerifyMagicLinkOptions({ client: sdk.client, query: { token } }) (grep the generated file for the exact arg shape) and document with one comment line. OUT OF SCOPE: do NOT convert ForgotPasswordForm or ResetPasswordForm - they already migrated to @bc-solutions-coder/forms's useAppForm and deliberately use its no-mutation escape hatch (forgot-password swallows every failure for anti-enumeration; reset-password owns its own status-code branching), and their file headers say so - re-introducing a mutation would restore exactly the error surface those comments forbid. Also delete the 8 dead retry:false overrides (find with grep -rn 'retry: false' apps/wallow-auth/src) in: ConsentScreen.tsx, InvitationScreen.tsx (two sites), ExternalProviders.tsx, LogoutScreen.tsx, MfaChallengeForm.tsx, VerifyEmailConfirm.tsx, routes/login.tsx (the useClientBranding query only - leave its prose comment about why an unresolved client must not gate the form). They are dead because createQueryClient() already sets retry:false globally and mutations never retried anyway.

HAZARDS — what was done about each:
1. Cache invalidation via `invalidations` predicates: NOTHING to preserve. Grepped the whole app before and after — wallow-auth never called invalidateQueries/queriesWithTag/queriesForOperation on any of these 9 writes. Every success path here NAVIGATES (globalThis.location.href / router) or hands the body to the shell, so the next screen refetches from a fresh client. No predicate was dropped and none was invented.
2. Redirect-on-success: the generated factories carry ONLY a mutationFn (asserted by the structural test), so passing one straight to useMutation would silently drop onSuccess. Every site that owns a redirect or state transition SPREADS it — InvitationScreen (location.href = HOME_HREF), MfaEnrollForm (both mutations) — or keeps its callbacks on the .mutate() second argument (PasswordLoginForm, OtpLoginForm, RegisterForm, MfaChallengeForm, MagicLinkLoginForm send). Verified by reading each onSuccess through to its destination, not by the compiler.
3. MFA step sequencing: MfaEnrollForm keeps THREE distinct steps. mfaEnrollTotp (start) and mfaConfirmEnrollment (confirm) are separate useMutation blocks — confirm does not reference the start op — and mfaExchangeEnrollmentToken stays an imperative await on the raw barrel because it is the post-confirm ticket exchange, not a user-triggered write. MfaChallengeForm's verify remains one mutation whose onSuccess narrows and then routes.
4. `useMutation({ ...factory() })` object-literal form is LOAD-BEARING, not style: the red-phase spec parses mutation blocks with /\buseMutation\s*\(\s*\{/ and asserts exactly one block per op, so `useMutation(factory())` in MfaEnrollForm would read as zero blocks. Kept the literal spread even where there are no extra options.
5. Magic-link one-time token: the `verifyStartedRef` latch survives verbatim and its comment now says WHY it is MORE load-bearing under fetchQuery (queryClient is stable across renders where the old mutation object was not, so the effect merely LOOKS dep-safe). No staleTime and no initialData — a replayed cache entry would hand back a signInTicket for a redemption that never happened. Failure is handled as a REJECTION (two-arg .then(onAuthResult, onFailure), deliberately not .then().catch(), so a throw inside onAuthResult is not misreported as a verify failure).
6. RFC 7807: no delta, as the red phase found — responseStyle: 'data' + global throwOnError already give raw bodies and rejections. Not re-litigated. description: Create a new private workspace package @bc-solutions-coder/auth that is the canonical current-user query, hooks, and role/permission helpers for every app - currentUserQuery, useCurrentUser, hasRole, hasPermission, ensureCurrentUser. Depends on packages/query (Task F1, must be built first) and packages/sdk. This becomes the ONE source of truth for current-user semantics; wallow-web's apps/wallow-web/src/lib/current-user.ts and wallow-auth's separate inline current-user probe both get deleted and repointed at this package in later features.
design: package.json mirrors packages/query's shape but with dependencies { '@bc-solutions-coder/query': 'workspace:*', '@bc-solutions-coder/sdk': 'workspace:*' } and peerDependencies { react: '^19.0.0' } (react also in devDependencies for local testing). The SDK must be built first (pnpm --filter @bc-solutions-coder/sdk build) or typecheck fails against a missing dist/. packages/auth/src/current-user.ts is apps/wallow-web/src/lib/current-user.ts moved VERBATIM (keep its full doc comment, adjust only the first line to note it now serves every app) with one import change: queryOptions comes from @bc-solutions-coder/query instead of @tanstack/react-query. Exported names stay currentUserQuery and CurrentUser. This is the canonical semantics: generated query key (from usersGetCurrentUserQueryKey), getCurrentUser 401-softening (resolves null = anonymous, not an error), a sub field renamed from id, and staleTime: 30_000. wallow-auth's own copy (no staleTime, no sub) is the one that dies later. packages/auth/src/authorization.ts exports hasRole(user, role) and hasPermission(user, permission) reading CurrentUser.roles/permissions arrays, returning false (not throwing) for null/undefined users or missing arrays. packages/auth/src/use-current-user.ts exports useCurrentUser(client: WallowSdk['client']) = useQuery(currentUserQuery(client)) from @bc-solutions-coder/query, deliberately importing no router (mirrors the SDK's route-context.ts pattern). packages/auth/src/ensure-current-user.ts exports an EnsureCurrentUserOptions interface { queryClient: QueryClient; client: WallowSdk['client'] } and ensureCurrentUser(options) = options.queryClient.ensureQueryData(currentUserQuery(options.client)) for use in a route's beforeLoad. packages/auth/src/index.ts re-exports currentUserQuery/CurrentUser, useCurrentUser, hasPermission/hasRole, ensureCurrentUser/EnsureCurrentUserOptions, plus re-exports isAdmin/loginRedirect/requireAuth/LoginRedirectOptions/RequireAuthOptions/WallowUser from @bc-solutions-coder/sdk so an app's auth imports come from one package. Tests: current-user.test.ts uses createWallowSdk + a stubbed global fetch (no SDK mocking) to assert the query key matches usersGetCurrentUserQueryKey, staleTime is 30_000, a 200 response resolves a user with sub filled from id, and a 401 response resolves null. authorization.test.ts covers role/permission membership and anonymous/claimless users. No browser-mode vitest project needed (node env only, like packages/query) - useCurrentUser's rendering behavior is covered by app component suites. Write packages/auth/CLAUDE.md: surface table, 'no router import' rule, canonical current-user semantics (generated key / 401->null / sub rename / 30s staleTime).

title: forms: decide revalidate-on-change vs submit-only validation
description: The forms plan's design specified revalidate-on-change behaviour, but useAppForm as built validates on submit only. Discovered while writing the package docs (Wallow-ov6w.5.1), which documented the as-built submit-only behaviour truthfully rather than the design's claim. All 5 migrated forms therefore validate on submit only. This is a deliberate follow-up decision, not a defect in the shipped code: the tests, migrations, and docs are internally consistent.
design: Decide whether submit-only validation is the intended UX. If revalidate-on-change is wanted, add it to useAppForm behind the existing validator wiring and update the 5 migrated forms plus the package guide. If submit-only is correct, no code change — just confirm and close.
acceptance_criteria: 1. A decision is recorded. 2. If change is wanted: useAppForm revalidates on change, the 5 migrated forms are covered by tests asserting it, and docs/CLAUDE.md guidance is updated. 3. Full quality gate passes.
notes:
COORDINATOR — USER DECISION (supersedes the open question on this bead): implement revalidate-on-change. The user has chosen to make the as-built behaviour match the plan's design doc: fields that have already been validated once (i.e. after a failed submit / once an error is showing) must re-validate as the user types, so the error clears/updates live rather than only on the next submit. Untouched, never-submitted fields must NOT start screaming errors on first keystroke. Scope is the shared @bc-solutions-coder/forms package so all 5 migrated forms inherit it — do not hand-configure each form. TDD red -> green -> verify as usual.
DECISION RECORDED + IMPLEMENTED (commit fb161782, on main). Revalidate-on-change is now the shared behaviour: useAppForm sets validationLogic: revalidateLogic() (TanStack defaults mode=submit / modeAfterSubmission=change) and the caller's zod schema moved from validators.onSubmit to validators.onDynamic. Set once in the hook, so all 5 migrated forms inherit it with no per-form config.

KEY FINDING — revalidateLogic runs ONLY the onDynamic validator; it ignores onChange/onBlur/onSubmit entirely. So this was not additive: leaving the schema on validators.onSubmit alongside the strategy validates NOTHING. The TOnDynamic generic slot in AppFormApi had to move with it (FormApi generics are 'in out', so the instantiation and the type must match exactly). Recorded as a gotcha in packages/forms/CLAUDE.md.

SECOND FINDING — app-level specs resolve @bc-solutions-coder/forms from dist/, not src/. The wallow-auth spec failed against behaviour the package's own specs proved working, purely because the bundle was stale. pnpm --filter @bc-solutions-coder/forms build is required after any hook change before consumer suites mean anything. Also recorded in packages/forms/CLAUDE.md.

TESTS: packages/forms/src/form/use-app-form.revalidate.test.tsx (7 cases — quiet-before-submit x2, live message swap, clear-on-valid, return-on-invalid, per-field blast-radius guard, onServer RFC 7807 regression guard). Red run failed exactly the 2 'message tracks the value live' cases; the rest already passed. Plus 2 cases on ForgotPasswordForm.forms.test.tsx proving a migrated consumer inherits the rule without configuring it.

DOCS: docs/development/forms.md updated in 3 places that claimed submit-only (schema option row, client-side-validation row, behaviour bullet); packages/forms/CLAUDE.md gained the two gotchas above.

title: packages/styles: toRootRelativeAssetUrl emits unprefixed asset URLs (e.g. /piggy-icon.svg) under a base path
description: Found during Wallow-vufu.2.2 (wallow-auth base-path support): packages/styles' toRootRelativeAssetUrl builds root-relative asset URLs that ignore any app base path, so branding assets 404 when the app is served under a prefix. Out of 2.2's file scope (packages/styles). See bd show Wallow-vufu.2.2 notes for context.
notes:
GREEN: FILES=packages/styles/src/asset-urls.ts, packages/styles/src/branding.ts, packages/styles/src/index.ts, packages/styles/CLAUDE.md, packages/styles/src/asset-urls.test.ts, packages/styles/src/branding.test.ts, apps/wallow-auth/src/lib/branding.ts (new), apps/wallow-auth/src/lib/branding.test.ts (new), apps/wallow-auth/src/routes/__root.tsx, apps/wallow-auth/src/components/auth-layout.tsx, apps/wallow-auth/src/routes/login.tsx.

SYMBOLS (packages/styles, all on the '.' entry):
  toRootRelativeAssetUrl(assetPath: string, basePath: string = ''): string  -- second param is NEW
  mergeClientBranding(fork: ForkBranding, client: ClientBranding | null, basePath: string = ''): ResolvedBranding  -- third param is NEW
  resolveForkBranding(basePath: string = ''): ResolvedBranding  -- NEW
  toAppIconUrl(basePath: string = ''): string  -- NEW
  appIconUrl / forkResolvedBranding constants UNCHANGED (they are now the basePath='' resolutions)
apps/wallow-auth/src/lib/branding.ts exports appIconUrl and forkResolvedBranding bound to BASE_PATH.

DESIGN: the base path is a PARAMETER, never a read. packages/styles ships a prebuilt dist bundle, so its own import.meta.env.BASE_URL freezes at '/' at package-build time -- reading it there would silently unprefix every consumer. toRootRelativeAssetUrl normalizes whatever shape arrives ('', '/', 'auth', '/auth', '/auth/', whitespace) so an app can hand over Vite's raw import.meta.env.BASE_URL or an already-normalized prefix. Prefixing is idempotent on a SEGMENT boundary (same rule as the passthrough's stripBasePath): '/auth/x.svg' under '/auth' is untouched, '/authentic/x.svg' is still prefixed. Absolute and protocol-relative URLs (a client's hosted logoUrl) stay untouched -- this app's prefix means nothing on someone else's origin.

WIRING: reused Wallow-vufu.2.2's single source of truth -- apps/wallow-auth/src/lib/base-path.ts BASE_PATH (= normalizeBasePath(import.meta.env.BASE_URL), itself derived from vite.config's AUTH_BASE_PATH). No second knob invented. The new apps/wallow-auth/src/lib/branding.ts binds it once; __root.tsx and auth-layout.tsx now import appIconUrl/forkResolvedBranding from THERE, not from the package, and login.tsx passes BASE_PATH to mergeClientBranding.

TEST_STATUS=pass. 18 new/changed assertions were confirmed RED first (toAppIconUrl/resolveForkBranding not functions, base-path cases failing). packages/styles 86/86; apps/wallow-auth 1011/1011 (incl. 8 new in src/lib/branding.test.ts); wallow-web 587, ui 1162, forms 118, query 88, auth 37, testing 68, minimal-app 27 all pass. pnpm typecheck all 10 projects Done; pnpm lint clean; pnpm format:check clean.

REAL-BUILD VERIFICATION (unit tests cannot see a build-time value): built with AUTH_BASE_PATH=/auth and ran the Nitro server. Client chunk contains 'var p=normalize(`/auth/`)' then 'var ht=E(p),gt=T(p)' -- i.e. appIconUrl=toAppIconUrl(BASE_PATH), forkResolvedBranding=resolveForkBranding(BASE_PATH), and mergeClientBranding threads it into logoUrl:g(e.appIcon,n). Served build answers 200 on /auth/piggy-icon.svg and 307 on /piggy-icon.svg (behind a path-based ingress that root is a different app, so the old URL was the bug). Rebuilt unprefixed afterwards so .output is back to the default.

ISSUES / OUT OF SCOPE: apps/wallow-web and apps/examples/minimal-app still import the package's unbased appIconUrl/forkResolvedBranding constants. That is correct today -- neither has base-path support (Wallow-vufu.2.2 covered wallow-auth only) and neither sets Vite 'base', so their BASE_URL is '/'. Whoever adds a WEB_BASE_PATH must mirror apps/wallow-auth/src/lib/branding.ts; the package side is already done. Unrelated: packages/sdk's openapi-regen.test.ts was failing mid-run during this task from a CONCURRENT agent's uncommitted Inquiries/OpenAPI regen -- not touched here.
close_reason: toRootRelativeAssetUrl and mergeClientBranding now take a basePath (normalized from any shape: bare, leading/trailing slashes, Vite's BASE_URL); new toAppIconUrl + resolveForkBranding accept it too. Taken as a PARAMETER, not read from import.meta.env.BASE_URL, because packages/styles ships prebuilt and would freeze that at '/'. wallow-auth binds it once in the new src/lib/branding.ts from Wallow-vufu.2.2's existing BASE_PATH, and __root/auth-layout/login import branding from there so a stray package-level import cannot reintroduce the unprefixed URL. Implementer also verified a real AUTH_BASE_PATH=/auth Nitro build: 200 on /auth/piggy-icon.svg, 307 on /piggy-icon.svg. Commit 151a2cb4. KNOWN GAP: wallow-web and examples/minimal-app still import the unbased package constants — correct today since neither has a base-path knob (base='' is the identity), but follow-up filed.

If sdk changes came in during the rebase, rebuild it before continuing: `pnpm --filter @bc-solutions-coder/sdk build`.
2. `pnpm --filter @bc-solutions-coder/sdk build && pnpm build` (SDK first -- apps and other packages typecheck against its dist/).
3. `pnpm check` -- the one-command gate (format:check + lint + typecheck + test + build + check:exports). Fix anything it surfaces before proceeding.

E2E on the rebased result: `./scripts/e2e.sh` (per .claude/rules/E2E.md, this is the containerized backend-dependent runner covering wallow-auth; also run `pnpm --filter ./apps/wallow-web test:e2e` if backend infra is separately available for wallow-web). 5. Merge back: `git checkout main && git merge --ff-only feat/forms-package` (linear history, no merge commit, so conventional-commit messages stay release-parseable by release-please). If the fast-forward fails, main moved during this epic's execution -- go back to step 1 and rebase again.

Close every completed bead in this epic's tree (mark this task and its ancestors completed); update any that remain in-progress with their real status.
7. `git pull --rebase && bd dolt push && git push` -- the epic's work is NOT complete until push succeeds; verify `git status` shows "up to date with origin" afterward. Then `git worktree remove ../Wallow-forms`.

- `phone` (TextField) -- required, same message, `inquiry-phone` / `inquiry-phone-error`.
