notes:
RED (red-4-3): apps/wallow-web/src/features/inquiries/components/CreateInquiryForm.forms.test.tsx — 15 tests, 10 confirmed FAILING against the hand-rolled form, 5 passing as deliberate regression guards. Command: pnpm --filter ./apps/wallow-web exec vitest run src/features/inquiries/components/CreateInquiryForm.forms.test.tsx (browser project, real headless Chromium, real SDK via createSdkHarness + renderWithWallow, nothing mocked).

FAILING (10) — what the migration must add:
1. renders through the forms shell (form.noValidate === true).
2. labels every control the form owns — 7 exact labels asserted: Name / Email / Phone / Project type / Budget range / Timeline / Message. Today NONE of the 8 controls has a label at all.
3. marks company optional in its label (accessible name contains "Company" and "optional").
4. associates each validation message with its control: aria-describedby + aria-invalid on inquiry-name (input) and inquiry-message (textarea), data-invalid on the inquiry-project-type Select trigger. This is the ErrorBanner -> Field.Error unification, testids unchanged.
5. keeps the message control a real textarea, now on the catalog recipe (tag TEXTAREA + classList contains min-h-20 and resize-y — the two utilities only textareaRecipe adds over inputRecipe).
6. disables every control and the submit while in flight (harness.pending(): 4 inputs .disabled, textarea .disabled, 3 select triggers data-disabled, submit .disabled).
7. routes a per-property RFC 7807 message to its field (errors:{ProjectType:[...]} -> inquiry-project-type-error) and shows NO banner.
8. keeps an unmatched property's message in the banner (errors:{Captcha:[...]} -> inquiry-error).
9. clears a server field error on the next submit rather than wedging the form.
10. falls back to "Could not submit the inquiry." when the failure carries no detail. GENUINE behaviour delta, verified: today errorText() prefers WallowError.message over the caller fallback, so the observed banner text is "Server error"; splitServerError uses `error.detail ?? fallback`, which is the fallbackError option.

PASSING GUARDS (5) — what the migration must not drop: the form testid stays inquiry-create-form while all 8 fields + submit stay on the bare `inquiry` prefix and every control stays under that one <form>; all 7 required messages read exactly "This field is required"; a whitespace-only value is rejected without reaching the endpoint; the submitted value is posted UNTRIMMED ("  Ada Lovelace  "); the success state replaces the form AND inquiry-create-heading AND inquiry-submit.

BLOCKER DECISION (textarea focus ring) — resolved as option (b): NARROW the restyle spec, do NOT extend the ui recipe. packages/ui is UNTOUCHED (git status confirms). CreateInquiryForm.restyle.test.tsx's CONTROL constant lost only `focus:outline-none focus:ring-2 focus:ring-ring`; both edits are comment-documented in the file. Evidence that the pinned classes are incidental to the hand-rolled implementation, not a user-visible guarantee the shared component must honour:
  (i) IN-FILE PRECEDENT, same spec, same situation: the sibling case "styles every select like the shared text input" was ALREADY narrowed when the selects became catalog Selects (Wallow-m5aq.5.3) — it dropped border-border AND the focus utilities with the comment "the recipe's own additions ... are the component's business, not this spec's". The textarea is the identical move one migration later.
  (ii) EXTENDING textareaRecipe ALONE IS FORBIDDEN BY ui's OWN CONTRACT: packages/ui/src/components/textarea/textarea.styles.ts documents its base as inputRecipe's string verbatim ("the two controls must not drift"), and packages/ui/src/components/textarea/textarea.test.tsx asserts the EXACT class set (toEqual on a sorted classList) plus a dedicated non-drift test. Adding a ring to Textarea would break that spec and split it from Input — so option (a) does not avoid a test edit, it just moves the edit into packages/ui and breaks a stated invariant while doing it.
  (iii) EXTENDING BOTH RECIPES WOULD STILL NOT SATISFY THE PIN: the catalog's own focus convention (menubar.styles.ts, toolbar.styles.ts, scroll-area.styles.ts) is `outline-none focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-ring`. The pinned string is the `focus:` variant, which fires on mouse click too — a catalog-conformant recipe could never match it. input.test.tsx also pins Input's exact class set, so this is a two-package, 23-call-site change.
  (iv) NO REGRESSION IN WHAT USERS SEE: the four ui Inputs in THIS SAME FORM have never had a focus ring, so the pin made the textarea the only ringed control on the page. Dropping `focus:outline-none` RESTORES the browser's native focus outline, so the textarea stays visibly focusable — focus visibility is preserved, and the form becomes internally consistent.
  (v) COVERAGE IS NOT WEAKENED, IT IS REDIRECTED: failing case 5 above now pins min-h-20/resize-y, i.e. that the control genuinely IS the shared catalog Textarea, which the old class-string pin could not distinguish from a hand-copy.
FOLLOW-UP WORTH FILING (not done, out of scope): give packages/ui Input AND Textarea a catalog-conformant `outline-none focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-ring` in one change, updating both components' exact-set specs. That is a real improvement to the catalog; it must not ride inside a form migration.

VERIFIED FOR THE GREEN PHASE (read from code, not assumed):

title: Migrate RegisterAppForm to @bc-solutions-coder/forms
description:
Migrate apps/wallow-web/src/features/apps/components/RegisterAppForm.tsx onto @bc-solutions-coder/forms. Second wallow-web migration -- proves select variety plus deliberately-out-of-catalog controls (scope toggle buttons, uncontrolled branding subsection) that stay untouched.

Current file already read in full by the scout. Co-located specs (must pass unchanged): RegisterAppForm.test.tsx, RegisterAppForm.catalog.test.tsx (pins the catalog-Select behavior for the client-type select), RegisterAppForm.branding.test.tsx (pins the uncontrolled BrandingSection). Route spec: apps/wallow-web/src/routes/dashboard/apps/register.test.tsx and register.restyle.test.tsx assert the `app-register-form` testid.

WHAT MIGRATES onto forms catalog fields:
- `displayName` (TextField) -- current validator `value.trim() ? undefined : "Display name is required"`, testids `app-display-name` / `app-display-name-error` (bare "app" prefix -- testId override required, see below).
- `clientType` (SelectField) -- currently wraps `SelectControl` directly with `CLIENT_TYPE_OPTIONS` = `[{ value: "public", label: "Public" }, { value: "confidential", label: "Confidential" }]`, default value "public", testid `app-client-type` (testId override required). No validator today (always has a value via the default).
- `redirectUris` (TextareaField) -- currently a RAW unstyled `<textarea data-testid="app-redirect-uris">`, newline-separated URIs, split/trimmed/filtered at submit time (`.split("\n").map(trim).filter(Boolean)`). No validator today. testId override "app-redirect-uris" required.
- `postLogoutRedirectUris` (TextareaField) -- same shape as redirectUris, testid `app-post-logout-redirect-uris`, same split/trim/filter transform at submit.

WHAT STAYS EXACTLY AS-IS, outside the forms catalog (deliberately -- these have no matching catalog field, YAGNI per the design doc's field list):
- `scopes` field: still a raw `form.AppField name="scopes"` (or equivalent escape hatch) wrapping the EXISTING `ScopeToggles` component (ToggleGroup + Toggle from ui, not a forms catalog field) -- forms has no multi-select-toggle catalog field, this is the documented "AppField render prop still exposes the raw field object" escape hatch from the design doc. Testids `app-scope-{scope-dashed}` unchanged.
- `BrandingSection` -- uncontrolled, presentational, NOT wired to any form.Field at all today (no state, no value/onChange). Render it exactly where it is today, untouched, still outside any `form.AppField`.
- The one-time success view (`SuccessView`, showing `mutation.data.clientSecret`) -- this reads `mutation.isSuccess`/`mutation.data` directly in the OUTER `RegisterAppForm` component (before rendering `RegisterAppFormFields`), so it needs the raw `useMutation` instance. Check whether `useAppForm`'s returned `form.wallow` extras expose the underlying mutation object/data, or whether this form should construct its own `useMutation` via `organizationsCreateMutation`-equivalent and pass it into `useAppForm({ mutation })` as an object it ALSO keeps a reference to outside the hook (so `SuccessView` can read `.data` from it) -- this is a real design question to resolve during implementation; note the answer in the commit message.

Field remap at submit (API request contract, preserve exactly): `displayName -> clientName`, `scopes -> requestedScopes`, `clientType` passes through, `redirectUris`/`postLogoutRedirectUris` each split on "\n", trimmed, blanks filtered.

Current testids (verbatim, must survive): `app-register-form` (form -- matches testIdPrefix="app-register" derivation directly, no override needed for the form element itself, unlike organization/inquiry), `app-display-name`, `app-display-name-error`, `app-client-type`, `app-redirect-uris`, `app-post-logout-redirect-uris`, `app-scope-{scope}` (unchanged), `app-branding` + children (unchanged), `app-register-error`, `app-register-submit`, `app-register-success` + `app-client-id` + `app-client-secret` + `app-client-secret-copy` (SuccessView, unchanged).
design:
Zod schema (values shape mirrors current defaultValues exactly):
```ts
z.object({
  displayName: z.string().trim().min(1, "Display name is required"),
  clientType: z.string(),
  redirectUris: z.string(),
  postLogoutRedirectUris: z.string(),
  scopes: z.array(z.string()),
})
```

useAppForm with `mutation: appsRegisterMutation({ client: sdk.client })`, `toVariables` doing the field remap and split/trim/filter transform exactly as today's inline `mutation.mutate({ body: {...} })` call does, `onSuccess` sweeping the Apps tag (`queriesWithTag("Apps")`), `fallbackError: "Could not register the app."`.

Markup:
```tsx
<form.AppForm testIdPrefix="app-register">
  <form.AppField name="displayName">
    {(f) => <f.TextField label="Display name" testId="app-display-name" />}
  </form.AppField>
  <form.AppField name="clientType">
    {(f) => <f.SelectField label="Client type" testId="app-client-type" options={CLIENT_TYPE_OPTIONS} />}
  </form.AppField>
  <form.AppField name="redirectUris">
    {(f) => <f.TextareaField label="Redirect URIs" testId="app-redirect-uris" />}
  </form.AppField>
  <form.AppField name="postLogoutRedirectUris">
    {(f) => <f.TextareaField label="Post-logout redirect URIs" testId="app-post-logout-redirect-uris" />}
  </form.AppField>
  <form.AppField name="scopes">
    {(f) => <ScopeToggles value={f.state.value} onChange={f.handleChange} />}
  </form.AppField>
  <BrandingSection />
  <form.FormError />
  <form.SubmitButton>Register app</form.SubmitButton>
</form.AppForm>

Keep `ScopeToggles`, `BrandingSection`, `SuccessView`, `CLIENT_TYPE_OPTIONS`, `AVAILABLE_SCOPES` exactly as today (delete only `DisplayNameField`, `ClientTypeField`, `RedirectUrisField`, `PostLogoutRedirectUrisField` -- the presentational components the catalog fields now replace).

Resolve the SuccessView/mutation.data seam noted in the description before finalizing -- read Wallow-ov6w.2.3's actual `use-app-form.ts` implementation once it exists to see what the `wallow` extras object exposes.

3. labels the client-type select and both textareas -> accessible name "" ; expects "Client type" / "Redirect URIs" / "Post-logout redirect URIs". These four label strings come from the bead DESIGN block; the field-label lookup is aria-labelledby-first (Base UI names the Select TRIGGER that way, a <label for> cannot name a button), falling back to label[for].
4. associates the required-field message with the input -> message element id is "" (ErrorBanner sibling); expects non-empty id IN aria-describedby + aria-invalid=true.
5. disables the controls and the submit while in flight -> display-name input .disabled false; also asserts both textareas + submit disabled (double submit here mints a SECOND client secret, only one of which is ever shown).
6. per-property message on the field not the banner -> RFC7807 errors {RedirectUris:[...]} must land at app-redirect-uris-error (element absent today) and the banner must NOT render.

This case is register-specific: displayName is remapped to clientName on the wire, so splitServerError's knownFields (defaultValues keys) matches RedirectUris but NOT ClientName -> that half must reach the banner via formError.
8. clears a server field error on the next submit rather than wedging the form -> deliberately does NO second edit: after the field error, the very next submit must reach the endpoint again (calls length 2 + success view). Isolates AppForm's clearServerErrors, no caret-position dependence.

9. keeps every control under ONE shell — closest('form') identity for app-display-name, app-client-type, both URI textareas, app-scope-inquiries-read, app-scope-offline_access, app-branding, app-branding-display-name, app-logo-input, app-register-submit. This is the guard for the SuccessView design question — the gate moves from mutation.isSuccess to state captured in useAppForm's onSuccess, and a gate that merely ADDED the reveal would leave a live form beside a secret that can never be shown again. description:
Migrate apps/wallow-auth/src/features/reset-password/components/ResetPasswordForm.tsx onto @bc-solutions-coder/forms. Second (and last) wallow-auth migration -- proves password fields and multi-field/cross-field validation. Current file already read in full by the scout. Co-located test: apps/wallow-auth/src/features/reset-password/components/ResetPasswordForm.test.tsx. E2E spec: apps/wallow-auth/e2e/reset-password.spec.ts.

CRITICAL BEHAVIOR TO PRESERVE -- this form is NOT a simple mutation-only migration, read carefully:

1. `email`/`token` arrive as PROPS (from the route's query string), not form fields. Keep `ResetPasswordFormProps { email?: string; token?: string }` and the component signature unchanged.
2. THREE distinct error conditions feed ONE error state (current `useState<string | null>`), rendered via `<ErrorBanner data-testid="reset-password-error">`:
   - Missing email or token in the URL -> `INVALID_LINK_MESSAGE` = "Invalid reset link. Please request a new password reset." (checked BEFORE calling the mutation, no network call happens)
   - Client-side password mismatch (`newPassword !== confirmPassword`) -> `PASSWORD_MISMATCH_MESSAGE` = "Passwords do not match." (checked before the mutation)
   - Server rejection with HTTP status 400 -> `EXPIRED_LINK_MESSAGE` = "This reset link is invalid or has expired. Please request a new one." (mapped via `resetFailureMessage`, which reads `(cause as { status }).status`, NOT via WallowError.fieldErrors -- this endpoint's failures are a bare `{ succeeded, error }` 400 body, not RFC 7807, so `splitServerError`/`WallowError.detail` do NOT apply here; keep the existing structural `resetFailureMessage(cause)` status-code narrowing as a plain onError side-effect, do not try to force this through the standard splitServerError path)
   - Any other rejection -> `GENERIC_FAILURE_MESSAGE` = "Failed to reset password. Please try again."
   This means `useAppForm`'s built-in server-error splitting (Wallow-ov6w.2.3's splitServerError) is the WRONG tool for this form's server error -- either bypass it by using the `mutation` option's own `onError` (if useAppForm exposes one) to set a manually-managed error string, or use the no-`mutation` `onSubmit` escape hatch and manage the WallowError-independent status-code logic inside it exactly as today. Decide during implementation which useAppForm surface fits; document the choice in the commit message since it deviates from the "typical" WallowError.fieldErrors flow every other migrated form uses.
3. Password mismatch and missing-link checks currently run BEFORE `setError(null)` and the mutation call, inside the parent's `handleSubmit`, not as a per-field zod validator (there's no live "as you type" mismatch check) -- preserve this submit-time-only cross-field check behavior; zod's `.refine()` on the object schema (comparing newPassword to confirmPassword) is one reasonable way to express it, but confirm the resulting error surfaces the exact same message ("Passwords do not match.") on the exact same `reset-password-error` testid (form-level banner), NOT a per-field error -- so it may need to route through FormError manually rather than a zod-per-field issue.
4. Field validators: `newPassword` has a REQUIRED-only client check with message "New password is required" (rendered at `reset-password-new-password-error`, `Field.Error`-style already in the current raw span). `confirmPassword` has NO validator of its own (its only check is the cross-field mismatch above).
5. Current testids (verbatim, must survive): `reset-password-new-password` (input), `reset-password-new-password-error`, `reset-password-confirm` (input, no error testid), `reset-password-submit`, `reset-password-error` (form-level banner).
6. On success: `navigate({ href: "/login?message=password_reset" })` using `href` not `to` (documented reason: /login's validateSearch is owned by a different in-flight task, must not couple to it) -- preserve this exact navigate call shape.
design:
Suggested approach given the constraints in the description:

Zod schema: `z.object({ newPassword: z.string().min(1, "New password is required"), confirmPassword: z.string() })` -- do NOT try to encode the mismatch check or the link-validity check in the schema; both are submit-time cross-cutting concerns this form's current code handles outside any single field's validator.

useAppForm options: use the no-`mutation` `onSubmit` escape hatch so the full existing `handleSubmit` logic (link validity check, mismatch check, setError(null), the mutation.mutate call with its onSuccess/onError) can be preserved close to verbatim inside it, OR pass `mutation` (wrapping accountResetPassword) plus a custom onError; pick whichever the actual `useAppForm` implementation (Wallow-ov6w.2.3) makes cleaner and note the choice. Either way:
- Keep a local `useState<string | null>` for the banner text (this form's error is NOT well-modeled by the generic WallowError.fieldErrors split -- see description point 2) and render it through `<form.FormError />`'s underlying testid contract manually, OR pass `serverError` explicitly into `<form.AppForm serverError={error}>` if useAppForm's automatic wiring can be overridden per-call (check Wallow-ov6w.2.3's AppForm-defaulting behavior -- it defaults FROM `form.wallow` only when the AppForm prop is omitted, so passing an explicit `serverError` prop should still let this form manage its own banner text independently of the hook's built-in mutation-error path).
- Preserve `resetFailureMessage(cause)` (the HTTP-400-means-invalid_token structural narrowing) verbatim as a helper function.
- Preserve the link-validity guard and the mismatch guard as the first two things the submit handler does, before calling the mutation, exactly matching current control flow and messages.

Fields:
```tsx
<form.AppField name="newPassword">
  {(f) => <f.PasswordField label="New password" testId="reset-password-new-password" />}
</form.AppField>
<form.AppField name="confirmPassword">
  {(f) => <f.PasswordField label="Confirm new password" testId="reset-password-confirm" />}

This matches how every packages/forms spec builds a form. .3.2 MUST use the same import-the-shell form. Only the FIELD render prop is off the instance: <form.AppField name="email">{(field) => <field.TextField .../>}</form.AppField>.
2. pending={form.wallow.pending} is NOT passed. AppForm already defaults resolvedPending off form.wallow.pending, so passing it is redundant. Same for serverError. Omitted per YAGNI.

TESTID DERIVATION -- ZERO OVERRIDES NEEDED, confirmed at runtime not just by reading test-id.ts. testIdPrefix="forgot-password" alone produces forgot-password-form, -email, -email-error, -submit. No testId prop appears anywhere in the migrated file. forgot-password-success stays a hand-written div outside the shell, as specified.

THE TRIM: values.email.trim() IS in the submit callback, exactly as the red report demanded. The schema .trim() only makes "   " fail min(1); it does not trim what onSubmit receives. Both the whitespace-only oracle case and the padded-input guard pass.

NO FormError IS RENDERED. Belt and suspenders as the scout said: the try/catch swallows every rejection so form.wallow.serverError stays null forever anyway.

GOTCHA THAT DID BITE (the red reports "possible vitest browser gotcha", now confirmed and fixed): the first run after the migration printed "dependency optimized: zod" followed by "[vitest] Vite unexpectedly reloaded a test". @bc-solutions-coder/forms itself pre-bundled fine; it is ZOD, imported by the app-level schema module, that the scanner misses on the first pass. Fixed by apps/wallow-auth/vitest.config.ts passing extraBrowserOptimizeDeps: ["zod"] to createVitestProjects (never by touching the shared preset). No Base UI subpath needed adding -- wallow-auth already renders ui Field/Input/Button elsewhere so the scanner finds them. .3.2 inherits this fix and needs no further optimizeDeps work.

FOR .3.2 (ResetPasswordForm) -- REUSE THIS:
- Deps and the vitest zod entry are DONE. Do not re-add either.
- Copy this files import line and the <AppForm form={form} testIdPrefix=...> shape verbatim.
- The confirmation/submitted swap pattern generalises: keep screen-level useState in the PARENT and give the form component a plain callback prop (here onSubmitted), wired as useAppForms onSuccess. onSuccess is typed (data: TData) => void, so a bare () => void is assignable -- onSuccess: onSubmitted needs no wrapper.

ISSUES / JUDGEMENT CALLS TO REVIEW:
1. VERTICAL RHYTHM CHANGED 4 -> 5. The old hand-rolled form carried className="space-y-4"; AppForms default rhythm is space-y-5 and no className override was passed, which is the point of the shared shell. Cosmetic, one gap, no test observes it. Flagging in case the epic wants space-y-4 preserved instead -- one prop if so.
2. Nothing else. No test weakened, no testid changed, no scope crossed (only apps/wallow-auth touched; packages/forms, packages/ui and apps/wallow-web untouched).
3. Nothing committed -- coordinator owns the commit.
VERIFY: [✓] ForgotPasswordForm.test.tsx (oracle) unmodified — confirmed via git status/diff, only new .forms.test.tsx is untracked; ran it standalone: 18/18 pass (--project=browser ForgotPasswordForm), and full app suite 674/674 pass (32 files). [✓] values.email.trim() survives explicitly in onSubmit (ForgotPasswordForm.tsx:107: `body: { email: values.email.trim() }`) — confirmed NOT relying on zod .trim() alone; guarded by forms-test 'trims the address before it reaches the endpoint', which passes. [✓] E2E: backend was live (localhost:5001/health=200), independently re-ran forgot-password.spec.ts + routes.spec.ts myself (not trusting the report) = 19/19 pass, including both anti-enumeration backend cases. [✓] typecheck clean (wallow-auth AND packages/forms). [✓] oxlint apps/wallow-auth --deny-warnings clean, oxfmt --check clean on all 3 changed/new files. [✓] No jsdom/happy-dom, no vi.mock of @bc-solutions-coder/ui, no stub assertions (grepped forgot-password/ dir, zero hits). [✓] pnpm-lock.yaml diff is purely additive (+6 lines, 2 importer blocks for wallow-auth only) — scope respected, no wallow-web files touched by this task (the untracked CreateOrganizationForm.forms.test.tsx belongs to the parallel lane, out of scope, ignored per instructions).

JUDGEMENT CALL — space-y-4 -> space-y-5: ACCEPTABLE, not a regression to correct. Reasoning: (1) AppForm's DEFAULT_RHYTHM=space-y-5 is a deliberate default of the shared shell (app-form.tsx:56), with an explicit className escape hatch designed for exactly the case where a caller wants to opt out — the implementer chose NOT to use it, which is the correct default choice, not an oversight. (2) No test or E2E spec anywhere asserts spacing/className, confirmed by reading both test files. (3) The whole point of migrating onto a shared forms package is visual/behavioural standardization across forms; special-casing one form back to space-y-4 while every other migrated form uses the shell default would undermine that goal and create an unexplained one-off inconsistency. (4) The delta is cosmetic and minor (16px vs 20px gap). Recommend leaving as-is; if the epic later wants uniform space-y-4 across the app, that should be a deliberate change to DEFAULT_RHYTHM in packages/forms, not a per-form className override.

ISSUE 1 (optimizeDeps.include entries do not resolve from packages/forms). Only the baseline's react/* + react-dom/client and this package's own @tanstack/react-form, @tanstack/react-query, zod resolve.

ROOT CAUSE: pnpm's strict node_modules. A package resolves only what it DECLARES. packages/forms/package.json declares neither @base-ui/react, class-variance-authority nor tailwind-merge (they arrive transitively through @bc-solutions-coder/ui) nor vitest-browser-react (transitive through @bc-solutions-coder/testing, and it is in the SHARED baseline from browserOptimizeDepsBaseline, not in this package's extras). title: 5.2: COOKIE_PASSWORD rotation via a keyed secret map (L3)
description: Rotating the single COOKIE_PASSWORD secret today mass-invalidates (401s) every existing session at once, because there is no way to accept old sealed cookies while sealing new ones under a fresh secret. iron-webcrypto's seal()/unseal() functions actually accept a keyed password MAP (not just a bare string), which this SDK does not yet use.
design: Files: packages/sdk/src/server/config.ts, packages/sdk/src/server/session.ts (+ their test files), docs/integrations/bff-pattern.md. Add support for an optional COOKIE_PASSWORDS environment variable: a JSON object like {"v2": "<32+ chars>", "v1": "<32+ chars>"} where the newest key ID seals new sessions and ALL key IDs remain valid for unsealing existing sessions (this is exactly how iron-webcrypto's map form works -- verify against the installed version's API rather than assuming). The existing single COOKIE_PASSWORD variable must keep working unchanged by being wrapped internally as {"1": <value>}. Also apply the same keyed-password path to packages/sdk/src/server/txstate.ts (the OIDC transaction-state cookie), which must not be left on the old single-secret path while sessions rotate. TDD: seal a cookie under password v1 only; then unseal it successfully using a config with BOTH {v2, v1} present; then confirm any NEW seal produced by that same config uses v2. Document the rotation procedure (add v2 alongside v1, deploy, wait for all v1-sealed sessions to expire, then remove v1) in docs/integrations/bff-pattern.md.
acceptance_criteria: New session.test.ts and config.test.ts cases (seal-under-v1/unseal-under-map, new-seals-use-newest-key) pass; txstate.ts uses the same keyed-password resolution as session.ts; the plain single-COOKIE_PASSWORD path is unaffected (regression-tested); docs/integrations/bff-pattern.md documents the rotation procedure; commit message 'feat(sdk): support cookie-password rotation via COOKIE_PASSWORDS'.
notes:
RED: 23 tests failing across 3 spec files. Scaffolded type surface only in config.ts/session.ts/txstate.ts — NO rotation logic. Did NOT touch handlers.ts or store/* (owned by 5.1/5.3 right now); see SEQUENCING below.

FILES TOUCHED (all mine per the bead; concurrency-safe):
- packages/sdk/src/server/config.ts (types + placeholder), config.test.ts (12 new cases)
- packages/sdk/src/server/session.ts (widened signatures + stub resolvers), session.test.ts (10 new cases)
- packages/sdk/src/server/txstate.ts (same), txstate.test.ts (4 new cases + a makeTx fixture)

=== TWO EMPIRICAL FINDINGS THAT CHANGE THE DESIGN (probed against the installed iron-webcrypto 1.2.1, then deleted the probe) ===

(1) THE BEAD'S DESIGN AS WRITTEN WOULD MASS-INVALIDATE EVERY LIVE SESSION — the exact bug it exists to prevent. The bead says wrap the single COOKIE_PASSWORD internally as {"1": password}. That BREAKS every cookie sealed by the current build. iron seals a bare-string password with an EMPTY id (blob field parts[1] === ""), and unseal() normalizes an empty id to the literal string 'default' before looking it up in the map (dist/index.js:274 'passwordId = passwordId || "default"'). So:
  - legacy blob + map {"1": pw}      => THROWS 'Cannot find password: default'
  - legacy blob + map {default: pw}   => OK
  - legacy blob + bare string pw      => OK (a string password ignores the id entirely)
  - blob sealed {id:'v1'} + bare string pw1 => OK  (rollback to the previous build is safe)
  - blob sealed {id:'v1'} + map {v2,v1} => OK ; + map {v2} only => THROWS 'Cannot find password: v1'
THEREFORE the wrapping key ID MUST be exactly 'default'. I exported 'DEFAULT_COOKIE_KEY_ID = "default"' from config.ts with the reasoning in its doc comment, and there is a dedicated test pinning the value so nobody 'tidies' it to '1' or 'v1' later. Two upgrade/rollback tests (session + txstate: 'unseals a cookie sealed by the OLD bare-string API using the wrapped set', 'unseals a cookie sealed under the wrapped set with the bare string again') are the real regression guards for this.

(2) KEY IDS MUST MATCH /^\w+$/ OR IRON REFUSES TO SEAL. seal() throws 'Invalid password id' (dist/index.js:228) for e.g. 'v-2' or '2026-07'. Unvalidated, that is a 500 in the login callback rather than a boot failure — the identical failure mode 4.1 just fixed for the password LENGTH. config.test.ts has 'rejects a key ID iron would refuse to seal with' for this. Validate it at load, aggregated like everything else.

=== DESIGN DECISION I HAD TO MAKE (flag if you disagree) ===
BffConfig.cookiePasswords is OPTIONAL ('cookiePasswords?: CookiePasswordSet'), not required. Two reasons: (a) BffConfig is PUBLIC API exported from the SDK server entry — a required new field is a breaking change for any fork that hand-builds a config, and this ships as 'feat(sdk)' (minor), not feat!; (b) five existing test files build a BffConfig via a makeConfig factory (handlers.test.ts:100, proxy.test.ts:165, bff-server.test.ts:93, oidc.test.ts:83, auth-logout.contract.test.ts:181) and a required field would break all of them, two of which 5.1/5.3 are editing right now. loadBffConfigFromEnv ALWAYS populates it, so call sites read 'config.cookiePasswords ?? config.cookiePassword' — that expression is exactly a CookieSecret, which is why the union type is shaped that way. Full-package tsc --noEmit: 0 errors, so nothing downstream broke.

=== TYPE SURFACE SCAFFOLDED (config.ts) ===
export interface CookiePasswordSet { activeKeyId: string; keys: Record<string, string> }
export type CookieSecret = string | CookiePasswordSet
export const DEFAULT_COOKIE_KEY_ID: string = 'default'
BffConfig gains optional 'cookiePasswords?: CookiePasswordSet'; cookiePassword keeps its exact shape and meaning (the ACTIVE secret).
sealSession/unsealSession/sealTx/unsealTx now take 'password: CookieSecret' instead of 'string' (widening — every existing caller still compiles).

=== WHERE THE GREEN PHASE PLUGS IN ===
- config.ts return object has a structural placeholder 'cookiePasswords: { activeKeyId: "", keys: {} }' with a comment — replace it with real resolution.
- session.ts and txstate.ts each have private 'sealPassword(secret)' / 'unsealPassword(secret)' stubs that pass a string straight through and THROW 'Keyed cookie passwords are not implemented yet' for the keyed branch. seal must return { id: activeKeyId, secret: keys[activeKeyId] }; unseal must return the WHOLE keys map (iron picks the entry via the embedded id — do NOT loop over keys manually). The two stubs are duplicated on purpose; their doc comments say the green phase should extract ONE shared helper (a small module both import — session.ts and txstate.ts have no import relationship today, so a new file is cleanest).

=== SEQUENCING (why some rotation call sites are untouched) ===
Per the coordinator, 5.1 owns handlers.ts and 5.3 owns store/*, so I left every call site on config.cookiePassword — still correct, just not rotation-aware. AFTER 5.1 and 5.3 land, the green phase must switch these 6 sites to 'config.cookiePasswords ?? config.cookiePassword': bff-server.ts:95 and :110, proxy.ts:726, handlers.ts:405 (default CookieSessionStore), :422 (sealTx in login), :449 (unsealTx in callback). store/cookie.ts and store/valkey.ts also need their 'password' field widened to CookieSecret to accept it (store/redis-adapter.ts:18 mentions cookiePassword in a doc comment only). Until those land, rotation covers session.ts/txstate.ts only.

=== TEST INVENTORY ===
config.test.ts, describe 'loadBffConfigFromEnv — COOKIE_PASSWORDS rotation' (12 cases, 10 failing): wraps single password into a one-key set; keys it by 'default' (PASSES — pins the exported constant); leaves cookiePassword untouched (PASSES — regression guard); parses COOKIE_PASSWORDS into every key; FIRST JSON key is active (newest-first, matching the bead's {v2,v1} example); cookiePassword becomes the ACTIVE secret; COOKIE_PASSWORDS alone is sufficient without a redundant COOKIE_PASSWORD; rejects non-JSON; rejects JSON that is not an object (array and bare string); rejects {}; applies the 32-char minimum per key naming the offending key id; rejects a non-\w key id; aggregates into the SAME 'Invalid BFF environment configuration' error as a missing OIDC_ISSUER; an EMPTY COOKIE_PASSWORDS falls back to the single-password path.
session.test.ts, describe 'sealSession / unsealSession — keyed password rotation' (10 cases, 9 failing): the three rotation states are named as fixtures ONLY_V1 / V2_THEN_V1 / ONLY_V2. Cases: unseal a v1-sealed cookie under {v2,v1} (the bead's core criterion); new seals use the ACTIVE key (asserted behaviourally — readable by ONLY_V2, null under ONLY_V1); the active key id is stamped into the blob (asserts sealed.split('*')[1] === 'v2' — the one test that touches iron's wire format, commented as such); null once the sealing key is dropped; null when a key id matches but the secret does not; the two legacy/rollback cases from finding (1); plain-string round-trip unchanged (PASSES — regression guard); ttl honoured with a keyed set exactly as with a string.
txstate.test.ts, describe 'sealTx / unsealTx — keyed password rotation' (4 cases, 3 failing): same v1-under-{v2,v1} round-trip, active-key sealing, the legacy bare-string upgrade case, and a plain-string regression guard (PASSES). Rationale in the describe comment: the tx cookie is sealed at the authorize redirect and unsealed at the callback seconds later, so leaving it on the single-secret path aborts every in-flight login the moment a rotation deploys.

4 of the 27 new cases pass by design (marked PASSES above): 3 are single-password regression guards that MUST stay green, 1 pins the exported DEFAULT_COOKIE_KEY_ID constant. Not a sign the specs did not run.

title: 5.3: In-process refresh mutex for the cookie session store (L5)
description: packages/sdk/src/server/store/cookie.ts's withRefreshLock is currently a no-op passthrough, so two concurrent requests in the SAME Node process (e.g. two browser tabs both triggering a token refresh at once) can both attempt to spend the same one-time OIDC refresh token, and one of the two refreshes fails or corrupts session state.
design: Files: packages/sdk/src/server/store/cookie.ts + its test file. TDD: two concurrent calls to withRefreshLock(sessionId, fn) for the SAME session id must run fn sequentially -- the second call's fn must only start after the first's fn has settled, and the second caller must observe the first call's result (not re-run the refresh itself); calls for DIFFERENT session ids must run fully concurrently with no serialization between them. Implement a per-sessionId promise-chain mutex: a Map<sessionId, Promise> that chains each new call onto the pending promise for that id and deletes the map entry once the chain settles (so the map does not grow unbounded). Note in a comment (and in the SDK docs if relevant) that this mutex only protects a SINGLE process -- multi-instance deployments still need the Valkey-backed session store for cross-process refresh safety; that tradeoff is unchanged by this task.
acceptance_criteria: New cookie.ts store test covers both the same-session-serializes and different-sessions-run-concurrently cases and passes; pnpm --filter @bc-solutions-coder/sdk exec vitest run src/server/store/cookie.test.ts passes; commit message 'fix(sdk): serialize same-session refreshes in the cookie store'.
notes:
RED (TDD red phase complete).

FILES: packages/sdk/src/server/store/cookie.test.ts (ONLY file touched — no changes to cookie.ts; no scaffolding was needed because CookieSessionStore.withRefreshLock already exists with the right signature).

TEST COUNT: 4 new tests in a new describe block 'CookieSessionStore — in-process refresh mutex'. 2 FAIL, 2 pass as regression guards. Scoped run of src/server/store/cookie.test.ts: 2 failed | 9 passed (11). The 5 pre-existing cookie tests (including 'withRefreshLock runs fn directly and returns its value' at the old line 65) all still pass unchanged.

*** DECISION THE GREEN IMPLEMENTER MUST READ FIRST — the bead DESIGN and the scout note contradict themselves on the core semantics. ***
The DESIGN says BOTH (a) 'the second call fn must only start after the first fn has settled' [= a plain serializing mutex, each caller runs its own fn] AND (b) 'the second caller must observe the first call result (not re-run the refresh itself)' [= single-flight coalescing, the second fn never runs]. The scout note has the same split: its prose says 'the SECOND caller awaits and returns the FIRST caller actual fn() result (not undefined, not a re-run)' but its code snippet 'pending.then(fn, fn)' implements (a), under which the second caller DOES re-run and returns its OWN result.

I resolved this to (b) COALESCING, and the tests encode that. Reason: (a) does not fix the bug in the bead DESCRIPTION. refreshUnderLock (proxy.ts:229-254) captures 'const refreshToken = session.refreshToken' BEFORE calling withRefreshLock, so a second callback that merely runs LATER still presents the one-time refresh token the first callback just spent — the double-spend the bead exists to prevent survives a pure serializing mutex. Only coalescing makes exactly one refresh happen. It is also the cookie-store analogue of valkey's 'lock held -> re-read the peer write': the cookie IS the state, so there is nothing to re-read and the in-flight promise is the only handle on the peer result. If the coordinator/verifier disagrees, this is the one decision to overturn BEFORE green starts — flipping it later means rewriting 2 of the 4 tests.

REQUIRED IMPLEMENTATION SHAPE (single-flight, not the scout chain snippet):
  private readonly refreshLocks = new Map<string, Promise<unknown>>();
  withRefreshLock<T>(ref, fn): Promise<T | undefined> {
    const inFlight = this.refreshLocks.get(ref);
    if (inFlight !== undefined) { return inFlight as Promise<T>; }   // JOIN — do NOT call fn
    const run = fn();
    this.refreshLocks.set(ref, run);
    // cleanup must not swallow the rejection nor create an unhandled one
    const clear = () => { if (this.refreshLocks.get(ref) === run) { this.refreshLocks.delete(ref); } };
    run.then(clear, clear);
    return run;
  }
(Use .then(clear, clear) or .finally() — but if you use .finally() do not return the derived promise to callers, return 'run', so both joined callers share one promise and neither sees an unhandled rejection.)

NEW TESTS:
 1. 'coalesces concurrent locks for the same ref: the callback runs once and both callers get its result' — FAILS today: expected secondRuns 0, received 1 (cookie.test.ts:158). Gates the first callback open, issues a second lock on the same ref, drains microtasks, asserts the second callback never ran, then asserts BOTH callers resolve to 'first-result' and firstRuns===1.
 2. 'runs a fresh callback for a lock taken after the previous one settled' — PASSES today. Regression guard for the Map cleanup: a leaked entry would make this return 'first' twice, so map-unboundedness is covered behaviourally rather than by reaching into the private Map.
 3. 'propagates a rejected callback to every joined caller and leaves the ref usable' — FAILS today: 'promise resolved second-result instead of rejecting' (cookie.test.ts:208). Asserts both callers reject with the SAME Error, the joined callback never ran, and a subsequent lock on that ref resolves normally (a failed refresh releases the lock, it does not poison the ref).
 4. 'does not serialize across different refs' — PASSES today. Regression guard: asserts ref-session-b completes while ref-session-a is still held, pinned by an explicit order array ['a-start','b-start'] then ['a-start','b-start','a-end'] — so a wrongly-global lock fails the ORDER assertion, it does not merely hang.

TEST MECHANICS: deterministic promise gates only (local deferred<T>() helper + flushMicrotasks() = two awaited Promise.resolve()). No fake timers, no real timers, no sleeps — per the task instruction.

DEFECT 1 — OpenIddict endpoints under PathBase. THE BEAD'S STATED ROOT CAUSE WAS WRONG.
There is no IStartupFilter. OpenIddict.Server.AspNetCore 7.6.0 contains ZERO IStartupFilter
references and no middleware type (types are Builder/Configuration/Constants/Defaults/
Extensions/Feature/Handler/HandlerFilters/Handlers/Options). Its request processing runs as
OpenIddictServerAspNetCoreHandler, an IAuthenticationRequestHandler inside
AuthenticationMiddleware — i.e. app.UseAuthentication(), Program.cs:519, which is 162 lines
AFTER app.UsePathBase() at Program.cs:357. UsePathBase demonstrably DID run: the failing
request reached AuthorizationController (whose route is "connect/authorize", no leading
slash, so it only matches the REBASED path) and 500'd there rather than 404ing.

ACTUAL ROOT CAUSE: root-relative endpoint URIs. OpenIddict resolves a relative endpoint URI
against the request's base URI (scheme+host+PathBase, WITH a trailing slash). A leading slash
makes the value an absolute-path reference, which per RFC 3986 replaces the base's entire path
and so discards the PathBase. We configured "/connect/authorize" etc.; OpenIddict's OWN
built-in defaults are relative — verified by extracting the UTF-16 string literals from
OpenIddict.Server.dll 7.6.0: '.well-known/openid-configuration', '.well-known/jwks' (no
leading slash). That asymmetry is exactly why the sweep saw jwks_uri keep the /api prefix
while authorization/token/end_session/userinfo lost it, and why discovery itself was reachable
at /api/... while /api/connect/authorize was not. One mechanism explains every symptom.

  NO REGRESSION at the origin root (PathBase unset): discovery unprefixed as before, authorize

WHY THE TEST GAP EXISTED, AND HOW IT IS CLOSED
The verifier's diagnosis was right. The old buildAuthorizeUrl tests built their mock Configuration with authorization_endpoint == doc.authorization_endpoint, so the doc string and the Configuration could never disagree and the disconnect was unobservable. The new fixture is the opposite by construction: discover() is driven through a REAL split horizon (metadataUrl on an internal container host, issuer http://localhost/api), and the openid-client mock is a buildLikeOpenIdClient() helper that faithfully replicates the library's actual behaviour — resolve the endpoint from the Configuration's RAW metadata, then append the caller's params. So the mock returns an internal-host URL exactly as production did, and the assertion is on the wrapper's output.

THE FIX
pinToBrowserEndpoint relocates the openid-client-built URL onto the doc's browser-facing endpoint, then both browser-bound builders route through it: buildAuthorizeUrl returns pinToBrowserEndpoint(url, doc.authorization_endpoint); the advertised-end_session branch of buildLogoutUrl returns pinToBrowserEndpoint(buildEndSessionUrl(...), doc.end_session_endpoint). The no-end_session fallback still uses rebaseToIssuer directly and is unchanged.

DESIGN CHOICES, and why the alternative was rejected
• Chose to pin the BUILT URL rather than rebase the Configuration's serverMetadata (the verifier offered both). Rebasing the Configuration would have been actively WRONG: the same Configuration backs authorizationCodeGrant, refreshTokenGrant and fetchUserInfo, which are BACKCHANNEL calls that must keep hitting the internal host directly instead of hairpinning out through the public proxy. Mutating it would have broken the token exchange to fix the redirect. The doc's endpoint strings already encode precisely the browser-facing/backchannel split that discover() decided, so they are the right source of truth. This is recorded in the helper's doc comment so the next reader does not 'simplify' it back.
• Only origin + path are replaced; built.search is left byte-for-byte as openid-client encoded it. Re-serialising through URLSearchParams would have risked altering openid-client's exact param encoding (e.g. space as '+' vs '%20') on PKCE/state/nonce values that are validated on the callback. The endpoint's own query (?tenant=acme) still survives because openid-client preserves it when building — which the new test pins.
• Origin components are assigned individually WITH an explicit url.port = target.port. This is the same port-leak trap 2.1 hit: assigning URL.host a host string carrying no port leaves the previous port in place, so a bare host assignment would have produced http://localhost:8080/... The test asserts url.port === '' specifically, so a regression here fails loudly rather than only in a live smoke.
• Consistent with 2.1: rebaseToIssuer is untouched and still owns the origin+path-prefix arithmetic; this change only makes its output actually reach the user agent.

ran against the DEV API instead of the isolated test stack's API on :5050.

{"succeeded":true} and the mail landed in test Mailpit within ~1s.

title: Phase 5 -- Lows (L1, L2, L3, L5, L6) + final verification
description: Final hardening pass covering the audit's remaining low-severity findings (idempotent anonymous logout, no-store caching header, cookie-password rotation, concurrent-refresh race in the cookie session store), followed by a full-stack verification sweep that exercises every change from all five phases together, including the path-topology smoke test that is the actual point of Phase 2.
design: Source: docs/plans/2026-07-29/0948-bff-csrf-and-topology-remediation.md Phase 5. Tasks 5.1-5.3 are independent SDK fixes; Task 5.4 is the final verification sweep and depends on all of them (plus every prior phase) being complete.
acceptance_criteria: pnpm check green; ./scripts/run-tests.sh green; ./scripts/e2e.sh green; the production-topology Docker Compose smoke (Caddy ingress, path-based routing) completes a full login -> dashboard -> mutation -> logout loop at http://localhost; work is pushed (git pull --rebase && bd dolt push && git push) with git status showing up to date with origin.
notes:
SCOUT — Phase 4 already landed (verified in current tree, do not re-do): config.ts's MIN_COOKIE_PASSWORD_LENGTH=32 check (lines 63-69, 150-157) is DONE — 4.1 complete. proxy.ts's client-IP forwarding, the 3 start.ts X-Forwarded-Proto fixes, and .4.4's docs (including L6/response_mode in bff-pattern.md's Security Notes) should already be in bff-pattern.md — 5.4's verification sweep should find L6 already documented there, NOT something Phase 5 needs to add (Phase 5's title lists L6 in parens only for grouping/reference against the source audit; the actual child tasks 5.1-5.4 do NOT include an L6 code task).

5.1 (packages/sdk/src/server/handlers.ts): logout handler is at lines 514-550. Current bug: 'if (!csrfTokenMatches(session?.csrfToken, presented))' at line 531 runs UNCONDITIONALLY, and csrfTokenMatches(undefined, presented) always returns false (proxy.ts:52-60, guards expected/presented both non-empty) — so session===null (anonymous) always 403s today, same as a real CSRF mismatch. FIX: add an early branch 'if (session === null) { clear cookies via clearSession(headers, request, config); return 204 (or redirect) }' BEFORE the csrfTokenMatches check, so only a NULL session skips CSRF — a session that EXISTS but has an undefined/empty csrfToken must still hit the existing csrfTokenMatches path and get 403 (fail-secure, per the task's own acceptance criteria). IMPORTANT NUANCE: this deliberately does NOT fix the OTHER half of audit finding L1 (a session minted without csrfToken can never logout via UI, permanent 403) — the task's acceptance criteria explicitly keep that path rejected; don't 'fix' it thinking it's in scope. clearSession(headers, request, config) is defined at handlers.ts:339 (private, already in scope); readSessionRef at handlers.ts:238 (exported). No discover()/buildLogoutUrl call needed for the anonymous path (those need an idToken/doc the anonymous case has none of) — the authenticated path (lines 541-549: store.destroy(ref) then discover+buildLogoutUrl redirect) stays unchanged and must be regression-tested. For the no-store header: 'user' handler at handlers.ts:502-512 does 'return Response.json(body);' at line 511 — change to 'Response.json(body, { headers: { "cache-control": "no-store" } })'. Test file packages/sdk/src/server/handlers.test.ts (already has session-store spy pattern around line 580-597 using a delegate + withRefreshLock wrapper — good template for the new session-store fixture if one test needs a null-session case). Run: pnpm --filter @bc-solutions-coder/sdk exec vitest run src/server/handlers.test.ts.

5.2 (COOKIE_PASSWORD rotation): iron-webcrypto 1.2.1's actual API (verified in node_modules/.pnpm/iron-webcrypto@1.2.1/.../index.d.ts) is the key unlock: seal()'s password param type is 'RawPassword = Password | password.Secret | password.Specific' where 'password.Secret = { id?: string; secret: Password }' — sealing with a specific key ID means passing '{ id: "v2", secret: passwords["v2"] }', which iron embeds the id INSIDE the sealed blob. unseal()'s password param is 'Password | password.Hash' where 'password.Hash = Record<string, Password|Secret|Specific>' — so unsealing must be handed the WHOLE map (e.g. '{ v2: "...", v1: "..." }'), and iron reads the embedded id to pick the right entry automatically — the caller does NOT need to try each key manually. This is the exact mechanism the task's DESIGN references ('verify against the installed version's API rather than assuming') — confirmed, use id+secret for seal, full Hash for unseal. Call sites needing the same treatment (currently all pass a single 'password: string' or 'config.cookiePassword' directly — grep confirmed, no other sites): session.ts sealSession/unsealSession (lines 66-93, password param currently typed 'string'), txstate.ts sealTx/unsealTx (lines 34,45, same), store/cookie.ts (CookieSessionStore.password field + read/write at lines ~38-52), store/valkey.ts (ValkeySessionStore also seals/unseals its ref — 'seal(webCrypto, id, this.password, defaults)' around line 108, check its unseal counterpart too — same webcrypto/iron-webcrypto import). Config-level call sites of 'config.cookiePassword' to update (grep-confirmed, exhaustive): bff-server.ts:95 (ValkeySessionStore ctor) and :110 (CookieSessionStore ctor) inside selectStore(); handlers.ts:402 (createBffHandlers' default CookieSessionStore), :419 (sealTx call in login handler), :446 (unsealTx call in callback handler); proxy.ts:726 (createApiProxy's default CookieSessionStore). Plan: add BffConfig.cookiePasswords (a resolved key->secret map, newest-first or with an explicit 'activeKeyId'), built in config.ts from an optional COOKIE_PASSWORDS env var (JSON object) OR wrapping the existing single COOKIE_PASSWORD as {"1": password} when COOKIE_PASSWORDS is unset — keep 'cookiePassword: string' on BffConfig too (still the ACTIVE/newest secret value, unchanged shape) so none of the 6 call sites above need to change their PARAMETER passing if the seal/unseal helper functions internally accept either a bare string (back-compat, wraps as single-entry) or a map+activeId. Docs: docs/integrations/bff-pattern.md — Security Notes section (~line 257) already has 'Session Cookie Flags' (267) and 'State Parameter' (278) subsections; add the rotation procedure as a new subsection there (add v2 alongside v1 via COOKIE_PASSWORDS, deploy, wait out old sessions' TTL, then drop v1). Test files: session.test.ts, config.test.ts, txstate.test.ts (check if it exists — grep 'ls packages/sdk/src/server/txstate.test.ts' before assuming), store/cookie.test.ts. Run each via pnpm --filter @bc-solutions-coder/sdk exec vitest run <path>.

5.3 (in-process refresh mutex, packages/sdk/src/server/store/cookie.ts): current CookieSessionStore.withRefreshLock (lines ~58-60 per the class body) is 'withRefreshLock<T>(_ref, fn) { return fn(); }' — a true no-op, ref param unused. IMPORTANT: cookie.ts's 'ref' argument is NOT a stable sessionId — for THIS store the ref IS the sealed cookie string itself (see write(): returns sealSession(...) as the ref), so two concurrent requests for the same browser session present the IDENTICAL ref string (same sealed cookie) until one of them rewrites it — keying a Map<string, Promise> by the literal 'ref' argument is therefore correct and sufficient, no extra plumbing needed to derive a sessionId. Reference exemplar with DIFFERENT (do-not-copy) semantics: store/valkey.ts's real ValkeySessionStore.withRefreshLock (lines 119-137) uses a Redis SET NX lock and returns undefined when the lock is held by a peer — callers (proxy.ts's refreshUnderLock, ~line 229-267) handle that undefined by RE-READING the session from the store to adopt the peer's write. Cookie store has NO persisted state to re-read (the cookie IS the state), so per the task's own acceptance criteria the fix must NOT mimic valkey's 'return undefined, caller re-reads' pattern — instead literally CHAIN: 'const pending = map.get(ref) ?? Promise.resolve(); const next = pending.then(fn, fn); map.set(ref, next); next.finally(() => { if (map.get(ref) === next) map.delete(ref); }); return next;' so the SECOND caller awaits and returns the FIRST caller's actual fn() result (not undefined, not a re-run). Existing test 'withRefreshLock runs fn directly and returns its value' (cookie.test.ts:65-76) must keep passing unchanged (single-call case). store/valkey.test.ts:117-156 ('withRefreshLock serializes concurrent refreshes...') is the closest existing TEST STRUCTURE template to pattern-match for the new same-session/different-session concurrent test cases, even though the underlying locking mechanism differs. Run: pnpm --filter @bc-solutions-coder/sdk exec vitest run src/server/store/cookie.test.ts.

5.4 (verification sweep, no code): DESIGN section in the bead itself already lists the 4 ordered steps verbatim (pnpm check; ./scripts/run-tests.sh; ./scripts/e2e.sh; the Caddy path-topology smoke via docker-compose.production.yml --env-file docker/.env.production with AUTH_BASE_PATH=/auth, hex secrets per 2.3, API_PUBLIC_URL/AUTH_PUBLIC_URL/WEB_PUBLIC_URL=http://localhost/*, COOKIE_SECURE=false for this http-only local smoke). docker/caddy/Caddyfile.example and the production compose's caddy service already exist from Wallow-vufu.2.3 (see that bead's CLOSE notes) — 5.4 should reuse them, not create new ones. title: 5.1: Idempotent anonymous logout + no-store on /bff/user (L1, L2)
description: Today POST /bff/logout with no existing session returns a 403 (the CSRF check fails because there is no session to hold a csrfToken), which surfaces to the user as a spurious 'Logout failed' even though an anonymous logout has nothing to protect. Separately, GET /bff/user returns identity claims and the CSRF token in its body but without a Cache-Control: no-store header, so an intermediary or the browser's own cache could retain sensitive session data.
design: Files: packages/sdk/src/server/handlers.ts + packages/sdk/src/server/handlers.test.ts. TDD -- three failing tests to add: (1) POST /bff/logout with NO session returns 204 (or an appropriate redirect) and clears session cookies, and must NOT be a 403 -- but the CSRF check must remain enforced whenever a session DOES exist, INCLUDING sessions that were minted without a csrfToken (those must stay fail-secure, i.e. still rejected, since a missing csrfToken should never be treated as 'no protection needed'); (2) authenticated logout with a valid session and matching CSRF token behaves exactly as before (regression guard); (3) GET /bff/user's 200 response carries a Cache-Control: no-store header.
acceptance_criteria: All three new/updated handlers.test.ts cases pass; pnpm --filter @bc-solutions-coder/sdk exec vitest run src/server/handlers.test.ts passes; commit message 'fix(sdk): idempotent anonymous logout and no-store on /bff/user'.
notes:
RED: 5 tests failing, confirmed for the right reason.

TEST FILE (the only file touched)
packages/sdk/src/server/handlers.test.ts — 9 new cases, 5 failing / 4 passing by design.
NO SCAFFOLD NEEDED: handlers.ts is UNTOUCHED. The fix is purely behavioural inside two existing handlers, so no new type or signature was required for the tests to compile.

FAILING (the spec for the green phase)
1. 'user handler > marks the identity response no-store' — expected '' to contain 'no-store'.
2. 'logout CSRF gate > answers an anonymous POST with 204 instead of 403' — expected 403 to be 204.
3. 'logout CSRF gate > clears the session and CSRF cookies on an anonymous POST' — expected undefined to be defined (no Set-Cookie at all today).
4. 'logout CSRF gate > answers 204 for an anonymous POST even when it carries a stale CSRF token' — expected 403 to be 204.
5. 'logout CSRF gate > treats an unreadable session cookie as anonymous rather than as a CSRF failure' — expected 403 to be 204.

PASSING BY DESIGN (guards that pin behaviour the fix must NOT change — they must still pass after green)
6/7. 'still rejects a POST for a session that exists but whose csrfToken is undefined' / '... is empty' (it.each) — 403 + CSRF_INVALID_CODE + destroys nothing + clears nothing. This is the fail-secure half the bead calls out explicitly: ONLY session===null may skip the gate.
8. 'leaves the authenticated logout redirect untouched' — 302, ref destroyed, /connect/logout, id_token_hint, session cookie cleared.
(Plus the pre-existing 405/CSRF-mismatch/crosstalk cases, all still green.)

DECISION: 204, NOT a redirect
The bead's DESIGN says '204 (or an appropriate redirect)'. I pinned 204 and VERIFIED the browser client already handles it with no change: packages/sdk/src/auth.ts endSession() (lines ~117-146) throws only when 'response.status >= HTTP_FIRST_ERROR', then does 'location.href = response.headers.get("location") ?? "/"'. So a 204 with no Location navigates to the app root — the correct anonymous-logout UX — and no SDK client change is in scope. A 302 would instead have sent an anonymous user to the IdP's end-session endpoint with no id_token_hint, which is a pointless round trip. If green wants a redirect anyway it must change tests 2/4/5, so treat 204 as decided.

GREEN PHASE
handlers.ts logout handler (lines 514-550): insert an early branch AFTER the readSession call and BEFORE the 'if (!csrfTokenMatches(...))' at line 531:
  if (session === null) { const headers = new Headers(); clearSession(headers, request, config); return new Response(null, { status: 204, headers }); }
Add a NO_CONTENT_STATUS = 204 const alongside the existing FOUND_STATUS/FORBIDDEN_STATUS block (handlers.ts:157-169) rather than a bare literal — that file has no naked status numbers.
Do NOT move or weaken the csrfTokenMatches call; a session that EXISTS with an undefined/empty csrfToken must keep 403ing (tests 6/7 enforce this, and csrfTokenMatches at proxy.ts:52-60 already returns false for both).
No discover()/buildLogoutUrl on the anonymous path — there is no idToken and no reason to contact the IdP.
handlers.ts user handler line 511: 'return Response.json(body);' -> 'return Response.json(body, { headers: { "cache-control": "no-store" } });'. Only the 200 is in scope; the 401 early-return at line 505 is untouched (no test asserts it either way).

WHY THE ANONYMOUS BRANCH MUST ALSO CLEAR COOKIES (test 3)
The common real-world trigger is a browser holding a cookie this server can no longer read — rotated COOKIE_PASSWORD, expired seal, stale build. readSession answers null, so the request looks anonymous, but the jar is still dirty. Returning 204 WITHOUT calling clearSession would leave the user in a loop where every logout succeeds and nothing changes. Test 5 pins the unreadable-cookie case specifically.

CONVENTIONS OBSERVED
- openid-client is mocked at the top of handlers.test.ts per the 'sdk-vitest-pattern-openid-client-must-be-mocked' memory; my tests reuse the existing makeLogout() fixture inside the 'logout CSRF gate' describe (it stubs discovery + a recording store), so no new mock was introduced.
- The CSRF companion cookie is referenced by its literal name 'wallow_bff-csrf' — csrfCookieName() is private to handlers.ts and every existing test uses the literal.
- Each test uses a UNIQUE issuer host, as makeConfig's doc comment requires (oidc.ts caches discovery per issuer at module scope).
- File is oxfmt-formatted and oxlint-clean.

COMMAND

Currently: 5 failed | 55 passed (60).
GREEN (TDD green phase complete).

SYMBOLS: no exported surface changed — no new/changed signatures, no barrel or dist API delta, no consumer updates needed. One new module-private const: NO_CONTENT_STATUS = 204, added to the existing status block (handlers.ts:157-172) beside BAD_REQUEST_STATUS/UNAUTHORIZED_STATUS/FORBIDDEN_STATUS rather than as a naked literal, per the file's convention.

TEST_STATUS: pass. src/server/handlers.test.ts = 60/60 passing (was 5 failed | 55 passed). Ran ONLY the scoped command per the concurrency instruction — no full suite, no build.

THE THREE EDITS
1. user handler (was handlers.ts:511): 'return Response.json(body);' -> 'return Response.json(body, { headers: { "cache-control": "no-store" } });'. The 401 early-return is untouched, as specified. Satisfies failing test 1.
2. logout handler: new early branch inserted AFTER readSession and BEFORE the csrfTokenMatches gate — 'if (session === null) { const headers = new Headers(); clearSession(headers, request, config); return new Response(null, { status: NO_CONTENT_STATUS, headers }); }'. clearSession already emits both wallow_bff and wallow_bff-csrf (plus any chunk cookies on the request), so test 3's two Set-Cookie assertions are covered with no new cookie code. No discover()/buildLogoutUrl/store.destroy on this path — destroyed stays [] as tests 2/4/5 assert. Satisfies failing tests 2, 3, 4, 5.
3. Consequential narrowing only: with the null case returned early, 'session?.csrfToken' at the gate and 'session?.idToken' at the redirect are no longer optional — both tightened to 'session.csrfToken' / 'session.idToken'. Same runtime values; this removes optional chains oxlint would otherwise flag as unnecessary. NOT a behaviour change.

FAIL-SECURE HALF PRESERVED (tests 6/7 still green)
The csrfTokenMatches call was NOT moved, weakened, or conditionalised. Only 'session === null' short-circuits; a session that EXISTS with an undefined or empty csrfToken still falls through to the same gate and still gets 403 + CSRF_INVALID_CODE, destroying nothing and clearing nothing. The other half of audit finding L1 (a csrfToken-less session can never log out via UI) is deliberately still unfixed, per the scout's explicit out-of-scope note.

204 DECISION HONOURED
Implemented 204 exactly as the red phase pinned it — no redirect, so tests 2/4/5 were not touched. auth.ts endSession()'s 'location.href = response.headers.get("location") ?? "/"' fallback handles the Location-less 204 by navigating to the app root; no client change in scope and none made.

title: 4.2: Client-IP forwarding through the BFF /api proxy (M6)
description: The reverse-proxy passthrough already has the plumbing for this (a CLIENT_IP_HEADER seam header, appended to X-Forwarded-For then stripped before forwarding -- packages/sdk/src/server/passthrough.ts:157-174) but the BFF's own session-owning proxy only forwards content-type/accept headers upstream (packages/sdk/src/server/proxy.ts:553), so every wallow-web user's mutation reaches the API with the SAME client IP and the API's rate limiter treats all wallow-web traffic as one client. This is the exact bug already fixed for wallow-auth's passthrough (see bd issue Wallow-tt5j) -- fix the BFF proxy the same way rather than duplicating logic.
design: Files: packages/sdk/src/server/proxy.ts (+ its test file), apps/wallow-web/src/routes/api/$.ts. TDD: write a failing proxy test first -- a request carrying 'x-wallow-client-ip: 1.2.3.4' must reach the upstream fetch with 'x-forwarded-for' ENDING in '1.2.3.4', the seam header (x-wallow-client-ip) stripped before forwarding, and (mirroring the passthrough's existing behavior) x-forwarded-proto / x-forwarded-host set from the inbound request URL ONLY when not already present. Implementation: extract the passthrough's existing header-forwarding logic into a shared 'applyForwardedHeaders' helper and call it from both proxy.ts and passthrough.ts rather than duplicating it. App side: in apps/wallow-web/src/routes/api/$.ts, stamp the inbound request.ip onto the CLIENT_IP_HEADER exactly as apps/wallow-auth/src/lib/api-passthrough.ts:53-62 already does -- MUTATE the request object, do not clone it (see that file's comment on why the srvx request class requires mutation).
acceptance_criteria: New proxy test (and any shared applyForwardedHeaders test) passes; pnpm --filter @bc-solutions-coder/sdk exec vitest run src/server/proxy.test.ts passes; commit message 'fix(sdk): forward the real client IP through the BFF api proxy'.

- packages/sdk/src/server/forwarded.ts (NEW): exports 'CLIENT_IP_HEADER: string = "x-wallow-client-ip"' and 'applyForwardedHeaders(headers: Headers, incoming: URL, forwardClientIp: boolean): void' with an empty body ('void headers; void incoming; void forwardClientIp;' + a TDD-scaffold comment). title: 4.3: Honor X-Forwarded-Proto for the SSR baseUrl (M7)
description: apps/wallow-web/src/start.ts (and the same derivation logic in apps/wallow-auth/src/start.ts, and apps/examples/minimal-app if it has an equivalent) construct the SDK's baseUrl for SSR requests directly from the request URL's protocol, ignoring any X-Forwarded-Proto header set by a terminating reverse proxy.
