4.1 COOKIE_PASSWORD length (packages/sdk/src/server/config.ts): loadBffConfigFromEnv (starts ~line 111) already uses a 'problems: string[]' aggregation array + a local 'require(key)' closure that pushes onto problems and returns ''. cookiePassword is read via require('COOKIE_PASSWORD') further down in the same function body (grep 'COOKIE_PASSWORD' to find the exact call site — read past line 120, the require() helper is defined at ~113). Pattern to mirror: add 'const MIN_COOKIE_PASSWORD_LENGTH = 32;' near the other consts (NO_PROBLEMS=0, MIN_SESSION_TTL_SECONDS=1 live right above the function, ~lines 60-65), then after the cookiePassword value is obtained, 'if (cookiePassword.length > 0 && cookiePassword.length < MIN_COOKIE_PASSWORD_LENGTH) problems.push(...)' — guard on length>0 so a MISSING password (already caught by require()) doesn't double-report. Final aggregated throw already exists at the end of loadBffConfigFromEnv with message 'Invalid BFF environment configuration' (grep that string) — just push onto problems, don't add a new throw. Test file: packages/sdk/src/server/config.test.ts (existing, follow its existing 'problems aggregation' test shape). Run: pnpm --filter @bc-solutions-coder/sdk exec vitest run src/server/config.test.ts. Related but NOT the same length concern: iron-webcrypto's actual seal() failure threshold — see memory iron-webcrypto-s-seal-unseal-used-by-packages for its ttl default gotcha (different issue, just context).

4.2 Client-IP forwarding (packages/sdk/src/server/proxy.ts + passthrough.ts): passthrough.ts already has the exact reusable logic — 'applyForwardedHeaders(headers, incoming, forwardClientIp)' at passthrough.ts:157-174, plus 'export const CLIENT_IP_HEADER = "x-wallow-client-ip"' at passthrough.ts:31. It sets x-forwarded-proto/host only if absent, and APPENDS (comma-join) the CLIENT_IP_HEADER value onto any existing x-forwarded-for, then deletes the seam header. Design wants this EXTRACTED to a shared helper called from both files rather than duplicated — since applyForwardedHeaders has zero passthrough-specific state (just needs Headers/URL/bool), it can likely move as-is to a new shared module (or stay in passthrough.ts and be imported into proxy.ts — passthrough.ts has no reverse import from proxy.ts today, check for cycles before choosing which file owns it). proxy.ts's own header-forwarding is separate/local: FORWARDED_REQUEST_HEADERS = ['content-type','accept'] at proxy.ts:553, used in a loop at proxy.ts:804-808 that builds 'forwardHeaders: Headers' (only copies those 2 named request headers + sets REQUEST_ID_HEADER at line 815) then calls forwardWithResilience with target/method/headers/body ~line 829. This is the exact spot to also call the extracted applyForwardedHeaders(forwardHeaders, new URL(request.url), true) before the fetch. proxy.ts's forwardWithResilience itself starts at line 334; 'const headers: Headers = new Headers(request.headers)' at line 388 is a DIFFERENT internal helper (retry path), not the header-build site — the one to touch is the ~804 block. Test file: packages/sdk/src/server/proxy.test.ts (existing). App side: apps/wallow-web/src/routes/api/$.ts just delegates to lib/bff.ts's handleApiRequest(request) (lazy-imported, Node-only) — need to find handleApiRequest's definition (likely in packages/sdk or apps/wallow-web/src/lib/bff.ts) and stamp request.ip onto CLIENT_IP_HEADER there the same way apps/wallow-auth/src/lib/api-passthrough.ts:53-77 does (MUTATE request.headers.set(CLIENT_IP_HEADER, clientIp) in place — a PeerRequest interface extends Request with 'readonly ip?: string' since srvx's Request subclass throws 'Cannot read private member #state' if cloned via new Request(request,{headers}); comment in that file explains why). Prior art: bd issue Wallow-tt5j (closed/archived) already solved this exact bug for wallow-auth's passthrough — read its DESIGN section for the trust-boundary discussion (API's UseForwardedHeaders at api/src/Wallow.Api/Program.cs:376-385 has KnownIPNetworks/KnownProxies both cleared, i.e. trusts X-Forwarded-For from ANY peer) if 4.2 needs to touch trust-boundary docs too (it doesn't per its own acceptance criteria, but useful background).

4.3 X-Forwarded-Proto for SSR baseUrl: THREE files have near-identical middleware, all following the same shape — a 'sdkMiddleware = createMiddleware().server(({ next, request }) => {...})' in each app's src/start.ts:
  - apps/wallow-web/src/start.ts: 'const requestOrigin: string = new URL(request.url).origin;' then 'baseUrl: `${requestOrigin}${API_MOUNT}`' (API_MOUNT='/api'). This is the line to change.
  - apps/wallow-auth/src/start.ts: same 'const requestOrigin = new URL(request.url).origin;' then 'baseUrl: withBasePath(requestOrigin, BASE_PATH)'.
  - apps/examples/minimal-app/src/start.ts: same pattern, 'baseUrl: requestOrigin' directly (no API_MOUNT/BASE_PATH — simplest case, good one to prototype the fix in first).
  Fix per the task design: 'const scheme = request.headers.get("x-forwarded-proto") ?? url.protocol;' where url is the already-parsed URL, then rebuild origin as `${scheme}://${url.host}` (url.protocol includes trailing ':', header value doesn't — normalize accordingly) instead of using url.origin directly. Extract as a small shared helper (e.g. 'requestOrigin(request: Request): string') so all 3 start.ts files call one function rather than reimplementing — no such helper exists yet in the SDK today (isomorphic constraint: start.ts files deliberately avoid importing '@bc-solutions-coder/sdk/server', so if extracted to the SDK it must live on the browser-safe root entry, or just be a tiny local util duplicated 3x with a comment referencing the others — task description doesn't mandate a shared module, just 'the same fix... identically'). New vitest spec: node-project (src/**/*.test.ts, no browser needed) per app or one shared location — check each app's vitest.config.ts node-project include glob before picking the file name/path.

4.4 Docs (files: docs/integrations/bff-pattern.md, docs/getting-started/fork-guide.md — docs/toc.yml untouched, confirmed both are existing pages already in nav): IMPORTANT — do NOT duplicate docs/operations/reverse-proxy.md, which ALREADY covers: cookie-domain widening (reverse-proxy.md:84-88, 'Authentication__CookieDomain' with a callout box — reference this, don't re-explain it) and the X-Forwarded-Proto/Host requirement + XFF append behavior (reverse-proxy.md section '4. Forwarded Headers', lines 163-178 — cross-link, don't restate). Also docs/operations/deployment.md section '2. Routing Topologies' (line 107) already covers path-based vs subdomain topology basics. What's genuinely MISSING and belongs in bff-pattern.md/fork-guide.md per this task: (a) the issuer-differs-per-environment table (dev=:3002 auth origin, e2e=:5050 API origin, prod=wallow.dev/api) framed from the SDK-consumer/fork perspective, not the ops-deployment perspective reverse-proxy.md already covers; (b) response_mode must stay top-level GET redirect because the tx-state cookie is SameSite=Lax (finding L6) — NO existing doc mentions response_mode or SameSite=Lax except the source audit plan docs/plans/2026-07-28/2358-tanstack-bff-csrf-audit.md:158-159 and docs/plans/2026-07-29/0948-bff-csrf-and-topology-remediation.md:294 (both are gitignored plans/ dir, not doc-site content — this task turns that into real docs for the first time). fork-guide.md's existing 'Frontend Authentication Policy: BFF-only' section (~line 204-256) ends with links to bff-pattern.md/typescript-sdk.md/integration-cookbook.md — natural anchor point to extend from. bff-pattern.md has an existing '## Security Notes' section (~line 257) with subsections 'Session Cookie Flags' (267), 'State Parameter' (278) — the response_mode/SameSite constraint fits as a new subsection there. Related closed work for context (do not re-litigate, just don't contradict): Wallow-vufu.2.3 already rewrote docker/docker-compose.production.yml + added docker/caddy/Caddyfile.example + rewrote docker/.env.production.example with an X-Forwarded-Proto-required-from-ingress note and switched cookie-secret generation from base64 to hex (L4); Wallow-vufu.2.1/2.2 fixed OIDC endpoint pinning and wallow-auth base-path support respectively — the per-environment issuer table this task adds should be consistent with 2.1's verified env matrix (its bead notes list the 4 concrete issuer/endpoint pairs verified: localhost:3002, localhost:5050, wallow.dev prod path-based, wallow.dev prod no-double-prefix).
4.2 follow-up (concrete app-side integration point, resolves the 'need to find handleApiRequest' item above): apps/wallow-web/src/lib/bff.ts:115 'export async function handleApiRequest(request: Request): Promise<Response>' just awaits getBffServer() then calls 'server.handleApi(request)' (server.handleApi comes from the SDK's createWallowBffServer, backed by proxy.ts's createBffApiProxy-equivalent — the ~804-829 header-forwarding block noted above). Neither handleApiRequest nor the routes/api/$.ts ANY handler currently reads/stamps '.ip' — the fix must add the same PeerRequest cast + CLIENT_IP_HEADER stamp that apps/wallow-auth/src/lib/api-passthrough.ts:53-77 does, most naturally either in routes/api/$.ts's ANY handler (before calling handleApiRequest) or as the first line inside handleApiRequest itself in lib/bff.ts (mutate request.headers.set(CLIENT_IP_HEADER, (request as PeerRequest).ip) when ip is a non-empty string) — TanStack Start's server route request is the same srvx-backed Request the wallow-auth splat routes receive, so the identical 'readonly ip?: string' interface and in-place-mutation constraint applies (do not clone via new Request(...)).

title: 3.3: CI runs the cross-app e2e journey (P3)
description: scripts/e2e.sh and the CI e2e-tests job currently only run the wallow-auth Playwright suite -- the wallow-web suite and the cross-app login-journey suite (which now, after Task 1.3, exercises the full login + authenticated mutation + logout loop) never run in CI. This is the audit's P3 finding and the first CI-shaped proof that the whole flow works.
design: Modify scripts/e2e.sh: after the existing wallow-auth suite run, bring up the same docker/docker-compose.test.yml stack (or reuse it if already up) and additionally run 'pnpm --filter ./apps/wallow-web test:e2e' and 'pnpm --filter ./apps/wallow-web test:e2e:cross-app' with E2E_BASE_URL=http://localhost:5053. Modify .github/workflows/ci.yml's e2e-tests job only if additional artifact paths or steps are needed to capture the new suites' Playwright reports.
acceptance_criteria: ./scripts/e2e.sh run locally end to end passes, now also exercising Task 1.3's authenticated-mutation-and-logout spec against the containerised compose stack -- the first CI-shaped proof of the whole login+mutate+logout loop. Commit message 'ci: run the wallow-web and cross-app e2e suites in the e2e job'.
notes:
GREEN (implement). FILES (6, all mine; verified via git diff -- the other dirty paths api/src/Wallow.AppHost/*, apps/wallow-web/src/lib/bff.ts, docfx.json, docker/docker-compose.test.yml belong to the concurrent 3.1/3.2 agents and were untouched by me):
- scripts/e2e.sh
- .github/workflows/ci.yml
- .claude/rules/E2E.md
- docs/development/testing-e2e.md
- docs/development/testing.md
- apps/wallow-web/README.md

CHANGES

scripts/e2e.sh (3 functional hunks + header rewrite):
1. Added WEB_URL=http://localhost:5053 (wallow-web's host-published port, compose 5053:3000).
2. `up -d --wait "$UP_SERVICE"` -> `up -d --wait "$UP_SERVICE" wallow-web`. One invocation; wallow-web's own depends_on (wallow-api, wallow-auth, valkey) pulls up the other two origins the cross-app journey traverses, so this is a superset of every prior UP_SERVICE choice. wallow-web carries a build block in docker-compose.test.yml, so a cold run with no prebuilt wallow-web-react:test image builds one rather than failing.
3. After the existing wallow-auth run, added two suites, BOTH pinned to container mode regardless of how wallow-auth was served:
     env E2E_BASE_URL=$WEB_URL pnpm --filter ./apps/wallow-web test:e2e
     env E2E_BASE_URL=$WEB_URL pnpm --filter ./apps/wallow-web test:e2e:cross-app
   Rationale recorded in a comment: playwright.cross-app.config.ts boots no server of its own and needs the three cross-wired origins only compose supplies; setting E2E_BASE_URL also stops apps/wallow-web/playwright.config.ts from starting a `pnpm dev` webServer, so the reachability gate hits the same container.
4. Header/env-knob docs rewritten: E2E_BASE_URL now documented as selecting the wallow-auth suite's serving mode ONLY; E2E_UP_SERVICE documented as an EXTRA service (wallow-web is always up). Noted that one `playwright install` covers both apps -- wallow-auth and wallow-web both resolve @playwright/test 1.61.1 (confirmed in pnpm-lock.yaml), so they share the per-version browser cache and neither CI nor the local branch needs a second install.

.github/workflows/ci.yml e2e-tests job (no new env vars, no new secrets, no ${{ }} interpolation added -- the injection surface is unchanged):
- Step 'Run wallow-auth E2E suite' renamed 'Run E2E suites'; same three env vars (E2E_SKIP_IMAGE_BUILD=1, E2E_UP_SERVICE=wallow-auth, E2E_BASE_URL=http://localhost:5051), same `run: ./scripts/e2e.sh`. All new coverage arrives through the script, so CI stays a thin caller.
- 'Upload Playwright report' renamed 'Upload wallow-auth Playwright report'; added a sibling 'Upload wallow-web Playwright report' (name playwright-report-wallow-web, path apps/wallow-web/playwright-report, if-no-files-found: ignore, retention-days: 5) mirroring the existing block. Both wallow-web configs write into that one directory. Note both configs use reporter:'list', so like the existing wallow-auth upload this is a safety net that normally finds nothing -- hence if-no-files-found: ignore.
- Confirmed no image work was needed: docker-images-app ALREADY builds, saves and restores wallow-web-react:test / :test-arm64, so the e2e job's existing 'Load Docker images' step already supplies the wallow-web image.
- apps/wallow-web/.gitignore already ignores playwright-report and test-results.

Docs kept in sync with the new behaviour: .claude/rules/E2E.md runner paragraph, docs/development/testing-e2e.md (runner section now lists all three suites; env-knob table + serving-mode paragraphs corrected), docs/development/testing.md CI job table row, apps/wallow-web/README.md E2E section (also documents the cross-app invocation). Left alone as still-accurate: CLAUDE.md:109, docker/CLAUDE.md, .claude/rules/TESTING.md.

VALIDATION EVIDENCE

* LITERAL ./scripts/e2e.sh RUN, exit 0, all three suites green (34 tests):
    COMPOSE_PROJECT_NAME=wallow-e2e-vufu33 E2E_SKIP_IMAGE_BUILD=1 E2E_UP_SERVICE=wallow-auth E2E_BASE_URL=http://localhost:5051 ./scripts/e2e.sh
  - wallow-auth suite: 30 passed (4.5s)
  - wallow-web suite: 2 passed (656ms)
  - wallow-web cross-app: 2 passed (1.8s) -- 'cross-app login journey establishes an authenticated wallow-web session' AND 'an authenticated mutation and logout complete on a real BFF session'. That second spec is Task 1.3's login+mutate+logout loop, so the acceptance criterion's 'first CI-shaped proof' is met by the real script in the real container stack (COOKIE_SECURE=false from 3.1 active in the same stack).
  - Log kept at /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-traveler-Repos-Wallow/b05dd916-d14c-440e-826e-fbe5956ba70e/scratchpad/e2e-run.log
  - The env vars are exactly CI's, so this run is CI's code path.

* ISOLATION (per memory docker-compose-test-project-collision): this WAS the literal script -- I overrode only COMPOSE_PROJECT_NAME, so the script's own two `down -v --remove-orphans` calls operated on project wallow-e2e-vufu33, never on the shared 'wallow' project. Proven first: docker-compose.test.yml declares NO top-level `name:`, and `COMPOSE_PROJECT_NAME=wallow-e2e-vufu33 docker compose -f docker/docker-compose.test.yml config --format json` reports name=wallow-e2e-vufu33 (shell env beats docker/.env's COMPOSE_PROJECT_NAME=wallow). After the run: 0 containers, 0 volumes, 0 networks left with the wallow-e2e-vufu33 prefix, and the dev-infra containers (wallow-postgres, wallow-valkey, wallow-garage, wallow-mailpit, wallow-alloy, wallow-docs, wallow-grafana-lgtm) were all still up. No AppHost was booted by me.

* scripts/e2e.sh: `bash -n` clean; shellcheck clean (no output, exit 0).
* .github/workflows/ci.yml: actionlint exit 0. Parsed the file with PyYAML and dumped the e2e-tests step list to confirm ordering, the unchanged env block on 'Run E2E suites', and both upload steps' with: blocks.
* pnpm format:check: 'All matched files use the correct format' (641 files). Note oxfmt's target list is `apps packages package.json pnpm-workspace.yaml tsconfig.base.json .oxlintrc.json .oxfmtrc.json` -- it covers none of scripts/*.sh, .github/**, .claude/**, or docs/**, so this gate is informational for these files rather than a real check of them. pnpm lint (oxlint apps packages) likewise has no bearing: I changed no TS/JS.

CI-ONLY / NOT PROVEN LOCALLY (honest gaps)
1. GitHub Actions cannot run here. The workflow change is validated by actionlint + YAML parse + the fact that the local run used CI's exact env vars and script. What remains unproven is GitHub-side behaviour only: that actions/upload-artifact@v7 accepts the second artifact name, and that the cached wallow-web-react:test image loads and boots on an ubuntu-latest x64 runner (my run used the local arm64 image).
2. LOCAL mode (E2E_BASE_URL unset) was NOT exercised end to end. That branch now also boots the wallow-auth + wallow-web containers alongside the `pnpm dev` wallow-auth server; port-wise it is clean (containers publish 5051/5053, dev server takes 3002, and bff-example's 3000 is not in wallow-web's depends_on chain so it never starts), but I did not run it. It is also materially slower on a cold checkout now, since compose must build the wallow-web Node image.
3. E2E_SKIP_IMAGE_BUILD=1 was used, so the dotnet publish branch (unchanged by me) did not run. Images consumed: wallow-api/migrations/seeder :test built 2026-07-28, wallow-auth-react:test and wallow-web-react:test rebuilt 2026-07-29 11:45-11:47 by the 3.1 agent. wallow-web-react:test therefore predates the concurrent 3.2 agent's apps/wallow-web/src/lib/bff.ts edit; that edit only adds session-store startup logging, so it cannot affect these results.

ISSUES=none. TEST_STATUS=pass (34/34 across three suites via the literal runner).

title: Phase 3 -- Dev/prod parity (M2, M3, P3)
description: Close three dev/prod parity gaps identified in the audit: (M2) the e2e Docker compose stack does not disable Secure cookies over plain HTTP; (M3) 'pnpm backend' (Aspire) silently runs cookie-based sessions instead of Valkey because the app only reads REDIS_URL, which Aspire's default wiring never sets; (P3) CI's e2e job never runs the wallow-web or cross-app Playwright suites, so the whole login+mutate+logout loop (including Task 1.3's new spec) is not gated in CI.
design: Source: docs/plans/2026-07-29/0948-bff-csrf-and-topology-remediation.md Phase 3. Three independent tasks: 3.1 (compose env var fix), 3.2 (Aspire AppHost C# change), 3.3 (CI script + workflow wiring).
acceptance_criteria: ./scripts/e2e.sh passes with COOKIE_SECURE=false active in the test stack; 'pnpm backend' selects the Valkey session store (verified via logs) instead of cookie sessions; ./scripts/e2e.sh additionally runs the wallow-web and cross-app suites end to end.
notes:
SCOUT findings for Phase 3 (dev/prod parity). bd memories checked -- nothing duplicative found; no new repo-wide memory needed (everything below is task-scoped). Read prior sibling notes: Wallow-vufu.1.3 (cross-app spec lives in apps/wallow-web/e2e-cross-app/login-journey.spec.ts, 2 tests: login journey + "authenticated mutation and logout"; run via `pnpm --filter ./apps/wallow-web test:e2e:cross-app`) and Wallow-vufu.2.3 (production compose Caddy ingress -- NOT touched by this feature; docker-compose.test.yml is untouched by Phase 2, confirmed still `config -q` exit 0 there).

TASK 3.1 (COOKIE_SECURE=false in e2e compose):
- docker/docker-compose.test.yml wallow-web service (lines 233-275) and bff-example service (lines 292-325) BOTH already set REDIS_URL (Valkey sessions already wired for e2e -- that part is done) but NEITHER sets COOKIE_SECURE. Add `COOKIE_SECURE: "false"` to both `environment:` blocks.
- Template comment to reuse verbatim (per task DESIGN): api/src/Wallow.AppHost/Program.cs:92-95 -- "Safari/WebKit refuses Secure cookies over plain-HTTP localhost (Chrome and Firefox allow them), so the BFF's login-transaction cookie never survives the redirect and every /bff/callback fails with a 400. Local dev is plain HTTP, so drop the flag here." AppHost's wallow-web resource ALREADY sets COOKIE_SECURE=false (line 95) -- only the compose file is missing it.
- Stale comment to fix (also in task DESIGN): docker-compose.test.yml bff-example header comment at lines 289-291 says "The SDK fetches discovery from it and rewrites the backchannel token_endpoint to that origin" -- WRONG per Wallow-vufu.2's audit (SDK uses the discovered endpoint verbatim, no rewrite). Correct to say the backchannel endpoint is already reachable via OIDC_METADATA_URL without rewriting.
- wallow-api service itself has no COOKIE_SECURE var (N/A, it's not a BFF).

TASK 3.2 (Valkey-backed sessions under Aspire):
- api/src/Wallow.AppHost/Program.cs: `valkey` resource declared line 11 (`IResourceBuilder<RedisResource> valkey = builder.AddRedis("valkey")`). wallow-web resource block (lines 75-97) has `.WithReference(valkey, connectionName: "Redis")` at line 78 -- this injects `ConnectionStrings__Redis`, which nothing reads. wallow-auth ALSO has `.WithReference(valkey, connectionName: "Redis")` (line 64) but wallow-auth is a stateless passthrough proxy (no session store) so that reference is harmless/unused there -- only wallow-web needs the fix.
- apps/wallow-web/src/lib/bff.ts:66 `connectRedisClient()` reads ONLY `process.env.REDIS_URL`; when empty/unset it returns `undefined` and `buildBffServer()` (line 82) passes `{}` to `createWallowBffServer`. IMPORTANT: packages/sdk/src/server/bff-server.ts `selectStore()` (lines 83-113) only THROWS when `env.REDIS_URL` is set with no `redisClient` supplied (lines 100-107) -- if REDIS_URL is simply absent (today's Aspire case) it silently falls through to `CookieSessionStore` at line 109 with NO error and NO log. bff.ts currently has zero startup logging of which store got picked -- add one (e.g. in connectRedisClient or buildBffServer) so the fix is independently verifiable per the task's acceptance criteria, without touching the SDK itself (host-only fix, SDK's contract of "only reads REDIS_URL" must stay unchanged).
- Verified Aspire.Hosting.Redis 13.4.6 (api/Directory.Packages.props:135, pinned) via decompiling the installed dll (`~/.nuget/packages/aspire.hosting.redis/13.4.6/lib/net8.0/Aspire.Hosting.Redis.dll`): `RedisResource` DOES expose both `PasswordParameter` and `PrimaryEndpoint` properties, matching the task's DESIGN snippet exactly -- `valkey.Resource.PasswordParameter` and `valkey.Resource.PrimaryEndpoint.Property(EndpointProperty.Host/Port)` are valid, no API-version escape hatch needed. Compose `redis://:{password}@{host}:{port}` via `ReferenceExpression.Create` and set `context.EnvironmentVariables["REDIS_URL"]` inside a `.WithEnvironment(context => {...})` on the wallow-web resource block (after line 91, alongside the other WithEnvironment calls), matching the COOKIE_SECURE comment style already there.

TASK 3.3 (CI runs cross-app e2e journey):
- .github/workflows/ci.yml `e2e-tests` job (lines 398-463) currently ONLY drives the wallow-auth suite: `E2E_UP_SERVICE: wallow-auth`, `E2E_BASE_URL: http://localhost:5051`, `run: ./scripts/e2e.sh`, then uploads `playwright-report-wallow-auth` from `apps/wallow-auth/playwright-report`.

title: 3.2: Valkey-backed sessions under Aspire (M3)
description: Aspire's AppHost injects a ConnectionStrings__Redis environment variable into the wallow-web resource by default, but the Node app's session-store selection logic only reads a single REDIS_URL variable (apps/wallow-web/src/lib/bff.ts:66) -- so 'pnpm backend' silently falls back to cookie-based sessions while both the e2e stack and production correctly use Valkey. This is a C# change in the AppHost; read .claude/rules/CONVENTIONS.md first and run 'dotnet format api/Wallow.slnx' before committing.
acceptance_criteria: Run 'pnpm backend'; wallow-web's logs (or bff.ts's session-store-selection code path) show the Valkey store selected, not cookie sessions; login and a dashboard mutation still work; logout truly revokes the session (using the browser back button after logout shows a signed-out state, not a cached authenticated page). Commit message 'fix(apphost): hand wallow-web a REDIS_URL so dev uses Valkey sessions like prod'.
notes:
GREEN: Aspire now hands wallow-web a REDIS_URL, and dev uses Valkey sessions like prod.

FILES:
- api/src/Wallow.AppHost/Program.cs (valkey resource + wallow-web env)
- api/src/Wallow.AppHost/Wallow.AppHost.csproj (NoWarn ASPIRECERTIFICATES001)
- apps/wallow-web/src/lib/bff.ts (one-line store-selection log in buildBffServer)

SYMBOLS: no new exports. Program.cs top-level statements only; bff.ts buildBffServer() gains a console.info.

WHAT CHANGED vs the task DESIGN -- two corrections, both verified empirically:

1. Use valkey.Resource.UriExpression, NOT a hand-composed ReferenceExpression.Create($"redis://:{PasswordParameter}@{host}:{port}"). RedisResource in Aspire.Hosting.Redis 13.4.6 exposes UriExpression documented as 'redis://[:{password}@]{host}:{port}, password segment omitted when no password is configured'. It is strictly better than the DESIGN snippet: the manifest shows it references valkey-password-URI-ENCODED (the raw PasswordParameter would inject an unescaped password into a URL) and it takes the scheme from the endpoint binding. One line: .WithEnvironment("REDIS_URL", valkey.Resource.UriExpression).

2. MUST ALSO disable Aspire's default TLS on the valkey endpoint, or the fix breaks the app. This is the non-obvious part. Aspire 13.4.6 runs the redis container with '--tls-port 6379 --port 6380' and its own dev certificate BY DEFAULT (verified: docker inspect Config.Cmd on the running container). With TLS on, UriExpression renders rediss:// and node-redis fails hard: 'Error: self-signed certificate; if the root CA is installed locally, try running Node.js with --use-system-ca'. Aspire configures certificate trust for .NET and container resources but NEVER sets NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS (grepped Aspire.Hosting.dll and Aspire.Hosting.JavaScript.dll 13.4.6 -- the string does not appear), so a JavaScript app resource has no way to trust it. That would have turned a silent cookie-session fallback into a hard BFF failure on every request -- strictly worse.
   Fix: builder.AddRedis("valkey").WithoutHttpsCertificate(). RedisResource.TlsEnabled is READ-ONLY (CS0200), so the property setter is not an option; WithoutHttpsCertificate is the only supported API and is still evaluation-only, hence ASPIRECERTIFICATES001 in the csproj NoWarn with a comment explaining why. Plain TCP also matches what docker-compose.test.yml and docker-compose.production.yml already run, which is the parity this feature is about.

VALIDATION EVIDENCE:
- Isolated throwaway AppHost (scratchpad, torn down) proved run-mode behaviour without disturbing anything: with WithoutHttpsCertificate the container Cmd loses --tls-port/--port 6380 and publishes ONE port instead of two, and an AddExecutable resource (same resource class as AddJavaScriptApp) resolved REDIS_URL=redis://:<pw>@localhost:<proxyport>. node-redis connected to that EXACT resolved URL and did a set/get roundtrip: OK. The rediss:// vs redis:// vs plaintext-port matrix was tested directly (rediss FAIL self-signed, redis-on-tls-port FAIL socket closed, plaintext OK).
- Full 'pnpm backend': api:5001 200, web:3000 200, auth:3002 200. wallow-web's vite process env carries REDIS_URL=redis://:<pw>@localhost:52003 (redis://, not rediss://); ConnectionStrings__Redis has no ,ssl=true so the API connects plaintext too. valkey container Cmd has no --tls-port.
- ACCEPTANCE, login + mutation + logout: 'pnpm --filter ./apps/wallow-web test:e2e:cross-app' against the Aspire stack, 2/2 PASSED ('cross-app login journey establishes an authenticated wallow-web session' and 'an authenticated mutation and logout complete on a real BFF session'). Ran green on two separate fresh boots.
- ACCEPTANCE, sessions really are server-side: valkey held only DataProtection-Keys before the run; after it, 'wallow:session:iOEa2m7RtBW7eZv3dv-hgQr5M5UaZRAg' (redis-cli KEYS in the Aspire valkey container). The logout test leaves no session key behind, so logout is a real revocation.
- ACCEPTANCE, store-selection log: 'BFF session store: redis/valkey (server-side)'. Aspire pipes resource stdout to its dashboard rather than the AppHost console, so this was captured by running the app's own pnpm dev on PORT=3005 with the exact Aspire-injected REDIS_URL. The app contract is unchanged -- it still reads only REDIS_URL; the SDK was not touched.

GATES: dotnet format api/Wallow.slnx clean; AppHost build 0 warnings 0 errors; oxfmt --check clean; oxlint --deny-warnings clean; wallow-web tsc --noEmit clean; wallow-web vitest 74 files / 471 tests ALL PASS.

TEST_STATUS=pass

title: 2.2: wallow-auth -- base-path support (P2)
description: wallow-auth must be servable at https://wallow.dev/auth/... with the /auth prefix intact end-to-end -- no ingress stripping. That means SSR HTML, /_build/* built assets, and browser fetch()es must all carry the /auth prefix. Introduce exactly one configuration knob: AUTH_BASE_PATH (default empty string = current unprefixed behavior; production sets it to /auth). Because this is a Vite build-time base path, the production Docker image must be built with the env var set -- it cannot be applied at runtime. THIS IS THE HIGHEST-UNCERTAINTY TASK IN THE PLAN: TanStack Start's basepath support varies by version. Spike first; if the pinned Start version cannot do it cleanly, STOP and escalate (options: upgrade Start, or revisit the path-based topology decision) rather than hand-rolling path-rewriting middleware.
design:
Files: modify apps/wallow-auth/vite.config.ts (base: process.env.AUTH_BASE_PATH ? `${process.env.AUTH_BASE_PATH}/` : '/', and pass the same value into the installed @tanstack/react-start plugin's router basepath option -- check that plugin's actual signature for router.basepath vs spa.basepath against the pinned version in apps/wallow-auth/package.json, do not assume); modify apps/wallow-auth/src/start.ts (browser/SSR SDK baseUrl construction around lines 55-58 must become origin + base path, not bare origin); modify apps/wallow-auth/src/routes/* API passthrough splat routes so that once the router knows the basepath, /auth/v1/** reaches handleApiPassthrough and the passthrough still forwards the UNPREFIXED /v1/** upstream -- decide whether to strip the base before passthrough.handle or configure the passthrough's prefix list by first spiking against packages/sdk/src/server/passthrough.ts:50-54's actual behavior; modify apps/wallow-auth/Dockerfile to add 'ARG AUTH_BASE_PATH' promoted to an ENV before 'pnpm build' runs; keep apps/wallow-auth/e2e/routes.spec.ts green with the default empty base, and add a vitest node spec for whatever base-resolution helper gets extracted.

Recommended sequence: (1) SPIKE FIRST -- build with AUTH_BASE_PATH=/auth, run 'pnpm --filter ./apps/wallow-auth start', curl -I localhost:3002/auth/login and confirm a 200 with asset URLs correctly prefixed; write down exactly what needed changing before writing any tests. (2) Encode the spike's findings as failing tests. (3) Implement minimally to pass them. (4) Confirm both 'pnpm --filter ./apps/wallow-auth test' and 'test:e2e' still pass with AUTH_BASE_PATH unset (default behavior byte-for-byte unchanged).
acceptance_criteria: With AUTH_BASE_PATH=/auth set at build time: the built app serves SSR HTML, /_build/* assets, and API passthrough calls all correctly under the /auth prefix (verified via curl -I localhost:3002/auth/login -> 200 with prefixed asset URLs). With AUTH_BASE_PATH unset: apps/wallow-auth/e2e/routes.spec.ts and the full 'pnpm --filter ./apps/wallow-auth test' suite pass unchanged. title: 2.3: Reference Caddy ingress + loopback ports in production compose
description: Add a reference ingress to the production Docker Compose stack that validates both Task 2.1 (path-preserving OIDC pinning) and Task 2.2 (wallow-auth base-path support) actually work together, and fixes three related hardening findings: M5 (no documented ingress reference), M9 (topology contract undocumented), L4 (COOKIE secrets generated with base64 can contain '+ / =' characters that break REDIS_URL).
design: Files: modify docker/docker-compose.production.yml -- add a caddy service doing path routing per the file's own header comment: /api/* routes to wallow-api:8080 with the /api prefix KEPT (the API uses UsePathBase('/api')), /auth/* routes to wallow-auth:8080 with the /auth prefix KEPT, everything else routes to wallow-web:8080; the ingress must stamp X-Forwarded-Proto. Change the three app services' 'ports:' mappings to '127.0.0.1:'-bound (still reachable for local debugging, but not exposed externally -- Caddy owns 80/443). Create docker/caddy/Caddyfile.example implementing that routing. Modify docker/.env.production.example to document the ingress, state that X-Forwarded-Proto: https is REQUIRED from any replacement ingress, and switch the secret-generation recipe from 'openssl rand -base64 32' to 'openssl rand -hex 32' (hex output has no '+ / =' characters, fixing L4's REDIS_URL breakage).
acceptance_criteria: docker compose -f docker/docker-compose.production.yml --env-file docker/.env.production config parses successfully with the new caddy service and 127.0.0.1-bound app ports. Full-stack smoke (exercised later in Task 5.4) confirms login -> dashboard -> mutation -> logout works through the ingress at http://localhost using /api and /auth prefixes. Commit message 'feat(docker): reference Caddy ingress, loopback port bindings, hex secrets for production compose'.
notes:
GREEN: reference Caddy ingress + loopback ports + hex secrets.

FILES=
- docker/caddy/Caddyfile.example (NEW): path routing, /api and /auth prefixes KEPT (handle, not handle_path), catch-all -> wallow-web; global 'admin localhost:2019' + 'auto_https off' for the local reference; commented subdomain site blocks; commented 'trusted_proxies' block.
- docker/docker-compose.production.yml: header comment rewritten (old 'strip the /auth prefix' text replaced with BUILT-with-AUTH_BASE_PATH/prefix-KEPT, subdomain section now says set BOTH API_PATH_BASE= and AUTH_BASE_PATH= empty, added the X-Forwarded-Proto requirement); new 'caddy' service (caddy:2-alpine, owns 80/443 tcp+udp, CADDYFILE_HOST_PATH bind, caddy_data/caddy_config volumes, depends_on all three apps service_healthy); all three app ports now 127.0.0.1-bound; wallow-auth gains a build: stanza; caddy_data/caddy_config added to volumes:.
- docker/.env.production.example: new INGRESS section (CADDYFILE_HOST_PATH, INGRESS_HTTP_PORT/INGRESS_HTTPS_PORT + the 3-point contract for a replacement ingress); PATH BASE section rewritten and AUTH_BASE_PATH=/auth added with the build-vs-runtime explanation; PORTS section documents the loopback binding; L4 fixed — every 'openssl rand -base64 N' recipe switched to '-hex N' with a header paragraph naming the concrete REDIS_URL breakage.
- .github/workflows/deploy.yml: comment-only. Documents that AUTH_BASE_PATH is deliberately NOT passed.
- docker/CLAUDE.md: ingress bullet + production-stack table row.
- .gitignore: docker/caddy/Caddyfile (the user's working copy) ignored; the .example stays tracked (verified with git check-ignore both ways).

SCOUT GAP 1 (stale 'strip /auth prefix' docs) — FIXED in both files, see above.

SCOUT GAP 2 (deploy.yml passes no AUTH_BASE_PATH) — RESOLVED as scout option (b), compose build stanza, NOT option (a). Rationale: AUTH_BASE_PATH is baked by 'vite build' into every asset URL, so one published image cannot serve both topologies. The published image must stay ROOT-built because docker-compose.test.yml/E2E and the subdomain topology both depend on it; passing --build-arg AUTH_BASE_PATH=/auth in CI would break every root-mounted consumer, and publishing a second path-based variant would double an already QEMU-slow arm64 auth build. So: build: {context: .., dockerfile: apps/wallow-auth/Dockerfile, args: {AUTH_BASE_PATH: \${AUTH_BASE_PATH-/auth}}}. 'up --build' (already this file's documented invocation) rebuilds with the prefix and tags over the pulled name. The residual hazard — 'docker compose pull && up -d' silently yields an auth container that 404s behind /auth — is called out in a HAZARD comment on the service, in the .env PATH BASE section, in docker/CLAUDE.md, and in deploy.yml itself so it is not rediscovered.

Note the '-' (not ':-') default in \${AUTH_BASE_PATH-/auth} is load-bearing: it lets AUTH_BASE_PATH= (empty, subdomain topology) stay empty instead of falling back to /auth. Matches the existing \${API_PATH_BASE-/api}.

TWO REAL BUGS FOUND AND FIXED BY LIVE TESTING (both would have shipped from a config-only review):
1. Healthcheck used http://localhost:2019 — Caddy's admin API binds IPv4 127.0.0.1 only while 'localhost' resolves to ::1 first in the container, so wget got ECONNREFUSED and the service would NEVER have become healthy (and, via depends_on, nothing gates on caddy so it would have failed silently). Now 127.0.0.1:2019, with the reason in a comment. Confirmed live: health=healthy at t+6s.
2. Explicit 'header_up X-Forwarded-Proto/Host' triggered 'Unnecessary header_up' warnings from caddy validate — Caddy sets X-Forwarded-{For,Proto,Host} by default. Removed; the default behavior is documented in the file header instead.

VALIDATION EVIDENCE:
- 'docker compose -f docker-compose.production.yml --env-file <stub> config' exit=0 for BOTH topologies (path-based stub, and a subdomain stub with API_PATH_BASE=/AUTH_BASE_PATH= empty). title: 1.1: SDK -- double-submit cookie fallback in the CSRF interceptor
description: The CSRF interceptor in packages/sdk/src/csrf.ts (around lines 67-74) only stamps the x-csrf-token header when setCsrfToken() was explicitly called. The only remaining caller of setCsrfToken is bff-demo.tsx, so every other dashboard mutation sends no CSRF header and the BFF rejects it with a 403 CSRF_INVALID. The fix: fall back to reading the non-HttpOnly '${cookieName}-csrf' double-submit cookie that the BFF writes at the OIDC callback (packages/sdk/src/server/handlers.ts:494) -- this cookie is already read by logout() via a private readCsrfCookie() in packages/sdk/src/auth.ts:117-134. This also fixes M1 (a module-global token store could leak one user's token to another during SSR) by gating that store behind a typeof document check, and M8 (first-match-wins cookie parsing) by preferring a __Host--prefixed cookie name when multiple '-csrf' cookies exist in the jar.

title: 1.2: Live verification of CSRF fix in dev
description: Manual smoke-test that Task 1.1's CSRF interceptor fallback actually unblocks dashboard mutations in a real dev environment (Aspire), since the SDK unit tests alone don't exercise the real cookie/network path.
design: Steps: (1) Run 'pnpm backend' to start the full stack via Aspire. (2) Log in at http://localhost:3000 with admin@wallow.dev (credentials per api/seed.json). (3) Perform one dashboard mutation (e.g. create an organization) -- expect it to succeed with no 403 CSRF_INVALID; inspect DevTools network tab to confirm the POST carries an x-csrf-token header matching the value of the wallow_bff-csrf cookie. (4) Log out -- expect it to complete without a 'Logout failed' error.
acceptance_criteria: Dashboard mutation succeeds with x-csrf-token present and matching the cookie; logout completes cleanly with no error.
notes:
LIVE-VERIFY: Full dev stack driven via a Playwright script (not the repo's Playwright suites -- a one-off Chromium automation in /tmp, since this task calls for interactive DevTools-style verification, not a committed test). Infra (postgres/valkey/garage) and the API (localhost:5001) were already running from a prior session; I built @bc-solutions-coder/sdk (pnpm --filter @bc-solutions-coder/sdk build -- picks up the uncommitted Task 1.1 fix in the working tree) and started apps/wallow-web (port 3000) and apps/wallow-auth (port 3002) myself via 'pnpm dev' with the exact env vars Wallow.AppHost/Program.cs wires for Aspire (OIDC_ISSUER=http://localhost:3002, OIDC_METADATA_URL=http://localhost:5001/.well-known/openid-configuration, OIDC_CLIENT_ID/SECRET=wallow-web-client/wallow-web-secret, OIDC_REDIRECT_URI=http://localhost:3000/bff/callback, BFF_API_BASE_URL=http://localhost:5001, COOKIE_PASSWORD=<32+ chars>, COOKIE_SECURE=false) -- 'pnpm backend' itself was not used because AppHost already binds 3000/3002/5001 and those were free but the API+infra were already up standalone, so I reused them and matched Aspire's env exactly. Both apps were torn down (killed) at the end; the pre-existing API/infra were left running as found.

CRITERION 1 -- 'Dashboard mutation succeeds with x-csrf-token present and matching the cookie': CONFIRMED. Logged in as admin@wallow.dev / Admin123! (api/seed.json) via the real /bff/login -> wallow-auth /login -> /bff/callback round trip (real Chromium, real cookies). Landed authenticated on /dashboard/organizations. Read the CSRF cookie from the browser's cookie jar: wallow_bff-csrf=<token>. Filled organization-name, clicked organization-create-submit. Captured the actual network request: 'POST http://localhost:3000/api/v1/identity/organizations' carried header x-csrf-token=<token> that is byte-identical to the wallow_bff-csrf cookie value, and the response was 201 Created (body {"organizationId":"<guid>"}) -- NOT a 403 CSRF_INVALID. The follow-up list refetch (GET, 200) has no CSRF header, correctly (safe method). Reproduced this 3 times across separate login sessions (3 different tokens each time), always 201 + matching header.

NEGATIVE CONTROL (extra, not required by the bead but strengthens the evidence): git stash'd the Task 1.1 diff, rebuilt the SDK, restarted wallow-web with the now-unfixed dist, repeated the identical flow. Result: the SAME POST got x-csrf-token=(none) and the API returned 403; the UI's organization-create-error banner appeared. This is the exact regression Task 1.1 fixes, and confirms the fix (not some other factor) is what makes the positive case pass. git stash pop restored the fix; rebuilt the SDK; reran the positive case once more -- 201 + matching header again. (Note: while stashed/popped, two unrelated concurrent teammate edits appeared in the tree -- docfx.json and a new docs/audits/ dir -- from other agents working the same shared repo; verified after pop that these were untouched/unaffected and only the 5 pre-existing csrf-fix files remained in my diff.)

CRITERION 2 -- 'logout completes cleanly with no error': CONFIRMED. Clicked dashboard-logout-link. Network: 'POST http://localhost:3000/bff/logout' carried x-csrf-token matching the same cookie, response 302 (redirect to sign-out complete). dashboard-logout-error was NOT visible. Landed back on http://localhost:3000/ (signed out). This also passed in the NEGATIVE CONTROL run (unfixed SDK) -- expected, because auth.ts's logout() already had its own private CSRF-cookie fallback before Task 1.1; the regression only affected the shared interceptor used by every OTHER mutation. Confirms Task 1.1's description precisely.

UNRELATED FINDING (not a CSRF issue, filing for awareness only, NOT blocking this task): after a successful 201 organization-create, the newly created org does not appear in the /dashboard/organizations list even after the automatic GET refetch (verified via response body: GET still returns only the original seeded 'Wallow' org). This looks like an org-membership/list-scoping issue on the backend or a query-invalidation gap in the mutation, unrelated to CSRF token handling (the POST itself is fully successful with a real organizationId returned). Recommend filing a separate bead if not already tracked.

VERDICT=CLOSE. Both acceptance criteria (mutation succeeds with matching x-csrf-token; logout completes without error) are directly confirmed via real browser network inspection in a live dev environment, with a negative control proving the fix is causal. Stack torn down cleanly (wallow-web/wallow-auth killed; pre-existing API/infra left as found); working tree returned to its pre-verification state (only Task 1.1's 5 files modified, no stray debug files).

title: 1.3: E2E -- authenticated mutation + logout coverage
description: Close the CI blind spot: no existing E2E spec exercises an authenticated mutation through the real CSRF path, which is why the Task 1.1 regression shipped undetected. Extend the cross-app login journey spec to perform a real mutation and a logout, and confirm the new assertions actually fail without Task 1.1's fix.
design: Read .claude/rules/E2E.md first (data-testid conventions: {page}-{element} kebab-case, wait for [data-app-ready='true']). GREEN: E2E coverage for the authenticated mutation + logout is in and regression-proven.

FILES (one file, no new testids needed -- every selector already existed):

title: Phase 1 -- CSRF regression (unblocks dev today)
description: Fix the CSRF regression that 403s all dashboard mutations in dev. The SDK's CSRF interceptor (packages/sdk/src/csrf.ts) only stamps x-csrf-token when setCsrfToken() was called, but the only remaining caller is bff-demo.tsx -- every other mutation gets no header and is rejected. The BFF already writes a non-HttpOnly '${cookieName}-csrf' double-submit cookie at OIDC callback (packages/sdk/src/server/handlers.ts near line 494); the interceptor must fall back to reading it.
design: Source: docs/plans/2026-07-29/0948-bff-csrf-and-topology-remediation.md Phase 1 (findings section 1, M1, M8). title: Fix CreateOrganizationAddressabilityTests regression from pu6a.1.13's IsGlobalAdmin-only tenant gate
description:
3 integration tests in api/tests/Modules/Identity/Wallow.Identity.IntegrationTests/Organizations/CreateOrganizationAddressabilityTests.cs currently FAIL: PostOrganization_ThenGetById_ViaReturnedId_Succeeds, PostOrganization_ThenAddAndListMember_ViaReturnedId_Succeeds, PostOrganization_ThenUpdateSettings_ViaReturnedId_Succeeds. Run: ./scripts/run-tests.sh integration -> 48/51 pass, these 3 fail (Expected OK/NoContent, found NotFound).

CAUSALITY (high confidence, evidence-based): this is a genuine regression, not a pre-existing/unrelated failure, caused by bead Wallow-pu6a.1.13.

History:
- Wallow-w6s6.5.2 (closed 2026-07-22) fixed the original orphaned-org bug in POST /v1/identity/organizations by making OrganizationsController.IsCurrentTenantOrg bypass the tenant-equality check for any caller holding the tenant-assignable 'admin' ROLE: `orgId == tenantContext.TenantId.Value || User.GetRoles().Contains("admin", OrdinalIgnoreCase)`. CreateOrganizationAddressabilityTests creates the org via SetTestUser(AdminUserId, "admin") (role, not a claim) and then reads/updates it via the returned id -- which only works because of that role bypass, since the freshly created org's id never equals the creator's own tenant id (that mismatch IS the tenant model: Organization IS the tenant, and creating a new org mints a NEW tenant id distinct from the creator's). w6s6.5.2's own close verification ran these 3 tests directly and confirmed 3/3 pass.
- Wallow-pu6a.1.13 (closed 2026-07-28) correctly identified that same role-based bypass as a real cross-tenant privilege-escalation hole: ANY caller holding the ordinary, tenant-assignable 'admin' role could reach/govern ANY OTHER tenant's org by guessing its GUID (view membership, add/remove members, change branding/settings, archive, reactivate, delete). The fix replaced the bypass with User.IsGlobalAdmin() (OrganizationsController.cs:29-31 today: `orgId == tenantContext.TenantId.Value || User.IsGlobalAdmin()`), removing the role-based escape hatch entirely. This is the right security fix on its own terms.
- pu6a.1.13's GREEN report ran ./scripts/run-tests.sh identity (1249/1249) and arch (288/288) but NEVER ran ./scripts/run-tests.sh integration -- so it never exercised CreateOrganizationAddressabilityTests (which lives in the separate Wallow.Identity.IntegrationTests project) and had no way to see it had just broken the addressability tests that depended on the exact bypass it removed.

CONCLUSION: pu6a.1.13's OrganizationsController change is the direct, sole cause of this regression. It was the correct security fix, but it silently reintroduced the T5.2 orphaned-org symptom (org creator gets a 404 reading their own just-created org) for any creator who is not a global admin, because nothing else grants the creator access to a tenant id that isn't their own.

FIX must not simply restore the role-based bypass (that re-opens the pu6a.1.13 vulnerability). Plausible correct directions to evaluate:
1. Have organization creation auto-materialize the creator as an OrganizationMember of the new org (and/or migrate the caller's own tenant context to the new org id) so ordinary tenant-scoped access works without any bypass.
2. Re-scope realm-admin org creation to require/assume global-admin for the creator (design decision -- may not match product intent for self-service org creation by tenant-scoped admins).
3. Have the POST response or a follow-up step explicitly grant temporary global-admin-equivalent access to the creator for their new org only (avoid if it reintroduces a broad escape hatch).

Whichever direction is chosen, CreateOrganizationAddressabilityTests must pass without reintroducing OrganizationsControllerCrossTenantTests' guarantees (role='admin' must NOT grant cross-tenant access to arbitrary other orgs -- only to the org the caller just created, if that path is chosen).
acceptance_criteria: ./scripts/run-tests.sh integration is green (0 failures) including all 3 CreateOrganizationAddressabilityTests cases, AND ./scripts/run-tests.sh identity stays green including OrganizationsControllerCrossTenantTests (tenant-assignable admin role must still be rejected on OTHER tenants' orgs -- only global admins or, if the chosen fix path grants it, the org's own creator/members may reach it).
notes:
FIX (green). Direction chosen: option 1 from the bead -- ownership relationship, NOT any role-based tenant bypass. pu6a.1.13's gate is untouched and unweakened.

WHY THIS WORKS WITHOUT NEW CODE IN THE SERVICE: OrganizationService.CreateOrganizationAsync ALREADY materializes the creator as an OrgMemberRole.Admin member of the new org (OrganizationService.cs:38-42), and OrganizationRepository.GetByIdAsync deliberately IgnoreQueryFilters (an org IS the tenant, so the ambient filter would hide every org but the caller's own). So the creator/org relationship already existed in the data; only the controller gate refused to look at it. The fix reads that existing relationship.

FILES (6, all staged; nothing else staged by me -- the sibling's unstaged AuthorizationControllerTests.cs was left alone):
- NEW api/src/Modules/Identity/Wallow.Identity.Application/Interfaces/IOrganizationAccessPolicy.cs
- NEW api/src/Modules/Identity/Wallow.Identity.Infrastructure/Services/OrganizationAccessPolicy.cs
- api/src/Modules/Identity/Wallow.Identity.Api/Controllers/OrganizationsController.cs
- api/src/Modules/Identity/Wallow.Identity.Infrastructure/Extensions/IdentityInfrastructureExtensions.cs (AddScoped<IOrganizationAccessPolicy, OrganizationAccessPolicy>() next to IOrganizationService)
- api/tests/.../Wallow.Identity.Tests/Api/Controllers/OrganizationsControllerCrossTenantTests.cs (ctor arg + 3 new ownership theories; all 1.13 assertions unchanged)
- api/tests/.../Wallow.Identity.Tests/Api/Controllers/OrganizationsControllerTests.cs (ctor arg only)

SYMBOLS:
- IOrganizationAccessPolicy.IsOrganizationAdminAsync(Guid organizationId, Guid userId, CancellationToken ct = default) -> Task<bool>
- sealed class OrganizationAccessPolicy(IOrganizationRepository organizationRepository) : IOrganizationAccessPolicy
- OrganizationsController ctor is now (IOrganizationService orgService, ITenantContext tenantContext, IOrganizationAccessPolicy accessPolicy)
- private bool IsCurrentTenantOrg(Guid) REPLACED by private async Task<bool> CanAddressOrganizationAsync(Guid orgId, CancellationToken ct); all 12 gated call sites now 'if (!await CanAddressOrganizationAsync(id, ct))'. Gate reads: orgId == tenantContext.TenantId.Value || User.IsGlobalAdmin() || (Guid.TryParse(User.GetUserId(), out Guid callerId) && await accessPolicy.IsOrganizationAdminAsync(orgId, callerId, ct)).

SECURITY RATIONALE (why this does not re-open pu6a.1.13):
1. No role string is consulted anywhere in the gate. GetRoles().Contains is still absent from api/src (repo-wide grep from 1.13 still returns zero hits). IsGlobalAdmin() remains the ONLY blanket cross-tenant escape hatch.
2. The new path is NARROW and per-organization: it grants access to exactly the org ids where the caller is already a recorded admin member. Owning org A confers nothing over org B (covered by a new test).
3. The relationship is NOT attacker-grantable. OrgMemberRole.Admin membership is minted in exactly two places in api/src: OrganizationService.CreateOrganizationAsync (the creator, for the org they just created) and TestSupportService (test-only endpoint). Public AddMemberAsync hardcodes OrgMemberRole.Member, so adding yourself/someone to a foreign org grants no governance. Confirmed by grep -rn 'OrgMemberRole.Admin' api/src.
4. [HasPermission] still applies on every endpoint; ownership only replaces the tenant-identity half of the check.
5. Deliberately a SEPARATE dependency from IOrganizationService so 1.13's TenantAdminRole_ForeignOrganization_NeverReachesTheOrganizationService(12) assertion keeps its full force: a rejected cross-tenant call still touches zero organization DATA. The only thing a rejected call performs is the boolean authorization lookup itself (this caller's own user id vs this org's roster), which is unavoidable for any ownership model.

TESTS ADDED to OrganizationsControllerCrossTenantTests (file keeps [Trait(\"Category\",\"CrossTenant\")], required by CrossTenantTestGateTests):
- OrganizationAdminMember_ThatOrganization_ReachesTheOrganizationService(12 endpoints) -- no admin role, no global-admin claim, ownership only.
- OrganizationAdminMember_ADifferentOrganization_IsRejected(3) -- owning one org grants nothing over another; service untouched.
- ForeignOrganization_AsksOwnershipOnlyForTheCallerAndTheRequestedOrganization -- the ownership question is asked with the caller's own user id and the requested org id only.
The _accessPolicy substitute defaults to false, so every pre-existing rejection assertion from 1.13 now also proves rejection of a caller with no ownership relationship.

TEST_STATUS=pass. ./scripts/run-tests.sh integration -> 51/51 PASS (was 48/51; all 3 CreateOrganizationAddressabilityTests now green, and they were NOT edited). ./scripts/run-tests.sh identity -> 1278/1278 PASS (was 1249 before the 3 new theories, incl. every OrganizationsControllerCrossTenantTests case). ./scripts/run-tests.sh arch -> 300/300 PASS. dotnet build api/Wallow.slnx -> 0 Warning(s) 0 Error(s) (warnings-as-errors). dotnet format api/Wallow.slnx scoped with --include to my 6 files -> clean, no solution-wide run (siblings have in-flight edits).

ISSUES=none.
VERIFY:
[✓] IOrganizationAccessPolicy grants access ONLY to admin members of that specific org — OrganizationAccessPolicy.IsOrganizationAdminAsync (Wallow.Identity.Infrastructure/Services/OrganizationAccessPolicy.cs:15-27) loads the target org via repository.GetByIdAsync and checks organization.Members.Any(m => m.UserId == userId && m.Role == OrgMemberRole.Admin) — scoped to the single organizationId param, no blanket role/claim check anywhere in the class. Controller gate (OrganizationsController.cs:38-47) is `orgId == tenantContext.TenantId.Value || User.IsGlobalAdmin() || (ownership lookup)` — IsGlobalAdmin() remains the only blanket cross-tenant escape hatch. repo-wide `grep -rn 'GetRoles().Contains' api/src` → 0 hits (re-verified independently).
