title: R24 scope splitting per module (design decision) + record F12 as resolved
description:
Two items were deliberately scoped OUT of Wallow-pu6a.6.5 (backend guardrails). This bead
carries the one that is genuinely open, and records the resolution of the one that turned
out not to be.

SOURCE DECODER (needed to read the references below). The review doc
docs/plans/2026-07-27/0908-sdk-review.md contains no literal "F<n>"/"R<n>" text anywhere.
"F<n>" = row n of section 2's numbered findings table (rows 1-14). "R<n>" = item n of
section 5's numbered recommended-sequence list (items 1-25). Any bead citing these numbers
needs this decode step first.

=== ITEM 1 (OPEN, the actual work): R24 second half, scope splitting ===

R24 verbatim, section 5 "Ongoing guardrails", item 24:
  "Audience-restrict access tokens; split scopes per module so a route compromise doesn't
   yield platform-wide authority."

The FIRST clause (audience restriction) is implemented under Wallow-pu6a.6.5: access tokens
get audience "wallow-api" stamped at issuance, and the OpenIddict validation handler
requires it via AddAudiences. The SECOND clause was scoped out because it is a design
decision, not a fix -- 6.5 was a test-first guardrail bead with a fixed set of findings to
close, and there is no single obviously-correct scope-splitting shape to write a failing
test against.

Why the second clause still matters even with the first one shipped: Wallow is a modular
MONOLITH. Every module is served by the same host on the same origin, so a single audience
value is platform-wide BY CONSTRUCTION. Audience restriction stops a token minted for
Wallow being replayed at some other system; it does nothing about the case R24 actually
describes, where a route compromise inside Wallow yields authority over every other module.
Shipping only the first clause and calling R24 done would leave the stated threat model
unaddressed.

What already exists (do not rebuild it):
  - Scopes are already per-module by naming convention and carry a "category" field in
    api/seed.json (apiScopes: users.*, roles.* categorised "Identity"; inquiries.*,
    notifications.*, storage.*, etc.).
  - Scopes are already ENFORCED, not decorative: PermissionExpansionMiddleware
    (api/src/Modules/Identity/Wallow.Identity.Infrastructure/Authorization/) maps granted
    scopes to permission claims via ScopePermissionMapper, for user tokens
    (ExpandUserScopes) and service-account tokens (ExpandServiceAccountScopes) alike, and
    [HasPermission] gates the endpoints.
  - ScopeSubsetValidator already stops a client requesting scopes beyond its grant.

So the gap is NOT "scopes don't exist" or "scopes aren't checked". The gap is that one
access token carries the union of everything the client was granted, and every module
honours every scope in it. A compromised route that can exfiltrate or misuse a token gets
whatever that token's full scope set allows across all seven modules.

The decision this bead must make first (this is design work, not implementation):
  (a) Per-module audiences -- issue/accept tokens whose aud names the module
      (e.g. wallow-api.storage), so a token is only valid at the module it was minted for.
      Strongest, but the monolith shares one resource-server pipeline, so it needs a real
      per-request audience check and a story for requests that legitimately span modules.
  (b) Down-scoped tokens -- keep one audience, but have clients request narrow scope sets
      per use, so the union is small by habit. Cheapest; relies on client discipline, which
      a fork will not inherit.
  (c) Enforce module ownership of scopes -- make it a build/architecture-test rule that a
      module's endpoints may only be gated by permissions derived from that module's own
      scope category, so cross-module authority requires an explicit, visible grant. Fits
      the repo's existing Wallow.Architecture.Tests idiom and is fork-inheritable, which
      R22's rationale argues is what matters most for a fork-first platform.

Recommendation to whoever picks this up: (c) is the best value-for-risk and matches how
this repo already enforces module boundaries; (a) is the correct long-term answer if the
monolith is ever split. Decide explicitly and record the reasoning, because "we did the
audience half" is otherwise going to read as R24 complete.

Implementing it would involve: agreeing the shape above; the seed.json scope catalogue and
its category field; ScopePermissionMapper + PermissionExpansionMiddleware; probably a new
guard in api/tests/Wallow.Architecture.Tests; and, for option (a), the AddAudiences
registration in IdentityInfrastructureExtensions plus the SetResources calls in
TokenController that Wallow-pu6a.6.5 introduces.

=== ITEM 2 (RESOLVED -- NO WORK NEEDED, recorded so it is not re-opened) ===

The open question raised during 6.5 was whether review finding row 12 was fully closed, and
whether bead Wallow-pu6a.3.3's "/api/** path-allowlist enforcement test (F12b)" covered the
same finding. Verified during 6.5 scouting; it does, and both halves of row 12 are closed.

F12 verbatim, section 2 findings table row 12 (severity Low, refs "proxy.ts;
handlers.ts:431"):
  "No path allowlist on /api/** (reaches /connect/*); /bff/logout is a GET with no CSRF
   check (logout CSRF)."

Half one -- path allowlist. CLOSED by Wallow-pu6a.3.3 (already closed). packages/sdk/src/
server/proxy.ts declares API_PREFIX "/api" as "the only path prefix this proxy forwards"
and rejects anything else before any other processing, using a segment-boundary test rather
than a bare startsWith so "/apifoo" cannot slip through. Test coverage: "createApiProxy path
allowlist" describe block in packages/sdk/src/server/proxy.test.ts.

Half two -- logout CSRF. CLOSED, though not by a bead that named F12; it came in with the
web-standard handler port. The logout handler in packages/sdk/src/server/handlers.ts now
rejects any non-POST with 405, then requires a CSRF header matching the session token via
csrfTokenMatches, and destroys nothing on either rejection path (a rejected logout that
still cleared cookies would be the same denial of service wearing a 403). Test coverage:
packages/sdk/src/server/handlers.test.ts has the 405 rejection theory plus CSRF
missing/mismatch/crosstalk/valid cases.

Conclusion: F12 needs no further work. It is documented here because the question was raised
and left open in 6.5's report, and the next person to read that report should find the
answer rather than re-investigate.
acceptance_criteria: A decision is recorded on this bead for how scopes are split per module (per-module audiences / down-scoped tokens / architecture-enforced module scope ownership), with the reasoning. If the decision is to implement, the change lands with a test that fails without it -- following the repo's test-first convention -- and ./scripts/run-tests.sh stays green. If the decision is to defer or accept the risk, that is recorded explicitly so R24 is not silently treated as complete by its audience half alone. No work is required for F12; the bead documents why.
notes: Closed as a deferral: R24's second half (per-module scope splitting) is explicitly deferred / risk-accepted by Bryan on 2026-07-29 — R24 is NOT complete via its audience half alone. F12 remains fully resolved as documented in the description. Reopen this bead if scope splitting becomes relevant (recommendation on record: option (c), architecture-enforced module scope ownership).
close_reason: Closed by Bryan: not necessary right now

title: Offline users get generic error instead of 'unable to reach the server' — status===undefined dead code
description:
Four wallow-auth error-mapper functions distinguish "server never answered" (offline/network fault) from an HTTP error by checking `readMember(cause, "status") === undefined`:
- apps/wallow-auth/src/features/login/otp-result.ts:115 (sendOtpFailureMessage) and :149 (verifyOtpFailureMessage)
- apps/wallow-auth/src/features/login/auth-result.ts:338 (loginFailureMessage)
- apps/wallow-auth/src/features/login/magic-link-result.ts:122 (sendMagicLinkFailureMessage) and :146 (verifyMagicLinkFailureMessage)

But `toWallowError` (packages/sdk/src/runtime-config.ts:50-80), wired as the error interceptor on every generated client instance via `wireWallowErrorInterceptor` (create-sdk.ts), ALWAYS supplies a numeric `status` — falling back to `FALLBACK_ERROR_STATUS = 500` (runtime-config.ts:36,62) for a transport fault (no response at all). So `status` is never `undefined` by the time it reaches these mappers; the `status === undefined` branch in all five call sites is unreachable dead code.

Net effect: a user with no network connection is told "An error occurred. Please try again." (the generic tail) instead of "Unable to reach the server." (UNREACHABLE_MESSAGE) — the intended, more actionable copy for that case.

This is a contract decision, not a one-line fix: packages/sdk/src/runtime-config.test.ts:203 explicitly asserts the 500 fallback for a transport fault, so the SDK side is pinned as designed. The fix has to happen on the wallow-auth mapper side — likely keying off a distinguishable code/status the interceptor can still produce for a genuine transport fault (e.g. a sentinel status, or a WallowError.code the interceptor sets only for the `error instanceof Error` branch), or by re-deriving "offline" some other way (e.g. `navigator.onLine`, or catching a fetch-level TypeError before it reaches toWallowError).

DISCOVERED BY: unmocking wallow-auth screen specs onto the real SDK harness (Wallow-pu6a.5.1) — the old `vi.mock` specs stubbed the SDK facade directly and were green while this was broken; 3 tests (LoginScreen x1, MagicLinkLoginForm x2) are currently kept at full assertion strength but unreachable/red because of this, pending this fix.
notes: RESOLVED BY Wallow-sx3r (duplicate of this bead — same five call sites). The remedy is the one this bead proposed: the SDK's error interceptor now sets a code only reachable from its 'error instanceof Error' branch. toWallowError reports a request that never landed as 503 + code NETWORK_ERROR — the same pair server/proxy.ts already raises for a dropped BFF->API forward — and all five wallow-auth mappers key on it via a new exported isServerUnreachable(cause) predicate in auth-result.ts. The 'status === undefined' dead arms are deleted from auth-result.ts, magic-link-result.ts (x2) and otp-result.ts (x2). Full report on Wallow-sx3r. wallow-auth 667/668 (the one remainder is Wallow-a6jr, unrelated), packages/sdk 917/917, wallow-web 471/471. Safe to close alongside sx3r.
close_reason: Duplicate of Wallow-sx3r, which fixes all 5 named call sites (auth-result.ts, magic-link-result.ts x2, otp-result.ts x2) via isServerUnreachable() keyed on the SDK's new 503 NETWORK_ERROR contract — verified by reading the code and rerunning the suites. See Wallow-sx3r for full verification detail.

title: docker-compose.test.yml shares the dev-infra Compose project name, so e2e.sh teardown kills the running dev stack
description:
SYMPTOM: running any docker-compose.test.yml teardown (including scripts/e2e.sh's own 'docker compose -f docker/docker-compose.test.yml down -v --remove-orphans') while the base dev-infra stack (docker/docker-compose.yml: wallow-postgres, wallow-valkey, wallow-garage, wallow-mailpit, wallow-alloy, wallow-docs, wallow-grafana-lgtm) is up will STOP AND REMOVE those base containers as orphans, even though they are not defined in docker-compose.test.yml.

ROOT CAUSE: docker/.env sets COMPOSE_PROJECT_NAME=wallow. Docker Compose resolves the 'project directory' (where it looks for .env) to the directory of the first compose file passed with -f, NOT the caller's cwd. Since docker-compose.test.yml also lives in docker/, it picks up the same docker/.env and therefore resolves to the SAME project name ('wallow') as the base stack. 'down --remove-orphans' then treats any running container carrying the project=wallow label that is not a service in the currently-loaded compose file as an orphan and removes it -- which includes the entire base stack.

Reproduced directly during verification of Wallow-pu6a.4.5: running scripts/e2e.sh's teardown wiped the already-running dev stack (postgres/valkey/garage/mailpit/alloy/docs/grafana-lgtm containers all disappeared from 'docker ps -a').

BLAST RADIUS IS LIMITED: named volumes are NOT shared -- docker-compose.test.yml's volumes (test_postgres_data, test_valkey_data, test_garage_data, test_garage_meta) are distinct from the base stack's (postgres_data, valkey_data, garage_data, garage_meta), so no data is destroyed. Only the containers themselves are stopped/removed.

RESTORE COMMAND (if this happens to you): cd docker && docker compose up -d -- this recreates the base containers against their existing (untouched) named volumes. Confirmed via postgres log 'Database directory appears to contain a database; Skipping initialization' -- full data recovery, just a ~15s restart.

FIX DIRECTION: give docker-compose.test.yml its own Compose project name so it can never collide with (or remove orphans from) the base dev-infra project. Two options: (a) add a top-level 'name: wallow-test' field to docker-compose.test.yml (Compose v2 supports this directly in the file, no env/flag needed at every call site), or (b) have scripts/e2e.sh pass '-p wallow-test' (or 'COMPOSE_PROJECT_NAME=wallow-test') explicitly to every docker compose invocation. Option (a) is preferred: it fixes every future invocation (manual docker compose -f docker-compose.test.yml ... too), not just the ones scripts/e2e.sh happens to wrap. After the fix, verify: bring up the base stack (cd docker && docker compose up -d), then run ./scripts/e2e.sh end to end, and confirm 'docker ps' still shows the base stack's containers running throughout and after teardown.

Related repo-wide memory already filed: docker-compose-test-project-collision (bd remember).
acceptance_criteria: docker-compose.test.yml (or scripts/e2e.sh) is scoped to a Compose project name distinct from the base dev-infra stack's ('wallow'). Verification: with the base stack up (cd docker && docker compose up -d), run ./scripts/e2e.sh to completion; 'docker ps' must show the base stack's containers (wallow-postgres, wallow-valkey, wallow-garage, wallow-mailpit, wallow-alloy, wallow-docs, wallow-grafana-lgtm) still running unaffected both during and after the e2e run.
notes:
FIX IMPLEMENTED (two layers, because option (a) alone proved insufficient): (1) top-level 'name: wallow-test' added to docker/docker-compose.test.yml; (2) scripts/e2e.sh now passes --project-name wallow-test in its COMPOSE array. VERIFIED during implementation: COMPOSE_PROJECT_NAME from docker/.env OUTRANKS the compose file's top-level name: field ('docker compose -f docker/docker-compose.test.yml config' still resolved name=wallow after adding name:), so the -p flag in e2e.sh is the load-bearing fix; the name: field covers environments without that env var, and the file header comment warns manual invokers to pass -p wallow-test when COMPOSE_PROJECT_NAME is set. Quick verification passed: with the dev stack up, 'docker compose -p wallow-test -f docker/docker-compose.test.yml down -v --remove-orphans' left all running containers untouched (before/after docker ps diff empty). Full ./scripts/e2e.sh acceptance run in progress. Follow-up for CONCURRENT e2e runs colliding with each other filed separately.
SECOND FIX FOUND DURING THE ACCEPTANCE RUN: the full e2e.sh run confirmed the project-name fix (test stack ran as wallow-test-*, teardown removed only wallow-test resources, all 7 dev-infra containers survived untouched), but the wallow-auth suite failed 6/30 — every failure was a vite-error-overlay from '[plugin:vite:import-analysis] Failed to resolve import @bc-solutions-coder/forms'. Cause: packages/forms (the newest workspace package) had no dist/, and e2e.sh's local mode only built @bc-solutions-coder/sdk before starting the dev server. Fixed e2e.sh to build the dev server's whole workspace dependency closure instead: pnpm --filter '@bc-solutions-coder/wallow-auth^...' build — covers sdk, forms, ui, styles, web-shell, testing, and any future package automatically. Rerun with E2E_SKIP_IMAGE_BUILD=1 in progress.
THIRD ISSUE DIAGNOSED AND FIXED (cold-start flake in the wallow-auth suite): after the forms-dist fix, the next cold e2e.sh run still failed 2/30 (login.spec, magic-link.spec) — Playwright call logs showed the page NAVIGATING mid-wait ('navigated to /login' while waiting for login-signed-in). Cause: Vite dep re-optimization full reload. e2e/global-setup.ts only warmed '/', so routes first visited during specs (/login pulls in the freshly built @bc-solutions-coder/forms graph) triggered 'optimized dependencies changed. reloading' MID-SPEC, wiping in-flight form state; whichever parallel specs had a pending submit lost. Proof: the two specs pass in isolation against the same stack, and three consecutive full-suite runs against a warm dev server pass 30/30 (rules out rate limiting / seeded-credential interference; reset-password.spec deliberately resets to the same password). Fix: global-setup now walks WARMUP_PATHS (/, /login, /register, /forgot-password, /reset-password) to hydration so the one-time reload happens in setup. Verification: cleared apps/wallow-auth/node_modules/.vite and re-ran the full ./scripts/e2e.sh from cold.

title: Stream response bodies in web-shell host writers (unblocks SSE)
description:
Both web-shell host writers fully BUFFER every response body before writing it to
the Node socket, so no response can reach the browser incrementally. This makes
server-sent events, chunked/progressive responses, and large downloads impossible
through either host, regardless of what the SDK proxy does upstream.

  - packages/web-shell/src/server/standalone-host.ts:80-98 — writeWebResponse()
    ends with `res.end(Buffer.from(await response.arrayBuffer()))`, which awaits
    the ENTIRE upstream body before the first byte is written.
  - packages/web-shell/src/server/dev-server.ts:129-142 — same function, ending
    `const body: string = response.body === null ? "" : await response.text()`.
    This one has a second defect: decoding to a string corrupts any non-UTF-8
    body. Dev currently gets away with it because Vite's own middlewares serve
    the binary assets, but it is a trap for anything the app itself streams
    (a proxied PDF, an avatar, a file download through /api/**).

Both writers handle status and multiple Set-Cookie correctly (getSetCookie() +
appendHeader) and must keep doing so — only the body write changes.
design:
Measured during the Wallow-pu6a.3.1 spike against a slow SSE upstream (4 events,
150ms apart), time to first client-visible byte:

  - buffered SDK proxy (today) ................................ TTFB 614ms, 1 chunk
  - streamed Response body + these buffering host writers ..... TTFB 612ms, 1 chunk
  - streamed Response body + a streaming host writer .......... TTFB 2ms,   4 chunks

The third row is byte-identical output to the first, just delivered incrementally.
The middle row is the point of this bead: bead Wallow-pu6a.3.3 changes the SDK
proxy to return `upstream.body` (a ReadableStream) instead of
`new Uint8Array(await upstream.arrayBuffer())`, but that buys nothing end-to-end
while the host re-buffers it one layer out. The SDK-side change is still correct
on its own (it drops a full-body copy from the proxy's memory profile), so the
two beads are independent -- this one is not blocked by 3.3, and landing it alone
also fixes the dev-server binary-corruption defect.

FIX DIRECTION
Replace the terminal buffering write in BOTH writers with a stream pipe, keeping
the null-body early return and the existing status/Set-Cookie handling untouched:

    if (response.body === null) { res.end(); return; }
    await response.body.pipeTo(Writable.toWeb(res) as WritableStream<Uint8Array>);

(`Writable` from "node:stream"; `pipeTo` closes the response when the stream ends.)

Watch for:
  - Do NOT set content-length when streaming; let Node use chunked encoding.
  - Client disconnect mid-stream rejects the pipeTo promise -- swallow/log it
    rather than letting it surface as an unhandled rejection or a 500.
  - Keep the two writers' behavior identical after this change; the only reason
    they differ today is the text-vs-bytes decision this bead removes.
  - Both files' existing multi-Set-Cookie regression tests
    (standalone-host.test.ts:171-180, dev-server.test.ts:386-395) must stay green.

The dev-server additionally reads the REQUEST body as a stream already
(dev-server.ts:120-125, `Readable.toWeb(req)` with duplex:"half"), so making the
response direction symmetric is the natural completion of that shape.
acceptance_criteria:
Both writeWebResponse implementations (standalone-host.ts, dev-server.ts) stream
the response body instead of buffering it. A test per host proves a slow
multi-chunk upstream is delivered incrementally -- first chunk observed well
before the upstream finishes, and the concatenated output byte-identical to the
buffered result. A binary (non-UTF-8) body survives the dev-server writer
unchanged. Existing multi-Set-Cookie and status tests stay green, and pnpm check
is green.
notes: SCOUT: OBSOLETE AS WRITTEN -- close as obsolete, not implement. Both files this task names (packages/web-shell/src/server/standalone-host.ts and dev-server.ts) were DELETED OUTRIGHT in bead Wallow-pu6a.4.5 (closed; D9 Nitro fallback confirmed NOT taken, so FULL deletion scope applied -- verified via bd show Wallow-pu6a.4.5's closing note, which lists the entire packages/web-shell/src/server/ dir as deleted, both host writers + their specs included). Verified independently: packages/web-shell/src/server/ does not exist on disk (only src/index.ts, src/query-client.ts, src/devtools-gating.test.ts remain -- the browser-only barrel). Grepped repo-wide for writeWebResponse / toWeb(res) / res.end(Buffer -- ZERO hits anywhere (apps included). apps/CLAUDE.md confirms: 'Hosting is per-app and owned by Start... dev-server.ts, vite.ssr.config.ts, and the web-shell ./server presets are all deleted' -- each app now runs on TanStack Start's own Nitro/h3 server (vite.config.ts: tanstackStart+react+nitro), which handles Response/ReadableStream bodies natively; there is no bespoke Node-socket host writer left anywhere for this task's fix to apply to. Separately verified the SDK-side half this task's design says is independent (bead 3.3, closed) DID land: packages/sdk/src/server/proxy.ts:810 already does 'return new Response(upstream.body, {...})' (streams the upstream ReadableStream through, not buffered) -- the only remaining .text()/.arrayBuffer() calls in proxy.ts (line 463, 784) are for ERROR-body parsing (RFC 7807) and request-body buffering for retry-replay respectively, not the success-path response body. RECOMMENDATION: close 6.8 as obsolete with a note that its premise (web-shell HOST writers exist and buffer) was invalidated by 4.5's deletion; if end-to-end streaming (SSE etc.) through the apps' own Nitro/h3 servers is still a concern, that would need a NEW task scoped against Nitro's response handling, not this one.

title: Widen typed-success invariant to non-204 2xx; fix untyped 201 on POST /v1/inquiries/{id}/comments
description: POST /v1/inquiries/{id}/comments declares a 201 whose content carries no schema — the same defect Wallow-pu6a.2.3 fixed for 200s, one status code over. Discovered while writing Wallow-pu6a.2.5's openapi-regen.test.ts invariant (deliberately scoped to 200 only, matching 2.3's AC, so this does not fail that test today).
design: 1) Add [ProducesResponseType(typeof(T), 201)] (or equivalent) for the inquiries comment-creation action. 2) Widen openapi-regen.test.ts's findOperationsWithUntypedSuccess (packages/sdk/src/openapi-regen.test.ts) from checking only responses['200'] to all non-204 2xx status codes — the detector already takes the status code as data, so this is a one-line change. 3) Regenerate the SDK snapshot.
notes:
GREEN (implementer, 2026-07-30).

RED-THEN-GREEN OBSERVATION (part 2 done FIRST, as instructed):
Widened findOperationsWithUntypedSuccess to all non-204 2xx BEFORE touching the backend, then ran
'pnpm --filter @bc-solutions-coder/sdk exec vitest run src/openapi-regen.test.ts' against the
UNCHANGED committed snapshot. It FAILED, and failed on exactly the predicted operation:
  AssertionError: expected [ 'POST /v1/inquiries/{id}/comments' ] to deeply equal []
  Test Files 1 failed | Tests 1 failed | 14 passed (15)
After the controller fix + snapshot regen the same test passes. The invariant therefore has teeth:
it was red before the fix and green after, not passing on both sides.

FILES:
  api/src/Modules/Inquiries/Wallow.Inquiries.Api/Contracts/InquiryCommentCreatedResponse.cs (new)
  api/src/Modules/Inquiries/Wallow.Inquiries.Api/Controllers/InquiriesController.cs
  packages/sdk/src/openapi-regen.test.ts
  packages/sdk/openapi/v1.json
  packages/sdk/src/generated/{types.gen.ts,index.ts,@tanstack/react-query.gen.ts}

SYMBOLS: sealed record InquiryCommentCreatedResponse(Guid Id) in namespace Wallow.Inquiries.Api.Contracts.
TS: export type InquiryCommentCreatedResponse = { id: string }; InquiriesAddCommentResponses['201']
went from 'unknown' to InquiryCommentCreatedResponse, and hey-api now also emits
InquiriesAddCommentResponse (the union alias it only emits once a 2xx is typed).

PART 1 — why the 201 was untyped and why the fix is shaped this way:
AddComment returns Task<IActionResult> (no inferable body) and declared a bare
[ProducesResponseType(StatusCodes.Status201Created)], while returning Created(uri, new { Id = ... }) —
an ANONYMOUS type, which is why no schema could be harvested. Replacing the anonymous type with the
named record and declaring [ProducesResponseType(typeof(InquiryCommentCreatedResponse), 201)] leaves
the wire shape byte-identical ({"id":"<guid>"}) — the existing controller test
AddComment_WithValidRequest_ReturnsCreated still asserts CreatedResult + Location and still passes.

SWEEP FOR OTHER OFFENDERS (asked for explicitly — I did NOT narrow the invariant to make it pass):
Scanned the committed snapshot for every non-204 2xx with no content key OR no content[].schema:
POST /v1/inquiries/{id}/comments was the ONLY one, both before and (now zero) after. Nothing was
suppressed or exempted. Source-side there are exactly TWO bare [ProducesResponseType(201)] in api/src:
this one and Identity InvitationsController.Create — the latter is NOT a defect, because it returns
ActionResult<InvitationResponse>, so ApiResponseTypeProvider fills the attribute's null Type from the
inferred return type and the snapshot's 201 there already carries a schema. Verified against the
snapshot, not assumed.

SNAPSHOT REGEN METHOD (reproduced CI's recipe, not a hand-edit):

R23/F13 FallbackPolicy (2 failing) — SCOUT CORRECTION, read this before implementing. The scout reported 'grepped Program.cs for FallbackPolicy — zero hits, not yet applied'. That is true of Program.cs but the conclusion is wrong: PermissionAuthorizationPolicyProvider.GetFallbackPolicyAsync (Wallow.Identity.Infrastructure/Authorization) already HARDCODES a RequireAuthenticatedUser policy, and AuthorizationMiddleware honours it, so endpoints are NOT anonymous today. The residual defect is different and narrower: (a) AuthorizationOptions.FallbackPolicy is never set in AddIdentityAuthorization, so deny-by-default is invisible at the registration site and any fork that replaces the custom policy provider — the documented way to add a requirement — silently loses it with nothing failing; (b) the provider ignores a configured fallback entirely. Fix = set options.FallbackPolicy in AddIdentityAuthorization's AddAuthorization callback, and change the provider to 'await _fallbackProvider.GetFallbackPolicyAsync() ?? <deny-anonymous>'. The '?? deny-anonymous' half is load-bearing: FallbackAuthorizationPolicyTests.GetFallbackPolicyAsync_WithNoConfiguredFallback_ShouldStillDenyAnonymous passes today and must keep passing, so pure delegation alone will regress it. Do NOT double-implement F13 and R23 — one fix, as the scout noted.

Issuance: TokenController must set the API resource on the signed-in principal for BOTH grant paths (HandleAuthorizationCodeOrRefreshAsync and HandleClientCredentialsAsync) — OpenIddict derives aud from principal resources. Validation: the AddValidation block in IdentityInfrastructureExtensions must call AddAudiences(...). The audience literal the tests pin is 'wallow-api'. AccessTokenAudienceTests also requires the literal to appear in at least 2 files under api/src/Modules/Identity, which is what forces both halves rather than one. F8 AppsController caller-supplied ClientType (5 failing). AppsController.Register at line ~76 forwards request.ClientType straight to RegisterClientAsync, and OpenIddictDeveloperAppService.RegisterClientAsync (line ~29) turns the string 'public' into a secret-less OpenIddict public client. Tests pin REJECTION (ValidationProblem + service never invoked), case-insensitively, not silent coercion — chosen to match how the same action already answers bad scopes and bad redirect URIs, so the caller learns the platform does not issue public clients. Register_WithConfidentialClientType_RegistersAConfidentialClient passes today and pins that the non-public path keeps working. Deliberately NOT tested: removing ClientType from RegisterAppRequest — that would move the OpenAPI snapshot and collide with the sibling SDK work.

title: Hygiene: testing/sdk/ui dependency + config cleanups
description: Hygiene track: small dependency/config cleanups across packages/testing, packages/sdk, and packages/ui, plus folding redundant per-app re-export shims if Phase 3/4 churn left them pointless.
design:
- `packages/testing`: replace its hand-rolled `deepMerge` with vitest's own `mergeConfig`.
- `packages/sdk`: align `@types/node` to `^24` and its `typescript` version pin with the apps.
- `packages/ui`: only if the CVA/tailwind-merge class-override bug is actually hit in practice, adjust its `clsx` + `tailwind-merge` usage (do not preemptively "fix" a bug that hasn't manifested).
- Fold each app's per-app `src/lib/branding.ts` re-export shim into one shared export IF Phase 3/4 churn has left them redundant duplicates of each other.
acceptance_criteria: `packages/testing` uses `mergeConfig` instead of a hand-rolled `deepMerge`; `packages/sdk`'s `@types/node`/`typescript` pins match the apps; `packages/ui`'s clsx/tailwind-merge usage is unchanged unless the override bug was actually observed (in which case it's fixed with a regression test); redundant per-app branding re-export shims are folded into one shared export where genuinely redundant. `pnpm check` green.
notes:
SCOUT: four sub-items, mixed obsolete/real status. (1) packages/testing hand-rolled deepMerge: EXISTS at packages/testing/src/vitest-projects.ts:91-99 (recursive plain-object merge used at line 141: 'return { node: deepMerge(node, nodeProjectOverrides), browser }'), REAL work remains -- replace with vitest's own mergeConfig (import from 'vitest/config'). (2) packages/sdk @types/node/typescript version alignment: VERIFIED mismatch -- packages/sdk/package.json:50 pins @types/node ^22.20.0 while apps/wallow-web/package.json:36 and apps/wallow-auth/package.json:33 both pin ^24.0.0 (matches .nvmrc's Node 24) -- REAL, align sdk to ^24. ALSO found a typescript version mismatch not explicitly named in the task's acceptance text but implied by 'typescript version pin with the apps': packages/sdk/package.json:52 pins typescript to the EXACT version '6.0.3' (no caret) while both apps pin '^5.6.0' -- this is a MAJOR version gap (TypeScript 6 vs 5), not just a patch drift; flag explicitly for the implementer since this could be a deliberate SDK-specific bump (Vite 8 / vitest 4 in sdk's devDependencies may require TS 6) rather than an oversight -- verify before blindly matching the apps' ^5.6.0. (3) packages/ui clsx+tailwind-merge override bug: cn.ts (packages/ui/src/core/cn.ts) already composes clsx+tailwind-merge (tailwind-merge ^3.6.0 per package.json:37) and is used in 40+ component files/tests with no open bug report found in bd notes or memories -- task's own acceptance criteria says leave UNCHANGED unless the bug has actually manifested; found no evidence it has. DEFER/no-op unless the implementer finds a live repro. (4) branding.ts re-export shims: VERIFIED genuinely redundant -- apps/wallow-auth/src/lib/branding.ts and apps/wallow-web/src/lib/branding.ts are BYTE-IDENTICAL in their export list (both re-export the same 15 names from @bc-solutions-coder/styles), differing ONLY in their doc-comment wording. REAL, fold-able: candidate target is a new packages/styles subpath or a shared re-export the two apps both import, OR move the shim itself into packages/styles as a convenience export so neither app needs its own src/lib/branding.ts file at all -- check whether apps/examples/minimal-app has a THIRD copy of this shim before designing the fold (grep showed only wallow-auth+wallow-web have src/lib/branding.ts, so check minimal-app doesn't need the same treatment separately).
GREEN: all four hygiene sub-items resolved (3 changed, 1 no-op per its own acceptance).

(1) packages/testing deepMerge -> mergeConfig. Removed the hand-rolled deepMerge/isPlainObject from packages/testing/src/vitest-projects.ts; nodeProjectOverrides now folds in via vitest/config's mergeConfig (Vite's own). Semantic delta to know: mergeConfig CONCATENATES arrays where deepMerge REPLACED them (nested plain objects still merge, so the preset's name/environment/include/exclude survive). No consumer passes nodeProjectOverrides today (both apps use only nodeTsxSpecs/extraBrowserOptimizeDeps), so nothing in tree changes behaviour. Added one spec, 'concatenates array fields onto the preset's', to vitest-projects.test.ts to lock the new semantics; the four existing nodeProjectOverrides assertions pass unchanged. mergeConfig returns Record<string, any>, so the result is cast back to VitestNodeProject (no 'as any').

(2) packages/sdk pins aligned to the apps. @types/node ^22.20.0 -> ^24.0.0 and typescript '6.0.3' (exact) -> ^5.6.0, matching apps/wallow-web, apps/wallow-auth, minimal-app, ui, styles, testing, web-shell (all ^5.6.0 / ^24.0.0). VERIFIED the scout's flag that the TS6 pin might be deliberate: it is NOT, it is inverted-stale. packages/sdk/tsconfig.build.json carried a rationale block saying the pin exists 'because the workspace is on TS7 and @hey-api/openapi-ts@0.64 is not TS7-compatible (peer typescript ^5.5.3)'. The workspace is NOT on TS7 (nothing resolves above 5.9.3) and openapi-ts is now ^0.99.0 whose peer is still typescript ^5.5.3 -- so the 6.0.3 pin put the SDK's own codegen OUTSIDE its supported peer range. Aligning to ^5.6.0 (resolves 5.9.3) both matches the apps and satisfies openapi-ts. Rewrote that stale comment block (it also still described tsup, which the Vite-lib-mode migration replaced, and apps/tanstack-min, which no longer exists). pnpm install updated pnpm-lock.yaml; the delta is scoped to the packages/sdk importer plus dropping the now-unreferenced typescript@6.0.3 / @types/node@22.20.1 / undici-types@6.21.0 entries -- bead 6.4's staged lockfile content is untouched.

(3) packages/ui clsx/tailwind-merge: NO-OP, as the acceptance text directs. Confirmed no live repro of the CVA/tailwind-merge override bug anywhere (packages/ui/src/core/cn.ts unchanged, no failing override test, no bd note reporting one). Left alone.

(4) branding shims FOLDED (full delete, not a re-export slim-down). Deleted apps/wallow-auth/src/lib/branding.ts and apps/wallow-web/src/lib/branding.ts outright; every importer now reads @bc-solutions-coder/styles directly. Decisive evidence this is the convention rather than a regression: apps/examples/minimal-app already imports @bc-solutions-coder/styles directly in src/routes/__root.tsx and src/features/hello/HelloCard.tsx with no shim of its own -- the two shims were the leftovers, and no third copy needed the same treatment. Scout's grep for 'lib/branding' MISSED two same-directory importers ('./branding'): apps/wallow-web/src/lib/site-links.ts and both apps' src/lib/brand-assets.test.ts -- caught by typecheck.
  Test seams rewired: apps/wallow-web/src/routes/index.gate.test.tsx and index.ssr-gate.test.ts mocked the shim path with a FULL-REPLACEMENT factory (vi.mock('../lib/branding', () => branding), only forkBranding+appIconUrl). Both now use the sanctioned partial-override form: vi.mock('@bc-solutions-coder/styles', async (importOriginal) => ({ ...(await importOriginal()), ...branding })), so every other branding export (theme rendering, asset URLs) stays real and only the landingPage.enabled flag is stood in. Strictly better than the old full replacement, which would have silently passed if the app started reading another branding export.

title: Request-id correlation: frontend WallowError to backend OTel traces
description: Add request-id correlation between the frontend and backend, and document how to use it to trace a frontend error into backend OTel traces in Grafana.
design: The BFF proxy (created in task 2.7/2.3) forwards the inbound `x-request-id` header to the upstream API, generating one when absent. `WallowError` carries this request id (extend the class/interceptor from task 4.2 if it has already landed, or the RFC 7807 passthrough logic in task 2.3 if not). Document the correlation workflow: given a `WallowError`'s request id, how to find the matching trace in Grafana's otel-lgtm stack.
acceptance_criteria: Every request through the BFF proxy carries an `x-request-id` (forwarded if present, generated if absent); `WallowError` instances expose the request id; a doc page explains how to correlate a frontend error's request id with a backend OTel trace in Grafana.
notes:
SCOUT: Real, unimplemented. BFF proxy is packages/sdk/src/server/proxy.ts (699->557 lines post-3.3 port to web-standard, closed). Grepped proxy.ts + handlers.ts + errors.ts: ZERO existing x-request-id / requestId handling anywhere in packages/sdk/src/server/. WallowError (errors.ts) currently carries status/code/title/detail only -- no request-id field. Task's own note says 'extend the class/interceptor from task 4.2 if it has already landed' -- 4.2 (minimal-app Start migration) is closed but is NOT a request-id task; there is no separate request-id interceptor bead anywhere in the epic, so this 4.2 reference in the design appears to be a misattribution/stale pointer -- build straight on proxy.ts's forwardWithResilience path + errors.ts's WallowError, not on anything from 4.2. Backend side: grepped for X-Request-Id / TraceIdentifier across api/src -- OTel/Grafana stack is otel-lgtm (Grafana at localhost:3001, per root CLAUDE.md); ASP.NET Core's HttpContext.TraceIdentifier and OTel's Activity.Current?.Id are the two backend-side correlation values to expose/log -- neither is currently forwarded to a response header for the frontend to read. New doc page goes under docs/operations/ (observability.md already exists there per docs/CLAUDE.md's structure list -- check if request-id correlation fits as a new section there vs a new page) per docs/CLAUDE.md's lowercase-kebab + toc.yml rules. NOT obsolete.

Exports REQUEST_ID_HEADER='x-request-id', MAX_REQUEST_ID_LENGTH=200, isValidRequestId(value), newRequestId(), resolveRequestId(headers). All three functions THROW 'not implemented'.
- src/errors.ts — WallowError gained 'readonly requestId?: string' and 'readonly traceId?: string' plus the matching init members. DECLARED BUT NOT ASSIGNED in the constructor: that one-line assignment is the green phase's job and is what most of the error tests are waiting on.

DESIGN THE TESTS PIN (green phase must implement exactly this):
1. TWO correlation members, not one. 'requestId' is the BFF-minted x-request-id; 'traceId' is the W3C trace id ASP.NET Core ALREADY writes into every problem details body (see the pre-existing extensions.traceId fixtures in errors.test.ts) and the id OTel exports the trace under. This is what makes the doc honest with ZERO backend changes — no C# middleware needed, so no collision with bead 6.5. Do not add backend work for this bead.
2. resolveRequestId VALIDATES before echoing: charset is a narrow token set, max 200 chars, no whitespace/control/CR-LF/markup. A caller-supplied id that fails validation is REPLACED by a generated one, never forwarded (header + log injection).
3. The proxy stamps the id at EVERY exit, not just the happy path: 404 rejected path, 401 no session, 403 CSRF, 200 success, upstream failure relayed verbatim, and 503 BFF fault. The two bodies the BFF synthesizes itself (CSRF rejection, network fault) must ALSO carry 'requestId' as a member, since a synthesized body has no upstream traceId to fall back on.
4. A reactive-401 replay reuses the SAME id on both attempts (one logical request = one trace).
5. parseProblemDetails reads requestId from the RESPONSE HEADER (signature unchanged) and traceId from the body, extensions.traceId winning over a flattened top-level traceId, exactly as readCode already prefers extensions.code.
6. Browser side: wireWallowErrorInterceptor must pass response.headers.get(REQUEST_ID_HEADER) into toWallowError's third param, and toWallowError must read traceId out of the body.
7. Doc deliverable is a NEW page docs/operations/request-correlation.md (not a section in observability.md) + a docs/toc.yml entry under Operations. The test requires it to name x-request-id, WallowError/requestId/traceId, say the BFF generates an id when the caller sends none, and mention Grafana + tempo/trace + localhost:3001.

SYMBOLS (all pre-declared by the red scaffold; no signature changed):
• isValidRequestId(value: string): boolean — length <= MAX_REQUEST_ID_LENGTH and /^[A-Za-z0-9._:-]+$/u. The '+' is what rejects the empty string (an explicit length>0 tripped oxlint no-magic-numbers). Charset admits UUID, W3C traceparent, bare hex span id, and req_01HQ8Z.4K9; rejects CR/LF, whitespace, control chars, and markup/quoting.
• newRequestId(): string — crypto.randomUUID() off the global, so it works in both runtimes with no import.
• resolveRequestId(headers: Headers): string — echoes a valid inbound header, otherwise mints. Case-insensitivity is Headers.get's, not ours.
• Private: readTraceId(problem) in BOTH server/errors.ts and runtime-config.ts — extensions.traceId wins over a flattened top-level traceId, mirroring readCode. Deliberately duplicated rather than shared: the two modules already carry their own readCode for the same reason (one takes ProblemDetails, the other a Record<string, unknown> off the browser's parsed body).

PROXY WIRING (the one structural change worth reviewing):
createApiProxy's handler body was EXTRACTED to a new module-private 'async function proxyRequest(request, requestId, config, store)'. The returned handler is now three lines: resolveRequestId, await proxyRequest, response.headers.set(REQUEST_ID_HEADER, requestId). Rationale: seven exits (404 rejected path, 401 no session ref, 401 no session, 403 CSRF, 404 unresolvable target, failure relay, success) each needed the header, and a single stamping point cannot be forgotten by a future exit. Every exit constructs a NEW Response, so the header guard is 'response' and set() is legal — no exit hands back a fetch() Response directly.
• forwardHeaders.set(REQUEST_ID_HEADER, requestId) is applied to the ForwardRequest headers, NOT per attempt, so the reactive-401 replay reuses the id (attemptForward copies request.headers into a fresh Headers per attempt).
• respondToFailure gained a third param 'requestId' and adds a 'requestId' member to the SYNTHESIZED problem body only. The UpstreamError branch still relays the API's body byte-for-byte (its traceId is the correlation key there).
• Bonus, not test-driven: logFault's header dump now includes x-request-id, so the BFF's own 'forward failed' log line names the id — this is what makes the doc's requestId-only path (CSRF/503/no-session, which never reach the API and so have no trace) actually actionable.

Two-member table, header lifecycle (kept/generated/replaced, both directions, replay reuse), a catch-block example, the Tempo lookup at localhost:3001 plus the LogQL line for Loki, and an explicit 'requestId with no traceId means it died in the BFF — read the BFF logs, not Tempo' branch. title: Spike build-time OpenAPI document emission
description: Spike build-time OpenAPI document emission (via `OpenApiDocumentsDirectory`) as an alternative to hitting a live running API to generate the document (R20 from docs/plans/2026-07-27/0908-sdk-review.md).
design: Resolve the `/alive` + `/events` delta against the existing byte-compare drift check before switching `openapi-drift.yml` off its current Postgres/Valkey stack dependency -- the build-time-emitted document currently differs from the live-served one specifically around those two operations; that delta must be understood and resolved (either fixed or explicitly accepted and documented) before the CI workflow can drop its infra dependency.
acceptance_criteria: The `/alive`/`/events` delta between build-time-emitted and live-served OpenAPI documents is either eliminated or explicitly documented as accepted; `openapi-drift.yml` either now runs without a Postgres/Valkey stack, or this task is closed with a note explaining why it still needs one.
notes:
SCOUT: Real, unimplemented spike -- no build-time OpenAPI emission exists yet (grep for OpenApiDocumentsDirectory across api/ returns zero hits; only AddOpenApi("v1", ...) at api/src/Wallow.Api/Extensions/ServiceCollectionExtensions.cs:47 for the live-served pipeline). CI workflow to modify: .github/workflows/openapi-drift.yml (currently boots Postgres+Valkey+migrations+the live API just to hit /openapi/v1.json -- see the 'Start API'/'Wait for OpenAPI endpoint' steps). The design's delta concern: /alive is mapped in api/src/Wallow.ServiceDefaults/Extensions.cs:61 and /events (SSE) in api/src/Wallow.Api/Program.cs:554, BOTH already carry .ExcludeFromDescription() -- so if build-time emission (Microsoft.Extensions.ApiDescription.Server / GetDocument.Insider) still diverges on them, it is likely an ORDERING issue (endpoints mapped after builder.Build(), per the review doc's own caveat in docs/plans/2026-07-27/0908-sdk-review.md item 20: 'GetDocument.Insider halts at builder.Build(), so /alive and /events (mapped after it) would likely be absent'), not a description-exclusion gap -- verify by diffing the two documents directly once the spike exists. Operation transformer pipeline (4 existing + the operationId one) lives in ServiceCollectionExtensions.cs:45-48/326-340. NOT obsolete -- premise still holds, real work remains.
SPIKE RESULT (2026-07-28): GO -- IMPLEMENTED AND LANDED (staged, not committed).

=== VERDICT ON THE /alive + /events DELTA: IT DOES NOT EXIST ===
Measured directly, not reasoned about. The build-time-emitted document and the
live-served document contain the SAME 115 paths and the SAME 110 component schemas.
Neither contains /alive or /events. Both endpoints carry .ExcludeFromDescription()
(Wallow.ServiceDefaults/Extensions.cs:61 and Wallow.Api/Program.cs:554), so they are
absent from BOTH documents. The scout's hypothesis that this was an ordering problem
is also wrong -- see the GetDocument.Insider finding below. Nothing needed fixing.

=== THE ONLY REAL DELTA: "servers" ===
A full recursive semantic diff of build-time vs live produced exactly ONE difference:
  /servers  BT: absent   LIVE: [{"url":"http://localhost:5001/"}]
ASP.NET Core populates document.Servers from the incoming HttpRequest, so at build time
there is no request and the key is simply not emitted. Stronger result: the live
document with its "servers" block textually removed is BYTE-IDENTICAL to the emitted
file (219843 == 219843 bytes, cmp clean). Emission is also deterministic -- two
independent builds produced byte-identical output.
"servers" is NOT cosmetic: hey-api bakes it into the generated client's default baseUrl
(packages/sdk/src/generated/client.gen.ts:18 and types.gen.ts:4 both carry
'http://localhost:5001/'). So the snapshot MUST keep it and the developer refresh flow
(boot API + scripts/generate.ts) is unchanged. The drift check now excludes "servers"
from the document comparison and asserts its committed value SEPARATELY, so the check is
no weaker than the old byte compare.

=== TWO CLAIMS IN docs/plans/2026-07-27/0908-sdk-review.md ITEM 20 ARE FALSE ===
1. "Microsoft.Extensions.ApiDescription.Server is already in the transitive graph" --
   NO. Zero hits in api/src/Wallow.Api/obj/project.assets.json. It had to be added as an
   explicit PackageReference plus a PackageVersion (central package management).
2. "GetDocument.Insider halts at builder.Build(), so /alive and /events would likely be
   absent" -- NO, not on .NET 10. The tool fully STARTS the host and stops it from the
   ApplicationLifetime.NotifyStarted hook (visible in the stack traces). Everything in
   Program.cs after builder.Build() runs, including every app.MapXxx call. This is why
   the endpoint sets match exactly, and it is also the reason for the finding below.

=== R20's PAYOFF IS ONLY PARTIALLY ACHIEVABLE: POSTGRES IS STILL REQUIRED ===
Because the host is fully started, the post-Build startup work runs too. Emission against
an unreachable Postgres FAILS at Program.cs:562 -- the DI-scoped IRecurringJobManager
block (Program.cs:558-592) calls Hangfire AddOrUpdate, which opens an Npgsql connection to
acquire a distributed lock. Verified by pointing DefaultConnection at 127.0.0.1:1: build
fails with Npgsql connect errors, no document produced.
Measured requirements (each verified by a separate run):
  * Postgres: REQUIRED.
  * Postgres migrations: NOT required. Emission against a freshly CREATE DATABASEd empty
    database succeeded and produced output byte-identical to the migrated-DB run
    (Hangfire installs its own schema). The MigrationService step is gone.
  * Valkey/Redis: NOT required. appsettings.Development.json already sets
    abortConnect=false, so the Redis-backed pieces degrade without failing the host.
    Verified twice with Redis pointed at 127.0.0.1:1.
  * Node/pnpm: NOT required. The check is now pure jq + diff.
So openapi-drift.yml still needs a Postgres service container. It no longer needs Valkey,
migrations, a live API process with a 200-second polling loop, corepack, Node, or
pnpm install. This satisfies the acceptance criterion's second branch (documented reason
the Postgres dependency remains).

=== FILES (staged, NOT committed) ===
api/Directory.Packages.props
  + PackageVersion Microsoft.Extensions.ApiDescription.Server 10.0.0 (required by central
    package management; CentralPackageTransitivePinningEnabled is on).
api/src/Wallow.Api/Wallow.Api.csproj
  + PackageReference with IncludeAssets='build; buildtransitive' + PrivateAssets='all'
    (verified it does NOT leak: building Wallow.Api.Tests emits nothing and warns nothing).
  + PropertyGroup: OpenApiGenerateDocumentsOnBuild=false (OPT-IN -- see below)
    and OpenApiDocumentsDirectory=$(MSBuildProjectDirectory)/$(BaseIntermediateOutputPath)openapi/
.github/workflows/openapi-drift.yml -- rewritten.

=== TWO NON-OBVIOUS IMPLEMENTATION CONSTRAINTS (do not regress these) ===
1. OpenApiGenerateDocumentsOnBuild MUST default to false. Merely referencing the package
   turns OpenApiGenerateDocuments (and therefore OnBuild) ON by default, which would make
   EVERY 'dotnet build' of Wallow.Api start the host and require a reachable Postgres --
   it would break plain local builds and ./scripts/run-tests.sh. CI opts in with
   -p:OpenApiGenerateDocumentsOnBuild=true. Verified: a default Release build with a bogus
   connection string succeeds in 3s and produces no obj/openapi directory.
2. OpenApiDocumentsDirectory MUST be ABSOLUTE. The package target does
   GetFullPath($(OpenApiDocumentsDirectory)), which resolves against the MSBuild PROCESS
   working directory, not the project directory -- a relative path would land wherever the
   developer happened to invoke dotnet from.
Also: the output file name is always <ProjectName>.json (Wallow.Api.json).
dotnet-getdocument 10.0.0 exposes NO file-naming switch (checked --help); the workflow
refers to the file by that name. And the emitted path is under obj/, confirmed gitignored
(.gitignore:3), so a local emission cannot dirty the tree or be committed by accident.

=== EXPECTED LOG NOISE (documented in the workflow so nobody 'fixes' it) ===
Every emission run logs a FATAL 'An error occurred starting the application /
Feature IServerAddressesFeature is not present'. Verified this is intrinsic to the tool's
stub server and appears even with real Postgres AND real Valkey present. The document is
still written and the build still succeeds. With Valkey absent there is one additional
non-fatal 'An error occurred while reading the key ring' (data protection).

=== VERIFICATION PERFORMED ===
* Baseline: the LIVE document from the running local API is byte-identical to the
  committed packages/sdk/openapi/v1.json, so the snapshot is a valid stand-in for live.
* Full local dry run of the new workflow's exact two steps against a freshly created
  EMPTY wallow_test database: emission succeeded, drift check printed 'in sync'.

title: Auto-regen SDK snapshot on backend OpenAPI-affecting merge
description: Close the last mile on auto-regenerating the SDK when the backend merges an OpenAPI-affecting change (R21 from docs/plans/2026-07-27/0908-sdk-review.md). The release-please + sdk-v* publish loop is already configured -- this task wires the missing trigger.
design: When a backend PR merges to main carrying a `feat(sdk):`-scoped commit (or equivalent OpenAPI-affecting change), automatically regenerate `packages/sdk/openapi/v1.json` + `src/generated/**` and open (or update) a PR with the result, feeding the existing release-please/sdk-v* publish pipeline.
acceptance_criteria: A merge to main containing an OpenAPI-affecting backend commit results in an automated PR regenerating the SDK snapshot, without a human needing to run the generator manually.
notes:
SCOUT: Real, unimplemented -- no GitHub Actions workflow currently regenerates the SDK snapshot on merge. Existing pieces to wire into: release-please.yml (already configures packages/sdk component w/ include-component-in-tag per review doc item 21), sdk-publish.yml (already triggers on sdk-v* tag push, unrelated trigger). openapi-drift.yml (the FAILURE-mode check) is the sibling to model the new automation-mode workflow after -- same boot-API-and-regenerate steps, but on backend-affecting merge to main it should COMMIT the regenerated packages/sdk/openapi/v1.json + src/generated/** and open a PR instead of just diffing and failing. Regen command: WALLOW_OPENAPI_URL=http://localhost:5001/openapi/v1.json pnpm --filter @bc-solutions-coder/sdk exec tsx scripts/generate.ts (packages/sdk/CLAUDE.md). NOT obsolete -- real work remains, and 6.1's spike (if it lands) would let this workflow drop its Postgres/Valkey dependency too, so scheduling 6.2 after 6.1 lands is more efficient even though bd shows no hard dependency edge.
GREEN (2026-07-28) — a backend merge to main that moves the API contract now opens an
automated SDK-regeneration PR. No human runs the generator.

=== FILES (staged, NOT committed) ===
.github/actions/openapi-document/action.yml   NEW composite action (emit + drift verdict)
.github/workflows/openapi-autoregen.yml       NEW automation-mode workflow (push: main)
.github/workflows/openapi-drift.yml           refactored onto the composite; push trigger removed
packages/sdk/CLAUDE.md                        regen bullet now describes both workflows
docs/integrations/typescript-sdk.md           new "Keeping the SDK in step with the API" section

=== DESIGN: ONE DEFINITION OF DRIFT, TWO REACTIONS ===
6.1 landed build-time emission plus a byte/jq comparison inside openapi-drift.yml. Rather
than copy that recipe into a second workflow, it moved into a composite action
.github/actions/openapi-document, which both workflows now `uses:`. It emits the document
(setup-dotnet + NuGet cache + `dotnet build -p:OpenApiGenerateDocumentsOnBuild=true`) and
outputs `document`, `drift` (true/false), `reason` (servers|document) and `diff-file`.
The check and the fix therefore cannot disagree about what drifted: the PR autoregen opens
is by construction the change that makes the drift check pass.

Reaction split:
  pull_request -> openapi-drift.yml prints the diff + the manual refresh commands, exits 1.
  push to main -> openapi-autoregen.yml rebuilds snapshot + client, force-pushes
                  automation/openapi-regen, opens or updates a PR.

=== WHY THE DRIFT WORKFLOW LOST ITS push: main TRIGGER ===
Deliberate, not an oversight. A stale snapshot on main now has an owner that fixes it;
leaving the old push trigger would paint main red for a condition already being repaired
and boot a second Postgres to learn what autoregen is learning anyway. Failure is still
surfaced: autoregen exits non-zero if the push or the `gh pr` call fails, and the auto-PR
is itself drift-checked (its paths touch packages/sdk/openapi/**).

=== THE LOAD-BEARING DETAIL: BYTE-IDENTICAL SNAPSHOT RECONSTRUCTION ===
The build-time document cannot carry "servers" (ASP.NET Core fills it from the incoming
request), but the committed snapshot MUST — hey-api bakes it into the generated client's
default baseUrl. So autoregen splices the block back in.

It splices TEXTUALLY (byte offset of the `  "paths": {` line via `grep -abm1`, then
head -c / printf / tail -c), NOT with jq. Measured reason: `jq . v1.json` is NOT a
round-trip of this document — it differs from the committed file at char 4331 (219877 vs
219921 bytes). Reserialising would have committed a whole-file reformat that the next
manual `WALLOW_OPENAPI_URL=... tsx scripts/generate.ts` refresh would immediately undo.
Both documents also end WITHOUT a trailing newline, which any line-oriented tool
(awk/sed print) would have added.

Guards in that step, each exercised: refuse if the emitted document already has a
"servers" key (would duplicate it); refuse if the `paths` line is not found; then
`jq empty` + assert servers[0].url + re-diff against the emitted document, so a bad
splice can never reach the commit.

=== SECURITY POSTURE ===
The two workflows are separate FILES on purpose, not two jobs in one. openapi-drift.yml is
the one that checks out pull-request code and it keeps `contents: read`. Only
openapi-autoregen.yml holds contents:write + pull-requests:write, and it is push/dispatch
only, so untrusted PR code is never built by a job with a writable token.
Every `${{ }}` is bound to an env var before reaching a run: block (github.sha ->
TRIGGER_SHA etc.); no interpolation inside a shell string.
Token: `secrets.RELEASE_PLEASE_TOKEN || secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN`. A PR opened with
GITHUB_TOKEN starts no workflows, which would leave the auto-PR unchecked by
openapi-drift.yml and js.yml; the existing release-please PAT avoids that, with
GITHUB_TOKEN as the fork fallback (documented in the workflow).
`git push --force` is scoped to the explicit refspec HEAD:refs/heads/automation/openapi-regen
— a bot-owned branch rebuilt from main each run.

=== RELEASE LOOP ===
Commit + PR title `feat(sdk): regenerate OpenAPI snapshot and typed client`. The commit
touches only packages/sdk/**, so release-please assigns it to the `sdk` component
(release-please-config.json, include-component-in-tag) -> minor bump of
@bc-solutions-coder/sdk -> sdk-v* tag -> sdk-publish.yml. The PR body tells the merger to
squash as `feat(sdk)!:` when the contract change removed or renamed an operation, since no
workflow can decide that.

No self-retrigger: the push paths are api/** + the two generator config files + the
workflow/action, and deliberately NOT packages/sdk/openapi/**, so merging the auto-PR
cannot loop.

=== VALIDATION (all run locally, nothing reasoned about) ===

It also resolves the local `uses: ./.github/actions/openapi-document` and its inputs.

of the splice step was copied verbatim into scratchpad scripts and driven against a

api/src/Wallow.Api/Wallow.Api.csproj -c Release -p:OpenApiGenerateDocumentsOnBuild=true`,
Build succeeded, "Writing document named 'v1' to obj/openapi/Wallow.Api.json").

  scenario 2 stale doc  -> drift=true  reason=document    (deleted an operation from the
                     snapshot; diff-file correctly shows the operation being re-added)

                     BYTE-IDENTICAL, 219921 == 219921
                     `pnpm --filter @bc-solutions-coder/sdk exec tsx scripts/generate.ts`
                     -> `diff -r` of src/generated vs baseline: IDENTICAL
                     re-run compare -> drift=false. Loop closes.
  scenario 3 wrong servers url -> drift=true reason=servers, message names both URLs;
                     splice repairs it, byte-identical again.
  guard: splice into a doc that already has servers -> exits 1, writes NO output file.
  guard: splice into a doc with no top-level paths key -> exits 1 with the intended

action's input default and the autoregen workflow's env. It is the same constant the
generated client carries; if the API's canonical local origin ever changes, both plus
packages/sdk/src/generated/client.gen.ts move together.

title: Add SDK claim helpers + typed route-context auth utilities
description: Add auth ergonomics to the SDK browser entry: claim helpers, a typed router-context contract, and SSR-safe auth-guard helpers; adopt them in wallow-web's dashboard guards.
design:
Files: SDK browser entry; `apps/wallow-web/src/routes/dashboard/route.tsx`.
- `isAdmin`/`hasRole`/`getRoles` claim helpers.
- Export a `WallowRouterContext` interface -- the typed shape apps put in router context (sdk instance, user, queryClient) -- so route files get a typed `context`.
- `requireAuth(context)` beforeLoad helper + `loginRedirect(returnTo)` href builder -- SSR-safe by construction: it must throw `redirect({ href })` (never `redirect({ to })` for an unregistered route, and never touch `location` directly -- follow the repo's existing SSR-safe redirect pattern for unauthenticated gated routes).
- Adopt these in wallow-web's dashboard guards, replacing whatever ad hoc auth-check logic exists there today.
acceptance_criteria: `isAdmin`/`hasRole`/`getRoles`, `WallowRouterContext`, `requireAuth`, and `loginRedirect` are exported from the SDK browser entry and are unit-tested; wallow-web's dashboard route guards use `requireAuth`/`loginRedirect` instead of ad hoc logic; `pnpm check` green. Commit: `feat(sdk): add claim helpers and typed route-context auth utilities`.
notes:
RED (Wallow-pu6a.5.6, claim helpers + typed route-context auth utilities).

FILES (all staged, nothing else touched):
- packages/sdk/src/claims.ts (scaffold, signatures + JSDoc only, every body throws "not implemented")
- packages/sdk/src/claims.test.ts (NEW, 30 tests)
- packages/sdk/src/route-context.ts (scaffold; WallowRouterContext + LoginRedirectOptions + RequireAuthOptions are REAL types, loginRedirect/requireAuth throw)
- packages/sdk/src/route-context.test.ts (NEW, 22 tests)
- packages/sdk/src/index.ts (+2 lines only: export * from "./claims"; export * from "./route-context"; the other index.ts deltas were already staged by earlier beads, my unstaged delta was exactly those 2 lines)
- apps/wallow-web/src/routes/dashboard/route.guards.test.ts (NEW, 6 tests, source-reading adoption spec)

TEST STATUS = confirmed failing.
- pnpm --filter @bc-solutions-coder/sdk exec vitest run src/claims.test.ts src/route-context.test.ts -> 44 failed | 8 passed (52)
- pnpm --filter @bc-solutions-coder/wallow-web exec vitest run --project node src/routes/dashboard/route.guards.test.ts -> 4 failed | 2 passed (6)
- pnpm --filter @bc-solutions-coder/sdk typecheck -> CLEAN (scaffolds typecheck)
- oxfmt + oxlint --deny-warnings on the 6 files -> clean

THE 10 TESTS THAT PASS IN RED ARE STRUCTURAL, NOT BEHAVIOURAL (expected, do not "fix"):
- 7x "browser entry surface > exports <name> from the package root" (5 in claims.test.ts, 2 in route-context.test.ts): the scaffolds are already barrel-exported, so the export-surface AC is satisfied at red. They exist so a green implementer who moves a helper to a deep path breaks something.
- 1x "WallowRouterContext > is satisfied by what the app router puts in context": the interface is real in the scaffold; the assertion is a `satisfies` type pin (enforced by `pnpm --filter sdk typecheck` and by index.test.ts's tsc test, not at runtime).
- 2x in route.guards.test.ts ("still redirects by href and never by a router `to`", "never imports the SDK's browser-only login()"): invariant-preservation assertions that are already true today and must STAY true after the rewrite.

EXPORTED SURFACE THE GREEN PHASE MUST IMPLEMENT (signatures are already in the scaffolds):
  getRoles(user: WallowUser | null | undefined): readonly string[]
  hasRole(user: WallowUser | null | undefined, role: string): boolean
  isAdmin(user: WallowUser | null | undefined): boolean
  isOperator(user: WallowUser | null | undefined): boolean
  isGlobalAdmin(user: WallowUser | null | undefined): boolean
  interface WallowRouterContext { readonly queryClient: QueryClient; readonly sdk: WallowSdk; readonly user?: WallowUser | null }
  interface LoginRedirectOptions { readonly href: string; readonly reloadDocument: true }
  loginRedirect(returnTo?: string): LoginRedirectOptions
  interface RequireAuthOptions<TUser extends WallowUser, TRedirect> { readonly user: TUser | null | undefined; readonly returnTo?: string; readonly redirect: (options: LoginRedirectOptions) => TRedirect }
  requireAuth<TUser extends WallowUser, TRedirect>(options: RequireAuthOptions<TUser, TRedirect>): TUser

DESIGN DECISIONS BAKED INTO THE RED CONTRACT (rationale, so green does not "simplify" them away):

1. redirect is INJECTED, not imported. requireAuth takes the router's redirect() as an option, so packages/sdk gains NO dependency on @tanstack/react-router (it has none today; adding one would be a new peer dep + lockfile churn in a shared tree with concurrent agents) and the guard is unit-testable with a vi.fn spy and no router. DE-RISKED: I probed assignability with a throwaway file under apps/wallow-web/src importing the real `redirect` and assigning it to `(options: LoginRedirectOptions) => ReturnType<typeof redirect>` — `pnpm exec tsc --noEmit` in wallow-web was CLEAN, so route.tsx can pass `redirect` straight through with no wrapper and no cast. Probe file deleted.

2. loginRedirect returns the OPTIONS OBJECT { href, reloadDocument: true }, not a bare href string. The bead's design line calls it an "href builder", but returning the object is what makes it SSR-safe BY CONSTRUCTION: `reloadDocument` is the thing a call site forgets, and forgetting it re-creates the not-found bug (/bff/login is a BFF endpoint outside the route tree). Call site reads `throw redirect(loginRedirect(location.pathname))`. Tests pin `reloadDocument === true` and pin that no `to` key is ever produced.

3. requireAuth takes the RESOLVED user, not the context. The bead sketch says requireAuth(context), but the user is not in wallow-web's router context — route.tsx resolves it in beforeLoad via `context.queryClient.ensureQueryData(userQueries.currentUser())`, and hard-coding that inside the SDK's browser entry would drag ./query (peer dep @tanstack/react-query, runtime import) into the barrel. So requireAuth is a synchronous narrow-or-throw over an already-resolved user; the caller keeps ownership of HOW the user is fetched. WallowRouterContext is still exported and is the typed context shape (queryClient + sdk, matching apps/wallow-web/src/router.tsx's `createRouter({ context: { queryClient, sdk } })`, plus an optional `user`).

4. isAdmin is the ROLE check only and deliberately does NOT consult is_global_admin (claims.test.ts pins this with a named test). The API keeps global admin as a distinct non-assignable CLAIM, never a role — TenantResolutionMiddleware gates on `IsGlobalAdmin() || IsOperator()` separately from any role check (beads 1.4/1.7) — and collapsing them browser-side would re-create the role/claim conflation that was removed server-side. This also preserves today's wallow-web behaviour exactly (isAdminUser gated only on the admin role), so route.test.tsx keeps passing unchanged.

5. isOperator/isGlobalAdmin mirror bool.TryParse: literal boolean true OR a trimmed case-insensitive "true" string. "1"/1/"yes"/"on"/{}/[] are all FALSE — presence must never be enough. Claim literals are exactly "is_operator" and "is_global_admin" (ClaimsPrincipalExtensions.OperatorClaimType / GlobalAdminClaimType).

6. getRoles mirrors GetRoles(): reads `roles` with a `role` fallback (roles wins when both present), accepts a bare string as one role, ignores non-string entries rather than coercing them (coercion would mint the role "[object Object]"), trims and drops blanks, and dedupes case-insensitively keeping the FIRST spelling (Distinct(StringComparer.OrdinalIgnoreCase)).

7. Nothing in route-context.ts reads location/document/window. The SDK specs run in the node environment, so both files assert `"location" in globalThis === false` as a precondition — a helper that reached for a browser global fails there, which is exactly the Wallow-zyxe SSR-500 shape.

GREEN PHASE — wallow-web adoption (apps/wallow-web/src/routes/dashboard/route.tsx):
Delete the local isAdminUser() and the inline `/bff/login?returnTo=${encodeURIComponent(...)}` literal; beforeLoad becomes roughly:
  const user = requireAuth({
    user: await context.queryClient.ensureQueryData(userQueries.currentUser()),
    returnTo: location.pathname,
    redirect,
  });

description: Optional quality-of-life track: do if cheap, explicitly skip (with a note on this task) if not. Two independent items.
design:
1. Gate Router/Query devtools to dev-only builds in all three apps (they should not ship in production bundles).
2. Spike (evaluation only, no adoption without a separate decision) hey-api's `zod` plugin for runtime validation at the BFF boundary.
acceptance_criteria: Either both items are done (devtools gated + zod-plugin spike written up), or this task is closed with an explicit note on this bead explaining what was skipped and why -- do not silently drop it.
notes:
GREEN Wallow-pu6a.5.7. Both items done: devtools gating implemented + zod-plugin spike run to a NO-GO verdict with evidence.

=== ITEM 1: DEVTOOLS GATING ===

FILES=packages/web-shell/src/devtools-gating.test.ts (new, 387 lines, staged). No other file touched. No dependency/lockfile change.
TEST_STATUS=pass (27 tests in packages/web-shell, 24 of them this spec). typecheck pass, oxlint --deny-warnings clean, oxfmt clean.

FINDING THAT RESHAPED THE TASK: there are NO devtools in this repo to gate. Swept every app and package (source + all four manifest dependency groups): zero devtools packages declared, zero devtools imports. The apps carry @tanstack/react-query, react-router, react-router-ssr-query and react-start only. `@tanstack/devtools-event-client` and `@vitejs/devtools` appear in pnpm-lock.yaml solely as transitive build-time deps of the router plugin / Start, never in an app's module graph. So "gate them to dev-only" had no target and the deliverable became the ABSENCE-pinning guard instead -- the repo's established idiom for exactly this shape (packages/sdk/src/server/h3-free.test.ts pins "the SDK ships no h3" the same way).

WHAT THE GUARD ENFORCES, for every app discovered under apps/ (derived, not hard-coded, so adding an app cannot silently escape it):
  1. no devtools package in `dependencies` (devDependencies is their only legal home);
  2. no STATIC devtools import in any app module -- a static import is an unconditional graph edge, so wrapping the JSX in `import.meta.env.DEV` does NOT remove it from the production bundle, it only stops it rendering. This is the actual trap and the fixture proves the guard catches it;
  3. a DYNAMIC `import("...devtools...")` is permitted only in a file that also carries a dev-mode guard (`import.meta.env.DEV`, or `NODE_ENV !== "production"`), which Vite splits into a chunk production never requests.

WHY IT EARNS ITS KEEP DESPITE GUARDING NOTHING TODAY: Wallow is fork-first and every TanStack Start template mounts Router/Query devtools unconditionally in the root route. A fork that copies that pattern ships a multi-hundred-kB debug panel to end users. The rule is now encoded rather than merely true-by-accident.

RED PROVEN TWO WAYS (the guard is not a scanner that finds nothing):
  a. Fixture tree (mkdtemp, torn down in afterAll) carrying one of each violation -- a devtools package in `dependencies`, a static import whose RENDER is dev-gated, an ungated dynamic import -- plus the compliant gated-dynamic form. The detectors flag exactly the three and clear the fourth. These cases are permanent, not a transient red.
  b. Live repo probe: temporarily wrote apps/examples/minimal-app/src/lib/__devtools-probe.ts with a static `@tanstack/react-query-devtools` import -> the sweep FAILED naming that exact file and specifier; probe deleted, suite back to 27/27 green. Nothing left behind (verified).

DETECTOR DETAIL WORTH KNOWING: devtools-package matching is per `/`-separated segment (segment === "devtools" or endsWith "-devtools"), NOT a substring test -- a substring test flags `@jsdevtools/ono`, which is already in this repo's tree via the OpenAPI toolchain and is not a debug panel. There is an explicit "finds the apps to sweep" case so a restructure of apps/ cannot make the derived it.each cases go vacuously green.

HOME: packages/web-shell, because the rule binds all three apps and no single app owns it; web-shell is the shared frontend-host package and already owns the QueryClient factory whose devtools panel this is. Its vitest is node-env with `include: src/**/*.test.ts`, so the spec runs with no extra wiring, and tsconfig.build.json's `include: [src/index.ts]` keeps it out of dist.

=== ITEM 2: ZOD-PLUGIN SPIKE -- VERDICT: NO-GO ===

Evaluation only; nothing adopted, packages/sdk untouched. Probe ran in the scratchpad against the CURRENT pin (@hey-api/openapi-ts 0.99.0, zod 4.4.3 already in the store) over the committed snapshot packages/sdk/openapi/v1.json. Generated a baseline (today's plugin list) and a zod variant (`+ "zod"`, `@hey-api/sdk` with `validator: true`). Baseline reproduced the committed src/generated byte-for-byte modulo the 2-line runtimeConfigPath difference, so the comparison is faithful. Both generations succeeded -- the plugin WORKS on the current pin; this is a value judgement, not a compatibility failure.

COST (esbuild, minified + gzipped, browser platform):
  - realistic 5-operation import: 4.1 kB -> 28.5 kB gzip (+24.4 kB, ~7x)
  - whole generated surface:      7.0 kB -> 32.6 kB gzip (+25.7 kB, ~4.7x)
  - zod 4 runtime floor alone:    19.2 kB gzip -- so the cost is ~19 kB of unavoidable runtime plus ~5-7 kB of schemas. Schemas DO tree-shake; the zod core does not.
  - generated source: sdk.gen.ts 1274 -> 2104 lines, plus a new 1858-line zod.gen.ts. +2688 lines / +94 kB of committed generated code (+51%), re-reviewed on every regen.
  - it would make zod a NEW production runtime dependency of all three browser bundles; today zod is build-time-transitive only (router-plugin / Start), in no app's module graph.

CORRECTNESS LANDMINES PROVEN EMPIRICALLY (ran the generated schemas against realistic .NET payloads):
  - `zAccountLoginResponse` REJECTS `mfaGraceDeadline: "2026-07-28T12:00:00+02:00"`. The plugin's default `dates.offset: false` emits `z.iso.datetime()`, which accepts only 'Z'. Any DateTimeOffset the API serializes with a non-UTC offset would throw at runtime on a 200 response. Fixable with `dates: { offset: true }`, but it must be set deliberately and nothing warns you.
  - `zMfaStatusResponse` REJECTS a payload with `method` omitted (spec models it required+nullable; a serializer that omits nulls produces exactly this). Same class of failure.
  - PASSES (checked, so these are NOT arguments against): fractional-second timestamps; and the MFA raw business-failure shape `{succeeded:false, error:"..."}` (bd memory mfa-endpoints-...) validates fine -- z.object is non-strict, and the generated client calls `await opts.responseValidator(data)` for its throw only, DISCARDING the return value, so zod's unknown-key stripping never mutates the payload and `error` survives.
  Net: turning validation on converts snapshot inaccuracies from harmless into production outages, and CI's openapi-drift job only checks the snapshot against the live spec -- never the spec against actually-serialized payloads. Nothing in the repo would catch these before users do.

ARCHITECTURAL CONFLICT WITH THE WORK IN FLIGHT: `responseValidator` fires INSIDE `if (response.ok)` (verified in the generated client, line ~171). Good news -- 4xx/RFC7807 bodies are NOT validated, so it does not fight the error path directly. Bad news -- a ZodError thrown from the SUCCESS path still falls into the same `interceptors.error.fns` chain that task 5.3's WallowError normalization owns, so an HTTP 200 would surface as an error (and under `throwOnError: false`, as an `{error}` result for a successful request). Adopting mid-collapse would force WallowError's semantics to be designed around a validation failure that is not an API error -- precisely the ambiguity 5.2/5.3 exist to remove.

PLACEMENT ARGUMENT (the real reason this is NO-GO rather than "not yet"): in a BFF topology the browser's peer is our OWN same-origin Node proxy, which the SDK itself owns. Validating in the browser bundle re-checks data that already crossed the trust boundary, and charges every end user ~19 kB gzip to do it. If runtime validation is wanted, the boundary that deserves it is the Node BFF talking to the API -- server-side, where bundle cost is zero and a failure can become a proper 502/WallowError at the real trust boundary. hey-api's `validator` flag cannot be scoped that way: it bakes the validators into sdk.gen.ts, which the browser entry re-exports.

VERDICT: NO-GO on adopting the hey-api zod plugin. Not a compatibility problem -- a cost/placement/timing one. No config change made. Filed the server-side alternative as a standalone P3 bead (see below) so the idea is not lost; deliberately NOT parented under this epic, since it is a different design from the plugin and out of Phase 4's scope.

REPRO ARTIFACTS (scratchpad, session-local): zod-spike/{openapi-ts.config.ts,openapi-ts.baseline.ts,out-base/,out-zod/,probe.ts,bundle-*.js}.
ISSUES=none.

FOLLOW-UP FILED: Wallow-q2no (P3, standalone, deliberately not parented under this epic) -- 'Spike: runtime response validation at the Node BFF boundary (server-side, not the browser bundle)'. Carries the placement argument and the two snapshot-fidelity gaps (non-UTC DateTimeOffset; required+nullable omitted props) that must be closed before any validator is switched on anywhere.
