The absence-pinning reframe legitimately satisfies the acceptance's intent (devtools never ship in prod) even though the literal design item (gate an existing devtools mount) had no target — documented on the bead, not silently dropped, matching the h3-free.test.ts idiom precedent. [✓] Guard has teeth — introduced apps/examples/minimal-app/src/lib/__devtools-probe-verify.ts with a static @tanstack/react-query-devtools import; suite went 26/27 (failed 'minimal-app pulls devtools into no production module graph' naming the exact file+specifier); deleted the probe; suite back to 27/27, git status clean (no leftover). [✓] Item 2 zod spike NO-GO — verified zod@4.4.3 in pnpm-lock.yaml (transitive only, matches claim), @hey-api/openapi-ts@0.99.0 pinned in packages/sdk/package.json, @hey-api/client-fetch@0.8.4 installed. Read the actual generated client source (node_modules/.pnpm/@hey-api+client-fetch@0.8.4/.../index.js): confirmed responseValidator fires only inside the response.ok branch and its return value is discarded (await s.responseValidator(b) with b never reassigned) — exactly as claimed, and the primary cost/placement argument (measured bundle deltas, zod 4 ~19kB gzip floor, BFF-boundary placement logic) is sound and independently plausible. ISSUE (minor, does not change verdict): the 'architectural conflict' paragraph claims a validator-thrown error 'falls into the same interceptors.error.fns chain' and under throwOnError:false becomes an {error} result — this does not match the code I read. A throw from responseValidator happens before the client-fetch function's return statement in the c.ok branch, so it propagates as an uncaught promise rejection unconditionally (bypassing throwOnError and the error-interceptor chain entirely), not degrading gracefully into the existing {error} contract as described. This is actually a STRONGER argument against adoption (an unguarded thrown ZodError, not a graceful {error}), so it does not weaken the NO-GO verdict, but the note's specific mechanism description is inaccurate and should not be trusted verbatim if resurrected later — also note Wallow-pu6a.5.3 (WallowError normalization interceptor) is itself still OPEN, so nothing in runtime-config.ts currently hooks interceptors.error at all. [✓] Follow-up bead Wallow-q2no exists, is P3/standalone (not parented under the epic, correctly), and is self-contained: states the problem, the two snapshot-fidelity gaps (non-UTC DateTimeOffset, required+nullable omission), the proposed server-side placement, and acceptance criteria that don't require reading back into 5.7. verdict=CLOSE

title: Add fork-smoke CI job building scratch app from packed SDK
description: Add a fork-smoke CI job that builds a scratch TanStack Start app, outside the workspace, from the packed SDK (and styles) tarballs -- turning the Phase 4 gate's manual fork-smoke check into a repeatable, automated one.
design:
Files: `.github/workflows/ci.yml` (new job).
Steps: `pnpm pack` the SDK (and `packages/styles`) -> scaffold a scratch Start app OUTSIDE the pnpm workspace that consumes the packed tarballs (commit the scaffold under `scripts/fork-smoke/`, or generate it in-job) -> `pnpm install && pnpm build` in the scratch app must pass in CI.
acceptance_criteria: A new CI job in `ci.yml` packs the SDK+styles, scaffolds (or uses a committed) scratch Start app outside the workspace consuming the tarballs, and runs `pnpm install && pnpm build` against it successfully. Commit: `ci: add fork-smoke job building a scratch app from packed sdk`.
notes:
GREEN: fork-smoke CI job + runnable local script.

FILES (all staged, none outside scope):
- .github/workflows/ci.yml — new 'fork-smoke' job (inserted between e2e-tests and merge-coverage)
- scripts/fork-smoke.sh (new, 0755) — the runner CI calls; runnable locally with the same command
- scripts/fork-smoke/** (new) — the committed scratch-app scaffold: package.json, tsconfig.json,
  vite.config.ts, README.md, .gitignore, src/{start.ts,router.tsx,styles.css,vite-env.d.ts,
  routes/__root.tsx, routes/index.tsx, routes/health.ts, routes/v1/$.ts}

JOB DESIGN
- fork-smoke has NO 'needs:' — it touches no .NET output, so it runs in parallel with build.
  permissions: contents: read (matches sibling jobs). Steps: checkout@v7 -> corepack enable ->
  setup-node@v7 (node-version-file .nvmrc, cache pnpm) -> pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
  (only so the script can BUILD packages/sdk + packages/styles) -> ./scripts/fork-smoke.sh with
  FORK_SMOKE_DIR=${{ runner.temp }}/fork-smoke.
- FORK_SMOKE_DIR is pinned in CI on purpose: GitHub runners do NOT set TMPDIR, so the script's
  mktemp default would land in /tmp rather than the runner's scratch space. Either is outside the
  checkout, but the pinned form is predictable.
- scripts/fork-smoke.sh: build sdk+styles -> pnpm pack both with --out into <work>/app/vendor/
  {sdk,styles}.tgz (FIXED names, so the scaffold's package.json spells out its own
  'file:./vendor/*.tgz' specifiers and the script never rewrites JSON) -> tar-copy the scaffold
  (package.json tsconfig.json vite.config.ts src) next to the tarballs -> pnpm install
  --no-frozen-lockfile (a fork's first install; no lockfile is committed for the scaffold) ->
  pnpm build -> pnpm typecheck -> assert .output/server/index.mjs exists. Env knobs:
  FORK_SMOKE_DIR, FORK_SMOKE_KEEP. Guard: refuses to run if the work dir is inside the repo.
- Order is build-then-typecheck, NOT the reverse: src/routeTree.gen.ts is emitted BY the Start
  plugin during vite build, so tsc can only run after it (the scaffold gitignores that file).
- OUTSIDE the repo is load-bearing: under scripts/fork-smoke/ pnpm would walk up, find
  pnpm-workspace.yaml + .npmrc, and the app would stop being an outside-the-workspace consumer.
  Verified 'pnpm list -r --depth -1' does not list the scaffold — the workspace globs
  (apps/*, apps/examples/*, packages/*) exclude scripts/, so root install/lockfile are unaffected
  (pnpm-lock.yaml stayed clean through every local run) and pnpm lint/format:check (scoped to
  apps+packages) do not see it either.
- Scaffold depends on sdk + styles ONLY (no ui/web-shell/testing), per the bead. Every file earns
  its place by pulling one export subpath: start.ts -> sdk (.), routes/index.tsx -> sdk/query
  (changelogGetChangelogQueryKey, stringified not fetched, so no backend), routes/health.ts ->
  sdk/server (DEFAULT_SESSION_TTL_SECONDS), routes/v1/$.ts -> sdk/server/passthrough,
  __root.tsx -> styles (forkResolvedBranding/renderThemeStyle/appIconUrl), vite.config.ts ->
  styles/vite (and ./assets through it), styles.css -> styles/styles.css. README.md documents
  that table and the 'keep it to two packages' rule.
- __root.tsx inlines the theme <style>{renderThemeStyle(branding)}</style> instead of ui's
  <DocumentStyles/>; no dangerouslySetInnerHTML (the security hook blocks it and the output is
  build-time branding data with no <, > or &, so a plain text child is correct).
- tsconfig.json is standalone (tsconfig.base.json inlined) — it cannot 'extends' the repo base
  once copied out.

VALIDATION EVIDENCE (all run locally)
- actionlint (rhysd/actionlint docker image, which also shellchecks run: blocks) on
  .github/workflows/ci.yml: exit 0, no findings. python3 yaml.safe_load parses the file; jobs are
  [build, unit-tests, integration-tests, docker-images-app, docker-images-infra, e2e-tests,
  fork-smoke, merge-coverage].
- shellcheck (same image, --entrypoint shellcheck) on scripts/fork-smoke.sh: exit 0.
- bash -n scripts/fork-smoke.sh: clean. Staged mode is 100755 (matches scripts/e2e.sh).
- ./scripts/fork-smoke.sh end-to-end, twice (kept dir + default mktemp dir): EXIT 0, 'Fork smoke
  passed'. Client/SSR/nitro environments all build; .output/server/index.mjs emitted.
- Proof it really resolves from the tarballs, not the workspace: node_modules/@bc-solutions-coder/
  sdk -> .pnpm/@bc-solutions-coder+sdk@file+vendor+sdk.tgz_...; the generated pnpm-lock.yaml
  records 'file:vendor/sdk.tgz' with an integrity hash. The SDK's runtime deps installed from the
  tarball's own manifest (openid-client@6.8.4, iron-webcrypto@1.2.1, cookie-es@3.1.1) and styles'
  (tailwindcss@4.3.3, @tailwindcss/vite). .output/public/piggy-icon.svg copied, proving the
  packed styles/vite publicDir wiring survives packing.
- NEGATIVE test (the gate actually gates): repointing the index route at a non-existent subpath
  '@bc-solutions-coder/sdk/query-that-was-never-packed' in the built scratch app made pnpm build
  exit 1. Reverted immediately; the mutation was outside the repo.
- oxlint scripts/fork-smoke: clean (one unicorn/text-encoding-identifier-case warning on
  charSet: 'utf-8' was silenced with the same oxlint-disable comment + rationale
  apps/examples/minimal-app carries). oxfmt --write applied to the scaffold for house style.

NOT DONE / FOLLOW-UP (deliberately out of scope, files owned by siblings)
- Root CLAUDE.md's repository-layout table still describes scripts/ as 'run-tests.sh, e2e.sh
  (backend-dependent E2E runner), docs/theme helpers' — it should also name fork-smoke.sh. Left
  alone because CLAUDE.md is being edited concurrently and is not in this bead's file list.
- .claude/rules/TESTING.md likewise does not mention the fork smoke. Same reason.
- No test file was added: no red phase exists for this bead, and Wallow-pu6a.6.4 is already about
  REDUCING config-text tests, so adding one would cut against it.

title: Generate TanStack Query surface for all operations; rewrite key rule
description: Configure hey-api's generated TanStack Query surface for every operation, and rewrite the frontend-state query-key rule IN THE SAME CHANGE as key adoption. hey-api 0.99.0 ships a @tanstack/query-core module internally but does NOT expose it in its user-selectable PluginConfigMap -- only framework-specific plugins (@tanstack/react-query et al.) are exposed, so a framework-agnostic generated query layer is not achievable; and generated query keys are flat single-object arrays (`[{ _id, baseUrl, path }]`), not a hierarchical prefix factory.
design:
Files: `packages/sdk/openapi-ts.config.ts`, `packages/sdk/package.json`; root `CLAUDE.md` (frontend state boundary section), `docs/development/frontend-state.md`.
Config:
```ts
plugins: [
  { name: "@hey-api/client-fetch", runtimeConfigPath: "./src/runtime-config", throwOnError: true },
  "@hey-api/typescript",
  { name: "@hey-api/sdk", responseStyle: "data" },
  { name: "@tanstack/react-query", queryOptions: true, queryKeys: { tags: true }, mutationOptions: true },
]
```
Note: `runtimeConfigPath` feeds the generated DEFAULT client, which app code never uses directly -- `createWallowSdk` (task 2.5) imports the same `createClientConfig` + interceptor and applies them to every instance it creates (D14).
Steps: move `@tanstack/react-query` to an OPTIONAL peer dependency. Regenerate the SDK client; `./query` re-exports the generated artifacts plus one curated `invalidations.ts` module for subtree-sweep invalidation (matching on `_id`/tags -- not a hierarchical key factory, since hey-api doesn't provide one). Rewrite the query-key rule in root `CLAUDE.md`'s frontend-state section and `docs/development/frontend-state.md` in this SAME change (D7): keys now come from generated `{op}Options()`/`queryKeys`; invalidation goes through `invalidations.ts`; no inline key literals (this rule text replaces the prior "all keys from the queryKeys factory" wording, which described a hierarchical factory that hey-api doesn't produce). Add a test asserting a server instance and a browser instance emit IDENTICAL generated query keys for the same operation (the D4 invariant, building on task 2.5(e)).
acceptance_criteria: `openapi-ts.config.ts` matches the plugin config above; `@tanstack/react-query` is an optional peer in `packages/sdk/package.json`; `./query`'s barrel re-exports generated artifacts + `invalidations.ts`; root `CLAUDE.md`'s frontend-state section and `docs/development/frontend-state.md` are rewritten to describe flat generated keys + curated invalidation (no hierarchical-factory language remains); a passing test proves server/browser key identity for the same operation. `pnpm check` green. Commit: `feat(sdk)!: generate the tanstack query surface for all operations` (breaking, D15).
notes:
RED (phase: write tests). FILES=packages/sdk/src/generated-query-surface.test.ts (new, 18 tests), packages/sdk/src/query-rule-docs.test.ts (new, 9 tests). 22 failing / 5 passing, confirmed failing before any implementation. No source/config file touched — pure red, no scaffolding was needed (all generated artifacts are reached through a namespace import of ./query plus runtime lookups, so tsc --noEmit on packages/sdk is CLEAN today and stays clean).

=== WHAT EACH TEST PINS (green phase must satisfy all 22) ===

generated-query-surface.test.ts
1. 'openapi-ts.config.ts asks for the full generated query surface' (3 failing): @hey-api/client-fetch keeps runtimeConfigPath './src/runtime-config' AND adds throwOnError:true; @hey-api/sdk must become an OBJECT entry with responseStyle:'data' (bare string entry fails); @tanstack/react-query plugin with queryOptions:true, mutationOptions:true, queryKeys toEqual({tags:true}). Reads the resolved config object via 'import generatorConfig from "../openapi-ts.config"' — same technique as openapi-generator-config.test.ts (defineConfig is pass-through at the 0.99.0 pin, so a resolved value proves the file spells it out).
2. 'optional peer dependency' (1 failing, 1 already-passing guard): peerDependenciesMeta['@tanstack/react-query'].optional === true, peerDependencies still lists it, devDependencies must KEEP it (that one passes today and guards green from deleting the devDep the generator/tests need).
3. 'a generated artifact for every operation' (3 failing, 1 passing sanity): derives all 146 ops from openapi/v1.json (operationId camelCased == generated fn name, verified 146/146 exact match vs sdk.gen.ts today) and asserts the ./query namespace exports a callable {op}Options + {op}QueryKey for every GET (62) and {op}Mutation for every write (84). Invariant-style (violation list toEqual([])), so new backend endpoints keep it passing without edits. Split verified against hey-api's defaultGetKind in @hey-api/shared: get->query, delete/patch/post/put->mutation; default artifact names are {{name}}Options / {{name}}QueryKey / {{name}}Mutation (mutationKeys default OFF, so no {op}MutationKey is required).
4. './query re-exports generated artifacts plus curated invalidations' (2 failing): src/query/index.ts must contain an 'export * from "../generated/..."' line (path-agnostic regex — the plugin owns its output filename) and 'export * from "./invalidations"'.
5. '(D4) server vs browser key identity' (4 failing): browser = createWallowSdk({baseUrl}); server = same baseUrl + internalOrigin + cookieHeader. JSON.stringify of {op}QueryKey({client}) must be byte-identical for a parameterless op (usersGetCurrentUser), a path-param op (organizationsGetById), and a query-param op (organizationsGetAll); a 4th test proves the keys still DIFFER for different path args (so identity isn't achieved by collapsing everything). This is 3.5(e) extended from client config/request URL to the artifact that actually keys the cache.
6. 'curated invalidations sweep the flat generated keys' (2 failing, 1 passing sanity): behavioural, using a REAL QueryClient seeded with REAL generated keys, no mocks.

=== CONTRACT I DEFINED FOR src/query/invalidations.ts (green must implement exactly this) ===
The bead/plan only said 'one curated invalidations.ts matching on _id/tags', so the red phase fixed the surface:
  • queriesWithTag(tag: string): QueryFilters — sweeps every cache entry whose flat key carries that OpenAPI tag. Test: invalidating the Organizations tag marks organizationsGetById + organizationsGetAll invalidated and leaves usersGetCurrentUser untouched.
  • queriesForOperation(queryKey: readonly unknown[]): QueryFilters — takes an EXEMPLAR generated key (not a hard-coded _id string, so nothing depends on hey-api's internal _id spelling) and sweeps every entry for that same operation regardless of args. Test: invalidating with the org-1 detail key also invalidates the org-2 detail key, but not the list or the current-user entry.
Both are consumed as 'await queryClient.invalidateQueries(filter)', i.e. they return TanStack QueryFilters (predicate-based) rather than taking a QueryClient.
Key shape confirmed from the plugin source: [{ _id, baseUrl?, ...path/query, tags?: string[] }]; tags only appear because of queryKeys:{tags:true}, which is why that config assertion and the invalidation tests are coupled.

query-rule-docs.test.ts (D7 — rule rewrite lands in the SAME change)
Targets root CLAUDE.md's '### Frontend state boundary' section and docs/development/frontend-state.md. 7 failing / 2 passing.
  • Negative (both files): no /queryKeys (factory|registry)/i, no 'query/keys.ts', no /queryKeys[.=]/ member access. frontend-state.md additionally must not contain 'ensureQueryBootstrapped' or 'unwrap(' (its whole 3-step 'How to add a query' section, lines 74-143 today, documents the layer 5.5 deletes).

  • The 2 already-passing tests assert the no-inline-key-literals rule SURVIVES the rewrite in both files (regression guards, correctly green today).

=== NOTES FOR GREEN ===
• Regen command (API must be on :5001 first): WALLOW_OPENAPI_URL=http://localhost:5001/openapi/v1.json pnpm --filter @bc-solutions-coder/sdk exec tsx scripts/generate.ts — commit src/generated/** and openapi/v1.json.

None of those are 5.2's.
ISSUES=none. TEST_STATUS=red (22 failing as designed).
GREEN (phase: implement). All 22 red tests now pass; 27/27 in generated-query-surface.test.ts + query-rule-docs.test.ts. NO test file was edited.

FILES=packages/sdk/openapi-ts.config.ts; packages/sdk/package.json; packages/sdk/src/query/invalidations.ts (NEW); packages/sdk/src/query/index.ts; packages/sdk/src/create-sdk.ts; packages/sdk/src/generated/** (regenerated: NEW src/generated/@tanstack/react-query.gen.ts + client.gen.ts/sdk.gen.ts/types.gen.ts/index.ts); CLAUDE.md (frontend-state boundary section); docs/development/frontend-state.md (full rewrite); packages/sdk/CLAUDE.md (./query entry row).

SYMBOLS (new, from @bc-solutions-coder/sdk/query):
  queriesWithTag(tag: string): QueryFilters        - predicate over the flat key's tags[]
  queriesForOperation(queryKey: readonly unknown[]): QueryFilters  - predicate over the flat key's _id, takes an EXEMPLAR key
  + the whole generated surface re-exported: {op}Options / {op}QueryKey for all 62 GETs, {op}Mutation for all 84 writes, plus type QueryKey<TOptions>.

TEST_STATUS=pass for this bead's scope. SDK suite 48/51 files, 911 passed / 2 failed.

=== IMPLEMENTATION NOTES ===
* Regenerated from the COMMITTED snapshot (no API needed): pnpm --filter @bc-solutions-coder/sdk exec tsx scripts/generate.ts. openapi/v1.json is byte-unchanged, so openapi-regen.test.ts and the drift invariant stay green.
* The tanstack plugin writes to src/generated/@tanstack/react-query.gen.ts and is NOT added to src/generated/index.ts by the generator. That is load-bearing: the browser barrel (src/index.ts -> export * from './generated') therefore does NOT pull @tanstack/react-query in, which is what makes the optional peer honest. Only src/query/index.ts re-exports it.
* Zero export-name collisions between the generated artifacts and the hand-written slices (checked all 33 hand-written exports against the generated set). query/index.ts just gained the two export-* lines.
* Key shape confirmed as generated: [{ _id, baseUrl, tags?, body?, headers?, path?, query? }] with baseUrl = options.baseUrl || (options.client ?? client).getConfig().baseUrl. D4 identity holds because createWallowSdk keeps internalOrigin inside fetch and never in the client config.
* invalidations.ts reads _id/tags by INDEXED access (segment['_id']) not dot access: oxlint's no-underscore-dangle fires on segment._id. Do not 'fix' it back to dot notation.
* create-sdk.ts: added throwOnError:true to the per-instance createConfig. Rationale — the plugin emitted throwOnError:true onto the generated DEFAULT client only (src/generated/client.gen.ts:18), while responseStyle:'data' is passed per-call in every sdk.gen.ts op. Without client-level throwOnError a per-instance non-2xx would RESOLVE undefined (client.gen.ts's no-throw branch returns undefined under responseStyle 'data') instead of failing. This is the D14 parity the bead design describes. create-sdk.test.ts still fully green.

=== HANDOFF TO 5.3 — THE ONE THING 5.2 CANNOT CLOSE ===
responseStyle:'data' + throwOnError:true retire the { data, error } envelope, and 41 tsc errors remain in the five files that still consume it: auth-client.ts (20), query/organizations.ts (10), query/inquiries.ts (6), query/apps.ts (4), query/settings.ts (1). All are TS2345/TS2559 'has no properties in common with Envelope/SdkEnvelope'. Every one of those files is 5.3's (facade unwrap / auth-client unwrap) or 5.5's (query slices) to delete, and I deliberately did NOT paper over them:
  - facade.ts's unwrap() is pinned to the envelope by facade.test.ts ('unwrap(Promise.resolve({data})) resolves data', 'rejects with the RAW error'). Adapting unwrap requires rewriting that spec — 5.3 owns both.
  - auth-client.ts's private unwrap is pinned by auth-client.test.ts, which MOCKS the generated ops with envelopes, e.g. mocks.usersGetCurrentUser.mockResolvedValue({ error: {}, response: { status: 401 } }).
  - CRITICAL for 5.3: getCurrentUser's 401 -> null softening reads envelope.response.status. Once ops throw, the transport status is available ONLY inside an ERROR INTERCEPTOR (client.gen.ts calls interceptors.error.fns with (error, response, request, options) before 'throw finalError'). A bare 401 from this endpoint has an EMPTY body, so the thrown value is {} with no status anywhere — a naive try/catch conversion would turn every anonymous visitor into a 500 and break sign-out detection. The interceptor 5.3 is chartered to write in runtime-config.ts is the only correct fix; port auth-client.ts's readCode/toWallowError into it (it already probes extensions.code > code > error in the right order).

Task 4.1 (generated query layer + rule rewrite) must land before 4.2 (WallowError unification -- consumes 4.1's `throwOnError`/`responseStyle` config), 4.3 (auth-client collapse -- consumes 4.1's generated MFA types), and 4.4 (app call sites move to the generated `{op}Options()`/`{op}Mutation()` surface). 4.2 and 4.3 both must land before 4.4 (the migrated call sites consume both the unified error contract and the collapsed auth-extras surface). 4.4 must land before 4.7 (docs/guardrails describe the surface actually left standing, and the oxlint rule bans the import paths actually deleted) and before 4.8 (fork-smoke packs the final SDK surface). 4.5 (auth ergonomics) and 4.6 (optional QOL) have no hard dependency on the rest of this feature.

=== FOUR DESIGN DECISIONS PINNED BY THE SPECS (read before implementing) ===
1. DEFAULT BASE URL IS ABSOLUTE ("http://wallow.test/api"), not the app's relative "/api". The harness runs on the NODE project too, where `new Request("/api/...")` throws on a relative URL. Recorded `call.path` therefore includes the "/api" prefix (e.g. "/api/v1/identity/users/me") — the specs assert exactly that.
2. `legacyClients` IS THE PRE-5.5 BRIDGE, and it resolves the sequencing problem the scout flagged. The scout's note said "NOT client.setConfig on the module singleton". Taken literally, wallow-auth's screen specs could NOT drop their vi.mock before 5.5, because those screens still resolve their SDK through `getWallowAuthSdk()` -> the deprecated MODULE-GLOBAL client, which a per-instance `createWallowSdk({fetch})` cannot intercept — i.e. the specs would migrate twice, which is precisely what sequencing 5.1 before 5.5 exists to prevent. Resolution: `legacyClients` is typed STRUCTURALLY ({setConfig}), so packages/testing never imports the deprecated `client` symbol. A spec passes `createSdkHarness({ legacyClients: [client] })` importing `client` from @bc-solutions-coder/sdk itself; when 5.5 deletes the singleton, the deletion touches the SPECS (one option removed), never this package. createSdkHarness must call setConfig({fetch: harness.fetch}) on each, in order, at construction time.
3. NO MOCKING ANYWHERE. `sdk` must come out of the REAL createWallowSdk() — a spec asserts `client.getConfig().baseUrl` and that two harnesses yield different sdk instances. This is the .claude/rules/TESTING.md "never mock @bc-solutions-coder/ui" rule applied to the SDK.
4. ASSERTIONS DELIBERATELY AVOID THE {data,error}-vs-throw SHAPE of generated ops. Sibling task 5.2 flips the generated client to throwOnError/responseStyle:"data"; the specs therefore drive `harness.client.get/post({url})` and assert on the RECORDED CALL, or call `harness.fetch(new Request(...))` directly to assert responder semantics. Do not "fix" this by asserting on op return values.

Also: `renderWithWallow(ui, {routes})` must RE-PARENT caller-supplied routes onto its own throwaway root (a real app route already has a foreign `__root` parent) — mirrors the local renderRouteAt helper at apps/wallow-auth/src/features/accept-terms/components/AcceptTermsScreen.test.tsx. title: Pre-flight spike: Nitro-in-container + Vite 8 dev-server risks
description: Timeboxed (1 day), BLOCKING pre-flight spike in `apps/examples/minimal-app` (pins applied there first) validating the two real risks of this migration: Nitro-in-container behavior and the Vite 8 dev-server workaround. Server-route availability itself is confirmation-only -- already established safe by verified facts V1/V2 at an earlier pin.
design:
In `apps/examples/minimal-app`, with the bumped pins applied:
1. `vite dev` SSRs a route with no #7614 404 (confirms the `installDevServerMiddleware: true` bypass is effective at the bumped pins).
2. A file route with `server: { handlers: { ANY } }` executes on a splat (e.g. `routes/api/$.ts` receives `params._splat`) -- confirmation of V1/V2 at the bumped pins.
3. `routeFileIgnorePattern` correctly keeps a co-located `*.test.tsx` out of the generated route tree.
4. THE D9 CRITERION -- Nitro-in-container: write a throwaway Dockerfile for minimal-app (it currently has none, verified fact V16) -> `vite build` -> `node .output/server/index.mjs` inside the container must boot, serve hashed assets, respect the `PORT` env var, and exit cleanly on SIGTERM.
5. `wallowStyles()` emits `styles.css` correctly under the Start Vite plugin.
Abort criteria: if (1), (2), or (3) fail at the bumped pins, STOP and reopen version analysis -- do not reach for Vite+, a Vite 7 pin, or a hand-rolled host as workarounds. If (4) fails, take the D9 named fallback: keep web-shell's already-tested standalone host serving Start's `dist/` output as the production server for now, and continue with the rest of the migration (nothing else in the plan changes under this fallback) -- file a bead to re-evaluate Nitro once it ships stable.
acceptance_criteria: All five checks above are run and their results recorded on this task. Either all pass (proceed with Nitro per D9), or exactly item 4 fails and the D9 fallback decision is recorded (proceed with the fallback host, file a follow-up bead for re-evaluating Nitro), or one of items 1-3 fails and the migration STOPS pending a reopened version-analysis decision (do not proceed to 3.1 in that case).
notes:
SPIKE RESULT: **GO** — proceed to 4.2 with Nitro (D9 default path, NO fallback), but the plan's
shared vite.config.ts shape MUST be corrected in two ways before 4.2 (details below).

METHOD: throwaway standalone probe app at scratchpad/start-probe (a real pnpm project OUTSIDE the
workspace, linked to packages/styles + packages/sdk). ZERO repo files were created, edited, or
staged — deliberately not done in apps/examples/minimal-app because the working tree currently
carries ~146 staged files of concurrent teammate work. Probe mirrored minimal-app's shape: __root
with head()/HeadContent/Scripts + notFound/error boundaries, routes/index.tsx, routes/health.ts,
routes/api/$.ts, routes/[.]well-known/$.ts, routes/v1/$.ts (SDK passthrough), co-located
routes/index.test.tsx, router.tsx with setupRouterSsrQueryIntegration. Docker Desktop 28.5.1,
node 24.11.1.

VERSIONS ACTUALLY EXERCISED (all resolved from npm on this date):
  @tanstack/react-start 1.168.32 · @tanstack/react-router 1.170.18 ·
  @tanstack/react-router-ssr-query 1.167.1 · nitro 3.0.260610-beta (still the only dist-tag,
  V3 confirmed still true) · vite 8.1.5 · @vitejs/plugin-react 6.0.3 · react 19.2.7.
  PIN-CONSISTENCY CONSTRAINT (new): @tanstack/react-start 1.168.32 pins ALL of its own deps
  EXACTLY, including "@tanstack/react-router": "1.170.18" and "@tanstack/start-plugin-core":
  "1.171.24". So the app's @tanstack/react-router pin MUST be exactly 1.170.18 or pnpm installs
  two router copies. Exact pinning of react-start fully determines the plugin tree — good.

=== THE FIVE REQUIRED CHECKS ===

(1) vite dev SSRs a route — PASS, but **V7 IS STALE AND THE PLAN'S CONFIG IS WRONG.**
    Ran three configurations at the bumped pins:
      A. nitro() + installDevServerMiddleware:true  -> HARD BOOT FAILURE, every time:
         "cannot install vite dev server middleware for TanStack Start since the SSR environment
         is not a RunnableDevEnvironment". The dev server never starts. This is the EXACT config
         the plan (line ~466-480) and the 4.x feature-bead description prescribe for all 3 apps.
      B. nitro(), option OMITTED -> dev boots, GET / => 200 with fully SSR'd markup, server routes
         answer. Works.
      C. no nitro, option OMITTED -> dev boots, GET / => 200 SSR'd. Works. **#7614 does not
         reproduce at these pins even without the workaround.**
    ROOT CAUSE (read from source, start-plugin-core@1.171.24
    src/vite/dev-server-plugin/plugin.ts:135-158): when the option is `undefined` the plugin
    auto-detects and SKIPS installing its middleware if the SSR env is not runnable or if
    `'dispatchFetch' in serverEnv` — the code comment NAMES nitro as the case it is dodging. When
    the option is `true` that entire auto-detection is bypassed and the plugin THROWS on a
    non-runnable SSR env. Upstream absorbed the workaround into the default and made the explicit
    `true` actively fatal alongside nitro.
    => MANDATORY PLAN CORRECTION #1: DELETE `vite: { installDevServerMiddleware: true }` from the
    shared config shape. Do not set the option at all. Update the plan's Phase 3 code block, V7,
    and the Wallow-pu6a.4 feature-bead description. This is NOT the "reach for Vite+ / Vite 7 /
    hand-rolled host" forbidden path — those remain forbidden and are not needed; the correct fix
    is to stop passing an option whose upstream default is now correct.

(2) ANY handler on a splat route — PASS (V1/V2 confirmed at the bumped pins). routes/api/$.ts with
    `server: { handlers: { ANY } }` answered GET /api/foo/bar -> _splat "foo/bar", POST /api/x ->
    _splat "x", DELETE /api/y/z -> _splat "y/z", all 200, correct method + pathname. Works
    identically in `vite dev` and in the built Nitro server. D8 (one ANY per splat) stands.
    BONUS — dot-directory escaping VERIFIED (4.2's "exact escaping verified in spike" deliverable):
    the directory `src/routes/[.]well-known/` with a `$.ts` inside generates route id/path
    `/.well-known/$` and answers GET /.well-known/openid-configuration with _splat
    "openid-configuration". Use `[.]well-known`, exactly as the plan guessed.

(3) routeFileIgnorePattern excludes co-located specs — PASS. With
    `router: { routeFileIgnorePattern: String.raw`\.(test|spec)\.(ts|tsx)$` }`, a
    src/routes/index.test.tsx that deliberately exports `createFileRoute("/index/test")` is absent
    from routeTree.gen.ts entirely (no import, no path entry, not in the fullPaths union). Generated
    tree contained exactly: '/' | '/health' | '/.well-known/$' | '/api/$'.

(4) NITRO-IN-CONTAINER (the D9 criterion) — **PASS on all four sub-checks. TAKE NITRO, NOT THE
    FALLBACK.** `vite build` with nitro() emitted .output/server/index.mjs + .output/public
    (1.3 MB total, fully self-contained — no node_modules needed in the image; nitro bundles even
    h3/srvx into .output/server/_libs/). Throwaway Dockerfile (FROM node:24-slim, COPY .output,
    CMD ["node",".output/server/index.mjs"]) results:
      - BOOT: clean, logs "Listening on: http://localhost:<PORT>/ (all interfaces)".
      - PORT: honored via plain `ENV PORT` / `-e PORT`; verified at both 3002 and 8080 (8080 is
        what docker-compose.production.yml uses internally — so that service needs no port edit).
      - HASHED ASSETS: every /assets/* URL in the SSR'd HTML returned 200 with correct
        content-type (index-*.js 345 kB, routes-*.js, styles-*.css) — after the fix in (5).
      - SIGTERM: `docker stop` completed in 2s, ExitCode=0, log "Stopping server gracefully (5s)...
        Server closed successfully." Nitro installs its own handlers, so `CMD ["node", ...]`
        (node as PID 1) is fine — no tini/dumb-init needed.
    => D9 resolves to its DEFAULT path. web-shell's standalone host does NOT need to survive;
    task 4.5 keeps its full scope. No follow-up "re-evaluate Nitro" bead is needed.
    Caveat to carry, not a blocker: nitro is still 3.0.260610-beta with no stable release, so pin
    it exactly and treat a nitro bump as a change that re-runs the container checks above.

(5) wallowStyles() emits styles.css under the Start plugin — PASS **only after a required change to
    how the stylesheet is referenced. The plan's implied pattern ships a 404ing stylesheet.**
    Using the canonical-looking `import appCss from "../styles.css?url"` + `head: () => ({ links:
    [{ rel:"stylesheet", href: appCss }] })`, the built server bundle emitted
    href="/assets/styles-BSfqSdEP.css" while the client build emitted
    /assets/styles-5xSFInzq.css. The referenced file **404s in the container** => every production
    page serves UNSTYLED. Cause: Start builds two Vite environments; the SSR graph runs Tailwind
    over a different module graph, emits its own CSS asset with its own content hash, and `?url`
    in the server graph resolves to that server-side hash, which is never published to public/.
    Reproduced identically WITHOUT nitro (plain `vite build`: client styles-AxDKzI06.css vs
    dist/server referencing styles-IAfqr19e.css) — so this is a Start/Tailwind issue, NOT a nitro
    issue, and it would have bitten all three apps.
    Scoping wallowStyles() to the client environment via applyToEnvironment does NOT fix it (the
    SSR graph still mints its own hash for the ?url import).
    FIX THAT WORKS (verified end-to-end, dev + prod + container): use a SIDE-EFFECT import in
    __root.tsx — `import "../styles.css";` — and emit NO stylesheet link from head(). Start's route
    manifest then owns the <link>. Result: exactly one CSS asset in .output/public
    (index-AxDKzI06.css), the SSR'd HTML references it, and it returns 200 in the container. In
    dev the CSS is served through Start's own /@tanstack-start/styles.css?routes=... entry, so dev
    styling works too.
    => MANDATORY PLAN CORRECTION #2: 4.2/4.3/4.4 must import the stylesheet for side effects in
    __root.tsx, never via `?url` + head().links. Add an assertion to each app's migration that the
    built server output and .output/public agree on the CSS filename.

=== ADDITIONAL VALIDATED FINDINGS (beyond the five checks) ===

(6) SDK PRESET INTEGRATION PROVEN (the actual core of the 4.2/4.3 recipe). Wired
    `src/routes/v1/$.ts` to `createApiPassthrough()` from @bc-solutions-coder/sdk/server/passthrough
    (the 3.7 deliverable) against a local echo upstream. Both `vite dev` and the built Nitro server
    forwarded method, pathname, body, and the inbound Cookie header, and returned the upstream
    Set-Cookie verbatim. The linked workspace SDK subpath bundles into .output correctly. Pattern
    that worked (memoise at module scope, construct lazily on first request, so a bare boot needs
    no upstream):
      let passthrough: ApiPassthrough | undefined;
      ANY: ({ request }) => { passthrough ??= createApiPassthrough(); return passthrough.handle(request); }

(7) X-FORWARDED-FOR SURVIVES — but only if the route stamps it. `createApiPassthrough`'s
    forwardClientIp needs the host to set `x-wallow-client-ip` (CLIENT_IP_HEADER) because a WHATWG
    Request has no socket; wallow-auth's auth-server.ts does this today (Wallow-tt5j). A Start
    server-route handler receives only a Request — BUT srvx exposes the peer address as
    `request.ip`, and I confirmed it is populated in BOTH `vite dev` ("127.0.0.1") and the built
    Nitro server ("::1"); the Request also carries `runtime`, `waitUntil`, `context`. There is no
    `request.node`. => 4.3/4.4 recipe: in the splat handler, clone the Request headers, set
    `x-wallow-client-ip` from `(request as ServerRequest).ip`, and hand that to the passthrough.
    Without this line the XFF chain silently loses this hop — a real security-relevant regression.

(8) PORT CONTRACT. `vite dev` DOES honor process.env.PORT (bound 3161 when PORT=3161). With PORT
    unset it binds 3000 — correct for wallow-web, WRONG for wallow-auth (3002) and minimal-app
    (3010). => every migrated app's vite.config.ts must add
    `server: { port: Number(process.env.PORT ?? <app default>) }`, otherwise that app's
    playwright.config.ts `webServer` (which waits on port 3002/3000 and does NOT inject PORT into
    the child env) times out. `node .output/server/index.mjs` honors PORT unconditionally.

(9) THE reactPluginInDev:false HYDRATION HAZARD IS GONE. minimal-app's dev-server.ts carries a long
    comment: react() is excluded in dev because the Fast Refresh preamble Vite prepends to <head>
    shifts what React hydrates against (the root route renders the whole document) and breaks the
    readiness signal. Under Start with react() wired normally, the dev-served HTML contains NO
    refresh preamble and no $RefreshReg$ in the document — Start injects the client entry through
    <Scripts/> and its own virtual entry instead of prepending to head. So Fast Refresh is
    available in dev with no hydration hazard, and that comment dies with dev-server.ts rather than
    needing to be carried forward. (0928 item 21's "Fast Refresh works in dev" payoff is real.)

=== ROUTE-TREE CODEGEN DRIFT (the scout's flagged risk — CONFIRMED, and it is worse than "update
    it in 4.5") ===
.github/workflows/route-tree-drift.yml regenerates via `pnpm --filter <app> routes:generate`
(tsr generate, router-cli, tsr.config.json) and then `git diff --exit-code` on the two committed
routeTree.gen.ts files. Every app migration DELETES routes:generate, @tanstack/router-cli, and
tsr.config.json. The workflow triggers on `apps/wallow-*/src/routes/**` and
`apps/wallow-*/tsr.config.json` — so the moment 4.3 (wallow-auth) lands, that workflow runs and
dies at ERR_PNPM_NO_SCRIPT, and stays red across 4.3 and 4.4 if the fix is deferred to 4.5.
MITIGATION (verified): the Start plugin regenerates src/routeTree.gen.ts as a side effect of
`vite build` — I deleted routeTree.gen.ts, ran `vite build`, and it came back byte-correct. So:
  - In 4.3's OWN commit, change the wallow-auth line to
    `pnpm --filter @bc-solutions-coder/wallow-auth build`; in 4.4's own commit do the same for
    wallow-web. Do NOT batch both into one commit — each app still has router-cli until its own
    migration lands.
  - In 4.5: drop `packages/web-shell/src/server/**` and `apps/wallow-*/tsr.config.json` from the
    `paths:` filters, add `apps/wallow-*/vite.config.ts`, and add minimal-app
    (`apps/examples/minimal-app/src/routes/**` + its routeTree.gen.ts, today unguarded) to both the
    paths and the git-diff list — as the bead already says.
  - Keep routeTree.gen.ts COMMITTED. Do not gitignore it: `pnpm check` runs typecheck before build,
    so a fresh clone would fail tsc without it.
  - REJECTED alternative: keeping router-cli + tsr.config.json just for CI. It would duplicate
    routeFileIgnorePattern across two configs that can silently disagree — the exact drift the
    workflow exists to catch.

=== E2E SURVIVAL ===
Nothing in either Playwright suite selects on host internals; all selectors are data-testid and the
readiness gate is [data-app-ready='true'], both of which the migration preserves. Specific items:
  - Both playwright.config.ts files keep `command: "pnpm dev"` and the WALLOW_API_INTERNAL_URL
    default — valid post-migration, CONDITIONAL on finding (8) (explicit server.port).
  - apps/wallow-web/e2e/routes.spec.ts asserts `/` renders for an anonymous visitor because
    beforeLoad's getUser() hits the app's own /bff/user and 401s off the absent session cookie. Its
    header comment names the h3 bridge and must be rewritten in 4.4's commit. More important: the
    config's comment records that src/lib/bff-server.ts calls loadBffConfigFromEnv() AT MODULE LOAD
    and throws on any missing key. In a Start server bundle a module-load throw can take down more
    than /bff/* — 4.4 should construct the BFF server lazily on first request (the memoise pattern
    in (6)), not at module scope.
  - e2e/global-setup.ts warms to hydration and explicitly credits web-shell's createDevServer for
    fixing the mid-request re-optimisation storm (504 "Outdated Optimize Dep") by pointing Vite's
    dep scan at the client entry. That fix dies with the host. Start owns its own entry, so the
    scan target changes; if a cold-cache first run regresses, the mitigation is
    optimizeDeps.include for the @base-ui/react subpaths @bc-solutions-coder/ui reaches (same
    gotcha already recorded for packages/ui's vitest browser project). Keep global-setup.ts either
    way — it is the suite's guard — but update its stale web-shell paragraph in 4.5's sweep.
  - The containerized path (E2E_BASE_URL, scripts/e2e.sh) is unaffected beyond each Dockerfile CMD
    becoming `node .output/server/index.mjs`; compose services carry no command: override, and the
    /health healthchecks keep working (verified: /health as a Start server route answers 200 in the
    container).

=== WHAT RETIRES THE TEMPORARY toH3Handler SHIM (D13a) ===
apps/wallow-web/src/lib/bff-server.ts:137's `// TEMPORARY until Phase 3 deletes this host` and the
toH3Handler() function exist only to wrap the SDK's web-standard handlers back into h3 for the
old host. Task 4.4 retires them by construction: the Start server routes call the SDK's web
handlers directly with the inbound Request and return the Response unmodified — proven in (6),
where createApiPassthrough().handle(request) was called straight from an ANY handler with no
adapter of any kind. Delete toH3Handler() and the h3 createApp/createRouter dispatch block
wholesale; keep the store-selection logic and the bff/apiProxy handler construction, which the new
routes call into. The h3 dependency then leaves wallow-web's package.json in the same commit.
Nothing else retires the shim, and nothing needs to survive it.

=== ABORT CRITERIA — NONE TRIPPED ===
Items 1-3 all pass at the bumped pins, so the migration does NOT stop and version analysis stays
closed. Item 4 passes, so the D9 fallback is NOT taken. Standing abort criteria for 4.2 (the first
real app): if, after applying corrections #1 and #2, minimal-app's `vite build` + container boot
cannot serve its own hashed CSS, or a Start server route cannot reach the SDK passthrough, STOP and
re-open this spike rather than hand-rolling an adapter — both were proven working here, so a
failure would mean an app-specific assumption is wrong, not a platform limit.

=== CORRECTED SHARED vite.config.ts FOR 4.2/4.3/4.4 ===
  import { wallowStyles } from "@bc-solutions-coder/styles/vite";
  import { tanstackStart } from "@tanstack/react-start/plugin/vite";
  import react from "@vitejs/plugin-react";
  import { nitro } from "nitro/vite";
  import { defineConfig } from "vite";

  export default defineConfig({
    server: { port: Number(process.env.PORT ?? <3010 | 3002 | 3000>) },
    plugins: [
      tanstackStart({
        router: { routeFileIgnorePattern: String.raw`\.(test|spec)\.(ts|tsx)$` },
      }),
      react(),
      nitro(),
      ...wallowStyles(),
    ],
  });
(no `vite: { installDevServerMiddleware: ... }` key at all; stylesheet imported for side effects in
__root.tsx.)

CLEANUP: probe processes killed, spike container and image removed, echo upstream stopped. The
probe project is left at scratchpad/start-probe purely as evidence and is outside the repo; the
repo working tree was never touched by this spike (the one staged apps/examples/minimal-app change
in the tree is task 0.9's AnyRouter removal by another teammate, not mine).

title: Migrate apps/examples/minimal-app to TanStack Start
description: Migrate `apps/examples/minimal-app` to a real TanStack Start application -- first of the three apps, carrying the version-pin risk before the two production apps take it. This app is NOT an Aspire resource and has no Dockerfile/production-compose service (verified fact V16) -- no Aspire/Docker steps belong in this task.
design:
Files:
- Rewrite: `vite.config.ts` (the shared shape from the feature description), `src/router.tsx`, `src/routes/__root.tsx`.
- Create: `src/routes/v1/$.ts`, `src/routes/connect/$.ts`, `src/routes/[.]well-known/$.ts` (exact bracket-escaping as proven in the 3.0 spike), `src/routes/health.ts`, `src/start.ts`.
- Delete: `server.ts`, `dev-server.ts`, `vite.ssr.config.ts`, `src/ssr.tsx`, `src/client.tsx`, `src/lib/proxy-server.ts` (139 lines), `src/lib/proxy-paths.ts` -- replaced by `createApiPassthrough` (task 2.7). This app has no `proxy-paths.test.ts`, so no spec dies with those two files.
- Modify: `package.json` -- exact version pins per the shared shape; drop the direct `h3` dependency; scripts: `dev` = `vite dev`, `build` = `vite build`, `start` = `node .output/server/index.mjs` (or the D9-fallback host, per task 3.0's outcome).

Steps:
1. `router.tsx`: inferred return type (no `AnyRouter` annotation -- see task 0.9), per-request `QueryClient`, `setupRouterSsrQueryIntegration({ router, queryClient })`.
2. `__root.tsx`: route-level `head()` + `<HeadContent/>` + `<Scripts/>`; keep the existing branding-theme injection + `ReadyIndicator` (`data-app-ready` marker); wire `defaultErrorComponent`, `defaultPendingComponent`, and a branded `notFoundComponent` (the old host's error handling dies with it, so these boundaries land in this same change).
3. Server routes: a single `ANY` handler per splat route delegating to `createApiPassthrough` (D8).
4. `src/start.ts`: global request middleware building `createWallowSdk` per request into router context.
5. Verify: `pnpm check` -> `pnpm dev` boot + manual smoke -> `vite build` + `node .output/server/index.mjs` boot. Confirm the migration payoffs actually land: Fast Refresh works in dev, `autoCodeSplitting` is on, built assets are content-hashed.
acceptance_criteria: `pnpm check` green; `pnpm dev` boots and a manual smoke passes; `vite build` followed by `node .output/server/index.mjs` (or the D9-fallback host command) boots successfully; Fast Refresh works in dev; `autoCodeSplitting` is enabled; built client assets are content-hashed; no Aspire/Docker changes were made to this app. Commit: `feat(examples)!: migrate minimal-app to tanstack start` (breaking, D15).
notes: GREEN — minimal-app migrated to TanStack Start + Nitro. Verified by doing: build, boot, dev-boot, real HTTP probes. FILES ADDED - src/start.ts — createStart({requestMiddleware:[sdkMiddleware]}), exports startInstance. Per-request createWallowSdk (baseUrl = ABSOLUTE request origin, not '/', because hey-api builds new Request(url) before the fetch seam and Node cannot parse a relative URL); internalOrigin from WALLOW_WEB_INTERNAL_URL. ISOMORPHIC IMPORTS ONLY — Start aliases the start entry into BOTH module graphs, so importing @bc-solutions-coder/sdk/server (openid-client/iron-webcrypto) here would poison the client bundle. The one process.env read sits inside the .server() callback. - src/lib/api-passthrough.ts — thin wrapper over createApiPassthrough(), lazily constructed + memoised at module scope. NOT in the bead's file list; created so the three splat routes do not triplicate the client-IP stamping. - src/lib/api-passthrough.test.ts — 4 node tests guarding the stamp + the no-clone rule (see DEVIATION 3). - src/routes/v1/$.ts, src/routes/connect/$.ts, src/routes/[.]well-known/$.ts — server:{handlers:{ANY}} splats, all delegating to handleApiPassthrough. - src/routes/health.ts — GET returns 'ready'. FILES REWRITTEN - vite.config.ts, src/router.tsx (createRouter -> getRouter), src/routes/__root.tsx (shellComponent + HeadContent/Scripts + side-effect '../styles.css'), package.json (exact pins, routes:generate dropped), tsconfig.json, src/vite-env.d.ts (declare module '*.css'), .gitignore (.output/.nitro/.tanstack), README.md, HelloCard body copy. FILES DELETED (git rm): server.ts, dev-server.ts, vite.ssr.config.ts, src/ssr.tsx, src/client.tsx, src/lib/proxy-server.ts, src/lib/proxy-paths.ts, tsr.config.json. RECIPE DEVIATIONS — 4.3/4.4 MUST APPLY 1 AND 3 1. NEW REQUIRED VITE KEY: environments.client.build.copyPublicDir = true. nitro/vite's configEnvironment does 'config.build.copyPublicDir ??= false' on the client env because it assumes it alone fills .output/public. Effect: wallowStyles()'s brandAssetsPlugin (publicDir -> packages/styles/assets) is silently dropped from the BUILD ONLY — dev serves /piggy-icon.svg fine, the built server 404s it, breaking both the favicon and ForkAttribution's . Nitro uses ??=, so spelling the flag out in the app config wins. CONFIRMED: .output/public/piggy-icon.svg present and 200 after the fix. This is the spike's Correction-2 class of bug for a different asset — 4.3/4.4 will hit it identically. 2. src/lib/sdk.ts left UNTOUCHED (out of scope; its 8 bootstrap tests pin configureBffClient({baseUrl:'/'}) and a regex that router.tsx side-effect-imports './lib/sdk'). The app therefore carries BOTH the legacy getSdk facade and the new per-request createWallowSdk. Only a stale doc-comment in sdk.bootstrap.test.ts was fixed (it named the deleted src/lib/proxy-server.ts); NO assertion changed. 3. DO NOT CLONE THE REQUEST TO STAMP THE CLIENT IP. The obvious 'passthrough.handle(new Request(request, { headers }))' compiles and THROWS AT RUNTIME: 'TypeError: Cannot read private member #state from an object whose class did not declare it' (undici Request ctor) -> every /v1, /connect, /.well-known request 500s. Cause: srvx's request is its own class that only claims to be a Request via Symbol.hasInstance, so undici's copy ctor passes the instanceof check then reads a private field that does not exist. FIX: set the header on the inbound request in place — request.headers.set(CLIENT_IP_HEADER, request.ip). title: Ship createWallowBffServer + createApiPassthrough server presets
description: Ship two server presets that absorb what every fork currently hand-assembles: `createWallowBffServer(config)` (env config load, session-store selection, handler + proxy construction) and `createApiPassthrough({ apiInternalUrl, prefixes, forwardClientIp })` (the reverse-proxy logic currently triplicated across `auth-server.ts` 201 lines and `proxy-server.ts` 139 lines). No `createPassthroughProxy` extraction into web-shell (D5) -- both presets ship from the SDK server entry.
design:
Files: new `packages/sdk/src/server/bff-server.ts`, `src/server/passthrough.ts` + tests; new subpath export `./server/passthrough`; `packages/sdk/package.json`.
Steps:
- `createWallowBffServer(config)`: env config load, store selection (`REDIS_URL` set -> Redis/Valkey adapter, else cookie store), handler + proxy construction -- returns `{ handleBff(request), handleApi(request), handleHealth() }`, all web-standard `Request -> Response`.
- `createApiPassthrough({ apiInternalUrl, prefixes, forwardClientIp })`: forwarded headers, X-Forwarded-For append, `Set-Cookie` preservation, and a prefix allowlist that MUST include `/.well-known/**` (omitting it broke OIDC discovery once before -- see the repo's h3-proxy memory). Ships as its OWN subpath (`./server/passthrough`) so passthrough-only apps don't pull in `openid-client`.
- Env-contract fail-fast: `loadBffConfigFromEnv` validates at boot and throws ONE error listing every missing/invalid variable -- no first-request 500s.
- Export mount-point constants `WALLOW_API_MOUNT = "/api"` and `WALLOW_BFF_MOUNT = "/bff"` so apps and the SDK agree on prefixes by import, not by string convention.
- Set `"sideEffects": false` in `packages/sdk/package.json`.
- Port the strongest existing test cases from the apps' current host test suites.
acceptance_criteria: `createWallowBffServer` and `createApiPassthrough` exist, are tested, and `createApiPassthrough`'s prefix allowlist includes `/.well-known/**`; `loadBffConfigFromEnv` throws one aggregated error listing every missing/invalid env var at boot; `WALLOW_API_MOUNT`/`WALLOW_BFF_MOUNT` are exported constants; `packages/sdk/package.json` declares `"sideEffects": false` and a `./server/passthrough` export. `pnpm --filter @bc-solutions-coder/sdk test` green. Plus src/index.test.ts > server entry > exports isWallowError (1 failing; the two BROWSER export-name specs already pass because the scaffold module is wired).

PASSING-BY-DESIGN (9, expected — the stub returns false so every negative case is trivially satisfied): the 8 'rejects <x>' cases (plain Error, TypeError, null, undefined, string, number, {}, unbranded look-alike {status,code,title}) and 'exports WallowError as a real Error subclass carrying the RFC 7807 members'. The 8 rejects only become meaningful once isWallowError has real logic; the unbranded-look-alike case is the one that forbids duck-typing on status/code/title.

HOW THE DUPLICATION TEST WORKS (this is the acceptance criterion's 'module-graph duplication scenario'): vi.resetModules() then await import('./index') yields a genuinely distinct module namespace. The spec asserts duplicate.WallowError !== WallowError as a GUARD (already passing — duplication is real, not a no-op) and 'fromDuplicate instanceof WallowError === false' (already passing — instanceof is genuinely broken), so the only assertion left for green is isWallowError(fromDuplicate) === true. It duplicates './index' (not the errors module) deliberately, so the spec stays valid wherever green re-homes the class. It also checks the symmetric direction: duplicate.isWallowError(ourInstance) === true.

The setPrototypeOf(error, Error.prototype) spec is the implementation-agnostic 'not instanceof' pin: it only rejects checks that consult prototype identity. It DOES require the brand to be reachable without the WallowError prototype — i.e. an OWN property set in the constructor (or a well-known/global-registry symbol), not a prototype member.

FOR GREEN (implementation guidance, do not edit test files):
- Home the class at packages/sdk/src/errors.ts (already scaffolded there, already re-exported from src/index.ts). Using Symbol.for('wallow.error') (global symbol registry) is the strongest option — it survives module duplication AND is not cloneable by accident. NEVER instanceof, and do NOT duck-type on status/code/title (an unbranded look-alike must be rejected).

title: Port server/proxy.ts to web-standard; fix URL-construction shape
description: Port `packages/sdk/src/server/proxy.ts` (699 lines) from h3 to web-standard `(request: Request) => Promise<Response>`, and fix an unsafe URL-construction shape (F11 from docs/plans/2026-07-27/0908-sdk-review.md). Do NOT change the refresh-lock, 401-retry, cookie-challenge-detection, Retry-After, or RFC 7807 passthrough logic -- this proxy's core logic is deliberately correct as-is (see the epic's "do not simplify" register) and only its transport shape changes.
design:
Files: `packages/sdk/src/server/proxy.ts` (699 lines) + tests (1446 lines).
Steps: same porting rules as task 2.2. Replace `new URL(stripped, base)` with the concatenation pattern already used in `auth-server.ts:150` plus explicit path normalization, with tests covering `//` and `..` path shapes. Add a test pinning the CSRF synchronizer binding: the double-submit cookie must be validated against `session.csrfToken`, not merely cookie == header, through the new `Request` shape. Add an `/api/**` path-allowlist enforcement test (F12b): a request addressed outside the configured proxy prefixes must be rejected, not forwarded upstream.
acceptance_criteria: Proxy tests pass calling the ported handler directly with `new Request(...)`; new tests cover `//`/`..` URL-normalization edge cases, the CSRF synchronizer-token binding (not just cookie==header), and the `/api/**` path-allowlist rejection (F12b). Refresh-lock/401-retry/challenge-detection/Retry-After/RFC-7807 behavior is unchanged (existing tests for those still pass). `pnpm --filter @bc-solutions-coder/sdk test` green. Commit: `feat(sdk)!: api proxy accepts web-standard request/response` (breaking, D15).
notes:
RED (WRITE TESTS phase) — proxy.ts port + F11 + F12b. Paired with Wallow-pu6a.3.2; both land together
(shared readSession/writeSession signatures — see the RED note on 3.2 for the exact API).

TEST_STATUS: red as intended.
Combined targeted run: npx vitest run src/server/handlers.test.ts src/server/proxy.test.ts src/server/config.test.ts
  -> 155 tests: 98 FAILING, 57 passing.  proxy.test.ts alone: 35 pass / 44 fail.
BASELINE before this phase: handlers.test.ts + proxy.test.ts = 89 tests, all passing.
The 35 still-passing proxy tests are deliberate: they cover the pure functions this bead must NOT touch
(ensureFreshSession, forceRefreshSession, forwardWithResilience, csrfTokenMatches, isStateChangingMethod).
If any of those 35 go red during green, the port changed something it was told not to.
Gate status: `tsc --noEmit` CLEAN, `oxlint --deny-warnings` CLEAN, `oxfmt --check` CLEAN.

FILES (staged, mine only):
  packages/sdk/src/server/proxy.ts       (transport shell stubbed; 700 -> 557 lines)
  packages/sdk/src/server/proxy.test.ts  (1446 -> 1958 lines)

=== TARGET API ===
export type ApiProxyHandler = (request: Request) => Promise<Response>;
export function createApiProxy(config: BffConfig, store?: SessionStore): ApiProxyHandler

=== WHAT WAS TOUCHED IN proxy.ts (scaffold) ===
Removed the whole `from \"h3\"` import block (defineEventHandler, getMethod, getRequestHeaders,
getRequestPath, readRawBody, setResponseHeaders, setResponseStatus, EventHandler, H3Event).
createApiProxy's body now throws NOT_IMPLEMENTED.
Deleted, needing a ported restore (all four change shape): changed(), respondToFailure(),
forwardableHeaders(), and the constant FORBIDDEN_STATUS = 403. Also removed the now-unused
`import { readSession, readSessionRef, writeSession, writeSessionRef } from \"./handlers\"` — green
restores it, with the new Request/Headers signatures.
Recover the h3 original with: git show HEAD:packages/sdk/src/server/proxy.ts

=== PRESERVED BYTE-IDENTICAL (the do-not-simplify register) ===
csrfTokenMatches, isStateChangingMethod, ensureFreshSession, refreshUnderLock, forceRefreshSession,
forceRefreshStored, forwardWithResilience, attemptForward, isAuthFailure, isRedirect, hasRefreshToken,
authFailureError, upstreamError, retryAfterMs, boundWait, delay, causeDetail, logFault, UpstreamError,
and every exported constant. Refresh-lock, 401-retry, cookie-challenge detection, Retry-After bounding
and RFC 7807 passthrough are OUT OF SCOPE for this bead — only the transport shell changes.

=== NEW COVERAGE ===
F11 unsafe URL construction (describe \"createApiProxy upstream URL construction\", 6 tests):
  The h3 proxy built its target with `new URL(strippedPath, config.apiBaseUrl)`. That is a RELATIVE
  resolution with the browser-supplied path as the relative part, so a path beginning `//` makes the URL
  parser read the next segment as an AUTHORITY: `/api//evil.test/steal` resolves to https://evil.test/steal
  and the proxy attaches the session bearer to a request aimed at the attacker's host. Tests:
  - protocol-relative and backslash-escaped-authority paths: EVERY fetch call's origin must remain
    https://api.example.com (asserted over all calls, not just the first).
  - `..` dot-segments must not climb above the API base path.
  - a path prefix on apiBaseUrl (https://api.example.com/v1) must be PRESERVED -> /v1/users. The old
    relative resolution silently discarded it.
  - a trailing slash on apiBaseUrl must not double.
  - the query string forwards verbatim, percent-decoding intact.
  Green approach: join the stripped path onto the base as a path (do not pass it as the relative part),
  then assert the resolved origin equals the configured API origin before forwarding.

F12b path allowlist (describe \"createApiProxy path allowlist\", 6 tests):
  Under h3 the mount point was the router's business, so the handler never checked the path. Called
  directly it is an open bearer-attaching relay. Tests: /internal/metrics, /, /bff/user, and /apiary/bees
  -> 404 with NO upstream fetch. /apiary is the one that matters: a naive startsWith(\"/api\") accepts it,
  so the check must be a segment-boundary test (path === \"/api\" || path.startsWith(\"/api/\")).
  DECISION: reject with 404 and no upstream call (not 403) — the proxy simply does not serve that path,
  and 404 leaks nothing about what the BFF does mount.
  One test asserts the rejection happens BEFORE the session is read (calls.read === 0).
  The literal \"/api\" mount stays a literal here; the WALLOW_API_MOUNT constant belongs to bead 3.7.

NEW RISK 2 — buffered request bodies (describe \"createApiProxy request-body buffering\", 4 tests):
  forwardWithResilience REPLAYS the request after a reactive 401. A ReadableStream body cannot be
  replayed — the first fetch consumes it and the retry throws \"Response body object should not be
  disturbed or locked\". Passing request.body straight through would pass every test where the token
  happens to be fresh and fail exactly when a user's token expires mid-POST. Use
  `await request.arrayBuffer()` (skip it entirely for GET/HEAD: fetch rejects a GET carrying a body).
  Tests: the forwarded body is not a ReadableStream and decodes to the original JSON; after a reactive
  401 both attempts carry the identical payload and the retry carries the rotated bearer; a non-UTF-8
  binary payload replays byte-for-byte (proves it was not round-tripped through text); a GET forwards
  `undefined` as its body.

Header handling (describe \"createApiProxy header handling\", 5 tests):
  - the client's cookie, host, and content-length are DROPPED from the upstream request while
    content-type/accept survive and authorization is the bearer. content-length matters: a stale value
    against a re-encoded body is a request-smuggling primitive — let the fetch layer compute it. cookie
    matters: the bearer must be the only credential the API sees.
  - EVERY upstream Set-Cookie passes through as its own header (asserted via getSetCookie(), so an
    object-literal init or a `set` would fail).
  - the re-sealed session cookie and an upstream Set-Cookie COEXIST — whichever is written second must
    not overwrite the first.
  - the upstream body streams through (res.body instanceof ReadableStream) — response-direction streaming
    stays lazy so a large download is not materialised in the BFF heap. Request direction buffers,
    response direction streams; do not make them symmetric.
  - upstream status/content-type/location pass through unchanged (201 + Location).

BEHAVIOUR DELTA to record: PROXIED_SAFE_METHODS is now SAFE_METHODS (GET, HEAD, OPTIONS). h3 answered
OPTIONS with a 405 of its own before the proxy ran, so the CSRF bypass for OPTIONS was untestable; called
directly it is observable and is now asserted. The stale comment saying otherwise is gone.

TEST HARNESS: makeHandle() is now a one-line direct call to createApiProxy(config, store). h3 is no
longer imported by proxy.test.ts.

ISSUES: none blocking. Same note as 3.2 — SDK dist/ deliberately not rebuilt so apps/wallow-web stays
green through red; the compat shim is bead 3.4.
GREEN: FILES=packages/sdk/src/server/proxy.ts (only createApiProxy and its private helpers; every pure function in the do-not-touch register is byte-identical to the h3 revision).

TEST_STATUS: proxy.test.ts 100% green -- every createApiProxy describe plus 'createApiProxy resilience', 'CSRF', 'upstream URL construction', 'path allowlist', 'request-body buffering', 'header handling'. CANARY INTACT: the 35 pure-function tests (ensureFreshSession, forceRefreshSession, forwardWithResilience, isStateChangingMethod, csrfTokenMatches) never went red at any point. Whole SDK suite 683/684; the single failure is in handlers.test.ts and is a test-harness bug documented on Wallow-pu6a.3.2 (completeCallback hardcodes the tx cookie name) -- nothing in proxy.ts is implicated. tsc --noEmit clean, oxlint --deny-warnings exit 0, oxfmt --check clean, build succeeds.

SYMBOLS: createApiProxy(config: BffConfig, store?: SessionStore): ApiProxyHandler, where ApiProxyHandler = (request: Request) => Promise<Response>. Signature unchanged from the red scaffold. No new exports. Restored as private: changed(), respondToFailure(), forwardableHeaders(), plus new strippedApiPath(), upstreamTarget(), mergeCookies(), bare(). New private constants FORBIDDEN_STATUS 403, NOT_FOUND_STATUS 404, API_PREFIX '/api', ROOT_PATH, PARENT_SEGMENT, EMPTY_BODY_LENGTH, FORWARDED_REQUEST_HEADERS, HOP_BY_HOP_HEADERS. New import: { readSession, readSessionRef, writeSession, writeSessionRef } from './handlers' (the cycle is safe under ESM -- no module-evaluation-time use of the other module's bindings).

HANDLER ORDER (h3 parity except where noted): path allowlist -> readSessionRef/401 -> readSession/401 -> CSRF gate -> ensureFreshSession (catch -> 401) -> re-seal if changed() -> build target -> forward -> re-seal if the reactive refresh rotated -> re-frame the upstream response.

F11 (upstream URL construction) as implemented -- two functions, and the second is the backstop for the first:
- strippedApiPath(pathname): segment-boundary prefix test, then collapses /{2,} -> / and rejects any '..' segment.
- upstreamTarget(config, path, search): parses apiBaseUrl, strips ONE trailing slash off its pathname, and builds new URL(`${base.origin}${basePath}${path}${search}`) -- an ABSOLUTE url string. The h3 bug was 'new URL(stripped, config.apiBaseUrl)', a RELATIVE resolution in which the browser-supplied path is the relative part: '//evil.test/x' re-roots the whole URL at an attacker authority WITH THE BEARER ATTACHED, and any path prefix on apiBaseUrl is silently discarded. Then it verifies target.origin === base.origin AND target.pathname.startsWith(basePath), returning null (-> 404) otherwise, so nothing forwards to a foreign origin even if the joining is wrong.
- Verified against all 6 tests: /api -> https://api.example.com/ ; /api/users with base /v1 -> /v1/users ; trailing-slash base does not double ; query appended verbatim from url.search.
- WORTH KNOWING FOR THE VERIFIER: two of the six attack tests are semi-vacuous because WHATWG URL normalisation fires first, at Request construction. '/api/../../admin/secrets' is already '/admin/secrets' by the time the handler sees it (-> allowlist 404), and '//evil.test/steal' never had the /api prefix (-> allowlist 404). The '..' rejection and the origin check are therefore defence in depth, not the thing those two tests actually exercise. The backslash test IS live: '\' is normalised to '/', so '/api/\/evil.test/steal' arrives as '/api//evil.test/steal' and it is the /{2,} collapse plus absolute joining that keeps it on api.example.com.

F12b (path allowlist) as implemented: 'path === "/api" || path.startsWith("/api/")'. A bare startsWith('/api') would also accept /apiary. The check runs FIRST, before readSessionRef, so a rejected path costs no session read (test asserts calls.read === 0) and no fetch. Bare /api forwards to the base root.

BODY DIRECTION ASYMMETRY (spike 3.1 NEW RISK 2): request bodies are BUFFERED -- new Uint8Array(await request.arrayBuffer()), and undefined for GET/HEAD or when byteLength is 0 so fetch is never handed a body it rejects. forwardWithResilience replays after a reactive 401, and a ReadableStream body cannot be replayed (the first fetch consumes it), so passing request.body straight through would have worked in every test where the token happened to be fresh and failed exactly when a user's token expired mid-POST. Response bodies STREAM: new Response(upstream.body, ...) so res.body stays a ReadableStream and a large download is never materialised in the BFF heap. 204/304 upstreams carry body === null, which the Response constructor accepts.

HEADERS:
- Upstream request: allowlist of content-type + accept only (h3 parity). cookie/host/content-length are excluded by construction, and authorization is added per attempt by attemptForward, so the rotated bearer rides the retry.
- Upstream response: forwardableHeaders now returns a Headers (was a Record, which silently dropped all but one Set-Cookie). It skips set-cookie inside forEach and then re-appends each line from getSetCookie(), which is the only safe way to read them. It drops transfer-encoding, content-encoding AND content-length -- content-length is NEW vs h3 and is deliberate: dropping content-encoding means the body has already been decoded, so a relayed length no longer matches the bytes on the wire, which is a request-smuggling primitive. Test asserts content-length is absent.
- COOKIE ACCUMULATOR: the BFF's own re-sealed session cookies are collected in a separate Headers during the request and merged (append, never set) into the success response AND into every failure response from respondToFailure. Losing a re-sealed cookie on an error path would leave the browser holding a refresh token that has already been spent. Verified: 'keeps the re-sealed session cookie alongside upstream Set-Cookie headers' passes with both present.
- Verified empirically on node v24.11.1 that Set-Cookie survives both the Response init fill and post-construction append, so neither path collapses duplicates.

changed(before, after) is byte-identical to h3 (version or accessToken differs). Note it cannot be replaced by a ref comparison: the test fake store's write() always returns the literal 'fake-ref', which equals the incoming cookie value, so a ref-equality check would never detect the reactive rotation and both re-seal tests would fail.

respondToFailure returns a Response now: UpstreamError relays the upstream status + forwardable headers + verbatim body (so ASP.NET errors[] and traceId survive); WallowError renders problem details with the machine code at the TOP level (matching the BFF's own convention, not the upstream extensions.code convention); anything else rethrows, exactly as h3 did.

title: Add createWallowSdk per-request factory + resolveInternalOrigin export
description: Add `createWallowSdk(options)`, a per-request factory that builds an SDK client instance over the generated `createClient()`, replacing the module-global client singleton model. Also export `resolveInternalOrigin(env, requestOrigin)` from the server entry so wallow-web's Phase-3 deletion of its own `ssr-origin.ts` has a replacement to import from.
design:
Files: new `packages/sdk/src/create-sdk.ts` + tests; mark `configureBffClient`/`configureSsrClient`/`facade.ts` `@deprecated` pointing at this factory (they and `src/client.ts`/`src/ssr.ts` are deleted outright in task 4.4). `src/runtime-config.ts` and `src/csrf.ts` survive (D14).
Signature: `createWallowSdk({ baseUrl, internalOrigin?, fetch?, cookieHeader? })`.
Steps -- write these as failing tests first: (a) two instances constructed with different `baseUrl` values do not bleed state into each other; (b) the CSRF interceptor registers exactly once per instance; (c) an SSR-side instance forwards the per-request cookie header; (d) `baseUrl` is a required option -- no baked `/api` default; (e) `internalOrigin` is applied ONLY inside the custom fetch implementation -- a server instance and a browser instance constructed with the same `baseUrl` must produce byte-identical generated query keys (this is what makes ssr-query hydration match, since query keys embed `baseUrl`); (f) export `resolveInternalOrigin(env, requestOrigin)` from the server entry, porting `resolveSsrInternalOrigin`'s existing logic and porting `ssr-origin.test.ts`'s test cases into this task's test file -- task 3.3 will delete wallow-web's `ssr-origin.ts` while its Phase-3 D13b bridge still needs these values, so ownership moves here first.
Implement `createWallowSdk` over the generated `createClient()`, binding the instance to each generated operation call via the standard `{ client }` call option (D14).
acceptance_criteria: All six (a)-(f) tests above pass; `resolveInternalOrigin` is exported from the server entry with `ssr-origin.test.ts`'s cases ported in; `pnpm --filter @bc-solutions-coder/sdk test` green. Commit: `feat(sdk): add per-request createWallowSdk factory`.

SCAFFOLD SIGNATURES (green must not change these shapes without noting why):

  interface CreateWallowSdkOptions { baseUrl: string; internalOrigin?: string; fetch?: typeof globalThis.fetch; cookieHeader?: string }
  interface WallowSdk { readonly client: Client }   // Client = generated ./generated/client

WHAT THE TESTS PIN (implementation constraints green must satisfy):
- Build a FRESH generated client per call via createClient(createConfig({ baseUrl })). Do NOT
  route through createClientConfig() (src/runtime-config.ts) — it HARD-CODES baseUrl:'/api'
  and would silently overwrite the caller's value. A test asserts getConfig().baseUrl is the
  caller's value verbatim.
- WallowSdk exposes only .client; generated ops bind via the standard { client: sdk.client }
  call option (one test drives usersGetCurrentUser that way).
- CSRF is the ONLY interceptor the factory registers: fns.filter(non-null).length === 1 for
  BOTH a plain instance and one with cookieHeader+internalOrigin. That means cookieHeader
  forwarding and internalOrigin retargeting must live INSIDE the instance's fetch wrapper,
  not as extra interceptors. Rationale: internalOrigin must not be visible to the interceptor
  chain (criterion e), so both per-request concerns sit on the same seam.
- The module-global generated client (src/client.ts) must gain no interceptors and no config
  mutation — two tests assert this.
- Criterion (e) is pinned two ways: (1) server and browser instances with the same baseUrl
  have byte-identical getConfig().baseUrl and internalOrigin never appears in
  JSON.stringify(getConfig()); (2) a test-registered interceptor captures the URL the client
  BUILDS (interceptors run after Request construction, before transport) and it must be
  byte-identical across both instances, while the transport-visible request.url is retargeted
  at internalOrigin. Fetch wrapper must preserve method, path, query AND body while
  retargeting (a POST-with-body test covers the Request-reconstruction hazard: you cannot
  pass a Request as RequestInit and keep its body — buffer it, e.g. await request.arrayBuffer()).
- empty/whitespace baseUrl throws rather than defaulting.
- resolveInternalOrigin precedence: WALLOW_WEB_INTERNAL_URL (empty = unset, trailing slashes
  stripped) -> http://localhost:${PORT} (numeric PORT only) -> requestOrigin (trailing slashes

2. resolveInternalOrigin takes requestOrigin as a FALLBACK (last in precedence). The wallow-web

3. Kept the env key name WALLOW_WEB_INTERNAL_URL (not a generic WALLOW_INTERNAL_URL) so every

4. Only resolveInternalOrigin moved — createSsrRequestContext (the other export of

5. Deprecated facade.ts's createConfiguredOnce only, NOT unwrap() — unwrap is the envelope

TEST FILE: packages/sdk/src/auth.test.ts (appended two describe blocks; no new file, no scaffolding needed — login/logout already exist and are exported). No production code touched. Ran targeted: pnpm exec vitest run src/auth.test.ts in packages/sdk => 15 tests, 4 FAILING, 11 passing.

FAILING (the spec):
1. 'login() throws a descriptive browser-context error rather than a bare ReferenceError' — asserts message matches /login\(\)/ and /browser/i and does NOT match /location is not defined/. Today: 'ReferenceError: location is not defined'.
2. 'logout() throws a descriptive browser-context error rather than a bare ReferenceError' — same shape for logout.

design: Replace the existing snapshot-diff assertion with an assertion that: every operation in `packages/sdk/openapi/v1.json` has (a) a unique `operationId` and (b) a typed 200 response schema. Dependency chain: task 2.1 (spike) must land first and gates 2.2/2.3 -- its abort criteria (multi-Set-Cookie survival, cookie chunking, streaming passthrough) determine whether the port proceeds as designed. 2.2 (port handlers.ts) and 2.3 (port proxy.ts) are independent of each other but both depend on 2.1, and both must land before 2.4 (drop h3 from the SDK -- needs the ported web-standard handlers/proxy to wrap), 2.5 (createWallowSdk factory -- built over the same web-standard surface), and 2.7 (server presets -- wrap the ported handler+proxy construction). 2.6 (SSR-safe login/logout) and 2.8 (export WallowError from browser entry) have no dependency on the rest of this feature's tasks and can be done anytime within Phase 2.
"Do not simplify" register applies here without exception: server/proxy.ts's OIDC refresh lock, 401 retry, cookie-auth challenge detection, Retry-After honoring, and RFC 7807 passthrough are ported (transport only, never redesigned); CSRF double-submit validation and session cookie chunking survive the port unchanged in behavior.
acceptance_criteria: PHASE 2 GATE: `pnpm check` green; SDK builds before apps; all three apps boot under `pnpm dev`; `./scripts/e2e.sh` green per 0.11 (no new failures, no new quarantines beyond task 0.11's recorded list -- this exercises the containerized wallow-auth suite only; the full three-suite comparison resumes at the Phase 3 gates).
notes:
SCOUT (Phase 2 SDK re-platform). Core files: packages/sdk/src/server/handlers.ts (467 lines, 4 h3 defineEventHandler exports: login/callback/user/logout), proxy.ts (700 lines, createApiProxy), config.ts (BffConfig+loadBffConfigFromEnv, cookieSecure at :48/:110-ish), session.ts (sealSession/unsealSession, iron-webcrypto), txstate.ts (sealTx/unsealTx), errors.ts (WallowError, no isWallowError yet), store/{cookie,valkey,redis-adapter,types}.ts (SessionStore interface unaffected by h3 port), server/index.ts (barrel). Consumers: apps/wallow-web/src/lib/bff-server.ts (imports createBffHandlers/createApiProxy from sdk/server, wraps in h3 createApp/router, exports handleBffRequest via toWebHandler — THE ONLY app importing sdk/server, confirms V9). apps/wallow-auth/src/lib/auth-server.ts and apps/examples/minimal-app/src/lib/proxy-server.ts are hand-rolled h3 PURE passthrough proxies that do NOT import sdk/server at all (own createProxyHandler/applyForwardedHeaders/resolveApiInternalUrl, near-duplicate code — this is what task 3.7's createApiPassthrough absorbs). auth-server.ts DOES already proxy /.well-known/** (line 192) alongside /v1/** and /connect/**, and stamps X-Forwarded-For via CLIENT_IP_HEADER (x-wallow-client-ip) — port this prefix-allowlist shape into createApiPassthrough.
