Iron ttl (bead 1.6/F7) is live at session.ts:69,71,91 — sealSession/unsealSession pass explicit `{...defaults, ttl: ttlMs}` to iron-webcrypto's seal/unseal, DEFAULT_SESSION_TTL_MS derived from config's DEFAULT_SESSION_TTL_SECONDS. Preserve both verbatim through the port (they're plain TS, unaffected by h3 removal, but re-verify with a targeted test after the file rewrite since the whole file is being rewritten).

The fix is exactly what the task describes: guard each function body with `typeof location !== "undefined"` and throw a clear `Error('login() must be called in a browser context...')`-style message in the else branch — do NOT add any TanStack/isomorphic-fn dependency. getUser() (auth.ts:66-85) is already SSR-safe (takes baseUrl/headers options) and needs no change.

3.7 (server presets): New packages/sdk/src/server/bff-server.ts + src/server/passthrough.ts. Template for createWallowBffServer: apps/wallow-web/src/lib/bff-server.ts:59-146 (env config load via loadBffConfigFromEnv, REDIS_URL branch building a ValkeySessionStore via createRedisAdapter vs CookieSessionStore fallback, then createBffHandlers(config,store)+createApiProxy(config,store) sharing one store) — port this whole block, replacing the h3 router.use/toWebHandler dispatch with a small path-based dispatcher over the (already web-standard, post-3.2/3.3) handlers, returning `{handleBff(request), handleApi(request), handleHealth()}`. Template for createApiPassthrough: apps/wallow-auth/src/lib/auth-server.ts (whole file, 201 lines — the more complete of the two near-duplicates, since it also stamps CLIENT_IP_HEADER/x-forwarded-for) merged with apps/examples/minimal-app/src/lib/proxy-server.ts (139 lines, simpler, no XFF stamping) — createApiPassthrough({apiInternalUrl, prefixes, forwardClientIp}) should generalize the hardcoded /v1/**,/connect/**,/.well-known/** prefix list into the `prefixes` option (defaulting to something including /.well-known/** — REQUIRED, confirmed by both existing hosts and the corrected memory below) and make the X-Forwarded-For/CLIENT_IP_HEADER stamping conditional on `forwardClientIp`. New package.json export needed: `./server/passthrough` subpath (mirrors existing `./server` shape in packages/sdk/package.json:17-20) — keeps it import-free of openid-client for passthrough-only consumers. Also add `WALLOW_API_MOUNT="/api"`/`WALLOW_BFF_MOUNT="/bff"` constants (new, no existing equivalent — currently these prefixes are string literals scattered across bff-server.ts routing and proxy.ts's `requestPath.replace(/^\/api/u,'')`) and `"sideEffects": false` to packages/sdk/package.json.

title: Spike: web-standard handler port risks (Set-Cookie, chunking, streaming)
description: Timeboxed (1 day) spike, in a scratch branch, proving the web-standard handler port is safe before doing it for real. Port the logout handler + one proxy path to `(request: Request) => Promise<Response>` and write tests proving three specific risks are handled.
design:
Write tests proving: (a) multiple `Set-Cookie` headers survive via `Headers.append` + `getSetCookie()` round-trip under Node 24; (b) session cookie chunking (indexed cookies + stale-chunk clearing) works through the new web-standard shape; (c) streaming response bodies pass through the proxy untouched.
Abort criteria: if multi-Set-Cookie cannot be made reliable, STOP and redesign before touching the rest of Phase 2 -- do not proceed to tasks 2.2/2.3 as currently scoped.
acceptance_criteria: Scratch-branch spike produces passing tests for (a), (b), and (c) above under Node 24, OR an explicit STOP decision with a redesign proposal if multi-Set-Cookie proves unreliable. Findings are recorded on this task before 2.2/2.3 are claimed.
notes:
SPIKE 3.1 RESULT: **GO** — port proceeds as scoped. All three abort-criteria risks validated empirically under Node 24.11.1 (v24 per .nvmrc) with runnable probes; 2 ADDITIONAL risks found that 3.2/3.3 MUST handle (one of them production-breaking). Probes live in the session scratchpad (probe-a/a2-setcookie, probe-b-chunking, probe-c-streaming, probe-d-miniport, probe-e/f-query, probe-g-replay .mts); nothing was written to the repo. Baseline before the port: `vitest run src/server/handlers.test.ts src/server/proxy.test.ts` = 89 passed / 2 files.

=== RISK (a) MULTI-SET-COOKIE — REAL CONSTRAINT, PROVEN SAFE ===
VERDICT: not an abort. `Headers.append("set-cookie", ...)` + `headers.getSetCookie()` carries N distinct cookies through a web-standard Response and survives a real HTTP round trip (server writer -> undici fetch client): a 302 carrying 3 Set-Cookie (incl. a Max-Age=0 chunk-clear) arrived as 3 separate headers. 16 Set-Cookie headers on one response (1 live chunk + 15 clears) also round-tripped fine.
CRITICAL: the host writers ALREADY do this correctly and are already tested — packages/web-shell/src/server/standalone-host.ts:80-98 and dev-server.ts:129-142 both skip set-cookie in `headers.forEach` then loop `getSetCookie()` -> `res.appendHeader`, with regression tests at standalone-host.test.ts:171-180 and dev-server.test.ts:386-395. So the wallow-web boundary needs NO change for this.
PROVEN RULES for the port (each verified, incl. negative controls):
  - `headers.append` or the array-of-pairs init `[["set-cookie",a],["set-cookie",b]]` are the ONLY ways to emit multiples.
  - An object-literal init CANNOT: duplicate JS keys collapse before Headers sees them (last wins). Never build cookie responses from an object literal.
  - `headers.set("set-cookie", ...)` after appends DESTROYS every prior cookie. Never use `.set` for set-cookie.
  - `headers.get("set-cookie")` comma-joins and is genuinely ambiguous — 2 cookies where one has `Expires=Wed, 21 Oct...` split into 3 pieces. Never parse it.
  - `headers.forEach` DOES fire once per set-cookie (Node 24), but folding that into a `Record<string,string>` keeps only the LAST. **This is a live latent bug in proxy.ts `forwardableHeaders` (:690-700), which builds exactly that Record** — today it silently drops all-but-one upstream Set-Cookie. 3.3 must return a `Headers` (skip set-cookie in forEach, then `for (const c of source.getSetCookie()) headers.append(...)`). Also drop `content-length` there, not just transfer-encoding/content-encoding, or a re-framed/streamed body mismatches.
  - Request side has no equivalent: one merged `cookie` header, parsed manually.

=== RISK (b) COOKIE CHUNKING — NOT A RISK ===
VERDICT: not an abort. Reimplemented readSessionRef/writeSessionRef/clearSession with zero h3 (cookie-es serialize/parse + Headers.append + `request.headers.get("cookie")`) and drove it over real HTTP through a simulated browser jar, using REAL sealed sessions from `CookieSessionStore`. All 12 assertions pass:
  - A realistic session (2.6KB access + 2.6KB id + refresh token) seals to 8475 chars -> 3 chunks, reassembles BYTE-IDENTICAL from the merged Cookie header and unseals to the original session (so the bead-1.6 iron `ttl` path is untouched by the transport change).
  - Stale-chunk clearing works: writing a 1-chunk session over a 3-chunk one leaves the jar holding exactly `[base]` and the short ref reads back with no contamination.
  - Logout emits one Set-Cookie per live cookie (base + `-csrf` + each `.N` chunk) in a single Response; jar ends empty.
  - `serialize()` of a full 3800-char chunk = 3872 bytes, still under the 4096 limit — cookie-es's default `encodeURIComponent` does NOT expand the iron alphabet (`Fe26.2**`, base64url, `*`), so MAX_COOKIE_VALUE_LENGTH=3800 stays correct. Do not change it.
  - F10 `__Host-` prefix composes correctly: `__Host-wallow_bff`, `__Host-wallow_bff.1`, `__Host-wallow_bff-csrf` all parse distinctly, and `serialize` output satisfies RFC 6265bis (Secure + Path=/ + no Domain). The whole probe was run under the `__Host-` name, so F10 is pre-validated for 3.2.
  - Pre-existing, unchanged by the port: a stale `.N` chunk left on the browser corrupts reassembly -> unseal fails -> treated as no session. Same in h3 today; it is why chunk clearing must survive verbatim.

=== RISK (c) STREAMING — SDK SIDE FINE; THE HOST IS THE BUFFER ===
VERDICT: not an abort, but the acceptance phrase "streaming passes through untouched" is only half-achievable in Phase 2. Measured against a slow SSE upstream (4 events, 150ms apart):
  - TODAY (`new Uint8Array(await upstream.arrayBuffer())`, proxy.ts:645): TTFB 614ms, 1 chunk — the client sees nothing until upstream ends.
  - `new Response(upstream.body, ...)` + web-shell's CURRENT buffering writer: TTFB 612ms — **still buffered**.
  - `new Response(upstream.body, ...)` + a streaming writer (`pipeTo(Writable.toWeb(res))`): TTFB 2ms, 4 chunks, body byte-identical to the buffered case.
  So 3.3 SHOULD return `upstream.body` directly (strictly better: no full-body buffering in the SDK, less memory), but real SSE end-to-end ALSO needs `writeWebResponse` in packages/web-shell/src/server/{standalone-host,dev-server}.ts to stop doing `await response.arrayBuffer()`/`await response.text()`. That is OUT OF SCOPE for 3.3 (different package, and dev-server's `text()` also corrupts binary) — **file a follow-up bead**; do not let 3.3 grow into web-shell.

=== NEW RISK 1 (HIGH — PRODUCTION-BREAKING IF PORTED NAIVELY) ===
The scout's mapping `getRequestURL(event) -> new URL(request.url)` is NOT behavior-preserving, and the blast radius is the OIDC token exchange.
  - h3's `getRequestURL` honors `x-forwarded-proto`/`host`: proven — the same request with `x-forwarded-proto: https, host: app.test` yields `https://app.test/bff/login?...`, without it yields `http://localhost/...`.
  - Both hosts build the Request as `new URL(req.url, `http://${req.headers.host}`)` (standalone-host.ts:135+, dev-server.ts:95+) — hardcoded `http:`, x-forwarded-proto ignored. So `new URL(request.url)` behind TLS termination gives `http://...` where today's code gives `https://...`.
  - Why it breaks: `handlers.ts:398` passes that URL as openid-client's `currentUrl`, and openid-client 6.8.4 derives the token-request `redirect_uri` from it — `redirectUri = stripParams(currentUrl)` (build/index.js:974) is handed to `authorizationCodeGrantRequest` (:993). Authorize-time sends `config.redirectUri` (oidc.ts:179). A scheme/host mismatch between the two = `invalid_grant` at the IdP, i.e. login breaks in any TLS-terminated deployment while passing every local test.
  - FIX for 3.2 (recommended, better than parity): build currentUrl from config, not from the request — `const currentUrl = new URL(config.redirectUri); for (const [k,v] of new URL(request.url).searchParams) currentUrl.searchParams.set(k,v);`. This makes the token-exchange redirect_uri provably identical to the authorize-time one and removes all dependence on proxy headers. Add a test asserting the URL handed to `exchangeCode` is rooted at `config.redirectUri` even when the request arrives as `http://localhost:3000/...`.

=== NEW RISK 2 (MEDIUM — CONSTRAINS 3.3's STREAMING CHANGE) ===
The REQUEST body must stay BUFFERED. `forwardWithResilience` replays the same `request.body` on the 401/login-redirect and 429 paths (proxy.ts:352-362 via `attemptForward`). Proven: an ArrayBuffer body replays across two fetches (both attempts saw 7 bytes); a `ReadableStream` body throws on the second attempt — "Response body object should not be disturbed or locked". So 3.3 maps `readRawBody(event,false)` -> `await request.arrayBuffer()` and MUST NOT forward `request.body` as a stream. Streaming is response-direction ONLY. (Streamed uploads would need a tee/buffer-on-retry design — out of scope, do not attempt.)

=== DEPENDENCY RECOMMENDATION ===
Add `cookie-es` as a DIRECT dependency of packages/sdk (validated: `serialize`, `parse`, `parseSetCookie`, `splitSetCookieString`). It is h3's own cookie layer, so behavior is identical to what `setCookie`/`getCookie` do today — the safest possible substitution. It is already in the store (`cookie-es@1.2.3` under h3, `cookie-es@3.1.1` transitively); take **^3.1.1** for a modern ESM-only build (v3 adds `allowMultiple` parse and drops the CJS dual build) unless the SDK's Vite externalization objects, in which case ^1.2.3 is proven working in the probes. Then packages/sdk/package.json:38 `h3` is removed by 3.4 and `cookie-es` replaces it. Do NOT hand-roll attribute serialization. Chunk-name string ops (`chunkCookieName`, MAX_COOKIE_VALUE_LENGTH, MAX_CHUNK_CLEAR) stay hand-rolled and unchanged — confirmed correct.

=== CONCRETE PORT PLAN — BEAD 3.2 (handlers.ts) ===
Mini-port already validated end-to-end (probe-d): logout + the F12a CSRF gate, driven by `new Request(...)` with no h3, all 9 assertions pass.
1. Types: `BffHandlers = { login, callback, user, logout }` where each is `(request: Request) => Promise<Response>`; drop the `EventHandler`/`H3Event` imports. `readSession`/`writeSession`/`readSessionRef`/`writeSessionRef` change their first parameter from `H3Event` to `Request` (read side) and to a `Headers` accumulator (write side) — proxy.ts imports all four, so 3.2 and 3.3 must land together in the same PR or 3.3 will not typecheck.
2. Cookie plumbing (shape proven in probe-b/d):
   - read: `parse(request.headers.get("cookie") ?? "")`
   - write: `headers.append("set-cookie", serialize(name, value, opts))` — one append per chunk, one per clear (value "", maxAge 0).
   - `clearSession(request, headers, config)` keeps reading the request's cookie names to find live `.N` chunks. Behavior unchanged.
3. Accessor map: `getQuery` -> `new URL(request.url).searchParams`; `getRequestURL` -> **see NEW RISK 1, do not use `new URL(request.url)` for the token exchange**; `sendRedirect` -> `new Response(null, {status:302, headers})` with `headers.set("location", url)` AFTER the cookie appends; `setResponseStatus+return null` -> `new Response(null, {status})`; the `user` handler's object return -> `Response.json({...user, csrfToken})` (h3 was JSON-serializing it implicitly).
4. returnTo (bead 1.5/F6) — PRESERVE VERBATIM. `safeReturnTo`/`isSafeReturnUrl` are pure and untouched by the port; keep BOTH call sites (login handlers.ts:344, callback re-check :437). One real behavior delta to cover with a test: for a REPEATED `?returnTo=` param h3's `getQuery` returns an ARRAY (so `typeof !== "string"` -> falls back to "/"), while `searchParams.get()` returns the FIRST value. Proven: `?returnTo=/safe&returnTo=//evil.test` -> h3 `["/safe","//evil.test"]` vs `searchParams.get` `"/safe"`. Both are safe because `safeReturnTo` sanitizes, but add a duplicate-param test so the delta is deliberate. (Non-issue confirmed: h3 1.15's getQuery does NOT type-coerce — `n=123`/`b=true` come back as strings, so no destr surprises.)
5. iron ttl (bead 1.6/F7) — session.ts is not touched by this bead at all. Re-verify with one test that a session written through the new write path unseals through the new read path (probe-b already proves the round trip holds with the real sealed values).
6. F12a logout CSRF gate — validated in probe-d, implement exactly this: non-POST -> `405` + `Allow: POST`, destroying NOTHING and clearing no cookies; POST with missing/mismatched `x-csrf-token` -> `403` problem+json `CSRF_INVALID`, `store.destroy` NOT called; POST + valid token -> destroy under the REASSEMBLED (multi-chunk) ref, clear base + `-csrf` + every chunk in one Response, 302 to the end-session URL with `id_token_hint`. Reuse `csrfTokenMatches`/`CSRF_HEADER` from proxy.ts. Write the RED tests first.
7. F10 `__Host-` default when `cookieSecure` — pre-validated by probe-b; config.ts:110 gets the conditional default plus an explicit env override mirroring the COOKIE_SECURE opt-out at config.ts:99-100.
8. Tests: `makeHandle` (handlers.test.ts:118-125) collapses to calling the handler directly; delete the `createApp/toWebHandler/App/H3Event` import at handlers.test.ts:1. Only 23 `new Request(` sites in that file — the assertions mostly survive; responses are now returned directly instead of via the app.

=== CONCRETE PORT PLAN — BEAD 3.3 (proxy.ts) ===
Mini-port validated (probe-d): prefix allowlist, 401-without-session, CSRF 403, bearer attach, prefix strip + query preservation — all pass through the new Request shape.
1. Accessor map: `getMethod` -> `request.method`; `getRequestHeaders(event)[k]` -> `request.headers.get(k)` (NOTE: h3 returns `undefined` for a missing header, `Headers.get` returns `null` — `csrfTokenMatches` takes `string|undefined`, so coerce with `?? undefined` at every call site or the CSRF check silently changes shape); `getRequestPath` -> `new URL(request.url).pathname`; `readRawBody(event,false)` -> `await request.arrayBuffer()` (NEVER the stream — NEW RISK 2); `setResponseStatus`/`setResponseHeaders` -> a single `new Response(bodyOrStream, {status, headers})`.
2. Response body: return `upstream.body` directly instead of `new Uint8Array(await upstream.arrayBuffer())` (proxy.ts:645). `respondToFailure` keeps buffering (it already consumed `bodyText`).
3. `forwardableHeaders` must return `Headers`, preserving multiple set-cookie via `getSetCookie()` and dropping `content-length` alongside transfer-encoding/content-encoding (see RISK (a)).
4. F11 URL construction — the vulnerability is confirmed, not theoretical: `new URL("//evil.test/steal", "http://api.internal:5001/").host === "evil.test"`, i.e. today's proxy.ts:604 lets a protocol-relative request path RETARGET the whole forward at an attacker host. Replace with concatenation + normalization (the auth-server.ts:150 pattern): collapse `/{2,}` -> `/`, REJECT any path whose segments include `..`, then `${base.replace(/\/$/,"")}${normalizedPath}${search}`. Both proven in probe-d (the evil path stays on the internal host; `..` throws). Test both cases.
5. F12b prefix allowlist BEFORE the `/api` strip — proven shape: reject unless `pathname === MOUNT || pathname.startsWith(MOUNT + "/")`, then strip.
6. DO NOT TOUCH (transport-shape only, per the "do not simplify" register): ensureFreshSession/refreshUnderLock/forceRefreshSession (:206-315), forwardWithResilience's retry/redirect/429 classification (:317-379), isAuthFailure (:428-437), retryAfterMs (:488-501). Their inputs are already web-standard (`ForwardRequest`/`fetch`/`Response`), so they need no change at all.
7. Tests: `makeHandle` (proxy.test.ts:335-341) collapses to a direct call; drop the h3 import at proxy.test.ts:3. 14 `new Request(` sites.

=== FOLLOW-UP BEADS TO FILE ===
(1) web-shell `writeWebResponse` streams instead of buffering, in BOTH standalone-host.ts and dev-server.ts (unblocks real SSE end-to-end; dev-server's `await response.text()` additionally corrupts binary bodies). (2) Optional: audit whether any deployment relies on the request-derived redirect_uri differing from `config.redirectUri` before 3.2 pins it to config.

title: Port server/handlers.ts to web-standard Request/Response
description: Port `packages/sdk/src/server/handlers.ts` (446 lines) from h3 to web-standard `(request: Request) => Promise<Response>` handlers, preserving byte-for-byte behavior where tests assert it (redirect shapes, cookie attributes, RFC 7807 bodies). While in the file, also land two security remediations that belong to this surface: F12a (logout must require POST+CSRF, not accept unauthenticated GET) and F10 (default the session cookie to a `__Host-` prefix whenever it's Secure, with an explicit opt-out for plain-http local dev).
design:
Files: `packages/sdk/src/server/handlers.ts` (446 lines) + `handlers.test.ts` (875 lines).
Steps: replace h3 accessors (`getCookie`/`setCookie`/`getQuery`/`sendRedirect`/etc.) with `Request`/`Response`/`Headers` equivalents; handlers become `(request: Request) => Promise<Response>` -- tests drop `createApp`/`toWebHandler` and call handlers directly with `new Request(...)`.
- F12a: write a failing test first -- a bare `GET /bff/logout` must return 405/403 and never clear the session; require `POST` + CSRF instead.
- F10: default the session cookie name to a `__Host-` prefix whenever the cookie is `Secure` (config default at `server/config.ts:110`), with an explicit config opt-out for plain-http local dev.
acceptance_criteria: `handlers.test.ts` passes calling handlers directly with `new Request(...)` (no h3 `createApp`/`toWebHandler`); a test proves `GET /bff/logout` is rejected and the session is not cleared; a test proves the `__Host-` cookie-name default when Secure, with dev opt-out. `pnpm --filter @bc-solutions-coder/sdk test` green. Commit: `feat(sdk)!: bff handlers accept web-standard request/response` (breaking -- SDK server contract change per D15).
notes:
RED (WRITE TESTS phase) — handlers.ts port + F12a + F10. Paired with Wallow-pu6a.3.3; both land together.

TEST_STATUS: red as intended.
Combined targeted run: npx vitest run src/server/handlers.test.ts src/server/proxy.test.ts src/server/config.test.ts
  -> 155 tests: 98 FAILING, 57 passing.
  handlers.test.ts  0 pass / 52 fail   (every test; whole module is a scaffold)
  proxy.test.ts    35 pass / 44 fail   (the 35 are the preserved pure-function register — see 3.3 note)
  config.test.ts   22 pass /  2 fail
BASELINE before this phase: handlers.test.ts + proxy.test.ts = 89 tests, all passing (2 files, 209ms).
Gate status: `tsc --noEmit` CLEAN, `oxlint packages/sdk/src/server --deny-warnings` CLEAN, `oxfmt --check` CLEAN.

FILES (staged, mine only):
  packages/sdk/src/server/handlers.ts       (rewritten as a signatures-only scaffold)
  packages/sdk/src/server/handlers.test.ts  (rewritten, 52 tests)
  packages/sdk/src/server/config.test.ts    (+8 tests for F10)

=== TARGET API the tests are written against ===
export type BffHandler = (request: Request) => Promise<Response>;
export interface BffHandlers { login: BffHandler; callback: BffHandler; user: BffHandler; logout: BffHandler }
export type BffUserResponse = BffSession[\"user\"] & { csrfToken?: string };
export function readSessionRef(request: Request, config: BffConfig): string | null
export function readSession(request: Request, config: BffConfig, store: SessionStore): Promise<BffSession | null>
export function writeSessionRef(headers: Headers, config: BffConfig, ref: string): void
export function writeSession(headers: Headers, config: BffConfig, store: SessionStore, session: BffSession): Promise<string>
export function createBffHandlers(config: BffConfig, store?: SessionStore): BffHandlers

DESIGN DECISION (binds 3.3 too): the READ side takes the incoming `Request`; the WRITE side takes the
`Headers` of the response under construction, NOT an H3Event and NOT a Response. Rationale: every cookie
must be Headers.append()-ed. `Headers.set` destroys cookies already written and an object-literal init
collapses duplicates before Headers ever sees them — either bug silently half-writes a chunked session.
Callers build `new Response(body, { headers })` from the accumulated Headers.

=== SCAFFOLD: what the GREEN implementer must restore ===
handlers.ts currently has signatures only; every body throws NOT_IMPLEMENTED. The h3 implementation is
intact in git — port it line by line rather than reinventing:
    git show HEAD:packages/sdk/src/server/handlers.ts
Deleted and needing a ported restore: baseCookieOpts, sessionCookieOpts, csrfCookieOpts, txCookieName,
csrfCookieName, chunkCookieName, clearSession, safeReturnTo, all four handler bodies, and the constants
MAX_COOKIE_VALUE_LENGTH=3800, MAX_CHUNK_CLEAR=16, FIRST_CHUNK_INDEX, SECOND_CHUNK_INDEX, CHUNK_STEP,
SINGLE_CHUNK, INITIAL_SESSION_VERSION, TOKEN_BYTES=24, MS_PER_SECOND, TX_COOKIE_MAX_AGE_SECONDS=600,
BAD_REQUEST_STATUS, UNAUTHORIZED_STATUS, FOUND_STATUS.
They were deleted rather than kept because oxlint correctness/no-unused-vars is an ERROR and `pnpm lint`
runs --deny-warnings, so h3-orphaned helpers would fail the gate during red.

=== NEW COVERAGE (beyond the ported 89) ===
F12a logout gate (describe \"logout CSRF gate\"), 8 tests:
  - GET/HEAD/PUT/DELETE /bff/logout -> 405 with an `Allow: POST` header, store.destroy NOT called, and
    res.headers.getSetCookie() EMPTY. The last assertion is the point: a rejected logout that still
    cleared the cookies is the same denial of service wearing a 403.
  - POST with no x-csrf-token -> 403 application/problem+json with body.code === CSRF_INVALID_CODE.
  - POST with a mismatched token -> 403; POST with a valid token minted for a DIFFERENT session -> 403.
  - POST with the session-bound token -> 302 + destroyed === [ref].
  Reuse csrfTokenMatches + CSRF_HEADER + CSRF_INVALID_CODE from proxy.ts; do not re-roll the comparison.
  TRAP: h3 returned `undefined` for a missing header, `Headers.get` returns `null`. Coerce with
  `?? undefined` or csrfTokenMatches receives null and the types lie.

NEW RISK 1 — token-exchange currentUrl (describe \"callback token-exchange currentUrl\"):
  currentUrl passed to authorizationCodeGrant must be built from config.redirectUri (origin + pathname)
  with the incoming code/state copied onto it — NOT `new URL(request.url)`. openid-client derives the
  token request's redirect_uri from currentUrl; the hosts build the Request as
  `http://${req.headers.host}${req.url}` and ignore x-forwarded-proto, so behind TLS termination the
  request arrives as http://localhost:3000/... and the IdP answers invalid_grant in production while
  every local test passes. The test drives exactly that: a request at http://localhost:3000 with a
  config.redirectUri of https://app.example.com/bff/callback.

F10 __Host- prefix — split across two files:
  config.test.ts (8 new tests, 2 currently failing): default cookieName becomes \"__Host-wallow_bff\" when
  cookieSecure; plain \"wallow_bff\" when COOKIE_SECURE=false (the browser DROPS a __Host- cookie over
  plain http — login would fail with no error anywhere); explicit COOKIE_NAME wins verbatim and is never
  double-prefixed; new opt-out env var COOKIE_HOST_PREFIX=false (chosen to mirror the COOKIE_SECURE=false
  pattern already in config.ts) relaxes the NAME only, leaving cookieSecure true; any unrecognized value
  fails secure and keeps the prefix.
  NOTE — 6 of those 8 pass ALREADY and are guards, not red: they assert \"wallow_bff\", which is today's
  default, so the opt-out paths coincide with current behaviour. Only the 2 that assert the new
  __Host-wallow_bff default are genuinely red. Do not delete the passing 6; they pin the opt-outs.
  handlers.test.ts (describe \"__Host- prefixed cookie names\", 3 tests) pins the handler side: the base,
  chunk (.1) and csrf (-csrf) names compose around the prefix without colliding, every emitted cookie
  satisfies Secure + Path=/ + no Domain, and a __Host- session round-trips through write/read.

Multi-Set-Cookie survival (describe \"multiple Set-Cookie headers\", 2 tests): a chunked callback emits
>=3 distinct Set-Cookie lines AND still carries its Location; logout emits one clearing line per live
cookie (base + every chunk + -csrf).

returnTo hardening (bead 1.5) is PRESERVED and extended, not weakened — sanitize-to-\"/\", never refuse.
  BEHAVIOUR DELTA the green implementer must know: h3's getQuery returned an ARRAY for a repeated
  parameter, which failed the `typeof === \"string\"` test and fell back to \"/\". searchParams.get returns
  the FIRST value, so `?returnTo=/safe&returnTo=//evil.test` now yields \"/safe\" (test asserts this) and
  the isSafeReturnUrl guard — not the parameter parser — is what has to reject a smuggled second value.
  A test with the unsafe value FIRST asserts it still sanitizes to \"/\".

iron-ttl (bead 1.6) is PRESERVED: session.ts is untouched, but the whole read/write transport around it
was rewritten, so the round trip is re-pinned through the new signatures — including a chunked session
(ref > 3800 chars) that must reassemble byte-exact, plus stale-higher-index-chunk clearing.

Other new coverage: /bff/user must set content-type application/json itself (h3 used to serialize the
returned object and stamp the header; nothing does that now).

TEST HARNESS: makeHandle() is a four-line path switch calling handlers.login/callback/user/logout
directly with new Request(...). No createApp, no toWebHandler, no defineEventHandler, no H3Event anywhere
in the file. h3 is no longer imported by handlers.test.ts.

ISSUES: none blocking. Note for the coordinator — the SDK dist/ was deliberately NOT rebuilt, so
apps/wallow-web (which typechecks against dist/ and is the only app importing sdk/server, via
src/lib/bff-server.ts) stays green through red; the compat shim is bead 3.4's job.
GREEN (1 blocked by TEST FAULT): FILES=packages/sdk/src/server/handlers.ts (ported h3 -> web-standard), packages/sdk/src/server/config.ts (F10), packages/sdk/package.json + pnpm-lock.yaml (cookie-es ^3.1.1 promoted from transitive h3 dep to a direct dep).

TEST_STATUS: SDK suite 683/684 pass (41 files, 40 green). handlers.test.ts 51/52. config.test.ts 8/8. proxy.test.ts fully green (canary intact: the 35 pure-function proxy tests never went red). tsc --noEmit clean. oxlint packages/sdk --deny-warnings exit 0. oxfmt --check clean. pnpm --filter @bc-solutions-coder/sdk build succeeds.

THE ONE FAILURE IS A TEST-HARNESS BUG, NOT AN IMPLEMENTATION BUG. handlers.test.ts:1202 'writes the session, chunk, and CSRF cookies under distinct __Host- names' fails with 'expected [] to include __Host-wallow_bff'. Cause: the shared helper completeCallback() (handlers.test.ts:943) sends a HARDCODED cookie name -- headers: { cookie: `wallow_bff_tx=${sealed}` } -- instead of deriving it from the config under test. The two __Host- tests pass cookieName: '__Host-wallow_bff', so the handler looks for '__Host-wallow_bff_tx', finds no tx cookie, and correctly answers 400 with zero Set-Cookie headers. names is therefore [] and the assertion fails.
PROOF: I copied handlers.test.ts verbatim to a scratch spec changing ONLY that line to `${config.cookieName}_tx=${sealed}` and ran it -> 52/52 PASS. Scratch file deleted; nothing left in the tree.
NOTE the sibling test at :1223 ('satisfies the __Host- attribute requirements on every cookie it writes') currently passes VACUOUSLY for the same reason -- it iterates an empty getSetCookie() array. Fixing the harness makes it assert for real (and it passes).
FIX (owner = whoever may touch tests; I must not): handlers.test.ts:943 -> cookie: `${config.cookieName}_tx=${sealed}`. I deliberately did NOT strip the __Host- prefix off the tx cookie name to make the test pass: that would write the PKCE verifier + state + nonce under an unprefixed name, re-opening the exact subdomain cookie-injection/login-fixation vector the prefix exists to close, and it contradicts the describe block's own stated intent ('the chunk (.1), CSRF (-csrf), and transaction (_tx) names all have to compose around it').

SYMBOLS (exported, unchanged signatures from the red scaffold):
- type BffHandler = (request: Request) => Promise<Response>
- interface BffHandlers { login; callback; user; logout: BffHandler }
- type BffUserResponse = BffSession['user'] & { csrfToken?: string }
- readSessionRef(request: Request, config: BffConfig): string | null
- readSession(request: Request, config: BffConfig, store: SessionStore): Promise<BffSession | null>
- writeSessionRef(headers: Headers, config: BffConfig, ref: string): void
- writeSession(headers: Headers, config: BffConfig, store: SessionStore, session: BffSession): Promise<string>
- createBffHandlers(config: BffConfig, store?: SessionStore): BffHandlers
server/index.ts already re-exported all of these; no edit needed there.

HOW THE SPIKE (3.1) MANDATES WERE MET:
- currentUrl from config.redirectUri, NOT request.url: private callbackUrl(config, incoming) builds new URL(config.redirectUri) and copies the incoming searchParams on with append(). Behind TLS termination the Node hosts build the Request as http://${host}${url} with no x-forwarded-proto, so using request.url would have sent the IdP an http:// redirect_uri and earned invalid_grant in every real deployment while every local test passed.
- Multi-Set-Cookie: every cookie goes through appendCookie() -> headers.append('set-cookie', serializeCookie(...)). Headers.set and object-literal init are never used for cookies anywhere in the file.
- cookie-es: parse() for reads, serialize() for writes. Its default encode/decode pair is symmetric (encodeURIComponent / decodeURIComponent-only-when-% -present), so sealed iron values (Fe26.2**, base64url) round-trip byte-exact and do not expand across the 3800-char chunk boundary. Clearing emits Max-Age=0 via maxAge: 0.
- CAUTION for later beads: cookie-es THROWS TypeError if a __Host--prefixed name is serialized without Secure, without Path=/, or with Domain. That makes F10's 'drop the prefix when not cookieSecure' rule load-bearing at runtime, and it means clearing cookies must still carry the full attribute set (I use clearCookieOpts = baseCookieOpts + maxAge 0), never a bare 'name='.
- returnTo (1.5) PRESERVED and extended: private safeReturnTo(v) = isSafeReturnUrl(v) ? v : '/' (imported from ../auth-oidc, the same guard the rest of the SDK uses). Applied at BOTH ends -- on the raw searchParams.get('returnTo') in login, and again on tx.returnTo in callback before the 302, so a tx cookie sealed by an older build cannot land the browser off-origin. Sanitize-to-'/', never refuse.
- iron-ttl (1.6) PRESERVED: the default store is still new CookieSessionStore({ password, ttlSeconds: config.sessionTtlSeconds }).

F12a (logout hardening) as implemented:
- Non-POST -> 405 with 'Allow: POST', zero Set-Cookie, and store.destroy NOT called.
- CSRF mismatch/missing -> 403 application/problem+json with the machine code at the TOP LEVEL (body.code === CSRF_INVALID_CODE), again zero Set-Cookie and no destroy. A rejected logout that still cleared cookies would be the same denial of service wearing a 403.
- Reuses csrfTokenMatches + CSRF_HEADER + CSRF_INVALID_CODE imported from proxy.ts; the comparison is not re-rolled. Header trap handled: request.headers.get() returns null where h3 returned undefined, so the read is '?? undefined'.
- The handlers.ts <-> proxy.ts import cycle is safe under ESM: neither module touches the other's bindings at module-evaluation time, only inside function bodies. Verified by the whole suite plus the vite build.

F10 (config.ts) as implemented: private DEFAULT_COOKIE_NAME 'wallow_bff', HOST_COOKIE_PREFIX '__Host-', and defaultCookieName(hostPrefixRaw, cookieSecure) = prefix only when hostPrefixRaw !== 'false' AND cookieSecure. New env var COOKIE_HOST_PREFIX (trimmed+lowercased) fails secure exactly like COOKIE_SECURE -- only the literal 'false' opts out. An explicit COOKIE_NAME short-circuits via ?? and is taken verbatim, never double-prefixed. JSDoc on BffConfig.cookieName and loadBffConfigFromEnv updated.

Other: /bff/user now answers with Response.json (h3 used to serialize + stamp content-type; nothing does that now).

ISSUES / HANDOFF (2, neither in this bead's file scope -- reporting, not fixing):
1. CALLER BREAK from F12a. packages/sdk/src/auth.ts:61-65 logout() does 'location.href = "/bff/logout"' -- a GET navigation, which the new gate answers 405. The browser-side logout() must become a POST (fetch with the x-csrf-token header, then navigate on the returned Location) or the reference apps lose logout. auth.ts is the browser entry and outside this bead; needs its own bead or an explicit scope extension. /bff/login is unaffected (still a GET navigation, still correct).
2. I rebuilt packages/sdk/dist as instructed (build was one of the gates). The red report had deliberately left dist stale so apps/wallow-web kept typechecking against the h3-era signatures. dist/ is gitignored so nothing is committed, but any agent typechecking apps/wallow-web now will see the new web-standard server contract until bead 3.4 lands the compat shim.

Staged (mine only): packages/sdk/package.json, pnpm-lock.yaml, src/server/config.ts, src/server/handlers.ts, src/server/proxy.ts. No test file touched. h3 and the shim untouched (3.4). No commit, no push, bead not closed.
DIAGNOSE: FAULT=test; FAILING='writes the session, chunk, and CSRF cookies under distinct __Host- names' (handlers.test.ts:1200-1219) — its vacuously-passing sibling 'satisfies the __Host- attribute requirements...' (:1223) has the same root cause. REASON: the shared helper completeCallback() (handlers.test.ts:918-944) builds the tx-cookie Cookie header with a HARDCODED literal at line 943 — headers: { cookie: `wallow_bff_tx=${sealed}` } — instead of deriving the cookie name from the config under test (${config.cookieName}_tx). Every other caller of completeCallback() uses makeConfig() with the default cookieName ('wallow_bff'), so the hardcode coincides with reality and stays green; only the two __Host- tests pass cookieName: '__Host-wallow_bff', so the handler looks for a cookie named '__Host-wallow_bff_tx', finds none (the test sent 'wallow_bff_tx' instead), and correctly answers 400 with zero Set-Cookie headers — hence 'expected [] to include __Host-wallow_bff'. VERIFIED INDEPENDENTLY: copied handlers.test.ts to a scratch file, changed ONLY line 943 to ${config.cookieName}_tx=${sealed}, ran npx vitest run -> 52/52 PASS (scratch file deleted, nothing left in tree). Confirms the implementer's own proof. The code (handlers.ts) is correct: it derives every cookie name from config.cookieName via chunkCookieName/csrfCookieName/txCookieName consistently, and deliberately keeps the __Host- prefix on the tx cookie (rejecting it would re-open the PKCE-verifier/state/nonce cookie-injection vector the prefix exists to close). FIX: handlers.test.ts:943 -> cookie: `${config.cookieName}_tx=${sealed}` (single-line change, test-only, matches every other cookie header in the file which already interpolate off wallow_bff/config values elsewhere for the same fixture pattern). Do NOT touch handlers.ts to make this pass.
VERIFY: gates — SDK suite 683/684 pass (1 known test-harness fault above, everything else green, matches implementer report exactly); tsc --noEmit clean; oxlint packages/sdk/src --deny-warnings clean; oxfmt --check packages/sdk clean; pnpm --filter @bc-solutions-coder/sdk build succeeds (dist/server/index.js emitted). Read handlers.ts in full: currentUrl correctly built from config.redirectUri via callbackUrl() (handlers.ts:382-388), never from request.url, with incoming code/state copied on via searchParams.append — matches spike mandate. cookie-es parse/serialize used throughout for read/write, confirmed as direct dep in package.json. Every cookie write goes through appendCookie() -> headers.append('set-cookie', ...) (handlers.ts:203-210); no headers.set on set-cookie anywhere in the file — multi-Set-Cookie mandate honored. Buffered-body / 401-replay mandate lives in proxy.ts (verified there, see 3.3 note) not handlers.ts. returnTo (bead 1.5) preserved: safeReturnTo() wraps isSafeReturnUrl from ../auth-oidc, applied at both login (:411) and callback re-check (:499) — sanitize-to-'/' behavior intact, not weakened. iron-ttl (bead 1.6) preserved: session.ts is untouched (not in this diff), default store still CookieSessionStore({password, ttlSeconds: config.sessionTtlSeconds}). F12a logout gate matches acceptance: non-POST -> 405 + Allow:POST with no destroy/no cookie clear (handlers.ts:520-525); CSRF mismatch -> 403 problem+json with CSRF_INVALID_CODE reused from proxy.ts, not re-rolled (:530-537); valid POST -> destroy then clear then redirect (:539-549). F10 __Host- default verified in config.ts: defaultCookieName() prefixes only when cookieSecure && hostPrefixRaw !== 'false', explicit COOKIE_NAME still wins verbatim via ??. VERDICT: CLOSE (once the test-harness fix above lands — see DIAGNOSE note). All acceptance criteria for 3.2 are met by the code; the sole failure is proven test-only.
TESTFIX (round 2, per verifier DIAGNOSE): handlers.test.ts:943 completeCallback() changed from hardcoded cookie: `wallow_bff_tx=${sealed}` to `${config.cookieName}_tx=${sealed}`. This is the single call site every caller of completeCallback() shares, so it fixed BOTH tests flagged by the verifier in one edit: 'writes the session, chunk, and CSRF cookies under distinct __Host- names' (:1202, was hard-failing) and 'satisfies the __Host- attribute requirements on every cookie it writes' (:1223, was vacuously passing on an empty getSetCookie() array — now asserts for real).

title: Declare typed 200 responses on ~67 undocumented operations
description: Declare typed success response bodies (`[ProducesResponseType(typeof(T), 200)]`) on the roughly 67 operations that currently lack them, so the generated SDK client has typed return values instead of `unknown` (R9 from docs/plans/2026-07-27/0908-sdk-review.md).
design: Files: enumerate the affected operations by diffing the regenerated OpenAPI spec for `200` responses that carry no content schema. Fix per module, one commit per module, adding the appropriate `[ProducesResponseType(typeof(T), 200)]` (or equivalent) attribute to each action.
acceptance_criteria: Regenerating the OpenAPI document shows zero `200` responses without a content schema. Commit (per module): `fix(<module>): declare typed 200 responses`.
notes:
RED (2026-07-28) — 8 new tests in api/tests/Wallow.Api.Tests/OpenApi/TypedSuccessResponseTests.cs (NEW file, NEW OpenApi/ folder); 7 confirmed FAILING, 1 passes by construction. Suite: ./scripts/run-tests.sh api -> 319 total, 306 pass, 13 fail (7 mine + 6 from sibling bead 2.2 running concurrently in Extensions/ServiceCollectionExtensionsTests.cs — NOT mine, do not touch). Build clean under TreatWarningsAsErrors. NO production scaffold was added: the entire fix for this bead is attributes/DTOs, so RED adds test code only.

=== RE-MEASURED INVENTORY (the plan's ~67 and the scout's 33 are BOTH WRONG) ===
ACTUAL: 83 controller actions + 2 minimal-API endpoints = 85 operations emit an untyped 200.

Why the earlier numbers were wrong — TWO independent detection bugs, both verified against packages/sdk/openapi/v1.json and against controller source:
(a) The scout's rule 'responses[200] has no content key' UNDERCOUNTS. Any controller carrying [Produces("application/json")] (11 controllers do) emits responses.200.content = {"application/json": {}} — a content key present but NO schema inside. Those are just as untyped for hey-api (yields unknown) and MUST be fixed. Re-running the scout's own script on the SAME stale snapshot with the corrected rule gives 33 (no content key) + 15 (content but no schema) = 48, not 33.
(b) Both earlier numbers were taken from the STALE committed snapshot, which predates the F6 Identity rework (it still lists /v1/identity/auth/* from a deleted AuthController; the live tree has AccountController). Re-measuring against CURRENT SOURCE gives 83.

CORRECT DETECTION RULE for task 2.5's document-level invariant — an operation is untyped iff responses['200'] exists AND (no 'content' key OR no content[<mediaType>].schema for any media type). Use BOTH clauses.

=== PER-MODULE COUNTS (one commit per module, per acceptance criteria) ===
Identity 56 | Notifications 10 | Storage 9 | Announcements 6 | Branding 1 | Inquiries 1 | ApiKeys 0 (already clean — its test PASSES today and is a regression guard).

=== DETECTION RULE THE TEST ENCODES (mirrors ApiResponseTypeProvider; validated line-by-line against OrganizationsController + the committed snapshot) ===
An action emits an untyped 200 iff ALL of:
- controller is visible to ApiExplorer: has [ApiController] (or [ApiExplorerSettings(IgnoreApi=false)]);
- controller is not [Tags("Test Support")] (excluded by 2.1) and neither controller nor action is [ApiExplorerSettings(IgnoreApi=true)];
- method is routed: not [NonAction], carries an IActionHttpMethodProvider ([HttpGet]/[HttpPost]/...);

- the return type does not infer a real T (Task<ActionResult<T>>/ValueTask<ActionResult<T>>/ActionResult<T>);

title: E2E fix-or-quarantine + re-enable CI e2e-tests job green
description: Re-establish a GREEN (not tolerated-red) E2E safety net before any SDK or app churn begins, and re-enable the disabled CI `e2e-tests` job. CI's `e2e-tests` job (header at `ci.yml:322`) is currently disabled via `if: false` at `ci.yml:324` and only covers the containerized wallow-auth suite. wallow-auth's Playwright suite last ran 65/76 locally (11 known failures); 9 of its 10 spec files need a live backend. Every later "green per 0.11" gate in this migration means: zero failures beyond what this task records as quarantined, and zero new quarantines added beyond this task's list.
design:
Files: `.github/workflows/ci.yml` (job header `:322`, `if: false` at `:324`); the failing spec files; this epic's notes.
Steps: run `pnpm --filter ./apps/wallow-auth test:e2e`, `pnpm --filter ./apps/wallow-web test:e2e`, and the cross-app journey `pnpm --filter ./apps/wallow-web test:e2e:cross-app` against a live backend (`pnpm backend`) -> triage every known failure: fix the cheap ones now; for the rest, quarantine in code with `test.fixme(...)` annotated with a bead ID per spec (one bead per root cause) -> record the quarantine list on this epic's notes via `bd note` -> run `./scripts/e2e.sh` (containerized) and confirm it is green -> flip `if: false` to enabled at `ci.yml:324` so the `e2e-tests` job runs again, green on re-enable day.
acceptance_criteria: `./scripts/e2e.sh` passes green; the CI `e2e-tests` job at `ci.yml:322` runs (not `if: false`) and is green; every remaining known failure is quarantined via `test.fixme(...)` with a bead-ID annotation, and that quarantine list is recorded via `bd note` on this epic. Commits: `test(e2e): fix or quarantine known failures` then `ci: re-enable e2e-tests job`.

- apps/wallow-web/e2e/global-setup.ts (new)

ROOT CAUSE (one cause behind all 11 'known failures'): createDevServer runs Vite with appType:'custom' + configFile:false, so Vite has no index.html to crawl and its cold dependency scan finds nothing. The browser bundle's real graph -- every @base-ui/react/* subpath @bc-solutions-coder/ui reaches for -- was therefore discovered only WHILE SERVING THE FIRST REQUEST. The mid-flight re-optimise invalidated the deps that page was already fetching, so the page died on a wall of 504 'Outdated Optimize Dep' and never hydrated, with no auto-reload. This was a real product defect, not flaky tests: every developer's first 'pnpm dev' page load was blank until a manual refresh, and a cold E2E run lost whichever specs the parallel scheduler started first.

FIX: optimizeDeps: { entries: ['src/client.tsx'] } in createDevServer, so the scan crawls the true client graph at startup before anything is served. Measured: first cold load 180s timeout/never-hydrates -> 460ms, 0 responses >=400, 0 'reloading'. Requires 'pnpm --filter @bc-solutions-coder/web-shell build' (apps consume dist/).

SECONDARY (suite-side guard, not the fix): globalSetup drives one page load to the [data-app-ready='true'] marker before the first spec. Playwright's webServer reports ready when the port accepts a connection, which is earlier than 'dev server can serve'; most flow specs wait on the marker with the DEFAULT 5s expect budget (routes.spec.ts already passed 15_000, which is exactly why routes passed cold and the flow specs did not). Against the prebuilt container E2E_BASE_URL drives in CI it is a sub-second no-op.

title: Scope DisableTransportSecurityRequirement to Development
description: Scope the unconditional `DisableTransportSecurityRequirement()` OpenIddict server call to Development only, so HTTPS is required for OIDC endpoints in every other environment (F9 from docs/plans/2026-07-27/0908-sdk-review.md).
design:
Files: Identity module OpenIddict server configuration (the unconditional `DisableTransportSecurityRequirement()` call) + test.
Steps: locate the call in the Identity OpenIddict setup -> wrap it in an environment check so only Development disables the HTTPS requirement on OIDC endpoints -> write a failing test first where practical (options-level assertion), otherwise follow the existing options-validation test pattern -> `./scripts/run-tests.sh Identity`.
acceptance_criteria: `DisableTransportSecurityRequirement()` is only reached when the environment is Development; a test asserts this; `./scripts/run-tests.sh Identity` green. Commit: `fix(identity): require https for oidc endpoints outside development`.
notes:
RED: 3 files, 15 test cases, 9 confirmed failing (Identity suite otherwise green: 1140 passed).

FILES ADDED (all staged):
- api/src/Modules/Identity/Wallow.Identity.Infrastructure/Extensions/OpenIddictTransportSecurityPolicy.cs (SCAFFOLD ONLY)
- api/tests/Modules/Identity/Wallow.Identity.Tests/Infrastructure/OpenIddictTransportSecurityPolicyTests.cs (12 cases)
- api/tests/Modules/Identity/Wallow.Identity.Tests/Infrastructure/OpenIddictTransportSecurityCallSiteTests.cs (3 cases)

SIGNATURE THE GREEN PHASE MUST IMPLEMENT (scaffold currently returns a hardcoded false):
  namespace Wallow.Identity.Infrastructure.Extensions;
  public static class OpenIddictTransportSecurityPolicy
  {
      public const string AllowPlainHttpKey = \"OpenIddict:AllowPlainHttpEndpoints\";
      public const string TestingEnvironmentName = \"Testing\";
      public static bool ShouldDisableTransportSecurityRequirement(IHostEnvironment environment, IConfiguration configuration);
  }
Required semantics (each is a test): ArgumentNullException.ThrowIfNull on both args FIRST (the null-configuration test uses Development, so the env short-circuit must not run before the guards) -> true when environment.IsDevelopment() || environment.IsEnvironment(TestingEnvironmentName), regardless of the flag -> otherwise true ONLY when AllowPlainHttpKey parses as boolean true (case-insensitive) -> false when the key is absent, blank, whitespace or false -> a non-boolean value (e.g. \"yes\") must throw InvalidOperationException whose message names the key. configuration.GetValue<bool>(AllowPlainHttpKey) satisfies the parse, the case-insensitivity AND the throw-naming-the-key case (ConfigurationBinder's message embeds the key path); blank/whitespace needs an IsNullOrWhiteSpace short-circuit first because GetValue<bool> throws on \"\".

CALL SITE the green phase must change: IdentityInfrastructureExtensions.cs:128 -- replace the unconditional aspNetCoreBuilder.DisableTransportSecurityRequirement(); with an if guard calling the policy, and rewrite the comment above it (it currently asserts the requirement 'must be off', which is now only true for Development/Testing or an explicit opt-in). Both environment and configuration are already in scope in that lambda. CallSiteTests assert: the call string still exists; the policy call appears BEFORE it in the file; and an 'if (' appears within the 5 lines preceding-or-on the call line. The obvious 3-line if block satisfies all three.

DESIGN DECISION -- deliberate, narrower-than-literal reading of the AC (the scout's gotcha on this bead was correct and is now CONFIRMED with evidence):
1. docker/docker-compose.production.yml:437,482-483 -- ASPNETCORE_ENVIRONMENT=Production, and the BFF is pointed at OIDC_METADATA_URL=http://wallow-api:8080/.well-known/openid-configuration plus BFF_API_BASE_URL=http://wallow-api:8080. Those are container-to-container calls that never traverse the reverse proxy, so they carry no X-Forwarded-Proto and Program.cs's UseForwardedHeaders cannot rescue them. A blanket Development-only gate WOULD break production OIDC discovery. Hence the explicit opt-in flag rather than a hard dev-only gate: production stays secure BY DEFAULT (F9 closed -- the fail-open disappears) and an operator who genuinely terminates TLS in front must now declare it.
2. 'Testing' is included alongside Development because api/tests/Wallow.Tests.Common/Factories/WallowApiFactory.cs:175 does builder.UseEnvironment(\"Testing\") and drives the OIDC endpoints over plain-http TestServer requests -- excluding it would break Wallow.Identity.IntegrationTests / Wallow.Api.Tests. This also matches the existing Development||Testing pairing at IdentityInfrastructureExtensions.cs:92 (cert loading) and the same pairing throughout Wallow.Api/Program.cs. docker/docker-compose.test.yml:117 uses Development, so the E2E stack is covered too.
3. Pattern followed: OpenIddictIssuerResolver.cs + OpenIddictIssuerResolverTests.cs -- the in-repo precedent for a small static config-reading helper living beside the un-unit-testable options lambda (IdentityInfrastructureExtensions is [ExcludeFromCodeCoverage] and its AddServer lambda cannot be invoked without bootstrapping the module).

FOLLOW-UP FOR THE GREEN PHASE (not done in red, deliberately): docker/docker-compose.production.yml's wallow-api service needs OpenIddict__AllowPlainHttpEndpoints: \"true\" added, or the shipped production stack breaks at the first discovery call. Also worth a line in docs/operations/deployment.md.

TESTS THAT PASS TRIVIALLY AGAINST THE SCAFFOLD (expected, not a spec gap): the three deployed-environment cases, the two blank-flag cases, the opt-in-false case, the key-name constant, both null-argument cases, and CallSite's 'still wires the switch' case. The scaffold had to keep the two ArgumentNullException.ThrowIfNull guards and the two consts because Roslynator RCS1163 + IDE0060 (unused parameter) are errors under TreatWarningsAsErrors, so a bare 'return false' body would not compile.

title: Phase 1 -- Backend OpenAPI (unblocks all codegen)
description: Backend OpenAPI document fixes that unblock all SDK codegen: exclude internal test-support endpoints from the public v1 document, emit unique operationIds, declare typed success response bodies, then regenerate the SDK's committed OpenAPI snapshot and generated client, and turn the drift test into an invariant assertion. Ordered: exclusion first, so the spec the rest of the phase measures is the public one.
design: Dependency chain: task 1.1 (exclude test-support endpoints) must land before 1.2 and 1.3 (both then measure the same public document). 1.2 (operationId transformer) and 1.3 (typed success bodies) are independent of each other and can run in parallel, but both must land before 1.4 (regenerate SDK snapshot) since 1.4 regenerates against the final document shape. 1.5 (rewrite the drift test as an invariant) depends on 1.4 having landed the new generated output.
acceptance_criteria: PHASE 1 GATE: `openapi-drift.yml` green on a PR; `pnpm check` green.
notes:
SCOUT (2026-07-28) — full plan source: docs/plans/2026-07-27/0908-sdk-review.md section 1 (R8/R9) + Phase 1 list (item 8-11). Pipeline file for ALL five tasks: api/src/Wallow.Api/Extensions/ServiceCollectionExtensions.cs (transformers registered in AddApiServices at lines ~41-49; four existing transformer methods live at the bottom of the file, lines ~184-263). Exemplar unit-test file for 2.1/2.2 C# tests: api/tests/Wallow.Api.Tests/Extensions/ServiceCollectionExtensionsTests.cs — mirror its pattern exactly (construct OpenApiDocument/OpenApiOperation + a fake OpenApiOperationTransformerContext/OpenApiDocumentTransformerContext with ApiDescription.ActionDescriptor, call the internal static method directly, assert on the mutated object — no TestServer/WebApplicationFactory needed for these). Library versions: Microsoft.OpenApi 2.10.0, Microsoft.AspNetCore.OpenApi (net10.0). Confirmed via package XML docs (no decompiler available in sandbox): OpenApiDocumentTransformerContext exposes DescriptionGroups (IReadOnlyList<ApiDescriptionGroup>); OpenApiOperationTransformerContext now also exposes .Document (net10 addition). OpenApiOperation.OperationId is a plain settable string. OpenApiOperation.Tags is HashSet<OpenApiTagReference> (see existing TransformOperationModuleTag); OpenApiTagReference.Name is the string to compare. OpenApiDocument.Paths is a dict of IOpenApiPathItem; OpenApiPathItem.Operations is a dict of OpenApiOperation.

--- 2.1 (Exclude Test Support endpoints) ---
Only ONE controller carries the tag today: api/src/Modules/Identity/Wallow.Identity.Api/Controllers/TestSupportController.cs ([Tags("Test Support")], route v{version}/identity/test/isolated-org, single POST action, already dev-only gated via IHostEnvironment.IsDevelopment() check inside the action — but it still SHIPS in the OpenAPI doc/SDK today). Confirmed in committed snapshot packages/sdk/openapi/v1.json: grep for "Test Support" hits both an operation tags array (~line 3428) and the top-level document.tags entry (~line 8068).
Implementation: add a 5th transformer, a DOCUMENT transformer (options.AddDocumentTransformer), because operation transformers can't delete whole paths. By the time ANY transformer runs, the framework has already populated operation.Tags from the [Tags] attribute (this is exactly the pre-existing state TransformOperationModuleTag's own guard checks for — "if the controller already has an explicit [Tags] attribute, don't override" — so operation.Tags containing an OpenApiTagReference named "Test Support" is reliably present pre-transform). So the transformer body: iterate document.Paths, for each PathItem check if ALL of its Operations.Values have a Tags entry with Name == "Test Support"; collect matching path keys; Remove them from document.Paths afterward (mutate outside the enumeration loop to avoid modifying while iterating). Optionally also strip the now-unused "Test Support" entry from document.Tags for cleanliness, but not required by acceptance criteria (only "zero Test Support endpoints" is asserted).
Test pattern: mirror TransformOperationModuleTag_* tests but construct an OpenApiDocument with Paths containing a PathItem/Operation carrying Tags=[new OpenApiTagReference("Test Support")], call the new transformer, assert document.Paths no longer contains that key; add a second test with a non-tagged path proving it survives.
Gotcha: this is a MODULE-agnostic mechanism (matches by tag string, not by controller type), so it will also catch any future test-support endpoint added anywhere with the same [Tags("Test Support")] convention — intentional per the task description's "whatever grouping/tag currently marks test-support-only endpoints" phrasing.

--- 2.2 (operationId transformer) ---
Add as the 5th (or 6th, after 2.1's) OPERATION transformer (options.AddOperationTransformer) in the same AddApiServices block. Derive from ControllerActionDescriptor, NOT from raw regex on the type name: `context.Description.ActionDescriptor as ControllerActionDescriptor` gives `.ControllerName` (already strips the "Controller" suffix, MVC built-in) and `.MethodInfo.Name` (the plan doc explicitly says to read MethodInfo.Name, not the possibly-[ActionName]-overridden ActionName). operationId = $"{descriptor.ControllerName}{descriptor.MethodInfo.Name}" e.g. "OrganizationsGetById". Existing repo memory 'deriving-openapi-operationid-from-bare-c-methodinfo-name' already documents that bare MethodInfo.Name alone collides (>=15 dupes, GetById x3 etc) — the Controller-name prefix is exactly what resolves that.
Verified today: ALL 149 operations in the committed v1.json snapshot currently have NO operationId at all (confirmed by scripting the json — 0/149 have the key). hey-api therefore currently names generated SDK functions from method+path (e.g. postV1IdentityAppsRegister, per openapi-regen.test.ts's own asserted names) — once operationId is added, hey-api's default naming switches to operationId-derived names, which IS the "one-time operation-name rename" 2.4 must absorb.
Test scope per task 2.2's own acceptance criteria is transformer-level (unit tests mirroring the ServiceCollectionExtensionsTests.cs pattern: construct a fake ControllerActionDescriptor + context, assert operation.OperationId set correctly; construct two descriptors with the same MethodInfo.Name but different ControllerName, assert distinct ids). Do NOT try to boot a WebApplicationFactory / TestServer here — the only such full-stack harness in the repo (WallowApiFactory in api/tests/Wallow.Tests.Common/Factories/WallowApiFactory.cs) spins up real Testcontainers Postgres+Redis and is overkill; the true whole-document uniqueness invariant belongs to 2.5 (which asserts it against the regenerated, committed packages/sdk/openapi/v1.json, not a live host).
Known remaining gotcha (flag, don't necessarily fix in 2.2): two actions in the SAME controller with the same MethodInfo.Name (C# method overloads selected by attribute routing/HTTP verb) would still collide under Controller+Method naming. Not found during this scout, but not exhaustively verified — the 2.5 invariant test will catch it if it exists.

--- 2.3 (typed 200 responses) ---
The 67-count is from a live/fresh regenerated document (per the plan doc, section 1); the CURRENTLY COMMITTED packages/sdk/openapi/v1.json is stale (its own openapi-regen.test.ts header comment says it predates the F6 Identity rework) and only shows 33 operations with a bare `200` response and no `content` schema, 31 of which are tagged Identity, plus 1 'Wallow.Api' + 1 'SseEndpoint'. DO NOT rely on this stale count — task 2.3 must re-derive the exact operation list from a document regenerated AFTER 2.1's exclusion lands (design note: "1.1 must land before 1.2 and 1.3 ... both then measure the same public document").
Source-level signal (grepped api/src/Modules/*/*.Api/Controllers/*.cs for action methods without an explicit [ProducesResponseType(typeof(T), 200/201)]): methods returning bare `Task<IActionResult>`/`Task<ActionResult>` (non-generic) are the real candidates — ASP.NET Core's built-in OpenApi generation DOES already infer a typed 200 schema for `ActionResult<T>`/`Task<ActionResult<T>>` return types with no attribute needed (see AppsController.cs — several actions already rely on this), so those are NOT part of the ~67. Raw grep count of bare-IActionResult/ActionResult action methods (no inferred generic) per module: Identity ~84 (66 Task<IActionResult> + 18 Task<ActionResult>), Storage 7, Notifications 10, Announcements 4, ApiKeys 1, Branding 1, Inquiries 1 — Identity dominates by far, consistent with it being the largest/oldest module. Not every one of these will actually resolve to an undocumented 200 in the OpenAPI doc (some only ever return 204/404/redirect for their 'success' path) — treat this as a starting-point grep, not the final list; the actual fix-list must come from diffing the regenerated spec's `responses.200` entries for a missing `content` key (same technique used in this scout: parse the JSON, for each get/post/put/patch/delete op check responses['200'] exists and has no 'content').
Recommended per-module fix pattern: add `[ProducesResponseType(typeof(TResponseDto), StatusCodes.Status200OK)]` (see AppsController.cs:115 `[ProducesResponseType(typeof(DeveloperAppResponse), StatusCodes.Status200OK)]` as the exact existing idiom to copy) above each flagged action, using whichever DTO/response record the action's Ok(...) call actually constructs. One commit per module per the acceptance criteria.

--- 2.4 (regenerate SDK snapshot) ---
Regen command (from packages/sdk/CLAUDE.md, REQUIRED reading before touching the SDK): with API running on :5001, `WALLOW_OPENAPI_URL=http://localhost:5001/openapi/v1.json pnpm --filter @bc-solutions-coder/sdk exec tsx scripts/generate.ts` (packages/sdk/scripts/generate.ts fetches the live spec, overwrites packages/sdk/openapi/v1.json, then shells out to `npx @hey-api/openapi-ts` using packages/sdk/openapi-ts.config.ts — plugins: @hey-api/client-fetch, @hey-api/typescript, @hey-api/sdk; postProcess: [] is deliberate, do not add a formatter). CI job openapi-drift.yml fails on ANY drift between this committed snapshot and a freshly-generated one — this is the acceptance-gate mentioned at the epic level.
Scope of the rename: hand-written consumers of the old path-derived generated names live in src/query/* (packages/sdk/src/query/{apps,auth,bootstrap,inquiries,keys,mfa,organizations,settings,user}.ts + index.ts, ~9 files), auth-client.ts, mfa-client.ts, facade.ts, client.ts, ssr.ts, and generated.test.ts — all in packages/sdk/src/. Per the plan doc (section 4 "SDK architecture") and the task's own design note, MOST of src/query/*, auth-client.ts, and mfa-client.ts are already scheduled for wholesale Phase-4 deletion — the task instruction is explicit: apply only the MINIMAL fix that compiles (rename references), mark any thin alias `// TEMPORARY alias until Phase 4`, do not refactor/beautify soon-to-be-deleted code. Also touches downstream call sites in apps/wallow-web and apps/wallow-auth wherever they import generated operation names directly (not just via the query layer/facades).
Verify success with `pnpm check` (per CLAUDE.md root) — this runs format:check + lint + typecheck + test + build across the whole workspace, the actual gate this task must turn green.

--- 2.5 (rewrite openapi-regen.test.ts) ---
Current file: packages/sdk/src/openapi-regen.test.ts — today it's a dated snapshot-diff assertion (checks specific deleted paths/operations from a past 'F6' Identity rework, hardcoded operation names like `getV1IdentityOrganizationDomainsMatch`, `postV1IdentityAppsRegister` — these are the OLD path-derived names that operationId will replace, so this whole test file's assertions are already stale post-2.4 and must be replaced, not patched). Replace with two invariants read directly off `packages/sdk/openapi/v1.json` (same loadSnapshot() helper/pattern, already present at top of file — keep that helper, just replace the describe blocks below it): (a) every path/method operation object has a non-empty `operationId` string; (b) the multiset of all operationId values has no duplicates (e.g. collect all, compare length vs a Set of them). Optionally also assert the typed-200 invariant here too (every 200 response has a `content` key) since 2.3's fix and this rewrite are both about durable document-shape guarantees, though the task description frames typed-200 as already covered elsewhere — check with the acceptance text ("uniqueness + typed 200)" is literally in this task's own title) so BOTH invariants belong in this rewritten file.
Do NOT touch the generated.test.ts file (separate meta-spec) unless it also references old path-derived names post-2.4 rename — check for stale name references there as a side effect of 2.4, not 2.5.

title: Decide and implement the global-admin design (needs owner)
description: DECISION TASK, needs an owner: resolve the global-`admin` design question (F5/R7 from docs/plans/2026-07-27/0908-sdk-review.md) -- currently a tenant admin may be able to grant global admin cross-tenant. Two options to present with evidence: (a) a realm superadmin as a distinct, non-assignable role, or (b) tenant-scoped admin only (no global admin concept at all). Evidence: `RolePermissionMapping.cs:19`, `UsersController.cs:142-178`.
design: Steps: present both options with the cited evidence to a human owner for a decision -> once decided, write a failing integration test first (a tenant admin attempts to grant global admin cross-tenant, must be rejected) -> implement whichever option was chosen -> green.
acceptance_criteria: An owner has signed off on option (a) or (b); the chosen design is implemented; the failing-first cross-tenant-grant test passes; `./scripts/run-tests.sh Identity` green.
notes:
SCOUT FINDINGS for the global-admin design decision.

(a) THE DECISION: RolePermissionMapping.cs:10 ("admin" role) grants
PermissionType.AdminAccess/SystemSettings (and every other permission) with zero
tenant scoping -- it's a flat FrozenDictionary<string,string[]> with no tenant
concept at all. UsersController.cs:142-156 AssignRole endpoint only requires the
CALLER to hold RolesUpdate + the TARGET user to belong to the caller's own tenant
(UserBelongsToTenantAsync) -- request.RoleName is an unrestricted free string.
So today: any tenant admin can call POST /users/{userId}/roles {"roleName":"admin"}
on anyone in their own org and that grants the SAME global "admin" role a realm
superadmin has. Confirmed further: TenantResolutionMiddleware.cs:94-100
HasRealmAdminRole(user) used to gate the X-Tenant-Id cross-tenant override header
(line 38) checks the IDENTICAL flat "admin" role string -- so a tenant-admin-granted
"admin" role ALSO grants cross-tenant X-Tenant-Id override today. This is the full
F5 exploit chain: AssignRole -> "admin" role -> AdminAccess/SystemSettings perms +
X-Tenant-Id override, all from a same-tenant grant.

(b) OPTIONS:
  Option A -- realm superadmin as a distinct, non-assignable concept. Precedent
  already exists in the codebase from sibling bead 1.4: TenantResolutionMiddleware
  now also accepts context.User.IsOperator() (ClaimsPrincipalExtensions.cs:10,88 --
  "is_operator" claim, checked via .IsOperator(), NOT settable through any
  user-facing endpoint, only mintable by TokenController for service accounts).
  Same shape applies here: add a realm-admin claim/flag that AssignRoleAsync
  cannot set (RoleName stays scoped to seed.json's roles: ["admin","manager","user"]
  which remain ordinary TENANT roles), provisioned only via seed.json bootstrap
  (BootstrapAdminService -- api/seed.json:175 "admin" block, the one seeded
  admin@wallow.dev in the single seeded "Wallow" org) or a future dedicated
  realm-admin provisioning path. HasRealmAdminRole would be replaced/supplemented
  by checking this new claim instead of (or in addition to) the "admin" role
  string. Net effect: "admin" role assigned via UsersController.AssignRole becomes
  ordinary tenant-scoped admin (AdminAccess/SystemSettings apply within caller's
  own tenant only, once permission checks are made tenant-aware); realm/cross-
  tenant powers require the new non-assignable flag. Bigger sub-decision this
  option needs: whether AdminAccess/SystemSettings PermissionType checks
  themselves need to become tenant-scoped (currently PermissionType is a flat
  enum with no tenant dimension anywhere in the permission-check pipeline --
  HasPermission attribute / PermissionExpansionMiddleware / ScopePermissionMapper
  all operate on bare permission strings, no tenant awareness at all). That's a
  materially bigger change than just gating the X-Tenant-Id header.
  Option B -- tenant-scoped admin only, no global admin concept. Delete
  HasRealmAdminRole entirely; X-Tenant-Id override becomes operator-claim-only
  (IsOperator() check on line 38 already stands alone once realm-admin is
  removed). Simpler, smaller diff, but removes ANY human (non-service-account)
  path to legitimate cross-tenant/platform administration -- e.g. no human
  support/ops user could ever inspect another tenant via X-Tenant-Id; would need
  a service-account-only operational model for cross-tenant work going forward.

(c) IS ONE OPTION CLEARLY IMPLIED?  Partially. Bead 1.4 (gate tenant override on
explicit operator flag, not sa- prefix) just established the exact pattern Option
A needs (non-assignable explicit claim beats reusing an overloaded string/prefix),
and Option A preserves existing human-realm-admin capability (bootstrap admin
already exists in seed.json, likely intentional) rather than removing it. That
tilts the codebase-direction evidence toward Option A. However the bead's own
acceptance criteria explicitly require an owner to sign off on (a) vs (b) before
implementation, and Option A's true scope (does AdminAccess/SystemSettings need
to become tenant-scoped everywhere, or does gating just the X-Tenant-Id override
suffice for the immediate F5 exploit) is a real product/security policy call I
cannot close from the codebase alone -- it changes the security model, not just
a fix path with one obviously correct outcome.

(d) OWNER REQUIRED: YES. Recommendation to hand the owner: proceed with Option A
(realm-admin as a distinct non-assignable claim, precedent from bead 1.4), scoped
narrowly for THIS bead's acceptance criteria to: (1) HasRealmAdminRole stops
trusting the "admin" role string alone and instead requires a new non-assignable
realm-admin claim/flag (seed-provisioned only), (2) add the failing-first
integration test (tenant admin attempts to grant "admin" then tries X-Tenant-Id
override or AdminAccess on another tenant, must be rejected). Explicitly defer the
larger "make AdminAccess/SystemSettings permission checks tenant-scoped everywhere"
question as a follow-up bead rather than silently expanding this one's scope --
flag that boundary in the acceptance-criteria writeup for owner sign-off.
OWNER DECISION (from user, 2026-07-28): Proceed with scout Option A at FULL scope — 'I'd like a Global Admin created that can govern all tenants.' Confirmed via explicit choice: Global Admin is a distinct, NON-ASSIGNABLE claim (seeded, mirroring the is_operator claim pattern from Wallow-pu6a.1.4), which (1) gates the cross-tenant X-Tenant-Id override and (2) grants admin permissions across ALL tenants — AdminAccess/SystemSettings permission checks become explicitly tenant-scoped everywhere, with the global-admin claim as the cross-tenant escape hatch. The assignable-role variant was explicitly rejected. Seed the global admin via seed.json/seeder (not assignable via UsersController.AssignRole).
RED (TDD red phase complete) — Global Admin, owner Option A at FULL scope.

=== CONTRACT THE GREEN PHASE MUST MATCH (tests hard-code these literals) ===

1. CLAIM: type "is_global_admin", value literally "true" (bool.TryParse semantics — "false",
   "1", "yes", "admin", "" and absence all deny). snake_case unprefixed, matching org_id /
   is_operator. Accessor: ClaimsPrincipalExtensions.GlobalAdminClaimType +
   .IsGlobalAdmin(this ClaimsPrincipal?). Null principal -> false. Explicitly asserted:
   holding the "admin" ROLE alone -> false, and holding is_operator alone -> false (operator
   and global admin are SEPARATE concepts; do not collapse them).

2. X-TENANT-ID GATE (TenantResolutionMiddleware.cs:38): must become
   `context.User.IsGlobalAdmin() || context.User.IsOperator()`.
   HasRealmAdminRole(user) (L92-97, the flat "admin" role-string check) must be DELETED —
   test InvokeAsync_TenantAdminRoleWithoutGlobalAdminClaim_DoesNotOverrideTenant fails if any
   role-based fallback survives. It asserts BOTH tenantContext.TenantId and
   context.Items["TenantId"] stay on the caller's own tenant. This is the F5 AC test.
   InvokeAsync_OperatorServiceAccount_StillOverridesTenant is a regression guard for bead
   1.4 — do not break it while removing the role gate.

3. TENANT-SCOPED AdminAccess/SystemSettings (PermissionExpansionMiddleware): the resolved
   tenant is HttpContext.Items["TenantId"] (stamped by TenantResolutionMiddleware, which
   Program.cs:523 registers BEFORE PermissionExpansionMiddleware at :529); the caller's own
   tenant is the org_id claim. Required behaviour:
   - own tenant + "admin" role -> AdminAccess AND SystemSettings present (already passes)
   - DIFFERENT tenant + "admin" role, no global-admin claim -> NEITHER present (2 reds)
   - is_global_admin=true and NO role claims at all -> BOTH present (red). The claim governs
     on its own; it is deliberately not backed by an assignable role.
   - is_global_admin=true + admin role on a DIFFERENT tenant -> BOTH present (passes today;
     guards against over-fixing and locking the global admin out)
   - is_global_admin="false" on a different tenant -> AdminAccess absent (red)
   I deliberately did NOT assert what happens to non-admin permissions cross-tenant, so green
   may legitimately be stricter (drop all role-derived perms cross-tenant) if it prefers.

4. NON-ASSIGNABLE via UsersController.AssignRole (UsersController.cs:137-152): the reserved
   global-admin name must be rejected with HTTP 400 BEFORE userManagement.AssignRoleAsync is
   called. Two theories x 8 spellings each: "global-admin", "global_admin", "globaladmin",
   "GlobalAdmin", "GLOBAL_ADMIN", "Global-Admin", "is_global_admin", "  global-admin  ".
   So green must normalise: TRIM + case-insensitive + ignore non-alphanumerics (compare on
   the letters/digits only, i.e. "globaladmin"/"isglobaladmin"). Assertion is on
   IStatusCodeActionResult.StatusCode == 400, so BadRequest(...) or Problem(statusCode:400)
   both satisfy it. "admin"/"manager"/"user" must STILL assign and return NoContentResult —
   a blanket allow-list of seed roles would break RolesController's custom roles, so use a
   reserved-name DENY check, not an allow-list.

5. SEEDING: api/seed.json's "admin" block must gain "isGlobalAdmin": true (JSON boolean, not
   a string) — SeedJsonGlobalAdminTests asserts the key and the ValueKind. seed.json is
   `merge=ours` fork config AND is currently staged-modified by bead 1.1, so I did NOT touch
   it; green owns that edit. seed.json "roles" must keep containing no global-admin-ish role
   (guard test, passes today with ["admin","manager","user"]).

GREEN GUIDANCE (read, not implemented):
- Provisioning wiring, all in the identity module or seeder:
  AdminBootstrapOptions (Wallow.Identity.Infrastructure/Options/AdminBootstrapOptions.cs) is
  what SeedOptions.Admin binds to — add the IsGlobalAdmin bool there; SeederWorker.
  BootstrapAdminAsync (api/src/Wallow.SeederService/SeederWorker.cs:110-145) is the only
  caller and already has admin.Email/Password/FirstName/LastName. IBootstrapAdminService /
  BootstrapAdminService (Wallow.Identity.Infrastructure/Services/BootstrapAdminService.cs)
  holds UserManager<WallowUser> — an ASP.NET Identity USER CLAIM
  (userManager.AddClaimAsync(user, "is_global_admin", "true")) is the natural non-assignable
  store, mirroring how 1.4 put the operator flag in the OpenIddict application property bag.
  NOTE seeder tests live in Wallow.SeederService.Tests, NOT in `run-tests.sh identity`.
- Issuance side for USER tokens is TokenController.HandleAuthorizationCodeOrRefreshAsync
  (api/src/.../TokenController.cs:~90-135) where roles are copied onto the identity via
  userManager.GetRolesAsync — the global-admin user claim must be minted there the same way,
  and it must NOT be derivable from anything the tenant controls.
- For a CLIENT-side global admin, the 1.4 precedent is the OpenIddict application property
  bag: TokenController.IsOperatorClientAsync reads "wallow:is_operator"; a
  "wallow:is_global_admin" sibling would slot in at HandleClientCredentialsAsync the same way
  (no EF migration needed). I did not write tests for that path — only add it if the green
  agent decides the client-credentials flow needs governance reach.
- BUILD GOTCHA carried forward from 1.4: Wallow.Identity.Api CANNOT
  `using Wallow.Shared.Kernel.Extensions;` — our GetScopes(ClaimsPrincipal?) is ambiguous
  with OpenIddict's. TokenController already aliases
  `using WallowClaims = Wallow.Shared.Kernel.Extensions.ClaimsPrincipalExtensions;`.
  UsersController.cs DOES have the plain using today and compiles, but if green adds a
