Cross-tenant role expansion is STRICT: when Items["TenantId"] differs from the org_id claim and the caller is not a global admin, ExpandUserRoles returns early and grants NOTHING role-derived (not just AdminAccess/SystemSettings). Rationale: a role is a tenant-issued grant and carries no authority elsewhere; the red report explicitly permitted this stricter reading. Missing org_id or missing Items["TenantId"] counts as NOT cross-tenant, so every existing single-tenant path is unchanged (PermissionExpansionMiddlewareGapTests all still pass).
2. ExpandUserScopes and ExpandServiceAccountScopes are UNCHANGED. Scope->permission mapping never yields AdminAccess/SystemSettings (verified: those two constants appear only in PermissionType.cs and RolePermissionMapping.cs), and the sa-/app-/api_key paths are bead 1.4's operator territory.
3. A global admin gets the FULL "admin" role permission set (RolePermissionMapping.GetPermissions(["admin"])), not merely AdminAccess+SystemSettings, in whichever tenant the request resolved onto. The tests only assert the two, but AdminAccess alone gates nothing useful (UsersRead etc. gate the actual endpoints), so a two-permission global admin could not 'govern all tenants' as the owner asked. ExpandGlobalAdmin runs for every authenticated branch and de-dupes against existing permission claims.
4. AssignRole deny check runs FIRST, before UserBelongsToTenantAsync, and returns BadRequest(ProblemDetails) with Extensions["code"]="Validation.ReservedRoleName" — matches the repo's RFC 7807 + extensions.code convention (ResultExtensions.cs). NOT ValidationProblem(ModelState): that resolves ProblemDetailsFactory from HttpContext.RequestServices and would throw in the controller unit tests. Normalisation strips non-alphanumerics + lowercases; deny set is {globaladmin, isglobaladmin}. It is a DENY list, so RolesController's custom roles stay assignable. RemoveRole deliberately not guarded (removing an ungrantable role is inert).
5. Issuance reads userManager.GetClaimsAsync(user), NOT the incoming principal, so a refresh token cannot keep a revoked global admin alive and nothing tenant-controlled can introduce the claim. title: Remove AnyRouter annotations; fix surfaced router type errors
description: Remove the three `: AnyRouter` type annotations from the three apps' `createRouter()` calls (parallel-safe, frontend-only) and fix every TypeScript error the restored inference surfaces. The annotation was masking latent Link/useParams/navigate type errors -- budget real time for this, the point of the task is fixing what surfaces, not just deleting the annotation.
design:
Files: `apps/wallow-web/src/router.tsx:54`, `apps/wallow-auth/src/router.tsx:30`, `apps/examples/minimal-app/src/router.tsx:18`.
Steps: remove `: AnyRouter` from each `createRouter()` call (restore type inference) -> run `pnpm typecheck` -> fix every surfaced error -> `pnpm check`.
acceptance_criteria: `grep -r "AnyRouter" apps/*/src/router.tsx apps/examples/*/src/router.tsx` returns nothing; `pnpm check` green across the whole workspace. Commit: `fix: remove AnyRouter annotations from app routers`.
notes:
RED PHASE REPORT (typecheck-driven task — no new unit tests written; the red signal is `tsc --noEmit`).

== WHAT I CHANGED (the spec change, not the fix) ==
Removed `type AnyRouter` from the import AND `: AnyRouter` from the `createRouter()` return annotation in all three files:
  apps/wallow-web/src/router.tsx (L7 import, L54 signature -> now `export function createRouter() {`)
  apps/wallow-auth/src/router.tsx (L2 import, L30 signature)
  apps/examples/minimal-app/src/router.tsx (L1 import, L18 signature)
`grep -rn AnyRouter apps/` now returns NOTHING — the bead's first acceptance criterion is already satisfied. No fixes applied; the tree is intentionally left red.

== BASELINE (before removal) ==
All three apps typechecked CLEAN. So every error below is genuinely surfaced by restoring inference, not pre-existing.

== RED SIGNAL ==
Command (per package, not workspace-wide):
  pnpm --filter ./apps/wallow-web typecheck
  pnpm --filter ./apps/wallow-auth typecheck
  pnpm --filter ./apps/examples/minimal-app typecheck

Results:
  wallow-auth      -> PASSES clean. Nothing to fix.
  minimal-app      -> PASSES clean. Nothing to fix.
  wallow-web       -> FAILS, exit 2, exactly 9 errors, ALL error TS2352, ALL in *.test.tsx files.

== THE 9 ERRORS (all one root cause) ==
8 of 9 are the identical line, verbatim, in 8 different specs:
  const paths = Object.keys((router as { routesByPath: Record<string, unknown> }).routesByPath);
at: routes/bff-demo.test.tsx:177 | routes/dashboard/apps/index.test.tsx:83 | routes/dashboard/apps/register.test.tsx:80 | routes/dashboard/inquiries/$inquiryId.test.tsx:57 | routes/dashboard/inquiries/index.test.tsx:96 | routes/dashboard/organizations/$orgId.test.tsx:60 | routes/dashboard/organizations/index.test.tsx:82 | routes/dashboard/settings.test.tsx:119

The 9th is the same idea on routesById, at routes/dashboard/route.test.tsx:178:
  const child = (router.routesById as Record<string, { parentRoute?: { id?: string } }>)[...]

ROOT CAUSE: `AnyRouter` was loose enough that these structural casts were legal. With inference restored, `routesByPath` is `FileRoutesByFullPath` and `routesById` is `FileRoutesById` — closed generated interfaces with NO index signature — so TS2352 rejects the cast to `Record<string, ...>` as insufficiently overlapping. The casts are now not just unnecessary but actively wrong.

== IMPORTANT: THIS CONTRADICTS THE 'DO NOT EDIT TEST FILES' RULE ==
Every surfaced error lives in a test file. The green implementer MUST edit these 9 test files — that is explicitly in scope here and is NOT a violation. There is no production-code fix available, and there must not be one: re-annotating router.tsx to re-hide the errors would defeat the whole task.

== THE CORRECT FIX (verified, then reverted to preserve red) ==
Simply DELETE the casts. The precisely-typed router already supports these reads directly:
  Object.keys(router.routesByPath)        // Object.keys accepts any object
  router.routesById['/dashboard/organizations/']   // then child?.parentRoute?.id
I probe-applied exactly this to route.test.tsx:178 (the only non-obvious one, since it reads .parentRoute?.id) and its TS2352 disappeared with no replacement annotation needed — `parentRoute.id` resolves on the inferred Route type. I then reverted the probe, so the bead is handed over red.

DO NOT 'fix' these with `as unknown as` — that re-hides exactly the type looseness this task exists to remove. Deleting the cast is the whole fix.

== ALSO NOTE ==
Bare (uncast) router reads already typecheck fine and need no change: src/router.test.tsx:18, src/router-codegen.test.ts:85, routes/dashboard/route.test.tsx:173 all do `Object.keys(router.routesById)` with no cast.
The bead's DESIGN predicted latent Link/useParams/navigate errors — NONE surfaced. Zero app/production source errors in any of the three apps. The masking was narrower than expected.

== NOT YET RUN (green phase owes these) ==
Only per-package typecheck was run, per instruction. Still owed for the AC: pnpm lint (the deleted casts may leave unused type imports), pnpm format:check, pnpm test for wallow-web, and full `pnpm check`. Note the 9 specs likely PASS at runtime today (vitest strips types), so `pnpm test` is not the gate — `pnpm typecheck` is.

GREEN PHASE REPORT

FILES (12 changed, all staged; nothing outside this bead touched):

- 9 wallow-web specs, casts deleted: routes/bff-demo.test.tsx:177, routes/dashboard/settings.test.tsx:119, routes/dashboard/apps/index.test.tsx:83, routes/dashboard/apps/register.test.tsx:80, routes/dashboard/inquiries/index.test.tsx:96, routes/dashboard/inquiries/$inquiryId.test.tsx:57, routes/dashboard/organizations/index.test.tsx:82, routes/dashboard/organizations/$orgId.test.tsx:60, routes/dashboard/route.test.tsx:178

- route.test.tsx: (router.routesById as Record<string, { parentRoute?: { id?: string } }>)['/dashboard/organizations/'] -> router.routesById['/dashboard/organizations/']; the explanatory comment moved above the statement (it no longer fits inside the index expression). child?.parentRoute?.id resolves on the inferred Route type, as the red probe predicted.

title: Reject unsafe returnTo in BFF login handler
description: Call the existing `isSafeReturnUrl` guard in the BFF login handler so `/bff/login?returnTo=` cannot be used for an open-redirect to a foreign origin (F6/R5 from docs/plans/2026-07-27/0908-sdk-review.md).
design:
Files: `packages/sdk/src/server/handlers.ts:326-327,416` + `handlers.test.ts`.
Steps: failing test: `/bff/login?returnTo=https://evil.example` must not round-trip to an absolute foreign origin after callback -> guard with the existing `isSafeReturnUrl` helper -> green -> `pnpm --filter @bc-solutions-coder/sdk test`.
acceptance_criteria: New test in handlers.test.ts proves a foreign-origin returnTo is rejected/sanitized; `pnpm --filter @bc-solutions-coder/sdk test` green. Commit: `fix(sdk): reject unsafe returnTo in BFF login handler`.
notes:
RED: packages/sdk/src/server/handlers.test.ts — 6 new tests in describe('returnTo open-redirect guard'), 5 confirmed FAILING, 1 intentionally passing.

NO SCAFFOLDING NEEDED: isSafeReturnUrl is already exported from packages/sdk/src/auth-oidc.ts and fully unit-tested in auth-oidc.test.ts. handlers.ts simply never calls it. The tests are purely behavioural (drive the real h3 handlers through toWebHandler); no new types or stubs were added.

FAILING (5):
 - login sanitizes a absolute foreign origin returnTo to '/'   (got 'https://evil.example/pwn')
 - login sanitizes a protocol-relative returnTo to '/'         (got '//evil.example/pwn')
 - login sanitizes a backslash-escaped protocol-relative ...    (got '/\evil.example/pwn')
 - login sanitizes a javascript scheme returnTo to '/'          (got 'javascript:alert(1)')
 - callback re-checks returnTo and redirects to '/' when the tx carries a foreign origin (got Location: https://evil.example/pwn)

PASSING BY DESIGN (1): 'login preserves a safe relative returnTo' (/dashboard?tab=apps). It passes today only because NO guard exists — it is the regression guard that stops the green phase from over-sanitizing every returnTo to '/'. Do not delete it.

SPEC DECISION THE IMPLEMENTER MUST FOLLOW — SANITIZE, DO NOT REFUSE.
The bead AC says 'rejected/sanitized'; the tests pin SANITIZE: an unsafe returnTo falls back to '/' and login still proceeds with a 302 to the authorize URL. Rationale (also recorded as a JSDoc block above the describe): /bff/login is a browser navigation entry point, so a hard 400 turns a merely-malformed link into a broken login. This deliberately DIVERGES from assertSafeReturnUrl in auth-oidc.ts, which throws — that helper is called by app code with a value it chose, not with attacker-supplied query input.

BOTH call sites must be guarded (matches the scout's finding on the parent bead):
 1. handlers.ts login handler ~L326-327 — guard the query-string returnTo BEFORE it is sealed into the LoginTx, so the tx cookie never carries an unsafe value.
 2. handlers.ts callback handler ~L416 — re-check tx.returnTo before sendRedirect. The callback test seals a tx directly with an unsafe returnTo (simulating a cookie issued by a build predating the login-side guard), so a login-side-only fix WILL leave that test red. Defence in depth is required, not optional.

Import to add in handlers.ts: import { isSafeReturnUrl } from '../auth-oidc';  (relative parent path — handlers.ts is in src/server/, auth-oidc.ts is in src/). Verify this does not drag browser-only code into the ./server entry: auth-oidc.ts is documented as PURE string-in/string-out with no fetch/client/session, so it should be safe, but confirm the server build stays clean (pnpm --filter @bc-solutions-coder/sdk build).

TEST HELPERS USED (already existed in the file, no new ones invented): setCookieFor(res, 'wallow_bff_tx') + cookieValueOf() to pull the sealed tx off Set-Cookie, then unsealTx() to inspect returnTo. unsealTx was added to the existing './txstate' import line.

LINT NOTES (already resolved, keep them): the backslash fixture uses String.raw to satisfy unicorn/prefer-string-raw, and the javascript: fixture carries an 'oxlint-disable-next-line no-script-url' comment. oxfmt + oxlint --deny-warnings are clean on the file.

RUN: pnpm --filter @bc-solutions-coder/sdk exec vitest run src/server/handlers.test.ts
GREEN: FILES=packages/sdk/src/server/handlers.ts (only file changed; handlers.test.ts untouched).

SYMBOLS: no new EXPORTED symbols. Added one module-private helper:
  function safeReturnTo(returnTo: string): string  -- returns returnTo when isSafeReturnUrl(returnTo) is true, else '/'.
Added import: import { isSafeReturnUrl } from '../auth-oidc';  (placed above the './claims' import, alphabetical-parent-first, oxfmt clean).

BOTH CALL SITES GUARDED as the red report required:
1. login handler -- the query extraction is now
     const returnTo: string = safeReturnTo(typeof query.returnTo === 'string' ? query.returnTo : '/');
   The old ' && query.returnTo !== "" ' clause was dropped because isSafeReturnUrl already rejects blank/whitespace, so an empty ?returnTo= still yields '/'. Guarded BEFORE sealTx, so the tx cookie can never carry an unsafe value.
2. callback handler -- sendRedirect(event, safeReturnTo(tx.returnTo), FOUND_STATUS). Defence in depth for tx cookies sealed by a build predating the login-side guard.

SANITIZE-NOT-REFUSE honoured: unsafe input falls back to '/' and login still 302s to the authorize URL. JSDoc on safeReturnTo records why this diverges from assertSafeReturnUrl's throw (browser navigation entry point vs app-chosen value).

title: Expire sealed session blobs via explicit iron ttl
description: Pass an explicit iron `ttl` derived from session config to seal/unseal (so a sealed session blob cannot outlive its session TTL), and document that the cookie session store is a dev-only default with Valkey required in production (F7/R6 from docs/plans/2026-07-27/0908-sdk-review.md).

Steps: failing test: unsealing a sealed blob older than the session TTL must fail -> pass an explicit `ttl` to seal/unseal derived from session config -> document that the cookie store is a dev default and Valkey is required in production, and explain why `destroy()` cannot revoke cookie-store sessions -> green.

GREEN IMPLEMENTATION NOTES:

Date.now() + opts.ttl : ''`; unseal rejects with 'Expired seal' when `exp <= Date.now() - opts.timestampSkewSec*1000` (default skew 60s). So expiry is bound AT SEAL TIME; unseal's ttl cannot extend or shorten an existing blob. Pass `{ ...defaults, ttl: ttlMs }` on both calls (harmless on unseal, keeps the API symmetric per the bead).

title: Unified TanStack Start migration + SDK streamlining
description:
All three React apps (apps/wallow-web, apps/wallow-auth, apps/examples/minimal-app) become real TanStack Start applications consuming a framework-neutral, mostly-generated SDK (@bc-solutions-coder/sdk) -- no hand-rolled SSR host, no h3, no module-global client singleton, no hand-written query layer -- so a fresh fork gets a working, secure app from "install the SDK, add tanstackStart(), mount the splat server routes, write feature screens."

Architecture: the SDK's server entry ports from h3 EventHandlers to web-standard Request -> Response handlers (its BFF/proxy/session core stays hand-written -- that is the product). Apps mount those handlers via Start file-based server routes and consume a per-request createWallowSdk() client on the server, a boot-created instance in the browser. @tanstack/react-router-ssr-query solely owns SSR dehydration. The operation + query surface is generated by hey-api (@hey-api/sdk + @tanstack/react-query plugins).

Tech stack: .NET 10 OpenAPI transformers, @hey-api/openapi-ts@0.99.0, @tanstack/react-start + @tanstack/react-router (pinned exact, current latest), @tanstack/react-router-ssr-query, Nitro (opt-in Vite plugin, beta -- conditional on a spike, D9) for the Node/Docker server, Vite 8, TanStack Query v5.

Source plan (for deep context only, not required reading): docs/plans/2026-07-27/1015-unified-start-sdk-migration-plan.md. It supersedes docs/plans/2026-07-27/0909-tanstack-start-migration-design.md and docs/plans/2026-07-27/0928-frontend-and-sdk-streamlining-plan.md (mark both `superseded` on acceptance -- edit only their status lines). docs/plans/2026-07-27/0908-sdk-review.md remains the findings record (not superseded): F1-F14 = its section-2 security-findings table, R1-R25 = its section-5 recommendation list -- every citation below is one of those two lists, never a bare number.
design:
Decision log (collision resolutions -- binding on every task below):
- D1: h3 is removed from the SDK entirely (packages/sdk/src/server/**); apps drop h3 in Phase 3 when their hosts are deleted. iron-webcrypto stays a direct dependency.
- D2: SDK surface collapse (Phase 4) comes AFTER the Start migration (Phase 3). Only web-standard handlers, createWallowSdk, SSR-safe auth redirects, server presets, and the browser WallowError export (all Phase 2) precede the migration.
- D3: @tanstack/react-router-ssr-query solely owns SSR dehydration. The SDK ships NO dehydration/hydration code, ever.
- D4: one SSR request-context design -- SDK ships per-request createWallowSdk(options); Start's global request middleware (src/start.ts) is the only consumption site, building the per-request SDK from getRequest() into router context. internalOrigin (container self-fetch origin) is a transport concern inside the SDK's custom fetch -- baseUrl stays byte-identical between server and browser instances so generated query keys (which embed baseUrl) hydrate correctly.
- D5: no createPassthroughProxy extraction into web-shell -- the passthrough preset ships from the SDK server entry (task 2.7); web-shell's server layer is deleted wholesale (task 3.4).
- D6: Start's session/CSRF utilities (getSession/sealSession/createCsrfMiddleware) are NOT used in the SDK -- the SDK stays portable; only the lesson (explicit iron ttl) is stolen, task 0.6.
- D7: query keys -- adopt hey-api's generated flat keys + queryKeys:{tags:true}; keep one small curated invalidations.ts for subtree sweeps (matching on _id/tags). The CLAUDE.md/frontend-state "all keys from the queryKeys factory" rule is rewritten in the SAME change as key adoption (task 4.1).
- D8: server routes use a single ANY method handler on splat routes (the ANY key exists and works at the installed @tanstack/start-client-core pin).
- D9: hosting is Nitro-on-Vite (nitro() plugin), CONDITIONAL on the container spike (task 3.0 item 4). Abort criterion: if .output/server/index.mjs fails any container check (boot, hashed-asset serving, PORT, clean SIGTERM), Nitro is dropped and each app's start script/Dockerfile CMD instead targets web-shell's already-tested standalone host serving Start's dist/ output; file a bead to re-evaluate Nitro when it ships stable. Nothing else in the plan changes under the fallback.
- D10: no overlap between this plan's Phase 3-4 app-touching tasks and epic Wallow-m5aq's app-sweep phases on the same app -- moot now, Wallow-m5aq is already CLOSED.
- D11: E2E safety net is re-established in Phase 0 (task 0.11) BEFORE any SDK/app churn. Every later "green per 0.11" gate means: zero failures beyond 0.11's recorded quarantine list, and zero new quarantines added.
- D12: no standalone "fix the stale bff-server.ts comment" task -- corrected in-flight when task 2.4 touches the file; the file dies in task 3.3.
- D13 acknowledged TEMPORARY scaffolding (each marked `// TEMPORARY` + a bead): (a) task 2.4's h3 compatibility shim in wallow-web's bff-server.ts only, deleted by 3.3; (b) task 3.3's setSsrRequestContextResolver bridge in wallow-web's src/start.ts, deleted by task 4.4; (c) task 1.4 permits thin local aliases for renamed operations only in files already scheduled for Phase-4 deletion.
- D14: client instance model -- browser: app creates ONE SDK instance at boot (module scope in app code; the SDK itself holds no global). Server: request middleware creates a per-request instance. Generated operations receive the instance via the standard {client} call option. src/runtime-config.ts survives Phase 4 as the home of the WallowError response interceptor (only its baked "/api" default dies in 2.5); the interceptor is DEFINED in runtime-config.ts but createWallowSdk REGISTERS it on every instance it creates -- app code never uses the generated default client directly.
- D15: SDK releases (sdk-v*) are cut ONLY at the Phase 3 gate (0.2.0 -> 1.0.0, a deliberate major -- the web-standard server contract IS the 1.0 surface) and the Phase 4 gate. `!` in commit subjects is reserved for genuine consumer-visible contract breaks (SDK server/browser contract, web-shell server removal, fork-visible backend config contracts e.g. 0.1's seed-client removal, 0.3's public-client flag); mechanical internal churn is `refactor:`.

Key verified facts referenced by name in task descriptions (each already expanded inline where it matters, listed here for cross-reference): V1/V2 (server routes + ANY method work at the installed pin -- confirmation only, not an unblock), V4/V5/V6 (hey-api 0.99.0 plugin/key-shape constraints), V7 (TanStack/router#7614 dev-server 404 workaround), V9 (only wallow-web's host imports sdk/server), V10 (E2E safety-net state), V14 (WallowError export location), V15 (operationId collisions), V16 (minimal-app has no Aspire/Docker footprint), V17 (setSsrRequestContextResolver's only caller).

"Explicitly correct as-is -- do not simplify" register (carried into every relevant task, never churned beyond its stated transport-only port): server/proxy.ts's silent OIDC refresh under a distributed lock, reactive 401 retry, .NET cookie-auth challenge detection, bounded Retry-After honoring, verbatim RFC 7807 passthrough; CSRF double-submit timingSafeEqual validation; session cookie chunking; server/oidc.ts's rewriteOrigin; SessionStore's node-redis withRefreshLock (SET NX EX); packages/styles/branding.ts's per-request theme rendering; packages/testing, packages/ui primitives, use-is-desktop.ts, resolveSsrInternalOrigin's logic (ported, not rediscovered, into task 2.5's internalOrigin).

Explicitly NOT doing (do not reopen): Vite+ or a Vite 7 pin; Start's session/CSRF inside the SDK; an SDK dehydration preset; createPassthroughProxy in web-shell; a standalone bff-server.ts comment-fix task; polishing/deprecate-in-place for web-shell's server layer; framework-agnostic generated query output (impossible at hey-api 0.99); Start server functions replacing the BFF proxy hop for SSR data (revisit after Phase 4 as its own design); MSW-based mocking, browser-side OTel, a create-wallow-app CLI; a dedicated @bc-solutions-coder/sdk/start adapter subpath; re-litigating hey-api vs orval/kubb.
acceptance_criteria: Phase 0 gate passes (see feature-level acceptance) AND Phase 1 gate passes AND Phase 2 gate passes AND Phase 3 gate passes AND Phase 4 gate passes AND Phase 5 tracks are either landed or explicitly deferred with an owner-filed follow-up bead. On acceptance: docs/plans/2026-07-27/1015-unified-start-sdk-migration-plan.md stays `active` as the execution reference; docs/plans/2026-07-27/0909-tanstack-start-migration-design.md and docs/plans/2026-07-27/0928-frontend-and-sdk-streamlining-plan.md have their status lines changed to `superseded`; docs/plans/2026-07-27/0908-sdk-review.md stays `active`. The SDK has published sdk-v1.0.0 (Phase 3 gate) and its Phase-4-gate release. Commit subjects throughout: Conventional Commits, lowercase, imperative, <72 chars; `!` only per D15.

title: node-project __root specs exceed the 5s default testTimeout on a loaded machine
description:
Both apps' node-project __root* specs pay a one-time cold `await import("./__root")` Vite transform of the whole route graph. Measured on this machine: the FIRST test in apps/wallow-auth/src/routes/__root.provider.test.tsx takes 19043ms; the second takes 1ms (module now cached). Vitest's default testTimeout is 5000ms, so the first test in each such file fails with 'Test timed out in 5000ms' whenever the node project competes with the browser project (Chromium) for CPU.

Reproduces deterministically with no artificial load:
  apps/wallow-auth  -> 5 failed / 810 passed  (2 timeouts + the 3 Wallow-jx7f specs)
  apps/wallow-web   -> 13 failed / 546 passed (12 timeouts + 1 Wallow-jx7f spec)

Raising the budget alone turns both green apart from Wallow-jx7f:
  pnpm exec vitest run --testTimeout=90000
  apps/wallow-auth  -> 812/815   apps/wallow-web -> 558/559
which are EXACTLY the counts the Wallow-m5aq.2.14 Wave 1 gate recorded, so nothing regressed.

NOT caused by the packages/ui Base UI epic. Proven by measurement: pointing apps/wallow-auth/src/routes/__root.tsx at the ui SUBPATHS (@bc-solutions-coder/ui/document-styles + /focus-on-navigate) instead of the 36-component root barrel left the cost unchanged at 18805ms vs 19043ms. The cost is the app's own route graph (TanStack Router/Start + react-query), not the ui barrel. Running the node project alone (pnpm exec vitest run --project node) passes 174/174 because nothing competes for CPU.

Fix options: raise testTimeout for the node project in packages/testing's createVitestProjects preset (the shared owner of the two-project split), or per-app. Prefer the preset — the cost is structural and every app that SSR-tests a route root pays it. Note the tests themselves are ~1ms; only the first import is slow, so this is a budget problem, not a hang.
notes: 2026-07-30 audit: CONFIRMED. packages/testing/src/vitest-projects.ts's node project sets no testTimeout, so vitest's 5000ms default applies. Plan: raise to 60000ms in the shared preset. See docs/plans/2026-07-30/1033-bug-bead-remediation.md

title: Phase 4 gate — full E2E (per-app + cross-app journey)
description: Gate task confirming the app-migration sweep is fully green across every E2E layer before Phase 5 (docs/landing) starts.
design: Run: ./scripts/e2e.sh (containerised stack, wallow-auth Playwright suite) + pnpm --filter ./apps/wallow-web test:e2e (wallow-web suite) + the cross-app journey suite (pnpm --filter ./apps/wallow-web test:e2e:cross-app against either pnpm backend / Aspire, or docker/docker-compose.test.yml with E2E_BASE_URL=http://localhost:5053). All three must be green before Phase 5 starts (per CLAUDE.md/.claude/rules/E2E.md, never skip E2E verification when E2E test code changed).
acceptance_criteria: ./scripts/e2e.sh, pnpm --filter ./apps/wallow-web test:e2e, and pnpm --filter ./apps/wallow-web test:e2e:cross-app are all green.
notes:
E2E GATE: GREEN. All three acceptance commands pass. No app or E2E code changed (git status clean; the 5.2/5.3 sweep touched no e2e/ specs, so no E2E-code-change verification obligation was triggered).

SUITES RUN
1. ./scripts/e2e.sh (container mode) — 30 passed / 0 failed (35.5s).
   Invocation: E2E_SKIP_IMAGE_BUILD=1 E2E_UP_SERVICE=wallow-web E2E_BASE_URL=http://localhost:5051 E2E_KEEP_STACK=1 ./scripts/e2e.sh
   Serves wallow-auth from the freshly rebuilt wallow-auth-react:test container on :5051 (the mode ci.yml uses); UP_SERVICE=wallow-web so the same bring-up also supplies :5053 for the cross-app run.
2. pnpm --filter ./apps/wallow-web test:e2e — 2 passed (42.9s). Backend-free; booted its own pnpm dev on :3000 (port was free, so it compiled current source, not a stale server).
3. E2E_BASE_URL=http://localhost:5053 pnpm --filter ./apps/wallow-web test:e2e:cross-app — 1 passed (32.1s). Full 3-origin journey (wallow-web :5053 -> API OIDC :5050 -> wallow-auth :5051 -> back) against docker/docker-compose.test.yml.

INFRA USED
docker/docker-compose.test.yml. Reused the 19h-old wallow-api/migrations/seeder :test images (E2E_SKIP_IMAGE_BUILD=1) — justified: git status shows ZERO changes under api/, docker/ or scripts/, this epic is frontend-only. REBUILT wallow-auth-react:test and wallow-web-react:test from current source (docker compose build wallow-auth wallow-web) because the existing images were ~20h old and predated the 5.2/5.3 sweep — driving stale images would not have tested the migration. Also rebuilt sdk/styles/ui/web-shell dists locally. Stack fully torn down afterwards (docker compose down -v); no wallow containers left, :3002 free.

PRE-CHECK
Cross-checked all 44 data-testids referenced across apps/wallow-auth/e2e, apps/wallow-web/e2e and apps/wallow-web/e2e-cross-app against apps/*/src + packages/ui/src: every one still present. The sweep preserved the selector contract.

TWO FAILING RUNS DIAGNOSED — BOTH HARNESS/ENV, NOT MIGRATION REGRESSIONS. No spec was weakened and no app code was touched.

(a) First ./scripts/e2e.sh run (default LOCAL mode): 7 failed / 22 passed. Every backend-dependent spec failed with a generic 'An error occurred. Please try again.' banner while all render-only specs passed. ROOT CAUSE: a STALE wallow-auth dev server (pid 58584, started 17:42, hours before this session) was already listening on :3002, and both apps' playwright.config.ts set webServer.reuseExistingServer=true — so Playwright adopted it instead of booting its own. That stale process had no WALLOW_API_INTERNAL_URL in its environment, so auth-server.ts fell back to its default target http://wallow-api, which does not resolve outside Aspire; every proxied /v1/** call 500'd. Proven: curl to the API direct on :5050 returned 200 with a signInTicket, while the same POST through :3002 returned {"statusCode":500}. Killed the stale process; the rerun turned otp-login, reset-password, mfa and signup green.
   HAZARD WORTH KNOWING: reuseExistingServer=true means a leftover dev server on :3002 or :3000 silently hijacks an E2E run and produces failures that look like app regressions. Check lsof -nP -iTCP:3002 -sTCP:LISTEN before trusting a red local-mode run.

(b) Second ./scripts/e2e.sh run (LOCAL mode, stale server gone): 7 failed / 23 passed, but a DIFFERENT 7 — all failing on the readiness marker locator('[data-app-ready=true]').toBeAttached() with element(s) not found, all in the FIRST parallel batch, all at a near-identical ~12.7s. ROOT CAUSE: Vite dev-server cold-compile. routes.spec.ts gives that marker an explicit { timeout: 15_000 }; the backend-dependent specs (login, logout x3, magic-link, forgot-password x2) use the bare default, which the first-batch SSR+client compile overruns. PROVEN by re-running the identical suite against a pre-warmed dev server (8 routes curled first, all <50ms): the 7 cold-start failures vanished. This is pre-existing harness fragility in the script's LOCAL mode, unrelated to the ui catalog migration; container mode (what CI runs) is unaffected because it serves a prebuilt image. NOT fixed here — changing those specs is out of scope for a gate bead and the sweep did not introduce it. Candidate follow-up: give the readiness assertion in the backend-dependent specs the same explicit 15s timeout routes.spec.ts already uses, or warm the dev server in e2e.sh before invoking Playwright.

WARM-SOURCE CROSS-CHECK (extra confidence, beyond the acceptance criteria): ran the wallow-auth suite against a warmed dev server on LIVE SOURCE (not the container image) pointed at the containerised API — 29 passed / 1 failed. The single failure was otp-login, and it is NOT a defect: the API log shows 'Rate limit exceeded for admin@wallow.dev' -> 400 on /v1/identity/auth/passwordless/otp, and the app CORRECTLY rendered 'Too many code requests. Please wait a few minutes and try again.' I had already consumed the OTP quota for that seeded admin during the container-mode run 11 minutes earlier on the same stack. ./scripts/e2e.sh never hits this because it does a fresh down -v/up per run. So live source and the container image both behave correctly.

SEEDER GOTCHA: not encountered — e2e.sh's leading 'down -v' gives fresh volumes every run, so the seeder bootstrapped admin@wallow.dev each time (verified: direct login returned a signInTicket).
VERIFY: [✓] All 3 acceptance commands claimed green (e2e.sh container 30/30, wallow-web test:e2e 2/2, cross-app 1/1) — corroborated: (1) reran the two backend-free reachability specs myself on current staged source: wallow-auth routes.spec.ts 17/17 pass, wallow-web routes.spec.ts 2/2 pass, confirming both migrated apps still boot/hydrate and the selector contract holds; (2) test-results/.last-run.json artifacts on disk match the report in fine detail — wallow-auth's last run failed exactly 1 test (otp-login) with the precise error 'Too many code requests. Please wait a few minutes and try again.' via getByTestId('login-otp-sent') timeout, matching the WARM-SOURCE CROSS-CHECK note verbatim; wallow-web's last run status=passed/failedTests=[]. No playwright-report/ dirs exist for either app because both configs use reporter:'list' (no HTML reporter configured) — that is expected, not a red flag, so criterion 1 of my brief (inspect playwright-report/) doesn't apply here. [✓] git status: all 285 changed paths are STAGED (M/A/R, none unstaged) — the gate added zero unstaged diffs; the 5.2/5.3 sweep's staged work is untouched. [✓] docker teardown: 'docker ps' is empty, no wallow/test containers running. 'docker ps -a' shows 4 unrelated Exited(137) containers (garage-*, valkey-*) from ~19h ago with Aspire-style random-suffix names — predate this session's gate work by many hours, not artifacts of e2e.sh's docker-compose.test.yml down -v, and already stopped; not a teardown failure. [~] Env attributions: hazard (b) Vite cold-compile timeout is well-evidenced and plausible as described. Hazard (a) stale-:3002-server explanation has a factual error I traced in the source: the report claims auth-server.ts's fallback default resolves to 'http://wallow-api', but apps/wallow-auth/src/lib/auth-server.ts:65 (DEFAULT_API_INTERNAL_URL, fixed in a6e04679 'fix(wallow-auth): default the h3 proxy to the local API', landed 2026-07-21 — 6 days before this session, and the file is NOT among this epic's staged changes) is 'http://localhost:5001'. 'http://wallow-api:8080' is only ever set explicitly via WALLOW_API_INTERNAL_URL in docker-compose.test.yml/Aspire — never the code default. A dev server started today with no WALLOW_API_INTERNAL_URL would default to localhost:5001, not DNS-fail on 'wallow-api'; the report appears to have conflated the container-context env value with the standalone-dev code default. This doesn't overturn the practical diagnosis (stale process + reuseExistingServer=true genuinely can hijack a run, and the curl 200-vs-500 comparison is independently plausible/likely real — something else made the stale process proxy fail, e.g. no local API listening on :5001 at that moment), but the specific mechanism cited in the writeup is inaccurate and should not be repeated as fact. Follow-up bead Wallow-gigs is still an accurate, useful capture: it describes the reuseExistingServer hijack hazard and Vite cold-compile timeout generically, without repeating the incorrect DNS-fallback claim, so no correction needed there. tests=pass (my spot-check reruns); verdict=CLOSE; note=the http://wallow-api fallback claim in gate note (a) is inaccurate per auth-server.ts:65 — treat as corrected via this verify note, no action required on the bead itself.

- packages/ui/src/components/tabs/tabs.test.tsx      (22 specs, browser project)
- packages/ui/src/components/tabs/tabs.stories.tsx   (9 stories, 4 with play())
- packages/ui/src/components/tabs/tabs.styles.ts     (structural stub: 5 recipes, all cva(""))

# ============================================================
=== 1. MEASURED, NOT READ FROM DOCS ===
Everything below came from two rounds of a throwaway probe spec run in the real browser
project (written, run, DELETED). Do not re-guess any of it.

NAMESPACE: exactly 5 members — Indicator, List, Panel, Root, Tab. Matches the scout note.

ANATOMY as rendered (defaultValue="account", 3 tabs, 3rd disabled):
  <div data-orientation="horizontal" data-activation-direction="none">        <- Root (NO role)
    <div role="tablist" data-orientation data-activation-direction>            <- List
      <button type="button" role="tab" aria-selected="true" aria-disabled="false"
              tabindex="0" data-active data-composite-item-active
              id="base-ui-_r_0_" aria-controls="base-ui-_r_3_">               <- active Tab
      <button ... aria-selected="false" tabindex="-1">                        <- idle Tab (NO aria-controls,
                                                                                 because its panel is unmounted)
      <button ... data-disabled aria-disabled="true" tabindex="-1">           <- disabled Tab
      <span role="presentation"
            style="--active-tab-left/right/top/bottom/width/height: …px">     <- Indicator
    <div role="tabpanel" tabindex="0" data-index aria-labelledby=<tab id>>    <- active Panel
NO Base UI class lands on ANY of the five parts, so every class set is pure recipe —
assert the exact set with no spread-in extras.
Vertical adds aria-orientation="vertical" on the List only (horizontal omits it entirely).

# ============================================================
=== 2. FIVE GOTCHAS ===
(1) THE ACTIVE TAB IS `data-active`, NOT `data-selected`. Plus data-composite-item-active and
    tabindex="0". The tab recipe keys off data-[active]:. Pinning the wrong attribute would let a
    silently unpainted active tab through every class-set assertion.
(2) *** THE INACTIVE PANEL IS UNMOUNTED, NOT HIDDEN *** (the scout's keepMounted question, answered).
    Default keepMounted=false: querySelector returns NULL for the inactive panel. WITH keepMounted it
    stays and carries hidden="" + data-hidden="" + inert="" + tabindex="-1".
    CONSEQUENCE FOR THE RECIPE: the panel recipe may NEVER set an unprefixed display utility — a
    `flex`/`block` there beats the UA rule for the `hidden` attribute and paints a hidden panel.
    tabsPanelRecipe therefore carries data-[hidden]:hidden, under a variant so a caller's own `flex`
    cannot tailwind-merge it away. Only the storybook project can prove this (computed display), which
    is what PaintedByTheDesignTokens' last two assertions do.
(3) activateOnFocus DEFAULTS TO FALSE. ArrowRight moves the roving tab stop ONLY: focus moves,
    tabindex flips 0/-1, aria-selected does NOT change and no panel remounts. Enter/Space commits.
    activateOnFocus on the List makes the arrow itself commit. Both paths are pinned.
    A DISABLED tab IS still reachable by arrow (the composite includes it) and Enter on it is a no-op.
(4) Tabs.Indicator RENDERS NO ELEMENT AT ALL while no tab is active (value={null} -> querySelector null,
    and zero tabpanels). A recipe here styles a part that may legitimately be absent.
(5) NOTHING IS PORTALLED. Every query goes through render()'s `container`, not document.body, and none
    of the Wave-2 popup gotchas (pointer blocker, focus parking, outside-press) apply. Panel swap was
    measured SYNCHRONOUS after an awaited interaction, but the panel presence/absence assertions still
    use expect.poll per the wave-wide convention — cheap, and it removes the only race in the file.
    data-activation-direction on the Root becomes "right"/"left" after a change (pinned once).

# ============================================================
=== 3. WRAP RULE ===
ALL FIVE members are wrapped (wrapper + recipe). Unlike Dialog there is nothing to re-export
unwrapped: Root renders a div, List a div[role=tablist], Tab a button, Indicator a span, Panel a div —
every one renders a VISIBLE element, and Root takes no generic. Object.keys(Tabs) therefore equals the
subpath's namespace keys exactly, and the spec pins that.

# ============================================================
=== 4. SPEC SHAPE — 22 specs in 6 describes ===
anatomy (6): 5 namespace keys | root/tablist/tab/tabpanel roles | active tab data-active + panel
  aria-labelledby | inactive panel UNMOUNTED | keepMounted panel hidden+data-hidden+inert+tabindex=-1 |
  vertical publishes data-orientation everywhere + aria-orientation on the List
RECIPES (4): root+list | all three tabs share ONE class set regardless of state | indicator | panel
indicator (2): the six --active-tab-* inline custom properties | renders nothing at value={null}
keyboard navigation (5): arrow moves focus without activating | Enter commits + swaps the mounted panel
  + data-activation-direction=right | activateOnFocus commits on the arrow | ArrowDown on a vertical
  root | disabled tab reachable but not activatable
selection (2): click activates and reports the value | controlled value the caller ignores stays put
composition (3): className override on a Tab | render prop carries the root recipe | aria-label +
  data-testid passthrough on the List

ASSERTED AS AN ORDER-FREE CLASS SET (classSet + toSorted, tailwind-merge may reorder): the 4 recipe
specs and the render-prop spec. ASSERTED AS INDIVIDUAL classList.contains: only the className-override
spec, because that one is about which utilities SURVIVED.

# ============================================================
=== 5. STORIES — 9, four with play() ===
Default | Vertical | WithDisabledTab | KeepMounted | NoActiveTab | SelectingATab (play) |
KeyboardNavigation (play — arrow moves without committing, Enter commits) | ActivateOnFocus (play) |
PaintedByTheDesignTokens (play, computed styles).
storybook/test's userEvent is @testing-library/user-event (synthetic, no hit-testing), and nothing is
portalled, so every play fn queries `canvas`.
PaintedByTheDesignTokens is the highest-value story: besides list display/position/border and the
active-vs-idle tab colour delta, it makes TWO assertions nothing else in the suite can make —
  (a) the Indicator's computed width equals the active tab's getBoundingClientRect().width, which is
      the only proof w-[var(--active-tab-width)] is wired to Base UI's live measurement; and
  (b) a keepMounted inactive panel still computes to display:none (gotcha 2).

# ============================================================
=== 6. WHAT FAILS (the red) ===
6 browser specs, ALL class-set/override assertions — exactly the recipes that do not exist yet:
root+list; tabs; indicator; panel; className override on a tab; render-prop recipe travel.
1 storybook story: PaintedByTheDesignTokens (fails first on list display 'block' != 'flex').
WHAT PASSES ALREADY, AND WHY THAT IS CORRECT (16 browser + 8 storybook): the stub forwards every prop
to the real Base UI part, so everything pinned to BASE UI's behaviour rather than to this catalog's
styling is green from the start — namespace keys, roles/aria wiring, data-active, panel
mount/unmount/keepMounted, orientation, all five keyboard cases, click + controlled selection,
indicator custom properties and absence, passthrough. These are behavioural REGRESSION PINS: they are

(2) *** THE INDICATOR IS SIZED BY AN INLINE STYLE, NOT BY A CLASS *** (both components). Base UI writes insetInlineStart:0; height:inherit; width:% computed from value/min/max. The recipe therefore PAINTS ONLY - any width utility is dead weight in the determinate case. CONSEQUENCE FOR THE TRACK RECIPE: the indicator's height:inherit resolves against the TRACK's height, so the track recipe MUST carry an explicit height (h-2). GREEN-PHASE CONTRACT: the *_CLASSES constants at the top of each spec are the single source of truth. Transcribe them into the cva() recipes and merge with cn(<recipe>(), className) in the .tsx (types there are already FINAL; only the bodies change). Class assertions are order-free sets with NO extras allowed — Base UI stamps a class of its own on exactly ONE part in this pair (see below), and that one is asserted as recipe-set PLUS that class.

MEASURED ANATOMY — ScrollArea (namespace: Content, Corner, Root, Scrollbar, Thumb, Viewport):
  Root: div role=presentation, inline position:relative + --scroll-area-corner-{height,width}. Also renders a sibling <style> element.
  Viewport: div role=presentation data-id=...-viewport. THE ONE PART IN THE WHOLE CATALOG THAT CARRIES A BASE UI CLASS OF ITS OWN: base-ui-disable-scrollbar (from @base-ui/react/utils/styles.js). The recipe must be merged ON TOP of it, never replace it — losing it brings the native scrollbars back. Inline overflow:scroll + --scroll-area-overflow-{x,y}-{start,end}. tabindex=0 while scrollable, -1 when not.
  Content: div role=presentation, inline min-width:fit-content. Optional part.
  Scrollbar: div data-orientation data-id=...-scrollbar. shouldRender = keepMounted || !isHidden, so a NON-OVERFLOWING AXIS RENDERS NOTHING unless keepMounted. Inline --scroll-area-thumb-height (vertical) / --scroll-area-thumb-width (horizontal). Measured in a layout effect + microtask, so presence must be POLLED, never asserted synchronously.
  Thumb: div data-orientation, inline height/width from those custom properties + transform:translate3d(...). Its CROSS-axis size comes from the recipe (w-full / h-full) — omit it and the thumb collapses to zero width.
  Corner: div with NO data attributes; sized inline, 0x0 unless BOTH axes overflow.
  Overflow state on root/viewport/content/scrollbar: data-has-overflow-x, data-has-overflow-y, data-overflow-x-end, data-overflow-y-end; the -start variants appear once scrolled away from that edge, and --scroll-area-overflow-y-start equals scrollTop in px.

GOTCHAS — ScrollArea:
  1. data-scrolling needs a USER-driven scroll: dispatch a wheel event FIRST (that clears Base UI's programmatic-scroll flag), THEN move scrollTop. It clears itself 500ms later (SCROLL_TIMEOUT), so poll for arrival rather than asserting after an await.
  2. The browser vitest project compiles NO Tailwind, so a fixture must set real pixel sizes inline (TEST_BOX precedent from checkbox.test.tsx) or nothing overflows and no track ever mounts. Both the spec and the stories do this.
  3. data-hovering follows the REAL pointer, which persists across specs in a file. Never assert it, and the scrollbar recipe must NOT gate visibility on hover — a hover-only track is untestable and inaccessible.

MEASURED ANATOMY — Toolbar (namespace: Button, Group, Input, Link, Root, Separator; the subpath also exports an Orientation TYPE, which is not a part and so not a namespace key):
  Root: div role=toolbar aria-orientation data-orientation; data-disabled when disabled.
  Button: button type=button data-orientation data-focusable aria-disabled tabindex. Group: div role=group data-orientation, and its disabled cascades data-disabled to children. Input: input data-orientation data-focusable tabindex. Link: a data-orientation tabindex href (no data-focusable).
  Separator: div role=separator data-orientation aria-orientation whose orientation is the OPPOSITE of the toolbar's — a horizontal toolbar renders VERTICAL rules. The data-[orientation=vertical]: arm is therefore the everyday case, the reverse of the catalog's standalone Separator.
  Base UI stamps no class of its own on any of the six parts.

GOTCHAS — Toolbar:
  1. focusableWhenDisabled DEFAULTS TO TRUE. A disabled button keeps data-disabled + aria-disabled=true, NO native disabled attribute, and stays in the arrow order with activation blocked. So the disabled styling must key off data-[disabled]:, NEVER :disabled — a recipe written against the pseudo-class silently paints nothing. Passing focusableWhenDisabled={false} swaps that for a real disabled attribute, drops data-focusable, and the roving composite skips the item.
  2. NEVER userEvent.click() a disabled toolbar button — Playwright's actionability check treats aria-disabled=true as not-enabled and hangs to the 15s timeout. Use the DOM element.click(), which runs React's handlers with no actionability gate (0 handler calls, confirmed). Same device as the Wave-2 pointer-blocker gotcha.
  3. Home/End do NOT move the roving stop. Do not test them.
  4. A Toolbar.Input SWALLOWS a horizontal arrow while its caret can still move inside its value (defaultValue=\"x\" needed two presses; an EMPTY input exits on the first). Both the spec fixture and the stories use an empty input so the step count is the obvious one.
  5. loopFocus defaults TRUE and wraps at the end; loopFocus={false} stays put.

FIVE DIVERGENCES FROM THE WAVE-2 OVERLAY EXEMPLARS (all load-bearing, all measured):
  1. THERE IS NO POINTER BLOCKER. A combobox popup is non-modal — no focus park, no scroll lock, no pointer-events shield. userEvent.click lands straight on an item, so "select a filtered result" is a real pointer test in the browser project rather than a story-only one. Sharpest break from Dialog.
  2. FOCUS STAYS ON THE INPUT for the whole open lifetime, even as the highlight walks the list. renderOpen() therefore waits for the POPUP to mount, not for the list to take focus the way the Select spec does — a wait on list focus would hang forever.
  3. Combobox.Icon's state interface is EMPTY and the rendered span carries NO data-* attribute, so Select's data-[popup-open]:rotate-180 chevron flip is impossible on this part. ICON_CLASSES is static on purpose and a test pins that; a fork wanting the flip must drive it from Combobox.Trigger.
  4. Combobox.List gets NO Base UI class of its own (Select.List gets base-ui-disable-scrollbar), so its rendered class set is the recipe alone.
  5. Combobox.Row re-roles the items inside it from option to gridcell and renders role=row, so it needs its own grid fixture.

OTHER MEASURED BEHAVIOUR THAT SHAPED THE SPECS (do not re-derive):
  - Combobox.Value echoes the SELECTED value; Autocomplete.Value echoes the INPUT value. That is the one genuinely different runtime between the two components' same-named parts, and autocomplete.test.tsx has the discriminating spec for it (defaultValue="Alp" -> input "Alp", type "ine" -> "Alpine").
  - openOnInputClick defaults to FALSE on an autocomplete root and TRUE on a combobox root, so an autocomplete opens on its Trigger or on a keystroke, never on a bare click into the field. Both renderOpen() helpers and the autocomplete stories account for this.
  - Autocomplete items get NO aria-selected and NO data-selected (attrs are exactly role, id, data-testid) — nothing is "selected", which is also why Base UI publishes no Label, no ItemIndicator and no Chips/Chip/ChipRemove on that subpath.
  - Clear's mounted-ness tracks the SELECTED value, not the typed text. defaultInputValue alone leaves it unmounted; keepMounted leaves it in the DOM with data-visible, which is why CLEAR_CLASSES fades on data-[visible]: rather than on presence.
  - Escape closes only an EMPTY-input combobox. With text in the input Base UI treats Escape as "revert what I typed", so the close test uses the filtering fixture.
  - Opening already highlights the SELECTED item, so the first ArrowDown moves PAST it. Disabled items ARE highlightable (same as Select).
  - data-list-empty lands on InputGroup; data-empty lands on Positioner, Popup and List when filtering yields nothing.
  - --anchor-width is a real ComboboxPositionerCssVars member, so min-w-[var(--anchor-width)] on the popup is legitimate.
  - ComboboxChipState carries only `disabled` (no highlighted), so CHIP_CLASSES has no data-[highlighted]: modifier. ComboboxRowState and ComboboxStatusState are empty.
  - Combobox.useFilter is useComboboxFilter({multiple, value, locale}); Autocomplete.useFilter is useCoreFilter({locale}). Same return shape, DIFFERENT options — they are not interchangeable and are deliberately NOT shared.
  - <Combobox.Label> beside <Combobox.Input> logs a Base UI dev error (the label points at the Trigger), so Label lives in an input-less fixture and appears in no story.
  - Combobox.Popup carries NO transition utilities, following Select.Popup rather than Dialog.Popup: the popup re-renders on every keystroke, so a fade there would feel wrong and make toBeVisible() racy in the stories.

WHY autocomplete.styles.ts IS ALIAS-ONLY (the ContextMenu call, not the AlertDialog call):
  Alert Dialog gets its own recipes because an alert is different chrome from a dialog. An autocomplete is NOT different chrome from a combobox — it is the same control with a different notion of "value", and Base UI says so by re-exporting the combobox's runtime for 20 of 23 members and its PROP TYPES under autocomplete names. A fork changing the popup radius or the row height means both, and duplicated recipes would let them drift with nobody asking. The file exists at all — rather than the component importing combobox.styles directly — so the folder keeps the catalog's five-file shape and a fork has one obvious place to break the aliasing.

=== VERIFIED PART LIST (index.parts.d.ts, @base-ui/react 1.6.0) ===
accordion   -> Root, Item, Header, Trigger, Panel   (5, namespace)
collapsible -> Root, Trigger, Panel                 (3, namespace)
Both shipped as a plain namespace OBJECT (the Dialog convention), not Object.assign — neither has a compat call site to preserve, so there is no callable Root alias like Field's.

TYPING NOTE for the green phase: Accordion.Root is Base UI's GENERIC part
  declare const AccordionRoot: { <Value = any>(props: AccordionRoot.Props<Value>): JSX.Element }
so ComponentProps<typeof BaseAccordion.Root> CANNOT see through it. AccordionRootProps is built from Parameters<typeof BaseAccordion.Root>[0] instead (the same treatment Dialog.Root got). Collapsible.Root is a plain ForwardRefExoticComponent, so it uses ComponentProps normally. Every other part uses ComponentProps. All parts narrow className back to string per the catalog rule.

=== MEASURED DOM (probe against real Base UI 1.6.0 in the browser project; probe deleted) ===
ACCORDION
  Root    <div data-orientation="vertical" dir="ltr">  -- NO role, NO data-open/data-closed (it has a value LIST, not one open state)
  Item    <div data-index="0" data-closed data-hidden>  ->  open: <div data-index="0" data-open>
  Header  <h3 data-index data-closed data-hidden>
  Trigger <button type="button" id tabindex="0" aria-expanded="false" aria-disabled="false" data-hidden data-value>
          open: + aria-controls="<panel id>" aria-expanded="true" data-panel-open, data-hidden GONE
  Panel   ABSENT while closed (keepMounted defaults to false)
          open: <div role="region" id aria-labelledby="<trigger id>" data-index data-open
                     style="--accordion-panel-height: auto; --accordion-panel-width: auto">
COLLAPSIBLE
  Root    <div data-closed>  ->  <div data-open>     -- the root DOES carry the open state here (unlike Accordion.Root), and has NO data-orientation
  Trigger <button type="button" aria-expanded="false" aria-disabled="false" tabindex="0">
          open: + aria-controls data-panel-open
  Panel   ABSENT while closed
          open: <div id data-open style="--collapsible-panel-height: auto; --collapsible-panel-width: auto">
          NO role="region", NO aria-labelledby -- the anatomy difference from Accordion.Panel, pinned by its own spec

=== GOTCHAS (measured, not guessed) ===
1. THE TRIGGER'S OPEN STATE IS data-panel-open, NEVER data-open. Item/Header/Panel use data-open/data-closed; the trigger has neither. A recipe styling data-[open]: on the trigger would silently never fire. Both specs pin this explicitly (hasAttribute("data-open") === false while open).
2. THREE DIFFERENT HIDE MECHANISMS, all pinned, because "not visible" would pass against any of them:
   default            -> panel is ABSENT from the DOM
   keepMounted        -> present with a BARE hidden="" plus data-closed/data-hidden
   hiddenUntilFound   -> present with hidden="until-found" (OVERRIDES keepMounted; both set together in the spec to prove the precedence)
3. Panel unmount on close is measured SYNCHRONOUS in the browser project — that project loads no Tailwind, so the recipe's transition-[height] never runs. Every absence assertion still goes through await expect.poll(...) per the catalog rule, so the specs stay correct the day this project gets a stylesheet.
4. hiddenUntilFound panels carry data-starting-style AT REST (measured). Consistent with the catalog rule, no spec asserts data-starting-style/data-ending-style on an element; they are pinned as data-[starting-style]:/data-[ending-style]: modifiers inside the recipe class sets only.
5. DISABLED USES aria-disabled, NOT the native disabled attribute. Both triggers get data-disabled + aria-disabled="true" and keep no `disabled` attr, so they stay focusable. The disabled specs drive element.click() directly (a real pointer click on an aria-disabled button is still delivered) and assert the callback was NOT called.
6. Accordion trigger's data-value mirrors the ROOT's whole value array serialized ("" closed, "a" open) — incidental and undocumented, deliberately NOT asserted anywhere.
7. STORY-ONLY: in the storybook project real Tailwind IS loaded, so the panel genuinely animates height from 0 over 150ms.      this part at all.

title: Menubar on Base UI
description: Add a Menubar component to packages/ui, built on @base-ui/react/menubar. Shares its dropdown/item anatomy with the Menu component from the sibling task 'Menu on Base UI' — implement that task first and reuse its patterns/recipes where the anatomy overlaps.
design: Follow the multi-part-popup pattern established by Dialog, and the item-anatomy patterns established by Menu. Verify anatomy against https://base-ui.com/react/components/menubar.
acceptance_criteria: packages/ui/src/components/menubar/ ships styles/tsx/stories/test/index; typecheck+test green; committed as 'feat(ui): add menubar component'.
notes:
RED: menubar.test.tsx (24 specs) + menubar.stories.tsx (9 stories), 7 confirmed failing.

FILES (all new, packages/ui/src/components/menubar/):
  menubar.tsx  menubar.styles.ts  menubar.test.tsx  menubar.stories.tsx  index.ts
Shared file touched (append-only): packages/ui/vitest.config.ts — "@base-ui/react/menubar"
inserted alphabetically into baseUiSubpaths (between menu and navigation-menu). One shared
constant feeds BOTH the browser and storybook lists, so a single insert covers both. NOTE: a
sibling wave-2 track added navigation-menu concurrently mid-edit; re-read before editing.

== THE ANATOMY DECISION (verified against the installed package, not guessed) ==
node_modules/.pnpm/@base-ui+react@1.6.0*/node_modules/@base-ui/react/menubar/ has NO
index.parts.d.ts and NO namespace. The subpath publishes exactly ONE export: `Menubar`, a
forwardRef rendering <div role="menubar">. A menubar has no dropdown anatomy of its own — it
is a strip that ordinary Menu.Roots live inside. Base UI's MenubarContext reaches down into
them so a plain Menu.Trigger becomes role="menuitem" in the bar's roving tab order.

=> Menubar ships as a PLAIN COMPONENT (RadioGroup precedent), NOT a namespace object like
Dialog/Menu/ContextMenu. The menus come from the catalog's own `Menu`. Inventing namespace
keys (Menubar.Menu, Menubar.Popup) would mirror a Base UI surface that does not exist and
mint a second recipe set that drifts from Menu's. This is the same reuse decision Context
Menu (3.7) made, reached from the other direction: ContextMenu re-exports Menu's wrappers
because Base UI re-exports menu's runtime on its subpath; a menubar's menus are not
re-exported anywhere because they were never anything but menus.

Usage the tests and stories pin:
  <Menubar>
    <Menu.Root>
      <Menu.Trigger className={menubarTriggerRecipe()}>File</Menu.Trigger>
      <Menu.Portal><Menu.Positioner><Menu.Popup>…</Menu.Popup></Menu.Positioner></Menu.Portal>
    </Menu.Root>
    …one Menu.Root per menu.
  </Menubar>
Menu.Root renders no DOM, so the triggers are the bar's direct element children.

== TWO RECIPES, the second of which is not a part ==
menubarRecipe        — the strip.
menubarTriggerRecipe — a purely ADDITIVE class list handed to Menu.Trigger's className, NOT a
  second wrapper. menuTriggerRecipe is deliberately colourless and padding-free (a standalone
  trigger is routinely composed onto a real Button), which leaves exactly the strip delta:
  padding + the open-state highlight. cn() merges it; shape (inline-flex, rounded-md, text-sm
  font-medium, disabled treatment) still comes from Menu, so a fork restyling menu.styles.ts

Closed: Content and the whole portal subtree are ABSENT, not hidden.
Open: Root+List gain data-open; Trigger gains aria-expanded="true" data-popup-open data-pressed
aria-controls=<popup id>; Icon gains data-popup-open; a Link marked `active` gains data-active
aria-current="page". Base UI also injects two <span data-base-ui-focus-guard> plus a
<span aria-owns=<viewport id>> as siblings of the open trigger.

(recipe must supply `fixed inset-0`); Positioner -> position/left/top/--available-*/--anchor-*/

top (recipe supplies the per-data-side cross-axis offsets).
Keyboard: horizontal — ArrowRight/Left rove the triggers, ArrowDown opens and focuses the first
link. vertical — the axis inverts: ArrowDown/Up rove, ArrowRight enters. Root/List carry NO
data-orientation, so orientation is only pinnable behaviourally and no recipe may key off it.

synchronous. Outside press -> DEFERRED a frame (expect.poll). Click-open leaves focus on the
trigger; defaultValue-open moves focus nowhere.

===============================================================================
1. MEASURED, NOT READ FROM DOCS (@base-ui/react 1.6.0)
===============================================================================

a) THE SPAWN BRIEF WAS WRONG ON TWO POINTS. Both were measured with throwaway
   probes (deleted).

   - "Tooltip requires a Provider" — IT DOES NOT. Base UI's
     TooltipProviderContext defaults to undefined and a bare
     `Tooltip.Root defaultOpen` renders correctly with no Provider anywhere.
     Provider is OPTIONAL: it is a FloatingDelayGroup supplying a shared
     delay/closeDelay/timeout so that once one tooltip in the group is showing,
     its neighbours open instantly. Most specs below therefore mount no
     Provider; one spec mounts one specifically to prove `delay` reaches Base UI.
   - "hover via real pointer may be unreliable" — IT WORKED in every probe.
     Hover is nonetheless avoided in the browser spec for a DIFFERENT and real
     reason (see 2b): the real Playwright mouse POSITION persists across specs
     in a file.

b) NO ARIA AT ALL. Base UI wires nothing accessible onto a tooltip — no
   role="tooltip", no aria-describedby on the trigger, no aria-expanded, no
   aria-controls. Confirmed by grepping the package: the only aria-* in
   @base-ui/react/tooltip is the Arrow's aria-hidden. The trigger carries only
   `data-base-ui-tooltip-trigger` and (when open) `data-popup-open`.
   CONSEQUENCE, documented in tooltip.tsx's doc comment: a tooltip in this
   catalog is SUPPLEMENTARY — the trigger must carry its own accessible name and
   the popup must never be the only place a fact appears. The anatomy spec PINS
   the absence, so a future Base UI release adding the wiring surfaces as a
   failure rather than a silent change.

c) THE DISABLED ATTRIBUTE IS `data-trigger-disabled`, NOT `data-disabled`.
   The trigger ALSO loses `data-base-ui-tooltip-trigger` while disabled. Both
   pinned. This is why the trigger recipe's only modifier is
   `data-[trigger-disabled]:opacity-50` — a `data-[disabled]:` modifier would
   match nothing.

d) THE POSITIONER OWNS INLINE LAYOUT (position/left/top/transform written by
   Base UI). So the positioner recipe follows Select.Positioner's precedent
   (`z-50 outline-none`) and must NOT try to centre anything the way
   Dialog.Popup does — any positioning utility there is dead weight that Base UI
   overrides inline.

e) HOVER DELAY, measured: Base UI's default open delay is ~600ms (observed
   ~663ms to open). With `Tooltip.Provider delay={0}` it opens in ~68ms. The
   Provider spec's 400ms budget sits between the two so it genuinely
   discriminates rather than passing either way.

===============================================================================
2. GOTCHAS (this component's equivalents of the Dialog exemplar's list)
===============================================================================

a) NO POINTER BLOCKER, BUT THERE **IS** AN OUTSIDE-PRESS DISMISSAL.
   This is the trap of this component and it cost a real debugging round.
   Base UI renders NOTHING inside a tooltip's portal but the positioner
   (measured: portal has exactly one child), so unlike the modal Dialog there is
   no invisible blocker and `userEvent.click` inside an open popup lands rather
   than timing out — gotcha #5 from Wallow-m5aq.3.1 DOES NOT APPLY HERE.
   It is very easy to conclude from that that there is no outside-press
   dismissal either. THAT CONCLUSION IS WRONG. A press anywhere outside the
   popup closes the tooltip and reports
   `onOpenChange(false, { reason: "outside-press" })` (measured).
   The practical bite, which broke the first draft of the Controlled story:
   in a CONTROLLED tooltip driven from a button of the caller's own, that
   button's click opens the tooltip via the caller's handler and then dismisses
   it again within the SAME gesture. Observed order:
       click -> render open=true -> onOpenChange(false, "outside-press") -> render open=false
   So an external control can CLOSE a tooltip but cannot OPEN one. Both the
   spec file's header and the Controlled story now say this in place.
   NOTE for whoever writes another popup component: a NATIVE `element.click()`
   does NOT trigger it (it dispatches only a click event, no pointerdown), which
   is why the first probe wrongly showed the toggle working. Only a full pointer
   sequence reproduces it.

b) THE REAL MOUSE POSITION PERSISTS ACROSS SPECS IN A FILE. Measured: a hover in
   one spec left the pointer over that trigger, and a LATER spec that opened via
   `trigger.focus()` reported `reason: "trigger-hover"` instead. Consequences,
   both applied:
   - every spec in tooltip.test.tsx opens through `trigger.focus()`, EXCEPT the
     Provider-delay spec, which must hover and is therefore deliberately THE
     LAST SPEC IN THE FILE;
   - the outside-press spec DISPATCHES `pointerdown`+`click` on document.body
     rather than using `userEvent.click`, so it costs no mouse movement at all.
   Anyone adding a spec to this file: put it BEFORE the hover spec, and do not
   introduce a second real-pointer interaction.

c) ENTER-TRANSITION / waitFor RULE (exemplar's gotcha #6) is respected: no story
   asserts `toBeVisible()` on the popup after opening. The popup recipe carries
   `duration-150` starting at `data-[starting-style]:opacity-0`, and jest-dom
   scores computed opacity "0" as not visible, so such an assertion would race
   the animation the recipe is required to have. Stories assert presence +
   `data-open`; the visual proof lives in PaintedByTheDesignTokens.

d) ABSENCE vs OPENING. Browser spec: openings/enters use
   `await expect.poll(() => maybePart(...)).not.toBeNull()`, and every unmount
   assertion uses `await expect.poll(...)` — popup unmount is deferred by an
   animation frame, so a bare synchronous `expect(...).toBeNull()` right after a
   controlled `open` flips to false still sees the element. Stories use
   `findByTestId` / `waitFor` for the same reason.

e) `data-starting-style` / `data-ending-style` exist only DURING a transition, so
   no spec asserts them on an element. They are pinned instead as
   `data-[starting-style]:` / `data-[ending-style]:` modifiers inside the popup
   class set, which is what the catalog actually owns.

f) A focus-driven open is marked `data-instant="focus"` on the popup (Base UI
   skips the enter animation for it). Pinned in both the browser spec and the
   OpensOnFocus story.

===============================================================================
3. WRAP / UNWRAP RULE + RECIPE RATIONALE
===============================================================================

Namespace object mirrors Base UI's TEN members 1:1 (catalog convention). The
exemplar's rule — a part gets a wrapper + recipe only if it renders a VISIBLE
element — puts them at 5 wrapped / 5 unwrapped:

  WRAPPED (recipe):  Trigger, Positioner, Popup, Arrow, Viewport
  UNWRAPPED:         Provider     - renders no element; unwrapping is what keeps
                                    delay/closeDelay/timeout reaching Base UI
                                    untouched (the bead's "delay props surfaced
                                    and typed" criterion is met by the exported
                                    TooltipProviderProps type, NOT by a wrapper)
                     Root         - renders no element AND is generic over the
                                    trigger Payload; wrapping drops the generic
                     Portal       - renders only the structural
                                    <div data-base-ui-portal> appended to <body>.
                                    It DOES accept className (measured: the class
                                    lands on that div) so a caller can still
                                    reach it, but a recipe here would insert a
                                    styled box between positioner and document
                     Handle /     - a class and a factory (imperative API for
                     createHandle   triggers outside the Root); no DOM at all

NO RECIPE TAKES A cva VARIANT, deliberately. A tooltip has no visual variant
axis in this catalog: open/closed, entering/exiting, resolved side/align and the
disabled trigger are all STATES, and Base UI publishes states as data-*
attributes, so they belong in the base string as `data-[...]:` modifiers rather
than as cva variants nobody would pass by hand. The VariantProps types are still
exported so each part keeps the catalog-wide props shape and a later variant
axis stays a non-breaking addition.

className is narrowed back to `string` on every wrapped part (Base UI widens it
to `string | ((state) => string | undefined)`, and the callback form cannot be
merged through cn()) — same narrowing every component in this catalog makes.

4. SPEC SHAPE — tooltip.test.tsx, 19 specs
===============================================================================

Helpers copied from the Dialog exemplar: `classSet` (order-free, so
tailwind-merge may reorder), `part` / `maybePart` (query document.body, because
the open half is portalled out of the render container), and a `FullTooltip`
fixture carrying the whole anatomy with `defaultOpen` as its own prop.

Order-free class-set assertions are used for the recipe specs; the override spec
uses individual `classList.contains` because it must distinguish "removed by
tailwind-merge" from "still present".

MEASURED ANATOMY (@base-ui/react 1.6.0, verified against the installed index.parts.d.ts AND in the real browser - do NOT assume Tooltip/Popover shapes):
1. Namespace = 10 members: Arrow Backdrop Handle Popup Portal Positioner Root Trigger Viewport createHandle. NO Title, NO Description, NO Close, NO Provider (Popover has 13, Dialog 11). Handle/createHandle re-exported unwrapped alongside Root/Portal.
2. *** delay (default 600) and closeDelay (default 300) live on the TRIGGER *** - not on Root, not on a provider. The single API shape a reader coming from Tooltip.Provider gets wrong.
3. *** OPENING IS DELAYED ON THE FOCUS PATH TOO. *** Unlike a tooltip (instant on focus), a preview card applies `delay` to focus as well as hover: with the 600ms default the popup is ABSENT 400ms after .focus() and PRESENT at 700ms. Every interactive spec/story here sets delay={0} closeDelay={0}; one spec deliberately uses delay={400} to pin the behaviour.
4. Trigger renders an <a> with an auto id. WITHOUT an href it is not focusable at all (.focus() leaves activeElement on BODY) - every fixture gives it one. Its only data attribute is data-popup-open.
5. Base UI wires NO ARIA on this component. Grep of the whole subpath: the only aria-* is the arrow's aria-hidden, the only role is 'presentation'. No aria-haspopup/expanded/controls/describedby. Popup has NO role, tabindex="-1", data-base-ui-focusable. The catalog documents this as pointer chrome rather than pretending the popup is announced; a spec pins it so a future Base UI that adds wiring fails loudly.
6. NO modal prop and NO pointer blocker: the portal's only children are backdrop + positioner, and a real userEvent.click inside the open popup lands in ~45ms (vs Dialog, where it times out).
7. Backdrop carries pointer-events:none INLINE (Popover's carries only user-select:none), so it can NEVER catch a press. Outside-press coverage cannot be driven through it - the spec dispatches pointerdown+click at document.body, and the story clicks ordinary page text. This is the difference from popover.stories.tsx's DismissOnBackdropPress.
8. THE POPUP IS NOT IN THE TAB ORDER AND TAB DISMISSES THE CARD: one Tab from an open card's trigger skips the card's own links entirely, lands on the next control in document order and unmounts the popup. No focus trap (Dialog), no tab-through-then-dismiss trail (Popover). Pinned by a spec.
9. Placement ownership: Positioner owns position:absolute/left/top/--positioner-*/--available-*/--anchor-*/--transform-origin inline; Popup's only inline styles are --popup-width/--popup-height; Arrow gets position:absolute + a side-dependent axis. Recipes must add stacking/paint only (gotcha 7 from Popover confirmed here).
10. Viewport wraps children in Base UI's own <div data-current="true">.
11. Close reasons measured: Escape -> "escape-key", dispatched outside press -> "outside-press", focus-open -> "trigger-focus". defaultOpen does NOT move focus. Blur close is rAF-deferred (popup still present synchronously, gone by +50ms) - every absence assertion uses expect.poll.

NEW GOTCHA FOUND WHILE WRITING THE STORIES (worth propagating to siblings):
  A controlled overlay must NOT be driven by a `setOpen(prev => !prev)` TOGGLE button placed outside it. Pressing the toggle is also an outside press, so Base UI fires onOpenChange(false) and closes the card FIRST; the button's handler then reads the already-false state and flips it straight back to open, so the card looks stuck open on every second press. My Controlled story failed exactly this way and now uses idempotent Open/Close buttons, with the trap documented in the story's doc comment. Any sibling writing a controlled story for a dismissible Base UI overlay will hit this.

CONVENTIONS CONFIRMED FOLLOWED: no `as any`; explicit return types; className narrowed to string on every wrapped part (Base UI widens it to a callback form cn() cannot merge); states as data-[...] modifiers, never cva variants; tokens only from @bc-solutions-coder/styles; class assertions as order-free sets (tailwind-merge reorders); never assert `transform` for rotate-45 (Tailwind v4 emits the individual `rotate` property) - gotcha 9 re-confirmed at v4.3.3; never assert toBeVisible() synchronously after opening (150ms enter transition from opacity-0) - gotcha 6.
