title: Menu on Base UI
description: Add a Menu component to packages/ui, built on @base-ui/react/menu, following the Dialog exemplar shape.
design: Follow the multi-part-popup pattern established by Dialog. Anatomy: Items/CheckboxItem/RadioItem/Separator/SubmenuTrigger (verify full list against https://base-ui.com/react/components/menu). Include a keyboard-navigation behavioral test (arrow keys move active item).
acceptance_criteria: packages/ui/src/components/menu/ ships styles/tsx (covering Items/CheckboxItem/RadioItem/Separator/SubmenuTrigger)/stories/test/index; a keyboard-navigation test passes; typecheck+test green; committed as 'feat(ui): add menu component'.
notes:
RED Wallow-m5aq.3.6 (Menu) — 11 failing (browser 10/28, storybook 1/7). Files:
packages/ui/src/components/menu/{menu.styles.ts,menu.tsx,menu.test.tsx,menu.stories.tsx,index.ts}
plus one append-only line in packages/ui/vitest.config.ts. All staged, NOT committed.

=== 1. MEASURED ANATOMY (probed against @base-ui/react 1.6.0, not docs) ===
Object.keys(Menu) from the real package = 22 members:
  Arrow, Backdrop, CheckboxItem, CheckboxItemIndicator, Group, GroupLabel, Handle, Item,
  LinkItem, Popup, Portal, Positioner, RadioGroup, RadioItem, RadioItemIndicator, Root,
  Separator, SubmenuRoot, SubmenuTrigger, Trigger, Viewport, createHandle
(The scout's "19 + Separator + Handle" reconciles to this; createHandle is the 22nd.)

Rendered tree when open:
  <button>              Trigger      (data-popup-open while open)
  body > portal div     Portal       (structural only)
    > div               Backdrop     — NO inline positioning from Base UI (only user-select),
                                       so `fixed inset-0` MUST come from the recipe.
                                       It is NOT a scrim; a menu does not dim the page.
    > div               Positioner   — Base UI writes inline position/left/top/transform here.
                                       Recipe may only add stacking/focus (z-50 outline-none),
                                       never layout. Mirrors selectPositionerRecipe; this is the
                                       OPPOSITE of Dialog, where the popup owns its own centring.
      > div role=menu   Popup        — owns the card look. Needs `relative` because…
        > div           Arrow        — absolute with an inline `left` but NO `top`, so the
                                       cross-axis offset is the recipe's job. Measured data-side
                                       values: bottom | top | inline-start | inline-end
                                       (logical, NOT left/right).
        > div           Viewport     — wraps content in its own <div data-current> child.
        > div role=group          Group / RadioGroup
        > div role=presentation   GroupLabel (Base UI wires aria-labelledby to the group)
        > div role=menuitem       Item, SubmenuTrigger (aria-haspopup=menu)
        > a   role=menuitem       LinkItem
        > div role=menuitemcheckbox / menuitemradio  CheckboxItem / RadioItem
        > span                    CheckboxItemIndicator / RadioItemIndicator
        > div role=separator      Separator

=== 2. GOTCHAS (measured; these shaped the spec — read before the green phase) ===
G1 PORTAL. Everything except the Trigger renders into document.body, outside the render
   container. All part queries go through document.body (helpers `part()`/`maybePart()`).
G2 POINTER BLOCKER (exemplar gotcha #5, confirmed for Menu). Base UI mounts a fixed
   full-window <div role="presentation" data-base-ui-inert style="position:fixed;inset:0">
   inside the portal, with a clip-path hole punched over the trigger only. vitest/browser's
   userEvent drives real Playwright input, which hit-tests, so a click on anything INSIDE the
   popup times out. The spec therefore drives the menu by KEYBOARD, or calls element.click()
   directly. Storybook's userEvent (@testing-library) does not hit-test and works normally.
G3 DEFERRED UNMOUNT (exemplar gotcha #5 corollary). Closing removes the popup an animation
   frame later. Every ABSENCE assertion uses `await expect.poll(() => maybePart(id)).toBeNull()`,
   never a synchronous expect.
G4 ENTER TRANSITION (exemplar ruling #6). In STORIES, never assert toBeVisible() synchronously
   after opening — every such assertion is wrapped in waitFor().
G5 ASYNC ROVING FOCUS — the one that cost a probe round. Base UI moves focus a tick AFTER each
   arrow key, so consecutive `userEvent.keyboard` calls land on a STALE activeElement (8 rapid
   ArrowDowns left focus parked on item 1 and the following ArrowRight did nothing). The spec
   never sends two keys back to back: helper
     `async function pressKey(key, expectedTestId) { await userEvent.keyboard(key);
        await expect.poll(focusedTestId).toBe(expectedTestId); }`
   polls focus after EVERY key. Keep this shape in ContextMenu/Menubar.
G6 data-starting-style / data-ending-style are unassertable — Base UI strips them within the
   same frame. The transition classes are pinned as CLASS STRINGS only, never as live state.
G7 INDICATORS ARE ABSENT WHILE UNCHECKED. CheckboxItemIndicator/RadioItemIndicator are not in
   the DOM at all until checked. An in-flow indicator would shift the label sideways on every
   toggle, so those two rows use a left GUTTER (`relative pr-2 pl-8`) with `absolute left-2`
   indicators.
G8 tailwind-merge TRAP. `pl-*` does NOT override `px-*`, so the shared item base deliberately
   contains NO px-2 — px-2 is added per-recipe by the three non-gutter rows only. Do not
   "tidy" px-2 into the shared base in the green phase; it will survive next to pl-8.

=== 3. WRAP/UNWRAP RULE (Dialog's rule, applied) ===
A part gets a wrapper + a recipe only if it renders a VISIBLE element. 17 wrapped, 5 exported
UNWRAPPED: Root (renders no DOM and is generic over the trigger Payload — wrapping would drop
the generic), SubmenuRoot (same, one level down), Portal (structural container only; a caller
className still reaches it because the part is re-exported unchanged), Handle (class) and
createHandle (factory) — the imperative open/close API, neither renders anything.
The namespace object therefore mirrors Base UI 1:1 with all 22 keys.
className is narrowed back to `string` on every wrapped part (Base UI widens it to
`string | ((state) => string | undefined)`, and the callback form cannot go through cn()).

=== 4. RECIPES (17) — VERIFIED, not guessed ===
menu.styles.ts ships 17 cva recipes with every base string stubbed `cva("")` and a matching
*RecipeProps VariantProps export. NO recipe takes a cva variant: open/highlighted/checked/
disabled/entering/exiting are STATES that Base UI publishes as data-* attributes, so they live
in the base string as data-[…]: modifiers. The VariantProps exports stay so a later variant axis
is a non-breaking addition.

I temporarily transcribed the real strings, ran BOTH suites (28/28 and 7/7 GREEN), then restored
the stubs — so these are measured to satisfy the specs, and the exemplar's documented risk ("a
story that passes against an EMPTY stub is not proof it passes against the real one — the stub
has no transition") is retired. Transcribe EXACTLY:

  ITEM_BASE (module-private const, composed into 5 recipes — no px-* here, see G8):
    flex cursor-default select-none items-center gap-2 rounded-sm py-1.5 text-sm outline-none
    data-[highlighted]:bg-accent data-[highlighted]:text-accent-foreground data-[disabled]:opacity-50

  menuTriggerRecipe        inline-flex items-center justify-center rounded-md text-sm font-medium transition-colors data-[disabled]:opacity-50
  menuBackdropRecipe       fixed inset-0
  menuPositionerRecipe     z-50 outline-none
  menuPopupRecipe          relative min-w-32 rounded-md border border-border bg-popover p-1 text-popover-foreground shadow-md outline-none transition-all duration-150 data-[starting-style]:scale-95 data-[starting-style]:opacity-0 data-[ending-style]:scale-95 data-[ending-style]:opacity-0
  menuArrowRecipe          size-2.5 rotate-45 rounded-sm border border-border bg-popover data-[side=bottom]:-top-1 data-[side=top]:-bottom-1 data-[side=inline-start]:-right-1 data-[side=inline-end]:-left-1

=== THE LOAD-BEARING DECISION: 17 OF 19 PARTS ARE MENU'S OWN WRAPPERS, REUSED ===
@base-ui/react/context-menu publishes 19 namespace members. Verified against the installed
1.6.0 index.parts.d.ts: only Root and Trigger are context-menu code; the other 17 (Backdrop,
Portal, Positioner, Popup, Arrow, Group, GroupLabel, Item, LinkItem, CheckboxItem,
CheckboxItemIndicator, RadioGroup, RadioItem, RadioItemIndicator, Separator, SubmenuRoot,
SubmenuTrigger) are LITERAL re-exports of @base-ui/react/menu's runtime. So ContextMenu
re-exports the Menu CATALOG component's already-styled wrappers (Menu.Popup etc.) and this
component owns exactly ONE recipe. Per the coordinator's instruction and Menu 3.6's published
"CANONICAL EXPORTS — do NOT re-wrap Base UI".
A spec asserts the reuse by IDENTITY (ContextMenu.Popup === Menu.Popup, x17, plus
Root/Trigger !== Menu's) so a re-wrap cannot creep back in silently.
*** THIS IS THE OPPOSITE CALL TO ALERT DIALOG, ON PURPOSE, AND IT IS DOCUMENTED IN THE FILE. ***
AlertDialog re-wraps Dialog's parts to keep its recipe layer independently themable (an alert
is different chrome from a dialog). A context menu is NOT different chrome from a menu — it is
the same menu card opened from elsewhere, so two identical recipe sets would let them drift.
NOTE for the barrel gate: this subpath has NO Viewport and NO Handle/createHandle (Menu has
both). 19 members is the whole surface.

=== MEASURED ANATOMY (two browser probe rounds against the real package; probe deleted) ===
- Trigger is a plain <div> with NO ARIA AT ALL: no role, no tabindex, no aria-haspopup, no
  aria-expanded, no aria-controls. Open adds exactly data-popup-open + data-pressed. The popup
  has no aria-labelledby. (Reach for Menu when a keyboard-reachable opener is needed.)
- POPUP IS ANCHORED TO THE CURSOR, NOT THE TRIGGER BOX — the defining difference from Menu.
  Positioner is position:fixed with --anchor-width:0px / --anchor-height:0px (zero-size virtual
  anchor at the pointer) where Menu reports the trigger's width and position:absolute. Pinned.
- FOCUS IS NOT RESTORED ON CLOSE. Menu returns focus to its <button> trigger; a context-menu
  trigger is a non-focusable <div>, so activeElement lands on BODY. Deliberately NO
  focus-restore spec — do not add one in green, it will fail for a correct implementation.
- Opening focuses the POPUP itself, not the first row (openContextMenu polls for that).
- ContextMenuRootProps = Menu.Root.Props minus modal/openOnHover/delay/closeDelay, with
  onOpenChange re-typed onto its own reason union. defaultOpen/open/actionsRef all survive.

=== GOTCHAS INHERITED AND CONFIRMED ===
- #5 POINTER BLOCKER: Base UI renders an unstyleable fixed inset-0 div inside the portal (2nd
  portal child) whether or not you render a Backdrop. The browser project loads no Tailwind so
  the popup's z-50 is inert and the blocker covers it -> vitest/browser userEvent.click on
  anything INSIDE the open popup times out on Playwright actionability. In-popup interaction
  goes via KEYBOARD or a direct element.click(); realistic pointer clicks live in the stories
  (@testing-library/user-event does not hit-test).
- #6 ENTER TRANSITION: every toBeVisible() in the stories is wrapped in waitFor (150ms
  opacity-0 enter).
- 3.2 non-event async: every absence assertion and every focus assertion is
  await expect.poll(...), never a bare synchronous read.
- #9 rotate: no assertion anywhere reads .transform.
- NEW, worth carrying: the trigger's ring is a Tailwind BOX-SHADOW, so
  PaintedByTheDesignTokens asserts boxShadow !== "none" (not .outline, not .transform).

Standalone Toggle:      <button type="button" tabindex="0" aria-pressed="false">
  defaultPressed  -> data-pressed="" + aria-pressed="true"

  disabled group -> data-disabled on the group AND data-disabled + aria-disabled="true" + native disabled on every child.
  single mode: click b -> onValueChange(["b"]) and a is released. multiple: click b -> onValueChange(["a","b"]), both stay pressed.

                               to baseUiSubpaths, alphabetical. A sibling agent added "switch" concurrently;
                               both survived, no collision.

=== DECISION: TWO FOLDERS (the bead's "if a separate folder is warranted") ===
checkbox/ and checkbox-group/ are SEPARATE folders. Rationale: package.json's exports map is
"./*" -> "./dist/components/*/index.js", so the folder name IS the public subpath. Two folders make
@bc-solutions-coder/ui/checkbox and @bc-solutions-coder/ui/checkbox-group mirror Base UI's own two
subpaths 1:1, which is the catalog's stated convention. They share NO runtime import — they meet
through Base UI's context — so nothing is coupled by the split. Only the checkbox-group SPEC/STORIES
import Checkbox, because a group is observable only through the boxes it drives.
Radio+RadioGroup (2.6) and Toggle+ToggleGroup (2.12) face the identical choice; recommend they match.

=== EXPORTED SURFACE (what the green phase must keep) ===
checkbox/index.ts:
  Checkbox                       ONE namespace object: { Root, Indicator } (keys mirror Base UI 1:1)
  type CheckboxRootProps         Omit<ComponentProps<typeof BaseCheckbox.Root>,"className"> & CheckboxRootRecipeProps & { readonly className?: string }
  type CheckboxIndicatorProps    same shape for Indicator
  checkboxRootRecipe, type CheckboxRootRecipeProps
  checkboxIndicatorRecipe, type CheckboxIndicatorRecipeProps
checkbox-group/index.ts:
  CheckboxGroup                  SINGLE part, plain component (no namespace — Base UI has no CheckboxGroup.Root)
  type CheckboxGroupProps
  checkboxGroupRecipe, type CheckboxGroupRecipeProps
NOTE: CheckboxRoot/CheckboxIndicator are intentionally NOT exported individually — the convention is
one namespace object. The green phase must not widen this.

=== NO CVA VARIANTS — deliberate, do not "fix" ===
All three recipes are base-string-only, zero variants. A checkbox has no visual variant axis in this
catalog; everything it looks like (ticked/mixed/disabled/read-only) is a STATE that Base UI publishes
as a data-* attribute, so it belongs in the base string as a data-[...]: modifier. VariantProps types
are still exported so the props keep the catalog-wide shape and a later variant is non-breaking.

=== THE EXACT CLASS SETS THE GREEN PHASE MUST PRODUCE (pinned as order-free sets in the specs) ===
checkboxRootRecipe (14):
  inline-flex size-4 shrink-0 items-center justify-center rounded-sm border border-input bg-background
  data-[checked]:border-primary data-[checked]:bg-primary
  data-[indeterminate]:border-primary data-[indeterminate]:bg-primary
  data-[disabled]:opacity-50
checkboxIndicatorRecipe (4):
  flex items-center justify-center text-primary-foreground
checkboxGroupRecipe (4):
  flex flex-col gap-2 data-[disabled]:opacity-50
Every colour utility verified against packages/styles/styles.css @theme: --color-input (border-input),
--color-background (bg-background), --color-primary (bg-primary/border-primary),
--color-primary-foreground (text-primary-foreground), --radius-sm (rounded-sm). No new token needed.
Green phase body per part is the exemplar one-liner:
  <BasePart className={cn(recipe(), className)} {...rest} />   (cn from ../../core/cn)

=== BASE UI 1.6.0 DOM/BEHAVIOUR — MEASURED, NOT GUESSED ===
Wrote a throwaway probe spec that rendered the real Base UI parts and dumped attributes/interactions,
then deleted it. Every assertion in both specs pins an OBSERVED fact:
  • Checkbox.Root renders <span role="checkbox" tabindex="0" aria-checked="false" data-unchecked> and a
    hidden <input type="checkbox" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"> as a SIBLING, not a child. So a
    single checkbox puts TWO element children in `container`; the specs select the root by
    [role="checkbox"], never container.firstElementChild.
  • States: data-checked / data-unchecked / data-indeterminate (+ aria-checked="mixed") /
    data-disabled (+ aria-disabled, tabindex=-1, and disabled on the hidden input) /
    data-readonly (+aria-readonly) / data-required (+aria-required).
  • Indicator is UNMOUNTED while unticked; keepMounted keeps it in the DOM carrying data-unchecked.
    It also carries data-checked when ticked.
  • name/value land on the hidden input, not the root.
  • render prop: className travels to the substituted element; Root defaults to a span so no
    nativeButton={false} is needed (unlike Button).
  • CheckboxGroup renders <div role="group">. disabled stamps data-disabled on the group AND on every
    child box. onValueChange receives (string[], eventDetails) — the WHOLE new array, 2 args.
    onCheckedChange receives (boolean, eventDetails) — 2 args.
  • Controlled `value` with no handler genuinely does not self-update (proved by click test).
  • parent checkbox: data-parent + data-indeterminate + aria-checked="mixed" + aria-controls while only
    some of allValues are ticked; clicking it ticks every child.

=== GOTCHA THAT WILL BITE EVERY OTHER WAVE-1 COMPONENT TASK ===
Tailwind is NOT compiled in the `browser` vitest project (only the `storybook` project attaches the real
Tailwind pipeline, via wallowStyles() in .storybook/main.ts). So a Base UI root span carrying size-4
measures 0x0, Playwright's actionability check never settles, and userEvent.click() TIMES OUT after ~15s
with "waiting for element to be visible, enabled and stable". This is not flake and not a Base UI bug.
Two workarounds, both used here:
  1. drive the KEYBOARD (element.focus() then userEvent.keyboard(" ")) — needs no box, works today;
  2. pass an explicit inline box: style={{ width:16, height:16, display:"inline-block" }} (const TEST_BOX
     in both specs, documented inline). Base UI passes `style` straight through.
Button never hit this because a <button> with text has intrinsic size. Every zero-size Base UI part
(checkbox, radio, switch thumb, slider thumb, toggle) will. Worth a bd memory if the gate agrees.

object literal). It is a regression guard on the multi-part convention, not a red-phase target. All 27

The root barrel packages/ui/src/index.ts does NOT re-export component folders generically; it lists each
component explicitly, and packages/ui/src/index.test.ts asserts the public runtime surface as an EXACT
set (PUBLIC_RUNTIME_EXPORTS, toEqual — not containment) plus a compile-time PublicTypeExports tuple.
So Checkbox/CheckboxGroup are reachable ONLY via their subpaths (@bc-solutions-coder/ui/checkbox) right

This is the SAME class of problem as the dist-structure.test.ts:189 exact-list issue 2.1 already routed

subpath-only, or (b) add them to the root barrel and loosen index.test.ts's exact-set assertion. Do not

description: Add Radio and Radio Group components to packages/ui, built on @base-ui/react/radio (+ radio-group).
design: Follow the COMPONENT-TASK TEMPLATE on this feature's parent bead. Verify anatomy against https://base-ui.com/react/components/radio and .../radio-group.
acceptance_criteria: packages/ui/src/components/radio/ (and radio-group) ships styles/tsx/stories/test/index; typecheck+test green; committed as 'feat(ui): add radio and radio group components'.
notes:

FILES (all new unless noted):
  packages/ui/src/components/radio/radio.styles.ts        scaffold: radioRootRecipe, radioIndicatorRecipe (cva, EMPTY strings)
  packages/ui/src/components/radio/radio.tsx              real prop surface, stub bodies (bare spans), Base UI import is TYPE-ONLY
  packages/ui/src/components/radio/radio.test.tsx         11 specs, all failing
  packages/ui/src/components/radio/radio.stories.tsx      6 stories (5 render + 1 play)
  packages/ui/src/components/radio/index.ts
  packages/ui/src/components/radio-group/radio-group.styles.ts   scaffold: radioGroupRecipe (orientation vertical|horizontal, EMPTY strings) + RadioGroupRecipeProps
  packages/ui/src/components/radio-group/radio-group.tsx         real prop surface, stub body (bare div), TYPE-ONLY Base UI import
  packages/ui/src/components/radio-group/radio-group.test.tsx    9 specs, all failing
  packages/ui/src/components/radio-group/radio-group.stories.tsx 6 stories (5 render + 1 play)
  packages/ui/src/components/radio-group/index.ts
  packages/ui/vitest.config.ts (MODIFIED, append-only): baseUiSubpaths += '@base-ui/react/radio', '@base-ui/react/radio-group', kept alphabetical. recipeRuntime NOT touched (package-wide, already done by 2.1).

TWO FOLDERS, not one — per the bead's own acceptance text ('radio/ (and radio-group)'). Radio is a 2-part namespace; RadioGroup is a single part. radio.test.tsx imports RadioGroup from ../radio-group and radio-group.test.tsx imports Radio from ../radio: a radio is meaningless outside a group, and the pairing is context-based exactly like checkbox/checkbox-group.

ANATOMY — VERIFIED, not guessed. Confirmed against https://base-ui.com/react/components/radio AND by rendering @base-ui/react 1.6.0 in this repo's headless Chromium (throwaway probe.test.tsx, deleted before staging). Parts: radio = Root, Indicator; radio-group = single RadioGroup export (no namespace, no Root). Real DOM:
  <div role=radiogroup [data-disabled|data-readonly|data-required] [aria-disabled/readonly/required]>
    <span role=radio tabindex aria-checked data-unchecked|data-checked [data-composite-item-active when checked] [data-disabled|data-readonly|data-required]>
      <span data-checked>            <- Radio.Indicator
    <input type=radio name value aria-hidden tabindex=-1 [disabled]>
THREE non-obvious facts the green phase must not break:
  1. The hidden <input> is a SIBLING of the root span (child of the group div), NOT a child of the root. Query it with container.querySelector('input'), never within the root.

@base-ui/react/switch exports namespace Switch = { Root, Thumb } - 2 parts, confirmed from index.parts.d.ts.

stateAttributesMapping - so data-checked/data-unchecked/data-disabled/data-readonly/data-required appear on BOTH parts.
That is why the thumb's travel utility (data-[checked]:translate-x-5) can live in the thumb recipe with no parent selector.

=== BLOCKER FOUND (wave-wide, affects EVERY interactive component task) ===
Tailwind's stylesheet is NOT loaded in the vitest BROWSER project. Proven: a <span className="h-6 w-11"> measures
w=0 h=0 there. Consequence for any component whose box comes only from its recipe (switch, checkbox, radio, slider,
toggle - anything with no text): the root is a 0x0 box, and Playwright's actionability check REFUSES to click it, so
`userEvent.click` from "vitest/browser" hangs for the full 15s timeout and fails NO MATTER HOW CORRECT the component is.
Reproduced: probe click timed out with "element is not visible" x32 retries.

  • pointer  -> plain DOM `root.click()`. No actionability gate; React's handler runs. Verified toggles root+thumb to
    data-checked AND fires onCheckedChange(true).
  • keyboard -> `root.focus(); await userEvent.keyboard(" ")`. Verified toggles. Keyboard needs no visibility.
This is the Wave-1 twin of 2.1's optimizeDeps blocker. The exemplar never hit it because a <button> with text has
intrinsic size. Recommend recording as a bd memory once a second component confirms it.

The storybook project DOES load real CSS (4 sheets / 90 rules, --primary resolves to the fork theme) AND its

REAL DOM (measured in the browser project, not guessed):
- Root -> <div>. Group -> <div role="group">. ScrubArea -> <span role="presentation"> + inline touch-action/user-select. Increment/Decrement -> <button type="button" tabindex="-1" aria-label="Increase"/"Decrease" aria-controls="<input id>">. Input -> <input type="text" inputmode="numeric" autocomplete="off" autocorrect="off" spellcheck="false" aria-roledescription="Number field">.
- name= produces a SECOND, hidden <input type="number" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1"> beside the visible text input; that is what carries the value into a form submission (same shape as Switch's hidden checkbox).
- data-disabled / data-readonly / data-required / data-scrubbing land on ALL parts (root, scrub area, group, both buttons, input) via context + the shared stateAttributesMapping. data-filled/dirty/touched/focused do NOT appear outside a Field.Root - do not assert them.

=== THREE MEASURED GOTCHAS (all documented in the spec header) ===
1. STEPPER PRESSES USE DOM button.click(), NOT userEvent.click. Same 0x0/actionability blocker Wallow-m5aq.2.7 found wave-wide. It also happens to be the CORRECT path: Base UI's shouldSkipClick skips clicks with event.detail !== 0 (real pointer clicks, already served by the press-and-hold pointerdown handler). A programmatic click() has detail === 0, so it runs the onClick handler and steps exactly once. Verified: 2 -> inc -> 3 -> dec -> 2, onValueChange reporting 3 then 2.
2. THE VALUE IS NOT READABLE SYNCHRONOUSLY AFTER A STEP. Measured: right after increment.click() the callback had already reported 3 but input.value was still "2", and a second click recomputed from the stale value (calls were [3,1,1] for inc/dec/dec). Every value read in the spec is preceded by `await flush()` (a setTimeout 0 macrotask); with it the sequence is correct ([3,4,3]). Any future spec touching this component needs the same await - this is a real trap.
3. SCRUBAREACURSOR IS NOT IN THE DOM AT REST. It is portaled into document.body and mounted only while isScrubbing && !webkit && !isTouchInput && !isPointerLockDenied. A pointerdown on the scrub area mounts it (with data-scrubbing, role=presentation) and headless Chromium then DENIES the Pointer Lock request asynchronously, unmounting it. Measured: present synchronously and at 5 consecutive ticks, GONE at 60ms. So its recipe is asserted SYNCHRONOUSLY after the pointerdown with no await; scrubbing is ended with a pointerup dispatched on `document`, not the scrub area. Do not add an await to that test.
Also measured: a synthetic pointermove during a scrub changes no value (movementX is 0 without real pointer lock), so the spec asserts data-scrubbing/cursor mount only, never a scrub-driven value change.

Probed empirically against the installed @base-ui/react 1.6.0 with a throwaway spec (deleted).
Base UI's Input is a SINGLE part (confirms the scout) and is literally `Field.Control` underneath:
    export const Input = React.forwardRef((props, ref) => <Field.Control ref={ref} {...props} />)
Consequence — OUTSIDE a Field.Root the ONLY state data-attribute it renders is `data-disabled`:
 • default standalone:  data-testid="p" | id="base-ui-_r_0_"          (no state attrs at all)
 • disabled:            data-disabled="" | disabled="" | id=...
 • after click (focus): NO data-focused
 • after typing:        NO data-filled, NO data-dirty
 • after blur:          NO data-touched
InputDataAttributes.d.ts lists disabled/valid/invalid/touched/dirty/filled/focused, but every one
except `disabled` is documented "(when wrapped in Field.Root)" and that is exactly what happens.
=> This spec asserts `data-disabled` only, on purpose. The Field-context attrs belong to task 2.3,
which owns the @base-ui/react/field subpath — do NOT add field to baseUiSubpaths from this bead.
=> Task 2.3 note: because Input IS Field.Control, wrapping our <Input> in a real Base UI Field.Root
should light up data-valid/invalid/touched/dirty/filled/focused for free, with no change to input.tsx.

   fires with the typed value through Base UI's mergeProps (probe saw "abc").

   all render as expected.

   `nativeButton={false}` equivalent is needed — Input has no such prop and logs no dev-mode error.
 • DELTA vs the pre-rebuild bare <input>: Base UI ALWAYS mints an id when the caller gives none
   (id="base-ui-_r_N_"), so Field.Label can point htmlFor at it. Pinned by its own test
   ("stamps a generated id when the caller supplies none"). Harmless at all 23 call sites; worth
   stating in the commit body.

vitest projects unless the subpath is in that project's optimizeDeps.include. Proven with a

=== THE EXEMPLAR TEST SHAPE (copy this) ===
1. One browser-mode `<name>.test.tsx` per component. No env pragma, no jsdom, NOTHING mocked —
   real Base UI part, real Chromium, real DOM (repo rule + bd memory).
2. Assert the recipe THROUGH the component. Never import the recipe and inspect its return
   value: that passes while the component forgets to apply it.
3. Class assertions are an ORDER-FREE SET, not an exact string:
     function classSet(el: Element) { return [...el.classList].toSorted(); }
     expect(classSet(button)).toEqual([...BASE_CLASSES, ...VARIANT_CLASSES[v]].toSorted());
   tailwind-merge is free to reorder, so exact-string is unstable; set equality is STRICTLY
   STRONGER than per-class contains() — a stray extra utility fails too. Declare BASE_CLASSES
   and a VARIANT_CLASSES record at the top of the file as the single source of truth.
4. Behavioural edges every component spec must cover:
   - state data-attributes Base UI adds (data-disabled here; data-checked/data-open/... elsewhere),
     BOTH present-when-on and absent-when-off;
   - a caller className overriding one recipe utility (className="bg-accent" removes bg-primary
     AND leaves rounded-md/text-primary-foreground alone) — this is the cn()/tailwind-merge proof
     and it is what a string-append implementation fails;
   - Base UI's `render` prop composing onto another element, asserting the recipe TRAVELS to the
     substituted element (render={<a href="/docs" />} nativeButton={false} — pass nativeButton
     when substituting a non-button or Base UI logs a dev-mode error);
   - native attribute + data-testid passthrough;
   - one interaction: `import { userEvent } from "vitest/browser"` (repo convention, matches
     apps/wallow-auth specs), vi.fn() spy, assert the caller's handler still fires through Base
     UI's mergeProps.
   DO NOT userEvent.click a DISABLED element — Playwright waits for actionability and it hangs.
   Assert `.disabled` + `data-disabled` instead.
5. Stories are the VISUAL half of the spec and are written in the RED phase too, because
   @storybook/addon-vitest turns each export into a browser test case. CSF3 (`satisfies
   Meta<typeof X>` + `StoryObj<typeof meta>`), `title: "Components/<Name>"`, callback spies from
   `fn()` in "storybook/test" (never vi.fn() in a story — the addon can only display a Storybook
   spy), play() uses the `canvas` from the play context. One story per variant + each state +

title: preserveModules build + wildcard subpath exports

preserveModulesRoot: 'src',

description: Rebuild the overlays wave: Dialog (EXEMPLAR for multi-part popups, full treatment like Wave 1's Button), Alert Dialog, Popover, Tooltip, Preview Card, Menu, Context Menu, Menubar, Navigation Menu, Drawer, Toast. Ends with a wave gate.

Dialog anatomy: Root/Trigger/Portal/Backdrop/Popup/Title/Description/Close. Recipes: backdrop (bg-foreground/50-style overlay), popup (bg-popover text-popover-foreground rounded-lg border border-border shadow-lg + open/close transition using Base UI's data-open/data-starting-style/data-ending-style attributes). notes:
SCOUT (Wave 2 overlays) — measured against installed @base-ui/react 1.6.0 in node_modules/.pnpm, not docs.

=== 1. ANATOMY PER COMPONENT (task descriptions are stale where noted) ===
All read from <pkg>/index.d.ts + index.parts.d.ts.

- Dialog (3.1): Root/Trigger/Portal/Backdrop/Popup/Title/Description/Close/**Viewport** + Handle/createHandle (store). Task desc omits Viewport (a positioning/scroll container between Popup and content) and Handle — both are real 1.6.0 parts; verified via dialog/index.parts.d.ts.
- AlertDialog (3.2): Root, Trigger are AlertDialog-specific. Backdrop/Close/Description/Popup/Portal/Title/Viewport are LITERALLY Dialog's own runtime components re-exported unchanged (alert-dialog/index.parts.d.ts: `export { DialogBackdrop as Backdrop } from "../dialog/backdrop/DialogBackdrop.js"` etc, for all 7). No Action/Cancel part exists — action buttons are caller-composed (hence task's buttonRecipe hint, for story/consumer code, not the component impl).
- Popover (3.3): Root/Trigger/Portal/Positioner/Popup/Arrow/Backdrop/Title/Description/Close/Viewport + Handle.
- Tooltip (3.4): Provider/Root/Trigger/Portal/Positioner/Popup/Viewport/Arrow + Handle. No Backdrop/Title/Description/Close (non-modal, no dismiss chrome). Provider carries delay props per task desc.
- PreviewCard (3.5): Root/Trigger/Portal/Positioner/Popup/Arrow/Viewport/Backdrop + Handle.
- Menu (3.6): 19 parts — Root/Trigger/Portal/Positioner/Popup/Backdrop/Arrow/Viewport/Group/GroupLabel/Item/LinkItem/CheckboxItem/CheckboxItemIndicator/RadioGroup/RadioItem/RadioItemIndicator/SubmenuRoot/SubmenuTrigger, plus `Separator` (a SHARED part imported from `../separator/Separator.js` — not menu-owned) + Handle.
- ContextMenu (3.7): Root, Trigger are ContextMenu-specific (trigger is right-click/long-press, not click). EVERY other part (Backdrop/Portal/Positioner/Popup/Arrow/Group/GroupLabel/Item/CheckboxItem/CheckboxItemIndicator/LinkItem/RadioGroup/RadioItem/RadioItemIndicator/SubmenuRoot/SubmenuTrigger/Separator) is Menu's own runtime component re-exported unchanged — same reuse shape as AlertDialog/Dialog.
- Menubar (3.8): SINGLE part, `export { Menubar } from "./Menubar.js"` — no namespace, no sub-parts, renders one <div>. Read Menubar.mjs: it is a bare composite-root container (orientation/modal/loopFocus/disabled props, `data-has-submenu-open`); a real menubar UI is built by nesting several independent `Menu.Root` trees inside it (each Menu's Trigger becomes a menubar item) — i.e. 3.8's component should literally reuse 3.6's Menu wrapper for the nested menus, wrapped by a thin Wallow `Menubar` (menubar.styles.ts recipe on the one <div>).
- NavigationMenu (3.9): Root/Trigger/Portal/Positioner/Viewport/List/Item/Content/Popup/Backdrop/Arrow/Link/Icon + Handle.
- Drawer (3.10): Root/Provider/Indent/IndentBackground/Trigger/Portal/Popup/SwipeArea/Content/Backdrop/Viewport/Title/Description/Close/VirtualKeyboardProvider + Handle. Task desc's "Drawer.VirtualKeyboardProvider" confirmed real.
- Toast (3.11): Root/Provider/Viewport/Content/Description/Title/Close/Action/Portal/Positioner/Arrow + `useToastManager()` (hook) + `createToastManager()` (standalone manager factory, for use outside React e.g. app-wide singleton) + Handle. useToastManager returns {toasts, add, close, update, promise}; createToastManager returns the same 4 methods plus an internal ' subscribe'. Both must be re-exported per the task's acceptance.

Every component above also exports a `Handle`/`createHandle` pair (imperative open/close/unmount API) not mentioned in any task description — worth a deliberate include/skip decision per task, not an oversight if skipped, but note it explicitly in the report either way.

=== 2. PORTAL + TEST-HARNESS INTERACTION ===
- Confirmed via dialog/portal/DialogPortal.mjs: portal wraps Floating UI's `FloatingPortal`, which by default appends to `document.body` (no `container` prop given). This is universal across ALL overlay Portals (Dialog/AlertDialog/Popover/Tooltip/PreviewCard/Menu/ContextMenu/NavigationMenu/Drawer/Toast) — they all use the same FloatingPortal.
- EXISTING PRECEDENT to copy directly: packages/ui/src/components/select/select.test.tsx already solves this exact portal-querying problem (Select.Popup portals to body). Copy its pattern:
  - `part(testId)` helper: `document.body.querySelector('[data-testid="..."]')`, asserts non-null, returns HTMLElement — use for required portalled parts.
  - `maybePart(testId)`: same but returns null instead of asserting — use for parts that are legitimately absent (e.g. unmounted-while-closed).
  - Header comment block documents the anatomy AND explicitly states "every open-state query goes through document.body, never through render's container" — copy this doc convention into every Wave-2 test file.
  - Nothing under `*.Portal` exists in the DOM AT ALL while closed (not hidden — absent), same as Select.
- vitest BROWSER project loads NO Tailwind stylesheet (memory packages-ui-vitest-browser-project-loads-no-tailwind) — class-attribute assertions only, never computed-style/visibility assertions, in .test.tsx files. Storybook project DOES load real CSS (per 2.14 gate note) so visual/computed-style checks belong in stories, not specs.
- ANIMATION/UNMOUNT TIMING GOTCHA (generalizes the 2.4 Form/Field.Error rAF finding to EVERY overlay in this wave): read utils/popupStateMapping.mjs + internals/stateAttributesMapping.mjs — ALL overlay Popups share one mechanism: `data-open`/`data-closed` on Popup, `data-popup-open` on Trigger, `data-starting-style`/`data-ending-style` during transitions, and actual DOM unmount is gated behind `useOpenChangeComplete` -> `useAnimationsFinished` (>=1 rAF + 1 microtask after the state flips), even with zero CSS/animations loaded (confirmed directly in DialogPopup.mjs's `useOpenChangeComplete` call, same primitive 2.4 traced in FieldError.mjs). CONSEQUENCE: any "close on Escape" / "close on outside click" spec asserting the popup/backdrop is GONE must use `await expect.poll(() => maybePart('...')).toBeNull()`, never a bare synchronous `expect(...).toBeNull()` — copy the exact pattern already landed at packages/ui/src/components/form/form.test.tsx:321 (the only existing use of expect.poll in this package). Storybook play-fn assertions (`await expect(...).not.toBeInTheDocument()`) already retry so are unaffected.
- OPEN-state assertions (element present) do not have this problem — `mounted` flips synchronously on open, only the CLOSE/unmount path is deferred.

=== 3. WAVE-1 REUSE ===
- buttonRecipe (packages/ui/src/components/button/button.styles.ts, subpath-only export) — AlertDialog's story/consumer code should compose real Wallow `Button` (not just the recipe) for Confirm/Cancel actions, per task 3.2's explicit hint; there is no Base UI Action/Cancel part.
- Given point 1's reuse findings: AlertDialog's OWN wrapper (alert-dialog.tsx) should import and reuse Dialog's already-wrapped Backdrop/Popup/Title/Description/Close/Portal/Viewport functions from '../dialog/dialog' (they wrap the IDENTICAL underlying Base UI component) rather than re-wrapping them — only Root/Trigger need new wrapper functions + recipes. Same for ContextMenu reusing Menu's wrapper functions for everything except Root/Trigger. This is deliberate cross-component reuse per the coordinator's brief, backed by Base UI's own re-export structure, not just recipe sharing.
- Menubar (3.8) should reuse Menu's (3.6) Root/Trigger/Popup/etc wrapper for the nested per-item menus, per point 1's Menubar finding.
- No Wave-1 recipes fit backdrop/popup styling (those are new overlay-specific recipes); Dialog is the template every later overlay recipe file should structurally match (backdrop + popup recipes using data-open/data-starting-style/data-ending-style variants, per the feature's own DESIGN section).

=== 4. baseUiSubpaths ===
Correction to the assignment brief: there is only ONE `baseUiSubpaths` array in packages/ui/vitest.config.ts (not separate browser/storybook lists) — it feeds BOTH the `browser` project's `optimizeDeps.include` (via `extraBrowserOptimizeDeps`) AND the `storybook` project's `optimizeDeps.include` from the same constant. One append serves both.

(insert each in correct alphabetical position, not just appended — the file's own comment says "EVERY component task ... must append its own subpath here as it lands", i.e. do it per-task, unlike the barrel — this array is NOT one of the 3 coupled exact-set files, so no gate deferral needed for it.)

=== 3.12/GATE PROTOCOL — CRITICAL, applies wave-wide ===
Read src/core/package-scaffold.test.ts's own comment (~line 285) plus the 2.14 gate's resolution: `COMPONENT_FOLDERS`, `src/index.ts` (root barrel), and `src/index.test.ts` (PUBLIC_RUNTIME_EXPORTS + PublicTypeExports) are THREE FILES THAT MOVE TOGETHER AS ONE UNIT because each asserts an EXACT set. Gate 2.14 ALSO settled that the destination is barrel+subpath (option a) — so 3.12 should plan to add all Wave-2 components to the root barrel too, exactly like 2.14 did for Wave 1's 25 folders. Individual Wave-2 tasks: do NOT edit package-scaffold.test.ts, src/index.ts, or src/index.test.ts — leave that to 3.12.

title: Rebuild @bc-solutions-coder/ui as a 37-component Base UI + CVA catalog
description: Rebuild packages/ui (@bc-solutions-coder/ui) from an 11-component flat catalog into a full 37-component Base UI (@base-ui/react ^1.6.0) catalog: headless Base UI parts wrapped in namespaced styled components (e.g. Dialog.Root, Dialog.Popup), CVA (class-variance-authority + tailwind-merge) recipes over the existing semantic Tailwind tokens from @bc-solutions-coder/styles, one folder per component under src/components/<name>/, per-component subpath exports (@bc-solutions-coder/ui/button) via a Vite preserveModules build alongside the root barrel, Storybook 10 (@storybook/react-vite + @storybook/addon-vitest) as both the component explorer and the render/interaction test suite, then a full sweep of both apps/wallow-auth and apps/wallow-web onto the new primitives. Source plan: docs/plans/2026-07-27/0932-base-ui-component-library-plan.md; design: docs/plans/2026-07-27/0930-base-ui-component-library-design.md (both restated in child beads — not required reading).
design:
Architecture decisions (pre-approved by the user):
- Layering: src/core/ (layer0, cn.ts + types.ts, imports nothing internal) -> src/components/<name>/ (layer1: <name>.tsx, <name>.styles.ts CVA-only/no-JSX, <name>.stories.tsx, <name>.test.tsx, index.ts) -> src/index.ts (layer2 barrel importing every folder). core never imports components; only root index.ts imports everything; cross-component imports only for deliberate reuse (e.g. AlertDialog reusing the button recipe).
- Styling: CVA recipes call ONLY semantic Tailwind utilities already in @bc-solutions-coder/styles (bg-primary, text-muted-foreground, rounded-md, border-border...). Missing token -> add to packages/styles first, never hardcode.
- Every styled part = a real Base UI headless part (import from its own subpath, e.g. @base-ui/react/dialog) wrapped with cn(recipe(...), className) + full prop passthrough incl. Base UI's render prop. Multi-part components export ONE namespace object mirroring Base UI's exact part names (export const Dialog = { Root, Trigger, Portal, Backdrop, Popup, Title, Description, Close }).
- Build: Vite lib mode, rollupOptions.output.preserveModules=true / preserveModulesRoot='src' -> dist/ mirrors src/ 1:1. package.json exports: '.' -> dist/index.js, './*' -> dist/components/*/index.js (types dist/components/*/index.d.ts), './source.css' passthrough. sideEffects:false.
- Test model: Storybook stories (@storybook/addon-vitest, real Chromium, vitest 'storybook' project) ARE render/interaction coverage. *.test.tsx covers ONLY behavioral edges stories can't express.
- No-mocking policy: ui's tests never mock anything; apps must never mock @bc-solutions-coder/ui either.
- Compat guarantee: the 11 existing exports (Button, Input, Label, Field, Card, ErrorBanner, MutedText, CenteredCardLayout, ForkAttribution, DocumentStyles, FocusOnNavigate, ReadyIndicator incl. READY_ATTRIBUTE) keep names/import paths/prop contracts throughout; both apps must keep compiling at every step.
- Verify each component's real Base UI part list against https://base-ui.com/react/components/<name> at implementation time — do not guess anatomy.
- Repo rules binding every task: Conventional Commits (feat(ui): ..., CLAUDE.md -> Versioning); real Chromium only for frontend tests, never jsdom (.claude/rules/TESTING.md); quality gate is 'pnpm check' (format:check+lint+typecheck+test+build); run package-scoped commands as 'pnpm --filter @bc-solutions-coder/ui <script>'.
acceptance_criteria: All 37 Base UI catalog components ship under packages/ui/src/components/<name>/ with recipe+stories+tests+index; root barrel (src/index.ts) exports all of them; per-component subpath imports resolve (@bc-solutions-coder/ui/<name>); 'pnpm check' is green at the repo root; both apps/wallow-auth and apps/wallow-web are fully swept onto the new primitives with zero hand-rolled equivalents remaining and every existing data-testid preserved; per-app E2E suites plus the cross-app journey suite (./scripts/e2e.sh, test:e2e, test:e2e:cross-app) are green; packages/ui/CLAUDE.md and .claude/rules/TESTING.md document the new conventions; plan+design docs marked status: completed and archived per CLAUDE.md; work is committed with Conventional Commits and pushed.

title: Sidebar: rework DashboardNav/DashboardLayout into expanded/rail/mobile-overlay modes
description: Using the decoupled state model and icon set from the state-model task, rework apps/wallow-web/src/components/DashboardNav.tsx and apps/wallow-web/src/components/DashboardLayout.tsx to render the three modes described on the parent feature bead (Wallow-0byr): expanded desktop (icon+label, current default), collapsed icon-rail desktop (icon-only with accessible name, toggle-only, no clipped text), and mobile overlay drawer (rail absent below the responsive breakpoint, menu button opens a full-content overlay with backdrop that closes on backdrop click / nav-link click / Escape key). Preserve existing data-testid attributes (dashboard-nav, dashboard-nav-<feature>, dashboard-nav-toggle, dashboard-nav-backdrop, dashboard-logout-link) and kebab-case {page}-{element} convention, adding new ones as needed for new controls (e.g. a mobile menu button distinct from the desktop collapse toggle, if they end up as separate controls).
design: Today's linkClass/aside/nav/button structure in DashboardNav.tsx and the NavToggle/NavBackdrop pair in DashboardLayout.tsx are the starting point — reuse their Tailwind v4 token classes (bg-foreground, text-background, etc. from @bc-solutions-coder/styles) rather than inventing new ones. Use a Tailwind responsive breakpoint (e.g. md:) to switch between the mobile-drawer rendering and the desktop rail rendering — this app has no responsive classes anywhere yet, so this is the first use of a breakpoint prefix in apps/wallow-web. Escape-to-close needs a keydown listener scoped to when the mobile drawer is open (add/remove on mount/unmount or via an effect keyed on the open state). isAdmin-gated Organizations link behavior (props.isAdmin !== false hides only when explicitly false) must be preserved unchanged in every mode.
acceptance_criteria:
- Desktop collapsed rail renders icon-only nav items with an accessible name (aria-label or visually-hidden text) — no visible or clipped text nodes.
- Desktop toggle switches expanded <-> collapsed only (the two ONLY desktop states); active-route highlighting works in both.
- Below the responsive breakpoint the icon rail is entirely absent (not just visually hidden/zero-width) and a menu button opens a full expanded-content overlay drawer with a backdrop.
- The mobile drawer closes on backdrop click, on clicking any nav link, and on pressing Escape.
- All nav destinations (Organizations when admin, Apps, Settings, Inquiries, Sign Out) stay reachable and keep accessible names in every mode.
- 'pnpm lint' passes (oxlint react/jsx-max-depth max 2 on apps/ — keep NavToggle/NavBackdrop-style component extraction if depth would otherwise be exceeded).
notes:
RED (TDD red phase complete) — 18 tests failing for the right reason. 23 tests in 2 NEW browser-mode spec files (17 fail / 6 pass structurally) plus 1 retargeted case in DashboardLayout.toggle.test.tsx. 0 import/syntax errors, tsc --noEmit CLEAN, oxlint exit 0. Every OTHER pre-existing dashboard assertion still passes (23/24 in those 5 files).

=== CRITICAL ENVIRONMENT FINDING (verified in real Chromium, affects every dashboard spec) ===
Vitest browser mode's DEFAULT viewport is 414x896 — a PHONE, BELOW Tailwind's md breakpoint (48rem/768px). Probed: default innerWidth=414, matchMedia('(min-width: 48rem)').matches=FALSE. Every existing dashboard component spec has therefore been running at mobile width all along. The moment .2 makes the nav viewport-aware, DashboardNav.test.tsx/.gate/.toggle and DashboardLayout.test.tsx/.toggle would ALL break for a reason unrelated to what they assert.
ALSO VERIFIED: page.viewport(w,h) DOES drive matchMedia inside the test iframe (1280 -> md=true, 390 -> md=false), so it is a usable mobile/desktop switch and needs no CSS.
MITIGATION APPLIED: all 5 pre-existing dashboard specs now pin `await page.viewport(1280, 800)` in beforeEach (plus reset isMobileNavOpen). No assertion in any of them was changed by this.
ALTERNATIVE GREEN MAY PREFER: set a desktop `browser.viewport` default in apps/wallow-web/vitest.config.ts (or the shared preset) and drop the per-spec desktop calls; the mobile spec would keep its own. Left as green's call — the explicit per-spec form states intent and touches no shared config.

=== TEST FILES ===
NEW  apps/wallow-web/src/components/DashboardNav.modes.test.tsx — 12 tests, 3 describes. DESKTOP ONLY (viewport 1280x800). Renders <DashboardNav/> directly.
NEW  apps/wallow-web/src/components/DashboardLayout.mobile.test.tsx — 11 tests, 2 describes. MOBILE ONLY (viewport 390x844). Renders <DashboardLayout/> (NOT DashboardNav) on purpose: the drawer, its backdrop and the button that opens them are one behaviour split across shell and nav, so the spec must not care which component owns which node. Green is free to place them either side.
MOD  DashboardNav.test.tsx, DashboardNav.gate.test.tsx, DashboardNav.toggle.test.tsx, DashboardLayout.test.tsx — viewport pin only, zero assertion changes.
MOD  DashboardLayout.toggle.test.tsx — viewport pin PLUS the backdrop retarget (see CONTRACT CHANGE below).
NOT touched: DashboardNav.tsx, DashboardLayout.tsx, ui-store.ts, nav-icons.ts — no scaffolding was needed; the new specs assert on DOM/testids only, so they compile and fail on assertions, never on imports.

=== TESTIDS ===
PRESERVED unchanged: dashboard-nav (aside id + testid), dashboard-nav-organizations|apps|settings|inquiries, dashboard-logout-link, dashboard-nav-toggle, dashboard-nav-backdrop, dashboard-welcome.
NEW (kebab {page}-{element}):
  dashboard-nav-mobile-menu — the MOBILE menu button. Distinct from dashboard-nav-toggle deliberately: they are different controls on different axes and are never on screen together. Contract: aria-label="Open navigation" (= navIconLabels.mobileMenu), aria-expanded reflecting isMobileNavOpen.
  dashboard-nav-drawer — the mobile overlay sheet. Present ONLY while isMobileNavOpen.

=== CONTRACT CHANGE GREEN MUST IMPLEMENT: the backdrop moves to the MOBILE axis ===
dashboard-nav-backdrop is KEPT but re-homed. Today it renders on DESKTOP whenever the rail is expanded, dimming the whole main column behind a persistent sidebar and dismissing it on click — that is overlay behaviour, and under the three-mode model the overlay is the phone drawer, not the rail. So: NO backdrop at desktop width in EITHER rail state; backdrop present exactly while the mobile drawer is open, wired to closeMobileNav, keeping aria-label="Close navigation".
Consequently DashboardLayout.toggle.test.tsx's two desktop-backdrop cases were retargeted, NOT deleted or weakened: "renders a backdrop while the drawer is open" -> "renders no backdrop while the rail is expanded either", and "closes the drawer when the backdrop is activated" -> "renders no mobile menu button at desktop width". Every backdrop behaviour they used to assert (exists when the overlay is open, dismisses it on click, carries an accessible name) is now asserted in DashboardLayout.mobile.test.tsx against the mobile drawer. Net coverage is equal or higher; nothing was skipped.

=== KEY DESIGN DECISION FORCED BY THE TEST ENVIRONMENT: aria-label, NOT sr-only ===
The acceptance criterion allows "aria-label OR visually-hidden text". Browser-mode specs load NO stylesheet, so an sr-only span and the clipped label this epic is about are INDISTINGUISHABLE from the DOM — there is no assertion that can tell a deliberate icon rail from the bug if the text node is present either way. The specs therefore pin the aria-label form: in the collapsed rail every item's trimmed textContent MUST be "" and its accessible name MUST come from aria-label. GREEN MUST NOT use sr-only spans for the collapsed rail. (This also matches .1's handoff note: icons aria-hidden, name from navIconLabels.)

=== WHAT EACH TEST ASSERTS ===
DashboardNav.modes.test.tsx — "expanded rail (desktop)" (isNavCollapsed=false):
 1 reports itself expanded (data-nav-open="true")                                    [PASSES today]
 2 renders an icon for every nav item — each of the 5 items contains an <svg>         [FAILS]
 3 renders the visible label alongside every icon (toHaveTextContent)                 [PASSES today]
 4 highlights the active route — active item's className differs from an inactive sibling's [FAILS]
"collapsed icon rail (desktop)" (isNavCollapsed=true):
 5 reports itself collapsed (data-nav-open="false")                                   [PASSES today]
 6 renders an icon for every nav item                                                 [FAILS]
 7 renders NO text node for any nav item (trimmed textContent === "") — THE EPIC BUG  [FAILS: got 'Organizations']
 8 names every icon-only item with aria-label = its label                             [FAILS]
 9 every destination reachable by accessible name (getByRole link/button)             [PASSES today]
10 highlights the active route (collapsed too)                                        [FAILS]
"desktop toggle":
11 toggling drops the labels and toggling back restores them (both directions)        [FAILS]
12 the rail stays MOUNTED with id="dashboard-nav" in both states (aria-controls target survives) [PASSES today]
DashboardLayout.mobile.test.tsx — "below the breakpoint" (390x844):
13 renders NO dashboard-nav rail — absent from the DOM, not narrowed/hidden           [FAILS]
14 renders NO dashboard-nav-toggle (nothing to collapse on a phone)                   [FAILS]
15 renders dashboard-nav-mobile-menu with aria-label="Open navigation", aria-expanded="false" [FAILS]
16 renders neither drawer nor backdrop while closed                                   [FAILS]
"mobile drawer":
17 clicking the menu button opens dashboard-nav-drawer + dashboard-nav-backdrop, sets aria-expanded="true" and isMobileNavOpen=true [FAILS]
18 the drawer shows every destination with its FULL label (it is expanded content, not a rail) [FAILS]
19 the backdrop carries aria-label="Close navigation"                                 [PASSES today]
20 backdrop click closes the drawer (node gone + isMobileNavOpen=false)                [FAILS]
21 nav-link click closes the drawer                                                    [FAILS]
22 Escape closes the drawer                                                            [FAILS]
23 dismissing the drawer leaves isNavCollapsed=false — cross-axis guard at the RENDER level [FAILS]

=== THE 6 PASSES ARE STRUCTURAL, NOT VACUOUS ===
#1/#5 data-nav-open is already wired by .1. #3 labels already render — this test is the guard against green over-correcting to icon-only in EVERY mode. #9 currently satisfied by the visible text; it becomes load-bearing the instant #7 removes that text and the name must come from aria-label. #12 pins that collapsing stays presentational. #19 the current desktop backdrop happens to carry the same aria-label; it becomes load-bearing once the backdrop moves to the mobile axis. None of them can stay green if green does the wrong thing on its paired failing test.

=== HOW THE SPECS SIMULATE A MOBILE VIEWPORT ===
`await page.viewport(390, 844)` in beforeEach (desktop specs use 1280x800). No CSS is involved and no media-query mock is used — real Chromium re-evaluates matchMedia when the iframe resizes, which is why this works and why it is the honest simulation. Green's component must therefore read the breakpoint at RUNTIME (window.matchMedia('(min-width: 48rem)') + a change listener, or an equivalent hook) — a pure Tailwind `hidden md:flex` cannot satisfy #13/#14, which require the rail to be ABSENT from the DOM, and that is deliberate per the acceptance criteria.

=== LINK STUB NOTE FOR GREEN ===
Both new specs stub @tanstack/react-router's Link as an anchor that (a) preventDefault()s so a click cannot navigate the test iframe, and (b) in modes.test.tsx applies activeProps.className when `to` matches a spec-controlled active path. So green must pass active styling to Link via `activeProps` (TanStack's own mechanism) for #4/#10. Because the stub still lets the click bubble, #21 passes whether green wires the close on the Link's onClick or on a container above it.

=== RUN EVIDENCE ===
pnpm exec vitest run --project browser src/components/DashboardNav.modes.test.tsx src/components/DashboardLayout.mobile.test.tsx
  -> Test Files 2 failed (2); Tests 17 failed | 6 passed (23). All 17 are assertion/timeout-on-absent-element failures; zero import, syntax or type errors.
The 5 pre-existing dashboard specs, re-run after the viewport pins + backdrop retarget:
  -> Test Files 1 failed | 4 passed (5); Tests 1 failed | 23 passed (24). The ONE failure is the deliberately-retargeted "renders no backdrop while the rail is expanded either" — red because DashboardLayout still renders the desktop backdrop, which is exactly what green removes. Nothing else in those files regressed, so the viewport pins are behaviour-neutral as claimed.
TOTAL RED FOR GREEN TO CLEAR: 18 tests.
pnpm --filter @bc-solutions-coder/wallow-web typecheck -> tsc --noEmit CLEAN, 0 errors.
pnpm exec oxlint apps/wallow-web/src/components --deny-warnings -> exit 0 (jsx-max-depth budget respected; the Link stubs are depth 1).
oxfmt --write applied to all 7 touched spec files.

=== SCOPE NOTE FOR .3 ===
These are the core acceptance-driving specs, not exhaustive edge cases. Left for .3: focus management/focus trap in the open drawer, body-scroll lock, drawer behaviour across a live viewport RESIZE (desktop -> mobile with the rail collapsed, and back), keyboard activation of the toggles, and the isAdmin gate re-checked inside the mobile drawer (the gate is currently only covered on the desktop rail by DashboardNav.gate.test.tsx).
GREEN (TDD green complete) — all 23 tests in the two new mode specs pass; no test file was edited.

FILES
MOD apps/wallow-web/src/components/DashboardNav.tsx — rewritten into rail + drawer.
MOD apps/wallow-web/src/components/DashboardLayout.tsx — two width-exclusive controls + mobile backdrop.
NEW apps/wallow-web/src/lib/use-is-desktop.ts — useIsDesktop(), the runtime breakpoint subscription.
NOT touched: ui-store.ts, nav-icons.ts (both taken as-is from .1), and every *.test.* file.

COMPONENT STRUCTURE (DashboardNav.tsx, top to bottom)
  interface NavDestination { to: LinkProps['to']; testid: string; icon: NavIconName }
  const destinations — the 4 Links as DATA, so the rail and the drawer cannot drift.
  NavItem            — one Link: <Icon aria-hidden/> + label text only when showLabel.
                       aria-label is set in EVERY mode from navIconLabels (harmless when the
                       text is also present, load-bearing when it is not). activeProps=
                       {{className: activeItemClass}} is passed unconditionally, which is what
                       makes the active highlight work in BOTH desktop states (tests #4/#10).
  NavDestinationList — <nav> over `destinations`, props {showOrganizations, showLabels, onNavigate}.
  NavLogout          — <div><button data-testid=dashboard-logout-link>, same icon/label/aria rules.
  NavRail            — <aside id=dashboard-nav data-nav-open> w-16 / data-[nav-open=true]:w-64,
                       showLabels={!isNavCollapsed}. `overflow-x-hidden` DELETED: it was the
                       mechanism that turned the labels into 'Settin'/'Sign O', and with no text
                       to clip it would only mask a future regression.
  NavDrawer          — <div id/data-testid=dashboard-nav-drawer> fixed inset-y-0 left-0 z-30 w-64,
                       showLabels always, onNavigate={closeMobileNav}.
  DashboardNav       — useIsDesktop(); desktop -> <NavRail/>; mobile -> drawer when open else null.
                       Owns the Escape effect (it owns the drawer). The listener is registered
                       unconditionally and keyed on [isMobileNavOpen, closeMobileNav], testing the
                       flag INSIDE the handler, so the effect has a single exit path — an early
                       `return` before the cleanup trips oxlint's consistent-return.

DashboardLayout.tsx: NavToggle (desktop only, now icon-only: aria-label='Toggle navigation',
aria-controls/aria-expanded unchanged), MobileMenuButton (mobile only, data-testid=
dashboard-nav-mobile-menu, aria-label='Open navigation', aria-expanded=isMobileNavOpen,
aria-controls=dashboard-nav-drawer, click toggles open/close), NavBackdrop (RE-HOMED to the mobile
axis exactly as the red report specified: rendered only while !isDesktop && isMobileNavOpen, wired
to closeMobileNav, aria-label from navIconLabels.close = 'Close navigation', fixed inset-0 z-20).
The shell renders `{isDesktop ? <NavToggle/> : <MobileMenuButton/>}` — the two controls are
mutually exclusive by construction, which is what test #14 and the retargeted 'no mobile menu
button at desktop width' assert from opposite sides.

WHY A RUNTIME MEDIA QUERY, NOT `md:` (the red report called this out and it held)
useIsDesktop = useSyncExternalStore over matchMedia('(min-width: 48rem)') with a change listener.
Tests #13/#14 require the rail and the desktop toggle to be ABSENT from the DOM on a phone, which
a `hidden md:flex` cannot do. getServerSnapshot() returns true (desktop = the dashboard's primary
form factor); useSyncExternalStore re-reads the live query in the first client render, so a phone
corrects itself after hydration instead of mismatching. 48rem is Tailwind v4's default md and
packages/styles overrides no breakpoints, so the string and the `md:` prefix stay one boundary.

I kept the red phase's per-spec `await page.viewport(...)` pins rather than setting a desktop
default in vitest.config.ts — the explicit form states each spec's intent, and changing the shared
default would silently re-point wallow-auth's specs too.

DECISIONS WORTH KNOWING
- aria-label form (never sr-only) for the collapsed rail, per the red report. Collapsed items have
  textContent === '' and take their name from aria-label.
- oxlint react/jsx-max-depth (max 2) is why NavItem/NavDestinationList/NavLogout are separate
  components: <aside> > <nav> > <Link> > <Icon/> would be depth 3. The list-as-a-component split
  also gives the drawer the rail's exact contents for free.
- `to` is typed LinkProps['to'], NOT string — hoisting the links into a data array with a plain
  `string` would fail tsc against the generated route tree. Verified: tsc --noEmit clean.
- Known cosmetic noise, not a failure: DashboardLayout.mobile.test.tsx's Link stub does not
  destructure activeProps, so React logs 'does not recognize the activeProps prop' for the drawer's
  anchors. It is the stub spreading an unknown prop onto <a>; no assertion touches it and I did not
  edit the spec to silence it.

TEST_STATUS (full wallow-web suite, pnpm exec vitest run)
  83 files / 540 tests -> 1 failed | 539 passed.
  The single failure is the known out-of-scope Wallow-jx7f: src/routes/__root.branding.test.tsx >
  'omits the /client.css stylesheet link in dev'. Nothing else in the suite fails.
  New specs alone: DashboardNav.modes.test.tsx (12) + DashboardLayout.mobile.test.tsx (11) = 23/23.
GATES: pnpm --filter @bc-solutions-coder/wallow-web typecheck CLEAN. oxlint apps packages
--deny-warnings exit 0 (fixed one consistent-type-definitions warning: NavDestination is an
interface). oxfmt applied to all 3 files; repo-wide format:check now flags only the known
out-of-scope Wallow-hjhd (apps/wallow-web/README.md).
ISSUES=none. Files staged, NOT committed.
VERIFY: [✓] Desktop collapsed rail icon-only w/ accessible name, no clipped/visible text — DashboardNav.tsx:59-64,72-91 iconOnlyItemClass + aria-label from navIconLabels + label rendered only when showLabel; DashboardNav.modes.test.tsx #6-9 pass (trimmed textContent==='' + aria-label match + reachable by role). [✓] Desktop toggle switches only expanded<->collapsed, active highlight works both — NavToggle (DashboardLayout.tsx:42-59) calls only toggleNavCollapsed; activeProps={{className:activeItemClass}} applied unconditionally on every Link (DashboardNav.tsx:85); modes.test #4/#10/#11/#12 pass. [✓] Below breakpoint rail entirely absent (not CSS-hidden), menu opens full drawer+backdrop — useIsDesktop() (apps/wallow-web/src/lib/use-is-desktop.ts) drives conditional return null in DashboardNav.tsx:203-206 and ternary NavToggle/MobileMenuButton in DashboardLayout.tsx:108; DashboardLayout.mobile.test #13/#14/#15/#17 pass. [✓] Drawer closes on backdrop click, nav-link click, Escape — NavBackdrop wired to closeMobileNav (DashboardLayout.tsx:86-97), onNavigate=closeMobileNav passed into NavDrawer's list (DashboardNav.tsx:176), Escape effect in DashboardNav.tsx:191-201; mobile.test #20/#21/#22 pass. [✓] All destinations reachable + accessible names in every mode — aria-label set unconditionally from navIconLabels (DashboardNav.tsx:83,128), NavDestinationList/NavLogout shared verbatim between NavRail and NavDrawer so isAdmin gate (showOrganizations) applies identically in both. [✓] pnpm lint passes — oxlint apps/wallow-web packages --deny-warnings exit 0 (verified directly, not just trusted). Read every changed file in full: DashboardNav.tsx, DashboardLayout.tsx, use-is-desktop.ts, nav-icons.ts, ui-store.ts, plus all 5 modified pre-existing specs and both new spec files — content matches the green report's line-by-line claims exactly, no discrepancies. Modified pre-existing specs (DashboardNav.test/.gate/.toggle, DashboardLayout.test/.toggle) carry ONLY the claimed viewport pin + the two backdrop-test retargets in DashboardLayout.toggle.test.tsx (renamed to 'renders no backdrop while the rail is expanded either' / 'renders no mobile menu button at desktop width') — no assertion weakened/removed. Nav state confirmed to live only in useUiStore (ui-store.ts, isNavCollapsed/isMobileNavOpen), no component-local useState duplicating it. data-testid conventions hold: dashboard-nav-drawer, dashboard-nav-mobile-menu are new kebab {page}-{element} names, all previously-existing testids preserved verbatim. Could not diff against a red-phase git commit (nothing committed yet per NOTES) but re-ran the red-phase test files verbatim and their content is unchanged from the RED report's own quoted contract — no drift detected. TESTS: pnpm --filter @bc-solutions-coder/wallow-web test -> 1 failed (Wallow-jx7f __root.branding, pre-existing/out-of-scope, confirmed unrelated) | 539 passed (540). title: Sidebar: decouple nav state model and select icon set
description: Rework apps/wallow-web/src/stores/ui-store.ts so desktop icon-rail collapse and mobile overlay-drawer open are independent state, not the single 'isNavOpen' boolean used today (which apps/wallow-web/src/components/DashboardNav.tsx reads for rail width and apps/wallow-web/src/components/DashboardLayout.tsx reads for both the toggle button aria-expanded and the backdrop). Also select and add an icon library/icon set for the nav items (Organizations, Apps, Settings, Inquiries, Sign Out, plus the nav-toggle/close controls) — none exists anywhere in the workspace today (checked apps/wallow-web/package.json, packages/ui/package.json, root package.json).
design: Suggested shape for apps/wallow-web/src/stores/ui-store.ts's UiState: replace 'isNavOpen'/'toggleNav'/'closeNav' with two independent slices, e.g. 'isNavCollapsed' (desktop rail: expanded=false default per the plan's 'expanded desktop default', toggled by 'toggleNavCollapsed') and 'isMobileNavOpen' (mobile drawer: closed by default, opened/closed by 'openMobileNav'/'closeMobileNav'). Keep doc-comments in the file's existing style (see current file header) explaining the two-axis boundary so a future reader doesn't re-conflate them. For the icon library: pick the lightest option that plays well with Tailwind v4 + React 19 and is tree-shakeable per-icon (avoid pulling a whole icon-font); check bundle-size/tree-shaking before locking it in, then add it as a dependency of apps/wallow-web/package.json (or packages/ui if it should be shared — check packages/ui/src for a pattern first, there is none yet for icons). Keep icons and their accessible names consistent (e.g. same icon for the same nav item across all three modes).
acceptance_criteria:
- apps/wallow-web/src/stores/ui-store.ts exposes independently-settable desktop-collapse state and mobile-drawer-open state (naming may differ from the suggestion above as long as the two axes are decoupled).
- ui-store.test.ts (apps/wallow-web/src/stores/ui-store.test.ts) is updated/extended to cover both state slices independently (e.g. collapsing the desktop rail does not open the mobile drawer and vice versa).

title: Give each app's Vite dev server a distinct HMR WebSocket port
description:
When apps/wallow-web and apps/wallow-auth dev servers run in parallel (root `pnpm dev` = `pnpm --parallel --filter @bc-solutions-coder/wallow-web --filter @bc-solutions-coder/wallow-auth dev`, each running `tsx dev-server.ts`), each independently calls the shared createDevServer() factory in packages/web-shell/src/server/dev-server.ts, which boots a Vite dev server via createViteServer({ ..., server: { middlewareMode: true } }) (current shape at dev-server.ts line 182-188, the server option is exactly `server: { middlewareMode: true }` with no hmr key). Because middlewareMode is on and no hmr.server/hmr.port is specified, Vite falls back to its own default standalone HMR WebSocket listener on port 24678. Both apps therefore try to bind the SAME port 24678 for their independent Vite instances, and the second one to start fails with "WebSocket server error: Port 24678 is already in use".

createDevServer already computes a per-app HTTP port at dev-server.ts line 159: `const port: number = Math.trunc(Number(process.env.PORT ?? config.defaultPort));` — wallow-web resolves to 3000 (its dev-server.ts sets defaultPort: "3000"), wallow-auth to 3002 (defaultPort: "3002"). This existing per-app `port` value must be used to derive a distinct HMR port per app WITHOUT requiring any changes in the two apps' own dev-server.ts files — the fix belongs entirely in the shared factory.
design:
In packages/web-shell/src/server/dev-server.ts, change the server object passed to createViteServer (currently `server: { middlewareMode: true }` at line ~187) to also set an hmr port derived deterministically from the already-computed `port` variable, e.g.:
```
server: { middlewareMode: true, hmr: { port: port + 20000 } },
```
(wallow-web -> HMR port 23000, wallow-auth -> HMR port 23002 — distinct, deterministic, and far from any other service in docker/.env or the 3000/3001/3002/5001/5004/8025 ports listed in the root CLAUDE.md Local Development table). The exact offset is an implementation choice; it must (a) be deterministic per app (no reliance on OS-assigned ephemeral ports, since two independent 'find a free port' calls could still collide under concurrent boot), and (b) not collide with any documented port in the root CLAUDE.md Local Development table or docker/.env.example.

Reference test file: packages/web-shell/src/server/dev-server.test.ts already captures the InlineConfig handed to the injected createViteServer via `harness.inlineConfig()` (see existing assertion `expect(cfg.server?.middlewareMode).toBe(true)` in the test "boots a Vite dev server in custom middlewareMode..." at line 201-209) — extend that test (or add a new one) asserting `cfg.server?.hmr` carries a port, and add a NEW test that starts two harnesses with different defaultPort/PORT values and asserts their resulting hmr ports differ (proving the derivation is port-dependent, not a hardcoded constant).

Do NOT restructure the server-creation order (i.e. do not try to create the Node http.Server first and pass `hmr: { server }}` — that would require moving the `createHttpServer`/`listen` call earlier than the Vite dev server instantiation, a much larger structural change not needed here since a distinct static port fully resolves the collision).
acceptance_criteria: 1. packages/web-shell/src/server/dev-server.ts sets a per-app-derived hmr.port in the InlineConfig passed to createViteServer. 2. dev-server.test.ts has a passing assertion that the captured InlineConfig's server.hmr carries a port value, and a passing assertion that two different defaultPort/PORT configs produce two different hmr ports. 3. pnpm --filter @bc-solutions-coder/web-shell test passes. 4. Running pnpm dev at the repo root starts both apps with NO 'WebSocket server error: Port ... already in use' in the log. 5. Both apps still serve correctly: wallow-web on http://localhost:3000, wallow-auth on http://localhost:3002. 6. pnpm typecheck and pnpm lint stay green.

   FAILS: expected 'undefined' to be 'number' (dev-server.ts:196 passes server: { middlewareMode: true } with no hmr key).
2. 'derives the HMR port from the app's own port so two apps started in parallel get different ones'
   Starts TWO harnesses with two distinct probed PORT values and asserts both hmr ports are numbers AND differ.
   FAILS at the first typeof assertion today. This is the guard that a HARDCODED constant (which would satisfy test 1 but still collide) is not enough — the derivation must track the per-app port.
3. 'keeps the derived HMR port inside the valid TCP range and clear of the app's own port and the documented dev-stack ports'
   FAILS: Number.isInteger(undefined) === false. Asserts integer, >1023, <65536, !== the app's own HTTP port, and not in DOCUMENTED_DEV_PORTS.

title: Suppress TanStack Router test-file warnings via routeFileIgnorePattern
description:
Both apps' TanStack Router codegen plugin instances warn on every *.test.ts(x) file under src/routes/ because routeFileIgnorePattern is never set. There are exactly TWO call sites that construct tanstackRouter({...}) options, both in the shared package packages/web-shell/src/server/, and BOTH must be updated (one drives `vite build` via createClientViteConfig, the other drives `pnpm dev` via createDevServer — apps do not read vite.config.ts in dev because dev-server.ts passes configFile: false):

1. packages/web-shell/src/server/vite-presets.ts, inside createClientViteConfig() (currently lines 37-42):
```
tanstackRouter({
  target: "react",
  routesDirectory: join(options.appDir, "src", "routes"),
  generatedRouteTree: join(options.appDir, "src", "routeTree.gen.ts"),
  autoCodeSplitting: false,
}),
```

2. packages/web-shell/src/server/dev-server.ts, inside createDevServer() (currently lines 172-177), same shape as above but for the dev seam's inline plugin list.

Neither currently sets routeFileIgnorePattern (confirmed via grep — it does not appear anywhere in apps/ or packages/). The @tanstack/router-generator option (packages/.pnpm/@tanstack+router-generator@1.167.21/.../config.d.ts:22, routeFileIgnorePattern: z.ZodOptional<z.ZodString>) accepts a string that is compiled into a RegExp internally and matched against route filenames; files matching it are silently skipped instead of warned on.

Add `routeFileIgnorePattern: "\\.(test|spec)\\.(ts|tsx)$"` (or equivalent) to BOTH tanstackRouter({...}) call sites so *.test.ts, *.test.tsx, *.spec.ts, *.spec.tsx files under src/routes/ in either app are ignored by the route generator. Do NOT touch routeFileIgnorePrefix (its default "-" behavior must be preserved — it is unrelated and not currently overridden).

Existing route files to verify are unaffected: apps/wallow-web/src/routes/ and apps/wallow-auth/src/routes/ (list them with `find apps/wallow-web/src/routes apps/wallow-auth/src/routes -type f` before/after to confirm no real route lost coverage and test files are excluded).
acceptance_criteria: 1. packages/web-shell/src/server/vite-presets.ts and packages/web-shell/src/server/dev-server.ts both pass routeFileIgnorePattern in their tanstackRouter({...}) options. 2. New/updated tests in vite-presets.test.ts and dev-server.test.ts assert the pattern is set and correctly matches .test.ts/.test.tsx/.spec.ts/.spec.tsx filenames while NOT matching normal route files. 3. pnpm --filter @bc-solutions-coder/web-shell test passes. 4. Running pnpm --filter ./apps/wallow-web dev and pnpm --filter ./apps/wallow-auth dev (or pnpm dev at root) produces no 'does not export a Route' warnings for any file under either app's src/routes/. 5. pnpm typecheck and pnpm lint stay green. 6. routeFileIgnorePrefix is untouched (not present in the diff).

title: Eliminate dev-log warnings: route-file test noise + HMR port collision in pnpm dev
description:
Running `pnpm dev` at the repo root starts apps/wallow-web and apps/wallow-auth in parallel via `pnpm --parallel --filter @bc-solutions-coder/wallow-web --filter @bc-solutions-coder/wallow-auth dev` (root package.json). The combined output is polluted with two classes of warnings:

1. TanStack Router warns for EVERY *.test.tsx/*.test.ts file under src/routes/ in both apps: "Warning: Route file '...' does not export a Route. This file will not be included in the route tree." Root cause: the @tanstack/router-generator plugin (v1.167.x, resolved at node_modules/.pnpm/@tanstack+router-generator@1.167.21/) defaults routeFileIgnorePrefix to "-" and routeFileIgnorePattern to undefined (confirmed in node_modules/.pnpm/@tanstack+router-generator@1.167.21/node_modules/@tanstack/router-generator/dist/esm/config.js:23). Neither app nor the shared web-shell package currently sets routeFileIgnorePattern, so any *.test.ts(x) file under src/routes/ is scanned and warned on.

2. "WebSocket server error: Port 24678 is already in use" — when apps/wallow-web and apps/wallow-auth dev servers run in parallel (pnpm --parallel), each independently boots a Vite dev server in middlewareMode via packages/web-shell/src/server/dev-server.ts's createDevServer(). Vite's default HMR websocket port (24678) is not overridden anywhere, so the second app's Vite instance fails to bind it.

Acceptance for the epic: `pnpm dev` from the repo root starts both apps with ZERO route-file warnings and ZERO WebSocket port errors, both apps still serve correctly (wallow-web on 3000, wallow-auth on 3002) with working HMR, and pnpm test / pnpm typecheck / pnpm lint stay green.

title: run-tests.sh false-green: prints RESULT: PASS with 0 tests when the test project fails to compile
description: Found during Wallow-mbe0 red phase: ./scripts/run-tests.sh reports RESULT: PASS with 0 tests executed when the target test project fails to COMPILE, masking failures. Details in the notes on bead Wallow-mbe0. Fix: treat build failure / zero-tests-run as FAIL.

ROOT_CAUSE (verified via scratch repro with a throwaway dotnet xunit project, NOT in this repo):
- When the target test project fails to COMPILE, 'dotnet test' exits nonzero (verified: exit 1) and writes ZERO .trx files to the results dir (confirmed empty dir after a deliberate CS1031 syntax error).
