title: wallow-web SSR self-origin fetch fails in containerised e2e (published port != internal port)
description: The wallow-web TanStack Start SSR path (src/lib/wallow-sdk.ts configureClient -> configureSsrClient(getSsrRequestContext()), baseUrl=context.origin) makes the SSR host fetch its OWN browser-facing origin (${origin}/api) during dashboard render. In docker/docker-compose.test.yml the container listens on PORT=3000 but is published at 127.0.0.1:5053:3000, so the browser Host is localhost:5053. During SSR of /dashboard/apps the container self-fetches http://localhost:5053/api -> ECONNREFUSED ('fetch failed') -> 500 -> error boundary ('Something went wrong!'), so data-app-ready is never stamped and apps/wallow-web/e2e-cross-app/login-journey.spec.ts fails at the post-landing hydration wait. Proven: inside the container localhost:3000/health=200 but localhost:5053/health=ECONNREFUSED. When wallow-web is made to listen on its published port (PORT=5053, ports 5053:5053), the journey PASSES (1 passed). Root cause is topology, not the auth flow: e2e.sh's backend auth-code+PKCE login (login.spec.ts) is green, and the journey is green whenever the SSR origin loops back (e.g. pnpm backend / Aspire on :3000).
design: Two candidate fixes: (A) low-risk test-infra: set docker-compose.test.yml wallow-web to PORT=5053 + ports 5053:5053 + healthcheck on 5053 so the documented 'E2E_BASE_URL=http://localhost:5053 pnpm --filter ./apps/wallow-web test:e2e:cross-app' works out of the box. (B) architectural (preferred long-term): during SSR, target an internally reachable origin (e.g. localhost:PORT or BFF_API_BASE_URL) instead of the browser-facing published origin, since a container generally cannot reach its own external origin (also fragile behind a prod reverse proxy). Note the login-journey spec header already documents pnpm backend/Aspire as the primary supported stack where self-origin loopback works.
acceptance_criteria: apps/wallow-web/e2e-cross-app/login-journey.spec.ts passes against docker/docker-compose.test.yml via the documented E2E_BASE_URL=http://localhost:5053 command, asserting dashboard-apps via app-level signal.
notes:
AUDIT 2026-07-25 (verify-web): STILL_VALID — neither candidate fix applied. compose test.yml wallow-web still ports 127.0.0.1:5053:3000 / PORT 3000 (:236,:240); ssr.tsx:39-42 still derives origin from request.url (browser-facing localhost:5053); sdk ssr.ts:84-87 configureSsrClient uses that origin with NO internal-URL escape hatch. Surrounding container wiring (BFF_API_BASE_URL, OIDC_METADATA_URL) is correct — SSR self-fetch is the one remaining browser-facing-origin path. RECOMMENDATION: fix (B) preferred — optional internal-origin field on SsrRequestContext/configureSsrClient populated from http://localhost:PORT or env var, fallback to request.url origin; also fixes reverse-proxy deployments. (A) (align compose ports to 5053) is a cheap test-only unblock. Verify per acceptance criteria with E2E_BASE_URL=http://localhost:5053 cross-app suite. Independent of zyxe (journey is authenticated) but same beforeLoad/SSR path — cheaper to fix both in one pass.
RED (red-spb5, TDD write-tests phase) — 21 tests failing across 2 packages. Fix (B) (internal-origin escape hatch) is the specced shape; no compose port change needed.

TEST FILES
1. packages/sdk/src/ssr.test.ts (+2 describes, 6 new tests) — 'resolveSsrFetchOrigin' (4) and 'configureSsrClient with a non-self-reachable request origin' (4, one of them a fetch-level repro). Pins: internalOrigin wins over the browser-facing origin; empty/undefined internalOrigin falls back to context.origin; baseUrl becomes ${internalOrigin}/api with credentials:'include' preserved; the SSR-time generated-client request URL is http://localhost:3000/api/... NOT http://localhost:5053/api/... while still carrying the wallow_bff cookie.

Pins internal-origin targeting, cookie forwarding, request-origin fallback, and relative '/bff/user' when there is no SSR context.
3. apps/wallow-web/src/lib/ssr-origin.test.ts (NEW, 14 tests) — the app-side resolver: resolveSsrInternalOrigin(env) derives http://localhost:${PORT} (tracks non-default PORT), lets WALLOW_WEB_INTERNAL_URL override it, trims a trailing slash, treats empty values and a non-numeric PORT as unset, and returns undefined when nothing indicates a split (so pnpm dev/Aspire keep today's working request-origin behavior). createSsrRequestContext(request, env) stamps { origin (browser-facing), cookie, internalOrigin }. title: T3.4 Token-recipe enforcement test in packages/styles
description: Add a test in packages/styles that asserts every CSS custom property emitted from forkBranding.theme (api/branding.json's theme block) is referenced somewhere in styles.css's @theme Tailwind v4 mapping -- so a new branding token can never silently go unmapped.
design: No new token groups and no manifest machinery per the plan's decisions -- this is a single enforcement test, not new infrastructure.
acceptance_criteria: Test fails if a var emitted by renderThemeStyle/forkBranding.theme has no corresponding reference in styles.css's @theme block; passes on current styles.css.
notes:
RED: packages/styles/src/theme-css.test.ts, 2 new tests, confirmed FAILING.

WHAT: Extended describe("the branding palette") with the reverse-direction enforcement (scout's cssVars-keys subset-of themedVars). Added shared helper referencesEveryEmittedVar(mode) + two it() blocks (light/dark): asserts every custom property toCssVars(forkBranding.theme[mode]) emits is referenced by var(--x) inside styles.css @theme. No production code, no new helpers/machinery -- reused themeTokens()/themedVarNames()/themedVars already in the file (per plan: single enforcement test, not new infra).

TEST_STATUS: 2 failing / 9 passing (11 total). Existing 9 (forward-direction guards + package contract) stay green.

FINDING (contradiction in acceptance criteria -- GREEN agent must resolve): the test FAILS on CURRENT styles.css, but the criteria says it should PASS on current styles.css. Cause is a REAL latent gap, exactly what this guard exists to catch: api/branding.json theme (light+dark) emits 20 tokens including popover/popoverForeground -> renderThemeStyle writes --popover and --popover-foreground onto :root, but styles.css @theme references only 18 vars and NEVER maps --popover / --popover-foreground to a Tailwind token. So both are silently dead tokens today. Failure msg lists exactly ["--popover", "--popover-foreground"].

GREEN options: (a) add the two missing mappings to packages/styles/styles.css @theme (--color-popover: var(--popover); --color-popover-foreground: var(--popover-foreground);) -- this actually exposes popover as a Tailwind color AND makes the guard pass, satisfying 'passes on current styles.css'; this is the fix that matches the plan's intent ('a new branding token can never silently go unmapped'). OR (b) if popover is deliberately direct-var-only (shadcn components read var(--popover) without a bg-popover utility), narrow the guard to an allowlisted exception -- but (a) is the truer fix. Recommend (a).

ISSUES: none with the test itself; the failure is the guard correctly firing on a pre-existing unmapped-token gap.
GREEN: FILES=packages/styles/styles.css (production fix). Added two @theme mappings after the card tokens: --color-popover: var(--popover); --color-popover-foreground: var(--popover-foreground); -- exposes the popover pair as real Tailwind colors (bg-popover / text-popover-foreground) AND satisfies the reverse-direction guard. Chose scout's option (a) over the allowlist: popover/popoverForeground are genuine shadcn semantic tokens emitted by forkBranding.theme (light+dark), so mapping them is the truer fix and matches the plan intent ('a new branding token can never silently go unmapped'). SYMBOLS=none (CSS @theme entries only; no exported TS symbols). Did NOT edit the test file. TEST_STATUS=pass -- full styles package suite 59/59 passing (the 2 previously-failing enforcement tests now green). oxlint clean, oxfmt applied. description: Compare apps/wallow-auth/src/features/mfa-enroll and apps/wallow-web/src/features/mfa (both drive the same enroll/confirm/backup-codes TOTP endpoints with parallel view logic). Decide whether the endpoint-wrapper/types layer is a clean extraction into packages/sdk's facade (coordinating with the unwrap()/createConfiguredOnce() helpers landed in W4). Both apps' mfa-enroll/mfa feature components import the typed wrappers from @bc-solutions-coder/sdk instead of hand-rolling their own API calls, but keep their own view/flow logic untouched. If extraction is judged NOT worthwhile (e.g. the two flows' API shapes have diverged too much to share cleanly), record that decision and rationale on this bead instead of forcing an extraction.

Both apps' MFA-related tests and e2e coverage remain green either way.
notes:
SCOUT (decision inputs, both apps read in full): WALLOW-AUTH already gets its MFA API surface from packages/sdk's shared facade -- apps/wallow-auth/src/lib/wallow-auth-sdk.ts's `auth` slice IS `createAuthClient()` from packages/sdk/src/auth-client.ts (the W4 facade). AuthClient (packages/sdk/src/auth-client.ts:101) already exports enrollTotp():Promise<unknown>, confirmEnrollment(body: MfaConfirmRequest):Promise<unknown>, exchangeEnrollmentToken(token):Promise<unknown> -- consumed directly by apps/wallow-auth/src/features/mfa-enroll/components/MfaEnrollForm.tsx via getWallowAuthSdk().auth.*. It has NO status/disable/regenerateBackupCodes methods (wallow-auth's mid-login flow never needs them). WALLOW-WEB hand-rolls its OWN independent MFA slice in apps/wallow-web/src/lib/wallow-sdk.ts (MfaSlice interface + sdk.mfa object, lines ~/mfa:/): status(), enrollTotp(), confirmEnroll(secret,code), disable(password), regenerateBackupCodes(password) -- calling the SAME generated ops (postV1IdentityMfaEnrollTotp, postV1IdentityMfaEnrollConfirm) as auth-client.ts, via packages/sdk/src/facade.ts's exported unwrap()/createConfiguredOnce() (the OTHER W4 helper, generic not auth-specific). It has NO exchangeEnrollmentToken (wallow-web is same-origin SPA, no cross-app relay token). Dev loads the proxy bridge THROUGH Vite (ssrLoadModule), not via a direct import, so the seam is loadProxyHandler(vite: ViteDevServer) => Promise<(req: Request)=>Promise<Response>>. Fields: appName, defaultPort, appDir (Vite root), isProxyPath, loadProxyHandler, reactPluginInDev?. Mirrors ShellConfig's shared field names/semantics but is its own interface (ShellConfig.handleProxy would be dead weight in dev).
- CRITICAL per scout guidance: createDevServer holds NO memoization slot. loadProxyHandler is invoked on EVERY proxy request; the APP owns memoization (wallow-auth caches its AuthServer instance in a closure; wallow-web loads handleBffRequest fresh each call). Test 'invokes loadProxyHandler per proxy request' pins loadCalls===2 after two /health hits, and 'does not load the proxy bridge at boot' pins loadCalls===0 at boot (proxy laziness).
- Testability seam: createDevServer accepts optional deps.createViteServer (defaults to real vite createServer). Tests inject a fake ViteDevServer (middlewares always next(); ssrLoadModule('/src/ssr.tsx')=>{render}) and capture the InlineConfig, so no real Vite boot is needed. GREEN impl MUST honor this injection point.
- reactPluginInDev gating asserted by inspecting captured InlineConfig.plugins names: true => a plugin whose name matches /react/i present; false/omitted => absent. GREEN impl will need @vitejs/plugin-react as a web-shell dep (NOT in root node_modules today; present in the apps) and should register it only when true (both apps pass false today per scout).
- wallowStyles() always spread in: test asserts plugins contains 'wallow:brand-assets'. GREEN impl imports wallowStyles from @bc-solutions-coder/styles/vite (add dep) and spreads [...(reactPluginInDev? react():[]), ...wallowStyles()].
- Vite InlineConfig asserted: root===config.appDir, appType==='custom', configFile===false, server.middlewareMode===true.
- Dispatch: proxy path (isProxyPath true) -> loadProxyHandler(vite) handler, response piped (status + multiple Set-Cookie preserved). Non-proxy -> vite.middlewares(req,res,next) then ssrLoadModule('/src/ssr.tsx').render; SSR status propagated (404 route). Reuse writeWebResponse/toWebRequest bridging from standalone-host (dev-server's writeWebResponse uses text() not arrayBuffer() — dev never serves binary assets, Vite middlewares do; either is fine for tests).

title: sdk: add unwrap()/createConfiguredOnce() facade helpers, collapse both app facades onto them
description: Extract the facade boilerplate common to apps/wallow-web/src/lib/wallow-sdk.ts (383 L) and apps/wallow-auth/src/lib/wallow-auth-sdk.ts (99 L) — the unwrap({data, error})-and-throw-ProblemDetails helper, and the configure-once singleton guard — into packages/sdk as exported helpers. The per-app facades and their namespaced slices STAY app-owned (identity endpoints vs dashboard slices are genuinely different surfaces and the fork-extension seam) — only the shared boilerplate moves.
design: packages/sdk exports: unwrap() — takes the {data, error} shape returned by the generated @hey-api client operations and either returns data or throws a parsed RFC 7807 ProblemDetails error (read the current inline implementation in either app's facade to preserve exact error-parsing behavior). createConfiguredOnce() (or createSdkFacade wrapper) — the guarded-singleton pattern that ensures configureBffClient + CSRF interceptor wiring happens exactly once. Both apps' facades (wallow-sdk.ts, wallow-auth-sdk.ts) shrink: they keep their own slice definitions (namespaced methods per feature) but call the SDK's unwrap()/createConfiguredOnce() instead of duplicating the boilerplate.
acceptance_criteria: Both wallow-sdk.ts and wallow-auth-sdk.ts are measurably shorter (boilerplate removed) while every existing facade method/slice keeps its exact public signature and behavior. Both apps' facade test suites (wallow-sdk.test.ts, wallow-auth-sdk.test.ts) pass unmodified in assertions (only import/setup changes).

Both fn bodies are 'throw new Error("not implemented")' (void-guard the params).

DESIGN DECISIONS (spec the green impl must honor):
1. unwrap() PRESERVES wallow-web's RAW-THROW semantics: return data on {data}; throw the RAW error object (by identity) on {error !== undefined}. 2. createConfiguredOnce(configure, build) two-arg form: getter runs configure() then build() exactly once on FIRST call, memoizes, returns same instance thereafter; NOTHING runs at creation time (lazy). Tests pin: lazy (no calls until first getter invocation), configure-once across N calls, build-once + same-instance memoization, configure-before-build ordering.

title: W3: @bc-solutions-coder/ui — shared component library
description:
Extract shared React components/primitives into a new private workspace package packages/ui (@bc-solutions-coder/ui), browser-only React, react/react-dom as peer deps, sdk-style build. Depends on W1 (component specs run on the shared vitest harness) and W2 (Tailwind scanning of package sources via wallowStyles()/@source wiring).

Tailwind scanning constraint: app @source "./" scans only the app tree; Tailwind v4 skips node_modules. ui therefore ships a source.css declaring @source "./src" relative to itself (shipped in package "files"), and each app's CSS entry gains one line: @import "@bc-solutions-coder/ui/source.css";. styles must NOT import ui — ui depends on styles conceptually, never the reverse.

Phase A (verbatim moves, near-zero risk) — see child task beads.
Phase B (extract auth's design language as primitives, sourced from measured recipe repetition in PasswordLoginForm, RegisterForm, MfaEnrollForm, apps/wallow-auth/src/components/auth-layout.tsx) — see child task beads.

Files: apps/wallow-auth/src/components/{ready-indicator.tsx,focus-on-navigate.tsx,auth-layout.tsx} + their tests, apps/wallow-web/src/components/ready-indicator.tsx + tests, apps/wallow-auth's ~20 feature components/screens (PasswordLoginForm, RegisterForm, MfaEnrollForm, etc.), both apps' CSS entry files.

title: fix(web): unauthenticated /dashboard SSR beforeLoad 500s (login() called server-side)
description:
Discovered as an out-of-scope defect during Wallow-cqoa verification (getUser() SSR fix).

A full-page SSR load of /dashboard/** while UNAUTHENTICATED still returns HTTP 500
(e.g. `curl /dashboard/apps` => 500). apps/wallow-web/src/routes/dashboard/route.tsx
beforeLoad calls getWallowSdk().user.me(); when it resolves null it calls the SDK's
login(location.pathname), which is browser-only (`location.href = ...` in
packages/sdk/src/auth.ts). Under Node SSR, `location` is undefined, so this throws
and the route 500s instead of redirecting.

This predates Wallow-cqoa: before that fix the same path 500'd for a different
reason (getUser() throwing on the relative-URL parse). Wallow-cqoa's SSR fix
turned the AUTHENTICATED path from 500 -> 200, but left the UNAUTHENTICATED path
500ing via this login() call.

FIX: guard the SSR case in dashboard/route.tsx's beforeLoad -- e.g. use TanStack's
server-side `redirect()`/Response instead of calling the browser-only login() when
import.meta.env.SSR is true (or when `location` is unavailable), so an
unauthenticated full-page load of /dashboard/** redirects instead of 500ing.

CAUTION: apps/wallow-web/src/routes/dashboard/route.test.tsx has an existing test
'redirects to login when unauthenticated (user.me resolves null)' that runs in the
node/SSR vitest project and currently asserts on the login() call path -- update
that test alongside the route fix so both the client and SSR behaviors stay
covered.

Confirmed still reproducible after Wallow-cqoa's fix: home (/) and /bff-demo SSR
both return 200; unauthenticated /dashboard/** SSR returns 500.
notes:
AUDIT 2026-07-25 (verify-web): STILL_VALID (statically confirmed; no live repro run). dashboard/route.tsx:44-51 beforeLoad still calls browser-only login() (sdk auth.ts:27-29 bare 'location') with no SSR guard; ssr.tsx:38-46 runs beforeLoad server-side; Node has no global location -> throw -> 500. DESCRIPTION DRIFT: (a) getWallowSdk().user.me() is gone — commit 29aff497 replaced it with context.queryClient.ensureQueryData(userQueries.currentUser()); mechanism unchanged. (b) test name is now 'redirects to login and returns isAdmin:false when the cached user is null' (route.test.tsx:71); its hoisted loginMock masks the defect in the node project. Fix: SSR branch should throw redirect({href:'/bff/login?returnTo=...'}); update test for both branches. ALSO: e2e-cross-app/login-journey.spec.ts:16-19 says the home route '/' shares this SSR defect and navigates around it — audit '/' and either widen this bead or file a sibling.
SCOUT FINDINGS (confirmed root cause + fix plan):

FILES:
- apps/wallow-web/src/routes/dashboard/route.tsx:1,44-51 -- beforeLoad calls login(location.pathname) unconditionally when the cached user (via ensureQueryData(userQueries.currentUser())) is null.
- packages/sdk/src/auth.ts:27-29 -- export function login(returnTo) { location.href = ... } -- bare 'location', no window/SSR guard; throws ReferenceError under Node SSR.
- apps/wallow-web/src/ssr.tsx:38-46 -- render() drives beforeLoad server-side via @tanstack/react-router/ssr/server createRequestHandler -- confirms beforeLoad executes in Node during full-page SSR, so the browser-only login() call is reached there.
- apps/wallow-web/src/routes/dashboard/route.test.tsx -- existing spec. Lines 26-31: vi.hoisted loginMock + vi.mock('@bc-solutions-coder/sdk', ...) replaces login with a spy for ALL tests in the file -- this masks the SSR defect (login never actually runs the throwing location.href assignment). Line 71-76 'redirects to login and returns isAdmin:false when the cached user is null' currently just asserts loginMock was called; must be rewritten to assert a thrown TanStack redirect() instead.
- apps/wallow-web/src/routes/index.tsx:43-56 ('/' route) -- SAME latent pattern at line 54 (login('/dashboard/apps') called unconditionally when landingPage disabled + user null), currently not manifesting because forkBranding.landingPage.enabled defaults true. Out of scope for this bead per current title/description (dashboard only) -- flag to coordinator/team-lead as a possible sibling bug, do not fix here unless bead is widened.
- apps/wallow-web/src/routes/index.tsx:49 -- existing redirect() usage pattern for a REGISTERED route: throw Object.assign(redirect({ to: '/dashboard/apps' }), { to: '/dashboard/apps' }) (to a route IN the route tree).

ROOT_CAUSE: dashboard/route.tsx's beforeLoad runs server-side during SSR (confirmed via ssr.tsx's createRequestHandler). When the cached current-user query resolves null, it calls the SDK's login() (packages/sdk/src/auth.ts:27-29), which does a bare browser-only 'location.href = ...' assignment. Node has no global 'location', so this throws, and TanStack's SSR request handler surfaces the throw as an HTTP 500 instead of a redirect.

FIX_APPROACH: Replace the login(location.pathname) call in dashboard/route.tsx's beforeLoad (null-user branch) with 'throw redirect({ href: `/bff/login?returnTo=${encodeURIComponent(location.pathname)}` })' from @tanstack/react-router. Use 'href', NOT 'to' -- /bff/login is an external BFF endpoint, not a route registered in the TanStack route tree (see repo memory: to only resolves registered/typed routes; unregistered/external destinations need href). A single redirect() call works identically on both SSR and CSR (TanStack throws it as a Response server-side and performs router navigation client-side), so no import.meta.env.SSR branching is needed -- this removes the login() call from this route entirely (browser-only login() stays valid/used elsewhere, e.g. index.tsx's Get Started link and its own beforeLoad).

TEST_LOCATION: apps/wallow-web/src/routes/dashboard/route.test.tsx -- runs in the NODE vitest project (explicitly listed in nodeTsxSpecs, apps/wallow-web/vitest.config.ts:56-65, alongside other beforeLoad/SSR route specs using renderToString, never a live DOM). Update/replace the existing 'redirects to login and returns isAdmin:false when the cached user is null' test (currently line ~71): remove or stop relying on the loginMock for this assertion, and instead assert the beforeLoad call throws a TanStack redirect (use isRedirect() from @tanstack/react-router on the caught/rejected value, and assert its href is '/bff/login?returnTo=%2Fdashboard%2Forganizations' given the test's fixed location.pathname of /dashboard/organizations from the runGate() helper at line 44). The runGate() helper (lines 38-48) directly invokes Route.options.beforeLoad with a fake { location, context } -- reuse it, just change what's asserted about the null-user branch's outcome (a throw, not a return value).

TEST_CMD: pnpm --filter @bc-solutions-coder/wallow-web test   (runs both vitest projects; package name confirmed via apps/wallow-web/package.json). To scope to just this file: pnpm --filter @bc-solutions-coder/wallow-web exec vitest run src/routes/dashboard/route.test.tsx
RED PHASE (TDD) — failing tests written, no fix logic.

FILES (1 changed, tests only):
- apps/wallow-web/src/routes/dashboard/route.test.tsx (rewritten auth-gate spec; runs in the vitest NODE project per vitest.config.ts nodeTsxSpecs)
- apps/wallow-web/src/routes/dashboard/route.tsx — UNCHANGED (implementer's file)

KEY CHANGE — the mock that masked the defect is GONE: removed the vi.hoisted loginMock + vi.mock('@bc-solutions-coder/sdk', ...) block. The spec now loads the REAL SDK, so the browser-only login() actually executes under Node (no global 'location') and reproduces the exact 500 mechanism. Verified the node project has no global location ('location' in globalThis === false) — that precondition assertion PASSES.

TESTS ADDED (4 new, all failing) + 2 rewritten:
1. 'throws a TanStack redirect to the BFF login when the cached user is null' — asserts isRedirect(thrown), thrown.options.href === '/bff/login?returnTo=%2Fdashboard%2Forganizations', and thrown.headers.get('Location') === same.
2. 'marks the BFF login redirect as a full-document navigation' — asserts thrown.options.reloadDocument === true. RATIONALE (verified in router-core 1.171.15 dist): redirect() only auto-infers reloadDocument for an ABSOLUTE href (new URL(href) must parse). For a RELATIVE href like /bff/login?..., router.navigate() falls through to buildAndCommitLocation() and commits it against the TanStack route tree -> not-found match, never reaching the BFF. So the implementer MUST pass reloadDocument: true explicitly. On SSR this is harmless: createRequestHandler merges redirect.headers (Location) into the response and sets statusCode 307.
3. 'never touches the browser-only location global when unauthenticated (SSR safety)' — the direct 500-regression guard: asserts the thrown value is NOT a ReferenceError and IS a redirect.
4. 'does not import the SDK browser-only login helper' — scans only the route module's import lines: must not contain \blogin\b, must contain \bredirect\b (matches the scout's FIX_APPROACH of removing login() from this route entirely).
Rewritten: the two authenticated cases ('isAdmin:true' / 'isAdmin:false') dropped their now-meaningless loginMock assertions and keep asserting the returned context. Added helpers catchGate(user) (runs the gate expecting a throw, returns it) and assertRedirect(thrown) (asserts + narrows to AnyRedirect, no casts — 'as any' stays banned).

TEST_STATUS=FAILING (correct reason).
Scoped run: pnpm --filter @bc-solutions-coder/wallow-web exec vitest run src/routes/dashboard/route.test.tsx -> Tests 4 failed | 8 passed (12).
Failure reasons: test 3 fails with 'AssertionError: expected ReferenceError: location is not defined to not be an instance of ReferenceError' — this IS the bug (the SSR handler surfaces that throw as HTTP 500). Tests 1 and 2 fail 'expected false to be true' from isRedirect (the gate currently returns { isAdmin: false } after calling login() instead of throwing). Test 4 fails on the still-present 'import { login, type WallowUser } from "@bc-solutions-coder/sdk"'.
Whole node project: pnpm --filter @bc-solutions-coder/wallow-web exec vitest run --project node -> Test Files 1 failed | 29 passed (30); Tests 4 failed | 188 passed (192). The ONLY failures are these 4 — removing the SDK mock regressed nothing else.
oxfmt + oxlint --deny-warnings: CLEAN on the changed file.

IMPLEMENTER NOTES:
- Expected green implementation in dashboard/route.tsx beforeLoad null-user branch: throw redirect({ href: `/bff/login?returnTo=${encodeURIComponent(location.pathname)}`, reloadDocument: true }) using redirect from '@tanstack/react-router' (location here is the beforeLoad PARAM, not the global). Drop the login import; keep the WallowUser type import.
- The route's docblock (lines 12-19) still describes the old login() behaviour — update it alongside the fix.
- Do NOT edit route.test.tsx.
- Out of scope but still latent (scout already flagged): apps/wallow-web/src/routes/index.tsx:52 has the same login() call in a beforeLoad, currently unreachable because forkBranding.landingPage.enabled defaults true.
GREEN PHASE (TDD) — SSR-safe redirect implemented, all red tests pass.

FILES=apps/wallow-web/src/routes/dashboard/route.tsx (ONLY file changed; route.test.tsx untouched by the implementer)

CHANGE:
• Import line 1: 'import { login, type WallowUser } from "@bc-solutions-coder/sdk"' -> 'import type { WallowUser } from "@bc-solutions-coder/sdk"' (browser-only login() is now unreachable from this route).
• Import line 3: added redirect -> 'import { createFileRoute, redirect } from "@tanstack/react-router"'.
• beforeLoad null-user branch now throws instead of returning:
    throw redirect({
      href: `/bff/login?returnTo=${encodeURIComponent(location.pathname)}`,
      reloadDocument: true,
    });
  ('location' is the beforeLoad PARAM, never the global — that is the SSR fix.) The old 'login(location.pathname); return { isAdmin: false }' pair is gone, so an unauthenticated SSR load can no longer hit the bare global 'location'.
• Docblock (lines 7-30) rewritten to describe the redirect: why NOT login() (Node has no global location -> HTTP 500), that a thrown redirect() works on both SSR (307 + Location header) and CSR, and why reloadDocument is required (/bff/login is a BFF endpoint, not a TanStack route, so a relative href would otherwise be committed against the route tree into a not-found match).
• Authenticated branch unchanged: still returns { isAdmin: isAdminUser(user) }.

SYMBOLS (exported, unchanged shape):
• Route: FileRoute<'/dashboard'> — createFileRoute('/dashboard')({ beforeLoad, component }). beforeLoad: async ({ context, location }) => Promise<{ isAdmin: boolean }> — now THROWS AnyRedirect on the null-user path instead of returning { isAdmin: false }. Callers that relied on the old falsy-admin return value get a redirect throw instead (correct: the navigation is aborted).
• No new exports. isAdminUser / DashboardShell remain module-private and unchanged.

TEST_STATUS=pass

title: upgrade NSubstitute 5.3.0 to 6.0.0 (mechanical nullable-annotation migration)
description:
Scoped by trial upgrade in a throwaway worktree (2026-07-21 team review). NSubstitute 6.0.0 works on .NET 10; no removed APIs, no Castle.Core issues, no analyzer package involved (repo does not reference NSubstitute.Analyzers). ALL 381 build errors share one root cause: v6 added nullable annotations to its public API and TreatWarningsAsErrors promotes the warnings. Migration plan:
1. Bump NSubstitute to 6.0.0 in api/Directory.Packages.props (one line).
2. CS8625 (~29 lines / 194 nulls): in Substitute.For<T>(...) ctor-arg lists replace bare null with null! — concentrated in Identity UserManager/SignInManager fixtures.
3. CS8602/CS8604 (~187 lines): in Arg.Is<T>(x => x.Prop...) lambdas change first deref to x!. (param is now T?; one ! per reported line suffices — flow analysis covers compound predicates; ! is legal in expression trees).
4. dotnet format api/Wallow.slnx, then full ./scripts/run-tests.sh.
~216 edit sites across 73 files, mostly regex-assisted, est. 2-4h. Fixes verified on branding/shared/kernel slices: build clean, all tests green, no runtime matcher-semantics drift. Heaviest project: Wallow.Identity.Tests (255 errors).
notes: AUDIT 2026-07-25 (verify-deps): STILL_VALID, nothing done — Directory.Packages.props:159 still NSubstitute 5.3.0; 6.0.0 is latest stable. Premise intact (Nullable enable + TreatWarningsAsErrors, Directory.Build.props:15,17). Scope re-measured and consistent: 214 test files reference Substitute./Arg., 72 files with Arg.Is<> lambdas (CS8602/CS8604 bucket), 22 files with bare-null Substitute.For args (CS8625 bucket, concentrated in Wallow.Identity.Tests). No NSubstitute.Analyzers reference. title: SeederService silently skips admin bootstrap when any user exists
description: Found during the 2026-07-17 wallow-auth Playwright login smoke (plan: docs/plans/2026-07-17-auth-cutover-reset.md Task 8). The seeded admin (admin@wallow.dev per api/seed.json) could not log in: 401 invalid_credentials. Root cause: SeederWorker's Bootstrap Admin step (api/src/Wallow.SeederService/SeederWorker.cs:116) only runs when ISetupStatusChecker.IsSetupRequiredAsync is true, and setup is considered done as soon as ANY user exists. The long-lived dev DB contained only sdkgen-admin@wallow.local (created 2026-07-05 by the SDK OpenAPI generation flow), so admin bootstrap was skipped while the seeder still logged 'completed successfully'. Every other step is idempotent-sync; admin is the only step that silently no-ops. Options: make admin bootstrap idempotent (ensure user + role, never touch an existing password), or at minimum log a warning that the configured seed admin does not exist. Workaround used: delete the stray user, re-run the seeder.
acceptance_criteria: Running the seeder against a DB that has users but lacks the configured seed admin either creates the admin (without altering existing users) or emits an explicit warning naming the missing admin email; a fresh-DB run is unchanged.
notes:
AUDIT 2026-07-25 (verify-infra): STILL_VALID but ROOT CAUSE CORRECTED. Setup is NOT 'done as soon as ANY user exists' — SetupStatusChecker.cs:11-21 checks whether any user HOLDS the admin role (GetUsersInRoleAsync('admin')); this was the original logic, never tightened. Bug still reproduces: POST /v1/identity/setup/admin (SetupController.cs:31-58 -> BootstrapAdminHandler.cs) assigns the admin role, so e.g. sdkgen-admin@wallow.local flips setupRequired false and the seed admin is silently suppressed. Skip is silent at SeederWorker.cs:109-136 (no Warning; only success-path LogAdminBootstrapped at :166), plus a SECOND silent no-op at :121-132 (userExists branch). scripts/e2e.sh:53-55 works around this with a volume wipe and cites this bead with the incorrect 'ANY user' framing — correct that comment. No test covers the skip path. FIX: make BootstrapAdminAsync idempotent on configured admin email independent of IsSetupRequiredAsync; add Warning LoggerMessage on both skip branches; regression test for populated-DB path.
SCOUT FILES: api/src/Wallow.SeederService/SeederWorker.cs:109-136 (BootstrapAdminAsync, PRIVATE method, bug lives here) | api/src/Modules/Identity/Wallow.Identity.Infrastructure/Services/SetupStatusChecker.cs:11-21 (IsSetupRequiredAsync — false as soon as ANY user holds 'admin' role via GetUsersInRoleAsync) | api/src/Modules/Identity/Wallow.Identity.Application/Commands/BootstrapAdmin/BootstrapAdminHandler.cs:11-35 (the ALREADY-CORRECT reference pattern: checks UserExistsAsync(email) directly, no dependency on IsSetupRequiredAsync, logs LogAdminAlreadyExists Info on skip) | api/src/Modules/Identity/Wallow.Identity.Infrastructure/Services/BootstrapAdminService.cs (IBootstrapAdminService impl: EnsureRoleExistsAsync/CreateUserAsync/AssignRoleAsync/UserExistsAsync) | api/src/Modules/Identity/Wallow.Identity.Infrastructure/Options/AdminBootstrapOptions.cs (IsConfigured = Email && Password non-empty) | api/src/Wallow.SeederService/NullMessageBus.cs (seeder registers this as IMessageBus; InvokeAsync<T> THROWS NotSupportedException, so fix CANNOT dispatch BootstrapAdminCommand via Wolverine — must replicate handler logic directly using the already-injected IBootstrapAdminService, see Program.cs:77-78) | scripts/e2e.sh:53-55 (stale comment citing pre-audit 'ANY user exists' framing, needs correcting to 'holds admin role').
ROOT_CAUSE (confirmed in code, matches 2026-07-25 audit): SeederWorker.BootstrapAdminAsync (SeederWorker.cs:113-116) gates the ENTIRE admin-ensure block on 'setupRequired' from ISetupStatusChecker.IsSetupRequiredAsync, which is false as soon as ANY user holds the 'admin' ROLE (SetupStatusChecker.cs GetUsersInRoleAsync('admin').Count==0) — independent of whether the specifically CONFIGURED seed admin (seedOptions.Value.Admin.Email, bound from api/seed.json) exists. So if a different user (e.g. sdkgen-admin@wallow.local) was ever granted the admin role, setupRequired flips false and the seeder never even reaches the admin.Email existence check at line 121 — total silent skip, zero log output (LogAdminBootstrapped only fires on the success path at :131/166). There is a SECOND, benign-but-also-silent no-op at :121-132 when userExists is true for the configured admin (correct behavior, just unlogged).
FIX_APPROACH: Rewrite SeederWorker.BootstrapAdminAsync to decouple from ISetupStatusChecker/IsSetupRequiredAsync entirely (that check stays valid for its real caller, SetupController's one-time first-run wizard — do not touch SetupController/SetupStatusChecker/IsSetupRequiredQuery, they are correct for THAT use case). New flow, mirroring the already-correct BootstrapAdminHandler.cs pattern: (1) if seedOptions.Value.Admin is not { IsConfigured: true } admin -> log new Warning LoggerMessage naming that no seed admin is configured (nothing to bootstrap), return. (2) else check bootstrapAdminService.UserExistsAsync(admin.Email, ct) DIRECTLY (no setupRequired involved) -> if true, admin already present: no-op is correct, add an Info LoggerMessage (mirror BootstrapAdminHandler.LogAdminAlreadyExists) so the skip is no longer silent. (3) if false: EnsureRoleExistsAsync('admin') -> CreateUserAsync(...) -> AssignRoleAsync(...) -> keep existing LogAdminBootstrapped Information call. Cannot dispatch via Wolverine/BootstrapAdminCommand (NullMessageBus.InvokeAsync<T> throws) — must inline the same decision logic using the already-DI'd IBootstrapAdminService (Program.cs:77). Secondary cleanup: fix stale comment in scripts/e2e.sh:53-55 (says 'ANY user already exists', should say 'holds the admin role') — low priority, not required for AC but flagged by 2026-07-25 audit.

title: pre-commit hook cannot commit packages/sdk/openapi/v1.json
description:
The lint-staged config's protected-path filter is anchored to repo-relative paths but lint-staged passes ABSOLUTE paths, so 'packages/sdk/openapi/**' never matches.

.lintstagedrc.mjs:16 filterProtected() builds regexes as new RegExp('^' + escaped + '$') from PROTECTED_PATTERNS and tests them against the file paths lint-staged supplies. Those are absolute (/Users/.../packages/sdk/openapi/v1.json). Patterns that START with '**' still match by luck ('**/generated/**' -> '^.*.*/generated/.*.*$' matches any absolute path), which is why the generated .gen.ts files ARE correctly filtered. But 'packages/sdk/openapi/**' -> '^packages/sdk/openapi/.*$' cannot match a path starting with '/Users/'.

Consequence: v1.json slips past the filter and is handed to the '*.{json,yml,yaml}' task's oxfmt --write. oxfmt's OWN .oxfmtrc.json ignorePatterns excludes packages/sdk/openapi/**, so it exits 1 with 'Expected at least one target file. All matched files may have been excluded by ignore rules.' lint-staged then SIGKILLs the sibling tasks and aborts the commit.

Net: ANY commit touching the OpenAPI snapshot fails pre-commit. This is not hypothetical -- it blocked Wallow-vec7.9, which must commit the regenerated snapshot because openapi-drift.yml fails on drift. That commit (0320b4da) was landed with --no-verify after running all gates manually; they pass.

FIX: make filterProtected path-normalize before testing -- resolve each file relative to the repo root (path.relative(process.cwd(), file)) and match the relative form. Do not just prepend '**' to the openapi pattern; that hides the same bug for the next non-'**'-prefixed pattern anyone adds. Worth a unit test that feeds absolute paths through filterProtected.

Found during cleanup/commit of epic Wallow-vec7.

title: fix(wallow-auth): move the org-domain interstitial pre-submit and drop the anonymous requestMembership call
description:
Frontend half of Wallow-vec7.8 (the API half is GREEN and merged; read that bead's notes first).

Wallow-vec7.8 fixed the 401 on the API side by keeping POST /v1/identity/membership-requests [Authorize] and instead having the ALREADY-ANONYMOUS POST /v1/identity/auth/register opt in via a new 'requestOrgMembership' flag, with the server deriving the domain from the address the caller actually registered. apps/wallow-auth has not been moved onto that path yet.

Today apps/wallow-auth/src/features/register/components/RegisterForm.tsx:701 still calls getWallowAuthSdk().auth.requestMembership({ emailDomain }) AFTER register returns, while the just-registered user is unverified and ANONYMOUS -> 401. The screen currently degrades honestly (the accept button stays 'Request access' rather than lying 'Request sent'), so this is a gap, not a live lie to users -- but the accept path has never actually worked.

Note this is a deliberate UX reorder vs the Blazor oracle (api/src/Wallow.Auth/Components/Pages/Register.razor:358 shows the interstitial AFTER register). The oracle has the SAME 401 bug; it just swallows it into a bool. Do not treat the oracle as correct here.
design:
Resolve the interstitial BEFORE submitting, then pass the user's answer into the register call.

1. GET /v1/identity/organization-domains/match is already [AllowAnonymous] (OrganizationDomainsController.cs:67-68), so the domain lookup can run pre-submit. A miss is a 404 REJECTION, not a null resolve -- keep the existing catch-and-fall-through (RegisterForm.tsx:707-711 documents why: an error banner must never be shown to a user whose registration succeeded).
2. On ACCEPT, submit register with requestOrgMembership: true. On DECLINE/miss, submit without it (it defaults false -- opt-in is explicit).
3. DELETE the membershipMutation (RegisterForm.tsx:700-705) and the 'KNOWN GAP: requestMembership REQUIRES AUTH' comment block (RegisterForm.tsx:89-97) -- both are obsolete once the flag lands.
4. A null/no-match result from the server is an ORDINARY answer, not a failure: registration still returns succeeded. Never surface it as an error.

Server contract already shipped by Wallow-vec7.8:
  AccountRegisterRequest(string Email, string Password, string ConfirmPassword, string? ClientId = null, string? LoginMethod = null, string? ReturnUrl = null, bool RequestOrgMembership = false)

REQUIRED PLUMBING (do not skip -- CI enforces it): packages/sdk must be regenerated so RegisterRequest gains requestOrgMembership, AND the packages/sdk/openapi/v1.json snapshot must be refreshed. .github/workflows/openapi-drift.yml FAILS on drift. Regen with:
  WALLOW_OPENAPI_URL=http://localhost:5001/openapi/v1.json pnpm --filter @bc-solutions-coder/sdk exec tsx scripts/generate.ts
then commit the snapshot. Build the SDK before typechecking apps (apps typecheck against dist/).
acceptance_criteria: The interstitial resolves before submit; ACCEPT registers with requestOrgMembership: true and the membership request is actually recorded server-side for the new user (no 401); DECLINE and no-match register without the flag and still succeed. The post-register requestMembership call and the KNOWN GAP comment block are both gone from RegisterForm.tsx. SDK + openapi/v1.json snapshot regenerated so openapi-drift.yml passes. Tests cover accept, decline, and no-match; pnpm typecheck and lint pass.
notes:
RED: spec revised for the pre-submit interstitial + requestOrgMembership flag.

FILES (tests only — component untouched this phase):
- apps/wallow-auth/src/features/register/components/RegisterForm.test.tsx

SYMBOLS (test-local scaffolding; no production symbols added):
- pendingRegister(): () => void — inside the interstitial describe; makes `register` hang so the in-flight window is assertable.
- MATCH = { organizationId: "org-1", domain: "example.com" } — unchanged; the shape the endpoint really sends (see Finding 2).
No structural type scaffolding was needed: the spec mocks the `lib/wallow-auth-sdk` facade wholesale, so it compiles and runs against the CURRENT component.

TEST_STATUS: 7 failing / 46 passing (53 total). All 7 failures are the new behaviour; NO pre-existing test regressed.
Failing (the RED set):
1. asks for a domain match using the typed email BEFORE creating the account  — ordering: lookup fires, register does NOT.
2. disables the submit while the domain lookup is still in flight — new pre-submit window, "one click, one account" must span it.
3. ACCEPT: registers with requestOrgMembership true, so the server records it
4. ACCEPT: lands the user on verify-email once the account exists
5. ACCEPT: disables both interstitial buttons while the registration is in flight
6. ACCEPT: a failed registration returns the user to the form with the reason
7. never calls the anonymous requestMembership endpoint  — THE BINDING TEST; 3-6 all still pass with the obsolete call left in beside them.

Also rewrote the file-header "FINDING 3" block: was "requestMembership REQUIRES AUTH (flagged, not fixed here)", now "RESOLVED — the interstitial now runs PRE-SUBMIT", carrying vec7.8's contract, the AllowAnonymous lookup, and the disclosed UX divergence from the Blazor oracle (oracle has the same 401 bug; not the authority).

RETIRED (deliberate deletions, not omissions):
- "ACCEPT path: requests membership for the email's domain and confirms it was sent" — asserted the exact call vec7.9 deletes.
- "does not claim a membership request was sent when it fails" — pinned the screen's honesty about a 401 that no longer has a caller. Its "Request sent"/`requested` button state is gone with it: accept now navigates away.
- "SKIP path: 'No thanks' ... without requesting membership" -> "DECLINE: registers WITHOUT the flag and still succeeds".

DESIGN DECISIONS I made in the spec (verifier: these are judgement calls, not derived from the bead):
- ACCEPT whose register FAILS returns to the form with the error banner. Unlike the old post-register membership failure the account does NOT exist yet, so every reject reason (email_taken, weak password) is actionable — but only on the fields, and the interstitial has none. Test 6.
- DECLINE/no-match are pinned with `expect.not.objectContaining({ requestOrgMembership: true })`: false AND absent both pass, only the truthy accident fails. Matches the server default (opt-in is explicit).
- Client sends the FLAG only, never an emailDomain — the server derives the domain from the registered address. A client-supplied domain was the enumeration surface vec7.8 refused.
- Guards still run before the lookup (test: "does not look up the domain when a local guard rejects the submit" — passes today, kept as a regression pin).

ISSUES (for the GREEN implementer):
- SDK REGEN IS A HARD PREREQUISITE, not cleanup. packages/sdk/src/generated/types.gen.ts:13 `AccountRegisterRequest` still lacks requestOrgMembership, and packages/sdk/openapi/v1.json:6887 likewise. The API half IS merged (AccountRegisterRequest.cs:3, AccountController.cs:719 `if (request.RequestOrgMembership)`). Adding the field to RegisterForm's local `RegisterRequest` interface BREAKS typecheck until the regen lands — which is why this phase left the component alone. Regen, rebuild the SDK, then implement.
- The lookup must move out of `suggestOrContinue` (RegisterForm.tsx:706-728) into the submit path, and the resolved answer has to be carried into the register call — the accept/decline handlers need the pending form values, so a submit-time snapshot or a stored pending-request object is the shape to reach for.
- DELETE per acceptance: membershipMutation (RegisterForm.tsx:700-705), handleRequestMembership, `membershipRequested` state, the OrgMatchInterstitial `requested` prop + "Request sent" label, and the "KNOWN GAP" header block (RegisterForm.tsx:89-97). The `requestMembership` spy STAYS in the test mock — it is what test 7 asserts against.
- oxfmt/oxlint/typecheck all pass as of this phase.
GREEN: all 53 RegisterForm tests pass (was 7 failing / 46 passing). No test file edited.

- packages/sdk/openapi/v1.json — REGENERATED against a live API (see PLUMBING below).
- packages/sdk/src/generated/{types.gen.ts,sdk.gen.ts,@tanstack/react-query.gen.ts} — regenerated.
- apps/wallow-auth/src/features/register/components/RegisterForm.tsx — the whole change.

SYMBOLS (all module-private; no new exports — RegisterForm/RegisterFormProps unchanged):
- interface RegisterRequest — gains 'readonly requestOrgMembership?: boolean'. OMITTED rather than sent false on decline/no-match: the server defaults it false, so absence already says no, and this is what makes the spec's expect.not.objectContaining pin honest.
- interface PendingRegistration { readonly request: RegisterRequest; readonly domain: string } — a submit awaiting the user's answer. The request is SNAPSHOT at submit-click rather than re-read from field state on answer (the shape the RED report pointed at).
- lookupMutation: useMutation<string | null, unknown, RegisterRequest> — the PRE-submit [AllowAnonymous] lookup. Resolves null for 'no org to offer'; catches the 404 rejection.

Regen needs a LIVE API and the e2e stack's postgres is on :5442 with a DB other agents are using, so I did NOT point the API at it. title: consent screen never discloses the requested scopes
description:
The OAuth consent screen renders an ALWAYS-EMPTY scope list, so users approve third-party client access without being told what they are granting. Pre-existing defect, identical in Blazor and React — NOT a regression from the wallow-auth React port.

The chain (all three links verified by reading, and reproduced live on the e2e stack):

1. AuthorizationController.cs:164 redirects to the consent screen as
   `{authUrl}/consent?returnUrl=<escaped>&client_id=<id>` — it never forwards a
   scopes parameter. The requested scopes exist only inside the escaped returnUrl
   (the original /connect/authorize query string), which nothing parses.
2. Both consent screens therefore ask for scopes they cannot name:
   - Blazor oracle Consent.razor:46 — `GetConsentInfoAsync(ClientId, Array.Empty<string>())`
   - React port ConsentScreen.tsx — `getWallowAuthSdk().auth.getConsentInfo(clientId)`
     (scopes argument omitted; the port is faithful to the oracle here, with a
     comment stating the scopes 'come back FROM this call').
3. OpenIddictDeveloperAppService.GetConsentInfoAsync:172 loops over the requested
   scopes it was handed and applies NO filtering — an empty list in is an empty
   list out. AppsController.cs:122 passes it straight through.

Result: ConsentInfoResponse.RequestedScopes is always [], the React ScopeList
renders `<ul data-testid=\"consent-scopes\">` with zero children, and Playwright
correctly reports the zero-height ul as not visible.

Found by AuthAppFlowTests.ConsentScreen_ShowsRequestedScopesForThirdPartyClient
(Wallow-vec7.5.1.4 GREEN E2E run). That test asserts the scope list is visible and
non-empty — behaviour the platform has never had. It is the only genuine product
defect the React E2E run surfaced. Left FAILING rather than weakened, because the
assertion is right and the product is wrong.

A LATENT SECOND BUG sits behind this one and must be fixed at the same time, or
the fix will silently produce garbage: the wire format does not agree with itself.
AuthApiClient.cs:401 serialises scopes as REPEATED params (`scopes=a&scopes=b`),
but AppsController.cs:128 binds `[FromQuery] string? scopes` and splits it on
SPACE. ASP.NET binds repeated params to the comma-joined `"a,b"`, which splits on
space into the single bogus scope `"a,b"`. Nothing catches this today only because
the list is always empty.

Fix sketch (needs a decision, hence not done under the port bead):
- Forward the authorize request's scopes on the consent redirect
  (AuthorizationController.cs:164), rather than making the screen re-parse returnUrl.
- Have both screens pass them to getConsentInfo.
- Settle ONE encoding (space-delimited single param reads most OAuth-native, and
  matches what the controller already tries to parse) and align client + controller.
- Consider whether an unknown scope name should be surfaced or refused: today
  FindByNameAsync returning null yields a scope with a null description, which the
  React screen renders as a bare protocol identifier with no explanation.

Scope: api/src/Modules/Identity/Wallow.Identity.Api/Controllers/AuthorizationController.cs,
api/src/Wallow.Auth/Services/AuthApiClient.cs,
api/src/Modules/Identity/Wallow.Identity.Api/Controllers/AppsController.cs,
apps/wallow-auth/src/features/consent/components/ConsentScreen.tsx,
packages/sdk/src/auth-client.ts

title: 4.x: Proxy /.well-known/** in dev-server.ts so Dev OIDC discovery/JWKS resolve
description:
apps/wallow-auth/dev-server.ts's isProxyRequest(pathname) helper (dev-server.ts:62-64) gates which paths reach the reverse-proxy bridge, and it checks ONLY '/health', '/v1/', and '/connect/'. It omits '/.well-known/'. Everything it does not claim is offered to Vite's middlewares and then falls through to router SSR, so a discovery or JWKS request 404s in dev.

This makes Wallow-vec7.4.4 (CLOSED) effectively DEAD IN DEV. That bead added router.use('/.well-known/**', proxy) to createAuthServer() (src/lib/auth-server.ts:148-150) precisely so 'the discovery document's jwks_uri advertises this same origin, so signing keys must resolve too'. But dev-server.ts never dispatches those paths to createAuthServer() at all, so the mount is unreachable under 'pnpm dev'. Same class of bug, one layer up: 7.4.4 fixed the router's route table; this fixes the caller's gate in front of it.

VERIFIED EMPIRICALLY, not inferred (PORT=3998 pnpm exec tsx dev-server.ts, upstream API deliberately down):
  GET /v1/ping                          => 500 application/json  (reached the proxy, upstream unreachable)
  GET /health                           => 200 text/plain 'ready'
  GET /.well-known/openid-configuration => 404 text/html         (fell through to the SSR router's 404)
  GET /.well-known/jwks                 => 404 text/html         (same)
The text/html 404 is the tell: those paths are being server-rendered, not proxied.

apps/wallow-auth/server.ts is NOT affected. It previously handed every path to createAuthServer(), and when Wallow-vec7.5.1.1 added its own isProxyRequest gate it deliberately included '/.well-known/' for this exact reason (see that bead's note). So the two hosts' helpers now differ on purpose, and this bead closes the gap from the other side. Discovered while implementing Wallow-vec7.5.1.1.
acceptance_criteria:
- apps/wallow-auth/dev-server.ts routes /.well-known/** to the reverse-proxy bridge instead of router SSR.
- Booted dev-server (pnpm dev, or PORT=<free> pnpm exec tsx dev-server.ts): GET /.well-known/openid-configuration and GET /.well-known/jwks reach the proxy rather than returning a text/html 404. With the API up they relay the upstream document verbatim; with the API down they surface the proxy's upstream error (500 application/json), NOT a rendered 404 page.
- /health, /v1/**, /connect/** unchanged; every auth route still SSRs (spot-check /login => 200 text/html).
- apps/wallow-auth typecheck, test, and oxlint/oxfmt all pass.
- If the predicate is lifted into src/lib per design option (a): server.ts's behaviour is unchanged and its host-level checks still pass.
notes:
DEPENDENCY REASONING — why this blocks Wallow-67xr (added: 67xr depends-on this).

67xr repoints api/src/Wallow.Api/appsettings.Development.json:66 top-level AuthUrl from http://localhost:5002 (legacy Blazor) to http://localhost:3002 — the port Wallow-vec7.5.4 assigned to dev-server.ts's DEFAULT_PORT. OpenIddictIssuerResolver.Resolve() falls back to that key whenever OpenIddict:Issuer is unset, and it is unset in every checked-in appsettings*.json, so AuthUrl alone determines the Dev issuer.

The moment 67xr lands, OpenIddict advertises issuer http://localhost:3002, and the SDK's loadBffConfigFromEnv defaults OIDC_METADATA_URL to ${OIDC_ISSUER}/.well-known/openid-configuration (packages/sdk/src/server/config.ts:113-114) when not explicitly overridden. Under the documented dev workflow (pnpm dev -> dev-server.ts, per docs/development/frontend-setup.md), :3002 IS dev-server.ts — the host with this gap. So Dev discovery, and the jwks_uri the discovery document advertises at that same origin, both 404 as text/html. 67xr's own stated constraint is 'at no committed state is Dev login broken'; landing it before this bead violates exactly that. Hence this blocks 67xr rather than merely relating to it.

67xr already depends on Wallow-vec7.5.2 (Aspire parallel run) for the separate reason that something must SERVE :3002 first. This bead is orthogonal to that and does not depend on 7.5.2: it is about what the host on :3002 does with /.well-known once it exists. Note 7.5.2 has not yet decided WHICH host it runs for wallow-auth (AppHost Program.cs:52 still runs the Blazor project, and 7.5.2's design says only 'add apps/wallow-auth as a service'). If 7.5.2 runs 'pnpm start' (server.ts) rather than 'pnpm dev', the Aspire path is already covered by Wallow-vec7.5.1.1's predicate — but plain 'pnpm dev' remains broken for every developer, and that is reason enough on its own. Fixing this is a one-line change either way, so it is not worth gating on 7.5.2's choice.

NOT wired to Wallow-vec7.5.5 (repoint compose Oidc__Authority / OIDC_ISSUER onto wallow-auth): that is the CONTAINER path, which runs server.ts, whose predicate already includes /.well-known/ (Wallow-vec7.5.1.1). No gap there.

ROOT CAUSE FRAMING for whoever picks this up: the missing prefix is the symptom; the real defect is that two hosts each keep their own private copy of the same routing predicate and nothing keeps them honest. Wallow-vec7.4.4 fixed the router's table, Wallow-vec7.5.1.1 fixed server.ts's gate, and this is the third visit to the same decision. Design option (a) — lift the predicate into src/lib and import it from both hosts — is preferred for that reason, not for the ~6 lines it saves.

Different function, same file in the worst case. Land xhw3, then tt5j rebases onto the final isProxyRequest/proxy-paths.ts shape.

If left duplicated (design option b), verify empirically: PORT=3998 pnpm exec tsx dev-server.ts (repo already has this exact repro recipe in the bead DESCRIPTION) and curl the 4 paths — /health, /v1/ping, /.well-known/openid-configuration, /.well-known/jwks — confirming the well-known ones stop returning text/html 404 and instead reach the proxy (500 application/json with API down, or the real document with API up). title: 4.1d: GREEN — run-e2e.sh green for apps/wallow-auth flows
description:
Make the acceptance criterion of the parent bead (Wallow-vec7.5.1) actually true:
`./scripts/run-e2e.sh` green for all auth E2E flows against apps/wallow-auth. This is the
task that runs the suite and fixes whatever narrow gaps surface — it does NOT design new
infrastructure (that's 4.1a/4.1b) or write new test coverage (already done, see below).

Test coverage is ALREADY WRITTEN and does not need porting:
- api/tests/Wallow.E2E.Tests/Flows/AuthAppFlowTests.cs (177 lines, builds clean today) — new
  coverage pinning that the auth origin is served by React (route rendering + readiness
  signal for /login, /register, /forgot-password, /logout, /terms, /privacy), that the login
  screen renders its fields, and the /consent screen (approve + deny paths) — consent had
  ZERO prior E2E coverage. Do not rewrite this file; it already builds and its assertions are
  the target.
- The 7 pre-existing Blazor-auth-origin suites — AuthFlowTests.cs, MfaFlowTests.cs,
  AltAuthFlowTests.cs, EmailVerificationFlowTests.cs, InvitationFlowTests.cs,
  StaticPagesFlowTests.cs, OrganizationInvitationFlowTests.cs (all in
  api/tests/Wallow.E2E.Tests/Flows/) — these already drive Docker.AuthBaseUrl through the
  shared page objects and become the port's behavioural oracle UNCHANGED now that the origin
  serves React instead of Blazor. A deliberate design decision (recorded on the parent bead,
  Wallow-vec7.5.1) rejected re-writing/duplicating these — do not create new flow-specific
  test files for login/register/MFA/logout; if something here fails, fix the app or the
  narrow test assertion, don't duplicate the file.
design:
Procedure per .claude/rules/E2E.md: `./scripts/run-e2e.sh` for the full lifecycle (builds,
publishes/builds images, starts the stack, runs tests, tears down); once the stack is up,
iterate fast with `./scripts/run-e2e.sh --no-build --keep` (or `--keep` on the first run to
leave the stack up). Use `--headed`/`--video`/`--tracing` if a failure needs visual
debugging.

Expected failure modes to watch for (things that were flagged as risk during scoping but not
verified at runtime, since nothing could run before 4.1a/4.1b landed):
- Timing/readiness races the fixture-level WaitForAuthReadyAsync doesn't cover (e.g. a screen
  that needs an extra settle beyond "React mounted", the way MFA/OTP screens sometimes do).
- Testid gaps: scoping diffed every GetByTestId/data-testid used by the page objects against
  apps/wallow-auth/src and found full parity (including template-literal/ternary testids like
  mfa-challenge-code / mfa-challenge-backup-code and login-tab-magic-link / login-tab-otp) —
  so a testid-not-found failure at runtime would be a genuine regression to fix in the React
  app, not evidence the diff was wrong; recheck the specific component before assuming it's a
  new gap.
- Cookie/session behavior across the proxy — Wallow-vec7.4.3 (cookie attributes across the
  proxy) already closed and is a dependency of this whole bead, so this should be solid, but
  it is a plausible source of a subtle failure (e.g. SameSite/Domain mismatch surfacing only
  under a real browser + container network).

api/src/Modules/Identity/Wallow.Identity.Api/Controllers/TokenController.cs:111-117 computes claim destinations BEFORE setting the scopes:

title: 4.1b: apps/wallow-auth Dockerfile + compose + run-e2e.sh wiring
description:
Package apps/wallow-auth as a container the E2E test stack can run, and stop the E2E test
stack from running the legacy Blazor Wallow.Auth image in its place.

Today docker/docker-compose.test.yml's `wallow-auth` service (lines 159-176) runs
`image: wallow-auth:test`, which scripts/run-e2e.sh:96-100 publishes from
api/src/Wallow.Auth/Wallow.Auth.csproj (the Blazor app) via `dotnet publish
/t:PublishContainer`. apps/wallow-auth has no Dockerfile at all today. This task adds one and
repoints the compose service + run script at it.
design:
Exact pattern to mirror — apps/wallow-web/Dockerfile (already working, same monorepo
constraints: pnpm workspace, `workspace:*` dep on @bc-solutions-coder/sdk, repo-root build
context). Read it in full before writing; do not invent a different shape. Key parts to
carry over 1:1, adjusted for wallow-auth:
- `FROM node:24-slim` + `RUN corepack enable` (pins pnpm from root package.json
  `packageManager`, matches .nvmrc).
- Copy workspace manifests first (package.json, pnpm-workspace.yaml, pnpm-lock.yaml,
  .npmrc, tsconfig.base.json) + packages/sdk/package.json + apps/wallow-auth/package.json,
  `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`, THEN copy full sources and build — this layering is what
  makes rebuilds cache on source-only changes.
- Build order: `pnpm --filter @bc-solutions-coder/sdk build` (the SDK apps typecheck/import
  against dist/) THEN `pnpm --filter @bc-solutions-coder/wallow-auth build` (runs `vite
  build && vite build --config vite.ssr.config.ts` per apps/wallow-auth/package.json,
  producing dist/client/client.js + dist/server/ssr.js — see 4.1a, which server.ts now
  imports at request time).
- `WORKDIR /repo/apps/wallow-auth`, `EXPOSE 3002`, `ENV PORT=3002` (wallow-auth's port per
  the root CLAUDE.md port table and apps/wallow-auth/server.ts's DEFAULT_PORT, already fixed
  to 3002 — NOT 3000 like wallow-web).
- `CMD ["pnpm", "start"]` (runs `tsx server.ts`, a devDependency — same single-stage
  full-workspace-install rationale as wallow-web's Dockerfile comment explains: server.ts
  runs the TS source directly via tsx, not a compiled dist/ entry for itself, so devDeps must
  be present at runtime).

Compose wiring — docker/docker-compose.test.yml, `wallow-auth` service (lines 159-176):
replace `image: wallow-auth:test` with BOTH an `image:` tag (compose still needs one, e.g.
`wallow-auth-react:test` — pick a name distinct from the legacy `wallow-auth:test` Blazor
image so nothing accidentally reuses a stale one) AND a `build:` block, mirroring the
`bff-example` service (compose lines 223-227):
```
build:
  context: ..
  dockerfile: apps/wallow-auth/Dockerfile
```
Port mapping: currently `127.0.0.1:5051:8080` (Blazor, ASP.NET on 8080 internally) — change
the container-side port to 3002 (wallow-auth's Node port) and pick an appropriate host port;
keep other services' `ServiceUrls__AuthPublicUrl`/`Oidc__Authority` etc. referencing whatever
host port you choose (grep the whole compose file for `5051` and update every reference, not

title: 4.1a: SSR host wiring for apps/wallow-auth/server.ts
description:
apps/wallow-auth/server.ts (the `pnpm start` production host — what a container will run)
currently only bridges Node HTTP to the reverse-proxy bridge built by createAuthServer()
(src/lib/auth-server.ts:132-175), which mounts ONLY /health, /v1/**, /connect/**,
/.well-known/**. Every other path (/login, /register, /forgot-password, /logout, /terms,
/privacy, /consent, ...) 404s. This task wires real server-side rendering + static client
asset serving into server.ts so the standalone host actually serves the app, matching what
dev-server.ts already does for local dev via a live Vite server.

This is prerequisite, non-test app work — a fresh Docker image built on today's server.ts
would pass the E2E fixture's /health wait and then 404 every auth screen the tests hit.
design:
Reference implementation, already proven, to mirror (NOT copy verbatim — that one uses a
live Vite dev server via ssrLoadModule; you use the PRE-BUILT output):

- apps/wallow-auth/dev-server.ts — the isProxyRequest(pathname) helper (checks
  /health, /v1/, /connect/ prefixes) and the toWebRequest/writeWebResponse Node<->Web
  Request/Response adapters already exist verbatim in server.ts today; keep them.
- apps/wallow-auth/vite.config.ts — client build. `pnpm build` emits
  apps/wallow-auth/dist/client/client.js (confirmed by running the build: verbatim output
  is `dist/client/client.js  481.24 kB`). The document shell hardcodes
  `<script type="module" src="/client.js">` (routes/__root.tsx) so this file must be served
  at request path exactly `/client.js`.
- apps/wallow-auth/vite.ssr.config.ts — SSR build. `pnpm build` emits
  apps/wallow-auth/dist/server/ssr.js (confirmed: `dist/server/ssr.js  296.41 kB`), which is
  the built form of src/ssr.tsx and exports `render(request: Request): Promise<Response>`
  (createRequestHandler + defaultRenderHandler over the TanStack router). This is the SAME
  function dev-server.ts loads via `vite.ssrLoadModule("/src/ssr.tsx")` — here you import it
  directly from the built file instead, e.g. `import { render } from "./dist/server/ssr.js"`
  (static import is fine; dist/server/ssr.js exists once `pnpm build` has run — note this in
  the Dockerfile task, 4.1b, as a build-before-run-time requirement).
- `pnpm build` (runs `vite build && vite build --config vite.ssr.config.ts`) must be run
  once locally to produce dist/ before server.ts can import from it — dist/ is gitignored
  (apps/wallow-auth/.gitignore:2) so this always happens at build/container-build time, never
  committed.

Request handling order in server.ts (replacing the current "everything but proxy is
whatever falls through" behaviour):
1. isProxyRequest(pathname) -> existing createAuthServer() proxy bridge (unchanged).
2. Exact-match static assets from dist/client (at minimum `/client.js`; check dist/client/
   for any other emitted files — e.g. sourcemaps — and serve those too, mirroring the
   content-type map pattern in apps/wallow-web/server.ts's static handler, which is a good
   reference for the read-file + content-type + 404 fallback shape even though wallow-web
   has no SSR).
3. Otherwise -> `render(request)` from dist/server/ssr.js. render() itself resolves 404 vs
   200 vs redirect (e.g. `/` -> `/login`) via the TanStack router; server.ts does not need
   its own route table.

Do not change dev-server.ts's behaviour or vite.config.ts/vite.ssr.config.ts build output
contracts — those are already correct and other code (the document shell) depends on the
`/client.js` path being stable.
acceptance_criteria:
- `pnpm --filter @bc-solutions-coder/wallow-auth build` succeeds (already does).
- `pnpm --filter @bc-solutions-coder/wallow-auth start` (or `node --import tsx server.ts`
  after build) boots and:
  - `GET /health` still returns the existing liveness payload (proxy path unaffected).
  - `GET /login` returns a 200 HTML response containing the login form's SSR markup (not a
    404), and the returned document's `<script src="/client.js">` resolves to a 200 when
    fetched.
  - `GET /` redirects to `/login` (per src/ssr.tsx's documented `/` -> `/login` contract).
  - `GET /v1/**` and `/connect/**` are still proxied (unchanged behaviour) — do not
    regress the existing proxy tests in apps/wallow-auth/src/lib/*.test.ts.
- `pnpm --filter @bc-solutions-coder/wallow-auth typecheck` and `pnpm --filter
  @bc-solutions-coder/wallow-auth test` both pass.
- No changes to dev-server.ts, vite.config.ts, or vite.ssr.config.ts's output paths/names.
notes:
Blocks 4.1b (Dockerfile can only serve real routes once this lands) and transitively 4.1d
(GREEN E2E run). Runs first in the 4.1a->4.1b->4.1c->4.1d chain (4.1c is independent and can
land any time, see its own bead).
GREEN: SSR host wiring landed and verified by driving the booted host, not just tests.

FILES:
- apps/wallow-auth/server.ts (modified) — proxy -> static -> SSR dispatch.
- apps/wallow-auth/src/lib/static-assets.ts (new) — built-asset reader.
- apps/wallow-auth/src/lib/static-assets.test.ts (new, 8 tests).

SYMBOLS (src/lib/static-assets.ts):
- interface StaticAsset { readonly contents: Buffer; readonly contentType: string }
- type StaticAssetReader = (pathname: string) => Promise<StaticAsset | undefined>
- createStaticAssetReader(rootDir: string): StaticAssetReader

TEST_STATUS=pass. pnpm --filter @bc-solutions-coder/wallow-auth test => 27 files / 675 tests pass (was 667; +8 new). typecheck clean, oxlint clean, oxfmt --check clean, build emits dist/client/client.js 481.24 kB + dist/server/ssr.js 296.41 kB unchanged.

TDD NOTE: server.ts is a listening side effect from its first line and cannot be imported under test, and vitest only collects src/**/*.test.ts. So the rule-bearing half (path -> file resolution, content-type naming, root containment, miss semantics) was extracted to src/lib/static-assets.ts and driven RED-first against a real temp dir (confirmed failing on missing module before implementing). The remaining ~30 lines of server.ts are pure wiring with no meaningful failing-test surface; they were verified instead by booting the host and driving every acceptance criterion over HTTP (evidence below).

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA — verified against a booted host (PORT=3999 pnpm exec tsx server.ts, upstream API deliberately DOWN):
- GET /health => 200 'ready' (unchanged proxy path).
- GET / => 307 -> http://127.0.0.1:3999/login (router-owned redirect contract).
- GET /login => 200 text/html, 6136 bytes of real SSR markup. Contains <script type="module" src="/client.js"></script> and testids: login-email, login-password, login-submit, login-remember-me, login-forgot-password, login-register-link, login-tab-password, login-tab-magic-link, login-tab-otp.
- GET /client.js => 200 text/javascript; charset=utf-8, 481247 bytes (the shell's hardcoded path resolves).
- All 9 auth routes render 200 HTML: /login /register /forgot-password /logout /terms /privacy /consent /reset-password /verify-email.
- GET /nope-not-a-route => 404 (router owns 404, host has no route table).
- /v1/ping, /connect/authorize, /.well-known/openid-configuration => 500 application/json (the h3 proxy failing to reach the downed upstream — i.e. still proxied, NOT falling through to SSR HTML). Proxy suites in src/lib/*.test.ts unchanged and green.
- No changes to dev-server.ts, vite.config.ts, or vite.ssr.config.ts.

THREE DECISIONS WORTH REVIEWING:

1. isProxyRequest here includes /.well-known/, unlike dev-server.ts's otherwise-identical helper which omits it. This is NOT a copy error — it is load-bearing. Until now server.ts handed EVERY path to createAuthServer(), whose router mounts /.well-known/** (auth-server.ts:148-150, comment: the discovery document's jwks_uri advertises this same origin, so signing keys must resolve too). Gating the proxy on dev-server's 3-prefix helper verbatim would have silently routed discovery + JWKS to SSR and 404'd them — a real regression on the OIDC path, which matters directly to Wallow-vec7.5.5 (repointing Oidc__Authority onto the wallow-auth origin). dev-server.ts appears to have this gap, but it is out of this bead's scope and I did not touch it. FLAGGING for a possible follow-up bead: dev dev-server.ts /.well-known/** requests fall through Vite to SSR and 404.

2. SSR entry loaded EAGERLY at boot via a runtime-URL dynamic import, with a boot-failing error message pointing at pnpm build. Two sub-decisions:
   - Eager, not lazy: a lazy load lets /health go green on an image whose render bundle is missing/broken, and the container then serves errors to every auth screen behind a healthy compose status — precisely the failure mode this bead exists to kill. Failing at boot keeps the compose healthcheck honest. RELEVANT TO 4.1b: the container MUST run pnpm build before pnpm start or it will not boot at all (loudly, by design).
   - Runtime URL (new URL("dist/server/ssr.js", import.meta.url).href) rather than the static import the bead suggested: tsconfig.json includes server.ts in typecheck, and dist/ is gitignored, so a literal import specifier makes tsc --noEmit fail on any clean checkout that has not built first. That would have broken the bead's own 'typecheck passes' criterion and CI. The SsrModule interface mirrors dev-server.ts's, so the render() call stays typed.

3. writeWebResponse now writes bytes (Buffer.from(await response.arrayBuffer())) instead of await response.text(). This host now serves built assets, and not all of them are UTF-8 (.ico today, fonts/images later) — text() would corrupt them. Byte-equivalent for the existing proxy path; null bodies short-circuit to res.end().

ISSUES: none blocking. Did not run ./scripts/run-e2e.sh (that gate is Wallow-vec7.5.1.4, and it needs 4.1b's Dockerfile/compose first). Stayed out of the concurrent 4.1c agent's files (PageObjects/*.cs, E2ETestBase.cs). Untracked DevelopmentIssuerOriginTests.cs (Wallow-67xr) left untouched and RED as instructed. title: 4.x: Repoint compose Oidc__Authority / OIDC_ISSUER overrides off the API origin onto wallow-auth
description:
Remove or repoint the docker-compose OIDC client Authority/issuer env overrides that currently pin every client at the API's OWN public origin, so the issuer-origin unification done in Phase 3 actually takes effect in the containerized stacks.

Context (found during the red phase of Wallow-vec7.4.2, 3.2 'Repoint every OIDC client Authority'). Wallow-vec7.4.2 makes Wallow.Web's OIDC client Authority fall back to ServiceUrls:AuthPublicUrl (the browser-facing unified auth origin) via a new WebOidcAuthorityResolver, but an EXPLICIT Oidc:Authority always wins over that fallback — by design, to preserve the compose override. Every compose file still sets that override to the API origin:
  • docker/docker-compose.test.yml:197        Oidc__Authority: 'http://localhost:5050'      (the API's own port)
  • docker/docker-compose.production.yml:484  Oidc__Authority: ${API_PUBLIC_URL:-https://wallow.dev/api}
  • docker/docker-compose.test.yml:235        OIDC_ISSUER: 'http://localhost:5050'          (bff-example / SDK client)
So Wallow-vec7.4.2 is INERT in every containerized stack until these lines change: the OIDC clients keep redirecting the browser to the API origin, not the unified wallow-auth origin, and Phase 3's whole point is unrealized in any deployed environment.

This was deliberately NOT fixed in Wallow-vec7.4.2. Per the Wallow-vec7.4 scout findings (note #1), the compose 'wallow-auth' service (test.yml:159, production.yml:408) is still the LEGACY Blazor Wallow.Auth container, which does NOT reverse-proxy /connect/**. Deleting the overrides before the container swap would point the OIDC clients at an app that cannot serve the OIDC endpoints, breaking login in the test and production stacks. The swap is Phase 4 work, which is why this lands here.
design:
Once apps/wallow-auth (TanStack) is the container behind the compose 'wallow-auth' service (Wallow-vec7.5.1 adds it to docker/docker-compose.test.yml; Wallow-vec7.5.3 completes the cutover):

1. docker/docker-compose.test.yml:197 and docker/docker-compose.production.yml:484 — DELETE the Oidc__Authority line, letting WebOidcAuthorityResolver fall back to ServiceUrls__AuthPublicUrl, which is ALREADY set to the correct auth origin in both files (test.yml:192 = http://localhost:5051; production.yml:480 = ${AUTH_PUBLIC_URL:-https://wallow.dev/auth}). Deleting beats repointing: it removes a duplicated origin literal and leaves ONE key per stack to repoint. If the team prefers an explicit override, set it to the same value as ServiceUrls__AuthPublicUrl instead.
2. docker/docker-compose.test.yml:235 — repoint the bff-example's OIDC_ISSUER from http://localhost:5050 to the wallow-auth origin (http://localhost:5051). The SDK's OIDC_ISSUER (packages/sdk/src/server/config.ts:72-119) is env-only with no source-config default, so this env value IS the repoint for that client.
3. LEAVE the MetadataAddress / metadata-URL half of the split ALONE — docker-compose.test.yml:198 Oidc__MetadataAddress, production.yml:485 Oidc__MetadataAddress, test.yml:239 OIDC_METADATA_URL. These deliberately point at the container-internal API (http://wallow-api:8080/..., http://host.docker.internal:5050/...) because the browser and the server reach the OP under different hostnames. Program.cs:116-134 keys its endpoint-rewrite logic off MetadataAddress differing from Authority, and the comment block at docker-compose.test.yml:216-222 explains the issuer-vs-metadata split. Breaking that split is a regression, not a cleanup.
4. Verify the OpenIddict issuer and each client's Authority RESOLVE TO THE SAME ORIGIN per stack, or ID token validation fails on the iss claim. After Wallow-vec7.4.1 the issuer derives from Wallow.Api's top-level AuthUrl: test.yml:133 = http://localhost:5051, production.yml:365 = ${AUTH_PUBLIC_URL}. Both already match their stack's ServiceUrls__AuthPublicUrl — so once the overrides are gone, issuer and Authority agree with no further edits.
5. Docs (bd memory wallow-web-local-dev-oidc-env-apps-wallow): apps/wallow-web/README.md:157 and :185 still document OIDC_ISSUER=http://localhost:5001. Repoint to the wallow-auth origin once Wallow-vec7.5.4 assigns the dev port.

Depends on Wallow-vec7.4.4 (/.well-known/** proxy): the SDK client at test.yml:235 sets an explicit OIDC_METADATA_URL so it does not need the proxied discovery route, but any client relying on the ${issuer}/.well-known/openid-configuration default does. Coordinate with Wallow-vec7.5.4 (dev port / Dev AuthUrl), which is the same repoint for the Development environment rather than the compose stacks.
acceptance_criteria: In docker/docker-compose.test.yml and docker/docker-compose.production.yml, no OIDC client's Authority/issuer resolves to the API's own origin: the Oidc__Authority overrides are removed (or set to the auth origin) and the bff-example's OIDC_ISSUER points at the wallow-auth origin. The Oidc__MetadataAddress / OIDC_METADATA_URL internal-discovery values are unchanged. The OpenIddict issuer and every client Authority resolve to the same origin within each stack. ./scripts/run-e2e.sh green for the auth + BFF login flows against the containerized wallow-auth (this is the only real verification — the change is env-only and no unit test covers it; per bd memory ci-s-e2e-job-is-permanently-disabled the E2E job is disabled in CI, so this MUST be run locally). dotnet format api/Wallow.slnx clean.
