title: 3.x: Proxy /.well-known/** through wallow-auth for OIDC discovery
description:
Extend apps/wallow-auth's reverse-proxy route table to include /.well-known/** so OpenIddict's discovery document resolves through the unified auth origin, not just the two prefixes it proxies today.

Context (verified by the verifier of Wallow-vec7.4.1, which closed CLOSE): that task changed the advertised OpenIddict issuer (api/src/Modules/Identity/Wallow.Identity.Infrastructure/Extensions/OpenIddictIssuerResolver.cs) to derive from the top-level 'AuthUrl' config key (the unified apps/wallow-auth origin) instead of the API's own request origin, once configured. The TypeScript SDK (packages/sdk/src/server/config.ts:113-114, loadBffConfigFromEnv) defaults OIDC_METADATA_URL to `${OIDC_ISSUER}/.well-known/openid-configuration` whenever OIDC_METADATA_URL is not explicitly set. Once any OIDC client's OIDC_ISSUER / Oidc:Authority is repointed at the wallow-auth origin (task 3.2, Wallow-vec7.4.2) WITHOUT an explicit metadata override, discovery fetches will 404: apps/wallow-auth/src/lib/auth-server.ts's router (createAuthServer) only mounts router.use("/v1/**", proxy) and router.use("/connect/**", proxy) — confirmed by reading the file directly, there is no /.well-known/** route, so a discovery request falls through to the app's catch-all 404.
design:
Add a third proxy route in apps/wallow-auth/src/lib/auth-server.ts's createAuthServer function, alongside the existing router.use("/v1/**", proxy) and router.use("/connect/**", proxy) calls (~lines 124-125): router.use("/.well-known/**", proxy). Reuse the SAME createProxyHandler(apiInternalUrl) reverse-proxy handler already used for the other two prefixes — no new logic needed, this is purely adding a third mount point so the existing verbatim pass-through (method/path/query/body/Cookie header in, status/body/Set-Cookie headers out) also covers /.well-known/openid-configuration and any other well-known document the API serves.

Add/extend tests in apps/wallow-auth/src/lib/auth-server.test.ts mirroring the existing /v1/** or /connect/** proxy test cases, asserting a request to /.well-known/openid-configuration on the wallow-auth server is forwarded to apiInternalUrl and the upstream response (status, body, headers) is relayed verbatim.

Do NOT change packages/sdk/src/server/config.ts — the existing explicit OIDC_METADATA_URL override pattern (already used by every docker-compose OIDC client today) must keep working unchanged. This task only makes the SDK's *default* (no explicit OIDC_METADATA_URL) also resolve correctly through the wallow-auth proxy, which is what the Wallow-vec7.4 (Phase 3) acceptance criterion 'discovery document resolves through the proxy origin' requires.
acceptance_criteria: New/updated test(s) in apps/wallow-auth/src/lib/auth-server.test.ts verify /.well-known/** requests are reverse-proxied to apiInternalUrl and responses (status/body/headers) relayed verbatim, mirroring existing proxy test coverage for /v1/** and /connect/**; pnpm --filter @bc-solutions-coder/wallow-auth test green; pnpm --filter @bc-solutions-coder/wallow-auth typecheck green; pnpm lint clean; a local/manual check (or ./scripts/run-e2e.sh once wallow-auth is wired into the E2E stack) confirms GET {wallow-auth origin}/.well-known/openid-configuration returns the OpenIddict discovery document unchanged from the upstream API's own response; commit message e.g. 'feat(wallow-auth): proxy well-known discovery through unified origin'.

The 2 discovery tests live in apps/wallow-auth/src/lib/auth-server.test.ts and are STAYING THERE. They were written under 7.4.2 only because its red phase hit the same gap first; the file is the one this bead's own DESIGN section names, so nothing needs to move. THIS BEAD IS NOW A GREEN-PHASE-ONLY TASK: the one-line route add.

WHAT EXISTS (all committed to the working tree, currently failing = correct RED):
• describe('auth-server discovery passthrough') with 2 tests:
  1. 'proxies GET /.well-known/openid-configuration to upstream' — asserts 200, body relayed verbatim, and lastRequest.target === '/.well-known/openid-configuration'.
  2. 'proxies the whole /.well-known subtree, including the jwks endpoint' — same for /.well-known/jwks.
• The fake upstream server in that file now serves both routes (DISCOVERY_DOCUMENT and JWKS_DOCUMENT consts near the top).
• The existing dispatch test title was updated to 'returns 404 for paths outside /health, /v1, /connect, and /.well-known' (its case is still /dashboard -> 404, unchanged behaviour).

WHY THE TESTS PIN THE SUBTREE WILDCARD AND NOT JUST openid-configuration — matters for the implementation:
This bead's DESIGN already says router.use('/.well-known/**', proxy), which is right, but the reason is worth stating: the discovery document's jwks_uri points at the SAME origin (/.well-known/jwks by OpenIddict default), and a client that resolves discovery through the proxy then fetches signing keys from that advertised jwks_uri. Proxying only /.well-known/openid-configuration would return a discovery document whose jwks_uri 404s — signature validation then fails, and it would fail LATER and more confusingly than a missing discovery route. Test 2 exists to stop a narrower exact-route fix from passing.

Zero regressions in the other 660. oxlint + oxfmt --check on the touched file: clean.

SO THE GREEN PHASE HERE IS: add router.use('/.well-known/**', proxy) alongside the two existing mounts in createAuthServer (auth-server.ts:124-125), reusing the same createProxyHandler(apiInternalUrl) — then those 2 tests go green. Do NOT edit the test file. Do NOT touch packages/sdk/src/server/config.ts (this bead's design correctly forbids it).

DEPENDENCY DIRECTION IS ALREADY CORRECT — no new edge needed. This bead BLOCKS Wallow-vec7.4.2 (verified via bd show on both). Without this the doc comment would have been stale/wrong the moment the route landed. This mirrors the red phase's update of the dispatch test title to 'returns 404 for paths outside /health, /v1, /connect, and /.well-known'.

title: 1.5: Add getCurrentUser auth-state facade method (unblocks InvitationLanding)
description: Add ONE method getCurrentUser(): Promise<CurrentUserResponse | null> to the SDK auth facade (packages/sdk/src/auth-client.ts), answering 'is this browser signed in'. Closes the auth-state gap the .3.9 red agent found: apps/wallow-auth has no server session and the auth cookie is HttpOnly, so no existing facade method can answer it. Unblocks Wallow-vec7.3.9 (InvitationLanding), the ONLY screen needing the seam.
design:
APPROVED SEAM (per scout on Wallow-vec7.3 / .3.9): probe the EXISTING GET /v1/identity/users/me through the EXISTING h3 /v1/** passthrough proxy. 200 => signed in (return CurrentUserResponse), 401 => anonymous (return null, MUST NOT throw). NO new API endpoint, NO new h3 /auth/session route, NO session store, NO BFF getUser() model — wallow-auth is the auth origin, not a BFF consumer.
WHY IT WORKS: UsersController.GetCurrentUser (UsersController.cs:72-82) is controller-level [Authorize], no extra permission; it IS cookie-authenticated via the API's SmartScheme policy scheme (IdentityInfrastructureExtensions.cs:255-327) which forwards to IdentityConstants.ApplicationScheme when no Bearer header is present; anonymous yields a CLEAN 401 not a 302 (OnRedirectToLogin overridden to StatusCode=401, :175-179); auth-server.ts createProxyHandler already forwards inbound Cookie verbatim => ZERO changes to lib/auth-server.ts.
IMPL: wrap generated op getV1IdentityUsersMe (generated/sdk.gen.ts:2191), typed CurrentUserResponse (types.gen.ts:299). The existing unwrap() THROWS on every non-2xx, so this method must BYPASS/soften unwrap for 401 only — anonymous is an expected state, not an error. Every other status keeps throwing WallowError (no error swallowing).
APP SIDE: apps/wallow-auth/src/lib/wallow-auth-sdk.ts exposes auth: createAuthClient() wholesale, so the method rides along with no source change; keep that file's test method inventory accurate.
SECURITY: HttpOnly preserved — JS never reads the cookie, it only observes the 200/401 of its OWN same-origin request. SameSite=Lax + CORS mean an attacker page cannot probe auth state cross-origin. Result is a UI AFFORDANCE ONLY; POST /v1/identity/invitations/{token}/accept is [Authorize]-enforced server-side regardless.
acceptance_criteria: getCurrentUser exists on AuthClient with signature getCurrentUser(): Promise<CurrentUserResponse | null>; delegates to getV1IdentityUsersMe; 200 returns the CurrentUserResponse body; 401 resolves null and NEVER throws; non-401 failures (403/500/network) still throw WallowError with status/code preserved; no change to lib/auth-server.ts; HttpOnly not weakened; SDK suite + wallow-auth suite green with no regression; typecheck + oxlint + oxfmt clean.
notes:

title: fix(identity): requestMembership is [Authorize] but the registration caller is anonymous
description: Observed by Wallow-vec7.3.8 (Register screen port) while porting the org-domain-match interstitial ACCEPT path. api/src/Modules/Identity/Wallow.Identity.Api/Controllers/MembershipRequestsController.cs is decorated class-level [Authorize] (line 16). RequestMembership (POST /v1/identity/membership-requests, line 26) carries no [AllowAnonymous]. The registration flow calls it immediately after Register returns, while the caller is still anonymous (no cookie/token yet — the user has not verified email or logged in), so the call gets 401 before reaching the action. Contrast: AccountController.Register is explicitly [AllowAnonymous]. Second latent fault: the action body does Guid.Parse(User.GetUserId()!) — for an anonymous principal GetUserId() is null, so even if authorization were bypassed this would throw rather than fail cleanly.
design: NOT INVESTIGATED — filed only, per instruction. Needs a real decision, do not blind-fix by slapping [AllowAnonymous] on it: an anonymous membership-request endpoint lets an unauthenticated caller enqueue membership requests for arbitrary email domains (spam/enumeration surface). Options to weigh: (a) have Register create the membership request server-side inside the already-anonymous Register action using the just-created user id, so the endpoint stays authorized; (b) a short-lived registration ticket scoped to the new user, mirroring the existing MfaPartial/exchange-ticket pattern; (c) defer the interstitial until after email verification when the caller IS authenticated. Option (a) matches how Register already resolves the tenant and adds org membership.
acceptance_criteria: The registration-time membership request either succeeds for the newly-registered user or is deliberately removed from the anonymous flow; no anonymous caller can enqueue a membership request for an arbitrary domain; regression test covers the registration-time path.
notes:

=== DESIGN DECISION MADE (the bead said "needs a real decision — do not blind-fix") ===
Chose OPTION (a) from the bead, refined after reading the code. NOT [AllowAnonymous].

The endpoint POST /v1/identity/membership-requests STAYS class-level [Authorize] with no
[AllowAnonymous]. The anonymous registration flow instead OPTS IN on the already-anonymous
POST /v1/identity/auth/register call, and the server creates the request for the user it just
created. Key security property: the anonymous caller NEVER names the domain — it is derived
server-side from the address that caller actually registered, and it must match a VERIFIED

title: 1.4: Preserve ProblemDetails error code through toWallowError (unblocks screen error mapping)
description: Three screen ports (.3.2 ResetPassword, .3.6 MfaChallenge, .3.8 Register) each degraded their error handling because WallowError.code was always UNKNOWN for auth endpoints, forcing status-only narrowing. ROOT CAUSE (differs from the original premise): the seam was NOT dropping a code the API sent under a standard member. The Identity auth endpoints (AccountController) do not emit RFC 7807 problem details at all — they return a bare anonymous object { succeeded: false, error: "invalid_code" }. toWallowError/parseProblemDetails probed only extensions.code and code, so the machine-readable token sitting under 'error' was never read. The code was always on the wire; the seam looked in the wrong place.
design: Add 'error' as a THIRD probe in readCode, in both seams (packages/sdk/src/auth-client.ts toWallowError and packages/sdk/src/server/errors.ts parseProblemDetails). Precedence, most authoritative first: extensions.code > code > error. Probing 'error' last means real problem details always win, so the change is purely additive — it only fires where the code was previously UNKNOWN. Non-string members are ignored rather than coerced (OAuth-style bodies can carry an object under 'error'; a stringified object is not a code). ProblemDetails interface documents the error/succeeded members.
acceptance_criteria: WallowError.code carries the API's error token for auth endpoints; real problem-details codes still win over a co-occurring error member; non-string error ignored (stays UNKNOWN); SDK suite green with no regression.
notes:
GREEN: FILES=packages/sdk/src/auth-client.ts (readCode), packages/sdk/src/server/errors.ts (readCode + ProblemDetails iface), packages/sdk/src/auth-client.test.ts (+5), packages/sdk/src/server/errors.test.ts (+3).

FINDING (premise correction): the epic assumed toWallowError DROPS a code the API sends. It does not. Both seams already probed extensions.code and code correctly. The real cause is on the API side of the seam: the Identity auth endpoints emit NO problem details — AccountController returns a bare anonymous object, e.g. Unauthorized(new { succeeded = false, error = "no_mfa_session" }). The token was always on the wire under 'error'; the seam never looked there. So this was fixable in the SDK with no API change, and no API-side bead was needed for the code-delivery gap.

CHANGE: readCode now probes extensions.code > code > error, in BOTH seams. Purely additive: 'error' is probed LAST, so real problem details always win; it only fires where code was previously UNKNOWN. Non-string 'error' is ignored, not coerced (OAuth-style bodies carry an object there).

TESTS: 414/414 pass (was 406/406 — +8, no regression). tsc --noEmit clean, oxlint clean, oxfmt --check clean across packages+apps.
Tests genuinely bind: 5 of the 8 are guard tests that PASSED BEFORE the fix (precedence over code/extensions.code, non-string ignored) — they exist to stop the fix over-reaching, and a naive impl that read 'error' first or coerced it would fail them. The 3 that were RED before the fix are the new capability.

SYMBOLS: no public API change. WallowError{status,code,title,detail} unchanged; only the VALUE of .code improves.

CAVEAT for consumers — .code is NOT a guaranteed-stable token on register. description: Remove the apps/wallow-auth/src/router.tsx collision that blocks parallel execution of the 15 screen-port tasks (Wallow-vec7.3.1-.3.15).   Scout finding #5 was right that nothing asserts the issuer today, and IdentityInfrastructureExtensions is [ExcludeFromCodeCoverage] + needs full DI/DB to construct — not unit-testable. So the red phase extracts the ONE decision that actually matters from IdentityInfrastructureExtensions.cs:70-74 into a pure, testable function: given configuration, what issuer do we advertise?
  Today that code is: issuer = configuration["OpenIddict:Issuer"]; if non-empty -> SetIssuer(new Uri(issuer)). Scout confirmed OpenIddict:Issuer is BLANK in every checked-in appsettings*.json and is only ever set by docker-compose env. So in source config the issuer today silently falls back to the API's OWN request origin — which is exactly the bug this bead exists to fix.

BEHAVIOUR THE TESTS PIN (the spec for the green phase):
  1. Explicit OpenIddict:Issuer wins (preserves the docker-compose/E2E env override; do not regress it).
  2. OpenIddict:Issuer unset/blank -> fall back to top-level "AuthUrl" = the unified auth origin. Blank-string handling is explicitly pinned (2 tests) because blank is the checked-in default and a null-only check would defeat the whole fallback.
  3. Neither configured -> return null (caller skips SetIssuer; OpenIddict keeps deriving from the request origin — preserves today's behaviour for forks that configure nothing).
  4. Path-base origins preserved (https://wallow.dev/auth) — production already uses a path-bearing issuer (${API_PUBLIC_URL:-https://wallow.dev/api}), so this must not be reduced to scheme+host.
  5. Relative or malformed value -> InvalidOperationException whose message NAMES the offending config key (asserted by wildcard on the key). Today new Uri(issuer) throws a bare UriFormatException with no key context.

WHY "AuthUrl" (top-level) AND NOT ServiceUrls:AuthUrl — decision worth reviewing:
  Grep shows the two keys mean different things and are inconsistent in Dev:
    • top-level "AuthUrl" (appsettings.Development.json:66 = http://localhost:5002) is THE AUTH APP ORIGIN. AccountController.cs:978-981 (GetRequiredAuthUrl) and AuthorizationController.cs:51,161 already redirect the browser to it for the login UI, and it already throws if unset.
    • "ServiceUrls:AuthUrl" (appsettings.Development.json:63 = http://localhost:5001) is the API's own port in Dev and is consumed by Wallow.Web's OIDC client (Program.cs:109) — that's task 3.2's surface, not this one.
  Under the migration the browser reaches BOTH the login UI and the proxied /connect/** on the SAME wallow-auth origin, so the issuer is definitionally the top-level AuthUrl. Deriving it means a fork repoints ONE key and the issuer follows. If the team disagrees and wants ServiceUrls:AuthUrl instead, say so now — it is a one-line change to the constant plus the test's key reference.

DIVERGENCE 1 — NO CODE MAP ON VERIFY (deliberate opposite of .3.12). SIGNED OFF. Verified against the endpoint myself, not from the report. PasswordlessService.ValidateOtpAsync returns exactly TWO tokens — 'Code expired or not found.' and 'Invalid code.' — both on 401 (AccountController.cs:866-877), and both mean the same thing to a user: that code did not work, type another. So:
• A code map here would be OBSERVATIONALLY IDENTICAL to the status rule for every input the API can produce => unbindable, and faking a test to bind it would be dishonest. Contrast .3.12, where 401 carries THREE tokens with TWO meanings ('Invalid token format.' vs spent) and IS bindable — I confirmed both endpoints and the asymmetry is real, not rationalised.
• A code map would also be strictly WORSE: an unrecognised future token would fall to the generic tail and hide the retry.
• Critically, the choice is NOT unpinned. test:773 ('unrecognised token on a 401 reads as a bad code') FAILS a code-mapped implementation, and test:811 (500 -> generic) FAILS a blanket-401 one. otp-result.ts:145-158 checks status===undefined FIRST so a network rejection cannot read as 'not 401 => generic'. This is the memory 'status rule only where status identifies a failure alone' applied correctly. The two beads diverge because the ENDPOINTS diverge — that is the right reason.

DIVERGENCE 2 — rememberMe OMITTED. MY CALL: CORRECT, NOT A REGRESSION WORTH REVERTING. Scrutinised hard against the oracle:
• REACHABILITY IS NARROW AND THE ORACLE'S IS ACCIDENTAL. Login.razor renders the Remember-me checkbox ONLY inside the password tab (:86-92). _rememberMe is shared field state and SwitchTab (:302-309) resets _errorMessage/_magicLinkSent/_otpSent/_otpCode but NOT _rememberMe. So the oracle's OTP verify sends whatever an INVISIBLE control on another tab happened to leave behind. The oracle author enumerated what to reset and missed this one; the field is consumed on a tab where it is not rendered. That asymmetry is the smell, and .3.12 makes the identical call on magic-link verify (which the endpoint likewise defaults false, AccountController.cs:840).
• THE DEFAULT PATH IS BYTE-IDENTICAL. A user who goes straight to the OTP tab gets rememberMe=false in BOTH oracle and port (VerifyOtpRequest.RememberMe defaults false, AccountController.cs:876). The ONLY divergent user is one who ticked a box on the password tab, switched away, and signed in with a code — at which moment the control is neither visible nor actionable.
• THE DIRECTION IS FAIL-SAFE. The loss is a SHORTER session, never a longer one. A remember-me divergence that erred the other way (persisting when the user did not ask) would be a security bug and I would reject it. This one costs an occasional re-login.
• IT IS COHERENT WITH THE PORT'S ACCEPTED ARCHITECTURE. The panel already holds email as panel-local state (necessary: ValidateOtpAsync keys Redis on the send address, PasswordlessService.cs:161, so the two halves must agree). Once tab state is panel-local and unmount-on-switch, a shared cross-tab _rememberMe has no coherent home. Honouring hidden state would be the inconsistency.
• IT IS DISCLOSED AND PINNED, not silent: OtpLoginForm.tsx:162-170 documents it, and test:590 asserts toHaveBeenCalledWith({email, code}) — an EXACT match, so re-adding rememberMe fails the suite rather than sliding in.
RESIDUAL, NON-BLOCKING: OTP sign-in now has no way to be persistent at all. The feature-preserving fix is a panel-local Remember-me checkbox on the OTP tab — but that is UI the oracle does not have, i.e. beyond-oracle scope, not this bead's. RECOMMEND the coordinator file a follow-up bead ('OTP tab has no remember-me control; oracle only leaked one cross-tab') so the capability gap is tracked rather than lost. That is a product decision, not a port defect, and does not block CLOSE.

ORACLE DIVERGENCES / FINDINGS (all verified by reading source, not assumed):

1. *** BLOCKER-ISH: THE AUTH-STATE GAP — COORDINATOR CALL NEEDED BEFORE GREEN CAN WIRE THE ROUTE. ***
InvitationLanding.razor:7,130 is the ONLY oracle in the phase injecting AuthenticationStateProvider — Blazor Server holds the cookie principal server-side for free. apps/wallow-auth has NO equivalent: h3 is a passthrough proxy with no session store (lib/auth-server.ts), the auth cookie is HttpOnly, and NONE of the SDK auth facade's 23 methods answers 'is this browser signed in' (checked auth-client.ts; the only [Authorize]d op exposed is the destructive POST /auth/sign-out; getMatchingOrgByDomain + redirect-uri/validate are both [AllowAnonymous]).
=> I made `isAuthenticated` a PROP of InvitationScreen and pinned BOTH branches against it (satisfies the acceptance criterion). I deliberately did NOT spec who computes it at the route — pinning a guess would bake a seam green cannot honour. Options for the coordinator: (a) add getCurrentUser()/session probe to packages/sdk auth facade — but packages/sdk is out of Phase 2 scope; (b) add an h3 /auth/session probe endpoint in lib/auth-server.ts — shared file, not mine. Needs a decision or a follow-up bead; otherwise green must ship the authenticated branch unreachable (route hardcoding isAuthenticated=false).

2. FOUR ORACLE BRANCHES COLLAPSE INTO REJECTIONS — mapped on STATUS, not code (this is the exception to the 'key on codes' guidance; verified the endpoints emit no codes at all).
AuthApiClient swallows non-2xx into sentinels (VerifyInvitationAsync -> null on any failure, AuthApiClient.cs:297-312; AcceptInvitationAsync -> IsSuccessStatusCode, :314-322), so the oracle forks sentinel-vs-catch and gives each its own copy (4 messages). The TS facade's unwrap() THROWS on every non-2xx, so each pair arrives as ONE rejection and that fork is gone. What survives is .status (toWallowError always populates it, falling back to Response.status then 500).
Both endpoints send NO machine-readable code: GET /v1/identity/invitations/verify/{token} has exactly ONE failure return, bare `NotFound()` with no body (InvitationsController.cs:71-80); POST /{token}/accept throws EntityNotFoundException / aggregate rejection (:82-91). readCode() finds nothing -> every rejection is code:'UNKNOWN' (bd memory wallow-auth-auth-client-ts-wallowerror-code-loss). A CODE-keyed mapping here would collapse all four messages into the generic one. So: 404 -> 'not valid/already used' resp. 'expired or already used'; anything else -> the 'catch' copy. Tests pin code:'UNKNOWN' on the rejection fixture so nobody keys on a code that never arrives.

3. INERT `email=` PARAM (oracle wart, ported deliberately + pinned as inert). Kept (oracle link contract, harmless, plausible follow-up) but the test comment says INERT so nobody reads it as proof the address prefills. Candidate follow-up bead: have /register honour email.

4. NO isSafeReturnUrl GUARD ON THIS SCREEN — and that is correct, not an oversight. The oracle's only [SupplyParameterFromQuery] is Token; this screen ACCEPTS no returnUrl, it BUILDS two (/invitation?token=...), safe by construction. The attacker-controlled part is the token, so instead of a guard the tests pin that the token is percent-encoded INTO the returnUrl (a token like 'x&returnUrl=//evil.example' yields exactly ONE returnUrl param, ours) and that the result still satisfies the real isSafeReturnUrl rule (restated locally, not stubbed true).

Accept-success is a FULL navigation `globalThis.location.href = '/'` (oracle NavigateTo('/', forceLoad:true), :179), matching the MfaEnroll HOME_HREF precedent; the reload is load-bearing since accepting changes tenant membership.

Expiry precedes the auth branch (:46-54), so an expired invitation offers no sign-in path either.

LIVE BUG FOUND IN THIS CLOSED BEAD'S SHIPPED CODE -> fixed under Wallow-vec7.3.17 (full report there). Raised by the .3.10 security adjudication's Advisory. VERDICT: REAL, and total for the affected cohort.

WHAT WAS WRONG: this bead's RETURNURL GUARD decision ('REFUSE, don't sanitize... Refused ON MOUNT -> navigate({href:'/error?reason=invalid_redirect_uri'})') was right in PRINCIPLE and wrong in RANGE. The screen navigates to returnUrl itself (globalThis.location.href = returnUrl on the no-ticket branch), so per the .3.10 governing rule -- guard where the CLIENT picks the destination, defer where the SERVER does -- a guard genuinely belongs here. But isSafeReturnUrl accepts ONLY relative paths, and AccountController.cs:313/335 send this screen an ABSOLUTE returnUrl for every external-login MFA user (L273-277 normalizes through IsAllowedAsync, which REQUIRES UriKind.Absolute, or the absolute authUrl fallback). Accept-sets provably disjoint => 100% of external-login + MFA users were bounced to /error BEFORE the code field rendered. They could not sign in at all. Password users were never affected (Login.razor:509 threads a RELATIVE returnUrl).

The .3.10 red-phase agent found the identical isSafeReturnUrl-vs-IsAllowedAsync mismatch on the accept-terms screen and refused to wire the guard in. The same wire evidence applied to THIS screen -- .3.10's own adjudication even cites 'mfa-challenge (MfaChallengeForm.tsx:297-308) navigates TO returnUrl itself -> guard is the only authority -> isSafeReturnUrl correct there', which is half right: a guard is correct here, but not THAT guard. The screens differ in whether a guard is needed; they did NOT differ in what the server sends.

HOW IT SURVIVED REVIEW: this bead's own test 'refuses an absolute return url' (test:595) PINNED the dead-end, using https://evil.example.com/steal. Refusing that URL is correct, so the test looked like a security assertion -- while the same code path also refused the legitimate allow-listed absolute the server actually sends. A single test with only a hostile fixture made a total outage look like a feature. LESSON: an open-redirect guard test needs BOTH poles -- the attack that must be refused AND the real traffic that must pass. A guard tested only against attacks cannot distinguish 'correct' from 'refuses everything'.

ALSO CONFIRMED (an oracle wart this bead did not catch): MfaChallenge.razor:157 'safeReturnUrl = IsSafe(ReturnUrl) ? ReturnUrl : null' means the BLAZOR oracle is broken here too -- an absolute returnUrl nulls out and falls to L170's 'No ReturnUrl -- direct login' branch, so external-login MFA users verify successfully and strand on a success screen with no redirect. The port faithfully inherited a broken assumption and hardened it into a pre-verify dead-end (strictly worse: the Blazor user at least ends up signed in). The bead's own note flagged 2 oracle warts; this was a third, in the returnUrl handling both the oracle and the port got wrong the same way.

FIX (Wallow-vec7.3.17, GREEN, 46/46): guard KEPT, taught the shape the server really sends. localDecisionOf -> accept (nullish / relative-safe, no probe) | refuse ('', IsNullOrEmpty parity) | ask (absolute) ; 'ask' -> auth.validateRedirectUri fail-closed on strict { allowed: true }, the .3.5 Logout precedent and the same allow-list that admitted the value at L274. Renders nothing while pending. evil.example.com and //evil.example.com still refused. No regression: SDK 429/429, typecheck/oxlint/oxfmt clean. Bead stays CLOSED; the fix is tracked on .3.17.
SPUN OUT: Wallow-vec7.3.18 (P3) -- exchange-ticket's Url.IsLocalUrl gate refuses the same absolute returnUrl its own controller sent, so the external user now signs in but lands on authUrl. Fail-closed, small impact today, API-side.

PORT DECISION — status-narrowing. Unlike .3.6 (401 ambiguous), the statuses here are CLEAN:

Retrying cannot mint a cookie, so 'try again' loops the user forever.

=== FINDING 1: error-branch switch is NOT portable as written (verified in source, not assumed) ===
Oracle switches on result.Error ('invalid_token' -> 'invalid or has expired'; _ -> 'Failed to verify email').   anything else -> 'An error occurred while verifying your email...'   (oracle catch arm)

=== FINDING 2: success is 'resolved', not 'succeeded === true' ===
Oracle reads result.Succeeded. Through this seam that read is redundant and is deliberately NOT spec'd: every 200 from the endpoint is Ok(new { succeeded = true }) (no 200-with-false exists), and every falsy case is a 400 unwrap() already turned into a throw. A resolved promise IS success.

The spec APPLIES the guard here too (unsafe returnUrl dropped -> plain /login), matching the sibling. Strictly narrows behavior, forwards nothing hostile. NOT the refuse-vs-sanitize case (bd memory returnurl-guard-refuse-dont-sanitize): nothing navigates on this page, the screen only declines to hand a hostile value to the next screen — so /error?reason=invalid_redirect_uri would be wrong here. Same reasoning for VerifyEmailConfirm's signin-link, where the oracle already does exactly this.

• ErrorPage reason->message map is a `ReadonlyMap`, NOT a Record. `reason` is
  attacker-supplied (/error?reason=<anything> is a URL anyone can send a victim); a record
  lookup resolves INHERITED keys, so ?reason=toString would find Object.prototype.toString

  a test (the spec's hostile input is "you-have-been-hacked-call-555-1234", which a Record
  survives) — flagging so it is not "simplified" back into an object literal.
• VerifyEmailConfirm uses useQuery with `enabled: linkIsComplete` (the oracle's
  IsNullOrEmpty guard, which runs BEFORE its try block) so a malformed link never reaches
  the network, and `retry: false` — a single-use token is not retryable; a 400 will never
  become a 200. `!linkIsComplete` is checked BEFORE `isPending` because a disabled query is
  also pending: the missing-parameter path must never show "Verifying your email...".
• Privacy/Terms sections are DATA (arrays), not 9 hand-written JSX blocks — the failure
  mode of porting a wall of text by eye is silently dropping one. Prose transcribed verbatim

  absent — a mangled link must render the screen and hit its own guard, not throw a
  search-validation error at a user who clicked a link in their email.

=== PORT DECISIONS GREEN MUST HONOUR (each is pinned by a test) ===

1. *** ORIGIN DIVERGENCE — the load-bearing decision, do NOT copy the oracle here. ***
Consent.razor:70-80 ends AppendToReturnUrl by prepending `ApiBaseUrl` (Configuration["ApiBaseUrl"] ?? "http://localhost:5001"). Its own comment gives the reason: the Auth app origin "does not host /connect/authorize". THAT PREMISE IS FALSE IN THIS APP. apps/wallow-auth's h3 server (src/lib/auth-server.ts) is a PASSTHROUGH REVERSE PROXY mounting /connect/** and /v1/** at ROOT — the same fact behind bd memory `wallow-auth-same-origin-baseurl-apps-wallow-auth` (why the facade configures baseUrl:'/' not '/api'). So the screen passes origin `""`:
  oidc.buildConsentSubmitUrl("", returnUrl, granted)
Pinned by 'builds the URL same-origin, granting/refusing consent'. Porting the prepend would (a) send the browser cross-origin for a request the proxy exists to keep same-origin, dropping the SameSite auth cookie /connect/authorize needs, and (b) reintroduce an ApiBaseUrl knob this app deliberately lacks — its only API URL, WALLOW_API_INTERNAL_URL, is a SERVER-side internal address (http://wallow-api under Aspire), not browser-resolvable at all.

2. NAVIGATION: full navigation via `window.location.href = url`, NOT router.navigate — /connect/authorize is served by the h3 proxy, not the client route tree.
JSDOM SEAM (probed empirically, don't re-derive): `vi.spyOn(window.location, "assign")` FAILS here ("Cannot redefine property"), but `location` is a configurable accessor and globalThis===window under jsdom, so `vi.stubGlobal("location", {href:""})` works. Tests use a stubLocation() helper + afterEach(vi.unstubAllGlobals). This is why the spec pins `.href =` assignment rather than `.assign()`.

3. OPEN-REDIRECT GUARD (the acceptance criterion; NOT in the oracle — the oracle applies NO guard on this screen). buildConsentSubmitUrl THROWS TypeError on a present-but-unsafe returnUrl (bd memory returnurl-guard-refuse-dont-sanitize). The screen refuses EARLY, on mount — before rendering a prompt and before fetching — per Login.razor L533-540, the one oracle call site that checks IsSafe before building a nav URL and bails to /error?reason=invalid_redirect_uri. Refusing at click time would mean rendering an Approve button whose destination we already know we'd refuse to build.
Bail target: navigate({ href: "/error?reason=invalid_redirect_uri" }) — `href` NOT `to`+`search`, per bd memory tanstack-router-redirect-to-an-unregistered-route-use-href-not-to AND because /error's validateSearch is being written CONCURRENTLY by Wallow-vec7.3.3; href decouples us from that in-flight shape.
Unsafe set pinned: "//evil.example/steal", "https://evil.example/steal", "javascript:alert(1)", "" (empty string is PRESENT-but-unsafe → IsNullOrWhiteSpace → guard fires; it is NOT the nullish-fallback case). Nullish returnUrl → "/" fallback and the guard must NOT fire ('falls back to the root when the link carries no returnUrl' asserts navigate not called).

4. MISSING LOADING STATE — an oracle WART, deliberately not ported. The oracle renders its error block on `_consentInfo is null`, which is ALSO true while the request is in flight — so the Blazor screen flashes "Unable to load consent information" at every user before its own fetch resolves. The scout inventory has no loading testid because the oracle has no loading state. The port renders NOTHING in flight: no error, no prompt. Fixes the flash without inventing a testid, and keeps consent-error meaning "this failed" not "this failed or hasn't happened yet". A port that copies the null-check literally fails exactly the two 'loading' absence tests.

5. displayName FALLBACK: ConsentInfoResponse.displayName is `null | string`. The oracle interpolates it unguarded, so null yields " is requesting access" — a prompt that doesn't say WHO is asking. Port falls back to clientId. Consent to an unnamed party is not consent.

6. ERROR STATE — null becomes a rejection at this seam. Oracle's _consentInfo is null in 2 cases, both → consent-error: (a) no client_id (OnInitializedAsync skips the call), (b) request failed — AuthApiClient.GetConsentInfoAsync (AuthApiClient.cs:397-416) returns null on ANY non-2xx. Case (b) arrives as a REJECTION here because unwrap() throws instead of returning null. NO status narrowing needed: this oracle has exactly ONE error message for every failure, so the WallowError code-loss gotcha (bd memory wallow-auth-auth-client-ts-wallowerror-code-loss) costs this screen NOTHING — unlike .3.2/.3.3. Empty-string clientId treated as missing.

7. getConsentInfo ARGS: oracle passes Array.Empty<string>(). Asserted on the FIRST arg only — the facade treats omitted `scopes` and `[]` identically (auth-client.ts:185-195, `scopes?.length ? … : …`), so pinning toHaveBeenCalledWith(CLIENT_ID) would fail an impl that faithfully passed the oracle's empty array. title: 0.3: Proxy server bridge with per-request cookie passthrough
description: The highest-value task in the whole migration: prove the reverse proxy forwards Set-Cookie per request with no relay, replacing the entire Blazor cookie-relay subsystem. Create createAuthServer(config) — an h3 app dispatching /health, /v1/**, /connect/** — with pure passthrough proxying to Wallow.Api.
design: Create apps/wallow-auth/src/lib/auth-server.ts + apps/wallow-auth/src/lib/auth-server.test.ts. Model on apps/wallow-web/src/lib/bff-server.ts's handleBffRequest structure, but this is simpler: pure passthrough proxy, not a BFF token tunnel. Behavior: /health -> 200 'ready'; /v1/** and /connect/** -> reverse-proxy to apiInternalUrl, forwarding method/path/query/body and inbound Cookie header, copying back upstream status/body and ALL Set-Cookie headers verbatim (use getSetCookie()/append so multiple cookies survive, no relay store/jar); everything else -> 404. Read apiInternalUrl from config (env WALLOW_API_INTERNAL_URL, Aspire default http://wallow-api). Expose handle(request): Promise<Response> via h3 toWebHandler. Watch the h3 sealSession/unsealSession name-collision gotcha noted in bd memory h3-name-conflict-h3-exports-its-own-sealsession if importing session helpers (likely N/A here since this is a pure proxy).
acceptance_criteria: Failing test written first (TDD): fake upstream server responding to POST /v1/identity/auth/login with a Set-Cookie header; assert res.headers.getSetCookie() contains it. Second test: request cookies forwarded upstream and echoed back. Third test: GET /connect/authorize?... proxies path+query unchanged. pnpm --filter @bc-solutions-coder/wallow-auth test auth-server passes. git commit feat(wallow-auth): add proxy server with per-request cookie passthrough.

Everything else -> router SSR via ssrLoadModule('/src/ssr.tsx'). AuthServer instance is lazily built on first proxy request and MEMOIZED (module-level 'let authServer'), so 'pnpm dev' boots with no API reachable.
2. server.ts (standalone 'start' host): does NOT re-implement the proxy. Imports createAuthServer from ./src/lib/auth-server (single source of proxy truth — 0.3's createAuthServer only exposes handle(), not the h3 app, so toNodeListener is not reachable without editing 0.3's file, which is out of scope) and bridges node req/res <-> WHATWG Request/Response with the same toWebRequest/writeWebResponse helpers. Result: /health -> 'ready', /v1/** + /connect/** proxied, else 404. It deliberately does NOT SSR — standalone SSR (serving login/register/reset) is a later phase, mirroring wallow-web whose server.ts serves built assets rather than SSR. Phase 0 only needs it to boot + expose the proxy (no Dockerfile/E2E wiring in Phase 0 per feature scout).
3. vite.config.ts: did NOT copy wallow-web's legacy library-build config (outDir 'public', fixed entry src/app.ts -> app.js) — wallow-auth has NO src/app.ts / browser entry in Phase 0, so that config's entry cannot resolve. title: Phase 3: Issuer-origin unification
description: Repoint OpenIddict issuer/discovery and every OIDC client Authority at the new unified apps/wallow-auth origin so ASP.NET Identity's host-only cookies stay first-party through the proxy. This is the #1 risk in the plan; do only after Phase 2 screens work against the live API in dev.
design: OpenIddict server config: api/src/Modules/Identity/Wallow.Identity.Infrastructure/Extensions/IdentityInfrastructureExtensions.cs (issuer/SetIssuer). Config: relevant appsettings*.json (AuthUrl/ApiBaseUrl/issuer keys). Downstream Authority consumers: apps/wallow-web BFF config (OIDC_ISSUER/Oidc:Authority), api/src/Wallow.Web OIDC options if present, resource-server token-validation Authority, seed/OIDC client redirect_uris (api/seed.json).
acceptance_criteria: Discovery document resolves through the proxy origin; wallow-web BFF Authorization Code + PKCE login still succeeds end-to-end against the unified origin; SameSite/Secure cookie attributes verified correct for top-level nav (/connect/*, exchange-ticket, logout) vs XHR; ./scripts/run-tests.sh identity green; dotnet format api/Wallow.slnx clean.
notes:
SCOUT findings for Phase 3 (issuer-origin unification).

1) ISSUER/DISCOVERY TODAY: OpenIddict server is registered in the SHARED Identity module extension api/src/Modules/Identity/Wallow.Identity.Infrastructure/Extensions/IdentityInfrastructureExtensions.cs:54-151, hosted by Wallow.Api (NOT Wallow.Auth — Wallow.Auth is UI-only, cookie-relay). Endpoints fixed at /connect/authorize, /connect/token, /connect/logout, /connect/userinfo (:63-66). Issuer override: `configuration["OpenIddict:Issuer"]` -> `options.SetIssuer(new Uri(issuer))` (:70-74), currently unset in any checked-in appsettings*.json (all blank) — it's ONLY set via docker-compose env: docker/docker-compose.test.yml:138 `OpenIddict__Issuer: "http://localhost:5050"` (== API's OWN public port, not an auth-app origin) and docker-compose.production.yml:364 `OpenIddict__Issuer: ${API_PUBLIC_URL:-https://wallow.dev/api}`. CRITICAL PHASING NOTE: docker-compose's `wallow-auth` service (test.yml:159, production.yml:408) is still the LEGACY BLAZOR Wallow.Auth container (ApiBaseUrl/ASPNETCORE_* env, ghcr wallow-auth image) — apps/wallow-auth (TanStack) has NO docker-compose entry yet; that swap is Phase 4 task 4.1/4.3 (Wallow-vec7.5.1, Wallow-vec7.5.3-ish), not this phase. So 3.1/3.2 change SOURCE config only (IdentityInfrastructureExtensions.cs + appsettings*.json); the "unified origin" is verified against apps/wallow-auth's local dev server (tsx dev-server.ts, PORT default 3000, same default as apps/wallow-web — must run on a distinct port locally, e.g. PORT=3001) reverse-proxying to the API, not yet wired into docker/Aspire.

2) EVERY Authority/Issuer/MetadataAddress SITE (must ALL be repointed together or auth breaks):
   - api/src/Modules/Identity/Wallow.Identity.Infrastructure/Extensions/IdentityInfrastructureExtensions.cs:70-74 `OpenIddict:Issuer` -> SetIssuer (the source of truth / advertised issuer).
   - api/src/Wallow.Web/Program.cs:108-133 Blazor Web app's OIDC client: `Oidc:Authority` (falls back to `ServiceUrls:AuthUrl` then `http://localhost:5001`) + `Oidc:MetadataAddress` (internal discovery URL, endpoints REWRITTEN to Authority's path so browser redirects stay same-site — see comment :116-129). Client id wallow-web-client (seed.json).
   - packages/sdk/src/server/config.ts:72-119 `loadBffConfigFromEnv`: required `OIDC_ISSUER`, optional `OIDC_METADATA_URL` (defaults to `${issuer}/.well-known/openid-configuration` per :34-35 doc comment). Consumed by apps/wallow-web (BFF, client id bcordes-bff) and the E2E bff-example container (docker-compose.test.yml OIDC_ISSUER=http://localhost:5050, OIDC_METADATA_URL=http://host.docker.internal:5050/... — env block ~line 215-222 has a comment explaining the issuer-vs-metadata split, mirror it for wallow-auth).
   - apps/wallow-web/README.md ~L155-163 local-dev OIDC env doc: OIDC_ISSUER=http://localhost:5001 etc (memory: wallow-web-local-dev-oidc-env-apps-wallow) — must be updated to the wallow-auth unified origin.
   - api/tests/... : NO test hardcodes an Authority/issuer expectation found (grep for SetIssuer/well-known/discovery in api/tests hit no Identity-module files) — 3.1 acceptance criterion `./scripts/run-tests.sh identity` is a smoke check, not a targeted regression test for the issuer value itself.
   - api/src/Wallow.Api resource-server validation uses `.AddValidation(options => { options.UseLocalServer(); options.UseAspNetCore(); })` (IdentityInfrastructureExtensions.cs:147-151) — LOCAL server validation (same process), so token validation does NOT depend on Authority/MetadataAddress config anywhere; unaffected by this phase except for the `iss` claim baked into tokens (see risk #4).
   - seed.json client redirect_uris (wallow-dev-client, wallow-web-client, bcordes-bff) point at CONSUMER callback URLs (:5001/callback, :5003/signin-oidc, :3000/bff/callback) — these are NOT the auth-app origin and do not need to change for issuer unification; do not conflate with Authority.
   - GAP/RISK: apps/wallow-auth's h3 proxy (apps/wallow-auth/src/lib/auth-server.ts:124-125) mounts ONLY `/v1/**` and `/connect/**` at root — it does NOT proxy `/.well-known/**`. If any client is left relying on the config.ts default `${OIDC_ISSUER}/.well-known/openid-configuration` (i.e. OIDC_METADATA_URL unset) once OIDC_ISSUER points at the wallow-auth origin, discovery fetch will 404 through the proxy. Every existing docker-compose OIDC client already sets an explicit OIDC_METADATA_URL/Oidc:MetadataAddress pointing at the internal API container — this pattern MUST be preserved (or auth-server.ts's proxy prefix list extended to include /.well-known/**) when repointing in 3.2.

3) COOKIE INVENTORY (3.3):
   - `.AspNetCore.Identity.Application` (default name, IdentityConstants.ApplicationScheme) — configured via `services.ConfigureApplicationCookie` (IdentityInfrastructureExtensions.cs:153-180): SameSite=Lax, HttpOnly=true, SecurePolicy=SameAsRequest(dev)/Always(prod), Domain=`Authentication:CookieDomain` (blank in Development, ".wallow.dev" in appsettings.json), Path explicitly "/" (comment :166-169 explains this avoids PathBase login loops), OnRedirectToLogin overridden to return 401 (no server-side redirect — API has no login page). Must remain same-site once /connect/* and API calls both flow through the wallow-auth proxy origin.
   - `Identity.MfaPartial` — api/src/Modules/Identity/Wallow.Identity.Infrastructure/Services/MfaPartialAuthService.cs:14,42-49: HttpOnly=true, Secure=true (hardcoded, NOT env-conditional — will reject on plain HTTP dev unless the dev origin is HTTPS or this is loosened), SameSite=Lax, MaxAge=5min, time-limited DataProtector-encrypted value (not a session token). Issued by AccountController/MfaController on password-verified-but-not-yet-MFA'd login; validated by MfaPartialAuthorizationHandler via the "MfaPartial" policy.
   - OpenIddict server cookies: none separate — auth code/token flow uses the Identity.Application cookie itself (User.Identity checked in AuthorizationController) plus standard OpenIddict authorization-code/PKCE state (not cookie-based).
   - Antiforgery: `app.UseAntiforgery()` called in both api/src/Wallow.Auth/Program.cs:137 (Blazor, being replaced) and api/src/Wallow.Web/Program.cs:291 — no explicit cookie options override found for antiforgery; default ASP.NET Core antiforgery cookie name/attrs apply. apps/wallow-auth's own CSRF handling is client-side (SDK interceptor), separate from ASP.NET antiforgery.
   - Wallow.Web's own auth cookie (CookieAuthenticationDefaults) + OIDC correlation/nonce cookies: Program.cs:92-107 — correlation/nonce use SameSite=None+Secure=Always in prod, downgraded to Unspecified on non-HTTPS dev via CookiePolicyOptions.OnAppendCookie (:75-85), because response_mode=form_post causes a cross-site POST back to Wallow.Web. NOT directly touched by 3.3 (Wallow.Web is a separate Blazor app, out of migration scope) but relevant precedent for how this codebase already handles SameSite=None-on-HTTP-dev fallback.

4) RISKS:
   - BREAKING FOR LIVE SESSIONS: changing SetIssuer changes the `iss` claim baked into every NEWLY minted access/ID/refresh token. Already-issued tokens (refresh tokens live 7 days per `OpenIddict:RefreshTokenLifetimeDays` default, id/access tokens shorter) are JWTs with the OLD issuer baked in and are NOT rewritten by a config change — but resource-server validation here uses UseLocalServer() (same-process DB/keys, not external issuer-string matching), so whether old tokens still work depends on whether OpenIddict's local validation handler checks the `iss` claim against the currently-configured issuer (needs a live check — WORTH VERIFYING BEFORE SHIPPING, not confirmed by static read). Treat as a probable forced re-login for any active session across the deploy — flag this explicitly in the 3.1/3.2 commit bodies since it is a session-breaking change, and only do the real prod cutover in Phase 4 (docker-compose/Aspire), not Phase 3.
   - Authorization codes are short-lived (seconds) — negligible risk of in-flight codes surviving a config change.
   - seed.json does NOT need reseeding: client redirect_uris are consumer callback URLs, independent of the issuer's own origin; issuer is a server-side SetIssuer call, not a seeded entity.
   - `.well-known` proxy gap (see #2) is a real regression risk once wallow-auth becomes the origin AND is the biggest unverified item for 3.1's acceptance criterion "discovery document resolves through the proxy origin."
   - `.gitattributes` marks `appsettings*.json` and `seed.json` (and `docker/.env*`) as `merge=ours` (fork config) — 3.1/3.2 editing `appsettings*.json` is fine (that's the intended per-fork config surface) but be aware upstream merges will NOT bring future changes to these files into forks automatically; don't put anything in appsettings*.json that isn't meant to be fork-overridable. seed.json is NOT expected to need edits per risk above — if a task DOES need to touch seed.json, flag it loudly since merge=ours means forks silently diverge.

5) TEST COVERAGE: No existing unit/integration test asserts the OpenIddict issuer value or `/.well-known/openid-configuration` shape (grepped api/tests for SetIssuer/OpenIddict:Issuer/well-known/discovery — only unrelated hits in ApiVersionRewriteMiddlewareTests, ServiceDefaultsTests, AsyncApiIntegrationTests, SsoConfigurationTests). E2E coverage that WOULD exercise this end-to-end lives in api/tests/Wallow.E2E.Tests/Flows/{AuthFlowTests,BffFlowTests,MfaFlowTests,AltAuthFlowTests,EmailVerificationFlowTests,OrganizationFlowTests}.cs + PageObjects/{LoginPage,LogoutPage,DashboardPage}.cs. CONFIRMED: .github/workflows/ci.yml line 311-316 `e2e:` job has `if: false` with comment "Disabled: the containerized E2E suite is flaky in CI... Run it locally with ./scripts/run-e2e.sh instead" — E2E NEVER runs in CI today. This means 3.3's acceptance criterion (cookie attrs verified across the proxy) and the whole phase's real regression coverage is 100% manual/local-only (`./scripts/run-e2e.sh`) until someone re-enables the job; there is no CI safety net for an issuer/cookie regression in this repo right now.

title: Phase 1: SDK auth slice (packages/sdk)
description: Add a typed auth facade to packages/sdk over the existing generated OpenAPI identity ops (login, register, password reset, email verify, magic link, OTP, MFA, invitations, org matching, client branding/tenant), plus non-spec OIDC handshake URL builders (connect/authorize, consent submit, exchange-ticket, connect/logout) and a client-side open-redirect guard. Then wire a guarded app-side singleton facade in apps/wallow-auth.
design: Mirror the unwrap+WallowError pattern already used in apps/wallow-web/src/lib/wallow-sdk.ts. Generated ops live in packages/sdk/src/generated/sdk.gen.ts. New facade: packages/sdk/src/auth-client.ts (createAuthClient). New OIDC helpers: packages/sdk/src/auth-oidc.ts, mirroring the server-side ReturnUrlValidator.IsSafe logic (starts with single '/', not '//') for isSafeReturnUrl. Endpoint map is in docs/plans/2026-07-15-wallow-auth-tanstack-migration-design.md section 6. App-side singleton: apps/wallow-auth/src/lib/wallow-auth-sdk.ts, reusing the CSRF interceptor pattern from apps/wallow-web/src/lib/csrf.ts, baseUrl same-origin ('/').
acceptance_criteria: packages/sdk/src/auth-client.ts exports createAuthClient with all 20 listed methods, each unit-tested via vitest mocking the generated op and asserting unwrap/throw-on-error. packages/sdk/src/auth-oidc.ts exports the 4 URL builders + isSafeReturnUrl, each unit-tested. packages/sdk/src/index.ts exports both. apps/wallow-auth/src/lib/wallow-auth-sdk.ts exposes getWallowAuthSdk() returning {auth, oidc} with CSRF wired, unit-tested. SDK built (pnpm --filter @bc-solutions-coder/sdk build) before app-side task runs.
notes:
SCOUT (Phase 1 SDK auth slice). TEMPLATE FILES: packages/sdk/src/auth.ts + auth.test.ts (browser BFF login/logout/getUser pattern, NOT the model for auth-client.ts — that one is unwrap-envelope style). REAL TEMPLATE for auth-client.ts is apps/wallow-web/src/lib/wallow-sdk.ts (unwrap<T>(p) helper at line 94-100, throws error as ProblemDetails; ensureConfigured()+configured module flag pattern lines 67-80; flat slice-object shape WallowSdk at line 229). packages/sdk/src/index.ts is a 3-line barrel: export * from './client'; export * from './auth'; export * from './generated'. Generated ops (postV1IdentityAuthLogin etc.) are ALREADY exported from the package root via generated/index.ts -> index.ts, so auth-client.ts must import them from '../generated' or './generated/sdk.gen' and index.ts needs one more 'export * from "./auth-client"' + './auth-oidc' line.

EXACT OP MAPPING for 2.1's 20 methods (verified against packages/sdk/src/generated/sdk.gen.ts + types.gen.ts): login->postV1IdentityAuthLogin(body:AccountLoginRequest{email,password,rememberMe}); register->postV1IdentityAuthRegister(body:AccountRegisterRequest{email,password,confirmPassword,clientId?,loginMethod?,returnUrl?}) [NOT postV1IdentityRegister, which is a different admin-facing RegisterClientRequest op]; forgotPassword->postV1IdentityAuthForgotPassword(body:AccountForgotPasswordRequest{email}); resetPassword->postV1IdentityAuthResetPassword(body:AccountResetPasswordRequest{email,token,newPassword}); verifyEmail->getV1IdentityAuthVerifyEmail(query:{email?,token?}); sendMagicLink->postV1IdentityAuthPasswordlessMagicLink(body:SendMagicLinkRequest{email,returnUrl?,clientId?}); verifyMagicLink->getV1IdentityAuthPasswordlessMagicLinkVerify(query:{token?,rememberMe?}); sendOtp->postV1IdentityAuthPasswordlessOtp(body:SendOtpRequest{email}); verifyOtp->postV1IdentityAuthPasswordlessOtpVerify(body:VerifyOtpRequest{email,code,rememberMe?}); verifyMfa->postV1IdentityAuthMfaVerify(body:MfaVerifyRequest{code,useBackupCode:false}); useBackupCode->SAME op postV1IdentityAuthMfaVerify(body:{code,useBackupCode:true}) - there is no separate backup-code op; enrollTotp->postV1IdentityMfaEnrollTotp() no body; confirmEnrollment->postV1IdentityMfaEnrollConfirm(body:MfaConfirmRequest{secret,code}); exchangeEnrollmentToken->postV1IdentityMfaEnrollExchangeToken(query:{token?}) no body; getConsentInfo->getV1IdentityAppsConsentInfoByClientId(path:{clientId},query:{scopes?:string}) returns TYPED ConsentInfoResponse{clientId,displayName,logoUrl,requestedScopes:ScopeInfo[]} - scopes is a comma-joined STRING not array; getExternalProviders->getV1IdentityAuthExternalProviders() no args; getClientTenant->getV1IdentityAuthClientTenantByClientId(path:{clientId}); getClientBranding->getV1IdentityAppsByClientIdBranding(path:{clientId}) returns TYPED ClientBrandingDto{clientId,displayName,tagline,logoUrl,themeJson} (structurally = apps/wallow-auth/src/lib/branding.ts's ClientBranding interface, built by 7.1.5 to consume exactly this shape); verifyInvitation->getV1IdentityInvitationsVerifyByToken(path:{token}); acceptInvitation->postV1IdentityInvitationsByTokenAccept(path:{token}) no body; getMatchingOrgByDomain->getV1IdentityOrganizationDomainsMatch(query:{email?}); requestMembership->postV1IdentityMembershipRequests(body:CreateMembershipRequest{emailDomain}).

UNTYPED-RESPONSE GOTCHA (extends memory wallow-web-mfa-ops-untyped-responses to auth ops broadly): login/register/forgotPassword/resetPassword/verifyEmail/sendMagicLink/verifyMagicLink/sendOtp/verifyOtp/verifyMfa/useBackupCode/enrollTotp/confirmEnrollment/exchangeEnrollmentToken/getExternalProviders/getClientTenant/verifyInvitation/acceptInvitation/getMatchingOrgByDomain/requestMembership ALL resolve '200: unknown' (no ProducesResponseType on those controller actions) - only getConsentInfo and getClientBranding are typed. Design doc section 6 (docs/plans/2026-07-15-wallow-auth-tanstack-migration-design.md line 218) confirms: 'Response shapes today are anonymous objects (succeeded, error, mfaRequired, mfaEnrollmentRequired, mfaGraceDeadline, signInTicket etc.) - define matching TS types in the slice where the generated types don't model them.' The design doc's table also lists validateRedirectUri (GET auth/redirect-uri/validate?uri=) as a slice method NOT in the bead's 20-method list - flag to implementer as an open question rather than silently adding/dropping it.

2.2 OIDC URL HELPERS - exact Blazor oracle source (reconciliation: bead DESIGN says 'find the C# validator under api/src/Modules/Identity' but it does NOT live there): api/src/Wallow.Auth/Helpers/ReturnUrlValidator.cs - IsSafe(url) = url.StartsWith('/') && !url.StartsWith("//"); Sanitize(url,fallback='/'). Port targets, one C# call site each: (1) Consent.razor AppendToReturnUrl (lines 70-80) - appends 'consent_granted=true'/'consent_denied=true' via ?/& based on existing '?', then prepends ApiBaseUrl/origin if the result starts with '/' (buildConsentSubmitUrl(origin,returnUrl,granted:boolean)); (2) Logout.razor LogoutUrl getter (lines 66-77) - `${origin}/connect/logout` + optional `?post_logout_redirect_uri=${encodeURIComponent(...)}`  when non-empty (buildConnectLogoutUrl(origin,postLogoutRedirectUri?)); (3) Login.razor lines 546-550 - `${origin}/v1/identity/auth/exchange-ticket?ticket=${enc(ticket)}&returnUrl=${enc(returnUrl)}` (buildExchangeTicketUrl(origin,ticket,returnUrl)); (4) buildConnectAuthorizeUrl(origin,params) has no single Blazor call site (it's the reverse direction - API redirects TO the login page) but must build `${origin}/connect/authorize?${new URLSearchParams(params)}` for completeness/tests. All 4 helpers take an explicit origin param (same-origin under the wallow-auth proxy, but keep it a param per the bead DESIGN, not hardcoded) plus MUST call isSafeReturnUrl first on any returnUrl-shaped input before building.

INTEGRATION POINTS / GOTCHAS for 2.3: (a) apps/wallow-auth/vitest.config.ts (already exists from 7.1.5) currently has NO 'server:{deps:{inline:[...]}}' entry for packages/sdk, unlike apps/wallow-web/vitest.config.ts which needs it so vi.mock('@bc-solutions-coder/sdk') reaches the real facade (see wallow-web/vitest.config.ts comment). 2.3's wallow-auth-sdk.test.ts will likely need the same server.deps.inline:[/packages[\/\\]sdk/u] addition to vitest.config.ts, or it must mock differently - confirm by running the test once written. (b) CSRF template: apps/wallow-web/src/lib/csrf.ts (isSafeMethod/setCsrfToken/wireCsrfInterceptor/CsrfInterceptorClient) is a 1:1 mirror target - copy verbatim into apps/wallow-auth/src/lib/csrf.ts (does not exist yet), 2.3 wires it via wireCsrfInterceptor(client) where client is the SDK's exported 'client' (packages/sdk/src/client.ts re-exports generated/client.gen.ts's client - see memory phase-7-two-client-bug). (c) apps/wallow-auth has no configureBffClient-equivalent call yet - 2.3's design says baseUrl same-origin '/' (not '/api' like wallow-web's BFF default) since the h3 proxy in apps/wallow-auth/src/lib/auth-server.ts (built by 7.1.3) forwards /v1/** and /connect/** directly at root, not under /api. Use configureBffClient({baseUrl:'/'}) or a wallow-auth-specific configure call - confirm against auth-server.ts's actual mount prefix before hardcoding. (d) index.test.ts (packages/sdk/src/index.test.ts) pins an exact BROWSER_VALUE_EXPORTS array (line 43-50) - 2.1/2.2 should add createAuthClient/auth-oidc helper names to that list to keep the export-surface contract test meaningful (test won't fail if omitted, but convention is to keep it exhaustive). (e) auth-layout.tsx (apps/wallow-auth/src/components/auth-layout.tsx, built by 7.1.5) takes ResolvedBranding as a prop and does NOT yet fetch per-client branding - that wiring (calling auth.getClientBranding + branding.ts's mergeClientBranding) is explicitly left for whichever later task adds the /login route, not 2.3 itself; 2.3 only needs to expose auth+oidc, not wire them into auth-layout.

title: Phase 2: Port screens
description: Port all 16 Blazor Wallow.Auth Razor pages to TanStack Start routes in apps/wallow-auth, using the SDK auth facade from Phase 1. Order: trivial screens first (establish route+form+testid pattern), then complex multi-step ones (MFA, Login 3-tab state machine, Register).
design: Blazor oracles live in api/src/Wallow.Auth/Components/Pages/*.razor (ForgotPassword, ResetPassword, VerifyEmailConfirm, VerifyEmail, Privacy, Terms, Error, Home, Consent, Logout, MfaChallenge, MfaEnroll, Login, Register, InvitationLanding, AcceptTerms). Each screen task follows the template in the plan (Phase 2 'Screen task template'): failing component/logic test -> implement route + form using getWallowAuthSdk() -> data-testid per element -> thread returnUrl/client_id query params -> apply open-redirect guard on navigation -> pass -> commit. Register routes in apps/wallow-auth/src/router.tsx (manual route tree, no codegen, mirrors apps/wallow-web/src/router.tsx).
acceptance_criteria: All 16 screens render, pass component tests, and are registered in src/router.tsx with data-testid={page}-{element} kebab-case selectors matching the plan's screen order.
notes:
SCOUT (Phase 2 port-screens, shared conventions for all 15 child tasks).

BLAZOR ORACLE: api/src/Wallow.Auth/Components/Pages/*.razor (one file per screen, see task DESIGN fields for exact filename). Shape: @page directive, @inject IAuthApiClient AuthApi + BrandingOptions, local _field state, HandleSubmit async method calling AuthApi.*Async, _loading/_submitted bool flags gating a BbButton spinner, error surfaced in a data-testid="{page}-error" BbAlert block near the top of BbCardContent. Home.razor is a 6-line NavigationManager.NavigateTo("login", forceLoad:true) redirect (mirrors index.tsx's existing beforeLoad redirect() pattern already in repo).

EXACT data-testid INVENTORY (verbatim from grep of the Blazor oracles — ports MUST reuse these, do not invent new names for elements that already have one):
- ForgotPassword: forgot-password-success, forgot-password-email, forgot-password-submit
- ResetPassword: reset-password-error, reset-password-new-password, reset-password-confirm, reset-password-submit
- VerifyEmailConfirm: verify-email-confirm-loading, verify-email-confirm-success, verify-email-confirm-continue, verify-email-confirm-error, verify-email-confirm-signin-link
- VerifyEmail (static): verify-email-heading, verify-email-description, verify-email-back-link
- Privacy: privacy-heading, privacy-content, privacy-back-button
- Terms: terms-heading, terms-content, terms-back-button
- Error: error-heading, error-message, error-sign-out-link, error-back-link
- Home: NO testids (bare redirect, nothing renders)
- Consent: consent-error, consent-heading, consent-scopes, consent-approve, consent-deny
- Logout: logout-confirm-heading (used on BOTH the confirm step AND the signed-out landing — same testid, different text), logout-confirm-button
- MfaChallenge: mfa-challenge-error, mfa-challenge-success, mfa-challenge-backup-code, mfa-challenge-code, mfa-challenge-submit, mfa-challenge-toggle-backup
- MfaEnroll: mfa-enroll-error, mfa-enroll-backup-codes, mfa-enroll-qr, mfa-enroll-secret, mfa-enroll-code, mfa-enroll-submit, mfa-enroll-begin-setup, mfa-enroll-cancel
- Register: register-error, register-email, register-password, register-confirm-password, register-terms, register-privacy, register-submit (NO testid found for password-strength meter or passwordless-toggle or org-domain interstitial in the oracle — those are new UI per the bead's design; invent {page}-{element} kebab names, e.g. register-password-strength, register-passwordless-toggle, register-org-match-*)
- InvitationLanding: invitation-loading, invitation-error, invitation-info, invitation-expired, invitation-accept-error, invitation-accept, invitation-decline, invitation-create-account, invitation-sign-in
- AcceptTerms: accept-terms-heading, accept-terms-error, accept-terms-checkbox, accept-terms-privacy-checkbox, accept-terms-submit
- Login (tasks 2.8a-e): login-error, login-tab-password, login-tab-magic-link, login-tab-otp, login-email, login-forgot-password, login-password, login-remember-me, login-submit, login-magic-link-sent, login-magic-link-email, login-magic-link-submit, login-otp-sent, login-otp-code, login-otp-verify-submit, login-otp-email, login-otp-send-submit, login-register-link. GAP: external-provider buttons (@foreach _externalProviders, Login.razor:189-208) have NO data-testid in the oracle at all — 2.8d must invent one, recommend `login-external-{provider}` (kebab, provider name lowercased) plus a container `login-external-providers`.

SHARED APP-SIDE INFRASTRUCTURE (already built, closed, read-only import points — do not re-derive):
- apps/wallow-auth/src/lib/wallow-auth-sdk.ts: getWallowAuthSdk() -> {auth, oidc}. THIS is the ONLY file allowed to import from @bc-solutions-coder/sdk (module-header convention comment). Screens import getWallowAuthSdk, never the SDK directly.
- auth: 23 methods (packages/sdk/src/auth-client.ts) covering every op the tasks need (). ONLY getConsentInfo and getClientBranding are typed responses (ConsentInfoResponse, ClientBrandingDto) — every other method resolves Promise<unknown>; screens must define their own local TS interfaces for the anonymous C# response shapes (succeeded/error/mfaRequired/mfaEnrollmentRequired/mfaGraceDeadline/signInTicket etc — see design doc docs/plans/2026-07-15-wallow-auth-tanstack-migration-design.md section 6) and narrow at their own boundary. Do not add these as SDK types.
- oidc: isSafeReturnUrl, buildConnectAuthorizeUrl, buildConsentSubmitUrl, buildExchangeTicketUrl, buildConnectLogoutUrl (packages/sdk/src/auth-oidc.ts). isSafeReturnUrl mirrors C# ReturnUrlValidator.IsSafe (starts with single '/', not '//'). Per bd memory returnurl-guard-refuse-dont-sanitize: on an UNSAFE returnUrl, REFUSE (route to /error?reason=invalid_redirect_uri like the Blazor oracle), do NOT silently fall back to '/' — that's the C# Sanitize() behavior, deliberately NOT ported. Only a NULLISH returnUrl gets '?? "/"' fallback; empty string '' is unsafe, not nullish.
- ERROR-SURFACING GOTCHA (verified by reading code, not assumed): auth-client.ts's unwrap()/toWallowError() throws a WallowError but only populates .code from problem.extensions.code or problem.code — it does NOT read a top-level .error field. Per bd memory 'mfa-endpoints-mfacontroller-return-business-failures-as-a', MFA/login business failures come back shaped {succeeded:false, error:'<code>'} (e.g. invalid_password, invalid_code, mfa_not_enabled), NOT RFC7807 problem+json. Because that shape has no .code/.extensions.code, toWallowError will produce WallowError{code:'UNKNOWN', title:'Unknown error', detail:undefined} for these — the real reason string is LOST through the WallowError seam. Screens 2.6 (MfaChallenge), 2.7 (MfaEnroll), 2.8a (Login password tab) MUST verify this empirically (log the caught error / hit a real 400) before assuming .code carries invalid_password/invalid_code — do not silently show only the generic 'Unknown error' title. If confirmed lost, the screen-local fallback is a generic "invalid code/password, try again" message (do not block on fixing the SDK — out of this bead's scope; flag as a follow-up bead if it blocks an acceptance criterion).
- apps/wallow-auth/src/lib/csrf.ts: wireCsrfInterceptor already wired inside wallow-auth-sdk.ts's getWallowAuthSdk(); screens never touch this directly.
- apps/wallow-auth/src/lib/branding.ts + src/components/auth-layout.tsx: AuthLayout wraps every screen's body (BrandingHeader + children + ForkFooter). It takes an OPTIONAL `branding` prop (ResolvedBranding), defaulting to forkResolvedBranding. The per-client (client_id query param) branding FETCH (auth.getClientBranding(clientId) + branding.ts's mergeClientBranding) is explicitly NOT wired anywhere yet — every screen that supports a client_id query param (basically all of them, since Login/Register/Consent etc all carry it) is responsible for wiring: read client_id from search params -> call auth.getClientBranding -> mergeClientBranding(forkBranding, response) -> pass into <AuthLayout branding={resolved}>. SCOUT (auth-state seam investigation — resolves Wallow-vec7.3.9 finding 1; binding for all Phase 2 screens).

RECOMMENDED SEAM: probe GET /v1/identity/users/me through the EXISTING h3 /v1/** passthrough proxy. 200 => signed in, 401 => anonymous. No new API endpoint, no new h3 route, no session store.

1. THE BLAZOR ORACLE'S AUTH STATE IS DEAD CODE — _isAuthenticated IS ALWAYS FALSE.
- Wallow.Auth has NO authentication at all: zero hits for AddAuthentication / UseAuthentication / AddCascadingAuthenticationState across api/src/Wallow.Auth AND api/src/Wallow.ServiceDefaults (Extensions.cs).
- AddRazorComponents().AddInteractiveServerComponents() DOES register the provider — verified EMPIRICALLY with a throwaway DI probe replicating Wallow.Auth/Program.cs exactly: resolves to Microsoft.AspNetCore.Components.Server.ServerAuthenticationStateProvider. So @inject resolves and the page renders (this is why the anonymous invitation E2E tests pass — the page is not broken).
- BUT ServerAuthenticationStateProvider is seeded from HttpContext.User at circuit start, and with no UseAuthentication middleware HttpContext.User is always an anonymous ClaimsPrincipal. CookieRelayMiddleware (Services/CookieRelayMiddleware.cs) only WRITES Set-Cookie headers; it never populates User.
=> InvitationLanding.razor:130-131 always yields false; the accept/decline branch at :54 is UNREACHABLE in Blazor today.
- Corroboration, not contradiction: the only tests that would catch this (OrganizationInvitationFlowTests.AuthenticatedUser_AcceptsInvitation_JoinsOrganization / _DeclinesInvitation_StaysUnenrolled, which click invitation-accept) NEVER RUN — .github/workflows/ci.yml:311-316 disables the entire e2e job with 'if: false' (documented as flaky). Those tests are stale/unverified, NOT evidence the branch works.
=> Matches bd memory blazor-oracle-dead-branch-pattern-check-the-wire-before-porting. The .3.9 RED agent pinning BOTH branches is CORRECT: it is a deliberate bug-fix-on-port, not oracle parity. Call it out in the commit body.

2. WHICH COOKIE / SCHEME.
- Wallow.Auth owns NO cookie. The auth cookie is ASP.NET Identity's IdentityConstants.ApplicationScheme cookie (.AspNetCore.Identity.Application), owned by Wallow.Api. Config at api/src/Modules/Identity/Wallow.Identity.Infrastructure/Extensions/IdentityInfrastructureExtensions.cs:153-180 — HttpOnly=true, SameSite=Lax, Path='/', SecurePolicy=Always in prod, optional Domain from Authentication:CookieDomain.
- API DefaultScheme is the 'SmartScheme' policy scheme (:255-327): Authorization: Bearer header -> OpenIddict validation; ELSE -> IdentityConstants.ApplicationScheme. So a cookie-only request to any [Authorize] endpoint authenticates via the cookie.
- CRUCIAL: options.Events.OnRedirectToLogin is overridden to set 401 instead of 302 -> /Account/Login (:175-179, 'The API has no login page'). An anonymous probe gets a CLEAN 401 — fetch-friendly, no redirect chasing.

3. wallow-auth IS NOT A BFF APP — the SDK getUser()/BffSession model DOES NOT APPLY.
- apps/wallow-web IS a BFF: bff-server.ts runs OIDC code+PKCE, stores the TOKEN SET in a sealed-cookie/Valkey session; getUser() reads THAT session.
- apps/wallow-auth IS the AUTH ORIGIN itself (the OpenIddict IdP UI). lib/auth-server.ts is a PURE passthrough reverse proxy (/health, /v1/**, /connect/** -> apiInternalUrl) forwarding Cookie inbound and ALL Set-Cookie outbound verbatim. No session store, no jar, no token set — there is nothing for getUser() to read.
- Do NOT introduce configureBffClient/getUser/BffSession/an h3 session here. That would re-create the cookie-relay subsystem task 1.3 deliberately deleted.

4. EXISTING ENDPOINT THAT REPORTS AUTH STATE: YES — no new one needed.
GET /v1/identity/users/me -> UsersController.GetCurrentUser (api/src/Modules/Identity/Wallow.Identity.Api/Controllers/UsersController.cs:72-82). Controller-level [Authorize], NO extra permission attribute. 200 CurrentUserResponse {id,email,firstName,lastName,roles,permissions} | 401 when anonymous. Reachable UNCHANGED through the existing /v1/** proxy (auth-server.ts createProxyHandler forwards the Cookie header verbatim).
Generated op ALREADY EXISTS: getV1IdentityUsersMe (packages/sdk/src/generated/sdk.gen.ts:2191), typed CurrentUserResponse (types.gen.ts:299, :3935). The facade packages/sdk/src/auth-client.ts does NOT expose it — .3.9's finding is accurate.

5. MINIMAL CORRECT SEAM (recommended).
- Add ONE facade method to packages/sdk/src/auth-client.ts: getCurrentUser(): Promise<CurrentUserResponse | null> wrapping getV1IdentityUsersMe, mapping 401 -> null. IMPORTANT: 401 must NOT throw — anonymous is an EXPECTED state, not an error; the existing unwrap() throws on every non-2xx, so this method must bypass/soften it.
- Honors the facade rule from .2.1 (generated ops imported in exactly one place).
- CLIENT-SIDE call, NOT an SSR loader: same-origin, the browser attaches the cookie automatically. An SSR loader would have to manually forward the inbound Cookie into the SDK fetch (the client is configured baseUrl '/' with no server-side cookie plumbing) — extra machinery for no gain, and auth state must never be SSR-cached.
- routes/invitation.tsx calls it and passes isAuthenticated down as the prop .3.9 already specced => prop shape UNCHANGED, the 28 RED tests stand as written.
- SCOPE: packages/sdk is outside Phase 2 and .2.1 is CLOSED => this needs a FOLLOW-UP BEAD (sdk facade + tests), not an in-place edit by .3.9's green agent. .3.9 green is BLOCKED on that bead.
- REJECT option (b) from .3.9 (a bespoke h3 /auth/session route): duplicates an existing API endpoint, puts an auth decision in the proxy tier, and starts the session-store slide 1.3 deleted.

6. SECURITY IMPLICATIONS.
- HttpOnly NOT weakened: JS never reads the cookie. The browser attaches it; JS only observes the 200/401 outcome of its OWN same-origin request. No cookie/token value is ever exposed to script.
- NO cross-origin leak: SameSite=Lax blocks the cookie on cross-site fetch/XHR, so an attacker page's credentialed probe is anonymous (401); CORS blocks reading the response regardless. The auth-state answer exists only same-origin.
- NOT an authorization decision: isAuthenticated is a UI AFFORDANCE ONLY. The API enforces independently — POST /v1/identity/invitations/{token}/accept is [Authorize] (InvitationsController.cs:82-84), so an anonymous accept is 401 no matter what the client believes. GET verify/{token} is [AllowAnonymous] (:67-70) and MUST stay anonymously callable — the unauthenticated branch depends on it.
- Anti-enumeration unaffected (cf. bd memory anti-enumeration-pattern...): users/me reveals only the CALLER's own identity.

7. WHICH SCREENS NEED THE SEAM: ONLY InvitationLanding (.3.9). NO CLOSED BEAD IS INCONSISTENT.
- Verified by grep over api/src/Wallow.Auth/Components/Pages/*.razor: AuthenticationStateProvider appears in EXACTLY ONE file (InvitationLanding.razor:7). Consent, AcceptTerms, Logout, Login, MfaChallenge reference no auth state whatsoever (no AuthenticationState, no IsAuthenticated, no @attribute [Authorize]).
- Architectural reason: the Auth UI is a DUMB RENDERER; the API owns the auth check. AuthorizationController.cs:49 ('if (User.Identity is not { IsAuthenticated: true })') challenges/redirects at /connect/authorize, so Consent (.3.4) is only ever reached already-authenticated. Logout (.3.5) is a confirm + POST sign-out.
- .3.4 (Consent, CLOSED) and .3.5 (Logout, CLOSED) make NO auth-state claims and their oracles never consult it — they correctly DODGED the gap rather than assuming something. .3.10 (AcceptTerms) and .3.11-.3.15 (Login chain) need no seam either (pre-auth or API-enforced).
=> Keep the seam scoped to .3.9. Do NOT retrofit it onto other screens.

SCOUT CRITICAL DIVERGENCE #1 (profile): the bead DESIGN wrongly assumes getV1IdentitySettingsUser/putV1IdentitySettingsUser (GET/PUT /v1/identity/settings/user) is a profile get/update endpoint. It is NOT — it's a generic tenant-scoped key/value settings store: GET returns ResolvedSetting[]{key,value,source,displayName,description,defaultValue}, PUT body is SettingUpdateRequest{key,value}. The Blazor oracle (api/src/Wallow.Web/Components/Pages/Dashboard/Settings.razor) does NOT call this endpoint for profile at all — it reads name/email/roles straight off the authenticated ClaimsPrincipal (AuthStateProvider.GetAuthenticationStateAsync(), .GetDisplayName()/.GetEmail()/.GetRoles()) and renders READ-ONLY, no update/mutation exists anywhere for profile fields. RECOMMENDATION for 6.1/6.2: settings facade slice should be getProfile() wrapping unwrap(getV1IdentityUsersMe()) (read-only query, no mutation, mirrors oracle) OR reuse the already-existing getWallowSdk().user.me() (WallowUser from BFF session claims: sub,email,name,[claim]). Do NOT wire getV1IdentitySettingsUser/putV1IdentitySettingsUser as 'profile' — that would be semantically wrong and untested against the oracle. If task 6.1's acceptance criterion demands a 'profile mutation', flag it to the coordinator: no backend endpoint exists to update firstName/lastName/email from this surface; the oracle is display-only.

Field source: name/email/roles all come from CurrentUserResponse (id,email,firstName,lastName,roles,permissions) via getV1IdentityUsersMe if using the settings.getProfile() query — no separate roles endpoint. dashboard-settings section root testid convention (task 6.5) should wrap both settings-* and mfa-* testid groups (Blazor mounts <MfaSettingsSection/> directly under the Settings.razor content, both share one page/route).
SCOUT MFA facade (6.3) op names + exact request/response shapes — OpenAPI response types are ALL 'unknown' for MFA endpoints (backend doesn't declare ProducesResponseType), so the facade/components must define local TS interfaces mirroring the C# response records and cast, same pattern as wallow-web-one-time-secret-ux memory (AppRegistrationResponse cast off mutation.data).
