Slice methods per bead DESIGN (status/enrollTotp/confirmEnroll/disable/regenerateBackupCodes) are correct op mappings — only the response-type gap needs local interfaces in mfa/types.ts.
SCOUT MFA enroll flow UX + testids (6.4) — oracle is api/src/Wallow.Auth/Components/Pages/MfaEnroll.razor (NOT a 'MfaSettingsSection.razor' file — that name in the bead description is imprecise; the settings-page MFA status card is api/src/Wallow.Web/Components/Shared/MfaSettingsSection.razor, a SEPARATE component from the enroll flow). 4-state flow, single component, testids: mfa-enroll-begin-setup (initial CTA, shown before secret exists) -> on click calls enrollTotp -> mfa-enroll-secret (secret text) + mfa-enroll-qr (QR container div, id=mfa-enroll-qr, populated via JS qrcode.generate in Blazor; TanStack impl should render an actual QR image/svg from the qrUri, e.g. via a QR lib, or at minimum keep the testid+secret text) + mfa-enroll-code (text input) + mfa-enroll-submit (button, calls confirmEnroll) -> on success mfa-enroll-backup-codes (container, one code per line/child) with a Done action; mfa-enroll-error (shown on any step's failure, message text); mfa-enroll-cancel (link/back-out, always visible). Order strictly: begin-setup -> secret+qr+code+submit -> backup-codes. Page object: api/tests/Wallow.E2E.Tests/PageObjects/MfaEnrollPage.cs. NOTE: the Blazor oracle also does a cross-app EnrollToken exchange (Web settings -> full-page redirect to Auth app /mfa/enroll?enrollToken=...) because Web and Auth are separate origins/apps there — this is IRRELEVANT to wallow-web/tanstack: the whole SPA is same-origin via the BFF proxy, so 6.4's component should call postV1IdentityMfaEnrollTotp directly with no token dance; only the 4-step UX + testids need to be mirrored, not the multi-app redirect plumbing.
SCOUT MFA settings-card testids (6.2/6.5, status display integrated alongside profile) — oracle api/src/Wallow.Web/Components/Shared/MfaSettingsSection.razor + E2E page object api/tests/Wallow.E2E.Tests/PageObjects/SettingsMfaSection.cs: settings-mfa-status (Enabled/Disabled text), settings-mfa-backup-count (shown only when enabled), settings-mfa-enable (button, shown when disabled — this is what should trigger the 6.4 enroll flow inline/route, no cross-app redirect needed in tanstack), settings-mfa-disable + settings-mfa-regenerate (buttons, shown when enabled, each opens a password-confirm sub-panel), settings-mfa-confirm-password (shared password input for both disable/regenerate confirm dialogs), settings-mfa-confirm-submit (shared submit button id for both flows), settings-mfa-error (shared error text). This status-card component is DISTINCT from the enroll-flow component (6.4) — 6.4's component is only entered when disabled+user clicks enable. title: 1.3: SPIKE — mount BFF + API proxy handlers as Start server routes
description: Port the h3 BFF handler construction from the old apps/wallow-web/server.ts into a Start-server-route-compatible module, and prove that createBffHandlers/createApiProxy's h3 handlers work when mounted as TanStack Start server routes.
design: Create src/lib/bff-server.ts: build config via loadBffConfigFromEnv, a store (CookieSessionStore or ValkeySessionStore), and handlers via createBffHandlers/createApiProxy — port directly from the old server.ts (read it before deleting). Export bff (login/callback/user/logout) and apiProxy. Create src/routes/bff/$.ts and src/routes/api/$.ts adapting Start's server-route request/response into the h3 defineEventHandlers (bridge as needed). Add a /health server route returning {status:"ok"}. Fallback if the bridge doesn't work cleanly: run standalone h3 server.ts as a sidecar and proxy /bff + /api from Start — document that choice inline in bff-server.ts. Do NOT proceed to Phase 2 work until /bff/user returns 401 and login issues a 302.
acceptance_criteria: Running the app: curl -i GET /bff/user (unauthenticated) returns 401. curl GET /health returns {"status":"ok"}. Login flow issues a 302 redirect. apps/wallow-web/server.ts and public/ are deleted only after the above verify. Commit: feat(wallow-web): mount bff + api proxy as start server routes.
notes:
RED (2.3 spike tests): FILES=apps/wallow-web/src/lib/bff-server.test.ts (new spec, node env), apps/wallow-web/src/lib/bff-server.ts (RED stub exporting bff:BffHandlers, apiProxy:EventHandler, handleBffRequest(Request):Promise). 6 tests: 2 exports-shape PASS (bff has login/callback/user/logout fns; apiProxy is fn), 4 behavioral FAIL for behavior-missing (stub rejects 'not implemented'): GET /health=>200 {status:'ok'}; unauth GET /bff/user=>401; GET /bff/login=>302 to ${issuer}/connect/authorize + Set-Cookie wallow_bff_tx; unauth GET /api/notifications=>401. Full suite: 4 failed | 17 passed (21). tsc --noEmit clean. TEST DESIGN: tests target the framework-agnostic bridge handleBffRequest (the toWebHandler-shaped web Request=>Response the green port must expose), NOT TanStack Start server-route files directly. Rationale in SPIKE RISK below. openid-client is hermetically mocked at the module boundary (vi.mock('openid-client')) reusing the SDK handlers.test.ts pattern — the mock intercepts the bare 'openid-client' import INSIDE the built SDK dist (confirmed dist/server/index.js imports it as bare specifier), so login yields a real 302 with no network. Required BFF env is seeded in beforeAll then bff-server is dynamically imported (config/store/handlers build at module load, mirroring server.ts). COOKIE_PASSWORD must be >=32 chars; COOKIE_SECURE=false for the http redirect_uri. GREEN GUIDANCE: port server.ts verbatim into bff-server.ts — loadBffConfigFromEnv()=>config; store = REDIS_URL? ValkeySessionStore(createRedisAdapter(node-redis client),password,ttl) : CookieSessionStore({password}); bff=createBffHandlers(config,store); apiProxy=createApiProxy(config,store). handleBffRequest = toWebHandler(app) where app is createApp()+createRouter() mounting GET /health=>{status:'ok'}, /bff/login,/bff/callback,GET /bff/user,/bff/logout, /api/** => apiProxy (proxy strips /api itself). Both factories MUST share one store. Then src/routes/{bff,api}/$.ts + a /health Start route delegate to handleBffRequest (or the sidecar fallback). Do NOT delete server.ts/public/ until curl verify passes (acceptance). SPIKE RISK (key finding): the installed TanStack stack has NO obvious server-route creator API — grep found no createServerFileRoute/createServerRoute/ServerRoute.methods in @tanstack/react-router@1.170.18, @tanstack/react-start@1.168.28, start-server-core@1.169.17, or router-core@1.171.15. This is exactly the bridge risk the epic flagged. Tests therefore pin the h3->web bridge (handleBffRequest), which is stable whether green mounts it via a Start server route OR the documented sidecar fallback (design explicitly allows either). The 'reachable as a Start HTTP route' proof stays with the C# BffFlowTests over live infra (curl /health, /bff/user 401, login 302) — not reproducible in vitest. Green must discover the actual server-route entrypoint for this version (likely code-generated by @tanstack/router-plugin, or fall back to the sidecar) and document the choice inline per the bead DESIGN. GREEN (2.3 spike): all 21 wallow-web tests pass (6/6 in src/lib/bff-server.test.ts), tsc clean, oxlint --deny-warnings clean, oxfmt clean. FILES: - apps/wallow-web/src/lib/bff-server.ts (green port): loadBffConfigFromEnv()->config; store=REDIS_URL? ValkeySessionStore(createRedisAdapter(node-redis)) : CookieSessionStore({password}); bff=createBffHandlers(config,store); apiProxy=createApiProxy(config,store) (SAME store). handleBffRequest=toWebHandler(app) where app=createApp()+createRouter() mounting GET /health->{status:'ok'}, /bff/login, /bff/callback, GET /bff/user, /bff/logout, /api/**->apiProxy. Exports: bff:BffHandlers, apiProxy:EventHandler, handleBffRequest(Request):Promise. Ported verbatim from server.ts. - apps/wallow-web/dev-server.ts (mount): path-prefix dispatch — /health,/bff/*,/api/* -> handleBffRequest (lazy vite.ssrLoadModule('/src/lib/bff-server.ts')); everything else -> router SSR. writeWebResponse preserves multiple Set-Cookie via getSetCookie()+appendHeader. - apps/wallow-web/vitest.config.ts (harness): inline SDK (realpath /packages/sdk/) so Vitest transforms it + alias 'openid-client' to its single resolved entry (via createRequire from packages/sdk, version-agnostic). Needed because the red test's vi.mock('openid-client') otherwise misses: externalized SDK dist loads openid-client natively AND pnpm resolves openid-client to different module ids across packages, so the factory-mock key didn't match. Root-caused + fixed; keeps tests against the built dist per the red design. MOUNTING APPROACH CHOSEN + WHY: No file-based Start server-route creator exists in the installed stack (createServerFileRoute/createServerRoute absent from @tanstack/react-start@1.168.28, react-router@1.170.18, start-server-core, router-core — confirmed the scout's SPIKE RISK). Took the design's documented fallback: mount the SDK h3 handlers at the Start SSR server layer (dev-server.ts) via path-prefix dispatch to the framework-agnostic handleBffRequest bridge — single Node process, NO sidecar, no createServerFileRoute dependency. If a future TanStack release adds a real server-route creator, src/routes/{bff,api}/$.ts can delegate to handleBffRequest unchanged. Decision documented inline in both bff-server.ts and dev-server.ts. LIVE CURL (booted 'pnpm dev' PORT=3000 with BFF env pointing at a local fake OIDC metadata endpoint on :4444; NODE_ENV=development for http discovery; CookieSessionStore): - GET /health -> 200, body {"status":"ok"} - GET /bff/user (unauth) -> 401 - GET /api/notifications (unauth) -> 401 - GET /bff/login?returnTo=/dashboard -> 302 Location http://localhost:4444/connect/authorize?response_type=code&client_id=wallow-web&redirect_uri=...%2Fbff%2Fcallback&scope=openid+profile+email+offline_access&state=&code_challenge=&code_challenge_method=S256&nonce=; Set-Cookie wallow_bff_tx=Fe26.2**... Max-Age=600 Path=/ HttpOnly SameSite=Lax - GET / -> 200 SSR html with

Welcome to Wallow

(BFF routes + Start SSR co-exist on one server layer). All ACCEPTANCE gates met live. server.ts/public/ NOT deleted (deviation from acceptance, deliberate): (1) src/bff-surface.test.ts (a test I must not edit) reads ../server.ts and asserts the /health,/bff/*,/api/** routes still exist — deleting server.ts fails that regression guard, so green REQUIRES keeping it; (2) Dockerfile + 'start' script still run 'tsx server.ts' and E2E DockerComposeFixture depends on that path — the scout flagged docker/start migration as a SEPARATE follow-up task, out of scope here. Recommend the follow-up: repoint Dockerfile/start at the Start server (dev-server.ts pattern) then delete server.ts/public and the bff-surface guard together. TEST_STATUS=pass (21/21). ISSUES=none blocking; note the vitest harness change (SDK inline + openid-client alias) is required for the hermetic mock and should stay for all future wallow-web tests that drive the SDK. VERIFY (live-booted pnpm dev on :3010 + fake OIDC discovery on :4444, no mocks): ✓ GET /health -> 200 {"status":"ok"} (dev-server.ts:118-124 dispatches to bff-server.ts handleBffRequest, health route registered bff-server.ts:128-131) ✓ GET /bff/user unauth -> 401 (verified curl) ✓ GET /bff/login?returnTo=/dashboard -> 302 to http://localhost:4444/connect/authorize?...code_challenge=...&code_challenge_method=S256... + Set-Cookie wallow_bff_tx=Fe26.2**...; HttpOnly; SameSite=Lax (PKCE present, matches report) ✓ GET /api/notifications unauth -> 401 ✓ GET / -> 200 SSR html, data-testid="home-heading" "Welcome to Wallow" present (SSR + BFF coexist on one Node process, dev-server.ts:60-62 isBffRequest prefix dispatch) All 5 live curl gates match the GREEN report byte-for-byte. Code read: apps/wallow-web/src/lib/bff-server.ts (ports server.ts verbatim: loadBffConfigFromEnv, Cookie/ValkeySessionStore switch on REDIS_URL, createBffHandlers/createApiProxy sharing one store, h3 app/router mounting /health,/bff/*,/api/**, toWebHandler bridge exported as handleBffRequest). apps/wallow-web/dev-server.ts (path-prefix dispatch: /health,/bff/*,/api/* -> lazy vite.ssrLoadModule('/src/lib/bff-server.ts'), else SSR render; writeWebResponse preserves multiple Set-Cookie via getSetCookie()+appendHeader). Both files document the MOUNTING DECISION inline (no createServerFileRoute/createServerRoute in @tanstack/react-start@1.168.28 / react-router@1.170.18 — confirmed absent by grep) and explain the sidecar-vs-SSR-layer tradeoff; this is the design's documented fallback, not an undocumented hack, and leaves a clean seam (`$.ts` routes could delegate to handleBffRequest unchanged) if a future TanStack release adds a real server-route creator. Tests NOT weakened: src/bff-surface.test.ts (regression guard reading ../server.ts, asserting /health,/bff/login,/bff/callback,/bff/user,/bff/logout,/api/** strings) is untouched and passes — confirmed server.ts is absent from `git diff` (unmodified) and still contains all 6 route markers. src/lib/bff-server.test.ts (6/6) drives the real port with a real openid-client mock (no behavior stubbed out) — 4 behavioral cases from RED now pass for real reasons (verified live curl independently reproduces every assertion). tests=pass: `pnpm exec vitest run` in apps/wallow-web = 6 files, 21/21 passed. `pnpm exec tsc --noEmit` = clean (no output). oxlint --deny-warnings on the 3 touched files (bff-server.ts, dev-server.ts, vitest.config.ts) = clean. No `as any`, no TODO/FIXME/"not implemented" left in touched files. No src/routes/bff/$.ts or src/routes/api/$.ts stub files were created (report is accurate — the design's Start-server-route file path was genuinely abandoned, not silently half-done). DEVIATION (flagged, not blocking): acceptance criterion "apps/wallow-web/server.ts and public/ are deleted only after the above verify" — verify passed but server.ts/public/ were deliberately NOT deleted. Reason is sound and documented: (1) bff-surface.test.ts is an explicit regression guard from 2.2 that reads server.ts and would fail if deleted; (2) Dockerfile CMD still runs `pnpm start` -> tsx server.ts and docker-compose.test.yml's bff-example service depends on it; the parent epic (Wallow-8w1h.2 DESIGN notes) already flags "docker-wiring follow-up task" as explicitly out of scope for 2.1/2.2/2.3, and later phase children (8.2 "preserve BFF smoke surface for BffFlowTests", 9.1-9.2 full verification) exist to carry this forward. For a SPIKE whose stated purpose is proving the h3-to-Start bridge (not file cleanup), this is a reasonable, well-documented judgment call rather than a hack — forcing deletion now would break the very regression guard the epic put in place and break E2E/Docker with no corresponding task to fix it in this bead's scope. verdict=CLOSE

title: Tighten Wolverine handler DI to drop ServiceLocationPolicy.AllowedButWarn
description:
Wolverine 6 defaults ServiceLocationPolicy to NotAllowed. We set it to AllowedButWarn in Wallow.Api Program.cs to keep booting after the 6.19.0 upgrade. Root cause: handler dependencies require runtime service location:
- ITenantContext / ITenantContextSetter are registered as opaque scoped lambda factories (Wallow.Shared.Kernel.MultiTenancy) - Wolverine cannot inline them.
- ISetupStatusChecker (SetupStatusChecker) depends on UserManager<WallowUser> and resolves via IServiceProvider directly.

Task: refactor these registrations so Wolverine can generate inline resolution (register concrete types / non-opaque factories; avoid direct IServiceProvider use in handler-reached services). Then remove opts.ServiceLocationPolicy = AllowedButWarn from Program.cs and confirm the API boots under the default NotAllowed. Watch the '[M:System] Utilizing service location for Message Handler...' warnings emitted at codegen time - each names a service to fix.

title: Enable strict oxlint ruleset and resolve findings
description: Replace the current permissive .oxlintrc.json (currently only correctness=error, suspicious=warn) with a strict category config, then fix or narrowly justify every resulting finding — no blanket suppressions — until 'pnpm lint' (which now runs with --deny-warnings per task Wallow-ve7q.2.1) is fully clean.
design:
Step 1: replace .oxlintrc.json with:
{

  "plugins": ["typescript", "unicorn", "oxc", "react"],
  "categories": {
    "correctness": "error",
    "suspicious": "error",
    "perf": "error",
    "pedantic": "warn",
    "style": "warn"
  },
  "rules": {},
  "env": { "builtin": true },
  "ignorePatterns": ["**/dist/**", "**/generated/**", "packages/sdk/src/generated/**"]
}
Verify category/plugin names against node_modules/oxlint/configuration_schema.json first. Rationale: correctness/suspicious/perf are hard errors; pedantic/style are warnings that --deny-warnings (added in task Wallow-ve7q.2.1) escalates to failures in pnpm lint and CI. Never add a blanket file-level or repo-level disable to silence a whole category. Re-run 'pnpm lint' until it PASSes with --deny-warnings (zero errors, zero warnings).

Step 5: run 'pnpm -r typecheck && pnpm -r build && pnpm -r test' to confirm lint fixes didn't change behavior.

Step 6: run 'pnpm format && pnpm format:check' to re-normalize (lint fixes may have shifted formatting) — expect PASS.

title: Rewrite apps/tanstack-min/Dockerfile off npm onto pnpm workspace
description: apps/tanstack-min/Dockerfile (build context is repo root via docker/docker-compose.test.yml service 'bff-example', which sets context: ..) is stale npm-based and will fail: it COPYs 'packages/sdk/package.json packages/sdk/package-lock.json' (package-lock.json does not exist -- this repo is a pnpm workspace with pnpm-lock.yaml at root), runs 'npm ci'/'npm install' (cannot resolve the SDK's workspace:* dependency on @bc-solutions-coder/sdk), and never copies pnpm-workspace.yaml/pnpm-lock.yaml into the build. Rewrite it as a pnpm multi-stage build. This is fully independent of the .NET src->api rename (Wallow-07t5.5.1) -- it touches zero .NET/src/api paths, only apps/tanstack-min and packages/sdk (pnpm workspace paths).
design:
Reference shape (adjust to apps/tanstack-min's actual package.json build/start scripts and the Node version pinned in .nvmrc at repo root, currently Node 24):
FROM node:22-slim AS build
RUN corepack enable
WORKDIR /repo
COPY package.json pnpm-workspace.yaml pnpm-lock.yaml .npmrc tsconfig.base.json ./
COPY packages/sdk/package.json packages/sdk/
COPY apps/tanstack-min/package.json apps/tanstack-min/
RUN pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
COPY packages/sdk packages/sdk
COPY apps/tanstack-min apps/tanstack-min
RUN pnpm --filter @bc-solutions-coder/sdk build && pnpm --filter tanstack-min build

FROM node:22-slim AS runtime
RUN corepack enable
WORKDIR /repo
# copy built output + production deps; run the app's actual start command -- check apps/tanstack-min/package.json 'scripts.start' and server.ts for the real entrypoint/port (current Dockerfile uses EXPOSE 3000 / ENV PORT=3000 / CMD npm start).
Confirm the exact pnpm package name for the example from apps/tanstack-min/package.json (referenced above as 'tanstack-min' -- verify, do not assume) before wiring the --filter flags. Keep the file at apps/tanstack-min/Dockerfile; no other files change.
acceptance_criteria: From docker/: 'docker compose -f docker-compose.test.yml build bff-example' succeeds using pnpm (no npm/npm-ci/package-lock.json references remain in the Dockerfile). Commit as 'fix(bff): rebuild tanstack-min Dockerfile on pnpm workspace'.

title: Add CI OpenAPI snapshot drift-check workflow (.github/workflows/openapi-drift.yml)
description: packages/sdk/openapi/v1.json is a committed OpenAPI snapshot (regenerated manually today via the SDK's 'generate' script -- packages/sdk/package.json has scripts.generate = 'openapi-ts', backed by packages/sdk/scripts/generate.ts using @hey-api/openapi-ts). Nothing today keeps this snapshot in sync with the live API contract. Add a CI job that starts the API, fetches its live /openapi/v1.json, regenerates the snapshot the same way a developer would, and fails the build if the committed snapshot has drifted -- with a message telling the developer to refresh and commit. Create this as its own small workflow file rather than adding a job to an existing workflow.
design:
Job outline for .github/workflows/openapi-drift.yml:
1. Checkout, setup .NET + pnpm/node (mirror the setup steps used in .github/workflows/ci.yml for both toolchains).
2. Start the API so /openapi/v1.json is servable -- either 'dotnet run' against the API project (check current project path at implementation time: it is src/Wallow.Api today but may already be api/src/Wallow.Api if Wallow-07t5.5.1 has landed first -- verify with 'ls' before hardcoding) or run the already-published container image from CI, whichever is simpler to wire in a short-lived CI job. Wait for it to be healthy before curling.
3. curl/fetch the live spec and diff it against packages/sdk/openapi/v1.json, OR run the SDK's own regeneration path: WALLOW_OPENAPI_URL=<local API base url> pnpm --filter @bc-solutions-coder/sdk run generate (confirm this is still the exact script name in packages/sdk/package.json at implementation time).
4. git diff --exit-code packages/sdk/openapi/v1.json -- fail with a clear message if there is drift (tell the developer to run the SDK's generate script and commit the updated snapshot).
Note: this workflow does not modify any existing file, so it carries no direct technical dependency on the .NET src->api rename (Wallow-07t5.5.1); it only needs to resolve wherever the API project happens to live at the time it is implemented (see step 2).
acceptance_criteria: python3 -c "import yaml; yaml.safe_load(open('.github/workflows/openapi-drift.yml')); print('OK')" prints OK (valid YAML). The job fails when packages/sdk/openapi/v1.json is stale relative to a locally-generated spec, and passes when it matches. Commit as 'ci: add OpenAPI snapshot drift-check for sdk'.
notes:
SCOUT: dep added on Wallow-07t5.5.1 (src->api rename) as a precaution, not a hard technical block -- the plan text for Task 9b does not itself reference src/ or api/ paths, but the new workflow's job must start the .NET API to curl /openapi/v1.json, which means picking a dotnet project path (src/Wallow.Api today, api/src/Wallow.Api post-rename) or wiring against a published image. Since .github/workflows/*.yml is exactly the file category the rename's Task 4 sweeps, sequencing this after the rename avoids writing a new CI workflow against soon-to-be-stale paths. If the implementer determines at pickup time that they will source the API via an already-built/published container image (path-agnostic), this dep could be dropped -- left in place here as the safer default.
GREEN: FILES=.github/workflows/openapi-drift.yml (new, 154 lines; no baseline snapshot needed — packages/sdk/openapi/v1.json already committed).

HOW DRIFT IS DETECTED: standalone workflow 'OpenAPI Drift' (pull_request + push on main, path-filtered to api/**, packages/sdk/openapi/**, openapi-ts.config.ts, scripts/generate.ts, and the workflow itself). title: Add RemoteSessionStore (server-side session store for scale-out)
description: SessionStore implementation that delegates session persistence to a central token-handler HTTP service, for topologies where multiple frontends share sessions/SSO beyond a single co-located Valkey. Deferred out of epic Wallow-jgr2 (Wallow SDK Shared Auth — Core BFF Path), which shipped CookieSessionStore and ValkeySessionStore.
design: Per docs/plans/2026-07-05-wallow-sdk-auth-architecture.md §6.1 and §7 (Option B, 'Central token-handler service (future, not now)'): RemoteSessionStore implements the existing SessionStore interface (read/write/destroy/withRefreshLock) by calling a token-handler service's HTTP API — it talks to a *service*, not a raw remote Redis connection; never expose Valkey across a trust boundary. ref = opaque session ID, same as ValkeySessionStore. withRefreshLock delegates lock coordination to the remote service. This store is 'designed now, not built now' per the doc — the SessionStore interface shape in epic Wallow-jgr2 was deliberately kept minimal (read/write/destroy/withRefreshLock over an opaque string ref) specifically so this implementation, and configureDirectClient/configureServiceClient (Wallow-idzh, Wallow-esrp), could be added later with no changes to createBffHandlers, createApiProxy, or route wiring.
acceptance_criteria: RemoteSessionStore class implements SessionStore against a configurable token-handler base URL; read/write/destroy/withRefreshLock all round-trip through the remote service's HTTP API; unit tests cover session hit/miss, write returning an opaque ref, destroy being no-op-safe, and refresh-lock delegation/contention; npm run typecheck and vitest pass; README/design doc note updated to mark this store as shipped rather than future.
notes: Confirmed not started: packages/typescript-sdk/src/server/store/ contains only cookie.ts and valkey.ts (+ types.ts). Note ValkeySessionStore (a336973a) already provides server-side revocation + refresh lock, which may cover much of the scale-out need — re-scope or close if Valkey suffices.
close_reason: bead reset 2026-07-17: archived in docs/plans/2026-07-17-bead-archive.md; re-file against React only if still real

title: Add configureServiceClient SDK preset (client-credentials, machine-to-machine)
description: Client preset for server-to-server calls with no user context: performs an OAuth2 client-credentials grant and attaches the resulting token to API requests. Deferred out of epic Wallow-jgr2 (Wallow SDK Shared Auth — Core BFF Path), which shipped only configureBffClient.
design: Per docs/plans/2026-07-05-wallow-sdk-auth-architecture.md §5.3: interface ServiceClientOptions { baseUrl: string; tokenEndpoint: string; clientId: string; clientSecret: string; scope?: string }. Mirrors bcordes.dev's existing service-client.ts. Should cache/reuse the client-credentials token until near expiry rather than re-fetching per request. The generated typed operations are mode-agnostic and unchanged by this preset. Interfaces in epic Wallow-jgr2 (client preset shape, generated-ops separation from transport) were deliberately shaped to admit this preset later with no route changes.
acceptance_criteria: configureServiceClient(options) exported from packages/typescript-sdk; performs client-credentials token exchange against tokenEndpoint, attaches Authorization: Bearer to requests, and refreshes the token before expiry; unit tests cover token acquisition, caching/reuse, and refresh-on-expiry; npm run typecheck and vitest pass; README documents usage for backend jobs/service accounts.
notes: Overlaps heavily with Wallow-pczj.3.2 (Service-account helper: client-credentials token + Wallow API calls) — substantially the same work. Verified neither exists: 'client_credentials' appears only in generated SDK code, and configureServiceClient is absent from packages/typescript-sdk/src/.

title: Add configureDirectClient SDK preset (bearer-token, no BFF)
description: Client preset that points the fetch client at the API base URL directly and attaches Authorization: Bearer from an injected async token source, bypassing the BFF proxy entirely. Deferred out of epic Wallow-jgr2 (Wallow SDK Shared Auth — Core BFF Path), which shipped only configureBffClient.
design: Per docs/plans/2026-07-05-wallow-sdk-auth-architecture.md §5.2: interface DirectClientOptions { baseUrl: string; getAccessToken: () => Promise<string | null> }. Requires CORS on the API. Intended for a SPA whose token-handler hands it a short-lived token — browser-resident refresh tokens are explicitly NOT a supported pattern (see design doc §9.1); prefer SPA -> token-handler. Ship as advanced/opt-in and document accordingly. The generated typed operations are mode-agnostic and unchanged by this preset — same operations work under configureBffClient, configureDirectClient, and configureServiceClient. Interfaces in epic Wallow-jgr2 (client preset shape, generated-ops separation from transport) were deliberately shaped to admit this preset later with no route changes.
acceptance_criteria: configureDirectClient(options) exported from packages/typescript-sdk; sets baseUrl and attaches Authorization: Bearer header per-request via getAccessToken(); no cookies/credentials sent; unit tests cover token attachment and null-token (no header) cases; npm run typecheck and vitest pass; README documents it as advanced/opt-in with the browser-refresh-token caveat.
close_reason: Won't-fix: configureDirectClient explicitly requires CORS on the API, which directly contradicts the locked no-CORS decision in docs/plans/2026-07-17-blazor-exit-design.md (CORS stays absent, no browser cross-origin access to the API, ever).

title: T5.2: Resilient forward in the BFF proxy
description: Add forwardWithResilience() to src/server/proxy.ts implementing Appendix B error behaviors: reactive 401/3xx/429/network handling with single retry. TDD.
design: Files: src/server/proxy.ts:112-156, src/server/proxy.test.ts. forwardWithResilience(req, config, store, session, ref): set redirect:manual on fetch; wrap in AbortController(30s); classify errors: upstream 401 -> refresh under lock + retry once; upstream 3xx with Location containing Account/Login -> treat as auth failure -> refresh + retry once; upstream 429 with Retry-After header -> wait (bounded, e.g. max 5s) + retry once; network throw -> 503 WallowError NETWORK_ERROR; AbortController timeout -> 503 WallowError NETWORK_TIMEOUT; non-OK JSON body -> parse as ProblemDetails preserve status. Log with redact(). Use in createApiProxy. Tests: each Appendix B behavior as a separate case. Second 401 after retry -> surfaces as WallowError.
acceptance_criteria: npx vitest run src/server/proxy.test.ts PASS (all resilience cases). Commit: feat(sdk): add reactive 401/3xx/429/network handling to the BFF proxy

- export interface ForwardResult { response: Response; session: BffSession }
- export async function forceRefreshSession(session, config, store, ref): Promise<BffSession>
- export async function forwardWithResilience(request: ForwardRequest, config, store, session, ref): Promise<ForwardResult>

SPEC the tests pin (green implementer read this):
1. forceRefreshSession = the reactive-path refresh: refreshes UNCONDITIONALLY (ignores expiresAt — local expiry says fresh but upstream rejected the token), inside store.withRefreshLock, bumps version, store.write()s, returns the new session. Throws when refreshToken is absent — message must match /refresh token/i. Refactor: extract the lock+refresh body of ensureFreshSession and have ensureFreshSession delegate to it (its 5 existing tests must keep passing).
2. forwardWithResilience attempt shape: fetch(target, { method, headers (authorization: Bearer <session.accessToken> set per attempt), body, redirect: 'manual', signal }) — signal must be an AbortSignal from an AbortController bounded by FORWARD_TIMEOUT_MS. Tests assert init.redirect === 'manual' and init.signal instanceof AbortSignal on EVERY attempt.
3. Happy path: response.ok -> { response, session: <unchanged session> }, exactly 1 fetch, zero withRefreshLock calls.
4. Reactive 401 -> forceRefreshSession + replay ONCE. Replay carries 'Bearer <new access token>' AND the same method+body. Returns { response, session: <rotated session> } — createApiProxy needs the rotated session back to re-seal the cookie.
5. Second 401 after the replay -> throw parseProblemDetails(response, bodyText): status 401, code from extensions.code. Exactly 2 fetches, exactly 1 refreshTokens call (no second refresh, no third attempt — the fetch stub REJECTS on an unscripted attempt, so over-retrying fails the test).
6. 401 with NO refreshToken on the session -> no retry, no refreshTokens call, throw WallowError immediately (1 fetch).
7. 3xx whose Location contains '/Account/Login' -> same treatment as a 401 (force refresh + replay once). Twice -> WallowError with status 401 (an auth failure regardless of the 302 it wore). A 3xx to any OTHER Location is NOT an auth failure: return the 302 response as-is, no refresh, no retry.
8. 429 -> wait Retry-After seconds (header '1' -> 1000ms), bounded by MAX_RETRY_AFTER_MS (header '3600' must still retry after 5s, not an hour), then replay ONCE. Not an auth failure: withRefreshLock must NOT be called. Second 429 -> WallowError status 429, code from extensions.code, NOT waited out again (2 fetches total). Wait must be a real setTimeout — tests drive it with vi.advanceTimersByTimeAsync.
9. fetch rejects (TypeError) -> WallowError { status: 503, code: NETWORK_ERROR_CODE }, NOT retried (1 fetch).
10. Attempt exceeds FORWARD_TIMEOUT_MS (abort fires; fetch rejects with an AbortError) -> WallowError { status: 503, code: NETWORK_TIMEOUT_CODE }. Must be distinguishable from case 9, i.e. check err.name === 'AbortError' / signal.aborted rather than treating every throw as NETWORK_ERROR.

TWO-CLIENT DISCONNECT (confirmed): src/client.ts:16 does 'export const client = createClient();' -- a FRESH, independent @hey-api/client-fetch client instance. But src/generated/sdk.gen.ts (e.g. line ~34) imports 'client as _heyApiClient from ./client.gen' and every generated op function defaults to '(options?.client ?? _heyApiClient)'. src/generated/client.gen.ts:16-18 creates ITS OWN client: 'export const client = createClient(createConfig<ClientOptions>({baseUrl:"http://localhost:5001/"}))'. (2) user handler at handlers.ts:357-370 currently 'return session.user;' (bare user object, not wrapped) - must add csrfToken into the response body, e.g. return { ...session.user, csrfToken: session.csrfToken }. - defineEventHandler(handler: (event:H3Event)=>any): EventHandler

- sendRedirect(event, location:string, code?:number): Promise<void>  — returns promise, must be returned from handler

  TX_COOKIE(name:string) = name+'_tx'
  readSession(event,config): reads getCookie(event,config.cookieName), calls unsealSession
  writeSession(event,config,session): calls sealSession then setCookie with baseCookieOpts (no maxAge = session cookie)

SCOUT PROXY.TS COMPOSITION PATTERN (T10):
EXPIRY_SKEW_MS = 30_000

ensureFreshSession(config:BffConfig, doc:DiscoveryDoc, session:BffSession): Promise<{session:BffSession,refreshed:boolean}>
  - if session.expiresAt - EXPIRY_SKEW_MS > Date.now() return {session, refreshed:false}
  - if !session.refreshToken throw new Error('Session expired and no refresh token')
  - tokens = await refreshTokens(config, doc, session.refreshToken)
  - return {refreshed:true, session:{...session, accessToken:tokens.access_token, refreshToken:tokens.refresh_token??session.refreshToken, idToken:tokens.id_token??session.idToken, expiresAt:Date.now()+tokens.expires_in*1000}}

createApiProxy(config:BffConfig): EventHandler
  - readSession or (setResponseStatus(401)+return)
  - discover(config)
  - ensureFreshSession (catch -> setResponseStatus(401)+return)
  - if refreshed: writeSession(event,config,result.session)
  - strip /api prefix: event.path or getRequestPath(event), new URL(stripped, config.apiBaseUrl)
  - fetch upstream with {method, headers:{Authorization:'Bearer '+session.accessToken, content-type, accept}, body}
  - setResponseStatus(event, upstream.status)
  - setResponseHeaders (exclude transfer-encoding, content-encoding)
  - return new Uint8Array(await upstream.arrayBuffer())

DIAGNOSE: ROOT CAUSE = @rendermode InteractiveServer with default prerender:true on Register.razor and AuthLayout.razor causes OnInitializedAsync to run TWICE (prerender phase + interactive phase after SignalR circuit connects), producing 6 sequential HTTP round-trips to the API before the page is interactive.

EVIDENCE (code, no live timing needed — structural analysis):

CHAIN on /register?client_id=...:
  Phase 1 – prerender (server-side, blocks HTML delivery):
    (a) AuthLayout.razor:95 → await BrandingClient.GetBrandingAsync(ClientId) → GET /v1/identity/apps/{clientId}/branding (ClientBrandingApiClient.cs:8)
    (b) Register.razor:217 → await AuthClient.GetExternalProvidersAsync() → GET /v1/identity/auth/external-providers (AuthApiClient.cs:113)
    (c) Register.razor:221 → await ResolveOrgNameAsync() → GET /v1/identity/auth/client-tenant/{clientId} (Register.razor:231) — sequential after (b)
  Phase 2 – interactive (after SignalR circuit connects): (a), (b), (c) ALL repeat identically.
  TOTAL: 6 sequential HTTP calls. At 50-150ms each → 600ms-1800ms of pure API-wait before the page is interactive.

CHAIN on /login (the page before Register):
  Same double-init: AuthLayout:95 GetBrandingAsync + Login.razor:253 GetExternalProvidersAsync = 4 sequential HTTP calls.

All Auth pages carry @rendermode InteractiveServer (no prerender:false anywhere in src/Wallow.Auth/Components/Pages/). BrandingTheme.razor in App.razor is fast (no I/O). CookieForwardingHandler.cs:28-33 seeds browser cookies from HttpContext during prerender; Register and Login initialization calls (GetExternalProvidersAsync, GetBrandingAsync, ResolveOrgNameAsync) do NOT require browser cookies — safe to disable prerender.

  #1 (DOMINANT) – double OnInitializedAsync from prerender:true on Register.razor + AuthLayout.razor — adds 3×2=6 sequential HTTP calls; the fix eliminates 3 of them entirely.

description: Edit .github/workflows/deploy.yml and .github/workflows/ci.yml build jobs to: (1) delete generated CSS files before dotnet build runs, (2) scope or tighten the restore-keys so stale generated static web assets cannot leak across commits, (3) bump the build cache key (e.g. add a v2 prefix) so the next deploy starts clean. design: deploy.yml build job: 'Restore previous build output' uses restore-keys: build-${{ runner.os }}- which is the cross-commit fallback. The cache key build-${{ runner.os }}-${{ github.sha }} is exact-match per commit. When a new commit runs, the fallback key picks up ANY previous build, including one with old CSS. Solution: add rm -f step before dotnet build AND change restore-keys to use a versioned prefix (e.g. build-v2-${{ runner.os }}-) and update the cache save/restore keys to match (build-v2-${{ runner.os }}-${{ github.sha }}). This ensures old caches are ignored while same-run artifact sharing still works. ci.yml has the identical pattern and needs the same treatment.

title: Add .NET Aspire AppHost for local development orchestration
description:
Replace the current multi-step local dev startup (docker compose up + 3 separate dotnet run commands) with a single aspire run command using .NET Aspire.

## What
- Create Wallow.AppHost project declaring full topology (Postgres, Valkey, GarageHQ, Mailpit, Api, Auth, Web)
- Create Wallow.ServiceDefaults project with shared OpenTelemetry, health checks, service discovery, and HTTP resilience
- Add custom container definitions for GarageHQ, Mailpit, ClamAV (no first-party Aspire integrations)
- Simplify Program.cs in Api/Auth/Web to use AddServiceDefaults() instead of manual OTLP boilerplate
- Update Directory.Packages.props with Aspire hosting + client packages

## Why
- Current workflow requires 4 steps: docker compose up, then 3 separate dotnet run commands in separate terminals
- Connection strings must be manually synced in appsettings.Development.json across developers
- Local observability requires running the full Grafana+Alloy+LGTM stack
- Aspire provides one-command startup, automatic connection string injection, health-checked startup ordering, and a built-in dev dashboard with distributed tracing

## Scope
- Local development only — do NOT change CI, E2E test infrastructure, or production docker-compose files
- Keep existing docker-compose.yml, docker-compose.test.yml, docker-compose.production.yml, and run-e2e.sh untouched
- Production telemetry configuration must continue to work independently of Aspire

title: Implement session creation + advisory-lock eviction logic
description: In ExchangeTicket flow: acquire PostgreSQL advisory lock pg_advisory_xact_lock(hashtext(userId::text)), count active sessions, if count >= limit (default 5) evict oldest by LastActiveAt (delete record + add to Redis revocation set + publish UserSessionEvictedEvent), then insert new ActiveSession. Advisory lock prevents race where concurrent logins both pass count check. Limit configurable per-org via tenant settings key security.max_concurrent_sessions.
acceptance_criteria: Session created on login. Oldest evicted when limit exceeded. Advisory lock prevents concurrent over-creation. Tenant setting overrides default limit.
notes: Depends on: ActiveSession entity and Redis session revocation middleware.

title: Implement Redis session revocation middleware
description: Create middleware that checks for revoked session IDs on each authenticated request. On eviction, add session:revoked:<sessionId> to Redis with 30-day TTL. Middleware checks this set — if session is revoked, reject the request (sign out + redirect to login). This provides surgical per-session revocation without affecting other user sessions (unlike SecurityStamp which nukes all sessions).
acceptance_criteria: Revoked session gets rejected on next request. Non-revoked sessions unaffected. Redis key has 30-day TTL.

title: Implement atomic Redis SET NX EX ticket replay prevention
description: In AccountController.ExchangeTicket, after validating the ticket: compute SHA256 hash of the ticket string, then use atomic StringSetAsync(ticket:used:<hash>, 1, 65s, When.NotExists). If returns false (key existed), return 401 ticket_already_used. The atomic SET NX EX eliminates the TOCTOU race condition. 65s TTL accounts for clock skew beyond the 60s ticket lifetime. Uses existing IConnectionMultiplexer.
acceptance_criteria: First exchange succeeds. Second exchange with same ticket returns 401. Concurrent exchanges — only one succeeds. Redis key expires after 65s.
notes: Depends on: Jti field task.

title: Implement MFA challenge handler and controller
description: Replace no-op DefaultMfaChallengeHandler with real implementation. CheckMfaRequiredAsync: check user.MfaEnabled and tenant MFA policy config. Wire into AccountController login flow — after password validates, call CheckMfaRequired, return mfa_required response if needed. Create MfaController with endpoints: POST /api/v1/identity/auth/mfa-verify, POST mfa/enroll, POST mfa/confirm, POST mfa/disable. Add Mfa config section to appsettings.json (DefaultPolicy, MaxAttempts, ChallengeTtlSeconds, BackupCodeCount).
acceptance_criteria: MFA challenge flow works end-to-end. Users with MFA enabled get challenged after password. TOTP codes validate correctly. Backup codes work. Account locks after max attempts. Enrollment generates QR code. Confirm activates MFA. Disable requires current code. All config from appsettings.
notes: Files to modify: DefaultMfaChallengeHandler.cs, AccountController.cs, appsettings.json. Files to create: MfaController.cs. See docs/plans/2026-03-23-auth-architecture-plan.md Task 5.3

Implement using System.Security.Cryptography for RFC 6238 TOTP. Use IDataProtectionProvider for secret encryption. QR URI format: otpauth://totp/{appName}:{email}?secret={secret}&issuer={appName}.
acceptance_criteria: ITotpMfaService interface exists. Implementation generates valid TOTP secrets. ValidateCode accepts correct codes within time window. Backup codes generated, validated, and marked as used. Tests cover generation, validation, expiry, and backup codes.

MFA challenge flow: password validates -> check MfaRequired -> return challenge token -> user submits TOTP code -> verify -> issue auth code. Tenant policy in Mfa config section. New MfaController for enrollment/verification endpoints. New MfaChallenge.razor and MfaEnroll.razor pages in Wallow.Auth.

design: ClientBrandingApiClient: uses IHttpClientFactory named client 'AuthApi', calls GET api/v1/identity/apps/{clientId}/branding. Returns ClientBrandingResponse? (null = use defaults). AuthLayout: reads ?client_id query param via [SupplyParameterFromQuery]. If non-null, fetches branding. Renders client logo/name/tagline in header, always shows Wallow branding in footer. HeadContent injects CSS variable overrides for client theme colors (light/dark), cascading over default BrandingTheme.razor output.

title: Server-Side Branding Service & API
description: ClientBrandingService with IMemoryCache caching and presigned URL resolution for logos. ClientBrandingController with public GET, authenticated POST (multipart/form-data with logo), and authenticated DELETE endpoints.
design: ClientBrandingService: queries repository, caches with 5-min sliding expiration, resolves logo presigned URLs (1-hour expiry) via IStorageProvider.GetPresignedUrlAsync. InvalidateCache on write. Controller: GET is AllowAnonymous with ResponseCache 300s. POST validates creator ownership via OpenIddict Properties creatorUserId. Logo validation: magic bytes for PNG/JPEG/WebP, 2MB max, no SVG. Theme JSON validation: only validates known color property names against oklch/hex/rem regex. DB save before logo upload to prevent orphans.

title: Identity Domain & Persistence
description: Domain entity, strongly-typed ID, EF Core configuration, repository, and database migration for ClientBranding in the Identity module.
design: ClientBranding entity extends Entity<ClientBrandingId> (NOT ITenantScoped — globally unique by ClientId). Fields: ClientId, DisplayName, Tagline, LogoStorageKey, ThemeJson, CreatedAt, UpdatedAt. Static Create factory with BusinessRuleException validation. Update method for modifications. ClearLogo for removal. EF config: snake_case columns, unique index on client_id, jsonb for theme_json. Repository: IClientBrandingRepository with GetByClientIdAsync, Add, Remove, SaveChangesAsync.

title: Client Branding for Registered Apps
description: Allow registered OAuth2 clients to customize the Auth UI (login, register, password reset) with their own branding — name, logo, tagline, and theme colors. When a user authenticates through a client's flow via ?client_id= query parameter, they see that client's branding. The 'A Wallow App' footer always remains visible.
design: New ClientBranding entity in Identity domain, stored in identity.client_brandings. Server-side ClientBrandingService queries DB and caches (IMemoryCache, 5-min sliding). Auth Blazor app uses ClientBrandingApiClient HTTP client to call public GET endpoint. Logos stored via IStorageProvider from Shared.Contracts (S3/local). Theme overrides injected via Blazor HeadContent. Spec: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-03-21-client-branding-design.md. Plan: docs/superpowers/plans/2026-03-21-client-branding.md

title: Client registration controller
description: Build the main registration endpoint POST /api/v1/identity/register. No [Authorize] attribute — auth via Bearer initial-access-token header. Flow: 1) Validate token (skip in dev via IHostEnvironment.IsDevelopment()), 2) Validate scopes against ApiScope table, 3) Determine client type from grant_types (client_credentials→sa- prefix, authorization_code→app- prefix, mixed→400), 4) Check existing client: exists→rotate secret + update name/URIs but NOT scopes, new→create OpenIddict app. Returns 201 Created or 200 OK. DTOs: ClientRegistrationRequest(ClientName, GrantTypes, ClientId?, Scope?, RedirectUris?, PostLogoutRedirectUris?), ClientRegistrationResponse(ClientId, ClientSecret, ClientName, GrantTypes, Scope?). 13 unit tests covering: new SA registration, re-registration with rotated secret, missing token 401, dev mode bypass, wrong prefix 400, invalid scope 400, mixed grant types 400, revoked token 401, expired token 401, token not found 401, auth code registration, auth code with wrong prefix 400.
acceptance_criteria: All 13 controller tests pass.

DTOs: CreateInitialAccessTokenRequest(DisplayName, ExpiresAt?), InitialAccessTokenResponse (with raw Token), InitialAccessTokenListResponse (without Token, with IsRevoked). 4 unit tests: create returns 201 with token, getAll returns list, delete existing returns 204 and revokes, delete missing returns 404.

title: Wallow.Web — Blazor Server Marketing & Dashboard App

title: Add complete-external-registration endpoint
description: Implement GET complete-external-registration on AccountController. Validates returnUrl early (before user creation). title: External Authentication Providers (Social Login)
description: Add Google, Apple, GitHub, and Microsoft social login to Wallow using ASP.NET Core external authentication handlers. Users authenticate with external providers, and the system creates or links accounts automatically. OpenIddict continues as the OIDC server for issuing tokens to Wallow clients.
design: Architecture: External auth providers register as ASP.NET Core authentication schemes alongside the existing OpenIddict server. AccountController gets three new endpoints: external-login (challenge), external-login-callback (link/create), and complete-external-registration (finalize new user after ToS). A utility class handles name extraction from provider claims. A new Blazor page in Wallow.Auth shows ToS acceptance for new social users. Spec: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-03-20-external-auth-providers-design.md. Plan: docs/superpowers/plans/2026-03-20-external-auth-providers.md

title: Add relative-path guard to AuthorizationController
description: In src/Modules/Identity/Wallow.Identity.Api/Controllers/AuthorizationController.cs, in Authorize() method, add a guard after building returnUrl from Request.PathBase + Request.Path + Request.QueryString. Check: if (Uri.TryCreate(returnUrl, UriKind.Absolute, out _)) redirect to error page. This prevents injection of absolute URLs. Both Authorize() (GET) and AuthorizePost() (POST) share the same code path, so one guard covers both.

title: SEC2: Reduce Keycloak service account roles to minimum needed
description:
## Vulnerability (INFRA-05, MEDIUM, Risk Score 8)

docker/keycloak/realm-export.json:305-308 grants service-account-foundry-api the manage-realm role. This is overly broad - if service account credentials are compromised, attacker gets full realm admin.

## Files to Modify
- docker/keycloak/realm-export.json

## Remediation
Remove manage-realm from service account role mappings. Keep only:
- manage-users (needed for user CRUD)
- view-users (needed for user queries)
- manage-clients (if needed for SCIM/SSO config)
- view-realm (if needed for realm info)

Remove: manage-realm, manage-authorization, manage-events, manage-identity-providers (unless specifically needed).

## Testing
- Verify API can still create/update/delete users
- Verify API can still manage organizations
- Verify SCIM operations still work
- Verify SSO configuration still works

Missing mappings for: StorageRead, StorageWrite, MessagingAccess, ConfigurationRead, ConfigurationManage, SsoRead, SsoManage, ScimManage, ApiKeysRead/Create/Update/Delete, OrganizationsRead/Create/Update/ManageMembers, RolesRead/Create/Delete, UsersCreate, UsersDelete, AnnouncementRead/Manage, ChangelogManage, BillingRead, BillingManage, etc. API keys with unmapped scopes silently grant no permissions.

## Files to Modify
- src/Modules/Identity/Foundry.Identity.Infrastructure/Authorization/PermissionExpansionMiddleware.cs
- src/Shared/Foundry.Shared.Kernel/Identity/Authorization/PermissionType.cs (reference for all permissions)
- src/Modules/Identity/Foundry.Identity.Domain/ApiKeys/ApiScopes.cs (reference for valid scopes)

## Remediation
Option A (convention-based): Auto-map scope names to permission names using a naming convention.
Option B (explicit): Add all missing scope mappings to MapScopeToPermission.

Ensure ApiScopes.ValidScopes and MapScopeToPermission are always in sync. Consider a unit test that verifies every valid scope has a corresponding permission mapping.

## Testing
- Verify all valid API key scopes map to correct permissions
- Verify API keys with storage/config/messaging scopes actually work
- Add unit test: every ApiScopes.ValidScopes entry has a MapScopeToPermission mapping

title: Adopt HybridCache for two-level caching
description:
Replace manual IMemoryCache + IDistributedCache (Valkey) patterns with the new HybridCache from ASP.NET Core 10. HybridCache provides automatic L1 (in-process) + L2 (distributed) caching with built-in stampede protection via GetOrCreateAsync.

Benefits:
- Stampede protection (only one thread fetches on cache miss)
- Automatic L1/L2 with single API
- Less boilerplate code
- Tag-based invalidation

Steps:
1. Add Microsoft.Extensions.Caching.Hybrid NuGet package
2. Register: builder.Services.AddHybridCache()
3. Identify current caching patterns in the codebase (search for IMemoryCache, IDistributedCache, ICacheService)
4. Replace with HybridCache.GetOrCreateAsync() calls
5. Configure serialization (System.Text.Json) and expiration policies
6. Valkey is already in docker-compose as the distributed backend

Key areas to apply:
- API key caching (Identity)
- Tenant configuration caching (Configuration module)
- Permission set caching (Identity/Authorization)
- Any read-heavy query results currently cached manually

title: SEC2: Add user to tenant organization on CreateUser
description:
## Vulnerability (NEW-IDENT-002, MEDIUM, Risk Score 9)

UsersController.cs:96-107 CreateUser creates a Keycloak user but doesn't add them to the current tenant's organization. The user is 'dangling' in the realm without organization membership.

## Files to Modify
- src/Modules/Identity/Foundry.Identity.Api/Controllers/UsersController.cs (CreateUser method)

## Remediation
After creating the user, add them to the current tenant's organization:
```csharp
[HttpPost]
[HasPermission(PermissionType.UsersCreate)]
public async Task<ActionResult<Guid>> CreateUser(CreateUserRequest request, CancellationToken ct)
{
    Guid userId = await _keycloakAdmin.CreateUserAsync(
        request.Email, request.FirstName, request.LastName,
        request.TemporaryPassword, ct);
    await _keycloakOrg.AddMemberAsync(_tenantContext.TenantId.Value, userId, ct);
    return CreatedAtAction(nameof(GetUserById), new { id = userId }, userId);
}
```

## Testing
- Verify created user belongs to current tenant's organization
- Verify user appears in GetUsers results (which filters by org)
- Verify user cannot be seen by other tenants

title: Standardize CreateCustomFieldDefinitionHandler to return Result
description:
CreateCustomFieldDefinitionHandler throws CustomFieldException directly when a duplicate field key is detected, instead of returning Result.Failure(). This is inconsistent with all other command handlers that use the Result pattern for expected failures.

Fix:
1. Replace throw CustomFieldException with return Result.Failure(Error.Conflict(...)) or Result.Failure(Error.BusinessRule(...))
2. Ensure the controller maps the failure result correctly via ToActionResult()
3. Verify the error response format matches other endpoints

File: src/Modules/Configuration/Foundry.Configuration.Application/Commands/ (CreateCustomFieldDefinitionHandler)

title: Map ScimFilterException to 400 in GlobalExceptionHandler
description:
ScimFilterException is a plain Exception subclass in Foundry.Identity.Infrastructure.Scim, not part of the DomainException hierarchy. When SCIM filter parsing fails, the exception hits GlobalExceptionHandler as a catch-all and returns 500 instead of 400 Bad Request.

Fix options:
1. Add ScimFilterException mapping in GlobalExceptionHandler → 400 Bad Request with detail including the parser position
2. Or make ScimFilterException extend BusinessRuleException with code 'Identity.InvalidScimFilter'
3. Or catch it at the ScimController level and return a SCIM-formatted 400 error (consistent with RFC 7644 SCIM error format)

Option 3 is preferred since SCIM endpoints already use their own error format.

File: src/Modules/Identity/Foundry.Identity.Infrastructure/Scim/ScimFilterException.cs
File: src/Modules/Identity/Foundry.Identity.Api/Controllers/ScimController.cs

title: SEC2: Fix metering decimal-to-long truncation
description:
## Vulnerability (B-3, MEDIUM, Risk Score 9)

ValkeyMeteringService.cs:64 uses db.StringIncrementAsync(key, (long)value) which truncates fractional values. A meter increment of 0.5 becomes 0, allowing unlimited usage for sub-1.0 increments.

## Files to Modify
- src/Modules/Billing/Foundry.Billing.Infrastructure/Services/ValkeyMeteringService.cs

## Remediation
Use the double overload of StringIncrementAsync:
```csharp
// Change from:
await db.StringIncrementAsync(key, (long)value, flags: CommandFlags.FireAndForget);
// To:
await db.StringIncrementAsync(key, (double)value, flags: CommandFlags.FireAndForget);
```

Also update GetCurrentUsageAsync to read as double:
```csharp
RedisValue val = await db.StringGetAsync(key);
return val.IsNull ? 0m : (decimal)(double)val;
```

## Testing
- Verify fractional increments (0.5, 0.1) are correctly tracked
- Verify integer increments still work
- Verify quota enforcement works with fractional values
- Verify GetCurrentUsageAsync returns correct fractional values

title: Remove orphan exception constructors that allow empty error codes
description:
Module-specific domain exceptions have parameterless constructors and (string message) constructors that bypass the code parameter, resulting in Code = string.Empty reaching the API response as "code": "".

Affected exceptions:
- InvalidInvoiceException (Billing)
- InvalidPaymentException (Billing)
- InvalidSubscriptionStatusTransitionException (Billing)
- InvalidEmailAddressException (Communications)
- InvalidPhoneNumberException (Communications)
- ConversationException (Communications)
- CustomFieldException (Configuration)
- FeatureFlagException (Configuration)

Fix:
1. Remove parameterless constructors from all module domain exceptions
2. Ensure all constructors require a non-empty code parameter, or default to a meaningful code based on the class name (e.g., 'Billing.InvalidInvoice')
3. Optionally add a guard in DomainException base constructor: throw ArgumentException if code is null/empty
4. Verify no callers use the parameterless constructors (compile errors will surface these)

title: Make Unauthorized() and Forbid() return ProblemDetails
description:
Controllers call return Unauthorized() and return Forbid() directly, which returns empty response bodies. This is inconsistent with all other error responses that use ProblemDetails format. Consumers cannot distinguish between auth failures without parsing the body.

Fix:
1. Replace Unauthorized() calls with a helper that returns ProblemDetails:
   ```csharp
   return Problem(statusCode: 401, title: "Unauthorized", detail: "User ID not found in claims");
   ```
2. Or configure ASP.NET Core to auto-produce ProblemDetails for 401/403 via:
   ```csharp
   builder.Services.AddProblemDetails();
   // This makes the framework produce ProblemDetails for all 4xx/5xx status codes
   ```
3. Verify traceId is included in the ProblemDetails response
4. Search all controllers for Unauthorized() and Forbid() calls and ensure consistency

title: SEC2: Auto-join tenant group on SignalR connect
SEC2: Remove or tenant-scope SendToAllAsync in realtime dispatcher
description:
## Vulnerability (NEW-API-3, MEDIUM, Risk Score 9)

SignalRRealtimeDispatcher.cs:45-58 SendToAllAsync uses hubContext.Clients.All.SendAsync(), broadcasting to every connected client across all tenants.

## Files to Modify
- src/Foundry.Api/Services/SignalRRealtimeDispatcher.cs
- src/Shared/Foundry.Shared.Contracts/Realtime/IRealtimeDispatcher.cs (if interface defined here)

## Remediation
Option A (preferred): Change SendToAllAsync to require tenantId and broadcast to tenant group only:
```csharp
public async Task SendToAllAsync(Guid tenantId, string method, object payload, CancellationToken ct = default)
{
    string tenantGroup = $"tenant:{tenantId}";
    await hubContext.Clients.Group(tenantGroup).SendAsync(method, payload, ct);
}
```

Option B: Remove the method if no callers need it. Check all references first with find_referencing_symbols.

Update the interface and all callers to pass tenantId.

## Testing
- Verify broadcasts only reach clients in the specified tenant
- Verify all callers pass correct tenantId
- Verify no cross-tenant data leaks via SignalR

title: Add OperationCanceledException handling in GlobalExceptionHandler
description:
When a client disconnects mid-request, OperationCanceledException is thrown. Currently this maps to 500 Internal Server Error, which pollutes error logs and metrics.

Fix:
1. Add OperationCanceledException catch in GlobalExceptionHandler
2. Return 499 Client Closed Request (nginx convention) or simply suppress the response (client is gone)
3. Log at Information/Debug level, not Error (client disconnection is not a server error)
4. Ensure the Activity/span is not marked as Error for cancellations

File: src/Foundry.Api/Middleware/GlobalExceptionHandler.cs

title: SEC2: Tenant-scope SignalR page context groups
description:
## Vulnerability (NEW-API-2, MEDIUM, Risk Score 9)

UpdatePageContext in RealtimeHub.cs:67-85 adds connections to group 'page:{pageContext}' without tenant prefix. Users from different tenants on the same page see each other's presence via PageViewersUpdated events. The Redis presence keys ARE tenant-scoped but the SignalR group name is NOT.

## Files to Modify
- src/Foundry.Api/Hubs/RealtimeHub.cs (UpdatePageContext method)

## Remediation
Change group name to include tenant prefix:
```csharp
string tenantPageGroup = $"page:{tenantId}:{pageContext}";
await Groups.AddToGroupAsync(Context.ConnectionId, tenantPageGroup);
```
Apply same pattern to RemoveFromGroup and broadcast calls.

Also add input validation for pageContext (reject empty, extremely long strings, or strings with path traversal characters).

## Testing
- Verify users in different tenants on same page do NOT see each other's presence
- Verify users in same tenant on same page DO see each other's presence
- Verify page context with special characters is handled safely

title: .NET 10 modernization
description: Adopt .NET 10 and C# 14 features to modernize the codebase. Includes: HybridCache for two-level caching, FrozenDictionary for startup-built lookups, C# 14 field keyword in value objects, EF Core 10 JSON column mapping for value objects, OpenTelemetry package upgrades for native .NET 10 instrumentation, and per-tenant rate limiting with keyed DI services.

title: SEC: Improve admin tenant override validation and audit
description:
MEDIUM (Risk 8). Admin tenant override via X-Tenant-Id header uses broad admin role, no target tenant validation, logs only via Serilog (no persistent audit).

FILES TO MODIFY:

FIX: 1) Validate target tenant GUID exists before allowing override. 2) Use case-insensitive role comparison. 3) Log admin overrides to audit table for persistent tracking.

Add tenant existence check: if (!await tenantValidator.TenantExistsAsync(overrideId)) return 400.
Log to audit: await auditService.LogAdminOverrideAsync(userId, resolvedTenantId, overrideId, requestPath).

TESTING: Verify invalid tenant GUIDs rejected. Verify audit entries created. Verify non-admin users cannot use X-Tenant-Id header.

COMPLEXITY: Medium

title: SEC: Add dedicated rate limiting to SCIM endpoints
description:
MEDIUM (Risk 8). SCIM endpoints create/delete Keycloak users but only use global rate limiter (1000/hour). Compromised SCIM token could rapidly provision rogue accounts.

FILES TO MODIFY:
- src/Foundry.Api/Extensions/ServiceCollectionExtensions.cs (or wherever rate limiting is configured) - Add scim rate limit policy
- src/Modules/Identity/Foundry.Identity.Api/Controllers/ScimController.cs - Add [EnableRateLimiting("scim")]

FIX: Register fixed window limiter: options.AddFixedWindowLimiter("scim", limiter => { limiter.PermitLimit = 100; limiter.Window = TimeSpan.FromHours(1); }). Apply to ScimController.

TESTING: Verify SCIM rate limit enforced independently of global limit.

COMPLEXITY: Small

title: SEC: Tighten auth endpoint rate limits
description:
MEDIUM (Risk 9). Per-IP rate limit of 5/5min is insufficient against distributed brute force.

FILES TO MODIFY:
- src/Foundry.Api/Extensions/RateLimitDefaults.cs:5-6

FIX: Change AuthPermitLimit from 5 to 3, AuthWindowMinutes from 5 to 10. Also ensure Keycloak brute force detection is enabled (operational - document in README).

TESTING: Verify rate limits enforced per IP at new thresholds.

COMPLEXITY: Small

title: SEC: Add token revocation/logout endpoint
SEC: Replace SCIM AllowAnonymous with proper auth scheme
description:
MEDIUM (Risk 10). ScimController uses [AllowAnonymous] bypassing ASP.NET Core auth pipeline. Auth handled solely by ScimAuthenticationMiddleware. Middleware reordering silently removes SCIM auth.

FILES TO MODIFY:
- src/Modules/Identity/Foundry.Identity.Api/Controllers/ScimController.cs:20 - Replace [AllowAnonymous] with [Authorize(AuthenticationSchemes = "ScimBearer")]
- src/Modules/Identity/Foundry.Identity.Infrastructure/Authorization/ScimAuthenticationMiddleware.cs - Extract token validation into ScimBearerAuthenticationHandler
- src/Modules/Identity/Foundry.Identity.Infrastructure/Extensions/IdentityInfrastructureExtensions.cs - Register ScimBearer scheme

FIX: Create ScimBearerAuthenticationHandler extending AuthenticationHandler<AuthenticationSchemeOptions>. Move token validation from middleware. Register with services.AddAuthentication().AddScheme<AuthenticationSchemeOptions, ScimBearerAuthenticationHandler>("ScimBearer", null).

TESTING: Verify SCIM endpoints accept valid bearer tokens. Verify invalid/missing tokens return 401.

COMPLEXITY: Medium

title: SEC: Fix Hangfire dashboard role case mismatch
description:
MEDIUM (Risk 12). HangfireDashboardAuthFilter checks IsInRole("Admin") with capital A, but RolePermissionMapping uses lowercase "admin". ClaimsPrincipal.IsInRole() is case-sensitive. Admins are locked out of Hangfire dashboard in production.

FILES TO MODIFY:
- src/Foundry.Api/Middleware/HangfireDashboardAuthFilter.cs:22-23

FIX: Replace httpContext.User.IsInRole("Admin") with case-insensitive claim check:
httpContext.User.Claims.Where(c => c.Type == ClaimTypes.Role).Any(c => string.Equals(c.Value, "admin", StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase))

TESTING: Verify admin users with lowercase role can access Hangfire dashboard. Verify non-admin users cannot access in production.

COMPLEXITY: Small

title: [M9] Add virus/malware scanning for file uploads
description:
## Severity: MEDIUM

## Summary
No antivirus or malware scanning is performed on uploaded files. Already documented as a known issue in src/Modules/Storage/CLAUDE.md.

## Finding
The Storage module validates file uploads for:
- Magic byte validation (JPEG, PNG, PDF, GIF, ZIP) — prevents content-type spoofing
- File name length (500 chars), content type (200 chars), path (500 chars)
- File size (> 0, max 100MB at controller level)
- Bucket-level content type and size restrictions

However, no virus/malware scanning is performed on the actual file contents.

## Impact
Malicious files (malware, ransomware) could be uploaded and stored, potentially affecting users who download them.

## Required Fix
Consider integrating:
1. ClamAV (open-source, Docker-based) — most common for .NET apps
2. VirusTotal API — cloud-based scanning
3. Windows Defender on Windows servers

Implementation approach:
- Add an IFileScanner interface in Storage.Application
- Implement ClamAV scanner in Storage.Infrastructure  
- Call scanner in UploadFileHandler before persisting
- Return 422 if malware detected
- Add health check for ClamAV availability
- Consider async scanning for large files (scan in background, quarantine until clean)

title: [M8] Add FluentValidation validators for Configuration module commands
description:
## Severity: MEDIUM

## Summary
9 commands across the codebase lack FluentValidation validators. Most critically, all 5 Configuration/FeatureFlag commands have no input validation — no length limits, no format checks.

## Finding
Commands missing validators:

**Configuration module (highest priority — ALL commands lack validators):**
- CreateFeatureFlagCommand (Key, Name, Description, FlagType, DefaultEnabled, RolloutPercentage)
- UpdateFeatureFlagCommand (Id, Name, Description, DefaultEnabled, RolloutPercentage)
- DeleteFeatureFlagCommand (Id)
- CreateOverrideCommand (FlagId, TenantId, UserId, IsEnabled, Percentage)
- DeleteOverrideCommand (Id)

**Communications module (lower priority — ID-only commands):**
- MarkAllNotificationsReadCommand (UserId only)
- MarkNotificationReadCommand (NotificationId, UserId)

**Identity module (lower priority — ID-only commands):**
- RevokeServiceAccountCommand (Id only)
- RotateServiceAccountSecretCommand (Id only)

## Impact
For Configuration commands with multiple string/nullable parameters: no input length limits, no format validation. A user could submit arbitrarily long strings, invalid rollout percentages (negative, >100), etc.

## Required Fix
1. Create validators for all 5 Configuration commands:
   - CreateFeatureFlagValidator: validate key format (alphanumeric/dashes, max length), name length, description length, rollout percentage (0-100 range), valid FlagType enum
   - UpdateFeatureFlagValidator: same constraints, validate Id is not empty
   - DeleteFeatureFlagValidator: validate Id not empty
   - CreateOverrideValidator: validate FlagId not empty, percentage 0-100
   - DeleteOverrideValidator: validate Id not empty
2. Optionally add validators for the ID-only commands in Communications and Identity (lower priority since the IDs are validated by the repository lookup)
notes: AUDIT 2026-02-28: Only CustomFieldValidator exists. All 5 FeatureFlag command validators still missing. Communications/Identity ID-only commands also still lack validators.

title: [M7] Fix changelog XSS — use HtmlSanitizationService instead of regex
description: ## Severity: MEDIUM ## Summary AdminChangelogController passes Title and Content directly to commands without HTML sanitization. The validator only blocks
notes: AUDIT 2026-02-28: AdminAnnouncementsController correctly uses IHtmlSanitizationService. AdminChangelogController still does NOT inject it — only has regex-based script tag validation in CreateChangelogEntryValidator. Fix scope is narrower than originally described.

title: [M6] Validate API key scopes against PermissionType enum
description:
## Severity: MEDIUM

## Summary
When creating an API key, the request.Scopes list is passed without validating that the scopes are legitimate permission values.

## Finding
**File:** src/Modules/Identity/Foundry.Identity.Api/Controllers/ApiKeysController.cs:85-91

Scopes are passed directly to the API key service without validating against known PermissionType enum values.

In ApiKeyAuthenticationMiddleware.cs:80-86, when scopes are present, they're added as raw 'scope' claims. The PermissionExpansionMiddleware then maps them via MapScopeToPermission(), which silently ignores unknown scopes.

Also related (from auth-investigator): API key auth middleware creates ClaimsIdentity with scopes but no role claims. PermissionExpansionMiddleware checks for 'azp' claim (service accounts) or role claims (users) — API key requests have neither, so permissions may not be properly expanded.

## Impact
Users can create API keys with arbitrary scope strings. Unknown scopes are silently ignored rather than rejected. API key permission expansion may be incomplete.

## Required Fix
1. Add validation in the CreateApiKey endpoint: reject scopes that don't map to valid PermissionType values
2. Verify PermissionExpansionMiddleware handles the auth_method=api_key case explicitly
3. Add tests for API key scope validation and permission expansion

title: [M5] Remove environment name and internal paths from info endpoint
description:
## Severity: MEDIUM

## Summary
The root / endpoint exposes the Environment name and internal paths like /hangfire and /scalar/v1 to unauthenticated users.

## Finding
**File:** src/Foundry.Api/Program.cs:326-334

```csharp
app.MapGet("/", () => Results.Ok(new
{
    Name = "Foundry API",
    Version = "1.0.0",
    Environment = app.Environment.EnvironmentName,
    Documentation = "/scalar/v1",
    Health = "/health",
    BackgroundJobs = "/hangfire"
})).ExcludeFromDescription();
```

## Impact
Attackers learn the deployment environment (Production/Staging/Development) and discover administrative endpoints.

## Required Fix
Option A: Make this endpoint development-only
Option B: Remove Environment name and internal paths (BackgroundJobs, Documentation) from production responses. Keep only Name, Version, and Health.

title: [M4] Restrict health check endpoint information disclosure
description:
## Severity: MEDIUM

## Summary
Health check endpoints (/health, /health/ready) are unauthenticated and return detailed information including individual service names, durations, descriptions, and exception messages.

## Finding
**File:** src/Foundry.Api/Program.cs:308-323, 408-424

The health check response writer returns: individual check names (postgresql, rabbitmq, redis, hangfire), their status, response durations in ms, descriptions, and exception messages. These endpoints are mapped without any authentication.

## Impact
Information disclosure. Attackers can discover infrastructure topology (what databases, message brokers, and caches are in use), identify slow or failing services, and read error messages that may contain connection details or internal paths.

## Required Fix
Option A (Recommended): In production, return only aggregate status for unauthenticated callers. Require authentication for the detailed /health endpoint. Keep /health/live public (no details, just 200/503).

Option B: Strip detailed information from production responses — return only overall status and individual check names/status without durations, descriptions, or error messages.

Note: /health/live already returns no details (Predicate = _ => false). This is correct for liveness probes.

title: [M3] Validate production CORS AllowedOrigins is not empty
description:
## Severity: MEDIUM

## Summary
Production and Staging appsettings set AllowedOrigins to an empty array. When WithOrigins() is called with an empty array, behavior is ambiguous — it may block all CORS requests (breaking the frontend) or enforce nothing.

## Findings
**Files:**
- src/Foundry.Api/appsettings.Production.json:46-48 — "AllowedOrigins": []
- src/Foundry.Api/appsettings.Staging.json:44-46 — "AllowedOrigins": []
- src/Foundry.Api/Extensions/ServiceCollectionExtensions.cs:80-89 — CORS registration

The expectation is that production origins are set via environment variables, but there's no validation that they're actually configured.

## Impact
Either the frontend won't work (broken CORS) or no origin restriction (open CORS). Both are problematic.

## Required Fix
1. Add startup validation that throws if AllowedOrigins is empty in non-Development environments
2. Ensure production deployment documentation mentions setting Cors:AllowedOrigins
3. Consider adding a comment in the appsettings files noting that these must be overridden via env vars

title: [M2] Fix JSON string interpolation in InvoiceRepositoryExtensions
description:
## Severity: MEDIUM

## Summary
InvoiceRepositoryExtensions uses string interpolation to build JSON for EF.Functions.JsonContains, which can break with special characters in input.

## Finding
**File:** src/Modules/Billing/Foundry.Billing.Infrastructure/Persistence/Repositories/InvoiceRepositoryExtensions.cs:18,50

```csharp
string jsonFilter = $"{{\"{fieldKey}\": \"{fieldValue}\"}}";
```

If fieldKey or fieldValue contain double quotes or backslashes, the JSON structure breaks. A crafted fieldValue like: value"}, "admin": "true could inject additional JSON keys.

Note: Line 33 in FindByCustomFieldsAsync correctly uses JsonSerializer.Serialize(criteria) which handles escaping. The single-field methods at lines 18 and 50 do not.

## Impact
Potential JSON injection if user-controlled values reach these methods. Could cause unexpected query behavior.

## Required Fix
Replace the string interpolation at lines 18 and 50 with JsonSerializer.Serialize:
```csharp
string jsonFilter = JsonSerializer.Serialize(new Dictionary<string, string> { { fieldKey, fieldValue } });
```
This matches the pattern already used at line 33.

title: [M1] Add centralized tenant filtering for Dapper queries
description:
## Severity: MEDIUM

## Summary
Dapper queries bypass EF Core's HasQueryFilter tenant isolation. All Dapper services accept tenantId as a method parameter and manually include WHERE TenantId = @TenantId, but this relies on callers passing the correct tenant ID rather than being automatically enforced.

## Findings
**Files:**
- src/Modules/Billing/Foundry.Billing.Infrastructure/Services/RevenueReportService.cs
- src/Modules/Billing/Foundry.Billing.Infrastructure/Services/InvoiceQueryService.cs
- src/Modules/Billing/Foundry.Billing.Infrastructure/Services/InvoiceReportService.cs
- src/Modules/Billing/Foundry.Billing.Infrastructure/Services/PaymentReportService.cs

All four services take Guid tenantId as a method parameter rather than reading from ITenantContext. The calling code must pass the correct tenant ID.

Note: All queries ARE properly parameterized with @TenantId — this is not an injection issue. It's a design concern about tenant isolation enforcement.

## Impact
If a caller passes the wrong tenantId (or a future developer creates a query without the filter), cross-tenant data access is possible. No centralized enforcement layer exists for Dapper queries.

## Required Fix
Consider one or more of:
1. Create a TenantAwareDapperService wrapper that injects ITenantContext and automatically adds tenant filtering
2. Change Dapper services to inject ITenantContext directly and use its TenantId, removing the parameter
3. Add an architecture test that verifies all Dapper queries include tenant filtering
4. At minimum, add unit tests that verify tenant filtering is present in all Dapper queries

4. Consider AsSplitQuery() for queries with multiple collection Includes

Highest risk: InventoryService.GetBulkAvailabilityAsync, Catalog hierarchical relationships

title: Add foundry.module span attribute via middleware
description:
Add a foundry.module attribute to every span so you can filter/group traces by module in Grafana.

Two middleware layers needed:

1. ASP.NET Core middleware — for HTTP request spans:
   - Extract module from route or controller namespace (e.g., /api/billing/invoices → Billing)
   - Set Activity.Current?.SetTag("foundry.module", moduleName)
   - Create src/Foundry.Api/Middleware/ModuleActivityTagMiddleware.cs
   - Register in Program.cs pipeline

2. Wolverine middleware — for message handler spans:
   - Derive module from message type namespace (Foundry.{Module}.* → Module)
   - Set Activity.Current?.SetTag("foundry.module", moduleName)
   - Set LogContext.PushProperty("Module", moduleName) for Serilog consistency
   - Create in Shared.Kernel or Shared.Infrastructure as a Wolverine middleware

Also consider adding tenant.id as a span tag when ITenantContext is available.

{
