title: Standardize naming conventions across modules
description:
Fix inconsistent naming patterns found across modules:

1. Domain event suffix: 3 patterns exist — *DomainEvent (Billing), *Event (Catalog), bare past-tense (event-sourced). Standardize: *DomainEvent for EF Core modules, bare past-tense for Marten event-sourced modules.
2. Integration events: Sales uses bare names (OrderPlaced, OrderCancelled, PaymentCompleted) while every other module uses *Event suffix. Add Event suffix and move to Events/ subfolder.
3. CancellationToken: split between cancellationToken (Billing, Notifications) and ct (Catalog, Identity, Inventory). Pick ct (shorter, modern convention).
4. Repository methods: Remove (Billing) vs Delete (Catalog). Pick one verb consistently.
5. Query naming: GetInvoiceById vs GetItem. Pick bare names (GetInvoice).
6. Duplicate PagedResult<T> in Catalog and Notifications with different property names. Extract to Shared.Kernel.
7. SendEmailRequestedEvent lives in Commands/ folder but named *Event. Rename or move.

Still valid: (1) domain event suffix split (*DomainEvent vs *Event), (2) CancellationToken naming (cancellationToken vs ct), (3) Remove vs Delete in repos (actually 3+ conventions). NOT valid: Sales integration events (none exist), duplicate PagedResult (names match), SendEmailRequestedEvent (correctly in Events/).

title: Resolve Async suffix naming policy (1,221 IDE1006 warnings)
description:
1,221 IDE1006 warnings for 'Missing suffix: Async' on async methods. This is a POLICY DECISION — most of these are intentional naming patterns, not code defects.

**Root causes:**
1. Wolverine handlers use 'Handle' / 'HandleAsync' by convention — .editorconfig already relaxes this to 'suggestion' but dotnet format still flags them
2. ASP.NET controller actions don't conventionally use Async suffix
3. Some internal async methods genuinely missing Async suffix

**Options (pick one):**

**Option A (Recommended): Suppress in .editorconfig for known patterns**
- Set the async naming rule severity to 'none' in .editorconfig (it's currently 'suggestion')
- OR add more specific suppressions for controller/handler methods
- Rationale: The Wolverine and ASP.NET conventions are well-established. Fighting them creates noise.

**Option B: Add Async suffix everywhere**
- Rename all 1,221 methods to add Async suffix
- Would require updating all callers
- NOT recommended — breaks Wolverine conventions

**Option C: Selective enforcement**
- Keep 'suggestion' severity (current setting)
- Don't add dotnet format check for IDE1006 to CI
- Only enforce via PR review
- This is effectively the current state

**Implementation:**
1. Decide which option to take
2. If Option A: Update .editorconfig to set async naming rule severity to 'none' (or 'silent')
3. Verify with 'dotnet format Foundry.sln --verify-no-changes' that IDE1006 Async warnings are gone
4. Note: The _ prefix IDE1006 warnings are handled by separate tasks

**Important:** This task has NO file overlap with the other code quality tasks — it only touches .editorconfig rules, not source files.

title: wire the network-escape guard into the six browser projects that install only navigation + console
description:
Wallow-nggf wired all three guards (navigation, console, network) into apps/minimal-app, packages/logger and packages/testing. The five older setup files (packages/navigation, packages/forms, packages/ui, apps/wallow-web, apps/wallow-auth) and packages/ui's .storybook/preview.tsx still install only installNavigationEscapeGuard + installConsoleGuard — no installNetworkEscapeGuard, so an unowned fetch in those projects still leaves for the real network (hangs in CI, passes against a live backend locally).

Wiring is mechanical (add the import, install, and a third independent afterEach per setup file; the storybook preview extends its beforeEach/afterEach exports), but each project's specs must be checked for legitimate global fetches first — a spec that deliberately reaches globalThis.fetch has to consume the record with consumeNetworkEscapes() instead of leaking it into the project afterEach. packages/testing/CLAUDE.md's census paragraph names this asymmetry and must be updated when it closes.
notes:
Wired installNetworkEscapeGuard into all six remaining browser-project doors, completing the guard trio repo-wide.

Setup files (packages/navigation, packages/forms, packages/ui, apps/wallow-web, apps/wallow-auth): each now imports installNetworkEscapeGuard + assertNoNetworkEscape from @bc-solutions-coder/testing/network-escape, installs at module top beside the other two guards, and registers a third independent afterEach — one hook per guard so one guard's failure cannot stop another clearing its record. Each header comment gained a paragraph naming why (unowned globalThis.fetch traffic hangs in CI, passes against a live backend locally; deliberate requests read back via consumeNetworkEscapes()).

packages/ui/.storybook/preview.tsx: guard added to the exported beforeEach, assertNoNetworkEscape appended to the afterEach assert loop (each assert still runs even when a prior one threw; AggregateError message generalized), doc comments updated to cover three guards.

Spec sweep found NO spec needing consumeNetworkEscapes(): the only global-fetch touches are two stub/spy specs (wallow-web bff-demo.test.tsx via vi.spyOn + restoreAllMocks; wallow-auth AcceptTermsScreen.test.tsx via vi.stubGlobal + unstubAllGlobals) which displace the guard's wrapper and restore it — compatible, untouched. packages/forms use-app-form.sdk-mutation.test.tsx only uses typeof globalThis.fetch as a type.

title: test(ui): audit keyboard-open specs for ambient-pointer focus steal (select, navigation-menu, combobox)
description:
Follow-up to Wallow-egxx, which proved the mechanism: the Playwright pointer position leaks across spec files, and Chromium re-dispatches hover events when new content mounts under a stationary cursor — so a keyboard-opened popup mounting under a parked pointer hover-highlights whatever row sits at that spot and steals focus/highlight from the row the spec asserts.

Wallow-egxx fixed the two observed/named files (menubar.test.tsx, menu.test.tsx) by naming the pointer state before every keyboard open: await userEvent.unhover(<fixture root>) after render — unhover moves the pointer to <body>, off the fixture footprint. Three more files share the exposed shape but have no observed failure yet:

- packages/ui/src/components/select/select.test.tsx — 'k-trigger' keyboard spec: focus + Enter + ArrowDown + Enter asserts onValueChange('beta'); a parked pointer over a row after the popup mounts moves the highlight ArrowDown steps from, selecting the wrong value. Select popups also align OVER the trigger, raising the odds the parked position coincides.
- packages/ui/src/components/navigation-menu/navigation-menu.test.tsx — 'opens the panel with ArrowDown and lands focus on its first link' (n-link-apps): identical shape to the menubar flake, and Base UI nav menus also open on hover.
- packages/ui/src/components/combobox/combobox.test.tsx — 'selects a highlighted result with the keyboard': narrower window (highlight is re-asserted right before Enter) but the same mechanism applies between ArrowDown and Enter.

Fix is mechanical per Wallow-egxx: after render, before the keyboard open, await userEvent.unhover(<fixture root>) with a one-line comment naming why. Do NOT park the pointer in a beforeEach (packages/ui/CLAUDE.md forbids compensating for unnamed state). context-menu.test.tsx is NOT exposed — its only open path is an explicit right-click that names the pointer itself. Verify with several forced runs of each file plus a full ui suite run.
notes:
Audited the three keyboard-open specs named by the bead and fixed all three with the Wallow-egxx pattern: after render, before the keyboard open, await userEvent.unhover(<anchor element>) with a one-line comment naming why — local to each spec, never a beforeEach park.

- select.test.tsx 'selects an item by keyboard and reports it to onValueChange': unhover(k-trigger). Comment notes the select popup aligns OVER its trigger, raising the coincidence odds.
- navigation-menu.test.tsx 'opens the panel with ArrowDown and lands focus on its first link': unhover(n-trigger-products); extended the existing 'no pointer at all' comment to say that has to be made true, not assumed.
- combobox.test.tsx 'selects a highlighted result with the keyboard': unhover(f-input).

context-menu.test.tsx left alone as the bead directed — its only open path is an explicit right-click.

Verified: three consecutive forced runs of the three files together (81 tests each run, green), then the full ui suite (122 files / 1481 tests, green), plus pnpm lint:tests clean. Note: per-file vitest runs in packages/ui also need --configLoader runner, same as the apps.

title: watch: post-completion turbo test wedge + first-run-after-dep-change Vite re-optimization kills
description:
Two low-frequency CI-reliability hazards observed during the 2026-08-27 Step 4
sweep (docs/plans/2026-08-27/1618-nav-leak-forensics-and-measurement.md) and
recorded here so they survive Wallow-xzy1.6's closure. Neither has been observed
to corrupt a result — both fail loud or hang loud — so this is a watch item, not
active work.

1. POST-COMPLETION WEDGE. In 6 of 25 uncapped `turbo run test --force
--continue` runs, turbo printed its complete final summary (including the
Failed: line) and the process then never exited; each was reaped by `timeout
600`. A prior sweep saw a 28-minute wedge before timeout wrapping was added. All
observed wedges were on uncapped runs that had at least one failing package.
Not yet observed at the supported --concurrency=1. If a capped run (or CI) ever
hangs after printing its summary, this is that. Candidate suspects: a vitest
browser-mode provider/playwright process not tearing down after a suite dies
mid-file — unverified.

2. FIRST-RUN-AFTER-DEP-CHANGE KILL. Observed once at the SUPPORTED
--concurrency=1: an in-repo edit to packages/testing source invalidated the Vite
dep cache, "Re-optimizing dependencies because vite config has changed" landed
mid-run, and 6 wallow-web spec files died with "Cannot connect to the iframe …
CORS". The immediately following run was green. Mechanism matches the
extraBrowserOptimizeDeps discipline documented in packages/navigation/CLAUDE.md.
Practical rule until fixed upstream or mitigated: treat the first `pnpm test`
after changing a package's dependency graph (or a vite config) as suspect —
rerun before believing a module-delivery failure.

Evidence: sweep logs and summary.txt were session-scratchpad artifacts (not
committed); the numbers and signatures are preserved on Wallow-x5da and
Wallow-xzy1.6 notes dated 2026-08-27.
notes: MITIGATED (hazard 1 blast radius), 2026-08-28: .github/workflows/js.yml now carries timeout-minutes: 30 on the build job (commit e4fd29ec). A CI wedge is now a 30-minute loud failure instead of GitHub's 360-minute default, with the full log intact (the wedge prints turbo's complete summary before hanging). No causal fix claimed for either hazard — the wedge cause remains undiagnosed (vitest browser provider/playwright teardown suspected, unverified) and the re-optimization kill remains mitigated only by the extraBrowserOptimizeDeps discipline plus the rerun-before-believing rule already documented here and in packages/navigation/CLAUDE.md.
close_reason: Closed as a watch item with blast radius capped: js.yml timeout-minutes: 30 (e4fd29ec) bounds a CI wedge; both hazards fail loud, neither observed at the supported --concurrency=1 config in a way that corrupts results, and the signatures + practical rules are preserved on this bead. On recurrence, file a new bead citing this one.

title: fix(storage): LocalStorageProvider's presigned URLs point at routes that do not exist
description:
LocalStorageProvider.GetPresignedUrlAsync returns {baseUrl}/api/storage/upload?key=... for uploads and {baseUrl}/api/storage/files/download?key=... for downloads. Neither route exists. StorageController is [Route("v{version:apiVersion}/storage")], so the real routes are /v1/storage/upload (multipart, bucket/path/isPublic form fields, no key parameter) and /v1/storage/files/{id:guid}/download (by file id, not by storage key). There is no /api prefix anywhere in the API and no endpoint that takes a raw storage key.

So on the default Local provider both presigned paths hand the caller a 404: GET /v1/storage/files/{id}/presigned-url and POST /v1/storage/presigned-upload. Only the S3 provider issues a URL that resolves.

Either add key-addressed local upload/download endpoints for the provider to point at, or make the Local provider fail loudly (Result failure / NotSupportedException) instead of returning a dead link.

Found while writing api/src/Modules/Storage/CLAUDE.md (Wallow-hr0p).
acceptance_criteria: With Storage:Provider=Local, a presigned URL either resolves to a working endpoint or the request fails with a clear error; no caller receives a URL that 404s.
notes:
Fixed. Root cause: GetPresignedUrlAsync returned placeholder /api/storage/... paths never backed by any route; blast radius included GET /v1/storage/files/{id}/download (redirects to the presigned URL) and Branding's anonymous logo URLs, which killed the fail-loudly option and required key-addressed signed endpoints.

Shipped:
- LocalPresignedUrlSigner (Application/Services — NOT Infrastructure, because CleanArchitectureTests bans Api->Infrastructure and the controller injects it): HMAC-SHA256 over method\nkey\nexpiresUnix, random per-process 256-bit key, constant-time Validate with expiry check. Restart invalidates outstanding URLs (accepted, dev-only).
- LocalStorageProvider now mints {baseUrl}/v1/storage/local/files?key&expires&sig — GET-signed downloads, PUT-signed uploads (S3 verb parity).
- LocalStorageController (Api): AllowAnonymous (signature IS the auth), GET streams via IStorageProvider.DownloadAsync with content type inferred from extension (octet-stream fallback), 403 on bad/expired/cross-method sig, 404 on missing file; PUT writes Request.Body, RequestSizeLimit 100MB. Hidden via ApiExplorerSettings(IgnoreApi=true) — presigned URLs are opaque strings, an SDK method would be uncallable; this also satisfied TypedSuccessResponseTests, and the regenerated OpenAPI doc is byte-identical to the committed snapshot (verified), so no SDK regen.
- Signer registered AddSingleton unconditionally (outside the provider switch) so the controller resolves under S3 config too; pinned by new StorageExtensionsTests theory.
- Tests: 8 signer facts, provider URL tests rewritten (3 new), 11 controller facts. storage 541/541, full fast 4967/4967, integration 261/261 (HandlerCodegenTests covers the new provider ctor). dotnet format clean.
- Docs: Storage CLAUDE.md (404 bullet replaced with restart-invalidation gotcha + presigned-model pattern), module README, docs/architecture/file-storage.md endpoint table.

title: Gate resolveRequestOrigin's x-forwarded-proto read on the trusted-proxy set
description:
packages/env/src/request-origin.ts honours `x-forwarded-proto` UNCONDITIONALLY. The comment there acknowledges the header is attacker-supplied and argues the http/https allowlist keeps it inert, which is a defensible position — an attacker can flip the resolved origin between http and https but cannot point it anywhere else.

Wallow-tvn3 (landed 2026-08-27) put a trusted-proxy set in the same package: `parseTrustedProxies` / `isTrusted` in packages/env/src/client-address.ts, configured by WALLOW_TRUSTED_PROXIES. Gating the proto read on the same check is now nearly free, and would make the two headers one policy rather than two.

The awkward part is the SHAPE, not the logic: resolveRequestOrigin(request) takes no peer and no trusted list, and the package may not read the environment itself (see packages/env/CLAUDE.md). Either it grows a factory like createClientAddressResolver(env), or the two resolvers merge into one per-app binding. Decide that before writing code.

Filed by docs/plans/2026-08-03/1639-proxy-trust-react-dupe-nav-flake.md §1 'Deliberately out of scope', which asked for a follow-up bead rather than widening tvn3.
notes:
Done. x-forwarded-proto is now gated on WALLOW_TRUSTED_PROXIES — one trust policy with x-forwarded-for.

Shape decision (the one the bead flagged): factory mirror, not entry merge. request-origin grew createRequestOriginResolver(env) mirroring createClientAddressResolver; resolveRequestOrigin became (request, peer, trusted) mirroring resolveClientAddress. Merging the two subpaths was rejected — it breaks the package's 'an import names the module' charter and doesn't solve the start.ts client-graph constraint anyway.

New export: isTrustedPeer(peer, trusted) in ./client-address — the public parse+membership gate both resolvers now share. Undefined/blank/unparseable peer or empty set => false; v4-mapped peers canonicalize before matching.

Call sites (5): the two log-ingest.server.ts files bind the factory at module scope (server-only, same shape as clientAddressFor). The three start.ts files CANNOT — they're aliased into the client graph — so each declares a module-scope let and memoizes inside the server callback: requestOriginFor ??= createRequestOriginResolver(process.env). Middleware request assigns to PeerRequest without a cast because ip is optional.

Behavior change accepted (pre-release policy): unset WALLOW_TRUSTED_PROXIES now ignores the header where it was previously honored unconditionally. Production compose defaults 'private' on both apps, so the golden path is unaffected; local dev/E2E have no TLS ingress.

Docs updated: packages/env/CLAUDE.md (section renamed 'gated AND validated', entries table, binding-shape note), reverse-proxy.md (one trust policy + the unset-behind-TLS misconfiguration), fork-guide.md contract #1, bff-pattern.md SSR base URL bullet, logging.md, packages/logger/CLAUDE.md, apps/CLAUDE.md, apps/wallow-auth/CLAUDE.md + README env table, docker/.env.production.example.

TDD: red first (11 failures across request-origin.test.ts gate matrix + isTrustedPeer block in client-address.test.ts), then green (100/100 in env), then full pnpm check green.

    This is the deliberate full-navigation escape hatch (/connect/** is served by
    the passthrough proxy, not the client route tree), so the rule is arguing with
    an intentional design decision -- likely an override, not a code change.

`pnpm lint:fix` is NOT a clean path: it clears 1090 -> 413 one-var across 140 files
while SURFACING 278 new `sort-vars` warnings and a second error
(`react(preserve-manual-memoization)`).

So this is a real piece of work with a decision in it: adopt the new style rules and
take the churn, or turn one-var/sort-vars off and keep the rest of 1.80.

HOW THIS WAS FOUND: a `pnpm install --force` run under pnpm 11 re-resolved the caret
range `^1.74.0` to 1.80.0 and rewrote package.json + the lockfile. Reverted; the tree
is back on 1.74.0 and green. See also the pnpm 11 upgrade, which removes the
self-rewriting packageManager field that made that happen silently.

title: chore(storage): sweep orphaned objects left by failed commits
description:
Split out of Wallow-rqqx (see its notes for the full four-handler audit).

Two Storage paths can leave an object in the store with no row referencing it. Both are the
DELIBERATE trade: an orphaned object is unreferenced garbage, whereas the reverse ordering leaves a
row pointing at bytes that are gone, which is a permanent 404 on read.

1. UploadFileHandler -- uploads, then inserts the row and saves. A failed save orphans the blob.
   NOT fixable by reordering: inserting the row first would leave a row pointing at an object that
   was never uploaded, which is the worse failure.
2. DeleteFileHandler / DeleteBucketHandler -- as of rqqx these commit the row removal and THEN
   delete from the object store. A crash in that window permanently orphans the object.

So a sweep is the only thing that reclaims either. Shape: enumerate keys under
tenant-<id>/<bucket>/ and delete those with no matching StoredFile.StorageKey, with an age
threshold so it never races an in-flight upload.

Low priority -- this is disk cost, not correctness, and there are no deployments yet.
notes:
Implemented in e143f9aa (TDD red->green, 9 new tests).

Design:
- IStorageProvider gained ListAsync(prefix, ct) -> IAsyncEnumerable<StorageObjectInfo> (key + LastModified). New record Wallow.Shared.Contracts/Storage/StorageObjectInfo.cs. Breaking interface change - fine pre-release; both implementations updated.
- LocalStorageProvider: walks BasePath with EnumerateFiles, derives '/'-separated keys via Path.GetRelativePath, prefix-filters; empty when BasePath missing.
- S3StorageProvider: paginated ListObjectsV2 (loops while IsTruncated == true, v4 SDK nullable); null/unspecified LastModified normalised to UTC, missing timestamp reported as "now" so it can never age into deletion.
- OrphanedObjectSweepJob (Wallow.Storage.Infrastructure/Jobs): lists under "tenant-" prefix, skips objects younger than 24h (const MinimumAge - safely above the minutes-clamped presigned-upload expiry, so it never races an in-flight upload), batches 500 keys, checks StoredFile.StorageKey via IgnoreQueryFilters (cross-tenant - background scope has no tenant), deletes unreferenced via provider.DeleteAsync, logs each deletion, returns count. SessionPruningJob template: primary ctor, [LoggerMessage] statics, try/catch-log-rethrow.
- Registered in Program.cs behind IsModuleEnabled<StorageModule>(): "storage-orphaned-object-sweep", Cron.Daily(). No DI registration needed (Hangfire ActivatorUtilities).

Residual (documented in api/src/Modules/Storage/CLAUDE.md): in a background scope ITenantContext is unresolved, so S3StorageProvider.ResolveBucket() falls back to the default BucketName - multi-region RegionBuckets non-primary buckets are never swept.

Docs updated: docs/architecture/background-jobs.md (recurring-jobs table + rationale), docs/architecture/file-storage.md (interface listing), module CLAUDE.md.

Verification: storage suite 588/588; full fast suite 4978/4978; integration tier 259/259 (includes Wolverine codegen guards + Testcontainers suites); dotnet format clean.

title: docs(fork-guide): document that merge=ours strands appsettings.json flag cleanup in forks
description:
.gitattributes marks appsettings*.json merge=ours (`.gitattributes:3`). That means when a fork
merges upstream Wallow after commit 51b20335 ("chore(api): reconcile the Modules.* feature flags
with the registry"), the fork's OWN appsettings.json/appsettings.Production.json win the merge
outright and keep their pre-51b20335 content: the phantom `FeatureManagement:Modules.Configuration`
key (names a module that has never existed), the inert `FeatureManagement:Modules.Identity` key
(Identity is IsCore, so ResolveEnabledModules short-circuits before ever asking IFeatureManager for
it), and the dead top-level `Wallow:Modules` block (nothing reads it; AddFeatureManagement binds
FeatureManagement by convention only).

Verified on disk 2026-08-05:
- .gitattributes:3 `appsettings*.json merge=ours`, confirmed present.
- 51b20335 added api/tests/Wallow.Architecture.Tests/Modules/ModuleFeatureFlagTests.cs, which loads
  the REAL checked-in appsettings*.json files off disk (ConfigurationBuilder.AddJsonFile, no mocking)
  and asserts the merged FeatureManagement Modules.* key set is EXACTLY the non-core registry
  modules, and that no second Wallow:Modules block exists. A fork whose appsettings.json still
  carries Modules.Configuration/Modules.Identity/the Wallow:Modules block after merging will FAIL
  both `MergedConfiguration_DeclaresExactlyTheNonCoreRegistryModules` and
  `BaseConfiguration_HasNoSecondModulesBlock` in Wallow.Architecture.Tests -- with no compile error
  and no runtime symptom pointing at the cause, just a red test suite after doing everything "right"
  (following docs/getting-started/fork-guide.md's own recommended merge-driver setup).

Where to document: docs/getting-started/fork-guide.md's existing "Merge Driver Setup" section
(the merge=ours table, ~line 57-75) is the natural home -- add a short note that appsettings*.json's
merge=ours protection is a double-edged sword: it also means a fork does not automatically pick up
upstream fixes to the FILE'S OWN STRUCTURE (like this flag cleanup), only to its literal file
content at fork time. The fix for an existing fork is manual: diff the fork's appsettings*.json
against upstream's after a merge and hand-apply any FeatureManagement/Wallow:Modules key changes,
the same way a fork already has to hand-reconcile any other upstream change to a merge=ours file.

Priority reasoning (P3, not higher): CLAUDE.md's Deployment Status section is explicit that Wallow
has never been deployed and has no real users -- and as of this bead, no actual fork of this repo
is known to exist yet. This is genuine future-proofing for the fork workflow, not a fix for a
present, felt pain. It is cheap (one paragraph) and worth doing because forking is this repo's
whole stated purpose and the trap is easy to explain once, but it is not urgent: no one is blocked
today, and CLAUDE.md separately says not to spend effort on rollout/compatibility edge cases for
their own sake. This is different from a compatibility shim -- it costs a fork nothing to ignore
until they actually hit it, and the note itself requires no code changes, so it does not conflict
with that guidance.
acceptance_criteria:
- docs/getting-started/fork-guide.md's Merge Driver Setup section explains that appsettings*.json's
  merge=ours protection means a fork will NOT automatically receive upstream structural fixes to
  that file (e.g. FeatureManagement/Modules.* key changes), only keep its own content verbatim, and
  that a fork should diff its appsettings*.json against upstream after merging to catch drift.
- The note references (or generically describes, without needing to cite the exact commit) the
  concrete failure mode: a stale FeatureManagement.Modules.* key set or a stray Wallow:Modules block
  fails Wallow.Architecture.Tests' ModuleFeatureFlagTests for a fork that has not hand-reconciled.
- No source or test file is changed -- this is a docs-only bead.
notes:
DONE (docs-only, commit 55a622bd).

VERIFICATION OF THE .gitattributes CLAIM
Bead said appsettings*.json merge=ours at .gitattributes:3 -- confirmed, and line 3 is right (line 1 is blank, line 2 is the comment header). The file carries FIVE merge=ours patterns, not one:
  3: appsettings*.json merge=ours
  4: branding.json merge=ours
  5: docker/.env merge=ours
  6: docker/.env.example merge=ours
  7: seed.json merge=ours
git check-attr confirms all five resolve: api/src/Wallow.Api/appsettings.json, packages/styles/branding.json, api/seed.json, docker/.env, docker/.env.example all report 'merge: ours'. Enumerated over tracked files, appsettings*.json expands to SIX files (base + Development/Production/Staging/Testing) -- the fork-guide table's one row hides that. docker/.env is untracked, so it never shows up in a tracked-file sweep; the new text says so and points at docker/.env.example instead.
Because the pattern list is broader than appsettings, the guidance is written for the general case and uses the appsettings cleanup only as the worked example, per the task brief.

WHAT WAS ADDED
docs/getting-started/fork-guide.md, new '#### The protection is unconditional -- diff these files after every sync' inside the existing '### Merge Driver Setup' (Approach A), immediately after the merge=ours table. ~30 lines. Three beats, matching the page's existing voice (the 'Two contracts a fork must not break silently' section was the tone model):
1. WHY IT BITES: merge=ours does not weigh the two sides -- it resolves to the fork's copy and reports success. No conflict markers, no merge message, nothing in git status. Correct for the VALUES in these files; applies just as unconditionally to upstream changes to a file's SHAPE (renamed key, deleted key, added block).
2. HOW TO NOTICE (concrete command, tested against this repo):
   git ls-files | git check-attr --stdin merge | grep ': merge: ours$' | sed 's/: merge: ours$//' \
     | xargs git diff upstream/main --
   Chosen over hardcoding the five patterns because it asks git itself, so it stays correct as the pattern list grows and it expands appsettings*.json to every overlay. Verified end-to-end: the enumeration returns the 8 tracked paths above, and piping into 'git diff --stat 51b20335^' correctly reports appsettings.json (13 deletions) + appsettings.Production.json (2 deletions).
3. HOW TO RECONCILE: manual by definition -- read the output rather than automate it (only the maintainer can separate deliberate customization from drift), hand-apply the upstream key changes, keep your own values.

WORKED EXAMPLE (this epic)
Names both deleted keys and why each was dead (Modules.Identity inert because Identity is core and registered regardless; Modules.Configuration names a module that never existed), plus the dead top-level Wallow:Modules block. States the real failure mode: the keys are INERT at runtime -- the app behaves identically -- but Wallow.Architecture.Tests' ModuleFeatureFlagTests loads the real checked-in appsettings*.json off disk and fails if the declared Modules.* set is not exactly the non-core registry modules, or if a second Wallow:Modules block exists. An unreconciled fork gets a red suite with no compile error and nothing pointing at the merge. Deliberately describes the tests by behaviour, not by commit hash (AC allows either; a hash is useless to a fork reading the rendered site).
Verified against the source before writing: api/tests/Wallow.Architecture.Tests/Modules/ModuleFeatureFlagTests.cs exists with MergedConfiguration_DeclaresExactlyTheNonCoreRegistryModules(string overlay) and BaseConfiguration_HasNoSecondModulesBlock, and both appsettings.json:80-87 and appsettings.Production.json:48-55 now carry exactly the six non-core keys.

NO DUPLICATION (task item 3)
Checked every existing merge=ours mention in docs/. configuration.md:52 and frontend-setup.md:659-679 already own the branding.json instance (two-level token fallback); reverse-proxy.md:359 owns the seed.json instance. The new text does NOT restate any of them -- it closes with one sentence noting branding.json is the same trap in the other direction (a token upstream ADDED, never received) and links to the Configuration Guide. Module flag semantics are already owned by this page's own '## Configuring Modules' section, so the example links to #configuring-modules instead of re-explaining the flags.

QUALITY GATE
docs/CLAUDE.md read first. No new file, so no toc.yml entry needed; naming/cross-reference rules (relative paths) followed. ./scripts/docs-serve.sh --build-only: 'Build succeeded', 0 errors, 3 warnings -- all three pre-existing and unrelated to docs prose (FailedToLoadAnalyzer for the Razor compiler, and two InvalidCref in TenantSaveChangesInterceptor.cs XML comments). No link warnings. Confirmed in the built HTML that both new links resolve: href='configuration.html' (file exists) and href='#configuring-modules' (id='configuring-modules' present on the page).

SCOPE
git status before commit showed exactly one modified file: docs/getting-started/fork-guide.md. Zero files outside docs/. No source or test file touched, per AC 3. One commit, type docs, 63-char subject, bead ID in body. Not pushed (coordinator owns that).

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA: all three met.
VERIFY: [✓] .gitattributes carries exactly 5 merge=ours patterns (line3 appsettings*.json, line4 branding.json, line5 docker/.env, line6 docker/.env.example, line7 seed.json) — confirmed by reading the file directly; new prose never enumerates them by name (uses a dynamic git command instead), so no enumeration-mismatch risk exists. [✓] Prose is accurate about git behaviour: merge=ours resolves wholesale to fork's copy with no conflict markers/git-status signal — matches git's real semantics, doesn't overstate/understate. [✓] The documented command 'git ls-files | git check-attr --stdin merge | grep : merge: ours$ | sed s/: merge: ours$// | xargs git diff upstream/main --' actually runs and correctly enumerates the 8 tracked merge=ours paths (verified independently); command syntax is correct. [✓] Worked example (Modules.* flag cleanup) verified against commit 51b20335: appsettings.json -13 lines / appsettings.Production.json -2 lines exactly as claimed; Development/Staging/Testing untouched — matches doc's implicit scope (only mentions base+Production). Modules.Identity/Modules.Configuration/Wallow:Modules block deletion description matches 51b20335's own commit message. [✓] Cross-links resolve in built HTML: href=configuration.html present and file exists; id=configuring-modules anchor present at fork-guide.md:351 Configuring Modules section. No duplication — configuration.md:52 owns branding.json two-level-fallback explanation, reverse-proxy.md:359 owns seed.json instance; new section correctly defers to configuration.md rather than restating. [✓] Commit 55a622bd is docs-only: git show --stat confirms single file docs/getting-started/fork-guide.md, 41 insertions, 0 deletions, 0 files outside docs/. [✓] docfx build succeeded independently re-run via ./scripts/docs-serve.sh --build-only: 'Build succeeded with warning', 0 errors, 3 warnings (2x InvalidCref in TenantSaveChangesInterceptor.cs, pre-existing/unrelated to this change). tests=N/A (docs-only bead, no code test suite applicable); docfx build=PASS. issues=none found. verdict=CLOSE (already closed; verification confirms the close was correct, no reopen needed).

title: OpenAPI regen never runs against shipped defaults — ApiKeys client surface stays in the SDK regardless of the module flag
description:
Follow-up from Wallow-3mbx.1 (commit 4f9b0f10), which made a disabled module's HTTP surface
(routing, Asp.Versioning ApiExplorer, and the OpenAPI document) actually disappear together —
before that fix, a disabled module's controllers stayed routed and 500'd instead of 404ing, and
the OpenAPI document kept advertising them regardless. The committing agent flagged an
unactioned consequence for the SDK; this bead verifies it and narrows it to the real, smaller
problem.

## Premise as originally flagged (partially wrong — corrected below)

The worry was: "the next OpenAPI regen against shipped defaults will drop
/v1/identity/auth/keys, and with it the generated ApiKeys TS client, because ApiKeys ships
disabled (`Modules.ApiKeys: false` in api/src/Wallow.Api/appsettings.json:88)."

VERIFIED ON DISK, 2026-08-05:
- packages/sdk/openapi/v1.json currently DOES carry the ApiKeys paths (`/v1/identity/auth/keys`
  at line 506, `/v1/identity/auth/keys/{keyId}` at line 617) and three operationIds
  (ApiKeysCreateApiKey, ApiKeysListApiKeys, ApiKeysRevokeApiKey).
- api/src/Wallow.Api/appsettings.json:88 ships `"Modules.ApiKeys": false` — this is the
  documented "shipped file verbatim" in docs/getting-started/fork-guide.md:319-334.
- BUT neither of the two places that actually regenerate/verify this document ever runs
  against that base file alone:
  - api/src/Wallow.Api/Properties/launchSettings.json sets
    `ASPNETCORE_ENVIRONMENT=Development` for the `Wallow` profile (and
    api/src/Wallow.AppHost/Properties/launchSettings.json does the same for the Aspire
    AppHost, i.e. `pnpm backend`) — this is what a dev has running on :5001 when they run the
    documented manual regen command
    (`WALLOW_OPENAPI_URL=http://localhost:5001/openapi/v1.json pnpm --filter
    @bc-solutions-coder/sdk exec tsx scripts/generate.ts`, see packages/sdk/CLAUDE.md).
  - .github/actions/openapi-document/action.yml:84 (shared by openapi-drift.yml and
    openapi-autoregen.yml) explicitly sets `ASPNETCORE_ENVIRONMENT: Development` for the
    build-time `dotnet-getdocument` emission used by CI drift-checking and auto-regen.
  - api/src/Wallow.Api/appsettings.Development.json:77 overrides the flag:
    `"Modules.ApiKeys": true`. FeatureManagement config layering means this wins under
    Development in every one of the above paths.

So in every regen pathway that actually exists today (manual dev regen, CI drift check, CI
auto-regen PR), ApiKeys is enabled and its paths stay in the document. The originally-flagged
"next regen silently drops the paths" scenario does not happen under current wiring. This
downgrades the concern from a latent build break to a design/documentation gap.

## The real gap

The committed OpenAPI document — and therefore the generated TS SDK client — reflects
`Modules.ApiKeys: true` (the Development override), not the shipped default
(`Modules.ApiKeys: false`, what a fresh fork's Production/base config ships with, per
appsettings.json and the fork guide). Nobody chose this on purpose; it falls out of
Development.json's flag existing for local dev convenience combined with the emission
tooling always running under Development. Two consequences:

1. **The published contract does not describe what a default-configured server actually
   exposes.** A fork that never touches `Modules.ApiKeys` gets a server that 404s
   `/v1/identity/auth/keys`, but an SDK client that still contains
   `apiKeysListApiKeys`/`apiKeysCreateApiKey`/`apiKeysRevokeApiKey` and will get a 404 if
   ever called — the type system offers a false promise.
2. Conversely, if the Development-only override were ever removed (e.g. someone "cleans up"
   appsettings.Development.json under the belief it's a stray dev knob), the very
   regen/drift-check pipeline would silently start emitting the smaller, ApiKeys-less document
   with no one having decided that was the intent — exactly because the current behavior is
   incidental, not policy.

## Consumption check (bears on priority)

Grepped apps/wallow-web/src, apps/wallow-auth/src, and apps/minimal-app/src, plus a
repo-wide grep for the three generated operation names
(apiKeysListApiKeys/apiKeysCreateApiKey/apiKeysRevokeApiKey) outside
packages/sdk/src/generated/: ZERO hits. No app consumes the ApiKeys client surface today.
Dropping it would NOT be a build break right now. (bd note the exact commands used are on
this bead's discovery trail if needed; re-run the same greps to reconfirm before starting.)

## The decision this bead exists to make

Pick, deliberately, which of two documents `packages/sdk/openapi/v1.json` should be:

- **A. Shipped defaults** — regenerate/verify against `Modules.ApiKeys: false` (i.e. against
  appsettings.json's base FeatureManagement block, or an environment that doesn't override
  it). Smaller, honest-to-a-fresh-fork surface; matches what `docs/getting-started/fork-guide.md`
  documents as "the shipped file verbatim". Cost: the ApiKeys TS client (and any future
  optional-module client surface) simply does not exist in the SDK until a fork turns the
  module on and regenerates — a fork wanting ApiKeys must know to flip the flag AND
  regenerate before building any UI against it.
- **B. All modules enabled** — make the regen/CI recipe explicit about enabling every optional
  module (rather than relying on the Development environment's incidental override), so the
  committed document is always the FULL surface a fork *could* have. Matches "what can this
  platform do," independent of any one deployment's flags. Cost: the SDK always ships client
  code for modules a given deployment may have off, which is exactly the "false promise"
  problem above, just made deliberate instead of accidental — every fork must know at runtime
  which subset of the typed client is actually live in gets non-404 (endpoints already 404
  correctly per Wallow-3mbx.1; this is a documentation/DX concern, not a correctness one).

RECOMMENDATION: (A), shipped defaults, made explicit rather than incidental. Reasoning:
- It's what the fork guide already tells forks to expect ("the shipped file verbatim").
- It keeps "does my server expose this" and "does my SDK offer this" in sync by construction
  for the common case (a fork that runs the shipped config unmodified), rather than requiring
  every fork to remember that the SDK is a superset of their live server.
- Wallow-3mbx.1's whole point was making the registry authoritative for the HTTP surface; a
  document that reflects an incidental Development override undermines that by keeping a
  second, un-gated "what modules exist" signal (CI's hardcoded ASPNETCORE_ENVIRONMENT) alive
  right next to the one the fix just made authoritative.
- A fork that enables ApiKeys (or any other optional module) already has to run its own regen
  before shipping a UI against it — CLAUDE.md's "API and contract changes are free" stance
  (root CLAUDE.md) says exactly that this is a cheap, expected step, not a burden worth
  designing around.
If (B) is chosen instead, appsettings.Development.json's ApiKeys override stops being
incidental and should be given a comment explaining it is deliberately "regen surface = all
modules", and the same override should be extended to cover every other optional module
(Storage/Notifications/Announcements/Inquiries/Branding are already true in Development,
matching base — only ApiKeys currently differs, so today's Development config is not
consistently "all modules on" either; it just happens to be for the one module that differs
from base).
acceptance_criteria:
- A decision is made and recorded (in this bead and, if (A), in packages/sdk/CLAUDE.md and/or
  .github/actions/openapi-document/action.yml's header comment) about whether the committed
  packages/sdk/openapi/v1.json is generated against shipped defaults or against all modules
  enabled.
- If (A) shipped defaults: the manual regen instructions and CI emission
  (.github/actions/openapi-document/action.yml) run without appsettings.Development.json's
  `Modules.ApiKeys: true` override in effect (e.g. emit against Production environment, or add
  an explicit FeatureManagement override at emission time that matches appsettings.json's
  base block) — regenerate the committed snapshot, confirm the ApiKeys paths and the three
  apiKeys* generated client functions are gone, and confirm no app/package breaks (none
  consume them today per the consumption check above — reconfirm with the same grep before
  removing).
- If (B) all modules enabled: appsettings.Development.json (or a dedicated emission-only
  config) explicitly documents/enables every optional module, not just ApiKeys by incidental
  side effect, and a comment at .github/actions/openapi-document/action.yml explains the
  document is deliberately the full-surface contract, not the shipped-default one.
- Either way: packages/sdk/src/openapi-regen.test.ts and the existing
  openapi-drift.yml/openapi-autoregen.yml workflows keep passing unmodified (they check
  invariants and diff-vs-emitted, not which modules are on) — no new test is required unless
  the reviewer wants one pinning the chosen module set for emission.
- docs/getting-started/fork-guide.md's module list block (currently lines ~319-334, "the
  shipped file verbatim") is checked for continued accuracy against whatever config
  the emission path now actually uses, and corrected if it drifted.
notes:
PLACEMENT: parented under Wallow-3mbx (backend epic), not Wallow-xzy1 (frontend epic), because the fix lives on the backend/CI side — appsettings.Development.json's incidental ApiKeys override and .github/actions/openapi-document/action.yml's ASPNETCORE_ENVIRONMENT=Development — even though the artifact affected is packages/sdk/openapi/v1.json. It is a direct, disk-verified consequence of Wallow-3mbx.1's module-gating fix (commit 4f9b0f10), which is what makes the module flag now load-bearing for the OpenAPI document at all.
DESIGN REVIEW (fresh session, 2026-08-05), read-only, empirically verified — not just re-reasoned from the existing bead text.

=== Q1: which modules are enabled under the config the doc is actually generated with ===
Base appsettings.json:81-86 (the "shipped defaults" a fresh fork gets): Branding/Storage/Notifications/Announcements/Inquiries = true, ApiKeys = false.
Both real regen pathways force ASPNETCORE_ENVIRONMENT=Development:
- api/src/Wallow.Api/Properties/launchSettings.json:9 and api/src/Wallow.AppHost/Properties/launchSettings.json:8 (what a dev has running for the documented manual regen command in packages/sdk/CLAUDE.md).
- .github/actions/openapi-document/action.yml:84 (shared by openapi-drift.yml/openapi-autoregen.yml), which builds api/src/Wallow.Api/Wallow.Api.csproj with -p:OpenApiGenerateDocumentsOnBuild=true.
appsettings.Development.json:77 overrides only Modules.ApiKeys to true; the other five already match base (true). Net effect: every regen pathway that exists today emits with ALL SEVEN modules on, never the shipped Production-shaped default. Matches the parent bead's own finding — reconfirmed independently.

=== Q2: is the committed v1.json stale? EXECUTED, not just reasoned ===
I reproduced the CI emission recipe exactly (own scratch Postgres container, not the tracked DB): `docker run postgres:18-alpine` on a scratch port, then
`ASPNETCORE_ENVIRONMENT=Development ConnectionStrings__DefaultConnection=<scratch> dotnet build api/src/Wallow.Api/Wallow.Api.csproj --configuration Release -p:OpenApiGenerateDocumentsOnBuild=true`
(the exact command action.yml's "Emit OpenAPI document at build time" step runs). Copied the emitted obj/openapi/Wallow.Api.json into my session scratchpad, then ran the SAME comparison action.yml's "compare" step runs: `jq -S 'del(.servers)'` on both the emitted file and the committed packages/sdk/openapi/v1.json, `diff -u`. Result: 0-line diff. Both have 125 paths, both include /v1/identity/auth/keys and /v1/identity/auth/keys/{keyId}. The only difference is servers[0].url, which the build-time document never carries at all (action.yml checks that separately via jq against EXPECTED_SERVER_URL — not part of the "document" drift check). CONCLUSION: the committed artifact is NOT stale. It matches today's code exactly, byte-for-byte modulo the servers block, under the wiring that actually exists.

=== Q3: openapi-regen.test.ts — read in full, packages/sdk/src/openapi-regen.test.ts ===
Five invariants against the committed snapshot only: every operation has an operationId, no duplicate operationIds, every non-204 2xx has a typed body schema, no orphaned component schema, no "Test Support"-tagged leakage — plus one check that the generated client's exported function names equal the snapshot's operationIds 1:1 (self-referential: generated FROM that same snapshot). It never fetches or compares against a live/emitted document — that comparison lives ONLY in .github/actions/openapi-document (action.yml), wired into openapi-drift.yml/openapi-autoregen.yml, never run by `pnpm test`. It has zero awareness of which modules are enabled. Removing ApiKeys' 2 paths/3 operations would not violate any of its five invariants (no dupes, no missing IDs, no untyped success, no orphans, no test-support tags), so it would pass identically on a smaller document. This epic's module-gating change (Wallow-3mbx.1) can neither break nor rescue this test either way — it is simply orthogonal to the module-set question. The REAL guard for "is the committed doc stale" is action.yml's diff, and per Q2 it currently passes truthfully. But that guard would ALSO pass silently if appsettings.Development.json's ApiKeys override were ever removed as "dead code cleanup" — it would just diff cleanly against the new (smaller) emission, auto-open a regen PR, and nobody would be prompted to notice a module's client surface vanished. So: adequate for catching accidental codegen/snapshot drift; provides ZERO protection for "which module set should this document represent," because nothing today asserts that.

=== Q4: is a shape-varying document actually wrong? ===
In principle "disabling a module shrinks the SDK" is correct/desired behavior. But that's not what's happening here: the document's shape is not driven by which modules a FORK has chosen to enable — it's driven by an incidental interaction between a hardcoded CI/dev environment name (Development) and a Development-only appsettings override that exists for unrelated local-dev convenience. Today this produces a document that's accurate to what the recipe actually does (Q2), so there is no live bug. The actual gap is provenance/documentation: nothing states that the committed document is deliberately the "all modules on" contract rather than the shipped-default one, so a future contributor who tidies away the ApiKeys override (a very plausible "why does dev override this one module and not the other five" cleanup) would silently shrink the SDK with no reviewer prompted to notice, and no test would complain (Q3).

=== Q5: cost of the bead's own suggested Option A — EMPIRICALLY MORE EXPENSIVE THAN THE BEAD ASSUMED ===
The bead's acceptance criteria for Option A say: "emit against Production environment, OR add an explicit FeatureManagement override at emission time that matches appsettings.json's base block." I tried both, for real, with a scratch Postgres:
(a) ASPNETCORE_ENVIRONMENT=Production: hard failure. `dotnet build ... -p:OpenApiGenerateDocumentsOnBuild=true` throws `System.InvalidOperationException: OpenIddict:SigningCertPath is required in non-development environments.` (api/src/Modules/Identity/Wallow.Identity.Infrastructure/Extensions/IdentityInfrastructureExtensions.cs:103) — action.yml's own header comment already predicted this ("Development is the environment the OpenAPI document is defined for: OpenIddict refuses to start elsewhere"), confirmed by direct reproduction, not just re-read.
(b) Env-var override of just FeatureManagement:Modules.ApiKeys, keeping ASPNETCORE_ENVIRONMENT=Development: does NOT work, and I isolated why. Built a minimal throwaway ASP.NET Core project (own scratch dir, not this repo) with the identical OpenApiGenerateDocumentsOnBuild wiring, and proved: an env var override of a TOP-LEVEL, DOT-FREE config key (e.g. `MyFlag=false`) DOES propagate correctly through `dotnet build`'s Exec-spawned dotnet-getdocument.dll child process. An env var override of a key whose name contains a literal "." (e.g. `FeatureManagement__Modules.ApiKeys=false`, or even a top-level `Modules.ApiKeys=false` with no nesting at all) does NOT propagate through that exact pipeline — it silently falls back to whatever appsettings.*.json already says — even though the identical key/override DOES work correctly through a plain `dotnet run` (verified with builder.Configuration directly, both a raw ConfigurationBuilder and a full WebApplicationBuilder, both showed correct override). So something between `dotnet build`'s outer process and the MSBuild-<Exec>-spawned dotnet-getdocument child process drops env vars whose name contains a period — and EVERY Wallow module flag is literally named "Modules.{X}" (a dot), so this technique cannot reliably gate ANY module during build-time OpenAPI emission, not just ApiKeys. This is new information the original bead did not have; its Option A acceptance criterion as written is not actually achievable the way it describes.
(c) The other IsDevelopment()-adjacent bypass, ASPNETCORE_ENVIRONMENT=Testing (IdentityInfrastructureExtensions.cs:96 also accepts `environment.EnvironmentName == "Testing"`), correctly avoids both the OpenIddict cert issue and the dotted-env-var issue (no appsettings.Testing.json override exists, so base Modules.ApiKeys=false flows through untouched) — but hits a NEW, separate wall: it lacks Development's Redis tolerance. Reproduced directly: the build fails with `StackExchange.Redis.RedisConnectionException: It was not possible to connect to the redis server(s)... use abortConnect=false`, because only appsettings.Development.json sets that; nothing in the emission path supplies a Redis connection or an equivalent override for Testing.
CONCLUSION: making Option A actually work requires a genuinely NEW emission-only config surface (its own appsettings.*.json or an ASPNETCORE_ENVIRONMENT value plus a Redis-tolerant connection string plus something satisfying/bypassing OpenIddict's cert check) — real infra work, not the "one env var" the bead's acceptance criteria assumed, and nothing would test that this new path stays correct over time.

=== RECOMMENDATION: WONT-DO (reverses the parent bead's tentative "(A) shipped defaults" lean, on evidence) ===
Given: (1) the committed artifact is proven NOT stale today: (2) Option A costs materially more than assumed — a new, fragile emission environment with no test coverage of its own, to fix a document that isn't currently wrong; (3) CLAUDE.md's pre-release doctrine says regeneration is free and discourages spending effort on rollout/compatibility edge cases; (4) the bead's own consumption check found zero consumers of the ApiKeys client surface today, so there is no live victim of the "false promise" risk. The proportionate response for a P3 with no current bug is the SMALLEST correct change: make the incidental choice deliberate with a two-line comment, not a new build path.
SMALLEST CORRECT CHANGE (if any edit is made at all): one comment above `"Modules.ApiKeys": true` in api/src/Wallow.Api/appsettings.Development.json, and one line in .github/actions/openapi-document/action.yml's header, stating plainly that the committed/emitted OpenAPI document is deliberately the "all modules on" full-surface contract (option B from the parent bead's own menu), not the shipped Production default — so a future "why does dev override just this one module" cleanup is warned before it silently shrinks the SDK on the next auto-regen PR. No new test needed for a two-line comment; if the team wants an actual pin, the smallest one would be a single assertion added to openapi-regen.test.ts checking `paths` contains "identity/auth/keys" (documents current intent, fails loudly if a future emission change drops it) — optional, not required by acceptance criteria as written ("no new test is required").
Otherwise: recommend closing Wallow-3mbx.6 as wont-do with this rationale, OR downgrading it to "add the two explanatory comments" if the team wants the paper trail — but NOT pursuing Option A's env/config plumbing, which this session found to be substantially more work than the original filer could have known, for a document that is not currently broken.

All docker containers used for verification were removed; api/src/Wallow.Api/obj and bin were reset to their pre-session state (build artifacts only, gitignored, no tracked files touched). git status confirms zero source changes from this session.
close_reason: wont-do: premise did not hold. Re-emitting the OpenAPI document via the CI recipe and diffing against the committed packages/sdk/openapi/v1.json produced a zero-line delta, so the artifact is not stale. The proposed shipped-defaults regen is also not achievable as specified: ASPNETCORE_ENVIRONMENT=Production hard-fails on OpenIddict, and env-var overrides of dotted config keys (every module flag is Modules.X) silently fail to propagate through the dotnet build -> Exec -> dotnet-getdocument pipeline. openapi-regen.test.ts is orthogonal to the module-set question and neither catches nor prevents this drift. Generating with all modules enabled is the deliberate choice; a fork that disables a module regenerates its own client. Full analysis in this bead's notes.

title: tidy the IWallowModule surface — collection types, per-access allocation, assembly anchors
description:
Polish on the IWallowModule surface itself
(api/src/Shared/Wallow.Shared.Infrastructure/Modules/IWallowModule.cs). None of this is a defect --
group it into one pass rather than filing three P3s, and fold it into whichever registry bead is
picked up first if that is cheaper.

## 1. Inconsistent collection types, both re-allocating per access

  IEnumerable<Assembly> HandlerAssemblies { get; }    (line 46)
  IReadOnlyList<Type> DbContextTypes { get; }         (line 59)

Two collection members, two different types, no reason for the difference. Every implementation is
an expression-bodied collection expression (e.g. IdentityModule.cs:22-26), so each get allocates a
fresh array. Reads happen a handful of times at startup so the allocation is irrelevant on its own,
but IEnumerable also means a caller could enumerate twice and get two different arrays. Make both
IReadOnlyList<T> and back them with static readonly fields.

## 2. Handler-assembly anchors are arbitrary types

  IdentityModule.cs:24     typeof(CreateServiceAccountHandler).Assembly
  StorageModule.cs:22      typeof(CreateBucketHandler).Assembly
  ApiKeysModule.cs:28      typeof(IApiKeyRepository).Assembly
  BrandingModule.cs:26     typeof(IClientBrandingRepository).Assembly

The Infrastructure entry is already anchored on the module type itself, which the interface's own
doc comment (IWallowModule.cs:42-44) prescribes precisely so it "cannot rot when the anchor type
moves". The Application entry gets no such protection: it points at whatever type happened to be
handy, and the two CQRS-less modules point at a repository interface with a comment explaining why.
Deleting or moving that one type is a build break rather than silent breakage, so this is a
readability issue, not a correctness one -- but a dedicated marker per Application assembly
(e.g. public sealed class IdentityApplicationAssembly) makes the anchor's purpose obvious and
un-deletable, and lets the comment shrink to one line.

## 3. Six modules carry an IHostEnvironment they never use

AddServices takes IHostEnvironment because AddIdentityModule needs it; the other six accept and
drop it (StorageModule.cs:33-38 and friends). The plan recorded this as a deliberate trade --
"six wrappers carry an unused parameter; that is cheaper than special-casing Identity out of the
registry" -- and it is the right call. Listed here only so a future reader does not re-open it.
Do NOT change this; the doc comment on IWallowModule.cs:73-76 already explains it.

## Acceptance

- HandlerAssemblies and DbContextTypes are both IReadOnlyList<T>, backed by static readonly fields
  in all seven implementations.
- Each module's Application assembly is anchored on a purpose-named marker type, or the bead
  records why it stayed as-is.
- No behaviour change: the same assemblies and context types are reported, and
  HandlerCodegenTests plus ModuleToggleTests pass unchanged.
- ./scripts/run-tests.sh and ./scripts/run-tests.sh integration green.
notes:
SCOUT: DEPENDS ON Wallow-3mbx.1 (already wired: bd dep add Wallow-3mbx.5 Wallow-3mbx.1) — both edit IWallowModule.cs and all 7 XModule.cs files; 3mbx.1 (P1 bug) goes first, this P3 polish bead follows and should also normalize the new ApiAssembly member 3mbx.1 adds.
CITATION DRIFT (verified on disk, do not re-litigate but note for whoever implements): "StorageModule.cs:22" should be line 20 (typeof(CreateBucketHandler).Assembly); "ApiKeysModule.cs:28" should be line 26 (typeof(IApiKeyRepository).Assembly). All other citations (IWallowModule.cs:46 HandlerAssemblies, :59 DbContextTypes, IdentityModule.cs:22-26, BrandingModule.cs:26, IWallowModule.cs:73-76 doc comment on the unused IHostEnvironment) verified EXACT.
Template for the fix: all 7 XModule.cs files are structurally identical — HandlerAssemblies and DbContextTypes are both expression-bodied properties returning a fresh collection expression per access; converting to IReadOnlyList<Assembly>/IReadOnlyList<Type> backed by `private static readonly` fields is a mechanical, identical edit across api/src/Modules/{Announcements,ApiKeys,Branding,Identity,Inquiries,Notifications,Storage}/*.Infrastructure/Modules/*Module.cs.

DESIGN: PARTIAL. Do concern #1 (collection-type unification only, no backing fields). WON'T-FIX concern #2 (marker-type anchors) — 3mbx.1's landed precedent argues against it. Concern #3 stays untouched per the bead's own instruction. Dep edge on 3mbx.1 is already gone (verified: bd dep list Wallow-3mbx.5 shows only the parent-child edge to the epic).

=== PREMISE CHECK, per concern ===

1. COLLECTION TYPES / PER-ACCESS ALLOCATION — real but the allocation half is negligible, confirmed by reading every call site, not assumed.
Read IWallowModule.cs and all 7 XModule.cs (Announcements/ApiKeys/Branding/Identity/Inquiries/Notifications/Storage). Confirmed exact: HandlerAssemblies is `IEnumerable<Assembly>` (IWallowModule.cs:46), DbContextTypes is `IReadOnlyList<Type>` (IWallowModule.cs:59), both implemented as expression-bodied collection expressions in all 7 modules — no behavioral reason for the type difference, it's drift.
Grepped every production consumer of both members (not just the two the bead names):
  - HandlerAssemblies: exactly ONE call site, Program.cs:200, inside `[ ..., .. enabledModules.SelectMany(module => module.HandlerAssemblies) ]` — a single LINQ pass at Wolverine setup, once per process start.
  - DbContextTypes: WallowModules.cs:302 (`.SelectMany` over core modules), :323 (`.SelectMany` over feature modules) — both inside `RunTestMigrationsAsync`, which only runs when `app.Environment.IsEnvironment("Testing")`; and ModuleMigrations.cs:53 (`foreach`) and :79 (`.SelectMany`) in `Wallow.MigrationService`, which is a separate short-lived migration-runner process, not the API host's steady state.
Every one of these is a single enumeration, at startup or in a one-shot migration run — never a request-time or loop-repeated read. No call site enumerates either property twice. So the bead's own hedge ("irrelevant on its own") is correct, and I did not find the "caller enumerates twice and gets two different arrays" failure mode anywhere in this codebase — it is a real possibility of the shape (`IEnumerable` doesn't promise stable identity across enumerations) but not an observed or currently-reachable bug.
VERDICT: the *type* inconsistency (IEnumerable vs IReadOnlyList) is real and cheap to fix; the *allocation* concern should not drive the design (matches the bead's own text) and does NOT justify adding backing static fields — see "REJECTED" below.

2. ASSEMBLY ANCHORS — real readability point (bead says so itself: "not a correctness one"), but 3mbx.1's landed code is fresh, on-point prior art that argues against the bead's proposed fix.
Confirmed the citation drift the epic scout already found: StorageModule.cs's `typeof(CreateBucketHandler).Assembly` is at line 20, not 22; ApiKeysModule.cs's `typeof(IApiKeyRepository).Assembly` is at line 26, not 28. Everything else (IdentityModule.cs:22-26, BrandingModule.cs:24-28, the doc comment) verified exact.
The Infrastructure entry (`typeof(XModule).Assembly`) is definitionally safe forever: XModule is only ever declared in its own Infrastructure project, so the anchor can never point anywhere else. The Application entry's anchor (a handler type, or for ApiKeys/Branding — which have no CQRS handlers — a repository interface, each already carries a class-level XML comment explaining the choice) is weaker in the sense the bead states, but not in the way a marker type actually fixes: if the anchor type is DELETED, both today's anchor and a hypothetical marker type fail the same way (compile error, self-correcting). If the anchor type MOVES to a different assembly, today's handler-typed anchor *moves with it* and keeps pointing at wherever the handlers now live — which is arguably more correct, not less, since HandlerAssemblies exists to track where handlers actually are. A purpose-built marker type sitting alone in the Application project doesn't share that property; it just sits still.
3mbx.1 landed the SAME category of decision one bead over, in the same file family, on the same day: `WallowModules.cs`'s `_moduleApiAssemblies` table anchors each module's `.Api` assembly on a **real controller type** (`typeof(UsersController).Assembly`, etc.) specifically *instead of* an assembly-name string or a purpose-built marker, with its own doc comment stating why: "Anchored on a real controller type rather than an assembly-name string, so renaming or deleting one is a compile error." That is the identical problem (safely pin an assembly reference) solved the identical way the Application-assembly anchors already work today — anchor on a real, meaningful type already in the assembly, not mint a placeholder. This is fresh, directly-applicable precedent the epic itself created, and it argues for leaving the existing handler/interface anchors alone, not for adding 7 new no-op `public sealed class FooApplicationAssembly` types whose only purpose is existing.
VERDICT: WON'T-FIX. The existing anchors are already load-bearing real types with class-level comments (ApiKeysModule.cs, BrandingModule.cs) explaining the CQRS-less case, and the interface's own XML doc (IWallowModule.cs:33-44) explains the general shape. Adding 7 marker classes increases each Application assembly's public surface for a purely cosmetic win the codebase just chose not to take on the sibling .Api side.

3. IHostEnvironment ON SIX UNUSED MODULES — bead itself says "Do NOT change this." Confirmed unchanged; not touched by this design.

=== WHAT TO DO (concern #1 only) ===

Change `IWallowModule.HandlerAssemblies` from `IEnumerable<Assembly>` to `IReadOnlyList<Assembly>`, matching `DbContextTypes`'s existing type. Do NOT add backing `private static readonly` fields to either member — see REJECTED below. The property bodies stay exactly as they are today (`=> [ ... ]` collection expressions); only the declared return type changes.

FILES / EXACT EDITS (12 files, all one-line type-signature changes, mechanical and identical in shape):

Interface (1):
  api/src/Shared/Wallow.Shared.Infrastructure/Modules/IWallowModule.cs:46
    `IEnumerable<Assembly> HandlerAssemblies { get; }` -> `IReadOnlyList<Assembly> HandlerAssemblies { get; }`

Production implementations (7), each `public IEnumerable<Assembly> HandlerAssemblies =>` -> `public IReadOnlyList<Assembly> HandlerAssemblies =>`, collection-expression body unchanged:
  api/src/Modules/Announcements/Wallow.Announcements.Infrastructure/Modules/AnnouncementsModule.cs:18
  api/src/Modules/ApiKeys/Wallow.ApiKeys.Infrastructure/Modules/ApiKeysModule.cs:24
  api/src/Modules/Branding/Wallow.Branding.Infrastructure/Modules/BrandingModule.cs:24
  api/src/Modules/Identity/Wallow.Identity.Infrastructure/Modules/IdentityModule.cs:22
  api/src/Modules/Inquiries/Wallow.Inquiries.Infrastructure/Modules/InquiriesModule.cs:18
  api/src/Modules/Notifications/Wallow.Notifications.Infrastructure/Modules/NotificationsModule.cs:18
  api/src/Modules/Storage/Wallow.Storage.Infrastructure/Modules/StorageModule.cs:18

Test-only IWallowModule stubs (4) — MUST change too, or they fail to compile against the narrowed interface (grep -rln ": IWallowModule" api/src api/tests confirms these are the ONLY other implementers, 10 total, matching the 7+3 count exactly, nothing missed):
  api/tests/Wallow.Api.Tests/WallowModulesApplicationPartsTests.cs:103        `public IEnumerable<Assembly> HandlerAssemblies => [];`
  api/tests/Wallow.Api.Tests/WallowModulesModuleEnablementTests.cs:110        `public IEnumerable<Assembly> HandlerAssemblies => [];`
  api/tests/Wallow.Api.Tests/Integration/RunTestMigrationsTests.cs:166        `public IEnumerable<Assembly> HandlerAssemblies => [];`  (ProbeFeatureModule stub)
  api/tests/Wallow.Api.Tests/Integration/RunTestMigrationsTests.cs:185        `public IEnumerable<Assembly> HandlerAssemblies => [];`  (ProbeCoreModule stub)
  Same edit in all four: `IEnumerable<Assembly>` -> `IReadOnlyList<Assembly>`.

CALL SITE — no code change needed, confirmed compiles as-is:
  api/src/Wallow.Api/Program.cs:200 `.. enabledModules.SelectMany(module => module.HandlerAssemblies)` — `SelectMany` accepts any `IEnumerable<T>`; `IReadOnlyList<Assembly>` satisfies that with no cast. Read the full surrounding collection-expression block (lines ~190-201) to confirm no other member access on the property (e.g. no `.Count`/indexer anywhere) that would need adjusting either way.

NOT TOUCHED (confirmed no code depends on the exact type, no change needed):
  api/src/Wallow.Api/WallowModules.cs (AddWallowModules, ResolveEnabledModules, RunTestMigrationsAsync, IsModuleEnabled<TModule> — none read HandlerAssemblies at all; DbContextTypes call sites at :302/:323 already consume IReadOnlyList<Type>, unaffected)
  api/src/Wallow.Modules.Registry/WallowModuleRegistry.cs — constructs `new XModule()` instances only, never touches either property
  api/src/Wallow.MigrationService/ModuleMigrations.cs — only reads DbContextTypes and SchemaName, never HandlerAssemblies
  api/tests/Wallow.Architecture.Tests/Modules/ModuleRegistryTests.cs, ModuleToggleTests.cs, ModuleRegistrationTests.cs, WolverineCodegenPolicyTests.cs — reflection/identity-based, none assert on HandlerAssemblies' declared type
  api/tests/Wallow.Api.Tests/Integration/HandlerCodegenTests.cs, BootstrapAdminHandlerCodegenTests.cs — compile Wolverine's HandlerGraph, downstream of Program.cs:200's already-correct SelectMany, unaffected by the property's declared type

REJECTED — backing static readonly fields (the bead's literal ask, and part of its stated acceptance criteria):
Would require adding, per module, a `private static readonly Assembly[] _handlerAssemblies = [...]` (and, if applied symmetrically, the same for DbContextTypes) plus rewriting the property to `=> _handlerAssemblies`, doubling each member from 1 line to ~2-3 and adding a field per property across all 7 modules (14+ new lines total) for a benefit that only exists if some caller enumerates the property more than once per module per process — which, per the exhaustive call-site grep above, none do, today. This is churn with no observable payoff: no test could distinguish the two forms (both produce equal content, in the same order, on every access), and "the allocation is irrelevant on its own" is the bead's own words. Recommend explicitly declining this half of the acceptance criteria rather than doing it to satisfy the letter of the bead.

=== TEST PLAN ===

This is a pure signature-narrowing refactor (IEnumerable<Assembly> -> IReadOnlyList<Assembly>, a widening of guarantees, not a behavior change — every existing collection-expression body already produces a concrete array, which already implements IReadOnlyList<Assembly>). The honest test story is exactly what the bead's own acceptance criteria says for behavior: "the same assemblies and context types are reported, and HandlerCodegenTests plus ModuleToggleTests pass unchanged" — no new test earns its cost here, and per .claude/rules/TESTING.md this repo does not write source-reading tests to enforce a type signature (that's a code-review concern, same class as 3mbx.3's now-closed "no string literal remains" grep).
  - Build is the primary gate: if any of the 12 sites above is missed, the mismatched interface/implementation signature is a compile error (CS0738/CS1715-class error), not a silent pass — the narrowing is compiler-enforced by construction.
  - `./scripts/run-tests.sh api` (fast tier) must stay green, in particular `HandlerCodegenTests.EveryDiscoveredHandler_Compiles` (proves Wolverine still discovers the same handler set through the now-`IReadOnlyList`-typed property) and anything in `Wallow.Architecture.Tests` (`ModuleRegistryTests`, `ModuleToggleTests`, `ModuleRegistrationTests`, `WolverineCodegenPolicyTests`) that touches module shape.
  - `./scripts/run-tests.sh api integration` must stay green for the same reason — `BootstrapAdminHandlerCodegenTests` and any handler-discovery-dependent integration path.
  - Never bare `dotnet test`, per .claude/rules/TESTING.md.
  - No new test file is proposed. If the reviewer wants an explicit regression guard beyond the compiler, the cheapest true one is a one-line addition to whichever architecture test already asserts module shape (e.g. `ModuleRegistryTests`) asserting `WallowModuleRegistry.All` items' `HandlerAssemblies` is assignable to `IReadOnlyList<Assembly>` — but this is redundant with the compiler and I would not add it unless asked.

=== RISKS / WHAT WOULD FALSIFY THIS DESIGN ===

- If a future module ever needs to LAZILY compute HandlerAssemblies (e.g. from a slow reflection scan) the IReadOnlyList narrowing would force eager materialization where IEnumerable allowed deferred execution — not a concern for any of the 7 current implementations (all are literal collection expressions), but worth a one-line note in the interface doc if that ever changes. No evidence this is coming; not blocking.
- If a future consumer starts enumerating HandlerAssemblies or DbContextTypes more than once per process in a genuinely hot path (not true today, verified exhaustively above), the "no backing field" call should be revisited — the REJECTED section above is conditioned on today's call sites, not a permanent ban.
- The WON'T-FIX on concern #2 rests on reading 3mbx.1's landed code as intentional precedent rather than an unrelated one-off choice; if a future reviewer disagrees with that reading, the marker-type option is fully specified in the bead body already and can be picked up as its own P3 without re-scouting.

=== SEAM LEFT FOR Wallow-3mbx.2 ===

Not this bead's job (per the coordinator's brief: "leave a seam, do not do its work"). Confirmed by reading: `SchemaName` (IWallowModule.cs:66, unaffected by this design — this design touches only `HandlerAssemblies`) is the member 3mbx.2 is about; nothing here changes its type or its declaration. 3mbx.2's own note already correctly identifies `IWallowModule.SchemaName`, `ModuleMigrations.cs:117-126`-area `AddSchemaScopedDbContext`, and each module's own `AddXModule` extension (e.g. `ApiKeysInfrastructureExtensions.cs:46`) as its three declarations to reconcile — this bead does not touch any of them, so there is no coordination needed between the two beads.
CITATION DRIFT (verified on disk again, matches epic scout's earlier finding, not re-litigated): StorageModule.cs's typeof(CreateBucketHandler).Assembly is at line 20 (bead cites 22); ApiKeysModule.cs's typeof(IApiKeyRepository).Assembly is at line 26 (bead cites 28). All other citations in the bead body verified exact.
DESIGN REVIEW: APPROVE (one minor, non-blocking correction).

Read IWallowModule.cs, all 7 XModule.cs, WallowModules.cs, ModuleMigrations.cs,
WallowModuleRegistry.cs, Program.cs, and the 4 test stub files on disk (not trusted
from the design note). Also read 3mbx.1's and 3mbx.3's landed designs/reports in full
to check compatibility.

=== 1. BOTH REJECTIONS ARE RIGHT, verified independently ===

ALLOCATION REJECTION — correct, and the repo-wide grep matches exactly.
grep -rn "HandlerAssemblies|DbContextTypes" over api/src (excluding obj/bin) finds:
- HandlerAssemblies: exactly ONE production call site, Program.cs:200, inside a
  collection-expression spread ".. enabledModules.SelectMany(module =>
  module.HandlerAssemblies)" built once per process at Wolverine setup.
- DbContextTypes: WallowModules.cs:365/386 (both inside RunTestMigrationsAsync,
  Testing-environment only) and ModuleMigrations.cs:53/79 (MigrationService, a
  short-lived one-shot process, both call sites confirmed startup-only in Program.cs:33/41).
Traced each: WallowModules.cs:365/386 split modules into disjoint IsCore/!IsCore
.Where() branches before .SelectMany, so a given module's DbContextTypes getter is
invoked at most once per process even though the property is textually referenced
twice. Same disjoint-branch shape in ModuleMigrations.CreateRunners (isCore:true vs
isCore:false), called exactly twice at MigrationService startup (Program.cs:33,41),
never per-request. No path enumerates any module's property twice. The rejection of
static-readonly backing fields is correct and well-evidenced, not hand-waved — declining
unearned churn here is the right call.

MARKER-TYPE REJECTION — correct, precedent is real and on-point.
Confirmed 3mbx.1's landed _moduleApiAssemblies table (WallowModules.cs:47-56) anchors
each module's Api assembly on a real controller type (typeof(UsersController).Assembly,
typeof(ApiKeysController).Assembly, etc.), explicitly instead of a marker or a
string. Same problem shape (pin an assembly reference safely), same answer (anchor
on a real, meaningful type already there) the existing HandlerAssemblies anchors
already use. Checked all 7 modules for a fragile case (a module with no stable public
type to anchor on): none exists — Identity/Storage/Announcements/Inquiries/Notifications
anchor on real CQRS handler types, ApiKeys/Branding (the two CQRS-less modules) anchor
on a real repository interface with a class-level XML comment already explaining the
choice (verified ApiKeysModule.cs:11-15, BrandingModule.cs). WON'T-FIX is sound.

=== 2. IS THE 12-FILE CHURN WORTH IT? Pure taste, not a defect, but cheap and safe ===

Checked whether the current IEnumerable<Assembly> type permits mutation of a
registry-owned collection: no. Every implementation is an expression-bodied collection
expression (`=> [...]`), so a FRESH array is allocated on every access — a caller
holding a reference from one call cannot corrupt what the next call returns, and
nothing anywhere calls .ToList()/.Add() against the result. So there is no live defect
here, contra a naive reading of "IEnumerable allows mutation" — the bead's own
"could enumerate twice and get two different arrays" is the correct framing, and
it's real-but-unobserved exactly as the design says. Given that, this is a pure
type-consistency win, but it is compiler-enforced (a missed call site is a build
error, not a silent bug), zero behavior change, and touches nothing outside the
property declarations — a reasonable, low-risk P3 given four sibling beads already
built and landed cleanly on this exact interface.

=== 3. COMPATIBILITY WITH WHAT LANDED — clean ===

Confirmed IsModuleEnabled<TModule>() (WallowModules.cs:204,
`this IReadOnlyList<IWallowModule> enabledModules`) does exact GetType() matching
against module INSTANCES themselves — it never reads HandlerAssemblies or
DbContextTypes. Unaffected by this design, confirmed by reading the method.
WallowModuleRegistry.cs only constructs `new XModule()` instances, touches neither
property. ModuleMigrations.cs only reads DbContextTypes (unaffected, unchanged type)
and SchemaName. The four Wallow.Architecture.Tests suites reflection/identity-checks
module shape, none assert HandlerAssemblies' declared type. Program.cs:200's
SelectMany accepts any IEnumerable<T>, so IReadOnlyList<Assembly> satisfies it with
no cast needed. No breakage found anywhere.

=== 4. CALL-SITE INVENTORY — one real (cosmetic) error, nothing missed ===

The design's own header claims "12 files." Verified via `grep -rn ": IWallowModule"`
over api/src + api/tests: the ONLY implementers beyond the interface are the 7
production XModule.cs files plus 4 test stubs — but those 4 stubs live in only 3
files, because api/tests/Wallow.Api.Tests/Integration/RunTestMigrationsTests.cs
declares TWO stub classes (ProbeFeatureModule at line 166, ProbeCoreModule at line
185). So the correct count is 11 FILES / 12 EDIT SITES, not "12 files." This is
cosmetic, not a missed-site risk: the design's own bullet list already names both
RunTestMigrationsTests.cs edits (:166 and :185) individually and correctly, so an
implementer following the list misses nothing and the build cannot break from this.
Recommend fixing the summary header to "11 files, 12 edit sites" before implementation
for accuracy — non-blocking, does not require re-review.

=== 5. SEAM FOR Wallow-3mbx.2 — correctly left untouched, minor sequencing note ===
