title: ResolveEnabledModules builds and abandons a ServiceProvider to read seven booleans
description:
ResolveEnabledModules (api/src/Wallow.Api/WallowModules.cs:114-125) builds a full ServiceProvider
out of a half-populated IServiceCollection, resolves one boolean per module from it, and
deliberately never disposes it. The XML comment explains WHY it is not disposed and is correct as
far as it goes -- services.AddSingleton(configuration) registers an existing instance, so disposing
the temp container would dispose the host's own IConfiguration. The underlying need does not
require a container at all.

## Verified state

  private static IReadOnlyList<IWallowModule> ResolveEnabledModules(IServiceCollection services)
  {
      ServiceProvider tempProvider = services.BuildServiceProvider();
      IFeatureManager featureManager = tempProvider.GetRequiredService<IFeatureManager>();
      return [.. _allModules.Where(module =>
          module.IsCore
          || featureManager.IsEnabledAsync($"Modules.{module.Name}").GetAwaiter().GetResult())];
  }

Called from AddWallowModules (WallowModules.cs:66), which first does
services.AddSingleton(configuration) (line 63) -- a duplicate registration, since the host has
already registered IConfiguration -- and services.AddFeatureManagement() (line 64).

Three smells in six lines:
- A ServiceProvider built from a partially-configured collection and abandoned. Whatever singletons
  it instantiates (the feature manager, its options/cache, IOptionsMonitor) live for the process,
  and the feature-management stack registers change-token callbacks on the host's IConfiguration
  that nothing will ever unregister.
- .GetAwaiter().GetResult() -- sync-over-async, once per module, during startup.
- The duplicate IConfiguration registration exists only to make the temp provider resolvable.

The comment on line 61-62 says the AddSingleton is there so AddWallowModules is self-contained for
tests; ModuleToggleTests (Wallow.Architecture.Tests/Modules/ModuleToggleTests.cs) does invoke it
with a bare ServiceCollection, so that constraint is real and must survive the fix.

## Fix

Read the flag straight off IConfiguration -- AddWallowModules already takes it:

  bool enabled = module.IsCore
      || configuration.GetValue<bool?>($"FeatureManagement:Modules.{module.Name}") ?? false;

That removes the temp provider, the sync-over-async and the reason for the duplicate
AddSingleton(configuration), and keeps AddWallowModules callable from a bare ServiceCollection.
AddFeatureManagement() stays -- IFeatureManager is still used elsewhere in the app (and see
Wallow-3mbx.3).

Caveat to confirm before writing it: this hard-codes the "FeatureManagement:" section prefix and
gives up any non-boolean feature filter (percentage, time-window). Wallow uses plain booleans for
Modules.* today. If keeping filter support matters, the alternative is to resolve IFeatureManager
from the FINAL provider and move module selection after Build() -- a much larger change, and
registration has to happen before Build(), so it is probably not viable. Record the decision on the
bead either way.

## Acceptance

- ResolveEnabledModules no longer calls BuildServiceProvider and no longer blocks on an async call.
- ModuleToggleTests passes unchanged (all three tests, including the absent-flag case which must
  still read as disabled).
- Flag semantics unchanged: absent key = disabled for optional modules, IsCore ignores the key.
- ./scripts/run-tests.sh arch and ./scripts/run-tests.sh api green.

ModuleToggleTests.cs (api/tests/Wallow.Architecture.Tests/Modules/ModuleToggleTests.cs) invokes AddWallowModules via reflection (Assembly.Load("Wallow.Api") + GetMethod("AddWallowModules", Public|Static)) against a bare ServiceCollection — confirmed this must keep working. docs and ILSpy-decompiling Microsoft.FeatureManagement.dll/Microsoft.Extensions.Configuration.Binder.dll
from ~/.nuget/packages directly (ilspycmd 10.1.1.8388 was on PATH) rather than trusting recall —
citations below are to decompiled source, not memory.

=== 1. PREMISE, VERIFIED ON DISK — citations have DRIFTED, corrected here ===

ResolveEnabledModules is now at api/src/Wallow.Api/WallowModules.cs:263-274 (bead body cites
114-125 — stale, +149 lines from 3mbx.1/3mbx.3's unrelated additions to the same file). Confirmed
it really does: `ServiceProvider tempProvider = services.BuildServiceProvider();` (265),
`tempProvider.GetRequiredService<IFeatureManager>()` (266), then
`featureManager.IsEnabledAsync($"Modules.{module.Name}").GetAwaiter().GetResult()` (272) per
module, filtered over `WallowModuleRegistry.All` (was `_allModules` in the bead's stale citation
— k2zp/lw4a already extracted that array into api/src/Wallow.Modules.Registry/WallowModuleRegistry.cs).
Called from AddWallowModules at line 79 (bead cites 66). services.AddSingleton(configuration) is
now line 76, services.AddFeatureManagement() line 77 (bead cites 63/64).

WHY it was written this way: IFeatureManager is a DI service (Microsoft.FeatureManagement.AspNetCore's
AddFeatureManagement() registers it), and ResolveEnabledModules needs an answer BEFORE the real
container exists — it decides which modules' AddServices even run. Building a scratch provider was
the mechanical way to get a resolvable IFeatureManager without waiting for services.BuildServiceProvider()
on the final, fully-populated collection (which doesn't exist yet at this point in Program.cs). The
duplicate services.AddSingleton(configuration) at line 76 exists ONLY to make that scratch provider
resolvable — the host's real WebApplicationBuilder already registers IConfiguration itself; grepped,
confirmed no other reason for the duplicate.

=== 2. IS THIS A REAL PROBLEM? Yes, three concrete costs, not merely inelegant ===

- Leaked change-token subscription: `services.AddSingleton(configuration)` registers the REAL
  IConfiguration instance, so ConfigurationFeatureDefinitionProvider (the IFeatureManager's default
  IFeatureDefinitionProvider) subscribes to that instance's reload token
  (`ChangeToken.OnChange(() => _configuration.GetReloadToken(), ...)` —
  Microsoft.FeatureManagement.dll, decompiled ConfigurationFeatureDefinitionProvider.cs:67-70). The
  scratch provider is deliberately never disposed (correctly — disposing it would dispose the
  host's real IConfiguration), so that subscription is NEVER unregistered either. Every config
  reload for the lifetime of the process re-triggers a no-op cache invalidation on an object nothing
  will ever query again. Small, but permanent and pointless.
- Sync-over-async once per module at startup (`GetAwaiter().GetResult()`), 7 times.
- A ServiceProvider built from a HALF-populated IServiceCollection (only IConfiguration +
  FeatureManagement registered at that point) and immediately abandoned — whatever singletons
  FeatureManagement wires (IFeatureManager, its IMemoryCache, IOptions<FeatureManagementOptions>)
  live for the process for no further purpose.

None of this is expensive (startup-only, 7 modules), so it is not a P1/P0 issue, but it is a real,
fixable smell with a low-risk fix — worth doing at P3.

=== 3. SEMANTIC EQUIVALENCE — the load-bearing question, verified by decompiling the actual
package, not assumed ===

Package: Microsoft.FeatureManagement.AspNetCore 4.6.0 (api/Directory.Packages.props:85), consumed
only by api/src/Wallow.Api/Wallow.Api.csproj:96 (PackageReference, no <Version> — CPM).

3.1. What Wallow's config ACTUALLY contains (verified, all 5 files):
appsettings.json:80-87, appsettings.Production.json:48-55 — flat boolean leaves under
"FeatureManagement": { "Modules.X": true|false }. appsettings.Development.json:76-78 overrides only
"Modules.ApiKeys": true. appsettings.Staging.json / appsettings.Testing.json — zero Modules.* keys
(grepped, confirmed, exit 1/no match). No EnabledFor array, no RequirementType, no filter, no
allocation, anywhere. scul (landed) already deleted the one thing that could have complicated this
(the dead "Wallow:Modules" duplicate block and the Modules.Configuration/Modules.Identity phantoms).
Also grepped all of api/src for FeatureFilter/PercentageFilter/TimeWindowFilter/Targeting/EnabledFor
— zero real usage (only unrelated hits: IAnnouncementTargetingService, a domain concept with no
relation to Microsoft.FeatureManagement).

3.2. Decompiled Microsoft.FeatureManagement.dll 4.6.0 (FeatureManager.cs, ConfigurationFeatureDefinitionProvider.cs)
to nail the exact evaluation semantics for THIS shape of config, method by method:

  - Missing key: FeatureManager.GetFeatureDefinition (line 755-770) calls
    _featureDefinitionProvider.GetFeatureDefinitionAsync(feature); if null and
    `!_options.IgnoreMissingFeatures` it throws, else it just returns null and EvaluateFeature's
    caller (line 560) skips straight to `_sessionManagers` (null in Wallow — no ISessionManager
    registered) and returns Enabled=false (the EvaluationEvent's default). FeatureManagementOptions.IgnoreMissingFeatures
    defaults to TRUE (FeatureManagementOptions.cs:21) and Wallow never overrides it (grepped
    "FeatureManagementOptions"/"Configure<FeatureManagementOptions>" across api/src — zero hits). So
    today: **missing key -> false, no throw**. That is EXACTLY `configuration.GetValue<bool?>(key) ?? false`.
  - Scalar "true"/"false" leaf: ConfigurationFeatureDefinitionProvider.ParseDotnetSchemaFeatureDefinition
    (lines 231-276) reads `configurationSection.Value` directly (non-null/non-empty for a scalar
    leaf); if `bool.TryParse(value, out result) && result` it adds a single "AlwaysOn" filter, else
    EnabledFor stays an EMPTY list (the "EnabledFor" child section has no children for a scalar
    node). Back in FeatureManager.IsEnabledAsync(FeatureDefinition,...) (line 666-753): empty
    EnabledFor -> `enabled = false` immediately (line 680-683); non-empty EnabledFor containing only
    "AlwaysOn" -> the literal `string.Equals(name, "AlwaysOn", OrdinalIgnoreCase)` branch (line 693)
    sets `enabled = true` and breaks, for RequirementType.Any (the untouched default — Wallow's
    config never sets RequirementType). So **"true" -> true, "false" -> false**, no filter ever
    invoked — an exact match for parsing the same string as a plain bool.
  - No app-context is ever passed (`featureManager.IsEnabledAsync($"Modules.{module.Name}")`, no
    second argument), so the useAppContext branch (targeting/contextual filters) never executes
    regardless of config shape.
  - Case sensitivity: GetDotnetSchemaFeatureDefinition matches keys via
    `StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase` (ConfigurationFeatureDefinitionProvider.cs:159) — same
    case-insensitivity IConfiguration itself already has. IWallowModule.Name values are fixed,
    exact-cased C# string literals ("Storage", "ApiKeys", ...), so this is a non-issue either way.

CONCLUSION: for every shape Wallow's config actually uses today, `configuration.GetValue<bool?>
($"FeatureManagement:Modules.{module.Name}") ?? false` is EXACTLY equivalent to
`featureManager.IsEnabledAsync($"Modules.{module.Name}")`, decompiled-and-verified, not inferred.

3.3. Where it stops being equivalent (the caveat the bead itself raised) — and the mitigation:
if a key is ever configured as an OBJECT instead of a scalar (the shape a percentage/targeting/
time-window filter needs — `"Modules.X": { "EnabledFor": [...] }`), IFeatureManager would evaluate
the filter; a raw `GetValue<bool?>` on an object-valued key throws inside .NET's own binder
(decompiled Microsoft.Extensions.Configuration.Binder 10.0.10, ConfigurationBinder.cs:
GetValue->ConvertValue->TryConvertValue, `System.SR.Error_FailedBinding` InvalidOperationException
on a non-scalar/non-convertible value) rather than silently returning something wrong — so it does
NOT silently misread a filter as "disabled"; it throws. To make that failure legible instead of a
generic binder exception, the design below adds an EXPLICIT guard: reject any Modules.{Name} config
node that has child keys (the object shape) with a message naming the incompatibility, before
GetValue ever runs. Given 3.1 (verified: zero forks/no fork exists yet, zero filters shipped
anywhere today) this caveat cannot fire on real config, but the guard turns "a future fork adds a
percentage rollout for a module flag" from a cryptic binder exception into a clear one that names
the actual constraint and the actual workaround (gate request-scoped behavior inside the module,
not the module's DI registration — module-level flags are an all-or-nothing "does this schema/DI/
routing exist" switch evaluated once at startup with no request context, which is not what
targeting/percentage filters are for anyway).

GARBAGE scalar value (e.g. a typo like "Modules.ApiKeys": "tru") is silently treated as DISABLED by

InvalidOperationException on the same malformed string. This cannot fire on any shipped file (every
value is a literal JSON true/false, verified 3.1) so it changes nothing observable today, but if it
ever does fire it fails loud instead of silently disabling a module — consistent with this
codebase's stated preference for the correct design over the silently-compatible one. Calling it
out explicitly rather than let a reviewer discover it unannounced.

=== 4. THE FIX ===

    private static bool ResolveModuleFlag(IConfiguration configuration, string moduleName)

- If a fork ever DOES want percentage/targeting/time-window semantics for a module-level flag, this
  design forecloses it (throws instead of silently misreading, per 3.3) — by design, but it is a
  real capability removal or a fork must re-add Microsoft.FeatureManagement itself. Falsifier: if
  the team has a concrete near-term plan to add such a filter to a Modules.* key, keep
  IFeatureManager instead of removing it (see 3.3's guard as the fallback-in-place option — the
  guard's own error message already tells you exactly this).
- If some other host (not Wallow.Api) ever calls AddWallowModules and expects
  `services.AddSingleton(configuration)`/`AddFeatureManagement()` to already be present in the
  passed-in `services` for some OTHER reason (not ResolveEnabledModules) — grepped, only Program.cs

  ambient IFeatureManager. New caller added later must register IConfiguration and (if it wants
  IFeatureManager for something else) FeatureManagement itself, same as any other DI service.
- If .NET's ConfigurationBinder ever changes GetValue<bool?>'s malformed-value behavior from
  "throws InvalidOperationException" to "returns null silently", the deliberate
  fail-loud-on-garbage-value improvement in 3.3 quietly degrades to today's silent-disable — low
  risk (a stable, long-shipped binder behavior), not falsifying the core equivalence claim, only
  the secondary improvement.
- Falsifier for the whole design: if `configuration.GetValue<bool?>` is ever observed disagreeing
  with `IFeatureManager.IsEnabledAsync` for any of the 5 shipped appsettings files or in any of the
   test suites in section 6 — that would mean this decompiled-source analysis missed something, and
  the fix should be reverted to keep IFeatureManager (temp-provider or not) until re-verified.

title: correct the stale ExtensionDiscovery.ManualOnly and RuntimeCompilation comments
description:
Plan: docs/plans/2026-08-04/2129-wolverine-module-registration.md — Problem 1, Phase 2.

DOCUMENTATION-ONLY. The plan's Phase 2 was DEMOTED during review from "drop
`ExtensionDiscovery.ManualOnly`" to "correct the comments". **Do not drop the flag.**

## Why demoted

`ManualOnly` governs `IWolverineExtension` AUTO-discovery, not handler discovery.
`opts.Include(extension)` is explicit registration and works fine under it. Dropping the
flag would unlock exactly one thing — letting `WolverineFx.RuntimeCompilation`
self-register — which the plan declines to take. Weighed against a macOS SIGSEGV/SIGABRT
(exit 139/134) that is refuted only by documentation and was never reproduced, the change
is not worth it.

## What IS wrong: two misleading comments

`api/src/Wallow.Api/Program.cs:180-181` currently reads:

    // Use ManualOnly to prevent Wolverine from scanning native DLLs (QuestPDF/Skia)
    // which can cause crashes on macOS (exit codes 139/134)

That describes pre-6.0 `AssemblyFinder`, which probed the bin directory at startup.
Wolverine 6.0 (GH-2902) replaced it with a compile-time source generator:
`JasperFx.SourceGenerator` emits a `JasperFx.Generated.DiscoveredExtensions` manifest per
assembly, and Wolverine reads those via the application's REFERENCE GRAPH. From
`guide/extensions.md`: "As of Wolverine 6.0 there is no runtime bin-directory assembly scan
for extensions". Wallow is on 6.21.0.

Rewrite it to say the bin-directory scan no longer exists in 6.x and that the flag is
retained for explicit control, not for the macOS crash.

`Program.cs:184-189` claims that referencing `WolverineFx.RuntimeCompilation` "does not
auto-register it here". True — but ONLY BECAUSE of `ManualOnly`. Say so, so the coupling
is not invisible to whoever next considers dropping the flag.

## Acceptance

Comments accurate; no behaviour change; `./scripts/run-tests.sh` green.

title: lint: add a wallow/* rule banning Node built-ins from packages/logger's browser entry
description:
packages/logger ships two entries: a browser core at packages/logger/src/index.ts and an app-server ingest handler at ./server. Only the server entry may touch Node built-ins; a node:fs (or node:path, node:process, ...) import reaching the browser entry breaks it in the browser.

That invariant used to be enforced by a spec that read source off disk. The spec was deleted under the no-source-tests rule (.claude/rules/TESTING.md): constraining how code is *written* is a linter's job — an AST rule fires in the editor, names the offending line, and cannot be defeated by formatting.

Add a wallow/* oxlint JS-plugin rule that bans node:* / Node built-in imports from the browser entry (and anything it transitively owns). Read packages/lint/CLAUDE.md first — it carries the config census, the rule pattern, and owns which config registers what.

Found by the 2026-08-04 documentation accuracy audit (pairs with audit findings W-H20/W-H21); see docs/plans/2026-08-04/1113-doc-accuracy-audit.md (section 6, non-doc issues found while auditing docs and deliberately not fixed in the doc pass).

## Acceptance
- A wallow/* rule fires on a node: import in packages/logger/src/index.ts and stays silent for ./server.
- A fixture covers both directions in packages/lint.
- pnpm check passes.
notes:
Shipped wallow/logger-no-node-builtins (packages/lint/src/rules/logger-no-node-builtins.ts), enabled repo-wide in the root .oxlintrc.json beside the other two self-gating rules — packages/logger has no nested config, so root enablement + a context.filename gate is the shape (the no-source-tests/module-lists-in-sync pattern).

Design: option-free; gates on the packages/logger/src/ path segment; treats every non-spec file there as browser-owned EXCEPT a three-file server allowlist (server.ts, otlp.ts, rate-limit.ts — the ./server graph per packages/logger/CLAUDE.md). Fail-safe: a new server helper needing a builtin draws a diagnostic naming the allowlist, rather than a new browser file silently shipping node:path. Built-in test is node:module's isBuiltin(), covering bare and node:-prefixed forms; three visitors (ImportDeclaration, ImportExpression, require) mirroring no-source-tests. import/no-nodejs-modules could not be the mechanism — deliberately off repo-wide for the SDK's node:crypto.

Fixture fixtures/logger-no-node-builtins/ recreates the path gate inside the fixture tree: invalid/packages/logger/src/{index.ts,log-event.ts} (5 annotated diagnostics across all import forms), valid side proves the server exemption (server.ts, rate-limit.ts with builtins, silent), the spec exemption (logger.test.ts), clean browser imports (wire.ts) and the path gate (elsewhere/src/index.ts importing node:fs, silent).

TDD: fixtures first, watched the harness fail with 'Rule logger-no-node-builtins not found in plugin wallow', then implemented to green (6/6 fixture dirs). Probe per packages/lint/CLAUDE.md: planted node:os in BOTH real entries — pnpm lint named index.ts:1 and stayed silent on server.ts; reverted.

Docs: packages/lint/CLAUDE.md census (root now enables THREE rules repo-wide; 'all six' paragraph), packages/logger/CLAUDE.md (node-builtin half of the unheld-constraint paragraph now names the rule and the allowlist-census pairing; the index-must-not-mention-server-symbols half stays unheld as before), root CLAUDE.md repo-layout row. Rationale: types:[] already fails a node:* import today but covers both entries indiscriminately and evaporates the day @types/node arrives for the server entry; the rule is entry-aware and editor-time.

pnpm check exit 0.

title: lint: add a wallow/* rule keeping packages/env's four module lists in sync
description:
packages/env maintains four parallel module lists that must stay in sync; a module added to one and missed in another silently misaddresses a Start app.

That invariant used to be enforced by a spec that read source off disk. The spec was deleted under the no-source-tests rule (.claude/rules/TESTING.md): constraining how code is *written* is a linter's job, not a test's.

Add a wallow/* oxlint JS-plugin rule that compares the four lists as AST and reports the entries missing from any of them. Read packages/lint/CLAUDE.md first — it carries the config census, the rule pattern, and owns which config registers what.

Found by the 2026-08-04 documentation accuracy audit (pairs with audit findings W-H20/W-H21); see docs/plans/2026-08-04/1113-doc-accuracy-audit.md (section 6, non-doc issues found while auditing docs and deliberately not fixed in the doc pass).

## Acceptance
- A wallow/* rule reports a module present in some lists but absent from others, naming the offending list.
- A fixture in packages/lint covers in-sync and out-of-sync cases.
- pnpm check passes.
notes: Shipped wallow/module-lists-in-sync (commit c3960012). Design: the rule anchors on a library's vite.config.ts — the one of the four lists oxlint lints — and reads package.json + tsconfig.build.json off disk (zone-dag pattern, line-comment stripping before JSON.parse). Entry keys normalize to exports subpaths (index ↔ ., <dir>/index ↔ ./<dir>, <name> ↔ ./<name>); tsconfig include is compared against entry VALUES (source paths). Skip semantics, all self-gating so root-wide enablement is safe: filename must be vite.config.ts; callee must be defineLibraryConfig; a spread/computed/non-literal entries map bails (excludes packages/ui); any * exports key skips that map (ui's ./*); exports keys are filtered to module targets .ts/.tsx/.js/.mjs (excludes ./styles.css passthroughs); an include with a glob or directory member is skipped; a missing/unparseable sibling skips that comparison. Diagnostics: entry-missing-from-list lands on the entry's own Property node; list-names-module-with-no-entry lands on the entries property. Enabled at root .oxlintrc.json beside no-source-tests — the second repo-wide rule. Verified: fixture harness green (in-sync, all four out-of-sync directions, wildcard skip, spread gate, filename gate); survey of all 11 packages found 10 in sync + ui gated out; plant-a-violation probe (removed ./request-origin from packages/env exports) drew the diagnostic at packages/env/vite.config.ts:13 naming the list, then reverted. Docs updated: lint/env/utils CLAUDE.md, root CLAUDE.md lint row, three stale vite.config comments (charter.test.ts references). Full pnpm check exit 0.

title: packages/styles is unpublished but not "private": true
description:
`packages/styles/package.json` declares `"version": "0.0.0"` and has **no** `"private": true` key, unlike every other unpublished workspace package. There is no publish workflow for it (only `sdk-publish.yml` exists, and it publishes `@bc-solutions-coder/sdk` off `sdk-v*` tags), so the package is de facto unpublishable — but nothing in the manifest says so, and `pnpm publish` from that directory would not be refused.

Two acceptable resolutions, pick one:

1. **Mark it private.** Add `"private": true` to `packages/styles/package.json`, matching `packages/config` and the rest of the unpublished set. Cheapest, and truthful about today's state.
2. **Publish it.** Give it a real version, a release-please entry in `.release-please-config.json` / `.release-please-manifest.json`, and a publish workflow. This is the larger change and only worth it if out-of-workspace consumers are meant to install `@bc-solutions-coder/styles` — which `docs/integrations/integration-cookbook.md` currently tells them they cannot.

Consequence for docs either way: `docs/integrations/integration-cookbook.md` step 1 carries an IMPORTANT callout stating the package is not installable outside a fork, and its Vite-config section explains that `wallowStyles()` is fork-only for the same reason. If option 2 is taken, both passages must be rewritten.

Source: docs accuracy audit `docs/audits/2026-08-04/0917-repo-docs-accuracy/report.md`, bead list item 6 (finding F17). Not a docs defect — F17 documents the current state correctly; this bead is the underlying config decision.
notes: Done in 6d9c1804. Took resolution 1: "private": true in packages/styles/package.json, placed after "version" like every other workspace package. docs/integrations/integration-cookbook.md's IMPORTANT callout explicitly asserted the opposite ('unlike the other workspace packages it is not marked "private": true') and is rewritten. packages/styles stays in scripts/check-exports.sh's list, which already covers seven other private packages, so pnpm check:exports is unaffected -- verified by a green pnpm check.

title: verify whether the Dockerfiles' package-build step is still needed
description:
docs/development/frontend-setup.md, in the Docker/branding section, says an app's Dockerfile must 'build the styles package before the app, e.g. pnpm --filter @bc-solutions-coder/styles build, since the app's Vite build imports the package's built dist/ output (brand asset paths), not its source'. Both apps' Dockerfiles do this for ALL packages: 'RUN pnpm --filter ./packages/* build && pnpm --filter <app> build'.

That rationale is the same one Wallow-l77c and Wallow-xzy1.1 found stale everywhere else: in-repo every @bc-solutions-coder/* exports map resolves to src/, so a Vite build reads package SOURCE. Locally an app builds with no dist present at all — verified while closing Wallow-xzy1.1 by moving all 11 packages/*/dist off disk.

NOT fixed with the others because a Docker image build is a different environment and I did not test it, and guessing is precisely the failure mode this queue exists to remove. Two things could genuinely make the image case differ:
- packages/styles' './assets' subpath and its brand-asset copying may emit files a bare source resolution does not produce (styles.css and ui's source.css are git-tracked, so those are NOT it)
- the Dockerfile comment claims 'omitting packages/config fails the package build below - not the app's', so at least one inter-package build ordering constraint is real

To settle it: docker build both app images with the 'pnpm --filter ./packages/* build' step removed. If they build and the resulting images serve a correctly branded page, drop the step and correct frontend-setup.md; if they fail, correct frontend-setup.md to state the real reason instead of the dist/-resolution one.
acceptance_criteria: Either the Dockerfiles' package-build step is removed and both images still build and serve a branded page, or it is kept and docs/development/frontend-setup.md states the actual reason it is required. Verified by a real docker build, not by reading.
notes:
VERDICT: the package-build step is NOT needed — removed from both Dockerfiles.

Experiment (real docker builds, per acceptance): edited both Dockerfiles to drop the 'pnpm --filter ./packages/* build' half of the RUN, then 'docker build -f apps/<app>/Dockerfile .' from the repo root. Both images built clean (exit 0).

Serve verification:
- wallow-auth: docker run (no env needed), GET /login -> 200, 15,953 bytes, body 10,233 chars — identical to the known-good baseline from Wallow-luni — containing 'Sign in to your account', title 'Wallow'. Built CSS (42,415 bytes) carries the theme tokens (--color-primary, oklch, --font).
- wallow-web: docker run with the 7 required BFF env vars set to dummy values (loadBffConfigFromEnv gate), GET / -> 200, 16,371 bytes, body 11,088 chars, title 'Wallow'. Built CSS (43,488 bytes) carries --color-primary.

WHY it was never needed: in-repo, every @bc-solutions-coder/* exports map resolves to the package's src/ (the publish-time swap), so the app's single vite build compiles workspace package source — styles and branding.json included — directly. Nothing resolves through dist/. The step was vestigial.

Changes: both RUN lines now build only the app; rewrote the stale 'Build all packages first' comment blocks and the COPY-block intro ('present and built' -> 'present') in both Dockerfiles; ported wallow-auth's corrected docker-workspace-copies.test.ts wording (Wallow-xg9t.1) into wallow-web's still-stale copy; corrected docs/development/frontend-setup.md 'Docker builds' section, which claimed the app's Vite build imports styles' built dist/ output — replaced with the src/-resolution fact and the verification note.

title: Remove the redundant per-tree wallow jsPlugins registrations after root registration soaks
description: Since chore/arch-tooling-adoption, the repo-root .oxlintrc.json registers @bc-solutions-coder/lint (and owns wallow/no-source-tests repo-wide); the five nested configs (apps/wallow-web, apps/wallow-auth, packages/ui, packages/forms, packages/navigation) still carry their own jsPlugins entry and workspace:* devDependency. Once the root registration has soaked, decide whether to delete the nested registrations. NOTE the inversion: packages/lint/CLAUDE.md used to say a config that registers without depending cannot load the plugin — with only the ROOT registering, the nested configs' devDependencies become the removable half, and per-tree rule ENABLEMENT/options must stay in the nested configs regardless (an oxlint override replaces options rather than merging). Keep the restated override blocks — nested-config globs are directory-relative ('The cost of nesting'). Justification: docs/plans/2026-08-02/2252-arch-tooling-adoption.md Task 12 + docs/plans/2026-08-02/2212-arch-rules-review.md §A.
notes:
SCOUT FINDINGS (recon only, no code changed).

ROOT CONFIG (.oxlintrc.json:7,20): confirmed — registers jsPlugins wallow=@bc-solutions-coder/lint, and is the ONLY place enabling wallow/no-source-tests ("error", repo-wide), with its doctrine-exemption override block at lines 381-400.

FIVE NESTED CONFIGS — each still carries a byte-identical `"jsPlugins": [{"name":"wallow","specifier":"@bc-solutions-coder/lint"}]` line, preceded by a comment claiming it is "load-bearing" because oxlint-guardrails.test.ts used to copy the root config to a temp dir where a root jsPlugins entry made it unloadable. THAT COMMENT IS STALE: verified packages/sdk/src/oxlint-guardrails.test.ts now (a) lints ad-hoc snippets with `-c <repoRoot>/.oxlintrc.json` directly against the real root file (no copy), and (b) its mirror-tree tests copy the config into `<repoRoot>/.lint-mirror/` (in-repo, resolves node_modules via walk-up), never os.tmpdir(). Neither depends on any nested config's own jsPlugins entry. The stale-comment rationale is what the bead is closing out.

Per-tree wallow/* enablement (must stay, per bead's own correct premise — oxlint overrides REPLACE options, never merge):
- apps/wallow-web/.oxlintrc.json: no-sidebar-inversion, no-source-tests, no-tinted-text, zone-dag (no per-rule options); test/story override explicitly turns OFF no-sidebar-inversion + no-tinted-text only, leaving zone-dag/no-source-tests on (commented as deliberate).
- apps/wallow-auth/.oxlintrc.json: no-hand-rolled-mutation, no-sidebar-inversion, no-source-tests, text-heading-variant(["error",{levels:{h1:false,h2:"subheading"}}]), zone-dag; plus a file-scoped override for src/shared/components/auth-layout.tsx narrowing text-heading-variant to {h2:"subheading"} only; test/story override off for no-hand-rolled-mutation/no-sidebar-inversion/text-heading-variant.
- packages/ui/.oxlintrc.json: all six, text-heading-variant(["error",{levels:{h2:"subheading"}}]) (no h1 entry — PageHeader owns it); file-scoped override src/components/drawer/drawer.styles.ts off no-sidebar-inversion; test/story override off 4 rules.
- packages/forms/.oxlintrc.json: all six, same text-heading-variant option; file-scoped override src/form/use-app-form.ts off no-hand-rolled-mutation; test/story override off 4 rules.
- packages/navigation/.oxlintrc.json: all six, same text-heading-variant option; test/story override off 4 rules (no file-scoped exemption here).

PACKAGE.JSON devDependencies: confirmed `"@bc-solutions-coder/lint": "workspace:*"` present in ALL SIX manifests (root + apps/wallow-web + apps/wallow-auth + packages/ui + packages/forms + packages/navigation). Bead's premise: only the root's devDependency is now load-bearing (jsPlugins specifier resolves from the REGISTERING config's directory); the five nested devDependency entries become the removable half alongside their jsPlugins entries.

NO OTHER REGISTRATION PATH: scripts/lint-tests.sh deliberately passes NO `-c` flag (comment explains why: an explicit config disables oxlint's nested-config lookup) so it relies entirely on whatever root+nested configs resolve per file — nothing independent to update there. packages/lint/src/fixtures.test.ts registers the plugin with its OWN synthetic config carrying an ABSOLUTE path (`join(PACKAGE_DIR,"src","index.ts")`), fully independent of both root and nested .oxlintrc.json files — it proves rule LOGIC works, not that the real configs load the plugin.

*** CRITICAL VERIFICATION GAP ***: No existing automated test proves the five nested configs' wallow/* rules actually FIRE against real source via oxlint's config resolution today. oxlint-guardrails.test.ts's "every nested oxlint config inherits the root" block only checks structural facts (extends path resolves to root; categories/plugins undefined; override globs are directory-relative) — it never asserts jsPlugins presence and never runs oxlint against real app/package source to confirm a wallow/* diagnostic fires. packages/lint/CLAUDE.md itself warns (lines 61-66): "A config that does not register the plugin lints its subtree with every wallow/* rule vacuously passing, and nothing fails" — exactly the silent-regression mode this removal risks, and nothing in the suite would catch it. Manual verification is required: before/after removing a nested jsPlugins entry, temporarily reintroduce a known violation (e.g. a bare bg-foreground in packages/ui) and confirm `pnpm lint` still reports the wallow/* diagnostic for that tree.

UNRESOLVED FACTUAL QUESTION (not answered by any doc in this repo): whether oxlint's `extends` mechanism propagates a parent config's `jsPlugins` registration down to a child config so the child's own `rules` block can reference `wallow/*` names with no jsPlugins entry of its own. The only analogous evidence is that nested configs already omit the built-in `plugins` array and `categories`, relying on `extends` for those (guardrail test enforces this and it demonstrably works for built-in rules) — but `jsPlugins` is a distinct plugin-LOADING mechanism, not a category/builtin-list, and no doc in this repo (packages/lint/CLAUDE.md, either plan doc, either guardrail test) states it inherits the same way. packages/lint/CLAUDE.md's own constraints are explicitly "measured on oxlint 1.74.0"; docs/plans/2026-08-02/2212-arch-rules-review.md §A itself says "Verify oxlint >=1.76 behaviour first; the constraint was measured on 1.74" for the root-registration change — the SAME caution applies here and has not yet been done for extends+jsPlugins specifically. Recommend checking installed oxlint version and consulting ref.tools/oxlint docs on jsPlugins + extends resolution before deleting anything, in addition to the manual pnpm-lint check above.

SOAK-TIME FLAG: docs/plans/2026-08-02/2212-arch-rules-review.md §A is marked "DONE (2026-08-03)" — i.e. root registration landed the SAME DAY this bead was created/started. The bead text says "once the root registration has soaked" but essentially zero soak time has elapsed as of this scouting pass.

knip/sherif: removing the devDependency from the five nested package.json files requires `pnpm install` (lockfile touches 5 manifests) then rerunning `pnpm lint:deps` (knip) and `pnpm lint:manifests` (sherif) to confirm no new unlisted/unused-dependency complaints. knip.json carries no oxlint-specific entry today, so this is PLAUSIBLY a non-issue but has not been empirically run/confirmed.

DOCS NEEDING UPDATES if/when removal proceeds: packages/lint/CLAUDE.md ("Where this is registered" section naming "six configs", and each per-config comment referencing the stale tmpdir rationale — replace with the extends-inheritance rationale once verified); apps/CLAUDE.md's paragraph "The plugin is registered at the repo root ... AND from the nested configs, which own per-tree enablement..." (registration language needs to become "enabled by" not "registered by" for the nested five); packages/ui/CLAUDE.md, packages/forms/CLAUDE.md, packages/navigation/CLAUDE.md each have a line "`.oxlintrc.json` here registers the wallow/* plugin and enables all six rules" — "registers" becomes inaccurate if jsPlugins is deleted from that file; reword to "enables" only. Root CLAUDE.md's packages/lint table row ("registered at the repo root ... and by five nested configs") also needs the same correction.

DO NOT TOUCH while doing this: the restated override blocks (test/story overrides, file-scoped exemptions) and each nested config's own `ignorePatterns` restatement — packages/lint/CLAUDE.md's "The cost of nesting" section is about override globs/ignorePatterns being directory-relative, which is UNRELATED to jsPlugins and must survive regardless of what happens to jsPlugins/devDependency.
DECISION: REMOVED. The five nested jsPlugins registrations and their five @bc-solutions-coder/lint devDependencies are deleted. Empirical proof, not soak time.

METHOD. Planted probe files in all five nested trees, ran the real gates BEFORE the removal, removed, ran them AFTER, and diffed the wallow/* diagnostics. Probes were plain string constants (both string-visiting rules read every Literal/TemplateElement, so no className plumbing needed) plus a <Text as=...> element for the option-carrying rule. Two negative controls were built in deliberately: a text-foreground/60 string in wallow-auth (which does NOT enable no-tinted-text) and a <Text as="h1"> in wallow-web (which does NOT enable text-heading-variant).

BEFORE (pnpm lint): 13 wallow/* diagnostics.
  apps/wallow-web       no-tinted-text, no-sidebar-inversion            (no text-heading-variant - control held)
  apps/wallow-auth      no-sidebar-inversion, text-heading-variant      (no no-tinted-text - control held)
  packages/ui           no-tinted-text, no-sidebar-inversion, text-heading-variant
  packages/forms        no-tinted-text, no-sidebar-inversion, text-heading-variant
  packages/navigation   no-tinted-text, no-sidebar-inversion, text-heading-variant
BEFORE (pnpm lint:tests): 5 no-source-tests diagnostics, one per tree.

AFTER: `diff` of the sorted diagnostic lines reports IDENTICAL for both passes - 13 and 5, same rules, same files, same line:column, same message text. Nothing stopped firing and nothing changed.

The option-carrying rule is the load-bearing part of that result. text-heading-variant fired at each tree's OWN configured levels after removal: wallow-auth reported \"<Text as=\"h1\"> is not this app's to open\" (its h1:false entry), while ui/forms/navigation reported \"must be variant=subheading\" (their h2:subheading entry). Per-tree options survive the removal intact, which is what the bead's own premise (overrides replace rather than merge) put at risk.

THE UNRESOLVED FACTUAL QUESTION IS NOW ANSWERED: oxlint's `extends` DOES propagate a parent config's jsPlugins registration to a child config, so the child's rules block can name wallow/* with no jsPlugins entry of its own. Measured on oxlint 1.74.0 (the installed version - not >=1.76). This was verified through the real resolution path, not a hoisting accident: pnpm install pruned packages/ui/node_modules/@bc-solutions-coder/ down to config, styles, testing - the `lint` symlink is GONE from all five nested node_modules trees - and the rules still fire.

SOAK-TIME CONCERN SUPERSEDED. The bead's \"once the root registration has soaked\" was a proxy for \"is root registration actually working\". That question is now answered directly by live measurement rather than by elapsed time, which is strictly stronger evidence than aging would have provided.

RISK FLAGS FROM SCOUTING, ALL CLEARED:
- Vacuous-pass silent regression: ruled out by the before/after diff above.
- knip/sherif after removing 5 devDependencies: pnpm lint:deps and pnpm lint:manifests both clean, no new complaints.
- Stale tmpdir comment in the three package configs: replaced with the extends-inheritance rationale.

BONUS FINDING (outside the bead's five trees, discovered while checking a doc claim): wallow/no-source-tests now fires REPO-WIDE, including in packages with no nested config at all. Probe planted at packages/utils/src/*.test.ts was reported by pnpm lint:tests. .claude/rules/TESTING.md still claimed the rule \"reaches every spec under the five trees that register the plugin ... Elsewhere the doctrine still holds; it is just unenforced\" - that was already false since root registration landed, and is corrected here.

WHICH PASS REPORTS WHAT: pnpm lint excludes **/*.test.*, so no-source-tests is reported ONLY by pnpm lint:tests. The other five wallow/* rules are reported by pnpm lint. Both passes were run before and after.

FILES CHANGED (13 + lockfile):
  configs (jsPlugins line deleted; ALL rule enablement, options, override blocks and ignorePatterns restatements untouched):
    apps/wallow-web/.oxlintrc.json, apps/wallow-auth/.oxlintrc.json
    packages/ui/.oxlintrc.json, packages/forms/.oxlintrc.json, packages/navigation/.oxlintrc.json
    (the three package configs also had their stale \"Registered HERE ... load-bearing ... copies the ROOT config to a temp directory\" comment replaced with the extends-inheritance rationale)
  manifests (@bc-solutions-coder/lint devDependency deleted; ROOT package.json keeps its registration AND its dependency):
    apps/wallow-web, apps/wallow-auth, packages/ui, packages/forms, packages/navigation
  pnpm-lock.yaml (regenerated by pnpm install)
  docs: packages/lint/CLAUDE.md (\"Where this is registered\" rewritten around one root registration + extends inheritance, with the empirical result recorded; the vacuous-pass warning kept but its remedy corrected to \"the extends line is load-bearing\" plus a probe recipe; the -c warning and the no-source-tests paragraph reworded), CLAUDE.md (packages/lint table row), apps/CLAUDE.md (registered-vs-enabled), packages/ui/CLAUDE.md, packages/forms/CLAUDE.md, packages/navigation/CLAUDE.md (all three: \"registers the plugin and enables\" -> \"enables\"), .claude/rules/TESTING.md (repo-wide reach, per bonus finding).

GATES: pnpm lint PASS, pnpm lint:tests PASS, pnpm lint:manifests PASS, pnpm lint:deps PASS, pnpm format:check PASS. Also ran the two specs that read these configs back: packages/sdk oxlint-guardrails.test.ts 96/96 pass (its \"every nested config inherits the root\" block is unaffected - it never asserted jsPlugins presence), packages/lint 4/4 pass.

ALL PROBE FILES DELETED - git status carries no probe debris.

NOTE FOR CLEANUP/COMMIT: git status also shows four modified files I did NOT touch - packages/navigation/src/app-nav.test.tsx, app-shell.catalog-control.test.tsx, app-shell.test.tsx, app-shell.toggle.test.tsx. Those are another agent's concurrent work in this shared checkout (TanStack Link stub changes), not part of this bead. Do not attribute them to Wallow-a0a6.

EVIDENCE SEARCH FOR A FIRED TRIGGER (i.e., a real cross-package regression that slipped past all four):
- `git log --oneline -30` and a broader `git log --all --grep` for cross-package/illegal-import/boundary/package-dag/dependency-cruiser turned up exactly one hit: 656b1eb5 "refactor(sdk): break the proxy/handlers import cycle" — but this is an INTRA-package cycle inside packages/sdk, caught by import/no-cycle itself (mechanism 4 working as designed), not a cross-package edge that evaded glob bans/sherif/knip/no-cycle. - `bd list` (open + closed) has no bead recording a cross-package dependency-direction regression. The two open beads referencing this bead (Wallow-cph8) and a related one (Wallow-vsi3.1, a billing-module DB boundary spike) are unrelated to a JS/TS import-graph incident.
- No evidence any team member has hit a case where a package imported something disallowed by role/direction (e.g. packages/utils importing react, or packages/env reaching into an app) that the existing four mechanisms failed to catch. The bottom-of-graph purity override (lines 240-327) explicitly already bans exactly this class via glob patterns, and it is enforced today.

title: reorder the 4 defective router-Link test stubs in packages/navigation (latent, defense-in-depth)
description:
packages/navigation's browser-project specs mock @tanstack/react-router's `Link`. Two shapes of that mock exist:

- SAFE shape (9 files: app-nav.catalog/contrast/destinations/modes/sidebar-surface.test.tsx, app-shell.mobile/responsive/ssr-flash.test.tsx, plus app-nav.theme which has no onClick at all): the stub destructures `onClick` OUT of `{...rest}` and wraps it, so `event.preventDefault()` always fires first and `rest` can no longer carry a conflicting `onClick`. Reference/copy shape: app-shell.mobile.test.tsx:17-40 (`LinkStubProps`).
- DEFECTIVE shape (4 files, listed below): the stub's own `onClick` (or nothing at all) is declared BEFORE `{...rest}` in the JSX. Per plain JSX object-literal semantics, a later spread's `onClick` wins over an earlier-declared one — so if `rest.onClick` exists, it silently clobbers the local `preventDefault()` (or, for the one file with no local handler at all, there was never a `preventDefault` to begin with).

The 4 defective files, each at lines 11-32 unless noted:

- packages/navigation/src/app-shell.toggle.test.tsx:11-32
- packages/navigation/src/app-shell.test.tsx:11-32
- packages/navigation/src/app-shell.catalog-control.test.tsx:11-32
- packages/navigation/src/app-nav.test.tsx:11-26 (this one has no local `onClick`/`preventDefault` at all — bare `<a href={to} {...rest}>`)

## Why this exists, and why it clobbers

`AppNav` renders each destination as `NavigationMenu.Link render={<Link ... />}` (app-nav.tsx:117), with `NavItem`'s `onClick={props.onNavigate}` (app-nav.tsx:122). Base UI's `mergeProps` (confirmed by reading the installed package, `node_modules/.pnpm/@base-ui+react@1.6.0.../merge-props/mergeProps.mjs`) merges that computed `onClick` into a single function and hands it to the render element (the mocked `Link`) as one ordinary `onClick` prop in `...rest`. So on a defective stub, clicking the rendered anchor CAN fire Base UI's merged handler instead of the stub's own `preventDefault`, letting a real navigation reach `location`/the DOM.

## THIS IS LATENT, NOT THE CAUSE OF ANYTHING OBSERVED — say this plainly, do not re-litigate it

This defect was found and fully diagnosed during the investigation of Wallow-tkyq (packages/navigation's real navigation-escape leak, now fixed by a central Navigation-API guard in packages/navigation/vitest.setup.ts). The scout who found this mechanism ALSO proved, by grepping every `userEvent.click`/keyboard-activation across all 13 nav spec files, that **none of the 4 defective-stub files ever clicks a nav-destination `Link`**:

- app-shell.toggle.test.tsx: all 5 clicks target `dashboard-nav-toggle`, a plain `<button>`.
- app-shell.test.tsx / app-shell.catalog-control.test.tsx / app-nav.test.tsx: no `Link` clicks either.
- The ONLY spec in the package that clicks a real nav-destination Link is app-shell.mobile.test.tsx:139 — and that file already has the SAFE stub shape.

A live reproduction during Wallow-tkyq's independent verification also confirmed the actual leak came from a toggle-button click, not a Link click. So this ordering bug is real and worth fixing as defense-in-depth, but it did NOT cause the Wallow-tkyq leak and must not be cited as though it did.

## Design

Reorder each of the 4 files' stub so `onClick` is destructured out of `{...rest}` and wrapped before render — the same shape app-shell.mobile.test.tsx:17-40 already uses. Copy that shape exactly rather than inventing a new one, so all router-Link stubs in the package converge on one pattern.

Optional, not required for acceptance: hoist the now-identical stub into a shared fixture (e.g. a `router-link.fixture.tsx` next to shell.fixtures.tsx, imported the way `shell.fixtures.tsx` already is: `import { ... } from "./shell.fixtures"`). This was verified safe during Wallow-tkyq: shell.fixtures.tsx is unexported from packages/navigation/src/index.ts, and packages/navigation/CLAUDE.md's "one entry" / "no ui barrel" rules govern the package's own PUBLIC subpath surface, not sibling spec/fixture imports inside src/. Do the hoist only if it does not complicate the reorder itself.

PLAN: docs/plans/2026-08-02/1744-no-source-tests-design.md (Phase 1's parent epic).
design: Reorder onClick destructuring to occur before {...rest} spread in all 4 files, matching app-shell.mobile.test.tsx:17-40's LinkStubProps shape. Do not touch app-shell.mobile.test.tsx or any of the 9 already-safe stubs. Do not attempt to fix or re-diagnose the Wallow-tkyq navigation-escape leak here — that is closed and unrelated.
acceptance_criteria:
1. All 4 files (app-shell.toggle.test.tsx, app-shell.test.tsx, app-shell.catalog-control.test.tsx, app-nav.test.tsx) have their router-Link stub reordered so a spread `onClick` in `...rest` can no longer silently override the local `preventDefault()`.
2. `cd packages/navigation && pnpm test` stays fully green (17 files / 136 tests, matching current baseline exactly — no test count regression).
3. `pnpm lint`, `pnpm lint:tests`, `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm format:check` all clean for the touched files.
4. The bead's own notes/close reason state explicitly that this fix is defense-in-depth and was NOT the cause of any previously-observed navigation-escape failure.
notes:
DEFERRED OUT OF EPIC Wallow-xg9t by coordinator decision, 2026-08-02, with the user's agreement. Reparented to the backlog so the epic is not held open by it.

Rationale: the scout that diagnosed Wallow-tkyq established this stub-ordering defect is LATENT — real, confirmed against Base UI's mergeProps source, but NOT what fired the observed navigation leak. It is defense-in-depth hygiene. The epic Wallow-xg9t is about guards that do not guard; this is a guard that does not currently need to fire. Wallow-xg9t.3 (wiring the navigation-escape guard into the other four browser projects) was kept in the epic because it closes a live silent-failure hole across four projects, which IS the epic's thesis.

Still worth doing. Nothing about the deferral says otherwise.
GREEN: all 4 defective router-Link stubs reordered to the SAFE shape.

FILES (all under packages/navigation/src/):
- app-shell.toggle.test.tsx — added a named `LinkStubProps` type alias above the vi.mock; Link now destructures `onClick` out of `...rest` and calls it AFTER `event.preventDefault()` inside the anchor's own handler. Previously the local preventDefault handler was declared before `{...rest}`, so a spread onClick would win.
- app-shell.test.tsx — same reorder, same alias.
- app-shell.catalog-control.test.tsx — same reorder, same alias; kept the file's existing comment about `activeProps` being dropped so it cannot land on a DOM attribute.
- app-nav.test.tsx — this one had NO local handler at all (bare `<a href={to} {...rest}>`), so it gained the full suppressing handler plus the alias, and `MouseEvent` was added to the existing `import type { ReactNode } from "react"`.

All four now use the identical shape copied verbatim from app-shell.mobile.test.tsx:17-40 — `Link: ({ to, children, activeProps: _activeProps, onClick, ...rest }: LinkStubProps)` rendering an anchor whose onClick calls `event.preventDefault()` then `onClick?.(event)`, with `{...rest}` last. Each file's stub comment was extended one sentence to say why onClick is destructured out. No new shape was invented.

OUT OF SCOPE, NOT TOUCHED: app-shell.mobile.test.tsx and the 9 already-safe stubs are unmodified. `git status` shows exactly the 4 files above and nothing else. The optional shared-fixture hoist (router-link.fixture.tsx) was deliberately SKIPPED per coordinator instruction — the bead marks it optional and the minimal reorder was wanted.

TEST_STATUS=pass. `cd packages/navigation && pnpm test` → 17 test files passed (17), 136 tests passed (136). Exactly the stated baseline; no count regression, no skips.

GATES (all from repo root, all exit 0):
- pnpm lint → clean (source pass; specs are excluded here by design)
- pnpm lint:tests → clean, 352 test/story files linted with the vitest plugin
- pnpm --filter @bc-solutions-coder/navigation typecheck → clean (tsc --noEmit, no output)
- pnpm format:check → clean (oxfmt needed no rewrites; the single-line destructure fits the print width)

ACCEPTANCE CRITERION 4 — stated explicitly: **this change is defense-in-depth only. It was NOT the cause of any previously observed navigation-escape failure.** The Wallow-tkyq leak was reproduced live and came from a toggle-BUTTON click, and the guard that now catches such escapes lives in packages/navigation/vitest.setup.ts. None of these 4 files ever clicks a nav-destination Link — the only spec in the package that does is app-shell.mobile.test.tsx:139, which already had the safe stub. The ordering defect was real (confirmed against Base UI's mergeProps, which collapses NavItem's onNavigate into one ordinary onClick prop inside ...rest) but latent: there was no live path by which it could fire. This fix removes the latent hazard and converges every router-Link stub in the package on one pattern; it does not fix, and must not be cited as fixing, any observed failure.

ISSUES=none. Not committed and bead not closed — session cleanup owns both.
VERIFY: ✓ criterion 1 (all 4 files reordered) — git diff shows app-shell.toggle.test.tsx, app-shell.test.tsx, app-shell.catalog-control.test.tsx, app-nav.test.tsx each add a LinkStubProps type alias, destructure onClick out of {...rest}, and call event.preventDefault() then onClick?.(event) inside the anchor's own handler, with {...rest} spread last — byte-identical shape to app-shell.mobile.test.tsx:17-40 (confirmed by diffing both). app-nav.test.tsx correctly gained the full handler plus the MouseEvent import (it had none before). app-shell.mobile.test.tsx and the 9 other safe stubs untouched. ✓ criterion 3 — the 4-file diff itself is clean (no as any, no TODOs, matches surrounding style). ✓ criterion 4 — bead note states explicitly and correctly that this is defense-in-depth, not the cause of any observed failure, citing the Wallow-tkyq toggle-button root cause and the per-file click-target audit. ~ criterion 2 — could NOT get a clean 17-file/136-test pnpm test run in packages/navigation: the shared working tree currently also has untracked packages/navigation/src/wallow-lint-probe.{test.ts,tsx} plus modified .oxlintrc.json/package.json (wallow plugin moved to root-level registration) — confirmed via git diff this is UNRELATED concurrent work from a different in-flight task in this session, not part of xg9t.2's diff. Full pnpm test in navigation shows 18 files/137 tests with the 1 extra probe file failing (by design — it deliberately reads a nonexistent path). Isolated run of exactly the 5 relevant Link-stub specs (the 4 changed + app-shell.mobile.test.tsx as reference) passes clean: 5 files, 44 tests, 0 failures, 0 regressions — confirms the reorder introduces no behavioral break. Could not reproduce the implementer's stated 17/136 baseline right now purely because of this contamination, not because of anything in this bead's diff. tests=pass (isolated 44/44); full-suite baseline unverifiable until the concurrent lint-registration work in this package settles. issues=workspace contamination from a concurrent unrelated task, not an implementation defect. verdict=CLOSE
close_reason: 4 router-Link stubs reordered to the safe LinkStubProps shape; 17 files/136 tests baseline held. Defense-in-depth only — this defect was latent and NOT the cause of any previously observed navigation-escape failure.

title: reconcile the Modules.* feature-flag block with the modules that actually exist
description:
The module feature-flag configuration declares keys nothing reads, names a module that does not
exist, and exists twice — once in a block with readers and once in a block with none. The drift is
mirrored into `appsettings.Production.json`.

## Verified state

`api/src/Wallow.Api/appsettings.json` `FeatureManagement` declares EIGHT keys: `Modules.Branding`,
`Modules.Identity`, `Modules.Storage`, `Modules.Notifications`, `Modules.Announcements`,
`Modules.Configuration`, `Modules.Inquiries`, `Modules.ApiKeys`.

`WallowModules.cs` reads SIX of them — Branding, Notifications, Announcements, Storage, ApiKeys,
Inquiries. Two are dead:

- **`Modules.Configuration`** names a module that does not exist. There is no Configuration module
  under `api/src/Modules/` and no reader anywhere. Setting it to `false` does nothing.
- **`Modules.Identity`** has no reader either — `WallowModules.cs:45-46` registers Identity
  unconditionally, with a comment saying so ("required platform dependency — always registered, not
  behind a feature flag"). Setting it to `false` does not disable Identity; it silently does
  nothing, which is worse than not offering the knob.

**A second, entirely unread copy.** The same file carries a `Wallow:Modules` block — `Identity`,
`Notifications`, `Announcements`, `Storage`, `Configuration`, `Inquiries`, `ApiKeys` — with the same
phantom `Configuration` entry and the same drift. Grepping `api/src` for a reader of `Wallow:Modules`
returns nothing. It is a duplicate of the `FeatureManagement` block that no code has ever consulted,
and the two can disagree without anything noticing.

**Mirrored into production.** `appsettings.Production.json` reproduces the full `FeatureManagement`
block, phantom key included. `appsettings.Development.json` overrides only `Modules.ApiKeys`.

## What to do

Delete `Modules.Configuration` everywhere. Delete `Modules.Identity` from the flag block, or make
`WallowModules.cs` actually honour it — the comment says the former is intended, so take that unless
there is a reason not to. Delete the unread `Wallow:Modules` block outright, or make one of the two
the single source and the other gone; do not leave both. Apply the same result to
`appsettings.Production.json` so the two files stop drifting apart.

Then guard it: an architecture test asserting that every declared `Modules.*` key has a reader and
every read key is declared. Without that, the block drifts again the next time a module is added or
removed. Note that `ModuleToggleTests` currently hardcodes `Modules.Identity` among the keys it
sets, so it asserts a toggle that does nothing — `Wallow-vmns.7` is deriving those lists and the two
beads should agree on what the key set is.

`appsettings*.json` is `merge=ours` in `.gitattributes`, so a fork's copies do not inherit this fix
automatically. Say so in the commit.
acceptance_criteria: Every Modules.* key declared in appsettings.json has a reader in WallowModules.cs and every key WallowModules.cs reads is declared — Modules.Configuration is gone, and Modules.Identity is either gone or honoured. Exactly one modules block survives in appsettings.json; the unread Wallow:Modules duplicate is gone. appsettings.Production.json matches. An architecture test fails if a declared key gains no reader or a read key is undeclared. ./scripts/run-tests.sh is green and the API starts with every module enabled and with each optional module disabled in turn.

title: delete the phantom Billing, Communications and Delivery modules from repo docs and contracts
description:
The repo's own documentation and integration-event contracts describe a **Billing** module and a
**Communications** module. Neither exists. There are seven modules under `api/src/Modules/` —
Identity, Storage, Notifications, Announcements, Inquiries, ApiKeys, Branding — and zero Stripe
references anywhere in `api/src`. The only tracked billing-named file in the repo is
`FakeBillingController.cs`.

This matters because the next reader believes the docs. `Wallow-vsi3`'s ground truth — that Billing
has to be built from nothing — is contradicted by four documents that read as though it already
ships.

## Verified sites

**Phantom Billing:**
- `api/src/Shared/README.md` — the integration-event catalog lists a **Billing** section
  (`InvoiceCreatedEvent`, `InvoicePaidEvent`, `InvoiceOverdueEvent`, `PaymentReceivedEvent`), and
  the read-only-interface list names `IInvoiceQueryService`, `ISubscriptionQueryService`,
  `IRevenueReportService` under Billing.
- `api/src/Wallow.Api/README.md` — the Module Wiring section says `WallowModules.cs` "calls each
  module's extension method (e.g., `AddIdentityModule()`, `AddBillingModule()`)". There is no
  `AddBillingModule`.
- `Shared.Contracts/Identity/Events/OrganizationCreatedEvent.cs:6` — `Consumers: Billing (setup org
  billing), Communications (org setup)`.

**Phantom Communications** — wider than a single file. `Communications` is named as the consumer in
the XML doc comment of TEN integration events under `Shared.Contracts/Identity/Events/`:
`OrganizationCreatedEvent`, `OrganizationMemberAddedEvent`, `OrganizationMemberRemovedEvent`,
`UserRegisteredEvent`, `UserRoleChangedEvent`, `InvitationCreatedEvent`, `MagicLinkRequestedEvent`,
`OtpCodeRequestedEvent`, `EmailVerificationRequestedEvent`, `EmailVerifiedEvent`. The actual
consumer of every one of them is **Notifications**. `ApiScopes.cs:31` carries a `// Communications`
section comment. `api/src/Shared/README.md` also lists a phantom **Delivery** module
(`EmailSentEvent`).

## One judgement call inside this bead

`Shared.Contracts` contains a real namespace `Wallow.Shared.Contracts.Communications.Email`
(`IEmailService.cs`). Decide whether that name is a vestige of the phantom module — in which case
rename it to match Notifications — or a deliberate contract-layer name, in which case leave it and
make the doc comments say `Notifications` rather than `Communications` so the two stop looking like
the same thing. Record the decision in the bead; do not leave it implicit in the diff. Renaming is
free here: pre-release, no consumers.

## Not this bead

`Wallow-75pg` deletes 14 phantom TYPES from `api/src/Shared/README.md` and
`api/src/Modules/Notifications/README.md`, including the Metering section on an adjacent line of the
same file. Different scope — phantom types vs phantom modules — but the same two files. Sweep them
together in one pass; do not merge the beads.
acceptance_criteria: Grepping api/src for 'Billing', 'Communications' and 'Delivery' returns no statement that any of them is an existing module: the Billing event and query-interface entries and the Delivery entry are gone from api/src/Shared/README.md, AddBillingModule() is gone from api/src/Wallow.Api/README.md, and every 'Consumers: Communications' doc comment under Shared.Contracts names Notifications instead. The Wallow.Shared.Contracts.Communications.Email namespace has been either renamed or explicitly kept, with the reason recorded on this bead. Any surviving mention of Billing is unambiguously forward-looking and points at Wallow-vsi3. ./scripts/run-tests.sh is green.
