# Membership dashboard screens (multi-org membership, plan task 6.7)

Epic bead: `Wallow-yp3e.3`. Parent epic: `Wallow-yp3e`. Branch `feat/multi-org-membership`.

The membership lifecycle landed on the backend across plan phases 1–6.5 and has **no operator
surface**. This plan builds three screens in `apps/wallow-web`:

1. **Pending access requests** — approve / deny the people waiting on a `Pending` membership.
2. **Outstanding invitations** — list and revoke the invitations already issued.
3. **Member role management** — grant and remove a role on an existing member.

It is written to be executed without reading
`docs/plans/2026-07-31/1954-multi-org-membership-implementation.md`. Everything below is
grounded in files opened on this branch at commit `137f9600`; every line number is from that
commit.

---

## 0. Hard dependency: the OpenAPI snapshot is stale

**Nothing in sections 3–5 can be written until `Wallow-yp3e.2` lands.**
`packages/sdk/openapi/v1.json` predates Phase 6. It still describes
`GET /v1/identity/organizations/mine` (operationId `OrganizationsGetMyOrganizations`) and
contains **none** of `members/pending`, `approve`, `deny`, `denial`, `suspend`, `reinstate`,
`leave`, or `me/organizations`. The generated client mirrors that: `packages/sdk/src/generated/
@tanstack/react-query.gen.ts:1072` still exports `organizationsGetMyOrganizationsQueryKey`.

Regeneration is the documented command in `packages/sdk/CLAUDE.md`:

```bash
WALLOW_OPENAPI_URL=http://localhost:5001/openapi/v1.json \
  pnpm --filter @bc-solutions-coder/sdk exec tsx scripts/generate.ts
```

Operation ids are mechanical:
`api/src/Wallow.Api/Extensions/ServiceCollectionExtensions.cs:337` sets
`operation.OperationId = $"{descriptor.ControllerName}{descriptor.MethodInfo.Name}"`, and
hey-api camel-cases that into `{operation}Options` / `{operation}QueryKey` /
`{operation}Mutation`.

### Already generated (verified present today)

| Symbol | Line in `react-query.gen.ts` |
| --- | --- |
| `organizationsGetMembersQueryKey` / `…Options` | 1029 / 1034 |
| `organizationsAddMemberMutation` | 1047 |
| `organizationsRemoveMemberMutation` | 1061 |
| `organizationsGetByIdOptions` | 1019 |
| `invitationsGetByTenantQueryKey` / `…Options` | 799 / 801 |
| `invitationsCreateMutation` | 811 |
| `invitationsRevokeMutation` | 822 |
| `usersAssignRoleMutation` | 1400 |
| `usersRemoveRoleMutation` | 1415 |
| `usersGetUsersOptions` | 1311 |
| `rolesGetRolesQueryKey` / `…Options` | 1204 / 1209 |

### Predicted after regeneration — **verify, do not trust**

`organizationsGetPendingMembersOptions` / `…QueryKey`, `organizationsApproveMemberMutation`,
`organizationsDenyMemberMutation`, `organizationsClearDenialMutation`,
`organizationsSuspendMemberMutation`, `organizationsReinstateMemberMutation`,
`organizationsLeaveMutation`, `meGetOrganizationsOptions` / `…QueryKey`.

`organizationsGetMyOrganizations*` **disappears** (the endpoint moved to `MeController`). A
repo-wide grep found no app or package consumer of it, so the rename costs nothing — but re-grep
before assuming.

The first act of any screen bead is: open the regenerated
`packages/sdk/src/generated/@tanstack/react-query.gen.ts`, read the real exported names, and use
those. A predicted name spelled into an import is a typecheck failure at best and a silently
wrong endpoint at worst.

### Query-key tags

`createQueryKey(..., ['Organizations'])` — the third argument is the tag the curated predicate
`queriesWithTag` matches. Observed tags: `Organizations`, `Invitations`, `Users`, `Roles`.
`MeController` carries `[Tags("Me")]` (`MeController.cs:19`), so `meGetOrganizations` will be
tagged **`Me`**, not `Organizations`. A sweep of `queriesWithTag("Organizations")` will **not**
touch it.

---

## 1. The real backend surface

All paths below are relative to the API root; the browser reaches them through the BFF proxy at
`/api/...` (see the harness assertions in
`apps/wallow-web/src/features/organizations/components/MemberList.test.tsx:100`, which expects
`/api/v1/identity/organizations/o1/members`).

### 1.1 `OrganizationsController` — `api/src/Modules/Identity/Wallow.Identity.Api/Controllers/OrganizationsController.cs`

| Line | Verb + path | Permission | Request | Response |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 100–110 | `GET  /v1/identity/organizations/{id}/members` | `OrganizationsRead` | — | `IReadOnlyList<UserDto>` |
| 115–128 | `POST /v1/identity/organizations/{id}/members` | `OrganizationsManageMembers` | `{ userId, role }` | 204 |
| 133–146 | `DELETE /v1/identity/organizations/{id}/members/{userId}` | `OrganizationsManageMembers` | — | 204 |
| 151–163 | `GET  /v1/identity/organizations/{id}/members/pending` | `OrganizationsManageMembers` | — | `IReadOnlyList<PendingMembershipDto>` |
| 168–182 | `POST /v1/identity/organizations/{id}/members/{userId}/approve` | `OrganizationsManageMembers` | — | 204 / 404 / 422 |
| 187–201 | `POST /v1/identity/organizations/{id}/members/{userId}/deny` | `OrganizationsManageMembers` | — | 204 / 404 / 422 |
| 206–220 | `DELETE /v1/identity/organizations/{id}/members/{userId}/denial` | `OrganizationsManageMembers` | — | 204 / 404 / 422 |
| 226–240 | `POST /v1/identity/organizations/{id}/members/{userId}/suspend` | `OrganizationsManageMembers` | — | 204 / 404 / 422 |
| 245–259 | `POST /v1/identity/organizations/{id}/members/{userId}/reinstate` | `OrganizationsManageMembers` | — | 204 / 404 / 422 |
| 270–277 | `POST /v1/identity/organizations/{id}/leave` | **none** | — | 204 |
| 450–467 | `PUT  /v1/identity/organizations/{id}/enrollment` | `OrganizationsUpdate` | enrollment policy | 204 |

Note `ClearDenial` is **DELETE**, not POST — it is the only membership-review verb that is not
POST, and the generated mutation will carry that method.

`Leave` (270–277) deliberately carries no `[HasPermission]` and no access-policy check: it is the
one endpoint a plain member may call against their own membership.

**`CanAddressOrganizationAsync` (38–47)** gates every other route: the caller's own tenant, or a
global admin, or a per-org permission.

**`GetAll` (69–79) returns at most one row.** Line 76–78 filters the service result down to the
caller's own tenant:

```csharp
IReadOnlyList<OrganizationDto> filtered = orgs.Where(o => o.Id == tenantId).ToList();
```

This matters in section 5.

### 1.2 `MeController` — `api/src/Modules/Identity/Wallow.Identity.Api/Controllers/MeController.cs`

- `[Tags("Me")]` at line 19.
- `GetOrganizations` at 34–40 → `GET /v1/identity/me/organizations`, **no permission attribute**,
  returns `IReadOnlyList<MyOrganizationDto>`.

### 1.3 `InvitationsController` — same directory

| Line | Verb + path | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 26–39 | `POST /v1/identity/invitations` | create |
| 41–52 | `GET  /v1/identity/invitations?skip=&take=` | **takes no organization id** |
| 54–64 | `DELETE /v1/identity/invitations/{id}` | revoke |
| 97–106 | `MapToResponse` | the DTO projection |

`GetByTenant` reads the ambient tenant at line 48 (`tenantContext.TenantId.Value`). There is no
org-id parameter and no way to ask for another organization's invitations. **The invitations
screen therefore cannot be org-parameterised** — see section 4.

### 1.4 `UsersController` / `RolesController`

- `UsersController.AssignRole` (151–181): `POST /v1/identity/users/{userId}/roles`. Rejects the
  reserved global-admin role name. Writes `tenantContext.TenantId.Value` at line **179**.
- `UsersController.RemoveRole` (187–200): `DELETE /v1/identity/users/{userId}/roles/{roleName}`.
  Same ambient tenant at line **198**.
- `UsersController.UserBelongsToTenantAsync` (216–220).
- `RolesController.GetRoles` (27–34): `GET /v1/identity/roles` → `[{ Name }]`.

**Both role writes ignore any organization id and apply to the caller's own tenant.** This is a
correctness trap, handled in section 5.

### 1.5 DTO shapes (exact records)

```csharp
PendingMembershipDto(Guid UserId, string Email, string FirstName, string LastName,
                     DateTimeOffset? RequestedAt)
MyOrganizationDto(Guid OrganizationId, string Name, string Slug, bool IsOwner)
UserDto(Guid Id, string Email, string FirstName, string LastName, bool Enabled,
        IReadOnlyList<string> Roles)
InvitationResponse(Guid Id, string Email, string Status, DateTimeOffset ExpiresAt,
                   DateTimeOffset CreatedAt, Guid? AcceptedByUserId)
OrganizationDto(Guid Id, string Name, string? Domain, int MemberCount)
```

`RequestedAt` is **nullable** — the pending list must render a fallback, and the service sorts
nulls last (`MembershipReviewService.cs:48`,
`OrderBy(m => m.RequestedAt ?? DateTimeOffset.MaxValue)`).

### 1.6 Error contract

`api/src/Wallow.Api/Middleware/GlobalExceptionHandler.cs` maps `BusinessRuleException` → **422**
(lines 67–70) and puts the machine code in `problemDetails.Extensions["code"]` (111–115) — never
a top-level `code`.

Codes the three screens can actually receive:

| Code | Thrown at | Means |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Identity.MemberNotFound` | `MembershipReviewService.cs:180-182` | no membership row for that user in that org |
| `Identity.MembershipNotDenied` | `MembershipReviewService.cs:104-106` | `clearDenial` on a non-denied membership |
| `Identity.LastOwner` | `LastOwnerGuard.cs:63-64` | suspend/leave would leave the org ownerless |

A screen narrows structurally — `error.status === 422` — never with `instanceof WallowError`;
`WallowError` lives on the SDK's `./server` entry only and a browser screen cannot import it
(`.claude/rules/TESTING.md`).

---

## 2. Route layout — the decision, and why

`apps/wallow-web/src/app/routes/dashboard/organizations/` currently holds four files:
`index.tsx`, `$orgId.tsx`, and their two specs. There is **no** `organizations.tsx` and no
`organizations/route.tsx`, and `routeTree.gen.ts:90-97` shows both routes attaching straight to
the `/dashboard` layout. That is the grounded fact this plan turns on: **a route directory with
no `route.tsx` creates path nesting and no layout component.**

`$orgId.tsx` renders `<OrganizationDetail>` inside a `PageContainer` and has **no `<Outlet/>`**
(`$orgId.tsx:20-27`). Adding a `$orgId/` directory *while `$orgId.tsx` still exists* would
promote `$orgId.tsx` to the layout for its children and blank every child page.

**Decision: convert to the directory form.** Move
`organizations/$orgId.tsx` → `organizations/$orgId/index.tsx`, and add siblings inside that
directory. No `$orgId/route.tsx` is created.

Rejected alternative: the trailing-underscore un-nesting convention
(`$orgId_.requests.tsx`). It is real — the installed generator strips a trailing `_` from the
path at `@tanstack+router-generator@1.167.21/dist/esm/utils.js:320` — but it has **zero precedent
anywhere in this repo**, and the directory form needs no convention at all.

### What the move touches

- `organizations/$orgId.tsx` → `organizations/$orgId/index.tsx`. The `createFileRoute` id
  becomes `"/dashboard/organizations/$orgId/"` (trailing slash), matching how
  `organizations/index.tsx:40` spells `"/dashboard/organizations/"`.
- `organizations/$orgId.test.tsx` → `organizations/$orgId/index.test.tsx`, and its
  `describe`/path assertions updated.
- `organizations/__screenshots__/$orgId.restyle.test.tsx/` → the matching path under
  `organizations/$orgId/__screenshots__/`.
- **`apps/wallow-web/src/app/routes/dashboard/page-shell.test.ts`** — a hand-kept list of
  dashboard page files at lines 27–35 (`PAGE_FILES`) and 42–48 (`TITLED_PAGE_FILES`). Change
  `"organizations/$orgId.tsx"` → `"organizations/$orgId/index.tsx"` and **add every new page
  file**. A page that is not in `PAGE_FILES` is silently exempt from the "width comes from
  `PageContainer`" and "no hand-rolled `<h1>`" invariants.
- **Existing `<Link to="/dashboard/organizations/$orgId">` call sites keep working.**
  `routeTree.gen.ts:131` shows index routes lose their trailing slash in `FileRoutesByTo`, which
  is the map `to` is typed against. `OrganizationList.tsx` needs no edit.

### New route files

| File | `createFileRoute` id | Screen |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `organizations/$orgId/index.tsx` | `/dashboard/organizations/$orgId/` | existing detail (moved) |
| `organizations/$orgId/requests.tsx` | `/dashboard/organizations/$orgId/requests` | pending access requests |
| `organizations/$orgId/members.tsx` | `/dashboard/organizations/$orgId/members` | member role management |
| `organizations/invitations.tsx` | `/dashboard/organizations/invitations` | outstanding invitations |

Invitations sits **outside** `$orgId/` on purpose: the endpoint is ambient-tenant scoped
(section 1.3), so an `$orgId` in its URL would be a lie.

### Route shape

Copy `organizations/$orgId.tsx:29-40` verbatim in shape — an authored `createFileRoute` with a
`loader` that prefetches through the router context:

```tsx
export const Route = createFileRoute("/dashboard/organizations/$orgId/requests")({
  loader: ({ context, params }) =>
    context.queryClient.ensureQueryData(
      organizationsGetPendingMembersOptions({
        client: context.sdk.client,
        path: { id: params.orgId },
      }),
    ),
  component: PendingRequestsPage,
});
```

The auth gate is inherited: `apps/wallow-web/src/app/routes/dashboard/route.tsx` runs
`ensureCurrentUser` in `beforeLoad` and puts `requireAuth` / `isAdmin` on context. New pages add
no gate of their own.

### Navigation

`apps/wallow-web/src/shared/components/dashboard-destinations.ts:27-38` is the nav manifest.
`id` is the testid suffix under the shell's `dashboard` prefix, and `requires: { role: ADMIN_ROLE }`
(`ADMIN_ROLE = "Admin"`, line 25) is the admin gate. Add **one** entry, for invitations:

```ts
{ id: "nav-invitations", to: "/dashboard/organizations/invitations", label: "Invitations",
  icon: MailPlus, requires: { role: ADMIN_ROLE } },
```

The two `$orgId`-scoped screens are reached by in-page links from the org detail page, not from
the global rail — the rail cannot supply an `orgId`.

---

## 3. Screen 1 — pending access requests

**Route:** `apps/wallow-web/src/app/routes/dashboard/organizations/$orgId/requests.tsx`
**Feature component:** `apps/wallow-web/src/features/organizations/components/PendingRequestList.tsx`

The template to copy, almost line for line, is
`apps/wallow-web/src/features/organizations/components/MemberList.tsx` (447 lines). Read it
first; it already demonstrates every pattern this screen needs.

### Data

```tsx
const { sdk } = useRouteContext({ from: "__root__" });          // MemberList.tsx:91
const queryClient = useQueryClient();                            // MemberList.tsx:92
const { data, isPending, isError, error } = useQuery(
  organizationsGetPendingMembersOptions({ client: sdk.client, path: { id: orgId } }),
);
```

Invalidation uses the curated predicate, exactly as `MemberList.tsx:85-87` does:

```tsx
function pendingOfOperation(client: WallowSdk["client"], orgId: string) {
  return queriesForOperation(
    organizationsGetPendingMembersQueryKey({ client, path: { id: orgId } }),
  );
}
```

Approving also changes the **active roster**, so `onSuccess` must sweep **both** the pending
operation and `organizationsGetMembersQueryKey` (via a second `queriesForOperation`). Denying
sweeps pending only — a denied membership appears in no list at all today (section 7).

### Mutations

Both are plain `useMutation` over the generated factory, in the `MemberList.tsx:96-100` shape:

```tsx
const approve = useMutation({
  ...organizationsApproveMemberMutation({ client: sdk.client }),
  onSuccess: () => { void queryClient.invalidateQueries(pendingOfOperation(sdk.client, orgId)); },
});
```

There is no form here — approve and deny are parameterless POSTs keyed by the row. Do **not**
route them through `useAppForm`; `useAppForm` exists for a form with fields
(`packages/forms/CLAUDE.md`).

### Render

`PendingMembershipDto` gives `email`, `firstName`, `lastName`, `requestedAt`. Render name +
email + a relative or absolute `requestedAt`, with a fallback for `null`.

Testids (kebab, `{page}-{element}`, per `.claude/rules/E2E.md`):
`organization-pending-requests-heading`, `organization-pending-requests-table`,
`organization-pending-request-item`, `organization-pending-request-approve`,
`organization-pending-request-deny`, `organization-pending-requests-empty`,
`organization-pending-requests-loading`, `organization-pending-requests-error`.

The error branch is the canonical one from
`OrganizationDetail.tsx:335` — `if (isError && data === undefined)`, so a background refetch
failure does not blank a list that already rendered. `MemberList.tsx:155` says the same thing
with `members === undefined`.

### Spec

`PendingRequestList.test.tsx`, modelled on `MemberList.test.tsx` (144 lines). Cover:

- roster renders one `-item` per DTO;
- empty state, no rows;
- loading state via `harness.pending()`;
- approve POSTs `/api/v1/identity/organizations/o1/members/u1/approve`;
- deny POSTs `.../deny`;
- a successful approve sweeps both the pending key and the members key
  (`expectSwept(invalidateSpy, organizationsGetPendingMembersQueryKey({ path: { id: "o1" } }))`);
- a 422 carrying `extensions.code === "Identity.MemberNotFound"` renders the error, and the list
  is still there.

For the mutation specs, answer by method the way `MemberList.test.tsx:84-91` does — one responder
serves both the POST and the post-success refetch, so branch on `call.method`.

---

## 4. Screen 2 — outstanding invitations

**Route:** `apps/wallow-web/src/app/routes/dashboard/organizations/invitations.tsx`
**Feature component:** `apps/wallow-web/src/features/organizations/components/InvitationList.tsx`

Everything this screen needs is **already generated** — no new SDK surface. It is therefore the
one screen that does not strictly block on `Wallow-yp3e.2`, though it should still land after it
so the whole epic ships against one client.

### Data

`invitationsGetByTenantOptions({ client, query: { skip, take } })`
(`react-query.gen.ts:801`). The endpoint is paged; the first cut may pass a fixed `take` and
render no pager, but the query object must be spelled explicitly so the key carries it.

**Do not add an `orgId` param.** `InvitationsController.cs:48` reads the ambient tenant. Passing
one would compile (it would land in the key as a stray arg) and silently do nothing.

### Mutation

`invitationsRevokeMutation({ client })` (`react-query.gen.ts:822`), `DELETE /invitations/{id}`,
`onSuccess` sweeping `queriesForOperation(invitationsGetByTenantQueryKey({ client, query }))`.
The key must be built with the **same** `query` object the list query used, or the predicate
matches nothing — this is the "ask the factory for the key, never spell a literal" rule from
`.claude/rules/TESTING.md`.

### Render

`InvitationResponse` gives `id`, `email`, `status`, `expiresAt`, `createdAt`,
`acceptedByUserId`. "Outstanding" means `status` is still pending — filter client-side, and note
in the component header that the API returns every invitation regardless of status.

Testids: `invitations-heading`, `invitations-table`, `invitation-item`, `invitation-revoke`,
`invitations-empty`, `invitations-loading`, `invitations-error`.

This is a **titled** page (it has no feature-owned heading to delegate to), so it composes
`PageHeader` — see `organizations/index.tsx:33` — and must be added to **both** `PAGE_FILES` and
`TITLED_PAGE_FILES` in `page-shell.test.ts`.

### Spec

`InvitationList.test.tsx`: roster, empty, loading, revoke issues
`DELETE /api/v1/identity/invitations/{id}`, revoke sweeps the invitations key, and a failed
revoke renders an error without dropping the list.

---

## 5. Screen 3 — member role management

**Route:** `apps/wallow-web/src/app/routes/dashboard/organizations/$orgId/members.tsx`
**Feature component:** `apps/wallow-web/src/features/organizations/components/MemberRoles.tsx`

### The trap that shapes this screen

`UsersController.AssignRole` writes `tenantContext.TenantId.Value` (line **179**) and
`RemoveRole` does the same (line **198**). **Neither takes an organization id.** On a route keyed
by `$orgId`, an operator who can *read* a foreign organization would issue a role grant that
lands silently in their **own** organization. Nothing in the API rejects it; the request returns
204.

**Mitigation, and it is not optional:** render the role controls only when `orgId` matches the
caller's own organization. The available check is `organizationsGetAllOptions` — which
`OrganizationsController.cs:76-78` filters down to exactly the caller's own tenant, so a single
returned row whose `id === orgId` is the condition. When it does not match, render the roster
read-only with an explanatory note (testid `member-roles-foreign-org`) and mount no mutation.

Record this in the component header. It is the single most consequential fact in this plan.

### Data

- Roster: `organizationsGetMembersOptions({ client, path: { id: orgId } })` — `UserDto[]`, each
  with `roles: string[]`. Note `OrganizationService.GetMembersAsync` (`OrganizationService.cs:
  201-231`) filters to `MembershipStatus.Active` at 211–212 and maps **per-org** role names.
- Role choices: `rolesGetRolesOptions({ client })` (`react-query.gen.ts:1209`) → `[{ name }]`.
- Own-org check: `organizationsGetAllOptions({ client })`.

### Mutations

`usersAssignRoleMutation` (1400) and `usersRemoveRoleMutation` (1415). Both sweep
`queriesForOperation(organizationsGetMembersQueryKey({ client, path: { id: orgId } }))`.

### The form

Assigning a role is the one place in these three screens with a field, so it goes through
`useAppForm` + `AppForm`. The shape to copy is `AddMemberForm` in `MemberList.tsx:211-267`:

```tsx
const form = useAppForm({
  schema: assignRoleSchema,                                   // zod
  defaultValues: { userId: "", roleName: "" },
  mutation: usersAssignRoleMutation({ client: sdk.client }),  // the WHOLE factory
  toVariables: (values) => ({ path: { userId: values.userId }, body: { roleName: values.roleName } }),
  onSuccess: () => { /* reset + invalidate */ },
  fallbackError: "Could not assign the role.",
});

return (
  <AppForm form={form} testIdPrefix="organization-member-role" className="space-y-4">
    …
  </AppForm>
);
```

Rules that bite here:

- **The generated factory goes in whole** (`MemberList.tsx:217`). `useAppForm` infers `TError`
  from it; destructuring it breaks the RFC 7807 error split.
- **Every testid derives from `testIdPrefix`** plus the kebab-cased field name, and the message
  id is that plus `-error`. With prefix `organization-member-role` and field `roleName` you get
  `organization-member-role-role-name` and `…-role-name-error`. An explicit `testId` prop
  overrides **both** — use it only when you need a specific id, and say why.
- **The field catalog is Text / Textarea / Select / Checkbox / Password only.** A role picker is
  a `SelectField`. Anything outside the catalog goes through the `AppField` render prop, which is
  the documented escape hatch (`packages/forms/CLAUDE.md`).
- **`Select` is not a native element.** It renders `role="option"` divs portalled to `<body>`, and
  only while open. Drive it in specs with `chooseOption` from
  `@bc-solutions-coder/testing/catalog-select` — `userEvent.selectOptions` only drives an
  `HTMLSelectElement` and will fail here.
- **`jsx-max-depth` is 2.** `AppForm > AppField > field.X` already spends it, which is why
  `OrganizationDetail.tsx:132-133` splits the field block into its own component. Expect to do
  the same.

### Spec

`MemberRoles.test.tsx`:

- roster renders each member with their role names;
- assigning POSTs `/api/v1/identity/users/{userId}/roles` with `{ roleName }`;
- removing DELETEs `/api/v1/identity/users/{userId}/roles/{roleName}`;
- both sweep the members key via `expectSwept`;
- **when `organizationsGetAll` returns an org whose id is not `orgId`, no mutation control
  renders and `member-roles-foreign-org` is present** — this is the spec that pins the mitigation;
- a 422 renders the error and leaves the roster mounted.

Fill fields with `userEvent.fill`, never `userEvent.type` (`.claude/rules/TESTING.md` — `type`
costs one CDP round trip per character and is a measured source of intermittent 15s timeouts).

---

## 6. Repo traps that apply to every bead here

Each of these has cost someone a debugging session. They are not style notes.

1. **`apps/wallow-web/e2e/routes.spec.ts` must NOT gain these routes.** The epic brief says to add
   them; that instruction is wrong for this app. The spec is a *backend-free reachability gate*
   and its header comment (lines 22–26) states that `/dashboard/**` stays excluded because it is
   auth-gated — `routes` is literally `["/", "/bff-demo"]` (line ~30). Adding an auth-gated route
   makes the gate redirect to OIDC and fail. Leave it alone.
2. **`routeTree.gen.ts` IS committed, and is never hand-edited.** It regenerates as a side effect
   of `vite dev` / `vite build`. `.github/workflows/route-tree-drift.yml` regenerates it via
   `pnpm --filter @bc-solutions-coder/wallow-web build` and fails on a diff. So: build the app,
   stage the regenerated file, commit it.
3. **react-query only through `@bc-solutions-coder/query`.** `useQuery`, `useMutation`,
   `useQueryClient`, every type. A direct `@tanstack/react-query` import fails `pnpm lint` on the
   root `no-restricted-imports` entry.
4. **Query keys come from the generated factory, never a literal.** The key embeds the client's
   `baseUrl`, so a drifted literal makes `getQueryData` return `undefined` rather than throw — a
   no-op assertion that every implementation passes.
5. **Invalidate through `queriesWithTag` / `queriesForOperation` only.** Generated keys are flat
   `[{ _id, baseUrl, tags, ...args }]` with no prefix to sweep by.
6. **Data imports go through the feature's `api.ts` seam.** Add each new symbol to
   `apps/wallow-web/src/features/organizations/api.ts` (currently 19–36) and expose the components
   through `index.ts`. Routes import from `@features/organizations`, never from
   `@bc-solutions-coder/sdk/query` directly.
7. **`page-shell.test.ts` is hand-kept.** Section 2 lists the edits. Forgetting them does not fail
   the build — it silently drops the new pages out of two invariants.
8. **Specs are linted by `pnpm lint:tests`, not `pnpm lint`.** Two passes over one partition;
   running only `pnpm lint` leaves every new spec unlinted.
9. **Component specs run in real headless Chromium.** Never jsdom, never happy-dom, no
   `@vitest-environment` pragma. A `.tsx` spec that renders through `react-dom/server` or asserts
   a `beforeLoad` redirect is named `*.ssr.test.tsx` so the preset routes it to the node project.
10. **Never mock `@bc-solutions-coder/ui`.** If a catalog component is awkward to drive, the
    component or the spec is wrong.
11. **Spec helpers live in `@bc-solutions-coder/testing`**, never under an app's
    `src/shared/testing/`. Use `./sdk-harness`, `./render-with-wallow`, `./invalidation`,
    `./catalog-select`.
12. **`createSdkHarness()` records a call BEFORE its responder runs.** The earliest non-racy
    "request is in flight" assertion is
    `await vi.waitFor(() => expect(harness.calls).toHaveLength(n))`.
13. **`getByText` matches by substring.** Two fixture emails that share a prefix will make a spec
    pass on the wrong row; pass `{ exact: true }`.
14. **Catalog-only elements.** `apps/wallow-web/.oxlintrc.json` forbids raw `p`, `span`, `legend`,
    `code`, `h1`–`h6` via `react/forbid-elements`, plus `wallow/no-sidebar-inversion`,
    `wallow/no-tinted-text` and `wallow/zone-dag`. Muted copy is `text-muted-foreground`, never
    `text-<token>/<alpha>`.
15. **Test comments: 8 lines max, present tense, no bead ids, no line citations into other
    files, no history verbs.** `.claude/rules/TESTING.md` lists the delete-on-sight categories.
    Note the existing route files violate this (`$orgId.tsx:11` cites `Wallow-8w1h.4.4`) — do not
    copy that habit into new files, and strip it from any file you move.
16. **Commit format:** conventional commits, `feat(identity):` style scope, lowercase, imperative,
    first line under 72 chars.

Gate before pushing: `pnpm check` (format:check + lint + lint:tests + typecheck + test + build +
check:exports). Build the SDK first — apps typecheck against `packages/sdk/dist/`.

---

## 7. Gaps found while planning — file, do not silently absorb

**A. Suspended and Denied memberships are unreachable from any list endpoint.**
`OrganizationService.GetMembersAsync` filters to `Active` (`OrganizationService.cs:211-212`);
`MembershipReviewService.GetPendingAsync` filters to `Pending`
(`MembershipReviewService.cs:32-33`). Nothing returns `Suspended` or `Denied`. That means
`reinstate` (`OrganizationsController.cs:245-259`) and `clearDenial` (206–220) have **no list to
drive them from** — the endpoints exist and are unreachable through any UI this plan can build.

This is a backend gap, not a screen gap. File it as a bead under `Wallow-yp3e` (not under
`Wallow-yp3e.3`): add a status filter to `GET {id}/members` or a sibling listing endpoint. Until
it lands, the three screens deliberately expose approve / deny / assign / remove / revoke and
**not** reinstate / clearDenial / suspend.

**B. `POST {id}/leave` has no surface either.** It is the member-facing counterpart and belongs on
a "my organizations" screen driven by `meGetOrganizations`, which is a fourth screen outside this
plan's brief. File it; do not scope-creep it in.

---

## 8. Bead decomposition

Under `Wallow-yp3e.3`, in dependency order. Every screen bead depends on `Wallow-yp3e.2` (the SDK
regeneration).

| Bead | Work |
| --- | --- |
| **R** route-shape migration | `$orgId.tsx` → `$orgId/index.tsx`, spec + screenshots moved, `page-shell.test.ts` updated, `routeTree.gen.ts` rebuilt and committed. Blocks the two `$orgId` screens. |
| **S1** pending access requests | Section 3. Depends on **R** and `Wallow-yp3e.2`. |
| **S2** outstanding invitations | Section 4. Depends on `Wallow-yp3e.2` only (no `$orgId`). |
| **S3** member role management | Section 5, including the own-org gate. Depends on **R** and `Wallow-yp3e.2`. |
| **N** nav + seam wiring | The `dashboard-destinations.ts` invitations entry and the final `api.ts` / `index.ts` exports. Depends on S1–S3. |

Each screen bead is TDD: a red phase writing the spec against the acceptance criteria, then green.

# Multi-Org Membership, Per-Org Roles, and Access Requests

Design doc. Establishes one identity per person, N tenant-scoped memberships, per-org role
assignment, self-service enrollment, an access-request notification routed to an
organization-configured email address, and the path for an external site to sign users in with
Wallow (§14).

All file/line references were read statically on 2026-07-31. **No code was executed** — every
runtime claim below is marked as needing verification where it matters.

---

## 1. Why

Three defects share one root cause: **membership and role authority are not modelled, so they
are inferred from row creation and from a flat global link table.**

### 1.1 Suspected privilege escalation across organizations — VERIFY FIRST

`PermissionExpansionMiddleware.cs:62-64` documents the intended rule:

> A role is granted by one tenant and carries no authority in another, so a request resolved
> onto a different tenant gets nothing from it — including AdminAccess and SystemSettings.

Nothing enforces it:

- `AspNetUserRoles` is a flat user→role link with **no tenant column**.
- `WallowRole.TenantId` exists, but `SeederWorker.cs:59-65` seeds every role with
  `TenantId = Guid.Empty`. Roles are global in practice.
- `AuthorizationController.cs:255` issues **all** of a user's roles into every token:
  `IList<string> roles = await userManager.GetRolesAsync(user);`

Traced consequence — Alice is `admin` in org A, and an ordinary member of org B:

1. Authorize gate (`AuthorizationController.cs:186-204`) passes; she *is* a member of B.
2. Token carries `org_id = B` (from the client, line 277) and `role = admin` (line 255).
3. `PermissionExpansionMiddleware.IsCrossTenantRequest` compares the token's `org_id` (B)
   against the resolved tenant (B). They match, so the guard does not fire.
4. `RolePermissionMapping["admin"]` grants `UsersCreate`, `UsersDelete`, `RolesCreate`,
   `RolesDelete`, `OrganizationsUpdate`, … **in org B**.

The cross-tenant guard only fires on an explicit cross-tenant *override*. It cannot fire on
"which org granted this role", because the grant records no org.

**This is a static reading of three independent facts. Confirm it on a live instance before
any other work in this doc.** Repro: user with `admin` in org A, plain membership in org B,
authenticate through a client bound to org B, inspect the `permission` claims on the request.
If confirmed, this is the highest-severity item here and Phase 1 ships alone.

### 1.2 Second-organization signup is a closed loop

An existing email address cannot join a second organization through any self-service path:

- **Register** — `AccountController.Register` resolves tenant B from `client_id` (line 721),
  then `CreateAsync` fails on `RequireUniqueEmail = true`
  (`IdentityInfrastructureExtensions.cs:46`) plus Identity's unique `NormalizedUserName` index
  (`WallowUser.Create` sets `UserName = email`). Line 751 maps this to `email_taken` and
  **returns at line 756**. `AddMemberAsync` is at line **769** — thirteen lines below the early
  return. No membership is created.
- **Login** — succeeds; `FindByEmailAsync` is global and unscoped. The OIDC authorize
  membership gate then redirects to `/error?reason=not_a_member`.
- **Error page** — `ErrorPage.tsx:84-94` offers exactly one action: *"Sign out and try a
  different account."* Signing out and back in returns to the same error.

The emergent rule is: *you may only join an organization by being the first person ever to use
that email address, on that organization's signup form.* The only working remedies are
out-of-band (an admin calling the member endpoints, or an invitation).

### 1.3 Three contradictory sources of tenant identity

- `WallowUserClaimsPrincipalFactory.cs:24-27` stamps `org_id` from `user.TenantId` — the
  **home** tenant, frozen at registration. Used by the auth cookie and exchange-ticket flow.
- `AuthorizationController.cs:277` stamps `org_id` from the **client's** tenant.
- `TokenController.cs:184` stamps **`tenant_id`** — a different claim name — on
  client-credentials tokens, read from the OIDC application's `tenant_id` property.

The first two agree only by coincidence. The third agrees with nothing, because
`ClaimsPrincipalExtensions.GetTenantId()` reads **only** `org_id`, and grepping the tree
shows *nothing* consumes a `tenant_id` claim: `TokenController.cs:184` is its only producer
and it has no consumer. A service-account token therefore resolves to **no tenant at all**,
not to the tenant its client is bound to.

That is why the `api/seed.json` disagreement — `bcordes-bff` in tenant *Wallow*,
`sa-bcordes-bff` in tenant *Dev* — looks cosmetic today. It is not cosmetic; the service
account simply has no tenant, so nothing has yet had the chance to disagree. Once roles are
resolved per-org, all three become authorization bugs. Phase 2 collapses them onto one claim.

---

## 2. Goals / non-goals

**Goals**

- One `WallowUser` per person, globally. Same email, many organizations.
- Role assignment scoped to `(user, organization)`. A role grants nothing outside its org.
- Self-service enrollment, governed by a per-organization policy.
- An access request notifies an address configured on the organization.
- Future routing of that notification to a role or group is **additive** — no contract or
  schema rework.
- A site outside this repo can offer "sign in with Wallow" through the SDK's BFF and read
  platform data as the signed-in user, with OIDC doing the authentication. §14.

**Non-goals (this doc)**

- Groups. Deferred to Phase 7; see §9.
- Per-org custom role *definitions*. Phase 1 scopes assignment only; see §4.1.
- Cross-org tokens. A token is single-org by design; see §5.
- Changing `WallowUser` to be tenant-scoped. Rejected — see §3.

---

## 3. Rejected alternative: tenant-scoped users

Considered and rejected: give each organization its own user rows, keyed
`(tenant_id, email)`.

- **Login precedes tenant context.** Password check, magic link, OTP, MFA verify, password
  reset, and email confirmation are all anonymous global `FindByEmailAsync` calls today. Each
  would need a tenant resolved from `client_id` first, correctly, every time. This is the same
  failure mode that already silently broke client branding
  (`ClientBrandingRepository.GetByClientIdAsync` runs with `TenantId = Guid.Empty` and returns
  nothing), reproduced across the most security-sensitive surface in the product.
- **ASP.NET Core Identity has no tenant parameter.** `UserManager` would need a custom
  `IUserStore` or a tenant-prefixing `ILookupNormalizer`, plus rework of Identity's own unique
  indexes. That is a permanent fork of the framework's core abstraction.
- **It removes SSO.** The same human would register, enroll MFA, and reset passwords once per
  site.
- **A shared table with a query filter is weaker isolation than it appears.** One missing
  `IgnoreQueryFilters()` already broke branding; the same omission on a users table is a
  cross-tenant data leak.

If two organizations must be genuinely un-correlatable (regulatory isolation), the honest
implementation is a separate schema or separate deployment per tenant — not another
`WHERE tenant_id =` that a repository can forget.

---

## 4. The model

`Membership` becomes the entity that carries authorization. Today `OrganizationMember` is a
`ValueObject` owned by `Organization`, carrying only `UserId` and `Role`
(`OrganizationMember.cs:6-9`).

```
Membership                     PK (UserId, OrganizationId)
  ├─ Status                    Pending | Active | Suspended | Denied
  ├─ Roles                     per-org role assignments (the only role system — §4.4.1)
  ├─ IsOwner                   ownership only; grants no permission (§4.4.1)
  ├─ JoinedAt
  ├─ RequestedAt / ReviewedAt / ReviewedBy   (access-request trail, §4.7)
  └─ Groups                    (Phase 6)
```

One `WallowUser` row. N memberships. Roles hang off the membership, never off the user.

### 4.1 Role definitions stay global in Phase 1

Two ways to scope roles:

| | Approach | Cost |
|---|---|---|
| **(a)** | Global role *catalog* (`admin`/`manager`/`user`), assignment scoped to `(user, org)` | One join table. Closes §1.1. |
| **(b)** | Per-org role *rows*, cloned per organization | `RoleExistsAsync` is a global check (`SeederWorker.cs:54`) and would collide; role lookup by name becomes ambiguous everywhere. |

**Take (a) for Phase 1.** The escalation is caused by unscoped *assignment*, not by shared
role definitions. Scoping assignment is a small, self-contained security fix. Per-org custom
role definitions are a feature, and belong in a later phase once memberships are proven.

This is a sequencing preference, not a compatibility constraint — there is no deployed data
forcing the split. (b) remains available later without rework, since the assignment table is
keyed on `RoleId` either way.

New table:

```
identity.membership_roles      (UserId, OrganizationId, RoleId)
```

`AspNetUserRoles` is retired as an authorization source in the same commit (§10).

### 4.2 Enrollment policy on `OrganizationSettings`

`OrganizationSettings` (`OrganizationSettings.cs`) already exists as the per-org config
aggregate and is `ITenantScoped`. Add:

```csharp
public EnrollmentPolicy EnrollmentPolicy { get; private set; }   // Open | RequestApproval | InviteOnly
public string? AccessRequestEmail { get; private set; }
public Guid DefaultRoleId { get; private set; }
```

| Policy | Behaviour on first authorize / register against this org |
|---|---|
| `Open` | Membership created `Active` with `DefaultRoleId`. Right for first-party sites. |
| `RequestApproval` | Membership created `Pending`; notification sent (§6); user sees "request submitted". |
| `InviteOnly` | Rejected. Today's de facto behaviour, made explicit. Safe default for a new org created without a policy. |

`OrganizationSettings.Update` gains the three parameters; `OrganizationSettingsUpdatedEvent`
gains the corresponding fields.

**Email verification is required before a second membership under any policy.** Otherwise
"register with an existing email" is an unauthenticated way to attach yourself to another
person's identity. Either require the credential at join time, or send a confirm-this-was-you
link to the address on file.

New members always receive `DefaultRoleId`, never an inherited role.

### 4.3 Decided: a `Pending` membership does not authenticate

A `Pending` membership grants nothing. Authorize does not issue a token for it — the user is
redirected to the request-submitted screen instead. The membership stays `Pending` until an
approver acts.

This is the strong form deliberately. The alternative — issue a token and let each downstream
`[HasPermission]` check refuse — puts tokens in circulation for people who have not been
approved and makes every permission check in the system the thing standing between an
unapproved requester and tenant data. One missed check becomes a breach. Refusing at token
issuance means there is nothing to miss.

Same rule for `Suspended`.

### 4.4 Who may approve — one permission governs the whole member lifecycle

Either of:

- the organization's owner (§4.4.1), or
- a member holding the **existing** `PermissionType.OrganizationsManageMembers`
  **in that organization**.

**No new permission.** Inviting, adding, removing, approving, denying and suspending are one
authority: whoever manages an organization's members. Splitting approve into its own
`MembershipsApprove` would buy the ability to delegate approve-without-remove to someone —
and there is nobody to delegate it to. Adding the split later is purely additive (a new
constant, a new `RolePermissionMapping` entry, a narrower `[HasPermission]` on the approve
endpoint); doing it now is a permission nobody holds and a second thing to keep in sync.

What reuse buys, concretely: no change to `PermissionType`, none to `RolePermissionMapping`,
and none to `ScopePermissionMapper` — `organizations.manage` already maps to
`OrganizationsManageMembers`, so the OAuth scope surface for this feature already exists.
`admin` and `manager` both already hold it, so a manager can approve join requests.

Because roles are per-org after Phase 1, "in that organization" is enforced by the same
mechanism as everything else: the approver's membership roles are resolved for the org being
acted on. Global admin remains the one cross-tenant grant (§5.3).

### 4.4.1 Decided: `OrgMemberRole` collapses into the role catalog

There are two per-org role systems in the tree today and the doc must not ship both:

| | System | What consumes it |
|---|---|---|
| `OrgMemberRole { Owner, Admin, Member }` | on `OrganizationMember` (the value object) | nothing that grants a permission |
| `WallowRole` catalog (`admin` / `manager` / `user`) | via `AspNetUserRoles` | `RolePermissionMapping` → every `[HasPermission]` check |

If `Membership` carries both `Roles` (catalog) and `OrgMemberRole`, there are two answers to
"what is this person in this org" — a smaller copy of the exact ambiguity that produced §1.1.

**Decision: the catalog is the only role system.** `OrgMemberRole` is dropped as an enum;
ownership survives as a single `Membership.IsOwner` boolean with **no permission semantics** —
it exists to answer "who is the last person who cannot be removed" (§4.7) and to seed the
owner fallback for access-request recipients (§6.2), nothing more. Every authorization
decision reads `membership_roles`.

The resolution chain, stated once because everything else depends on it:

```
membership_roles(UserId, OrganizationId, RoleId)
  → WallowRole.Name                  ("admin" | "manager" | "user")
  → RolePermissionMapping.GetPermissions
  → "permission" claims
```

This is what makes §4.1's "role *definitions* stay global" work: the catalog is shared, the
assignment is per-org, and the mapping in between is unchanged.

### 4.5 Decided: the policy lives on the organization, not the client

An organization may have several OIDC clients bound to it, and they all share one enrollment
policy. A native app and a web app that serve the same product belong to **one** organization
and enroll identically.

**The org boundary is a data boundary, not a site boundary.** This is the rule that decides
where a new client goes, and it is easy to get backwards. `Organization.Id == TenantId`, and
every `ITenantScoped` read is filtered on it — so a client bound to org X can only ever see
X's rows. The question to ask about a new site is therefore never "is this a different site"
but **"whose data does it read"**:

- Reads the same data as an existing org → its client belongs to **that** organization,
  however different the site looks or where it is hosted. Two front doors onto one room.
- Reads data nobody else may see → a **new** organization.

A separate domain, a separate deployment, and a separate design language are all irrelevant
to this choice. `bcordes.dev` signing people in to reach Wallow-tenant data is the first case,
not the second — see §14.1. Only a genuinely separate data set earns a new organization.

Rejected: a per-client enrollment policy. Two doors into the same room would be able to
disagree about who may enter — one client set to `Open` silently becomes an enrollment bypass
for every other client in that org, because membership is granted at the org level regardless
of which client the user came through. That is a security bug waiting to be introduced by a
later, well-meaning config change.

The consequence to accept deliberately: **a person using two products has two memberships**,
and their roles in each are independent. That is the intended behaviour, not a cost — it is
the same property §5 relies on for per-org tokens.

Corollary for `api/seed.json`: a service account belongs in the **same** organization as the
user-facing client it serves. `sa-bcordes-bff` (tenant *Dev*) and `bcordes-bff` (tenant
*Wallow*) serve one product and must be reconciled onto one organization.

The failure this causes is worse than "two tenants that cannot see each other", and worth
stating precisely because it changes the fix: per §1.3 the service account's `tenant_id`
claim has **no consumer**, so `sa-bcordes-bff` resolves to *no* tenant rather than to *Dev*.
Correcting `seed.json` alone therefore fixes nothing observable — the claim collapse in
Phase 2 is what makes the seeded tenant take effect. Do both, in that order.

### 4.6 The enrollment settings need their own gate — otherwise this feature unlocks itself

`RolePermissionMapping["user"]` grants `OrganizationsRead`, `OrganizationsCreate` **and
`OrganizationsUpdate`**. Every plain member can already update their organization. Today that
is merely generous. Combined with §4.2 it becomes an escalation:

1. Org is `Open` with `DefaultRoleId = user` (the configuration §4.2 exists to enable).
2. Anyone self-enrolls and lands with `OrganizationsUpdate`.
3. `OrganizationSettings.Update` is about to gain `EnrollmentPolicy`, `AccessRequestEmail`
   and `DefaultRoleId`.
4. The new member flips `DefaultRoleId` to the admin role, or repoints `AccessRequestEmail`
   at their own address and approves themselves out of band.

The feature hands out the key to its own lock. It is created by this design, not inherited,
so it is this design's job to close.

**Two changes, both before Phase 4 ships:**

- **Strip `OrganizationsUpdate` (and `OrganizationsCreate`) from the `user` role.** A plain
  member editing the organization was never intended; nothing in the product depends on it.
- **Gate the three new settings on `OrganizationsManageMembers`**, not on
  `OrganizationsUpdate`. They govern who may join, which is member management by another
  name — the same authority §4.4 just consolidated. `RequireMfa`, `AllowPasswordlessLogin`
  and `MfaGracePeriodDays` stay where they are.

Sequencing note: this is a permission narrowing, so it must land in the **same** commit as
the settings fields. Adding the fields first leaves a window where the escalation is live.

### 4.7 The rest of the member lifecycle

The doc so far covers joining. These are the states either side of it, and none of them exist
in the code today.

**Denial.** `Denied` is a real status, not the absence of a row — otherwise §12.4's
one-pending-request-per-`(user, org)` rule is trivially defeated by re-requesting, and each
retry mails the organization. On deny: record `ReviewedAt`/`ReviewedBy`, notify the requester
(they asked; silence is the worst outcome), and refuse a new request from the same
`(user, org)` for a **cooldown window** — 30 days, configurable later alongside the invitation
TTL. An approver may clear the denial at any time, which is the escape hatch for a mistake.
A denied user signing in again sees the denial screen, never the `not_a_member` dead end.

**Leaving.** A member may remove their own membership without holding any permission — it is
their membership. It transitions to removed (row deleted; the access-request trail is not
worth preserving for a voluntary exit) and revokes their tokens for that org (§5.2).

**Last-owner protection.** `Membership.IsOwner` (§4.4.1) exists for this: an organization must
retain at least one `Active` owner. Removing, suspending, denying, or self-leaving the last
owner is rejected with a domain error. There is no such guard anywhere in the code today, and
adding memberships is what makes it reachable.

**Suspension.** The mirror of approval, on the same permission. §4.3 already decides a
`Suspended` membership does not authenticate; §5.2 is what makes that true for tokens already
in circulation.

**Audit.** Every transition in this section — invite, accept, request, approve, deny, suspend,
reinstate, role change, leave, remove — emits an audit event. The repo already has the
infrastructure (`docs/operations/audit-events.md`); membership changes are precisely what it
is for, and "who let this person in" is the first question anyone asks of a system like this.

## 5. Token issuance

A token is **single-org**, and that is what keeps this design simple. Each client belongs to
one organization, so each token carries one organization's roles. The same login yields
different role sets on different clients. Do not encode multi-org authority in one token.

### 5.0 There are four role-resolution sites, not one

`AuthorizationController.cs:255` is the obvious one and the only one an earlier draft of this
doc named. Fixing it alone does **not** close §1.1. All four change in Phase 1 or Phase 1 is a
false sense of closure.

**(1) `AuthorizationController.cs:255` — the role claim.**

```csharp
IList<string> roles = await userManager.GetRolesAsync(user);
```

Resolves roles for the membership `(user, tenantInfo.TenantId)` instead. `tenantInfo` is
already resolved at line 190 for the membership gate, so the data is in hand.

**(2) `AuthorizationController.cs:315` — the scope gate, inside
`ValidateRequestedScopesAsync`.** The same global `GetRolesAsync`, used to decide whether the
caller may request a permission-bearing scope. This is a **second, independent** escalation
path that survives fixing (1): Alice is `admin` in org A, authorizes against a B-bound client
requesting `users.manage`, the gate approves it from her global `admin`, and the middleware
expands the *scope* into `UsersDelete` in org B without ever consulting a role claim.

**This one requires reordering.** `ValidateRequestedScopesAsync` is called at line 99;
`tenantInfo` is not resolved until line 190. Tenant resolution and the membership gate must
move **above** the scope gate. That reordering is itself an improvement — it stops the
consent screen from being rendered (lines 169-183) to someone who is about to be refused for
not being a member.

**(3) `TokenController.cs:120` — the refresh-token grant.**
`HandleAuthorizationCodeOrRefreshAsync` rebuilds the identity from scratch on every refresh
and re-injects global roles from `AspNetUserRoles`. It carries `org_id` forward from the
incoming principal (lines 135-145), so the org is in hand and simply unused. Every seeded
client requests `offline_access`, so the escalation returns on the first refresh — within an
hour of a "fixed" authorize. The correct shape is already in the same method: lines 126-132
deliberately re-read global admin from the claim store rather than trusting the incoming
principal, with a comment explaining why. Roles need the same treatment, per-org.

**(4) `WallowUserClaimsPrincipalFactory`** inherits `UserClaimsPrincipalFactory`, whose
`GenerateClaimsAsync` stamps role claims from `AspNetUserRoles` into the **auth cookie**. The
override currently only adds `org_id`. It must also suppress the inherited global role claims,
or the cookie principal keeps them for the exchange-ticket flow.

### 5.1 `PermissionExpansionMiddleware` does need one change

An earlier draft said it needed none. Not true: `ExpandUserRoles` returns early on
`IsCrossTenantRequest` (lines 65-68), and `ExpandUserScopes` (lines 89-106) — which runs
immediately after, on the same principal — has **no such guard**. Scope expansion is therefore
the bypass for role expansion. Put both behind the same check.

With that, the `IsCrossTenantRequest` guard becomes meaningful rather than vestigial, because
the roles and scopes reaching it are now org-specific.

Remaining consequences:

- `WallowUserClaimsPrincipalFactory.cs:24-27` must stop stamping `org_id` from
  `user.TenantId`. Either derive it the same way `AuthorizationController` does, or drop the
  claim and let the exchange-ticket flow carry the client through. One source of truth.
- `WallowUser.TenantId` is demoted to `OriginTenantId` — provenance only, never read for
  authorization — or dropped entirely. With no deployed data (root `CLAUDE.md`), prefer
  dropped.
- The `tenant_id` claim (§1.3) collapses onto `org_id` in the same pass, so client-credentials
  tokens resolve to a tenant at all.

### 5.2 A refresh token must re-check membership, and suspension must revoke

§4.3 promises that a `Pending` or `Suspended` membership issues no token, and argues that
refusing at issuance means "there is nothing to miss". That promise is enforced in exactly one
place — the membership gate at `AuthorizationController.cs:196-203` — and refresh does not go
through it. Suspend a member and they keep refreshing until the refresh token expires.

Two additions, both Phase 2:

- **Re-check membership status in the refresh branch.** `HandleAuthorizationCodeOrRefreshAsync`
  already re-checks that the user exists (line 95) and re-reads global admin (line 129); the
  membership for `org_id` is the third thing that must be re-read rather than trusted. A
  membership that is not `Active` fails the grant with `invalid_grant`.
- **Revoke on exit.** When a membership leaves `Active` — suspended, denied, removed, or the
  user leaves — revoke that subject's tokens and authorizations for that client set via
  `IOpenIddictTokenManager` / `IOpenIddictAuthorizationManager`. Without this, "does not
  authenticate" means "stops authenticating within the access-token lifetime", which is not
  what §4.3 claims.

Also fix the gate itself while it is open: `AuthorizationController.cs:196-203` currently asks
only *does a row exist*, via `GetUserOrganizationsAsync` → `Organization.Members`. Phase 1
moves that projection onto `Membership`; Phase 2 makes it assert `Status == Active`.

### 5.3 Global admin is unchanged and stays cross-tenant

`PermissionExpansionMiddleware.ExpandGlobalAdmin` grants the administrative permission set in
whichever tenant the request resolved onto, independent of membership. That is correct and
stays: it is the one way a human governs organizations they do not belong to, and it is the
deliberate exception to every per-org rule in this doc.

Consequences to keep true as memberships arrive:

- Global admin must **not** require a `Membership` row in the target org. It is not a
  membership grant; it is an override.
- It must continue to bypass the §4.3 pending/suspended gate — a global admin whose own
  membership is `Pending` somewhere is still a global admin.
- It remains seeded-only and never assignable through a tenant-facing endpoint.

### 5.4 Decided: no org switcher — the client selects the org

A consequence of "one client, one org, one token" that is easy to miss and worth stating so
nobody builds the wrong thing: **a user belonging to three organizations does not switch
between them inside one app.** Each org's client is a separate front door, and `wallow-web`
can only ever serve the organization its client is bound to.

Rejected: an org-selection screen, or an `organization` parameter on `/connect/authorize` that
lets the caller pick which membership the token represents. Both would make `org_id` a runtime
choice by the user rather than a property of the client — reintroducing, on the authorize
endpoint, exactly the "which org is this request for" ambiguity §5 exists to remove. Every
guard downstream would have to re-derive the answer.

The cost to accept: multi-org membership is deliberately invisible to a single app. A person in
three orgs uses three URLs. That is the same trade §4.5 already made and should not be
relitigated per-app.

Two things follow, both small and both currently missing:

- **`GET /v1/identity/me/organizations`** — a read-only list of the caller's `Active`
  memberships, so an app can *link* to the other doors even though it cannot open them. This is
  the honest version of a switcher.
- **`org_id` / `org_name` on userinfo** (§14.5), so a relying party can at least display which
  organization the current session belongs to.

## 6. Access requests and notification routing

### 6.1 Flow

1. User authenticates against a client whose org is `RequestApproval` and has no membership.
2. Identity creates a `Pending` membership, resolves recipients (§6.2), publishes
   `AccessRequestedEvent`.
3. User is redirected to a "request submitted" screen — replacing today's
   `not_a_member` → sign-out dead end (`ErrorPage.tsx:84-94`).
4. Notifications sends the email.
5. An approver flips the membership to `Active` via an organization endpoint. That publishes
   the existing `OrganizationMemberAddedEvent`, so the current welcome email keeps working.

### 6.2 Recipient resolution lives in Identity, not Notifications

Modules communicate only through Wolverine integration events in `Shared.Contracts` — there
are no direct references, so Notifications cannot query organizations or members. Identity
therefore resolves recipients and publishes **already-resolved addresses**.

```csharp
public sealed record AccessRequestedEvent : IntegrationEvent
{
    public required Guid TenantId { get; init; }
    public required string OrganizationName { get; init; }
    public required Guid RequesterUserId { get; init; }
    public required string RequesterEmail { get; init; }
    public required string RequesterName { get; init; }
    public required IReadOnlyList<string> RecipientEmails { get; init; }
    public required string ReviewUrl { get; init; }
}
```

**`RecipientEmails` is a list from day one.** This is what makes the future role/group routing
free: it becomes a change inside Identity's resolver, with zero change to the contract, the
handler, or the template. See §8.

**There is no `RequestId`.** An earlier draft carried one, which contradicted §4 — `Membership`
is keyed `(UserId, OrganizationId)` and there is no separate request entity. The pending
membership *is* the request; `RequesterUserId` + `TenantId` identify it exactly. Introducing an
`AccessRequest` aggregate alongside it would mean two rows that can disagree about whether
someone is waiting.

**`ReviewUrl` has no source today.** `AuthUrl` and the web app's base URL are single global
config values, so with more than one organization the review link is correct for at most one of
them. Options, in preference order: (a) resolve it from the organization's own client
registrations — the org's user-facing client already carries the redirect URI whose origin is
the right host; (b) add an explicit `OrganizationSettings.AppBaseUrl` next to
`AccessRequestEmail`. Prefer (a): it derives from data that must already be correct rather than
adding a field someone can forget to set. Whichever is chosen, decide it before Phase 5 —
the resolver in §6.2 is where it lands.

Resolution order:

1. `OrganizationSettings.AccessRequestEmail` if set.
2. Otherwise, fall back to the email addresses of the organization's owners
   (`Membership.IsOwner`, §4.4.1), so an org that never configured an address still gets
   notified.
3. If both are empty, log and skip the send — never fail the request. The membership row is
   the durable record; the email is a convenience.

### 6.3 Notifications side

Follows the established pattern exactly — compare
`InvitationCreatedNotificationHandler.cs`:

- New static handler `Application/EventHandlers/AccessRequestedNotificationHandler.cs`,
  signature `public static async Task Handle(AccessRequestedEvent message, ...)`. Wolverine
  auto-discovers it; no registration.
- New `"access-request"` case in `SimpleEmailTemplateService`'s template switch (line 28),
  wrapped with `WrapInLayout` like `"invitation"` at line 228.
- One `SendEmailCommand` per recipient, dispatched via `bus.InvokeAsync`.

## 7. Invitations — the other join path

Access requests are pull (the user asks). Invitations are push (the org asks). Both must end
at the same place: an `Active` membership with `DefaultRoleId`.

### 7.1 What already exists

More than expected. `Invitation` is an aggregate with `Email`, `Token`, `Status`
(`Pending | Accepted | Revoked | Expired`), `ExpiresAt`, `AcceptedByUserId`, and the
`Accept` / `Revoke` / `MarkExpired` transitions. `InvitationsController` has Create, list
(`GetByTenant`, paged), Revoke, `Verify(token)` (anonymous), and `Accept(token)`.
`ExpiredInvitationPruningJob` sweeps expired rows via `InvitationService.CleanupExpiredAsync`.

So the two asks look met, with one caveat:

- **TTL** — `ExpiresAt` is set at creation (hardcoded to 7 days, `InvitationService.cs:23`).
  The sweep is *not* effective: see the tenant-filter note in §7.2.
- **Seeing which emails have outstanding invitations** — `GET /invitations` already returns
  paged invitations for the tenant with email and status, gated on
  `OrganizationsManageMembers`. It needs a dashboard screen, not a backend.

The token itself is sound — `Invitation.GenerateToken` is 32 bytes from
`RandomNumberGenerator`, base64url-encoded. Not a defect; noted so Phase 3 does not relitigate it.

### 7.2 Defects that must be fixed for this to work

**A–C are the blocking bugs**: with any of them unfixed, invitations do not function. **D–F
are hardening** that ships in the same phase — each one lives in the exact files A–C already
touch, and each is a trap laid for the developer doing that work.

**A. Accepting an invitation does not create a membership.** `InvitationService.cs:62-69`:

```csharp
Invitation invitation = await invitationRepository.GetByTokenAsync(token, ct)
    ?? throw new EntityNotFoundException("Invitation", token);
invitation.Accept(userId, timeProvider);
await invitationRepository.SaveChangesAsync(ct);
```

It flips the status and records who accepted. It never calls `AddMemberAsync`. **Accepting an
invitation today makes you a member of nothing** — you then hit `not_a_member` on the next
authorize, exactly like the register dead end (§1.2). This resolves the previously-open
question about whether the invitation flow handles a pre-existing user: it does not handle
membership at all, for new or existing users.

**B. Expiry is not enforced on accept.** `Invitation.Accept` guards only
`Status != InvitationStatus.Pending`. An invitation past `ExpiresAt` whose sweep has not run
is still `Pending`, so it accepts. The TTL is advisory until the background job happens to
fire. `Accept` must check `ExpiresAt` against `TimeProvider` and reject, marking the row
`Expired` on the way out.

**C. Any authenticated user holding the token can accept an invitation addressed to someone
else.** `AcceptInvitationAsync(token, userId)` never compares the invitation's `Email` to the
accepting user's. A forwarded or leaked invite email lets the wrong person join the org — and
because invitations are the privileged join path, that is the most valuable token in the
system to steal. Accept must require that the authenticated user's **verified** email matches
`Invitation.Email`. Compare on the *normalized* email (`NormalizedEmail`, upper-invariant) —
`Invitation.Email` is stored as typed, so a case difference would otherwise reject a
legitimate acceptance.

**Prerequisite: the tenant query filter blocks all three fixes.** `Invitation` is
`ITenantScoped` and `IdentityDbContext` is a `TenantAwareDbContext`, but neither
`InvitationRepository.GetByTokenAsync` nor `InvitationService.CleanupExpiredAsync`'s
`dbContext.Invitations` query calls `IgnoreQueryFilters()`. Consequences:

- `Verify(token)` is `[AllowAnonymous]`, so no tenant is resolved and the lookup runs against
  `Guid.Empty` — it can never match.
- `Accept(token)` is `[Authorize]`, so the filter uses the caller's *current* `org_id` — which
  is precisely the org they are **not** yet in. Cross-org invitation acceptance, the entire
  point of the feature, cannot resolve the row.
- `CleanupExpiredAsync` runs from a background job with no tenant, so the pruning sweep
  matches nothing and the TTL is never enforced anywhere.

This is the same defect as `ClientBrandingRepository` (§13) — a tenant-scoped entity read on a
path where no tenant is resolvable. Same fix, same precedent (`ServiceAccountRepository`,
`OrganizationRepository`, `MfaExemptionChecker`): look the invitation up with
`IgnoreQueryFilters()` and treat the token as the authorization, since a 32-byte random token
*is* the tenant selector. It is listed as a prerequisite rather than a numbered defect because
A, B and C are each unverifiable until it is fixed.

**D. `GetPagedByTenantAsync` ignores its `tenantId` parameter.**

```csharp
// InvitationRepository.cs
public Task<List<Invitation>> GetPagedByTenantAsync(Guid tenantId, int skip = 0, ...)
{
    return context.Invitations
        .OrderByDescending(i => i.CreatedAt)   // tenantId is never referenced
        .Skip(skip).Take(take).ToListAsync(ct);
}
```

The result is scoped correctly today, but by the global query filter — not by the parameter.
That makes it a trap for exactly this phase: the prerequisite above adds `IgnoreQueryFilters()`
to the token lookups *in this same file*, and a method named `GetPagedByTenantAsync(tenantId)`
reads as if it filters on its own. Adding the escape hatch here too — or "cleaning up" what
looks like a redundant filter — turns the org-admin invitation list into every pending
invitation in every organization, i.e. every invited email address in the system. Fix: use the
parameter in an explicit `Where`, so the query states its own scope and survives the filter
being bypassed.

**E. `CreateInvitationAsync` ignores its `tenantId` parameter.** Same shape as D — the
signature takes `Guid tenantId` and the body passes `tenantContext.TenantId` to
`Invitation.Create`. Harmless today only because `InvitationsController` happens to pass the
ambient tenant. Fix: honour the parameter, or drop it and read the ambient tenant openly.
A parameter that silently does nothing is worse than either.

**F. No duplicate or already-member guard on create.** Nothing checks for an existing `Pending`
invitation for the same `(tenant, email)`, nor whether that email is already a member. Clicking
"invite" five times mints five independently valid 32-byte tokens for the same seat, and
`Revoke` acts on one invitation by id — so revoking the invite visible in the UI leaves the
other four live. Fix: reuse or refresh the existing pending invitation rather than minting a
second, and reject outright when the email already has an `Active` membership in that org.
This is the invitation-side counterpart of the one-pending-request-per-`(user, org)` rule
already decided for access requests (§12.4).

### 7.3 The two accept flows

`Accept` is `[Authorize]`, so the flow forks on whether the email already has an account.
`Verify(token)` is `[AllowAnonymous]`, which is what lets the auth app decide the fork before
anyone signs in.

**Existing user** — clicks the link → `/invitation?token=…` → `Verify` renders the org name
and invited email → user signs in (or is already signed in) → accept → membership created
`Active` → redirected into the app.

If the signed-in user's email differs from the invited email, do **not** silently accept
(defect C). Show whose invitation it is and offer to sign out and back in as that person.

**New user** — same link, same `Verify`, but the email has no account. The user is sent to
registration with the token carried through, registers, verifies their email, and the
invitation is accepted automatically on first successful sign-in.

The token must survive registration → email verification → sign-in. `AccountController.Register`
already threads a validated `returnUrl` through the verification link (lines 776-780), so the
mechanism exists; the invitation token rides the same path. The invitation is **not** accepted
at registration time — only after email verification, or defect C reopens as "register with
someone else's invited address and take their seat."

Both flows converge on one service method that creates the membership transactionally with the
status flip. An invitation acceptance bypasses `EnrollmentPolicy` entirely — being invited is
the authorization, so an `InviteOnly` org is joinable this way and only this way.

## 8. Future: route requests to a role or group

Asked for explicitly as a later nice-to-have. Because §6.2 resolves recipients inside Identity
and the event carries a list, this is genuinely small:

- Add `AccessRequestRecipientRoleId` / `AccessRequestGroupId` to `OrganizationSettings`.
- Extend the resolver: look up active memberships in this org holding that role (or in that
  group), project their users' emails, union with `AccessRequestEmail`.
- Nothing else changes — same event, same handler, same template.

Deliberately **not** built now. Building it before memberships exist means writing a resolver
against a table that does not yet hold per-org roles.

---

## 9. Deferred: groups

A group is "a named bundle of roles within one organization, with members." It is a
convenience layer over role assignment, not a separate authorization primitive — everything a
group expresses, per-org roles already express more verbosely.

Build it after Phase 1-5 land. Building groups alongside memberships means debugging two
indirections at once, and the one carrying the security guarantee is roles.

Shape when it arrives: `Group (OrganizationId, Name)` → `GroupRoles` → `GroupMembers`, with
effective roles being the union of direct membership roles and group-granted roles.

## 10. Schema change — no migration required

Wallow has never been deployed outside local development; there are no users and no data worth
preserving (root `CLAUDE.md`, "Deployment Status"). So this is a **reshape and re-seed**, not a
migration.

1. **Reshape the schema directly.** Replace the `OrganizationMember` value-object table with
   the `Membership` entity table and add `membership_roles`. Regenerate the EF migration rather
   than layering a new one onto the old shape.
2. **Delete `AspNetUserRoles` as an authorization source outright.** No dual-read window, no
   deprecation release. Identity still owns the table for its own plumbing; authorization stops
   consulting it in the same commit that adds `membership_roles`.
3. **Re-seed.** `api/seed.json` gains `enrollmentPolicy`, `accessRequestEmail`, and
   `defaultRoleId` per organization, plus explicit per-org role assignments for seeded users.
   Drop local databases and re-run `Wallow.SeederService`.
4. **Put `bcordes-bff` and `sa-bcordes-bff` in the same organization — the one whose data they
   read.** They are one product: a user-facing client and the service account acting on its
   behalf. Today `bcordes-bff` is in tenant *Wallow* and `sa-bcordes-bff` in tenant *Dev*.
   Apply §4.5's rule rather than guessing: the site reads Wallow-tenant data (§14.1), so
   **both belong to `Wallow`** — an earlier draft suggested minting a dedicated `bcordes` org,
   which would isolate the site from the very data it exists to show. Note that correcting
   `seed.json` alone changes nothing observable until the `tenant_id` claim collapse lands
   (§1.3). Fix the redirect URIs at the same time: `bcordes-bff` currently shares
   `http://localhost:3000/bff/callback` with `wallow-web-client`, so the two cannot run
   locally at once — give it its own port.
5. **Choose seed defaults deliberately** — there is no legacy behaviour to preserve. Set the
   dev/demo orgs to whichever `EnrollmentPolicy` best exercises the flow (likely
   `RequestApproval`, so the access-request path is reachable without setup).
6. **Change the claim and event contracts in the same commit** as the code that reads them.
   `org_id` semantics, `AccessRequestedEvent`, and the OpenAPI snapshot all move together;
   regenerate `packages/sdk/openapi/v1.json` and the SDK client.

The only hard requirement is that the resulting migrations apply cleanly to a **fresh**
database and that `pnpm check` and `./scripts/run-tests.sh` pass.

## 11. Phasing

| Phase | Scope | Ships |
|---|---|---|
| **0** | Verify §1.1 on a live instance | Confirmation, or a corrected threat model |
| **1** | `Membership` entity + `membership_roles`; `OrgMemberRole` collapses to `IsOwner` (§4.4.1); **all four** role-resolution sites issue per-org roles (§5.0); `ExpandUserScopes` behind the cross-tenant guard (§5.1); reshape + re-seed §10 | **Closes the escalation** |
| **2** | Collapse all three tenant-claim sources (§1.3); drop `WallowUser.TenantId`; `Pending`/`Suspended` do not authenticate (§4.3) — including refresh-time re-check and revoke-on-exit (§5.2) | One tenant identity per session |
| **3** | Invitation repair (§7.2 A–F): accept creates a membership, enforces expiry, binds to the invited email; tenant-filter prerequisite; honest `tenantId` parameters; duplicate/already-member guard | **Invitations actually work** |
| **4** | `EnrollmentPolicy` + `DefaultRoleId` on `OrganizationSettings`, gated per §4.6 **in the same commit**; strip `OrganizationsUpdate`/`OrganizationsCreate` from `user`; fix `Register`'s `email_taken` dead end; invite-through-registration (§7.3) | Same email joins a second org |
| **5** | `AccessRequestEmail`, `AccessRequestedEvent`, handler, template; `ReviewUrl` resolution (§6.2); `not_a_member` → request-access screen | The requested feature |
| **5.5** | External-RP path (§14): scope-gate narrowing, consent/scope seeding, org claims on userinfo, logout decision | **Sign in with Wallow from another site** |
| **6** | Approve/deny/suspend/leave endpoints and the rest of §4.7 (denial cooldown, last-owner guard, audit); pending-request and outstanding-invitation dashboard screens | Closes the loop |
| **7** | Per-org custom role definitions; groups; role/group request routing (§8) | Later |

Phases 1 and 2 are security work. Phase 3 is also security work — defect C (§7.2) is a live
account-takeover path on the most privileged join route, independent of everything else here,
and it is worth pulling forward if Phase 1 slips.

**Phase 1 acceptance criterion, non-negotiable.** One integration test: authenticate a user
holding `admin` in org A through a client bound to org B, and assert **zero** `permission`
claims on a request resolved onto B — then repeat the assertion after a token refresh, and
again with a permission-bearing scope (`users.manage`) requested at authorize time. All three
must hold. Any one of them passing alone means only a subset of §5.0 was fixed, which is the
specific failure this phase exists to prevent.

**Phase 3 acceptance criteria.** Each is one integration test in
`Wallow.Identity.IntegrationTests`; Phase 3 is not done until all nine are green:

1. Accepting a valid invitation creates an `Active` membership in the invitation's tenant with
   `DefaultRoleId`, and the invitation lands `Accepted` — both in one transaction (defect A).
2. Accepting an invitation past `ExpiresAt` is rejected and leaves the row `Expired`, with no
   membership created (defect B).
3. Accepting with an authenticated user whose normalized email differs from `Invitation.Email`
   is rejected, with no membership created (defect C).
4. Accepting with an authenticated user whose email matches but is **unverified** is rejected
   (defect C, registration path — §7.3).
5. `Verify(token)` anonymously resolves an invitation belonging to a tenant other than the
   ambient one, and `Accept` succeeds for a user whose current `org_id` is a *different* org
   (the tenant-filter prerequisite).
6. `CleanupExpiredAsync`, invoked with no tenant resolved, transitions expired `Pending`
   invitations across every tenant to `Expired` (the tenant-filter prerequisite).
7. With invitations existing in two organizations, `GET /invitations` as an admin of one
   returns only that organization's rows — asserted with the tenant query filter **bypassed**,
   so the test fails if the scoping rests on the filter alone (defect D).
8. `CreateInvitationAsync` called with a `tenantId` that is not the ambient tenant either
   honours it or does not compile — the parameter is not silently discarded (defect E).
9. Inviting the same email twice yields one live token, not two, and inviting an existing
   `Active` member is rejected (defect F).

Phases 4-6 are the feature, and are substantially easier once membership is a real entity,
which is why they follow rather than lead.
