Red proved it takes 19 failures to 12 and cures only the glob case. A regex cannot carry string/template/regex-literal context, so this is a left-to-right scanner. It is ~90 lines, has no options and no configurability, and is not a JS parser. === WHAT IT RECOGNISES, AND WHY EACH BRANCH EARNS ITS PLACE === Six states: normal code, line comment, block comment, quoted string, template literal, regex literal — plus one targeted rule. 1. `://` is a URL scheme, not a comment. This is the ONLY way url-in-jsx-text can pass: `

Read https://example.com/terms first.

` carries no quoting at all, and knowing it is JSX text requires parsing JSX. Requiring the colon to be IMMEDIATELY adjacent keeps it from swallowing a real comment. 2. Regex-literal detection keys off the last significant token before the `/` (punctuation set + a small keyword list), read from the code emitted so far. `<`, `>`, `{` and `}` are DELIBERATELY EXCLUDED from that set: in .tsx they are almost always JSX, and reading `

`, `/>` or `{/` as a regex start would let the scan run past a real comment — the same over-deletion by another route. Comment detection is checked BEFORE regex detection, so the very common `{/* ... */}` JSX comment is still stripped. 3. `'` and `"` strings terminate at their line's newline whether or not they closed. A quoted string cannot span a line in JS, and this is what keeps an apostrophe in JSX prose (`Don't have an account?`) from opening a "string" that suppresses comment detection for the rest of the file. Template literals may span lines, so only a backtick ends one. 4. An unterminated block comment runs to EOF (the language does the same). Red pinned the old under-deleting behaviour as "safe"; the fixture asserts only that the testid survives and GENUINE-COMMENT goes, and both hold either way. `${}` nesting inside template literals is deliberately NOT tracked. A template scanned backtick-to-backtick emits every character regardless, so a nested template can only mis-PAIR, never delete — the safe direction — and no fixture or real source needs it. === NON-VACUITY, MEASURED NOT ASSUMED === Broke each branch, ran, restored: drop the `://` guard -> 2 failed / 135 passed never recognise a regex literal -> 4 failed / 133 passed never recognise a quoted literal -> 2 failed / 135 passed restore the two-pass regex -> 19 failed / 118 passed (EXACTLY red's state) as written -> 0 failed / 137 passed The last line is the important one: reinstating the old stripper reproduces red's count precisely, so these are the same tests and this scanner is what cures them. The end-to-end guard passes too — violation-behind-glob's `

` behind a `// ... /v1/** ...` line comment is now CAUGHT by both the element sweep and the colour sweep, which is the whole point of the bead. === EXTRACTION: ONE IMPLEMENTATION, TWO CONSUMERS === Red found the identical two-pass stripper inlined in BOTH src/typography.test.ts and src/app/typography.test.ts. It now lives once, in `@shared/testing/strip-comments`, and both call it. Placement was forced by the zone DAG, not chosen for taste: src/app/typography.test.ts is in zone `app`, so a helper at the src ROOT would be a cross-zone relative hop and zone-dag.test.ts fails it. `shared/testing/` is a sanctioned shared subdir, `@shared/*` is already how 30+ specs reach `harness-routes`/`style-contract`/ `invalidation`, and app -> shared is a legal DAG edge spelled as an alias. src/typography.test.ts is zone `root`, which zone-dag excludes from the product graph, so it uses the same alias for consistency. === FOLLOW-UP BEAD FILED (required by the coordinator, and done) === Wallow-e6gz — "Repo-wide: ~20 guard specs share the blind two-pass comment stripper" (P3, bug, discovered-from Wallow-lrlm.14). It lists every copy red found (5 more in wallow-web, 7 in wallow-auth, minimal-app's sdk-wiring, 5 packages/ui composition specs, packages/forms query-facade), names this scanner and the 11 fixtures as the proven fix, and records that the real home is a shared entry in @bc-solutions-coder/testing — a cross-package decision this bead deliberately did not make. Sweeping those copies was OUT OF SCOPE here and none were touched. === ONE THING THE NEXT AGENT SHOULD KNOW === The new stripper strips LESS than the old one in every case where the old one was wrong, so more real source is now visible to both sweeps. That could have surfaced a genuine violation the old blindness was hiding. It did not — the full wallow-web suite is green — but that is a measured result, not a guarantee that holds after the next component lands. title: the .dark wrapper-div story decorators render light mode, in six ui story files
description:
False coverage of the same class Wallow-lrlm.6.4 removed - found while fixing it.

Six packages/ui story files scope a scheme with a wrapper `<div className="dark">` and comment that this is safe because 'the token blocks renderThemeStyle emits are class-scoped, so a wrapper is enough':
  empty-state, list-card, list-row, page-header, text, theme-toggle (theme-toggle's is fixed by 6.4).

A wrapper is NOT enough. renderThemeStyle emits :root/.dark/.light blocks carrying the RAW --sidebar-style variables, while Tailwind's @theme declares the token --color-*: var(--raw, ...) on :root alone. A var() inside a custom property is substituted at computed-value time on the DECLARING element, so a descendant .dark rebinds the raw variable while the already-computed --color-* token keeps the light value. Every utility under the wrapper paints light.

Measured on this architecture (wallow-web browser project, real fork theme): bg-sidebar is rgb(40,21,12) under BOTH a .light and a .dark wrapper, and only becomes rgb(35,17,8) with .dark on documentElement. bg-secondary likewise 234,227,220 under both wrappers vs 59,41,33 on documentElement.

Consequence: every story named Dark / SystemDark / *OnDark in those files renders the LIGHT palette in the Storybook explorer and in the storybook vitest project. Nothing currently ASSERTS a scheme difference in them, so no test is lying - but a human reviewing the dark variant is being shown light, which is what these stories exist for.

Options (a decision this bead should make first):
  a) stamp/clear the class on documentElement via a decorator with cleanup - stories share one document, so leakage is the risk to design around;
  b) drop the dark stories and move any scheme comparison that must be MEASURED to an app browser spec that can stamp documentElement, which is what 6.4 did;
  c) change the token layer so .dark re-declares the --color-* tokens, not just the raw vars - widest blast radius, affects every consumer.

Also correct the 'a wrapper is enough' comment wherever it appears; that sentence is what propagated the wrong model into 6.4.
notes:
RED (Wallow-lrlm.11) — 15 tests failing, all for the right reason.

## TRUE affected-file count: SIX story files — the bead's list is correct, but two of its claims are not

Re-derived from disk (grep of every className carrying a bare `dark`/`light` token across
apps/, packages/, tools/, docs/). The wrapper anti-pattern exists in exactly six files, 12
decorators (one light + one dark each), and NOWHERE else in the repo:

  packages/ui/src/components/empty-state/empty-state.stories.tsx   (L28 light, L35 dark)
  packages/ui/src/components/list-card/list-card.stories.tsx       (L29 light, L36 dark)
  packages/ui/src/components/list-row/list-row.stories.tsx         (L27 light, L34 dark)
  packages/ui/src/components/page-header/page-header.stories.tsx   (L27 light, L34 dark)
  packages/ui/src/components/text/text.stories.tsx                 (L28 light, L35 dark)
  packages/ui/src/components/theme-toggle/theme-toggle.stories.tsx (L40 dark, L47 light)

Every other repo-wide hit for `className="dark"` is prose DESCRIBING the defect
(apps/CLAUDE.md, packages/ui/CLAUDE.md, docs/development/component-library.md,
docs/development/frontend-setup.md, DashboardLayout.catalog-control.test.tsx's header).
No spec, and no story outside these six, uses a wrapper to select a scheme.

TWO CORRECTIONS to the bead body:

1. "theme-toggle's is fixed by 6.4" is WRONG. 6.4 fixed that file's COMMENT (its header now
   explains the token/raw mechanism correctly) and rewrote `OnTheSidebarSurface` to one
   scheme — but `darkScheme` (L37-41) and the two stories that use it, `Dark` and
   `SystemDark`, are still wrapper-scoped and still render light. theme-toggle is the worst
   case in the set: documented-correct, implemented-wrong.

2. "Six ... story files ... comment that this is safe because 'the token blocks
   renderThemeStyle emits are class-scoped, so a wrapper is enough'". That sentence exists in
   ONE file only — text.stories.tsx:21-22. Four files (empty-state:20-22, list-card:21-23,
   page-header:19-21, text:18-20) carry the weaker misleading sentence "The `.dark`/`.light`
   wrappers scope a scheme to the story's own subtree rather than stamping
   `document.documentElement`: stories share one document, so a story that flipped the real
   root class would leak into every story after it." list-row carries NO scheme comment at
   all; theme-toggle's is already correct. Green must fix 4 comments + 1 extra sentence, and
   must NOT "correct" theme-toggle's (it already says the right thing).

Story census in the six files: 45 stories — 15 dark-decorated, 30 light-decorated.

## The decision this bead had to make first: option (a), with the leak designed against

Options (b) "drop the dark stories" and (c) "re-declare --color-* under .dark" are both
rejected. (b) throws away the only place in the workspace where dark-mode rendering of these
six components is visible at all — the `browser` project loads no Tailwind, so nothing else
can show them. (c) is a token-layer change touching every consumer of packages/styles and is
not this bead's blast radius. (a) it is: the decorator stamps `document.documentElement` and
removes the class on unmount.

## What the tests are, and why they live where they do

NEW FILE (the spec — do not edit in green):
  packages/ui/.storybook/scheme-assertions.ts
    exports `expectScheme(scheme: "dark" | "light"): (context: { canvasElement: HTMLElement })
    => Promise<void>` — a play function factory.

WIRING (42 one-line `play:` entries across the six story files): every one of the 45 stories
gets `play: expectScheme("<its scheme>")` except the three that already own a play
(list-row `AsLink`, theme-toggle `Cycling`, theme-toggle `OnTheSidebarSurface` — all
light-scoped; left untouched so no existing coverage is disturbed).

PROJECT CHOICE — `storybook`, and it is the ONLY project that can see this.
`--color-background` is declared by styles.css's `@theme`, which reaches the page only
through the Tailwind pipeline; the raw `--background` reaches it only through
preview.tsx's inlined `renderThemeStyle(forkResolvedBranding)`. packages/ui's `browser`
project has neither, so every reading there would be `rgba(0,0,0,0)` and any colour
assertion would be vacuous. The `storybook` project has both (.storybook/preview.css +
preview.tsx) and runs the same headless Chromium.

HOW IT MEASURES (no class strings anywhere in this spec). The play appends a throwaway probe
`<div>` inside the story's own scheme scope (`canvasElement.querySelector(".bg-background")`,
falling back to the canvas — located by the SURFACE class, not the scheme class, so it keeps
working once the scheme moves to documentElement), paints a CSS value on it, reads the colour
back with `computedColor`/`relativeLuminance`/`isTransparent` from
`@bc-solutions-coder/testing/contrast` — canvas sRGB readback, never a getComputedStyle regex
(the palette is oklch). Verified in the run: the contrast import resolves in the storybook
project's own Vite server with no mid-run dep re-optimization, so no vitest.config.ts change
was needed.

THREE ASSERTIONS, none of them hard-coding a colour (api/branding.json is fork config):
  0. tripwire — `--color-background` / `--color-foreground` must not be transparent, so a
     theme-less page fails loudly instead of passing everything.
  1. the palette is the right way up: relative luminance of background < foreground iff the
     story claims dark. This is the headline failure.
  2. `--color-background` and `--background` must paint the SAME colour at that point in the
     tree. They diverge exactly when a block rebound the raw variable below the element the
     token was computed on — the mechanism, stated where it is directly visible.

## Failing now, for the right reason

`pnpm exec vitest run` in packages/ui: 22 failed / 1488 passed.
  MINE — 15, exactly the 15 dark-decorated stories, no others:
    empty-state: Message Only Dark, With Icon Dark, With Action Dark
    list-card:   Dark
    list-row:    Dark, As Link Dark
    page-header: Title Only Dark, With Description Dark, With Description And Actions Dark
    text:        Default Dark, Type Scale Dark, Colours Dark, Semantic Elements Dark
    theme-toggle: Dark, System Dark
  Message: "this story paints the LIGHT palette while claiming dark (relative luminance:
  background 0.911, foreground 0.010): expected false to be true" — i.e. rgb(249,244,239)
  where `--background` in force is rgb(47,25,15).
  FOREIGN — 7, all Wallow-lrlm.10's in-flight navigation-menu work (navigation-menu.stories
  `Trigger Sidebar Surface`, navigation-menu.test.tsx x2, sidebar-surface.test.ts x4).
  Untouched by this bead; reported, not fixed.

## Non-vacuity — proven in BOTH directions by experiment, then reverted

Temporarily replaced text.stories.tsx's two decorators with one that stamps
`document.documentElement` in a `useLayoutEffect` and removes it in the cleanup:
  - with cleanup:    13/13 pass (the 4 dark stories flip red -> green, the 9 light stay green)
  - WITHOUT cleanup: 4 fail again — the leaked `light` from the first story out-cascades the
    `.dark` block (renderThemeStyle emits `.dark` before `.light`), so a leaking
    implementation is caught too.
  - restored to the wrapper: 4 fail again.
So the spec fails on the defect, passes on the fix, and fails on a fix that forgets cleanup.

## Leakage: how it is handled, and what green still has to check

One shared document. The design does not try to prevent leakage — it makes leakage FAIL:
every light story asserts it paints light and every dark story asserts it paints dark, so a
class left behind by any story breaks whichever story runs next, in either direction, and
within any file. Proven above. Two residual risks for the green phase to check, which
per-file runs cannot show:
  - CROSS-FILE: run the whole `storybook` project (`pnpm exec vitest run --project storybook`),
    not one file, before declaring green.
  - the last story in empty-state, list-row (AsLinkDark is 4th of 5) and page-header is/near a
    dark one, so a missing cleanup surfaces in the NEXT file.

## Notes for the green implementer

- Do NOT edit `.storybook/scheme-assertions.ts` or any `play:` line — those are the spec.
  Change ONLY the `lightScheme`/`darkScheme` decorators and the misleading comments.
- The natural shape is one shared decorator pair (suggested home:
  `packages/ui/.storybook/scheme-decorators.tsx`, beside the assertions and outside `src/`, so
  nothing ships in dist/) imported by all six files, stamping the class in a layout effect and
  removing it in the cleanup. Keep `bg-background text-foreground p-6` on the wrapper div: it
  frames the story, and the spec's probe host looks for `.bg-background` (it degrades to the
  canvas if you drop it, but the reading is then less precise).
- Also worth landing: packages/ui/CLAUDE.md's Gotchas paragraph says "Six story files ... still
  carry the wrapper anti-pattern"; that sentence needs updating when the fix lands.

Files touched (red): packages/ui/.storybook/scheme-assertions.ts (new) + the six
*.stories.tsx files. format + typecheck + oxlint clean on all seven (the only lint errors in
packages/ui are Wallow-lrlm.10's unused imports in navigation-menu.stories.tsx).
GREEN (Wallow-lrlm.11) — 361/361 storybook, 1510/1510 packages/ui. Zero foreign failures remain.

FILES
  NEW  packages/ui/.storybook/scheme-decorators.tsx  — the fix
  MOD  packages/ui/src/components/{empty-state,list-card,list-row,page-header,text,theme-toggle}/*.stories.tsx
  MOD  packages/ui/CLAUDE.md            (Gotchas)
  MOD  docs/development/component-library.md   (Theming and dark mode)
  MOD  docs/development/frontend-setup.md      (Scoping Dark Mode)
  UNTOUCHED: .storybook/scheme-assertions.ts, every `play:` line, every existing play function.

## The fix — option (a), one shared decorator pair

packages/ui/.storybook/scheme-decorators.tsx exports `lightScheme` / `darkScheme`
(`Decorator`), each rendering a `SchemeScope` that:
  • adds the scheme class to `document.documentElement` in a `useLayoutEffect`,
  • removes it in the effect cleanup,
  • keeps the framing `<div className="bg-background text-foreground p-6">` — WITHOUT the
    scheme class, which on a wrapper does nothing but look convincing. `expectScheme`'s probe
    host still resolves to it via `.bg-background`, so the reading stays precise.

All twelve local decorator consts are deleted; the six files import the pair. Nothing ships:
tsconfig.build.json's `include` is `src/index.ts` alone, so `.storybook/` is outside the build
graph.

## Non-vacuity re-proved on THIS implementation (not inherited from red)

Ran the experiment red described, against the shared decorator:
  • cleanup present  → 361/361 pass
  • cleanup removed (`classList.remove` commented out, everything else identical)
    → EXACTLY the same 15 dark stories fail, same message ("paints the LIGHT palette while
      claiming dark ... background 0.911, foreground 0.010"). The leaked `.light` out-cascades
      `.dark` at equal specificity because renderThemeStyle emits `.light` last.
  • restored → 361/361.
So the suite catches both the wrapper regression (red's state) and the forgot-to-clean-up
regression. Cross-file leakage checked by running the WHOLE storybook project, not per file.

## Comments

Rewrote the scheme paragraph in all six headers. Corrected beyond red's inventory:
  • text.stories.tsx — the "token blocks are class-scoped, so a wrapper is enough" sentence.
  • empty-state / list-card / page-header / text — the weaker "wrappers scope a scheme to the
    story's own subtree" sentence.
  • list-row — had NO scheme comment; now carries the correct one.
  • theme-toggle — red said "do not correct it, it already says the right thing". Its MECHANISM
    paragraph was right and is preserved, but two claims of fact became FALSE the moment the fix
    landed and had to be updated: "no story touches `document.documentElement`" (they now all do)
    and "These wrappers ... are honest about nothing more. A scheme comparison that has to be
    measured belongs [in wallow-web]" (it can now be measured here, and is). This is not a
    reversal of 6.4's correction — it is the same mechanism, restated for the implementation
    that now matches it.
Each of the six now points at .storybook/scheme-decorators.tsx and says never to reintroduce a
wrapper.

## Docs

  • packages/ui/CLAUDE.md Gotchas — the sentence naming the six files as "still carry the wrapper
    anti-pattern ... do not copy any of them" was false after the fix. Replaced: names
    .storybook/scheme-decorators.tsx as THE reference implementation, says the six files now
    import it and ARE the pattern to copy, and records that expectScheme is what keeps it fixed.
  • docs/development/component-library.md — the blockquote's rule was still true, but the line
    "controlled ... is how a story renders one face without touching the real document" was not
    (stories now do stamp the document); narrowed it to "without a real ThemeProvider or a
    localStorage round-trip". Blockquote extended with the decorator pair + expectScheme.
  • docs/development/frontend-setup.md#scoping-dark-mode — its rule was already correct and
    named no implementation; added the worked example.
  • Checked and deliberately NOT changed: apps/CLAUDE.md's "theme class belongs on
    documentElement" bullet and the two wallow-web spec headers
    (DashboardLayout.catalog-control.test.tsx, DashboardNav.sidebar-surface.test.tsx) — all
    describe the mechanism, all still true.

## ONE stale comment left behind, deliberately — needs a decision

.storybook/scheme-assertions.ts:13-16 opens "Six story files scope a scheme with a wrapper
<div className='dark'> and none of them assert anything about colour, so every story named *Dark
has been rendering the LIGHT palette". Present tense, and now false. I did not touch it: the
green-phase instruction was explicit that this file is the spec and must not be edited, and a
comment edit there is indistinguishable from tampering in a diff. It is prose only — no assertion
depends on it. Suggested rewording for whoever owns the follow-up: past tense ("used to scope ...
which is why this exists"). Flagging rather than fixing.

## Gates

  pnpm typecheck   → all 9 packages/apps Done
  pnpm lint        → clean (oxlint --deny-warnings, repo-wide)
  pnpm format:check→ clean, 891 files

all passing now — that agent's work landed while this ran. Nothing of theirs was touched here.

title: navigationMenuTriggerRecipe has no surface arm, unlike the Link recipe
description:
Consistency gap, not a live defect.

Wallow-lrlm.6.4 gave navigationMenuLinkRecipe a `surface` axis so a nav row composed onto the inverted rail paints from the sidebar-* family instead of the page palette. navigationMenuTriggerRecipe did NOT get the same axis and still carries page-palette colour in its base string (hover:bg-accent, data-[popup-open]:bg-accent).

Why this is not a defect today: verified by search that neither app renders NavigationMenu.Trigger at all - only packages/ui stories and tests do. DashboardNav uses Root/List/Item/Link only. Root/List/Item/Content carry no colour; Popup/Arrow carry bg-popover but never render on the rail.

Why it is still worth closing: a Trigger dropped into a sidebar would reproduce exactly the bug 6.4 just fixed, and the recipe pair now reads inconsistently - a reader who sees the Link recipe's surface axis will reasonably assume the Trigger has one.

Scope: add the matching `surface` arm to navigationMenuTriggerRecipe (sidebar arm mapping hover:bg-accent -> hover:bg-sidebar-accent and the data-[popup-open] pair likewise), plus a story exercising it. Do not rename any token - Wallow-lrlm.6.6 ruled KEEP on the sidebar-* family.
notes:
RED (Wallow-lrlm.10) — 7 tests failing across 3 files. Scaffold only; no colour logic written.

FILES
- packages/ui/src/sidebar-surface.test.ts        (node project — class-list half, 4 new failing)
- packages/ui/src/components/navigation-menu/navigation-menu.stories.tsx (storybook project — MEASURED half, 1 new failing story)
- packages/ui/src/components/navigation-menu/navigation-menu.test.tsx    (browser project — 2 failing)
- packages/ui/src/components/navigation-menu/navigation-menu.styles.ts   (SCAFFOLD: surface axis with EMPTY arms + defaultVariants page)
- packages/ui/src/components/navigation-menu/navigation-menu.tsx         (SCAFFOLD: Trigger destructures `surface`, passes it to the recipe)

WHICH VITEST PROJECT, AND WHY
The measured coverage is a STORY (`TriggerSidebarSurface`), i.e. the `storybook` project. The `browser`
project compiles no Tailwind, so it cannot see colour at all; `storybook` is the only project with the
real Tailwind pipeline AND the fork theme attached. Probed and confirmed in this browser: `bg-sidebar-accent`
computes to `oklch(0.3 0.035 45)` there. Colours go through `@bc-solutions-coder/testing/contrast`
(canvas normalisation) — computed values really do come back as `oklch(...)`, measured, so an rgb() regex
would silently never match. That helper is pure DOM and imports no vitest, so the story stays safe in the
standalone explorer.

TWO THROWAWAY PROBES (written, run, deleted)
1. `storybook/test`'s userEvent (testing-library) does NOT set `:hover` — measured
   `matches=false`, background unchanged. `vitest/browser`'s userEvent DOES (`matches=true`,
   background `oklch(0.3 0.035 45)`). So a real pointer is reachable from a play function, but only by
   importing `vitest/browser` into a story, which would break `pnpm --filter @bc-solutions-coder/ui storybook`
   (a supported script) — that import throws outside browser mode. DECISION: no pointer hover in a ui story.
   The `hover:` pair is pinned by class list in sidebar-surface.test.ts; the `data-[popup-open]:` pair, which
   names the SAME two tokens, is what proves those tokens paint legibly. Documented in the story's header.
2. `defaultValue` opens the menu with NO pointer and Base UI stamps `data-popup-open` on the trigger it
   opened (measured) — that is the hover-free way into a trigger's active paint, and it is what the story uses.

WHAT THE PROBE MEASURED ON A REAL `bg-sidebar` RAIL, BEFORE ANY FIX
- rail            = oklch(0.22 0.035 45)
- trigger at rest = rgb(0,0,0) PURE BLACK. A `<button>` takes no colour from an ancestor's `text-*` the way
  its sibling `<a>` does, and the trigger recipe named no rest text at all. ~1.1:1 on the rail.
- trigger OPEN    = bg oklch(0.88 0.035 75) — the page `bg-accent`, a light chip on a dark rail.
So the gap is worse than "inconsistent with the Link": a trigger on a rail is illegible at rest today.

DESIGN DECISION THE GREEN PHASE MUST HONOUR (flagged — slightly beyond the bead's literal words)
The arms mirror `navigationMenuLinkRecipe` 1:1, which means the page arm GAINS `text-foreground` (a rest-text
dimension the trigger never had). Reasons: (a) CLAUDE.md rule 2 requires the sidebar arm to restate rest text,
and the dimension-parity spec then forces the page arm to name it too; (b) the trigger "has to sit flush beside
the Link rows in the same list" and the Link already names it; (c) measured, the unnamed dimension is what
paints black. TRIGGER_CLASSES in navigation-menu.test.tsx was updated accordingly — that constant is the file's
declared source of truth, so the green phase transcribes it, it does not renegotiate it.

NON-VACUITY EVIDENCE

  transparent, and the `bg-accent` / `bg-sidebar-accent` swatches measure genuinely different colours. So the

- The scaffold is provably structural: the axis exists, both arms are empty strings, so the trigger still

title: Normalise glob paths in wallow-web's drift guard so ./-prefixed and gitignore-style spellings cannot be dropped silently
description:
apps/wallow-web/src/lint-gate.test.ts carries a drift guard ("the nested oxlint config does not drift from the root") that exists because the F5 lint gate had to live in a NESTED config: apps/wallow-web/.oxlintrc.json restates the root's wallow-web override block and the root's ignorePatterns, because oxlint matches an override's `files` and a config's `ignorePatterns` relative to the CONFIG FILE's directory, so the root's repo-rooted spellings stop matching the moment this app is linted through its own config. A restatement is a copy, and a copy drifts.

The guard resolves both configs the way oxlint does — compile each glob to a RegExp, match it against real paths, fold the matching blocks in order, last one wins — and it is genuinely good: it catches a rule added to the root's wallow-web block, a root block re-globbed with brace alternation, a nested block appended after the restatement, and it FAILS LOUDLY on a glob whose syntax it cannot model (extglob, character class, negation).

THE ROOT CAUSE THIS BEAD FIXES. That loud default is keyed on a whitelist of literal characters, so it catches an unmodelled SYNTAX but not a mis-normalised PATH. A glob spelled entirely in whitelisted characters compiles without complaint and then silently matches nothing — which is exactly the invisible non-application the guard exists to make visible, reproduced one level up. Fix the class, not the two cases below.

TWO SPELLINGS THAT EVADE IT TODAY (both demonstrated with the real binary while verifying Wallow-lrlm.5.6; full evidence in that bead's round-3 note):

N1 — A `./`-PREFIXED OVERRIDE GLOB. oxlint treats `./apps/<app>/**/*.{ts,tsx}` exactly like the unprefixed form; measured, a wallow-auth file reports `error eslint(eqeqeq)` under both spellings and a warning under neither. With the root carrying
    {"files":["./apps/wallow-web/**/*.{ts,tsx}","./apps/wallow-auth/**/*.{ts,tsx}"],"rules":{"eqeqeq":"error"}}
    wallow-auth (root config only) -> ERROR   — the declaration is real and effective
    wallow-web  (nested config)    -> WARNING — silently does not apply
    the drift guard -> 37/37 PASS. Not caught.
globToRegExp compiles the leading `./` literally, so the compiled pattern matches no repo-relative path and the block reads as not reaching this app. This is not an exotic spelling: the repo already writes `./`-prefixed paths in these very files (both configs' `$schema` keys).

N2 — A GITIGNORE-STYLE BARE ignorePatterns ENTRY. oxlint's ignorePatterns are gitignore-semantic: an unanchored bare name matches at ANY depth. Measured — adding "probecov" hides apps/wallow-auth/probecov/probe-eq.ts from a directory walk, the anchored "probecov/**" does NOT, and "**/probecov/**" does. With the root's ignorePatterns gaining "probecov":
    walk apps/wallow-auth -> [] (root pattern effective)
    walk apps/wallow-web  -> still reports apps/wallow-web/probecov/probe-eq.ts — the nested config never restated it
    the drift guard -> 37/37 PASS. Not caught.
REQUIRED_IGNORES builds `apps/wallow-web/<candidate>` and asks the pattern to match it; a bare name compiled to an anchored `^probecov$` never does, so the pattern is dropped. This is precisely the harm the guard's own comment names — the linter starts reading generated output and blaming this app for what it finds there.

MINOR, NOT LIVE TODAY: APP_FILES walks only .ts/.tsx, so a root block declared for `**/*.{js,jsx,mjs,cjs}` inside this app would be compared against nothing. wallow-web has 0 such files today (verified), so nothing is uncovered right now.

NOT A GATE DEFECT. The F5 lint gate itself (Wallow-lrlm.5.6) is proven firing and was closed on that basis; this is defence-in-depth on the guard that protects the gate's configuration, which is why it was split out rather than cycled.
design:
Fix the normalisation, not the two spellings — the same defect will return in a third form otherwise.

Both misses live in the same place: apps/wallow-web/src/lint-gate.test.ts's globToRegExp / compileGlob / globMatches, and the REQUIRED_IGNORES derivation built on them. The guard is textual by design and for a stated reason (the failure mode it hunts is the CHILD being SILENT about something the root declares, and silence has no diagnostic to observe; measuring it behaviourally would mean mutating the root config mid-run, which races pnpm lint). Keep that design. Only the path model needs to become faithful.

Two semantics to model, both measured against oxlint 1.74.0 rather than assumed:
  - an override `files` glob may be written `./`-prefixed and means the same thing unprefixed;
  - `ignorePatterns` are gitignore-semantic, so an unanchored pattern (one containing no `/`) matches at any depth, and a directory pattern covers everything beneath it — while an anchored one (`probecov/**`) does not float.

Then close the class: the existing "understands every glob spelling the two configs use" case only proves a glob COMPILES. Make it also prove the compiled form is canonical, so a spelling that compiles but normalises wrong is as loud as one that does not compile at all. Asserting each declared glob round-trips through a canonical form is one way; any mechanism that turns "I modelled this differently from oxlint" into a named failure is acceptable.

Do not touch the gate itself: the rule config in apps/wallow-web/.oxlintrc.json, the element list, the ban set, the bare-form-only equality test in tools/oxlint/wallow-lint-plugin.js, the carve-outs (BACKDROP_SCRIM, LandingPage.tsx's bare border-foreground, the Wallow-6uqv-linked MFA deferral) and the app scope are all verified correct and out of scope here.
acceptance_criteria:
1. A root override block globbed `./apps/wallow-web/**/*.{ts,tsx}` that declares a rule the nested config does not restate FAILS the drift guard. (Today: 37/37 green.)
2. A root `ignorePatterns` entry written gitignore-style as a bare unanchored name, not restated in the nested config, FAILS the drift guard. (Today: 37/37 green.)
3. The loud default is extended from "this glob does not compile" to "this glob does not normalise the way oxlint resolves it", so a third mis-normalised spelling is named rather than silently dropped.
4. No false positives: a root pattern anchored at another package or another app (packages/sdk/src/generated/**, apps/wallow-auth/.vite/**) is still NOT demanded of this app's config, and the guard stays green on the unmutated tree.
5. Every previously-caught case still fails the guard — the root's wallow-web block gaining a rule, a brace-alternation root glob, an appended nested block that turns a restatement off, and an extglob or character-class glob.
6. pnpm --filter @bc-solutions-coder/wallow-web test, pnpm lint, pnpm typecheck and pnpm format:check all pass, and the F5 gate still fires on a reintroduced raw text element and a bare sidebar-inversion class.
notes:
Filed by the verifier while ruling on Wallow-lrlm.5.6 (round 3). That bead was CLOSED: its acceptance criterion is the gate, and the gate is proven firing (pnpm lint exit 1 naming react(forbid-elements) and wallow(no-sidebar-inversion) on a reintroduced violation), with 5158/5158 tests and lint/typecheck/format:check all clean. This bead is the residue only. Reproduction for both cases, and the oxlint semantics probes behind them (./-prefix equivalence, gitignore-style bare-name matching at any depth, last-wins override resolution, child-blocks-after-root-blocks fold order, and the config-directory-relative jsPlugins resolution that forces the nested config in the first place) are all written out in Wallow-lrlm.5.6's round-3 note. Read that before starting — every claim there was measured against oxlint 1.74.0, not recalled. Priority set to P3: this hardens a test, not shipped behaviour, and the guard already catches every drift anyone proposed across three verification rounds except these two corners. Bump it if the root config starts being edited often. RED. apps/wallow-web/src/lint-gate.test.ts only (37 -> 128 cases; 21 failing, 107 passing). lint 0, format:check 0, typecheck 0. git status: only this file modified (the untracked MemberList.picker.test.tsx belongs to Wallow-lrlm.6.1's agent, not me). === HOW THE CLASS IS CLOSED, NOT THE TWO CASES === The guard's misses are unobservable by construction: a mis-normalised glob resolves to nothing, which is indistinguishable from "this block does not reach this app". So the new cases do not assert against a table of remembered spellings -- they ASK OXLINT what each glob means, on every run, and hold the guard to that answer. A spelling nobody has tried is then either resolved correctly or NAMED; it can no longer be silently dropped. THE ORACLE (new, in-spec): a throwaway miniature of this repo's shape written to a mkdtemp dir OUTSIDE the repo, with its own self-contained .oxlintrc.json, linted by the repo's own oxlint. oxlint resolves overrides/ignorePatterns relative to the CONFIG FILE's directory, so the sandbox is judged by exactly the rules the real configs are judged by. No config pnpm lint reads is touched and nothing races it -- which is what the design note required. probeReported/oxlintOverrideReach/oxlintIgnoreReach + guardOverrideReach/guardIgnoreReach. `measures the real binary, on a tree that discriminates` guards the oracle itself: if the sandbox linted nothing, every comparison would compare two empty lists and pass. ORACLE GOTCHA, MEASURED, COST ME A DEBUG CYCLE -- WORTH KNOWING FOR THE FIX: `-c` must be handed the config path RELATIVE to cwd. title: F6.T6 — Decide whether the sidebar-* token family should be renamed inverse-*
description:
The sidebar-* token family (--color-sidebar / --color-sidebar-foreground / --color-sidebar-accent, packages/styles/styles.css:43-45, fed by sidebar/sidebarForeground/sidebarAccent in api/branding.json) is now used by FOUR surfaces, only one of which is a sidebar:

  - the dashboard rail and mobile drawer (Wallow-lrlm.5.4) — an actual sidebar
  - PublicLayout's footer (Wallow-lrlm.5.3, ruling C1)
  - LandingPage's StepsBand (Wallow-lrlm.5.3, ruling J6)
  - LandingPage's outline CTA hover (Wallow-lrlm.5.3, ruling C2)

plus packages/ui's Text component, whose color prop spells the family as color="onSidebar". Wallow-lrlm.5.3's adjudication raised renaming the family to inverse-* (or another surface-neutral name) as an explicit follow-up candidate and deferred it; Wallow-lrlm.5.4's verification confirmed it is still open and owned by nobody. It exists only as prose in two beads' notes today, which is how it gets lost.

This is a DECIDE-THEN-EXECUTE task: the first deliverable is a yes/no, and 'no, keep sidebar-*, and record why' is an acceptable outcome that closes it.
design:
DECIDE FIRST. The case for renaming: three of the four consumers are not sidebars, so the name misdescribes the token and invites a fork to rebrand its footer by editing a key called sidebar. The case against is a hard fork-compatibility constraint that must be weighed before any renaming starts:

  api/branding.json is marked merge=ours in .gitattributes. A fork's copy never receives new or renamed keys from an upstream merge. Rename sidebar -> inverse in branding.json and every existing fork silently loses the palette: their file still says sidebar, the theme emits --sidebar, and the new --color-inverse finds nothing.

The existing two-level fallback was designed for exactly this class of problem — packages/styles/styles.css:43-45 is var(--sidebar, var(--foreground)) etc. — so a rename that is safe for forks must keep reading the OLD property name in the fallback chain, e.g. --color-inverse: var(--inverse, var(--sidebar, var(--foreground))). Any proposal that does not do this should be rejected outright.

IF THE DECISION IS TO RENAME, the blast radius is: packages/styles/styles.css @theme; api/branding.json (both light and dark blocks) and its branding types; packages/styles/src/theme-css.test.ts's token map and palette list; packages/ui's Text color prop value onSidebar and its stories/specs; every consumer class string in apps/wallow-web (DashboardNav.tsx, DashboardLayout.tsx, PublicLayout.tsx, LandingPage.tsx) and their restyle specs; apps/wallow-web/src/shared/testing/style-contract.ts; and any wallow-auth adoption that has landed by then.

SEQUENCING (recommendation, no dependency edge added): if this is approved, run it BEFORE Wallow-lrlm.7.1, so wallow-auth adopts the final name once instead of being renamed twice. It should also land after Wallow-lrlm.5.6's lint gate so the gate's patterns are written against the final names.
acceptance_criteria:
1. A decision is recorded on this bead with its reasoning, explicitly addressing the branding.json merge=ours fork-compatibility constraint.
2. If the decision is NO: the bead closes with the rationale recorded, and packages/styles/styles.css gains a comment stating that the sidebar-* family is the theme's general inverted-surface family and is deliberately used by non-sidebar surfaces — so the question is not reopened a third time. No code changes.
3. If the decision is YES: the rename is applied across every consumer listed in DESIGN; the @theme fallback chain still resolves the OLD property name so a fork whose branding.json predates the rename keeps its palette; no fork-facing key is silently orphaned; and pnpm check is green repo-wide.
notes:
RULING (decide-only pass; no code touched): **KEEP `sidebar-*`. Do not rename to `inverse-*`, and do not add an `inverse-*` alias.** Execute AC #2. This is a final ruling — the next agent should not re-litigate it.

== 1. RE-DERIVED CONSUMER INVENTORY (searched, not trusted) ==
174 `sidebar` hits across 30 files; the ones that touch the TOKEN FAMILY (the rest are docfx nav prose, docs/toc wording, and navigation-menu `data-testid`s, which are NOT the family):

DEFINITION
- packages/styles/styles.css:43-45 (@theme), :15-19 (header comment already explains the fork-safe fallback)
- api/branding.json:29-31 (light), :56-58 (dark)

packages/ui (PUBLISHED @bc-solutions-coder/ui)
- src/components/text/text.styles.ts:44 `onSidebar: "text-sidebar-foreground"` — a PUBLIC prop value
- src/components/text/text.test.tsx:78, text.stories.tsx:64
- src/components/text/__screenshots__/text.test.tsx/Text-semantic-colour-maps-color-onSidebar-onto-text-sidebar-foreground-1.png (committed baseline; the NAME is in the filename)
- token allowlists: button/button.test.tsx:106-108, badge/badge.test.tsx:113, empty-state/empty-state.composition.test.ts:168

apps/wallow-web (the ONLY app that consumes the family)
- shared/components/DashboardNav.tsx:95,98,211,232,276 (rail + mobile drawer)
- shared/components/PublicLayout.tsx:93,102,116,133 (footer band)
- features/landing/components/LandingPage.tsx:123 (outline-CTA hover), :208-219 (StepsBand Text), :245,:247 (band section)
- shared/components/DashboardLayout.tsx:47,115 — COMMENTS ONLY; the scrim deliberately does not use the family
- specs: DashboardNav.restyle/.catalog, DashboardLayout.restyle/.ssr-flash, PublicLayout.restyle, LandingPage.restyle, shared/components/dashboard-chrome-tokens.test.ts:27,68,93-118, src/typography.test.ts:121-164
- 2 committed screenshot baselines whose FILENAMES encode "sidebar token pair": shared/components/__screenshots__/PublicLayout.restyle.test.tsx/..., features/landing/components/__screenshots__/LandingPage.restyle.test.tsx/...
- apps/wallow-web/.oxlintrc.json:14,74 + tools/oxlint/wallow-lint-plugin.js — rule id `wallow/no-sidebar-inversion`, whose message text names bg-sidebar/text-sidebar-foreground/hover:bg-sidebar-accent

ZERO CONSUMERS: apps/wallow-auth (no `sidebar`, no `inverse`, no `bg-foreground`/`text-background` anywhere in src/); all of api/**/*.cs (no C# binds theme keys — the theme block is open-ended `Record<string,string>`); docs/** (no guide names these tokens; frontend-setup.md's add-a-theme-key recipe is generic); scripts/generate-docs-theme.mjs (names only background/primary/card/border/accent).

CORRECTION TO THIS BEAD'S OWN DESIGN: it lists `apps/wallow-web/src/shared/testing/style-contract.ts` in the blast radius. That file exists (11.9 KB) and contains ZERO `sidebar` references. The DESIGN inventory is wrong there — one more instance of the epic-wide "inventories in bead bodies are incomplete/incorrect" lesson.

== 2. THE CRUX: is it a general inverse-surface family today? ==
YES — 3 of 4 consumers are not sidebars (footer band, StepsBand, outline-CTA hover). The name genuinely misdescribes the family. That is the ENTIRE case for renaming, and it is a real but purely cosmetic one: every consumer already carries an in-file comment saying the family means "inverted band" (LandingPage.tsx:208-210, PublicLayout.tsx:114-115, dashboard-chrome-tokens.test.ts:25-27), so no contributor is actually being misled by it in the tree today.

== 3. THE CASE AGAINST — three costs, one of them decisive ==

(a) DECISIVE, and NOT fixable by the fallback chain: renaming the branding key silently DISABLES existing per-client theme overrides.
packages/styles/src/branding.ts mergeClientBranding merges `{...forkLight, ...parseThemeCssVars(themeJson,"light")}` — a per-OAuth-client override wins only when the KEY NAME MATCHES the fork's. ThemeJson is opaque operator-authored data stored in the Branding module's DB (POST /v1/identity/apps/{clientId}/branding), passed through verbatim.
After a rename, upstream branding.json emits `--inverse`; a stored client row still says `sidebar` and emits `--sidebar`. No key collision, so BOTH are declared, and `--color-inverse: var(--inverse, var(--sidebar, ...))` resolves to the FORK's colour — the client's override stops applying, with no error and no build failure. CSS `var()` fallback is first-defined-wins, not most-specific-source-wins, so no fallback chain can express "prefer the client's old-named value over the fork's new-named one." The mitigation this bead's DESIGN mandates therefore protects the fork-file case but cannot protect the client-branding case at all. A silent per-tenant colour regression in a multi-tenant product is a worse defect than an imprecise token name.

(b) It is a breaking change on TWO public surfaces for a cosmetic gain: the fork-facing `branding.json` key (merge=ours, so forks are stranded on the old name forever and the tree carries both names permanently) AND `Text`'s `color="onSidebar"` prop value in the published @bc-solutions-coder/ui. Either alone would require `feat!:`/`BREAKING CHANGE:`. Spending a major bump on a rename is not proportionate.

(c) Blast radius is ~15 source/spec files plus 3 committed screenshot baselines that must be renamed AND regenerated, plus the lint rule id and its message. Every one of those edits is churn with zero behavioural delta.

ALIAS-AND-DEPRECATE REJECTED SEPARATELY: adding `--color-inverse` next to `--color-sidebar` ships two Tailwind utility families for one colour. It does not remove the bad name (that was the whole point), it forces every future contributor and every lint pattern to handle both, and design-token aliases added "temporarily" are how a tree ends up with both names permanently. It buys nothing (a) does not already veto.

== 4. WHAT UNBLOCKS Wallow-lrlm.7.1 ==
7.1 IS ALREADY EFFECTIVELY UNBLOCKED, UNDER EVERY OUTCOME. Verified: apps/wallow-auth/src has zero references to the family, zero `bg-foreground`/`text-background` to migrate, and no inverted band (no footer band, no StepsBand equivalent). 7.1's scope is Text/PageHeader/Button/ThemeToggle adoption; none of those force `color="onSidebar"` unless wallow-auth grows an inverted surface, which it has not.
=> The DESIGN's sequencing argument ("run this before 7.1 so wallow-auth is not renamed twice") is VOID — there is no second migration to save. Under KEEP, 7.1 proceeds with no constraint whatsoever. Coordinator can drop any dependency edge from 7.1 to this bead.

== 5. EXECUTION (AC #2) — the only change this bead authorises ==
ONE doc-comment edit, no behavioural change:
- packages/styles/styles.css — EXTEND THE FILE-HEADER COMMENT (lines 15-19, i.e. ABOVE `@theme {`). State that `sidebar-*` is the theme's GENERAL INVERTED-SURFACE family, deliberately used by non-sidebar surfaces (dashboard rail + drawer, PublicLayout footer, LandingPage StepsBand, outline-CTA hover), that the name is retained deliberately, and cite reason (a): renaming a branding key silently disables per-client themeJson overrides that still use the old key, because mergeClientBranding merges by key name.

*** HARD TRAP — VERIFIED BY RUNNING THE PARSER ***
DO NOT put the comment INSIDE the `@theme` block immediately above `--color-sidebar`. themeTokens() in packages/styles/src/theme-css.test.ts:41-57 splits the block body on `;` and matches each fragment with `/^\s*(?<name>--[\w-]+).../su`. A comment line preceding a declaration lands inside that declaration's fragment, the `^\s*--` anchor fails, and the token DISAPPEARS from the parse. Reproduced: with `/* ... */` above `--color-sidebar`, the parse returns `--color-ring` and `--color-success` but NOT `--color-sidebar`, so "maps --color-sidebar through the palette with a fork-safe fallback" fails. Safe placements: the file header (recommended), or after the LAST declaration's `;` and before `}`. A comment must also never contain `}` (the block regex is `[^}]*`).

Optional, cheap, same commit: a one-line doc comment on `onSidebar` in packages/ui/src/components/text/text.styles.ts:44 saying it means "on any inverted band, not only a sidebar." No prop rename.

COMMIT TYPE: `docs(styles):` or `style(styles):` — NOT a `feat!:`. Nothing behavioural changes; theme-css.test.ts's token pins stay green by construction.

Bead closes on that comment landing.
GREEN: Executed AC #2 (KEEP ruling already binding on this bead — not relitigated). FILES=packages/styles/styles.css (file-header comment only, extended lines 15-19 block, added 17 lines after the existing fallback-chain paragraph; NOT inside @theme, NOT above --color-sidebar — verified the trap was avoided). Comment states sidebar-* is the general inverted-surface family, lists the non-sidebar consumers, and cites the decisive reason: branding.ts mergeClientBranding merges per-client themeJson over the fork palette BY KEY NAME, so a rename would silently stop applying stored client overrides still spelled sidebar (CSS var() fallback is first-defined-wins and cannot express 'prefer client override over fork's new name'); also notes the two-public-surface breaking-change cost (branding.json key + ui's Text color="onSidebar"). No behavioural change, no code touched outside the comment. TEST_STATUS: pnpm --filter @bc-solutions-coder/styles test = 6 files / 98 tests PASS, including theme-css.test.ts token pins (--color-sidebar still parses correctly, header-only placement confirmed safe). oxfmt --check packages/styles/styles.css = pass. pnpm lint (repo-wide) has 3 pre-existing errors in apps/wallow-web/src/features/organizations/components/OrganizationDetail.tsx and warnings in RegisterAppForm.tsx — both FOREIGN to this task (other agents live there per coordinator), zero lint issues in packages/styles. Commit type for this change: docs(styles):.
VERIFY (change had LANDED, fully — confirmed by reading the working tree, not trusting the report):

The known trap was avoided: @theme block (lines 40-68) is byte-for-byte unchanged, --color-sidebar/-foreground/-accent declarations untouched.

title: Thread base path into wallow-web and minimal-app branding assets when they gain a prefix knob
description:
After Wallow-8via, packages/styles' toRootRelativeAssetUrl / toAppIconUrl / resolveForkBranding / mergeClientBranding all accept a basePath, and wallow-auth binds it via src/lib/branding.ts from its BASE_PATH. wallow-web and apps/examples/minimal-app still import the UNBASED package-level constants appIconUrl / forkResolvedBranding directly:

  apps/wallow-web/src/routes/__root.tsx, src/components/PublicLayout.tsx, src/features/landing/components/LandingPage.tsx
  apps/examples/minimal-app/src/routes/__root.tsx, src/features/hello/HelloCard.tsx

This is CORRECT today — neither app has a base-path knob, and basePath='' is the identity, so their URLs are unchanged. It becomes a live bug the moment either app gains a prefix (the wallow-auth AUTH_BASE_PATH equivalent): their icons would resolve at the site root, which behind a path-based ingress is a different app.

When adding a base path to either app, mirror wallow-auth's pattern — a per-app src/lib/branding.ts binding the prefix once, with screens importing branding from there rather than from @bc-solutions-coder/styles.
notes:
AUDIT 2026-08-02 (docs/audits/2026-08-02/0824-bead-backlog) — VERDICT: CLOSE (not needed). NOT CLOSED YET: its own precondition is unmet.

WHY IT IS NOT NEEDED: this is a conditional filed where its trigger will never be read. packages/env's ./base-path entry exists, but neither apps/wallow-web/src nor apps/examples/minimal-app/src consumes a base-path knob, and none of the 66 active beads proposes giving either app a prefix. The trigger for this bead lives OUTSIDE the tracker — nothing in the backlog will ever cause someone to read it. DEFER is therefore the wrong disposition: a deferred bead still waits on a tracker event, and there is none.

PRECONDITION BEFORE CLOSING: the guidance in this bead's description (mirror wallow-auth's pattern — a per-app src/lib/branding.ts binding the prefix once, screens importing the bound helpers rather than the package-level constants) must first be moved to where a future implementer will actually be standing: apps/wallow-auth/src/shared/lib/base-path.ts and the fork guide (docs/getting-started/fork-guide.md). Close only once that relocation has landed; otherwise the knowledge is lost with the bead.

This note is a hand-off — the relocation is a repo edit and was out of scope for the agent applying the audit's bead actions.
TRIAGE 2026-08-27 (docs/plans/2026-08-27/1127-backlog-triage-and-sequencing.md) - CLOSING; the 2026-08-02 audit's stated PRECONDITION has now been satisfied.

The audit verdict was CLOSE-not-needed, blocked only on relocating this bead's guidance to where a future implementer would actually be standing. That relocation has landed:

title: Isolate concurrent e2e.sh runs from each other (parameterized project name + host ports)
description: Wallow-kd2e scoped the e2e stack to Compose project 'wallow-test' so teardown can no longer remove the dev-infra stack. title: Backend-dependent auth E2E specs hardcode docker-compose.test.yml endpoints
description:
Three wallow-auth backend-dependent specs pin ports that only exist in docker/docker-compose.test.yml, so they cannot pass against an Aspire-run backend (pnpm backend):

1. e2e/mailpit.ts:20 - MAILPIT_URL defaults to http://127.0.0.1:8035, which is ONLY the compose test stack mapping (127.0.0.1:8035:8025). Under Aspire the API delivers to the standing wallow-mailpit on :8025 (or the Aspire-managed mailpit on a random host port). Affects magic-link, otp-login, reset-password, mfa. There IS an E2E_MAILPIT_URL override, but the default makes a bare Aspire run fail with ECONNREFUSED.
2. e2e/logout.spec.ts:21 - ALLOWED_REDIRECT_URI hardcodes http://localhost:5051/after-logout, the compose stack's AuthUrl that OpenIddictRedirectUriValidator allow-lists. Under Aspire the AuthUrl differs, no return link renders, spec fails. Worth deriving from env.
3. The API's dev passwordless rate limiter (raised in 551066a9) still trips magic-link + otp-login after repeated local runs and does not clear within 5 minutes, making back-to-back local iteration impossible.

Suggested fix: derive all three from env with compose values as fallback, matching how WALLOW_API_INTERNAL_URL is already handled in the playwright configs.

Evidence: Wallow-ov6w.5.2 notes (part 3 gate). Pre-existing; NOT caused by the forms epic - proven by a control run of the same specs on the main tree, which fails identically.
notes:
2026-07-30 audit: parts 1 and 2 CONFIRMED still present (e2e/mailpit.ts:20, e2e/logout.spec.ts:21). Part 3 (dev passwordless rate limiter) is STALE — api/src/Wallow.Api/appsettings.Development.json now sets Passwordless.RateLimitMaxRequests: 1000. Drop part 3 from scope.
Fixed in 02c4e26d.

The bead's framing (and the plan's) assumed E2E_BASE_URL could tell a local backend from a containerised one. It cannot: it selects how the wallow-auth APP is served, and scripts/e2e.sh's DEFAULT mode leaves it unset while still driving the containerised API. Deriving ports from it read :8025/:3002 against a stack serving :8035/:5051 — proved by a real run, 5 specs red (the 4 mailpit readers + the logout allow-list check).

Ownership inverted instead: e2e.sh exports E2E_MAILPIT_URL and E2E_AUTH_ORIGIN on every path it takes, and the specs default to a local backend.

Second blocker found while verifying, fixed in the same commit: a local Mailpit is long-lived, so waitForEmailBody matched a PREVIOUS run's email (redeemed magic link / OTP, or a reset token invalidated by that run's own password change). It relied on the empty volumes e2e.sh gets from 'down -v'. Added seenEmailIds() + an 'ignore' option; the three fixed-recipient specs snapshot before triggering. Matching IDs, not timestamps — no clock is shared with Mailpit's container. mfa/signup use per-run addresses and were never exposed.

Verified: ./scripts/e2e.sh green (30 + 2 + 2), and a local backend (dev-infra + dotnet run Wallow.Api + seeder) run twice back-to-back so the second faced a dirty inbox (30, 30).

Part 3 of this bead (dev passwordless rate limiter) is stale and was deliberately not touched.

title: Spike: runtime response validation at the Node BFF boundary (server-side, not the browser bundle)
description: Follow-up from the Wallow-pu6a.5.7 zod-plugin spike, which returned NO-GO on hey-api's zod plugin. The plugin's validators are baked into sdk.gen.ts and therefore land in every app's BROWSER bundle (measured: +24.4 kB gzip for a 5-operation import, of which ~19.2 kB is the zod 4 runtime floor), re-validating data that already crossed our own same-origin BFF proxy. This bead captures the placement that would actually be worth paying for, if runtime validation is wanted at all.
design: Validate on the NODE side (packages/sdk/src/server), where the proxy talks to the real API: bundle cost is zero for end users, and a validation failure can be turned into a proper 502 / WallowError at the actual trust boundary instead of surfacing as a thrown ZodError on an HTTP 200. Prerequisite finding from 5.7: the committed openapi/v1.json snapshot has fidelity gaps that any validator will trip on -- z.iso.datetime() rejects non-UTC DateTimeOffset values (proven against AccountLoginResponse.mfaGraceDeadline), and required+nullable properties throw when the serializer omits them (proven against MfaStatusResponse.method). CI's openapi-drift job checks the snapshot against the live spec, never the spec against actually-serialized payloads, so those gaps must be closed (or the validator configured around them, e.g. dates.offset) BEFORE any validation is switched on anywhere. Do not start this while the Phase 4 WallowError unification is still in flight.
acceptance_criteria: Either a working server-side validation design with measured cost and a plan for the snapshot-fidelity gaps, or an explicit written-up decision that Wallow does no runtime payload validation and relies on the generated types plus the drift check.
notes:
AUDIT 2026-08-02 (docs/audits/2026-08-02/0824-bead-backlog) — RETYPED task -> chore (applied). DO NOT CLOSE IT BARE.

The 'do not start yet' gate in this bead HAS cleared: WallowError is now unified via the global symbol registry, and there is zero zod in the SDK. But no open bead consumes this spike's answer — a ten-bead sweep found none; the nearest, Wallow-qw03.5, is about compile-time type generation, which is a different thing.

So the spike framing is dead, but the bead still carries the only durable record of two live SDK/OpenAPI fidelity gaps, and closing it bare would lose them:
  1. AccountLoginResponse.mfaGraceDeadline is nullable-typed in the generated client where the API does not treat it as nullable.
  2. MfaStatusResponse.required omits 'method', while 'method' is itself nullable.

STILL OUTSTANDING (not applied here — the audit assigns the rewrite separately): rewrite this as a documentation chore whose deliverable is recording those two gaps somewhere durable. Once they are written down, this bead can close.
RESOLVED PER THE 2026-08-02 AUDIT REWRITE, 2026-08-28: the durable record now exists in docs/integrations/typescript-sdk.md, section 'No runtime payload validation — a deliberate decision' (under 'Keeping the SDK in step with the API'). It records (a) the explicit decision that Wallow does no runtime payload validation — generated types + openapi-drift are the contract, with the measured browser cost (+24.4 kB gzip / ~19.2 kB zod floor) and the server-side BFF placement that would be the design if ever revisited; and (b) both fidelity gaps, re-verified against the current committed snapshot today before writing: AccountLoginResponse.mfaGraceDeadline is still a nullable date-time (non-UTC offset hazard for z.iso.datetime()), and MfaStatusResponse.method is still required+nullable (serializer-omission hazard). This satisfies acceptance-criteria option 2 (explicit written-up no-validation decision). Note: this bead's 2026-08-02 audit note restated gap 1 as a client-nullability mismatch — that restatement does not match the original spike finding or the current spec; the doc records the original, proven form.
close_reason: Acceptance criteria met via option 2: docs/integrations/typescript-sdk.md now carries the explicit decision that Wallow does no runtime payload validation (generated types + openapi-drift are the contract), with the measured browser cost, the server-side BFF placement if ever revisited, and both snapshot-fidelity gaps (mfaGraceDeadline non-UTC offsets, MfaStatusResponse.method required+nullable omission) re-verified against the current snapshot and written down durably. Not closed bare — the gaps the audit wanted preserved are in user-facing docs now.

title: Local-mode E2E cold-start fragility in backend-dependent specs
description: Found during the Wallow-m5aq.5.4 E2E gate: in local (non-container) mode, Vite cold-compile can overrun the Playwright webServer readiness timeout, and a stale dev server on :3002 can be hijacked via reuseExistingServer. Container mode unaffected. Pre-existing, not caused by the ui-catalog epic. Evidence on Wallow-m5aq.5.4 notes.
notes:
2026-07-30 audit: both filed symptoms now appear fixed in apps/wallow-auth/e2e/global-setup.ts — a 120s route-by-route warm-up to data-app-ready (WARMUP_PATHS) covers the Vite cold-compile overrun, and assertAppTargetsTheExpectedApi() compares the OIDC discovery issuer served through the app against the one read from WALLOW_API_INTERNAL_URL, throwing with an lsof diagnostic on mismatch, which covers the reuseExistingServer hijack. Close after one confirming local-mode run of the wallow-auth suite.
2026-07-30 verification: both filed symptoms confirmed fixed against a live local stack (dev-infra + dotnet run Wallow.Api on :5001). Closing.

1. Vite cold-compile overrun -- FIXED by the WARMUP_PATHS walk in apps/wallow-auth/e2e/global-setup.ts.
   Deleted apps/wallow-auth/node_modules/.vite, then ran 'pnpm --filter ./apps/wallow-auth test:e2e'.
   The run rebuilt the dep cache from scratch (294 files in node_modules/.vite/deps) and still reported
   '30 passed (11.8s)', exit 0 -- no spec paid the pre-bundle cost, the global setup absorbed it on its
   120s budget. Slowest spec was 4.5s (mfa totp enrollment), nowhere near the default 5s expect budget
   that used to lose the race.

2. reuseExistingServer hijack -- FIXED by assertAppTargetsTheExpectedApi() in the same file.
   Reproduced the exact filed scenario: an orphan 'pnpm dev' on :3002 wired to the real API
   (WALLOW_API_INTERNAL_URL=http://localhost:5001), then ran the suite with
   WALLOW_API_INTERNAL_URL pointed at a DIFFERENT reachable API. Playwright adopted the orphan
   (webServer.env never reaches a server it did not start) and global setup aborted the whole run
   before any spec, exit 1, with the intended diagnostic:
     'the app under test is proxying to the WRONG API.
        app under test  http://localhost:3002 -> issuer http://localhost:3002/
        expected        http://localhost:5099 -> issuer http://stub-api.invalid:5099/'
   plus the lsof hint. The mismatch branch (global-setup.ts:120) is what threw.

   Note the second API was a throwaway node stub serving only /.well-known/openid-configuration --
   the guard's whole logic is an issuer-string comparison, and both origins were genuinely reachable,
   so the stub exercises the real mismatch path. A wrong-but-UNREACHABLE URL (e.g. :9999) does NOT
   test this: readIssuer throws, the catch warns and returns, and the check is skipped by design.

Local-mode context: this ran after the Wallow-ll6c fix (commit 02c4e26d), which is what makes a
local-backend run of the mail specs viable at all.

title: Collapsed dashboard nav rail clips its link labels instead of showing icons
description: In apps/wallow-web the dashboard nav drawer (apps/wallow-web/src/components/DashboardNav.tsx) is w-16 when collapsed and w-64 when open, with overflow-x-hidden. In the collapsed default state the full text labels (Apps, Settings, Inquiries, Sign Out) are still rendered at full size and are simply clipped by the rail, so the sidebar reads as broken text ('Settin', 'Inquir', 'Sign O') rather than as a deliberate icon rail. Expanding via the Menu toggle works correctly (256px, full labels, active highlight). Pre-existing on main - untouched by the design-restore branch; last changed by commit 0682d684. Fix direction: either render icon-only affordances in the collapsed rail or hide the labels, rather than clipping them.
design: Rework apps/wallow-web/src/components/DashboardNav.tsx + DashboardLayout.tsx from today's single-boolean model (useUiStore.isNavOpen, shared by both the desktop w-16/w-64 rail width AND the click-outside backdrop) into three deliberate modes: (1) expanded desktop (~w-64, icon+label per item, current default preserved), (2) collapsed icon-rail desktop (toggle-only, icon-only with accessible name, no clipped text), (3) mobile overlay drawer below the responsive breakpoint (rail absent entirely, menu button opens a full-content overlay with backdrop, closes on backdrop click / nav click / Escape). Desktop rail collapse and mobile drawer-open are DIFFERENT axes of state today conflated into one boolean — they need decoupling (e.g. isNavCollapsed for desktop rail + isMobileNavOpen for the mobile drawer) since a mobile-open drawer must NOT imply a desktop-collapsed rail and vice versa. No icon library exists anywhere in the workspace yet (checked apps/wallow-web, packages/ui, root package.json) — one must be selected and added as a dependency. Nav items today: Organizations (admin-gated), Apps, Settings, Inquiries, Sign Out — all four/five need an icon. Sidebar state is Zustand-only per docs/development/frontend-state.md (apps/wallow-web/src/stores/ui-store.ts), never TanStack Query.
acceptance_criteria:
- Desktop collapsed state renders icons only — no text nodes visible/clipped.
- Desktop toggle switches expanded <-> collapsed; active-route highlight (existing TanStack Router active-link styling) works in both.
- On a mobile-width viewport the icon rail is entirely absent; the menu button opens an overlay drawer with backdrop; the drawer closes on backdrop click, on nav-link click, and on Escape key.
- All nav destinations (Organizations when admin, Apps, Settings, Inquiries, Sign Out) remain reachable in every mode and keep accessible names (aria-label or equivalent on icon-only controls).
- Vitest browser-mode component tests (real Chromium, never jsdom) cover all three modes.
- Existing wallow-web tests, 'pnpm check', and the wallow-web Playwright route-reachability suite (apps/wallow-web/e2e/routes.spec.ts) pass.
notes:
SCOUT FILES: apps/wallow-web/src/components/DashboardNav.tsx (76 lines) - aside#dashboard-nav w-16/data-[nav-open=true]:w-64 overflow-x-hidden, single 'isNavOpen' from useUiStore, one linkClass const, 4 Link testids (dashboard-nav-organizations/apps/settings/inquiries kebab {page}-{element}) + dashboard-logout-link button calling sdk logout(). apps/wallow-web/src/components/DashboardLayout.tsx - NavToggle (dashboard-nav-toggle, aria-controls=dashboard-nav, aria-expanded={isNavOpen}) + NavBackdrop (dashboard-nav-backdrop, only rendered when isNavOpen, fixed left-64 z-10) both extracted as separate fns purely to satisfy oxlint react/jsx-max-depth (default max via pedantic:warn category, no override in .oxlintrc.json). Root data-testid=dashboard-welcome. Rendered by the /dashboard layout route (search 'DashboardLayout' import in apps/wallow-web/src/routes for the route file).

SCOUT ICONS: confirmed NO icon library/package anywhere in the workspace - grepped lucide|heroicons|react-icons|@tabler|phosphor|@radix-ui/react-icons|feather across root package.json, apps/*/package.json, packages/*/package.json: zero hits. packages/ui/src has no icon component pattern either. Must be added fresh as a workspace dep (apps/wallow-web/package.json unless shared -> packages/ui). No existing aria-label/sr-only pattern for icon-only controls anywhere in wallow-web except DashboardLayout.tsx's NavBackdrop (aria-label='Close navigation') - that's the only accessible-icon-button precedent to mirror.

SCOUT STATE: apps/wallow-web/src/stores/ui-store.ts - single Zustand store (zustand ^5.0.8, create<UiState>()((set)=>...)), UiState={isNavOpen, toggleNav, closeNav}. Module-scope singleton (see 'shares one instance across importers' test). ui-store.test.ts asserts Object.keys(getState()).toSorted() EXACT MATCH ['closeNav','isNavOpen','toggleNav'] - this test WILL need rewriting to the new key set, don't just extend it, the exact-keys assertion will fail otherwise. docs/development/frontend-state.md confirms Zustand=UI-only/no queryKey state (sidebar collapsed/expanded is the doc's own example of what belongs here).

SCOUT BREAKPOINTS: packages/styles/styles.css defines only color/radius theme tokens via @theme - no custom breakpoints, so Tailwind v4 DEFAULT breakpoints apply (sm=40rem/640px, md=48rem/768px, lg=64rem/1024px). Precedent for md:/sm: prefixes ALREADY EXISTS elsewhere in wallow-web (LandingPage.tsx uses md:grid-cols-2/3, lg:grid-cols-3; MfaSettingsSection.tsx uses sm:grid-cols-2) - task .2's design note claiming 'this app has no responsive classes anywhere yet' is inaccurate for the app as a whole (true only for DashboardNav/DashboardLayout specifically). Recommend md: as the mobile/desktop boundary to match existing convention.

SCOUT TEST-PATTERNS: apps/wallow-web/src/components/DashboardNav.test.tsx + .toggle.test.tsx + .gate.test.tsx and DashboardLayout.test.tsx + .toggle.test.tsx are the 5 files to extend (all vitest-browser-react + vitest/browser page/userEvent, real Chromium). All mock @tanstack/react-router's Link as a plain anchor (vi.mock pattern shown at top of each file); DashboardLayout specs also mock Outlet. .toggle.test.tsx files reset store via useUiStore.setState({isNavOpen:false}) in beforeEach - the new decoupled state needs both isNavCollapsed/isMobileNavOpen reset per new store shape. apps/wallow-web/e2e/routes.spec.ts is backend-free and explicitly EXCLUDES /dashboard/** routes (auth-gated, needs BFF login) - confirmed it does not touch dashboard-nav-* testids at all, so .3's acceptance 'routes.spec.ts passes unchanged' should hold with no edits needed there.

GOTCHAS: (1) ui-store.test.ts's exact-keys assertion is a deliberate trip-wire per its own comment ('force the discussion') - expect it to fail immediately until rewritten for the new two-axis shape. (2) NavToggle/NavBackdrop's jsx-max-depth-driven extraction pattern should be mirrored for any new mobile-menu-button/mobile-drawer components rather than inlining deeper JSX. (3) DashboardNav currently takes NO breakpoint-driven conditional rendering at all - introducing md: there is genuinely new for these two files even though not new for the app.
FEATURE-LEVEL VERIFY (union of .1+.2+.3, independently re-checked):
[✓] Desktop collapsed renders icons only, no clipped/visible text — DashboardNav.tsx NavItem: label rendered only when showLabel=true, aria-label always set from navIconLabels; confirmed by direct code read.
[✓] Desktop toggle switches expanded<->collapsed only; active-route highlight works both — activeProps={{className:activeItemClass}} applied unconditionally on every Link; NavToggle calls only toggleNavCollapsed. title: routeTree.gen.ts ordering differs between tsr generate (CLI) and the vite router-plugin
description:
Running 'vite build' or the dev server rewrites apps/wallow-web/src/routeTree.gen.ts and apps/wallow-auth/src/routeTree.gen.ts with a different import/route-declaration ORDER than the committed content, dirtying the tree on every build. The diff is a pure reorder (verified: 0 net-unique lines both files).

The committed content is what 'pnpm --filter ./apps/<app> routes:generate' (tsr generate, @tanstack/router-cli) emits - verified byte-for-byte on wallow-web from a clean tree. The reorder comes from @tanstack/router-plugin used by vite. The two packages are on skewed versions in apps/wallow-web/package.json (@tanstack/router-cli ^1.167.21 vs @tanstack/router-plugin ^1.168.20).

Pre-existing on main, not introduced by feat/restore-web-design (wallow-auth's routeTree is untouched by that branch and shows the same reorder).

Fix: align the router-cli and router-plugin versions, then regenerate and commit whichever ordering both agree on. Until then, discard the post-build diff (git show HEAD:<path> > <path>; do NOT use git checkout -- per the destructive-git memory).
design: Root cause is version skew between @tanstack/router-cli (used by the 'routes:generate' script, ^1.167.21) and @tanstack/router-plugin (used by vite, ^1.168.20) in both apps/wallow-web/package.json and apps/wallow-auth/package.json. Align both packages to the same version (bump router-cli to match router-plugin, or pin both to whichever latest version keeps them equal) in both apps, pnpm install, then regenerate: run 'pnpm --filter ./apps/<app> routes:generate' AND a 'vite build' (or dev-server start) and commit whichever routeTree.gen.ts ordering both tools now agree on for wallow-web and wallow-auth.
acceptance_criteria:
- apps/wallow-web/package.json and apps/wallow-auth/package.json pin @tanstack/router-cli and @tanstack/router-plugin to matching versions.
- After running 'routes:generate' AND a 'vite build' (or starting the dev server) for each app, 'git status' stays clean — no routeTree.gen.ts churn in either apps/wallow-web/src/routeTree.gen.ts or apps/wallow-auth/src/routeTree.gen.ts.
- 'pnpm check' passes.
notes:
GREEN: routeTree ordering churn fixed — both toolchains now agree.

ROOT CAUSE (refined from the bead's original diagnosis): the skew is NOT between the router-cli and router-plugin version numbers directly — they are separate release lines that can never share a version (@tanstack/router-cli is frozen at 1.167.21, latest; @tanstack/router-plugin latest is 1.168.23). The real invariant is the SHARED, exact-pinned @tanstack/router-generator both wrap:
  - @tanstack/router-cli@1.167.21      -> @tanstack/router-generator 1.167.21
  - @tanstack/router-plugin@1.168.20   -> @tanstack/router-generator 1.167.19   <-- the skew
  - @tanstack/router-plugin@1.168.23   -> @tanstack/router-generator 1.167.21   <-- the fix
Generator 1.167.19 vs 1.167.21 emit different import/route-declaration ORDER; both were installed side-by-side in node_modules/.pnpm.

KEY CORRECTION to the bead description: the COMMITTED content was the PLUGIN's (1.167.19) output, not the CLI's. Verified from a clean tree: 'routes:generate' alone dirtied wallow-web (62 ins / 62 del). Direction did not change the fix.

CRITICAL SCOPE FINDING: bumping only the two app package.json files would NOT have worked. The vite build and dev server both import tanstackRouter from packages/web-shell (packages/web-shell/src/server/vite-presets.ts:11 and dev-server.ts:38), so the plugin resolves from web-shell's OWN dependency, not the apps'. web-shell had to be bumped too — that is the load-bearing edit.

FILES (4 package.json, @tanstack/router-plugin ^1.168.20 -> ^1.168.23):
  - packages/web-shell/package.json      (dependencies)  <-- the one that actually governs the build
  - apps/wallow-web/package.json         (devDependencies)
  - apps/wallow-auth/package.json        (devDependencies)
  - apps/examples/minimal-app/package.json (devDependencies) — kept consistent

Regenerated + STAGED (not committed, per instructions):

  - apps/wallow-auth/src/routeTree.gen.ts  (250 lines, pure reorder, 0 net-unique)
NOT touched: pnpm-workspace.yaml (its js-yaml override is another agent's concurrent work).

VERSIONS AFTER FIX — all four workspace packages resolve router-plugin 1.168.23 -> generator 1.167.21, identical to router-cli 1.167.21 -> generator 1.167.21. (router-plugin 1.168.20 remains in the store because @tanstack/start-plugin-core@1.171.20 exact-pins it, but it is NOT on our codegen path — vite-presets/dev-server import tanstackRouter directly, never tanstackStart, so it never generates a tree.)

ACCEPTANCE VERIFICATION (all proven empirically, not asserted):
  1. routes:generate (CLI) both apps -> hashes a5784eee (web) / 990ee6fe (auth).
  2. vite build (plugin path) wallow-web -> hash UNCHANGED a5784eee.
  3. vite build wallow-auth -> hash UNCHANGED 990ee6fe.
  4. Staged that baseline, ran a SECOND full cycle (routes:generate x2 + vite build x2) -> 'git diff --quiet' clean. NO CHURN.
  5. Dev-server path also verified: PORT=3111 pnpm dev on wallow-web, GET /bff-demo -> HTTP 200, routeTree still clean.

A pnpm override pinning '@tanstack/router-generator: 1.167.21' in pnpm-workspace.yaml would make the invariant explicit and carry an explanatory YAML comment. The existing packages/web-shell/src/route-tree-drift-workflow.test.ts CI guard would catch a regression either way.

VERIFY (independent re-run, all evidence gathered fresh):
