title: Clear Dependabot alert #53: js-yaml <4.3.0 via @hey-api/json-schema-ref-parser
description: Dependabot alert #53 (high): js-yaml >=4.0.0 <4.3.0 — YAML merge-key chains can force quadratic CPU consumption. Patched in 4.3.0. Sole vulnerable resolution is js-yaml 4.2.0 pulled by @hey-api/openapi-ts 0.99.0 -> @hey-api/json-schema-ref-parser 1.4.4 (dev-time SDK codegen only; runtime paths already resolve js-yaml 4.3.0). Fix options: (a) pnpm override js-yaml >=4.3.0 in root package.json, or (b) bump @hey-api/openapi-ts once upstream updates ref-parser. Alert: https://github.com/bc-solutions-coder/wallow/security/dependabot/53
design: Prefer bumping @hey-api/openapi-ts if a release now pulls a fixed json-schema-ref-parser (check its changelog/registry for a version depending on js-yaml >=4.3.0). If no such release exists yet, add a pnpm override in the root package.json: "pnpm": { "overrides": { "js-yaml": ">=4.3.0" } }. Then run 'pnpm install' to regenerate the lockfile.
acceptance_criteria:
- 'pnpm why js-yaml' and pnpm-lock.yaml show no resolution of js-yaml < 4.3.0.
- SDK codegen still works: the OpenAPI client regen command documented in packages/sdk/CLAUDE.md runs cleanly and produces no unexpected diff against the committed generated client (packages/sdk/openapi/v1.json + generated client dir).
- 'pnpm check' passes (format:check + lint + typecheck + test + build).
notes:
GREEN: FILES=pnpm-workspace.yaml, pnpm-lock.yaml (root package.json NOT changed — see APPROACH).

APPROACH: Option (b), pnpm override — option (a) is unavailable. Verified against registry.npmjs.org: @hey-api/openapi-ts 0.99.0 IS the latest published version, and it pins '@hey-api/json-schema-ref-parser': '1.4.4' EXACTLY; 1.4.4 is also that package's latest, and it pins 'js-yaml': '4.2.0' EXACTLY. No upstream release resolves the alert today, so there is nothing to bump to.

Two deliberate deviations from the bead's DESIGN text, both required:
1. Override lives in pnpm-workspace.yaml, NOT root package.json. pnpm 10.20.0 no longer reads the 'pnpm' field from package.json — the first install printed: '[WARN] The "pnpm" field in package.json is no longer read by pnpm. The following keys were ignored: "pnpm.overrides".' and the lockfile was unchanged. Moving it to the pnpm-workspace.yaml top-level 'overrides:' key worked. Root package.json was reverted and is untouched in the final diff.
2. Range is '^4.3.0', not '>=4.3.0'. '>=4.3.0' would resolve to js-yaml 5.2.2 (5.x is published), silently major-bumping js-yaml for xmlbuilder2 (TanStack Start's sitemap path) as well as the ref-parser. '^4.3.0' still fully satisfies the acceptance criterion (nothing < 4.3.0) with zero major-version risk. Added a comment above the override explaining why it exists and when to drop it.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA:
1. NO js-yaml < 4.3.0 — PASS. 'grep js-yaml@ pnpm-lock.yaml' now returns only js-yaml@4.3.0 (both the packages: and snapshots: sections); the js-yaml@4.2.0 entries are deleted. 'pnpm why js-yaml -r' shows zero occurrences of 4.2.0. On disk, every js-yaml symlink under node_modules/.pnpm resolves to js-yaml@4.3.0, including @hey-api+json-schema-ref-parser@1.4.4's (confirmed via its package.json = 4.3.0). Lockfile diff is 4 insertions / 9 deletions — the override stanza plus removal of the 4.2.0 package+snapshot blocks.
2. SDK codegen clean — PASS. Ran 'pnpm --filter @bc-solutions-coder/sdk exec tsx scripts/generate.ts' (no WALLOW_OPENAPI_URL, so it generates from the committed openapi/v1.json snapshot per scripts/generate.ts). Exit 0, '✓ ./src/generated · 4 files · 114ms'. 'git status --porcelain packages/sdk' is EMPTY — zero diff against the committed generated client and snapshot. The SDK meta-spec openapi-regen.test.ts also passes.
3. 'pnpm check' — BLOCKED BY A PRE-EXISTING FAILURE UNRELATED TO THIS BEAD (see ISSUES). Every stage that this change could affect passes: lint exit 0; typecheck exit 0 (all 9 projects); build exit 0 (all 9 projects); test 577/578 passing.

This is PRE-EXISTING and NOT caused by this change: README.md is unmodified in my working tree ('git status --porcelain' shows only pnpm-lock.yaml and pnpm-workspace.yaml), and it was last touched by HEAD commit 08872a65 'fix(apphost): disable Secure BFF cookies for plain-http local dev'. Recommend a separate chore bead. Both files I did touch pass oxfmt --check clean. Not committed, per instructions.
VERIFY (independent re-check, files read line-by-line, all commands re-run):

Note: node_modules/.pnpm/js-yaml@4.2.0 physically still exists on disk (stale, unreferenced store entry, not committed/gitignored) but zero symlinks point to it (confirmed via readlink scan) -- harmless, not a real resolution, does not affect the criterion.

This is the known pre-existing failure (Wallow-hjhd) per the coordinator's brief -- correctly excluded from this bead's scope.

Unrelated concurrent edits (consentInfo scopes / clientBranding in query/auth.ts + keys.ts, auth-client.ts additions) belong to other beads — do not revert them.

title: Thread client_id onward through the external-login flow so the callback actually receives it
description:
Follow-up from Wallow-9jab green phase.

AccountController now scopes every IRedirectUriValidator.IsAllowedAsync call to the request's client id, but nothing UPSTREAM supplies that id on the external-login return path, so in production these endpoints still receive clientId=null and fall back to the AuthUrl-only origin set. The per-client scoping is therefore correct but inert on this path.

Gaps:
1. ExternalLogin builds its callback with Url.Action(nameof(ExternalLoginCallback), new { returnUrl }) — no clientId, so ExternalLoginCallback gets null.
2. The accept-terms redirect and both mfa/challenge redirects in ExternalLoginCallback carry returnUrl but not client_id, so CompleteExternalRegistration and ExchangeTicket get null when the auth app calls back.

Why it was NOT bundled into Wallow-9jab: adding a query param to the OAuth callback URL changes the redirect_uri presented to third-party IdPs, and Google requires an exact registered redirect_uri match — so this needs deliberate design plus its own tests. It also requires the React auth app (apps/wallow-auth) to echo client_id back on the accept-terms and mfa-challenge screens, which is a frontend change.

Acceptance: an origin registered only by client B is rejected end-to-end through the real external-login -> accept-terms/mfa -> exchange-ticket journey when client A initiated the flow. Covers both the .NET controller and the wallow-auth screens.
notes:
RED (TDD red phase complete):

FILES (test, new):
api/tests/Modules/Identity/Wallow.Identity.Tests/Api/Controllers/AccountControllerExternalLoginClientIdFlowTests.cs — 11 tests (7 FAILING, 4 intentional guards that must STAY green). Self-contained setup mirroring AccountControllerClientScopedRedirectTests (own substitutes + EphemeralDataProtectionProvider + TestServiceProvider).

FILES (test, modified):
apps/wallow-auth/src/features/accept-terms/components/AcceptTermsScreen.test.tsx — 5 tests added (3 FAILING, 2 guards). New describe 'AcceptTermsScreen client_id relay' + 2 tests in the existing '/accept-terms route' block. No existing assertion changed.

FILES (scaffold, DECLARATION ONLY — NO fix logic):
apps/wallow-auth/src/features/accept-terms/components/AcceptTermsScreen.tsx — AcceptTermsScreenProps gained 'readonly clientId?: string' so the tests typecheck. The prop is NOT destructured and NOT used; the component body is untouched. (Declaring an unused interface member trips no oxlint rule, so unlike the C# side in Wallow-9jab this scaffold needs no placeholder discard — there is nothing for green to delete, only a prop to start reading.)

NOTE: NO .NET production scaffold was needed. Wallow-9jab already added the clientId parameter to all 6 actions, so the tree compiled as-is (dotnet build -> 0 warnings 0 errors). Green touches BODIES only.

=== THE DESIGN THE TESTS PIN (this is the part that needed deciding) ===

The bead's blocker was: adding a query param to the OAuth callback URL changes the redirect_uri presented to third-party IdPs, and Google requires an EXACT registered match. The tests resolve it by NOT putting the client id on the callback URL at all — it rides the challenge's AuthenticationProperties, which round-trip through the provider in the OAuth state and come back on ExternalLoginInfo.AuthenticationProperties. The redirect_uri stays byte-identical, so no provider registration changes.

  ExternalLogin: properties.Items['client_id'] = clientId   (NOT Url.Action route values)
    -> provider round trip (OAuth state) ->
  ExternalLoginCallback: recover from info.AuthenticationProperties, use for IsAllowedAsync
    -> hand-offs to the auth app carry client_id ->
  accept-terms / mfa-challenge screens echo it back as clientId

SPELLING CONTRACT (deliberate, both directions asserted):
• Auth-app-facing redirects use snake_case 'client_id' — the spelling AuthorizationController already uses on its login redirect ({authUrl}/login?returnUrl=...&client_id=...).
• API endpoints keep binding camelCase 'clientId' — the [FromQuery] string? clientId params from Wallow-9jab. Unchanged, so NO OpenAPI drift this time.
• The AuthenticationProperties item key is 'client_id'.

ORDERING CONSEQUENCE FOR GREEN: ExternalLoginCallback currently validates returnUrl at line ~352 BEFORE calling GetExternalLoginInfoAsync at ~360. The stashed id lives on that info, so green must fetch the external login info (or at least its properties) BEFORE the IsAllowedAsync call. That reordering is what tests 4/5 force.

=== .NET TESTS (11) ===

FAILING (7) — the acceptance criteria:
1. ExternalLogin_StashesRequestClientIdInChallengeProperties
   -> 'Expected challenge.Properties!.Items {empty} to contain key "client_id".'
2. ExternalLoginCallback_RecoversClientIdStashedByTheChallenge
   -> redirect was 'http://localhost:5002' (AuthUrl fallback), expected 'https://a.example.com/callback'. THE BUG, exactly as the bead describes it.
3. ExternalLoginCallback_PassesTheStashedClientIdToTheRedirectValidator
   -> NSubstitute: Expected IsAllowedAsync("https://a.example.com/callback", "client-a", any CT); Received IsAllowedAsync("https://a.example.com/callback", *<null>*, CT).
4. ExternalLoginCallback_NewUser_AcceptTermsRedirectCarriesClientId
   -> '.../accept-terms?returnUrl=...&email=...&name=...' to contain 'client_id=client-a'.
5. ExternalLoginCallback_UserWithMfaEnabled_MfaChallengeRedirectCarriesClientId
   -> '.../mfa/challenge?returnUrl=...' to contain 'client_id=client-a'.
6. ExternalLoginCallback_OrgRequiresMfaOutsideGrace_MfaChallengeRedirectCarriesClientId
   -> same, for the org-MFA-policy branch (the SECOND mfa/challenge redirect; both are separate code paths and both are covered).
7. CompleteExternalRegistration_TermsRequiredBounce_CarriesClientId
   -> '.../accept-terms?error=terms_required&returnUrl=...' to contain 'client_id=client-a'.

GUARDS (4) — currently green, must STAY green:
8. ExternalLogin_DoesNotAddClientIdToTheProviderCallbackUrl — THE DESIGN PIN. Captures the UrlActionContext handed to IUrlHelper and asserts the route values contain returnUrl but NOT clientId/client_id. A green phase that 'threads' the id by appending it to the callback URL breaks every configured IdP; this test fails it loudly instead.
9. ExternalLogin_WithoutClientId_StashesNothingInChallengeProperties — no empty stash.
10. ExternalLoginCallback_NewUserWithoutClientId_AcceptTermsRedirectCarriesNone — no empty 'client_id=' on the hand-off. Matters because an unknown/blank client fails CLOSED to the AuthUrl-only origin set, so an empty relay would refuse the returnUrl the user is mid-journey to, where sending nothing falls back cleanly.
11. ExternalLoginCallback_WithExplicitClientId_StillValidatesAgainstIt — Wallow-9jab regression guard: an explicit query param must keep winning where present, so recovering from the stash must not displace it.

Isolation note: tests 4-7 use AllowEveryReturnUrl() rather than AllowOnlyForClient(), so a missing client_id on the hand-off is the ONLY thing that can fail them — the redirect-shape concern is not conflated with the validation-scoping concern (tests 2/3 own that).

=== FRONTEND TESTS (5, wallow-auth accept-terms) ===

FAILING (3):
1. 'echoes the flow's client id back to complete-external-registration' — searchParams.get('clientId') expected 'client-a', got null. Asserted by NAME, not by pinning the whole query string, so param ORDER stays green's business.
2. 'percent-encodes clientId so it cannot inject extra query parameters' — hostile 'client-a&acceptedTerms=false'; same injection guard returnUrl already has. Unencoded it smuggles a second acceptedTerms in, and ASP.NET binds a duplicated [FromQuery] bool as 'true,false', which fails to parse and drops the user on the !acceptedTerms branch — turning a completed consent into a terms_required bounce.
3. '/accept-terms route > threads client_id out of the callback redirect into the handoff' — the whole relay end-to-end through a real memory router (the snake_case in -> camelCase out hop). Green must widen validateSearch in apps/wallow-auth/src/routes/accept-terms.tsx AND read the prop in the screen.

GUARDS (2), currently green:
4. 'omits clientId entirely when the flow carries none' — also pins the exact legacy query string, so green cannot append an unconditional '&clientId=undefined'.
5. '/accept-terms route > treats a non-string client_id as absent' — TanStack Router JSON-parses scalar search values, so ?client_id=42 arrives as the NUMBER 42 (bd memory tanstack-router-default-search-parser-json-parses-values). validateSearch must typeof-narrow it like the other four params.
NOTE: three PRE-EXISTING accept-branch tests assert the exact string '?acceptedTerms=true&returnUrl=<enc>' with toBe(). They render without a clientId, so they are a free extra guard against an unconditional append. Green must emit the param only when the id is present.

TEST_STATUS: RED — 10 failing for the correct reason, zero regressions.
• ./scripts/run-tests.sh identity -> 1097 total, 1090 passed, 7 failed. (1086 pre-existing pass, matching Wallow-9jab's closing count, + my 4 guards.)
• ./scripts/run-tests.sh arch -> 276/276 PASS.

• dotnet build -> succeeded, 0 warnings 0 errors.
• dotnet format --include <new test file> --verify-no-changes -> clean, exit 0. Scoped with --include deliberately: other agents are editing this worktree concurrently (git status shows ~40 unrelated modified files), so a whole-solution format would rewrite their in-flight work.
• wallow-auth typecheck -> clean. oxlint apps/wallow-auth --deny-warnings -> exit 0. oxfmt --check -> clean.

=== NOT COVERED HERE — the remaining piece of the acceptance criteria ===

The wallow-auth MFA-CHALLENGE screen is NOT covered by these tests, and the bead's acceptance criteria does name it. Deliberately deferred rather than half-done, because it is a genuinely separate workstream that lands in packages/sdk, not in the app:

• MfaChallengeForm reaches exchange-ticket through the SDK builder buildExchangeTicketUrl(origin, ticket, returnUrl) (packages/sdk/src/auth-oidc.ts:144), which has no clientId parameter. Carrying the id needs an optional 4th param there.
• The same screen's allow-list probe goes through authQueries.redirectValidation(returnUrl) (packages/sdk/src/query/auth.ts), which likewise passes no clientId — so /redirect-uri/validate is unscoped from that screen too, and the queryKeys factory entry would have to take the id as well or two clients would share a cache key.
• SEQUENCING HAZARD: packages/sdk/src/query/auth.ts, query/keys.ts and auth-client.ts are ALREADY modified in this worktree by a concurrent agent. Whoever picks this up should re-read them first rather than assume the shapes above.
• A naive fix also breaks a sibling assertion: MfaChallengeForm.test.tsx:584 asserts toHaveBeenCalledWith('', TICKET, RETURN_URL) exactly, so passing an undefined 4th argument unconditionally fails it.

Recommend a follow-up bead for the mfa-challenge + SDK half. The .NET side of that path is already done and tested here: both mfa/challenge redirects carry client_id (tests 5 and 6), so the API is ready for the screen to echo it whenever that lands.

GREEN SCOPE (what green owns):
1. AccountController.ExternalLogin — stash clientId in the challenge properties; do NOT touch the Url.Action route values.
2. AccountController.ExternalLoginCallback — fetch external login info BEFORE validating returnUrl; recover the stashed id (query param wins if present); append client_id to the accept-terms redirect and BOTH mfa/challenge redirects, only when non-blank.
3. AccountController.CompleteExternalRegistration — append client_id to the terms_required bounce, only when non-blank.
4. apps/wallow-auth accept-terms route validateSearch — read+narrow client_id; screen — relay it as encodeURIComponent'd clientId, omitted when absent.
Do NOT edit any test file.
GREEN (TDD green phase complete): all 10 red tests pass, zero test files edited.

FILES (production, modified):

- apps/wallow-auth/src/features/accept-terms/components/AcceptTermsScreen.tsx
- apps/wallow-auth/src/routes/accept-terms.tsx

SYMBOLS (new, all private -- no public API surface added, so NO OpenAPI drift):
- AccountController.ExternalLoginClientIdKey : const string = "client_id"
  The AuthenticationProperties item key AND the auth-app-facing query spelling. One
  constant for both ends of the round trip, since the red report pinned them equal.
- AccountController.GetStashedClientId(AuthenticationProperties?) : static string?
  Recovers the id from info.AuthenticationProperties; null when absent.
- AccountController.BuildClientIdQuery(string?) : static string
  Returns "&client_id=<escaped>" or "" for null/empty. The single place the
  "omit rather than send blank" rule lives; used by all four hand-offs.
Frontend:
- AcceptTermsScreenProps.clientId is now DESTRUCTURED and read (red left it declared
  but unused); handleAcceptTerms builds `clientIdParam` = "&clientId=<encoded>" or "".
- accept-terms route: AcceptTermsSearch gained `readonly clientId?: string`;
  validateSearch narrows `search.client_id` with the same typeof guard the other four
  use; AcceptTermsRoute passes it down. The snake_case-in/camelCase-out hop lives
  entirely in these two lines.

WHAT CHANGED, per the pinned design:
1. ExternalLogin: properties.Items["client_id"] = clientId, only when non-blank.
   Url.Action route values UNTOUCHED, so redirect_uri stays byte-identical (guard 8 green).
2. ExternalLoginCallback: GetExternalLoginInfoAsync now runs BEFORE the returnUrl
   validation (the reordering tests 4/5 forced). flowClientId = explicit query param
   if non-blank, else the stashed one -- so Wallow-9jab's explicit-wins guard (11) holds.
   IsAllowedAsync is called with flowClientId; the accept-terms redirect and BOTH
   mfa/challenge redirects append BuildClientIdQuery(flowClientId).
3. CompleteExternalRegistration: terms_required bounce appends BuildClientIdQuery(clientId).

=== ONE UNPLANNED PRODUCTION CHANGE -- PLEASE ADJUDICATE ===

ExternalLogin now reads:
    AuthenticationProperties properties =
        signInManager.ConfigureExternalAuthenticationProperties(provider, callbackUrl)
        ?? new AuthenticationProperties { RedirectUri = callbackUrl };

The `??` fallback was NOT in the green scope. It is required because two PRE-EXISTING
Wallow-9jab tests broke on the first green attempt:
  AccountControllerClientScopedRedirectTests.ExternalLogin_ValidatesReturnUrlAgainstRequestClientId
  AccountControllerClientScopedRedirectTests.ExternalLogin_PassesRequestClientIdToRedirectValidator
Both failed with NullReferenceException at the new `properties.Items[...]` line. Cause:
neither test stubs ConfigureExternalAuthenticationProperties, and it is virtual, so the
NSubstitute SignInManager returns NULL. The old code never dereferenced the result -- it
handed it straight to Challenge(), which accepts null -- so the latent null only became
reachable when this bead started writing into Items. I could not fix it test-side (the
rule forbids editing test files, and they are another bead's).

Rejected alternative: `if (properties is not null && ...)`. That compiles but the null
test narrows the flow state of a NON-nullable local, so the later Challenge(properties,
provider) then raises CS8604 -- a build ERROR under TreatWarningsAsErrors. The `??` form
keeps the local non-null throughout and needs no `!` suppression.
Production impact: none. The real SignInManager never returns null here, so the fallback
is unreachable outside substitutes; when it does fire the challenge still carries the
same RedirectUri it would have had. Flagging it because it is defensive code the scope
did not ask for -- if a verifier prefers it gone, the two tests above must gain a stub.

DOC COMMENTS CORRECTED (they asserted the opposite of the new behaviour):

  external-login-callback redirects here with returnUrl, email and name only."
- AcceptTermsScreen.tsx header claimed "The four props are the oracle's four

description: Found during Wallow-ur11 green phase: OpenIddictRedirectUriValidator.IsAllowedAsync now supports per-client validation, LogoutController is wired, but AccountController's 6 call sites still call it without a clientId. See Wallow-ur11 bead notes for the fix pattern.

FILES (test, new):

FILES (scaffold, SIGNATURE ONLY — NO fix logic):
api/src/Modules/Identity/Wallow.Identity.Api/Controllers/AccountController.cs — 6 actions gained a clientId parameter. Bodies still call IsAllowedAsync WITHOUT it.

  • ExternalLoginCallback(returnUrl, [FromQuery] string? clientId = null)
  • CompleteExternalRegistration(acceptedTerms, returnUrl, [FromQuery] string? clientId = null)
  • ExchangeTicket(ticket, returnUrl, [FromQuery] string? clientId = null)
  • ValidateRedirectUri(uri, [FromQuery] string? clientId, CancellationToken ct)   <- inserted BEFORE ct (CA1068 requires CancellationToken last), so this one is NOT source-compatible
  • SignOut(postLogoutRedirectUri, [FromForm] string? clientId = null)
  Register needs NO signature change — AccountRegisterRequest.ClientId already exists and is already used at the tenant-resolve step.

FILES (mechanical compile fixups forced by the ValidateRedirectUri signature):
  • AccountControllerTests.cs — 3 ValidateRedirectUri call sites gained a null middle arg. No assertions changed.

ANALYZER GOTCHA (important for green): IDE0060 (severity=warning, api/.editorconfig:375) AND Roslynator RCS1163 BOTH fire on an unused parameter even on PUBLIC controller actions, and TreatWarningsAsErrors makes them build errors. A pure signature-only scaffold therefore does NOT compile. Each of the 6 methods carries a placeholder immediately above its IsAllowedAsync call:
    // TODO: pass clientId to IsAllowedAsync so validation is scoped to the requesting client.
    _ = clientId;
GREEN MUST delete all 6 TODO+discard pairs and pass clientId into IsAllowedAsync instead. Leaving the discard in place while also passing clientId would build, but is dead code.

CALL-SITE COUNT CORRECTION: the bead title says 6; there are actually 7 IsAllowedAsync call sites in AccountController (pre-change lines 261, 278, 409, 599, 619, 633, 719). Line 719 (Register) is the 7th and was omitted from the ur11 survey's headline count. All 7 are covered by these tests.

TESTS ADDED (14, all failing) — 2 per call site:
Behavioural (7) — prove the per-client allow list actually changes the endpoint outcome:
 1. ExternalLogin_ValidatesReturnUrlAgainstRequestClientId — expects ChallengeResult; got RedirectResult (error?reason=invalid_redirect_uri).
 2. ExternalLoginCallback_ValidatesReturnUrlAgainstRequestClientId — expects redirect to client-a's URL; got AuthUrl fallback.
 3. CompleteExternalRegistration_ValidatesReturnUrlAgainstRequestClientId — expects accept-terms redirect to carry the escaped client-a returnUrl; got the escaped AuthUrl.
 4. ExchangeTicket_ValidatesReturnUrlAgainstRequestClientId — expects redirect to client-a's URL; got AuthUrl.

 6. SignOut_ValidatesPostLogoutRedirectUriAgainstRequestClientId — expects post_logout_redirect_uri= in the redirect; got error?reason=invalid_redirect_uri.
 7. Register_ValidatesReturnUrlAgainstRequestClientId — expects the published EmailVerificationRequestedEvent.VerifyUrl to carry returnUrl=; VerifyUrl had none.
Forwarding (7) — *_PassesRequestClientIdToRedirectValidator for each of the 7 endpoints. All fail identically with NSubstitute:
  Expected: IsAllowedAsync("https://a.example.com/callback", "client-a", any CancellationToken)
  Received: IsAllowedAsync("https://a.example.com/callback", *<null>*, CancellationToken)
That <null> IS the bug.

title: MfaPartialAuthService hardcodes cookie Secure=true (breaks plain-HTTP dev flows)
description: Re-filed from archived Wallow-mexo after live re-verification (2026-07-25 bead audit). api/src/Modules/Identity/Wallow.Identity.Infrastructure/Services/MfaPartialAuthService.cs:45 still hardcodes Secure = true on the partial-auth cookie regardless of environment/request scheme, so the MFA partial-auth flow cannot work over plain HTTP (local/dev scenarios without TLS).
acceptance_criteria: Cookie Secure flag follows environment/request policy (e.g. CookieSecurePolicy.SameAsRequest or config), remains Secure in production; test covers both.
notes:
Archive record: ~/Documents/wallow-plans-archive/2026-07-17-bead-archive.md (Wallow-mexo). Verified live at HEAD c2c9499b.
SCOUT FINDINGS.

FILES:
- api/src/Modules/Identity/Wallow.Identity.Infrastructure/Services/MfaPartialAuthService.cs:36-53 (IssuePartialCookieAsync) — the buggy code. Line 41: HttpContext httpContext = _httpContextAccessor.HttpContext!; Line 42-49: httpContext.Response.Cookies.Append(CookieName, protectedValue, new CookieOptions { HttpOnly = true, Secure = true, SameSite = SameSiteMode.Lax, MaxAge = _cookieLifetime, IsEssential = true }); — Secure is a literal 'true', ignoring request scheme/environment.
- api/tests/Modules/Identity/Wallow.Identity.Tests/Infrastructure/MfaPartialAuthServiceTests.cs — EXISTING test file for this exact class, already has full xunit + NSubstitute + FluentAssertions coverage of IssuePartialCookieAsync/ValidatePartialCookieAsync/DeletePartialCookie/UpgradeToFullAuthAsync. New Secure-flag tests must be ADDED here, not a new file. Ctor pattern: DefaultHttpContext _httpContext = new(); IHttpContextAccessor substitute returns it; DataProtectionProvider.Create("test"); SignInManager substitute via NSubstitute. SUT built in ctor as _sut.
- api/src/Modules/Identity/Wallow.Identity.Api/Controllers/AccountController.cs:382-389 — a SEPARATE cookie (ExternalLoginState) has the SAME hardcoded Secure=true bug, but it is OUT OF SCOPE for this bead (bead only names MfaPartialAuthService.cs:45). Do not touch it unless asked.

ROOT_CAUSE: MfaPartialAuthService.IssuePartialCookieAsync builds a raw Microsoft.AspNetCore.Http.CookieOptions manually (not via CookieBuilder/ConfigureApplicationCookie) and hardcodes Secure = true unconditionally, so the cookie is dropped by browsers over plain HTTP (local/dev without TLS), breaking the MFA step-up flow in dev.

PRECEDENT PATTERN (how the rest of the repo decides Secure): api/src/Modules/Identity/Wallow.Identity.Infrastructure/Extensions/IdentityInfrastructureExtensions.cs:153-164 (ConfigureApplicationCookie) sets options.Cookie.SecurePolicy = environment.IsDevelopment() ? CookieSecurePolicy.SameAsRequest : CookieSecurePolicy.Always. Internally, ASP.NET Core's CookieBuilder implements SameAsRequest as: secure = request.IsHttps. Wallow.Api.Program.cs:376-385 registers UseForwardedHeaders with ForwardedHeaders.XForwardedFor|XForwardedProto BEFORE auth middleware, so httpContext.Request.IsHttps correctly reflects the original scheme even behind a TLS-terminating proxy in production — meaning Request.IsHttps is a safe, already-production-correct signal.

FIX_APPROACH: Replace 'Secure = true' (line 45) with 'Secure = httpContext.Request.IsHttps' — mirrors the framework's own SameAsRequest semantics, needs no new DI dependency (httpContext is already resolved on line 41 before the CookieOptions is built), stays Secure=true whenever the request (real or forwarded) is HTTPS, and is Secure=false only for genuine plain-HTTP dev traffic. No IWebHostEnvironment injection needed/wanted — request-scheme-based is more correct than environment-based since it also protects against a misconfigured prod HTTP listener.

TEST_LOCATION: api/tests/Modules/Identity/Wallow.Identity.Tests/Infrastructure/MfaPartialAuthServiceTests.cs — add cases to (or near) the existing IssuePartialCookieAsync_AppendsCookieNamedIdentityMfaPartial test. Pattern: set _httpContext.Request.Scheme = "https" (or IsHttps = true) before calling IssuePartialCookieAsync, then assert _httpContext.Response.Headers.SetCookie.ToString() contains 'secure' (case-insensitive, ASP.NET Core lowercases the attribute). Add a second case with default DefaultHttpContext (Scheme defaults to "http", IsHttps=false) asserting the Set-Cookie header does NOT contain 'secure'. DefaultHttpContext.Request.IsHttps has a public setter (backed by Scheme) so tests can set it directly.

TEST_CMD: ./scripts/run-tests.sh identity   (runs Wallow.Identity.Tests via api/tests/coverage.runsettings; NEVER bare dotnet test per .claude/rules/TESTING.md)
RED PHASE REPORT.

FILES (only file touched): api/tests/Modules/Identity/Wallow.Identity.Tests/Infrastructure/MfaPartialAuthServiceTests.cs — added 3 tests + 1 private helper + 'using Microsoft.Net.Http.Headers;'. NO production code touched (MfaPartialAuthService.cs is untouched; Secure = true is still hardcoded at line 45).

TESTS ADDED (all in the EXISTING test class, placed right after IssuePartialCookieAsync_AppendsCookieNamedIdentityMfaPartial, per scout guidance — no new test file):
1. IssuePartialCookieAsync_OverHttps_MarksCookieSecure — sets _httpContext.Request.IsHttps = true, asserts parsed Set-Cookie .Secure is true. STATUS: PASSES ALREADY (expected — hardcoded Secure=true happens to be correct for HTTPS). This is the production-safety regression guard for the acceptance criterion 'remains Secure in production'; it must keep passing after the fix.
2. IssuePartialCookieAsync_OverPlainHttp_DoesNotMarkCookieSecure — sets _httpContext.Request.IsHttps = false, asserts .Secure is false. STATUS: FAILS — this is the bug-exposing red test.
3. IssuePartialCookieAsync_OverPlainHttp_KeepsHttpOnlyAndSameSiteLax — asserts HttpOnly=true and SameSite=Lax still hold on plain HTTP. STATUS: PASSES. Guard so the green phase does not loosen the other hardening attributes while relaxing Secure.

ASSERTION STYLE: tests parse the response header with Microsoft.Net.Http.Headers.SetCookieHeaderValue.ParseList and assert typed properties (.Secure/.HttpOnly/.SameSite) instead of substring-matching 'secure' in the raw header — the protected cookie VALUE is an opaque base64 blob that could coincidentally contain the substring, so substring matching would be flaky. Helper added: private SetCookieHeaderValue ExtractSetCookie(string cookieName). Note SameSiteMode is ambiguous between Microsoft.AspNetCore.Http and Microsoft.Net.Http.Headers once both are imported — test 3 fully qualifies Microsoft.Net.Http.Headers.SameSiteMode.Lax. ParseList takes IList<string> (non-nullable), and StringValues.ToArray() gives string?[], so the helper projects with .Select(header => header ?? string.Empty).ToList() (a bare .ToArray() is CS8620, which fails the build under TreatWarningsAsErrors).

TEST_STATUS: RED — 1 failing / 1063 total via ./scripts/run-tests.sh identity (1062 passed, 0 skipped).
FAILURE REASON (verified, correct reason — not a compile/setup error): 'Expected cookie.Secure to be False, but found True.' at MfaPartialAuthServiceTests.cs:97. That is exactly the hardcoded Secure = true at MfaPartialAuthService.cs:45.

GREEN PHASE NOTE: the scout's one-line fix (replace 'Secure = true' with 'Secure = httpContext.Request.IsHttps' at MfaPartialAuthService.cs:45) satisfies all three tests. httpContext is already in scope on line 41. Do NOT inject IWebHostEnvironment. Do NOT edit the test file. Out of scope per the bead: the same hardcoded-Secure bug in AccountController.cs ExternalLoginState cookie.

WORKING-TREE CAUTION for whoever commits: at the time of this run, git status also showed unrelated modifications from CONCURRENT team work in apps/wallow-web/src/routes/dashboard/route.test.tsx, packages/sdk/src/query/auth.ts, packages/sdk/src/query/keys.ts. Those are NOT part of this bead — stage only the Identity test file (and later the Identity service file).

FORMAT: dotnet format api/Wallow.slnx --include <the test file> --verify-no-changes passes clean.
GREEN PHASE REPORT.

FILES: api/src/Modules/Identity/Wallow.Identity.Infrastructure/Services/MfaPartialAuthService.cs (only production file touched; single line changed at line 45 inside IssuePartialCookieAsync). Test file MfaPartialAuthServiceTests.cs was NOT edited in this phase (red-phase content unchanged).

CHANGE: 'Secure = true' -> 'Secure = httpContext.Request.IsHttps' in the CookieOptions initializer passed to httpContext.Response.Cookies.Append(CookieName, ...). This is exactly the scout's FIX_APPROACH. httpContext was already resolved on line 41, so no new field, constructor parameter, or DI registration was added; IWebHostEnvironment was deliberately NOT injected. This mirrors ASP.NET Core's own CookieSecurePolicy.SameAsRequest semantics (secure = request.IsHttps), matching ConfigureApplicationCookie in IdentityInfrastructureExtensions.cs. Because Wallow.Api.Program.cs registers UseForwardedHeaders (X-Forwarded-Proto) before auth middleware, Request.IsHttps still reports true behind a TLS-terminating proxy, so the cookie remains Secure in production.

SYMBOLS: no public/exported API surface changed. IMfaPartialAuthService and the MfaPartialAuthService constructor signature are untouched; IssuePartialCookieAsync(MfaPartialAuthPayload payload, CancellationToken ct) -> Task keeps its exact signature. No new symbols added.

TEST_STATUS: pass. ./scripts/run-tests.sh identity => 1063 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped (Wallow.Identity.Tests, net10.0). The previously red test IssuePartialCookieAsync_OverPlainHttp_DoesNotMarkCookieSecure now passes; the two guard tests (IssuePartialCookieAsync_OverHttps_MarksCookieSecure and ..._KeepsHttpOnlyAndSameSiteLax) still pass, so the HTTPS/production path and the HttpOnly+SameSite=Lax hardening were not weakened.

FORMAT: dotnet format api/Wallow.slnx --include <the changed service file> --verify-no-changes exits 0 (clean, no formatting fixes needed). CONVENTIONS respected: explicit type (HttpContext httpContext) already in place, no var introduced, [LoggerMessage] source-gen logging left as-is.

STAGED: only the two Identity files (MfaPartialAuthService.cs + MfaPartialAuthServiceTests.cs). Concurrent unrelated team edits remain UNSTAGED and untouched: apps/wallow-web/src/routes/dashboard/route.test.tsx, packages/sdk/src/query/auth.ts, packages/sdk/src/query/keys.ts, plus an untracked apps/wallow-auth/src/routes/login.test.tsx; note apps/wallow-web/src/routes/dashboard/route.tsx was ALREADY staged by another agent before this phase began -- I did not stage or modify it.

ISSUES: none blocking. Out of scope and still present per the bead: AccountController.cs (~line 382-389) has the same hardcoded Secure = true on the ExternalLoginState cookie -- deliberately left alone; worth a follow-up bead.
VERIFY: [✓] Cookie Secure flag follows request policy — MfaPartialAuthService.cs:45 changed 'Secure = true' to 'Secure = httpContext.Request.IsHttps', mirroring ASP.NET Core's CookieSecurePolicy.SameAsRequest. [✓] Remains Secure in production — Program.cs:376-385 registers UseForwardedHeaders (X-Forwarded-Proto) before UseAuthentication(519)/UseAuthorization(532), so Request.IsHttps reflects the real scheme behind a TLS-terminating proxy. [✓] Test covers both — MfaPartialAuthServiceTests.cs adds IssuePartialCookieAsync_OverHttps_MarksCookieSecure and IssuePartialCookieAsync_OverPlainHttp_DoesNotMarkCookieSecure, both using SetCookieHeaderValue.ParseList for typed assertion (not substring match, avoids false positives against the opaque protected cookie value). Guard test IssuePartialCookieAsync_OverPlainHttp_KeepsHttpOnlyAndSameSiteLax confirms HttpOnly/SameSite=Lax were not weakened by the fix. tests=pass (./scripts/run-tests.sh identity => 1063 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped). dotnet format --verify-no-changes clean on both files. Conventions: explicit types throughout (HttpContext httpContext, List<string>, IList<SetCookieHeaderValue>), no var, [LoggerMessage] logging untouched, no production API surface changed. Diff is minimal (1 line prod change + 3 new test methods + 1 helper), matches scout FIX_APPROACH exactly, no scope creep (AccountController ExternalLoginState cookie correctly left untouched per bead scope). issues=none blocking. verdict=CLOSE

title: Reconcile seed clientId drift (bcordes-dev-client vs bcordes-client)
description:
The OIDC clientId is inconsistent across seed config and its documentation. The live api/seed.json uses 'bcordes-dev-client', while the seed example file, surrounding comments, and docker/.env.production.example annotations refer to 'bcordes-client'.

A fork operator following the example values gets a clientId that does not match the seeded client, and the OIDC flow fails with no obvious cause.

Action: pick one canonical clientId, then align all of: api/seed.json, the seed example file, the explanatory comments, and the docker/.env.production.example annotations.
notes:
AUDIT 2026-07-25 (verify-infra): STILL_VALID but it is a THREE-WAY drift and the bead's file attributions are wrong. api/seed.json uses NEITHER variant named in the title — its clients are wallow-dev-client, wallow-web-client, sa-bcordes-bff, bcordes-bff, plus documentation-only bcordes-web-client (:284 under _productionExampleClients). Actual drift for the index-1 client: bcordes-dev-client = seeded value (docker/seed.production.json:52; also api/src/Wallow.Api/appsettings.json:77 FirstPartyClients and a comment at docker-compose.test.yml:142); bcordes-client = documented value only (docker-compose.production.yml:282, .env.production.example:134); bcordes-web-client = dev-side example (api/seed.json:284, pinned by SeedJsonProductionExampleTests.cs:16). Array order is load-bearing for Clients__1__Secret injection (docker-compose.production.yml:279-288). ADDITIONAL SCOPE: appsettings.json:77 declares bcordes-dev-client first-party but no such client exists in api/seed.json — the dev first-party list points at nothing. bcordes-bff / sa-bcordes-bff are consistent everywhere; leave them alone. FIX: pick one canonical name, align seed.production.json:52 + appsettings.json:77 + api/seed.json:284 + the two prose sites + test constant.
RED (TDD) — 6 failing tests, 1 passing guardrail. No production code touched.

FILES (new, only file I created):
- api/tests/Wallow.Architecture.Tests/SeedClientIdConsistencyTests.cs

HOME/HARNESS RATIONALE: this is config-only, but it IS testable — no throwaway harness
needed. Wallow.Architecture.Tests already does static config inspection over these exact
files: TraceSamplerConfigurationTests reads docker/docker-compose.production.yml AND
api/src/Wallow.Api/appsettings.json via a FindRepoRoot() (walks up to pnpm-workspace.yaml);
CiAuthImageBuildTests does the same over .github/workflows. I mirrored that pattern exactly.
Considered and rejected: (a) Identity.Tests/Infrastructure/SeedJson*Tests — its
GetSolutionRoot() resolves to api/ (finds Wallow.slnx), so docker/ is out of reach without
an extra Parent hop; (b) apps/wallow-web/src/service-identity.test.ts (vitest node project,
already reads docker-compose.test.yml + api/seed.json from repo root) — right capability,
wrong owner: assertions about production seed client naming do not belong to wallow-web.

INVESTIGATION — the drift is a THREE-WAY split, and one leg is NOT what the bead title says.

1) docker/seed.production.json is GITIGNORED (.gitignore:26 'seed.*.json'). It exists only
   as a local/host file. Its clients[1].clientId = 'bcordes-dev-client'
   (redirect https://bcordes.dev/auth/callback). CI can never assert on it — so the
   committed files that DESCRIBE it are the only enforceable surface. Called out in the
   test class XML doc so nobody later tries to add a seed.production.json assertion.

2) Index-1 fork SPA client, three names for one thing:
   - bcordes-dev-client  = seeded reality (docker/seed.production.json:52) and the value
                           already in committed api/src/Wallow.Api/appsettings.json:78.
   - bcordes-client      = documented-only, docker-compose.production.yml:282 (the
                           Clients__<index>__Secret map) and docker/.env.production.example:140
                           (BCORDES_CLIENT_ID checklist). Inert prose, zero runtime effect.
   - bcordes-web-client  = api/seed.json:284 under _productionExampleClients.

CANONICAL CHOICE = 'bcordes-dev-client'. Rationale: it is already registered in the deployed
OpenIddict application table for the reference deployment. Renaming it costs a re-seed plus an
SPA reconfiguration; the two 'bcordes-client' sites are comments/checklist text that cost
nothing to correct. Fix the prose, not the live client.

SCOPE CORRECTION — bcordes-web-client is deliberately NOT in scope, and the audit note's
'three-way drift' framing over-reaches here. It is a DIFFERENT client: redirect
https://bcordes.dev/bff/callback (confidential BFF), which matches seed.production.json
clients[3] 'bcordes-bff', NOT clients[1]'s /auth/callback SPA. docker-compose.production.yml's
index map confirms it (0=wallow-web-client, 1=<the SPA>, 2=sa-bcordes-bff, 3=bcordes-bff) —
bcordes-web-client appears nowhere in that map. Renaming it to the SPA's id would make the
docs describe a BFF client under the SPA's name. Therefore SeedJsonProductionExampleTests.cs:16
(ExampleClientId = 'bcordes-web-client') is CORRECT AS-IS and must NOT be edited. Left green.
FOLLOW-UP (separate bead, not this one): _productionExampleClients documents the production
shape of 'bcordes-bff' but names it 'bcordes-web-client' — a naming smell worth its own bead.
Note it cannot simply be renamed to 'bcordes-bff': the existing
ProductionExample_IsNotAnActiveSeedClient test would then fail, since bcordes-bff IS active.

ADDITIONAL SCOPE CONFIRMED (real bug, not just docs): appsettings.json:78
Identity:FirstPartyClients = ["bcordes-dev-client"], but api/seed.json seeds only
wallow-dev-client, wallow-web-client, sa-bcordes-bff, bcordes-bff. First-party matching is by
client id, so the dev list matches NOTHING and local OIDC never skips consent.
CRITICAL CONSTRAINT for the GREEN implementer: REPLACE index 0's value, do NOT delete the
entry. docker/docker-compose.test.yml:144,147 append positionally
(Identity__FirstPartyClients__1, __2); removing index 0 leaves a hole those overrides cannot
fill. DevFirstPartyClients_ShouldNotBeEmpty exists purely to catch a fix-by-deletion and
already PASSES today — it is a guardrail, not a red test.
RECOMMENDED value: 'wallow-dev-client'. It is genuinely seeded, and it is the only seeded id
that does not duplicate what docker-compose.test.yml already appends (bcordes-bff at __1,
wallow-web-client at __2). The test only enforces the invariant (non-empty + subset of seeded
ids), so another seeded id is acceptable if justified.

 RED   ProductionCompose_ClientSecretIndexMap_ShouldNameTheSeededForkClientId
 RED   ProductionCompose_ClientSecretIndexMap_ShouldNotNameTheDriftedClientId
 RED   EnvProductionExample_ClientIdChecklist_ShouldNameTheSeededForkClientId

Note on the 'ShouldNotName' pairs: they are not redundant with the positive assertions. The
positive one passes as soon as the canonical id is ADDED; the negative one forces the stale
name to be REMOVED rather than left alongside it.
Substring safety verified: 'bcordes-dev-client' does not contain 'bcordes-client', and the
NotContain checks are ordinal/case-sensitive so the uppercase BCORDES_CLIENT_ID /
BCORDES_CLIENT_SECRET env var names do not false-positive.

RUN: ./scripts/run-tests.sh architecture
RESULT: TOTAL 283 | PASSED 277 | FAILED 6 | SKIPPED 0  (277 pre-existing all still green)

FAILURE OUTPUT (assertion conclusions, file dumps elided):
- EnvProductionExample_..._ShouldNameTheSeededForkClientId: expected source to contain

- TestCompose_ShouldNotNameAProductionOnlyClientId: expected source not to contain

GREEN PHASE EDIT LIST (4 files, all config/comment text):
 1. docker/docker-compose.production.yml:282  '#   1 = bcordes-client' -> 'bcordes-dev-client'
    (keep alignment of the index map comment block, lines 279-288).

    '# BCORDES_CLIENT_ID=bcordes-dev-client' (keep the trailing '# -> clients[1].clientId').

GlobalUsings.cs), NOT FluentAssertions. Two gotchas hit while writing, recorded so GREEN/FIX

overload — arg 2 is the 'because' string, passing StringComparison is CS1503; (b) the project
runs TreatWarningsAsErrors with AnalysisMode=All, so private helpers returning

dotnet format api/Wallow.slnx --verify-no-changes passes on the new file.
GREEN (TDD) — all 6 red tests now pass, guardrail still green. No test files edited; changes are config/comment text only, exactly the 4-file edit list from the RED report.

title: migrate Wolverine service-location usages before Wolverine 6.0 makes them throw
description: API runtime logs emit Wolverine deprecation warnings: service-location for ITenantContext and IsSetupRequiredQuery "will throw in Wolverine 6.0". Refactor the affected handler registrations/injections to constructor/parameter injection per Wolverine guidance so a future Wolverine bump does not break at runtime. Surfaced by the 2026-07-21 HTTP smoke-test review (not related to the Blazor removal).
notes:
GREEN (pending final host-test confirmation): Fixed the Wolverine 'will throw in Wolverine 6.0' service-location warnings.

ROOT CAUSE: api/src/Wallow.Api/Program.cs set ServiceLocationPolicy=AllowedButWarn as a stopgap. Wolverine 6 codegen inlines 'new X()' for dependencies it can see (AddScoped<I,Impl>) but falls back to service location (the warned path) for opaque registrations. Two genuine cases:
 - ITenantContext / ITenantContextSetter: registered via forwarding lambda 'AddScoped<ITenantContext>(sp => sp.GetRequiredService<TenantContext>())' (Shared.Kernel ServiceCollectionExtensions.cs:16-17) so both interfaces + concrete share ONE request-scoped mutable TenantContext. Service location is REQUIRED here: inlining 'new TenantContext()' would give handlers/middleware a fresh empty tenant instead of the instance the HTTP tenant-resolution middleware populated. Consumed by TenantStamping/TenantRestoring Wolverine middleware (fire on every message) and handlers (CreateBucket, SendNotification/Sms/Email, CreateAnnouncement, Inquiry* SSE handlers).
 - ISetupStatusChecker (behind IsSetupRequiredHandler, invoked by SetupController via messageBus): cleanly registered AddScoped<ISetupStatusChecker,SetupStatusChecker> but its deps UserManager<WallowUser>/RoleManager<WallowRole> are ASP.NET Identity framework factory registrations codegen can't see through, so the whole handler service-locates.

FIX (Wolverine-prescribed, verified against decompiled WolverineFx 6.19.0 + JasperFx 1.18.0): switched to the strict ServiceLocationPolicy.NotAllowed (v6 default, so new accidental service location fails fast at codegen) and opted the three genuinely-opaque types in via opts.CodeGeneration.AlwaysUseServiceLocationFor<T>(). That API registers a LazyServiceLocationVariableSource so those types resolve from the scoped provider (correct behavior preserved) and are NOT emitted as service-location reports -> no warning, no throw. Confirmed AlwaysUseServiceLocationFor<T>() exists on JasperFx.GenerationRules (opts.CodeGeneration) in 1.18.0; the WolverineOptions.ServiceLocationPolicy XML doc explicitly recommends this pattern for opaque lambda factories.

FILES: api/src/Wallow.Api/Program.cs (only file). Added usings: Wallow.Identity.Application.Queries.IsSetupRequired, Wallow.Shared.Kernel.MultiTenancy.
SYMBOLS: no public API changed; Wolverine config only.
BUILD: dotnet build api/Wallow.slnx = 0 errors. dotnet format applied+staged.
TEST_STATUS: build green; host (api) + identity integration slices running under Testcontainers to confirm codegen doesn't throw under NotAllowed for any exercised handler. Will update if any additional opaque type surfaces.
COMMIT: 38cc58c0
AUDIT 2026-07-25 (verify-misc): PARTIALLY_DONE — THE FIX IS STRANDED: commit 38cc58c0 (per the earlier note) is real but sits at the tip of UNMERGED branch chore/post-blazor-cleanup; it is NOT an ancestor of HEAD (refactor/web-blazor-to-react) nor origin/main. At HEAD, Program.cs:186-192 still has ServiceLocationPolicy.AllowedButWarn and rg finds NO AlwaysUseServiceLocationFor anywhere — warnings still live. All three flagged opaque registrations remain exact: ITenantContext/ITenantContextSetter forwarding lambdas (Shared.Kernel ServiceCollectionExtensions.cs:16-17; duplicated SeederService Program.cs:70-71) and ISetupStatusChecker (IdentityInfrastructureExtensions.cs:348, SeederService Program.cs:78; UserManager-dependent impl). IDocumentSession/Marten: no-op for this repo. TITLE PREMISE STALE: already on WolverineFx 6.19.0 (Directory.Packages.props:57-61) — doesn't throw only because of the explicit AllowedButWarn opt-back; this is live tech debt, not a pending-upgrade risk. REMAINING: (1) merge/cherry-pick 38cc58c0 onto the active line (touches only Wallow.Api/Program.cs +22/-7 plus two usings — should pick cleanly); (2) the note's 'pending final host-test confirmation' was NEVER recorded — run ./scripts/run-tests.sh api + integration under NotAllowed before closing.

title: wallow-auth: FocusOnNavigate has no React equivalent (accessibility regression)
description: Blazor's FocusOnNavigate component moved keyboard/screen-reader focus to the main content region on route change. apps/wallow-auth has no equivalent, which is an accessibility regression versus the Blazor baseline.
design: Add a router-level effect (e.g. in __root.tsx or a route-change listener) that moves focus to the main landmark on navigation, mirroring Blazor's FocusOnNavigate behaviour.
acceptance_criteria: Navigating between auth screens (e.g. login -> register) moves DOM focus to the new screen's main content region, verified manually or via a Playwright accessibility check.
notes:
TRIAGE: FIX-NOW. Confirmed as a genuine, unaddressed accessibility regression. The Blazor oracle (api/src/Wallow.Auth/.../Routes.razor) has <FocusOnNavigate RouteData="routeData" Selector="h1" /> wired directly into the router's <Found> block — every route change moves focus to the page's <h1>. grep for 'focus' across apps/wallow-auth/src turns up nothing: no router-level effect, no useEffect on route change, nothing. The target is trivially available: apps/wallow-auth/src/components/auth-layout.tsx renders an <h1> on every screen (auth-layout.tsx:80), so a direct 1:1 port (a route-change effect in routes/__root.tsx's RootComponent or a small hook that finds/focuses the nearest h1 on router.subscribe('onResolved')) is cheap and low-risk. Matches team priority guidance (accessibility regressions matter more than deployment-flexibility items). Recommend: fix now, in-scope for epic.
RED (Wallow-ffpq.2.8): TDD red phase complete. 5 tests, 3 failing for the right reason (focus stays on <body>, no focus logic in scaffold), 2 passing guard/contract tests.

FILES:
- apps/wallow-auth/src/components/focus-on-navigate.tsx (NEW, scaffold only — no focus logic)
- apps/wallow-auth/src/components/focus-on-navigate.test.tsx (NEW, RED spec)

SYMBOLS (scaffolded, to be implemented GREEN):
- export function FocusOnNavigate(): null  — router-level component; mount at root in routes/__root.tsx next to <ReadyIndicator/> (both belong at 'every auth page'). Must move DOM focus to the page's main <h1> after each client-side navigation.
- export const MAIN_HEADING_SELECTOR = 'h1'  — mirrors Blazor Selector='h1'; auth-layout.tsx renders exactly one <h1>/screen (auth-layout.tsx:80ish).

TEST CONTRACT (the 5 cases):
1. pins MAIN_HEADING_SELECTOR === 'h1' (PASSES on scaffold — contract/doc test).
2. moves focus to destination <h1> on client-side nav (login->register) (FAILS).
3. applies tabindex='-1' to the heading so .focus() actually lands AND heading stays out of Tab order (FAILS). NOTE for GREEN: a bare <h1> is not focusable; impl MUST set tabindex=-1 before focus() or jsdom (and real browsers for the tab-order concern) won't focus it. This is the standard SPA route-change focus pattern.
4. focus follows EACH navigation, not a stale heading (FAILS).
5. does NOT steal focus on initial page load — activeElement stays document.body (PASSES on scaffold — regression guard).

GREEN GUIDANCE:
- Consume the real router (e.g. useRouterState select pathname, or router.subscribe('onResolved')); on navigation query document.querySelector('h1'), set tabIndex=-1 if needed, call .focus() (preventScroll ok). Skip the FIRST run/mount so initial load is not hijacked (use a ref-guard). Wire <FocusOnNavigate/> into routes/__root.tsx RootComponent tree. Do NOT edit router.tsx (closed) or test files.

TEST_STATUS=fail (3 target tests red, as intended)

Blazor's FocusOnNavigate fires on initial RouteData too, but the bead's stated rationale is client-side navigation, and stealing focus on first paint is a documented a11y anti-pattern. SYMBOLS: export function FocusOnNavigate(): null; export const MAIN_HEADING_SELECTOR = 'h1'.

IMPLEMENTATION NOTE (root cause the prior attempts missed): keying the effect on state.location.pathname does NOT work. On a client-side nav TanStack re-renders the root with the new location.pathname while the <Outlet/> still shows the OLD route (pending transition); the destination <h1> commits in a LATER render that does not change location.pathname, so a pathname-keyed effect fires against the stale heading (querySelector('h1') returned login-heading). Fix: key on state.resolvedLocation?.pathname — it advances only once the destination route has committed, so the new screen's <h1> is guaranteed in the DOM. title: wallow-auth: per-client_id branding overlay is ported but never called

title: Identity.MfaPartial hardcodes Secure=true — breaks on non-localhost plain-HTTP dev origins
description: api/src/Modules/Identity/Wallow.Identity.Infrastructure/Services/MfaPartialAuthService.cs:42-49 appends the Identity.MfaPartial cookie with Secure = true hardcoded, unlike the durable .AspNetCore.Identity.Application cookie which derives it from environment (IdentityInfrastructureExtensions.cs:163-167: SecurePolicy.SameAsRequest in Development, Always otherwise). On a plain-HTTP origin that the browser does NOT treat as trustworthy, the browser silently drops the cookie and the MFA step breaks with no server-side error. Raised during Wallow-vec7.4.3 and deliberately RULED OUT of its scope — see DESIGN for the reasoning and for why this is low priority rather than a live bug.
design:
SCOPE CALL (made in Wallow-vec7.4.3, recorded here so it is not silently re-litigated): this is NOT a proxy defect and does not belong to 7.4.3. Three reasons: (1) Secure=true here is hardcoded, not policy-derived, so it is unaffected by the X-Forwarded-Proto fix 7.4.3 makes — the API's forwarded scheme has no bearing on it. (2) The wallow-auth proxy relays Set-Cookie verbatim; there is no proxy header/cookie handling change that could fix or break this, and 7.4.3's DESIGN scopes fixes to 'adjust proxy header/cookie handling there [auth-server.ts] if needed'. (3) It therefore has no failing-test surface at 7.4.3's seam.

WHY P3 — NO SUPPORTED PATH IS BROKEN TODAY: prod serves an HTTPS origin, so Secure is correct and desirable there. Local dev is http://localhost:3000/3001 (apps/wallow-auth/dev-server.ts:47-48) and Chromium/Firefox treat http://localhost as a trustworthy origin and DO accept Secure cookies from it. E2E is Chromium-only against localhost (api/tests/Wallow.E2E.Tests/Fixtures/PlaywrightFixture.cs:18). So every path we currently support works.

THE ACTUAL FAILURE MODES (both real but off the supported path): (a) Safari, which historically does NOT accept Secure cookies over http://localhost — anyone doing local dev in Safari hits a silent MFA failure; (b) any non-localhost plain-HTTP origin (LAN IP, docker hostname reached directly from a browser), where no browser treats the origin as trustworthy.

BEFORE FIXING: confirm (a) empirically rather than trusting this note — the Safari/localhost behavior is stated here from general knowledge, not from a test run in this repo, and it is the main thing justifying the bead. If Safari accepts it, this bead is arguably just (b) and could be closed as wontfix.

LIKELY FIX: mirror the durable cookie's pattern — inject IHostEnvironment (or the existing configuration) into MfaPartialAuthService and set Secure = !environment.IsDevelopment(), or thread CookieSecurePolicy through. Do NOT blanket-disable Secure: this is a short-lived credential-bearing cookie on the password-verified-but-not-yet-MFA'd path, so it must stay Secure everywhere except a knowingly-insecure dev origin. Follow project conventions: explicit types not var, [LoggerMessage] source-gen.
acceptance_criteria: Identity.MfaPartial's Secure attribute is environment-derived rather than hardcoded, staying Secure=true outside Development and never weakening prod; the Safari/localhost assumption in DESIGN is confirmed or refuted first and the finding recorded (a refutation may close this wontfix); unit test pins the attribute in both Development and non-Development; ./scripts/run-tests.sh identity green; dotnet format api/Wallow.slnx clean; conventional commit e.g. 'fix(identity): derive mfa partial cookie secure flag from environment'.
close_reason: bead reset 2026-07-17: archived in docs/plans/2026-07-17-bead-archive.md; re-file against React only if still real

title: fix(identity): exchange-ticket drops the absolute returnUrl its own controller sent
description:
Second-order finding traced while fixing Wallow-vec7.3.17. NOT a dead-end and NOT a security hole -- it fails closed -- but the external-login MFA user silently loses their destination.

AccountController.ExchangeTicket (AccountController.cs:590) gates its redirect on 'Url.IsLocalUrl(returnUrl)', which accepts ONLY local/relative URLs. But the SAME controller's external-login-callback (L313/L335) hands /mfa/challenge an ABSOLUTE returnUrl (L273-277 normalizes it through IsAllowedAsync, which REQUIRES UriKind.Absolute, or the absolute authUrl fallback). The MFA screen then threads that value straight back into exchange-ticket.

Result for an external-login + MFA user, post-.3.17: ticket validates, user IS signed in, then IsLocalUrl(absolute) = false -> falls through to 'Redirect(authUrl)' (L595-597). They land on the auth root instead of the returnUrl the flow carried the whole way.

Two validators disagree about the same value on the same controller: IsAllowedAsync says 'absolute or nothing', IsLocalUrl says 'relative or nothing'. Any value that satisfies one is refused by the other.

IMPACT IS SMALL TODAY, which is why this is P3 and was not folded into .3.17: on the external path returnUrl is usually the auth origin anyway (Login.razor:315 sends 'ReturnUrl ?? currentUrl', and a RELATIVE ReturnUrl would already have been refused by external-login at L257-260 since IsAllowedAsync cannot pass one). So authUrl and the intended returnUrl are near-identical in practice. It becomes real as soon as a fork registers a client whose origin is not the auth app.

DO NOT fix by widening IsLocalUrl to accept any absolute URL -- that is an open redirect on a ticket-exchange endpoint. The fix is to accept an absolute returnUrl only when redirectUriValidator.IsAllowedAsync admits it, keeping the authUrl fallback: 'if (!IsNullOrEmpty(returnUrl) && (Url.IsLocalUrl(returnUrl) || await redirectUriValidator.IsAllowedAsync(returnUrl)))'. Same allow-list the flow already used to admit the value, still fail-closed. Needs Wallow.Identity.Tests coverage for both shapes plus the evil-origin refusal.
acceptance_criteria:
1. exchange-ticket honours an ABSOLUTE returnUrl that redirectUriValidator.IsAllowedAsync admits.
2. exchange-ticket still honours a LOCAL/relative returnUrl (no regression on the password path).
3. exchange-ticket still falls back to authUrl for a non-allow-listed absolute returnUrl (https://evil.example.com) -- the open-redirect refusal, fail-closed.
4. exchange-ticket still falls back to authUrl for a blank/missing returnUrl.
5. Unit coverage in api/tests/Modules/Identity for all four shapes.
6. ./scripts/run-tests.sh identity green.
notes:
RED: api/tests/Modules/Identity/Wallow.Identity.Tests/Api/Controllers/AccountControllerExchangeTicketReturnUrlTests.cs — 10 tests, 1 confirmed failing (the bug), 9 passing as regression guards.

SCAFFOLDING: none. The fix is a change inside the EXISTING AccountController.ExchangeTicket (AccountController.cs:590) — no new production types/signatures were needed, so nothing was stubbed.

FILES: api/tests/Modules/Identity/Wallow.Identity.Tests/Api/Controllers/AccountControllerExchangeTicketReturnUrlTests.cs (new, only file touched)
SYMBOLS: public class AccountControllerExchangeTicketReturnUrlTests (no production symbols added)

TEST_STATUS: 1 failing / 9 passing (10 total, isolated run of this class).

THE FAILING TEST (AC1 — this is the bug):
  ExchangeTicket_WithAllowListedAbsoluteReturnUrl_RedirectsToReturnUrl
  Expected redirect.Url 'https://app.example.com/dashboard', actual 'http://localhost:5002' (authUrl).
  Fails for exactly the reason the bead describes: IsAllowedAsync admits the absolute
  returnUrl, but Url.IsLocalUrl(absolute) = false so it falls through to Redirect(authUrl).

PASSING-BY-DESIGN (regression guards — expected green today, must STAY green after the fix):
  AC1  ExchangeTicket_WithAllowListedAbsoluteReturnUrl_StillSignsUserIn (sign-in already happens
       before the redirect branch — this pins that the fix does not disturb it)
  AC2  ExchangeTicket_WithLocalReturnUrl_RedirectsToReturnUrl [Theory x2: /dashboard,
       /organizations/settings?tab=security] — password path, no regression
  AC3  ExchangeTicket_WithNonAllowListedAbsoluteReturnUrl_FallsBackToAuthUrl [Theory x3:
       https://evil.example.com, https://evil.example.com/steal?token=1,
       //evil.example.com/protocol-relative] — open-redirect refusal, fail-closed
  AC4  ExchangeTicket_WithBlankReturnUrl_FallsBackToAuthUrl [Theory x2: null, ""]
  AC4  ExchangeTicket_WithBlankReturnUrl_DoesNotConsultAllowList (pins the IsNullOrEmpty
       short-circuit so the fix cannot start calling the validator on a blank value)

TEST DESIGN NOTES FOR THE GREEN PHASE:
- Exemplar mirrored: AccountControllerTicketReplayTests.cs (same ctor wiring, same
  CreateTicketViaLogin() helper that mints a REAL protected ticket via the login path,
  same EphemeralDataProtectionProvider + substituted IConnectionMultiplexer/IDatabase).
- Redis StringSetAsync is stubbed true in the ctor (ticket not previously exchanged), so the
  replay guard never interferes with these assertions.
- _controller.Url is a REAL UrlHelper over an ActionContext (NOT a substitute) so IsLocalUrl
  keeps production relative-only semantics. A substituted IUrlHelper would return false for
  everything and make AC2 vacuous.
- _redirectUriValidator.IsAllowedAsync is stubbed per-test; NSubstitute returns false by
  default, which is what makes the AC3 evil-origin cases meaningful.
- The AC3 '//evil.example.com/protocol-relative' case is deliberate: IsLocalUrl already
  refuses protocol-relative URLs, and IsAllowedAsync must not admit it either.

ISSUES:
- Only 1 of 10 fails. This is correct for a bug-fix bead: ACs 2/3/4 assert behaviour that is
  already right and must not regress. Do not 'fix' the passing tests.
- The identity suite has 7 OTHER failures right now that are NOT from this bead and NOT
  pre-existing on HEAD — they are concurrent agents' red tests:
  AccountControllerExternalLoginTests.GetExternalProviders_* (6, file is 'M' in git status)
  and Infrastructure/DevelopmentIssuerOriginTests (1, untracked file). AC6
  ('run-tests.sh identity green') cannot be judged on the full suite until those beads land;
  verify this bead with --filter FullyQualifiedName~AccountControllerExchangeTicketReturnUrlTests.
- Reminder from the bead: do NOT widen IsLocalUrl to accept any absolute URL. Expected fix is
  'if (!string.IsNullOrEmpty(returnUrl) && (Url.IsLocalUrl(returnUrl) || await redirectUriValidator.IsAllowedAsync(returnUrl)))'.
GREEN: FILES=api/src/Modules/Identity/Wallow.Identity.Api/Controllers/AccountController.cs (ExchangeTicket, L592-604 only — the other hunks in this file's diff belong to the concurrent external-login and vec7.8 registration agents, NOT this bead).

THE FIX (exactly as the bead prescribed — no widening of IsLocalUrl):
  if (!string.IsNullOrEmpty(returnUrl)
      && (Url.IsLocalUrl(returnUrl) || await redirectUriValidator.IsAllowedAsync(returnUrl)))
Plus a 4-line comment explaining why the absolute shape reaches this endpoint (external-login -> /mfa/challenge -> exchange-ticket) and that the authUrl fallback keeps it fail-closed.

WHY THE OPERAND ORDER MATTERS (pins the passing regression guards):
• IsNullOrEmpty short-circuits FIRST -> the validator is never consulted on a blank value (AC4 DoesNotConsultAllowList stays green).
• IsLocalUrl is evaluated BEFORE IsAllowedAsync -> relative URLs never hit the allow-list, so the password path is unchanged and needs no client registration (AC2 stays green).
• Non-allow-listed absolutes get false from both -> fall through to Redirect(authUrl) (AC3 stays green, incl. the protocol-relative case).

SYMBOLS: none added/changed. Signature of ExchangeTicket(string ticket, string? returnUrl) is untouched; redirectUriValidator was already a primary-ctor dependency, so no DI or call-site changes. IsAllowedAsync's ct defaults, matching the existing L258/L275 call style in this controller.

TEST_STATUS: pass — 10/10 in AccountControllerExchangeTicketReturnUrlTests (scoped run: --filter FullyQualifiedName~AccountControllerExchangeTicketReturnUrlTests, 210ms). The AC1 test that was RED (ExchangeTicket_WithAllowListedAbsoluteReturnUrl_RedirectsToReturnUrl) now returns 'https://app.example.com/dashboard' instead of the authUrl. The 9 regression guards all stayed green — no test file was edited.

dotnet format api/Wallow.slnx run against the changed file; no formatting changes were produced for this hunk.

ISSUES: none blocking. Two notes for the verifier:
• Test runs were deliberately scoped per the spawn instruction (concurrent agents own AccountControllerExternalLoginTests / DevelopmentIssuerOriginTests and the vec7.8 registration work), so a FULL ./scripts/run-tests.sh identity has NOT been run against this change. This hunk touches only the ExchangeTicket redirect branch, so cross-test fallout is unlikely, but a full-module run should happen once the concurrent beads land.
• The bead's own analysis still holds: today authUrl and the intended returnUrl are near-identical on the external path, so this fix is latent-correctness — it becomes observable when a fork registers a client whose origin is not the auth app.
VERIFY:
AC1 ✓ absolute returnUrl admitted by IRedirectUriValidator.IsAllowedAsync honoured — AccountController.cs:592-604 (git diff hunk confirmed, ONLY hunk in this file attributable to this bead; other hunks belong to sibling agents per report and confirmed by diff context). Condition: '!string.IsNullOrEmpty(returnUrl) && (Url.IsLocalUrl(returnUrl) || await redirectUriValidator.IsAllowedAsync(returnUrl))' — matches bead's prescribed fix exactly, operand order preserved (short-circuit on blank, local-first). Test ExchangeTicket_WithAllowListedAbsoluteReturnUrl_RedirectsToReturnUrl passes.
AC2 ✓ local/relative returnUrl still honoured — Url.IsLocalUrl evaluated first, unchanged semantics; ExchangeTicket_WithLocalReturnUrl_RedirectsToReturnUrl[/dashboard, /organizations/settings?tab=security] pass.
AC3 ✓ non-allow-listed absolute falls back to authUrl — ExchangeTicket_WithNonAllowListedAbsoluteReturnUrl_FallsBackToAuthUrl[evil.example.com, evil.example.com/steal, //evil.example.com protocol-relative] all pass; validator stubbed false, confirms fail-closed.
AC4 ✓ blank/missing returnUrl falls back to authUrl, validator not consulted — ExchangeTicket_WithBlankReturnUrl_FallsBackToAuthUrl[null,''] and ExchangeTicket_WithBlankReturnUrl_DoesNotConsultAllowList pass (IsNullOrEmpty short-circuit confirmed via DidNotReceive assertion).
AC5 ✓ unit coverage — api/tests/Modules/Identity/Wallow.Identity.Tests/Api/Controllers/AccountControllerExchangeTicketReturnUrlTests.cs, 10 tests covering all 4 shapes + sign-in regression pin. Ran isolated: 10/10 pass, 187ms.
AC6 ✓ full ./scripts/run-tests.sh identity run (not scoped, per verifier task instructions): 1634 passed / 1 failed / 1635 total. The single failure is Wallow.Identity.Tests.Infrastructure.DevelopmentIssuerOriginTests.DevelopmentIssuer_DoesNotOccupyAPortOwnedByAnotherApp — explicitly out of scope per this bead's sibling Wallow-vec7.4 (untracked new test file, not touched by this bead). All AccountControllerExternalLoginTests (previously reported failing by concurrent agents) now pass — those sibling beads have landed. No other regressions.

SECURITY REVIEW (open-redirect shape): Read OpenIddictRedirectUriValidator.cs (api/src/Modules/Identity/Wallow.Identity.Infrastructure/Services/). IsAllowedAsync builds its allow-list ONLY from: (1) redirect_uris and post_logout_redirect_uris of OpenIddict applications registered via IOpenIddictApplicationManager (admin-controlled OAuth client registrations, cached 5min), and (2) the configured AuthUrl origin. The uri parameter itself is never trusted as an origin source — it is only checked for absolute-URI-parseability then its origin is set-membership tested against the precomputed allow-list. An anonymous caller cannot inject an arbitrary origin into that set. This is the SAME validator instance already used earlier in this controller (external-login callback, admits absolute returnUrl before /mfa/challenge) and by redirect-uri/validate — exchange-ticket now applies identical, pre-existing trust semantics rather than introducing a new trust boundary. Confirmed NOT an open redirect: verified by reading the validator source, not just trusting the report.

CONVENTIONS: dotnet format --verify-no-changes clean on both changed files. LoggerMessage usage unchanged (LogExchangeTicketRedirecting/NoReturnUrl reused, no new raw ILogger calls). No 'var', no TODO/placeholder, comment explains the security rationale in-line as prescribed.

ISSUES: none. Fix matches the bead's prescribed exact code, tests are correctly designed (real UrlHelper preserves IsLocalUrl production semantics, NSubstitute IRedirectUriValidator defaults to false so AC3 is meaningful), full-suite run requested by the coordinator confirms no regression outside the known out-of-scope sibling bead.

title: Use FrozenDictionary for startup-built lookup caches

Replace Dictionary<K,V> with FrozenDictionary<K,V> for lookup tables that are built once at startup and never modified. FrozenDictionary is optimized for read performance with zero-overhead lookups.

Candidate locations:
- Role-to-permission mapping tables (PermissionExpansionMiddleware)
- Module registry lookups (FoundryModules.cs)
- Feature flag default values cache
- Any static/readonly Dictionary<> fields used for configuration mapping

Steps:

2. Replace with FrozenDictionary where the data is built once and only read thereafter
3. Use .ToFrozenDictionary() extension method
4. Namespace: System.Collections.Frozen (available since .NET 8, no new package needed)

Note: Only use for truly immutable lookup data. Do NOT use for caches that need invalidation.

title: SEC2: Add plugin system security controls
description:
## Vulnerability (NEW-API-8, MEDIUM, Risk Score 8)

PluginLoader.cs loads DLLs from a configured directory and executes Activator.CreateInstance on any IFoundryPlugin class. Plugins run with full host process permissions - access to all tenant data, infrastructure credentials, and services. No sandboxing exists beyond assembly load context isolation.

## Files to Modify
- src/Shared/Foundry.Shared.Infrastructure.Plugins/PluginLoader.cs
- src/Shared/Foundry.Shared.Infrastructure.Plugins/PluginAssemblyLoadContext.cs
- New: PluginManifest.cs, RestrictedServiceProvider.cs

## Remediation (defense-in-depth, since .NET doesn't support AppDomain sandboxing)
1. Plugin allow-list: Only load plugins whose DLL hash matches an approved manifest
2. Plugin manifest validation: Require declared permissions, validate at load time
3. DI scope restriction: Provide plugins with a restricted IServiceProvider that excludes sensitive services (no direct DB context, no IConfiguration with secrets)
4. File integrity verification: Verify DLL hashes against manifest before loading
5. Logging: Log all plugin loads with hash and source

## Testing
- Verify only allow-listed plugins load
- Verify plugins cannot access restricted services
- Verify unsigned/unmanifested plugins are rejected
- Verify plugin load events are logged

title: SEC2: Add participant check to SendMessage controller

## Vulnerability (CS-3, MEDIUM, Risk Score 6)

MarkConversationReadHandler.cs:12-30 loads a conversation and calls MarkReadBy(command.UserId) without verifying the user is a participant. While the domain method is a no-op for non-participants, it confirms conversation existence (IDOR). title: Qodana Phase 5: Dead Code Cleanup (~280 issues)
description: Review and remove unused non-private members (173), unused types (30), unused parameters (30), members not accessed via base type (49), unused return values (23), visibility reductions (22), and misc dead code. CAUTION: Many may be used via reflection, serialization, or Wolverine handler discovery. Each needs manual review. Grouped by module.

title: Qodana Phase 4: C# Modernization (~1,500 issues)
description: Apply modern C# syntax across the codebase: target-typed new() (1004), collection expressions (304), primary constructors (169), object/collection initializers (48), init-only properties (63), pattern merging (22), nameof for enums (29), and misc style improvements. Most are IDE-automatable. Grouped by module for parallel execution.

title: I11: Fix inconsistent GitHub Actions versions
description: Files: .github/workflows/security.yml:24, .github/workflows/ci.yml:17, .github/workflows/publish.yml:72. Issue: setup-dotnet@v4 vs setup-dotnet@v5. Trivy uses @master (unstable). Fix: Standardize all setup-dotnet to @v5. Pin trivy-action to a specific version tag.

title: I12: Remove BuildServiceProvider anti-pattern in Communications
description: File: src/Modules/Communications/Foundry.Communications.Infrastructure/Extensions/CommunicationsModuleExtensions.cs:119-124. Issue: BuildServiceProvider() called inside DI registration to log a warning about unrecognized email provider. Fix: Use a different logging approach during registration (e.g., Console.WriteLine, or defer the validation to runtime via a hosted service or startup filter).

title: I10: Add Dependabot grouping strategy
description: File: .github/dependabot.yml. Issue: Simple config with no groups. Each dependency update creates a separate PR. Fix: Add groups for nuget (e.g., microsoft-*, aspnet-*, ef-core-*, test-*) and github-actions to batch related updates.

title: I9: Fix Trivy scan ordering in publish workflow
description: File: .github/workflows/publish.yml:59-77. Issue: Docker image pushed before Trivy scan. Vulnerable images published before scanning. Fix: Use load: true instead of push: true in build step, run Trivy scan, then push in a separate step only if scan passes.

title: Q12: Fix Payment.Create() misleading domain event
description: File: src/Modules/Billing/Foundry.Billing.Domain/Entities/Payment.cs:65-70\nIssue: PaymentReceivedDomainEvent fires at creation (status=Pending), not when payment is actually received. Complete() method raises no event.\nFix: Rename to PaymentCreatedDomainEvent, or move the event to the Complete() method and rename appropriately.

title: I8: Pin Docker image tags for Mailpit and Grafana
description: Files: docker/docker-compose.yml:34,110, docker/docker-compose.dev.yml:18, docker/docker-compose.staging.yml:24. Issue: Using :latest tags for Mailpit and Grafana LGTM. Fix: Pin to specific version tags (e.g., axllent/mailpit:v1.x.x, grafana/otel-lgtm:0.x.x).

title: Q10: Add duplicate participant check to Conversation
description: File: src/Modules/Communications/Foundry.Communications.Domain/Messaging/Entities/Conversation.cs:49-64,91-106\nIssue: AddParticipant() and CreateGroup() allow duplicate participants. If creatorId is in memberIds, the creator is added twice.\nFix: Add uniqueness check in AddParticipant(). In CreateGroup(), deduplicate memberIds and ensure creatorId is not duplicated.

title: Q9: Upgrade Storage entities to AggregateRoot
description: Files: StoredFile.cs:12, StorageBucket.cs:15\nIssue: Both extend Entity<T> instead of AggregateRoot<T>. Cannot raise domain events, no audit trail.\nFix: Change both to extend AggregateRoot<T> (or AuditableEntity<T> for audit trail). Add domain events for file upload/delete and bucket creation if appropriate.

title: Q6: Clean up IAuditableEntity dead code
description: File: src/Shared/Foundry.Shared.Kernel/Domain/AuditableEntity.cs:45-54\nIssue: Interface defined but never implemented. Zero references. Misleading contract.\nFix: Delete the IAuditableEntity interface. If the interface is intended for future use, implement it on AuditableEntity<TId> instead.

title: Q5: Replace DateTime.UtcNow with TimeProvider in infrastructure and application layers
